proximal convoluted tubule.definition: A section of the nephron in the kidney cortex after Bowman's capsule, lined by simple cuboidal cells with a dense apical brush border; it reabsorbs the majority of filtered solutes and water (about 65–70%), including Na+, Cl−, glucose, and amino acids, reclaims bicarbonate, and secretes hydrogen ions and organic acids, thereby supporting isotonic reabsorption of filtrate and maintenance of acid–base balance.

distal convoluted tubule.definition: A segment of the nephron after the loop of Henle that reabsorbs sodium and chloride via the Na-Cl cotransporter, is largely impermeable to water, and participates in calcium reabsorption and potassium secretion under hormonal control (e.g., aldosterone and PTH).

bowman’s capsule.definition: A cup-shaped, double-walled structure surrounding the glomerulus in the kidney; collects filtrate from the blood (Bowman's space) and marks the start of the nephron's tubular system.

glomerulus.definition: A tuft of capillaries in the nephron’s renal corpuscle (within Bowman's capsule) where plasma is filtered to form the glomerular filtrate; filtration occurs across the glomerular filtration barrier, which includes fenestrated endothelium, a glomerular basement membrane, and podocyte slit diaphragms.

descending limb of henle.definition: Portion of the loop of Henle that descends into the medulla; it is highly permeable to water but relatively impermeable to solutes, so water reabsorption concentrates the tubular fluid as it moves downward, helping establish the medullary osmotic gradient.

thick ascending limb of henle.definition: A segment of the nephron within the loop of Henle, between the thin ascending limb and the distal tubule; it has a thick epithelium and high metabolic activity, is impermeable to water, and reabsorbs Na+, K+, and 2Cl− via the NKCC2 transporter, contributing to the medullary osmotic gradient and to dilution of tubular fluid as part of the countercurrent multiplier system.

thin ascending limb of henle.definition: Part of the loop of Henle in the nephron; a thin-walled segment that is impermeable to water but permeable to solutes, allowing passive reabsorption of Na+ and Cl− and contributing to the dilution of tubular fluid and the medullary osmotic gradient.

loop of henle.definition: AU-shaped segment of the nephron in the kidney that extends into the medulla; the descending limb is permeable to water, while the thick ascending limb actively reabsorbs ions (Na+, K+, Cl−) and is relatively impermeable to water, creating a medullary osmotic gradient used to concentrate urine (countercurrent multiplier).

papilla.definition: A small, nipple-like projection on a tissue or organ, formed by a core of connective tissue covered by epithelium; examples include dermal papillae at the base of hair follicles and lingual papillae on the tongue that bear taste buds.

collecting duct.definition: A segment of the kidney nephron that collects urine from several distal tubules; located mainly in the renal medulla; concentrates urine by reabsorbing water under ADH and reabsorbs Na+ under aldosterone, with intercalated cells contributing to acid–base balance; drains into the papillary (Ducts of Bellini) ducts.

nephron.definition: The microscopic functional unit of the kidney that filters blood to form urine; consists of the renal corpuscle (glomerulus and Bowman's capsule) and the renal tubule (proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule, collecting duct), where filtration, reabsorption, and secretion occur.

hair shaft.definition: A keratinized, nonliving portion of the hair that extends above the skin surface; produced by the hair follicle’s matrix and composed of the cuticle, cortex, and, in thicker hairs, the medulla.

stratum corneum.definition: The most superficial layer of the epidermis.

stratum granulosum.definition: The granular layer of the epidermis, located between the stratum spinosum and stratum corneum, comprising about 3–5 layers of keratinocytes that are undergoing keratinization; these cells contain keratohyalin granules and lamellar bodies and progressively lose their nuclei to form the stratum corneum.

stratum spinosum.definition: The second, or prickle cell, layer of the epidermis above the stratum basale and below the stratum granulosum, consisting of several keratinocyte layers bound by desmosomes; it provides mechanical strength and contains Langerhans immune cells.

stratum basale.definition: A single, mitotically active layer of keratinocytes at the base of the epidermis, resting on the basement membrane; it serves as the source of new epidermal cells and contains melanocytes and Merkel cells.

dermis.definition: The dermis is the thick, inner layer of the skin between the epidermis and the subcutaneous tissue, consisting mainly of connective tissue with collagen and elastin fibers; it contains blood vessels, nerves, hair follicles, and glands, and provides structural support and nourishment to the epidermis.

epidermis.definition: The outer layer of your skin.

hypodermis.definition: The layer of tissue beneath the dermis, consisting mainly of adipose (fat) and connective tissue (subcutaneous tissue); it stores fat, insulates the body, cushions underlying structures, and contains larger blood vessels and nerves.

meissner corpuscle.definition: A rapidly adapting mechanoreceptor in the dermal papillae of glabrous skin (notably fingertips and lips) that detects light touch and low-frequency vibration.

pacinian corpuscle.definition: A large, encapsulated mechanoreceptor in the skin formed by a nerve ending surrounded by concentric lamellae; it detects high-frequency vibration and deep pressure and is rapidly adapting.

hair follicle.definition: A small sac in the skin from which a hair grows; it anchors the hair and contains the hair bulb and root sheath, along with associated structures such as the sebaceous gland and arrector pili muscle.

arrector pili muscle.definition: Small smooth muscle in the dermis attached to a hair follicle; its contraction causes the hair to stand erect (piloerection) and produces goosebumps, innervated by the sympathetic nervous system.

sweat gland.definition: An exocrine skin gland that produces sweat; the two main types are eccrine (merocrine) glands, which are widely distributed and secrete a dilute fluid for thermoregulation, and apocrine glands, located in hair-bearing areas and secreting a thicker fluid that can produce odor when acted on by skin bacteria.

subcutaneous layer.definition: The layer of tissue beneath the dermis of the skin, composed mainly of adipose (fat) tissue and loose connective tissue, containing larger blood vessels and nerves; provides insulation, energy storage, cushioning, and anchors the skin to underlying structures.

external ear.definition: The outer portion of the ear, consisting of the auricle (pinna) and the external auditory canal; it collects sound waves and funnels them toward the tympanic membrane.

auricle.definition: In anatomy, the auricle refers to the external ear (pinna), the visible cartilaginous structure that collects sound; it also denotes the small pouch-like atrial appendage of the heart.

pinna.definition: A visible, external part of the ear composed of cartilage and skin that collects sound waves and funnels them into the external auditory canal, contributing to sound localization.

external acoustic meatus.definition: A canal in the external ear that conducts sound waves from the auricle to the tympanic membrane; it comprises a lateral cartilaginous portion and a medial bony portion and is lined with skin bearing hairs and ceruminous glands.

semicircular canals.definition: A set of three loop-shaped, fluid-filled passages in the inner ear that detect rotational head movements by endolymph movement bending hair cells in the crista ampullaris of each ampulla, contributing to balance.

oval window.definition: A membrane-covered opening in the vestibule of the inner ear that forms the boundary between the middle ear and the cochlea; the footplate of the stapes sits in it and it transmits vibrations from the middle ear into the cochlear fluids. Also known as fenestra ovalis.

vestibular nerve.definition: A sensory branch of the vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII) that transmits afferent signals from the inner ear's vestibular apparatus (utricle, saccule, and semicircular canals) to the brain, helping to maintain balance and spatial orientation; it has superior and inferior divisions.

cochlear nerve.definition: An afferent component of the vestibulocochlear nerve (cranial nerve VIII) that carries auditory information from hair cells in the cochlea to the brainstem; its cell bodies reside in the spiral (spiral ganglion) and it synapses in the cochlear nuclei.

cochlea.definition: Part of the ear that converts sound into electrical signals that the brain interprets as a particular sound.

round window.definition: A membrane-covered opening in the medial wall of the middle ear, leading to the basal turn of the cochlea (fenestra rotunda); it relieves pressure in the inner ear by allowing perilymph movement when the oval window is driven by the stapes.

auditory tube.definition: A narrow osseocartilaginous canal that connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx; it is normally closed and opens briefly during swallowing or yawning to equalize middle-ear pressure and drain secretions. Also known as the Eustachian tube.

malleus.definition: One of the three auditory ossicles in the middle ear; it connects the tympanic membrane to the incus and transmits sound vibrations. Also known as the hammer.

stapes.definition: A small stirrup-shaped bone in the middle ear; the innermost of the auditory ossicles that transmits vibrations from the incus to the oval window of the cochlea.

auditory ossicles.definition: Three tiny middle-ear bones—the malleus (hammer), incus (anvil), and stapes (stirrup)—that transmit and amplify sound vibrations from the tympanic membrane to the oval window of the inner ear, acting as a lever system to boost pressure and enable cochlear fluid movement.

optic disk.definition: The front surface of the optic nerve, where all the retinal nerve fibers come together to carry an image to the brain.

lacrimal caruncle.definition: A small, pink mass at the inner corner of the eyelid (medial canthus) consisting of skin-bearing tissue with hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and sweat glands.

pupil.definition: The dark, circular opening in the middle of the iris of the eye.

lens.definition: The transparent, biconvex, avascular structure of the eye that focuses light onto the retina; its curvature is adjusted by the ciliary muscles to enable accommodation.

visual axis.definition: A line joining the fovea to the object of regard (fixation point) that passes through the eye’s nodal point; it represents the direction of gaze.

cornea.definition: The clear dome that covers the front of the eye.

iris.definition: The pigmented, circular diaphragm of the eye that regulates the size of the pupil and thus the amount of light reaching the retina; it lies between the cornea and lens and contains the sphincter and dilator pupillae muscles.

ciliary body.definition: Part of the eye that produces the aqueous humor (fluid that nourishes the eye) and contains the ciliary muscle, which controls focusing of the lens.

suspensory ligament.definition: A fibrous band that attaches an organ to surrounding structures to support and suspend it, maintaining its position within the body; for example, the zonular fibers suspend the lens, and a peritoneal fold anchors the ovary to the pelvic wall.

retina.definition: The innermost layer of the eye, which converts light energy to electrical energy and sends visual images to the brain via the optic nerve.

choroid.definition: A thin layer of blood vessels and connective tissue between the white of the eye (sclera) and the retina.

sclera.definition: The white of the eye; a tough, protective coating of collagen and elastic tissue that, with the cornea, makes up the outer layer of the eyeball.

fovea centralis.definition: Small depression in the retina at the center of the macula lutea containing a high density of cone photoreceptors, lacking rods, with thinning of inner retinal layers and avascularity, enabling very high-acuity, color vision in bright light.

macula.definition: The area in the center of the retina that produces sharp, clear central vision and allows one to see fine detail.

central retinal artery and vein.definition: An end artery supplying the inner retina, arising from the ophthalmic artery and traveling within the optic nerve to give rise to retinal arterioles.

the principal venous drainage of the ret.word: The principal venous drainage of the retina
the principal venous drainage of the ret.definition: Formed by retinal venules and traveling with the optic nerve to exit the eye and drain into the cavernous sinus (often via the superior ophthalmic vein).

canal of schlemm.definition: A circular venous channel at the limbus that drains aqueous humor from the anterior chamber into the episcleral veins; part of the conventional aqueous humor outflow pathway.

aqueous humor.definition: Clear fluid that fills the front part of the eye.

vitreous humor.definition: The clear, gel-like substance that fills the space behind the lens of the eye and supports the shape of the rear portion of the eye.

posterior chamber.definition: The part of the eye behind the iris and in front of the lens that is filled with aqueous humor.

anterior chamber.definition: A fluid-filled space in the anterior segment of the eye, between the cornea and the iris (and lens), containing aqueous humor and helping maintain intraocular pressure.

scleral venous sinus.definition: A circular venous channel at the limbus in the sclera that collects aqueous humor from the anterior chamber and drains it into the episcleral venous system; it is part of the conventional outflow pathway and is also known as the canal of Schlemm.

cribriform plate.definition: The sieve-like part of the ethmoid bone forming the roof of the nasal cavity and the floor of the anterior cranial fossa, perforated by numerous foramina that transmit olfactory nerve fibers from the nasal mucosa to the olfactory bulbs.

ethmoid bone.definition: A light, spongy cranial bone between the orbits, forming part of the anterior skull base and the medial walls of the orbits; it contributes to the roof of the nasal cavity and contains the perpendicular plate (nasal septum), the cribriform plate with olfactory foramina, and the ethmoidal air cell labyrinth.

frontal sinus.definition: One of the paired paranasal sinuses located in the frontal bone above the orbits; drains into the nasal cavity via the frontonasal duct, typically into the middle meatus.

perpendicular plate of ethmoid.definition: A thin vertical bony plate of the ethmoid bone that forms the superior portion of the nasal septum, descending from the cribriform plate and articulating with the vomer to separate the nasal cavities.

septal cartilage.definition: A plate of hyaline cartilage forming the anterior portion of the nasal septum, providing structural support and dividing the nasal cavity into two nostrils.

vomeronasal cartilage.definition: A small piece of cartilage that supports the vomeronasal (Jacobson’s) organ in the nasal cavity, a chemosensory structure for detecting pheromones; in humans the organ is vestigial.

vomer.definition: A thin, flat, unpaired bone forming the inferior portion of the nasal septum in the midline; it articulates superiorly with the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid and inferiorly with the palatine processes of the maxilla and the palatine bone, contributing to the bony nasal septum.

palatine bone.definition: A paired, irregularly shaped facial bone forming the posterior part of the hard palate and contributing to the floor of the orbit and the lateral wall of the nasal cavity.

cribriform plate of ethmoid bone.definition: A sieve-like portion of the ethmoid bone that forms part of the floor of the anterior cranial fossa and the roof of the nasal cavity, perforated by olfactory foramina for the passage of olfactory nerve fibers (CN I) from the nasal mucosa to the olfactory bulbs.

incisive foramen.definition: A small midline opening on the hard palate just posterior to the maxillary central incisors; the oral end of the incisive canal, through which the nasopalatine nerve and accompanying vessels pass between the nasal cavity and the oral cavity.

crista galli of ethmoid bone.definition: A vertical median ridge of the ethmoid bone that projects upward from the cribriform plate in the anterior cranial fossa and serves as the attachment site for the falx cerebri.

central incisor.definition: A front tooth located at the midline of the upper or lower jaw; one of the two central incisors in an arch, typically with a broad, chisel-shaped crown and a single root, used for cutting food.

incisive canal.definition: An anatomical passage within the maxilla that runs from the nasal cavity to the incisive foramen at the anterior hard palate, carrying the nasopalatine nerve and accompanying blood vessels (nasopalatine artery and veins).

palatine process of maxilla.definition: The palatine process of the maxilla is the horizontal extension of the maxilla that forms the anterior portion of the hard palate; the two processes fuse at the midline (intermaxillary suture) and with the horizontal plates of the palatine bones to form the bony roof of the mouth.

horizontal plate of palatine bone.definition: The horizontal plate is the horizontal (posterior) portion of the palatine bone that forms the posterior part of the hard palate and contributes to the floor of the nasal cavity; it articulates anteriorly with the palatine process of the maxilla and with the opposite palatine bone along the midline.

sphenoid bone.definition: An unpaired, butterfly-shaped bone at the skull base that articulates with all cranial bones; it has a central body containing the sphenoidal sinuses and greater/lesser wings with the pterygoid processes, forming part of the cranial base and orbital walls and housing the sella turcica for the pituitary gland.

sphenoid sinus.definition: An air-filled cavity within the body of the sphenoid bone, one of the paranasal sinuses, located posterior to the nasal cavity; it communicates with the nasal cavity via an ostium and is lined with respiratory mucosa.

sella turcica.definition: A saddle-shaped depression in the sphenoid bone at the base of the skull that houses the pituitary gland (hypophysis).

superior nasal concha.definition: One of the three scroll-like bony shelves on the lateral wall of the nasal cavity, formed by the ethmoid bone, that increases mucosal surface area to warm, humidify, and filter inspired air.

middle nasal concha.definition: A thin, curved bony plate formed by the ethmoid bone that projects into the nasal cavity, forming part of the lateral wall and the upper boundary of the middle meatus; one of the nasal turbinates.

inferior nasal concha.definition: A scroll-like bony plate on the lateral wall of the nasal cavity that is covered by mucosa and increases surface area to warm, humidify, and filter inhaled air.

nasal septum.definition: A partition inside the nose that divides the nasal cavity into right and left halves; anteriorly formed by the septal cartilage and posteriorly by the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone and the vomer, all covered by nasal mucosa.

paranasal sinuses.definition: Air-filled cavities in the skull bones surrounding the nasal cavity, connected to the nasal cavity by small openings; lined with respiratory epithelium and mucous-secreting cells, draining mucus into the nasal cavity. They include the maxillary, frontal, ethmoidal, and sphenoidal sinuses and function to lighten the skull, humidify and warm inspired air, produce mucus, and contribute to voice resonance.

nasal concha.definition: Scroll-like bony shelves inside the nasal cavity (superior, middle, and inferior nasal conchae) covered with mucosa; they warm, humidify, and filter inhaled air by increasing surface area and creating turbulent airflow.

opening of auditory tube.definition: The pharyngeal (nasopharyngeal) opening of the Eustachian tube, the passage that connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx and helps equalize middle-ear pressure.

aaron’s sign.definition: A sign of peritoneal irritation from acute appendicitis in which palpation of the abdomen provokes pain referred to the epigastric region.

mcburney’s point.definition: A surface landmark in the right lower quadrant about one-third of the distance from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus, used to assess for appendicitis; tenderness at this point suggests appendiceal inflammation.

aarskog syndrome.definition: An X-linked genetic disorder characterized by facial dysmorphism (e.g., hypertelorism, ptosis, broad nasal bridge), short stature, limb/skeletal and genital anomalies (shawl scrotum in males); caused by mutations in the FGD1 gene.

aase’s syndrome.definition: A rare congenital syndrome characterized by macrothrombocytopenia (giant platelets) and skeletal abnormalities, resulting in a bleeding tendency due to defective platelet production.

abacavir.definition: A nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used in combination antiretroviral therapy to treat HIV-1 infection; a guanosine analogue that inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase after intracellular phosphorylation.

tau protein.definition: An axonally enriched microtubule-associated phosphoprotein that stabilizes microtubules by binding to tubulin; hyperphosphorylation causes detachment from microtubules and aggregation into neurofibrillary tangles seen in Alzheimer's disease and other tauopathies.

amyloid.definition: A protein that collects in tissues when certain diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease, are present.

alzheimer’s disease.definition: A progressive brain disease that causes memory loss, impaired thinking, and personality changes.

amyloid precursor protein.definition: A normal brain protein that under certain circumstances produces beta amyloid, abnormal protein deposited in the brain in Alzheimer’s disease. Usually abbreviated as APP.

abapical.definition: Pertaining to or located away from the apex of a structure; opposite of apical; toward the base or root.

abdomen.definition: The region of the trunk between the diaphragm and the pelvic inlet that contains most abdominal viscera (e.g., stomach, intestines, liver, pancreas, spleen, kidneys); bounded anteriorly by the abdominal wall and musculature, laterally by the body wall, and posteriorly by the vertebral column.

aorta.definition: The large artery emerging from the heart's left ventricle that distributes blood to the body.

abarelix.definition: A gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) receptor antagonist that rapidly suppresses luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone release, thereby lowering testosterone production; used in the palliation of advanced prostate cancer and given by injection, with a risk of severe hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis) and withdrawal from some markets.

prostate.definition: A gland in the male body that makes semen.

cancer.definition: Occurs when new cells grow rapidly, even when they are not needed. These cells crowd out other cells. Cancer can occur anyplace in your body. There are many types of cancer, including those that begin in your blood (leukemia), in specific organs (kidney cancer) or tissues (soft tissue sarcoma).

pregnancy.definition: When you are expecting a baby.

latex.definition: Milky fluid produced by rubber trees (notably Hevea brasiliensis) that coagulates to form natural rubber; can trigger allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

allergy.definition: An immune system reaction (for example, rash, fever, sneezing, or headaches) to something that is normally harmless.

lactation.definition: Using the milk from a mother's breast to feed a baby.

hypersensitivity.definition: When your body has more of a reaction to 1) things that you see, hear, touch, or smell or 2) drugs, pollen from plants, food, or insect stings.

breast.definition: Paired mammary glands on the anterior chest wall that produce milk during lactation; each breast contains glandular lobes and lobules with ducts converging on the nipple, surrounded by connective tissue and fat, with an areola surrounding the nipple.

enlargement.definition: A general increase in the size or volume of a body part or organ; in medicine, enlargement may result from hypertrophy, hyperplasia, edema, inflammation, or tumor growth.

nipple.definition: A raised projection on the breast or udder that contains the openings of the lactiferous (milk) ducts and serves as the milk outlet; surrounded by the pigmented areola and present in both sexes but typically more prominent in females.

tenderness.definition: Pain or discomfort elicited by palpation of a body area; a clinical sign indicating inflammation, injury, or pathology in the underlying tissues.

injection.definition: The administration of a drug or other substance into the body through a needle and syringe, typically by intradermal, subcutaneous, intramuscular, or intravenous routes.

site.definition: In medicine, the exact location in the body where a disease process, injury, or clinical finding is occurring or being studied (e.g., site of infection, lesion, injection site).

reactions.definition: The body's responses to a stimulus, such as immune responses to foreign substances (antigens or pathogens) or inflammatory processes; in pharmacology, it also refers to adverse drug reactions.

bone.definition: Hard connective tissue that forms the skeleton; composed of a mineralized collagen matrix (primarily hydroxyapatite) with bone-forming and bone-resorbing cells, providing structural support, protecting organs, enabling movement, storing calcium and phosphate, and housing bone marrow.

density.definition: A measure of mass per unit volume of a substance (e.g., g/cm^3 or kg/m^3); in medicine, it describes how densely matter is packed in tissues or bones and affects radiographic attenuation.

anaphylaxis.definition: A serious allergic reaction that happens quickly and can be fatal.

systemic.definition: Something that is all through your body.

allergic.definition: Having a sensitivity to one or more normally harmless substances.

headache.definition: A pain or discomfort in the head or upper neck region, which can be a primary headache (migraine, tension-type, cluster) or secondary to another medical condition.

dizziness.definition: When you feel lightheaded, woozy, or confused.

fatigue.definition: A tired, weak feeling of the whole body; feeling tired all over.

nausea.definition: A subjective sensation of abdominal discomfort with an urge to vomit; may occur with pregnancy, motion sickness, gastroenteritis, medications, or other medical conditions.

constipation.definition: A symptom defined by infrequent or difficult passage of stools, often with hard, dry stools and straining, commonly considered as fewer than three bowel movements per week.

diarrhea.definition: Loose, watery stools three or more times a day. It can be sudden (due to a virus, for example), persistent, or chronic, that is, lasting a long time.

dysuria.definition: When it is difficult or painful to pee.

urinary.definition: Relating to urine or to the urinary system (the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra).

frequency.definition: The rate at which a repeating event occurs within a defined period of time; in clinical contexts it is often expressed as occurrences per unit time (e.g., heartbeats per minute).

retention.definition: In medicine, retention is the inability to expel a bodily substance or the abnormal accumulation of it, most commonly urinary retention (incomplete bladder emptying) or fluid retention (edema).

back.definition: The posterior (dorsal) aspect of the trunk, extending from the neck to the buttocks, comprising the vertebral column and the structures overlying it, including muscles, ligaments, nerves, and skin.

pain.definition: An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with actual or potential tissue damage.

hot.definition: Relating to elevated body or tissue temperature; in medicine, "hot" commonly refers to fever (pyrexia) when core body temperature is elevated above normal (generally >38°C/100.4°F), and can also describe warm or inflamed tissue due to infection or inflammation.

flashes.definition: Brief, transient episodes; in medicine, commonly used for hot flashes (sudden warmth with sweating and facial flushing during menopause) and photopsias (brief flashes or specks of light seen in the visual field, which can occur with migraine or retinal/optic disorders).

abarognosis.definition: Loss or impairment of the ability to perceive the weight of objects held in the hand by touch, a form of tactile agnosia due to somatosensory dysfunction.

abasia.definition: Inability to walk or stand due to impaired gait coordination or balance, not explained by muscle weakness.

astasia.definition: Inability to stand upright or maintain an upright posture due to impaired postural stability despite preserved muscle strength, typically from dysfunction in balance-control systems (vestibular, cerebellar, or proprioceptive pathways).

abatacept.definition: A CTLA-4–Ig fusion protein that blocks T-cell activation by binding to CD80 and CD86 on antigen-presenting cells, preventing the CD28 costimulatory signal; used as a biologic DMARD for autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

rheumatoid.definition: Relating to rheumatism; describing inflammatory joint disease, typically autoimmune in origin.

arthritis.definition: A disease of the joints that causes swelling, pain, heat, and stiffness.

angioedema.definition: Swelling of the deeper layers of the skin and mucous membranes, typically affecting the face, lips, tongue, or throat, caused by increased vascular permeability; can be allergic (histamine-mediated) or bradykinin-mediated and may threaten the airway if laryngeal edema occurs.

hypotension.definition: When your blood pressure is low. For some people, this is normal, but it may cause problems for other people.

cough.definition: A sudden, forceful expulsion of air from the lungs initiated by a protective reflex in response to irritation of the airway mucosa, aimed at clearing mucus, irritants, or foreign material; it can be acute or chronic and may be productive (with sputum) or nonproductive (dry).

rhinitis.definition: Inflammation of the nasal mucosa causing congestion, runny nose (rhinorrhea), sneezing, and itching; commonly due to allergic, infectious, or irritant triggers and may be seasonal or perennial.

upper.definition: Situated toward the head or above another structure; in anatomy, used to denote the superior portion of a part (e.g., the upper extremity refers to the arm, the upper airway to the nose–pharynx–larynx, the upper GI tract to the esophagus and stomach).

respiratory.definition: Relating to respiration or the respiratory system; involving breathing and the organs that perform gas exchange, principally the lungs and airways.

tract.definition: A tract is a bundle of nerve fibers in the central nervous system that transmits impulses between brain regions, and in broader usage can refer to a tubular passage or channel in the body (for example, the digestive tract or urinary tract).

aortography.definition: An imaging procedure in which a contrast agent is injected into the aorta to visualize the aorta and its major branches on X-ray or cross‑sectional imaging, used to diagnose aneurysms, dissections, occlusions, and other aortic diseases.

aponeurosis.definition: A flat, broad sheet of dense connective tissue that acts as a tendon, attaching a muscle to bone or to another structure, and distributing the muscle's tensile force over a wide area.

arteries.definition: Blood vessels that transport blood away from the heart to tissues throughout the body; in systemic circulation they usually carry oxygenated blood, whereas the pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood. They have thick, muscular walls with elastic fibers to withstand high pressure and regulate blood flow, and they branch into smaller arterioles. Their walls contain three layers: intima, media, and adventitia.

celiac.definition: A major arterial branch of the abdominal aorta that supplies the foregut organs (stomach, liver, spleen, pancreas, duodenum, etc.).

celiac disease.definition: A chronic autoimmune disorder in which ingestion of gluten (a protein in wheat, barley, and rye) triggers an immune response that damages the small intestinal mucosa (villous atrophy) in genetically predisposed individuals, causing malabsorption; treated with a lifelong gluten-free diet.

superior.definition: Towards the top half of the body, where the head is.

mesenteric.definition: Relating to the mesentery, the peritoneal fold that attaches the intestines to the posterior abdominal wall and contains vessels, nerves, and lymphatics supplying the intestines.

inferior.definition: Towards the bottom of the body, away from the head.

middle.definition: Central portion or point; located at or near the middle. In anatomy, the midline refers to an imaginary line or plane that divides the body into left and right halves and to structures situated near that line.

suprarenal.definition: Situated above the kidney; of or relating to the adrenal glands.

testicular.definition: Relating to the testis (the male reproductive gland) or to the testes.

ovarian.definition: Relating to the ovary; pertaining to the ovaries.

iliac.definition: Relating to the ilium, the large wing-shaped bone that forms the upper part of each side of the pelvis.

inguinal.definition: Relating to the groin; the area of the lower abdomen near the junction with the thigh, including structures such as the inguinal canal and inguinal ligament.

abdominohysterectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which the uterus is removed via an abdominal incision.

uterus.definition: Womb, or where a baby grows when a woman is pregnant.

cyst.definition: Pus or other liquid under your skin.

ectopic.definition: Located or occurring in an abnormal place; outside the usual or normal anatomical location.

placenta.definition: The part of the mother’s womb that supplies oxygen and nutrition to her unborn baby.

paracentesis.definition: A procedure to remove fluid from the peritoneal cavity by inserting a needle or catheter through the abdominal wall, often to relieve ascites or obtain ascitic fluid for diagnostic analysis.

fimbriated.definition: Having fimbriae; fringe-like, finger-like projections or a fringed margin.

fallopian.definition: Relating to the fallopian tubes, the paired ducts that transport eggs from the ovaries to the uterus.

tube.definition: A hollow cylindrical medical device used as a conduit to deliver or remove fluids and gases, or to maintain access to a body cavity or airway; it may be inserted into the body for ventilation, feeding, drainage, or administration of medications.

embryo.definition: An unborn baby, age 5 weeks to 10 weeks.

fetus.definition: An unborn baby, from 12 weeks of age to birth.

ligament.definition: The tissue that connects a bone to another bone.

pelvic.definition: Relating to the pelvis; the basin-shaped bony structure at the base of the spine formed by the hip bones, sacrum, and coccyx, or to the pelvic cavity and its contents.

inflammatory.definition: Relating to inflammation; causing or characterized by the body's inflammatory response (redness, heat, swelling, pain) to tissue injury or infection.

ruptured.definition: Having broken or burst open; torn or ruptured, typically referring to a structure such as a blood vessel or organ that has sustained a rupture, often with leakage or bleeding.

sac.definition: A membranous cavity or pouch in the body that contains fluid or other material, formed by folds of tissue and often lined by a membrane (as in amniotic sac, serous sacs, or synovial sacs).

pancreatic.definition: Relating to the pancreas, the gland behind the stomach that produces digestive enzymes and hormones (including insulin and glucagon).

carcinoma.definition: A type of cancer that begins in your skin or the lining of an organ.

pancreatitis.definition: When the pancreas is swollen and irritated by its own fluids.

peptic.definition: Relating to digestion in the stomach, especially to gastric acid and the enzyme pepsin.

ulcer.definition: An open sore that can develop in many areas of your body.

cholecystitis.definition: Inflammation of the gallbladder, usually due to gallstone–induced obstruction of the cystic duct; presents with right upper quadrant pain, fever, and leukocytosis; diagnosed by imaging and treated with antibiotics and cholecystectomy.

cholelithiasis.definition: Formation of gallstones (calculi) within the gallbladder or biliary ducts; may be asymptomatic or cause biliary colic, cholecystitis, or pancreatitis if obstruction occurs.

diverticulitis.definition: Occurs when one or a few of the pouches in the wall of your colon become inflamed.

foregut.definition: An anatomical and embryological region of the digestive tract extending from the esophagus to the proximal duodenum, including the stomach, and giving rise to the liver, biliary apparatus, and pancreas.

midgut.definition: Anatomical portion of the digestive tract extending from the distal half of the duodenum to the proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon, including the jejunum, ileum, cecum, appendix, and ascending and proximal transverse colon; supplied by the superior mesenteric artery.

hindgut.definition: In embryology, the posterior portion of the primitive gut that gives rise to the distal third of the transverse colon, descending and sigmoid colon, rectum, and the upper part of the anal canal.

lupus.definition: A disease in which the immune system attacks healthy cells and tissues by mistake; there are several types of lupus, and the type determines which body parts are affected.

erythematosus.definition: A red rash, often on your face.

lead.definition: A metal that is sometimes found in paint or plumbing, especially in older buildings, and in folk medicine; it may also be found in workplaces such as auto repair or construction.

poisoning.definition: An injury or illness caused by exposure to a toxic substance (poison) via ingestion, inhalation, skin contact, or injection, resulting in harmful physiological effects that may range from mild to life-threatening.

hypercalcemia.definition: Elevated calcium in the blood, usually defined as a serum calcium level above the upper limit of normal (approximately >10.5 mg/dL or >2.62 mmol/L). It can result from hyperparathyroidism, malignancy, vitamin D excess, granulomatous disease, certain medications, or immobilization, and may be asymptomatic or cause symptoms such as polyuria, polydipsia, nausea, constipation, weakness, and confusion.

sickle.definition: An abnormal crescent-shaped morphology of red blood cells caused by polymerization of hemoglobin S under low oxygen (hypoxic) conditions, leading to hemolytic anemia and vaso-occlusive crises.

cell.definition: The basic building block of all living organisms.

anemia.definition: A low red-blood count. Your blood does not have enough of the cells that carry oxygen (hemoglobin) to your body. Also called “tired blood” or “low iron.”

acidosis.definition: A condition in which body fluids become too acidic, lowering the blood pH below the normal range (about 7.35–7.45) due to excess acid or loss of bicarbonate; can be metabolic or respiratory in origin.

porphyria.definition: A group of inherited or acquired disorders caused by defects in heme biosynthesis enzymes, leading to accumulation of porphyrins or their precursors; presentations vary by type, with acute neurovisceral symptoms (pain, nausea, neuropathy, psychiatric symptoms) in some forms and photosensitivity with blistering in cutaneous porphyrias.

tabes.definition: An advanced form of neurosyphilis in which the dorsal columns and dorsal roots of the spinal cord degenerate, causing sensory ataxia, lancinating pains, loss of proprioception and vibration sense, reduced reflexes, and a positive Romberg sign; often with Argyll Robertson pupils.

dorsalis.definition: A Latin adjective meaning "of the back" or "dorsal," used in anatomy to denote the posterior surface or back side of a structure.

peritoneal.definition: Relating to the peritoneum, the serous membrane that lines the abdominal cavity and covers most of the abdominal organs.

hemacytometer.definition: A specialized counting chamber—a glass microscope slide with a ruled grid (often a Neubauer chamber)—used to count cells in a known volume of a liquid so that cell concentration (e.g., of blood cells or cultured cells) can be calculated.

urokinase.definition: A human kidney–derived serine protease that activates plasminogen to plasmin, catalyzing fibrin clot breakdown; used pharmacologically as a thrombolytic agent.

abciximab.definition: A chimeric monoclonal antibody fragment that inhibits platelet aggregation by blocking the glycoprotein IIb/IIIa (integrin αIIbβ3) receptor on activated platelets; used intravenously during percutaneous coronary intervention or in acute coronary syndromes.

monoclonal.definition: Originating from a single clone of cells; in immunology, describes antibodies produced by identical immune cells that recognize a single epitope.

antibody.definition: Cells in your blood that fight infections or other abnormal substances.

fab.definition: Fragment antigen-binding (Fab) portion of an antibody responsible for binding to an antigen.

fragment.definition: A small piece broken off from a larger structure; in medicine, a fragment can refer to a detached piece of bone, tissue, or other material resulting from injury or a pathological process.

platelets.definition: Small, anucleate cell fragments derived from megakaryocytes in the bone marrow; circulate in blood and mediate hemostasis by forming platelet plugs and releasing granules that promote coagulation.

percutaneous.definition: A medical method where the body's inner area is accessed by poking a needle through the skin.

transluminal.definition: Relating to or occurring through the lumen (the interior space) of a hollow organ or vessel; describes procedures or approaches that pass through the inside channel rather than through the wall.

coronary.definition: Related to the blood vessels that bring blood to the heart.

angioplasty.definition: A procedure used to open blocked or narrowed arteries, most commonly by inserting a thin tube, or catheter, into the affected artery and inflating a balloon.

atherectomy.definition: A procedure to remove atherosclerotic plaque from an artery or blood vessel, typically using a catheter-based device (e.g., rotational, directional, laser, or aspiration atherectomy) to restore or improve blood flow.

stroke.definition: An abrupt disruption of brain function due to a problem with a blood vessel in the brain. It is also called a cerebral accident or cerebrovascular accident (CVA); ischemic type is caused by a clot blocking a brain vessel, and hemorrhagic type by a ruptured vessel that bleeds into the brain.

thrombocytopenia.definition: A condition in which the number of platelets (the small cells essential for blood clotting) is low, which can cause unusual bleeding.

edema.definition: Swelling caused by too much fluid in your body.

atrial.definition: Relating to the atrium, the upper chamber of the heart; used to describe structures or functions associated with the atria (left or right).

fibrillation.definition: Rapid, irregular, and unsynchronized quivering or contraction of muscle fibers; when it involves the heart, it refers to chaotic electrical activity producing a fast, irregular rhythm with ineffective atrial or ventricular contraction.

bleeding.definition: Escape of blood from the circulatory system due to rupture or injury of a blood vessel, which may be external (visible) or internal (within body tissues or cavities).

nephrectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove one kidney, typically performed for kidney cancer, donation, or to treat a diseased kidney.

contractions.definition:
Two main meanings:
- In obstetrics, rhythmic tightening of the uterus during labor that facilitates cervical dilation and delivery.
- In physiology, transient shortening and tightening of muscle fibers (e.g., skeletal or smooth muscle) due to actin–myosin cross-bridge cycling, producing movement or force.

uterine.definition: Relating to the uterus, the muscular organ in the female pelvis where gestation occurs and the fetus develops.

abdominal reflex.definition: A superficial reflex elicited by stroking the skin of the abdomen; the normal response is ipsilateral contraction of the abdominal wall muscles with the umbilicus moving toward the stimulus, testing the integrity of the T7–T12 spinal segments and corticospinal pathways. Absence of the reflex can suggest a pyramidal tract (upper motor neuron) lesion or peripheral nerve/segmental pathology.

pyramidal tract.definition: A major motor pathway (primarily the corticospinal tract) that originates in the motor cortex, descends through the internal capsule and brainstem, passes through the medullary pyramids where fibers decussate, and terminates on spinal motor neurons to control voluntary movement (with corticobulbar fibers reaching cranial nerve nuclei for head and neck movement).

superficial reflex.definition: An involuntary response elicited by gentle stimulation of the skin or mucosa, mediated at the level of the spinal cord or brainstem, used to assess nervous system integrity (examples include the abdominal, cremasteric, and plantar reflexes).

small intestine.definition: A section of the digestive system that includes the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum and plays the major role in absorbing nutrients for the body.

descending colon.definition: An area of the large intestine on the left side of the abdomen, extending from the splenic (left colic) flexure to the sigmoid colon; it is secondarily retroperitoneal and functions to absorb water and electrolytes and form/store feces before passage to the sigmoid colon.

hypochondriac region.definition: Two upper lateral regions of the abdomen, located on the right and left sides of the epigastric region and beneath the costal margins.

epigastric region.definition: An anatomical region of the upper central abdomen, just below the rib cage and above the umbilicus, overlying the stomach and portions of the liver, pancreas, and proximal duodenum.

umbilical region.definition: Central region of the abdomen surrounding the umbilicus (navel); one of the nine abdominal regions used in anatomical subdivision.

hypogastric region.definition: Central lower abdominal region located inferior to the umbilical region and superior to the pubic area; bounded laterally by the inguinal (iliac) regions, it commonly contains parts of the ileum and sigmoid colon, the urinary bladder, and, in females, the uterus and ovaries.

right inguinal region.definition: An anatomical region on the right side of the lower anterior abdominal wall near the groin; essentially the right groin area, bounded inferiorly by the inguinal ligament, anteriorly by the external oblique aponeurosis, and medially by the lateral border of the rectus abdominis, containing the right inguinal canal (through which the spermatic cord in males or the round ligament in females passes) and related structures.

left inguinal region.definition: Left inguinal region: the left groin area of the lower anterior abdominal wall, overlying the left inguinal canal; bordered inferiorly by the inguinal ligament and superiorly by a line from the anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle.

inguinal ligament.definition: A thick, fibrous band formed by the inferior border of the external oblique aponeurosis, extending from the anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle; it forms the base of the inguinal canal and the superior border of the femoral triangle (Poupart's ligament).

cartilages of the ninth rib.definition: A hyaline cartilage that extends from the anterior end of the ninth rib to articulate with the costal cartilage of the eighth rib; it contributes to the costal margin and does not articulate directly with the sternum (it is part of the false ribs 8–10).

ninth rib.definition: One of the twelve thoracic ribs; the ninth rib is a false rib (ribs 8–10) that does not attach directly to the sternum. Its costal cartilage fuses with the cartilage of the eighth rib, and its head articulates with the bodies of T8 and T9 with a tubercle articulating with the transverse process of T9.

abdominal wall.definition: A muscular and fascial boundary of the abdomen that encloses the abdominal cavity and viscera; comprises the external oblique, internal oblique, transversus abdominis, and rectus abdominis muscles with their fascia and the linea alba, plus overlying skin and subcutaneous tissue.

viscera.definition: The internal organs, especially those found in the abdomen.

abdominopelvic cavity.definition: A continuous ventral body cavity inferior to the diaphragm that includes the abdominal and pelvic subdivisions, containing most of the digestive, urinary, and reproductive organs and lined by peritoneum.

fallopian tube.definition: A pair of slender tubes that transport eggs from the ovaries to the uterus; lined with ciliated epithelium and smooth muscle to propel the oocyte by peristalsis; fertilization typically occurs in the ampulla, with fimbriae near the ovary helping to capture the ovulated egg.

salpingectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove one or both fallopian tubes (unilateral or bilateral salpingectomy), commonly performed for sterilization or to treat tubal disease or ectopic pregnancy.

celiosalpingectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which one or both fallopian tubes are removed through an abdominal (open abdominal) approach.

laparosalpingectomy.definition: Removal of one or both fallopian tubes using a laparoscopic (minimally invasive) approach, typically for sterilization or treatment of tubal disease (e.g., ectopic pregnancy, hydrosalpinx).

appendectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove the vermiform appendix, typically to treat appendicitis; can be performed via open or laparoscopic surgery.

cholecystectomy.definition: Removal of the gallbladder through surgery, typically to treat gallstone disease or cholecystitis; usually performed laparoscopically but can be done as open surgery.

gastrectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove part or all of the stomach; partial gastrectomy removes a portion, while total gastrectomy removes the entire stomach, usually followed by reconstruction to restore continuity of the GI tract (e.g., esophagojejunostomy).

herniorrhaphy.definition: Surgical repair of a hernia, typically involving returning the protruded tissue to its proper place and closing the defect in the abdominal wall with sutures, often reinforced with mesh to reduce recurrence.

laparotomy.definition: A surgical procedure that involves making an incision through the abdominal wall to open the peritoneal cavity and allow access to the abdominal organs for exploration, diagnosis, or treatment.

tenaculum.definition: A surgical instrument with a curved, pointed hook used to grasp and hold tissue (notably the cervix) to apply traction during gynecologic procedures.

undescended testis.definition: A congenital condition in which one or both testes fail to descend into the scrotum, remaining in the abdomen or inguinal canal; it may be palpable or nonpalpable and is typically diagnosed in infancy or early childhood. If not corrected, it can be associated with infertility and an increased risk of testicular cancer.

heimlich maneuver.definition: A first-aid technique to treat choking by delivering quick upward abdominal thrusts to the abdomen to expel a foreign object blocking the airway.

abdominal thrust.definition: A first-aid maneuver to relieve choking by applying quick inward and upward abdominal thrusts to expel an obstructing object from the airway; also known as the Heimlich maneuver.

abdominal ultrasound.definition: A noninvasive imaging test that uses high-frequency sound waves to visualize abdominal organs (such as the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, kidneys, and spleen) and detect stones, masses, fluid collections, or other abnormalities, without ionizing radiation; often augmented with Doppler to assess blood flow.

kidneys.definition: Two bean-shaped retroperitoneal organs that filter blood to form urine, removing wastes and excess fluids; regulate electrolyte and acid-base balance and blood pressure, and produce hormones such as erythropoietin and renin.

ureters.definition: The tubes that carry waste or water from your kidneys to your bladder.

bladder.definition: A hollow organ that stores pee (urine).

abdominocentesis.definition: A procedure in which fluid from the peritoneal cavity is aspirated through the abdominal wall using a needle or catheter, typically to obtain ascitic fluid for diagnostic analysis or to relieve ascites.

abdominovesical.definition: Pertaining to or involving the abdomen and the urinary bladder; describing anatomical relations between the abdominal cavity and the bladder.

abdominocystic.definition: Relating to the abdomen and to a cyst; describing a cyst located in the abdominal cavity or a process affecting both abdominal structures and a cyst.

abdominothoracic arch.definition: A nonstandard term; generally denotes the curved boundary between the abdominal and thoracic cavities formed by the diaphragm—the diaphragmatic arch that separates the chest from the abdomen.

abdominovaginal.definition: A gynecologic surgical approach that uses both an abdominal incision and a vaginal route to access and remove pelvic organs (most commonly a uterus), combining abdominal visualization with vaginal removal to improve exposure and facilitate the procedure.

abdominohysterotomy.definition: A surgical delivery in which an incision is made through the abdominal wall and the uterus to access and deliver the fetus, effectively a cesarean section performed via a transabdominal approach.

abdominoperineal.definition: Relating to the abdomen and the perineum; describing procedures or approaches that involve both the abdominal and perineal regions.

abdominoplasty.definition: A procedure to remove excess abdominal skin and tighten the underlying stomach muscles. Also known as a tummy tuck.

tummy tuck.definition: A cosmetic surgical procedure to remove excess abdominal skin and fat and to tighten the abdominal muscles, resulting in a flatter abdomen. Also known as abdominoplasty.

abduction.definition: Movement of a body part, such as an arm or leg, away from the center of the body.

abductor digiti minimi of the foot.word: abductor digiti minimi of the foot
abductor digiti minimi of the foot.definition: A muscle of the plantar aspect of the foot that abducts the little toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint; it originates from the calcaneal tuberosity (and plantar fascia) and inserts on the base of the proximal phalanx of the fifth toe, innervated by the lateral plantar nerve, and functions to abduct the fifth toe.

abductor digiti minimi of the hand.word: abductor digiti minimi of the hand
abductor digiti minimi of the hand.definition: A hypothenar intrinsic hand muscle that abducts the little finger (5th digit) at the metacarpophalangeal joint; innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

abductor hallucis.definition: An intrinsic muscle of the plantar foot that abducts the big toe (hallux) and assists in its flexion; it originates from the calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis and inserts on the proximal phalanx of the hallux, innervated by the medial plantar nerve.

abductor pollicis brevis.definition: A muscle of the thenar eminence that abducts the thumb at the carpometacarpal and metacarpophalangeal joints; innervated by the recurrent branch of the median nerve.

abductor pollicis longus.definition: A muscle of the posterior forearm that abducts (radially deviates) and extends the thumb at the carpometacarpal and metacarpophalangeal joints.

abducens muscle.definition: The lateral rectus muscle of the eye, which abducts the eyeball (moves it laterally); it is innervated by the abducens nerve (cranial nerve VI).

lateral rectus muscle.definition: A muscle of the eye that abducts the eyeball (moves it laterally); it is one of the extraocular muscles innervated by the abducens nerve (cranial nerve VI).

wolff-parkinson-white syndrome.definition: An accessory pathway–mediated pre-excitation syndrome in which an abnormal conduction tract shortcuts the AV node to the ventricles (most often the Bundle of Kent), causing early ventricular activation; ECG shows a short PR interval with a delta wave and a widened QRS, and it predisposes to reentrant supraventricular tachycardias and, rarely, rapid-conduction atrial fibrillation.

paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia.definition: Sudden-onset, self-terminating episodes of rapid heart rhythm arising from above the ventricles (atria or AV node), typically due to reentrant circuits such as AV nodal reentrant tachycardia or AV reentrant tachycardia.

antidromic circus movement tachycardia.definition: A reentrant supraventricular tachycardia in which the impulse travels antegrade through an accessory pathway and retrograde through the AV node, producing a wide-complex tachycardia commonly seen in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

aberrant conduction.definition: Abnormal propagation of electrical impulses through the heart, typically due to a block or delay in the conduction system (most commonly a bundle-branch block), resulting in an abnormal and often widened QRS complex during ventricular activation.

avc.definition: Sudden onset of neurologic deficit caused by a disturbance of cerebral blood flow, due to ischemia from an occluded vessel or intracranial hemorrhage; may present with weakness, slurred speech or aphasia, vision changes, or other focal neurological signs, and requires urgent medical evaluation and treatment.

aberration.definition: A departure from what is normal or expected in anatomy, physiology, or development; an abnormality or deviation from typical structure, function, or pattern.

aberrant.definition: Departing from the normal or expected course or form; anomalous or atypical in anatomy or physiology.

abortion.definition: Termination of a pregnancy, either spontaneously (miscarriage) or induced by medical or surgical means; typically defined as pregnancy loss before fetal viability, usually before about 20 weeks' gestation.

abortion pill.definition: A medical abortion regimen using prescription medications—most commonly mifepristone followed by misoprostol—to terminate an early pregnancy by blocking progesterone and inducing uterine contractions.

mifepristone.definition: A selective progesterone receptor antagonist (antiprogestin) used in combination with misoprostol to terminate early pregnancy; it blocks progesterone action, leading to decidual breakdown and abortion, typically up to about 70 days (10 weeks) gestation.

abortifacient.definition: A substance that terminates a pregnancy by causing abortion, typically by disrupting hormonal support or triggering uterine contractions.

abortive infection.definition: An abortive infection is a viral infection in which the virus enters a host cell but fails to complete its replication cycle, producing no infectious progeny and resulting in no productive infection.

abortus fever.definition: A zoonotic febrile illness caused by Brucella abortus infection (a form of brucellosis), acquired from infected cattle or unpasteurized dairy products and historically called undulant fever; presents with intermittent fevers, night sweats, malaise, and musculoskeletal pain.

rio grande fever.definition: Historically, a non-specific febrile illness described in the Rio Grande region; not a currently recognized, defined disease.

brucella abortus.definition: A Gram-negative, facultative intracellular bacterium of the genus Brucella that primarily infects cattle, causing brucellosis, and can infect humans via ingestion of unpasteurized dairy products or contact with infected animals; in humans it presents with fever, sweats, malaise, and musculoskeletal symptoms.

brucellosis.definition: A zoonotic bacterial infection caused by Brucella species, acquired from infected animals or unpasteurized dairy products. It classically presents with fever that fluctuates (undulant fever), drenching night sweats, malaise, and myalgias; it can become chronic and involve the bones/joints, liver/spleen (hepatosplenomegaly), or rarely the heart or central nervous system.

gilles de la tourette’s syndrome.definition: A neurodevelopmental disorder defined by multiple motor tics and at least one vocal tic, beginning in childhood and persisting for more than a year with waxing and waning; commonly associated with obsessive-compulsive symptoms and ADHD.

aboiement.definition: The act or sound of barking; a harsh, abrupt vocalization produced by a dog, sometimes used in medicine to describe a barking cough seen in conditions such as croup.

ablation.definition: To remove or destroy a body part or tissue. This can be done in many ways, including surgery, radiation, or drugs.

abducent.definition: Relating to abduction; in anatomy, describing the abducens nerve (cranial nerve VI), which innervates the lateral rectus muscle to move the eye laterally.

vascular conduction.definition: Not a standard medical term; if used, it would describe the transmission of regulatory signals influencing vascular tone and blood flow within the vascular system, noting that blood vessels do not conduct electrical impulses like nerves.

aberrancy.definition: State of deviation from the normal; an abnormality or irregularity in anatomy, development, or physiological function, such as an atypical tissue location or conduction pathway.

spontaneous abortion.definition: The natural loss of a pregnancy prior to fetal viability, most commonly before 20 weeks’ gestation; also called miscarriage.

induced abortion.definition: Deliberate termination of a pregnancy by medical (pharmacologic) or surgical means, typically before fetal viability.

habitual abortion.definition: An older term for recurrent pregnancy loss, defined as three or more consecutive spontaneous abortions before 20 weeks of gestation.

threatened abortion.definition: A first-trimester vaginal bleeding with a closed cervical os and a viable intrauterine pregnancy, indicating risk of spontaneous abortion.

complete abortion.definition: Expulsion of all products of conception from the uterus, resulting in an empty uterus with cessation of bleeding and cramping, and with serum hCG levels falling to undetectable.

missed abortion.definition: A pregnancy loss in which the embryo or fetus has died in utero but remains in the uterus without being expelled, often with a closed cervix and little or no vaginal bleeding; diagnosis is typically made by ultrasound showing absence of fetal cardiac activity and may be supported by falling or plateauing hCG levels.

therapeutic abortion.definition: An abortion performed for medical reasons to protect the health or life of the pregnant person, or because the fetus has a condition incompatible with life or severe morbidity.

medical abortion.definition: Non-surgical termination of pregnancy using medications, usually a two-drug regimen (eg, mifepristone followed by misoprostol) that induces detachment of pregnancy tissue and uterine contractions to expel it, typically effective up to about 10 weeks’ gestation depending on guidelines.

elective abortion.definition: A voluntary termination of a pregnancy requested by the pregnant person for nonmedical reasons; can be performed medically or surgically, typically in the first trimester, and distinct from abortions performed for medical indications.

abortionist.definition: A person who performs abortion procedures; typically a licensed clinician who provides abortion care, including medical (drug) or surgical abortion.

abruptio placentae.definition: A premature separation of the placenta from the uterine wall before delivery, causing vaginal bleeding, abdominal pain or tenderness, and potential fetal hypoxia as well as maternal hemorrhage.

placentae.definition: The placentae are temporary, disc-shaped organs that form in the uterus during pregnancy to provide oxygen and nutrients to the fetus, remove waste products from fetal blood, and produce hormones to sustain pregnancy.

abg.definition: A blood test that measures oxygen (PaO2), carbon dioxide (PaCO2), pH, and bicarbonate (HCO3−) in arterial blood to assess gas exchange and acid–base status; typically obtained via arterial puncture.

arterial blood gas.definition: A diagnostic blood test on arterial blood to assess oxygenation, ventilation, and acid–base status by measuring pH, PaO2, PaCO2, bicarbonate (HCO3−), and related parameters.

abi.definition: A noninvasive test that compares the systolic blood pressure measured at the ankle with that measured at the arm to assess for peripheral artery disease; a reduced ratio indicates PAD.

ankle-brachial index.definition: A test that compares blood pressure at the ankle with blood pressure at the elbow. A difference between the two indicates the presence of peripheral artery disease.

abr.definition: A neurophysiological test that records the brainstem's electrical activity in response to sound, used to assess hearing sensitivity and the integrity of auditory pathways.

auditory brainstem response.definition: An objective electrophysiologic test that measures the brainstem's electrical response to sound using scalp electrodes; used to assess the integrity of the auditory pathway and estimate hearing thresholds, particularly in infants or uncooperative patients.

abls.definition: An educational program and guideline framework for the initial assessment and management of burn injuries, emphasizing airway and breathing assessment, prompt fluid resuscitation, circulation support, temperature regulation, pain control, and early wound care to improve survival in the acute phase of burn care.

advanced burn life support.definition: A structured, evidence-based protocol and training program for the initial stabilization and resuscitation of burn patients, focusing on airway protection and ventilation, fluid therapy, pain control, wound care, infection prevention, temperature regulation, hemodynamic monitoring, and timely transfer to a burn center.

abms.definition: A nonprofit umbrella organization that certifies physicians in medical specialties through its member boards and oversees the standards for board certification and recertification.

american board of medical specialties.definition: A national non-profit organization that administers and coordinates physician board certification through its member specialty boards; it sets standards for training, examinations, and ongoing maintenance of certification, and serves as the umbrella for physician certification in the United States.

abp.definition: Arterial blood pressure: The pressure exerted by circulating blood on the walls of arteries, determined by cardiac output and systemic vascular resistance; usually expressed as systolic over diastolic pressure (e.g., 120/80 mmHg).

arterial blood pressure.definition: The pressure exerted by circulating blood on the walls of the arteries, typically expressed as systolic over diastolic pressure (e.g., 120/80 mmHg); it reflects cardiac output and systemic vascular resistance.

abo blood group.definition: An inherited classification of human blood based on the presence or absence of A and B antigens on red blood cells and the corresponding antibodies in plasma; the four main groups are A, B, AB, and O, and this system determines transfusion compatibility.

hypocholesterolemia.definition: An abnormally low concentration of cholesterol in the blood; may reflect malnutrition, chronic illness, liver disease, hyperthyroidism, genetic disorders, or lipid-lowering therapy.

arthroplasty.definition: Surgically rebuilding or replacing a joint, usually to relieve arthritis or fix an abnormality.

abscess.definition: Caused by an infection; a pocket of pus. You can get them anywhere in your body.

abreact.definition: To release or discharge an emotional reaction by reliving and expressing a previously repressed or traumatic memory or feeling; a cathartic process used in psychotherapy.

abreaction.definition: Reliving and expressing the intense emotions attached to a traumatic memory to achieve cathartic emotional release; used in some psychodynamic therapies to resolve affect associated with trauma.

abrosia.definition: A historical/rare term for loss of appetite; not commonly used in modern medical practice (often considered synonymous with anorexia).

abruption.definition: The premature separation of a normally implanted placenta from the uterus before delivery, often presenting with vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain, and potentially causing fetal distress and maternal hemorrhage.

ablatio placentae.definition: Premature separation of the placenta from the uterus before delivery, causing vaginal bleeding, abdominal pain, and potential fetal distress or maternal hemorrhage.

placenta previa.definition: An obstetric condition in which the placenta implants in the lower uterine segment and partially or completely covers the cervix (internal os), causing painless vaginal bleeding in the second or third trimester; diagnosis is by ultrasound and most often management is cesarean delivery.

placental abruption.definition: Premature detachment of placental tissue from the uterine wall before delivery, usually after 20 weeks’ gestation, causing vaginal bleeding, abdominal pain, and uterine tenderness; can be concealed or overt and may result in fetal hypoxia or demise and significant maternal hemorrhage; a medical emergency.

cesarean section.definition: A surgical delivery of a baby through incisions in the mother's abdomen and uterus, usually performed when vaginal delivery is not safe for the mother or fetus; can be planned or emergent.

extravasation.definition: The leakage of a fluid from a vessel into surrounding tissue, such as IV medications or contrast escaping from a vein, which can cause local edema, inflammation, and potential tissue injury.

shock.definition: A serious medical condition in which there is too little blood flow to the outer portions of the body, resulting in cold, sweaty skin; a weak pulse; irregular breathing; and dilated pupils. Shock can be caused by blood loss, severe heart problems, severe infections, allergic reactions, or drug overdoses.

preeclampsia.definition: High blood pressure during pregnancy accompanied by such signs as protein in the urine and swelling of the hands and feet; can progress to eclampsia, characterized by seizures.

amniotomy.definition: Artificial rupture of the amniotic sac during labor, performed with a sterile instrument to induce or augment labor or enable internal fetal monitoring.

uterine wall.definition: It comprises three layers: an inner endometrium (mucosal lining that thickens and sheds with the menstrual cycle), a thick middle muscular layer (myometrium) that contracts during menstruation and childbirth, and an outer serous covering (perimetrium) that is continuous with the peritoneum.

fibrinogen.definition: A soluble plasma glycoprotein produced by the liver that is converted by thrombin into fibrin, forming the mesh of a blood clot; it is known as coagulation factor I.

coagulation.definition: The process by which blood changes from a liquid to a semi-solid gel to form a clot, primarily involving platelet activation and a cascade of coagulation factors that culminate in fibrin mesh formation to stop bleeding.

exsanguination.definition: The loss of a large amount of blood from the body, potentially resulting in hypovolemia or death.

3-hz spike-and-wave discharges.definition: A generalized electroencephalographic pattern of synchronous spike-and-wave complexes occurring at approximately 3 Hz, classically associated with absence seizures.

absence seizure.definition: A brief generalized nonconvulsive seizure presenting as a sudden, short lapse in consciousness with a blank stare (often with eyelid flutter), typically lasting 5–10 seconds and ending abruptly with immediate return to baseline.EEG commonly shows 3 Hz generalized spike-and-wave discharges.

absentia epiletica.definition: Absence seizures are brief generalized seizures characterized by sudden impairment of consciousness with a vacant stare and minimal motor activity (often accompanied by subtle automatisms); recovery is rapid with no postictal confusion, and EEG typically shows generalized 3 Hz spike-and-wave discharges. They commonly begin in childhood and may occur many times per day.

petit mal seizure.definition: A brief impairment of consciousness with unresponsiveness and a blank stare lasting a few seconds, often with automatisms (e.g., eye blinking, lip-smacking); the person resumes activity immediately afterward and usually has no memory of the event.

epilepsy.definition: A brain disorder that causes seizures (jerking of muscles) or loss of consciousness.

ethosuximide.definition: A succinimide anticonvulsant used to treat absence seizures; it works by inhibiting T-type calcium channels in thalamic neurons, thereby reducing abnormal thalamocortical rhythmic activity.

trimethadione.definition: An older anticonvulsant of the hydantoin class previously used to treat absence seizures; its use is now limited due to significant teratogenicity and toxicity.

valproic acid.definition: A broad-spectrum anticonvulsant used to treat epilepsy, bipolar disorder, and migraine prophylaxis; it increases brain GABA levels and modulates neuronal excitability, with risks including hepatotoxicity and teratogenicity.

anticonvulsant.definition: A medication that suppresses seizure activity in the brain and is used to prevent or control epileptic seizures; it may also be prescribed for other conditions such as neuropathic pain, mood stabilization, or migraine prevention.

periapical abscess.definition: A focal collection of pus in the periapical tissues at the root apex, usually arising from pulpal necrosis due to caries or trauma; presents with localized toothache and swelling, and radiographs show periapical radiolucency; treated with drainage and definitive therapy (root canal treatment or extraction), with antibiotics if there is systemic spread.

periodontal abscess.definition: A localized pus-containing infection of the periodontium (gums and supporting tissues), usually arising from a periodontal pocket; presents with acute pain, swelling, and tenderness and is managed by drainage and control of the etiologic factors (plaque/calculus) with periodontal therapy.

tooth abscess.definition: A localized pus-filled infection around a tooth, usually caused by bacteria that invade the dental pulp or surrounding tissues after decay or trauma; it causes pain, swelling, and sometimes fever, and is treated by drainage and removing the source of infection (such as root canal therapy or extraction), with antibiotics if systemic signs are present.

periapical.definition: Around the apex of a tooth root; relating to the tissues surrounding the root tip.

periodontal.definition: Relating to the periodontium, the tissues that surround and support the teeth, including the gingiva (gums), periodontal ligament, cementum, and alveolar bone.

tooth.definition: A hard, calcified structure in the mouth used for biting and chewing; it has an enamel-covered crown, one or more roots anchored in the jawbone, and consists of enamel, dentin, cementum, and pulp.

root.definition: The portion of the tooth below the gum line.

absidia.definition: A genus of mold fungi in the order Mucorales; environmental saprophytes, with some species that are opportunistic pathogens capable of causing mucormycosis in humans.

absidia corymbifera.definition: An opportunistic pathogenic mold of the order Mucorales that can cause mucormycosis in immunocompromised individuals; infections can involve the rhinocerebral, pulmonary, cutaneous, or disseminated systems, and the organism is commonly found in soil, decaying vegetation, and dust.

absidia species.definition: A genus of environmental filamentous fungi (molds) in the order Mucorales; saprobes found in soil and decaying matter, with some species capable of opportunistic infection (mucormycosis) in immunocompromised hosts. Several species historically placed in Absidia (e.g., Absidia corymbifera) have been reclassified into the genus Lichtheimia.

mucormycosis.definition: A serious, angioinvasive fungal infection caused by Mucorales molds (e.g., Rhizopus, Mucor) that predominantly affects immunocompromised individuals (notably diabetic ketoacidosis) and presents as rhinocerebral, pulmonary, or cutaneous disease; it causes rapid tissue necrosis and requires urgent surgical debridement plus antifungal therapy, typically amphotericin B followed by posaconazole or isavuconazole.

zygomycosis.definition: An invasive fungal infection caused by molds of the order Mucorales (historically called zygomycetes), occurring chiefly in immunocompromised individuals, characterized by rapidly progressive tissue necrosis that commonly involves the sinuses/face (rhinocerebral), lungs, or skin.

mucorales.definition: An order of fungi (molds) in the phylum Mucoromycota, characterized by broad, nonseptate (or sparsely septate) hyphae with wide-angle branching; commonly saprophytic in soil and decaying matter, with several species that are opportunistic pathogens causing mucormycosis in humans.

bacteria.definition: Very small living things, or “bugs,” that can be helpful (they help to digest food) or can cause illness (strep throat, for example).

pyogenic bacteria.definition: Pus-forming bacteria; microorganisms that cause suppurative (pus-producing) infections by provoking acute neutrophilic inflammation, often leading to abscesses and purulent discharge.

staphylococci.definition: Gram-positive, nonmotile cocci that occur in grape-like clusters. They are facultative aerobes and common inhabitants of human skin and mucous membranes. Most are harmless, but some species—most notably Staphylococcus aureus—are opportunistic pathogens capable of causing skin and soft tissue infections, pneumonia, bacteremia, endocarditis, osteomyelitis, and toxin-mediated illnesses. They are catalase-positive; S. aureus is coagulase-positive, which helps distinguish it from coagulase-negative staphylococci.

parasites.definition: An organism that lives on or in a host organism and derives nutrients or other benefits at the host's expense, often causing harm or disease; includes protozoa, helminths (worms), and ectoparasites.

foreign substances.definition: Substances not native to the body and recognized as non-self by the immune system, including pathogens, toxins, allergens, and implanted or foreign materials, which may trigger immune, inflammatory, or toxic responses.
