autologous graft.definition: Transplantation of tissue from one site to another within the same individual, using the patient's own tissue to minimize immune rejection (e.g., skin, bone, or fat grafts).

autologous stem cell transplantation.definition: A procedure in which a patient’s own hematopoietic stem cells are collected (often from peripheral blood after growth-factor mobilization), stored, and reinfused after high-dose chemotherapy or radiation to restore bone marrow function and enable higher-intensity treatment; used for certain hematologic cancers (e.g., multiple myeloma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma) and some autoimmune diseases.

asct.definition: A procedure in which a patient’s own hematopoietic stem cells are collected, stored, and reinfused after high-dose chemotherapy or radiation to restore bone marrow function. This autologous transplantation is used for certain hematologic cancers, such as multiple myeloma and some lymphomas.

autologous transfusion.definition: Transfusion of a patient’s own blood, collected and stored for later reinfusion, typically around surgical procedures.

autolysis.definition: Self-digestion of tissue by its own lysosomal enzymes, leading to breakdown of cells and tissues (often observed as postmortem autolysis).

aed.definition: A portable device that analyzes heart rhythms and delivers an electrical shock to restore a normal rhythm during sudden cardiac arrest.

automated reagin test.definition: A laboratory assay that automates the non-treponemal serologic test for syphilis, detecting antibodies to cardiolipin-lecithin-cholesterol complexes (reagins) in patient serum; used for initial screening and monitoring disease activity, with reactive results typically confirmed by a treponemal-specific test.

rapid plasma reagin test.definition: An indirect screening serologic test for syphilis that detects non-treponemal antibodies (reagin) to cardiolipin-lecithin-cholesterol antigens; used to screen for infection and monitor treatment, with results reported as titers, and positives typically confirmed with treponemal-specific tests.

rpr test.definition: A non-treponemal serologic test for syphilis that detects antibodies to cardiolipin-lecithin-cholesterol complexes; used for initial screening and for monitoring treatment, with potential false-positive results in various conditions.

autopsy.definition: Surgically opening and examining a body after death to see if any diseases are present and to determine the cause of death.

autopsy pathology.definition: A branch of pathology involving the postmortem examination and tissue analysis of a deceased patient to determine the cause and manner of death and to document diseases present at death; it typically includes gross examination, histology, toxicology, and ancillary studies.

autoregulation.definition: Intrinsic mechanism by which an organ maintains relatively constant blood flow despite changes in arterial pressure, achieved through local adjustments of arteriolar resistance driven by myogenic responses and local metabolic/endothelial signals.

autosensitization.definition: A secondary, disseminated inflammatory skin eruption at sites distant from a primary lesion, believed to be caused by immune sensitization to antigens released by the primary infection or inflammation; it often resolves after treating the primary lesion.

autosepticemia.definition: An historical term for septicemia caused by organisms originating from the patient’s own body (endogenous flora) rather than from an external source; today this concept is usually described as endogenous bacteremia or endogenous septicemia.

autoserous treatment.definition: Using a patient’s own tissue or cells for therapy or transplantation, harvested from the same individual and reintroduced for treatment (e.g., autologous stem cell transplantation, autologous fat grafting, or autologous platelet-rich plasma), thereby minimizing immune rejection and reducing risk from donor-derived infections.

autosite.definition: A viable host twin in a parasitic-twinning relationship, into which a nonfunctional parasitic fetus is attached and dependent on the host for blood supply; the parasitic tissue cannot survive independently.

autosome.definition: Non-sex chromosomes that carry most of an organism’s genes; in humans they are chromosomes 1 through 22, present as homologous pairs and not involved in sex determination.

autosomal-dominant inheritance.definition: A pattern of genetic transmission in which a pathogenic variant in one autosomal gene is sufficient to cause disease when present in one copy (heterozygous). It typically shows vertical transmission (seen in successive generations), affects males and females equally, and each child of an affected person has about a 50% chance of inheriting the mutation and being affected.

autosomal-recessive inheritance.definition: An inheritance pattern in which an abnormal allele must be present on both copies of an autosomal (non-sex) chromosome for the trait or disorder to be expressed; individuals with one mutated allele are typically carriers, and two carrier parents have a 25% chance of an affected child, a 50% chance of a carrier child, and a 25% chance of an unaffected, non-carrier child. Males and females are equally affected.

autosomal inheritance.definition: Pattern of inheritance in which a gene on an autosome (non-sex chromosome) influences a trait or disorder, with equal involvement of sexes; includes autosomal dominant (one mutant allele is sufficient, often with vertical transmission and ~50% risk to offspring) and autosomal recessive (two mutant alleles required, often with carrier parents and ~25% risk to siblings).

polydactyly.definition: A congenital condition characterized by the presence of more than the usual number of digits (fingers or toes) on a hand or foot; the extra digit can be fully formed or rudimentary and may occur alone or with other anomalies.

marfan’s syndrome.definition: An autosomal dominant inherited connective tissue disorder caused by mutations in the FBN1 gene (fibrillin-1), characterized by tall stature with long limbs and arachnodactyly, chest wall deformities and scoliosis, lens dislocation, and progressive dilation of the aortic root with risk of dissection.

lesch-nyhan syndrome.definition: A rare X-linked recessive metabolic disorder caused by deficiency of hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT), leading to hyperuricemia with gout and kidney stones, and severe neurobehavioral abnormalities including dystonia, chorea, spasticity, cognitive impairment, and self-mutilating or aggressive behaviors; typically presents in infancy with developmental delay.

neuroblastomas.definition: A malignant tumor of neural crest origin arising from neuroblasts of the sympathetic nervous system, most often in the adrenal medulla or paraspinal ganglia, occurring predominantly in infants and young children.

ewing’s sarcoma.definition: An aggressive malignant tumor that arises in bone or soft tissue, most common in children and adolescents; it is part of the Ewing sarcoma family of tumors and is typically driven by EWSR1 gene fusions (most often EWSR1-FLI1), treated with multimodal therapy including chemotherapy, surgery, and radiotherapy.

autografts.definition: A graft in which tissue is transplanted from one site to another within the same individual, thereby avoiding immune rejection; commonly used for skin grafts, bone grafts, and other tissues.

capillary blood specimen.definition: A small blood sample obtained by puncturing a capillary bed (commonly by fingerstick or heelstick) for laboratory or point-of-care testing; the specimen is a mixture of capillary, arterial, and venous blood with some interstitial fluid, collected when only a small volume is needed.

lancet.definition: A small, sharp surgical blade with a slender, pointed tip used for precise incisions or punctures in minor surgery and for puncturing or lancing procedures to obtain samples. In hematology, an elongated red blood cell with pointed ends, giving a spear-like appearance.

corneal tissue.definition: An avascular, transparent tissue forming the anterior part of the eye, responsible for most of the eye's refractive power; it consists of five layers—epithelium, Bowman's layer, stroma, Descemet's membrane, and endothelium—and provides a protective barrier and optical transparency.

infiltration.definition: A process by which a substance diffuses into or enters body tissue; in IV therapy it denotes leakage of IV fluid into surrounding tissue, and in pathology it can refer to malignant cells invading adjacent tissues (infiltrating carcinoma).

intravenous infusion.definition: A method of delivering fluids, medications, or nutrients directly into the venous circulation through an intravenous line over a set period, typically using an infusion pump or gravity drip.

intracellular enzymes.definition: Enzymes that catalyze biochemical reactions inside cells (in the cytosol or within organelles) rather than in the extracellular space; they participate in metabolic pathways, DNA replication and repair, and other intracellular processes.

cardioverter defibrillator.definition: An implanted device that monitors the heart’s rhythm and delivers electrical therapy to treat life-threatening arrhythmias; it can provide high-energy shocks to stop ventricular fibrillation or VT and may also deliver pacing to maintain a normal heart rate.

automatic implanted cardioverter defibri.definition: An implantable device placed under the skin (usually in the chest) that continuously monitors heart rhythm and automatically delivers electrical therapy—pace, cardioversion, or defibrillation—to terminate life-threatening arrhythmias and prevent sudden cardiac death.

arrhythmias.definition: Abnormalities of the heart's rhythm or rate caused by dysfunction in the heart's electrical conduction system, resulting in rhythms that are too fast (tachyarrhythmias), too slow (bradyarrhythmias), or irregular. They range from benign to potentially life-threatening and can be caused by structural heart disease, electrolyte disturbances, medication effects, or conduction system disorders.

convulsions.definition: An abnormal, excessive electrical discharge in the brain causing sudden, involuntary muscle contractions or rhythmic jerking, usually presenting as a seizure and may include loss of consciousness.

necropsy.definition: A postmortem examination of an animal to determine the cause of death or investigate disease processes; the veterinary counterpart of an autopsy.

thanatopsy.definition: A postmortem examination of a body to determine the cause and manner of death; essentially another term for autopsy.

atropine sulfate.definition: A tropane alkaloid anticholinergic agent that competitively inhibits muscarinic acetylcholine receptors; used clinically to increase heart rate in bradycardia, reduce secretions before anesthesia, produce mydriasis, and treat organophosphate/nerve agent poisoning.

adrenergic drugs.definition: Adrenergic drugs are agents that stimulate the sympathetic nervous system by activating adrenergic receptors (primarily alpha and beta), either directly as receptor agonists or indirectly by increasing norepinephrine release or inhibiting its reuptake; they produce effects such as vasoconstriction, increased heart rate and contractility, and bronchodilation.

parasympathetic nervous system.definition: Part of the nervous system that calms body systems excited by the stress hormones.

sympathetic nervous system.definition: An offshoot of the autonomic nervous system; it sends signals to prepare the body for action when stress hormones are released in response to perceived or real dangers.

autonomic nervous system.definition: The part of the nervous system that controls involuntary actions, such as blood pressure and breathing; it also mediates the fight-or-flight response to danger.

autonomic reflex.definition: A reflex arc mediated by the autonomic nervous system that elicits an involuntary visceral response (in smooth muscle, cardiac muscle, or glands) to a sensory stimulus, typically without conscious control.

vasomotor epilepsy.definition: An historical/obsolete term for epileptic seizures in which autonomic vasomotor symptoms predominate—such as flushing, pallor, sweating, tachycardia, and blood pressure changes—often accompanying focal seizures; today these are described as focal seizures with autonomic manifestations rather than a distinct epilepsy syndrome.

parasitic fetus.definition: A rare congenital anomaly in which a malformed fetus is enclosed within and dependent on its twin’s body, effectively a parasitic twin; most often presents as an abdominal or retroperitoneal mass and is treated by surgical removal.

autosomatognosis.definition: An awareness and recognition of one’s own body and its parts, including ownership and the ability to localize body parts in space (intact somatognosis).

avian_influenza.definition: A viral infection of birds caused by influenza A viruses; there are low-pathogenic and highly pathogenic strains, with highly pathogenic avian influenza causing severe disease in birds and occasionally infecting humans or other mammals, usually through contact with infected birds or contaminated environments.

avian_tuberculosis.definition: A chronic granulomatous infectious disease of birds caused by Mycobacterium avium complex (and related mycobacteria), leading to weight loss and granulomatous lesions in internal organs (especially liver, spleen, and intestines); transmitted mainly by ingestion of contaminated feed or water, with a low but possible zoonotic risk to immunocompromised humans.

cerebrovascular_accident.definition: A sudden neurological deficit resulting from disrupted cerebral blood flow due to ischemia or hemorrhage, commonly referred to as a stroke.

leptospirosis.definition: An acute zoonotic infection caused by pathogenic spirochetes of the genus Leptospira, transmitted to humans via exposure to water or soil contaminated with the urine of infected animals; it ranges from mild febrile illness to Weil disease with jaundice, renal failure, and hemorrhage.

mud_fever.definition: Equine pastern dermatitis; a skin infection and inflammation of the pastern region in horses caused by prolonged exposure to mud and moisture, frequently due to Dermatophilus congolensis, and also referred to as greasy heel or rain scald.

cystic_fibrosis.definition: A hereditary autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the CFTR gene, leading to defective chloride transport and thick, sticky secretions in the lungs and digestive tract, resulting in chronic respiratory infections, pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, malnutrition, and elevated sweat chloride.

galactosemia.definition: An inherited deficiency of enzymes (most commonly galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase) needed to metabolize galactose, causing accumulation of galactose and galactose-1-phosphate and presenting in newborns with feeding difficulties, jaundice, hepatomegaly, and cataracts; managed by a lifelong galactose-restricted diet.

mycobacterium_avium.definition: An environmental, slow-growing species of non-tuberculous mycobacteria that causes pulmonary disease and disseminated infection in immunocompromised hosts; part of the Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) along with M. intracellulare.

alveolar_socket.definition: The tooth socket in the jawbone (alveolar process) that houses a tooth root; also called the dental alveolus.

awake_anesthesia.definition: Anesthesia technique in which the patient remains awake or only lightly sedated during a procedure, usually achieved with local or regional anesthesia plus minimal sedation (monitored anesthesia care), preserving airway reflexes and allowing intraoperative neurological or functional assessment.

endoscopy.definition: A procedure where a long, tiny tube with a camera goes inside the body to look at something up close.

brain_surgery.definition: A surgical procedure to treat brain disorders by removing, repairing, or altering brain tissue or vessels; commonly performed for tumors, aneurysms, vascular malformations, epilepsy, stroke-related lesions, or traumatic injury, typically by a neurosurgeon under anesthesia with imaging guidance.

eye_infection.definition: An eye infection is an infection of any ocular tissue or surrounding structures (most commonly the conjunctiva) caused by bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites; it typically presents with red eye, discharge, irritation or itching, tearing, and sometimes blurred vision, with management depending on the cause (e.g., topical antibiotics for bacterial conjunctivitis, antiviral or antifungal therapy for specific infections) and urgent evaluation if vision is affected, there is severe pain, or trauma is involved.

conscious_sedation.definition: A pharmacologic technique in which sedatives (often with analgesics) are used to depress the level of consciousness to a light to moderate level, allowing the patient to be awake and responsive to verbal or tactile stimulation while maintaining the airway and spontaneous breathing; provides anxiolysis, amnesia, and analgesia for minor procedures.

monitored_anesthesia_care.definition: Monitored anesthesia care is a level of anesthesia service in which an anesthesia professional provides analgesia and sedation during a procedure, often with local or regional anesthesia, while continuously monitoring vital signs and respiratory status and maintaining spontaneous ventilation; the depth of sedation is titrated to the patient's needs, and the clinician is prepared to convert to general anesthesia if required.

atrioventricular_block.definition: A disorder of cardiac conduction in which impulses from the atria are delayed or blocked as they pass through the AV node and His-Purkinje system, resulting in slowed or absent ventricular activation. It is categorized by degree: first-degree (prolonged PR with all impulses conducted), second-degree (some impulses fail to conduct; Mobitz types I and II), and third-degree (complete dissociation between atria and ventricles).

arteriovenous_crossing.definition: An anatomical point in the retina where a retinal artery crosses a retinal vein; the vessels pass one over the other without fusing, and the crossing can be implicated in hypertensive retinopathy when arterial thickening compresses the vein (AV nicking).

av_nicking.definition: A retinal finding in hypertensive retinopathy in which thickened arteriolar walls compress the underlying venule at a retinal arteriovenous crossing, causing the vein to appear narrowed or “nicked” as it crosses the artery; reflects chronic hypertension and arteriolosclerosis.

avascular_necrosis.definition: A condition in which bone tissue dies as a result of reduced or interrupted blood flow (osteonecrosis), leading to joint pain, reduced function, and possible collapse of the affected bone, most commonly the femoral head.

avascular_graft.definition: A tissue graft that contains no intrinsic blood vessels and depends on host neovascularization and inosculation to establish blood flow after transplantation; without rapid revascularization, it is at risk of ischemic necrosis.

avascularization.definition: The process of becoming avascular or de-vascularized; the loss or absence of blood vessels in a tissue or region, resulting in reduced or absent blood supply.

avobenzone.definition: A UVA ultraviolet-filter used in sunscreen to absorb ultraviolet A radiation; it is photounstable in sunlight and is typically stabilized with other filters to improve photostability.

bevaczizumab.definition: A humanized monoclonal antibody against vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) that inhibits angiogenesis by preventing VEGF from activating its receptors; used in the treatment of various cancers and administered intravenously.

bevacizumab.definition: A humanized monoclonal antibody that binds vascular endothelial growth factor-A (VEGF-A), inhibiting VEGF signaling and angiogenesis; used in cancer therapy (various solid tumors) often in combination with chemotherapy, and administered intravitreally off-label for neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

avastin.definition: A humanized monoclonal antibody against vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) that inhibits angiogenesis; used to treat several cancers (e.g., metastatic colorectal cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, glioblastoma, renal cell carcinoma) and is typically given intravenously.

rosiglitazone.definition: An oral thiazolidinedione antidiabetic agent that activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR‑γ) to increase insulin sensitivity in adipose tissue, muscle, and liver, thereby improving glycemic control in type 2 diabetes; may cause edema, weight gain, and increased risk of heart failure and possibly cardiovascular events.

avandia.definition: Brand-name rosiglitazone; a thiazolidinedione antidiabetic agent that improves insulin sensitivity by activating PPAR-γ; used to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes, usually as add-on therapy; adverse effects include edema, weight gain, and an increased risk of congestive heart failure and ischemic events; contraindicated in patients with known heart failure and used with caution in liver disease.

interferon_beta_1a.definition: A recombinant human type I interferon used as a disease-modifying therapy for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis; administered by intramuscular or subcutaneous injection to reduce relapse rate and lesion activity on MRI; common adverse effects include flu-like symptoms and injection-site reactions.

avonex.definition: An injectable disease-modifying therapy for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis; a recombinant human interferon beta-1a administered by intramuscular injection once weekly to reduce relapse rate and slow disease progression.

avitaminosis.definition: A deficiency disease caused by inadequate intake, absorption, or utilization of vitamins, resulting in various clinical syndromes depending on which vitamins are deficient.

aversion_therapy.definition: A form of behavioral therapy that pairs an unwanted behavior with an aversive stimulus to produce a negative response and reduce or stop the behavior.

aversive_stimulus.definition: An unpleasant or discomfort-inducing stimulus that, when presented after a behavior, decreases the likelihood of that behavior occurring again (punishment) or promotes avoidance of the stimulus in the future. Examples include electric shock, loud noise, or bitter taste.

axenic_culture.definition: A culture containing no other living organisms; a sterile, pure culture of a single microbial species or cell line that is free of contaminants.

av_interval.definition: Time interval between atrial activation and subsequent ventricular activation; in pacemaker programming, the programmed delay from an atrial event (sensed or paced) to the next ventricular activation, used to optimize atrioventricular synchrony.

axillary abscess.definition: A localized collection of pus in the armpit (axillary region) from infection of hair follicles or sweat glands, typically presenting as a painful, fluctuating, red nodule that may drain.

axillary block anesthesia.definition: A regional anesthesia technique in which local anesthetic is injected around the brachial plexus in the axillary region to block sensation of the upper limb, providing anesthesia for procedures of the forearm and hand; duration depends on the anesthetic used.

axillary dissection.definition: A surgical procedure in which axillary (underarm) lymph nodes are removed to stage or treat breast cancer; typically involves removal of Level I and II nodes, and sometimes Level III nodes in a more extensive dissection.

axillary node.definition: A lymph node located in the armpit (axilla) that filters lymph from the upper limb, lateral breast, and chest wall; part of the axillary lymph node basin and involved in immune defense and, in breast cancer, staging of metastatic spread.

axillary node dissection.definition: A surgical procedure in which one or more axillary (armpit) lymph nodes are removed to stage breast cancer or assess nodal involvement, typically involving levels I and II (and sometimes level III) nodes, and may follow or accompany a sentinel lymph node biopsy.

axillary region.definition: Anatomical region of the armpit (axilla), the area beneath the shoulder where the upper limb attaches to the trunk; it contains the axillary vessels and nerves (brachial plexus), lymph nodes, and fat, and is bounded anteriorly by the pectoralis major/minor, posteriorly by the subscapularis, teres major and latissimus dorsi, medially by the thoracic wall, and laterally by the humerus (intertubercular sulcus).

axillary temperature.definition: A measurement of body temperature taken from the armpit (axilla) with a thermometer; readings are typically about 0.5°C to 1.0°C lower than oral readings and it is less accurate for core body temperature, though convenient and noninvasive.

axillary vein.definition: A large vein of the upper limb that drains venous blood from the arm; formed by the union of the brachial veins and basilic vein near the lower border of the teres major, and continuing as the subclavian vein at the lateral border of the first rib.

axillary walls.definition: The axilla is bounded by four walls: anterior wall formed mainly by the pectoralis major and minor (plus subclavius and clavipectoral fascia); medial wall by the upper thoracic wall and serratus anterior; posterior wall by the subscapularis, teres major, latissimus dorsi, and the scapula; and lateral wall by the intertubercular groove of the humerus.

axillofemoral bypass graft.definition: A vascular bypass procedure in which a graft is anastomosed proximally to the axillary artery and distally to the femoral artery to bypass occlusive disease of the distal aorta/iliac arteries and restore blood flow to the lower limb; typically performed when aorta-iliac surgery is not feasible.

axis deviation.definition: An abnormal direction of the heart’s mean electrical axis in the frontal plane, typically seen on ECG; the normal QRS axis is about -30° to +90°, with left axis deviation roughly -30° to -90° and right axis deviation about +100° or more.

axis traction.definition: A form of orthopedic traction applied along the long axis of a limb or body segment to realign fractures or dislocations, usually using weights and pulleys to provide a continuous pulling force during treatment.

axis artery.definition: Definition not found for "axis artery" in standard medical dictionaries. It may be a misspelling or misnomer. Please confirm the intended term (e.g., an upper-extremity artery or a cerebral artery) and I’ll provide the definition.

axis cylinder.definition: The axon of a neuron; the elongated cylindrical process of a nerve cell that conducts impulses away from the cell body.

axion.definition: Not a recognized medical term; there is no medical definition for this word. It refers to a hypothetical elementary particle in particle physics and has no established role in clinical medicine.

axoplasm.definition: The cytoplasm inside a neuron’s axon, including the axonal cytosol and organelles (such as mitochondria, vesicles, and neurofilaments) enclosed by the axonal membrane and distinct from the soma and dendrites.

axoplasmic flow.definition: The movement of cytoplasm and its contents along the axon within the axoplasm, traditionally described as slow anterograde transport from the neuron's cell body toward the synaptic terminal.

axodendritic synapse.definition: A synapse where the axon terminal of one neuron forms a contact with the dendrite of another neuron, typically a chemical synapse in which neurotransmitters are released into the synaptic cleft and bind to receptors on the dendritic membrane to propagate the signal.

axodendrosomatic synapse.definition: A synapse in which the presynaptic axon forms a contact on the soma (cell body) and/or proximal dendrites of the postsynaptic neuron; essentially an axosomatic and/or axodendritic connection.

axoaxonic synapse.definition: Synaptic contact where the axon terminal of one neuron forms a synapse onto the axon terminal of another neuron, thereby modulating the release of neurotransmitter from the latter terminal and influencing the strength of transmission to the postsynaptic neuron. This presynaptic modulation can be inhibitory or facilitatory depending on the circuit.

axonography.definition: Imaging or visualization of nerve axons; an old/rare term for techniques that depict axonal fibers within nerves, now more commonly performed with MR neurography or diffusion-based nerve imaging.

axonotmesis.definition: A peripheral nerve injury in which the axon and its myelin sheath are disrupted with Wallerian degeneration distal to the lesion, while the surrounding connective tissue framework (endoneurium) remains intact, permitting axonal regeneration along preserved tubes.

axon reflex.definition: A reflex where stimulation of a peripheral sensory nerve fiber causes antidromic impulse conduction along its collateral endings, releasing neuropeptides (e.g., CGRP, substance P) at nearby terminals and producing localized vasodilation and neurogenic inflammation, usually without central nervous system involvement.

axon sheath.definition: A fatty insulating layer surrounding many axons, produced by glial cells (Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system and oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system) that speeds electrical impulse conduction via saltatory conduction; gaps between segments are the nodes of Ranvier.

axosomatic synapse.definition: A chemical synapse in which the presynaptic axon terminal forms a synaptic contact directly on the soma (cell body) of the postsynaptic neuron, allowing strong modulation of the postsynaptic cell's excitability (often inhibitory, but can be excitatory depending on the neurotransmitter).

axotomy.definition: A surgical or traumatic transection of a nerve axon, interrupting axonal continuity and transport; the distal segment typically undergoes Wallerian degeneration, while the proximal segment may attempt regeneration depending on the environment.

ayurveda.definition: A traditional system of medicine originating in India that aims to balance the body's doshas (Vata, Pitta, and Kapha) through individualized diet, herbal remedies, lifestyle modifications, and body therapies.

aygestin.definition: A brand-name medication containing norethindrone, a synthetic progestin used for contraception and to treat certain menstrual disorders such as abnormal uterine bleeding and endometriosis.

norethindrone acetate.definition: A synthetic progestin and prodrug of norethindrone (the acetate ester); used in some combined hormonal contraceptives and for gynecologic conditions such as abnormal uterine bleeding and endometriosis; it binds progesterone receptors, suppresses ovulation, and induces secretory changes in the endometrium.

azacitidine.definition: A nucleoside analog of cytidine (5-azacytidine) used as a hypomethylating agent in myelodysplastic syndromes and certain leukemias; it inhibits DNA methyltransferases, leading to DNA hypomethylation and reactivation of silenced genes, and is typically given by subcutaneous or intravenous injection.

myelodysplastic syndrome.definition: A clonal hematologic disorder characterized by ineffective hematopoiesis in the bone marrow, leading to peripheral blood cytopenias and an increased risk of progression to acute myeloid leukemia.

azygos.definition: An adjective meaning not paired; in anatomy, the main unpaired vein on the right side of the thorax that drains the posterior thoracic wall and empties into the superior vena cava.

azygous vein.definition: A major vein of the posterior mediastinum on the right that ascends from the abdomen (via the ascending lumbar vein), receives blood from the posterior intercostal veins and other thoracic veins, arches over the root of the right lung to drain into the superior vena cava, and forms part of the azygos venous system that provides a collateral pathway between the inferior and superior vena cavae.

azygos lobe.definition: An anatomical variant of the right upper lung lobe produced when the azygos vein arches over the apex and invaginates into the lung, creating the azygos fissure; it is not a true separate lobe and usually has no clinical significance.

azygography.definition: A radiographic procedure in which contrast medium is used to opacify the azygos venous system, visualizing the azygos vein and its tributaries to assess thoracic venous anatomy, anomalies, or obstruction.

azathioprine.definition: An immunosuppressive purine analog (a prodrug of 6-mercaptopurine) that inhibits de novo purine synthesis, reducing lymphocyte proliferation; used to prevent organ transplant rejection and treat various autoimmune diseases.

azelaic acid.definition: A naturally occurring nine-carbon dicarboxylic acid used topically as an anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial treatment for acne and rosacea, and as a depigmenting agent by inhibiting tyrosinase and reducing melanin synthesis.

azelastine.definition: A second-generation antihistamine (H1 receptor antagonist) used to treat symptoms of allergic rhinitis and allergic conjunctivitis; administered as a nasal spray or eye drops; it blocks histamine receptors with less sedation than first-generation antihistamines.

azelex.definition: A topical azelaic acid preparation used to treat acne and rosacea; it has antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory effects and helps normalize skin keratinization to reduce pimples and redness.

azilect.definition: A selective monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) inhibitor used in Parkinson's disease to increase and sustain dopamine levels in the brain; can be given as initial monotherapy or as an add-on to levodopa.

rasagiline.definition: A selective, irreversible monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) inhibitor used to treat Parkinson disease by increasing brain dopamine levels through inhibition of dopamine breakdown; used as monotherapy in early disease or as an adjunct to levodopa in later stages.

azithromycin.definition: A macrolide antibiotic (an azalide) used to treat a range of bacterial infections by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis through binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit; commonly used for respiratory tract infections, skin infections, otitis media, and certain sexually transmitted infections.

azlocillin.definition: A semisynthetic broad-spectrum penicillin antibiotic of the ureidopenicillin subclass, active against many Gram-negative bacteria (including Pseudomonas aeruginosa) and some Gram-positive cocci; used for serious infections caused by susceptible organisms and administered parenterally. It is susceptible to beta-lactamase degradation.

azlocillin sodium.definition: A parenteral broad-spectrum penicillin (ureidopenicillin) in the sodium salt form; inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis and is active against many Gram-negative bacteria (including Pseudomonas species) and some Gram-positive cocci; susceptible to beta-lactamases; used for serious infections caused by susceptible organisms.

azidothymidine.definition: A nucleoside analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used in HIV treatment and for prevention of mother-to-child transmission; it inhibits viral DNA synthesis by acting as a chain terminator during reverse transcription.

azt.definition: A nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used to treat HIV infection and reduce mother-to-child transmission; it inhibits viral DNA synthesis by acting as a chain terminator during reverse transcription.

retrovir.definition: A brand-name antiretroviral medication containing zidovudine (AZT); a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used to treat HIV infection.

azulfidine.definition: Brand name for sulfasalazine, a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) used to treat inflammatory conditions such as ulcerative colitis and rheumatoid arthritis; it is a prodrug activated in the colon to sulfapyridine and 5-aminosalicylic acid.

sulfasalazine.definition: A sulfa-containing prodrug used as a disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drug and anti-inflammatory for ulcerative colitis; it is cleaved in the colon to 5-aminosalicylic acid and sulfapyridine, which provide its therapeutic effects.

azatadine.definition: A first-generation oral antihistamine (H1 receptor antagonist) used to treat allergic rhinitis and urticaria; commonly causes drowsiness and anticholinergic effects.

azatadine maleate.definition: A salt form of azatadine; a first-generation antihistamine (H1 receptor antagonist) used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, conjunctivitis, and urticaria; may cause drowsiness and anticholinergic adverse effects.

azole.definition: A class of antifungal medications characterized by an azole ring; they inhibit fungal ergosterol synthesis by blocking the cytochrome P450 enzyme lanosterol 14-α-demethylase (CYP51), thereby disrupting fungal cell membrane formation.

azoospermia.definition: Absence of measurable sperm in the ejaculate, diagnosed when semen analysis shows no spermatozoa (usually confirmed with two separate samples). It may result from impaired sperm production (nonobstructive) or from a blockage of the reproductive tract (obstructive).

azotemia.definition: An elevation of nitrogenous waste products (primarily blood urea nitrogen and creatinine) in the blood due to reduced kidney filtration, often reflecting kidney dysfunction. It is categorized as prerenal (reduced renal perfusion), intrinsic (renal parenchymal disease), or postrenal (urinary tract obstruction).

azoturia.definition: A condition in which there is an excess of nitrogenous waste, particularly urea, in the urine, usually reflecting increased protein breakdown or muscle damage (exertional rhabdomyolysis can be a contributing cause).

machado-joseph disease.definition: A hereditary autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cerebellar ataxia and brainstem signs (often including oculomotor abnormalities and dysarthria), caused by a CAG-repeat expansion in the ATXN3 gene; the most common form of spinocerebellar ataxia, also known as spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3).

ulcerative colitis.definition: Causes inflammation and sores (also called ulcers), in the lining of the rectum and colon.

systemic inflammatory diseases.definition: A group of immune-mediated disorders in which inflammation involves multiple organ systems, often with constitutional symptoms (fever, malaise) and elevated inflammatory markers, arising from dysregulated innate and adaptive immune responses.

invasive breast cancer.definition: Invasive breast cancer is cancer that has spread beyond the ducts or lobules into surrounding breast tissue and may metastasize to lymph nodes or distant organs.

lumpectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which a growth in the breast is removed; the growth may be cancerous or non-cancerous.

modified radical mastectomy.definition: A breast cancer surgery that removes the entire breast, including the nipple–areola complex and axillary lymph nodes, while preserving the pectoralis major muscle.

mastectomy.definition: Surgery to remove all or part of a breast.

propionibacterium acnes.definition: A gram-positive, anaerobic, nonmotile rod that is part of the normal human skin flora, particularly in hair follicles, and is implicated in the pathogenesis of acne vulgaris by hydrolyzing sebum and triggering inflammation.

esophageal veins.definition: Veins draining the esophagus, forming the esophageal venous plexus; they drain into the azygos/hemiazygos system (upper and mid esophagus) and into the left gastric vein (lower esophagus), providing a portosystemic anastomosis; dilation can lead to esophageal varices in portal hypertension.

right brachiocephalic vein.definition: A short, wide vein formed behind the right sternoclavicular joint by the union of the right internal jugular and right subclavian veins; it drains blood into the superior vena cava and collects blood from the right side of the head and neck, the right upper limb, and parts of the thoracic wall.

hemiazygos veins.definition: A vein on the left side of the posterior thorax that drains the lower left posterior intercostal veins (typically the 9th–11th) and left subcostal veins; it ascends on the left of the thoracic vertebrae and crosses to the right to join the azygos vein around the T9–T11 level, forming part of the azygos venous system and providing collateral drainage to the superior vena cava if obstructed.

intertubercular sulcus.definition: A groove on the anterior surface of the proximal humerus between the greater and lesser tubercles that houses the tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii (also called the bicipital groove).

skull.definition: The bones that form the head, enclosing and protecting the brain.

vertebrae.definition: One of the bones that compose the spinal column; each has a vertebral body, a vertebral arch with processes, and articulating facets that connect with adjacent bones, collectively protecting the spinal cord and supporting the body's weight.

long head of triceps brachii.definition: One of the three heads of the triceps brachii muscle. It originates from the infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula, inserts on the olecranon via the common tendon, and primarily extends the elbow; it also assists in shoulder extension and adduction because it crosses the glenohumeral joint. Innervated by the radial nerve.

subscapularis.definition: A large triangular muscle on the anterior surface of the scapula, forming part of the rotator cuff; it medially rotates the arm and stabilizes the shoulder by keeping the humeral head in the glenoid, originating from the subscapular fossa and inserting on the lesser tubercle of the humerus.

pectoralis minor.definition: A thin, triangular muscle beneath the pectoralis major that originates from the 3rd–5th ribs and inserts on the coracoid process of the scapula; it protracts and downwardly rotates the scapula, stabilizes the shoulder, and assists in forced inspiration by elevating the ribs.

subclavius.definition: A small triangular muscle beneath the clavicle that depresses and stabilizes the clavicle during shoulder movements; it arises from the first rib and inserts on the inferior surface of the clavicle and is innervated by the nerve to subclavius (C5–C6).

clavipectoral fascia.definition: A fascial layer of the anterior chest wall that extends from the clavicle to the costal region, enclosing the subclavius and pectoralis minor; it splits around the pectoralis minor, continues inferiorly as part of the axillary fascia, and is pierced by structures such as the cephalic vein and thoracoacromial vessels.

deltoideus.definition: A muscle of the shoulder that forms the rounded contour; it abducts the arm. Its anterior fibers flex and medially rotate the arm, the middle fibers abduct, and the posterior fibers extend and laterally rotate the arm.

bronchogram.definition: A radiographic sign in which air-filled bronchi are visualized as dark, branching structures within an area of lung opacification; it can also refer to the radiographic image produced during bronchography outlining the bronchial tree.

parvovirus b19.definition: Small nonenveloped, single-stranded DNA virus of the Parvoviridae family (genus Erythrovirus) that infects humans; commonly causes erythema infectiosum (fifth disease) in children and can cause transient aplastic crises in individuals with hemolytic anemia, as well as fetal infection that may result in hydrops fetalis or miscarriage.

erythema infectiosum.definition: A contagious viral illness caused by parvovirus B19, most common in children; characterized by a bright red facial rash ('slapped cheek') followed by a fine, lace-like rash on the trunk and extremities; usually mild and self-limited.

fifth disease.definition: A contagious viral illness caused by parvovirus B19 (also known as erythema infectiosum) that chiefly affects children; it typically begins with fever and malaise, followed by a characteristic bright red, "slapped-cheek" facial rash and a lace-like rash on the trunk and limbs, usually self-limited.

babesia.definition: An intraerythrocytic protozoan parasite of the genus Babesia that infects red blood cells and causes babesiosis, transmitted mainly by Ixodes tick bites (and less commonly via blood transfusion); presents with malaria-like symptoms and hemolytic anemia, and is diagnosed by blood smear or PCR with treatment varying by severity (e.g., atovaquone–azithromycin for mild disease, clindamycin–quinine for severe).

ixodes dammini.definition: An older taxonomic synonym for Ixodes scapularis, the black-legged tick (deer tick); a three-host tick native to North America and a vector for Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi) and other pathogens such as Anaplasma phagocytophilum and Babesia microti.

hemolysis.definition: Describes when red blood cells start breaking down before they are supposed to.

clindamycin.definition: A lincosamide antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit; effective against many anaerobic bacteria and some Gram-positive cocci, and used to treat a variety of infections when penicillin is contraindicated or ineffective; available in oral, intravenous, and topical forms.

lyme disease.definition: Caused by small bugs (parasites) that suck blood and can pass on disease.

babesiasis.definition: A tick-borne protozoal infection caused by Babesia spp. (most often Babesia microti) transmitted by Ixodes ticks; it causes fever and hemolytic anemia and can be severe in asplenic or immunocompromised individuals. Diagnosis is by identification of Babesia in red blood cells on a blood smear or by PCR; treatment for mild–moderate disease is atovaquone plus azithromycin, while severe disease is treated with clindamycin plus quinine (and may require exchange transfusion).

babinski reflex.definition: Stroking the lateral sole elicits dorsiflexion of the great toe with fanning of the other toes; normal in infants due to immature corticospinal tracts, but in adults indicates upper motor neuron (corticospinal tract) dysfunction.

babinski sign.definition: A neurological sign indicating corticospinal (upper motor neuron) tract dysfunction; when the lateral sole is stroked, the big toe dorsiflexes and the other toes fan out. It is normal in infants but suggests UMN pathology in adults.

dorsiflexion.definition: Upward bending of the foot at the ankle joint, bringing the toes closer to the shin; the opposite of plantarflexion.

extensor plantar response.definition: A neurological sign in which stroking the sole of the foot produces dorsiflexion of the great toe (and often fanning of the other toes), indicating corticospinal (upper motor neuron) tract dysfunction; also known as a positive Babinski sign.

pronation.definition: When a foot or lower arm turns down. For example, when your palm is down.

supination.definition: The upward rotation of the lower arm or foot. Describes when the palm is up, or the foot is leaning outward.

genu recurvatum.definition: Hyperextension deformity of the knee in which the leg extends beyond its normal neutral position, typically seen during weight-bearing; may result from ligament laxity or injury (such as posterior cruciate ligament insufficiency), neuromuscular weakness, or congenital/developmental factors.

baby bottle caries.definition: A form of early childhood caries characterized by rapid decay of primary teeth in infants and toddlers, commonly the maxillary incisors, caused by prolonged nighttime exposure to fermentable sugars in a bottle or sippy cup, which allows acid produced by oral bacteria to demineralize enamel.

caries.definition: Holes in your teeth. Also called cavities or tooth decay.

tooth decay.definition: Infectious disease that attacks the teeth. Also called dental caries.

mycobacterium bovis.definition: A slow-growing, acid-fast bacterium of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex that primarily causes tuberculosis in cattle (bovine tuberculosis) but can infect humans; transmission is via inhalation of respiratory droplets or ingestion of unpasteurized dairy products. It is inherently resistant to pyrazinamide, and attenuated strains from M. bovis are used to make the BCG vaccine.

bladder cancer.definition: A malignant tumor arising from the urinary bladder lining (most often urothelial/transitional cell carcinoma); it commonly presents with painless hematuria and is associated with smoking, exposure to certain industrial chemicals, and chronic bladder irritation.

intravesical.definition: Located within the urinary bladder; describes administration of substances directly into the bladder or procedures targeting the bladder.

carcinoma in situ.definition: A malignant epithelial neoplasm in which cancerous cells are confined to the epithelium and have not invaded through the basement membrane, noninvasive but with a high risk of progression to invasive carcinoma if not treated.

in situ.definition: Latin for "in its original place"; describes a lesion or tumor that remains confined to its tissue of origin and does not invade neighboring tissues or penetrate the basement membrane.

granuloma.definition: A focal area of chronic inflammation consisting of a collection of macrophages (often epithelioid cells) with or without multinucleated giant cells, typically surrounded by lymphocytes; forms in response to persistent antigenic stimulation such as certain infections (e.g., Mycobacterium tuberculosis), foreign material, or immune-mediated diseases (e.g., sarcoidosis).

disseminated tuberculosis.definition: A form of tuberculosis in which Mycobacterium tuberculosis spreads hematogenously to cause widespread infection of multiple organs, often with fever, weight loss, night sweats, and fatigue; may show millet-seed–like nodules in the lungs on imaging and involvement of liver, spleen, bone marrow, meninges, and other tissues (also called miliary TB) and can be life-threatening if not treated.

pulmonary tuberculosis.definition: A contagious infection of the lungs caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, transmitted via airborne droplets. It typically presents with a chronic productive cough (often with sputum or blood), chest pain, fever, night sweats, and weight loss; diagnosis is by sputum smear/culture or molecular tests and chest imaging. Treatment requires a prolonged, multi-drug anti-tuberculous regimen, usually for about 6 months or longer.

bacillus cereus.definition: A Gram-positive, rod-shaped, spore-forming bacterium found in soil and food; a common cause of food poisoning with vomiting (emetic) or diarrheal syndromes due to toxin production, often linked to reheated rice and other leftovers.

bacilli.definition: Rod-shaped bacteria; a morphological category of bacteria with cylindrical, elongated cells. The term bacilli (plural) refers to such bacteria, which can be Gram-positive or Gram-negative and include spore-forming genera such as Bacillus and Clostridium.

bacillemia.definition: The presence of bacilli (rod-shaped bacteria) in the bloodstream, i.e., a form of bacteremia that may be associated with systemic infection or sepsis.

bacillaceae.definition: A family of Gram-positive, rod-shaped, endospore-forming bacteria within the order Bacillales; includes genera such as Bacillus and Geobacillus; widely distributed in soil and water; many species are environmental, with some being medically or industrially important.

enterotoxin.definition: A toxin produced by certain bacteria that acts on the gastrointestinal tract to stimulate secretion of fluids and electrolytes into the intestinal lumen, often causing diarrhea.

pullorum.definition: An avian infectious disease of young poultry caused by a Salmonella bacterium, transmitted vertically from infected breeders to offspring, and characterized by septicemia and high mortality.

pullorum disease.definition: A contagious infection of poultry caused by Salmonella enterica serovar Pullorum, primarily affecting young chicks and causing high mortality; transmitted vertically through eggs from infected breeders, and presenting with diarrhea, pallor, depression, and poor growth.

bacillary dysentery.definition: An acute bacterial infection of the colon, most commonly due to Shigella species (shigellosis), causing inflammatory colitis with fever, abdominal cramps, and frequent small-volume, bloody or mucus-containing stools with tenesmus; transmitted by fecal-oral contamination from contaminated food or water.

shigellosis.definition: A bacterial infection of the large intestine caused by Shigella species, characterized by acute fever, abdominal cramps, and inflammatory, often bloody diarrhea (dysentery); transmitted by the fecal-oral route via contaminated food or water.

cat scratch fever.definition: An infection caused by Bartonella henselae transmitted by cat scratches or bites, presenting with a papule at the inoculation site followed by tender regional lymphadenopathy and often low-grade fever; it is usually self-limited in healthy individuals, with supportive care and antibiotics (e.g., azithromycin) used in more severe cases or in immunocompromised patients.

tuberculin test.definition: A diagnostic test for latent tuberculosis infection in which purified protein derivative (PPD) tuberculin is injected intradermally and the size of the resulting induration is measured after 48–72 hours to determine prior TB infection.

tuberculin.definition: A purified protein derivative of Mycobacterium tuberculosis used in tuberculin skin testing (Mantoux test) to detect prior TB infection by eliciting a delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction after intradermal injection; the reaction is read by measuring induration at 48–72 hours.

hypogammaglobulinemia.definition: A deficiency of one or more immunoglobulin (antibody) isotypes in the blood, most often low IgG with or without low IgA/IgM, leading to impaired humoral immunity and increased susceptibility to recurrent infections (especially sinopulmonary and gastrointestinal), occurring as primary (inherited) or secondary to disease or therapy.

immunosuppression.definition: When your body can't fight diseases.

isoniazid.definition: A bactericidal antitubercular prodrug activated by mycobacterial KatG that inhibits mycolic acid synthesis in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, used to treat active TB and prevent TB infection.

immunodeficiency.definition: A state in which the immune system's ability to fight infections is reduced or absent, leading to increased susceptibility to infections. It can be primary (inherited) or secondary (acquired) due to diseases (e.g., HIV), medications (e.g., immunosuppressants), malnutrition, or other factors.

protozoa.definition: A diverse group of single-celled, eukaryotic microorganisms that are typically motile and heterotrophic, feeding by phagocytosis; historically classified as protists.

tetracycline.definition: A broad-spectrum antibiotic of the tetracycline class that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by reversibly binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit; used to treat acne, respiratory and genitourinary infections, and infections by atypical pathogens. Contraindicated in pregnancy and in children under 8 due to risk of tooth discoloration and effects on bone growth; common adverse effects include GI upset and photosensitivity; absorption can be reduced by dairy products and certain metal ions (e.g., calcium, magnesium, aluminum, iron).

trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.definition: A fixed-dose antibiotic combination of trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole that inhibits sequential steps in bacterial folate synthesis, blocking DNA synthesis and bacterial growth; used to treat and prevent a range of infections (e.g., urinary tract infections, bronchitis, certain gastrointestinal infections, and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prophylaxis in immunocompromised patients).

rifampicin.definition: An antibiotic of the rifamycin class that inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, blocking RNA synthesis; bactericidal against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and other bacteria, used to treat tuberculosis and other mycobacterial infections and for meningococcal prophylaxis; a strong CYP450 inducer with potential hepatotoxicity and drug interactions.

bacteremic.definition: The presence of bacteria in the bloodstream; can be transient or persistent and may lead to systemic infection (septicemia), often detected by blood cultures.

bacteraemia.definition: The presence of viable bacteria in the bloodstream, which may be transient or persistent and can occur during infection or after medical procedures; it may lead to septicemia if the host immune response becomes systemic.

septicemia.definition: A very serious infection in your blood caused by a germ (a bacteria). Also called sepsis.

vaginosis.definition: An abnormal vaginal discharge and odor caused by disruption of the normal vaginal flora—typically reduced lactobacilli with overgrowth of anaerobic bacteria (most commonly Gardnerella vaginalis)—often referred to as bacterial vaginosis and not caused by a fungal infection.

bacterium.definition: A single-celled prokaryotic microorganism that lacks a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; typically has a cell wall containing peptidoglycan and reproduces by binary fission; some species are pathogenic, while others are harmless or beneficial.

spirochetes.definition: A group of slender, spiral-shaped bacteria (Spirochaetes) that move by axial filaments, producing a corkscrew-like motion; includes notable pathogens such as Treponema pallidum, Borrelia burgdorferi, and Leptospira spp.

vibrios.definition: A genus of curved, Gram-negative, motile bacteria that inhabit marine and brackish environments; several species are human pathogens causing cholera, gastroenteritis, wound infections, and septicemia, typically acquired via contaminated seafood or water.

cholangitis.definition: Acute bacterial inflammation of the bile ducts, typically caused by biliary obstruction (e.g., gallstones or a stricture); presents with fever, jaundice, and right upper quadrant pain and can progress to sepsis; managed with antibiotics and biliary drainage (often via ERCP).

enteritis.definition: Inflammation of the mucosa of the small intestine, typically caused by infection or irritation, presenting with abdominal pain and cramping, diarrhea (often watery), and sometimes nausea, vomiting, or fever.

gastroenteritis.definition: When the lining of your intestines is swollen and irritated. It is caused by different kinds of germs (a virus, bacteria, or parasites). Also called "stomach flu," but it is not really the flu.

weakness.definition: A reduced ability to generate muscular force, resulting in decreased strength or endurance; can be due to deconditioning, fatigue, malnutrition, systemic illness, or neuromuscular disorders.

itch.definition: A sensation on the skin that provokes the urge to scratch; commonly caused by irritation or inflammation but can arise from systemic conditions, and is mediated by specialized itch pathways and mediators such as histamine.

vulvovaginitis.definition: Inflammation of the vulva and vagina presenting with itching, burning, redness, and often discharge; commonly due to infections (such as Candida, bacterial vaginosis, or Trichomonas) but also caused by irritants, allergies, hormonal changes, or other dermatologic conditions.

vagina.definition: An elastic, muscular canal in the female reproductive tract that extends from the external opening to the cervix, forming part of the birth canal and serving as the passage for sexual intercourse, menstrual flow, and childbirth.

lavage.definition: The washing out or irrigation of a body cavity or organ with a fluid (often saline) to remove contents, dilute toxins, or obtain a diagnostic sample.

bactrim.definition: A fixed-dose antibiotic combination of sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim (co-trimoxazole) used to treat a range of bacterial infections; it acts by sequentially inhibiting bacterial folate synthesis.

gentamicin.definition: An aminoglycoside antibiotic that irreversibly binds the 30S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis and causing misreading of mRNA; used for serious gram-negative infections (and certain gram-positive infections in combination), typically administered parenterally, with notable risks including nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity and the need for therapeutic drug monitoring.

bacteriuria.definition: Presence of bacteria in the urine, which may be asymptomatic or associated with a urinary tract infection; typically diagnosed by positive urine culture or urinalysis showing bacteria.

laryngitis.definition: Swelling and irritation of the voice box (larynx), usually caused by a viral infection; results in hoarseness.

vessel.definition: A tubular structure that conducts blood or lymph through the body, including arteries, veins, capillaries, and lymphatic vessels.

valves.definition: Structures consisting of leaflets that divide the chambers of the heart and prevent the backflow of blood from one chamber to another during contraction of the heart.

culture.definition: The growth and propagation of microorganisms (e.g., bacteria, fungi) on or in a nutrient medium under controlled conditions; a sample that has been cultured for diagnostic or research purposes.

murmur.definition: A sound heard during a heart examination produced by turbulent blood flow through the chambers or valves of the heart, often due to valve abnormalities; most of these sounds are benign, but some indicate underlying heart disease.

balanitis.definition: Inflammation of the glans penis (the head of the penis), often due to infection (most commonly Candida), irritation, or dermatitis, presenting with redness, swelling, itching, and sometimes pain or discharge.

balanitis diabetica.definition: Inflammation of the glans penis in the setting of diabetes mellitus, most often due to infectious balanitis (commonly Candida) or irritant dermatitis; associated with hyperglycemia and poor glycemic control.

balanitis xerotica obliterans.definition: A chronic inflammatory, sclerosing disease of the glans penis and foreskin (penile lichen sclerosus), presenting with white, atrophic plaques that can cause phimosis or meatal stenosis. Management includes potent topical corticosteroids, with circumcision or other surgery for refractory cases; there is a potential risk of progression to penile cancer with long-standing disease.

balanoposthitis.definition: An inflammatory condition of the glans penis and the foreskin (prepuce), usually due to infection (most commonly Candida or bacteria) or irritation, often associated with poor hygiene or diabetes; presents with redness, swelling, itching or burning, and sometimes discharge; treated with hygiene measures, topical antifungal or antibiotic therapy, and management of underlying causes.

balanorrhagia.definition: Bleeding from the glans penis; a symptom that can result from balanitis, trauma, infection, or penile lesions.

balantidiasis.definition: An intestinal infection caused by Balantidium coli, a ciliate protozoan; acquired by ingestion of cysts in contaminated food or water; typically presents with dysentery and chronic diarrhea with abdominal pain, sometimes blood or mucus in stool; treated with tetracycline or metronidazole.

balanic hypospadias.definition: A congenital malformation in which the urethral opening is located on the glans penis (balan) rather than at the distal tip of the penis; a distal form of hypospadias often with a hooded foreskin and possible mild ventral curvature, usually corrected surgically in childhood.

glandular hypospadias.definition: A congenital defect where the urethral opening is on the ventral surface of the glans penis (the gland), near the corona, representing a distal form of hypospadias.

hypospadias.definition: A congenital malformation in males in which the urethral opening is on the ventral (underside) surface of the penis rather than at the tip, often with penile curvature (chordee) and an abnormal foreskin; management is typically surgical repair in infancy or early childhood.

urethral stenosis.definition: A narrowing of the urethral lumen causing partial or complete obstruction to urinary flow; typically due to scar tissue from infection, inflammation, trauma, or prior instrumentation, and may cause a weak or interrupted stream, hesitancy, and incomplete bladder emptying.

glans penis.definition: The rounded, highly innervated distal end of the penis, formed by the expanded corpus spongiosum; it bears the external urethral opening and is usually covered by the foreskin in uncircumcised males.

glans clitoridis.definition: A small, highly sensitive, erectile distal part of the clitoris—the exposed knob at the anterior end of the clitoral body—formed by erectile tissue, usually covered by the clitoral hood, and engorging with blood during arousal.

craniosynostosis.definition: Premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures in infancy, preventing normal skull expansion as the brain grows; can cause abnormal head shape and, if severe, elevated intracranial pressure and potential neurodevelopmental issues. Management often involves surgical release/remodeling of the affected sutures.

baller-gerold syndrome.definition: An extremely rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by craniosynostosis (premature fusion of skull sutures) and radial ray defects (radial aplasia/hypoplasia or thumb anomalies), often with facial dysmorphism and short stature; caused by biallelic mutations in the RECQL4 gene.

bamboo spine.definition: A radiographic appearance seen in advanced ankylosing spondylitis in which vertical syndesmophytes ossify and bridge adjacent vertebral bodies, producing a rigid, bamboo-like spine.

poker spine.definition: Not a recognized medical term. I couldn’t find a standard definition for “poker spine” in medical dictionaries. If you meant a different term or can share context (symptoms, area, spelling), I can help define the correct term.

ball-and-socket joint.definition: A synovial joint in which a rounded head of one bone fits into a cup-shaped socket of another bone, allowing movement in multiple planes (flexion–extension, abduction–adduction, and rotation); examples are the shoulder and hip.

ballance's sign.definition: A sign of intra-abdominal bleeding (classically from splenic rupture) in which percussion reveals dullness in the left upper quadrant or left flank due to intraperitoneal blood pooling.

ballottement.definition: A clinical sign in which a freely movable structure within a fluid-filled cavity rebounds when tapped, used to detect intrauterine pregnancy or joint effusion.

ballottable head.definition: A fetal head that is not yet engaged and can be displaced by palpation and then rebounds to its original position when pressure is released; indicates a floating presenting part within the uterus.

ball of the foot.definition: The padded region of the sole of the foot just behind the toes, over the heads of the metatarsal bones, that bears weight and assists in propulsion during walking.

mitral valve.definition: The valve that controls the one-way flow of blood from the left atrium to the left ventricle.

pulmonary arteries.definition: Arteries that carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs for oxygenation; the main vessel is the pulmonary trunk, which divides into the left and right pulmonary arteries that branch throughout the lungs to reach the alveolar capillaries, where gas exchange occurs. Blood then returns to the left atrium via the pulmonary veins.

portal hypertension.definition: An abnormal increase in pressure within the portal venous system, usually due to hepatic cirrhosis or obstruction of portal blood flow; it predisposes to variceal bleeding, ascites, and splenomegaly. It is quantified by the hepatic venous pressure gradient, with a gradient above 5 mmHg indicating portal hypertension and higher thresholds (>10–12 mmHg) associated with variceal bleeding risk.

portacaval shunt.definition: A surgical procedure that creates a connection between the portal venous system and the systemic venous circulation (typically portal vein to the inferior vena cava) to decompress portal hypertension by diverting portal blood away from the liver; historically used to prevent or treat variceal bleeding but carries a high risk of hepatic encephalopathy.

bangkok hemorrhagic fever.definition: An historical term for dengue hemorrhagic fever, a severe form of dengue infection caused by dengue virus, characterized by high fever, hemorrhagic manifestations (bleeding, bruising), thrombocytopenia, plasma leakage with hemoconcentration, and potential progression to hypovolemic shock; transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes in tropical regions.

pericardial effusion.definition: A pathological accumulation of fluid in the pericardial cavity surrounding the heart, which can impair cardiac filling and, if rapid or large, cause cardiac tamponade; etiologies include infection, inflammation, malignancy, uremia, autoimmune disease, trauma, and idiopathic.

sydenham's chorea.definition: An autoimmune movement disorder associated with acute rheumatic fever, caused by cross-reactive antibodies after a group A Streptococcus infection; presents with abrupt, involuntary, irregular choreiform movements of the face, tongue, and limbs, often with hypotonia and emotional lability in children; typically self-limited, resolving over weeks to months, with management targeting the underlying rheumatic fever and symptomatic control.

hemiballismus.definition: A rare hyperkinetic movement disorder characterized by sudden, violent, flinging movements of the proximal limbs on one side of the body, typically caused by a lesion in the contralateral subthalamic nucleus (most often due to lacunar stroke).

ballism.definition: Ballism is a hyperkinetic movement disorder with involuntary, abrupt, large-amplitude, flinging movements of the proximal limbs, typically unilateral (hemiballismus) due to a lesion of the contralateral subthalamic nucleus (often from a stroke); bilateral cases can occur with metabolic disturbances such as severe hyperglycemia.

trigeminal neuralgia.definition: Pain from a disorder of the trigeminal nerve, the chief sensory nerve of the face. Also called tic douloureux.

balloon tamponade.definition: A technique that uses a balloon-tipped catheter placed in a bleeding site and inflated to apply pressure (tamponade) to compress bleeding vessels and halt hemorrhage; commonly used for epistaxis and postpartum uterine bleeding, among other sites.

balloon septostomy.definition: A catheter-based procedure in which a balloon is passed across the atrial septum, inflated, and withdrawn to tear or enlarge the opening, creating an interatrial communication to improve mixing of venous and arterial blood in certain congenital heart defects (most notably transposition of the great arteries).

rashkind procedure.definition: A percutaneous catheter-based emergency palliation in neonates with transposition of the great arteries that creates or enlarges an interatrial communication by tearing the atrial septum (balloon atrial septostomy) to improve systemic oxygenation until definitive repair.

circumcision.definition: The removal of the foreskin of the penis in surgery.

irrigation.definition: The washing or flushing of a body part, wound, or cavity with a steady stream of fluid—usually sterile saline—to cleanse debris, reduce contamination, and sometimes deliver medications.

smear.definition: A sample of cells or other material spread in a thin layer on a glass slide for microscopic examination, used to assess cellular morphology or detect pathogens (e.g., blood smear, Pap smear).

mesalamine.definition: A 5-aminosalicylic acid derivative that acts locally in the colon to reduce inflammation; used to treat inflammatory bowel diseases such as ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease with colitis, typically in colon-targeted oral or rectal formulations.

balsalazide.definition: A prodrug of 5-aminosalicylic acid (mesalamine) used to treat inflammatory bowel disease, especially ulcerative colitis; the azo bond links mesalamine to a carrier that is cleaved by colonic bacteria to release active mesalamine.

balneotherapy.definition: Therapeutic bathing in mineral-rich waters (and sometimes mud) used to treat or alleviate musculoskeletal and skin conditions, as well as for relaxation.

balneology.definition: The science of therapeutic bathing and the medical use of mineral waters, muds, and other bath therapies for health promotion and disease treatment.

balkan tubulointerstitial nephritis.definition: A chronic, slowly progressive tubulointerstitial nephritis occurring in populations of the Balkan region, traditionally linked to aristolochic acid exposure from Aristolochia-containing plants; histology shows interstitial fibrosis with tubular atrophy and inflammation, leading to chronic kidney disease and a markedly increased risk of upper tract urothelial carcinoma (renal pelvis/ureter). Also known as Balkan endemic nephropathy.

hip.definition: Region of the body where the thigh meets the pelvis; the hip joint is a ball-and-socket joint formed by the acetabulum of the pelvis and the head of the femur, permitting movements such as flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, and rotation.

shoulder.definition: The shoulder is the region where the upper limb attaches to the trunk, comprising the glenohumeral (shoulder) joint between the head of the humerus and the glenoid cavity of the scapula, the shoulder girdle (scapula and clavicle), and the surrounding muscles, ligaments, and tendons that enable wide-ranging movement of the arm.

barium sulfate.definition: An insoluble radiopaque contrast agent used to visualize the gastrointestinal tract on X-ray studies; administered as a suspension (by mouth or enema) and coats the mucosa to provide a high-contrast image. It is not absorbed from the GI tract and can cause complications such as aspiration pneumonitis, constipation, or inflammatory reaction if leaked into the peritoneum in the setting of perforation.

entecavir.definition: An antiviral medication (guanosine nucleoside analogue) that inhibits HBV DNA polymerase, used to treat chronic hepatitis B by suppressing viral replication.

baralyme.definition: A carbon dioxide absorbent used in anesthesia machines; a solid mixture of barium hydroxide and calcium hydroxide (with moisture) that scrub CO2 from exhaled gases, but can produce toxic carbon monoxide when desiccated or used with certain halogenated anesthetics.

barany's test.definition: A vestibular function test in which warm or cold water (or air) is introduced into the external auditory canal to provoke endolymphatic currents in the horizontal semicircular canal, causing nystagmus; used to assess the integrity of the vestibular system, especially unilateral vestibular function.

caloric test.definition: A vestibular function test in which warm or cold water (or air) is introduced into the external auditory canal to stimulate the horizontal semicircular canal and evoke the vestibulo-ocular reflex (nystagmus); used to assess vestibular integrity, especially unilateral function, and often performed as part of ENG or VNG testing.

sycosis barbae.definition: A chronic bacterial folliculitis of the beard region, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus, presenting as erythematous papules and pustules around hair follicles, often with crusting and sometimes tender nodules or abscesses; treated with topical or systemic antibiotics.

barbiturate.definition: A class of sedative-hypnotic drugs derived from barbituric acid that depress central nervous system activity by enhancing GABA-A receptor–mediated chloride influx; they produce sedation and sleep at lower doses and anesthesia at higher doses, have been used as sedatives, hypnotics, anticonvulsants, and anesthetics, but carry risks of tolerance, dependence, withdrawal, and overdose.

barbiturate coma.definition: A medically induced coma achieved by high-dose barbiturate administration (e.g., pentobarbital, thiopental) to suppress cerebral activity, lower cerebral metabolic demand and intracranial pressure, and control refractory intracranial hypertension or seizures in neurocritical care.

barbiturate poisoning.definition: Barbiturate poisoning is an overdose of barbiturate sedative-hypnotic drugs causing central nervous system depression ranging from sedation to coma, with respiratory depression, hypotension, hypothermia, and potential death; management is supportive (airway protection and ventilation, circulatory support), with gastrointestinal decontamination if early and observation for complications; no specific antidote exists.

barbiturism.definition: Habitual or addictive use of barbiturate drugs, typically with tolerance, physical dependence, withdrawal symptoms upon cessation, and a risk of overdose.

os trigonum.definition: An accessory ossicle on the posterior talus formed when a secondary ossification center fails to fuse; it can be asymptomatic or cause posterior ankle impingement and pain, particularly with plantar flexion.

barre's pyramidal sign.definition: An obscure or possibly obsolete sign indicating dysfunction of the pyramidal (corticospinal) tract, i.e., an upper motor neuron lesion.

barrett's esophagus.definition: The abnormal growth of stomach or small intestine cells in the esophagus, resulting from damage caused by the reflux of stomach acid; occasionally may transform into cancer.

barrett's syndrome.definition: A premalignant condition in which chronic gastroesophageal reflux causes replacement of the distal esophageal squamous epithelium with metaplastic columnar (intestinal-type) epithelium, often with goblet cells; associated with an increased risk of esophageal adenocarcinoma and monitored by endoscopic surveillance with biopsies.
