bartholin's abscess.definition: A localized, painful pus collection from infection of the Bartholin gland, typically due to ductal obstruction that permits bacterial infection; presents as a tender, unilateral vulvar swelling near the lower vestibule and is treated with incision and drainage (I&D) and antibiotics, with marsupialization as an option for recurrent abscesses.

bartholin's cyst.definition: A fluid-filled dilation of the Bartholin (greater vestibular) gland caused by duct obstruction at the vaginal introitus; typically presents as a painless or mildly tender swelling at the posterior aspect of the introitus and may become an infected Bartholin abscess if bacteria are involved.

bartholin's duct.definition: A small duct of the Bartholin (greater vestibular) gland that carries mucus-like secretions from the gland to the vestibule of the vagina, near the introitus, contributing to lubrication.

bartholin's gland.definition: Two small mucus-secreting glands in the superficial perineal pouch, located at the posterolateral aspects of the vaginal opening; they secrete mucus to lubricate the vestibule during sexual arousal and drain via ducts into the vestibule. Obstruction can lead to a cyst or abscess.

bartholinian abscess.definition: A localized, painful pus-filled infection of the Bartholin gland (at the posterior vaginal opening) caused by duct obstruction with secondary bacterial infection; presents as a tender, unilateral swelling near the vaginal introitus and is typically treated with incision and drainage, with antibiotics as indicated.

bartholin's gland carcinoma.definition: A rare malignant tumor arising from the Bartholin gland, a mucous-secreting gland located at the posterior aspect of the vaginal introitus; it often presents as a unilateral vulvar mass that may be mistaken for a Bartholin cyst, and is diagnosed by biopsy. Treatment typically involves wide local excision with clear margins and evaluation of inguinal lymph nodes, with adjuvant radiotherapy or chemotherapy for high-risk or advanced disease.

bartonellosis.definition: An infection caused by bacteria of the genus Bartonella; most commonly presents as cat scratch disease with fever and regional lymphadenopathy after exposure to cats or cat fleas, and can cause bacillary angiomatosis in immunocompromised individuals.

cat-scratch fever.definition: A zoonotic infection caused by Bartonella henselae transmitted by cat scratches or bites, presenting with tender regional lymphadenopathy near the inoculation site and often low-grade fever; usually self-limited in healthy individuals.

bacillary angiomatosis.definition: A vascular proliferative infection caused by Bartonella species (primarily B. henselae or B. quintana) in immunocompromised patients, presenting as red to purple cutaneous nodules and sometimes visceral lesions that can mimic Kaposi sarcoma.

trench fever.definition: A bacterial infection caused by Bartonella quintana transmitted by the human body louse; presents with fever and severe shin pain (calf pain), headache, and malaise; historically associated with WWI trench outbreaks; usually self-limited but can cause bacteremia or endocarditis in rare cases.

peliosis of the liver.definition: A rare vascular disorder of the liver in which multiple blood-filled, cavernous spaces develop in the hepatic parenchyma due to dilation of hepatic sinusoids; these spaces may be asymptomatic or rupture, causing hemorrhage or liver dysfunction.

barotrauma.definition: An injury caused by pressure-related damage to air- or fluid-filled spaces due to a mismatch between external pressure and internal pressure, typically occurring during rapid changes in ambient pressure (eg, diving or flying) and can involve the ears (tympanic membrane rupture), sinuses, or lungs (pulmonary barotrauma).

infantile scurvy.definition: A vitamin C deficiency presenting in infancy (scurvy), characterized by irritability, pallor/anemia, edema, swollen and bleeding gums, perifollicular hemorrhages, and subperiosteal hemorrhages with pseudoparalysis; treated with dietary vitamin C supplementation (ascorbic acid).

barlow's disease.definition: A degenerative disease of the mitral valve characterized by myxomatous degeneration and redundancy of the valve leaflets, causing them to prolapse into the left atrium during systole and frequently resulting in mitral regurgitation (often with a midsystolic click).

barlow's syndrome.definition: A historical term for mitral valve prolapse due to myxomatous degeneration of the mitral valve leaflets, often with mitral regurgitation; the modern term is simply mitral valve prolapse.

mitral valve prolapse.definition: Occurring when the mitral valve doesn't close tightly. It is a common heart valve condition and sometimes causes regurgitation.

floppy-valve syndrome.definition: An historical term for a syndrome attributed to mitral valve prolapse, in which abnormally floppy, redundant mitral valve leaflets billow into the left atrium during systole and may cause mild mitral regurgitation, often with chest pain, palpitations, and autonomic symptoms.

mitral regurgitation.definition: Mitral regurgitation is a valvular heart disease in which the mitral valve does not close properly during systole, causing retrograde flow of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium.

aerotitis.definition: Inflammation or injury of the ear resulting from rapid changes in ambient air pressure (barotrauma), commonly occurring with flying or diving due to inadequate equalization of middle-ear pressure; may cause ear pain, muffled hearing, vertigo, and tympanic membrane injury.

aerotitis media.definition: An injury to the middle ear caused by rapid changes in ambient pressure (barotrauma), most often during air travel or diving, resulting from failure of the Eustachian tube to equalize pressure; presents with ear pain, fullness, muffled hearing, and may include tympanic membrane rupture or middle-ear effusion.

baroreceptor.definition: Stretch-sensitive mechanoreceptors located primarily in the carotid sinus and aortic arch that detect changes in arterial pressure by sensing vessel-wall stretch; they send afferent signals to the medulla via the glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves, initiating a reflex that adjusts heart rate, contractility, and vascular tone to maintain stable blood pressure.

pressoreceptor.definition: A mechanoreceptor that responds to changes in mechanical pressure; in the cardiovascular system, baroreceptors in the carotid sinus and aortic arch detect arterial pressure and reflexively regulate heart rate, stroke volume, and vascular tone to maintain blood pressure.

intussusception.definition: A condition in which a portion of the intestine folds into the immediately following segment (telescopes into itself), causing bowel obstruction and potential compromise of blood flow; most common in infants and young children, frequently at the ileocecal junction.

proton pump inhibitors.definition: A class of medications that irreversibly inhibit the gastric proton pump (H+/K+-ATPase) in parietal cells, leading to a sustained reduction in gastric acid secretion; used to treat GERD, peptic ulcers, and other acid-related disorders. Common examples include omeprazole, esomeprazole, pantoprazole, and lansoprazole.

h2 blockers.definition: A class of medications that block histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells, reducing gastric acid secretion; used to treat and prevent ulcers, GERD, and other acid-related disorders.

esophageal cancer.definition: An invasive malignant neoplasm of the esophagus, usually squamous cell carcinoma or adenocarcinoma, arising from the esophageal epithelium; presents with progressive difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and weight loss.

reflux.definition: When food or drink flows back from your stomach into your throat.

lower esophageal sphincter.definition: A ring of muscle where the esophagus and stomach meet. It relaxes to let food into the stomach and closes to prevent stomach acids from backing up and irritating the esophagus.

double-contrast barium enema.definition: A radiologic study of the large intestine in which barium sulfate is introduced to coat the mucosa, followed by insufflation of air to create a double-contrast image that enhances visualization of the mucosal surface for detecting polyps, diverticula, inflammatory disease, and neoplasia.

barium swallow.definition: A radiographic examination in which the patient swallows a barium-based contrast and fluoroscopic imaging is used to visualize the esophagus (often the stomach) to assess anatomy and motility and diagnose structural or functional esophageal disorders.

barium meal.definition: A radiographic examination of the upper gastrointestinal tract in which the patient ingests a barium sulfate contrast medium to visualize the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum on X-ray, used to detect structural or functional abnormalities such as ulcers, strictures, tumors, or obstruction.

gastrointestinal series.definition: A radiologic examination of the gastrointestinal tract in which the patient ingests contrast material (typically barium) to visualize the esophagus, stomach, and small intestine under fluoroscopy.

baritosis.definition: A benign pneumoconiosis caused by inhalation of barium-containing dust (barite), characterized by diffuse radiopaque particles in the lungs on radiographs and typically asymptomatic with no progressive disease.

barosperse.definition: Not found in standard medical dictionaries; likely a misspelling of a term related to pressure effects—barosensitivity (sensitivity to pressure changes) or barotrauma (injury from pressure differences).

bartonella henselae.definition: A Gram-negative, facultative intracellular bacterium that infects cats and is transmitted to humans by scratches or bites, causing cat-scratch disease (fever and tender regional lymphadenopathy); in immunocompromised individuals it can cause bacillary angiomatosis.

bartonella bacilliformis.definition: A Gram-negative, rod-shaped, facultative intracellular bacterium of the genus Bartonella that causes Carrión disease (Oroya fever and verruga peruana) in the Andes. Transmitted by sandflies, it presents acutely with fever and severe anemia (Oroya fever) or chronically with cutaneous angioproliferative lesions (verruga peruana). Diagnosis by blood smear showing bacilli within erythrocytes, plus serology or PCR. Treated with antibiotics such as chloramphenicol, ciprofloxacin, or azithromycin.

sandfly.definition: A small hematophagous fly of the subfamily Phlebotominae (family Psychodidae) whose female blood meals can harbor and transmit Leishmania parasites, causing leishmaniasis (cutaneous, mucocutaneous, or visceral) in humans and some animals; typically active at dawn or dusk in warm, humid climates.

bone pain.definition: Pain arising from bone tissue, typically deep, dull, and persistent, which can result from fracture, infection (osteomyelitis), tumors or metastases, osteoporosis-related microfractures, or other bone disorders; may be worsened by movement or weight bearing.

nodular skin lesions.definition: Palpable, solid skin lesions that extend into the dermis and often into the subcutaneous tissue; typically dome- or rounded in shape and larger than a papule, and they may be benign or malignant.

verrucous skin lesions.definition: A class of skin lesions that are wart-like with a rough, keratotic surface due to papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia and marked hyperkeratosis; may be benign (verrucae) or malignant in the form of verrucous carcinoma.

carrions disease.definition: A vector-borne bacterial infection caused by Bartonella bacilliformis, transmitted by sandflies in the Andean highlands (Peru, Ecuador, Colombia). It has two phases: an acute febrile illness with severe hemolytic anemia (Oroya fever) and a later cutaneous eruption of wart-like lesions (verruga peruana).

oroya fever.definition: An acute febrile illness caused by Bartonella bacilliformis transmitted by sandflies in the Andean region, characterized by severe anemia due to intravascular hemolysis and high bacteremia; the acute phase of Carrion’s disease, which can progress to verruga peruana.

verruga peruana.definition: An endemic cutaneous vascular proliferative lesion of bartonellosis caused by Bartonella bacilliformis (Carrión disease), presenting as friable, nodular skin growths that may ulcerate or bleed, typically on the face and extremities after acute infection; transmitted by sandflies in Andean regions; treated with antibiotics such as doxycycline, azithromycin, ciprofloxacin, or rifampin.

basedows goiter.definition: A diffuse, symmetric enlargement of the thyroid caused by Graves' disease (autoimmune hyperthyroidism), typically with hyperthyroid symptoms and often ophthalmopathy; also known as toxic diffuse goiter.

thyroid gland.definition: A two-lobed gland located in the front of the neck below the larynx (voice box). It secretes hormones that help regulate the body's metabolism and calcium balance.

thyroid hormone.definition: Two iodine-containing hormones called thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). They help regulate the body's metabolism and calcium balance.

barton forceps.definition: A type of obstetric forceps historically used to assist vaginal delivery by grasping and guiding the fetal head; designs and indications have varied, and many older variants are less common today.

bartons fracture.definition: An intra-articular distal radius fracture with dislocation of the radiocarpal joint, typically involving the volar (palmar) rim or, less commonly, the dorsal rim, usually from a fall on an outstretched hand.

bartter syndrome.definition: A group of rare autosomal recessive renal tubulopathies caused by defects in transport proteins in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, leading to impaired NaCl reabsorption with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hyperreninemia and hyperaldosteronism, and usually normal or low blood pressure.

basal lamina.definition: Thin extracellular matrix secreted by epithelial cells that underlies the epithelium and forms the basal component of the basement membrane; it provides structural support, promotes cell adhesion and differentiation, and participates in filtration, with components including type IV collagen, laminin, nidogen, and heparan sulfate proteoglycans.

basal cell carcinoma.definition: The most common skin cancer; it does not spread to internal organs.

basal cell epithelioma.definition: A malignant skin tumor arising from the basal cells of the epidermis; typically slow-growing and locally invasive with rare metastasis, often presenting as a pearly, telangiectatic papule or nodule on sun-exposed skin.

basaloma.definition: Not a recognized medical term; it likely refers to basal cell carcinoma, a common skin cancer arising from the basal cells of the epidermis.

basiloma.definition: Likely a misspelling of a common skin cancer arising from basal cells of the epidermis; it typically presents as a slow-growing, pearly papule or nodule with telangiectasia and rarely metastasizes.

carcinoma basocellulare.definition: Malignant skin cancer arising from basal keratinocytes of the epidermis; typically slow-growing and locally invasive, often presenting as a pearly papule or plaque with telangiectasia; metastasis is rare; treated mainly by surgical excision or Mohs micrographic surgery.

basal cell papilloma.definition: A benign epithelial neoplasm consisting of basal-type keratinocytes that forms papillary (wart-like) projections from the surface epithelium; typically noninvasive and slow-growing.

basaloid carcinoma.definition: A high-grade malignant tumor characterized by nests of small, basaloid (basal-like) cells with scant cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei, often showing peripheral palisading; commonly refers to basaloid squamous cell carcinoma, a variant of squamous cell carcinoma with aggressive behavior.

basal energy expenditure.definition: The energy required by the body at rest to maintain basic physiological processes in a thermoneutral environment after an overnight fast; the minimal caloric requirement for sustaining life, typically expressed in kcal/day.

basal body temperature.definition: The body's lowest resting temperature, measured immediately after waking and before any activity (typically with a basal thermometer). It is used in fertility awareness to track the menstrual cycle, with a slight, sustained rise after ovulation due to progesterone.

basal body temperature method.definition: An ovulation-tracking method that involves daily measurement of the body's resting temperature upon waking with a basal thermometer and charting the results; after ovulation, basal body temperature typically rises by about 0.4–0.8°F (0.2–0.4°C) and remains elevated until menstruation, helping identify the fertile window and luteal phase.</analysis>

basal body temperature chart.definition: A daily record of basal body temperature measured first thing after waking, used to monitor ovulation and fertility. The chart typically shows a slight rise in temperature after ovulation (about 0.4–1.0°C or 0.7–1.5°F), which helps identify the fertile window; readings can be affected by sleep quality, illness, or other factors and are plotted across the cycle to reveal patterns.

basal ganglia.definition: Clusters of nerve cells deep in the brain that play an important role in movement.

putamen.definition: A large subcortical gray-matter nucleus of the basal ganglia, constituting the striatum within the lentiform nucleus; it modulates voluntary movement and motor learning by receiving cortical input and projecting to pallidal and nigral structures.

substantia nigra.definition: A midbrain structure of the basal ganglia comprising the pars compacta and pars reticulata; it contains dopaminergic neurons (pigmented by neuromelanin) that regulate movement, with the pars compacta sending dopamine to the striatum (nigrostriatal pathway) and the pars reticulata serving as an output nucleus to motor thalamus; degeneration of its dopaminergic neurons is a hallmark of Parkinson disease.

subthalamic nucleus.definition: A lens-shaped nucleus in the ventral diencephalon, part of the basal ganglia; it provides excitatory input to the internal globus pallidus and substantia nigra pars reticulata and modulates voluntary movement, with overactivity linked to Parkinson disease and commonly targeted by deep brain stimulation.

pallidum.definition: A subcortical structure of the basal ganglia involved in the regulation of voluntary movement; consists of the internal and external segments (GPi and GPe) and serves as a major output nucleus to the thalamus.

basel nomina anatomica.definition: An early historical standard international list of Latin names for human anatomical structures, compiled in Basel to standardize terminology across languages and medical literature and reduce confusion from vernacular terms; it served as a precursor to later standardized nomenclatures such as Nomina Anatomica and Terminologia Anatomica.

foramen ovale.definition:
Two meanings:
- In the fetal heart, a small opening in the interatrial septum that allows blood to pass from the right atrium to the left atrium, bypassing the nonfunctional fetal lungs; it usually closes after birth to form the fossa ovalis.
- In the skull base, a rounded opening in the sphenoid bone through which the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3) and accompanying vessels pass.

foramen lacerum.definition: An irregular triangular opening at the skull base, bounded by the sphenoid, temporal, and occipital bones; in life it is filled with fibrocartilage and transmits the nerve of the pterygoid canal (Vidian nerve) and small emissary veins, while the internal carotid artery passes over it in a groove rather than through it.

carotid canal.definition: A bony passage in the petrous part of the temporal bone that transmits the internal carotid artery and its accompanying sympathetic nerve fibers from the neck into the cranial cavity.

jugular foramen.definition: A large opening at the base of the skull, formed by the temporal and occipital bones, through which the internal jugular vein and cranial nerves IX (glossopharyngeal), X (vagus), and XI (spinal accessory) pass from the posterior cranial fossa to the neck.

mastoid process.definition: A bony prominence of the temporal bone behind the external auditory canal, containing the mastoid air cells that communicate with the middle ear and serving as an attachment for the sternocleidomastoid muscle.

vomer bone.definition: A thin, plow-shaped, unpaired facial bone that forms the inferior and posterior part of the nasal septum; it articulates superiorly with the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid and anteriorly with the maxilla and palatine bones.

stylomastoid foramen.definition: A small foramen in the temporal bone, between the styloid and mastoid processes, through which the facial nerve (cranial nerve VII) exits the skull to innervate the muscles of facial expression (often accompanied by a branch of the stylomastoid artery).

occipital condyle.definition: A rounded articular projection on the occipital bone that articulates with the atlas (the first cervical vertebra) to form the atlanto-occipital joints, enabling head nodding and limited lateral movement.

base of skull.definition: The base of the skull (cranial base) is the inferior portion of the skull that forms the floor of the cranial cavity; it is organized into the anterior, middle, and posterior cranial fossae and is formed primarily by the occipital, sphenoid, temporal, and ethmoid bones, providing foramina and passages for cranial nerves and vessels.

base of gastric gland.definition: The lower, deepest portion of a gastric gland, located below the neck/isthmus, predominantly containing chief (zymogenic) cells that secrete pepsinogen.

base of the heart.definition: The broad, posterior surface of the heart, formed mainly by the left atrium (with a small contribution from the right atrium); it faces posteriorly toward the esophagus and vertebral column and is related to the posterior mediastinum.

basement lamina.definition: A thin extracellular matrix layer secreted by epithelial cells that lies just beneath the epithelium as part of the basement membrane; it is largely composed of laminin, type IV collagen, nidogen, and heparan sulfate proteoglycans, organized into sublayers (lamina rara/lucida and lamina densa). It provides structural support, mediates adhesion between epithelium and underlying tissue, and influences cell behavior and filtration in certain tissues.

basophil.definition: A circulating granulocyte white blood cell with blue-staining granules containing histamine and heparin; participates in inflammatory and allergic responses (especially type I hypersensitivity) and helps defend against parasitic infections; normally makes up about 0.5–1% of circulating leukocytes.

basilar artery insufficiency syndrome.definition: An ischemic syndrome caused by reduced perfusion of the basilar artery and its branches, producing posterior circulation–brainstem and cerebellar dysfunction; presenting features range from vertigo, diplopia, dysarthria, and ataxia to cranial nerve palsies, quadriparesis, altered consciousness, and, in severe pontine infarction, coma or “locked-in” syndrome.

basilar artery occlusion.definition: Blockage (thrombosis or embolism) of the basilar artery causing ischemia of the brainstem and cerebellum; presents with acute posterior circulation stroke symptoms such as dysarthria, dysphagia, diplopia, vertigo, ataxia, limb weakness, and altered consciousness; can progress to coma or locked-in syndrome; requires emergent reperfusion therapy if eligible.

basilar membrane.definition: A stiff, fibrous membrane forming the boundary between the scala media and scala tympani in the cochlea; it supports the organ of Corti hair cells and vibrates in response to sound with a gradient of stiffness along its length, enabling frequency-specific (tonotopic) stimulation.

basilar plexus.definition: A venous network on the basilar part of the occipital bone (clivus) within the dura of the posterior cranial fossa; communicates with the inferior petrosal sinuses and the vertebral venous plexus via emissary veins, aiding drainage from the posterior brain regions.

basilar sulcus.definition: An anatomical groove on the basilar part of the occipital bone (the clivus) that accommodates the basilar artery as it runs along the ventral surface of the brainstem.

basilar vertebra.definition: Not a standard anatomical term; there is no discrete vertebra by that name. The term basilar generally refers to the base region, such as the basilar part of the occipital bone at the skull base, and is not used to designate a specific vertebra.

basiliximab.definition: A chimeric monoclonal antibody directed against CD25 (the IL-2 receptor alpha chain) on activated T cells; it inhibits IL-2–mediated T-cell activation and proliferation and is used as induction immunosuppression to prevent acute rejection in kidney transplantation.

acute allograft rejection.definition: An immune-mediated rejection of a transplanted organ that occurs weeks to months after transplantation, caused by recipient T cells (and sometimes antibodies) recognizing donor alloantigens (primarily HLA), leading to graft dysfunction; often reversible with intensified immunosuppression.

renal transplant.definition: A surgical procedure in which a diseased kidney is replaced with a healthy donor kidney (from a living or deceased donor) to treat end-stage renal disease; the transplanted kidney is typically placed in the iliac fossa and connected to the recipient’s blood vessels and ureter, with lifelong immunosuppressive therapy to prevent rejection.

cardiac failure.definition: A clinical syndrome in which the heart is unable to pump or fill sufficiently to meet the body's metabolic needs, causing fatigue, dyspnea, and signs of fluid overload (e.g., edema, orthopnea, pulmonary congestion); it results from structural or functional cardiac abnormalities that impair systolic or diastolic function and can be acute or chronic (left-, right-, or biventricular).

moniliasis.definition: A fungal infection caused by Candida species (most commonly Candida albicans) affecting mucous membranes and skin, commonly presenting as oral thrush or vaginal candidiasis.

tremors.definition: A rhythmic, involuntary oscillation of a body part caused by alternating contractions of opposing muscle groups; tremors are most common in the hands and may be rest, postural, kinetic, or intention in nature, reflecting underlying neurologic, metabolic, or pharmacologic conditions.

chest pain.definition: Pain, pressure, or discomfort in the chest region that may originate from cardiac causes (such as ischemia, angina, or myocardial infarction) or noncardiac causes (such as gastroesophageal reflux, musculoskeletal strain, or anxiety). Urgent medical evaluation is advised if the chest pain is severe, persistent, or accompanied by shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, fainting, or radiation to the arm, jaw, or back.

lead poisoning.definition: A sickness caused by swallowing or inhaling lead; in children, it can injure the brain and slow growth and development.

batten disease.definition: A group of inherited neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disorders (neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses) caused by mutations in various genes; characterized by accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigments in neurons, leading to progressive vision loss, seizures, cognitive and motor decline, usually presenting in childhood and often resulting in severe disability and early death.

battered baby syndrome.definition: An historically used term for physical abuse of an infant or young child resulting from nonaccidental trauma, often presenting with intracranial injuries (eg, subdural hematoma) and retinal hemorrhages, and with symptoms such as irritability, lethargy, poor feeding, vomiting, seizures, or coma.

battered woman syndrome.definition: A cluster of psychological and behavioral symptoms arising from sustained intimate-partner violence, including fear and hypervigilance, learned helplessness, cognitive distortions, dissociation, depression, and anxiety, with diminished self-esteem and an apparent inability to leave the abuser; not a formal DSM diagnosis, but used in clinical and forensic contexts to explain why victims stay in abusive relationships or act in self-defense.

entomophthoromycosis.definition: A rare fungal infection caused by fungi in the order Entomophthorales (primarily Basidiobolus ranarum and Conidiobolus spp.), typically presenting as chronic subcutaneous or rhinofacial lesions in otherwise healthy individuals in tropical/subtropical regions; diagnosed by histopathology and culture, and treated with azole antifungals (e.g., itraconazole) or potassium iodide, sometimes with surgical excision.

basophilic adenoma.definition: An anterior pituitary tumor consisting of basophilic-staining cells; it may secrete pituitary hormones such as ACTH, TSH, or the gonadotropins (FSH/LH).

basophilic stippling.definition: Basophilic stippling is the presence of small blue ribosomal RNA–containing granules within red blood cells on a peripheral smear, due to impaired RNA degradation; classically associated with lead poisoning but also seen in sideroblastic and megaloblastic anemias and other heavy-metal poisonings.

basophilic erythrocyte.definition: An immature red blood cell precursor in bone marrow that stains blue (basophilic) with basic dyes due to abundant ribosomal RNA; an early erythropoietic stage before maturation into a normoblast and eventual erythrocyte.

basosquamous cell carcinoma.definition: A skin cancer composed of a mixture of basal cell carcinoma–like basaloid cells and areas of squamous differentiation; behaves more aggressively than a typical basal cell carcinoma, with a higher risk of local invasion and metastasis. Management typically involves wide surgical excision with clear margins (often Mohs micrographic surgery) and may include radiotherapy for advanced cases.

basis pedunculi cerebri.definition: The ventral part of the midbrain containing the cerebral peduncles (crus cerebri), primarily comprising descending motor pathways from the cortex to the brainstem and spinal cord (corticospinal, corticobulbar, and corticopontine tracts).

basioccipital.definition: The basilar part of the occipital bone; a wedge-shaped region at the skull base lying anterior to the foramen magnum that articulates with the body of the sphenoid to form the clivus.

basion.definition: A cranial base anatomical landmark defined as the midpoint of the anterior edge of the foramen magnum; used as a reference point in radiographs and cephalometric analysis.

bathesthesia.definition: Not a standard medical term; not found in contemporary medical dictionaries. If intended to describe sensory abnormalities, it may refer to an abnormal, unpleasant sensation (dysesthesia) or, in some usages, to loss of sensation (anesthesia).

bathyanesthesia.definition: A diminished or distorted perception of deep (proprioceptive) sensation, i.e., impaired deep touch, position sense, or vibration.

bathmic evolution.definition: Historical changes in the depth and shape of the ocean floor in a region over geological time, driven by tectonic plate motion (uplift, subsidence, seafloor spreading), sedimentation and erosion, and sea-level fluctuations; reconstructed from seismic data, cores, and other geophysical evidence.

bathycardia.definition: Not a standard medical term; it may be a misspelling of bradycardia. Bradycardia is a slower-than-normal heart rate, typically defined as a resting heart rate below 60 beats per minute in adults; it can be harmless in well-trained athletes or indicate underlying conditions such as heart block, hypothyroidism, or medication effects.

purkinje cell.definition: A large inhibitory neuron of the cerebellar cortex with an extensive dendritic tree; it is the cortex's primary output neuron, sending GABAergic signals to the deep cerebellar nuclei to regulate motor coordination.

basket cell.definition: An inhibitory GABAergic interneuron that forms perisomatic synapses around the soma of neighboring neurons, creating a pericellular “basket” of synaptic terminals; notably, cerebellar basket cells surround Purkinje cell bodies to regulate their firing.

basolateral membrane.definition: The portion of an epithelial cell's plasma membrane that faces the basal-lateral surface toward the basement membrane and neighboring cells, opposite the apical (lumen-facing) surface; it contains transporters and channels (such as Na+/K+-ATPase) and mediates ion and solute exchange between the cell and underlying tissue, contributing to epithelial polarity.

oxytocin.definition: A peptide hormone produced by the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary; it stimulates uterine contractions during labor and milk ejection during lactation, and it is involved in social bonding. Clinically, it is used to induce or augment labor and to prevent postpartum hemorrhage.

bassen-kornzweig syndrome.definition: An ultra-rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by failure to form apolipoprotein B–containing lipoproteins, leading to fat malabsorption and deficiency of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K), often with acanthocytosis, retinitis pigmentosa, and progressive neurological symptoms.

bacille calmette-guérin.definition: A live attenuated vaccine derived from Mycobacterium bovis, used to prevent tuberculosis; administered intradermally. It is also used as intravesical therapy for superficial bladder cancer.

mycobacterium intracellulare.definition: A slow-growing, non-tuberculous mycobacterium in the Mycobacterium avium complex; an environmental organism that can cause pulmonary disease, lymphadenitis, or disseminated infection in immunocompromised hosts.

pulmonary disease.definition: Any disorder affecting the lungs or airways that impairs ventilation or gas exchange, including obstructive, restrictive, infectious, inflammatory, or vascular conditions.

surgical resection.definition: A surgical procedure to remove part or all of a diseased organ, tissue, or lesion.

battledore placenta.definition: A placenta with marginal cord insertion: the umbilical cord attaches at the edge of the placenta instead of the center.

placenta battledore.definition: A placenta in which the umbilical cord inserts at the placental edge rather than centrally.

battle's sign.definition: A bruise over the mastoid region behind the ear, indicating a basilar skull fracture; it often appears hours to days after head trauma.

bracken poisoning.definition: Bracken poisoning is toxicosis from ingesting bracken fern (Pteridium aquilinum), due to toxins such as thiaminase (causing thiamine deficiency) and the carcinogen ptaquiloside; in livestock it can cause neurologic signs (grass staggers) and GI upset, and chronic exposure in humans is linked to an increased risk of esophageal and gastric cancers.

baudelocque's diameter.definition: A pelvic diameter described by Baudelocque; the diagonal conjugate—the distance from the sacral promontory to the inferior border of the pubic symphysis, used to estimate the obstetric conjugate.

external conjugate.definition: An obstetric pelvic measurement: the distance from the pubic symphysis to the sacral promontory, measured externally on the abdomen; used as a rough estimate of the pelvic inlet size.

lacrimal bay.definition: The lacrimal bay (lacrimal lake) is the tear reservoir that pools at the medial canthus of the eye, formed by the eyelids and lacrimal caruncle; tears drain from this pool into the lacrimal puncta and canaliculi toward the lacrimal sac.

exenatide.definition: A synthetic incretin mimetic that acts as a GLP-1 receptor agonist; used to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes, administered by subcutaneous injection (twice daily or once weekly as an extended-release), it enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, and slows gastric emptying, often resulting in weight loss.

eosinophilic encephalitis.definition: A form of encephalitis characterized by eosinophil-rich inflammation of the central nervous system (CSF and brain tissue), usually due to parasitic infections or hypersensitivity/drug reactions; presents with fever, headache, altered mental status, and seizures, and is diagnosed by eosinophilia in the CSF with compatible clinical findings. Treatment targets the underlying cause and provides supportive care.

larva migrans.definition: An infection caused by the migratory movement of nematode larvae through human tissues. A skin-p predominant form produces pruritic, serpiginous tracks under the skin as larvae move there. A systemic form results when larvae disseminate to organs (notably liver and lungs, and sometimes eyes or brain), causing fever, eosinophilia, hepatomegaly, and other systemic symptoms, usually in children.

baylisascaris.definition: A genus of parasitic nematodes (roundworms); the raccoon roundworm species can infect humans via ingestion of eggs from contaminated soil or objects, causing severe larva migrans with potential central nervous system and ocular involvement.

goblet cell.definition: A mucus-secreting unicellular gland found in the epithelial lining of the respiratory and intestinal tracts. It synthesizes and releases mucins that blend with water to form mucus, which lubricates and protects the mucosal surface.

below-elbow amputation.definition: A surgical removal of the forearm and hand distal to the elbow joint, preserving the elbow; also known as a transradial amputation.

brain electrical activity map.definition: A map showing the distribution of electrical activity across brain regions, typically derived from EEG data and displayed as a topographic representation of signal amplitude or power across the cortex.

bundle branch block.definition: A disorder of the heart's electrical conduction in which one of the bundle branches (right or left) is blocked or delayed, causing asynchronous ventricular activation and a widened QRS complex on ECG; can be complete or incomplete and may occur with or without structural heart disease.

dermal ulcers.definition: Ulcers of the skin characterized by loss of epidermal tissue with breakdown extending into the dermis (and possibly deeper), typically arising from ischemia, prolonged pressure, venous or arterial insufficiency, infection, neuropathy, or inflammatory disease, and often presenting as chronic, non-healing wounds.

becaplermin.definition: Topical recombinant human platelet-derived growth factor-BB (rhPDGF-BB) used as a gel to stimulate healing in chronic diabetic foot ulcers.

becker's muscular dystrophy.definition: An X-linked recessive muscular dystrophy caused by mutations in the DMD gene encoding dystrophin, leading to reduced or abnormal dystrophin and progressive proximal muscle weakness that typically begins in adolescence or early adulthood; milder and slower progression than Duchenne, with calf pseudohypertrophy and risk of cardiomyopathy.

benign pseudohypertrophic muscular dystr.definition: An X-linked dystrophinopathy (Becker muscular dystrophy) caused by mutations in the dystrophin gene resulting in reduced or abnormal dystrophin; presents with proximal muscle weakness and calf pseudohypertrophy beginning in adolescence or early adulthood, with slower progression than Duchenne and often preserved ambulation for years; cardiomyopathy may occur.

duchenne's muscular dystrophy.definition: A severe X-linked recessive muscular dystrophy caused by mutations in the DMD gene that result in absent or nonfunctional dystrophin protein; it typically presents in early childhood with proximal muscle weakness, calf pseudohypertrophy, and a positive Gowers sign, progressing to loss of ambulation and cardiopulmonary failure in adolescence or young adulthood.

beals' syndrome.definition: An autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder characterized by arachnodactyly (long, slender fingers), congenital contractures of multiple large joints, scoliosis, dolichostenomelia (long limbs), and crumpled ears; caused by mutations in the FBN2 gene encoding fibrillin-2.

kyphoscoliosis.definition: A spinal deformity in which the spine has both kyphosis (excessive forward curvature) and scoliosis (lateral curvature), typically resulting in a fixed three‑dimensional deformity that can be due to congenital, neuromuscular, or other etiologies; may impair respiratory function in severe cases.

auricles.definition: Two meanings: (1) the external ears (pinnae) that collect sound; (2) the small muscular appendages of the atria of the heart (atrial appendages).

lymphocyte.definition: A type of white blood cell that can recognize foreign substances in the body.

b cell.definition: White blood cells that come from bone marrow, and produce antibodies to fight off disease.

b cell lymphoma.definition: Malignant proliferation of B lymphocytes, a form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma; comprises multiple subtypes with varying aggressiveness and sites of involvement, often presenting with swollen lymph nodes and sometimes constitutional symptoms or extranodal disease.

plasma cell.definition: An antibody-secreting cell derived from B lymphocytes; a mature B cell that differentiates in response to antigen to produce large amounts of immunoglobulins as part of the humoral immune response.

memory cell.definition: A long-lived lymphocyte that remains after an initial infection or vaccination and mounts a faster, more robust immune response upon re-exposure to the same antigen.

b memory cell.definition: A long-lived, antigen-experienced B lymphocyte that persists after an initial immune response and, when re-exposed to the same antigen, rapidly proliferates and differentiates into antibody-secreting plasma cells, enabling a faster, stronger secondary antibody response.

pyloric canal.definition: A short passage of the distal stomach between the pyloric antrum and the pyloric sphincter that conveys chyme into the duodenum and is controlled by the pyloric sphincter.

pyloric stenosis.definition: An infantile condition in which progressive hypertrophy and elongation of the pyloric sphincter narrows the gastric outlet, causing nonbilious projectile vomiting and dehydration; commonly presents within the first weeks of life and is treated with pyloromyotomy.

coronary occlusion.definition: A blockage or closure of a coronary artery that reduces or stops blood flow to the heart muscle, potentially causing myocardial ischemia or infarction.

interleukin-4.definition: A cytokine produced mainly by Th2 cells (also by mast cells and basophils) that promotes humoral immunity by stimulating B-cell proliferation and class-switch recombination to IgE (and IgG4 in humans), supports Th2 differentiation, and signals through the IL-4 receptor to activate the JAK-STAT6 pathway; it contributes to allergic inflammation and alternative (M2) macrophage activation.

interleukin-5.definition: A cytokine produced mainly by Th2 cells that promotes the production, recruitment, activation, and survival of eosinophils, thereby driving eosinophilic inflammation in allergic diseases and parasitic infections; it signals through the IL-5 receptor on eosinophils.

interleukin-6.definition: A cytokine produced in response to infection or tissue injury that signals through the IL-6 receptor–gp130 complex to activate JAK-STAT pathways, promoting hepatic acute-phase protein production, fever, and B-cell maturation, with context-dependent pro- and anti-inflammatory effects.

beau's lines.definition: Transverse grooves or depressions across the nail plate caused by a temporary arrest of nail matrix growth, typically due to systemic illness or physiological stress (e.g., severe infection, malnutrition, trauma, chemotherapy); the lines move outward as the nail grows.

beck's triad.definition: A clinical triad associated with acute cardiac tamponade: hypotension, jugular venous distension, and muffled heart sounds.

cardiac tamponade.definition: When fluid or blood pools within the sac surrounding the heart, squeezing the heart and interfering with its ability to pump.

jugular venous distention.definition: A physical examination finding where the neck's jugular veins are visibly distended due to elevated central venous pressure, usually assessed at 30–45 degrees; commonly indicates conditions such as right‑sided heart failure, volume overload, tamponade, constrictive pericarditis, or SVC obstruction.

central venous pressure.definition: The pressure in the thoracic vena cava near the right atrium, reflecting right atrial pressure and preload of the right heart; measured via a central venous catheter and used to assess intravascular volume status and guide fluid management (typical values ~2–8 mmHg, influenced by intrathoracic pressure).

beckwith's syndrome.definition: An overgrowth syndrome caused by dysregulation of imprinted genes on chromosome 11p15.5, characterized by macrosomia, macroglossia, omphalocele/visceromegaly, neonatal hypoglycemia, hemihyperplasia, and an increased risk of embryonal tumors such as Wilms tumor and hepatoblastoma.

beckwith-wiedemann syndrome.definition: A congenital overgrowth syndrome caused by dysregulation of imprinted genes on chromosome 11p15, characterized by macrosomia, macroglossia, omphalocele or abdominal wall defects, visceromegaly/hemihyperplasia, neonatal hypoglycemia, and an increased risk of embryonal tumors such as Wilms tumor and hepatoblastoma.

neonatal hypoglycemia.definition: A condition in which a newborn has an abnormally low blood glucose level, typically defined as plasma glucose below about 40–47 mg/dL (2.2–2.6 mmol/L) in the first 24–48 hours of life, which may cause symptoms and potential neurologic injury if not promptly treated.

hyperinsulinism.definition: A condition in which insulin levels or action are inappropriately high relative to blood glucose, causing hypoglycemia; it may result from endogenous overproduction (e.g., beta-cell disorders), insulin-secreting tumors, or exogenous insulin use.

macroglossia.definition: An abnormal enlargement of the tongue that can cause speech, swallowing, and airway difficulties; can be congenital or acquired and is associated with various conditions such as hypothyroidism, amyloidosis, acromegaly, Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, and Down syndrome.

omphalocele.definition: A congenital ventral abdominal wall defect in which abdominal contents protrude through the umbilicus into a protective sac formed by peritoneum and amnion, due to failure of the lateral body wall folds to close at the umbilical ring.

umbilical hernia.definition: Protrusion of abdominal contents through a defect in the umbilical ring at the navel, usually presenting as a soft, reducible bulge that worsens with crying or straining; most common in infants and often resolves spontaneously, but persistent or symptomatic cases, especially in adults, typically require surgical repair.

visceromegaly.definition: Enlargement of one or more internal organs (viscera), typically due to disease processes such as infection, infiltration, or congestion.

hyperplasia of the kidney and pancreas.word: hyperplasia of the kidney and pancreas
hyperplasia of the kidney and pancreas.definition:
An increase in the number of renal cells, leading to enlargement of kidney tissue; can be a physiologic (growth, compensatory hyperplasia after nephron loss) or pathologic response (hormonal or inflammatory stimuli).

An increase in the number of pancreatic cells, leading to enlargement of pancreatic tissue; may involve exocrine, ductal, or islet cells and occur in response to increased functional demand or hormonal stimuli; differs from hypertrophy.

diazoxide.definition: A potassium channel opener that inhibits insulin release from pancreatic beta cells and causes systemic vasodilation; used to treat severe hyperinsulinism (hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia) and hypertensive emergencies.

glucocorticoid therapy.definition: Glucocorticoid therapy is the medical use of glucocorticoids (steroid hormones or their synthetic analogs) to produce anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects, delivered systemically (e.g., oral, intravenous) or locally (e.g., inhaled, topical, intra-articular) for inflammatory, autoimmune, allergic, and certain hematologic conditions; long-term use can cause metabolic and musculoskeletal complications and requires tapering to prevent adrenal insufficiency.

subtotal pancreatectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which most of the pancreas is removed, leaving a residual portion of pancreatic tissue.

beta cell hyperplasia.definition: An increase in the number of insulin-secreting beta cells in the pancreatic islets, leading to expanded beta-cell mass and potential excess insulin production (hyperinsulinemia), which can cause hypoglycemia in some contexts (e.g., nesidioblastosis or congenital hyperinsulinism).

nesidioblastosis.definition: A condition characterized by diffuse proliferation (hyperplasia) of pancreatic islet cells, especially beta cells, leading to excessive insulin secretion and recurrent hypoglycemia; a common cause of congenital hyperinsulinism in neonates/infants.

beta cell tumor of the pancreas.word: beta cell tumor of the pancreas
beta cell tumor of the pancreas.definition: A pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor arising from insulin-secreting beta cells (insulinoma) that causes endogenous hypoglycemia due to excess insulin; most are benign, may be solitary, and can be associated with MEN1; diagnosis relies on a supervised fasting test showing hypoglycemia with inappropriately elevated insulin, C‑peptide, and proinsulin; treatment is surgical removal or enucleation.

emg syndrome.definition: Not a widely recognized term in standard medical references; a closely related rare systemic inflammatory illness presents with severe muscle pain and weakness, fatigue, rash, and blood eosinophilia, historically linked to contaminated L-tryptophan supplements. If you meant a different term or spelling, please provide context.

beclomethasone dipropionate.definition: A synthetic glucocorticoid (corticosteroid) used as an inhaled anti-inflammatory agent for asthma management and in nasal or topical formulations to treat allergic rhinitis and inflammatory skin conditions; it exerts its effects by glucocorticoid receptor–mediated suppression of inflammatory mediators.

bronchial asthma.definition: A chronic inflammatory disorder of the airways characterized by reversible episodes of airflow obstruction and bronchial hyperresponsiveness, leading to wheezing, coughing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath. Symptoms are often triggered by allergens, irritants, exercise, or viral infections and are typically managed with inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators.

chronic rhinitis.definition: A chronic inflammatory condition of the nasal mucosa characterized by persistent symptoms such as nasal obstruction, rhinorrhea, sneezing, and itching for more than 12 weeks; it may be due to allergic or nonallergic etiologies (perennial or seasonal).

acute asthma.definition: An abrupt or rapidly worsening episode of asthma symptoms (wheezing, coughing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath) due to acute bronchoconstriction and airway inflammation, typically requiring intensified therapy (such as inhaled bronchodilators and often systemic corticosteroids) and sometimes urgent medical care.

hoarseness.definition: A rough, raspy, or breathy voice quality resulting from impaired vibration of the vocal cords, typically due to laryngeal inflammation, edema, or lesions, and sometimes from vocal overuse or irritation.

fungal infections.definition: An infection caused by fungi (yeasts, molds, or other fungi) that can affect the skin, nails, mucous membranes, or internal organs; common examples include yeast infections and athlete’s foot.

oropharynx.definition: A part of the pharynx located behind the oral cavity, extending from the soft palate to the superior border of the epiglottis; contains the palatine and lingual tonsils and functions in swallowing and airway protection.

intramuscular injection of penicillin.definition: A method of administering penicillin by injecting a penicillin preparation directly into a muscle (eg, deltoid or gluteal), from which the drug is absorbed into the bloodstream; formulations vary in onset and duration, with short-acting aqueous penicillin G for rapid effect and long-acting benzathine penicillin G for extended coverage.

bejel.definition: A chronic endemic treponemal infection caused by Treponema pallidum subsp. endemicum, transmitted nonsexually (often in childhood) and characterized by mucocutaneous lesions; part of the treponematoses.

endemic syphilis.definition: A chronic, nonvenereal treponemal infection caused by Treponema pallidum subsp. endemicum, transmitted by nonsexual close contact in certain regions, characterized by mucocutaneous lesions and progressive bone and soft-tissue involvement if untreated.

treponema pallidum subsp. endemicum.definition: A subspecies of Treponema pallidum that causes bejel (endemic syphilis), a chronic infectious disease transmitted primarily by nonsexual close contact, characterized by mucocutaneous lesions and potential late bone and dental involvement.

venereal form of syphilis.definition: A sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum, transmitted through sexual contact, with stages including a primary chancre, secondary systemic symptoms, a latent phase, and potential tertiary disease; curable with antibiotics such as penicillin.

behçet's disease.definition: A chronic relapsing multisystem inflammatory vasculitis characterized by recurrent oral and genital ulcers and uveitis, often with skin lesions and arthritis, and may involve vascular, gastrointestinal, or neurologic systems; diagnosed clinically and treated with anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive therapies (e.g., corticosteroids, colchicine, and biologics).

behçet’s syndrome.definition: A chronic, relapsing inflammatory disorder characterized by recurrent oral and genital ulcers and ocular inflammation (uveitis), often with skin lesions and systemic involvement of joints, vasculature, gastrointestinal tract, and central nervous system; caused by vasculitis of small- to medium-sized vessels and frequently associated with HLA-B51.

bekhterev-mendel reflex.definition: Definition not found in standard references under common spellings. Could you provide alternate spellings (e.g., Bechterew-Mendel reflex) or the context where you saw it (specific disease or neurology exam)? I can re-check with that.

mendel's reflex.definition: There is no widely recognized reflex named Mendel's reflex in standard medical references; it may be a misnomer or an obscure/obsolete term. If you have context or alternate spelling, I can check again.

bell's palsy.definition: Acute, idiopathic unilateral facial nerve (cranial nerve VII) palsy causing sudden weakness of facial muscles on one side; thought to result from inflammation of the facial nerve within the facial canal; most patients recover within weeks to months; treatment may include corticosteroids and measures to protect the affected eye.

bell's phenomenon.definition: A reflex upward rotation of the eyeball that occurs when the eyelids are forcibly closed, often with scleral visibility above the iris; commonly seen in facial nerve palsy due to orbicularis oculi weakness.

bell's spasm.definition: An acute unilateral lower motor neuron palsy of the facial nerve (cranial nerve VII) of unknown origin, presenting with sudden weakness of ipsilateral facial muscles, inability to close the eye and asymmetrical facial expression, often with drooping of the mouth corner; most cases recover within weeks to months.

bell-magendie law.definition: An anatomical-neurophysiological principle stating that the dorsal (posterior) roots of the spinal nerves carry sensory (afferent) information into the spinal cord, while the ventral (anterior) roots carry motor (efferent) information from the spinal cord to muscles, demonstrating a functional separation of sensory and motor pathways.

belladonna alkaloids.definition: A group of tropane alkaloids, chiefly atropine (hyoscine), hyoscyamine, and scopolamine, derived from Atropa belladonna and related plants; they are competitive antagonists of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, producing anticholinergic effects such as mydriasis, reduced secretions, tachycardia, delirium, urinary retention, and dry mouth.

taenia saginata.definition: A large intestinal tapeworm acquired by humans after ingestion of undercooked beef containing cysticerci; the adult resides in the small intestine and can cause taeniasis, often asymptomatic. Diagnosis is by stool examination for eggs or proglottids; treatment is typically with praziquantel or niclosamide.

beef tapeworm.definition: An intestinal cestode acquired by ingestion of cysticerci in undercooked beef; the adult tapeworm resides in the human small intestine and commonly causes mild or no symptoms; diagnosis is by stool examination for eggs or proglottids, and treatment with praziquantel or niclosamide; prevention includes thorough cooking of beef and meat inspection.

beef tapeworm infection.definition: A taeniasis caused by Taenia saginata acquired by ingesting undercooked beef containing cysticerci; infections are usually asymptomatic or cause mild gastrointestinal symptoms. Diagnosis is by detecting eggs or proglottids in stool; treatment with praziquantel or niclosamide; prevention includes thorough cooking of beef and proper meat inspection to prevent cysticerci from entering the food supply.

tapeworm.definition: A parasitic flatworm of the class Cestoda that lives in the small intestine of vertebrates; it has a long, ribbon-like body made of repeating segments (proglottids) and a head (scolex), and it is acquired by ingesting undercooked or raw meat or fish containing larval cysticerci; treated with antiparasitic medications such as praziquantel or niclosamide.

anaphylactic shock.definition: A life-threatening systemic allergic reaction that occurs rapidly after exposure to an allergen, causing airway edema and bronchospasm, widespread vasodilation with capillary leak leading to hypotension (shock); urgent treatment with intramuscular epinephrine and supportive care is essential.

venom.definition: A toxin produced by certain animals and delivered by a bite, sting, or other injection, consisting of a complex mixture of enzymes, peptides, and proteins that disrupt normal physiological processes to immobilize or kill prey or defend the animal.

nail bed.definition: The skin beneath the nail plate, extending from the proximal nail fold to the hyponychium; composed of epidermis and underlying dermis, richly vascular, providing nutrients to the growing nail and anchoring the nail plate to the fingertip.

nail beds.definition: The skin and underlying tissue beneath the nail plate, rich in blood vessels, that supports nail growth and determines nail color.

cimex lectularius.definition: A small, flat, reddish-brown nocturnal insect of the family Cimicidae that feeds on human blood; an ectoparasite commonly infesting sleeping areas; bites may cause itching and local skin reactions; not known to transmit infectious disease to humans.

cimex hemipterus.definition: A tropical bed bug species in the family Cimicidae; a hematophagous ectoparasite that feeds on human blood, causing itchy bites and sleep disturbance; not conclusively proven to transmit human pathogens.

pessary.definition: A device placed in the vagina to support or correct the position of the uterus, rectum, or bladder.

bedpan.definition: A shallow, portable receptacle placed at the bedside for collecting urine or feces from patients who are bedridden or unable to use a toilet.

bedrest.definition: A period during which a patient stays in bed or limits physical activity as prescribed by a clinician to promote healing after illness, injury, or surgery.

bedridden.definition: Confined to bed and unable to get out of bed or ambulate due to illness, injury, or severe debility; often requires assistance with daily activities.

bedside thermometer.definition: A device used to measure a patient’s body temperature at the bedside, typically a digital or infrared thermometer that can read from multiple sites (oral, rectal, axillary, or tympanic/forehead) for fever assessment and monitoring.

clinical thermometer.definition: A device used to measure body temperature in a patient, typically by placing it in the mouth, rectum, or under the armpit; can be digital or glass and provides a numeric temperature reading.

bedsore.definition: A localized injury to the skin and underlying tissue over a bony prominence caused by prolonged pressure, often with shear, typically in immobilized individuals; commonly known as a pressure ulcer.

enuresis.definition: A condition characterized by repeated involuntary urination, especially during sleep (nocturnal enuresis), commonly known as bedwetting.

belonephobia.definition: An excessive, persistent fear of needles or injections that leads to avoidance of medical procedures and may cause acute anxiety or fainting.

below-elbow.definition: Anatomical region of the upper limb distal to the elbow joint—the forearm. In surgical contexts, it also denotes a below-elbow (transradial) amputation, i.e., an amputation through the forearm below the elbow.

below-knee.definition: Located below the knee; referring to the lower leg (the crural region) or to structures, conditions, or procedures situated beneath the knee joint.

benadryl.definition: An over-the-counter oral antihistamine (diphenhydramine) that blocks H1 histamine receptors to relieve allergic symptoms (itching, sneezing, runny nose); also used to prevent motion sickness and as a short-term sedative/sleep aid; common side effects include drowsiness, dry mouth, and dizziness.

diphenhydramine.definition: A first-generation antihistamine (H1 receptor antagonist) used to treat allergic symptoms (rhinitis, urticaria), nausea or motion sickness, and, in some preparations, as a short-acting sedative; it commonly causes drowsiness and anticholinergic effects.

radiographs.definition: Images produced by radiography using ionizing X-ray radiation to create two-dimensional representations of internal anatomy, commonly used to evaluate bones, the chest, teeth, and other tissues for abnormalities.

xray.definition: A radiographic image produced by exposing a part of the body to ionizing radiation; differences in tissue absorption create contrast on film or a digital detector, allowing visualization of bones and internal structures.

myeloma.definition: A malignant neoplasm of plasma cells that originates in the bone marrow, typically characterized by clonal proliferation of plasma cells producing a monoclonal immunoglobulin; commonly presents with bone lesions, anemia, hypercalcemia, renal dysfunction, and increased susceptibility to infections.

hyperplasia.definition: An increase in the number of cells in a tissue or organ, causing the organ to enlarge; it can be benign (noncancerous) or an early sign of cancer.

prostatectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove all or part of the prostate gland, commonly performed for prostate cancer (radical prostatectomy) or benign prostatic hyperplasia (simple/prostatectomy).

bendroflumethiazide.definition: A thiazide diuretic used to treat hypertension and edema; it inhibits the Na+-Cl- cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule, increasing urinary excretion of sodium and water.

diuretic.definition: A substance or drug that increases urine production by the kidneys (diuresis), typically by inhibiting sodium reabsorption in the nephron and promoting the excretion of water and electrolytes; used to treat edema, hypertension, and certain heart or kidney conditions.

paroxysmal.definition: Relating to a sudden, brief episode or attack of symptoms; occurring in abrupt, intermittent bursts.

positional.definition: Relating to or dependent on body position; used to describe signs or symptoms that vary with changes in posture or orientation.

epley.definition: A canalith repositioning procedure for benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) that uses a series of head and body movements to move otoliths out of the posterior semicircular canal and into the utricle, thereby reducing vertigo.

brandt-daroff.definition: A set of movements used to treat benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) in which a person from a seated position repeatedly lies on each side with the head turned and lowered, holding briefly, to provoke vertigo and promote habituation or dislodgement of canaliths in the inner ear.

ct.definition: Computerized X-rays that provide detailed views of the body and brain.

lymphoreticulosis.definition: A nonspecific term referring to disease of the lymphoreticular system (lymphoid tissue and reticuloendothelial cells), often presenting with generalized lymphadenopathy.

mesenchymoma.definition: A rare neoplasm consisting of two or more distinct mesenchymal tissue types (e.g., cartilage, bone, fat, or muscle) within a single lesion, derived from mesenchymal tissue, usually without an epithelial component; the tumor may be benign or malignant.

pemphigoid.definition: A group of autoimmune blistering diseases characterized by autoantibodies against basement membrane zone components, causing subepidermal, tense blisters; most common form presents in older adults with pruritic, non-scarring bullae on normal or red skin, with occasional mucosal involvement.

fibroma.definition: Benign neoplasm composed of fibrous connective tissue, typically formed by proliferating fibroblasts with dense collagen; generally slow-growing and well circumscribed, and does not metastasize; treatment is surgical excision if symptomatic.

nephrosclerosis.definition: Hardening and thickening of the kidney's small arteries and arterioles (arteriolosclerosis) due to long-standing hypertension or diabetes, leading to reduced renal blood flow, ischemic nephron loss, and chronic kidney disease; histology typically shows hyaline arteriolosclerosis with glomerulosclerosis and interstitial fibrosis.

pemphigus.definition: An autoimmune blistering disorder in which antibodies target desmosomal proteins (desmogleins) in the epidermis, causing loss of keratinocyte adhesion (acantholysis) and resulting in flaccid bullae and erosions on skin and mucous membranes; includes variants such as pemphigus vulgaris and pemphigus foliaceus. Diagnosis is by direct immunofluorescence showing intercellular IgG (and sometimes C3) in the epidermis; treated with systemic corticosteroids and immunosuppressants (e.g., rituximab).

bentonite.definition: A naturally occurring absorbent clay mineral, primarily montmorillonite, that swells when hydrated and adsorbs water, toxins, and other substances; used in medicine as an oral adsorbent for diarrhea and as an excipient or topical base in various preparations.

bentoquatam.definition: A polymer-based barrier cream applied to the skin that prevents urushiol, the oil in poison ivy/oak/sumac, from penetrating the skin, thereby reducing the risk of allergic contact dermatitis.

benzocaine.definition: A local anesthetic of the ester class used topically to numb skin or mucous membranes; commonly found in over-the-counter topical analgesics and throat lozenges. It works by reversibly blocking voltage-gated sodium channels in peripheral nerves.

benzyl benzoate.definition: An ester formed from benzoic acid and benzyl alcohol; used topically as an antiparasitic agent to treat scabies and lice, and also employed as a solvent and fragrance ingredient in cosmetics.

bepridil.definition: A potassium-channel–blocking antiarrhythmic (class III) that prolongs the cardiac action potential and QT interval; may also have calcium channel–blocking effects; historically used for refractory arrhythmias but limited by a high risk of torsades de pointes and other adverse effects.

beractant.definition: A natural bovine-derived surfactant replacement used to prevent or treat respiratory distress syndrome in premature infants; contains phospholipids (notably DPPC) and surfactant proteins B and C, and is administered intratracheally to reduce alveolar surface tension and improve lung compliance.

berdon's syndrome.definition: A rare congenital urogenital and gastrointestinal disorder defined by megacystis (an enlarged bladder), microcolon, and severe intestinal hypoperistalsis, typically presenting in infancy with urinary obstruction and feeding/ digestive difficulties; prognosis is generally poor and management is mainly supportive.

berger's disease.definition: Primary glomerulonephritis in which IgA-containing immune complexes deposit in the glomerular mesangium, causing hematuria (often episodic and following mucosal infections) with variable proteinuria; may progress to chronic kidney disease or renal failure. It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis worldwide.
