bladder calculus.definition: A stone formed within the urinary bladder (cystolithiasis); typically mineral deposits such as calcium oxalate, uric acid, or calcium phosphate, and may cause dysuria, frequency, hematuria, or suprapubic pain, often requiring endoscopic fragmentation or removal.

vesical calculus.definition: A stone formed in the urinary bladder (bladder stone), typically from precipitation of minerals in urine and often associated with urinary stasis, infection, or obstruction.

calculous disease.definition: A condition characterized by the formation or presence of calculi (stones) within a body organ or duct, often causing obstruction, inflammation, pain, or infection. Common sites include the biliary tract (gallstones) and urinary tract (kidney/urinary stones).

excretory urography.definition: A radiographic imaging study of the urinary tract in which intravenously administered iodinated contrast is used and serial X-rays are taken to visualize the kidneys, ureters, and bladder, assessing anatomy and excretory function.

cystoscopy.definition: A procedure in which a cystoscope—a thin, lighted instrument—is inserted through the urethra into the bladder to visualize the bladder lining and urethra, often to diagnose conditions, obtain biopsies, or perform therapeutic interventions.

transurethral biopsy.definition: A biopsy obtained from tissues of the lower urinary tract (bladder, urethra, or prostatic urethra) via instrumentation passed through the urethra, typically during cystoscopy, to diagnose lesions such as tumors or inflammatory conditions.

transitional cell carcinoma.definition: A cancer arising from the urothelium (transitional epithelium) lining the urinary tract, most commonly the bladder; it can be papillary or flat and ranges from noninvasive, low-grade lesions to invasive, high-grade disease.

squamous cell carcinoma.definition: Malignant neoplasm arising from squamous epithelial cells, characterized by invasive growth of atypical keratinizing squamous cells that may form keratin pearls; commonly occurs in sun-exposed skin and mucosal surfaces.

fulguration.definition: Destruction of tissue by burning with a high-frequency electrical current (electrocautery/fulguration), typically via a spark from an electrode, used to destroy or remove diseased tissue.

open loop resection.definition: An open-loop resection is a surgical removal of tissue performed through an open (non-endoscopic) approach without real-time navigation or feedback, relying on the surgeon's direct visualization and manual technique.

segmental resection.definition: A surgical procedure in which a defined segment of a tubular organ (most commonly the bowel) is removed and the remaining ends are reconnected (anastomosed).

total cystectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove the urinary bladder in its entirety; in men it may include removal of the prostate and seminal vesicles, and in women removal of the uterus and part of the vagina, typically followed by urinary diversion (e.g., ileal conduit or neobladder).

urinary diversion.definition: A surgical procedure that diverts urine away from the bladder to a newly created drainage pathway (stoma or reservoir), typically after bladder removal or severe bladder dysfunction.

radiation therapy.definition: A cancer treatment that uses high-energy radiation to kill cancer cells.

internal irradiation.definition: A form of radiotherapy in which a radioactive source is placed inside the body or adjacent to the treatment area to deliver high-dose, localized radiation to the tumor while minimizing exposure to surrounding healthy tissue (includes intracavitary and interstitial techniques).

radioisotopes.definition: An unstable variant of an element whose atoms have the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons; it undergoes radioactive decay with emission of alpha, beta, or gamma radiation and is used as tracers in medicine and research for imaging and therapy, as well as in industry.

balloon catheter.definition: A catheter with an inflatable balloon near its distal end; when inflated with saline, the balloon can dilate a narrowed lumen (such as a blood vessel or urethra) or occlude/secure the catheter for placement and procedural use.

radon seeds.definition: A historical brachytherapy source in which radon-222 gas was sealed in a small capsule and implanted to deliver localized radiation; the seeds are now obsolete due to safety concerns and the availability of safer, more controllable radioisotope sources (e.g., iodine-125, palladium-103, iridium-192).

bcg.definition: A live attenuated vaccine derived from Mycobacterium bovis, used to prevent tuberculosis; it is also used intravesically to treat non-muscle invasive bladder cancer by stimulating a local immune response against tumor cells.

bladder cancer markers test.definition: A urine- or blood-based assay that detects cancer-associated biomarkers (such as tumor proteins, antigens, or DNA/chromosomal changes) related to bladder cancer to aid in detection or monitoring; not diagnostic on its own and typically used alongside cystoscopy and cytology.

vesicouterine fold.definition: A peritoneal reflection between the urinary bladder and uterus that forms the vesicouterine pouch, the anterior pelvic space between these organs.

bladder hernia.definition: A herniation of the urinary bladder through a defect in the pelvic or abdominal wall (most commonly into the inguinal canal or scrotum), with part or all of the bladder protruding into the hernia sac; may present as a groin bulge with urinary symptoms and carries a risk of bladder injury during hernia repair.

bladder irrigation.definition: A procedure in which sterile fluid is instilled into the bladder via a catheter and then drained to flush out blood clots or debris, maintain catheter patency, and, when done continuously, prevent obstruction after urologic procedures.

bladder neck dyssynergia.definition: A condition in which the bladder neck does not relax (and may contract) during micturition, causing functional outlet obstruction and reduced urine flow; it reflects discoordination between detrusor contraction and sphincter relaxation, commonly seen with neurogenic bladder or spinal cord injury.

smooth sphincter dyssynergia.definition: Paradoxical contraction or failure to relax the internal anal sphincter (a smooth muscle sphincter) during attempted defecation, causing functional outlet obstruction and constipation; typically demonstrated on anorectal manometry as inadequate IAS relaxation.

bladder neck incision.definition: A surgical procedure in which one or more incisions are made at the bladder neck (the junction of the bladder and urethra) to widen the bladder outlet and relieve urinary obstruction, usually performed endoscopically as a treatment for bladder outlet obstruction from benign prostatic hyperplasia or similar conditions; potential risks include incontinence, retrograde ejaculation, and urethral or bladder neck stricture.

bladder neck resection.definition: A transurethral procedure in which tissue at the bladder neck is resected to widen the bladder outlet and relieve lower urinary tract obstruction; typically used for bladder neck obstruction and sometimes alongside prostate procedures, with risks including bleeding, infection, incontinence, and retrograde ejaculation.

bladder neck suspension.definition: A surgical procedure to elevate and suspend the bladder neck and proximal urethra to restore support and prevent urine leakage during activities that increase abdominal pressure, typically by attaching tissues to the pubic bone or pelvic ligaments (commonly referred to as a Burch colposuspension).

marshall-marchetti-krantz operation.definition: A surgical procedure to treat stress urinary incontinence in women in which the bladder neck and proximal urethra are suspended to the pubic bone (pubic symphysis) using sutures passed through the vagina to provide urethral support.

burch procedure.definition: A surgical procedure to treat stress urinary incontinence by suspending and elevating the bladder neck and proximal urethra with retropubic sutures attached to the Cooper's ligament (iliopectineal ligament) to provide urethral support.

pereyra procedure.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. If you can provide context (specialty, country) or an alternate spelling, I can try to verify or offer a closely related procedure.

stamey procedures.definition: A historical surgical treatment for stress urinary incontinence in which the bladder neck and proximal urethra are suspended to the pubic bone (retropubic urethropexy/pubocystourethropexy) to provide urethral support.

colposuspension.definition: A surgical procedure to treat stress urinary incontinence by suspending the bladder neck and proximal urethra to the pubic symphysis or Cooper's ligaments, thereby elevating and stabilizing the urethrovesical junction to prevent leakage during activities that increase intra-abdominal pressure.

bladder outlet obstruction.definition: A condition in which urine flow is impeded at the bladder outlet (bladder neck or proximal urethra), leading to a weak or interrupted stream, hesitancy, straining, and incomplete bladder emptying. Common causes include benign prostatic enlargement in men and urethral strictures or bladder neck dysfunction; chronic obstruction can raise bladder pressures and cause detrusor hypertrophy.

bladder retraining.definition: A behavioral therapy for urinary urgency and incontinence that teaches postponing urination, gradually extending the time between voids, and voiding at scheduled intervals; typically includes a bladder diary, urge-suppression techniques (e.g., paced breathing, distraction, pelvic floor exercises), and avoidance of bladder irritants to increase functional bladder capacity and reduce episodes of urge incontinence.

bladder sphincter.definition: A circular smooth muscle at the bladder neck (the internal urethral sphincter) that closes the bladder outlet to prevent urine leakage; it remains contracted to maintain continence and relaxes during voiding to allow urine flow, under autonomic nervous system control.

bladder wall.definition: Wall of the urinary bladder consisting of an inner mucosa (urothelium with lamina propria), submucosa, and the muscularis (detrusor) smooth muscle arranged in layers, with an outer adventitial coat (or serosa where peritoneum covers). The detrusor muscle contracts to expel urine.

sengstaken-blakemore tube.definition: A balloon tamponade device used to temporize upper GI bleeding from esophageal or gastric varices. It is a multi-lumen tube with two balloons (a gastric balloon inflated in the stomach to compress varices at the gastroesophageal junction and an esophageal balloon inflated in the distal esophagus) plus a lumen for drainage/ suction; it provides temporary hemostasis while definitive therapy is arranged and carries risks such as airway compromise, esophageal perforation, and aspiration.

blalock-taussig procedure.definition: A palliative procedure that creates a systemic-to-pulmonary artery shunt (most often connecting the subclavian artery to the pulmonary artery) to increase pulmonary blood flow and improve systemic oxygenation in cyanotic congenital heart defects (e.g., tetralogy of Fallot), bridging to corrective surgery.

right pulmonary artery.definition: A branch of the pulmonary trunk that transports deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the right lung for oxygenation; one of the two primary pulmonary arteries.

black creek canal virus.definition: A rodent-borne hantavirus of the genus Orthohantavirus (family Hantaviridae) first identified in North America; transmitted to humans via inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta; infection can cause hantavirus disease, including febrile illness and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome.

hantavirus.definition: A genus of enveloped, negative-sense RNA viruses in the family Hantaviridae, carried by rodents and transmitted to humans mainly through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta; associated with diseases such as hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Europe and Asia.

hantavirus pulmonary syndrome.definition: A severe viral illness caused by infection with hantaviruses, transmitted to humans through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta. It typically begins with fever and myalgias and rapidly progresses to noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and respiratory failure; mortality can be substantial without supportive care. Diagnosis is by serology or PCR; treatment is supportive, and prevention focuses on reducing rodent exposure.

rickettsia rickettsii.definition: An obligate intracellular, Gram-negative bacterium and the etiologic agent of Rocky Mountain spotted fever, transmitted by ticks (primarily Dermacentor species); causes febrile illness with headache, myalgias, and a diffuse rash that can progress to vasculitis and organ involvement; treated with doxycycline.

black widow spider.definition: A venomous spider of the genus Latrodectus (commonly known as the black widow) whose bite can cause latrodectism, a neurotoxic syndrome with severe pain, muscle cramps, abdominal rigidity, and autonomic symptoms; bites are rarely fatal and treatment is supportive, with antivenom reserved for severe cases.

latrodectus mactans.definition: A venomous spider species (the eastern black widow) whose bite causes neurotoxic envenomation (latrodectism), presenting with severe abdominal and muscle cramps, pain, and autonomic symptoms.

periorbital ecchymosis.definition: Bruising around the eye(s) in the periorbital region due to blood extravasation into the soft tissues after trauma; presents as dark discoloration around the eyelids and surrounding areas and may accompany orbital or facial fractures.

hemoglobinuria.definition: The presence of free hemoglobin in the urine, typically arising from intravascular hemolysis; urine is often dark, and a dipstick may be positive for blood with few or no red blood cells on microscopy.

intravascular hemolysis.definition: Destruction of red blood cells within the bloodstream, resulting in release of free hemoglobin into plasma and urine; typically associated with low haptoglobin, elevated LDH, and indirect hyperbilirubinemia.

falciparum malaria.definition: Falciparum malaria is the most severe form of malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum infection, characterized by high parasite burden and potential for rapid progression to cerebral malaria, severe anemia, metabolic acidosis, hypoglycemia, renal failure, and multi-organ dysfunction; requires urgent antimalarial therapy and supportive care.

hemorrhagic measles.definition: A rare, life‑threatening complication of measles (rubeola) in which bleeding occurs from mucous membranes and skin (e.g., purpura, ecchymoses, epistaxis) due to a hemorrhagic diathesis or disseminated intravascular coagulation during the acute infection.

tick-borne illness.definition: An infection transmitted to humans by infected ticks, caused by bacteria, protozoa, or viruses; includes diseases such as Lyme disease, anaplasmosis, babesiosis, and tick-borne encephalitis; symptoms vary but often include fever, fatigue, headache, and muscle aches, with treatment depending on the specific pathogen.

vitamin a deficiency.definition: A deficiency of vitamin A due to inadequate intake, malabsorption, or increased requirements, characterized by impaired vision (night blindness), xerophthalmia with dryness of the conjunctiva and cornea, Bitot spots, skin changes, and increased susceptibility to infections; a leading preventable cause of childhood blindness in many regions.

blastocyst.definition: A hollow, spherical embryonic structure formed about 5–6 days after fertilization in mammals, consisting of an inner cell mass that becomes the embryo and an outer trophoblast that forms the placenta; it implants into the uterine wall.

cardiac bypass.definition: An operative procedure to restore blood flow to the heart by bypassing narrowed or blocked coronary arteries with grafts (usually a vein from the leg or an internal mammary artery), creating alternative routes for blood to reach the heart muscle; typically performed with cardiopulmonary bypass.

subclavian artery.definition: A major artery that supplies blood to the upper limb and parts of the neck and thorax, and contributes to brain circulation via the vertebral artery. The right subclavian arises from the brachiocephalic trunk and the left from the aortic arch; it runs laterally across the first rib and becomes the axillary artery at the lateral border of the first rib.

pulmonary artery.definition: An artery that carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs for oxygenation; the pulmonary trunk divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries.

systemic circulation.definition: The portion of the cardiovascular system that delivers oxygenated blood from the left ventricle through the aorta to body tissues and returns deoxygenated blood to the right atrium via the systemic venous system.

heart surgery.definition: A broad term for operative procedures performed on the heart or great vessels to repair, replace, or bypass cardiac structures or correct congenital defects, often performed with cardiopulmonary bypass.

hypothermia.definition: A medical condition in which the core body temperature falls below 35°C (95°F) due to cold exposure or impaired thermoregulation, causing shivering, confusion or drowsiness, slowed heart and breathing, and potential organ dysfunction.

pneumonitis.definition: Inflammation of the lung parenchyma causing swelling of lung tissue; not necessarily caused by infection and can result from irritants, hypersensitivity, autoimmune processes, or drug/radiation injury.

itraconazole.definition: A triazole antifungal agent that inhibits fungal cytochrome P450 14α-demethylase, reducing ergosterol synthesis and disrupting fungal cell membrane integrity. Used to treat a range of systemic and superficial fungal infections (e.g., histoplasmosis, blastomycosis, aspergillosis, candidiasis, onychomycosis, sporotrichosis); administered orally (capsules or solution) and, in some cases, via intravenous infusion. Monitor liver function and potential drug interactions.

blastomycosis.definition: A systemic fungal infection caused by a dimorphic fungus, acquired by inhalation of airborne spores; it typically presents as acute or chronic pulmonary disease and can disseminate to skin, bone, and other tissues.

north american blastomycosis.definition: An endemic fungal infection caused by Blastomyces dermatitidis in North America, usually presenting as pneumonia with possible disseminated disease to skin and bone; treated with antifungals such as itraconazole or amphotericin B.

gilchrist's disease.definition: I couldn’t locate a reliable, current medical definition for “Gilchrist’s disease.” It appears to be an obsolete or regionally used term with varied meanings in older literature. If you can share the context (field, symptoms, era, or related conditions), I can help identify the closest modern diagnosis or provide definitions for related terms.

gallbladder disease.definition: A broad term for disorders affecting the gallbladder, a pear-shaped organ beneath the liver that stores and concentrates bile. It encompasses conditions such as gallstones (cholelithiasis), inflammation of the gallbladder (cholecystitis), biliary dyskinesia (functional gallbladder disorder), gallbladder polyps, and, rarely, gallbladder cancer.

idiopathic spastic constipation.definition: A chronic functional constipation due to unknown cause, characterized by increased colonic muscle tone and spasms that lead to infrequent, hard-to-pass stools with abdominal discomfort, in the absence of an identifiable organic disease.

mucous colitis.definition: A historical term for a functional bowel disorder characterized by intermittent abdominal pain and mucus in the stool in the absence of detectable inflammatory or structural disease; it is largely equivalent to what is now described as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), often called spastic colon.

preimplantation genetic diagnosis.definition: An IVF-based genetic test of embryos where a few cells are biopsied to detect specific genetic mutations or chromosomal abnormalities, enabling the selection of unaffected embryos for transfer.

blastomere biopsy.definition: A procedure used in preimplantation genetic testing during IVF in which one or more blastomeres (cells from a day-3 cleavage-stage embryo) are removed by micromanipulation for genetic analysis, such as aneuploidy testing or mutation screening, to assess embryo chromosomal/genetic status before transfer. Removal is performed at the 4–8 cell stage and carries risks to embryo viability and potential mosaicism.

blastomerotomy.definition: A procedure involving incising an early embryonic cell (blastomere) during early embryonic development; not part of standard medical practice and typically encountered only in experimental embryology.

blastotomy.definition: A surgical procedure involving cutting into a blastema (embryonic or regenerative tissue); a historical/rare term for incising developing tissue, not commonly used in modern practice.

blepharitis.definition: An inflammation of the eyelid margins, usually chronic, presenting with redness, itching or burning, irritation, tearing, and crusting along the lash margins; classified as anterior (lash-margin involvement) or posterior (meibomian gland dysfunction).

bleeding time test.definition: A historical test of primary hemostasis that measures how long it takes for bleeding to stop after a standardized superficial skin incision, reflecting platelet function and vasoconstriction; several techniques exist (e.g., Ivy, Duke), but the test is largely supplanted by modern hemostasis assays and has variable results.

ivy method.definition: I can’t find a standard medical definition for “ivy method.” Could you provide context or clarify the specialty or spelling (e.g., is it an acronym like IVY, or a specific procedure in a certain field)? If you have any related details, I’ll help define it.

blastocyst cavity.definition: A fluid-filled cavity inside the developing blastocyst that forms as the morula becomes a blastocyst; it enlarges as trophoblast cells line the cavity and the inner cell mass sits at one pole.

blastocoele.definition: A fluid-filled cavity inside the blastula (blastocyst in mammals) formed during early embryogenesis; it is bounded by the outer trophoblast layer and the inner cell mass, and its formation enables subsequent gastrulation.

blastodisk.definition: A disc-shaped region on the surface of a yolk in oviparous animals where cleavage occurs and from which the embryonic blastoderm develops into the embryo.

blastomere.definition: A cell produced by the division (cleavage) of a fertilized egg during early embryogenesis; blastomeres are initially undifferentiated and form the morula, giving rise to the blastocyst.

ulcerative blepharitis.definition: An inflammatory condition of the eyelid margin in which the lid epithelium forms ulcers with crusting and possible marginal erosion, often with purulent discharge and conjunctival irritation, typically due to bacterial infection (e.g., Staphylococcus or Moraxella) or inflammatory skin disease.

pannus.definition: An abnormal layer of tissue that forms over joints or the cornea of the eye.

ectropion.definition: Outward turning of the eyelid (usually the lower lid) away from the eyeball, exposing the palpebral conjunctiva and causing irritation, tearing, and dry eye, with potential corneal complications.

chalazia.definition: Chronic, sterile granulomatous inflammation of a meibomian gland in the eyelid due to duct obstruction, presenting as a painless, firm eyelid lump that enlarges slowly; usually self-limited but may require warm compresses, lid hygiene, or incision and drainage if persistent.

sties.definition: An acute eyelid infection causing a painful, swollen lump at the eyelid margin due to obstruction and infection of an eyelid oil gland (most often Meibomian or Zeis/Moll), usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus; managed with warm compresses, lid hygiene, and topical antibiotics if indicated.

eyelid.definition: A movable fold of skin and underlying tissue that protects the eyeball and helps distribute tears during blinking; consists of an upper and a lower lid with a margin that bears eyelashes and contains muscle and connective tissue.

eyelashes.definition: Short, curved hairs along the edge of the eyelids that help protect the eye from debris by trapping particles and triggering reflex blinking when touched.

lash follicles.definition: An eyelid margin hair follicle that grows a lash; part of the eyelid’s pilosebaceous unit, typically with associated sebaceous glands (glands of Zeis and Moll) and an arrector pili muscle; eyelashes help protect the eye from debris and aid in tear film spread.

lid margins.definition: The free edge of the eyelid where the eyelashes insert and the openings of the meibomian and other glands reside; the mucocutaneous junction forms the lid margin and it helps distribute the tear film and protect the ocular surface.

blighted ovum.definition: A pregnancy in which the fertilized egg implants in the uterus but the embryo fails to develop, resulting in an empty or nonviable gestational sac (anembryonic pregnancy).

blindness.definition: Complete or near‑complete loss of vision due to eye or visual pathway disease or injury, such that vision cannot be corrected to normal with standard interventions (eg, glasses or surgery).

blind spot.definition: A region on the retina (the optic disc) where the optic nerve exits the eye and photoreceptors are absent, creating a physiologic blind spot in the visual field.

colostomy.definition: Surgery that brings one end of the large intestine out through an opening in the abdomen for elimination of stool.

ileotransverse.definition: A surgical connection between the ileum and the transverse colon (an ileotransverse anastomosis), created to restore bowel continuity after resection.

suction curettage.definition: A procedure in which suction is used to evacuate the contents of the uterus, typically for termination of an early pregnancy or evacuation after miscarriage; the cervix is dilated and a suction cannula is inserted to remove tissue, often followed by curettage to ensure complete evacuation.

incontinentia pigmenti.definition: A rare X-linked dominant genodermatosis caused by mutations in the IKBKG (NEMO) gene, presenting with skin lesions that follow Blaschko lines and progress through vesicular, verrucous, hyperpigmented, and atrophic/hypopigmented stages, often accompanied by dental, hair, ocular, and CNS abnormalities; predominantly affects females, with male conceptuses often nonviable.

ambivalence.definition: The simultaneous presence of opposing feelings, attitudes, or motivations toward a person, object, or idea, often leading to indecision or uncertainty.

blepharoadenoma.definition: A benign eyelid tumor arising from glandular tissue of the eyelid (adnexal glands, such as sweat or sebaceous glands), typically presenting as a slow-growing, painless, well-circumscribed nodular lesion; treated with complete surgical excision.

blepharoadenomata.definition: Benign eyelid tumors arising from adnexal sweat glands, comprising glandular and ductal elements; typically slow-growing, painless nodules with treatment by complete surgical excision and an excellent prognosis.

blepharoatheroma.definition: A lipid-laden lesion on the eyelid forming a soft, yellowish plaque, typically associated with hyperlipidemia (a type of eyelid xanthomatous lesion).

blepharochalasis.definition: A condition of recurrent, painless swelling of the eyelids (usually the upper lids) beginning in childhood, resulting in thinning and stretching of the eyelid skin with permanent lid laxity (dermatochalasis) and sometimes ptosis.

blepharoclonus.definition: Involuntary, brief, rhythmic contractions of the eyelid muscles (orbicularis oculi), causing repetitive blinking or eyelid jerks.

blepharophimosis.definition: A congenital condition characterized by markedly narrowed horizontal palpebral fissures due to underdeveloped eyelids, commonly with ptosis and epicanthus inversus (and sometimes telecanthus).

blepharoplasty.definition: Cosmetic surgery to improve the appearance of droopy eyelids by removing excess skin and fat.

blepharoplegia.definition: Paralysis of the muscles that move the eyelid, resulting in impaired eyelid movement (commonly presenting as ptosis and may include incomplete eyelid closure).

blepharospasm.definition: A focal dystonia characterized by involuntary, repetitive or sustained contractions of the eyelid and periorbital muscles (primarily the orbicularis oculi), causing frequent blinking, eyelid squeezing, or forceful eyelid closure that can impair vision.

blister.definition: A small pocket of fluid that develops between the upper layers of skin; often caused by friction or burns.

bulla.definition: A large, fluid-filled blister on the skin or mucous membranes, typically greater than 1 cm in diameter.

vesicant.definition: A substance that causes vesication (blistering) of skin or mucous membranes upon contact; includes certain chemical warfare agents and vesicant chemotherapy drugs that can cause tissue necrosis if extravasated.

oxime.definition: A chemical functional group (R1R2C=NOH) formed by the reaction of hydroxylamine with aldehydes or ketones; oximes include compounds such as pralidoxime used as antidotes to organophosphate poisoning.

lewisite.definition: A vesicant (blistering) organoarsenic chemical warfare agent that causes rapid, painful skin and mucous membrane blistering; exposure can lead to systemic arsenic toxicity.

distilled mustard.definition: An extract obtained by distilling mustard seeds or mustard oil to concentrate volatile constituents; historically used as a topical irritant or counterirritant, but not a standard or widely used medical preparation today due to irritation and variability.

mustard gas.definition: A sulfur-containing vesicant chemical warfare agent (bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide) that causes delayed-onset blistering of skin and mucous membranes, with potential severe injury to the eyes and respiratory tract; it acts as an alkylating agent, damaging DNA and proteins.

nitrogen mustard.definition: A class of alkylating chemotherapy agents derived from mustard gas that form cross-links in DNA, inhibiting replication and causing tumor cell death; used to treat various cancers, with common adverse effects including bone marrow suppression, nausea, and mucositis.

sulfur mustard.definition: A vesicant chemical warfare agent (bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide) that alkylates DNA and other cellular components, causing delayed-onset blisters on skin and mucous membranes, with potential severe eye and respiratory tract injury; exposure requires immediate decontamination and supportive medical care.

tachypnea.definition: Abnormally rapid breathing defined by an increased respiratory rate (in adults, typically >20 breaths per minute); the depth of breathing may be shallow or normal.

antilewisite.definition: A chelating antidote used to treat arsenic- and other heavy metal poisonings, and to counter exposure to the arsenical chemical warfare agent lewisite; also known as British anti-Lewisite (BAL); chemical name 2,3-dimercapto-1-propanol.

british antilewisite.definition: A chelating agent used as an antidote for acute poisoning by arsenic, mercury, and certain other heavy metals, and historically for exposure to Lewisite.

ointment.definition: A semisolid topical preparation containing an active drug dispersed in a greasy base (commonly petrolatum) for application to the skin or mucous membranes to deliver medication and provide protective occlusion.

drops.definition: An archaic term for edema (dropsy), the abnormal accumulation of fluid in body tissues leading to swelling.

coumadin.definition: A brand-name anticoagulant (warfarin) that inhibits synthesis of vitamin K–dependent clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X; used to prevent and treat thromboembolism; requires regular INR monitoring and a consistent dietary intake of vitamin K.

timolol.definition: A nonselective beta-adrenergic receptor antagonist (beta-blocker) used as an ophthalmic solution to lower intraocular pressure in open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension by decreasing aqueous humor production.

blocadren.definition: A brand name for propranolol, a non-selective beta-adrenergic blocker used to treat hypertension, angina, certain tachyarrhythmias, and to prevent migraine and reduce anxiety-related physical symptoms.

gow-gates.definition: A dental regional anesthesia technique that blocks the entire mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve by injecting near the neck of the mandible, providing anesthesia to the teeth and soft tissues supplied by that nerve on the same side.

inferior alveolar block.definition: A dental local anesthesia technique in which a local anesthetic is injected near the inferior alveolar nerve as it enters the mandibular canal at the mandibular foramen to produce reversible anesthesia of the ipsilateral mandibular teeth (typically from the first molar to the midline) and the associated buccal mucosa and soft tissues supplied by branches of the inferior alveolar and mental nerves.

local infiltration.definition: A technique in which a local anesthetic is injected directly into tissues around a surgical site to block nerve conduction and produce numbness/analgesia of that area, enabling minor procedures without general anesthesia.

capillaries.definition: The body’s smallest blood vessels; they deliver oxygen and nutrients to tissues.

leukocyte.definition: A white blood cell; a nucleated cell of the immune system that defends the body against infection and foreign invaders.

uric acid.definition: A waste product of purine metabolism; the end product of nucleic acid breakdown that is normally dissolved in blood and excreted by the kidneys in urine; elevated levels (hyperuricemia) can cause gout and uric acid kidney stones.

cushing's disease.definition: A pituitary-origin form of Cushing syndrome caused by an ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma that drives excess cortisol production by the adrenal cortex.

hypopituitarism.definition: A disorder in which the anterior pituitary fails to produce sufficient quantities of one or more pituitary hormones (e.g., ACTH, TSH, LH/FSH, GH, prolactin), resulting in secondary endocrine deficiencies. It may be partial or complete (panhypopituitarism) and is managed with hormone replacement and treatment of the underlying pituitary pathology.

congenital adrenal hyperplasia.definition: A group of genetic conditions that limit hormone production in the adrenal glands (above the kidneys).

ectopic acth-producing tumors.definition: A tumor located outside the pituitary that secretes adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), leading to excess cortisol production by the adrenal cortex and resulting in Cushing syndrome; commonly associated with neuroendocrine tumors such as small cell lung carcinoma and bronchial carcinoids.

hbv.definition: A small enveloped DNA virus of the Hepadnaviridae family that infects hepatocytes and causes hepatitis B; transmitted through blood and body fluids; can be acute or chronic and may lead to cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma; preventable by vaccination.

clostridium perfringens.definition: A Gram-positive, anaerobic, spore-forming bacillus; a common cause of gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis) and food poisoning, producing toxins (notably alpha-toxin) that destroy tissue and cell membranes; found in soil and the intestinal tracts of humans and animals, with infection typically arising from contaminated wounds or ingestion of contaminated meat.

lactate.definition: A salt or ester of lactic acid; in physiology, the lactate ion results from pyruvate reduction during anaerobic glycolysis and can serve as an energy substrate; elevated lactate levels reflect increased anaerobic metabolism or hypoxia and are used clinically as a marker of tissue hypoperfusion.

thrombocyte.definition: A small, anucleate cell fragment in blood that participates in hemostasis by forming a plug at sites of vascular injury and aiding coagulation; derived from megakaryocytes in the bone marrow; in humans, commonly referred to as platelets.

culture medium.definition: A prepared, sterile substrate (liquid or solid) that provides nutrients and the right conditions—pH, moisture, and sometimes selective or differential additives—to support the growth and maintenance of microorganisms or cells in vitro.

blood culture.definition: A laboratory test in which a blood sample is cultured to detect the growth of bacteria or fungi in the bloodstream, used to diagnose bacteremia or fungemia and guide antimicrobial therapy.

sensitivity test.definition: A test used to determine how responsive a patient or organism is to a given agent or stimulus. In microbiology, it commonly refers to testing an organism’s susceptibility to specific antimicrobial drugs to guide treatment.

donor.definition: A person who donates blood, plasma, an organ, or tissue for transplantation, research, or therapeutic use; donations may come from living or deceased individuals.

recipient.definition: In medicine, a recipient is a patient who receives an organ, tissue, blood products, or other implanted material as part of a transplant or therapeutic intervention.

blood donor.definition: A healthy individual who donates blood or blood components for transfusion to others; donors are screened for infectious diseases and other contraindications, and donations may be whole blood, plasma, or platelets (allogeneic) or for autologous use.

blood bank.definition: A facility that collects, tests, processes into components, stores, and distributes human blood and blood products for transfusion, with donor safety, infectious disease screening, and compatibility testing.

schistosoma haematobium.definition: A parasitic flatworm (trematode) that causes urogenital schistosomiasis in humans. It inhabits the venous plexus of the bladder, with eggs provoking granulomatous inflammation leading to hematuria and dysuria; transmission occurs via freshwater snails, and diagnosis is by detecting eggs in urine. Treated with praziquantel.

schistosoma japonicum.definition: An parasitic trematode (blood fluke) that causes schistosomiasis japonica in humans; transmitted via freshwater snails (Oncomelania) as the intermediate host; adults reside in the mesenteric veins of the small intestine, and eggs deposited in tissues induce granulomatous inflammation, potentially causing intestinal and hepatic disease; endemic to parts of East Asia.

schistosoma mansoni.definition: An etiologic species of parasitic flatworm (trematode) that causes intestinal schistosomiasis in humans; adults reside in the mesenteric veins, and eggs released by the worms induce intestinal and hepatic inflammation; transmitted through contact with freshwater containing snail-derived cercariae (Biomphalaria spp.).

hydrogen ion.definition: A positively charged ion produced when a hydrogen atom loses its electron; essentially a proton. In aqueous solutions, it is present mainly as hydronium (H3O+), and its concentration determines the acidity (pH) of the solution.

po2.definition: Partial pressure of oxygen; the oxygen tension in a gas mixture or in arterial blood, expressed in millimeters of mercury (mmHg), used to assess oxygenation and gas exchange.

pco2.definition: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide in the blood; a measure of alveolar ventilation and the respiratory component of acid–base balance, normally about 35–45 mm Hg in arterial blood.

so2.definition: A colorless, irritating gas that causes mucous membrane irritation (eyes, nose, throat) and can provoke coughing and bronchospasm; high concentrations may lead to serious respiratory effects such as pulmonary edema. It is a common air pollutant from burning sulfur-containing fuels and certain industrial processes.

fasting plasma glucose.definition: Measurement of blood glucose after an overnight fast (usually at least 8 hours). It helps diagnose diabetes and prediabetes; normal is <100 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L); impaired fasting glucose is 100–125 mg/dL (5.6–6.9 mmol/L); diabetes is ≥126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) on two separate occasions.

blood glucose.definition: The concentration of glucose in the bloodstream, usually measured in mg/dL or mmol/L, reflecting the body's current energy availability.

glucose test.definition: A laboratory or point-of-care test that measures the amount of glucose (sugar) in blood or urine, used to diagnose, monitor, or manage diabetes and assess glycemic control.

abo.definition: An inherited blood group system defined by the presence or absence of A and B carbohydrate antigens on red blood cells. Individuals with type A have A antigens and anti-B antibodies; type B have B antigens and anti-A antibodies; type AB have both antigens and no anti-A or anti-B antibodies; type O have neither antigen and both anti-A and anti-B antibodies. These patterns determine transfusion compatibility and ABO typing is used to match blood for transfusions.

rh.definition: A D antigen on the surface of red blood cells that determines whether blood is positive or negative for this antigen and is important for transfusion compatibility and the risk of hemolytic disease of the newborn.

mns.definition: An acronym that denotes various medical conditions depending on the context; there is no single, universally accepted definition. If you provide the intended expansion or field, I can define it precisely.

p.definition: Not a standalone medical term; a single-letter abbreviation used for various terms depending on context (e.g., post- meaning after; pulse; parity; phosphorus; proton), with the exact meaning defined by the surrounding notes.

kell.definition: A human blood group system of red blood cell antigens; antibodies to these antigens can cause hemolytic transfusion reactions and hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn.

duffy.definition: A glycoprotein receptor on red blood cells and endothelial cells that binds chemokines; determines the Fy(a) and Fy(b) blood group antigens and is encoded by the DARC gene.

kidd.definition: A human blood group antigen system comprising the Jka and Jkb antigens on red blood cells; antibodies to these antigens can cause hemolytic transfusion reactions and hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn; the antigens are encoded by the SLC14A1 gene.

lutheran.definition: Not a medical term; there is no standard medical definition.

kx.definition: Not a standard medical term or widely used acronym; its meaning is context-dependent. Please provide the context (specialty, notes, or source) to give an accurate definition.

h.definition: An abbreviation for hour, a unit of time equal to 60 minutes, used in medical contexts to indicate dosing intervals and durations.

xg.definition: There is no widely recognized medical term abbreviated as "xg" in standard dictionaries. If you can share the context or capitalization (e.g., XG vs xg, field of use), I can identify a specific meaning or offer a targeted definition.

blood group.definition: Classification of blood based on the presence or absence of specific antigens on red blood cells (most notably the ABO and Rh systems), used to determine compatibility for transfusions and other therapies.

globulin.definition: A group of plasma proteins divided into alpha, beta, and gamma fractions; they participate in transport of lipids and metals, act in various enzymatic processes, and provide immune defense (the gamma fraction consists of antibodies).

plasma protein.definition: Proteins dissolved in blood plasma, including albumin, globulins, and fibrinogen; they are mainly synthesized by the liver and perform functions such as maintaining oncotic pressure, transporting substances, immune defense, and blood coagulation.

serum protein.definition: Proteins present in blood serum—the liquid portion of clotted blood after the fibrin clot forms. The major components are albumin and globulins (including immunoglobulins); they originate mainly from the liver and plasma cells and help maintain oncotic pressure, transport substances, and provide immune defense.

systolic.definition: The top number of a blood pressure measurement. Describes the pressure in the blood vessels when the heart is beating.

diastolic.definition: The bottom number of a blood pressure measurement; the pressure in the arteries when the heart is at rest between beats.

sphygmomanometer.definition: A device for measuring blood pressure.

auscultation.definition: A physical examination technique that involves listening to the internal sounds of the body, usually with a stethoscope, to evaluate the heart, lungs, and abdomen for normal sounds and abnormalities.

stethoscope.definition: A medical instrument used to auscultate internal body sounds, most commonly heart, lung, and bowel sounds; it consists of a chest piece connected by tubing to earpieces.

korotkoff.definition: Sounds heard over an artery with a stethoscope during cuff deflation in auscultatory blood pressure measurement, used to determine systolic and diastolic pressures.

phlebotomy.definition: A procedure to draw blood from a vein (venipuncture) for laboratory testing, blood donation, or transfusion preparation.

bloodletting.definition: Historically, a medical practice in which blood was withdrawn from a patient to treat disease, based on balancing the body's humors. In modern medicine it is rarely used as a general therapy, though therapeutic phlebotomy is employed for conditions such as hemochromatosis or polycythemia vera.

epidural blood patch.definition: A procedure in which autologous blood is injected into the epidural space to seal a cerebrospinal fluid leak and relieve headaches caused by intracranial hypotension, typically after a dural puncture.

blood patch.definition: An autologous blood patch is a procedure in which the patient’s own blood is injected into the epidural space to form a clot and seal a cerebrospinal fluid leak, commonly to treat a post-dural puncture headache.

dextran.definition: A complex, branched polysaccharide made of glucose units linked mainly by α-1,6-glycosidic bonds with occasional α-1,3 branches; produced by certain bacteria from sucrose and used clinically as a plasma volume expander and in laboratory procedures as a density/viscosity modifier.

hetastarch.definition: A synthetic colloid plasma-volume expander derived from hydroxyethyl starch, given intravenously to increase intravascular volume in hypovolemia or shock; associated with coagulopathy and potential kidney injury; use is restricted in some guidelines.

plasma protein fraction.definition: The protein component of blood plasma, including albumin, globulins, fibrinogen, and other plasma proteins; the isolated protein fraction obtained by fractionation of plasma for diagnostic or therapeutic use.

perfluorocarbon emulsions.definition: A colloidal suspension of droplets of a perfluorocarbon liquid in water, stabilized by emulsifying agents; because perfluorocarbons dissolve large amounts of gases, these emulsions have been explored as artificial oxygen carriers to enhance tissue oxygenation and as imaging contrast agents.

blood substitute.definition: A substance that mimics one or more functions of blood—primarily oxygen delivery and/or volume expansion—to sustain circulation when donor blood is unavailable or unsafe; examples include hemoglobin-based oxygen carriers and perfluorocarbon emulsions.

polycythemia.definition: An abnormal increase in red blood cell mass, resulting in elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit; it can be primary (polycythemia vera) or secondary to increased erythropoietin production (e.g., due to hypoxia or tumors), or relative due to reduced plasma volume.

digitalis.definition: A plant genus (foxglove) and the cardiac glycoside medications derived from it (e.g., digoxin, digitoxin) used to treat heart failure and certain arrhythmias by increasing myocardial contractility; they inhibit Na+/K+-ATPase, raising intracellular calcium, with a narrow therapeutic index and potential toxicity.

digitalis-like drugs.definition: A class of cardiac glycosides that inhibit the Na+/K+-ATPase pump, increasing intracellular calcium in cardiac myocytes to produce a positive inotropic effect; historically used for heart failure and certain tachyarrhythmias, but with a narrow therapeutic index and potential toxicity.

multiple myeloma.definition: A malignant proliferation of monoclonal plasma cells within the bone marrow (a plasma cell dyscrasia) that causes bone lesions, anemia, hypercalcemia, renal impairment, and increased susceptibility to infection.

renal function.definition: The kidneys' ability to filter blood to form urine, regulate fluid and electrolyte balance and acid-base status, concentrate urine, and produce hormones (e.g., erythropoietin, renin) and activate vitamin D.

kidney failure.definition: When your kidneys stop working. Also called chronic kidney disease or end stage kidney disease.

urea.definition: A waste product of protein digestion and metabolism.

osmolality.definition: A measure of the concentration of osmotically active solutes per kilogram of solvent, expressed in milliosmoles per kilogram (mOsm/kg); it determines osmotic pressure and drives water movement across semipermeable membranes; in body fluids, normal values are about 275–295 mOsm/kg.

osmolality test.definition: A laboratory measurement of the concentration of osmotically active solutes in a body fluid (usually serum/plasma), expressed as milliosmoles per kilogram of water (mOsm/kg); it can be measured directly with an osmometer or estimated from sodium, glucose, and BUN. It helps assess hydration status and detect disturbances of water balance or solute concentrations (e.g., hyponatremia, hypernatremia).

potassium.definition: An essential intracellular cation and electrolyte (chemical element potassium, symbol K) critical for nerve impulse transmission, muscle contraction, and maintaining cellular membrane potential; normal serum concentration is about 3.5–5.0 mmol/L.

blood transfusion.definition: Transfusion of blood or blood components from a donor to a recipient to restore circulating blood volume and/or improve oxygen-carrying capacity, used to treat acute blood loss or anemia; components include red blood cells, plasma, and platelets.

transfusion reaction.definition: An adverse event that occurs during or after a blood transfusion, caused by immune or nonimmune responses to donor blood components, ranging from mild febrile or allergic symptoms to life‑threatening hemolysis, pulmonary injury, or circulatory overload.

rh type.definition: Presence or absence of the D antigen in the Rh (Rhesus) blood group system on red blood cells; D-positive means the antigen is present, D-negative means it is absent. Used to determine blood type and transfusion compatibility and to assess risk of Rh incompatibility in pregnancy.

abo group.definition: An immunohematologic classification of human blood based on the presence or absence of A and B antigens on red blood cells and the corresponding anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma, yielding four major types (A, B, AB, O) and used to determine compatibility for blood transfusions.

agglutinogens.definition: An antigen that causes agglutination by specific antibodies; in red blood cells, the surface A and B antigens that determine blood type.

abo antigens.definition: Carbohydrate antigens on the surface of red blood cells that determine the ABO blood group. The H antigen is the precursor; A antigen is formed by adding N‑acetylgalactosamine and B antigen by adding galactose to the H antigen. IA and IB encode the transferases for A and B, while ii (O) lacks functional transferases and presents only H. People typically have naturally occurring anti-A and/or anti-B antibodies capable of agglutinating incompatible blood.

saline.definition: A watery solution that contains a small amount of salt and is often used to administer drugs or as a substitute for plasma.

blood warming coil.definition: A device that warms blood or blood products by circulating them through a heated coil/heat exchanger (often in a warmed bath or via an electric heater) to raise their temperature to near body temperature before transfusion or during bypass, helping to prevent perioperative hypothermia.

cord blood.definition: Blood remaining in the umbilical cord and placenta after birth; it contains hematopoietic stem cells that can be collected, stored, and used for transplantation to treat certain hematologic and immune disorders.

blood plasma.definition: The straw-colored liquid component of blood that remains when cells are removed; it is mostly water with dissolved proteins (including albumin, globulins, and fibrinogen), electrolytes, nutrients, hormones, and waste products. It serves as the transport medium for substances throughout the body and provides clotting factors for hemostasis.

interstitial fluid.definition: Fluid that surrounds and bathes tissue cells in the interstitial space; a component of extracellular fluid derived from blood plasma by capillary filtration and exchanged with plasma via capillaries and lymphatics, providing the medium for diffusion of nutrients, electrolytes, and waste between blood and cells.

extracellular fluid.definition: Extracellular fluid is the body’s fluid outside cells, comprising plasma (intravascular fluid), interstitial fluid, and other fluids (lymph and transcellular fluids). It provides the medium for exchange of nutrients and wastes between cells and the blood, helps maintain extracellular ion balance and osmolarity, and amounts to about 20% of body weight (roughly 14 liters in a 70-kilogram adult).

intracellular fluid.definition: The fluid contained within cells; makes up about two-thirds of total body water; high in potassium, phosphate, and proteins; separated from extracellular fluid by the cell membrane.

blood vessel.definition: Tiny tubes that move blood around the body. Includes three main types (arteries, veins, capillaries).

biliverdin.definition: A green bile pigment formed during heme catabolism when heme is cleaved by heme oxygenase to biliverdin; it is subsequently reduced to bilirubin by biliverdin reductase.

bodansky unit.definition: A Bodansky unit is a historical measure of the neutralizing potency of diphtheria antitoxin, defined by the Bodansky mouse-protection assay as the amount of antitoxin necessary to protect a standard dose of diphtheria toxin in vivo; it is largely obsolete and has been superseded by modern international units.

mongolian spot.definition: A benign congenital dermal melanocytosis presenting as a flat blue-gray patch (often on the lower back or buttocks) caused by melanocytes remaining in the dermis; common in newborns of Asian, African, or Latin American descent and typically fades during early childhood.

blue nevus.definition: A benign pigmented skin lesion in which melanocytes are located in the dermis, producing a blue to blue-black papule or nodule; color due to light scattering (Tyndall effect).

blue dot sign.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. Could you share the clinical context (e.g., dermatology, pediatrics, radiology) or the condition you’re studying? I can look for a more precise definition in that specific area or provide a provisional description once clarified.

blue dome cyst.definition: Historically, a blue dome cyst refers to a benign, fluid-filled cystic lesion that is dome-shaped and blue-tinged on examination; the blue color results from translucency of the cyst contents with the overlying skin. The exact diagnosis (e.g., epidermoid, mucous-retention, or ganglion-type cyst) depends on the location and histology.

blue rubber bleb nevus.definition: A congenital vascular malformation of the skin presenting as soft, compressible, blue-purple papules or nodules due to dilated venous channels; commonly associated with a syndrome that also involves venous malformations in the gastrointestinal tract, potentially causing GI bleeding and anemia.

pediculosis corporis.definition: Infestation of the body by the human body louse (Pediculus humanus corporis), in which lice live on clothing and migrate to the skin to feed, causing pruritus and excoriations; transmission via infested clothing or bedding; treatment includes delousing the person and their clothing (hot washing/drying, ironing) and using topical pediculicides or, if needed, oral agents.

pediculosis pubis.definition: A pubic lice infestation of the hair and skin in the pubic area, caused by the louse Pthirus pubis, typically presenting with intense itching and possible visible lice or nits on hair. It is usually transmitted through sexual contact but can spread via shared clothing or bedding; treatment involves topical pediculicides (e.g., permethrin or pyrethrin with piperonyl butoxide) and washing or sealing contaminated items.

blue cohosh.definition: A herbal remedy from the root of Actaea racemosa (formerly Cimicifuga racemosa), traditionally used as an emmenagogue and uterine stimulant to induce labor or treat menstrual symptoms; efficacy is not well supported by evidence, and it is contraindicated in pregnancy due to risk of fetal harm and potential maternal adverse effects (e.g., hypotension, liver toxicity).

cerebral vascular accident.definition: A sudden loss of brain function caused by an interruption of blood supply to a part of the brain, usually from ischemia or hemorrhage, leading to focal neurological deficits such as weakness, speech disturbance, or vision changes.

neurodevelopmental treatment.definition: A therapeutic approach in neurorehabilitation that uses hands-on facilitation and inhibition of movement to promote normal motor patterns and postural control in individuals with central nervous system impairments, aiming to reduce abnormal tone and reflex activity and improve functional movement.

blunt dissection.definition: A surgical technique in which tissues are separated along natural planes using non-cutting instruments (e.g., fingers, blunt dissectors) rather than by cutting, to minimize tissue damage and preserve underlying structures.

northern blot.definition: A laboratory method for detecting and quantifying specific RNA molecules. RNA is separated by size on a denaturing gel, transferred to a membrane, and probed with a labeled complementary nucleic acid; the resulting signal indicates the presence and abundance of the target RNA.

southern blot.definition: A molecular biology technique for detecting a specific DNA sequence in a sample: DNA is digested and separated by gel electrophoresis, transferred to a membrane (blotted), and probed with a labeled DNA probe complementary to the target sequence, with detection of the bound probe.

western blot.definition: A laboratory method that detects a specific protein in a sample by separating proteins by gel electrophoresis, transferring them to a membrane, and probing with an antibody specific to the target protein; detection yields a band whose presence and intensity indicate the protein's presence and approximate quantity.

nitrocellulose membrane.definition: A thin, porous sheet of nitrocellulose derived from nitrated cellulose used as a solid support in blotting techniques to immobilize biomolecules (proteins, DNA, RNA) for detection by probes or antibodies (e.g., Western, Southern, Northern blotting).

phlegmasia cerulea dolens.definition: A severe, limb‐threatening form of deep venous thrombosis due to extensive iliofemoral venous thrombosis with obstruction of venous outflow, causing massive leg swelling and cyanosis (painful blue swelling); can progress to venous gangrene if not treated promptly, and is managed with urgent anticoagulation and often thrombolysis or surgical thrombectomy.

bochdalek's hernia.definition: A congenital posterolateral diaphragmatic hernia due to failure of the pleuroperitoneal membranes to close, usually on the left, allowing abdominal contents to herniate into the thoracic cavity and causing pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory distress in neonates.

pericardial cavity.definition: A potential space between the visceral (epicardial) and parietal layers of the serous pericardium, normally containing a small amount of lubricating pericardial fluid to reduce friction during heart movement.

pleural cavity.definition: A potential space between the visceral and parietal pleura surrounding the lungs, normally containing a small amount of lubricating serous fluid; this fluid reduces friction during respiration and the negative pressure helps keep the lungs expanded.

mediastinum.definition: Central compartment of the thoracic cavity between the lungs, extending from the superior thoracic aperture to the diaphragm; contains the heart and pericardium, great vessels, trachea, esophagus, thymus, lymph nodes, and relevant nerves (phrenic, vagus) and other structures; subdivided into superior and inferior parts, with the inferior further divided into anterior, middle, and posterior divisions.

thoracic cavity.definition: A chest cavity within the thorax bounded by the ribs, sternum, vertebral column, and diaphragm; it contains the lungs (in their pleural sacs) and the mediastinal contents. It is subdivided into two pleural cavities and the mediastinum, which houses the heart, great vessels, trachea, and esophagus (the pericardial cavity lies within the mediastinum around the heart).

abdominal cavity.definition: The space within the abdomen bounded superiorly by the diaphragm and inferiorly by the pelvic inlet, containing most of the digestive organs (stomach, intestines, liver, pancreas, spleen), the kidneys and adrenal glands; lined by peritoneum.

pelvic cavity.definition: An enclosed space within the bony pelvis bounded by the pelvic bones and pelvic floor that contains the pelvic viscera—the urinary bladder and distal ureters, portions of the reproductive organs (uterus and ovaries in females; prostate and seminal vesicles in males), and the rectum—and communicates with the abdominal cavity through the pelvic inlet.

dorsal body cavity.definition: A posterior body cavity within the skull and vertebral column that houses the brain and spinal cord; it comprises the cranial cavity and the vertebral (spinal) cavity.

ventral body cavity.definition: The ventral body cavity is the anterior cavity of the trunk, subdivided into the thoracic cavity and the abdominopelvic cavity; it houses the heart and lungs in the thoracic portion and most abdominal and pelvic organs in the abdominopelvic portion, and is separated from the dorsal cavity by the diaphragm and lined by serous membranes (pleura, pericardium, and peritoneum).

major body cavities.definition:
Cavities are enclosed spaces within the body that house and protect internal organs. The major ones are:
- Dorsal cavity: cranial cavity (brain) and vertebral/spinal cavity (spinal cord).
- Ventral cavity: thoracic cavity (pericardial space around the heart and pleural spaces around the lungs) and abdominopelvic cavity (abdominal cavity and pelvic cavity).

gi tract.definition: A continuous digestive tube from the mouth to the anus that ingests, digests, and absorbs nutrients and eliminates waste; it includes the esophagus, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine.

appendix testis.definition: A vestigial remnant of the Müllerian (paramesonephric) duct located at the upper pole of the testis; it is sometimes called the hydatid of Morgagni and is usually asymptomatic but can undergo torsion, causing acute scrotal pain.

appendix epididymis.definition:
- An elongated, blind-ended tubular structure attached to the cecum in the lower right abdomen; part of the digestive tract, containing lymphoid tissue, with an uncertain exact function and prone to inflammation.

- A highly coiled tube adjacent to the testis that stores, concentrates, and matures sperm before passage to the vas deferens; part of the male reproductive tract with head, body, and tail sections.

transposition of the great vessels.definition: A congenital heart defect in which the aorta arises from the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery arises from the left ventricle, creating two parallel circulations and causing systemic hypoxemia unless there is a shunt that allows mixing; definitive treatment is early surgical correction (arterial switch operation).

congenital atelectasis.definition: A neonatal condition in which all or part of the lung is collapsed or fails to inflate at birth, typically due to insufficient surfactant causing alveolar collapse or congenital airway obstruction, leading to impaired gas exchange.

blue spot.definition: A blue-gray patch on the skin caused by pigment-containing cells in the dermis; most often used to describe congenital dermal melanocytosis (Mongolian spot) in newborns, which typically fades with time.

blue baby.definition: A newborn with central cyanosis due to low arterial oxygen saturation, typically from congenital heart defects that cause mixing or right-to-left shunting of blood; a historical term for a cyanotic infant.

cyanobacteria.definition: A phylum of photosynthetic, prokaryotic organisms that perform oxygenic photosynthesis; formerly called blue-green algae; widely found in aquatic and terrestrial environments; some species fix nitrogen; some blooms can produce toxins.

blue-green algae.definition: Blue-green algae is a lay term for cyanobacteria, photosynthetic bacteria found in freshwater and marine environments; these organisms can form blooms, and some species produce toxins (e.g., microcystins, cylindrospermopsins, anatoxins) that may contaminate drinking water and cause liver or nervous system injuries in humans and animals.

rickettsiosis.definition: An umbrella term for infections caused by Rickettsia bacteria (obligate intracellular organisms) transmitted to humans by arthropod vectors (ticks, mites, fleas, lice), typically presenting with fever, headache, myalgias, and a rash; diagnosed by serology or molecular tests and treated with doxycycline.

typhus.definition: A group of infectious diseases caused by intracellular bacteria of the genera Rickettsia or Orientia, transmitted to humans by arthropod vectors such as body lice, fleas, mites, or chiggers. It typically presents with abrupt fever, severe headache, myalgias, and often a diffuse maculopapular rash; treated with doxycycline and prevented by vector control.

htlv.definition: Human T-lymphotropic virus (HTLV) is a retrovirus that infects T lymphocytes; HTLV‑1 is associated with adult T‑cell leukemia/lymphoma and HTLV‑1–associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis, and the virus is transmitted through blood, sexual contact, and breastfeeding; there is no widely available cure or vaccine.

blv-htlv retroviruses.definition: A group of enveloped, positive-sense single-stranded RNA retroviruses in the genus Deltaretrovirus, including bovine leukemia virus (BLV) and human T-lymphotropic viruses (HTLV-1/HTLV-2). They reverse-transcribe their RNA into a DNA provirus and integrate it into the host genome, with infection that can lead to lymphoid malignancies such as enzootic bovine leukosis in cattle and adult T‑cell leukemia/lymphoma in humans.

sarcoidosis.definition: A systemic inflammatory disease of unknown etiology characterized by the formation of noncaseating granulomas in multiple organs, most commonly the lungs and intrathoracic lymph nodes.

boeck's disease.definition: A multisystem granulomatous inflammatory disease of unknown etiology, characterized by noncaseating granulomas in involved tissues. It most commonly affects the lungs and intrathoracic lymph nodes but can involve skin, eyes, liver, and other organs.

boerhaave syndrome.definition: A spontaneous, full-thickness rupture of the esophagus after forceful vomiting, leading to leakage of esophageal contents into the mediastinum and pleural space; a life-threatening surgical emergency.

mediastinitis.definition: Mediastinitis is inflammation of the mediastinum, the central compartment of the thoracic cavity, usually due to infectious processes (for example after esophageal perforation or cardiac surgery) and can be life-threatening if not promptly treated.

retching.definition: An involuntary, rhythmic series of abdominal and esophageal contractions occurring with nausea that precedes vomiting but expels no gastric contents; also called a dry heave.

bohr effect.definition: A physiological mechanism whereby increased carbon dioxide and hydrogen ion concentration (lower pH) decreases hemoglobin’s affinity for oxygen, shifting the oxygen dissociation curve to the right and promoting oxygen unloading at tissues (reversed in the lungs when CO2 is expelled).

oxyhemoglobin.definition: A form of hemoglobin in which oxygen is bound to the iron in the heme groups (HbO2); enables transport of oxygen from the lungs to tissues and is the bright red form of arterial blood, with binding being reversible to release oxygen in tissues.

co2.definition: A colorless, odorless gas produced by cellular metabolism and combustion; it is expelled from the body via the lungs and acts as a waste product and a volatile acid that helps regulate blood pH.

internal hemorrhage.definition: Bleeding that occurs inside the body, within tissues or a body cavity, not visible externally; it can result from injury, disease, or surgery and may lead to hypovolemia or shock if substantial.

machupo.definition: An arenavirus of the New World group that causes Bolivian hemorrhagic fever; transmission to humans occurs via contact with infected rodent excreta or close contact with infected people; natural reservoir is the rodent Calomys callosus; enveloped, segmented, negative-sense RNA virus; outbreaks have high mortality; no widely available vaccine; treatment is supportive (ribavirin may help if given early).

bombay phenotype.definition: A rare blood group phenotype (hh) in which red blood cells lack the H antigen due to a FUT1 gene mutation; without H antigen, ABO antigens cannot be expressed, and individuals typically have anti-H antibodies, meaning they can only receive blood from Bombay phenotype donors.

palatal cysts.definition: Non-odontogenic cystic lesions located in the palate, arising from embryologic epithelial remnants in palatal sutures or the nasopalatine duct. The most common forms are the incisive canal (nasopalatine duct) cyst in the anterior hard palate and the median palatine cyst in the midline of the posterior hard palate. They usually present as a painless palatal swelling; imaging shows a well-defined midline radiolucency. Treatment is surgical enucleation with rare recurrence.

bohn's nodules.definition: Small, benign keratin-filled nodules on the hard palate or gingival/alveolar mucosa of newborns, arising from remnants of mucous gland tissue; they typically resolve spontaneously within a few weeks.

old bone infarcts.definition: A chronic, healed osteonecrosis lesion resulting from prior interruption of blood supply to bone, in which necrotic bone has been replaced by sclerotic bone or fibrous tissue and is often radiographically well-demarcated; clinically, it is frequently asymptomatic but may predispose to fracture.

osteosarcoma.definition: A malignant primary bone tumor in which cancerous osteoblasts produce osteoid or immature bone; the most common primary bone cancer, typically affecting children and young adults and usually arising in the metaphysis of long bones; it is locally aggressive and frequently metastasizes to the lungs.

ewing's sarcoma.definition: A malignant bone tumor of children and adolescents in the Ewing sarcoma family, characterized by small round blue cells and the EWSR1-FLI1 fusion gene from a t(11;22) translocation; typically arising in the diaphysis of long bones and pelvis and treated with multimodal chemotherapy, surgery, and radiotherapy.

chondrosarcoma.definition: A malignant tumor that produces cartilage, arising from cartilaginous cells within bone or soft tissue; typically treated with wide surgical excision, as it generally responds poorly to chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

fibrosarcoma.definition: A malignant soft-tissue sarcoma arising from fibroblasts that produce collagen; composed of spindle-shaped cells often arranged in a herringbone pattern; may invade locally and metastasize (most commonly to the lungs); treated primarily by wide surgical excision with clear margins, with adjuvant radiotherapy or chemotherapy as indicated.

bone cancer.definition: A malignant tumor that originates in bone tissue. Primary bone malignancies arise from bone- or cartilage-forming cells (examples include osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, and Ewing sarcoma); many bone lesions are metastases from cancers arising elsewhere (such as breast, prostate, or lung cancer).

osteoblastic tumors.definition: A bone-forming tumor characterized by neoplastic osteoblasts that synthesize osteoid and new bone, producing sclerotic (dense) areas on radiographs.

tomography.definition: A technique for producing cross-sectional images of the body by reconstructing data from multiple projections to isolate a single plane, thereby suppressing information from surrounding planes.

radioisotopic scanning.definition: A nuclear medicine imaging technique that uses radiolabeled compounds containing a radioisotope administered to a patient; their emitted radiation is detected to create images showing the distribution and functional activity of an organ or tissue.

resection.definition: The surgical removal of a lesion or part or all of an organ or other body structure.

serum calcium.definition: The concentration of calcium ions in the blood serum; tightly regulated by parathyroid hormone, vitamin D, and calcitonin, and used to evaluate calcium metabolism and disorders of bone, parathyroid, and kidney function.

urinary calcium.definition: Calcium excreted in urine, reflecting renal handling of calcium and overall calcium metabolism; commonly measured as 24-hour urinary calcium excretion or a urinary calcium-to-creatinine ratio to evaluate hypercalciuria, kidney stone risk, or disorders of parathyroid or vitamin D metabolism.

epiphysis.definition: End portion of a long bone that participates in forming a joint surface; composed of cancellous bone and covered with articular cartilage. In children, it is separated from the shaft by the growth plate (physes); after maturation, the growth plate fuses and a bony line may remain.

diaphysis.definition: A long bone's shaft between the proximal and distal ends, a cylindrical region composed mainly of compact bone surrounding a medullary cavity that contains bone marrow (yellow marrow in adults).

proximal epiphysis.definition: The proximal end of a long bone—the end nearest the trunk—composed of cancellous bone and capped with articular cartilage, and in growing individuals containing the growth plate (epiphyseal plate).

distal epiphysis.definition: The end portion of a long bone farthest from the trunk that forms a joint surface with adjacent bones; it is separated from the shaft by the metaphysis and, in children, contains the epiphyseal (growth) plate.

epiphyseal disks.definition: A cartilaginous growth plate between the epiphysis and diaphysis of a long bone; it provides for longitudinal bone growth in children and gradually ossifies, disappearing after puberty to leave the epiphyseal line.

spongy bone.definition: Porous bone, also called trabecular bone, often found at the center of long bones.

compact bone.definition: Hard, tightly-packed tissue that forms the outer shell of bones. Also called cortical bone or lamellar bone.

red marrow.definition: Hematopoietic (blood-forming) tissue within certain bones that is rich in hematopoietic stem cells and a supporting vascular stroma, responsible for producing red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets; in adults, it is predominantly located in the axial skeleton and the proximal ends of long bones, with other marrow gradually converting to yellow (fatty) marrow.

yellow marrow.definition: A fatty tissue within the medullary (central) cavity of most adult bones, consisting mainly of adipocytes; it stores fat and can convert back to hematopoietic (red) marrow under certain conditions.

medullary cavity.definition: The hollow interior of a bone’s shaft that contains bone marrow and is lined by the endosteum; red marrow is present in children and yellow marrow in adults.

endosteum.definition: An inner bone membrane lining the internal surfaces of bone (including the medullary cavity), containing osteogenic cells, osteoblasts, and osteoclasts, and participating in bone growth, remodeling, and repair.

bone-anchored hearing aid.definition: A hearing device that transmits sound to the inner ear via bone conduction using a surgically implanted titanium fixture in the skull, to which an external sound processor is attached; by bypassing the outer and middle ear, it treats conductive or mixed hearing loss and sometimes single-sided deafness.

osseointegrated titanium fixture.definition: An implant component made of titanium that is surgically placed into bone (typically the jaw) and capable of forming a direct, functional bond with living bone (osseointegration), providing stable, long-term support for a dental prosthesis.

pediculus humanus corporis.definition: A hematophagous ectoparasite that infests human clothing and bites the skin to feed; causes pediculosis corporis and can transmit epidemic typhus (Rickettsia prowazekii), trench fever (Bartonella quintana), and relapsing fever (Borrelia recurrentis).

louse.definition: A tiny wingless parasitic insect that lives on the skin or hair of a host (most commonly humans) and feeds on blood or skin debris; in humans, lice infest the scalp (head louse), body (body louse), or pubic area (pubic louse).

lice.definition: A blood-sucking parasite known as Pediculus humanus capitis that can cause an itchy scalp; infestations are highly contagious and especially common in school-age children.

bromhidrosis.definition: An unpleasant body odor produced by the bacterial breakdown of sweat, especially from apocrine glands in the axillae or groin.

adduction.definition: Movement of a body part toward or across the midline.

extension.definition: Movement that increases the angle between two bones or parts of a joint, effectively straightening a limb from a flexed position; the opposite of flexion; when the angle exceeds the neutral range, it may be called hyperextension.

flexion.definition: A bending movement that decreases the angle between two adjacent body parts at a joint; e.g., bending the elbow or knee (opposite of extension).

rotation.definition: Rotation is a movement around a bone’s longitudinal axis that turns the part toward or away from the midline; internal (medial) rotation brings the part toward the midline, while external (lateral) rotation moves it away from the midline.
