telangiectasis.definition: Dilation of small superficial blood vessels (capillaries) near the surface of the skin or mucous membranes, producing visible red, thread-like markings.

hepatorenal_syndrome.definition: A functional renal failure occurring in advanced liver disease (typically cirrhosis) characterized by marked renal vasoconstriction and reduced glomerular filtration rate with little or no intrinsic kidney pathology, driven by decreased effective arterial blood volume from splanchnic vasodilation; often precipitated by infection or volume shifts and classified into type 1 (rapid) and type 2 (slower).

hepatic_encephalopathy.definition: A neuropsychiatric syndrome due to severe liver dysfunction or portosystemic shunting, causing accumulation of neurotoxins (notably ammonia) and presenting with altered mental status, cognitive/behavioral changes, sleep disturbances, and neuromuscular signs such as asterixis; management focuses on reducing ammonia production/absorption and treating precipitating factors.

peritoneovenous_shunt.definition: A surgical procedure in which ascitic fluid is diverted from the peritoneal cavity into the venous circulation via a subcutaneous shunt (e.g., Denver or LeVeen shunt) to treat refractory ascites.

gastric_lavage.definition: A procedure in which the stomach is washed out by inserting a tube (commonly a nasogastric tube) and flushing with fluid to remove or dilute its contents, often for decontamination in poisoning or to obtain gastric material for diagnostic analysis.

variceal_sclerosis.definition: A procedure in which sclerosant agents are injected into esophageal or gastric varices to induce inflammation and thrombosis, causing fibrosis and obliteration of the variceal lumen to prevent bleeding in portal hypertension.

esophageal_balloon.definition: An inflatable balloon catheter inserted into the esophagus to occlude the lumen and apply pressure to a bleeding site, typically used for tamponade therapy in upper GI hemorrhage (most notably variceal bleeding) as part of a tamponade tube.

renal_failure.definition: A condition in which the kidneys fail to adequately filter waste products from the blood, leading to buildup of toxins, fluid overload, and electrolyte and acid-base imbalances. It can be acute (sudden onset, potentially reversible) or chronic (progressive kidney damage that may lead to end-stage renal disease requiring dialysis or transplantation).

esophageal_varices.definition: Dilated submucosal veins in the distal esophagus that arise from portal hypertension (most often due to cirrhosis) and carry a high risk of life-threatening upper gastrointestinal bleeding if they rupture.

circle_of_willis.definition: A circle of arteries at the base of the brain, connecting major brain arteries and supplying blood to all parts of the brain.

anterior_cerebral_artery.definition: A paired artery arising from the internal carotid artery that supplies the medial aspects of the frontal and parietal lobes (including the leg area of the motor and sensory cortices) and surrounding structures; connected to its counterpart via the anterior communicating artery within the circle of Willis.

posterior_communicating_artery.definition: A cerebral artery arising from the internal carotid artery and coursing posteriorly to join the posterior cerebral artery, forming part of the circle of Willis and providing collateral circulation between the anterior and posterior cerebral circulations; aneurysms at its origin can cause subarachnoid hemorrhage and oculomotor nerve palsy.

anterior_communicating_artery.definition: A small vessel that connects the left and right anterior cerebral arteries across the midline, forming part of the circle of Willis; a common site of berry aneurysms.

middle_cerebral_artery.definition: A major cerebral artery, a terminal branch of the internal carotid, that supplies the lateral surface of the cerebral hemispheres (frontal, temporal, and parietal lobes) and deep structures via perforating branches; occlusion commonly causes contralateral motor and sensory deficits and aphasia when the dominant hemisphere is involved.

basilar_artery.definition: The artery that supplies blood to the cerebellum, the brainstem, and the back of the brain.

vertebral_artery.definition: One of two blood vessels that run up the back of the neck and join at the base of the skull to form the basilar artery. The vertebral arteries carry blood from the heart to the brain.

internal_carotid_artery.definition: A major artery arising from the common carotid artery that ascends into the skull via the carotid canal to supply the brain, giving rise to branches such as the ophthalmic artery and the anterior and middle cerebral arteries, forming part of the cerebral circulation.

cardiac_catheterization.definition: A procedure to diagnose or treat heart problems; a long, thin, flexible tube is inserted into a blood vessel in the arm, neck, or upper thigh and maneuvered into the heart to evaluate various heart functions.

myocardial_infarction.definition: Occurs when the flow of blood to the heart is stopped by a blood clot or a spasm of an artery. Also called a heart attack or MI.

circulation.definition: The flow of blood through the body.

circulatory.definition: Relating to the circulation of blood through the body, including the heart, arteries, veins, and capillaries.

radioisotope.definition: An unstable isotope of an element that emits radiation and is used in medicine to diagnose and treat disease. Also called radionuclide.

saccharin.definition: A synthetic, non-nutritive artificial sweetener used to sweeten foods and beverages; it is about 300–400 times sweeter than sucrose and provides no calories because it is not metabolized by the human body and is excreted unchanged.

cirsoid aneurysm.definition: A cirsoid aneurysm is a high-flow arteriovenous fistula characterized by multiple dilated, tortuous feeding arteries and draining veins that form a serpiginous vascular network; it commonly involves the scalp or skull and presents as a pulsatile mass with a bruit, with potential for hemorrhage or heart strain from shunting.

racemose aneurysm.definition: A vascular lesion in which multiple small dilated arteries form a grape-like, ramifying network—an arteriovenous malformation—rather than a single saccular aneurysm.

transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic.definition: A radiologically guided procedure that creates a channel within the liver connecting a branch of the portal vein to a hepatic vein, using a stent inserted via the jugular vein to divert blood flow and reduce portal hypertension, thereby decreasing risk of variceal bleeding and helping manage refractory ascites.

lactulose.definition: A synthetic disaccharide osmotic laxative that is not absorbed in the small intestine; it is fermented by colonic bacteria to organic acids, which draw water into the colon and lower colonic pH, converting ammonia to ammonium and reducing blood ammonia levels; used to treat constipation and hepatic encephalopathy.

bacterial flora.definition: The community of bacteria that normally inhabit a particular environment (most notably the human body), forming the microbiota; these organisms participate in digestion and metabolism, contribute to immune development and regulation, and help protect against pathogenic infections.

esophageal bleeding.definition: Bleeding from the esophagus, most commonly due to esophageal variceal hemorrhage in portal hypertension or mucosal lesions such as ulcers, esophagitis, erosions, or Mallory‑Weiss tears; presents with hematemesis (vomiting blood) and/or melena and may cause anemia or shock; diagnosed by endoscopy and treated with resuscitation, endoscopic hemostasis, and management of the underlying cause.

bloody stools.definition: Passage of visible blood with stool, usually bright red, indicating lower gastrointestinal bleeding; common causes include anorectal sources (such as hemorrhoids or anal fissures) and conditions like diverticulosis, inflammatory bowel disease, angiodysplasia, or colorectal cancer.

alcohol cirrhosis.definition: A form of liver cirrhosis due to chronic heavy alcohol use, in which long-term injury leads to fibrosis and nodular regeneration, impaired liver function, and complications such as portal hypertension, ascites, jaundice, and hepatic encephalopathy.

liver transplantation.definition: An operation in which a diseased liver is removed and replaced with a healthy liver from a living or deceased donor. It is performed for end-stage liver disease or acute liver failure, requires lifelong immunosuppression to prevent rejection, and carries risks such as graft failure, infection, bleeding, biliary complications, and vascular complications.

cisatracurium.definition: A nondepolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent of the benzylisoquinolinium class used to produce skeletal muscle relaxation during anesthesia; it is the stereoisomer of atracurium that undergoes Hofmann elimination and ester hydrolysis, providing organ-independent clearance with an intermediate duration of action.

claforan.definition: A third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic (cefotaxime) used to treat moderate to severe bacterial infections; inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin‑binding proteins; active against many Gram-negative bacteria and some Gram-positive bacteria; administered by injection.

hodgkin's lymphoma.definition: Malignant lymphoma arising from B lymphocytes, defined by the presence of Reed-Sternberg cells in affected lymph nodes; typically presents with painless lymphadenopathy (often in the neck or mediastinum) and may be accompanied by fever, night sweats, and weight loss (B symptoms).

testicular tumors.definition: Neoplasms of the testis; most are germ cell tumors (seminomas and non-seminomatous tumors) that may be malignant; typically present as a painless unilateral testicular mass; diagnosed with scrotal ultrasound and serum tumor markers; treated with inguinal orchiectomy with adjuvant therapy based on histology and stage.

prostatic tumors.definition: A neoplasm arising from the prostate gland; the most common malignant form is prostate adenocarcinoma, often presenting with elevated PSA and/or urinary symptoms and potentially metastasizing to bone; diagnosis is by histologic confirmation on biopsy.

ovarian tumors.definition: A neoplasm arising from ovarian tissue, ranging from benign cystic lesions to malignant cancers; commonly presents as a pelvic or adnexal mass with possible pain or fullness. Evaluation typically involves pelvic ultrasound and tumor markers, with management depending on histology and stage (surveillance for benign lesions; surgical removal with staging and possible oncologic therapy for malignant disease).

citanest hydrochloride.definition: The hydrochloride salt form of prilocaine, an amide-type local anesthetic used for infiltration and nerve block anesthesia in dentistry and minor surgical procedures.

prilocaine hydrochloride.definition: A salt form of prilocaine, an amide-type local anesthetic, used to produce local or regional anesthesia by blocking voltage-gated sodium channels in nerve membranes; commonly administered by infiltration or nerve block and often formulated with epinephrine to prolong duration.

citicoline.definition: A medication/supplement that provides CDP-choline (citicoline), a precursor to phosphatidylcholine used in brain membrane repair and metabolism; used to support cognitive function and recovery after stroke in some countries.

cisternal puncture.definition: A procedure to obtain cerebrospinal fluid by puncturing the cisterna magna (the cerebellomedullary cistern) via a suboccipital approach; historically used for CSF sampling but now largely abandoned due to risks such as brainstem injury, hemorrhage, and herniation, with lumbar puncture usually preferred.

cisterna chyli.definition: A dilated, sac-like portion at the lower end of the thoracic duct that collects lymph from the lower limbs and abdominal viscera via the lumbar and intestinal trunks, before the lymph ascends the thoracic duct.

cisterna subarachnoidea.definition: A widened region of the subarachnoid space where cerebrospinal fluid pools around the brain (and spinal cord), serving as a reservoir and conduit for CSF circulation.

krebs cycle.definition: A sequence of mitochondrial enzymatic reactions that oxidizes acetyl‑CoA to CO2, producing NADH and FADH2 for the electron transport chain, yielding a small amount of ATP, and regenerating oxaloacetate.

citrated plasma.definition: Plasma in which citrate anticoagulant (commonly sodium citrate) has been added to chelate calcium and prevent coagulation, used for coagulation testing and in transfusion medicine.

folinic acid.definition: A reduced, active form of folate (5-formyltetrahydrofolic acid), also known as leucovorin; it bypasses the dihydrofolate reductase step to replenish tetrahydrofolate pools and is used to treat folate deficiency and to mitigate methotrexate toxicity (and to enhance certain chemotherapies).

citrulline.definition: A non-proteinogenic amino acid that serves as an intermediate in the urea cycle; formed from ornithine and carbamoyl phosphate in the mitochondria and, after transport to the cytosol, combines with aspartate to form argininosuccinate (ultimately yielding arginine and fumarate); not incorporated into proteins and sometimes used as a dietary supplement to raise arginine/nitric oxide levels.

citrullinemia.definition: An inherited disorder of the urea cycle due to deficiency of an enzyme (most commonly argininosuccinate synthetase, ASS1) that impairs ammonia detoxification, causing elevated citrulline and hyperammonemia with symptoms such as poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy, and seizures in newborns.

ornithine.definition: A non-proteinogenic amino acid that functions as an intermediate in the urea cycle; it is produced from arginine by arginase and then combines with carbamoyl phosphate to form citrulline, helping dispose of excess nitrogen as urea.

argininosuccinic acid synthetase.definition: An enzyme of the urea cycle that catalyzes the ATP-dependent condensation of citrulline and aspartate to form argininosuccinate; deficiency causes citrullinemia type I.

thromphlebitis.definition: Inflammation of a vein with the formation of a thrombus (blood clot) within the vein, most often affecting superficial leg veins.

urine retention.definition: An inability to empty the bladder completely, leading to retention of urine; it can be acute (emergency) or chronic and is often due to bladder outlet obstruction, detrusor muscle dysfunction, or neurologic impairment.

aortoclasia.definition: A historical surgical procedure involving deliberate fracture (clasia) of the aorta to treat certain aortic conditions; now largely obsolete.

osteoclasia.definition: The surgical deliberate fracture of a bone to correct a deformity or malalignment, after which the bone is realigned and immobilized.

colloidoclasia.definition: Destruction or fragmentation of colloid material, typically referring to breaking down the colloid within thyroid follicles in the treatment of colloid goiters.

clasmatocyte.definition: Not a standard medical term; likely a misspelling of plasmatocyte (plasma cell), a differentiated B lymphocyte that secretes antibodies.

clasmatodendrosis.definition: A histopathologic change in astrocytes characterized by swelling and fragmentation (beading) of their processes, with disruption of normal astrocytic architecture, typically seen after ischemic or hypoxic brain injury.

clasmatosis.definition: An obsolete or rarely used histopathologic term describing fragmentation or dissolution of cells/tissue, typically related to mechanical injury or degenerative processes; not part of current standard medical vocabulary.

clasp.definition: A device or part used to fasten, grasp, or retain tissue, tooth, or a prosthesis; in dentistry, the metal clasp encircles a tooth to provide retention for a removable partial denture.

clasp-knife.definition: A phenomenon in neurological examination where passive stretching of a spastic muscle meets initial high resistance that suddenly yields, producing a brief “give way”—a sign of upper motor neuron–type spasticity.

claustrum.definition: A slender subcortical sheet of gray matter between the insular cortex and putamen with widespread connections to the cortex; thought to coordinate cortical activity, with a possible role in consciousness, though its exact function is not fully understood.

claustrophobia.definition: An anxiety disorder characterized by an intense, irrational fear of enclosed or confined spaces, leading to avoidance and panic in situations such as elevators, small rooms, or crowded areas.

cesarean-section.definition: A surgical delivery in which the baby is delivered through an incision in the mother's abdomen and uterus, typically performed when vaginal birth is unsafe or not possible.

computed-tomography.definition: A special type of imaging that creates three-dimensional X-rays. Also called CT scans or CAT scans (computed axial tomography).

epidemic-typhus.definition: An acute febrile infectious disease caused by the bacterium Rickettsia prowazekii and transmitted by the human body louse; it presents with sudden high fever, severe headache, myalgias, and a maculopapular rash that typically starts on the trunk and may spread to the limbs. Untreated, it can be severe or fatal.

visceral-leishmaniasis.definition: A systemic parasitic disease caused by Leishmania donovani complex, transmitted by sandflies; it predominantly affects the reticuloendothelial system (spleen, liver, bone marrow) and presents with fever, weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and hypergammaglobulinemia, potentially fatal if untreated.

leishmania-donovani.definition: A protozoan parasite that causes visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) in humans; transmitted by female phlebotomine sandflies; it infects macrophages of the reticuloendothelial system, existing as intracellular amastigotes in humans and flagellated promastigotes in the sandfly vector.

phlebotomus-argentipes.definition: A species of Old World phlebotomine sandfly that transmits Leishmania donovani, the parasite responsible for visceral leishmaniasis in parts of South Asia.

angioclast.definition: A cell that resorbs or destroys blood vessels; its activity is involved in vascular remodeling or regression of vessels.

cranioclast.definition: An obstetric instrument historically used to crush the fetal skull to facilitate vaginal delivery in obstructed labor; its use is largely obsolete and replaced by safer methods.

myeloclast.definition: Historically, a marrow-resorbing cell; a clastic cell in the bone marrow that resorbs hematopoietic tissue or bone, analogous to an osteoclast. The term is rarely used in modern practice.

hemoclast.definition: A rarely used term for an agent or process that destroys blood cells (i.e., causes hemolysis); not a standard term in modern medical dictionaries.

clear-cell-carcinoma.definition: An epithelial malignancy whose tumor cells have clear, empty-looking cytoplasm on routine histology, typically due to glycogen or lipid content; most commonly describes clear cell renal cell carcinoma but can arise in other organs such as the ovary and endometrium.

renal-cell-carcinoma.definition: A malignant tumor arising from the renal cortex, most commonly from proximal tubular epithelial cells; it is the most common type of adult kidney cancer and can invade the renal vasculature and metastasize, with presentations such as hematuria, flank pain, or an abdominal mass, and management ranging from nephrectomy to targeted/systemic therapies depending on stage.

clear-cell-renal-cell-carcinoma.definition: Malignant kidney tumor originating from proximal renal tubular epithelium; the most common subtype of renal cell carcinoma. Histology shows cells with clear cytoplasm due to lipid and glycogen content, often associated with inactivation of the VHL gene on chromosome 3p.

deltopectoral-triangle.definition: A small triangular region on the anterior shoulder bounded medially by the edge of the pectoralis major, laterally by the edge of the deltoid, and superiorly by the clavicle; the cephalic vein ascends through this area to drain into the axillary vein, and it contains accompanying vessels and lymph nodes.

cephalic-vein.definition: A superficial vein of the upper limb that drains the lateral aspect of the hand and forearm, ascends along the arm, and drains into the axillary vein (typically via the deltopectoral triangle).

clavipectoral-fascia.definition: A layer of deep fascia in the shoulder region that envelops the subclavius and pectoralis minor, extending from the clavicle to the coracoid process; it forms the costocoracoid membrane and contributes to the suspensory ligament of the axilla.

pyramidal-tract.definition: A motor pathway of the central nervous system (the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts) that originates in the motor cortex and descends to synapse on spinal and brainstem motor neurons to mediate voluntary, skilled movements; most fibers decussate in the medullary pyramids.

clawfoot.definition: A foot deformity with claw-like toe posture; the toes are flexed at the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints and often hyperextended at the metatarsophalangeal joints, and it is frequently associated with a high-arched foot (pes cavus) or neurologic/ muscular conditions.

clawhand.definition: A hand deformity characterized by hyperextension of the metacarpophalangeal joints and flexion of the interphalangeal joints (especially in the ring and little fingers) due to paralysis or imbalance of intrinsic hand muscles, most commonly from ulnar nerve palsy.

main-en-griffe.definition: Claw hand deformity due to ulnar nerve palsy, in which the metacarpophalangeal joints of the ring and little fingers are hyperextended while the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints are flexed, from paralysis of the intrinsic hand muscles (interossei and the medial two lumbricals).

claw-type-traction-frame.definition: A device used in orthopedic traction consisting of an external frame with claw-like clamps that grip skeletal pins or tines to transmit controlled traction forces to an injured limb, enabling gradual realignment and immobilization of fractures or dislocations. It is an external skeletal traction system that allows multi-directional adjustment and is typically used before definitive fixation or in nonoperative fracture management.

clean-catch-specimen.definition: A urine sample collected after cleansing the external genitalia and obtaining urine midstream to minimize contamination from urethral or skin flora; used for urinalysis and culture.

cleansing-enema.definition: A procedure in which a liquid solution is introduced into the rectum to evacuate stool and cleanse the colon, typically to prepare for diagnostic procedures or surgery or to relieve constipation; solutions include warm water, saline, or commercially prepared cleansing formulations.

clearance.definition: In pharmacology, the volume of plasma from which a drug or substance is completely removed per unit time (commonly expressed as mL/min or L/h); it equals the rate of elimination divided by the plasma concentration and reflects combined renal and hepatic elimination.

clear-liquid-diet.definition: An eating plan consisting of clear liquids only (e.g., water, broth, clear fruit juices without pulp, tea/coffee without milk, gelatin, and certain electrolyte beverages) that leave no residue in the GI tract; used before GI procedures, after surgery, or during GI illness to rest the bowel.

cleavage.definition: 1) The rapid series of mitotic divisions of a zygote after fertilization that increases cell number without overall growth, forming a multicellular embryo (blastula). 2) The cytokinetic process in animal cells where a contractile actin-myosin ring creates a cleavage furrow that pinches the membrane inward to divide the cell into two daughter cells.

cleavage-plane.definition: The plane along which a cell divides during embryonic cleavage (the orientation of cytokinesis); in surgical anatomy, a natural plane of separation between tissue layers along which dissection occurs.

cleavage-fracture.definition: A brittle fracture in which the crack propagates along a cleavage plane (a plane of weakness in the material), producing a flat, faceted fracture surface.

cleavage-lines.definition: Lines of natural skin tension in the dermis corresponding to the orientation of collagen fibers; incisions made parallel to these lines tend to heal with less scarring (also known as Langer lines).

cleft lip.definition: A congenital deformity in which there is a gap or split in the upper lip caused by incomplete fusion of the maxillary and medial nasal processes during early embryonic development; it may be unilateral or bilateral and can occur with or without a cleft palate.

harelip.definition: A congenital malformation in which the upper lip does not fuse properly, producing a split or gap in the lip that may be unilateral or bilateral and can involve the nose; commonly referred to as a cleft lip.

cleft jaw.definition: A congenital defect characterized by a fissure or gap in the lip and/or palate resulting from incomplete fusion of facial processes during embryonic development; ranges from isolated cleft lip to cleft palate or both, and may require surgical repair.

cleft foot.definition: A congenital deformity with a midline cleft of the foot due to missing or underdeveloped central foot rays, producing a lobster-claw appearance; commonly part of ectrodactyly (split-hand/split-foot malformation) and may be associated with syndactyly or other anomalies.

cleft hand.definition: A congenital malformation in which the central digits of the hand are absent or underdeveloped, creating a midline cleft (lobster-claw deformity) often with syndactyly of the remaining fingers.

pes cavus.definition: An excessively high, often rigid, longitudinal arch of the foot (high-arched foot) with hindfoot varus and forefoot supination, often accompanied by clawed toes and calluses; frequently associated with neuromuscular or congenital disorders.

talipes cavus.definition: A foot deformity with an excessively high, rigid arch (pes cavus), often with plantarflexed forefoot and clawed toes, leading to abnormal weight bearing and commonly associated with neuromuscular disorders.

deltoid.definition: The muscle in your upper arm.

paranasal-sinuses.definition: Air-filled cavities within the bones surrounding the nasal cavity that communicate with the nasal mucosa; major examples are the maxillary, frontal, ethmoid, and sphenoid sinuses.

supernumerary teeth.definition: An extra tooth or teeth that develop in addition to the normal dentition; these may be erupted or unerupted, and can be supplemental (tooth-like in appearance) or rudimentary (conical or tuberculate), most commonly occurring in the maxillary anterior region (mesiodens) and potentially causing crowding, diastema, eruption delay, or displacement of adjacent teeth.

unerupted teeth.definition: A tooth that has not erupted into the mouth by the expected time, often remaining embedded in the jawbone or covered by gum tissue (potentially referred to as an impacted or unerupted tooth).

dental amalgam.definition: A filling material formed by combining a powdered alloy (primarily silver, tin, and copper) with liquid mercury; after mixing, it hardens into a durable restoration used chiefly in posterior teeth.

cleidocranial dysostosis.definition: An autosomal dominant congenital skeletal dysplasia due to RUNX2 mutations, characterized by hypoplastic or absent clavicles, delayed closure of cranial sutures and fontanelles, facial/craniofacial abnormalities (often midface hypoplasia), and dental anomalies such as supernumerary teeth and delayed eruption.

cleidocranial dysplasia.definition: A rare autosomal dominant skeletal dysplasia caused by mutations in the RUNX2 (CBFA1) gene, characterized by hypoplastic or aplastic clavicles, delayed closure of cranial fontanelles and sutures, midface hypoplasia, and dental anomalies including supernumerary and impacted teeth.

dysostosis.definition: A congenital defect in bone development due to abnormal formation or segmentation of skeletal elements, resulting in an abnormal number, shape, or position of bones.

cranial sutures.definition: Fibrous joints between the flat bones of the skull (calvaria) that allow skull growth during infancy and childhood; composed of dense connective tissue, they progressively ossify and become immovable (synarthroses) with age.

nasal cavities.definition: Two air-filled cavities within the skull behind the nostrils, separated by the nasal septum and lined with a mucous membrane; they condition (warm, humidify, and filter) inhaled air, contain the olfactory epithelium in their superior parts, and contribute to voice resonance.

median nasal process.definition: A midline embryologic prominence of the frontonasal region that, formed by the fusion of the two medial nasal processes, gives rise to the intermaxillary segment—the philtrum of the upper lip, the premaxilla with the maxillary incisors, and the anterior (primary) palate.

maxillary process.definition: An embryologic prominence of the first pharyngeal (branchial) arch that forms the upper jaw (maxilla) and adjacent midface structures; in adult anatomy, a maxillary process is any bony projection that articulates with the maxilla (for example, the maxillary process of the zygomatic bone or palatine bone).

embryology.definition: The branch of biology that studies the development of the embryo from fertilization to the fetal stage, including fertilization, cleavage, gastrulation, organogenesis, and fetal growth.

embryonic development.definition: Embryonic development is the series of developmental processes that transform a fertilized egg into a multicellular embryo, including cleavage, gastrulation with germ layer formation, differentiation, and organogenesis (morphogenesis of tissues and organs).

craniofacial malformations.definition: A group of congenital abnormalities of the skull and facial bones and soft tissues that arise from abnormal embryologic development, producing abnormal craniofacial morphology and potential functional impairments.

centric occlusion.definition: The occlusion of the maxillary and mandibular teeth when the mandible is in centric relation and the teeth are in maximum intercuspation.

click-murmur syndrome.definition: A clinical manifestation of mitral valve prolapse (myxomatous degeneration of the mitral valve leaflets) presenting with a midsystolic click followed by a late systolic murmur best heard at the apex; the click and murmur change with maneuvers (standing/Valsalva: earlier click, louder murmur; squatting: later click, softer murmur).

clergyman's sore throat.definition: An historical term for sore throat in clergy, essentially occupational laryngitis or pharyngitis from prolonged vocal use; not a distinct modern diagnosis.

dysphonia.definition: An abnormal voice quality resulting from pathology of the vocal cords or larynx, typically presenting as hoarseness, breathiness, roughness, or decreased vocal strength.

bladder-neck destruction.definition: Destruction or ablation of the tissue at the bladder neck (the junction of the bladder and urethra) to relieve bladder outlet obstruction; typically achieved by energy-based methods (electrocautery, laser, etc.) and may affect continence.

clemastine.definition: A first-generation H1 antihistamine used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, conjunctivitis, and urticaria; it antagonizes histamine at H1 receptors and crosses the blood–brain barrier, causing sedation and anticholinergic effects (e.g., dry mouth, blurred vision).

monoamine oxidase inhibitors.definition: Medications used to treat depression. They work by making the chemical messengers serotonin and norepinephrine more available.

cleocin.definition: A lincosamide antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit; used to treat a range of infections caused by susceptible anaerobic bacteria and certain Gram-positive cocci; available in oral, topical, and injectable forms.

tent device.definition: A device designed to create and hold open a tent-like space beneath tissue or bone to preserve room for healing or graft material, often by supporting overlying tissue and preventing collapse.

croupette.definition: A rare or obsolete term for a mild form of croup (laryngotracheobronchitis) in children, characterized by inflammation of the larynx and trachea with a barking cough and sometimes inspiratory stridor; usually self-limited.

elbow restraints.definition: An immobilization device applied to the arm to restrict elbow movement (flexion and/or extension), typically padded and secured with straps around the upper arm and forearm; used to prevent self-injury or interference with medical devices and to keep the limb in a prescribed position.

parenteral fluids.definition: Fluids delivered by injection or infusion that bypass the gastrointestinal tract (eg, intravenous or subcutaneous fluids) to restore hydration and electrolyte balance or to deliver medications.

velopharyngeal insufficiency.definition: An inadequate closure of the velopharyngeal mechanism (soft palate against the posterior pharyngeal wall) during speech, producing hypernasal resonance and nasal air emission; typically due to structural factors such as cleft palate, submucous cleft, or postoperative tissue deficiency.

hypernasality.definition: Excessive nasal resonance in speech due to incomplete closure of the velopharyngeal mechanism, causing air to escape through the nose during articulation of oral sounds.

speech impairment.definition: A broad term for disorders affecting the production of spoken language, resulting in unclear articulation, abnormal speech-sound patterns, fluency problems (e.g., stuttering), or impaired motor control of the speech muscles (as in dysarthria or apraxia of speech).

hearing loss.definition: Hearing loss is a partial or total reduction in the ability to hear sounds, due to problems in the outer or middle ear (conductive loss) or inner ear or auditory nerve (sensorineural loss), and may be temporary or permanent.

speech therapy.definition: A clinical service provided by speech-language pathologists to evaluate and treat communication and swallowing disorders, including difficulties with articulation, language, fluency, voice, cognitive-communication skills, and swallowing safety.

hearing therapy.definition: A set of interventions designed to improve hearing and communication in people with hearing loss. It typically includes auditory training to improve speech perception, counseling, and the fitting and use of amplification devices (hearing aids, cochlear implants) and other assistive listening strategies.

oral and maxillofacial surgeon.definition: A dental specialist trained to diagnose and surgically treat diseases, injuries, and defects of the mouth, jaws, face, and neck. Procedures include tooth extractions (including wisdom teeth), dental implants, orthognathic (jaw) surgery, facial trauma reconstruction, cleft lip/palate repair, and management of temporomandibular joint disorders; training typically follows dental school plus an accredited oral and maxillofacial surgery residency, with the option to provide anesthesia.

plastic surgeon.definition: A licensed physician trained in plastic and reconstructive surgery who performs procedures to restore, reconstruct, or alter the form and function of body tissues, including treatment of congenital defects, trauma, burns, and elective cosmetic surgeries.

orthodontist.definition: A dentist who treats problems with spacing of your teeth or jaws.

dentist.definition: A doctor who treats diseases in your teeth and gums.

ventilatory support.definition: A range of medical interventions that support or replace spontaneous breathing by delivering oxygen-rich air and removing carbon dioxide, including noninvasive methods such as CPAP or BiPAP and invasive mechanical ventilation via endotracheal or tracheostomy tubes.

suture.definition: The process of sewing tissues together after surgery; or the stitch itself.

operation.definition: A surgical procedure; an invasive intervention performed to diagnose, treat, or repair a medical condition.

repair.definition: The process of mending damaged tissue or structures to restore continuity and function, either by surgical reapproximation of tissue edges or by natural wound healing with scar formation.

surgical correction.definition: A surgical procedure aimed at restoring normal anatomy or function by correcting a deformity, defect, or abnormality.

dystocia.definition: Abnormally slow or arrested labor resulting from problems with the fetus (e.g., large fetal size or malpresentation), the birth canal (pelvic contraction or abnormal shape), or uterine contractions (inadequate or uncoordinated powers).

andropause.definition: An age-related decline in testosterone production in men, often referred to as late-onset hypogonadism, accompanied by symptoms such as reduced libido, fatigue, decreased muscle mass and strength, increased abdominal fat, mood changes, and erectile dysfunction, usually with low morning serum testosterone.

lincomycin.definition: An antibiotic of the lincosamide class that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit; primarily active against Gram-positive bacteria and anaerobes; typically bacteriostatic (can be bactericidal for some organisms) and used for certain infections when penicillin is inappropriate; associated with gastrointestinal toxicity, including pseudomembranous colitis.

blood test.definition: A laboratory analysis of a blood sample to measure cells, chemicals, enzymes, and other components in order to diagnose disease, monitor medical conditions, assess organ function, or screen for abnormalities.

clinitest.definition: A chemical screening test on urine to detect reducing substances (reducing sugars) using a copper-reduction reaction; it produces a color change from blue to green/yellow/orange/brick red proportional to the amount of reducing substances.

gingival crevice.definition: The natural shallow space between the tooth and the gingival margin (the gingival sulcus), usually 0–3 mm in depth in health, lined by sulcular epithelium and containing gingival crevicular fluid; it may deepen into a periodontal pocket with periodontal disease.

crown/root ratio.definition: A measurement of the proportion of the visible crown height to the root length of a tooth, usually assessed radiographically; a favorable ratio is about 1:2 or better (root length at least twice the crown height), whereas a higher ratio suggests reduced retention and a poorer prognosis for restorations or post placement.

clinodactyly.definition: Fixed inward curved deviation of a finger (usually the little finger) toward the adjacent finger in the plane of the hand, typically due to a wedge-shaped middle phalanx (delta phalanx) or other developmental bone deformity; often congenital and may be associated with other skeletal or genetic conditions.

clinocephaly.definition: A nonstandard or historical term referring to an abnormal inclination or tilt of the skull (cranial vault); not a widely recognized or precise diagnosis in modern medical terminology.

clinocephalism.definition: An obscure, historical term referring to a skull shape abnormality in which the cranial vault is inclined or sloped; not widely used in modern medical terminology.

clinocephalic.definition: Relating to a skull shape with a high, vaulted cranial vault; an anthropometric term describing a head form that is relatively tall.

clinocephalous.definition: Having a sloping or oblique cranial shape; a skull in which the cranial vault is tilted rather than upright.

clinodactylism.definition: An inherited or congenital curvature of a finger (usually the little finger) toward the adjacent digit caused by an angular deformity of the middle phalanx (delta phalanx); it may be isolated or associated with syndromes and can affect finger alignment or grip in severe cases.

clinodactylic.definition: Pertaining to clinodactyly; an abnormal sideways curvature of a finger, most commonly the little finger, in the plane of the palm, usually due to congenital phalangeal abnormality.

clinodactylous.definition: A congenital curvature or angulation of a finger (most often the little finger) toward the adjacent finger, caused by abnormal development of the middle phalanx (often a delta phalanx) or other phalangeal deformity.

clinoid processes.definition: Bony projections of the sphenoid bone (the anterior and posterior clinoid processes) that form the margins of the sella turcica and optic canal and serve as attachment sites for the tentorium cerebelli and diaphragma sellae.

clinometer.definition: A device for measuring tilt angles; in medical settings, used to assess range of motion in joints or spinal alignment/posture.

clinoscope.definition: A specialized endoscopic instrument used to visualize the anterior clinoid process of the sphenoid bone, typically employed in skull-base neurosurgery to aid exposure and assessment of the optic nerve and internal carotid artery.

sulindac.definition: A nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) of the propionic acid class; a prodrug converted to an active metabolite that inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2) to reduce prostaglandin synthesis and relieve pain and inflammation, used for conditions such as osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.

clinoril.definition: A brand name for sulindac, a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to treat pain and inflammation in conditions such as osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis; it inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes, reducing prostaglandin synthesis.

clitoridectomy.definition: Excision of the clitoris or clitoral tissue; a surgical removal of all or part of the clitoris, historically practiced in some cultures as part of female genital mutilation.

labia.definition: The folds of skin and mucous membrane that surround and protect the openings of the vagina and urethra; comprising the outer labia majora and the inner labia minora.

labia minora.definition: Two slender, hairless folds of skin and mucosa that form the inner lips of the female external genitalia (vulva), enclosing the vaginal and urethral openings in the vestibule, extending from the clitoral area anteriorly to merge posteriorly (forming the fourchette), and varying in size, color, and shape among individuals.

labia commissure.definition: The junction where the labia minora meet, forming the anterior and posterior labial commissures at the openings of the vulva.

clitoritis.definition: Inflammation of the clitoris, often due to infection, irritation, or dermatologic conditions, presenting with redness, swelling, itching, or pain.

clivus.definition: A sloping portion of the skull base formed by the basioccipital and basilar part of the sphenoid, extending from the dorsum sellae to the foramen magnum; it forms part of the posterior cranial fossa and supports the brainstem.

cloaca.definition: A single posterior chamber through which the digestive, urinary, and reproductive tracts open in many animals; in humans, it denotes an embryologic structure that later divides to form separate anorectal and urogenital outlets.

cloacal fold.definition: Two bilateral folds of surface ectoderm surrounding the cloacal membrane in the developing embryo; they participate in perineal formation and contribute to partitioning the cloaca into the ventral urogenital sinus and the dorsal anorectal canal.

cloacal membrane.definition: A transient embryologic structure composed of surface ectoderm and endoderm without intervening mesoderm that covers the cloaca at the caudal end of the embryo; it ruptures to establish the external openings of the anorectal and urogenital tracts as the cloaca is subdivided by the urorectal septum.

cloacal septum.definition: An embryologic mesodermal partition that divides the primitive cloaca into a ventral urogenital sinus and a dorsal anorectal canal during development, and eventually fuses with the cloacal membrane.

cloacal sphincter.definition: A circular muscle surrounding the cloacal opening that constricts to regulate the passage of feces, urine, and reproductive secretions through the cloaca; present in animals with a cloaca (e.g., birds, reptiles, amphibians, some mammals). In humans, the cloaca is an embryologic structure that subdivides during development, so there is no distinct adult cloacal sphincter.

clobetasol propionate.definition: A super-potent topical corticosteroid used to treat severe inflammatory skin conditions (e.g., plaque psoriasis, eczema, dermatitis); applied as cream, ointment, gel, or solution and typically for short-term use due to risk of skin thinning and systemic absorption.

clobetasol.definition: An extremely potent topical corticosteroid used to treat inflammatory and pruritic skin conditions (e.g., plaque psoriasis, atopic dermatitis) in creams, ointments, or gels; prolonged use can cause skin thinning, striae, telangiectasia, and may suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, so it is generally used for short durations under medical supervision.

clocortolone pivalate.definition: A mid-strength topical corticosteroid; the pivalate ester of clocortolone used on the skin to reduce inflammation, itching, and redness in inflammatory dermatoses.

clocortolone.definition: A synthetic topical corticosteroid used to treat inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema and dermatitis; it reduces swelling, redness, and itching by activating glucocorticoid receptors and suppressing inflammatory mediators.

pivalate.definition: A salt or ester of pivalic acid (2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid).

clonidine hydrochloride.definition: A central alpha-2 adrenergic agonist antihypertensive agent that reduces sympathetic outflow from the brain to lower blood pressure; the hydrochloride salt is a common formulation; it is also used off-label for ADHD and to manage withdrawal symptoms in some regimens.

clomiphene.definition: Selective estrogen receptor modulator used to induce ovulation in women with anovulatory infertility (e.g., PCOS). It antagonizes estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus, reducing negative feedback and increasing GnRH, FSH, and LH release to stimulate ovulation; it can have antiestrogenic effects on the endometrium and cervical mucus and carries risks such as multiple pregnancy and ovarian hyperstimulation.

clomiphene citrate.definition: An oral selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) used to induce ovulation in women with anovulatory infertility (often PCOS). It works by blocking estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus, reducing negative feedback and increasing GnRH secretion, leading to increased FSH and LH and ovulation.

clomid.definition: A brand-name infertility drug (clomiphene citrate) used to induce ovulation in women with anovulatory infertility; it is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that antagonizes estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus, reducing negative feedback and increasing the release of FSH and LH to stimulate ovulation.

clomipramine.definition: A tricyclic antidepressant that predominantly inhibits serotonin reuptake (with some norepinephrine reuptake blockade); used mainly for obsessive-compulsive disorder and depressive disorders; commonly causes anticholinergic and sedative side effects.

oligoovulation.definition: Infrequent or irregular ovulation, resulting in infrequent menstrual cycles (oligomenorrhea) and potentially reduced fertility; typically defined as fewer than about 6–8 ovulations per year.

clomiphene stimulation test.definition: A reproductive endocrinology test used to assess ovarian reserve by administering clomiphene citrate during a menstrual cycle and measuring serum FSH (and sometimes estradiol) before and after the challenge; an elevated FSH on cycle day 3 and/or a rise in FSH after the clomiphene challenge suggests diminished ovarian reserve and reduced likelihood of successful ovarian stimulation.

clonazepam.definition: A long-acting benzodiazepine used as an anticonvulsant and anxiolytic; it enhances GABA-A receptor activity to produce sedative, anticonvulsant, and muscle-relaxant effects, and is commonly prescribed for panic disorder and certain seizures. It is a Schedule IV controlled substance with potential for dependence and withdrawal.

benzodiazepine.definition: A class of psychoactive drugs that enhance GABA-A receptor–mediated inhibition, producing sedation, anxiolysis, anticonvulsant effects, and muscle relaxation; used for anxiety, insomnia, seizures, and withdrawal, with potential for dependence and withdrawal symptoms.

opisthorchis sinensis.definition: A liver fluke (a trematode) that infects the bile ducts after ingestion of raw or undercooked freshwater fish; causes opisthorchiasis with biliary inflammation and obstruction, and chronic infection is associated with an increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma.

clonorchis sinensis.definition: A small liver fluke (trematode) transmitted to humans by consuming raw or undercooked freshwater fish; it resides in the biliary ducts, causing clonorchiasis with biliary inflammation and obstruction and is associated with an increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma.

clonorchiasis.definition: A parasitic infection caused by the liver fluke Clonorchis sinensis, acquired by eating raw or undercooked freshwater fish; the flukes inhabit and inflame the intrahepatic bile ducts, causing biliary obstruction and cholangitis and increasing the risk of cholangiocarcinoma.

clonus.definition: A series of involuntary, rhythmic muscle contractions in response to a sudden stretch (most commonly elicited by dorsiflexion of the foot), indicating upper motor neuron dysfunction and hyperreflexia; commonly referred to as ankle clonus when occurring at the ankle.

clonic.definition: Relating to clonus; characterized by rapid, rhythmic, involuntary muscle contractions and relaxations (jerking). In neurology, clonic movements refer to the jerking phase of a generalized seizure.

clopidogrel.definition: A thienopyridine-class antiplatelet medication that is a prodrug activated in the liver; it irreversibly inhibits the P2Y12 ADP receptor on platelets, thereby reducing platelet aggregation and lowering the risk of thrombotic events such as myocardial infarction and stroke.

cushing syndrome.definition: A hormonal disorder characterized by prolonged exposure to excess cortisol, usually from endogenous overproduction (such as a pituitary or adrenal tumor) or chronic exogenous glucocorticoid use; typical features include centripetal obesity with moon facies and a buffalo hump, skin thinning with easy bruising, proximal muscle weakness, hypertension, and glucose intolerance.

hypothalamic.definition: Relating to the hypothalamus, a brain region that regulates autonomic functions and endocrine activity by controlling the pituitary gland.

alpha2-adrenergic.definition: Alpha-2 adrenergic receptors are inhibitory G protein–coupled receptors (Gi/o) that decrease norepinephrine release by inhibiting adenylate cyclase; they act as presynaptic autoreceptors to dampen sympathetic outflow and are targeted by drugs like clonidine to lower blood pressure and produce sedation.

kava-kava.definition: An herb (Piper methysticum) whose root is prepared as a beverage with sedative and anxiolytic effects, traditionally used to relieve anxiety and promote relaxation. Its active constituents are kavalactones; use can cause liver injury in rare cases and may interact with alcohol and other CNS depressants. Caution is advised in liver disease, pregnancy, and with long-term use; regulatory status varies by country.

valerian.definition: A perennial herb whose dried root is used in traditional herbal medicine as a sedative and anxiolytic to help insomnia and mild anxiety. Evidence for efficacy is mixed and not well established; commonly taken as capsules, tablets, teas, or tinctures. Possible adverse effects include headache, dizziness, upset stomach, and daytime drowsiness, and it may interact with CNS depressants or alcohol; not recommended in pregnancy or lactation without medical advice.

trematode.definition: A parasitic flatworm of the class Trematoda (a fluke) that infects vertebrates; typically leaf-shaped with oral and ventral suckers and a complex life cycle usually involving snail intermediate hosts.

cholangiosarcoma.definition: A rare malignant tumor of the biliary tract arising from mesenchymal (sarcomatous) tissue in the bile ducts; a non-epithelial sarcoma of the biliary tree, distinct from cholangiocarcinoma which is typically an epithelial adenocarcinoma. Presents with biliary obstruction symptoms (e.g., jaundice, abdominal pain); diagnosis by imaging and histopathology; prognosis is generally poor.

opisthorchiasis.definition: An infection of the liver and biliary tract caused by parasitic flukes of the genus Opisthorchis (e.g., Opisthorchis viverrini, Opisthorchis felineus) acquired by ingesting raw or undercooked freshwater fish; it can cause biliary inflammation, obstruction, cholangitis, and is associated with cholangiocarcinoma in chronic infection.

ducts.definition: A tubular passage that conveys secretions or excretions from a gland or organ to a target site, such as a body surface or lumen; part of exocrine systems (e.g., bile ducts, pancreatic ducts, tear ducts).

saddle-shaped skull.definition: A skull deformity in which the central portion of the skull is depressed or flattened, producing a saddle-like contour with relatively higher frontal and occipital regions. This is a descriptive radiologic or clinical term used in certain skeletal dysplasias or metabolic bone conditions.

cloquet’s hernia.definition: A rare interparietal inguinal hernia in which the hernial sac lies between layers of the abdominal wall (often between the internal oblique and transversus abdominis) and may present as a groin swelling without a typical inguinal canal sac.

closed-wound suction.definition: A postoperative drainage method using a sealed reservoir and tubing to apply negative pressure, continuously drawing fluid from a wound to reduce accumulation and infection risk.

musculoskeletal pain.definition: Discomfort, soreness, or aching arising from structures of the musculoskeletal system (muscles, bones, joints, tendons, ligaments); caused by injury, overuse, inflammation, degenerative disease, or systemic conditions.

femoral hernia.definition: A protrusion of abdominal contents through the femoral ring into the femoral canal, just below the inguinal ligament; a groin hernia more common in women with a relatively high risk of incarceration.

crural hernia.definition: A hernia that passes through the femoral (crural) canal in the groin, just below the inguinal ligament; essentially a femoral hernia. It often presents as a lump in the groin or upper thigh, is more common in women, and carries a relatively high risk of incarceration or strangulation.

chloride.definition: A negatively charged chlorine ion (Cl−); the major extracellular anion that helps maintain osmotic balance and acid–base homeostasis, commonly present as part of table salt.

clorazepate.definition: A long-acting benzodiazepine tranquilizer; a prodrug of nordazepam used to treat anxiety disorders, alcohol withdrawal, and certain seizures by enhancing GABA-A–mediated inhibition.

alcohol withdrawal.definition: A set of signs and symptoms that occur after cessation or reduction of heavy, prolonged alcohol use in individuals with alcohol dependence. Symptoms typically begin within hours to a few days and include autonomic hyperactivity (sweating, tachycardia, hypertension), tremors, anxiety, insomnia, nausea/vomiting, and perceptual disturbances; severe cases can progress to delirium tremens and seizures. Treatment focuses on supportive care, benzodiazepines for withdrawal, thiamine supplementation, hydration, and monitoring for complications.

acute narrow-angle glaucoma.definition: A sudden, emergency rise in intraocular pressure caused by abrupt closure of the iridocorneal angle, blocking aqueous humor outflow through the trabecular meshwork; typically presents with severe eye pain, redness, halos around lights, blurred vision, and often nausea or vomiting, requiring prompt treatment to prevent vision loss.

withdrawal symptoms.definition: Physiological and psychological symptoms that occur after reducing or stopping a substance to which a person is dependent, reflecting neuroadaptive changes; symptoms vary by drug but commonly include anxiety, irritability, insomnia, sweating, tremors, nausea or vomiting, and cravings, and can be severe in alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal.

closed-angle glaucoma.definition: A form of glaucoma caused by blockage of the drainage angle between the iris and cornea, preventing aqueous humor from exiting the eye and causing elevated intraocular pressure; the acute form presents with sudden eye pain, red eye, halos around lights, headache, and nausea and is an ophthalmic emergency.

closed bite.definition: In dentistry, a closed bite is the condition in which the upper and lower teeth come together and contact when the jaws are closed, representing full occlusion (as opposed to an open bite).

overbite.definition: Vertical overlap of the upper front teeth over the lower front teeth beyond the normal amount, commonly described as a deep bite.

eruption of teeth.definition: Tooth eruption is the physiological process by which a tooth moves from its developmental position within the jawbone to its functional position in the dental arch, culminating in the clinical emergence of the crown through the gingiva.

tympanomastoidectomy.definition: An otologic operation in which the middle ear and mastoid air cells are accessed and diseased tissue removed, typically involving a mastoidectomy with tympanic membrane and/or middle ear reconstruction, commonly performed to treat chronic otitis media with cholesteatoma.

tympanoplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair a perforated tympanic membrane (eardrum) and, if needed, reconstruct the middle ear ossicles to improve or restore hearing.

closed-chain.definition: A movement or kinetic chain in which the distal segment (hand or foot) is fixed against a non-moving surface, so multiple joints and muscles act in a linked, weight-bearing sequence.

carbocyclic.definition: Relating to or consisting of carbon atoms arranged in a ring; a chemical structure in which the ring is composed entirely of carbon atoms (no heteroatoms).

closed-chain exercise.definition: A type of resistance exercise in which the distal segment (hand or foot) remains fixed against a surface, so movement occurs across multiple joints and involves coordinated activation of multiple muscle groups; commonly performed with the limb in contact with a stable surface (e.g., squats, push-ups).

closed-circuit breathing.definition: A breathing system in which exhaled gas is recycled after CO2 is removed and re-inhaled by the patient, with minimal venting of gas to the environment and controlled addition of oxygen/air to maintain the desired gas composition.

closed-circuit helium dilution.definition: A method to measure lung volumes by having the patient breathe from a sealed system containing a known volume of helium; after equilibration between the lungs and the circuit, the measured helium concentration is used to calculate lung volumes (typically total lung capacity and related volumes).

helium.definition: An inert, nonflammable noble gas used in medicine as part of heliox therapy (a helium–oxygen mixture) to reduce airway resistance and work of breathing in patients with acute airway obstruction; pure helium is unsafe to inhale and must be mixed with oxygen.

dilution.definition: A process of reducing the concentration of a solute in a solution by adding more solvent, resulting in a more dilute solution; often described by the dilution factor or the relationship C1V1 = C2V2.

functional residual capacity.definition: The volume of air left in the lungs after a normal, passive exhalation; it equals the sum of expiratory reserve volume and residual volume (ERV + RV) and reflects the resting level of the lung–chest wall system.

residual volume.definition: The amount of air remaining in the lungs after a maximal exhalation; it cannot be expelled and is normally about 1.1–1.5 liters (roughly 20–25% of total lung capacity).

closed dislocation.definition: A dislocation in which the joint surfaces are displaced but the overlying skin and soft tissues remain intact, with no open wound communicating with the exterior.

dislocation.definition: When your joint is injured and the bones are pushed out of position.

closed drainage.definition: A drainage system that channels bodily fluids from a wound or cavity into a sealed collection device, often with suction, to keep the system closed and reduce infection risk.

closed chest drainage system.definition: A sterile, sealed chest drainage setup connected to a chest tube that evacuates air, blood, or fluid from the pleural space while preventing backflow; typically comprises a collection chamber, a water-seal chamber, and an suction-control chamber, used to reexpand the lung and prevent reaccumulation.

closed fracture.definition: A fracture in which the bone is broken but the skin over the fracture remains intact.

simple fracture.definition: A fracture in which the bone is broken but the skin over the fracture remains intact, i.e., a closed fracture.

compound fracture.definition: An open fracture in which the broken bone communicates with the outside environment through an open wound in the skin, exposing bone and surrounding tissues to contamination and infection.

denis browne splint.definition: A device used in the management of clubfoot (talipes equinovarus) to maintain correction after casting, consisting of a rigid bar with shoes attached at each end by adjustable straps to hold the feet in abduction and dorsiflexion.

talipes.definition: A congenital deformity of the foot and ankle in which the foot is malpositioned, typically twisted inward and downward, and may be stiff, affecting gait if not treated.

equinovarus.definition: A fixed deformity of the foot in which the ankle is plantarflexed (equinus) and the hindfoot is inverted (varus), often with forefoot adduction; commonly observed in congenital clubfoot.

calcaneovalgus.definition: A deformity of the foot in which the hindfoot is in valgus (heel eversion) and the ankle is dorsiflexed (calcaneus), so the sole faces upward; commonly congenital and may improve with casting or require surgical correction if persistent.

calcaneovarus.definition: A hindfoot deformity in which the heel bone (calcaneus) is inverted (varus) relative to the tibia, commonly seen in congenital talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) or other hindfoot malalignments.

splints.definition: A device applied to an injured part to immobilize and support it, reducing movement to promote healing; splints can be rigid (plaster or fiberglass with a hard backing) or soft/flexible (bandage or foam) and are often used as temporary stabilization before casting or surgery.

clostridial.definition: Relating to the genus Clostridium; anaerobic, gram-positive, spore-forming bacilli that cause diseases such as tetanus, botulism, gas gangrene, and clostridial food poisoning.

clostridial myonecrosis.definition: An acutely progressive bacterial infection of skeletal muscle caused by Clostridium species (most often C. perfringens) with gas production in tissues, rapid myonecrosis, severe pain and edema, and systemic toxicity; requires emergent surgical debridement and broad-spectrum antibiotics (often with adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen in select cases).

clostridial toxin assay.definition: A laboratory test to detect and quantify toxins produced by Clostridium species (primarily botulinum toxin) in clinical samples or foods, used in the diagnosis of botulism and related foodborne illness.

pseudomembranous enterocolitis.definition: A toxin-mediated inflammatory disease of the colon (and sometimes the small intestine) characterized by the formation of yellowish pseudomembranes on the mucosa, most often due to Clostridioides difficile infection after antibiotic exposure.

closure.definition: The process of closing a wound or surgical incision by approximating and securing its edges (e.g., with sutures, staples, or adhesive) to promote healing and restore tissue integrity.

clotrimazole.definition: A broad-spectrum antifungal azole that inhibits fungal cytochrome P450–dependent 14α-demethylase, disrupting ergosterol synthesis and compromising fungal cell membrane integrity; used topically for dermatophyte and Candida infections (e.g., athlete's foot, ringworm, jock itch) and in vaginal/oral preparations for candidiasis.

imidazole.definition: A five-membered aromatic heterocycle containing two nitrogen atoms (a 1,3-diazole); a common scaffold in many drugs and biological molecules, capable of acting as a weak base and participating in hydrogen bonding and metal coordination.

tinea cruris.definition: A fungal infection of the skin of the groin and proximal thighs caused by dermatophyte fungi, presenting as an intensely itchy, well-demarcated, red, scaly rash often referred to as jock itch.

tinea corporis.definition: A superficial fungal infection of the skin of the body caused by dermatophyte organisms, presenting as annular, scaly plaques with an expanding active border and central clearing; commonly known as ringworm. Treated with topical antifungals, with systemic antifungals for extensive or refractory disease.

tinea versicolor.definition: A common superficial fungal infection of the skin caused by Malassezia species, presenting as hypo- or hyperpigmented, mildly scaly macules or patches on the trunk and proximal limbs. It tends to recur and is more noticeable in warm, humid weather; treated with topical antifungals (e.g., selenium sulfide, zinc pyrithione, ketoconazole) and, for extensive disease, oral antifungals (e.g., fluconazole or itraconazole).

oral candidiasis.definition: A fungal infection of the oral mucosa caused by Candida species (most often Candida albicans). It presents with white, curd-like plaques on the tongue or other oral surfaces that can be scraped off to reveal a red, raw base; may be painful and cause taste disturbance. Risk factors include immunosuppression, diabetes, denture use, antibiotic use, or inhaled corticosteroids.

vaginal candidiasis.definition: A fungal infection of the vagina caused by Candida species (most commonly Candida albicans), presenting with vulvar itching, irritation, and a thick white discharge; usually with normal vaginal pH and may be confirmed by microscopy or culture; treated with topical azole antifungals or a single-dose oral fluconazole.

neutropenic.definition: Having an abnormally low absolute neutrophil count, a type of white blood cell, which increases the risk of bacterial and fungal infections; commonly defined clinically as an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) below 1.5 x 10^9/L (1500/µL), with severe neutropenia often ANC < 0.5 x 10^9/L (500/µL).

troches.definition: A medicated lozenge or pastille that dissolves in the mouth to release a drug for local or systemic absorption, typically via the buccal or sublingual mucosa.

mastectomies.definition: A surgical procedure to remove all or part of one or both breasts, typically to treat breast cancer or to reduce cancer risk. Variants include simple/total mastectomy (removing the entire breast), modified radical mastectomy (breast tissue plus axillary lymph nodes removed), and, less commonly, radical mastectomy (breast, chest wall muscles, and lymph nodes removed); reconstruction may follow.

breast augmentations.definition: Cosmetic surgery to increase the size of the breasts.

plastic and reconstructive procedures.definition: Procedures that repair, rebuild, reshape, or replace body tissues and structures to restore function and/or appearance, typically after injury, disease, congenital defects, or aging, and include both reconstructive and cosmetic (plastic) techniques.

urological procedures.definition: Medical and surgical interventions performed to diagnose, treat, or manage disorders of the urinary tract (kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra) and the male reproductive system.

urogenital procedures.definition: A broad category of medical procedures involving the urinary tract and genital/reproductive organs, including diagnostic tests, surgical interventions, and therapies affecting structures such as the kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra, prostate, uterus, ovaries, and external genitalia.

suction tubes.definition: A flexible or rigid tube connected to a suction device (vacuum source) used to aspirate fluids, secretions, or debris from a body cavity, wound, airway, or surgical field.

silicone tubing.definition: A flexible, biocompatible tube made from silicone elastomer used to transport fluids or drain/irrigate within the body; known for chemical inertness, clarity, and sterilizability.

stab wound.definition: A penetrating injury produced by a pointed instrument that breaches the skin and underlying tissues; the external wound is often small, but a deep wound tract can injure internal structures such as organs or vessels, with potential for significant bleeding and infection.

staple.definition: A small fastener (usually metal or polymer) used to close surgical incisions or join segments of tissue; applied with a stapling device and commonly used as an alternative to sutures for skin closure or internal anastomosis.

exudate.definition: Fluid that leaks from capillaries into inflamed tissue, high in protein and cellular content (eg, neutrophils) due to increased vascular permeability; contrasts with transudate.

exudates.definition: A protein- and cell-rich fluid that leaks from blood vessels into surrounding tissue during inflammation, due to increased vascular permeability; it may be serous, fibrinous, purulent (pus), or hemorrhagic.

clot.definition: A semisolid mass formed when blood coagulates at the site of tissue injury, composed of a fibrin mesh, platelets, and trapped blood cells; functions to seal the wound and stop bleeding, but can form within vessels as a thrombus.

blood clotting.definition: The process by which blood forms a clot to stop bleeding, initiated by vascular injury that triggers platelet adhesion and aggregation, followed by activation of coagulation factors that convert soluble fibrinogen to insoluble fibrin, creating a stable fibrin mesh that traps blood cells.

clot retraction.definition: A process in which a formed blood clot contracts and becomes smaller and firmer as platelets pull on fibrin strands, expelling serum and bringing wound edges together to stabilize the clot.

clot retraction test.definition: A laboratory assay that assesses platelet function by measuring the extent and rate of clot retraction in a formed blood clot; platelets contract the fibrin mesh, pulling the clot tighter and expelling serum. Reduced or absent retraction suggests platelet dysfunction, thrombocytopenia, or dysfibrinogenemia.

clotting time.definition: A crude test of hemostasis that measures the time from blood collection to the formation of a clot, reflecting both platelet function and coagulation factors; results are affected by temperature, anticoagulants, and hematocrit, and it is largely replaced by more specific tests such as PT and aPTT.

bleeding time.definition: An historical test of primary hemostasis in which a standardized skin incision or puncture is made and the time until bleeding stops is measured, reflecting platelet function and capillary/vessel integrity; results are highly operator dependent and largely replaced by modern platelet function assays.

hemophilia.definition: A genetic bleeding disorder caused by deficiency or dysfunction of clotting factors (most commonly factor VIII in hemophilia A or factor IX in hemophilia B), leading to prolonged bleeding after injury and spontaneous or recurrent bleeding into joints and muscles.

glanzmann’s thrombasthenia.definition: An autosomal recessive platelet function disorder caused by deficiency or dysfunction of the platelet membrane receptor glycoprotein IIb/IIIa (integrin αIIbβ3), leading to defective fibrinogen-mediated platelet aggregation and mucocutaneous bleeding with a normal platelet count; platelet aggregation is reduced or absent with ADP, epinephrine, and collagen, while ristocetin-induced aggregation is normal.

clostridium botulinum.definition: A gram-positive, obligate anaerobic, spore-forming bacterium that produces botulinum neurotoxin; found in soil and aquatic sediments and capable of contaminating improperly canned foods, causing botulism, a severe neuroparalytic illness characterized by flaccid paralysis.

botox.definition: Brand name for a drug made of botulinum toxin type A that is injected into muscles and weakens them to ease the appearance of wrinkles.

gas gangrene.definition: A rapidly progressive necrotizing infection of muscle caused by Clostridium species, characterized by gas production in tissues (crepitus), severe pain, edema, and systemic toxicity; typically follows penetrating trauma or contaminated wounds and requires urgent surgical debridement and antibiotic therapy.

cloxacillin.definition: A penicillinase‑resistant, semisynthetic penicillin antibiotic active against penicillinase‑producing Staphylococcus aureus and susceptible streptococci; it inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin‑binding proteins and is ineffective against MRSA and most Gram‑negative bacteria.

penicillinase-resistant penicillin.definition: An antibiotic in the penicillin family that is resistant to hydrolysis by penicillinase (beta-lactamase) produced by some bacteria, thereby retaining activity against penicillinase-producing Staphylococcus aureus; part of the antistaphylococcal (isoxazolyl) penicillins.

cluster analysis.definition: A set of unsupervised multivariate statistical techniques that group similar observations into clusters, revealing natural subtypes or patterns in data such as patient phenotypes or disease subgroups.

cluster of differentiation antigen.definition: A cell-surface marker used to identify and classify leukocytes; CD antigens are specific glycoproteins or proteins designated by numbers (e.g., CD4, CD8) and are used in immunophenotyping by flow cytometry to define immune cell subsets.

cd.definition: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by transmural inflammation that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract, often presenting with abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, and sometimes fever; complications include strictures, fistulas, and abscesses.

staphylococcal.definition: Relating to Staphylococcus bacteria, a genus of gram-positive cocci that form grape-like clusters and can cause infections such as skin and soft-tissue infections, pneumonia, or bloodstream infections, most often due to Staphylococcus aureus or coagulase-negative staphylococci.

food poisoning.definition: An illness caused by consuming food contaminated with germs (pathogens); also called a foodborne illness.

endospores.definition: Dormant, highly resistant, nonreproductive structures formed by certain Gram-positive bacteria (notably Bacillus and Clostridium) in response to nutrient limitation or other stress. They contain a copy of the genome, essential enzymes, and minimal cytoplasm, surrounded by a thick cortex and protein coat, enabling survival through heat, desiccation, radiation, and chemical disinfectants; they germinate back into vegetative cells when conditions become favorable.

cloverleaf nail.definition: A rare nail deformity in which the nail plate shows lobulated, leaf-like projections at the distal edge, producing a cloverleaf appearance.

cloverleaf skull deformity.definition: A severe, syndromic form of craniosynostosis in which premature fusion of multiple cranial sutures produces a trilobed, cloverleaf-shaped skull, often with midface hypoplasia and proptosis, and commonly associated with syndromes such as Pfeiffer or Apert.

facial anomalies.definition: Congenital or acquired abnormalities of the face’s structure or appearance, leading to deviations in size, shape, or symmetry of facial features (e.g., cleft lip/palate, craniofacial dysmorphism, facial asymmetry).

skeletal deformities.definition: Abnormalities in the size, shape, or alignment of bones or the skeleton, which can be congenital or acquired and may impair function or appearance.

talipes equinovarus.definition: A congenital deformity of the foot in which the foot is turned inward and downward (clubfoot), with plantar flexion (equinus), inversion (varus), and adduction of the forefoot.

cluttering.definition: A fluency disorder characterized by unusually rapid or irregular speech with frequent disfluencies and reduced intelligibility, often accompanied by disorganized phrasing and poor self-awareness, and may co-occur with language impairment or attention problems.

dysfluency.definition: Abnormal interruptions in the normal flow of speech, such as hesitations, repetitions, prolongations, or blocks, often seen in stuttering.

clysis.definition: The introduction of fluids into a body cavity or tissue by infusion or irrigation, used to hydrate, deliver medications, or flush out the cavity.

carpometacarpal.definition: Relating to the carpals (wrist bones) and the metacarpals (hand bones); also used to describe the joints between these bones—the carpometacarpal joints.

chronic myelogenous leukemia.definition: A myeloproliferative neoplasm driven by the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene from a t(9;22) Philadelphia chromosome, causing clonal expansion of granulocytic precursors. It typically progresses from a chronic phase with leukocytosis to accelerated and blast-crisis phases; symptoms may include fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and splenomegaly. First-line treatment is targeted therapy with BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g., imatinib), with allogeneic stem cell transplantation considered in resistant or advanced cases.

hemophilia b.definition: A hereditary X-linked recessive bleeding disorder caused by deficiency or dysfunction of coagulation factor IX, leading to impaired blood clotting and prolonged bleeding; also known as Christmas disease.

hemophilia c.definition: A rare inherited bleeding disorder caused by deficiency of coagulation factor XI (FXI), leading to a variable bleeding tendency, often mild, with prolonged bleeding after trauma or surgery.

factor vii a.definition: Activated form of coagulation factor VII; a vitamin K–dependent serine protease that, in complex with tissue factor, initiates the extrinsic coagulation pathway by activating factor X (and to a lesser extent IX) on phospholipid surfaces, and is used pharmaceutically as recombinant activated factor VII to promote hemostasis in certain bleeding disorders.
