glycogenosis.definition: An inherited group of metabolic disorders caused by defects of enzymes involved in glycogen metabolism, leading to abnormal storage or structure of glycogen in liver, muscle, and other tissues.

corneal abrasion.definition: A superficial defect of the corneal epithelium caused by trauma (e.g., a scratch, irritants, or contact lens friction), presenting with acute eye pain, tearing, redness, and photophobia; fluorescein staining reveals the epithelial defect, and it typically heals within 24–72 hours with lubricants and topical antibiotics.

keratocyte.definition: A quiescent stromal cell of the cornea that maintains the extracellular matrix and collagenous framework, helping preserve corneal transparency; upon injury it can become an activated fibroblast or myofibroblast involved in wound healing and scarring.

corneal grafting.definition: A surgical procedure in which diseased or damaged corneal tissue is replaced with donor corneal tissue to restore corneal transparency and vision; typically performed as penetrating keratoplasty (full-thickness) or lamellar keratoplasty (partial-thickness).

corneal graft.definition: A surgical transplant in which healthy donor corneal tissue is transplanted to replace diseased or damaged recipient corneal tissue, restoring optical clarity; it can be a full-thickness graft (penetrating keratoplasty) or partial-thickness graft (lamellar keratoplasty).

corneal transplant.definition: A surgical procedure in which a diseased or damaged cornea is replaced with healthy donor corneal tissue to restore vision, improve clarity, and relieve pain.

corneal transplantation.definition: A surgical procedure in which a diseased or scarred cornea is replaced with healthy donor corneal tissue, typically by penetrating keratoplasty (full-thickness) or lamellar keratoplasty (partial-thickness), to restore vision and/or relieve pain.

keratoplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to replace damaged or diseased corneal tissue with donor tissue; can be penetrating keratoplasty (full-thickness) or lamellar keratoplasty (partial-thickness).

corneal loupe.definition: A magnifying lens (often head-mounted or handheld) used by ophthalmologists to magnify the corneal surface for detailed examination or microsurgical manipulation of the anterior segment.

coronal plane.definition: A vertical anatomical plane that divides the body into anterior (front) and posterior (back) portions; also known as the frontal plane.

coronal section.definition: A coronal section (frontal plane) is an anatomical plane that runs vertically from side to side, dividing the body or an organ into anterior (front) and posterior (back) portions.

corona radiata.definition:
- Neuroanatomy: A fan-shaped sheet of white-matter fibers in the brain that carries projection fibers between the internal capsule and the cerebral cortex, lying just beneath the cortical gray matter.

- Reproductive anatomy: The layer of granulosa cells surrounding the oocyte in the ovarian follicle (the cumulus oophorus), providing nutrients to the oocyte.

cad.definition: A condition in which the coronary arteries become narrowed or blocked due to atherosclerosis, reducing blood flow to the heart muscle and potentially causing angina, myocardial infarction, or heart failure.

coronary arteriovenous fistula.definition: An abnormal connection between a coronary artery and a cardiac chamber or another vascular structure, bypassing the myocardial capillary bed and creating a coronary arteriovenous shunt. It can be congenital or acquired and may cause myocardial ischemia due to coronary steal, volume overload, heart failure, or arrhythmias; management depends on size and symptoms.

coronary artery scan.definition: A noninvasive imaging test that visualizes the coronary arteries to detect atherosclerotic plaque and any narrowing or blockages, typically using CT angiography with contrast or non-contrast calcium scoring to assess coronary artery disease risk.

coronary angiography.definition: A test that shows how blood moves through the blood vessels supplying the heart to identify narrowed arteries. It uses x-rays and the injection of a fluid called a contrast agent that can be seen on the x-rays.

coronary arteriography.definition: An invasive diagnostic procedure in which radiopaque contrast is injected into the coronary arteries via a catheter and X-ray imaging (angiography) is used to visualize the arteries for stenosis or occlusion.

isosorbide dinitrate.definition: A nitrate vasodilator that releases nitric oxide, causing relaxation of vascular smooth muscle with prominent venodilation and reduced preload; used to prevent angina pectoris and to treat heart failure in certain patients.

beta-adrenergic blocker.definition: A class of medications that antagonize beta-adrenergic receptors, reducing sympathetic stimulation of the heart and other tissues; they decrease heart rate, contractility, and blood pressure, and are used to treat hypertension, angina, certain arrhythmias, and heart failure. They can be cardioselective (β1) or nonselective (β1 and β2); nonselective agents may cause bronchospasm in susceptible individuals.

antidiabetic medications.definition: A class of medications used to treat diabetes mellitus by lowering blood glucose levels. They include insulin and a range of oral and injectable agents that act through diverse mechanisms—such as increasing insulin secretion, improving insulin sensitivity, reducing hepatic glucose production, or slowing intestinal glucose absorption.

cornual pregnancy.definition: A pregnancy implanted in the uterine horn (cornual region), typically in the interstitial portion of the fallopian tube within the myometrium; a form of ectopic pregnancy.

cataract surgery.definition: A surgical procedure to remove a cloudy natural lens (cataract) from the eye and usually replace it with an artificial intraocular lens (IOL); most commonly performed using phacoemulsification with a small corneal incision.

pilocarpine.definition: A nonselective muscarinic receptor agonist (parasympathomimetic alkaloid) used topically in the eye to induce miosis and enhance aqueous humor outflow to lower intraocular pressure in glaucoma; also used systemically to stimulate saliva in xerostomia.

miotic.definition: An eye drop that constricts the pupil; used to treat glaucoma.

dilatation.definition: Enlargement or widening of a hollow organ or lumen, such as a blood vessel, heart chamber, esophagus, or pupil, due to dilation of its walls.

myotomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which a muscle is incised to relieve constriction or spasm and improve function.

gastric acid reflux.definition: A condition in which stomach acid and other gastric contents flow upward into the esophagus, causing symptoms such as heartburn and regurgitation and potentially esophageal irritation; often due to transient relaxation or incompetence of the lower esophageal sphincter and reduced esophageal clearance, with chronic cases termed gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

fifth cranial nerve.definition: The trigeminal nerve is the primary sensory nerve of the face and the motor nerve to the muscles of mastication; it has three divisions (V1, V2, V3) that provide facial sensation and innervate the muscles of mastication.

seventh cranial nerve.definition: A mixed cranial nerve that innervates the muscles of facial expression, transmits taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, and provides parasympathetic innervation to the lacrimal, submandibular, and sublingual glands; it exits the skull through the stylomastoid foramen after traversing the facial canal.

radiogram.definition: An X-ray image obtained by radiography to visualize the internal structures of the body for diagnostic purposes.

left anterior descending artery.definition: A major branch of the left coronary artery that travels along the anterior interventricular sulcus, supplying the anterior left ventricle and most of the interventricular septum; it gives septal perforator and diagonal branches and is a common site of occlusion in myocardial infarction.

posterior descending artery.definition: A coronary artery that travels in the posterior interventricular sulcus and supplies the posterior portion of the interventricular septum and adjacent portions of the ventricles; it usually arises from the right coronary artery in right-dominant hearts, but can arise from the left circumflex artery in left-dominant hearts.

right marginal coronary artery.definition: A branch of the right coronary artery that supplies the right ventricle, coursing along the acute margin of the right ventricle and giving perforating branches to the RV myocardium.

internal mammary artery.definition: An artery arising from the subclavian artery that courses along the inner surface of the thoracic wall (internal thoracic wall), supplying the chest wall and breasts; it is frequently used as a durable arterial graft in coronary artery bypass surgery.

bowman's membrane.definition: An acellular, collagen-rich layer of the cornea located between the epithelial basement membrane and the stroma; it provides structural support and rigidity to the cornea and has limited regenerative capacity after injury.

descemet's membrane.definition: A basement membrane secreted by the corneal endothelium, located between the stroma and the endothelial cell layer; forms the posterior limiting membrane of the cornea and provides structural support for the endothelium.

substantia propria.definition: The loose connective tissue layer beneath the epithelium of mucous membranes (the lamina propria) that contains blood vessels, nerves, lymphatics, and resident immune cells, providing structural support and nourishment to the overlying epithelium.

corneal epithelium.definition: The outermost, non-keratinized, stratified squamous epithelium of the cornea, typically 5–7 cell layers thick, that provides a protective barrier against abrasions and pathogens and helps maintain corneal transparency; it is continually regenerated by limbal stem cells.

reperfusion.definition: Re-establishing blood flow, such as when a blockage in a coronary artery that is causing a heart attack is cleared.

coronary collateralization.definition: A process by which collateral vessels gradually develop in the coronary circulation to bypass a narrowed or occluded coronary artery, restoring blood flow to the myocardium in response to chronic ischemia (often via arteriogenesis and angiogenesis).

coronary plexus.definition: A network of autonomic nerve fibers around the heart, forming part of the cardiac plexus and accompanying the coronary arteries; it provides sympathetic and parasympathetic innervation to the myocardium and coronary vessels.

coronary vein.definition: Veins that drain the myocardium and return deoxygenated blood to the right atrium, primarily via the coronary sinus; include the great, middle, and small cardiac veins, with some anterior cardiac veins draining directly into the right atrium.

coronary valve.definition: No widely recognized anatomical structure named 'coronary valve'. If you meant the valve at the coronary sinus ostium into the right atrium, that's the Thebesian valve—a small flap that helps prevent backflow from the right atrium into the coronary sinus.

coronavirus.definition: A group of viruses that cause a variety of diseases, including severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) and Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS).

coronaviridae.definition: A family of enveloped, positive-sense single-stranded RNA viruses with crown-like spike proteins, belonging to the order Nidovirales; it includes the genera Alpha-, Beta-, Gamma-, and Delta-coronavirus, which infect birds and mammals (including humans) and include pathogens such as SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, and SARS-CoV-2.

sars.definition: A viral respiratory illness caused by SARS-CoV; presents with fever, cough, and dyspnea, may progress to pneumonia and acute respiratory distress syndrome; transmitted primarily by respiratory droplets and close contact; caused a global outbreak in 2002–2003 and controlled with infection-control measures.

rhinoviruses.definition: A group of nonenveloped, positive-sense, single-stranded RNA viruses in the Picornaviridae family that cause the common cold; they replicate best in the nasal mucosa at about 33°C, are transmitted by respiratory droplets and surface contact, and are acid-labile with no widely effective vaccine.

infectious peritonitis.definition: An infection of the peritoneal cavity causing inflammation of the peritoneum, usually bacterial, typically resulting from intra‑abdominal perforation or contamination (including peritoneal dialysis-related infection); presents with abdominal pain and tenderness, fever, and leukocytosis, and is treated with antibiotics and source control.

corpus luteum.definition: The egg follicle remnant left behind after an egg has been released during ovulation. The corpus luteum secretes the hormone progesterone to stimulate the growth of the endometrium.

corpora lutea.definition: The plural form of the ovarian structure formed after ovulation from the ruptured follicle; a yellowish body in the ovary that secretes progesterone (and some estrogen) to maintain the luteal phase, is maintained by hCG if pregnancy occurs, and degenerates into the corpus albicans if not.

corpus spongiosum.definition: A cylinder of soft tissue surrounding a man’s urethra and running the length of the penis.

epithalamus.definition: A part of the diencephalon comprising the pineal gland and habenular nuclei; lies posterior to the thalamus and links the limbic system to the midbrain, and regulates circadian rhythms via melatonin secretion.

corpus uteri.definition: The main central portion of the uterus between the fundus and the cervix; the body of the uterus, consisting of the thick muscular myometrium and the inner endometrium, which enlarges during pregnancy.

fallopian tubes.definition: A pair of slender ducts that extend from the upper uterus toward the ovaries; they capture the ovulated egg and transport it toward the uterus, with fertilization typically occurring inside the tube; also called the oviducts.

ovarian follicle.definition: A fluid-filled sac in the ovary that contains a developing oocyte; it grows during the follicular phase of the menstrual cycle, secretes estrogen, and ruptures (ovulates) to release the oocyte when mature.

gestation.definition: Pregnancy or the development of something over time.

decidual.definition: Relating to the decidua, the hormone-modified endometrium of the uterus during pregnancy that lines the uterus and supports implantation and placental development.

corpus vitreum.definition: The vitreous body of the eye—a transparent, gel-like, avascular mass occupying the vitreous chamber between the lens and retina; it maintains the eyeball’s shape and provides a clear medium for light transmission to the retina.

corpora cavernosa.definition: A pair of sponge-like erectile tissue cylinders in the penis that fill with blood during arousal, producing an erection; each is enclosed by tunica albuginea and runs along the dorsal aspect, flanking the corpus spongiosum.

coronoid process.definition: Two anatomical structures named coronoid process: (1) the triangular eminence on the ramus of the mandible that serves as the attachment for the temporalis muscle; (2) the anterior projection of the proximal ulna that participates in elbow articulation with the humerus.

coronoid fossa.definition: A shallow depression on the distal anterior aspect of the humerus that accommodates the coronoid process of the ulna during elbow flexion.

ramus.definition: A branch or division of a bone, nerve, or blood vessel; an extension from the main body of a structure that supplies a region or forms part of an articulation. In bones, it is a projecting part that can form joints or serve as an attachment site.

canine.definition: Relating to dogs (Canis familiaris) or to the dog family; in dentistry, a pointed tooth between the incisors and premolars, also called a cuspids or eye tooth.

premolars.definition: The teeth right behind the canine teeth. They help to grind food. Also called bicuspids.

molars.definition: The 3 back teeth on each side of your upper and lower jaws, that help you to chew your food.

coronoid process of the mandible.definition: A triangular projection on the superior border of the mandible's ramus that serves as the insertion point for the temporalis muscle.

coronoid fossa of the mandible.definition: A small, shallow depression on the anterior border of the ramus of the mandible, just above the mandibular notch, that accommodates the coronoid process of the mandible during jaw movement.

mandibular notch.definition: A concave notch on the superior border of the mandible's ramus that separates the coronoid process anteriorly from the condylar process posteriorly.

condylar process.definition: A projection of the mandible at the superior end of the ramus, consisting of the rounded condyle (head) and neck; it articulates with the mandibular fossa of the temporal bone to form the temporomandibular joint, enabling hinge and gliding jaw movements.

greater tubercle.definition: A prominent projection on the proximal humerus that serves as the insertion site for the rotator cuff tendons—supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and teres minor.

intertubercular groove.definition: A groove on the anterior aspect of the proximal humerus between the greater and lesser tubercles that houses the tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii.

lesser tubercle.definition: A small eminence on the anteromedial aspect of the proximal humerus; the insertion site for the tendon of the subscapularis muscle.

trochlea.definition: A groove in front of the femur where the patella moves as the knee bends and straightens.

humeral condyle.definition: Two distal articular surfaces on the humerus forming part of the elbow joint: the capitulum (lateral) articulates with the head of the radius, and the trochlea (medial) articulates with the trochlear notch of the ulna.

lateral epicondyle.definition: A bony prominence on the outer aspect of the distal humerus that serves as the attachment site for the forearm extensor muscles.

radial fossa.definition: A small depression on the distal end of the humerus, on the anterior aspect, that accommodates the head of the radius when the elbow is flexed.

coronary sulcus.definition: An external groove encircling the heart between the atria and ventricles (the atrioventricular groove) that marks the boundary between these chambers and houses portions of the coronary vessels, including the right coronary artery and the coronary sinus.

cortical radiate arteries.definition: Small arteries arising from the arcuate arteries that radiate into the renal cortex to supply cortical nephrons by giving rise to afferent arterioles and forming the cortical capillary networks (glomerular and peritubular capillaries).

ibutilide.definition: An intravenous class III antiarrhythmic agent used to rapidly convert recent-onset atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter to sinus rhythm by prolonging the myocardial action potential (IKr blockade); associated with QT prolongation and risk of torsades de pointes, and typically requires ECG monitoring.

corvert.definition: A brand name for amiodarone, a broad-spectrum class III antiarrhythmic used to treat and prevent various tachyarrhythmias (e.g., ventricular fibrillation, pulseless VT, and atrial fibrillation); typically given IV in acute settings and orally for long-term rhythm control.

renal glomeruli.definition: Microscopic tufts of fenestrated capillaries within the renal corpuscles of nephrons that filter plasma to form the ultrafiltrate, supplied by the afferent arteriole and drained by the efferent arteriole.

interlobular arteries of kidney.definition: Small arteries of the renal cortex that originate from the arcuate arteries and extend into the cortex as cortical radiate arteries, supplying the nephron glomeruli by giving rise to afferent arterioles.

cortical rim sign.definition: A radiologic sign in which a thin rim of intact cortical enhancement surrounds an infarct or necrotic area on contrast-enhanced imaging, reflecting residual cortical perfusion around the lesion.

rim sign.definition: A radiologic finding showing a thin, well-defined border surrounding a lesion or cavity on imaging, often reflecting a capsule, calcified rim, or interface between differing densities, which helps delineate the structure from surrounding tissue.

cortical necrosis.definition: Cortical necrosis is the death of cells in the cortex (the outer portion) of an organ; most commonly it refers to renal cortical necrosis, a rare ischemic injury of the kidney cortex usually due to disseminated intravascular coagulation or obstetric complications.

renal vein thrombosis.definition: A blood clot in the renal vein causing obstruction of venous outflow from the kidney, which can lead to flank pain, hematuria, and impaired renal function; risk factors include nephrotic syndrome, dehydration, malignancy, and other hypercoagulable states.

cortical substance of cerebellum.definition: Thin outer layer of gray matter that covers the cerebellum; composed of three histological layers (molecular, Purkinje cell, granular); contains Purkinje cells whose axons provide the main output, integrating mossy and climbing fiber inputs to coordinate and refine voluntary movement, balance, and posture.

corticomedullary border.definition: The boundary between the renal cortex and renal medulla; the junction where the outer cortex transitions into the inner medulla, used to assess corticomedullary differentiation on imaging.

corticopontocerebellar fibers.definition: A projection from the cerebral cortex to the pontine nuclei, whose pontine neurons project to the contralateral cerebellar cortex via the middle cerebellar peduncle; part of the pathway that transmits motor planning information from cortex to the cerebellum for coordination.

corticopontine fibers.definition: Nerve fibers from pyramidal neurons of the cerebral cortex that project to the pontine nuclei in the ventral pons, forming the corticopontine tract; they relay motor planning and other cortical information to the cerebellum via the pontocerebellar pathway.

pontocerebellar fibers.definition: Afferent fibers from the pontine nuclei to the cerebellum that originate from neurons receiving input from the cerebral cortex; they cross to the contralateral cerebellar hemisphere via the middle cerebellar peduncle and form part of the cerebrocerebellar pathway involved in planning and coordinating movement.

corticospinal tract.definition: A major descending motor pathway from the cerebral cortex to the spinal cord that enables voluntary motor control, especially of the limbs; it travels through the internal capsule and brainstem, with most fibers decussating at the medullary pyramids, and terminates on interneurons and alpha motor neurons in the anterior horn. It consists of the lateral corticospinal tract (primarily distal limb control) and the anterior corticospinal tract (more trunk/proximal control).

anterior corticospinal tract.definition: A subdivision of the corticospinal tract that descends on the anterior (ventral) surface of the spinal cord and largely terminates in the ventral horn of spinal cord segments, providing voluntary control of trunk and proximal limb muscles; its fibers typically decussate at the level of the spinal cord.

lateral corticospinal tract.definition: A major descending motor pathway that originates in the motor cortex, decussates at the medullary pyramids, and travels in the lateral funiculus of the spinal cord to synapse on lower motor neurons and interneurons in the ventral horn, controlling voluntary movement of the limbs, especially fine motor skills.

mineralocorticoids.definition: Mineralocorticoids are corticosteroid hormones that regulate electrolyte and fluid balance, mainly by increasing sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion in the renal distal tubules and collecting ducts; aldosterone is the principal mineralocorticoid produced by the adrenal cortex.

corticosterone.definition: A steroid hormone produced by the adrenal cortex that acts as a glucocorticoid, regulating glucose metabolism, energy homeostasis, the stress response, and immune function; it also has some mineralocorticoid activity. In humans, cortisol is the principal glucocorticoid, with corticosterone present in relatively smaller amounts.

adrenal glands.definition: Glands that sit on top of each kidney and secrete stress hormones.

hypocortisolism.definition: Abnormally low cortisol production by the adrenal glands, typically due to primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) or secondary/tertiary adrenal insufficiency from pituitary/hypothalamic dysfunction, leading to fatigue, weakness, hypotension, weight loss, hypoglycemia, and hyponatremia (with hyperkalemia and, in primary disease, hyperpigmentation possible).

cushing’s disease.definition: An endogenous form of Cushing's syndrome caused by a pituitary adenoma that secretes ACTH, leading to overstimulation of the adrenal cortex and excess cortisol production.

nelson’s syndrome.definition: A pituitary ACTH-secreting macroadenoma that enlarges after bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing disease, producing excess ACTH and often causing hyperpigmentation and visual field defects from mass effect.

corti’s organ.definition: A sensory organ in the cochlea of the inner ear containing hair cells on the basilar membrane; it transduces sound-induced mechanical vibrations into neural impulses transmitted by the auditory nerve.

corticotroph.definition: A type of anterior pituitary cell that secretes adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) in response to corticotropin-releasing hormone, thereby stimulating the adrenal cortex to produce cortisol.

corticotroph adenoma.definition: An ACTH-secreting tumor of the anterior pituitary that increases adrenocorticotropic hormone production, causing hypercortisolism (Cushing disease).

corticotropic cell.definition: An endocrine cell of the anterior pituitary that secretes adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) in response to corticotropin-releasing hormone, stimulating the adrenal cortex to produce cortisol.

corticosteroid-binding globulin.definition: A liver-produced transport glycoprotein that binds cortisol and other corticosteroids with high affinity, limiting the amount of free, biologically active hormone in the circulation.

transcortin.definition: A hepatic plasma glycoprotein that binds cortisol and other corticosteroids with high affinity, regulating their free (bioactive) circulating levels; also known as corticosteroid-binding globulin (CBG).

cor triatriatum.definition: A rare congenital heart defect in which a fibromembranous membrane subdivides the left atrium into two chambers, potentially obstructing pulmonary venous return to the mitral valve and causing symptoms ranging from none to dyspnea; definitive treatment is surgical resection or fenestration of the membrane.

corynebacterium.definition: A genus of Gram-positive, non–spore-forming, rod-shaped bacteria (coryneform); many species are part of the normal flora of skin and mucous membranes, while some pathogenic species (notably Corynebacterium diphtheriae) cause diseases such as diphtheria; most are aerobic or facultatively anaerobic.

corynebacterium acnes.definition: A Gram-positive, anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium that colonizes hair follicles and sebaceous glands and is a major contributor to acne; historically called Propionibacterium acnes and now reclassified as Cutibacterium acnes.

corynebacterium diphtheriae.definition: A Gram-positive, non–spore-forming bacillus that colonizes the nasopharynx and, when toxigenic, causes diphtheria—a toxin-mediated infection of the upper respiratory tract (often with a pseudomembrane) that is vaccine-preventable and treated with antitoxin and antibiotics.

propionibacterium.definition: A genus of Gram-positive, anaerobic (often aerotolerant), non-spore-forming, rod-shaped bacteria that produce propionic acid as a metabolic end product; part of normal skin flora (notably the acne-associated species formerly Propionibacterium acnes, now Cutibacterium acnes) and includes dairy-associated species; can cause opportunistic infections, particularly with implanted devices, and are typically slow-growing.

coryza spasmodica.definition: Paroxysmal rhinitis with sudden episodes of nasal discharge and obstruction, usually accompanied by sneezing; an archaic description of spasmodic nasal inflammation.

corzide.definition: Not a standard medical term; no widely accepted definition. If Corzide is a brand name, its active ingredients and indicated use vary by product and region—please provide context (country, manufacturer, or indication) for a precise definition.

cosmegen.definition: A cytotoxic antibiotic (antineoplastic) used in chemotherapy; it intercalates into DNA and inhibits RNA synthesis, and is employed in regimens for certain cancers (e.g., Wilms tumor, rhabdomyosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma).

cosmetic acne.definition: A form of acne caused or aggravated by cosmetic products or practices (such as makeup, moisturizers, sunscreens, or styling products) containing comedogenic or irritating ingredients, leading to clogged pores and inflammatory lesions in areas where the product is applied.

cosmetic dermatitis.definition: An inflammatory skin reaction to cosmetic products, usually a form of contact dermatitis caused by irritants or allergens in cosmetics, presenting with redness, itching, and a pruritic rash that may include papules or vesicles; management includes stopping the offending product, considering patch testing, and using topical corticosteroids and emollients as needed.

cosmetic surgery.definition: A branch of plastic surgery focused on enhancing cosmetic appearance by altering normal body structures; procedures are elective and aim to improve aesthetic appearance rather than restore function or treat disease.

rhinoplasty.definition: Reshaping the cartilage and bone of the nose to achieve the desired profile. Commonly known as a nose job.

rhytidoplasty.definition: A plastic surgery procedure to improve signs of aging in the face and neck by lifting and tightening the skin and underlying tissues, and often repositioning or removing fat; commonly known as a facelift.

cosmetic.definition: Pertaining to the outward appearance; intended to improve aesthetics rather than to treat disease or restore function.

cosmic radiation.definition: A form of high-energy ionizing radiation originating from outer space, composed mainly of charged particles (protons, alpha particles, and heavier nuclei) and high-energy photons; it ionizes biological tissue and can cause DNA damage, increasing cancer risk. Earth's atmosphere and magnetic field provide shielding, so exposure is greatest at high altitude or in space.

costa.definition: One of the bones forming the thoracic cage; articulates posteriorly with a thoracic vertebra and anteriorly with the sternum (via costal cartilage).

costae.definition: Ribs; the paired bones forming the thoracic cage, articulating posteriorly with the thoracic vertebrae and anteriorly with the sternum or costal cartilage, protecting thoracic organs and aiding respiration. They are categorized as true (1–7), false (8–10), and floating (11–12).

costal.definition: Relating to the ribs or costae; pertaining to the rib cage.

costal arch.definition: A curved border of the rib cage formed by the costal margins—the costal cartilages of the lower ribs that meet toward the sternum to form the inferior edge of the thoracic cage.

costal groove.definition: A groove along the inferior border of a rib that houses the intercostal vessels and nerve (the intercostal neurovascular bundle).

costal notch.definition: A notch on the edge of the sternum where a costal cartilage articulates with the sternum (typically on the manubrium for the first rib and along the body for ribs 2–7).

costochondral.definition: Relating to the rib and its costal (cartilaginous) connection; the junction between a rib and its costal cartilage.

costochondritis.definition: An inflammation of the costal cartilages at the rib–sternum joints that causes localized chest wall pain tender to touch and worsened by movement or deep breathing; typically self-limited and managed with NSAIDs and rest, with evaluation to exclude cardiac causes.

costocervical.definition: Relating to the ribs and the neck; used in anatomy to describe structures that involve both the costal (rib) and cervical (neck) regions.

costoclavicular.definition: Relating to the first rib (costal) and the clavicle; describes structures between these bones, such as the costoclavicular space or the costoclavicular ligament.

costosternal.definition: Relating to the joints between the costal cartilages and the sternum; the sternocostal joints that connect the ribs to the sternum.

costotransverse articulation.definition: A synovial, plane-type joint between the tubercle of a thoracic rib and the transverse process of the corresponding vertebra, reinforced by costotransverse ligaments; it permits small gliding movements of the rib during respiration.

costovertebral.definition: Relating to the ribs and the vertebrae; pertaining to the costovertebral joints (rib–vertebra articulations).

costophrenic angle.definition: The sharp angle at the lung bases where the diaphragmatic pleura meets the parietal (costal) pleura, i.e., the costophrenic sulcus; blunting of this angle on imaging suggests pleural effusion.

cot death.definition: Sudden, unexplained death of an apparently healthy infant, most often during sleep and usually under 1 year of age, in which a thorough investigation (including autopsy and examination of the death scene) fails to identify a cause.

cotton-wool exudate.definition: A fluffy white exudate produced by inflammatory processes; it resembles cotton wool and is composed of fibrin, inflammatory cells, and necrotic debris, typically seen on mucosal surfaces in acute or chronic infections and inflammatory conditions.

cottonmouth.definition: A subjective feeling of dry mouth caused by reduced saliva production (xerostomia). Common causes include dehydration, mouth breathing, medications with anticholinergic effects, diabetes, Sjögren syndrome, and head/neck radiation therapy. Management focuses on hydration, saliva substitutes or stimulants, and addressing the underlying cause.

water moccasin.definition: A venomous pit viper (Agkistrodon piscivorus) native to wetlands of the southeastern United States; also known as cottonmouth.

cotazym.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. If you can share the active ingredient(s), country of sale, or the intended use, I can provide a precise definition. Please also check the spelling or provide context.

pancrelipase.definition: A pancreatic enzyme replacement preparation containing porcine-derived lipase, amylase, and protease; used to treat exocrine pancreatic insufficiency by improving the digestion and absorption of fats, carbohydrates, and proteins.

cotyledon.definition: A seed leaf of the embryo in seed-bearing plants that stores nutrients and forms the seedling's first leaves; in placental mammals, one of the lobes of the placenta formed by chorionic villi.

counterirritant.definition: A substance that produces a mild local irritation or inflammation with the intention of relieving pain or discomfort in the same area or a nearby area by counterirritation (diverting or modulating sensory nerve signals).

cotyloid.definition: Relating to the cotyloid cavity (acetabulum) of the pelvis; the cup-shaped socket that articulates with the femoral head in the hip joint.

cotyloid cavity.definition: The acetabular (acetabular) cavity of the pelvis; a cup-shaped socket that forms the hip joint and articulates with the head of the femur.

coudé catheter.definition: A urinary catheter with a curved distal tip that helps bypass urethral obstructions (such as urethral stricture or prostatic enlargement) during catheterization, reducing trauma to the urethra.

allergies.definition: An exaggerated immune response to normally harmless substances (allergens), mediated by IgE antibodies and histamine release, causing symptoms in the nose, eyes, skin, airways, or digestive tract and potentially life-threatening reactions (anaphylaxis).

tracheobronchial tree.definition: The airway system formed by the trachea and its successive branches (the bronchi) that conduct air from the larynx to the bronchioles in the lungs.

expectorant.definition: A medication that loosens and thins mucus in the airways to facilitate productive coughing and clearance of secretions; commonly used to treat chest congestion (guaifenesin is a typical example).

coumarin.definition: A fragrant crystalline lactone (2H-1-benzopyran-2-one) found in tonka beans and many plants; it is the core structure of many anticoagulant drugs such as warfarin and of numerous 4-hydroxycoumarin derivatives.

hemocytometer.definition: A precision counting chamber—an etched grid on a glass slide—that holds a known volume of sample to enable counting cells and calculating their concentration; widely used for blood cell counts and cell‑culture measurements.

coulter counter.definition: An automated device that counts and sizes microscopic particles, especially blood cells, by detecting changes in electrical impedance as each particle passes through a narrow aperture (the Coulter principle).

coxiella burnetii.definition: A small, Gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacterium that causes Q fever in humans; transmitted mainly by inhalation of contaminated aerosols from infected livestock, and can cause acute febrile illness with pneumonia or hepatitis, with rare progression to chronic endocarditis.

rickettsia burnetii.definition: Not a correct term; the etiologic agent of Q fever is Coxiella burnetii, a small, gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacterium transmitted mainly by inhalation of aerosols from infected livestock, causing febrile illness that can manifest as pneumonia or hepatitis, with possible chronic endocarditis.

coxsackieviruses.definition: Coxsackieviruses are nonenveloped, positive-sense RNA enteroviruses (Coxsackie A and Coxsackie B) that infect humans and cause a range of illnesses from mild febrile or upper-respiratory infections to hand-foot-mouth disease, herpangina, aseptic meningitis, myocarditis, and pleurodynia.

aseptic meningitis.definition: Aseptic meningitis is meningitis with negative bacterial cultures of the cerebrospinal fluid, most often caused by viruses; patients typically have headache, fever, photophobia, and neck stiffness, and CSF shows a lymphocytic pleocytosis with normal or mildly elevated protein and normal glucose. The illness is usually self-limited and managed supportively, with antibiotics started only until bacterial meningitis is excluded; etiologies include enteroviruses and other viruses such as mumps, herpes simplex, varicella-zoster, and arboviruses.

countershock.definition: An electrical shock delivered to the heart to terminate a life-threatening arrhythmia (e.g., ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia) and restore a normal rhythm; delivered by an external defibrillator (unsynchronized) or, when needed, synchronized cardioversion.

countertransference.definition: A clinician's emotional reactions to a patient, typically stemming from the clinician's own unresolved conflicts or past experiences, that can influence judgment, perception, and behavior in the therapeutic encounter.

counterconditioning.definition: A behavioral therapy technique in which an undesirable response to a stimulus is replaced with a more desirable response by pairing the stimulus with an incompatible, positive response (often relaxation or safety), thereby reducing the original reaction.

countercurrent.definition: Two fluid streams move in opposite directions to maximize the exchange of heat, ions, or water between them; a countercurrent exchange mechanism seen in the kidney (loop of Henle and vasa recta) and in fish gills.

countercurrent multiplication.definition: A renal mechanism by which active reabsorption of NaCl in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle (water-impermeable) creates a hyperosmotic medullary interstitium; as filtrate moves down the water-permeable descending limb it loses water and concentrates, and as it moves up the ascending limb more NaCl is reabsorbed, amplifying the gradient. This osmotic gradient enables the collecting ducts to concentrate urine.

bigeminal rhythm.definition: A cardiac rhythm pattern in which every normal heartbeat is followed by a premature (ectopic) beat, producing a regular two-beat cycle; most commonly due to premature ventricular contractions (ventricular bigeminy).

coupled pacing.definition: A pacing method in which a stimulus is delivered at a fixed coupling interval after a preceding intrinsic or paced beat, so the artificial beat is temporally linked to the ongoing rhythm; commonly used in electrophysiology testing and pacemaker programming to assess conduction or to entrain tachyarrhythmias.

coxa.definition: The hip region; the area where the femur articulates with the pelvis to form the hip joint, and, in anatomy, the hip bone (os coxa) that makes up part of the pelvic girdle.

coxa magna.definition: An abnormal enlargement of the femoral head (the ball of the hip joint).

coxa plana.definition: A condition in which the femoral head becomes flattened (loss of spherical contour) due to osteochondrosis/ischemic necrosis of the capital femoral epiphysis, typically in children, causing hip pain and restricted range of motion.

coxa valga.definition: A deformity of the hip in which the femoral neck–shaft angle is increased beyond the normal range (typically greater than about 135 degrees), resulting in a more vertical femoral neck; it can be congenital or acquired and may lead to altered hip biomechanics, limp or abnormal gait, potential leg‑length discrepancy, and hip instability.

coxa vara luxans.definition: A hip deformity in which the femoral neck–shaft angle is decreased (coxa vara) and the femoral head is dislocated (luxated) from the acetabulum.

coxal articulation.definition: A synovial ball-and-socket joint between the acetabulum of the os coxae and the femoral head, allowing multiaxial movement (flexion/extension, abduction/adduction, internal/external rotation, circumduction) and stabilized by the joint capsule, ligaments, and the acetabular labrum.

head of the femur.definition: The rounded proximal end of the femur that articulates with the acetabulum to form the hip joint; it is covered with articular cartilage and connected to the femur by the femoral neck.

courvoisier's law.definition: A palpable, distended gallbladder in a patient with jaundice suggests malignant obstruction of the biliary tract (e.g., pancreatic head carcinoma) rather than gallstone disease.

cowper's syringocele.definition: A cystic dilation of the ducts of Cowper's glands (bulbourethral glands) within the bulbar urethra, often due to ductal obstruction; it may communicate with the urethral lumen and can cause obstructive urinary symptoms or be asymptomatic.

cowper's cyst.definition: A cyst of the bulbourethral (Cowper) gland, typically a benign retention cyst caused by obstruction of the gland’s ducts, leading to accumulation of secretions and a perineal or periurethral mass.

vaccinia.definition: A large, enveloped double-stranded DNA virus of the Orthopoxvirus genus, used as the live vaccine agent for smallpox vaccination.

variola.definition: Smallpox, a disease that has been eliminated in the world.

cat pox.definition: A poxvirus infection in cats, historically attributed to cowpox-like viruses; characterized by vesicular or crusted skin lesions (often on the face, ears, or limbs), sometimes with fever, and typically self-limiting with supportive care. Zoonotic transmission to humans can occur but is uncommon.

uteroplacental apoplexy.definition: Premature separation of the placenta from the uterine wall before delivery, typically presenting with vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain, and possibly causing fetal distress or demise. Also known as placental abruption.

intervillous space.definition: A space in the placenta around the chorionic villi that contains maternal blood and bathes the villi, allowing exchange of gases, nutrients, and wastes between maternal and fetal blood across the placental barrier.

fetal vessels.definition: Blood vessels that comprise the fetus's circulatory system, including the two umbilical arteries and one umbilical vein, linking the fetus to the placenta to exchange gases, nutrients, and wastes; part of fetal circulation and connected to shunts such as the ductus venosus, foramen ovale, and ductus arteriosus.

uterine musculature.definition: Smooth muscle layer of the uterus (the myometrium) responsible for rhythmic contractions during menstruation and labor; composed of interlacing smooth muscle fibers arranged in inner longitudinal, middle circular, and outer longitudinal layers surrounding the endometrium.

ejaculatory orifice.definition: The opening of the ejaculatory duct(s) into the prostatic urethra, through which semen is expelled into the urethral lumen during ejaculation.

utricle.definition: A sensory organ in the vestibular system of the inner ear that detects linear acceleration and head position relative to gravity, via its horizontally oriented macula and otoliths (statoconia); one of the otolith organs along with the saccule.

cowden's disease.definition: A genetic disorder (PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome) characterized by multiple hamartomas and mucocutaneous lesions, with increased risk of breast, thyroid (often follicular), and endometrial cancers; caused by germline mutations in the PTEN tumor suppressor gene.

hamartoma syndrome.definition: A descriptive term for a spectrum of disorders characterized by multiple hamartomas (benign, disorganized overgrowths) in various tissues, often due to germline PTEN mutations; included conditions such as Cowden syndrome and Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndrome, with mucocutaneous lesions, developmental abnormalities, and an increased risk of certain cancers.

gingival fibromatosis.definition: Benign, often hereditary gingival overgrowth in which dense fibrous connective tissue enlarges the gums (with minimal inflammatory change), producing firm, thick gingival tissue that can impair tooth eruption; managed with periodontal therapy and surgical reduction when indicated.

hemangiomas.definition: A benign vascular tumor composed of an abnormal proliferation of blood vessels; most commonly occurs in infancy as a red to purple skin lesion (infantile hemangioma) that typically enlarges during the first months and gradually involutes over years, with treatment reserved for complications, functional impairment, or cosmetic concerns.

postpubertal fibroadenomatous breast enl.definition: A benign, postpubertal breast condition in which diffuse or multifocal fibroepithelial proliferation leads to bilateral breast enlargement; typically estrogen-influenced and self-limiting, with management ranging from observation to biopsy or excision if masses are symptomatic or suspicious.

congenital polycystic disease.definition: An inherited disorder characterized by the development of multiple kidney cysts present at birth or in early infancy, leading to enlarged, echogenic kidneys and progressive renal insufficiency; the classic form is autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD), which may be associated with congenital hepatic fibrosis.

c-peptide.definition: A peptide fragment produced during the processing of proinsulin in pancreatic beta cells; released in equimolar amounts with insulin. It serves as a marker of endogenous insulin production and beta-cell function because it is present with insulin but is absent from most therapeutic insulin preparations.

c-peptide test.definition: A blood test that measures C-peptide, a byproduct of endogenous insulin production; it reflects how much insulin the pancreas is making and helps assess beta-cell function and differentiate types of diabetes or evaluate hypoglycemia.

proinsulin.definition: A single-chain precursor of insulin produced in pancreatic beta cells; it is proteolytically processed to yield mature insulin (A and B chains) and the C-peptide, which is released into the bloodstream.

insulinoma.definition: A pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that autonomously secretes insulin, causing recurrent endogenous hypoglycemia and neuroglycopenic symptoms; most are benign but can be malignant, with treatment typically involving surgical resection and management of hypoglycemia.

factitious hypoglycemia.definition: Hypoglycemia caused by deliberate self-administration of insulin or other hypoglycemic agents in a patient without a genuine medical indication, a form of factitious disorder (factitious disorder imposed on self) intended to assume the sick role.

radical pancreatectomy.definition: Surgical removal of the entire pancreas, usually with en bloc resection of adjacent organs to achieve oncologic clearance (often including the spleen, duodenum, part of the stomach, and bile ducts); results in lifelong insulin-dependent diabetes and pancreatic exocrine insufficiency due to loss of pancreatic function.

pancreas transplant.definition: A surgical procedure that places a donor pancreas into a recipient to restore insulin production and regulate blood glucose, usually with concurrent kidney transplantation; requires lifelong immunosuppression and carries risks such as rejection, infection, and graft failure.

creatine kinase.definition: An enzyme that leaks into the bloodstream in high amounts if a muscle is damaged. Can be used to detect heart attack or muscle damage from other diseases.

continuous positive pressure breathing.definition: A mode of respiratory support that delivers a constant positive airway pressure throughout the breathing cycle to keep the airways open during spontaneous respiration; typically administered via a nasal or full-face mask and used to treat obstructive sleep apnea and other forms of hypoventilation or respiratory distress.

calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate.definition: A calcium-containing pyrophosphate crystal that deposits in joint cartilage and synovium, forming rhomboid-shaped, positively birefringent crystals and causing CPPD deposition disease (pseudogout).

cranial arteritis.definition: Inflammation and damage to blood vessels supplying blood to the head and neck. Also called giant cell arteritis.

temporal arteritis.definition: When the arteries in your head, neck and arms are swollen, so that the blood does not flow well. Also called giant cell arteritis.

loss of libido.definition: A decrease in sexual desire or interest that may be temporary or persistent. It can result from hormonal changes, medical illnesses, medications, psychological factors such as depression or stress, substance use, or relationship issues; when persistent and distressing, it may meet criteria for hypoactive sexual desire disorder.

craniopharyngioma.definition: Benign, slow-growing epithelial tumor in the sellar/suprasellar region arising from remnants of Rathke's pouch; most commonly occurs in children and young adults; can cause pituitary hormone deficiencies and visual disturbances; often cystic with calcifications on imaging; treated with surgical resection, with adjuvant radiotherapy depending on extent.

rathke's pouch tumor.definition: A benign, slow-growing neoplasm arising from remnants of Rathke's pouch in the sellar/suprasellar region, typically presenting with headaches, visual disturbance, and pituitary hormone deficiencies; histology shows cystic and solid components, with adamantinomatous type featuring enamel-like epithelium and "wet keratin" (often with calcifications) and papillary type displaying papillary architecture.

craniopharyngeal duct tumor.definition: A benign, slow-growing tumor of the sellar/suprasellar region derived from embryologic remnants of the craniopharyngeal duct (Rathke's pouch); it typically presents with visual disturbance and pituitary dysfunction and often contains cystic components with calcifications on imaging.

craniectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which a portion of the skull is removed to relieve intracranial pressure or to access the brain, with the bone flap not being immediately replaced (unlike a craniotomy); the removed bone may be stored for later cranioplasty.

cranioplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair a skull defect by replacing or reconstructing the cranial bone using autologous bone grafts or implants to restore skull contour and protect the brain, often performed after craniectomy or traumatic injury.

craniopharyngeal.definition: Relating to the skull (cranium) and the pharynx; in embryology, used to describe structures that connect the developing brain to the oral cavity.

craniofacial.definition: Relating to the skull (cranium) and facial bones; pertaining to the bones and structures of the head and face.

craniofacial dysostosis.definition: An umbrella term for disorders featuring craniosynostosis—premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures—leading to abnormal skull and facial development, frequently with midface hypoplasia and associated ocular/airway anomalies.

cranium.definition: The bones that are part of the head.

cranial.definition: Relating to the skull (cranium) or directed toward the head.

hypophysis.definition: The pituitary gland, a small endocrine gland at the base of the brain connected to the hypothalamus by the infundibulum; it consists of the anterior lobe (adenohypophysis) and posterior lobe (neurohypophysis) and secretes hormones that regulate growth, metabolism, reproduction, and the activity of other endocrine glands (thyroid, adrenal, gonads).

hypophyseal stalk.definition: A slender neural stalk (infundibulum) connecting the hypothalamus to the pituitary gland; it contains the axons of hypothalamic neurons that terminate in the posterior pituitary and carries the hypothalamic-hypophyseal portal vessels linking the hypothalamus to the anterior pituitary.

exophthalmos.definition: Forward displacement of the eyeball(s) from the orbit due to increased orbital contents or a space-occupying lesion, resulting in protruding eyes; most commonly associated with thyroid eye disease (Graves' ophthalmopathy).

hypertelorism.definition: An abnormally increased distance between the eyes due to widening of the orbits; commonly seen as a feature of craniofacial anomalies and congenital syndromes.

parrot-beaked nose.definition: A nasal deformity characterized by a beak-like, downward-curved projection of the nasal tip and dorsum, giving a parrot-beak appearance; commonly due to congenital malformation or trauma and may be corrected surgically.

hypoplastic maxilla.definition: Underdevelopment of the maxilla (upper jaw), resulting in an underdeveloped or retruded midface; may be associated with craniofacial anomalies and malocclusion.

mandibular prognathism.definition: A skeletal malocclusion in which the lower jaw (mandible) projects anteriorly beyond the upper jaw, resulting in an underbite (Class III malocclusion); may be due to excess mandibular growth, maxillary deficiency, or both.

lambdoid suture.definition: A dense fibrous joint between the occipital bone and the two parietal bones at the posterior skull, forming a lambda-shaped cranial suture that allows growth in infancy and typically ossifies with age.

lambda.definition: A type of immunoglobulin light chain; one of the two light-chain isotypes that pair with heavy chains to form antibodies; abnormal levels or ratios can indicate monoclonal plasma cell disorders.

granular foveolae.definition: Small pit-like depressions in a mucous membrane whose lining cells have granular cytoplasm due to secretory mucin granules; typically used to describe the gastric foveolae (gastric pits) lined by mucous (foveolar) cells.

middle meningeal artery.definition: A large branch of the maxillary artery that enters the cranial cavity through the foramen spinosum, runs in the epidural space between skull and dura mater, and supplies the dura mater and calvaria; rupture can cause an epidural hematoma.

craniometaphyseal dysplasia.definition: A rare genetic skeletal disorder characterized by progressive hyperostosis (excessive bone growth) of the skull and facial bones and metaphyseal widening of the long bones, often causing facial deformities, dental eruption problems, and potential cranial nerve compression.

freeman-sheldon syndrome.definition: A rare autosomal dominant distal arthrogryposis syndrome characterized by severe congenital contractures of the distal limbs and distinctive facial features (“whistling face” with pursed lips and micrognathia), often due to MYH3 gene mutations.

craniocervical.definition: Relating to the skull (cranium) and the cervical spine (neck); specifically, pertaining to the craniocervical region and the craniocervical junction where the occipital bone articulates with the atlas (C1) and axis (C2).

craniocervical junction.definition: An anatomical region at the base of the skull where the occipital bone articulates with the first two cervical vertebrae (atlas C1 and axis C2), comprising the occipitoatlantal and atlantoaxial joints, their ligaments (e.g., alar and cruciform), and surrounding neurovascular structures; it forms the transition between skull and spine and enables head movement (nodding and rotation) while protecting the brainstem and upper spinal cord.

craniotabes.definition: A softening of the skull bones in infants that yields to gentle pressure, due to delayed or defective ossification; commonly associated with rickets and sometimes congenital syphilis, and can be a normal finding in newborns.

craniospinal.definition: Relating to the brain and spinal cord; involving or affecting both the cranium and the spinal canal.

craniospinal therapy.definition: A radiotherapy regimen delivering radiation to the entire brain and spinal canal to treat or prevent tumor spread within the cerebrospinal fluid, commonly used for medulloblastoma and leptomeningeal metastases.

craniosacral therapy.definition: A form of alternative medicine in which practitioners use very light touch on the skull and sacrum to purportedly release restrictions in the craniosacral system; proponents claim it improves pain, mobility, and well‑being, but there is no robust evidence of clinical benefit, and it is not recommended as a treatment for medical conditions.

crankcase-spool catheter.definition: Not a standard medical term; there is no established definition in reliable medical references. If you have a source or context for this term, please share it and I can help interpret.

pubic lice.definition: A parasitic infestation of the pubic region by the crab louse (Phthirus pubis) that feeds on blood and causes intense itching; transmitted mainly through sexual contact or close personal contact; treated with topical pediculicides (e.g., permethrin or pyrethrins) and by washing clothing and bedding.

pediculosis.definition: Infestation with lice (ectoparasitic insects of the order Phthiraptera) on the scalp, body, or pubic region, typically causing pruritus and possible secondary bacterial infection.

pthirus pubis.definition: A pubic louse (Phthirus pubis), a small crab louse that infests human pubic hair and other coarse body hair, causing pediculosis pubis. Transmission is primarily through sexual contact or close body contact. Symptoms include intense itching in the affected area. Diagnosis is by visualizing lice or nits on hair; treatment involves topical pediculicides (e.g., 1% permethrin creme rinse) and washing of clothing and bedding; sexual partners should be treated to prevent reinfestation.

pediculus pubis.definition: A parasitic louse that infests pubic and other coarse body hair, causing pediculosis pubis (pubic lice); transmitted mainly by sexual contact; treated with topical pediculicides and thorough laundering of clothing and bedding.

crack cocaine.definition: Crack cocaine is a potent, free-base (smokable) form of cocaine derived from cocaine hydrochloride; it produces a rapid, intense but short-lasting euphoric and stimulant effect, with a high potential for addiction and serious cardiovascular, neurological, and psychiatric complications.

crack baby.definition: A historic, stigmatizing, nonmedical label for an infant who was exposed to cocaine in utero (often with other substances). It is not a medical diagnosis; possible neonatal effects include low birth weight and prematurity, and neurobehavioral signs such as irritability, feeding difficulties, and sleep disturbances; long-term outcomes vary and depend on multiple factors including continued substance exposure and the postnatal environment.

permethrin.definition: A synthetic pyrethroid insecticide used topically to treat ectoparasitic infections such as head lice and scabies; it disrupts insect voltage-gated sodium channels in nerve membranes, causing paralysis and death. Available in creams, lotions, and shampoos; generally well tolerated but can cause local irritation or hypersensitivity in some individuals.

pyrethrin.definition: A natural insecticide derived from chrysanthemum flowers (pyrethrum), comprising several pyrethrin esters that disrupt the insect nervous system by prolonging sodium-channel opening, causing paralysis; used in pesticides and pediculicidal products; relatively low toxicity to mammals but can cause skin or eye irritation or allergic reactions.

uti.definition: An infection of the urinary tract caused by microorganisms (most often bacteria such as Escherichia coli), affecting any part from the urethra to the kidneys; commonly presents with burning on urination, increased frequency and urgency, and suprapubic pain, and may include fever with upper tract involvement; diagnosed by urinalysis and/or culture and treated with antibiotics.

crackle.definition: A discontinuous, brief lung sound heard on auscultation, typically during inspiration, caused by the sudden opening of small airways or by movement of fluid/secretions in the airways; also referred to as rales; can be described as fine (high-pitched) or coarse (low-pitched).

rale.definition: A crackling or bubbling sound heard on lung auscultation, caused by air moving through fluid-filled or collapsed small airways; commonly associated with conditions such as pulmonary edema, pneumonia, or interstitial lung disease.

rhonchus.definition: A coarse, low-pitched rattling breath sound heard on auscultation, produced by secretions or obstruction in the large airways; often improved or cleared with coughing.

coarse crackle.definition: Low-pitched, discontinuous breath sounds heard during inspiration produced by air passing through secretions in the large airways; they are coarser and longer than fine crackles and may clear with coughing, commonly heard with bronchitis, pneumonia, or pulmonary edema.

cradle cap.definition: A type of dandruff that babies get.

seborrhea capitis.definition: A chronic inflammatory dermatitis of the scalp characterized by greasy, white to yellow scales (flakes), often with itching, frequently associated with overgrowth of Malassezia yeast.

crp.definition: A liver-produced protein; elevated levels indicate inflammation and may be associated with atherosclerosis (arterial clogging).

creatine.definition: A naturally occurring nitrogenous compound stored in skeletal muscle as phosphocreatine that donates a phosphate group to rapidly regenerate ATP during brief, high‑intensity exercise; synthesized endogenously and obtained from dietary sources such as meat and fish; commonly used as a dietary supplement to enhance athletic performance and lean body mass.

kinase.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate group from ATP to a substrate, commonly modulating the substrate's activity; protein kinases phosphorylate serine, threonine, or tyrosine residues.

phosphocreatine.definition: A high-energy phosphate reserve in muscle and other tissues that donates a phosphate group to ADP to rapidly regenerate ATP during brief, intense activity; a key component of the phosphagen energy system, synthesized from creatine and ATP by creatine kinase and replenished by dietary creatine or endogenous synthesis.

creatinuria.definition: An excretion of creatinine in the urine; used to assess renal function and to verify the completeness of urine collection (such as in 24-hour urine tests).

creatorrhea.definition: Discharge of creatinine in the stool; a rare term typically indicating urinary contamination of the bowel, such as via a urinary–bowel fistula.

cremaster.definition: A thin layer of striated muscle surrounding the testis and spermatic cord, derived from the internal oblique, that elevates the testis in response to cold or tactile stimulation and participates in the cremasteric reflex.

cremasteric.definition: Relating to the cremaster muscle, the skeletal muscle surrounding the testis that elevates the testis.

cricoid.definition: A ring-shaped hyaline cartilage that forms the inferior part of the larynx, located below the thyroid cartilage and above the trachea; it is the only complete ring of cartilage in the larynx and provides support and an articulation surface for the arytenoid cartilages.

cricoid_pressure.definition: A maneuver in which firm pressure is applied to the cricoid cartilage against the vertebral bodies to occlude the esophagus, intended to prevent regurgitation and aspiration during induction of anesthesia or rapid sequence intubation.

cricoidectomy.definition: Surgical removal of part or all of the cricoid cartilage, typically to remove a lesion in the larynx or subglottic region or to relieve airway obstruction, often requiring reconstruction.

cricoarytenoid.definition: Relating to the larynx, specifically the cricoid and arytenoid cartilages; it often refers to the cricoarytenoid joint, a synovial joint between these cartilages that allows movement of the arytenoid cartilages to abduct or adduct the vocal folds.

crepitus.definition: Grating, grinding, or popping sound or feeling made when a joint is moved.

crepitant.definition: Having a crackling sensation or sound on palpation or auscultation, typically due to air or gas in tissues (crepitus) or to crackling lung sounds.

crescendo.definition: A gradual increase in the loudness or intensity of a sound, signal, or symptom; in medicine, used to describe a murmur, bruit, or symptom that becomes progressively louder over time.

pectoris.definition: Latin for "of the chest"; used in medical terms to denote chest-related conditions, such as chest pain due to reduced blood flow to the heart.

raynaud.definition: Episodic vasospasm of the small arteries and arterioles of the extremities, typically the fingers and toes, causing transient color changes (pale, then blue, then red) with numbness or tingling and coldness; usually triggered by cold or emotional stress and can be primary (idiopathic) or secondary to autoimmune/connective-tissue diseases.

phenomenon.definition: A fact or event that can be observed or measured; in medicine, an observable sign, symptom, or physiological process seen during examination or investigation.

dysfunction.definition: Impaired or abnormal functioning of a bodily organ, system, or physiological process, resulting in reduced or abnormal performance relative to normal physiology.

sclerodactyly.definition: Thickening, hardening, and tightening of the skin of the fingers (and sometimes toes), typically due to excessive collagen deposition in systemic sclerosis (scleroderma), often with reduced finger mobility.

cretin.definition: A historical, now obsolete term for a person with severe congenital hypothyroidism, resulting in profound intellectual disability and stunted physical development if untreated; early thyroid hormone replacement can prevent or lessen these outcomes.

cretinism.definition: A congenital hypothyroid condition resulting from insufficient thyroid hormone at birth (often due to thyroid dysgenesis or severe maternal iodine deficiency) that leads to severe intellectual disability and growth retardation, with characteristic coarse facial features and developmental delay.

cretinous.definition: Relating to cretinism; marked by severe mental and physical retardation due to congenital hypothyroidism; also used colloquially to mean very stupid or foolish.

creutzfeldt-jakob.definition: A rare, untreatable, rapid form of dementia that is fatal.

prion.definition: A protein that is not made (or "folded") correctly that can make other proteins fold work wrong. Can be spread by infection.

cribriform.definition: Having many small perforations or openings, like a sieve. In anatomy, used to describe a sieve-like structure such as the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone, which contains numerous foramina for olfactory nerve fibers.

plate.definition: A flat, thin, rigid structure; in orthopedic surgery, a bone plate is a flat metal implant screwed to a fractured bone to stabilize it during healing.

ethmoid.definition: An irregular, light, spongy bone between the orbits that forms part of the medial orbital wall and the roof of the nasal cavity; contains the ethmoid air cells (ethmoid sinuses) and features the cribriform plate for olfactory nerves, the perpendicular plate forming part of the nasal septum, and the superior and middle nasal conchae.

genital.definition: Relating to the reproductive organs; the external and internal organs involved in sexual reproduction.

spermatic.definition: Relating to sperm or to the structures of the male reproductive system, especially the testis and the spermatic cord.

round.definition: Shaped like a circle or sphere; circular or spherical in outline. In clinical context, used to describe a lesion or mass that is round and well-demarcated.

death.definition: The permanent cessation of all vital biological functions necessary to sustain life, typically defined clinically as irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions, or irreversible cessation of all brain activity (brain death).

sudden.definition: Happening abruptly and unexpectedly, with rapid onset of symptoms or events and little to no warning.

bacterial.definition: Relating to bacteria (the single-celled microorganisms); or caused by bacteria.

neoplastic.definition: Relating to neoplasia (abnormal, uncontrolled growth of cells) or to a neoplasm; describing tissue that forms a new, abnormal growth that may be benign or malignant.

sedimentation.definition: Process by which solid particles suspended in a liquid settle to the bottom under the influence of gravity, forming a sediment.

tracheal.definition: Relating to the trachea, the windpipe that conducts air from the larynx to the bronchi.

tubes.definition: A hollow cylindrical medical device, either flexible or rigid, inserted into the body to convey or drain fluids or gases, establish or maintain a lumen or airway, or deliver medications or nutrition.

iodized.definition: Containing iodine; commonly refers to salt to which iodine has been added to prevent iodine deficiency disorders.

salt.definition: A chemical compound consisting of positively charged ions and negatively charged ions; formed by the neutralization of an acid with a base. In medicine, electrolyte salts such as sodium chloride are important for fluid balance, nerve transmission, and muscle function.

silver.definition: A chemical element (symbol Ag, atomic number 47); a soft, white, lustrous metal with antimicrobial properties used in some medical products such as wound dressings, creams, and implants.

nitrate.definition: A salt or ester of nitric acid; the nitrate ion (NO3−) forms inorganic nitrates (e.g., sodium nitrate) and organic nitrate esters (e.g., nitroglycerin) that act as nitric oxide donors to relax vascular smooth muscle and dilate blood vessels.

pseudohypertrophic.definition: Relating to apparent muscle enlargement due to fatty and fibrous replacement of muscle tissue, rather than true muscle fiber growth; the muscle is typically weak despite its enlarged appearance (commonly seen in Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy).

dystrophy.definition: A disorder characterized by progressive degeneration or weakness of tissue or organ, typically due to defective development, nutrition, or genetic factors; commonly refers to muscular dystrophy, a group of inherited diseases causing progressive muscle weakness and wasting.

muscular.definition: Relating to muscles; composed of muscle tissue or characterized by well-developed musculature.

myoclonus.definition: A sudden, brief, involuntary jerk of a muscle or group of muscles (positive myoclonus) or a brief loss of muscle tone (negative myoclonus), usually due to a brief discharge in the nervous system; can occur in normal conditions (e.g., startle, sleep onset) or in association with neurological or metabolic disorders.

cricopharyngeal.definition: Relating to the cricopharyngeus muscle, the part of the inferior pharyngeal constrictor that forms the upper esophageal sphincter at the junction of the pharynx and esophagus; it maintains tonic contraction to prevent air entry and reflux and relaxes transiently during swallowing to allow passage of the bolus.

crimean-congo-hemorrhagic-fever.definition: Tick-borne viral hemorrhagic fever caused by Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus; transmitted mainly by Hyalomma ticks and through contact with blood or tissues from infected animals, with possible person-to-person spread via infected body fluids. Onset is abrupt with high fever, myalgias, headache, and GI symptoms; severe cases may progress to hemorrhagic manifestations and multi-organ failure. Case-fatality rates vary by region; no widely available vaccine exists, and management is supportive (ribavirin used in some cases).

rapid-sequence-intubation.definition: A technique to secure the airway by rapidly inducing unconsciousness and paralysis to enable prompt endotracheal intubation, aiming to minimize aspiration risk and minimize ventilation between induction and tube placement; typically involves a fast-acting induction agent and a neuromuscular blocker.

cricoid-pressure.definition: A technique used during anesthesia induction in which firm backward pressure is applied to the cricoid cartilage to compress the esophagus against the cervical spine, with the aim of preventing regurgitation and aspiration of gastric contents. Also known as the Sellick maneuver. Its usefulness is debated, and improper application can hinder ventilation or airway management.

laryngoscopy.definition: An examination of the larynx performed with a laryngoscope (direct: rigid or flexible endoscope; indirect: mirror) to visualize the vocal cords and airway and to diagnose laryngeal conditions or assist intubation.

sellicks-maneuver.definition: A technique used during anesthesia induction in which firm pressure is applied to the cricoid cartilage to occlude the esophagus against the vertebral column, thereby reducing the risk of regurgitation and aspiration of gastric contents (cricoid pressure).

cricopharyngeus.definition: A muscle forming the upper esophageal sphincter at the junction of the pharynx and esophagus; it maintains resting tone and relaxes during swallowing to allow passage of the bolus.

belching.definition: The audible expulsion of gas from the stomach through the mouth (eructation), typically resulting from swallowed air or gas produced during digestion; it can be a normal phenomenon or associated with conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux or aerophagia.

cricothyroid-membrane.definition: A midline fibrous membrane spanning the gap between the cricoid and thyroid cartilages of the larynx; forms part of the laryngeal framework and is a common site for emergency airway access (cricothyrotomy).

cricothyroid-ligament.definition: A fibrous membrane spanning the anterior cricoid and thyroid cartilages, forming part of the laryngeal framework; the midline portion is the median cricothyroid ligament, and it is the site used for emergency cricothyrotomy.

thyroid-cartilage.definition: The unpaired hyaline cartilage of the larynx forming the anterior wall and the laryngeal prominence (Adam’s apple); it protects the glottis and vocal cords and serves as an attachment for ligaments and muscles, with two laminae fused anteriorly and superior and inferior cornua.

cricoid-cartilage.definition: A ring-shaped hyaline cartilage forming the lower part of the larynx, located inferior to the thyroid cartilage and superior to the trachea; it is the only complete ring around the airway and serves as a structural support and attachment point for laryngeal muscles and joints (e.g., with the thyroid cartilage).

thyroid-gland.definition: A two-lobed gland located in the front of the neck below the larynx (voice box). It secretes hormones that help regulate the body's metabolism and calcium balance.

sternal-notch.definition: A shallow indentation on the anterior chest at the superior border of the sternum, between the medial ends of the clavicles; a surface landmark for the trachea and major mediastinal vessels.

cricotracheal-ligament.definition: A fibrous band extending from the inferior border of the cricoid cartilage to the superior border of the first tracheal ring, forming the cricotracheal membrane and anchoring the larynx to the trachea.

crigler-najjar-syndrome.definition: An autosomal recessive inherited disorder caused by deficiency or absence of hepatic UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT1A1), leading to severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Type I features little to no UGT1A1 activity with persistent neonatal jaundice and a high risk of kernicterus, often requiring liver transplantation. Type II has partial enzyme activity and a milder course, sometimes responsive to phenobarbital.

glucuronyl-transferase.definition: An enzyme that transfers the glucuronyl (glucuronic acid) moiety from UDP-glucuronate to a substrate, forming a glucuronide conjugate; a key step in detoxification and excretion of drugs and bilirubin (UDP-glucuronosyltransferase family).

unconjugated-bilirubin.definition: Bilirubin that has not yet been conjugated with glucuronic acid in the liver; it is fat-soluble, circulates mainly bound to albumin in the bloodstream, and is produced from heme breakdown before hepatic conjugation.

neonatal-hyperbilirubinemia.definition: Elevated serum bilirubin in a newborn causing jaundice; commonly due to immature hepatic bilirubin conjugation and/or increased bilirubin production, generally benign but may require phototherapy or exchange transfusion if levels are high.

crohns-disease.definition: A chronic, relapsing inflammatory bowel disease characterized by transmural inflammation that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract, most often the terminal ileum and colon, causing abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, and complications such as fistulas, strictures, and malnutrition.
