regional-enteritis.definition: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn disease) characterized by transmural, segmental inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract, most often involving the terminal ileum and/or colon, with skip lesions and potential fistulas, strictures, and abscess formation.

ulcerative-colitis.definition: Causes inflammation and sores (also called ulcers), in the lining of the rectum and colon.

ileitis.definition: Inflammation of the ileum, the final portion of the small intestine. It can result from infection, inflammatory bowel disease (especially Crohn disease), ischemia, or drug-induced reactions; symptoms typically include abdominal pain and diarrhea.

cronkhite-canada-syndrome.definition: An extremely rare, nonhereditary syndrome characterized by diffuse hamartomatous polyposis throughout the gastrointestinal tract, chronic diarrhea with weight loss, and ectodermal changes including alopecia, onychodystrophy, and skin hyperpigmentation.

cromolyn-sodium.definition: A mast cell stabilizer that prevents degranulation and release of mediators (e.g., histamine) from mast cells; used prophylactically for allergic asthma, allergic rhinitis, and conjunctivitis, with forms for inhalation, nasal spray, or ophthalmic administration; not for acute bronchospasm.

cromoglycic-acid.definition: A mast cell stabilizer used to prevent allergic reactions by inhibiting degranulation and release of mediators (e.g., histamine) from mast cells; used prophylactically in allergic conditions such as bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, and conjunctivitis; administered topically (eye drops, nasal spray) or by inhalation and generally has limited systemic absorption.

cromer-blood-group.definition: A rare, ISBT-recognized human blood group system defined by a set of antigens on red blood cells; antibodies against these antigens can cause alloimmune hemolytic transfusion reactions or hemolytic disease of the newborn and are detected in serologic compatibility testing.

nairovirus.definition: A genus of enveloped, negative-sense, segmented RNA viruses in the family Nairoviridae, transmitted primarily by ticks; includes pathogens such as Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus and Nairobi sheep disease virus, causing hemorrhagic fever in humans and disease in livestock.

bunyaviridae.definition: A family of enveloped, negative-sense, single-stranded RNA viruses with segmented genomes (typically tripartite: S, M, L). Members were largely arthropod- or rodent-borne and included genera such as Hantavirus, Orthobunyavirus, Phlebovirus, Nairovirus, and Tospovirus; many species cause human or animal diseases.

crista-ampullaris.definition: The sensory epithelium within the ampulla of each semicircular canal, containing hair cells embedded in the gelatinous cupula; it detects angular head acceleration and transduces it into neural signals via the vestibular nerve (CN VIII).

crista-galli.definition: A vertical midline projection of the ethmoid bone that rises from the cribriform plate in the anterior cranial fossa and serves as the attachment point for the falx cerebri (the dura mater).

crista-obliqua.definition: A crest (ridge) on a bone that runs obliquely; a site for muscle or ligament attachment. The term literally means "oblique crest."

crista-terminalis.definition: A prominent muscular ridge in the right atrium that marks the border between the smooth posterior sinus venarum and the anterior rough-walled atrium (containing pectinate muscles); it extends from the opening of the superior vena cava to the opening of the inferior vena cava and serves as a landmark for locating conduction tissue.

esophoria.definition: Latent inward deviation of an eye (nasal drift) that occurs when binocular fusion is interrupted; the eye tends to drift medially and is kept aligned by fusional vergence during normal binocular viewing.

amblyopia.definition: A condition in which one eye doesn't work properly with the brain, resulting in reduced vision in that eye; it is also called lazy eye.

crossed-extension-reflex.definition: A spinal withdrawal reflex in which noxious stimulation of one limb causes the stimulated limb to withdraw (flex) while the opposite limb extends to maintain posture; mediated by spinal circuits and used to assess spinal cord and corticospinal pathway integrity.

crossed-leg-palsy.definition: A compression neuropathy of the common peroneal nerve caused by prolonged crossing of the legs, leading to weakness of ankle dorsiflexion and toe extension (often foot drop), possible weakness of foot eversion, and sensory loss over the dorsum of the foot and the first web space.

cross-bite.definition: A dental malocclusion in which the upper teeth bite inside (mesially to) the lower teeth when the jaws are closed.

cross-eyed.definition: A colloquial term for strabismus, a condition in which the eyes are misaligned and do not look in the same direction at the same time. It can be constant or intermittent and may be due to problems with eye muscles, nerves, or refractive errors; untreated, it can lead to double vision (diplopia) or amblyopia (lazy eye) in children.

cross-hatch-grid.definition: A cross-hatch grid is a calibration and measurement tool consisting of two perpendicular sets of parallel lines that create a cross-hatched pattern, used in imaging and microscopy to assess scale, orientation, and spatial resolution or to aid morphometric quantification.

crossed-grid.definition: A radiographic grid arrangement consisting of two linear grids placed at right angles to each other to absorb scattered radiation from multiple directions, thereby improving image contrast; it increases patient dose and requires precise alignment, and is less commonly used today in favor of single focused grids or digital scatter-correction methods.

crocodile-shagreen.definition: A descriptive dermatologic term for a coarse, leather-like, grid-like or pebbled skin surface that resembles crocodile skin; used to describe certain textured patches or plaques (for example shagreen patches in tuberous sclerosis) and is not a diagnosis itself.

descemets-membrane.definition: A basement membrane produced by corneal endothelial cells, located between the stroma and the endothelium; it forms the endothelium’s basement membrane and helps maintain corneal structure and transparency, thickening with age.

bowmans-membrane.definition: An acellular, transparent layer of the cornea between the epithelium and stroma; the anterior limiting lamina (Bowman’s layer) composed of randomly arranged collagen fibers, providing structural support but not regenerating after injury.

protein-losing-enteropathy.definition: A disorder in which excessive amounts of plasma proteins are lost into the gastrointestinal tract due to mucosal disease or lymphatic obstruction, leading to hypoalbuminemia, edema, and potential immune or coagulation-related complications.

malabsorption.definition: A disorder in which the small intestine absorbs nutrients inadequately from the diet, resulting in malnutrition, weight loss, and deficiencies of vitamins and minerals (often with steatorrhea when fat absorption is affected).

toxic-megacolon.definition: A life-threatening complication of severe inflammatory or infectious colitis characterized by acute nonobstructive dilation of the colon (often with maximal dilation >6 cm) with systemic toxicity (fever, tachycardia, leukocytosis, dehydration) and risk of perforation; requires urgent medical management and often surgical intervention.

fistulas.definition: A connection that is not normal between 2 organs or blood vessels. You can be born with a fistula or it can develop after surgery or a disease.

bronchial-asthma.definition: A chronic inflammatory disorder of the airways characterized by episodic reversible airflow obstruction, bronchial hyperresponsiveness, and symptoms such as wheeze, cough, chest tightness, and shortness of breath, often triggered by allergens, irritants, infections, or exercise; obstruction typically improves with bronchodilators and anti-inflammatory therapy.

mucous-membranes.definition: Mucous membranes (mucosae) form moist linings of cavities and passages that communicate with the exterior, including the mouth, nose, respiratory, digestive, urinary, and reproductive tracts. They consist of an epithelium over a connective tissue lamina propria and mucus-secreting cells or glands; mucus moistens and protects surfaces, traps pathogens, and aids in lubrication, absorption, and secretion.

neuroepithelium.definition: An epithelium of neural origin that lines the neural tube's ventricular system (the ependyma) and serves as the proliferative neural progenitor layer giving rise to neurons and glial cells.

vestibular-nerve.definition: A sensory branch of the vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII) that carries afferent information about head position and movement from the inner ear’s vestibular apparatus (utricle, saccule, and semicircular canals) to the brainstem and cerebellum, enabling balance and the vestibulo-ocular reflex; it consists of superior and inferior divisions.

decay-accelerating-factor.definition: A cell-surface glycoprotein that regulate the complement system by accelerating the decay of C3/C5 convertases (C4b2a and C3bBb), thereby preventing progression of the complement cascade and protecting host cells from complement-mediated lysis; it is anchored to the membrane by a GPI linkage.

arbo-virus.definition: A virus transmitted by mosquitoes or other member of the arthropod phylum.

acute laryngotracheobronchitis.definition: An acute viral infection causing inflammation and edema of the larynx, trachea, and bronchi (croup), most common in children, presenting with a barky cough, hoarseness, and inspiratory stridor, with varying degrees of respiratory distress.

acute epiglottitis.definition: An acute, potentially life-threatening infection and inflammation of the epiglottis (and surrounding supraglottic tissues) causing rapid airway swelling and obstruction; it most often affects children and presents with fever, severe throat pain, odynophagia, muffled voice, drooling, and inspiratory stridor; requires urgent airway management and empiric antibiotics.

laryngeal obstruction.definition: Blockage or narrowing of the larynx that impedes airflow, leading to stridor and respiratory distress; causes include edema, foreign body, trauma, infection, allergic reactions, or tumor, and it may require emergency airway management.

subepiglottic narrowing.definition: A narrowing of the laryngeal airway in the subepiglottic region (just below the epiglottis), resulting in reduced airway caliber and potential obstruction; causes include edema, inflammation, infection, trauma, or congenital stenosis, and it may be seen on endoscopy or imaging.

humidity.definition: Amount of water vapor in the surrounding air; commonly described as relative humidity (RH), the percent of the maximum water vapor the air can hold at a given temperature. Abnormal humidity levels can dry mucous membranes, irritate airways, and affect wound healing and infection risk.

nebulizer.definition: A device that provides medicine for asthma in the form of a mist.

cold mist tent.definition: A historical respiratory therapy device in which the patient is enclosed in a tent that delivers a fine, cold, humidified aerosol mist to the airways to moisten secretions and ease breathing; now largely obsolete.

parainfluenza virus type 1.definition: A human paramyxovirus (HPIV-1) that causes respiratory tract infections, most notably croup (laryngotracheobronchitis) in children; it is an enveloped, negative-sense, single-stranded RNA virus in the Paramyxoviridae family, transmitted by respiratory droplets.

influenza a.definition: An enveloped, negative-sense, segmented RNA virus of the Orthomyxoviridae family; a subtype of influenza viruses that infects humans and many animals, capable of antigenic drift and shift, and responsible for seasonal influenza outbreaks and occasional pandemics.

influenza b.definition: Influenza B is a type of influenza virus in the family Orthomyxoviridae that infects humans, causing seasonal flu; unlike influenza A, it has no significant animal reservoir capable of initiating pandemics and circulates mainly in two lineages, Victoria and Yamagata.

blood group compatibility.definition: The matching of a donor's and recipient's blood groups to prevent immune reactions during transfusion or organ transplantation, primarily based on ABO and Rh antigen compatibility. Incompatibility can trigger hemolytic reactions, while compatibility is established by serologic typing and crossmatching (with additional antigen matching considered for certain transplants).

histocompatibility.definition: The degree of immunologic compatibility between donor and recipient tissues, primarily determined by matching human leukocyte antigen (HLA) antigens and other minor histocompatibility antigens; it governs the risk of allograft rejection or graft-versus-host disease in transplantation.

cross-infection.definition: Transmission of an infectious agent from one person to another, typically in healthcare settings, through contaminated hands, instruments, or surfaces, often due to lapses in infection control.

xenotransplant.definition: The transplantation of organs, tissues, or cells from one species into another species.

cross-species transplant.definition: Transplantation of living cells, tissues, or organs between different species; used in research and experimental clinical applications, but limited by immune rejection and risk of cross-species infection.

crossed extension reflex.definition: A polysynaptic spinal reflex in which a noxious stimulus to one limb causes withdrawal by flexing that limb and, simultaneously, extension of the opposite limb to maintain balance.

chiasmatypy.definition: Not a recognized medical term; there is no standard definition.

chromosomes.definition: Structures within cells that carry genetic material; in eukaryotes, chromosomes are long DNA molecules wrapped around proteins and organized into discrete units that contain genes and regulatory sequences. In humans, there are 46 chromosomes (23 pairs: 22 autosomes and 2 sex chromosomes).

genes.definition: The cells that carry the traits that you get (inherit) from your parents.

poems syndrome.definition: A rare multisystem disorder caused by a clonal plasma cell neoplasm, characterized by a progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy, organomegaly (eg, liver, spleen, or lymph nodes), endocrinopathy (eg, diabetes, thyroid issues, or hypogonadism), monoclonal protein (M-protein) in serum or urine, and skin changes; often associated with elevated vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF).

crow-fukase syndrome.definition: A rare multisystem disorder caused by a plasma cell dyscrasia, defined by polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal gammopathy (M protein), and skin changes; also known as POEMS syndrome.

crouzon's disease.definition: A genetic craniosynostosis syndrome caused mainly by FGFR2 mutations, leading to premature fusion of cranial sutures with resulting abnormal skull shape (often brachycephaly), midface hypoplasia, shallow orbits with proptosis, and usually normal intelligence.

crouzon's syndrome.definition: A genetic craniofacial disorder (craniofacial dysostosis) characterized by premature fusion of cranial sutures (craniosynostosis) leading to midface hypoplasia, shallow orbits with proptosis, and hypertelorism; intelligence is usually normal; autosomal dominant, most commonly caused by FGFR2 mutations.

divergent squint.definition: A form of strabismus in which one or both eyes deviate outward (exotropia); the eyes diverge away from the nose, and the deviation may be intermittent or constant.

optic atrophy.definition: Degeneration of the optic nerve fibers leading to pallor of the optic disc and progressive, often irreversible, vision loss; typically results from damage to the optic nerve or its blood supply due to ischemia, inflammation, compression, toxins, or hereditary optic neuropathies.

crown-root ratio.definition: An expression of the relative lengths of the clinical crown and the portion of the root embedded in bone; defined as crown height to root height, used to assess periodontal support and tooth prognosis. A typical favorable ratio is about 1:2 (crown height roughly half the root height).

crown-heel length.definition: A measurement of an infant's length taken with the child in a supine position, from the crown of the head to the heel; used to assess growth when standing height cannot be obtained.

crown-rump length.definition: A measurement of the length of the embryo or fetus from the crown (top of the head) to the rump (buttocks), obtained by ultrasound, used to estimate gestational age during the first trimester.

cruciate ligament.definition: Two ligaments inside the knee that cross to form an X and stabilize the joint by preventing anterior or posterior displacement of the tibia relative to the femur.

cruciate.definition: Shaped like a cross; in anatomy, used to describe structures that cross each other, most famously the knee ligaments that cross to form a cross.

cruciform ligament.definition: A cross-shaped ligament of the craniovertebral region that stabilizes the odontoid process (dens) against the anterior arch of the atlas; it comprises the transverse ligament of the atlas and the superior and inferior longitudinal bands.

cruciate anastomosis.definition: An arterial cross-shaped network around the hip formed by the inferior gluteal artery, the medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries, and the first perforating branch of the profunda femoris, providing collateral blood supply to the femoral head and surrounding region when the femoral artery is occluded.

anthelix.definition: The curved inner ridge of the external ear cartilage, located just inside the outer rim, forming two branches and shaping the ear’s contour by separating the concha from the fossa triangularis.

crura.definition: Paired, leg‑like extensions in anatomy that serve as attachments or anchoring points for a structure; for example, the diaphragm attaches to the lumbar spine via its two crura, and there are proximal erectile components of the penis and clitoris forming similar anchoring structures.

vastus intermedius.definition: A muscle of the quadriceps femoris group, the deepest of the four, lying beneath the rectus femoris; it originates from the anterior and lateral surfaces of the femoral shaft and inserts into the quadriceps tendon (and patellar region), functioning to extend the knee (innervated by the femoral nerve).

cloquet's hernia.definition: An outdated term for an indirect inguinal hernia in which the hernial sac extends through the internal inguinal ring along the pathway of the processus vaginalis into the inguinal canal, potentially reaching the scrotum.

crest syndrome.definition: A limited form of systemic sclerosis characterized by calcinosis, Raynaud phenomenon, esophageal dysmotility, sclerodactyly, and telangiectasia.

c-reactive protein.definition: A protein made by the liver. High amounts of it may indicate that arteries are clogged (atherosclerosis).

crst.definition: Definition not found for "crst" in standard medical dictionaries. Please provide the expanded form of the acronym or the clinical context (e.g., disease, test, procedure, specialty) so I can give an accurate definition. If you meant CREST syndrome (limited systemic sclerosis) I can define that.

cross-section.definition: A two-dimensional slice of a three-dimensional structure produced by cutting with a single plane; in anatomy, commonly a transverse (axial) section that reveals internal tissues at the cut level.

cross-sectional anatomy.definition: Anatomical study of structures as seen in thin transverse or sectional slices through the body or an organ, illustrating spatial relationships between tissues and organs; commonly demonstrated by imaging modalities such as CT or MRI.

crutchfield tongs.definition: A skull-traction device in which pins or tines are inserted into the skull to apply controlled traction to the cervical spine for reduction and immobilization of cervical spine injuries.

cryoglobulin.definition: A serum immunoglobulin or immune complex that precipitates at cold temperatures (below normal body temperature) and redissolves when warmed; associated with cryoglobulinemia.

cryoglobulinemia.definition: A condition defined by the presence of cryoglobulins—immunoglobulins that precipitate at cold temperatures and redissolve with warming—in the blood, often causing immune complex–mediated vasculitis with symptoms such as palpable purpura, arthralgias, weakness, and renal involvement; cryoglobulins commonly accompany hepatitis C infection and certain hematologic disorders.

parietal region.definition: The region of the head overlying the parietal bones of the skull; in neuroanatomy, the cortical area corresponding to the parietal lobe.

collodion dressing.definition: A wound dressing made from collodion (nitrocellulose dissolved in ether and alcohol) that dries to a clear, flexible film, forming an occlusive protective barrier over a wound and helping secure dressings in place.

cervical spine.definition: The part of the spine located in the neck and consisting of the top seven vertebrae.

crutch gait.definition: Ambulation with the aid of two crutches, using a coordinated sequence of movements to transfer weight through the crutches and legs; most commonly a three-point gait when one leg is non–weight bearing, in which both crutches and the injured leg are advanced together followed by the unaffected leg.

crutches.definition: A pair of mobility aids with upright shafts, underarm rests, and hand grips used to support and transfer weight from the legs to the arms to enable walking, typically after injury or surgery; available as axillary or forearm crutches.

gait.definition: The pattern of walking, including rhythm, step length, base of support, and coordination of the limbs and trunk; reflects musculoskeletal strength, balance, and the integrity of the nervous system.

two-point gait.definition: A gait pattern using two points of support where the patient moves a crutch (or cane) and the opposite foot together, then switches to the other crutch and its opposite foot, providing smoother, faster ambulation with partial weight bearing.

three-point gait.definition: A gait pattern used with crutches or a walker in which the affected leg is non–weight bearing; the patient advances the crutches and the affected leg forward together, then moves the unaffected leg forward past them, resulting in three points of ground contact (two crutches and the unaffected leg).

four-point gait.definition: A four-beat gait pattern used with two crutches or canes in which the right crutch is advanced, followed by the left leg, then the left crutch, followed by the right leg; sequence repeats for stability in severe lower-extremity weakness.

swing-through gait.definition: A crutch-assisted gait in which the body is supported by the arms and both legs are swung forward beyond the crutches, so the feet pass in front of the crutches.

swing-to gait.definition: A gait pattern with assistive devices (such as crutches or a walker) in which both legs swing forward to land at the same point as the devices, with the feet not advancing beyond the device tips.

paraplegia.definition: When the lower half of your body cannot move.

axillary area.definition: Anatomically, the axillary area (axilla) is the pyramidal space beneath the shoulder joint, between the thorax and the upper limb, that contains the axillary vessels and nerves, lymph nodes, and adipose tissue; it serves as a conduit for neurovascular structures passing from the neck to the arm.

elbow extensors.definition: Muscles that extend the elbow by straightening the forearm, principally the triceps brachii (long, lateral, and medial heads) with assistance from the small anconeus muscle.

wrist extensors.definition: A group of extensor muscles in the posterior forearm that extend the wrist (and some also extend the fingers); they originate from the common extensor origin at the lateral epicondyle of the humerus and insert on the dorsal surfaces of the hand and fingers, innervated mainly by the radial nerve.

palsy.definition: Paralysis in part of the body, often with loss of sensation and uncontrolled body movements.

cruveilhier-baumgarten syndrome.definition: A historical term for portal hypertension caused by obstruction of the portal vein (often due to thrombosis) with cavernous transformation and the development of extensive portosystemic collaterals; clinically features include caput medusae, abdominal wall varices, splenomegaly, and sometimes ascites, with hepatic function frequently preserved if liver parenchyma is not primarily diseased.

paraumbilical veins.definition: Small abdominal-wall veins that form portosystemic collateral channels around the umbilicus by connecting the portal venous system with the systemic venous system (via the superficial epigastric veins); they are remnants of the fetal umbilical vein that may recanalize in portal hypertension, contributing to caput medusae.

cryptosporidiosis.definition: A protozoal intestinal infection caused by Cryptosporidium species. It typically presents with profuse watery diarrhea and abdominal cramps; transmitted via the fecal-oral route through contaminated water or food and can be more severe in immunocompromised individuals.

cryptosporidium hominis.definition: A protozoan parasite species within Cryptosporidium that primarily infects humans and causes cryptosporidiosis, characterized by watery diarrhea and abdominal cramps; transmitted by ingestion of thick-walled oocysts in contaminated water or food; diagnosed by stool examination for oocysts or antigen detection; management is supportive with nitazoxanide typically effective in immunocompetent individuals and more severe in immunocompromised patients.

cryptococcus neoformans.definition: An encapsulated yeast (fungus) that causes cryptococcosis, most notably cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised individuals; acquired from environmental exposure to bird droppings (especially pigeons).

cryptococcus.definition: A genus of encapsulated yeasts (including Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii) that causes cryptococcosis, most often meningitis in immunocompromised individuals; acquired from the environment (e.g., bird droppings); diagnosed by cryptococcal antigen testing or India ink staining; treated initially with amphotericin B and flucytosine, followed by fluconazole.

cryptodidymus.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard dictionaries; it does not have a defined medical meaning. If you meant cryptorchidism, that refers to failure of one or both testes to descend into the scrotum (congenital or sometimes acquired). If you have a different spelling or context, please provide it.

crypt of iris.definition: A natural opening in the anterior border layer of the iris that extends into the iris stroma, creating irregular surface markings (iris crypts) and representing a normal anatomical feature, more noticeable in lighter-colored irises.

crypt of fuchs.definition: Not a standard term in modern anatomy or histology. It may be a misnomer for other structures (e.g., crypts of Lieberkühn in the intestine) or a context-specific historic usage. If you can specify the organ or context, I can provide a precise definition.

crypt of lieberkühn.definition: A tubular gland located at the base of the intestinal villi in the mucosa of the small intestine (and colon) that extends into the lamina propria; it contains stem cells for continuous epithelial renewal and secretory cells such as goblet and Paneth cells.

lieberkuhns glands.definition: Tubular glands in the mucosa of the small intestine and colon, located at the bases of the intestinal villi; they secrete intestinal juice and house stem cells that renew the epithelium, with Paneth and goblet cells contributing to antimicrobial defense and mucus production.

cryptocephalus.definition: A historical term meaning “hidden head”; an obsolete label used to describe a congenital cranial deformity in which the skull is concealed or markedly underdeveloped, and is not a standard modern diagnosis.

cryptocephalic.definition: A rare congenital cranial deformity in which the calvaria (skull vault) is underdeveloped or abnormally shaped, often resulting in a smaller head; the term is largely historical and not commonly used in modern practice.

cryptocephalous.definition: An obsolete term describing a congenital cranial abnormality in which the skull is abnormally formed or underdeveloped, giving a “hidden head” appearance; in modern terminology this would typically be described as craniosynostosis or cranial hypoplasia depending on the specific pathology.

cryptocephaly.definition: A rare congenital cranial vault abnormality in which the calvarial bones are underdeveloped or incompletely ossified, resulting in a markedly small or flattened skull with a thin, often fragile vault.

cryptogenic.definition: Of unknown origin; referring to a disease or condition for which no cause can be identified after appropriate evaluation.

cryptogenic infection.definition: An infection whose causative organism or source cannot be identified despite standard diagnostic evaluation.

cryptogenic septicemia.definition: A bloodstream infection in which the primary source of infection cannot be identified after evaluation, historically used to describe sepsis without an identifiable focal source.

cryptomenorrhea.definition: Menstrual blood is produced but not expelled due to obstruction of the vaginal outflow tract (e.g., imperforate hymen or vaginal septum), leading to accumulation of blood in the vagina/uterus (hematocolpos/hematometra) and cyclic abdominal pain with primary amenorrhea.

cryptomenorrheal.definition: A condition in which menstrual blood is produced but cannot be expelled due to obstruction of the outflow tract (e.g., imperforate hymen or vaginal/cervical stenosis).

cryptophthalmos.definition: A rare congenital condition in which the eyelids fail to form properly, resulting in a continuous skin covering over the eye with little to no palpebral fissure; eyelids may be fused (ankyloblepharon) and the cornea may be exposed or malformed.

cryptophthalmos syndrome.definition: A rare autosomal recessive congenital disorder characterized by cryptophthalmos (eyelids absent or fused with the eye surface exposed) often accompanied by syndactyly and anomalies of the kidneys/genitourinary tract, and sometimes other malformations.

frasers syndrome.definition: A rare autosomal recessive congenital malformation syndrome characterized by cryptophthalmos (hidden eyelids/eye anomalies), syndactyly (fusion of fingers or toes), and genital and renal malformations, often with ear and airway anomalies; caused by mutations in genes such as FRAS1 and FREM1 that disrupt epidermal–mesenchymal adhesion during development.

cryptorchid testis.definition: An undescended testis that has failed to descend into the scrotal sac, typically located in the abdomen or inguinal canal.

cryptorchis.definition: A congenital condition in which one or both testes fail to descend into the scrotum; may be unilateral or bilateral, can impair fertility and increase the risk of testicular cancer if not corrected, and is often treated with surgical relocation (orchiopexy) if descent does not occur spontaneously by early childhood.

nitazoxanide.definition: A broad-spectrum antiparasitic and antiviral prodrug that inhibits pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase–dependent energy metabolism in susceptible organisms; used to treat Giardia lamblia and Cryptosporidium parvum infections (giardiasis and cryptosporidiosis) and studied for other infections.

cryoprecipitate.definition: A plasma-derived blood product prepared from thawed donor plasma; the cryoprecipitate contains concentrated fibrinogen, factor VIII, factor XIII, and von Willebrand factor (and fibronectin) and is used to replace fibrinogen and certain coagulation factors in bleeding patients.

cryostat.definition: A temperature-controlled instrument used to freeze tissue and cut thin frozen sections with a microtome for rapid histological diagnosis, often during surgery.

cryotherapy.definition: Use of extreme cold to freeze and destroy diseased tissue.

cryoanesthesia.definition: Temporary loss of sensation produced by cooling of tissue, typically achieved by applying cold to the area to inhibit nerve conduction.

tissue biopsy.definition: A procedure to obtain a small sample of tissue from the body for histopathological examination under a microscope to diagnose disease or assess pathology.

parkinsons disease.definition: A movement disorder that occurs when the brain does not produce enough of a chemical.

crystalline lens.definition: Part of the eye that changes shape so that the eye can focus on objects at different distances.

crystallization.definition: The process by which a solid crystal forms from a solution, melt, or gas as molecules organize into a regular, repeating lattice.

digitoxin.definition: A cardiac glycoside formerly used to treat heart failure and certain arrhythmias; inhibits Na+/K+-ATPase, increasing intracellular calcium and thereby augmenting myocardial contractility; has a long half-life and a narrow therapeutic index, with toxicity risks including gastrointestinal symptoms, confusion, vision changes, and arrhythmias; largely replaced by digoxin and other therapies and is mainly metabolized by the liver.

colony-stimulating factor.definition: A cytokine/growth factor that stimulates the proliferation and differentiation of hematopoietic progenitor cells in the bone marrow to increase production of mature neutrophils and other white blood cells; used clinically to treat neutropenia after chemotherapy or bone marrow transplantation.

contractions stress test.definition: An obstetric test that assesses fetal well‑being by monitoring fetal heart rate in response to induced uterine contractions (typically via nipple stimulation or IV oxytocin). A reassuring result shows no late decelerations during contractions; an abnormal result shows repetitive late decelerations, indicating possible uteroplacental insufficiency and fetal distress.

daptomycin.definition: A cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic that binds calcium-dependently to Gram-positive bacterial membranes, causing rapid depolarization and inhibition of protein, DNA, and RNA synthesis, leading to bacterial cell death. It is active mainly against Gram-positive organisms (e.g., MRSA, VRE) and is used for complicated skin and soft-tissue infections and bacteremia/endocarditis; it is not active against most Gram-negative bacteria and is not effective for pneumonia due to inactivation by pulmonary surfactant.

cul-de-sac.definition: A blind-ended pouch or recess in anatomy; a closed sac formed by folds of tissue, such as recesses in the peritoneal cavity (e.g., the rectouterine and rectovesical pouches).

culdocentesis.definition: An old diagnostic procedure in which a needle is inserted through the posterior vaginal fornix into the rectouterine (Douglas) pouch to withdrawn peritoneal fluid, historically used to diagnose intraperitoneal bleeding (e.g., a ruptured ectopic pregnancy) when imaging was not available.

culdotomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which an incision is made into the cul-de-sac (the rectouterine pouch) through the posterior vaginal fornix to access the peritoneal cavity; historically used to evaluate or treat intraperitoneal bleeding, such as from a ruptured ectopic pregnancy.

culdoscope.definition: A rigid endoscope introduced through the posterior vaginal fornix to visualize the rectouterine pouch (cul-de-sac) for diagnostic assessment of pelvic pathology; historically used for culdocentesis and evaluating pelvic bleeding.

posterior fornix.definition: The posterior fornix of the vagina is the recess behind the cervix between the posterior vaginal wall and the cervix; it is the deepest part of the vaginal canal and forms the anterior boundary of the rectouterine pouch (pouch of Douglas).

hip replacement.definition: A surgical procedure in which the damaged hip joint is replaced with artificial components (a prosthetic implant) to relieve pain and restore movement.

knee replacement.definition: A surgical procedure to replace the damaged knee joint with artificial implants (prostheses) to relieve pain and restore function, typically performed for severe arthritis or knee injury; available as a total knee replacement or a partial (unicompartmental) replacement.

cup arthroplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to implant or replace the acetabular cup component of a total hip prosthesis, creating the socket for the femoral head to restore hip joint function and stability.

cubital fossa.definition: A triangular space on the anterior elbow bounded laterally by the brachioradialis, medially by the pronator teres, and with a base between the humeral epicondyles; roof is the bicipital aponeurosis, floor is brachialis and supinator. Contents (lateral to medial) include the radial nerve (dividing into branches) in the lateral part, the biceps brachii tendon, the brachial artery and its bifurcation, and the median nerve.

cubitus.definition: The elbow; the region of the upper limb where the arm meets the forearm, including the elbow joint and surrounding structures.

cuboidal epithelium.definition: A type of epithelial tissue made up of cube-shaped cells with roughly equal height and width; nuclei are typically round and centrally located. Simple cuboidal epithelium lines kidney tubules and many gland ducts and functions in secretion and absorption; stratified cuboidal epithelium, a rarer variant, lines some larger ducts of glands (e.g., sweat, mammary, and salivary glands) and provides protection.

cuboid bone.definition: A cube-shaped tarsal bone on the lateral aspect of the foot that articulates posteriorly with the calcaneus, anteriorly with the fourth and fifth metatarsals, and medially with the navicular; it helps stabilize the lateral column of the foot.

os cuboideum.definition: A cube-shaped tarsal bone on the lateral aspect of the foot that articulates with the calcaneus, navicular, and the fourth and fifth metatarsals; forms part of the calcaneocuboid joint and contributes to stability of the lateral longitudinal arch of the foot.

cuneiform bone.definition: One of the three wedge-shaped tarsal bones in the midfoot, located between the navicular and the bases of the first through third metatarsals; helps form the arches of the foot.

cuneiform.definition: A wedge-shaped bone of the foot; one of the three cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) between the navicular and the bases of the first through third metatarsals, contributing to the foot’s arches.

cuneus.definition: A wedge-shaped region on the medial surface of the occipital lobe, forming the superior bank of the calcarine sulcus; part of the primary visual cortex involved in processing visual information.

cupula.definition: A gelatinous, glycoprotein-rich mass that covers the hair cells on the crista ampullaris in the ampulla of each semicircular canal; its deflection by endolymph movement transduces angular acceleration by bending vestibular hair cells.

cupola.definition: A gelatinous, dome-shaped membrane in the inner ear that spans the ampulla of each semicircular canal and covers the hair cells of the crista ampullaris; movement of endolymph deflects it, bending the hair cells and signaling angular acceleration.

cup/disc ratio.definition: The proportion of the optic cup diameter to the optic disc diameter seen on the fundus, used to assess glaucomatous cupping; a higher ratio suggests greater cupping and possible glaucoma.

rectouterine pouch.definition: A peritoneal recess between the posterior surface of the uterus and the anterior surface of the rectum in females; the lowest part of the peritoneal cavity when upright; also known as the pouch of Douglas.

parietooccipital sulcus.definition: A groove on the medial surface of the cerebrum that marks the boundary between the parietal lobe and the occipital lobe.

postcalcarine sulcus.definition: A groove on the medial surface of the occipital lobe located posterior to the calcarine sulcus.

cochlear duct.definition: A membranous duct within the cochlea filled with endolymph; it houses the organ of Corti and is bounded superiorly by Reissner's membrane and inferiorly by the basilar membrane, separating the scala vestibuli and scala tympani.

laryngeal cartilage.definition: The cartilaginous structures that form the skeleton of the larynx (voice box) in the neck, including the thyroid, cricoid, arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform, and epiglottis; they provide structural support, maintain airway patency, and anchor the vocal folds and laryngeal muscles involved in phonation and swallowing.

parietal peritoneum.definition: A serous membrane lining the walls of the abdominal and pelvic cavities (parietal layer of the peritoneum), continuous with the visceral peritoneum that covers intraperitoneal organs.

pouch of douglas.definition: A peritoneal recess between the posterior surface of the uterus and the anterior surface of the rectum in females; the lowest point of the peritoneal cavity when standing, a potential space that can accumulate fluid, pus, or blood (clinically accessed by culdocentesis).

tubocurarine chloride.definition: A nondepolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent used during anesthesia to produce skeletal muscle relaxation by competitively inhibiting nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction; the chloride salt form of d-tubocurarine.

curare.definition: A plant-derived arrow poison; in modern medicine, a nondepolarizing neuromuscular blocker that competitively inhibits nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, causing flaccid skeletal muscle paralysis and relaxation during anesthesia; effects are reversible with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and ventilation.

curariform.definition: Resembling curare; describing drugs that induce skeletal muscle relaxation by competitive blockade of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction (curare-like nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockers).

curette.definition: A small, spoon-shaped surgical instrument with a sharp edge used to scrape tissue from a body cavity or surface, typically for curettage or sampling.

hartmann's curet.definition: A scoop-shaped surgical instrument used to scrape tissue from a body cavity or surface during curettage.

copper sulfate.definition: A blue crystalline inorganic copper salt (CuSO4) used as a fungicide and algicide and as a laboratory reagent; ingestion or significant exposure can cause copper poisoning with gastrointestinal irritation, liver and kidney injury, and requires prompt medical attention.

cupric sulfate.definition: A blue crystalline copper salt (CuSO4) soluble in water; used as a fungicide and algaecide and as a laboratory reagent; historically employed as an emetic and caustic antiseptic; ingestion is highly toxic.

cupric.definition: Relating to copper in the +2 oxidation state; containing copper as Cu2+, as in copper(II) salts.

cuprimine.definition: A brand-name oral copper-chelating agent (D-penicillamine) used to treat Wilson disease by binding copper and promoting its excretion; also used as a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug for severe rheumatoid arthritis. Adverse effects include hypersensitivity reactions, nephrotoxicity, bone-marrow suppression, and a lupus-like syndrome.

d-penicillamine.definition: A thiol-containing amino acid derivative, the D-enantiomer of penicillamine, used as a chelating agent to promote urinary excretion of copper in Wilson’s disease (and formerly used for rheumatoid arthritis).

curling's ulcer.definition: A duodenal ulcer that develops after severe burns or major physiologic stress, caused by mucosal ischemia from reduced blood flow (a type of stress ulcer).

curonium.definition: A neuromuscular blocking drug (aminosteroid class) used to induce reversible skeletal muscle paralysis during anesthesia; examples include vecuronium, rocuronium, and pancuronium.

cushingoid.definition: A full, round face, like a patient with high levels of the hormone cortisol.

nelson's syndrome.definition: A complication following bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing disease, characterized by growth of an ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma with markedly elevated ACTH levels, leading to hyperpigmentation and possible mass effect such as headaches and visual field defects.

pituitary adenoma.definition: A benign, typically slow-growing tumor arising from pituitary gland cells (adenohypophysis); it may be hormonally active (secreting prolactin, growth hormone, ACTH, or other pituitary hormones) or nonfunctioning, and can cause hormonal imbalances or mass effects.

moon facies.definition: A rounded, puffy facial appearance with fullness of the cheeks and often periorbital edema, typically seen in Cushing syndrome due to excess glucocorticoids.

facial hair.definition: A region of hair growth on the face, including the mustache, beard, and sideburns; its development is strongly influenced by androgens, with hair often transitioning from fine vellus to coarser terminal hair during puberty, and excessive facial hair in women may indicate hirsutism.

poor wound healing.definition: Impaired or delayed healing of tissue after injury, with prolonged or incomplete progression through the normal wound-healing phases (inflammation, proliferation, remodeling), often resulting in chronic, nonhealing wounds. It commonly stems from local factors such as poor perfusion, infection, edema, necrosis, or foreign bodies, and systemic conditions such as diabetes, malnutrition, anemia, aging, smoking, immunosuppression, or corticosteroid use.

ecchymoses.definition: A bruise; a subcutaneous hemorrhage causing bluish-black discoloration of the skin from leakage of blood into surrounding tissues, usually larger than 1 cm in diameter.

thin skin.definition: Thin skin is skin that is thinner than normal due to reduced epidermal and dermal thickness, often resulting from aging or long-term topical corticosteroid use; it tends to be more fragile, easier to tear or bruise, and slower to heal.

muscle weakness.definition: A reduced ability of a muscle or muscle group to generate normal force, resulting in decreased strength or power, often due to neuromuscular, muscular, metabolic, or systemic conditions, injury, or disuse.

muscle atrophy.definition: A decrease in skeletal muscle mass and cross-sectional area with a corresponding loss of strength, arising from disuse, denervation, aging (sarcopenia), or chronic illness.

central obesity.definition: Excess fat around the midsection, especially visceral abdominal fat, associated with higher risk of metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease.

adrenal lesion.definition: An abnormal area within the adrenal gland detected by imaging or pathology that may reflect benign processes (e.g., adenoma or cyst) or malignant processes (e.g., carcinoma or metastasis), and often requires evaluation of hormonal activity and radiologic characteristics to assess function and malignancy risk.

adrenal tumor.definition: A growth arising from the adrenal gland; it can be benign (e.g., adrenal adenoma) or malignant (e.g., adrenocortical carcinoma), and may be hormonally active (secreting corticosteroids, aldosterone, androgens, or catecholamines in pheochromocytoma) or nonfunctional; many are discovered incidentally on imaging as adrenal incidentalomas.

abdominal striae.definition: Linear atrophic dermal scars on the abdomen resulting from rapid skin stretching or hormonal changes; they typically start pink or reddish and fade to pale or white over time, often seen with pregnancy, rapid weight gain, or endocrine conditions.

stretch marks.definition: Linear dermal scars caused by rapid skin stretching or mechanical stress that disrupts collagen and elastin in the dermis. They commonly occur during puberty, pregnancy, or rapid weight gain or loss, and in Cushing’s syndrome. They typically begin as red or purple bands (early stage) and later become pale or white.

na+.definition: A positively charged ion of the element sodium; the major extracellular cation that helps regulate extracellular fluid volume and osmolarity, and is essential for nerve impulse transmission and muscle contraction. Normal serum concentration is approximately 135–145 mEq/L, maintained by renal excretion and dietary intake.

adrenal steroids.definition: Steroid hormones produced by the adrenal cortex, including mineralocorticoids (e.g., aldosterone), glucocorticoids (e.g., cortisol), and adrenal androgens; they regulate electrolyte balance, metabolism, the stress response, immune and inflammatory processes, and sexual development.

cpt.definition: A standardized coding system used in the United States to describe medical, surgical, and diagnostic services for reporting and billing; maintained by the American Medical Association, with five-digit codes organized into categories I, II, and III for procedures and services.

current procedural terminology.definition: A standardized coding system used to describe medical, surgical, and diagnostic procedures and services for billing and administrative purposes; codes are five-digit numbers and are maintained by the American Medical Association.

cpt codes.definition: A standardized coding system used to describe and bill medical, surgical, and diagnostic services; it uses five-digit codes for specific procedures and services and is maintained and updated annually by the American Medical Association.

curschmann's spiral.definition: Spiral-shaped mucus plugs (casts) from desquamated epithelial cells of the small bronchi, seen in the sputum of patients with bronchial asthma.

curtain effect.definition: A transient, curtain-like loss of vision in one eye (amaurosis fugax) due to brief retinal ischemia, commonly from carotid artery disease or embolic events; symptoms typically resolve within minutes and may herald an increased risk of stroke.

curvature.definition: The degree to which a structure deviates from a straight line or normal contour; in medicine, an abnormal bending or contour of a body part, such as the spine (kyphosis, lordosis, scoliosis) or the shape of an organ.

curvature myopia.definition: A form of refractive myopia in which an abnormally steep corneal curvature increases the eye's optical power, causing light to focus in front of the retina and resulting in blurry distance vision.

discoid lupus erythematosus.definition: A chronic cutaneous form of lupus erythematosus characterized by well-demarcated, erythematous plaques with adherent scales that heal with atrophy and scarring, most often on sun-exposed areas of the face, ears, and scalp; it may occur with or without systemic lupus erythematosus.

subacute lupus erythematosus.definition: A form of cutaneous lupus erythematosus characterized by photosensitive, non-scarring skin lesions, typically annular or psoriasiform plaques on sun-exposed areas, often with anti-Ro/SSA antibodies; systemic disease, if present, is usually milder than in systemic lupus erythematosus.

acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.definition: An acute, photosensitive skin eruption seen in lupus erythematosus, most often presenting as a malar (butterfly) rash or other erythematous, non-scarring lesions on sun-exposed areas, frequently associated with systemic lupus erythematosus.

cutaneous lupus erythematosus.definition: An autoimmune inflammatory skin disorder that is a manifestation of lupus erythematosus; it presents with chronic, erythematous, scaly or discoid plaques (often photosensitive) and may be limited to the skin or occur with systemic lupus.

cutaneous immunofluorescence biopsy.definition: A skin biopsy prepared for direct immunofluorescence to detect in situ immune deposits (such as IgG, IgA, IgM, and C3) along the epidermal–dermal junction or other skin structures, used to diagnose autoimmune blistering diseases and related dermatologic conditions.

immunofluorescence.definition: A laboratory method that uses fluorescently labeled antibodies to detect and visualize specific antigens in cells or tissues under a fluorescence microscope; it can be direct (a labeled antibody binds the antigen) or indirect (a labeled secondary antibody detects an unlabeled primary antibody).

cutaneous larva migrans.definition: A creeping eruption of the skin caused by the subepidermal migration of dog or cat hookworm larvae (most commonly Ancylostoma braziliense) after contact with contaminated soil or sand; presents as intensely pruritic, serpiginous, erythematous tracks that migrate over days to weeks.

leishmania tropica.definition: A protozoan parasite species transmitted by Phlebotomus sandflies that causes Old World cutaneous leishmaniasis; infections typically produce dry, slowly enlarging skin ulcers, often on the face, with a chronic course.

sand fly.definition: A small blood-sucking fly of the subfamily Phlebotominae that serves as the vector for Leishmania parasites, causing leishmaniasis in humans and animals.

oriental sore.definition: An old term for cutaneous leishmaniasis of the Old World, typically caused by Leishmania tropica; presents as a chronic, slowly enlarging ulcer or indurated nodule on exposed skin (most often the face) after a sandfly bite.

delhi boil.definition: Not a recognized medical term. If referring to a boil (furuncle): a localized skin infection of a hair follicle or sweat gland, usually due to Staphylococcus aureus, presenting as a painful, red nodule that may suppurate and drain pus; treatment includes warm compresses, possible incision and drainage for larger lesions, and antibiotics if there is surrounding cellulitis or systemic symptoms.

old world leishmaniasis.definition: Leishmaniasis occurring in the Old World (Africa, Asia, Europe), caused by Leishmania species transmitted by Phlebotomus sandflies; includes cutaneous forms (e.g., caused by L. tropica, L. major) and visceral disease (e.g., caused by L. donovani, L. infantum) depending on the species.

tropical sore.definition: A chronic, non-healing ulcer of the skin and subcutaneous tissue, typically on the lower limbs in tropical regions after minor trauma, often associated with malnutrition, edema, and infection; requires wound care, antimicrobial therapy, and treatment of underlying factors.

infrared therapy.definition: Treatment using non-ionizing infrared radiation to heat tissues, increasing local blood flow and metabolism, which may reduce pain and stiffness and aid healing; delivered by infrared lamps, pads, or LEDs (near- or far-infrared).

sodium antimony gluconate.definition: A pentavalent antimonial compound used to treat leishmaniasis (primarily visceral and some cutaneous forms), administered parenterally; its mechanism is not fully understood but is thought to disrupt parasite energy metabolism, with notable toxicities including cardiotoxicity, pancreatitis, and hepatotoxicity, and resistance in some regions.

curvularia lunata.definition: A dematiaceous (pigmented) mold in the genus Curvularia; an opportunistic human pathogen that can cause keratitis, sinusitis, pulmonary and cutaneous infections, especially in immunocompromised individuals; characterized by pigmented colonies and curved (geniculate) conidia.

cutis laxa.definition: A rare hereditary or acquired disorder of elastic connective tissue presenting with lax, inelastic, sagging skin due to defective elastin fibers; can be associated with systemic problems such as hernias, airway and vascular abnormalities.

cutis marmorata.definition: A transient, benign mottling of the skin caused by dilation of superficial cutaneous vessels in response to cold, producing a lace-like marbled pattern most common in newborns and infants; typically resolves with warming and does not require treatment.

cutaneous horn.definition: A keratinous, horn-shaped projection on the skin produced by marked hyperkeratosis; it may overlie benign, premalignant, or malignant epidermal lesions, and biopsy of the base is recommended to determine underlying pathology.

cutis nevus.definition: Benign pigmented skin lesion consisting of melanocytic nevus cells; commonly called a mole. It can be junctional (at the dermoepidermal junction), compound, or intradermal, and is typically harmless but should be monitored for changes suggesting malignant transformation.

cutaneous nevus.definition: A benign pigmented skin lesion composed of nevus (melanocytic) cells; commonly called a mole, it can be congenital or acquired and may be junctional, compound, or intradermal based on the location of nevus cells.

cutaneous papilloma.definition: Benign epithelial tumor of the skin characterized by papillary outgrowths of squamous epithelium with a fibrovascular core; typically exophytic and pedunculated or sessile, and non-malignant.

cutaneous tag.definition: A common, benign skin lesion consisting of a small, soft, pedunculated projection from the skin, typically flesh-colored and composed of fibrous tissue and vascular stroma; often occurs in areas of friction or skin folds (e.g., neck, axilla, groin, eyelids) and may increase with age or obesity.

skin tag.definition: A benign, pedunculated skin lesion (acrochordon) consisting of fibrous tissue and a vascular core that protrudes from the skin; typically flesh-colored, soft, and painless, and common in areas of friction such as the neck, axillae, and groin.

duodenal ulcer.definition: A peptic ulcer in the duodenum (the first part of the small intestine), most commonly due to Helicobacter pylori infection or NSAID use; it causes intermittent epigastric pain that often improves with meals and may be associated with nausea, vomiting, GI bleeding, or rarely perforation.

hyperadrenalism.definition: A condition characterized by overactivity of the adrenal glands with excessive production of adrenal hormones (cortisol, aldosterone, or catecholamines), due to hyperfunction of the adrenal cortex or medulla; it encompasses disorders such as Cushing's syndrome, primary hyperaldosteronism, and pheochromocytoma.

adrenocortical steroids.definition: Steroid hormones produced by the adrenal cortex, including glucocorticoids (e.g., cortisol) and mineralocorticoids (e.g., aldosterone), along with adrenal androgens; they regulate metabolism, immune responses, stress response, and electrolyte and water balance.

cyanide poisoning.definition: An acute poisoning from exposure to cyanide that inhibits mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase, blocking oxidative phosphorylation and causing histotoxic hypoxia despite adequate oxygenation. It can occur via inhalation, ingestion, or dermal exposure to cyanide-containing compounds and may cause rapid neurologic and cardiovascular deterioration.

cyanobacteria poisoning.definition: Illness caused by exposure to cyanotoxins produced by cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) in contaminated water, which can cause hepatotoxic, neurotoxic, or dermal effects depending on the toxin; symptoms range from GI upset and liver injury to neurologic symptoms and skin irritation after ingestion or contact with algal blooms.

intrinsic factor.definition: A glycoprotein secreted by gastric parietal cells that binds vitamin B12 (cobalamin) and enables its absorption in the terminal ileum; deficiency leads to impaired B12 absorption and pernicious anemia.

extrinsic factor.definition: An extrinsic factor is an influence that comes from outside the body and affects health or biological processes (e.g., environmental exposures, diet, pathogens), as opposed to intrinsic factors that originate internally.

cyanomethemoglobin.definition: A stable complex formed when cyanide binds to ferric iron in methemoglobin, producing cyanmethemoglobin, used in the cyanmethemoglobin method for spectrophotometric hemoglobin measurement.

cyanmethemoglobin.definition: A stable ferric (Fe3+) heme–cyanide complex formed when cyanide binds to methemoglobin; used in the Drabkin method for spectrophotometric determination of hemoglobin.

cyanopsia.definition: A blue-tinted color vision disturbance in which all colors are perceived with a blue hue; a rare phenomenon that can be drug-induced (notably by PDE-5 inhibitors such as sildenafil) or result from retinal/optic pathway pathology.

cyanosed.definition: Blue discoloration of the skin and mucous membranes caused by increased deoxygenated hemoglobin in the blood, typically indicating hypoxemia or reduced oxygen delivery.

chorionic villus biopsy.definition: An early prenatal diagnostic procedure in which placental tissue (chorionic villi) is sampled to obtain fetal DNA for chromosomal and genetic testing, typically performed in the first trimester (about 10–13 weeks) by transabdominal or transcervical sampling; used to diagnose chromosomal abnormalities and certain genetic disorders. The procedure carries a small risk of miscarriage and other complications.

common variable immunodeficiency.definition: Common variable immunodeficiency is a primary immunodeficiency defined by hypogammaglobulinemia (typically low IgG with reduced IgA and/or IgM) and impaired antibody responses to vaccines, leading to recurrent infections; caused by defects in B-cell differentiation with variable clinical features, including autoimmunity, lymphoproliferation, and an increased risk of lymphoma.

cyclic neutropenia.definition: A rare congenital disorder characterized by recurrent, cyclic episodes of neutropenia (low neutrophil counts), typically on a roughly 21-day cycle, resulting in recurrent infections such as oral ulcers and gingivitis; often due to mutations in the ELANE gene affecting neutrophil development.

cyclic vomiting.definition: A disorder characterized by recurrent, episodic bouts of severe vomiting with abrupt onset and spontaneous resolution, separated by symptom-free intervals. Episodes last hours to days and are often stereotyped for the individual; accompanying symptoms may include nausea, pallor, diaphoresis, abdominal pain, and lethargy, and it is frequently linked to migraine or autonomic dysfunction.

cyclic adenosine monophosphate.definition: A second messenger in cellular signaling produced from ATP by adenylyl cyclase; it activates protein kinase A and other targets to regulate metabolism, gene transcription, and ion channel activity, and is degraded by phosphodiesterases.

cyclic guanosine monophosphate.definition: A chemical in the body that widens blood vessels in the penis. This increases blood flow to the penis, causing an erection.

cyclin.definition: A family of regulatory proteins that control cell cycle progression by binding and activating cyclin-dependent kinases; their levels oscillate during the cycle to drive transitions between G1, S, G2, and M phases.

cyclin-dependent kinase.definition: A family of serine/threonine protein kinases that require binding to a regulatory cyclin subunit to become active; they phosphorylate key substrates to drive cell cycle progression (notably G1/S and G2/M transitions) and, in some cases, regulate transcription, with activity tightly controlled by cyclin levels and other regulatory mechanisms.

cyclamate.definition: A synthetic nonnutritive sweetener; the sodium (or calcium) salt of cyclamic acid used to sweeten foods and beverages; about 30 times sweeter than sucrose; often used in combination with saccharin; regulatory status varies due to animal carcinogenicity concerns.

cyclandelate.definition: A vasodilator medication used to improve peripheral circulation in conditions such as intermittent claudication and Raynaud phenomenon; it works by relaxing vascular smooth muscle to increase blood flow.

cyclarthrosis.definition: An archaic term for a synovial joint that allows circular or rotary movement around a fixed axis; essentially a rotational joint.

cyclencephaly.definition: A nonstandard term referring to a severe congenital brain malformation in which the cerebral hemispheres are markedly underdeveloped or abnormally formed, leading to grossly abnormal brain morphology and substantial neurodevelopmental impairment; the exact description and classification vary across sources.

cyclothymic disorder.definition: A chronic mood disorder in the bipolar spectrum characterized by numerous periods of hypomanic symptoms that do not meet full hypomanic-episode criteria and numerous periods of depressive symptoms that do not meet criteria for a major depressive episode, lasting at least 2 years in adults (1 year in children/adolescents) with symptoms present most of the time and minimal periods of remission.

cyclothymic.definition: Relating to cyclothymia, a mood disorder marked by chronic, mild mood fluctuations with alternating hypomanic and depressive symptoms that do not meet criteria for a major depressive episode or a manic/hypomanic episode.

cyclotomy.definition: A surgical procedure involving an incision into the ciliary body of the eye.

cyt???.definition: Combining form from the Greek kytos meaning "cell," used to form terms relating to cells (e.g., cytology—the study of cells; cytoplasm—the material within a cell; cytotoxic—toxic to cells).

cytosporin.definition: An immunosuppressant calcineurin inhibitor used to prevent organ transplant rejection (and in some autoimmune diseases); it blocks T-cell activation by inhibiting calcineurin, thereby reducing interleukin-2 production. Common adverse effects include nephrotoxicity, hypertension, tremor, and hirsutism.

cyclosporin.definition: A potent immunosuppressant and calcineurin inhibitor used to prevent organ transplant rejection and treat certain autoimmune disorders; it suppresses T-cell activation by inhibiting calcineurin, thereby reducing interleukin-2 production.

cyclosporin a.definition: A cyclic peptide immunosuppressant that inhibits calcineurin, blocking IL-2 transcription and T-cell activation; used to prevent organ transplant rejection and treat certain autoimmune conditions; has a narrow therapeutic index with nephrotoxicity as a principal adverse effect, plus hepatotoxicity and increased infection risk; metabolized by CYP3A and has numerous drug interactions.

ciclosporin.definition: An immunosuppressant calcineurin inhibitor used to prevent organ transplant rejection and treat certain autoimmune diseases; it blocks T-cell activation by inhibiting calcineurin, reducing interleukin-2 production. Common adverse effects include nephrotoxicity, hypertension, tremor, hirsutism, and gingival hyperplasia.

cyclopia.definition: A rare congenital anomaly in which there is a single median eye in the midline of the face, due to failure of the forebrain (prosencephalon) to properly separate the orbits (holoprosencephaly); often associated with severe brain malformations and usually incompatible with life.

cyclocephaly.definition: An abnormal skull shape characterized by a roughly circular or globular head, with width and length dimensions nearly equal.

cycloplegia.definition: Paralysis of the ciliary muscle of the eye, resulting in loss of accommodation (inability to focus on near objects) and typically accompanied by pupil dilation; it can be pharmacologically induced for eye examinations or occur due to nerve damage.

cycloplegic refraction.definition: A refractive assessment performed after pharmacologic cycloplegia (paralysis of accommodation) to eliminate the eye’s focusing reflex, allowing measurement of the true refractive error; commonly used in children and in cases of suspected latent hyperopia or accommodative esotropia.

cycloplegic eyedrops.definition: Eye drops that temporarily paralyze the ciliary muscle (cycloplegia) and dilate the pupil (mydriasis) by blocking muscarinic acetylcholine receptors; used to obtain accurate refractions and to facilitate a dilated eye examination.

cyclopropane.definition: A colorless, highly flammable hydrocarbon with the formula C3H6 forming a three-membered ring; historically used as an inhalational anesthetic but largely obsolete due to toxicity and safety concerns.

cyclotropia.definition: A form of strabismus with a manifest torsional (rotational) misalignment of one eye about its visual axis, resulting in intorsion or extorsion; it may be congenital or acquired and can cause torsional diplopia that varies with gaze.

prostaglandin endoperoxide synthase.definition: A bifunctional enzyme that catalyzes the two-step conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandin G2 and then prostaglandin H2, the first step in prostanoid biosynthesis; also known as cyclooxygenase (COX) with two main isoforms, COX-1 and COX-2, and a common target of NSAIDs.

cyclodestruction.definition: Destruction or ablation of the ciliary body to reduce production of aqueous humor and lower intraocular pressure in glaucoma; performed by techniques such as laser cyclophotocoagulation or cyclocryodestruction.

cyclodialysis.definition: A surgical procedure in which the ciliary body is separated from the scleral spur to create a cyclodialysis cleft, thereby increasing aqueous humor outflow via the uveoscleral pathway and lowering intraocular pressure.

cycloduction.definition: A torsional (rotational) movement of the eye around its visual axis (line of sight); incycloduction (intorsion) rotates the top of the eye toward the nose, and excycloduction (extorsion) rotates it away from the nose.

intraocular pressure.definition: The fluid pressure inside the eye, resulting from the production and drainage of aqueous humor; normal values are typically about 10–21 mmHg.

aqueous fluid.definition: A clear, watery, low-protein fluid that fills the anterior and posterior chambers of the eye (aqueous humor), produced by the ciliary body and involved in nutrient transport and intraocular pressure regulation.

ophthalmology.definition: The branch of medicine and surgery focused on the diagnosis, treatment, and management of eye diseases and the visual system.

optic neuritis.definition: An inflammatory demyelinating condition of the optic nerve that causes acute vision loss, often with pain on eye movement; may be associated with multiple sclerosis.

cardiotoxicity.definition: Damage to heart tissue caused by toxic substances (e.g., certain medications, drugs, or chemicals) that leads to impaired myocardial function, arrhythmias, or cardiomyopathy.

hemorrhagic cystitis.definition: Inflammation of the bladder mucosa with bleeding into the urine (gross or microscopic hematuria), often with dysuria; commonly caused by alkylating chemotherapy (acrolein from cyclophosphamide or ifosfamide), radiation therapy, viral infections (e.g., adenovirus), or intravesical therapies such as BCG.

macrocytic anemia.definition: The presence of larger-than-normal red blood cells in circulation—even though there are too few of them—caused by lack of folate and vitamin B12.

cyclospora infection.definition: An intestinal infection caused by the protozoan parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis, typically acquired from ingesting contaminated food or water. It presents with watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, bloating, nausea, and weight loss, with an incubation of about 1–14 days. Diagnosis is via stool testing for oocysts (often modified acid-fast staining or PCR). Treatment is trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for 3–7 days; alternatives exist for sulfa allergy. Prevention focuses on safe food handling and hygiene.

cysteine.definition: A sulfur-containing, nonessential amino acid with a thiol (-SH) side chain; participates in disulfide bond formation in proteins and serves as a precursor to glutathione.

cystine.definition: A disulfide-linked dimer of the amino acid cysteine; the oxidized form of two cysteine residues.

nephropathic cystinosis.definition: A rare autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by CTNS gene mutations, leading to accumulation of cystine in lysosomes; the kidneys are typically affected first with proximal tubulopathy (Fanconi syndrome) and may have corneal crystals causing photophobia, with potential progression to kidney failure if untreated. Treatment with cysteamine lowers lysosomal cystine and slows disease progression.

cystitis coli.definition: An older/rare term referring to inflammation of the colon (colitis).

cystitis cystica.definition: A benign bladder mucosal lesion in which nests of urothelium (Brunn’s nests) in the lamina propria undergo cystic dilation to form mucin-filled cysts, usually in the setting of chronic cystitis and often linked with cystitis glandularis.

cystadenocarcinoma.definition: A malignant epithelial tumor that forms cystic spaces and gland-like (adenocarcinomatous) structures; commonly arises from ovarian cystadenomas (serous or mucinous) and can show invasive growth and metastasis.

cystadenoma.definition: A benign neoplasm arising from glandular epithelium that forms cystic spaces; typically lined by cuboidal or columnar cells and filled with serous or mucinous fluid, most commonly occurring in the ovary as serous or mucinous cystadenoma.

cystadenomata.definition: A benign epithelial neoplasm that forms cystic glandular spaces, lined by glandular epithelium (often seen in the ovary as serous or mucinous cystadenoma).

cylindroma.definition: A benign skin adnexal tumor arising from sweat glands (eccrine), typically presenting as a slow-growing scalp nodule; histology shows well-circumscribed nests of basaloid cells with duct-like structures and a surrounding hyaline basement membrane-like sheath. Often referred to as a "turban tumor" when multiple lesions occur.

cylindromas.definition: A benign skin adnexal tumor arising from eccrine sweat glands, typically presenting as firm nodules on the scalp or face. Histology shows well-circumscribed nests of basaloid cells surrounded by a thick, hyaline basement membrane material (PAS-positive), producing a jigsaw-like pattern. Lesions are usually solitary but can be multiple in Brooke-Spiegler syndrome; treatment is complete surgical excision.

cylindromata.definition: Benign skin adnexal tumors derived from sweat glands (usually eccrine), presenting as solitary or multiple nodules—most commonly on the scalp where lesions may coalesce into a “turban” tumor; histology shows nests of basaloid cells in a jigsaw-puzzle pattern surrounded by thick hyaline basement membrane material.

cyma line.definition: A curvilinear anatomical landmark in craniofacial anatomy used as a reference line on radiographs or in surgical planning.

talonavicular.definition: Relating to the talus and navicular bones; the talonavicular joint is the articulation between the head of the talus and the navicular bone in the midfoot.

calcaneocuboid.definition: Relating to the heel bone (calcaneus) and the cuboid bone of the foot; describes the joint between these two tarsal bones, a synovial joint in the midfoot that allows limited gliding movements and contributes to midfoot flexibility.

duloxetine.definition: A serotonin–norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) antidepressant that increases synaptic levels of serotonin and norepinephrine and is used to treat major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, and certain chronic pain conditions such as diabetic peripheral neuropathy and fibromyalgia.

cymbalta.definition: A serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) antidepressant used to treat major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, fibromyalgia, and certain chronic pain conditions (e.g., diabetic peripheral neuropathy, musculoskeletal pain); it increases synaptic serotonin and norepinephrine by inhibiting their reuptake.

cyproheptadine.definition: A first-generation H1 histamine receptor antagonist with antiserotonergic and anticholinergic effects, used to treat allergic symptoms (e.g., rhinitis, urticaria and pruritus) and sometimes prescribed to stimulate appetite in underweight patients.

cyproheptadine hydrochloride.definition: A first-generation antihistamine with anticholinergic properties and anti-serotonergic (serotonin receptor antagonist) effects; used to treat allergic conditions such as rhinitis and urticaria and sometimes as an appetite stimulant in children.

meconium ileus.definition: A neonatal intestinal obstruction caused by inspissated (thickened) meconium obstructing the ileum, often associated with cystic fibrosis.

cystic fibrosis transmembrane regulator.definition: A chloride and bicarbonate channel protein encoded by the CFTR gene, regulating salt and water transport across epithelial surfaces; mutations cause cystic fibrosis.

transmembrane conductance regulator.definition: A membrane protein that forms a regulated chloride channel in epithelial cells, controlling chloride (and bicarbonate) ion transport; its activity is regulated by cAMP-dependent phosphorylation and ATP binding/hydrolysis, and mutations cause cystic fibrosis.

cystic goiter.definition: A thyroid enlargement in which nodules have undergone cystic degeneration, producing fluid-filled spaces within the thyroid tissue.

cystic hygroma.definition: A congenital lymphatic malformation consisting of one or more large, cystic, fluid-filled spaces—most often in the neck—caused by failure of embryonic lymphatic channels to connect with the venous system.

cystic lymphangioma.definition: A benign congenital malformation of the lymphatic system characterized by cystic dilation of lymphatic channels, forming a soft, compressible, usually transilluminant mass most often in the neck or axilla; may enlarge with infection or hemorrhage and is typically treated with sclerotherapy or surgical excision.

cystic mole.definition: A gestational trophoblastic disease in which placental villi become hydropic and cystic due to abnormal fertilization, producing a molar pregnancy. It is classified as complete mole (no fetal tissue, paternal origin) or partial mole (fetal tissue present with abnormal villi).

hydatid mole.definition: A gestational trophoblastic disease caused by abnormal fertilization in which placental chorionic villi become edematous (hydropic) and trophoblastic tissue proliferates; most commonly a complete mole with no viable fetus (paternal genetic origin), though a partial mole with fetal tissue can occur. It typically presents with vaginal bleeding, uterine enlargement out of proportion to gestational age, and very high hCG; ultrasound may show a snowstorm pattern. Management is uterine evacuation (usually suction curettage) with serial hCG monitoring to confirm resolution.

cystic myxoma.definition: Benign connective-tissue tumor composed of spindle- to stellate-shaped cells embedded in a mucopolysaccharide-rich, gelatinous stroma, with cystic (fluid-filled) spaces that arise from degenerative changes.

cystic nephroblastoma.definition: A pediatric malignant renal tumor (a cystic variant of Wilms tumor) arising from nephrogenic blastemal cells, presenting as a predominantly cystic renal mass; histology typically shows triphasic Wilms tumor elements—blastemal, epithelial (immature tubules), and stromal components.

nephroblastoma.definition: An embryonal malignant kidney tumor that occurs in children, arising from primitive renal precursor cells.
