cystic neuroma.definition: A benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor (a schwannoma/neurilemmoma) with cystic degeneration, containing fluid-filled or gel-filled cystic spaces within the tumor; a cystic variant of schwannoma.

false neuroma.definition: A nonneoplastic proliferation of peripheral nerve fibers and supporting tissue at the end of a damaged nerve (nerve stump), forming a painful lump at the site of injury.

cystic pyelitis.definition: An inflammatory condition of the renal pelvis characterized by cystic dilatations of the collecting system, usually due to chronic infection or obstruction.

cystic pyeloureteritis.definition: An uncommon inflammatory disorder of the renal pelvis and ureter in which cyst-like dilatations develop within the pelvicalyceal system, typically related to chronic infection or obstruction; presents with upper urinary tract symptoms and is seen on imaging as cystic dilatations of the collecting system.

cystic renal dysplasia.definition: A congenital disorder in which renal parenchyma is abnormal and replaced by dysplastic tissue with multiple cysts, resulting in nonfunctional renal tissue; may be unilateral or bilateral, with bilateral disease potentially causing oligohydramnios and renal failure in infancy.

cystic tumor.definition: A neoplasm in which cysts (fluid-filled spaces) predominate or are a major component; the lesion may be benign or malignant.

cystoid macular edema.definition: An eye condition in which the retina (the macula) becomes swollen with fluid.

cystojejunostomy.definition: A surgical procedure that connects a cyst to the jejunum to drain cyst contents into the small intestine, commonly used for pancreatic pseudocysts.

cystolith.definition: A stone (calculus) formed in the urinary bladder.

cystolithalopaxy.definition: A procedure to fragment bladder stones and remove the fragments endoscopically, usually through a cystoscope, using a lithotrite, laser, or ultrasonic device.

cystolithotomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove stones from the urinary bladder by making an incision in the bladder wall (cystotomy) and extracting the stones.

cystoma.definition: A cystic tumor; a neoplasm characterized by cyst formation or cyst-like spaces, which may be benign or malignant.

cystomata.definition: A cystic tumor; a benign neoplasm composed of cysts or cyst-like spaces, often lined by epithelium.

cystometer.definition: An instrument used in urodynamic testing to measure intravesical pressure during bladder filling, typically via a catheter connected to a pressure transducer, to record a cystometrogram and assess bladder capacity, compliance, and detrusor function.

cystometrogram.definition: A urodynamic test in which the bladder is filled via a catheter while intravesical pressure is measured, enabling assessment of bladder capacity, compliance, and detrusor activity to diagnose disorders such as detrusor overactivity, underactivity, or neurogenic bladder.

cystometrography.definition: A urodynamic test in which the bladder is gradually filled with sterile fluid via a catheter while intravesical pressure and volume are recorded to assess detrusor function, bladder capacity, and outlet function.

cystometry.definition: A urodynamic procedure in which the bladder is gradually filled with sterile saline via a catheter while intravesical pressure and detrusor activity are recorded to assess bladder capacity, compliance, and detrusor function; used to diagnose voiding disorders such as overactive or neurogenic bladder.

cystoscope.definition: An endoscopic instrument used to visualize the interior of the bladder and urethra, inserted through the urethra; it may be rigid or flexible and is equipped with a light source and camera, often with channels to perform biopsy, treatment, or irrigation.

cystoscopic.definition: Relating to cystoscopy or performed with a cystoscope; pertaining to the inspection of the bladder interior via a cystoscope inserted through the urethra.

retrograde cystoscopy.definition: A procedure in which a cystoscope is inserted through the urethra and advanced toward the bladder (retrograde approach) to visualize the bladder mucosa and urethra and to perform diagnostic or therapeutic maneuvers such as biopsy or lesion assessment.

cystoscopic urography.definition: A diagnostic radiologic study of the urinary tract performed under cystoscopic guidance, in which contrast is injected via the ureteral orifices to outline the ureters and renal pelvis (retrograde urography).

cystocele.definition: A prolapse of the urinary bladder into the vagina due to weakness of the anterior pelvic floor supporting tissues, causing a bulge in the anterior vaginal wall and possible urinary symptoms.

cystodynia.definition: Pain originating from the urinary bladder; bladder pain.

cystomyoma.definition: A benign smooth muscle tumor (leiomyoma) with cystic changes or cystic degeneration.

cystic diverticulum.definition: A sac-like outpouching from a hollow organ that contains a cystic, fluid-filled cavity and communicates with the organ’s lumen.

hepatic diverticulum.definition: An embryologic ventral outgrowth of the distal foregut endoderm (the liver bud) that gives rise to the liver parenchyma and the biliary apparatus (intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts) as it differentiates during early gestation.

computed tomographic scan.definition: A radiologic imaging modality that uses rotating X-ray beams and computer reconstruction to produce cross-sectional images of the body; allows detailed visualization of internal organs and tissues and can be reformatted into 3D images; often uses intravenous contrast and involves ionizing radiation.

cystogram.definition: A radiographic examination of the bladder performed after instilling contrast material via catheter to visualize the bladder on imaging; used to assess bladder integrity, anatomy, and conditions such as injury, diverticula, tumors, or vesicoureteral reflux.

cystography.definition: A radiologic imaging study in which contrast is instilled into the bladder to visualize its structure on X-ray, used to detect abnormalities such as rupture, stones, tumors, or leaks; can be performed as a static study or during voiding (voiding cystourethrogram).

taenia solium.definition: A parasitic cestode (tapeworm) known as the pork tapeworm; it resides in the human small intestine as an adult (causing taeniasis) and is acquired by eating undercooked pork containing cysticerci; its eggs can cause cysticercosis if ingested, leading to tissue infections such as neurocysticercosis.

cysticercus.definition: The larval form of Taenia solium (pork tapeworm) that develops as cysts in tissues and contains an invaginated scolex; this cysticercus can cause cysticercosis when humans harbor the larvae (commonly in muscle, brain, or subcutaneous tissue).

serous cystadenoma.definition: Benign ovarian epithelial tumor consisting of a multilocular cystic mass filled with clear serous fluid and lined by serous (ciliated) epithelium; usually unilateral and cured by surgical excision.

vitamin b6.definition: A group of related vitamers—pyridoxine, pyridoxal, and pyridoxamine—that are converted to the active coenzyme pyridoxal phosphate (PLP); they function as cofactors in amino acid metabolism and in the synthesis of neurotransmitters, heme, and niacin from tryptophan. Deficiency can cause dermatitis, glossitis, anemia, and neuropathy; dietary sources include meat, fish, poultry, eggs, fortified cereals, and legumes.

mucolytic agents.definition: Mucolytic agents are medications that thin or break down mucus in the airways to facilitate clearance by coughing or suctioning. They reduce mucus viscosity, often by breaking disulfide bonds in mucin glycoproteins (for example, N-acetylcysteine, carbocisteine) or by enzymatically cleaving sputum DNA (for example, dornase alfa).

sweat chloride test.definition: A diagnostic test that measures the concentration of chloride in sweat after stimulation of sweat glands (usually by pilocarpine iontophoresis); values ≥60 mmol/L support a diagnosis of cystic fibrosis, while values <30 mmol/L are typically normal, with 30–59 mmol/L considered intermediate and requiring further evaluation.

kupffer cells.definition: A liver-resident macrophage located in the hepatic sinusoids; part of the reticuloendothelial (mononuclear phagocyte) system; phagocytoses bacteria, debris, and aged red blood cells, and modulates immune responses via cytokine production.

cystospaz.definition: A sudden, involuntary contraction of the urinary bladder (detrusor muscle) causing urgent need to void, sometimes with pain or retention; can be triggered by bladder irritation, infection, catheterization, or neurologic disease.

cytochrome-c-oxidase.definition: An enzyme of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (Complex IV) that transfers electrons from cytochrome c to molecular oxygen, reducing O2 to water and pumping protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane to contribute to the proton motive force used for ATP production; inhibited by cyanide and carbon monoxide.

distension.definition: An abnormal enlargement or swelling of a hollow organ or body cavity, typically due to accumulation of gas, fluid, or other contents.

l-hyoscyamine.definition: A levorotatory enantiomer of hyoscyamine; a tropane alkaloid with antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) activity used to relax GI smooth muscle and decrease secretions.

cystostomy.definition: A surgical procedure that creates an opening from the bladder to the outside of the body to allow urine drainage, typically through the abdominal wall.

cystotomy.definition: A surgical incision into the urinary bladder.

cystoureterography.definition: A radiographic study in which contrast material is introduced into the bladder (often via catheter) to visualize the bladder and ureters, used to evaluate vesicoureteral reflux, bladder/ureteral abnormalities, and obstruction.

cystourethrogram.definition: A radiographic study of the lower urinary tract in which contrast material is introduced into the bladder (and often the urethra) and imaged with fluoroscopy to evaluate anatomy and function; a voiding cystourethrogram specifically images the bladder during urination to detect vesicoureteral reflux and urethral abnormalities.

cystourethrography.definition: Radiographic examination of the bladder and urethra in which contrast is introduced (usually via catheter) and images are taken during filling and voiding to evaluate anatomy and function, including vesicoureteral reflux and urethral obstruction.

contrast medium.definition: A dye that helps make tissues or organs more visible on an X-ray or CT scan.

liver cysts.definition: Liver cysts are fluid-filled sacs within the liver, most commonly benign simple cysts lined by biliary epithelium and containing clear fluid; they are usually asymptomatic and found incidentally on imaging.

cystic kidney disease.definition: A group of disorders characterized by the development of multiple fluid-filled cysts in the kidneys, which can enlarge and replace normal renal tissue, often leading to chronic kidney disease. Many forms are inherited (e.g., autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease).

arabinosylcytosine.definition: A cytosine nucleoside analog (antimetabolite) used in chemotherapy; it inhibits DNA synthesis by incorporation into DNA and inhibition of DNA polymerase, and is used to treat acute myeloid leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and other hematologic malignancies.

ara-c.definition: A pyrimidine nucleoside analogue chemotherapy agent (antimetabolite) used to treat certain leukemias; it inhibits DNA synthesis by being incorporated into DNA and inhibiting DNA polymerase.

myelocytic leukemia.definition: A cancer of the myeloid cell lineage characterized by uncontrolled proliferation of abnormal myeloid cells in the bone marrow and peripheral blood, most commonly referring to acute myeloid leukemia (AML) or chronic myeloid leukemia (CML).

erythroleukemia.definition: A rare form of acute leukemia in which erythroid precursors predominate in the bone marrow and there is a significant population of myeloblasts; traditionally defined as bone marrow containing >50% erythroid cells with ≥20% blasts among the non-erythroid cells (FAB M6).

fanconi syndrome.definition: A disorder of proximal renal tubule function characterized by impaired reabsorption of glucose, amino acids, phosphate, and bicarbonate, causing glycosuria with normoglycemia, aminoaciduria, hypophosphatemia from phosphate wasting, and metabolic acidosis; it can be inherited or acquired.

sensorineural deafness.definition: Damage or dysfunction of the inner ear (cochlea) or the vestibulocochlear nerve, causing permanent hearing loss with reduced sound perception and poorer speech discrimination, not due to middle-ear pathology.

ocular defects.definition: A broad term for abnormalities of the eye or its adnexa, which may be congenital or acquired and can impair the structure or function of the visual system.

cardiac defects.definition: Structural abnormalities of the heart or great vessels that impair its function, most often congenital (present at birth); examples include septal defects, valve malformations, and outflow tract anomalies.

liver toxicity.definition: An injury or dysfunction of the liver caused by exposure to toxins—such as certain medications, alcohol, or environmental chemicals—that damages liver cells or bile flow, possibly leading to elevated liver enzymes, jaundice, fatigue, and impaired hepatic function.

aminoglutethimide.definition: A nonsteroidal inhibitor of aromatase (CYP19) and cholesterol side-chain cleavage (P450scc) that decreases estrogen and overall steroid hormone synthesis; historically used as adjuvant therapy for hormone-sensitive breast cancer and for adrenal disorders.

cytadren.definition: A medication that inhibits the enzyme 11β-hydroxylase (CYP11B1) in the adrenal cortex, decreasing cortisol synthesis; used in diagnostic adrenal function testing (the metyrapone test) and, in some settings, to treat Cushing's syndrome. It may cause increased ACTH and androgen excess, plus electrolyte disturbances.

cytoanalyzer.definition: An instrument that automates the analysis of cells in a sample, providing quantitative data on cell counts, size, morphology, and sometimes viability or fluorescence; used in hematology and cytology to quantify and characterize cell populations.

cytoarchitectonic.definition: Relating to the organization and arrangement of cells within a tissue, particularly the layered cellular architecture of the cerebral cortex, used to delineate distinct brain regions.

cytoarchitecture.definition: The arrangement and pattern of cells within a tissue, including cell types, densities, and layering, that defines its microscopic structure and helps distinguish anatomical regions (e.g., the layered cerebral cortex).

cytobiotaxis.definition: A process in which a cell directs its movement toward or away from a living stimulus (a biotic signal), i.e., migration guided by signals from other cells or organisms.

cytobiotactic.definition: The directed movement or orientation of cells in response to a biological (biotic) stimulus, i.e., movement toward or away from signals produced by living organisms.

cytoctony.definition:
The term as spelled does not appear in medical dictionaries. It may be a misspelling. Possible intended meanings include:
- A surgical incision into the urinary bladder.
- The study and diagnosis of diseases at the cellular level by examining cells under a microscope.

cytode.definition: Not a standard medical term; not found in reputable medical dictionaries. If you can share the context or confirm the spelling, I can help with the intended term.

cytodendrite.definition: Not a standard medical term; if used, it would refer to a dendrite-like cytoplasmic projection extending from a cell body, typically involved in receiving signals or intercellular communication; the conventional term is dendrite.

cytodiagnosis.definition: Diagnosis based on the microscopic examination of cells obtained from tissues or body fluids (cytology), used to detect diseases—especially malignancies (e.g., Pap test, fine-needle aspiration cytology).

cytodieresis.definition: The division of the cytoplasm during cell division, producing two separate daughter cells; it completes cytokinesis following nuclear division.

cytodiereses.definition: Cytodieresis is the division of the cytoplasm during cell division, completing cytokinesis to form two separate daughter cells; in animal cells it occurs via a cleavage furrow, while in plant cells it occurs by the formation of a cell plate that divides the cytoplasm.

cytodifferentiation.definition: The process by which precursor or stem cells develop into mature, specialized cell types with distinct structure and function, guided by regulated gene expression and signaling in response to the cellular microenvironment.

cytofluorograph.definition: A device that detects and measures fluorescence emitted by labeled cells or particles, usually as part of flow cytometry, to quantify and analyze multiple cellular markers and produce per-cell fluorescence data.

cytogony.definition: The origin and development of the cytoplasm within a cell; the formation and growth of cytoplasmic material and organelles during cellular development. This is a rarely used term and is not common in modern medical literature.

cytohistogenesis.definition: The origin and development of cells and tissues, integrating cellular differentiation and tissue formation to explain how cells arise and organize into tissues (as in embryogenesis and tumor histogenesis).

cytohyaloplasm.definition: The clear, non-granulated portion of the cytoplasm (the hyaloplasm or cytosol) of a cell, constituting the ground substance in which organelles are suspended.

cytoid.definition: Resembling a cell; cell-like in appearance.

cytoid body.definition: An eosinophilic apoptotic keratinocyte (necrotic basal cell) typically located at the dermoepidermal junction, seen in lichenoid dermatoses such as lichen planus; also called Civatte bodies or colloid bodies.

cytokerastic.definition: Not a standard medical term; likely a misspelling of cytokeratotic or cytokeratosis. If intended, it would describe keratinization or keratin-containing changes in epithelial cells (keratin formation within epithelial cells). If you meant a different spelling (e.g., cytokeratotic), I can check that exact term.

cytokine assay.definition: A laboratory test that quantifies levels of cytokines—immune signaling proteins such as interleukins, interferons, and tumor necrosis factor—in a biological sample (e.g., blood, serum, plasma, cell culture supernatant), typically using immunoassays like ELISA or multiplex bead-based assays.

cytokine network.definition: A complex, interconnected system of cytokines and their receptors that regulate immune and inflammatory responses through autocrine, paracrine, and endocrine signaling; characterized by redundancy, pleiotropy, feedback loops, and cross-talk among pathways to coordinate initiation, amplification, suppression, and resolution of immune reactions.

interleukin-1.definition: A group of proinflammatory cytokines, primarily IL-1α and IL-1β, produced by activated macrophages and other cells; they mediate fever and inflammatory responses by signaling through the IL-1 receptor and inducing expression of adhesion molecules, chemokines, and other cytokines. Activity is regulated by the IL-1 receptor antagonist.

interleukin-3.definition: A hematopoietic growth factor (cytokine) produced mainly by activated T cells that stimulates proliferation and differentiation of multipotent hematopoietic progenitors into multiple myeloid lineages (including granulocytes, erythrocytes, megakaryocytes, and monocytes) and supports survival of basophils and mast cells; it acts through the IL-3 receptor.

interleukin-7.definition: A cytokine of the IL-2 family that promotes T-cell development and homeostasis. It is produced mainly by stromal and epithelial cells and signals through the IL-7 receptor (CD127 and the common gamma chain) to support thymopoiesis and the survival and homeostatic proliferation of naive and memory T cells via JAK-STAT signaling.

interleukin-9.definition: A cytokine produced primarily by Th9 cells (and other immune cells) that signals through the IL-9 receptor to promote the growth and survival of mast cells and other hematopoietic cells and to enhance mucosal immunity and allergic inflammation, including mucus production in the airways.

interleukin-10.definition: A cytokine with anti-inflammatory effects produced by monocytes, macrophages, dendritic cells, and certain T cells; it suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokines, downregulates antigen presentation, and promotes B-cell survival and antibody production.

interleukin-11.definition: A cytokine in the IL-6 family that stimulates megakaryocyte maturation and thrombopoiesis, increasing platelet production. It is produced by stromal and some immune cells, signals through a receptor complex of IL-11 receptor alpha and gp130, and activates JAK/STAT signaling. Clinically, recombinant forms have been used to prevent chemotherapy‑induced thrombocytopenia.

interleukin-12.definition: A proinflammatory cytokine produced by antigen-presenting cells that promotes differentiation of naive CD4+ T cells into Th1 cells and stimulates IFN-γ production by NK and T cells; it is a heterodimer (p35 and p40 subunits) that signals through the IL-12 receptor to activate the JAK-STAT pathway.

interleukin-13.definition: A Th2-associated cytokine that promotes allergic inflammation and tissue remodeling; it signals through the IL-4Rα/IL-13Rα1 receptor complex to drive IgE class switching, goblet cell hyperplasia and mucus production, airway hyperresponsiveness, and alternative macrophage activation, and can be neutralized by the decoy receptor IL-13Rα2.

interleukin-14.definition: A cytokine reported in some studies as a B-cell activating factor that may promote B-cell growth and survival, but its receptor and exact function are not well established and it is not a widely accepted standard interleukin.

interleukin-15.definition: Interleukin-15 is a cytokine in the IL-2 family that promotes the development, survival, and activation of natural killer cells and memory CD8+ T cells; it signals through the IL-2/15 receptor beta and gamma chains and is often presented in trans by cells expressing IL-15 receptor alpha.

interleukin-16.definition: A proinflammatory cytokine that acts as a chemoattractant for CD4+ T lymphocytes (and other immune cells); produced as a precursor and cleaved to a mature secreted form that binds CD4 and promotes recruitment of immune cells during immune responses.

interleukin-17.definition: A pro-inflammatory cytokine of the IL-17 family (primarily IL-17A) produced by Th17 cells and other immune cells; it stimulates epithelial and stromal cells to produce chemokines and cytokines, promoting neutrophil recruitment and inflammation, and plays a role in defense against extracellular bacteria and fungi as well as in autoimmune disease.

interleukin-18.definition: A proinflammatory cytokine of the IL-1 family produced as an inactive pro-form and activated by caspase-1 in the inflammasome; it induces interferon-γ production by NK and T cells, promoting Th1 responses and contributing to inflammatory and metabolic diseases.

interleukin-19.definition: A cytokine of the IL-10 family produced by activated monocytes/macrophages and keratinocytes; it signals through IL-20 receptor complexes to activate JAK–STAT signaling and modulate inflammatory responses, often promoting Th2-type inflammation and implicated in inflammatory skin diseases such as psoriasis.

interleukin-20.definition: A cytokine in the IL-10 family that signals through IL-20 receptor complexes and acts on keratinocytes to promote inflammatory responses; produced by keratinocytes and immune cells and implicated in skin inflammation such as psoriasis.

interleukin-21.definition: A cytokine of the IL-2 family produced primarily by activated CD4+ T cells (especially T follicular helper cells) that signals through the IL-21 receptor to regulate B-cell differentiation and antibody production, and to enhance CD8+ T-cell and NK-cell responses; involved in humoral and cellular immunity and in autoimmunity and cancer.

interleukin-22.definition: A cytokine in the IL-10 family produced by Th17/Th22 cells, γδ T cells, and innate lymphoid cells; it acts on epithelial and other non-hematopoietic cells via the IL-22 receptor (IL-22R1/IL-10R2) to stimulate antimicrobial peptide production, promote barrier integrity, and drive tissue repair, signaling primarily through STAT3. It provides mucosal protection but can contribute to inflammatory pathology in chronic diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis.

interleukin-23.definition: A pro-inflammatory cytokine heterodimer (subunits p19 and p40) of the IL-12 family produced mainly by activated dendritic cells and macrophages; it signals via the IL-23 receptor to promote differentiation and maintenance of Th17 cells and stimulate IL-17 production, contributing to inflammatory and autoimmune responses.

interleukin-24.definition: A cytokine in the IL-10 family produced by activated immune cells; it signals through receptor complexes IL-20R1/IL-20R2 or IL-22R1/IL-20R2, activating JAK-STAT pathways, and has immunomodulatory and tumor-suppressive effects, including selective induction of apoptosis in many cancer cells with relatively low toxicity to normal cells.

interleukin-25.definition: A cytokine in the IL-17 family (also called IL-17E) produced by epithelial and Th2 cells; it signals through the IL-17RA/IL-17RB receptor complex to promote type 2 immunity by inducing IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13 production and activating ILC2s, contributing to allergic inflammation and defense against helminths.

interleukin-26.definition: A proinflammatory cytokine of the IL-10 family produced by activated T cells (notably Th17) and some myeloid cells; it signals through a receptor complex of IL-20R1 and IL-10R2 to promote production of other cytokines/chemokines and contribute to mucosal immunity and inflammatory or autoimmune diseases.

interleukin-27.definition: A heterodimeric cytokine of the IL-12 family produced by activated antigen-presenting cells; composed of subunits p28 and EBI3; signals through the IL-27 receptor (WSX-1/GP130) to regulate innate and adaptive immunity, promoting early Th1 responses while limiting Th17 and Th2 differentiation and inducing anti-inflammatory IL-10 in some T cells.

interferon.definition: A protein that signals the body that viruses or bacteria are inside.

alpha-interferon.definition: A type I interferon produced mainly by leukocytes; it has antiviral, antiproliferative, and immunomodulatory effects, acting through the IFNAR receptor to activate JAK-STAT signaling and induce interferon-stimulated genes. It is used therapeutically as interferon-α in certain viral infections and cancers.

beta-interferon.definition: A recombinant type I interferon used as a disease-modifying therapy for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis; it modulates the immune response and reduces inflammatory activity in the central nervous system, typically administered by injection.

gamma-interferon.definition: A cytokine of the interferon family produced primarily by natural killer cells and Th1-type CD4+ T cells (and some CD8+ T cells); it activates macrophages, upregulates antigen presentation by increasing MHC expression, promotes Th1 responses, and has antiviral and antiproliferative effects; signals via the JAK-STAT pathway and is used therapeutically to boost cellular immunity in certain immunodeficiencies such as chronic granulomatous disease.

tumor necrosis factor.definition: A proinflammatory cytokine produced mainly by activated macrophages (also by other immune cells) that mediates systemic inflammation, fever, and apoptotic cell death, and acts by binding to TNF receptors (TNFR1 and TNFR2); it has two main forms, TNF-α and TNF-β (lymphotoxin-α).

tnf.definition: A pro-inflammatory cytokine produced mainly by activated macrophages; exists as TNF-α and TNF-β (lymphotoxin); drives inflammation, fever, apoptosis, and the acute-phase response by signaling through TNF receptors TNFR1 and TNFR2; a major target in autoimmune disease therapy (e.g., anti-TNF drugs).

g-csf.definition: A hematopoietic growth factor (cytokine) that stimulates the bone marrow to produce and release neutrophils (a type of granulocyte) into the bloodstream; used to prevent or treat neutropenia after chemotherapy and to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells for transplantation.

granulocyte colony-stimulating factor.definition: A hematopoietic growth factor (glycoprotein) that stimulates the bone marrow to increase production and maturation of neutrophils (granulocytes) and release them into the bloodstream; used to treat neutropenia, such as after chemotherapy.

gm-csf.definition: A cytokine that stimulates the production and differentiation of granulocytes and macrophages from hematopoietic progenitors and enhances the phagocytic and microbicidal activity of mature neutrophils and macrophages; produced by T cells, macrophages, and other cells in response to inflammation.

granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulatin.definition: A hematopoietic cytokine that stimulates the proliferation and differentiation of progenitor cells into granulocytes and macrophages, and activates mature neutrophils and macrophages; used clinically to treat neutropenia and promote hematologic recovery.

m-csf.definition: Macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF), also known as CSF-1, is a cytokine that promotes the survival, proliferation, and differentiation of hematopoietic progenitor cells into monocytes and macrophages, acting through the CSF1 receptor (CSF1R/CD115).

cytapheresis.definition: A procedure in which specific blood cells are selectively removed from the peripheral blood by apheresis, used therapeutically (for example, to remove granulocytes or lymphocytes in hematologic or autoimmune conditions).

apheresis.definition: A procedure in which blood is drawn, separated into its components, a targeted component (e.g., plasma or platelets) is removed, and the remainder is returned to the patient.

red cells.definition: A type of blood cell containing hemoglobin that transports oxygen from the lungs to tissues and carbon dioxide from tissues back to the lungs; typically enucleate in mammals and has a biconcave shape.

granulocytes.definition: A class of white blood cells with cytoplasmic granules; includes neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils; produced in the bone marrow and part of the innate immune system, performing phagocytosis, antiparasitic and allergic responses, and release of inflammatory mediators.

ophthalmoscope.definition: An instrument with a light and mirrors for examining the deep interior of the eye.

cystosarcoma phylloides.definition: An older name for a fibroepithelial breast tumor with leaf-like stromal projections (phyllodes tumor), which can be benign, borderline, or malignant and typically presents as a rapidly enlarging breast mass treated with wide local excision with clear margins.

cytochrome-p-450.definition: A superfamily of heme-containing monooxygenase enzymes that metabolize many drugs and endogenous compounds by inserting one oxygen atom into substrates (often via hydroxylation), using NADPH and molecular oxygen; chiefly expressed in the liver and central to phase I drug metabolism and the synthesis of steroids and cholesterol.

cytokinesis.definition: The division of the cytoplasm at the end of cell division, following mitosis or meiosis, resulting in two separate daughter cells. In animal cells, an actin-based contractile ring forms a cleavage furrow that pinches the cell membrane to divide; in plant cells, vesicles coalesce at the center to form a cell plate that becomes separating cell walls.

adrenalitis.definition: Inflammation of one or both adrenal glands, commonly due to infection or autoimmune disease, which may impair production of adrenal hormones and cause adrenal insufficiency.

asymptomatic infections.definition: An infection in which a person harbors a pathogen but remains symptom-free, though they may still shed and transmit the organism to others.

pathological fracture.definition: A fracture that occurs in bone weakened by disease, such that it can happen with minimal or no trauma; commonly seen with osteoporosis, metastatic cancer, primary bone tumors, infection, or other metabolic bone disorders.

hearing.definition: The sense that enables the perception of sound; the process by which mechanical vibrations (sound waves) are captured by the outer ear, transmitted through the middle ear, and transduced into neural signals by the inner ear for interpretation by the brain.

ocular abnormalities.definition: Any deviation from normal eye structure or function, including congenital or acquired defects of the eye itself or its surrounding structures, that can affect vision.

dental abnormalities.definition: Any deviation from normal dentition, including abnormalities in tooth number, size, shape, structure, eruption, or alignment, often of developmental origin and may include enamel or dentin defects, impaction, malocclusion, or supernumerary teeth.

psoriatic arthritis.definition: Causes pain, stiffness, and swelling in the joints. Some people also develop the skin rash of psoriasis.

pyrosis.definition: A burning sensation in the chest or throat caused by reflux of stomach acid into the esophagus, commonly known as heartburn.

decitabine.definition: A cytidine analog and DNA methyltransferase inhibitor (also known as 5-aza-2′-deoxycytidine) used as a hypomethylating agent in myelodysplastic syndromes and certain leukemias; it incorporates into DNA and inhibits DNMT, leading to DNA hypomethylation and reactivation of silenced genes.

dideoxythymidine.definition: A 2',3'-dideoxythymidine (ddT), a nucleoside analog of thymidine lacking the 3'-hydroxyl group, used as a chain-terminating nucleotide in Sanger DNA sequencing; its triphosphate form is ddTTP.

d4t.definition: A nucleoside analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used to treat HIV infection; a thymidine analog that inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase, terminating viral DNA synthesis.

daclizumab.definition: Humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the IL-2 receptor α chain (CD25); inhibits IL-2–mediated T-cell activation, used to prevent organ transplant rejection (e.g., kidney transplantation).

dacogen.definition: A cytidine analog that inhibits DNA methyltransferase, producing DNA hypomethylation; used as a hypomethylating agent to treat myelodysplastic syndromes and certain leukemias.

cytovene.definition: An intravenous antiviral drug (cidofovir) used to treat cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in patients with AIDS; inhibits viral DNA polymerase and is associated with nephrotoxicity, often mitigated by co-administration of probenecid.

cytoxan.definition: An alkylating chemotherapy agent (cyclophosphamide) used to treat a variety of cancers and some autoimmune diseases; it cross-links DNA to inhibit replication and cell division, and is given orally or intravenously. Common adverse effects include bone marrow suppression and hemorrhagic cystitis.

nasolacrimal duct.definition: A duct that drains tears from the lacrimal sac into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity, forming part of the lacrimal drainage system; obstruction can cause epiphora.

lacrimal sac.definition: A sac in the tear drainage system that collects tears from the canaliculi and drains into the nasolacrimal duct; located in the lacrimal fossa of the maxilla near the medial canthus.

dacryocystorhinostomy.definition: A surgical procedure that creates a new drainage route between the lacrimal sac and the nasal cavity to bypass obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct and relieve chronic epiphora.

dacryocystectomy.definition: The surgical excision (removal) of the lacrimal sac, typically performed to treat chronic dacryocystitis or lacrimal sac tumors.

dacryocystitis.definition: An infection and inflammation of the lacrimal sac, typically due to obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct, presenting with tearing, swelling and tenderness over the lacrimal sac and purulent discharge; it may be acute or chronic and can lead to orbital cellulitis if untreated.

dacryoadenitis.definition: An inflammation of the lacrimal gland, usually presenting with swelling and tenderness of the upper-outer eyelid and tearing; it can be acute or chronic and may result from infection (viral or bacterial) or inflammatory/autoimmune conditions.

dacryocele.definition: A cystic dilation of the lacrimal sac caused by obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct, presenting as a medial canthal swelling with tearing; in newborns it may be a congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction (dacryocystocele).

dacryorrhea.definition: Discharge of tears from the eye; excessive or continuous watery tearing due to irritation, inflammation, or obstruction of the lacrimal apparatus or its drainage (nasolacrimal duct).

type ii pneumocytes.definition: Alveolar epithelial cells that synthesize and secrete pulmonary surfactant, a lipid-protein complex that lowers surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse; they also serve as progenitor cells that can differentiate into type I pneumocytes to regenerate the alveolar epithelium after injury.

pneumocytes.definition: Alveolar epithelial cells of the lungs; two main types: Type I pneumocytes are thin squamous cells forming most of the gas-exchange surface of the alveolar wall, while Type II pneumocytes are cuboidal cells that secrete pulmonary surfactant and serve as progenitors capable of differentiating into Type I cells during repair.

chloroplasts.definition: A double-membrane–bound organelle in plant and algal cells that carries out photosynthesis; it contains chlorophyll and the photosynthetic machinery, including thylakoid membranes organized into grana and a stroma with enzymes of the Calvin cycle, and it contains its own circular DNA and ribosomes.

organelles.definition: Subcellular structures within a cell that perform dedicated functions necessary for cellular life; they include components such as the nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and ribosomes (most are membrane-bound, though some are not).

cytoplasm.definition: The jelly-like substance inside the cell, excluding the nucleus, comprising cytosol, organelles, and the cytoskeleton; the site of most metabolic activities and protein synthesis.

cytoplasmic bridge.definition: A transient cytoplasmic connection between developing germ cells (spermatids) after incomplete cytokinesis, permitting exchange of cytoplasm and coordinated maturation.

intercellular bridge.definition: A cytoplasmic connection between two adjacent cells that remains after incomplete cytokinesis, forming a bridge through which cytoplasm and organelles can pass and cells can coordinate development; most notably described between developing spermatids during spermatogenesis.

perikaryon.definition: The cell body of a neuron, containing the nucleus and most of the cytoplasm and organelles; the metabolic center from which dendrites and the axon arise.

langhans' layer.definition: Not a standard anatomical term; no widely accepted definition. If encountered, it may refer informally to the granulomatous tissue region containing Langhans giant cells (multinucleated macrophages with peripherally arranged nuclei) seen in diseases such as tuberculosis.

igm.definition: A primary antibody isotype produced early in the humoral immune response; secreted mainly as a pentamer (five monomer units) with a joining (J) chain and circulating in serum; highly effective at agglutination and neutralization of pathogens and a potent activator of the classical complement pathway; also serves as the B cell receptor on naive B cells.

immune globulin.definition: Part of your blood that helps to fight disease.

torch syndrome.definition: A group of congenital infections acquired in utero that can cause fetal or neonatal abnormalities, including toxoplasmosis, rubella, cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex virus, and other infections such as syphilis, varicella-zoster, and parvovirus B19.

dactylus.definition: A digit of the hand or foot (a finger or toe); used in anatomical terminology to denote a finger or toe.

dactyly.definition: The condition of having fingers or toes; the digits of the hands or feet.

dactylia.definition: Pertaining to the digits (fingers or toes); a terse or historical term sometimes used to denote digit-related anomalies, such as polydactyly or syndactyly.

diffuse axonal injury.definition: A traumatic brain injury caused by rapid acceleration–deceleration forces that shear axons in the white matter, resulting in widespread neuronal disruption. It often presents with immediate coma or prolonged unconsciousness and may show small hemorrhages in the corpus callosum and brainstem on imaging.

dapre.definition: A rehabilitation protocol for progressive resistance exercise in which the resistance is adjusted daily based on the patient’s performance, typically using a four-set scheme to determine the appropriate load for subsequent sessions.

dakin’s solution.definition: An antiseptic wound-irrigation solution consisting of dilute sodium hypochlorite (household bleach) in saline, typically around 0.5% active chlorine; it acts as an oxidizing disinfectant but can be irritating and cytotoxic to tissue, and its use has declined in modern practice in favor of gentler irrigants.

dalfopristin.definition: A streptogramin antibiotic used in combination with quinupristin (as quinupristin/dalfopristin) to treat certain Gram-positive infections; it binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis, with synergistic bactericidal activity when paired with quinupristin.

dalteparin sodium.definition: A low molecular weight heparin anticoagulant derived from porcine heparin; it inhibits factor Xa (via antithrombin III) with less effect on thrombin, and is used to prevent and treat thromboembolic disorders such as deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, and in selected acute coronary syndrome settings; administered subcutaneously with more predictable pharmacokinetics and typically without routine coagulation monitoring.

daltonism.definition: A hereditary color vision deficiency characterized by impaired ability to distinguish red and green hues, due to abnormal or absent L- or M-cone photopigments; most commonly inherited in an X‑linked pattern.

danaparoid.definition: A heparinoid anticoagulant derived from porcine mucosa, consisting mainly of dermatan sulfate, heparan sulfate, and chondroitin sulfate; inhibits factor Xa (and to a lesser extent thrombin) and is used to prevent and treat thrombosis, notably in heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.

danazol.definition: A synthetic, orally active androgen derivative (17α-ethinyl testosterone analogue) that suppresses the pituitary-ovarian axis by inhibiting gonadotropin (FSH and LH) release, thereby reducing estrogen production; used to treat endometriosis, hereditary angioedema, and fibrocystic breast disease. It can cause androgenic side effects (hirsutism, acne, virilization) and is contraindicated in pregnancy and liver disease.

fibrocystic breast disease.definition: A common benign breast condition characterized by fibrous tissue proliferation and fluid-filled cysts, causing lumpiness, tenderness, and swelling that often fluctuate with the menstrual cycle; it is not cancer and typically requires evaluation only to exclude malignancy if a suspicious mass is present.

hereditary angioedema.definition: An autosomal dominant genetic disorder characterized by recurrent, nonpitting angioedema (swelling) of subcutaneous and mucosal tissues caused by deficiency or dysfunction of C1 esterase inhibitor, leading to excess bradykinin; episodes may involve the face, gastrointestinal tract, or airway and can be life-threatening if the airway is affected.

dandy-walker cyst.definition: A congenital posterior fossa cyst resulting from dilation of the fourth ventricle that communicates with the subarachnoid space, typically with cerebellar vermis hypoplasia or agenesis and enlargement of the posterior fossa (Dandy-Walker malformation).

dandy-walker malformation.definition: Congenital brain malformation characterized by agenesis or hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis, cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle, and enlargement of the posterior fossa, often with hydrocephalus.

histoplasmosis.definition: A fungal infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, acquired by inhalation of airborne spores from soil contaminated with bird or bat droppings; clinical spectrum ranges from asymptomatic or mild respiratory illness to chronic pulmonary disease or disseminated disease, especially in immunocompromised hosts; treatment depends on severity (often itraconazole for mild to moderate disease; amphotericin B for severe or disseminated disease).

hydatid cyst.definition: A parasitic cyst formed by the larval stage of Echinococcus tapeworm (most often E. granulosus), usually in the liver or lungs; the cyst contains hydatid fluid and brood capsules with protoscolices, and rupture may cause anaphylaxis or spread of infection.

danocrine.definition: A synthetic androgen used to treat endometriosis and hereditary angioedema; it suppresses the pituitary-ovarian axis, reducing estrogen production; may cause masculinization, weight gain, acne, liver toxicity, and is contraindicated in pregnancy.

danthron.definition: A stimulant laxative derived from an anthraquinone compound, used historically to treat constipation by stimulating colonic peristalsis; prolonged use or high doses can cause cramps and electrolyte disturbances and may carry a carcinogenicity risk, leading to restricted or discouraged use in many countries.

dantrium.definition: A brand name for dantrolene, a skeletal muscle relaxant that inhibits calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum in skeletal muscle; used to treat malignant hyperthermia and to reduce spasticity.

dantrolene.definition: A skeletal muscle relaxant that inhibits calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum by blocking the ryanodine receptor (RyR1), used to treat malignant hyperthermia and to reduce spasticity in certain neurological conditions.

dantrolene sodium.definition: An oral or injectable skeletal muscle relaxant that inhibits calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum by antagonizing the ryanodine receptor (RYR1), reducing skeletal muscle contraction; used to treat and prevent malignant hyperthermia and to lessen severe spasticity; long-term use carries risk of hepatotoxicity.

dapiprazole.definition: A topical ophthalmic agent that acts as an alpha-adrenergic receptor antagonist to reverse pharmacologic mydriasis (pupil dilation) caused by adrenergic agonists such as phenylephrine.

dapsone.definition: A sulfone antibiotic used to treat leprosy and dermatitis herpetiformis; it inhibits bacterial dihydropteroate synthase, blocking folate synthesis, and is also used for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prophylaxis in selected patients.

daraprim.definition: A brand-name antiparasitic drug containing pyrimethamine; a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor used to treat toxoplasmosis and, in combination with sulfadiazine and leucovorin, for certain malaria regimens.

darbepoetin alfa.definition: Darbepoetin alfa is an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA), a recombinant analog of erythropoietin with extra sialic acid residues that prolong its half-life; it stimulates red blood cell production in the bone marrow and is used to treat anemia associated with chronic kidney disease, chemotherapy-induced anemia, and other causes.

darbid.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard medical dictionaries; may be a misspelling, a brand name, or a nonstandard acronym.

darier’s disease.definition: A rare autosomal dominant genetic skin disorder characterized by greasy, keratotic papules and plaques in seborrheic and flexural areas, often with nail abnormalities and mucosal changes; caused by mutations in ATP2A2 encoding the SERCA2 calcium pump, leading to defective keratinocyte adhesion (acantholysis) and dyskeratosis during keratinization.

darier’s sign.definition: A sign of cutaneous mastocytosis in which stroking or rubbing the skin produces a localized urticarial wheal and itching due to histamine release from dermal mast cells.

darkfield microscopy.definition: A microscopy technique that uses oblique illumination with a special condenser to make only light scattered by the specimen enter the objective, producing a bright image of transparent or unstained specimens against a dark background.

darling’s disease.definition: There is no widely accepted medical condition defined by that name; the term appears obscure or outdated and is not used in modern medical literature. If you can share context (organ system involved, key symptoms, era, or alternate spellings), I can suggest likely conditions or provide the modern terminology.

dartoic tissue.definition: A layer of subcutaneous tissue in the scrotum containing the dartos muscle (smooth muscle) that wrinkles the scrotal skin to reduce heat loss and help regulate testicular temperature.

dartos.definition: A layer of smooth muscle in the scrotal wall (the dartos muscle) that wrinkles the scrotal skin; helps regulate testicular temperature for spermatogenesis.

tunica dartos.definition: A subcutaneous layer of smooth muscle in the scrotum (the dartos muscle) that wrinkles the scrotal skin; its contraction reduces surface area to conserve heat and helps regulate testicular temperature.

auricular tubercle.definition: A small cartilaginous eminence or knob on the external ear (auricle), representing a tubercle on the auricular cartilage.

darwinian tubercle.definition: A small, rounded eminence on the helix (rim) of the external ear; a normal anatomical variation in ear morphology with no functional consequence.

darunavir.definition: A protease inhibitor antiretroviral used to treat HIV-1 infection; it inhibits the HIV-1 protease enzyme, preventing cleavage of Gag-Pol polyprotein and producing noninfectious viral particles. It is usually given orally with a boosting agent such as ritonavir or cobicistat and taken with food.

darvocet-n.definition: A combination prescription analgesic containing propoxyphene napsylate and acetaminophen; formerly used for mild-to-moderate pain, but withdrawn from the market due to risk of serious heart rhythm abnormalities.

darvon.definition: A brand name for the opioid analgesic propoxyphene; previously used to treat mild to moderate pain but withdrawn from the market because of risk of life-threatening heart rhythms and other serious safety concerns.

darvon compound.definition: A historical brand-name analgesic that combined the opioid propoxyphene (Darvon) with another analgesic component (traditionally aspirin) for relief of moderate to severe pain; its use declined and it was withdrawn from many markets due to safety concerns with propoxyphene.

darvon-n.definition: A prescription opioid analgesic combination product containing propoxyphene (usually as the napsylate salt) with acetaminophen, used for relief of moderate to moderately severe pain.

dasatinib.definition: A potent oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting BCR-ABL and several other kinases (including SRC family), used to treat Philadelphia chromosome–positive leukemias such as chronic myeloid leukemia and acute lymphoblastic leukemia, particularly after resistance or intolerance to imatinib.

denver articulation screening examinatio.definition: A brief, clinician-administered screening tool used to identify possible articulation disorders in children by evaluating the accuracy of consonant production across selected phonemes; designed to indicate whether a comprehensive speech-language pathology assessment is warranted.

total hip replacement.definition: A surgical procedure in which the damaged or diseased hip joint is removed and replaced with an artificial joint (prosthesis) made of metal, ceramic, and/or plastic to relieve pain and restore function. Also known as a total hip arthroplasty.

malignant hyperthermia.definition: A pharmacogenetic disorder of skeletal muscle calcium regulation triggered by certain anesthetics (notably volatile inhalational agents and succinylcholine) causing a life-threatening hypermetabolic crisis with rapid hypercarbia, tachycardia, muscle rigidity, hyperthermia, acidosis, and rhabdomyolysis; treated emergently with dantrolene and supportive care.

malignant hyperpyrexia.definition: A life-threatening pharmacogenetic disorder of skeletal muscle calcium regulation, usually inherited, triggered by certain anesthetics (eg, volatile inhaled agents) and depolarizing muscle relaxants (eg, succinylcholine), leading to uncontrolled calcium release, a hypermetabolic state with rapid CO2 production, acidosis, tachycardia, hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, rhabdomyolysis, and potentially death unless treated promptly with dantrolene.

cerebrovascular hemorrhage.definition: Bleeding within the brain or surrounding coverings caused by rupture of cerebral blood vessels; includes intracerebral and subarachnoid hemorrhages and presents with sudden neurologic deficits.

leprosy.definition: A long-term disease caused by a germ (a bacteria) that affects the nerves around the outside of the body, skin, and eyes. Also called Hansen's disease.

pneumocystis carinii.definition: A fungus that causes Pneumocystis pneumonia, an opportunistic lung infection seen in immunocompromised individuals; in humans, the organism is now usually called Pneumocystis jirovecii.

keratolytic shampoo.definition: A medicated shampoo containing keratolytic agents (e.g., salicylic acid, sulfur, or urea) that softens and loosens scales on the scalp by breaking down keratin, aiding their removal; used for dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, and psoriasis.

keratinized epithelium.definition: A type of stratified squamous epithelium in which the superficial cells accumulate keratin and die, forming a tough, keratin-rich protective outer layer (the stratum corneum), as seen in the epidermis.

mucositis.definition: Mucositis is inflammation and ulceration of the mucous membranes, most commonly the oral mucosa, often caused by chemotherapy or radiation therapy, leading to painful ulcers, soreness, and an increased risk of infection. It can affect any mucosal surface along the gastrointestinal tract.

grasp reflex.definition: A primitive infant reflex elicited by stroking the palm, causing finger flexion and a grasp around the object; it typically disappears by about 3–6 months of age, with persistence or re-emergence in later life suggesting frontal lobe dysfunction or other neurological pathology.

ventriculogram.definition: A radiographic study in which contrast material is injected into the cerebral ventricular system to visualize the ventricles and CSF pathways, used to evaluate hydrocephalus, obstruction, or shunt function.

dead fetus syndrome.definition: An obstetric condition in which fetal death occurs in utero but the dead fetus is retained in the uterus for an extended period, risking infection (endometritis or sepsis) and maternal coagulopathy; management involves prompt removal of the fetal remains and treatment of infection and any coagulopathy.

systemic infection.definition: An infection that has spread beyond the original site to involve multiple organ systems or the entire body, typically via the bloodstream, and may progress to sepsis.

anthracycline.definition: A class of chemotherapy agents known as antitumor antibiotics derived from Streptomyces species that intercalate into DNA and inhibit topoisomerase II, causing DNA breaks and cancer cell death. Used to treat a variety of cancers; examples include doxorubicin, daunorubicin, epirubicin, and idarubicin. Notable adverse effect is cumulative cardiotoxicity.

liposomal daunorubicin.definition: An anticancer drug (daunorubicin) enclosed in lipid-based vesicles (liposomes) to modify pharmacokinetics and tissue distribution, enabling tumor delivery with reduced cardiotoxicity compared with standard daunorubicin.

davidson regimen.definition: I couldn’t find a standard definition for “Davidson regimen” in trusted medical references. Could you share the condition or the source/context (e.g., cancer type, era, or study) so I can give a precise definition?

da vinci surgical system.definition: A robotic-assisted surgical system that translates a surgeon’s hand movements at a console into precise robotic-arm motions for minimally invasive procedures, featuring 3D high-definition visualization and EndoWrist instruments.

robotic surgery.definition: A minimally invasive surgical approach in which a computer-assisted robotic system guides miniature instruments and provides high-definition, magnified visualization, enabling greater precision and dexterity than traditional laparoscopy.

minimally invasive surgery.definition: A surgical technique that uses small incisions and specialized equipment (such as a laparoscope or robotic systems) to perform procedures with minimal tissue disruption, typically resulting in shorter recovery, less pain, and fewer complications than open surgery.

ureterotomy.definition: An incision into the ureter, typically performed to relieve obstruction, facilitate stone removal, or repair damage to the ureter.

davis ureterotomy.definition: A surgical procedure involving an incision into the ureter (ureterotomy) to relieve obstruction or to remove a stone; the Davis ureterotomy refers to a Davis-named variation of this incision.

ureteropelvic junction.definition: The junction between the renal pelvis and the ureter, where urine exits the kidney into the ureter; obstruction at this site can impede urine flow and cause hydronephrosis.

dawn phenomenon.definition: An early-morning rise in fasting blood glucose in people with diabetes, caused by the release of counter-regulatory hormones (eg, growth hormone, cortisol, glucagon, catecholamines) during the predawn hours, increasing hepatic glucose production.

somogyi effect.definition: A pattern of rebound hyperglycemia in the morning following nocturnal hypoglycemia, caused by counterregulatory hormone release (glucagon, epinephrine, cortisol, growth hormone) in response to low overnight glucose.

ephemeralopia.definition: A temporary, short-lived disturbance of vision that resolves without lasting sequelae.

nyctalopia.definition: Difficulty seeing in low light or darkness; a symptom of impaired night vision, often due to retinal dysfunction (especially rod cells) or vitamin A deficiency.

d&c.definition: A surgical procedure in which the cervix is dilated and the lining of the uterus (endometrium) is scraped or suctioned (curettage) to obtain tissue for diagnosis or to remove tissue, commonly used for abnormal uterine bleeding, incomplete abortion, or miscarriage management.

dacrocystorhinotomy.definition: A surgical procedure involving an incision into the lacrimal sac via the nasal cavity, typically to relieve obstruction of the nasolacrimal drainage system and promote tear drainage.

denver developmental screening test.definition: A developmental screening tool used for children from birth through about 6 years to identify potential developmental delays, assessing four domains—personal-social, fine motor/adaptive, language, and gross motor—through age-appropriate tasks and using pass/fail criteria to flag the need for further evaluation.

developmental disability.definition: Problems that last a long time and have an effect on daily life, like Down Syndrome or learning differences.

desmopressin acetate.definition: A synthetic analogue of vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone) that increases water reabsorption in the renal collecting ducts and raises plasma levels of factor VIII and von Willebrand factor; used to treat central diabetes insipidus, nocturnal enuresis, and certain bleeding disorders (von Willebrand disease and mild hemophilia A).

zalcitabine.definition: A nucleoside analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) formerly used to treat HIV infection; it is 2',3'-dideoxycytidine and inhibits HIV replication by terminating DNA chain elongation after incorporation by reverse transcriptase; use is now largely limited by toxicity (e.g., pancreatitis, peripheral neuropathy, anemia) and resistance.

2′3′-dideoxycytidine.definition: A nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) antiretroviral agent; a cytidine analogue in which the 2′ and 3′ hydroxyl groups of the ribose are missing, causing chain termination of viral DNA synthesis when incorporated by HIV reverse transcriptase. Also known as zalcitabine.

dead-end host.definition: A host that can be infected by a pathogen but does not contribute to onward transmission because the pathogen does not reach sufficient levels to infect a vector or spread to other hosts.

dead space.definition: The portion of each breath that does not participate in gas exchange; anatomically it is the conducting airways (anatomical dead space), and physiologically it includes the sum of anatomical dead space and any alveolar dead space (ventilated but underperfused alveoli).

anatomical dead space.definition: A portion of the tidal volume that remains in the conducting airways (nose to terminal bronchioles) and does not participate in gas exchange; roughly 150 mL in a healthy adult (about 1 mL per kilogram of body weight).

physiological dead space.definition: The portion of a tidal breath that does not participate in gas exchange because alveoli are ventilated but not perfused; it comprises both the anatomic dead space (airways) and any alveolar dead space (ventilated but nonperfused alveoli).

pulmonary circulation.definition: Portion of the circulatory system that carries blood between the heart and lungs for gas exchange: deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle through the pulmonary arteries to the lungs, where it is oxygenated, and then returns to the left atrium via the pulmonary veins.

thromboembolus.definition: A blood clot that has formed and then detached, traveling through the circulation to lodge in a distant vessel and obstruct blood flow.

plasmin.definition: An enzyme that breaks down the protein involved in clotting blood (fibrin), dissolving the clot.

thrombolytic therapy.definition: A medical therapy using thrombolytic (fibrinolytic) agents that dissolve clots by converting plasminogen to plasmin, which degrades fibrin; used to restore blood flow in acute thrombotic events such as STEMI, ischemic stroke, and massive pulmonary embolism, when benefits exceed the risk of bleeding.

d-dimer.definition: A degradation product of cross-linked fibrin produced during plasmin-mediated breakdown of a blood clot; measured in blood as a marker of thrombotic activity. A negative result helps rule out acute thrombosis in appropriate clinical settings, while a positive result is non-specific and can be elevated in many conditions (e.g., infection, inflammation, pregnancy, liver disease, cancer, recent surgery or trauma).

d-dimer test.definition: A blood test that measures D-dimer, a fibrin degradation product released when a blood clot is broken down; it is used to help rule out thromboembolic conditions such as deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism and disseminated intravascular coagulation, with high sensitivity but limited specificity.

dcc gene.definition: A tumor suppressor gene encoding a transmembrane receptor for netrin-1, involved in axon guidance and neuronal migration; loss of function is associated with colorectal cancer and the gene maps to chromosome 18q21.2.

colorectal carcinoma.definition: A malignant neoplasm of the colon or rectum, typically an adenocarcinoma arising from the glandular lining; often develops from adenomatous polyps and may invade locally and metastasize.

dcr.definition: A surgical procedure that creates a direct drainage path between the lacrimal sac and the nasal cavity to bypass an obstructed nasolacrimal duct, relieving chronic tearing (epiphora).

definitive host.definition: In parasitology, the host in which a parasite reaches sexual maturity and reproduces; the adult, sexually reproducing stage of the parasite occurs in the definitive host.

intermediate host.definition: An organism that harbors the larval or asexual stages of a parasite, enabling its development and transmission to the definitive host; the parasite does not reach sexual maturity in this host.

reservoir host.definition: An organism (often an animal or arthropod) that harbors a pathogen in nature, maintaining the infection and serving as a source from which others can become infected; the reservoir host is frequently asymptomatic or only mildly affected.

trichinosis.definition: An infection caused by ingestion of Trichinella larvae (usually from undercooked pork or wild game) that encysts in skeletal muscle, causing fever, muscle pain (myalgia), periorbital edema, and eosinophilia, often with GI symptoms; diagnosed by serology or muscle biopsy; treated with albendazole or mebendazole, sometimes with corticosteroids.

pediculicide.definition: A substance or preparation used to kill lice (Pediculus species) and their eggs (nits), typically applied topically to treat pediculosis.

scabicide.definition: A medication or agent that kills the mites (and often their eggs) that cause scabies, typically used topically (e.g., permethrin, benzyl benzoate) or orally (ivermectin).

delousing.definition: The act of removing lice and their eggs (nits) from a person, animal, or object to eradicate a pediculosis infestation, typically by combing, washing, heat, or pediculicidal treatment.

scabies.definition: An itchy skin condition caused by a tiny bug (called a mite).

algor mortis.definition: Postmortem decrease in body temperature as the body cools after death due to cessation of metabolic heat production and heat loss to the surrounding environment; the rate is influenced by ambient temperature, clothing, body size, and environmental conditions.

death chill.definition: A colloquial term for the cooling of the body after death (algor mortis), caused by cessation of metabolism and ongoing heat loss; may be described as a chill felt by the dying person or observers.

death mask.definition: A plaster or wax impression of a person’s face made after death, used to preserve facial features for identification, memorialization, or forensic/anthropological analysis.

death rate.definition: Number of deaths in a defined population during a specified time period divided by the population at risk, typically expressed per 1,000 or 100,000 persons per year.

death rattle.definition: A gurgling, rattling respiratory sound caused by pooled oral/pharyngeal secretions in the upper airway of a dying patient who is no longer able to swallow or clear secretions.

death trance.definition: A nonstandard historical term for a trance-like, death-like immobility with markedly reduced consciousness that is said to occur near death; not an officially recognized medical diagnosis and is typically conflated with syncope, coma, or catalepsy.

death with dignity.definition: A legal option in some jurisdictions whereby a terminally ill, mentally competent adult may voluntarily obtain and self-administer prescribed medications to hasten death, typically under physician supervision, in order to relieve unbearable suffering.

debakey forceps.definition: A type of atraumatic surgical forceps with long, slender, rounded jaws and fine longitudinal serrations designed to grip delicate tissue and blood vessels without crushing, commonly used in vascular, cardiovascular, and microvascular procedures.

strictures.definition: An abnormal narrowing or constriction of a hollow organ or duct (such as the esophagus, urethra, bile duct, or intestine), usually due to scar tissue or inflammatory fibrosis, which can cause partial or complete obstruction and site-specific symptoms.

ureteral incision.definition: A surgical incision into the ureter to access its lumen for stone removal, relief of obstruction, or repair of injury or a stricture.

arterial blood.definition: Blood carried by arteries away from the heart; typically oxygenated and bright red in systemic circulation, though the pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

venous blood.definition: Blood in the venous system returning from tissues to the heart, typically deoxygenated with higher carbon dioxide content and a darker appearance than arterial blood.

oxygen–carbon dioxide exchange.definition: The diffusion-driven transfer of oxygen from inhaled air in the lungs into the pulmonary blood, and of carbon dioxide from the blood into the alveolar air to be exhaled; it occurs across the alveolar–capillary membrane and is driven by partial pressure differences, enabling cellular respiration and maintenance of acid–base balance.

deaf.definition: When you can't hear any sounds at all.

deafferentation.definition: Loss or disruption of afferent (sensory) input to a body region, resulting in diminished or absent sensation and altered sensory processing; may occur from injury to sensory nerves, dorsal roots, or the spinal cord.

deaf-mute.definition: An outdated, stigmatizing label for a person who is deaf and nonverbal; today, the term is avoided, and people are described as deaf or hard of hearing, with communication via sign language or speech.

deaf-mutism.definition: An historical term for a person who is deaf and cannot speak; refers to coexisting deafness and muteness, often considered a consequence of deafness rather than a primary speech disorder.

hearing aids.definition: A small electronic device worn in or behind the ear that amplifies sound for people with hearing loss, typically consisting of a microphone, amplifier, and speaker (receiver) powered by a battery, to improve hearing by increasing the volume and clarity of sounds.

amplification of sound.definition: A process that increases the amplitude (and thus the loudness) of a sound wave, typically achieved with an amplifier or hearing aid.

speech reading.definition: Understanding spoken language by integrating visual information from the speaker’s lips and facial movements with any available auditory information; commonly used by individuals with hearing loss to supplement or replace auditory input.

sign language.definition: A natural language expressed through manual signs, facial expressions, and body movements, used primarily by Deaf and hard-of-hearing communities to convey complex ideas; it has its own grammar, lexicon, and syntax distinct from the surrounding spoken language.

external auditory canal.definition: An approximately 2.5 cm long passage of the external ear that conducts sound to the tympanic membrane; its outer portion is bony and the inner portion is cartilaginous, lined with skin containing hairs and ceruminous glands that secrete cerumen.

debility.definition: A generalized state of weakness and fatigue with reduced strength and endurance, often due to chronic illness, malnutrition, aging, or other debilitating conditions; not a specific disease but a description of frailty.

decidua basalis.definition: The portion of the endometrium beneath the implanted embryo that has undergone decidualization during pregnancy; it forms the maternal portion of the placenta (the placental bed) and is shed with the decidua at delivery.

decidua capsularis.definition: The portion of the decidua that covers the implanted embryo in the uterus; it lines the uterine cavity over the conceptus and is eventually obliterated as it fuses with the decidua parietalis during pregnancy.

decidua vera.definition: A portion of the decidua that lines the non-placental part of the uterus during pregnancy; the maternal endometrium transformed into decidua that covers the rest of the uterine cavity away from the implantation site.

decidua reflexa.definition: A region of the maternal decidua in pregnancy where the endometrium folds back (reflexes) around the site of implantation, forming a reflexed rim surrounding the developing conceptus.

decidua serotina.definition: The portion of the endometrium (decidua) that overlies the placental implantation site late in pregnancy and is shed along with the placenta at delivery.

decidual endometritis.definition: Inflammation of the decidualized endometrium (the endometrium transformed during pregnancy), typically due to intrauterine infection, characterized histologically by neutrophilic infiltration of the decidual stroma.

decidua menstrualis.definition: The portion of the endometrium that is shed during menstruation; the nonpregnant, functional layer of the uterine lining that thickens under hormonal influence and is expelled if implantation does not occur.

decidua parietalis.definition: A portion of the decidua that lines the rest of the uterine cavity during pregnancy, i.e., the endometrium not directly involved in the placental implantation site.

deciduoma.definition: A localized, benign mass of decidualized endometrial tissue (decidua) formed under progesterone influence during pregnancy or hormonal stimulation; resembles placental decidua but is a discrete lesion and is not a true neoplasm.

deciduous dentition.definition: The primary (baby) dentition: the first set of teeth in children, consisting of 20 teeth (incisors, canines, and molars) that erupt in infancy and early childhood and are eventually shed and replaced by the permanent dentition.

decadron.definition: A potent synthetic glucocorticoid corticosteroid with anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressant effects, used to treat inflammation, autoimmune diseases, allergic reactions, certain cancers, cerebral edema, and to prevent chemotherapy-induced nausea; administered orally or by injection.

nandrolone decanoate.definition: An injectable, long-acting anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from testosterone (a 19-nor compound) with a decanoate ester; used medically to treat wasting syndromes and certain anemias by promoting protein synthesis and weight gain, with androgenic and anabolic effects and potential for virilization, acne, edema, lipid abnormalities, and suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis.

hydrotherapy.definition: Therapeutic use of water in any form—such as baths, immersion, compresses, or steam—to treat disease or injury and relieve symptoms, with applications including pain relief, improved circulation, and wound healing.

oxygen debt.definition: An amount of oxygen that the body must take in after strenuous activity beyond resting needs to restore metabolic balance—replenishing ATP and phosphocreatine stores, oxidizing lactate produced during anaerobic metabolism, and returning body systems to baseline; the period of this elevated oxygen uptake is also called excess post-exercise oxygen consumption (EPOC).

debrox.definition: An over-the-counter otic preparation containing carbamide peroxide, used to soften and loosen earwax (cerumen) to aid its removal.

endometritis.definition: Inflammation of the endometrium (the uterine lining), usually from infection, most often occurring after delivery or abortion; can be acute or chronic and typically presents with fever, uterine tenderness, abdominal pain, and often foul-smelling vaginal discharge.

capric acid.definition: A saturated medium-chain fatty acid with ten carbon atoms (C10:0), also known as decanoic acid.

decanoic acid.definition: A saturated fatty acid with ten carbon atoms (C10:0); a medium-chain fatty acid also known as capric acid, present in small amounts in dairy fats and some plant oils such as coconut and palm kernel oil.

decalcification.definition: Removal of calcium salts from tissue or bone, causing demineralization and softening; in histology, a laboratory procedure using acids or chelating agents to decalcify specimens for thin-section preparation.

oxalic acid.definition: A simple dicarboxylic acid (HOOC-COOH) with the chemical formula C2H2O4; occurs naturally in many plants and foods and can form calcium oxalate crystals; toxic in large amounts, potentially causing metabolic acidosis and renal injury.

osteoblastic.definition: Relating to osteoblasts, the bone-forming cells; involved in bone formation and mineralization.

osteoclastic.definition: Relating to bone-resorbing cells involved in breaking down bone tissue during remodeling and calcium homeostasis.

mesencephalic region.definition: A portion of the brainstem (the midbrain) located between the diencephalon above and the pons below; it contains the tectum and tegmentum, including the superior and inferior colliculi, substantia nigra, and red nucleus, and is involved in visual and auditory processing, motor control, and reflexes related to arousal and coordination.

decussation.definition: Crossing of nerve fibers or tracts from one side of the nervous system to the opposite side; a classic example is the pyramidal decussation in the medulla, where most corticospinal fibers cross to control contralateral body movements.

pyramids.definition: Cone-shaped regions of the kidney medulla containing parallel bundles of collecting ducts, draining urine into the minor calyces via the renal papillae.

decorticate posture.definition: A flexor posturing pattern seen with severe brain injury in which the upper limbs are flexed at the elbows with adduction and internal rotation (often with flexed wrists and fists) and the lower limbs are extended or internally rotated; indicates corticospinal tract damage above the red nucleus (supratentorial).

decorticate rigidity.definition: A posturing pattern seen with severe brain injury in which the upper limbs are flexed (elbows, with adduction and internal rotation of the shoulders and flexed wrists) and the lower limbs are extended; indicates damage to the corticospinal tract above the red nucleus (cerebral hemispheric injury).

decerebrate posture.definition: An abnormal posturing in which the arms and legs are rigidly extended (the arms extended and pronated, the wrists extended), reflecting brainstem injury (usually at or above the midbrain) and indicating severe brain damage with a poor prognosis.

decerebrate rigidity.definition: An abnormal extensor posturing pattern in which the arms are extended and pronated, with extended wrists and fingers, and the legs are extended; it results from brainstem injury (typically at or below the level of the red nucleus) causing loss of inhibitory control of extensor pathways and indicates severe brain injury with poor prognosis.

decerebration.definition: Separation of the cerebrum from the brainstem, either surgically or due to severe injury; clinically it denotes a brainstem-dominated state with rigid extension of the limbs (decerebrate posture), indicating severe brain injury.

decortication.definition: Removal of the outer layer or fibrous rind from an organ; most commonly, surgical stripping of the pleural peel from the lung to allow expansion (pulmonary decortication), and it can also refer to the removal of the cerebral cortex in neurosurgical contexts.
