aflatoxin.definition: Group of mycotoxins produced by Aspergillus species (notably A. flavus and A. parasiticus) that commonly contaminate stored grains, peanuts, and other nuts; they are potent hepatotoxins and hepatocarcinogens, especially the B1 variant, acting after metabolic activation to reactive intermediates that form DNA adducts and trigger mutations.

molybdenum.definition: A trace element that serves as a cofactor for several molybdoenzymes, including sulfite oxidase, xanthine oxidase, and aldehyde oxidase; essential for the metabolism of sulfur-containing amino acids and purines; deficiency is rare and can cause sulfite accumulation and related metabolic problems; excessive intake can be toxic.

betel-nut chewing.definition: Chewing of areca (betel) nut, typically wrapped in betel leaf with slaked lime and sometimes tobacco; a mild stimulant associated with dental staining and an increased risk of oral mucosal lesions, leukoplakia, submucous fibrosis, and oral cancer.

cervical adenopathy.definition: Enlargement of the lymph nodes in the neck (cervical lymph nodes), usually due to infection or inflammation, but can also reflect malignancy or systemic disease; persistent, hard, or rapidly enlarging nodes or those with systemic symptoms warrant medical evaluation.

persistent cough.definition: A cough that lasts longer than the typical recovery period from an acute respiratory illness—generally more than 8 weeks in adults (more than 4 weeks in children).

left vocal cord paralysis.definition: Paralysis of the left vocal cord due to dysfunction of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve, causing a fixed left vocal cord with impaired glottic closure and resulting in hoarseness or breathy voice, with potential dysphagia or aspiration; causes include surgical nerve injury, tumor compression, viral neuropathy, or idiopathic causes.

great vessels.definition: The large vessels connected to the heart that carry blood to and from the systemic and pulmonary circulations; typically includes the aorta, the pulmonary trunk, and the superior and inferior venae cavae.

fiberoptic esophagoscopy.definition: A diagnostic (and sometimes therapeutic) procedure in which a flexible fiberoptic endoscope is inserted through the mouth into the esophagus to visualize the esophageal mucosa and, if needed, obtain biopsies or perform minor interventions.

cytological examination.definition: Microscopic evaluation of cells collected from a body specimen (such as exfoliated cells, aspirates, or body fluids) to detect abnormalities, infections, or malignancy.

primary lesion.definition: The initial, primary lesion is the first morphologic change on the skin or mucous membranes produced by a disease process, from which secondary lesions (such as crusts, scales, excoriations, or scars) may develop.

regional nodes.definition: A group of lymph nodes that drain a specific anatomical region; the first echelon of lymphatic drainage from that region, often the initial site of regional metastasis in cancer.

esophagogastrostomy.definition: A surgical procedure that creates an anastomosis between the esophagus and the stomach, establishing a direct passage for food after esophageal resection or to bypass an obstructed esophagus.

esophagojejunostomy.definition: A surgical connection (anastomosis) between the esophagus and a segment of jejunum to restore continuity of the digestive tract after gastrectomy or esophageal resection; usually performed as an end-to-end or end-to-side anastomosis, often in a Roux-en-Y configuration.

esophagomyotomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which the muscular layer of the esophagus is cut (myotomy) to relieve obstruction at the lower esophageal sphincter, most commonly to treat achalasia; typically performed laparoscopically or thoracoscopically and often combined with a fundoplication to prevent reflux.

esophagoscopy.definition: A procedure in which a flexible or rigid endoscope is inserted into the esophagus to visualize the esophageal mucosa, obtain biopsies, remove foreign bodies, or perform therapeutic interventions such as dilation or stent placement.

esophagogastroscopy.definition: A procedure using a flexible endoscope inserted through the mouth to visualize the esophagus and stomach, enabling biopsies, diagnostic assessment, and potential therapeutic interventions.

esophagospasm.definition: Sudden, involuntary, often nonperistaltic contraction of the esophageal smooth muscle that disrupts normal swallowing, frequently causing retrosternal chest pain and dysphagia; a type of esophageal motor disorder.

esophoric.definition: Relating to the esophagus, the muscular tube that carries swallowed food from the pharynx to the stomach.

essential hypertension.definition: Occurs when the diastolic pressure is 90 or higher or the systolic pressure is 140 or higher. The most common kind of high blood pressure, it often develops as you age. Also called primary hypertension.

essential mixed cryoglobulinemia.definition: An idiopathic form of mixed cryoglobulinemia in which no underlying trigger (such as hepatitis C infection, autoimmune disease, or malignancy) is identified. It involves circulating cryoglobulins—immune complexes typically containing IgM with rheumatoid factor activity and polyclonal IgG—that precipitate at low temperatures and cause small-vessel vasculitis, presenting with palpable purpura, arthralgias, fatigue, and sometimes renal involvement.

essential nutrients.definition: Nutrients that cannot be synthesized by the human body in sufficient amounts and must be obtained from the diet to maintain health; examples include essential amino acids, essential fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, and water.

essential fatty acid.definition: An essential fatty acid is a dietary fatty acid that the human body cannot synthesize in sufficient amounts and therefore must be obtained from the diet; it is required for normal growth, cell membrane structure, and the production of signaling molecules (e.g., linoleic acid and alpha-linolenic acid).

ulcers.definition: A sore or break in the skin or mucous membrane characterized by tissue loss; lesions may be shallow or deep and are caused by inflammation, infection, ischemia, pressure, or underlying disease, and may heal with scarring.

obstructions.definition: Blockages that impede the normal flow of a substance through a hollow organ or conduit (e.g., bowel, airway, or duct), causing impaired function. Causes include mechanical obstructions (tumor, stone, adhesions, foreign body) and functional obstructions due to reduced motility (ileus).

enteral tube feeding.definition: Delivery of nutritionally complete or supplemental formula directly into the gastrointestinal tract via a feeding tube (e.g., nasogastric, nasojejunal, gastrostomy, or jejunostomy) for patients who cannot meet needs by mouth or cannot safely swallow.

esophageal dilator.definition: An instrument used to mechanically widen a narrowed esophagus (esophageal stricture), usually in the form of bougie or balloon dilators used during endoscopic dilation to relieve dysphagia.

esophageal lead.definition: An esophageal lead is an electrode placed in the esophagus to record cardiac electrical activity (often atrial signals) or to deliver pacing, primarily used during electrophysiology studies when surface or transvenous leads provide suboptimal signals.

esophageal peristalsis.definition: Coordinated, wave-like contractions of the esophageal muscle that propel a swallowed bolus from the pharynx to the stomach; primary peristalsis is initiated by swallowing, with secondary peristalsis triggered by esophageal distension, both mediated by the enteric and vagal nervous systems and coordinated with relaxation of the upper and lower esophageal sphincters.

esophageal spasm.definition: Disorder of esophageal motility characterized by abnormal, sometimes simultaneous or high-amplitude esophageal contractions, leading to intermittent chest pain that may resemble angina and to dysphagia.

esophageal web.definition: A thin mucosal membrane that projects into the esophageal lumen, forming a shelf-like constriction (usually in the upper esophagus) and potentially causing dysphagia; can be congenital or acquired and is sometimes associated with iron-deficiency anemia or Plummer-Vinson syndrome; diagnosed by barium swallow or endoscopy and often treated with dilation.

chronic hepatitis.definition: A long-standing inflammation of the liver, typically persisting for at least six months, caused by viral, autoimmune, alcoholic, drug-induced, or metabolic etiologies, which can progress to fibrosis and cirrhosis and may increase the risk of liver failure and hepatocellular carcinoma; management targets the underlying cause and monitoring for liver damage.

leishmania brasiliensis.definition: A protozoan parasite of the genus Leishmania, a cause of New World tegumentary leishmaniasis, typically presenting as cutaneous ulcers with potential progression to mucosal disease; transmitted by phlebotomine sandflies and characterized by intracellular amastigotes in macrophages.

breda's disease.definition: Not found in standard medical references. Please provide context or alternate spelling. If you meant thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger disease), I can provide its definition.

extrasensory perception.definition: An asserted ability to perceive information or events without using the ordinary senses or external stimuli, exemplified by telepathy, clairvoyance, and precognition; not supported by credible scientific evidence and generally regarded as pseudoscience by the medical community.

electric shock therapy.definition: A medical procedure in which brief, controlled electrical currents are delivered to the brain under anesthesia to induce a temporary seizure; used primarily for treatment-resistant depression and certain other severe psychiatric conditions, often requiring multiple sessions.

estar.definition: Not a medical term; in Spanish, this verb means "to be" and is used to describe temporary states or locations; it does not denote a medical condition or diagnosis.

oestrone.definition: A natural estrogen steroid hormone produced mainly by the ovaries and adipose tissue; one of the major estrogens and weaker than estradiol, it acts on estrogen receptors to regulate female reproductive tissues, bone density, and metabolism, and becomes the predominant circulating estrogen after menopause.

estazolam.definition: An intermediate-acting benzodiazepine hypnotic used for short-term treatment of insomnia; it enhances GABA-A receptor activity to produce sedation and sleep induction, with risks including daytime drowsiness, dependence, and withdrawal.

estradiol.definition: A potent estrogen steroid hormone produced mainly by the ovarian follicles; the principal circulating estrogen in premenopausal women. It regulates the menstrual cycle and supports uterine, vaginal, and breast development, as well as bone health, by binding estrogen receptors in target tissues.

estriol.definition: A weak estrogen produced mainly by the placenta during pregnancy; one of the three major estrogens; has relatively low estrogenic potency compared with estradiol and estrone; levels rise during pregnancy and are used clinically as a marker of placental-fetal function.

estramustine.definition: A cytotoxic chemotherapy agent that combines an estrogen moiety with a nitrogen mustard alkylating group; used mainly for metastatic prostate cancer and administered as estramustine phosphate.

estrin.definition: A nonstandard or historical term for an estrogen or estrogenic compound; not commonly used in modern medicine (estrone is a specific estrogen).

estinyl.definition: A brand name for ethinyl estradiol, a synthetic estrogen used in oral contraceptives and estrogen replacement therapy.

estrace.definition: A brand-name formulation of estradiol, an estrogen hormone used in hormone replacement therapy to treat menopausal vasomotor symptoms and vaginal atrophy, and to address estrogen deficiency in women.

estratab.definition: An estrogen-containing medication sold under a brand name; typically an oral tablet used for hormone replacement therapy in menopause or, in some formulations, as part of a combined hormonal contraceptive—the exact composition and indication vary by product.

estropipate.definition: A synthetic estrogen medication; an esterified form of estrone used orally in hormone replacement therapy to treat menopausal symptoms.

ethionamide.definition: A second-line antitubercular thioamide prodrug activated by Mycobacterium tuberculosis KatG, which inhibits mycolic acid synthesis and slows growth of M. tuberculosis; used for drug-resistant TB or when first-line therapy is unsuitable.

ethambutol.definition: An antimycobacterial agent (bacteriostatic) used to treat tuberculosis; it inhibits mycobacterial cell-wall synthesis by blocking arabinosyl transferases involved in arabinan formation. Adverse effects include optic neuritis with decreased visual acuity and color vision changes, particularly red–green, requiring monitoring and possible dose adjustment in renal impairment.

ethacrynic.definition: Relating to ethacrynic acid, a non-sulfonamide loop diuretic that inhibits the Na⁺-K⁺-2Cl⁻ cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, used to treat edema (especially in sulfonamide-allergic patients).

ethaverine.definition: A spasmolytic (antispasmodic) drug used to relieve smooth muscle spasms of the gastrointestinal and biliary tracts.

etanercept.definition: A biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (bDMARD) consisting of two soluble TNF receptor–p75 moieties fused to an IgG1 Fc fragment; it binds tumor necrosis factor (TNF-α and lymphotoxin-α) to neutralize its inflammatory effects, thereby reducing immune-mediated inflammation in conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, plaque psoriasis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis. Administered by subcutaneous injection.

nesacaine.definition: A brand-name local anesthetic solution used to produce regional or local anesthesia for minor procedures; administered by injection into tissue and may include a vasoconstrictor (such as epinephrine) to prolong effect. Exact active ingredient and concentration vary by formulation and country.

procaine.definition: A short-acting ester local anesthetic used for infiltration anesthesia and minor procedures; it blocks voltage-gated sodium channels in peripheral nerves, inhibiting neural conduction. It is hydrolyzed to p-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and diethylaminoethanol and can cause hypersensitivity reactions; often administered with a vasoconstrictor to extend duration.

tetracaine.definition: A long-acting ester-type local anesthetic that blocks voltage-gated sodium channels to prevent nerve impulse propagation; used for topical ophthalmic anesthesia and for regional or spinal anesthesia.

eswl.definition: A noninvasive treatment in which externally generated shock waves are focused onto a kidney or ureteral stone to fragment it into smaller pieces that are expelled in the urine, usually with imaging guidance and anesthesia.

placental.definition: Relating to the placenta, the vascular organ formed during pregnancy that provides nutrients and oxygen to the developing fetus and removes waste products via the maternal blood supply.

kraurosis.definition: A chronic atrophic sclerosis of the vulvar and vaginal mucosa, typically in postmenopausal women, causing thinning, dryness, loss of elasticity, and introital stenosis.

antituberculous.definition: Relating to drugs used to treat tuberculosis; active against Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

ethmocarditis.definition:
Not a standard medical term; it may be a misspelling. Likely intended terms:

- Ethmoiditis: inflammation or infection of the ethmoid sinuses.
- Endocarditis: infection of the endocardial surface of the heart, usually the valves.

ethmoidal.definition: Relating to the ethmoid bone of the skull, or to the ethmoid air cells (ethmoidal sinuses) within it.

ethmoidectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove all or part of the ethmoid sinus air cells (ethmoid bone) through the nasal cavity, commonly performed as part of endoscopic sinus surgery to treat chronic rhinosinusitis, polyps, mucoceles, or tumors.

infundibulum.definition: Funnel-shaped structure in anatomy. One sense is the funnel-shaped end of the fallopian (uterine) tube near the ovary, with fimbriae that capture the ovulated oocyte. Another sense is the pituitary stalk, the funnel-shaped connection linking the hypothalamus to the posterior pituitary.

lacrimal.definition: Relating to tears; pertaining to the lacrimal glands and tear ducts that produce and drain tears.

paget.definition: A group of conditions named after a 19th‑century physician; the most common is a chronic bone remodeling disorder with excessive osteoclast activity followed by increased bone formation, leading to enlarged, deformed bones and higher fracture risk. Less commonly, the term also refers to a form of cancer involving the nipple associated with underlying carcinoma, or to a rare vulvar intraepithelial adenocarcinoma presenting as an itchy, eczematous lesion.

heterotopic.definition: Relating to tissue or an organ located in an abnormal place; normal-appearing tissue present outside its usual anatomical site (heterotopia).

corneal.definition: Relating to the cornea—the transparent front part of the eye that covers the iris and pupil.

erythrodermic.definition: Relating to erythroderma; presenting as widespread, diffuse redness of the skin, often with scaling and possible edema or itching.

etodolac.definition: A nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with preferential COX-2 inhibition, used to relieve pain and inflammation in conditions such as osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.

etomidate.definition: An ultra-short-acting intravenous hypnotic used to induce anesthesia; rapid onset with brief duration, producing hypnosis with minimal analgesia and relatively stable hemodynamics, but associated with adrenal suppression, myoclonus, pain on injection, nausea/vomiting, and potential respiratory depression.

etoposide.definition: A semisynthetic topoisomerase II inhibitor used in chemotherapy. It binds to DNA and topoisomerase II, stabilizing the enzyme-DNA complex and causing double-strand breaks that lead to cancer cell death; used for various malignancies such as testicular cancer, small cell lung cancer, lymphomas, and leukemias, and administered orally or intravenously.

perphenazine.definition: A phenothiazine-derived, typical antipsychotic that antagonizes dopamine D2 receptors to treat schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders; commonly associated with extrapyramidal symptoms and sedation.

progestin.definition: A synthetic compound that produces effects similar to those of the hormone progesterone.

etretinate.definition: A synthetic retinoid (vitamin A derivative) formerly used orally for severe psoriasis; highly teratogenic with an extremely long half-life and is metabolized to acitretin.

ethotoin.definition: An older hydantoin-class anticonvulsant used to treat seizures; it stabilizes neuronal membranes and reduces seizure activity by blocking voltage-gated sodium channels, and is largely replaced by newer anticonvulsants.

ethynodiol.definition: A synthetic progestin (progestogen) used in hormonal contraception; a 19-nor steroid derivative that provides progestational effects.

ethinyl.definition: An acetylene substituent (-C≡CH) attached to a molecule; an acetylenic functional group used in organic and medicinal chemistry to denote a carbon–carbon triple bond in the substituent.

euglobulin.definition: A fraction of plasma obtained by partial precipitation (e.g., with ammonium sulfate) that is enriched in fibrinogen and plasminogen, with reduced levels of fibrinolysis inhibitors, used in laboratory fibrinolysis tests such as the euglobulin clot lysis time.

fibrinolysis.definition: The enzymatic dissolution of fibrin in blood clots, mediated by plasmin generated from plasminogen by activators such as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) and urokinase; it helps regulate hemostasis by removing clots.

eugnathia.definition: Normal jaw relation and dental occlusion; a eugnathic (well-aligned) jaw and dental arches with no malocclusion.

eugnathic anomaly.definition: An abnormality of tooth alignment or occlusion that occurs despite normal jaw relationships (eugnathic); i.e., a malocclusion associated with an eugnathic skeletal base rather than with skeletal disproportions.

eukaryocyte.definition: A cell that contains a membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles (e.g., mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum), characteristic of eukaryotic organisms.

eukaryon.definition: A cell or organism whose cells have a true nucleus enclosed by a nuclear envelope and containing membrane-bound organelles, in contrast to prokaryotes.

eukaryosis.definition: Not a widely recognized medical term. Etymologically, it would imply a condition involving nuclei in eukaryotic (nucleus-containing) cells, but there is no accepted clinical definition for it in major medical dictionaries. If you have context or a spelling variant (e.g., karyosis, karyomegaly), I can help with that.

eukaryote.definition: An organism whose cells have a true nucleus enclosed by a membrane and contain membrane-bound organelles; includes animals, plants, fungi, and protists.

eukaryotic.definition: Relating to cells that have a true nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane and membrane-bound organelles; characteristic of eukaryotes (plants, animals, fungi, protists) as opposed to prokaryotes.

eulexin.definition: A nonsteroidal antiandrogen that competitively blocks the androgen receptor and is used in the treatment of metastatic prostate cancer, typically with a GnRH agonist to suppress testosterone.

eunuch.definition: A man who has been castrated, especially before puberty, leading to very low testosterone levels, diminished or absent secondary sexual characteristics, and infertility.

eunuchism.definition: The state or condition of being a eunuch; typically resulting from castration leading to low testosterone, infertility, and diminished secondary sexual characteristics.

eunuchoidism.definition: A state of male hypogonadism characterized by tall, slender stature with eunuchoid habitus (proportionally long limbs and arm span greater than height) due to delayed epiphyseal closure from low testosterone, typically with underdeveloped secondary sexual characteristics and reduced androgen effects.

euphoretic.definition: Producing or capable of producing euphoria; relating to an abnormally elevated mood or feeling of well-being, often drug-induced.

euploid.definition: Having a chromosome number that is an exact multiple of the haploid set, i.e., a complete, balanced complement of chromosomes; not aneuploid (in humans, typically diploid with 46 chromosomes).

euploidy.definition: A state in which the chromosome number is an exact multiple of the haploid set (e.g., 2n in somatic human cells), as opposed to an abnormal number (aneuploidy).

eupnea.definition: Normal, unlabored breathing at rest with regular rate, depth, and rhythm (typically about 12–20 breaths per minute in adults).

eurax.definition: A brand-name topical antipruritic containing crotamiton (often 10%), used to relieve itching and to treat scabies; applied to the skin as directed (often with two applications within 24 hours).

european blastomycosis.definition: A systemic fungal infection caused by Blastomyces species (primarily Blastomyces dermatitidis), usually presenting as pulmonary disease with potential dissemination to skin, bone, and other organs; in Europe it is rare and often travel- or imported-related; diagnosed by culture or histopathology and treated with itraconazole for mild–moderate disease or amphotericin B for severe cases.

torus tubarius.definition: A cushion-like elevation on the mucosa of the nasopharynx surrounding the opening of the pharyngotympanic (Eustachian) tube, formed by the underlying cartilaginous portion of the auditory tube.

eustachian cushion.definition: A circular mucosal elevation around the nasopharyngeal opening of the auditory (Eustachian) tube.

eustachian salpingitis.definition: Inflammation of the Eustachian (pharyngotympanic) tube, causing obstruction of middle-ear ventilation and drainage with symptoms such as ear fullness, pressure, muffled hearing, pain, and potential middle-ear effusion or infection.

eustress.definition: A positive form of stress arising when a person perceives a situation as within their coping resources, perceived as exciting or motivating, leading to improved performance, focus, and resilience. It uses the same physiological arousal pathways as distress but yields beneficial outcomes rather than harm.

euthenics.definition: The science of improving human health and well-being by altering environmental and living conditions—such as nutrition, housing, sanitation, education, and other social determinants.

euthymia.definition: A normal, stable mood state in which there are no clinically significant depressive or manic symptoms.

euthymic.definition: A normal, stable mood without significant depressive or manic symptoms; the baseline affective state in which mood is neither depressed nor elevated.

euthymism.definition: A state of normal, stable mood with no depressive or manic symptoms; a baseline or balanced emotional state.

euthyroid.definition: Normal thyroid function; thyroid hormone levels (free T4 and T3) are within the reference range and TSH is normal, with no clinical signs of hypo- or hyperthyroidism.

evacuant.definition: An agent that promotes bowel evacuation; a laxative or purgative used to empty the intestine.

evacuate.definition: To empty or remove the contents of a body cavity or hollow organ, or to drain a pathological collection.

evacuator.definition: A device that uses suction to evacuate fluids, blood, irrigation media, and debris from a surgical field or wound; commonly called a suction evacuator used in operating rooms and dental settings.

evagination.definition: The outward projection or outgrowth of a tissue or organ from a surface or cavity, forming a pouch or diverticulum; the opposite of invagination.

evans blue.definition: A blue dye that binds tightly to serum albumin and is used to measure plasma volume and assess vascular permeability; after intravenous injection it remains largely intravascular by virtue of albumin binding, with leakage indicating increased permeability.

evoked potential.definition: An electrical potential recorded from the nervous system in response to a specific sensory stimulus (e.g., visual, auditory, or somatosensory) and measured with surface electrodes; used to assess the functional integrity of sensory pathways.

evoked response.definition: A measurable neural response elicited by a specific sensory or cognitive stimulus, used to assess the integrity of neural pathways (e.g., visual, auditory, or somatosensory evoked potentials).

evoked response audiometry.definition: An electrophysiological test that records auditory-evoked potentials in response to sound (e.g., clicks or tone bursts) to estimate hearing thresholds and assess the integrity of the auditory pathway, particularly in infants or non-cooperative patients; it commonly includes the auditory brainstem response (ABR) and other related evoked potentials.

evoked potential studies.definition: Neurophysiological tests that measure the brain's electrical responses elicited by timed sensory stimuli (visual, auditory, or somatosensory). Recordings, usually via surface electrodes, assess the functional integrity of sensory pathways from peripheral nerves to cortex, with latency and amplitude of responses used to diagnose and monitor neurologic disease and to guide intraoperative monitoring.

electrocardiograms.definition: A noninvasive diagnostic test that records the heart’s electrical activity over time using surface electrodes placed on the chest and limbs, producing a tracing used to detect arrhythmias, ischemia, infarction, and other cardiac conduction abnormalities.

avulsed tooth.definition: A tooth that has been completely displaced from its socket in the alveolar bone due to trauma.

excavator.definition: A heavy construction machine with a hydraulic arm and bucket used to dig and move earth and other materials.

excoriation.definition: Superficial skin injury caused by scratching or other mechanical trauma, resulting in loss of the outer skin layer and presenting as a scratch‑like erosion.

exfoliation.definition: Exfoliation is the shedding or desquamation of surface tissue, particularly the outer layer of skin (epidermis); in dentistry, it also denotes the natural shedding of deciduous (baby) teeth.

exanthem.definition: A widespread skin eruption accompanying a systemic illness (often viral infection), typically presenting as a diffuse erythematous maculopapular rash.

exanthem subitum.definition: A common pediatric viral illness (roseola infantum) caused by human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6); presents with a high fever for several days followed by a sudden, diffuse maculopapular rash as the fever resolves; typically affects children under 2 years and is usually self-limited.

roseola infantum.definition: A common viral illness of infancy/early childhood caused mainly by human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6). It presents with a sudden high fever for about 3–5 days, followed by a rose-pink maculopapular rash that starts on the trunk and spreads to the face and extremities; the illness is typically self-limited.

middle ear cavity.definition: An air-filled cavity in the temporal bone (the tympanic or middle ear), located medial to the eardrum and containing the auditory ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) and tympanic muscles; it communicates with the nasopharynx via the Eustachian tube and with the inner ear through the oval and round windows.

secondary sex characteristics.definition: Features that arise during puberty under the influence of sex hormones to differentiate the sexes but are not part of the reproductive organs; examples include breast development and hip widening in females, facial and body hair, a deeper voice, and increased muscle mass in males.

sexual potency.definition: The ability to engage in sexual activity, including sexual desire (libido) and the physiological capacity to achieve and sustain sexual arousal and response (e.g., erection in males and vaginal lubrication and orgasmic potential in females).

thyroid gland function.definition: An endocrine gland in the neck that synthesizes and releases thyroid hormones (primarily T4 and T3), regulated by TSH from the pituitary; these hormones regulate basal metabolic rate, energy expenditure, heat production, and normal growth and development, while calcitonin helps regulate calcium homeostasis.

prokaryon.definition: A prokaryon is a unicellular organism whose cells lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; its DNA is not enclosed by a nuclear membrane and is located in a nucleoid region (found in bacteria and archaea).

exchange transfusion.definition: An procedure in which a patient’s blood is removed and replaced with donor blood or plasma in a series of exchanges to rapidly reduce circulating substances such as bilirubin, autoantibodies, or toxins.

umbilical venous line.definition: A catheter inserted through the umbilicus into the umbilical vein to access the neonatal central venous system for administration of fluids, medications, parenteral nutrition, and for blood sampling; the tip typically lies in the right atrium or the lower inferior vena cava depending on advancement.

donor blood.definition: Blood collected from a healthy person for transfusion to another person; it is typed for ABO/Rh, screened for infectious diseases, crossmatched as needed, and often processed into components (e.g., red blood cells, plasma, platelets).

plasmanate.definition: A historical brand-name plasma volume expander, a colloid solution containing plasma proteins (such as albumin) used to restore circulating blood volume in hypovolemia.

ivp.definition: A radiographic imaging study of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder performed after intravenous administration of iodinated contrast material to visualize the urinary tract and assess anatomy and function.

exenteration.definition: Radical surgical procedure to remove all contents of a body cavity and often the surrounding tissues; commonly used for locally advanced cancers, such as orbital exenteration (removal of the eye and orbital contents) or pelvic exenteration (removal of pelvic organs).

exencephaly.definition: A severe neural tube defect in which the cranial vault fails to form, leaving brain tissue exposed outside the skull and typically resulting in death.

thrombus formation.definition: The process by which a clot forms within a blood vessel, typically starting with endothelial injury and platelet activation, followed by activation of the coagulation cascade that converts fibrinogen to fibrin to stabilize the clot; it can lead to vessel occlusion and is a key component of thrombosis.

random blood glucose.definition: A blood glucose measurement taken at any time, regardless of when the person last ate.

exemestane.definition: A steroidal, irreversible aromatase inhibitor that lowers estrogen production; used in the treatment of estrogen receptor–positive breast cancer in postmenopausal women, including advanced/metastatic disease and as adjuvant therapy.

metformin.definition: An oral biguanide antidiabetic agent that lowers blood glucose by inhibiting hepatic gluconeogenesis and improving peripheral insulin sensitivity; first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes. Commonly causes gastrointestinal upset; rare but serious risk of lactic acidosis, especially with renal impairment or acute illness; contraindicated in significant renal dysfunction, metabolic acidosis, or acute decompensation.

exercise-induced anaphylaxis.definition: An uncommon systemic allergic reaction in which physical activity triggers anaphylaxis; it can occur with exercise alone or only whenexercise is preceded or accompanied by a specific trigger (such as a particular food or other cofactors). Symptoms include flushing, hives, swelling, throat tightness, wheezing, abdominal pain, dizziness, and possible loss of consciousness. Requires prompt treatment with intramuscular epinephrine and avoidance of triggers; patients should carry an epinephrine autoinjector and have a management plan.

abdominal distension.definition: An abnormal enlargement of the abdomen due to accumulation of gas, fluid (ascites), or a mass within the abdominal cavity, or dilated bowel, leading to increased abdominal girth.

gavage.definition: Administration of a substance directly into the stomach through a tube passed via the mouth or nose; commonly used for force-feeding or delivering nutrients or medications to animals (and in some clinical contexts).

jitteriness.definition: A tremor-like, fine, rapid tremor or restlessness with involuntary movements, often due to anxiety, stimulant use, withdrawal, or metabolic/neurologic disturbances.

air embolus.definition: Blockage of a blood vessel by air bubbles in the circulation, which can impair tissue perfusion and cause ischemia; it can occur with trauma, intravascular procedures, or rapid decompression.

ambulation.definition: The act of walking; the ability to move about on foot.

autonomic.definition: Relating to the autonomic nervous system, which regulates involuntary bodily functions such as heart rate, digestion, respiration, and pupil size through its sympathetic and parasympathetic branches.

exogenous.definition: Originating from outside the body; introduced from external sources rather than produced endogenously.

exeresis.definition: The surgical removal of tissue, a lesion, or an entire organ, typically by excision.

exfoliative.definition: Relating to or characterized by the shedding or peeling of surface epithelial cells, especially skin cells; used to describe conditions with widespread desquamation or procedures that collect shed cells.

orbital.definition: Relating to the orbit (eye socket); of or pertaining to the bones around the eye or the contents of the eye socket.

exophthalmometer.definition: A clinical instrument used to quantify the forward protrusion of the eyeball relative to the lateral orbital rims, providing an objective measurement of exophthalmos (read in millimeters).

exophytic.definition: Describes a lesion or tumor that grows outward from an epithelial surface, protruding into the lumen or external space, rather than invading the underlying tissue.

exostosis.definition: A benign bony outgrowth on the surface of a bone (a bone spur); usually asymptomatic but may cause pain or mechanical irritation if it impinges on nearby tissues.

hyperostosis.definition: Excessive bone formation or thickening of bone tissue due to increased osteoblastic activity, which can be focal or diffuse and may occur as part of various skeletal disorders or idiopathic processes.

exostotic.definition: Relating to exostosis; characterized by or containing exostoses, which are benign bony outgrowths on the surface of a bone.

exophoria.definition: Latent outward misalignment of one or both eyes that is kept in check by binocular fusion and becomes manifest only when fusion is disrupted; a type of heterophoria.

exophoric.definition: Relating to exophoria; a latent outward deviation of the eyes in which they tend to drift outward when binocular fusion is disrupted.

graves.definition: An autoimmune hyperthyroidism caused by TSH receptor–stimulating antibodies, leading to excess thyroid hormone production and often presenting with diffuse goiter and may include ophthalmopathy and dermopathy.

proptosis.definition: Forward bulging or displacement of an organ, especially of an eye. See exophthalmos.

nigra.definition: A Latin word meaning "black"; used in anatomy to denote dark-pigmented tissues or structures, most notably a midbrain region that contains neuromelanin in dopaminergic neurons.

mycetoma.definition: A chronic granulomatous infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissues caused by certain fungi (eumycetoma) or bacteria (actinomycetoma), characterized by painless swelling with sinus tracts that discharge granules (grains).

cavernous.definition: Having large, hollow, blood-filled spaces; in anatomy, describing erectile tissue that engorges with blood and other structures with cavernous spaces.

tendons.definition: Tendons are dense fibrous connective tissues that attach muscles to bones, transmitting the force of muscle contraction to enable joint movement. They are composed mainly of parallel bundles of type I collagen, with relatively poor blood supply, making them strong in tension but slow to heal.

composite.definition: Characterized by being made up of two or more different constituents whose combined properties differ from those of any individual component.

crowns.definition:
- A fixed dental prosthesis that covers a damaged tooth to restore its shape, size, strength, and function.
- The portion of a tooth that is visible above the gum line, usually covered by enamel, in contrast to the root.

impressions.definition: Clinician’s provisional diagnosis or overall assessment of a patient’s condition based on history, examination, and initial data, guiding management and informing the differential diagnosis; in dentistry, a negative mold of the teeth and surrounding oral tissues used to fabricate restorations, appliances, or casts.

restorations.definition: In dentistry, dental restorations are procedures that repair or replace missing tooth structure caused by decay, fracture, or wear, using materials such as fillings, crowns, inlays/onlays, or veneers.

orthodontic.definition: Related to braces or teeth straightening.

archwire.definition: An orthodontic wire threaded through brackets that delivers continuous forces to teeth to guide their alignment; typically made of stainless steel or nickel-titanium alloy and available in round or rectangular cross-sections to influence tooth movement.

bands.definition: Immature neutrophils with a nonsegmented, band-shaped nucleus; released from the bone marrow during infection or inflammation. Their increased presence on a CBC (a "left shift") suggests acute bacterial infection or stress; they participate in phagocytosis and microbial killing.

exoskeleton.definition: A rigid external skeleton that surrounds and protects the body and provides attachment sites for muscles; found in many invertebrates (e.g., insects, arachnids, crustaceans), it is secreted by epidermal cells and is shed (molted) as the organism grows.

osteon.definition: A cylindrical unit of compact bone composed of concentric lamellae around a central Haversian canal containing blood vessels and nerves; osteocytes reside in lacunae between lamellae and communicate through canaliculi.

cartilaginea.definition: Of, relating to, or composed of cartilage; cartilaginous.

endonuclease.definition: An enzyme that cleaves phosphodiester bonds within nucleic acids (DNA or RNA) at internal sites, producing fragments; unlike exonucleases, which remove nucleotides from the ends.

exon.definition: An exon is a sequence of a gene that is transcribed and retained in the mature mRNA after splicing; it contains the coding sequence for a protein and may include untranslated regions (UTRs).

exonuclease.definition: An enzyme that cleaves nucleotides one at a time from the end of a DNA or RNA strand, shortening the molecule; the direction of removal is 3′→5′ or 5′→3′ depending on the specific exonuclease.

exocytosis.definition: A cellular process in which membrane-bound vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane, releasing their contents into the extracellular space and incorporating the vesicle membrane into the plasma membrane. This mechanism underlies secretion of neurotransmitters, hormones, and enzymes and can be regulated (triggered by intracellular signals) or constitutive.

exoenzyme.definition: An enzyme secreted by a cell that functions outside the cell to digest substrates in the extracellular environment.

terpin.definition: Not a standard medical term; it may be a misspelling of a terpene name (such as terpinene or terpineol), which are monoterpene hydrocarbons found in essential oils and turpentine and are not themselves medical conditions or procedures.

guaifenesin.definition: An expectorant medication that loosens and thins mucus in the airways, helping to cough up phlegm and relieve chest congestion.

intraocular.definition: Situated within the eyeball; relating to the interior of the eye.

intraorbital.definition: Situated within the orbital cavity (the bony socket that houses the eye).

ischia.definition: Plural of ischium; one of the paired bones forming the lower posterior part of the hip bone (pelvis), contributing to the acetabulum and bearing weight when sitting; each ischium has a body, ramus, and ischial tuberosity.

exstrophy.definition: A congenital malformation in which the mucosa of a hollow organ, most commonly the urinary bladder, is exposed on the abdominal surface because the anterior abdominal and bladder walls fail to fuse during development; may be associated with the bladder-epispadias complex.

metacarpal.definition: Long bones of the hand between the wrist (carpal) bones and the proximal phalanges (finger bones); there are five metacarpal bones (I–V), forming the knuckles at their distal ends.

micturition.definition: Emptying the bladder. Also called urination or voiding.

metacarpophalangeal.definition: Relating to the joint between a metacarpal bone and the proximal phalanx of a finger; these joints are condyloid joints in the hand that permit flexion and extension of the fingers and, to a lesser extent, abduction and adduction of the digits.

dental pulp.definition: The soft tissue inside a tooth containing nerves, blood vessels, and connective tissue, located in the pulp chamber and root canals.

pulp chamber.definition: The portion of the dental pulp contained within the crown of a tooth; a cavity that houses nerves and blood vessels and connects with the root canal system.

caries excavation.definition: A dental procedure to remove decayed dentin from a tooth cavity to halt caries progression and prepare the tooth for restoration.

explantation.definition: The surgical removal of a previously implanted medical device or prosthesis from the body.

exploratory operation.definition: An operative procedure to investigate and diagnose the cause of symptoms by direct visualization and examination of internal organs, usually performed when noninvasive tests are inconclusive.

insulin-zinc suspension.definition: An injectable insulin preparation in which crystalline insulin is stabilized with zinc and suspended in solution, producing an intermediate-acting form with slower onset and longer duration of action than regular soluble insulin.

extendryl.definition: A brand-name over-the-counter medication used to relieve allergy and cold symptoms, typically a combination product containing an antihistamine to reduce sneezing and runny nose and a decongestant to relieve nasal congestion.

phenylephrine hydrochloride.definition: The hydrochloride salt of phenylephrine, a direct-acting alpha-1 adrenergic agonist used as a nasal decongestant, ocular mydriatic, and vasopressor to raise blood pressure by vasoconstriction.

chlorpheniramine maleate.definition: A first-generation antihistamine (H1 receptor antagonist) in the maleate salt form used to relieve allergic symptoms such as sneezing, itching, runny nose, and conjunctival irritation; it is sedating and can cause drowsiness and anticholinergic effects.

methscopolamine nitrate.definition: A quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) agent used as a gastrointestinal antispasmodic; it blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, reducing smooth muscle tone and secretions in the GI tract, with minimal central nervous system effects due to limited CNS penetration.

expressive aphasia.definition: An expressive language disorder due to injury to the dominant inferior frontal gyrus (Broca's area) causing nonfluent, effortful speech with relatively intact comprehension; speech is slow and halting, with short, agrammatic sentences and impaired repetition (writing may also be affected).

expulsive stage of labor.definition: A portion of the second stage of labor from complete cervical dilation to delivery, during which uterine contractions and the mother's voluntary pushing propel the fetus through the birth canal and result in birth.

expiratory center.definition: A medullary region containing expiratory neurons—primarily in the ventral respiratory group—that initiates and modulates the expiration phase by activating expiratory muscles during breathing.

expiration.definition: The act of exhaling air from the lungs; the phase of respiration during which air is expelled from the lungs, opposite of inspiration.

expiratory retard.definition: A slowing or prolongation of the expiratory phase of respiration (prolonged exhalation), typically due to airway resistance/obstruction or reduced elastic recoil of the lungs.

expulsive inertia.definition: A state during the second stage of labor in which bearing-down efforts are inadequate or poorly coordinated with uterine contractions, resulting in ineffective fetal descent and delayed expulsion.

tympanic canaliculus.definition: A small bony canal in the petrous part of the temporal bone that transmits the tympanic nerve (a branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve, CN IX) into the middle ear to form the tympanic plexus.

external shunt.definition: A temporary externally connected conduit that diverts fluid from inside the body to an external drainage system, used for temporary drainage or decompression rather than a permanently implanted shunt (most commonly cerebrospinal fluid).

beam radiotherapy.definition: A cancer treatment that uses high-energy ionizing radiation beams delivered from outside the body to target a tumor. The radiation damages DNA in cancer cells, slowing or stopping their growth, and is shaped and timed to minimize exposure to surrounding healthy tissue. Commonly delivered with a linear accelerator.

external beam therapy.definition: A form of radiotherapy in which high-energy radiation is delivered from outside the body to a tumor using machines like a linear accelerator, typically given in multiple fractions over several weeks to destroy cancer cells while limiting damage to surrounding healthy tissue.

common carotid arteries.definition: A pair of large arteries in the neck that supply oxygenated blood to the head and neck; each arises from the aortic arch (left) or brachiocephalic trunk (right), ascends within the carotid sheath, and typically divides into the internal and external carotid arteries around the level of the upper thyroid cartilage.

external carotid nerves.definition: Not a standard anatomical term. Likely refers to the carotid plexus—a network of postganglionic sympathetic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion that accompanies the external carotid artery and its branches, providing vasomotor innervation to head and neck structures and integrating with the arterial branches.

superior cervical ganglion.definition: An enlargement of the sympathetic trunk in the neck at the C2–C3 level; the largest sympathetic ganglion of the head and neck, containing postganglionic neurons that form the internal carotid plexus and innervate structures such as the dilator pupillae, Müller's muscle, lacrimal and facial glands, and head vasculature.

sympathetic fibers.definition: Efferent autonomic nerve fibers of the sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system; they originate in the thoracolumbar spinal cord, synapse in sympathetic ganglia, and innervate target organs to mediate fight-or-flight responses. Preganglionic fibers are cholinergic and synapse on nicotinic receptors; postganglionic fibers are typically adrenergic (norepinephrine), with sweat glands being an exception and using acetylcholine.

external cervical os.definition: The external cervical os is the external opening of the cervical canal at the cervix, forming the boundary between the endocervical canal and the vaginal canal; it is visible on pelvic examination and is typically circular in nulliparous women and slit-like in multiparous women.

internal cervical os.definition: The opening at the proximal end of the cervical canal where the uterus communicates with the endocervical canal; it marks the superior boundary of the cervix and expands during labor.

baudeloque's diameter.definition: Definition not found in standard medical references for "baudeloque's diameter." It may be a misspelling or a very obscure term. Please provide the correct spelling or some context (anatomical site, field, or source), and I’ll define it. If you’re thinking of a related term, I can also define common diameter measurements (e.g., pelvic or skull diameters).

conjugate diameter.definition: Anteroposterior dimension of the pelvic inlet, measured from the sacral promontory to the posterior surface of the pubic symphysis; it represents the narrowest AP diameter the fetal head must pass, and is referred to as the obstetric conjugate when used in childbirth assessments.

obstetric calipers.definition: A measuring instrument used in obstetrics to determine pelvic dimensions (pelvimetry) or fetal head size, to help assess the likely course of labor.

counterpulsation.definition: A mechanical circulatory support method in which a catheter-mounted balloon in the aorta inflates during diastole to increase coronary perfusion and deflates just before systole to reduce left-ventricular afterload, thereby improving myocardial oxygen supply and cardiac output (commonly via an intra-aortic balloon pump).

lateral cuneiform bone.definition: A small, wedge-shaped tarsal bone in the foot, one of the three cuneiform bones; it lies on the lateral side of the tarsus between the navicular proximally and the cuboid distally, and articulates with the navicular, cuboid, and the base of the third metatarsal.

external fixation.definition: A method of fracture stabilization in which percutaneous pins or wires are inserted through the skin into bone fragments and connected to an external frame to maintain alignment and immobilize the fracture during healing.

pin fixation.definition: A method of stabilizing fractures by inserting pins (usually Kirschner wires) through the skin into bone to hold fracture fragments in alignment, often connected to an external fixator or used for percutaneous fixation.

pins.definition: A slender metal pin used in orthopedic surgery to immobilize and align fractures; inserted percutaneously or through an incision, and may be temporary (e.g., Kirschner wires) or permanent.

internal fixation.definition: A surgical method of stabilizing a broken bone by fixing the fragments with implanted hardware inside the body (eg, plates, screws, rods, or intramedullary nails) to maintain proper alignment during healing.

iliac node.definition: A lymph node located along the iliac vessels in the pelvis (including external, internal, or common iliac nodes); it is part of pelvic lymphatic drainage, filtering lymph from the lower limb and pelvic/lower abdominal structures and typically draining to the lumbar (para-aortic) nodes.

iliac nodes.definition: Group of lymph nodes located along the pelvic vessels that filter lymph from the pelvis, lower abdomen, and lower limbs; drain into the lumbar (para-aortic) lymph nodes.

parietal node.definition: A lymph node located along the parietal aspect of a body cavity or body wall; it filters lymph from the parietal region (somatic tissues and associated serous membranes) and is part of the regional lymphatic drainage system.

malleolus fibulae.definition: Distal end of the fibula forming the lateral malleolus; a bony prominence at the outer ankle that articulates with the talus and serves as an attachment for lateral ankle ligaments.

occipital crest.definition: A midline ridge on the external surface of the occipital bone (external occipital crest) that serves as an attachment site for the nuchal ligaments.

occipital protuberance.definition: Midline bony prominence on the posterior skull at the occipital bone, serving as an attachment point for the nuchal ligament and neck muscles and as a palpable anatomic landmark.

perimysium.definition: A sheath of connective tissue surrounding a bundle of skeletal muscle fibers (a fascicle); located between the endomysium (around individual fibers) and the epimysium (around the entire muscle), and containing blood vessels and nerves that supply the fascicle.

epimysium.definition: The dense irregular connective tissue layer surrounding an entire skeletal muscle, binding its fascicles together and continuing into the tendon at the muscle’s ends.

pterygoid muscle.definition: One of the two muscles of mastication—the medial pterygoid and lateral pterygoid—that move the mandible; the medial pterygoid elevates and helps protrude the jaw, while the lateral pterygoid depresses and protrudes the jaw and aids in side-to-side grinding.

pterygoideus lateralis.definition: One of the muscles of mastication; a paired muscle in the infratemporal fossa that protracts and depresses the mandible and assists in opening the mouth. The superior head inserts on the articular disc and TMJ capsule, the inferior head on the neck of the mandible; innervated by the mandibular division (V3) of the trigeminal nerve.

keloids.definition: A benign overgrowth of scar tissue that extends beyond the original wound margins due to abnormal wound healing and excessive collagen formation; it typically presents as a firm, raised scar that may be pink or dark and can itch or be tender, often recurring after treatment.

dermatologic conditions.definition: Diseases and disorders of the skin, hair, nails, and their appendages arising from genetic, inflammatory, infectious, autoimmune, vascular, or neoplastic processes, typically presenting with lesions, itching, scaling, hair loss, or nail changes.

pemphigus vulgaris.definition: A rare autoimmune blistering disorder characterized by flaccid intraepidermal bullae and painful mucosal erosions due to acantholysis from autoantibodies against desmoglein-3 (often with desmoglein-1), commonly presenting with a positive Nikolsky sign and requiring systemic immunosuppressive therapy.

photochemotherapy.definition: A treatment that uses a photosensitizing agent (usually psoralen) and exposure to ultraviolet A (UVA) light to induce a photochemical reaction in skin cells, used to treat conditions such as psoriasis, vitiligo, eczema, and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

extracorporeal membrane oxygenator.definition: A device used in extracorporeal membrane oxygenation that oxygenates blood and removes carbon dioxide outside the body by circulating blood through a semipermeable membrane in contact with a gas, effectively functioning as an artificial lung.

extracorporeal photochemotherapy.definition: An apheresis-based therapy in which the patient’s leukocytes are collected outside the body, treated with a photosensitizing agent (commonly 8-mydroxypsoralen) and exposed to ultraviolet A (UVA) light, then reinfused. The procedure modulates immune function and is used for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and graft-versus-host disease, among other immune-mediated conditions.

extracorporeal shock-wave lithotripsy.definition: Noninvasive procedure that uses externally generated shock waves to fragment a renal or ureteral stone so that the fragments can pass in the urine.

extracorporeal circulation.definition: A technique in which blood is diverted from the body, circulated through an external pump-oxygenator circuit, and returned to the circulation to provide cardiopulmonary support during surgery or when the heart or lungs are failing.

perfusion technologist.definition: A perfusion technologist is a healthcare professional who operates extracorporeal circulation equipment (such as the heart-lung machine) during procedures requiring bypass, and who monitors perfusion parameters, oxygenation, temperature, and circuit integrity while assisting the surgical team. They may also manage anticoagulation, cardioplegia delivery, and related aspects of patient care during the procedure.

extracranial.definition: Outside the skull; relating to or located beyond the cranial cavity.

extracapsular ankylosis.definition: A form of joint ankylosis where fusion occurs outside the joint capsule (pericapsular), typically due to fibrous or osseous tissue bridging the periarticular structures and causing loss of movement.

extracapsular dendrite.definition: Not a standard medical term; there is no formal definition. If used, it would imply a dendrite (a neuron's input process) located outside a capsule surrounding a tissue or organ, but this usage is not recognized in neuroanatomy or histology.

extracapsular fracture.definition: A fracture occurring outside the joint capsule of a synovial joint; in the hip, classic examples are intertrochanteric and subtrochanteric fractures.

extracapsular retainer.definition: Not a standard medical term; if used, it would describe a device or appliance that retains or stabilizes anatomical structures located outside a capsule (extracapsular).

extracoronal.definition: Outside the crown of a tooth; referring to restorations or attachments placed on the exterior of the tooth crown rather than within the crown.

extracoronal retainer.definition: An extracoronal retainer is a retention component of a removable partial denture that engages an undercut on the external (coronal) surface of an abutment tooth, typically via a clasp or external attachment mounted to the crown to resist dislodgement.

extracellular.definition: Outside the cells; relating to the extracellular space outside cell membranes, including extracellular fluid (interstitial fluid and plasma) and the extracellular matrix that surrounds and supports cells.

extracellular space.definition: The space outside cells containing extracellular fluid (interstitial fluid and plasma) that surrounds cells and mediates exchange of nutrients, gases, and waste with the circulatory system.

extrachromosomal.definition: Located outside the chromosomes; genetic material that exists outside the nuclear genome, such as plasmids or mitochondrial DNA, often replicating independently of chromosomal DNA.

extradural anesthesia.definition: An regional anesthesia produced by injecting local anesthetic into the extradural (epidural) space outside the dura mater to block nerve roots, providing analgesia or anesthesia to the lower trunk and limbs; commonly used for labor analgesia and lower abdominal or lower limb surgery, often via a catheter for continuous infusion.

extradural hemorrhage.definition: An accumulation of blood between the dura mater and the skull, usually from traumatic rupture of an artery (often the middle meningeal artery); it can produce a lucid interval followed by rapid neurological deterioration and requires urgent neurosurgical evacuation (burr hole or craniotomy).

epidural hemorrhage.definition: A collection of blood between the dura mater and the skull (epidural space), typically caused by traumatic rupture of a meningeal artery, presenting with a brief lucid interval followed by rapidly worsening headache, vomiting, confusion, or focal neurological deficits; a neurosurgical emergency.

caudal anesthesia.definition: A regional anesthesia technique in which a local anesthetic is injected into the caudal epidural space via the sacral hiatus to produce anesthesia and analgesia of the lower spinal nerve roots, commonly used for pediatric procedures involving the lower abdomen, perineum, or legs.

joint capsule.definition: A fibrous envelope surrounding a synovial joint, composed of dense irregular connective tissue (outer fibrous layer) and lined on the inside by the synovial membrane; it encloses the joint cavity, provides stability, and contains synovial fluid for lubrication.

extrabronchial.definition: Outside the bronchus; located exterior to the bronchial tree or bronchial lumen.

vertex presentation.definition: A cephalic fetal presentation in which the head is flexed so the occipital region presents first through the birth canal; the most common and favorable position for vaginal delivery, typically with the occiput oriented toward the mother's anterior pelvis (occiput anterior).

perineal nerves.definition: Branches of the pudendal nerve (S2–S4) that innervate the perineal region, including motor innervation to the deep perineal muscles via the deep perineal branch and sensory innervation to the skin of the perineum and the posterior scrotal/labial regions via the posterior scrotal (labial) nerves.

abutment tooth.definition: A natural tooth that provides support for a dental prosthesis (e.g., a crown-supported fixed partial denture or bridge), typically prepared with a full-coverage crown to anchor the prosthesis.

cast crown.definition: A dental crown fabricated by casting a metal alloy (typically via the lost-wax process) to fit over a prepared tooth; commonly gold or base-metal crowns, used for full-coverage restoration and sometimes as a framework for porcelain.

direct clasp-type retainer.definition: A retentive component of a removable partial denture that engages the undercut of an abutment tooth with a clasp to provide direct retention and resist dislodgement of the denture.

clasp-type retainer.definition: A dental appliance that retains a removable orthodontic or prosthetic appliance by engaging one or more adjacent teeth with metal clasps.

removable partial denture.definition: A dental prosthesis that replaces missing teeth in a partially edentulous jaw and is supported by the remaining natural teeth and/or implants; it is designed to be removable by the patient for cleaning and maintenance.

cast restoration.definition: In dentistry, a metal restoration created by casting a molten alloy into a mold around a wax pattern (lost-wax technique) to restore tooth structure; commonly used for inlays, onlays, and crowns.

extraembryonic.definition: Relating to structures outside the embryo that support its development, such as the amnion, chorion, yolk sac, and allantois.

exocoelom.definition: A transient embryonic cavity formed early in development between the hypoblast-derived membrane and the surrounding trophoblast, surrounding the yolk sac; it is the primitive yolk sac cavity and is later replaced by the expanding extraembryonic coelom (chorionic cavity).

extraembryonic mesoderm.definition: A mesodermal layer derived from migrating epiblast cells that lines the extraembryonic membranes (chorion, amnion, yolk sac) and the walls of the extraembryonic coelom, differentiates into somatic (parietal) and splanchnic (visceral) mesoderm, and contributes to the formation of the body stalk and placental vasculature.

extraperitoneal.definition: Situated outside the peritoneum or peritoneal cavity; referring to tissues or spaces that lie outside the lining of the abdominal cavity.

paravesical space.definition: A potential extraperitoneal space in the pelvis located on each side of the urinary bladder, between the bladder medially and the pelvic wall laterally, formed by endopelvic fascia and peritoneal reflections; it communicates with the retroperitoneal space and contains surrounding vessels and nerves.

extraperitoneal cesarean section.definition: A cesarean delivery performed via an extraperitoneal approach, in which the peritoneal cavity is not entered; the uterus is accessed through the extraperitoneal space by dissecting around the peritoneum to reach the lower uterine segment.

extrapleural.definition: Situated outside the pleura; referring to structures beyond or outside the pleural cavity, specifically the space between the parietal pleura and the endothoracic fascia (thoracic wall).

endothoracic fascia.definition: A thin sheet of loose connective tissue between the parietal pleura and the inner surface of the thoracic wall (ribs, intercostal muscles, and diaphragm) that lines the thoracic cavity and anchors the pleura to the chest wall; it is continuous with surrounding cervical and mediastinal fascial layers.

extravascular.definition: Outside the blood vessels; located in or occurring in tissues beyond the vascular system.

extravascular fluid.definition: Fluid located outside the blood vessels; includes interstitial fluid surrounding tissues and various transcellular fluids such as cerebrospinal, pleural, peritoneal, synovial, and other body fluids.

extrarenal.definition: Located outside the kidney; pertaining to tissue, structures, or processes occurring outside the kidneys (as opposed to intrarenal).

extrarenal uremia.definition: An historical term for the uremic syndrome caused by factors outside the kidneys—i.e., elevated nitrogenous wastes arising from non-renal production or systemic processes rather than from intrinsic renal failure.

extramedullary.definition: Outside the bone marrow; referring to tissue or processes that occur outside the medullary cavity of bones (for example, extramedullary hematopoiesis).

plasmacytoma.definition: A solitary neoplastic mass of plasma cells arising in bone (solitary plasmacytoma of bone) or soft tissue (extramedullary plasmacytoma), with no evidence of systemic multiple myeloma at diagnosis; it may progress to multiple myeloma over time.

extramedullary myeloma.definition: A manifestation of multiple myeloma in which malignant plasma cells infiltrate tissues outside the bone marrow (extramedullary sites), indicating disseminated disease and often associated with a poorer prognosis.

extramedullary plasmacytoma.definition: A solitary tumor of monoclonal plasma cells arising outside the bone marrow, most often in soft tissues of the head and neck; a localized plasma cell neoplasm that can progress to multiple myeloma, typically lacking systemic bone marrow involvement at presentation and treated primarily with radiotherapy or surgical excision.

extramedullary myelopoiesis.definition: Extramedullary myelopoiesis is the production of hematopoietic tissue outside the bone marrow (most often in the liver and spleen), occurring as a compensatory response to marrow failure or increased demand for blood cells; it is seen in conditions like chronic anemia and myelofibrosis and can cause hepatosplenomegaly.

ectopic myelopoiesis.definition: Hematopoiesis occurring outside the bone marrow, typically in organs such as the liver or spleen, usually as a compensatory response to marrow failure or severe anemia (extramedullary hematopoiesis).

extraocular movement.definition: Movements of the eyeball produced by the six extraocular muscles (four rectus and two obliques) that allow gaze in all directions; clinically assessed by testing ocular motility and the function of cranial nerves III (oculomotor), IV (trochlear), and VI (abducens).

extraocular muscle palsy.definition: Weakness or paralysis of one or more of the extraocular muscles that move the eye, leading to restricted gaze, ocular misalignment (strabismus), and double vision (diplopia); often due to cranial nerve III, IV, or VI palsy or other orbital motor pathology.

extraocular muscles.definition: Muscles that move the eyeball, located outside the globe, comprising six muscles: the four rectus (superior, inferior, medial, lateral) and the two obliques (superior, inferior); they are innervated by cranial nerves III (oculomotor), IV (trochlear), and VI (abducens).

extraoral anchorage.definition: An orthodontic technique that uses external devices attached to the head or neck (e.g., headgear or a facebow) to apply forces to teeth, providing anchorage and enabling controlled tooth movement while minimizing undesired movement of the anchor teeth.

extraoral orthodontic appliance.definition: A device used in orthodontics that applies forces to teeth or jaws from outside the mouth, typically anchored to the head or neck (such as headgear or a facemask), to influence tooth movement or jaw growth.

extubation.definition: Removal of an endotracheal tube after a period of intubation and mechanical ventilation, performed when the patient can maintain adequate oxygenation and ventilation, protect the airway, and breathe spontaneously or with minimal support.

extubate.definition: The removal of an endotracheal tube from a patient, typically after anesthesia or once the patient can breathe independently and protect the airway following mechanical ventilation.

extrusion.definition: The process of being pushed or forced out; in medicine, displacement of tissue through an opening or defect; in spinal disc disease, a herniation where nucleus pulposus protrudes through the annulus fibrosus and extends beyond the disc margin while remaining connected to the disc.

extrusion reflex.definition: A primitive oral reflex in which tactile stimulation of the mouth or oral mucosa elicits extrusion or forward thrust of the tongue; common in newborns and usually diminishes with development, but persistence or exaggeration can indicate neurologic impairment.

exudation.definition: The leakage of fluid containing plasma proteins and cells from capillaries into surrounding tissues or body cavities, occurring during inflammation due to increased vascular permeability.

exudative.definition: Relating to or consisting of exudate; a fluid produced at inflammation that escapes from vessels and is rich in protein, cells, and other inflammatory components.

exudative enteropathy.definition: An inflammatory enteropathy in which plasma proteins leak into the intestinal lumen from damaged mucosa, causing protein loss (protein-losing enteropathy) and possibly hypoalbuminemia.

coats' disease.definition: A rare, congenital retinal vascular disorder characterized by unilateral retinal telangiectasia with lipid-rich subretinal exudation that can progress to exudative retinal detachment, most often presenting in children and potentially causing vision loss if untreated.

coats' retinitis.definition: A rare unilateral retinal vascular disorder characterized by telangiectatic and aneurysmal peripheral retinal vessels with lipid-rich exudation in the retina and subretinal space, potentially causing exudative retinal detachment; typically presents in children or young adults, more often in males, and is not primarily inflammatory.

exudative retinitis.definition: An inflammatory retinal condition in which inflammatory exudates accumulate in the retina and subretinal space due to breakdown of the blood–retina barrier; often presents with lipid‑rich yellowish exudates, macular edema, and possible serous retinal detachment, and is typically associated with systemic inflammatory or infectious diseases.

eye bank.definition: An organization that procures, evaluates, preserves, stores, and distributes donor ocular tissue—primarily corneas—for transplantation, research, and education, including donor screening and infectious disease testing.

eyebrow.definition: An area of hair located above the eye in the superciliary region; its function includes deflecting sweat away from the eye, shading the eye from sunlight, and aiding in facial expression.

eyelash.definition: One of the fine hairs growing from the margin of the eyelids; they help protect the eye by trapping dust and debris and by stimulating the blinking reflex.

palpebra.definition: An eyelid: a movable, skin-covered fold that protects the eyeball; the upper and lower lids open and close to distribute tears and shield the ocular surface, consisting of skin, orbicularis oculi muscle, tarsal plate, and conjunctiva.

vitreous body.definition: An avascular, transparent gel filling the vitreous chamber of the eye between the lens and retina; it maintains the globe’s shape, transmits light, and helps hold the retina in place. It consists mainly of water with collagen and hyaluronic acid.

hyaloid canal.definition: A narrow, transparent channel within the vitreous body extending from the posterior surface of the lens to the optic disc; it represents the path of the hyaloid artery during fetal development and is typically obliterated in adulthood.

extramammary.definition: Situated outside the mammary gland; outside the breast.

plasma cell tumor.definition: A neoplasm composed of malignant plasma cells derived from B lymphocytes; it can be solitary (solitary plasmacytoma) or part of systemic disease such as multiple myeloma.

patching.definition: The act of applying a patch to cover, seal, occlude, or protect tissue or a defect, typically for wound care, surgical repair, or therapeutic purposes (e.g., occluding one eye in amblyopia therapy or patch closure of a heart defect).

ezetimibe.definition: A drug that is used along with changes in diet, weight loss, and exercise to reduce the amounts of certain fats (cholesterol) in the blood. It can help reduce the chance of developing heart disease, heart attacks, or strokes.

eye wash.definition: A sterile isotonic solution (often saline) used to rinse the eyes to remove debris or chemical irritants, typically delivered via an eyewash station or manual eyewash bottle.

homozygous low-density lipoprotein recep.definition: Bi-allelic mutations in the LDL receptor gene that cause markedly elevated LDL cholesterol from birth, leading to premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease; commonly presents with tendon xanthomas and corneal arcus.

homozygous sitosterolemia.definition: An autosomal recessive inherited metabolic disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in ABCG5 or ABCG8, leading to defective intestinal absorption and biliary excretion of plant sterols. This results in markedly elevated plasma plant sterol levels (e.g., sitosterol, campesterol) and can cause xanthomas, premature atherosclerosis, and sometimes macrothrombocytopenia or hemolysis.

antilipemic agent.definition: A medication that lowers lipid levels in the blood (such as cholesterol and triglycerides) to reduce the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease; includes statins, fibrates, bile acid sequestrants, niacin, and PCSK9 inhibitors.

fabry syndrome.definition: An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient alpha-galactosidase A activity, leading to accumulation of globotriaosylceramide in vascular endothelium and other tissues, and presenting with neuropathic pain, angiokeratomas, hypohidrosis, corneal verticillata, and progressive kidney, heart, and cerebrovascular disease.

fab fragment.definition: An antigen-binding fragment of an antibody containing one complete light chain (VL-CL) and the variable domain of the heavy chain plus the CH1 domain (VH-CH1), forming a single antigen-binding site; produced by proteolytic cleavage of IgG (e.g., with papain), yielding two Fab fragments and an Fc fragment.

fatty acid.definition: A carboxylic acid with a long, unbranched hydrocarbon chain (typically 4–28 carbons) that is a principal component of lipids; they can be saturated (no double bonds) or unsaturated (one or more double bonds) and may exist as free fatty acids or as esterified forms in triglycerides and phospholipids.

fab classification.definition: An historical morphological and cytochemical classification system for acute myeloid leukemia that divides cases into subtypes M0–M7 based on cytomorphology and staining patterns, developed by French-American-British investigators.

fabere.definition: A clinical test used to evaluate hip and sacroiliac joint pathology. With the patient supine, the leg is flexed, abducted, and externally rotated, and the knee is gently lowered toward the table; reproduction of groin or sacroiliac pain indicates pathology in the hip or SI joint.

face.definition: Anatomical region of the head comprising the anterior surface from the forehead to the chin, including the skin, facial muscles, bones, and soft tissues that form the facial features and expressions.

facies.definition: The overall facial appearance and expression, especially as it reflects a patient’s health status or a characteristic pattern of a disease.

face bow.definition: A dental device used to record the spatial relationship of the maxillary arch to the skull and transfer that relation to a dental articulator, so that dental casts can be mounted with correct orientation to the patient's hinge axis for accurate occlusion and prosthodontic procedures.

face lift.definition: A cosmetic surgical procedure to tighten and re-drape facial skin and underlying tissues, remove excess skin, and reposition fat to reduce wrinkles and sagging (rhytidectomy).

rhytidectomy.definition: A surgical procedure that involves removing excess skin and tightening the underlying muscle to correct sagging around the jaws, jowls, and neck. Does not include work on the eyes or forehead. Commonly known as a face lift.

face presentation.definition: A cephalic presentation in which the fetal face is the presenting part; the head is extended so that the chin (mentum) leads through the birth canal.

facet joint.definition: A synovial joint between the superior articular process of one vertebra and the inferior articular process of the vertebra above it (a zygapophysial joint) that guides and limits spinal motion; it is enclosed by a capsule and innervated by the medial branches of the dorsal rami.
