medial plantar nerve.definition: A branch of the tibial nerve in the foot that supplies motor innervation to the intrinsic muscles of the sole (abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, flexor hallucis brevis, and the first lumbrical) and sensory innervation to the medial sole and the plantar surfaces of the medial three and a half toes.

lateral plantar nerve.definition: Branch of the tibial nerve that runs along the lateral sole, supplying most intrinsic plantar muscles (except those innervated by the medial plantar nerve) and providing sensory innervation to the lateral sole and the lateral one-and-a-half toes.

plantar aponeurosis.definition: A thick band of connective tissue on the sole of the foot that extends from the calcaneal tuberosity to the base of the toes, supporting the longitudinal arch and aiding propulsion via the windlass mechanism during toe-off.

flexor digitorum longus.definition: A muscle of the deep posterior compartment of the leg that flexes the distal phalanges of the toes (digits 2–5) and assists with plantarflexion and inversion of the foot; it originates from the tibia and inserts onto the distal phalanges of the toes and is innervated by the tibial nerve.

flexor digitorum brevis.definition: An intrinsic muscle of the sole of the foot arising from the calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis; it splits into four tendons that insert on the sides of the middle phalanges of toes 2–5, and it flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints of these toes (assisting flexion at the metatarsophalangeal joints).

flexor digiti minimi brevis.definition: A small intrinsic hand muscle of the hypothenar eminence that flexes the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint; originates from the hook of the hamate (and flexor retinaculum) and inserts on the base of the proximal phalanx of the little finger; innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

flexor carpi radialis.definition: A superficial flexor muscle of the forearm that originates from the medial epicondyle of the humerus and inserts on the bases of the second (and usually third) metacarpal bones; it flexes the wrist and abducts (radially deviates) the hand. Innervation is via the median nerve (C6–C7).

flexor carpi ulnaris.definition: A superficial forearm flexor on the ulnar side that flexes and adducts the wrist; it has two heads (humeral and ulnar) and inserts on the pisiform, with tendinous extensions to the hook of the hamate and base of the 5th metacarpal via the pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments. Innervated by the ulnar nerve (C8–T1).

palmaris longus.definition: A slender superficial flexor of the forearm that originates from the medial epicondyle of the humerus and inserts into the palmar aponeurosis; it tenses the palmar fascia and assists wrist flexion, and is variably absent (agenesis) in many individuals.

abductor digiti minimi.definition: A hand muscle in the hypothenar eminence that abducts the little finger (fifth digit) away from the ring finger; innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

flexor hallucis brevis.definition: A short intrinsic muscle of the sole with two heads that originates from the cuboid and lateral cuneiform and inserts on the sides of the proximal phalanx of the great toe to flex the first toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint; innervated by the medial plantar nerve.

flange.definition: A projecting rim or lip of a bone or medical device that provides attachment for soft tissue, helps stabilize a prosthesis, or forms a seal; in dentistry, the portion of a denture that extends beyond the base to cover the alveolar mucosa.

anterior interosseous nerve.definition: A pure motor branch of the median nerve in the forearm that travels along the interosseous membrane and innervates the flexor pollicis longus, the radial (lateral) half of the flexor digitorum profundus, and the pronator quadratus.

flexor digitorum sublimis.definition: A forearm muscle that flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints of digits 2–5; its tendons insert on the sides of the middle phalanges and it is innervated by the median nerve.

flexor hallucis longus.definition: A muscle of the deep posterior compartment of the leg whose tendon passes behind the medial malleolus to insert on the distal phalanx of the great toe; it flexes the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints and assists in plantarflexion of the foot and maintenance of the medial longitudinal arch. Innervated by the tibial nerve.

flexor pollicis brevis.definition: A thenar muscle that flexes the proximal phalanx of the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint; it has superficial and deep heads, with origins from the flexor retinaculum and carpal bones (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate) and insertion on the base of the proximal phalanx; innervation is usually the recurrent branch of the median nerve, though the deep head may be supplied by the ulnar nerve.

retinaculum.definition: A band of thickened deep fascia or connective tissue that binds down a tendon as it crosses a joint, preventing bowstringing and guiding tendon movement.

calcaneum.definition: The heel bone, the largest tarsal bone of the foot, forming the heel and providing the insertion site for the Achilles tendon; it articulates with the talus superiorly and with the cuboid anteriorly.

medial malleolus.definition: The distal medial bony projection of the tibia forming the inner ankle; it articulates with the talus to complete the ankle mortise and serves as the attachment site for the deltoid ligament.

metacarpophalangeal joint.definition: A synovial ellipsoidal (condyloid) joint between the head of a metacarpal bone and the base of the proximal phalanx of a finger (including the thumb); it mainly allows flexion and extension with limited abduction/adduction and circumduction, and is stabilized by the volar plate and radial and ulnar collateral ligaments.

thumb.definition: Short, thick first digit of the hand that is opposable to the other fingers, enabling grip and fine manipulation; it has two phalanges (proximal and distal) and a metacarpal base, with a saddle-shaped carpometacarpal joint allowing opposition.

plantarflexion.definition: Movement at the ankle that points the toes downward (toward the plantar surface), as in standing on tiptoes; the opposite movement is dorsiflexion.

proximal phalanx.definition: A long bone of a finger or toe that lies between the metacarpal/metatarsal bone and the middle phalanx; it forms the metacarpophalangeal joint with the palm bone and the proximal interphalangeal joint with the middle phalanx (in the thumb it articulates with the distal phalanx).

great toe.definition: The medial, largest toe of the foot, consisting of two phalanges (proximal and distal); essential for balance and propulsion during gait.

flow cytometry.definition: A laboratory technique in which cells or particles in suspension are passed single file through a focused laser beam, and the resulting light scatter and fluorescence are measured to analyze physical characteristics (size and granularity) and the expression of multiple biological markers.

rotameter.definition: An instrument that measures and indicates the flow rate of a gas by means of a floating indicator inside a tapered, vertically oriented tube; as flow increases, the float rises, and its position on a calibrated scale specifies the flow rate (often used in anesthesia equipment).

uroflowmetry.definition: A noninvasive test that measures the rate and pattern of urine flow during urination using a uroflowmeter, providing metrics such as maximum flow rate (Qmax), average flow rate, voided volume, and duration to evaluate lower urinary tract symptoms and possible obstruction or detrusor dysfunction.

flow-volume curve.definition: A graph from spirometry that plots airflow rate (L/s) on the vertical axis against lung volume (L) on the horizontal axis for both forced expiration and rapid inspiration; the resulting flow-volume loop helps assess airway obstruction and other ventilatory abnormalities.

flow-volume dysequilibrium.definition: An abnormal, discordant relationship between instantaneous airflow and lung volume during forced breathing maneuvers, typically reflected as an atypical flow–volume loop and indicating ventilatory impairment such as dynamic airway obstruction, restrictive/neuromuscular weakness, or ventilatory asynchrony.

floater.definition: Little cobwebs or spots that float in your vision.

retinal vein occlusion.definition: An obstruction of retinal venous drainage, most often from thrombosis, causing sudden, painless visual disturbance; can be central (CRVO) or branch (BRVO) and is associated with hypertension, glaucoma, atherosclerosis, and hypercoagulable states; macular edema often underlies vision loss.

vitreous hemorrhage.definition: Bleeding into the vitreous humor (the gel filling the back of the eye), causing sudden vision loss or distortion and floaters; often due to retinal disease (e.g., diabetic retinopathy), retinal tear/trauma, or vein occlusion; evaluation is via dilated eye exam and imaging, with treatment addressing the underlying cause and sometimes surgical clearance if the hemorrhage persists.

proliferative diabetic retinopathy.definition: An advanced stage of diabetic retinopathy in which retinal ischemia stimulates neovascularization (new, fragile blood vessels) on the retina or optic disc, potentially forming fibrovascular membranes that can cause vitreous hemorrhage and tractional retinal detachment; commonly treated with panretinal laser photocoagulation or intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy.

flocculation.definition: The aggregation of fine particles in a colloidal suspension into larger clumps (flocs), usually promoted by coagulating agents or changes in ionic strength, to facilitate settling or filtration.

flocculant.definition: A substance that promotes the clumping of fine suspended particles into larger aggregates (flocs), causing them to settle out of a liquid; used to clarify suspensions or remove particulates.

flocculation test.definition: A laboratory procedure to evaluate the aggregation of colloidal particles in a suspension when a coagulant or flocculant is added, typically involving rapid mixing, slow mixing, and settling, with measurement of turbidity or sedimentation to assess treatment efficacy and optimize dosing.

isoflurophate.definition: An organophosphate acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used as an ophthalmic agent to treat glaucoma by causing miosis and lowering intraocular pressure; it is an irreversible AChE inhibitor.

intraocular hemorrhage.definition: Bleeding inside the eye, typically into the anterior chamber (hyphema) or the vitreous body (vitreous hemorrhage), which can cause vision loss and arises from trauma, intraocular disease, or systemic vascular disorders.

radiofrequency pulse.definition: A brief burst of radiofrequency energy used to perturb nuclear spins (primarily protons) in MRI; delivered by an RF coil, it tips the net magnetization away from the main magnetic field by a specific flip angle to generate or modify the MR signal, with duration, frequency, and amplitude influencing image contrast and SAR.

tarsal tunnel.definition: A fibro-osseous tunnel on the medial aspect of the ankle formed by the flexor retinaculum and the underlying bones (medial malleolus, talus, calcaneus). It contains the tibial nerve and its branches, the posterior tibial vessels, and the tendons of tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus, and flexor hallucis longus; compression within this tunnel causes neural and vascular symptoms in the foot.

flow-volume loop.definition: A graphical plot of airflow (usually in liters per second) against lung volume obtained during spirometry, displaying the inspiratory and expiratory limbs; used to assess ventilatory mechanics, characterize airway obstruction (obstructive vs restrictive patterns), and help localize airway obstruction (intrathoracic vs extrathoracic).

floxuridine.definition: An antineoplastic fluorinated pyrimidine nucleoside analog used in chemotherapy, often via hepatic arterial infusion for liver metastases from colorectal cancer; it inhibits DNA synthesis by blocking thymidylate synthase and incorporating into DNA.

gastrointestinal cancer.definition: Cancers that originate in the digestive tract, from the esophagus to the anus, including malignant tumors of the esophagus, stomach, small intestine, colon, and rectum.

fludarabine.definition: A purine analogue antineoplastic agent used in chemotherapy for hematologic malignancies; after intracellular phosphorylation to fludarabine triphosphate, it inhibits DNA synthesis by interfering with DNA polymerases and ribonucleotide reductase, and is used especially for chronic lymphocytic leukemia and related lymphoid malignancies.

non-hodgkin’s lymphoma.definition: A group of lymphoid cancers that originate from B, T, or NK cells and arise in lymph nodes or extranodal sites; they range from indolent to aggressive and typically present with painless lymphadenopathy, sometimes with systemic symptoms, and are distinguished from Hodgkin lymphoma by the absence of Reed-Sternberg cells.

acute leukemias.definition: Rapidly progressive cancers of the bone marrow and blood characterized by uncontrolled proliferation of immature hematopoietic precursors (myeloid or lymphoid), leading to impaired production of normal blood cells and presenting with fatigue, infections, bleeding, and other cytopenia-related symptoms; urgent systemic chemotherapy is the mainstay of treatment, with possibilities including targeted therapy or stem cell transplantation in some cases.

hallucinations.definition: A false sensory perception in the absence of external stimuli, in which a person experiences sensations (often auditory or visual) that are not actually present.

cns effects.definition: Effects on the brain and spinal cord (the central nervous system). They manifest as changes in consciousness, mood, cognition, sensation, or motor function and may include sedation, dizziness, headache, ataxia, confusion, seizures, or coma; caused by drugs, toxins, or neurologic disease.

fludara.definition: A purine analog antineoplastic agent used to treat certain hematologic cancers (e.g., chronic lymphocytic leukemia and some non-Hodgkin lymphomas); administered as a phosphate prodrug and activated inside cells to inhibit DNA synthesis and induce apoptosis in malignant lymphocytes.

2-deoxy-d-glucose.definition: A glucose analog in which the 2-hydroxyl group is missing; it is taken up by cells and phosphorylated to 2-deoxy-D-glucose-6-phosphate but cannot be further metabolized via glycolysis, thereby inhibiting glycolytic processes. Used in metabolic research and as a radiotracer analogue in imaging studies.

fluorodeoxyglucose.definition: A radiolabeled glucose analog used in positron emission tomography (FDG, 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-D-glucose); it is taken up by glucose transporters and phosphorylated to FDG-6-phosphate, which is trapped in cells, enabling imaging of metabolically active tissues such as cancers.

brain disorders.definition: A broad category of conditions that affect the brain's structure or function, due to injury, disease, or dysfunction, resulting in impairments of cognition, movement, sensation, behavior, or other brain-related functions.

primary syphilis.definition: The initial, infectious stage of syphilis caused by Treponema pallidum, typically presenting with a painless, indurated ulcer (chancre) at the site of inoculation, often accompanied by regional lymphadenopathy; without treatment, it may progress to secondary syphilis.

late syphilis.definition: The late stage of untreated syphilis (tertiary syphilis) developing years after infection, characterized by granulomatous gumma formation, cardiovascular involvement (eg, aortitis and aneurysm), and neurosyphilis (eg, tabes dorsalis, general paresis).

fluorescent antibody test.definition: A laboratory technique that uses fluorescently labeled antibodies to detect specific antigens in a specimen, observed under a fluorescence microscope; can be direct (labeled antibody binds the antigen) or indirect (unlabeled primary antibody binds the antigen, followed by a labeled secondary antibody).

fta-abs test.definition: Serologic test for syphilis that detects antibodies to Treponema pallidum using indirect immunofluorescence; serves as a confirmatory treponemal test after a reactive non-treponemal test (e.g., RPR/VDRL) and tends to remain positive for life even after treatment.

treponemal antibody absorption test.definition: A laboratory serologic test used to confirm syphilis by absorbing non-treponemal antibodies from the patient’s serum and detecting antibodies directed against Treponema pallidum, typically by a fluorescent antibody method; historically used to verify treponemal infection but largely replaced by more modern treponemal tests.

fluorescent in situ hybridization.definition: A molecular cytogenetic technique that uses fluorescently labeled DNA probes to detect and localize specific DNA sequences on chromosomes in fixed cells or tissue, enabling visualization of genetic abnormalities such as translocations, deletions, duplications, and gene amplifications.

fish.definition: An aquatic vertebrate that breathes through gills, has fins, and usually a scale-covered body; major groups include bony fish and cartilaginous fish.

chromosome painting.definition: A cytogenetic technique that uses chromosome-specific fluorescent DNA probes to label (paint) entire chromosomes or chromosome regions on metaphase chromosomes or interphase nuclei, enabling multicolor visualization to detect chromosomal rearrangements, translocations, and numerical abnormalities.

fluorescent microscopy.definition: An optical imaging method that uses fluorescent labels to visualize and localize specific components of a specimen: fluorophores are excited by light at specific wavelengths and emit light at longer wavelengths, which is detected through filters to form an image.

ultraviolet microscopy.definition: A microscopy technique that uses ultraviolet light to illuminate a specimen, typically to excite fluorescence from fluorophores or to visualize autofluorescent components, producing high-contrast images.

pancreolauryl test.definition: A historical test of pancreatic exocrine function in which ingestion of pancreolauryl is followed by measurement of a urinary metabolite; reduced urinary excretion indicates pancreatic insufficiency. It is largely obsolete today.

pancreatic function.definition: The pancreas has both exocrine and endocrine functions: exocrine secretion of digestive enzymes (amylase, lipase, proteases) and bicarbonate into the duodenum to aid digestion, and endocrine secretion of hormones (primarily insulin and glucagon, plus somatostatin and pancreatic polypeptide) into the bloodstream to regulate blood glucose and metabolism.

pancreolauryl.definition: A historical diagnostic test for pancreatic exocrine function; after ingestion of a pancreolauryl substrate, pancreatic enzymes hydrolyze it and the resulting metabolite is excreted in urine, allowing assessment of pancreatic secretory capacity (often via fluorometric or colorimetric measurement).

fluorescein.definition: A water-soluble fluorescent dye (sodium fluorescein) used diagnostically to visualize ocular structures and perfusion; when excited by blue light, it emits bright yellow-green fluorescence, enabling staining of the cornea/tear film and visualization of retinal vasculature during fluorescein angiography. It is typically administered topically for ocular staining or intravenously for angiography and is excreted by the kidneys.

fluorescein dilaurate.definition: A diester of fluorescein in which two lauric acid (laurate) groups are attached, forming a lipophilic substrate used to assay lipase or esterase activity; it becomes fluorescent fluorescein upon enzymatic hydrolysis.

fluoridation.definition: An public health measure in which fluoride is added to drinking water at an optimal level to reduce the incidence of dental caries (tooth decay).

fluoride poisoning.definition: Toxicity from excessive fluoride intake, which can be acute or chronic. Acute exposure causes gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea) and sometimes neurologic or cardiovascular effects; severe cases may lead to hypocalcemia, seizures, and death. Chronic exposure leads to dental fluorosis and skeletal fluorosis.

fluorosis.definition: Chronic fluoride toxicity from prolonged excessive fluoride intake, most often causing mottled enamel in teeth (dental fluorosis) and, at higher exposures, skeletal fluorosis with bone pain and stiffness.

sodium fluoroacetate.definition: A highly toxic metabolic poison; the sodium salt of fluoroacetic acid. It is metabolized to fluorocitrate, which inhibits aconitase in the citric acid (Krebs) cycle, halting cellular energy production and leading to rapid organ failure; used as a potent rodenticide and pesticide with significant risks to humans and non-target animals.

methyl fluoroacetate.definition: The methyl ester of fluoroacetic acid; a toxic organofluorinated acetate that inhibits aconitase in the citric acid cycle, leading to disruption of cellular energy production; historically used as a pesticide/toxin and in biochemical research.

hydrogen fluoride.definition: A colorless, highly corrosive gas or liquid that forms hydrofluoric acid when dissolved in water; exposure can cause severe tissue burns and systemic fluoride toxicity, affecting calcium metabolism and potentially causing life-threatening hypocalcemia and arrhythmias.

fluke.definition: A parasitic flatworm (a trematode) that infects humans; a leaf-shaped endoparasite typically residing in the liver, biliary tract, intestines, or lungs and transmitted via snail hosts.

bacterial infections.definition: An infection caused by pathogenic bacteria that invade and multiply within body tissues, provoking an inflammatory response; it can be localized (e.g., skin, lungs, urinary tract) or systemic (bacteremia or sepsis) and is typically treated with antibiotics tailored to the organism and site of infection.

fluocinonide.definition: Potent topical corticosteroid used to treat inflammatory and pruritic skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis, and psoriasis; applied to the skin as a cream, ointment, or solution.

coanda effect.definition: A fluid-dynamics phenomenon in which a jet of fluid tends to attach to and follow a nearby surface, rather than continuing in a straight path, due to viscosity and entrainment of the surrounding fluid.

clinitron bed.definition: A specialized hospital bed that uses a fluidized bed of small, inert beads (usually glass or aluminosilicate) that are aerated to behave like a liquid, distributing body weight evenly to reduce pressure and shear on tissues; used to prevent and treat pressure ulcers and to aid wound healing in burn or other injuries.

fluidized bed.definition: A bed of solid particles that is energized by an upward flow of gas (or liquid) through the bed, causing the particles to behave like a fluid and to flow around objects; used for uniform mixing or heat transfer, and in medicine refers to an air-fluidized bed that suspends beads with air to evenly redistribute pressure and aid wound healing.

fluorination.definition: The chemical process of introducing fluorine atoms into a molecule, typically by replacing a hydrogen atom with fluorine, used to synthesize organofluorine compounds and to alter a compound’s metabolic stability, lipophilicity, and reactivity.

fluoride application.definition: Topical administration of fluoride to the teeth to strengthen enamel, promote remineralization, and reduce caries risk; commonly delivered as varnish, gel, or foam by a clinician.

fluoroacetic acid.definition: A highly toxic organofluorine carboxylic acid (F-CH2-COOH) that is metabolized to fluoroacetyl-CoA and then to fluorocitrate, which inhibits aconitase in the citric acid cycle and disrupts cellular energy production; the sodium salt (sodium fluoroacetate, 1080) is used as a pesticide.

flupenthixol hydrochloride.definition: A typical antipsychotic of the thioxanthene class used to treat schizophrenia and other psychoses; it acts as a dopamine D2 receptor antagonist in the central nervous system and is supplied as the hydrochloride salt for oral or injectable use.

sodium fluoride.definition: A water-soluble inorganic fluoride salt (NaF) used in dentistry to prevent dental caries by promoting enamel remineralization; used in topical fluoride products and water fluoridation, with toxicity at high doses.

tooth enamel.definition: The hard covering on the outside of each tooth.

osteosclerosis.definition: An abnormal increase in bone density (hardening of bone tissue) detectable radiographically; can be focal or generalized and may accompany various conditions such as osteopetrosis, fluorosis, chronic osteomyelitis, or healing fractures, and may be asymptomatic.

acute fluoride poisoning.definition: A rapidly developing toxicity from exposure to an excessive amount of fluoride (most often via ingestion) that causes gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain), hypocalcemia with neuromuscular irritability, metabolic disturbances, and potentially cardiovascular and central nervous system dysfunction; treated with supportive care and calcium administration (e.g., calcium gluconate) to bind fluoride.

fluorochrome stain.definition: A staining technique that uses fluorescent dyes (fluorochromes) to label cellular components, emitting visible light when excited by specific wavelengths, enabling visualization under fluorescence microscopy and often used to detect specific antigens, nucleic acids, or microorganisms.

acid-fast bacilli.definition: They are slender, rod-shaped bacteria with lipid-rich cell walls containing mycolic acids that resist decolorization by acid alcohol and retain the red dye on acid-fast staining (eg, Ziehl-Neelsen), most notably Mycobacterium species such as M. tuberculosis.

acridine orange stain.definition: A fluorescent stain that binds nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) and emits green fluorescence when bound to DNA and orange/red fluorescence when bound to RNA, used in fluorescence microscopy to visualize cellular/nucleic material and to help assess viability or integrity of cells and bacteria.

auramine o.definition: A fluorescent fluorochrome used in acid-fast staining to detect acid-fast bacilli; it binds to mycolic acids in the cell walls of mycobacteria and, when excited by blue light, emits bright yellow to yellow-green fluorescence for rapid visualization under a fluorescence microscope.

fluorodopa.definition: A radiolabeled analogue of L-dopa used in positron emission tomography (FDOPA) to measure presynaptic dopaminergic function; it is taken up by dopaminergic neurons and decarboxylated to fluorodopamine, enabling visualization of dopamine terminal integrity, especially in Parkinson disease.

fluoroplex.definition: A proprietary name for a fluoroscopy-based imaging system or contrast agent kit used to visualize internal structures in real time during radiographic procedures.

fluoroquinolone.definition: A class of broad-spectrum antibiotics that inhibit bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, enzymes required for DNA replication and transcription, thereby stopping bacterial growth. Used to treat a variety of infections; examples include ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin.

nalidixic acid.definition: A synthetic quinolone antibiotic, the first in its class, historically used to treat urinary tract infections caused by Gram-negative bacteria; it inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II), blocking DNA replication. Its use has declined due to limited spectrum and the availability of newer fluoroquinolones.

fluoroscope.definition: A medical imaging device that uses X-rays to produce real-time, moving images of the interior of the body, allowing dynamic visualization during diagnostic or interventional procedures.

fluorometric.definition: Relating to fluorometry; the measurement of fluorescence emitted by a sample to quantify or analyze substances, usually using a fluorometer.

fluorothane.definition: An inhaled volatile general anesthetic, a halogenated hydrocarbon formerly widely used for induction and maintenance of anesthesia; it has a relatively slow onset and recovery compared with modern agents and can cause rare but serious hepatotoxicity (halothane hepatitis) and cardiac sensitization to catecholamines, with widespread use largely replaced by newer agents.

halothane.definition: A volatile inhalational general anesthetic agent (a halogenated hydrocarbon) formerly widely used to induce and maintain general anesthesia; it can cause hepatotoxicity and cardiac sensitization to catecholamines, and is largely replaced by newer agents.

fluoxetine hydrochloride.definition: A selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant in the hydrochloride salt form, used to treat major depressive disorder and various anxiety-related disorders by increasing serotonin levels in the brain.

serotonin reuptake inhibitor.definition: A substance that inhibits the reuptake of serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine) into presynaptic neurons, increasing serotonin availability in the synaptic cleft and enhancing serotonergic neurotransmission.

androgenic and anabolic steroid.definition: Synthetic derivatives of testosterone that have both anabolic (tissue-building, especially muscle) and androgenic (masculinizing) effects; they are used medically for hormone deficiencies and certain wasting conditions but are often misused to enhance athletic performance, with potential adverse effects including liver toxicity, cardiovascular risks, hormonal imbalance, and behavioral changes.

priapism.definition: An erection that lasts longer than three hours. Emergency medical treatment is required to prevent permanent damage to the penis.

menstrual irregularities.definition: A broad term for deviations from normal menstrual patterns, including irregular cycle length (cycles shorter than 21 days or longer than 35 days), irregular timing, and abnormal bleeding volume or duration.

fluphenazine hydrochloride.definition: A potent phenothiazine antipsychotic medication that antagonizes dopamine D2 receptors in the CNS to treat schizophrenia and other psychoses; available as the hydrochloride salt in oral and long-acting injectable forms; commonly associated with extrapyramidal symptoms and other dopamine-blockade–related adverse effects.

flupenthixol decanoate.definition: A long-acting injectable antipsychotic (depot) formulation of flupenthixol, a dopamine D2 receptor antagonist used for maintenance treatment in schizophrenia to prevent relapse; administered by intramuscular injection at regular intervals (commonly every 2–4 weeks).

flupenthixol.definition: A typical thioxanthene antipsychotic that blocks dopamine D2 receptors; used to treat schizophrenia and other psychoses; available as oral and long-acting injectable formulations; associated with extrapyramidal symptoms and other dopamine-blockade adverse effects.

flurandrenolide.definition: A potent synthetic corticosteroid for topical use that treats inflammatory and pruritic skin conditions (e.g., dermatitis, eczema) by reducing inflammation and immune response; typically formulated as ointment or cream, with possible adverse effects including skin thinning, stretch marks, irritation, and, with prolonged use or large areas, potential systemic effects.

flurazepam hydrochloride.definition: A long-acting benzodiazepine hypnotic (the hydrochloride salt form) used for short-term treatment of insomnia. It enhances GABA-A receptor–mediated inhibition, promoting sleep initiation and maintenance. Because of active metabolites with a prolonged half-life, it can cause daytime sedation and carries risks of tolerance, dependence, and withdrawal; use with caution in the elderly or hepatic impairment and avoid in pregnancy or in conditions like sleep apnea or myasthenia gravis.

flurbiprofen.definition: A nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) of the propionic acid class used to relieve pain and inflammation by inhibiting cyclooxygenase and decreasing prostaglandin synthesis; available in oral and topical formulations.

flurbiprofen sodium.definition: A salt form of flurbiprofen, a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes to reduce prostaglandin synthesis, providing analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antipyretic effects; the sodium salt enhances water solubility for certain formulations.

ophthalmic surgery.definition: Ophthalmic surgery is a surgical procedure performed on the eye or its adnexa to diagnose, repair, or treat diseases, injuries, or disorders of the eye, including operations on the cornea, lens, retina, vitreous, optic nerve, orbit, and eyelids.

flutamide.definition: A nonsteroidal antiandrogen that competitively antagonizes the androgen receptor to block androgen signaling and slow the growth of androgen-dependent prostate cancer; often given with a GnRH analogue. Common adverse effects include hepatotoxicity, gynecomastia, hot flashes, and nausea.

leuprolide.definition: A synthetic gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonist that, with continuous exposure, suppresses pituitary LH and FSH secretion, thereby decreasing sex hormone (testosterone and estrogen) production; used to treat hormone-responsive conditions such as advanced prostate cancer, endometriosis, uterine fibroids, and central precocious puberty.

metastatic prostate cancer.definition: Metastatic prostate cancer is prostate cancer that has spread beyond the prostate to distant sites (most commonly bone and distant lymph nodes). It is designated M1 disease and is typically treated with systemic therapy rather than local treatment alone.

loss of sex drive.definition: A decreased or absent interest in sexual activity, thoughts, or fantasies, lasting for a significant period and causing distress or impairment; can be due to hormonal changes, medical conditions, medications, psychological factors, or relationship issues, and when persistent and distressing may be diagnosed as hypoactive sexual desire disorder.

stomach upset.definition: A non-specific symptom of the upper gastrointestinal tract characterized by mild to moderate abdominal discomfort, nausea, bloating, or indigestion; usually transient and self-limited but may reflect gastritis, gastroenteritis, dyspepsia, or other GI conditions.

fluticasone.definition: A synthetic corticosteroid (glucocorticoid) with potent anti-inflammatory effects used to treat asthma, allergic rhinitis, and various inflammatory skin conditions; available in inhaled, intranasal, and topical formulations.

nasal polyps.definition: Noncancerous, edematous mucosal outgrowths in the nasal cavity or paranasal sinuses, typically arising from chronic rhinosinusitis; they cause nasal obstruction, discharge, and loss of smell, and are managed with intranasal corticosteroids and sometimes endoscopic sinus surgery.

intranasal.definition: Relating to the nasal passages; administered through the nose (for example, by spray or drops) for local or systemic effect.

intrauterine fetal transfusion.definition: An in utero procedure in which donor blood is transfused directly into the fetal circulation (typically via the umbilical vein under ultrasound guidance) to treat fetal anemia, most commonly due to maternal alloimmunization.

flutter-fibrillation.definition: An atrial tachyarrhythmia in which atrial activity shows both organized flutter waves (sawtooth pattern) and irregular fibrillatory activity, often reflecting intermittent degeneration of atrial flutter into atrial fibrillation and typically producing an irregular, rapid ventricular response.

fluvastatin.definition: A statin medication (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor) used to lower LDL cholesterol and reduce cardiovascular risk by inhibiting hepatic cholesterol synthesis and increasing LDL receptor activity.

primary hypercholesterolemia.definition: An inherited disorder of lipid metabolism characterized by elevated low‑density lipoprotein cholesterol due to defects in LDL receptor–mediated clearance (or related genes), present from birth and increasing the risk of premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease; excludes elevations due to secondary causes.

coronary atherosclerosis.definition: A form of atherosclerosis in which lipid-rich plaques build up within the coronary arteries, causing narrowing (stenosis) of the vessels and reduced blood flow to the myocardium, which can lead to angina, myocardial infarction, or sudden cardiac death.

lens opacities.definition: Opacity of the crystalline lens of the eye, reducing its clarity and causing decreased vision; commonly referred to as a cataract; may be age-related, congenital, or due to trauma, systemic disease (e.g., diabetes), smoking, or ultraviolet exposure.

fluvoxamine.definition: A selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant that inhibits serotonin reuptake in the central nervous system, increasing serotonin availability; primarily used to treat obsessive-compulsive disorder and social anxiety disorder.

suicide attempts.definition: A suicide attempt is a nonfatal self-directed act with explicit or implicit intent to die.

mania.definition: A psychiatric syndrome characterized by persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood with abnormally increased energy or activity, lasting at least one week (or any duration if hospitalization is required) and accompanied by features such as grandiosity, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, racing thoughts, distractibility, and increased goal-directed or risky activity; a core mood state in bipolar disorder.

formylmethionine.definition: N-formylmethionine (fMet) is a formylated derivative of the amino acid methionine that serves as the initiating amino acid for protein synthesis in bacteria and in the organelles of eukaryotic cells; the formyl group is typically removed from the initiating residue during maturation.

frankfurt-mandibular incisor angle.definition: An orthodontic cephalometric measurement defined as the angle between the Frankfort horizontal plane and the long axis of the mandibular incisor, used to quantify mandibular incisor inclination relative to the cranial base.

foreign medical graduate.definition: A physician who completed medical school outside the country where they intend to practice, often needing credential verification and additional training or licensure examinations to obtain a license.

fluorometholone.definition: A synthetic fluorinated topical corticosteroid used as ophthalmic drops to treat ocular inflammation and allergic conjunctivitis; it suppresses inflammatory mediators and leukocyte activity, with potential adverse effects including increased intraocular pressure, cataract formation, and risk of ocular infection.

fragile x syndrome.definition: An inherited developmental disability that can make it harder to learn; it can cause social or emotional issues, such as anger, or problems with talking.

focal dermal hypoplasia.definition: A rare X-linked dominant genetic disorder (Goltz syndrome) caused by PORCN mutations, characterized by focal dermal hypoplasia (thin, atrophic dermis with herniation of subcutaneous fat) and a spectrum of ectodermal–mesodermal anomalies, including limb malformations, skeletal defects, dental and ocular abnormalities, and patchy, linear skin lesions.

goltz syndrome.definition: A rare X-linked dominant disorder caused by PORCN gene mutations, characterized by focal dermal hypoplasia with patchy skin thinning and fat herniation, often along Blaschko lines, and associated with limb malformations as well as ocular and dental anomalies.

focal emphysema.definition: A localized area of emphysema in which alveolar walls are destroyed and airspaces are enlarged in a discrete region of the lung, rather than diffusely affecting the entire lung.

focal glomerular sclerosis.definition: A pattern of glomerular injury where scarring (sclerosis) affects only some glomeruli (focal) and only portions of those glomeruli (segmental), typically presenting with proteinuria and possible nephrotic syndrome; may be idiopathic or secondary to various diseases (e.g., HIV, obesity, heroin use, genetic factors).

focal glomerulosclerosis.definition: A histologic pattern of kidney disease in which scarring (sclerosis) affects some glomeruli (focal) and only parts of those glomeruli (segmental), often presenting with proteinuria and potentially progressing to progressive renal dysfunction.

heroin-abuse nephropathy.definition: A kidney disease seen in chronic heroin users characterized by nephrotic-range proteinuria and progressive renal insufficiency, most commonly associated with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis on renal biopsy.

focal seizures.definition: Seizures that originate in a localized area of one cerebral hemisphere (focal onset) and may remain confined or evolve to generalized seizure; symptoms depend on the involved region and can be motor, sensory, autonomic, or cognitive, with consciousness preserved in simple focal seizures and impaired in complex focal seizures.

focal motor seizures.definition: A seizure that originates in a localized region of one cerebral hemisphere and presents primarily with motor symptoms—such as unilateral jerking, stiffening, or repetitive movements of a limb or face; consciousness is usually preserved in simple focal motor seizures, though the seizure may spread to involve other regions and potentially become generalized.

fogarty catheter.definition: A balloon-tipped vascular catheter used for embolectomy/thrombectomy; the deflated balloon is advanced beyond a thrombus, inflated, and then withdrawn to drag the clot out of the vessel.

follicular adenocarcinoma.definition: Malignant gland-forming epithelial tumor with follicular (follicle-like) differentiation; arises from follicular cells of a gland and shows invasive growth with potential for metastasis. Note: this term is not commonly used; site-specific entities (e.g., follicular thyroid carcinoma) are usually preferred.

follicular thyroid carcinoma.definition: A malignant thyroid tumor from follicular epithelial cells that invades the capsule and/or blood vessels, with a propensity for hematogenous metastasis; typically treated with surgical removal and often radioactive iodine.

papillary adenocarcinoma.definition: A malignant gland-forming tumor in which tumor cells grow in delicate papillary (finger-like) fronds with fibrovascular cores; a histologic pattern of adenocarcinoma seen in several organs, with behavior dependent on the primary site.

follicular antrum.definition: A fluid-filled cavity that develops within a secondary (antral) ovarian follicle; formed by granulosa cell secretions, it contains follicular fluid and the oocyte with its cumulus oophorus, enlarging as the follicle matures toward the Graafian stage.

follicular cyst.definition: An ovarian functional cyst that forms when a developing follicle fails to rupture and release an ovum, continuing to grow and fill with clear fluid. It is typically benign, measures about 3–8 cm, and often resolves spontaneously within 1–3 menstrual cycles; it may cause mild pelvic pain or pressure if large or ruptured.

follicular phase.definition: The first phase of the menstrual cycle, from the start of menstruation to ovulation, during which ovarian follicles mature under FSH influence, estrogen rises, and the endometrium proliferates; ovulation occurs at the end of this phase due to the LH surge.

follicle-stimulating hormone.definition: An anterior-pituitary gonadotropin that stimulates growth and maturation of ovarian follicles and estrogen production in females, and promotes spermatogenesis in males.

fsh.definition: A gonadotropin secreted by the anterior pituitary that stimulates ovarian follicle development and estrogen production in females and promotes spermatogenesis in males; regulated by GnRH.

fsh-releasing hormone.definition: A hypothalamic decapeptide that stimulates the anterior pituitary to secrete follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH); released in a pulsatile manner to regulate the reproductive axis.

fsh-rf.definition: A G-protein-coupled receptor for follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) expressed mainly on ovarian granulosa cells and testicular Sertoli cells; binding FSH activates cAMP signaling to promote follicular growth and estrogen production in females and spermatogenesis in males.

luteinizing hormone.definition: A hormone that controls ovulation in women. In men, luteinizing hormone triggers production of testosterone.

follicle fluid.definition: Fluid within an ovarian follicle (the antral follicle), produced by granulosa and theca cells; provides the microenvironment for the maturing oocyte and is rich in hormones (notably estradiol), proteins, electrolytes, and growth factors; released during ovulation.

leucovorin.definition: A form of reduced folate (folinic acid, 5-formyltetrahydrofolate) used to rescue normal cells from methotrexate toxicity by supplying downstream tetrahydrofolate derivatives, and as a chemotherapy modulator to enhance 5-fluorouracil efficacy.

pteroylglutamic acid.definition: A water-soluble B vitamin (folate) consisting of pteroic acid linked to glutamate; the synthetic form of folate (folic acid) used in supplements and fortification, serving as a cofactor in one-carbon transfer reactions essential for DNA synthesis and amino acid metabolism.

folate deficiency anemia.definition: Anemia due to insufficient folate (vitamin B9) causing impaired DNA synthesis and resulting in megaloblastic, macrocytic red blood cells; commonly due to poor intake, malabsorption, increased demand (e.g., pregnancy), or certain medications; treated with folic acid supplementation and correction of the underlying cause.

folacin.definition: A water-soluble B vitamin (vitamin B9) found as dietary folates and synthetic folic acid in supplements; essential for DNA synthesis and repair, one-carbon metabolism, and fetal neural tube development.

folate test.definition: Measurement of folate (vitamin B9) level in the blood to assess folate status, typically as serum folate or red blood cell folate; used to diagnose deficiency, investigate megaloblastic anemia, and monitor supplementation.

folic acid test.definition: A blood test that measures the level of folate (folic acid) in the blood to assess folate status and diagnose deficiency; tests may include serum (plasma) folate and sometimes red blood cell folate to distinguish recent from long-term deficiency.

foetus.definition: A developing human organism from the end of the embryonic period (approximately 8 weeks after fertilization) until birth; during this fetal period, the major organs and tissues mature and grow.

gonadorelin acetate.definition: A synthetic gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) decapeptide in acetate salt form that stimulates the anterior pituitary to release luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH); used mainly as a diagnostic agent to assess hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal function and, when given pulsatile, to induce gonadotropin release in research or therapy.

gonadorelin.definition: A synthetic decapeptide identical to endogenous gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) that stimulates the anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH; used in diagnostic GnRH stimulation tests and, when given pulsatile, to induce ovulation in fertility treatment.

gonadotropin-releasing hormone.definition: A hypothalamic decapeptide releasing hormone that stimulates the anterior pituitary to secrete the gonadotropins luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH); released in a pulsatile manner to regulate puberty and reproduction, and used clinically in synthetic forms to induce ovulation or treat infertility.

glomeruli.definition: A tuft of capillaries within the renal corpuscle of a nephron where blood is filtered to form the filtrate that becomes urine, through the filtration barrier composed of fenestrated endothelium, glomerular basement membrane, and podocyte slit diaphragms.

follicle recruitment.definition: Process by which a cohort of small ovarian follicles is activated and begins to grow, entering the developing pool in response to rising FSH during the early follicular phase; from this cohort, a dominant follicle is selected while the others typically undergo atresia.

dust emphysema.definition: A form of emphysema caused by chronic inhalation of inorganic dusts (such as coal dust or silica) leading to destruction of alveolar walls and enlargement of air spaces, often seen in pneumoconiosis.

terminal bronchioles.definition: The smallest airways of the conducting portion of the respiratory tract, located distal to the bronchi and proximal to the respiratory bronchioles; they lack cartilage and mucous glands, are lined by simple cuboidal epithelium with club (Clara) cells, and conduct air to the gas-exchange zones, with no gas exchange occurring there.

focal lesion.definition: A localized abnormality in tissue, confined to a specific area within an organ or structure, as opposed to diffuse involvement of the entire organ.

focal plane.definition: The plane within a specimen along the depth (z) axis that is in best focus for an optical imaging system; it is the plane at which light converges to form a sharp image, while structures above or below this plane are progressively out of focus.

focal zone.definition: A region at a specific depth in ultrasound imaging where the transducer focuses the beam to produce the narrowest beam and thus the best lateral resolution; focal zones can be adjusted to optimize image quality at different depths.

focal symptom.definition: A symptom that arises from a localized area of the body, indicating focal (localized) pathology rather than a diffuse process.

folie à deux.definition: A rare psychiatric syndrome in which a delusion held by one person is transmitted to and adopted by another person in close association, resulting in two or more individuals sharing the same delusional belief; often referred to as a shared psychotic disorder. Treatment typically involves separating the individuals and addressing the underlying psychosis.

folie circulaire.definition: A historical term for a cyclic mood disorder in which episodes of mania and depression recur in a circular, repeating pattern, with intervals of relative remission; today often understood as a form of bipolar affective disorder.

folie du doute.definition: A historical term for a fixed, false belief characterized by persistent, pathological doubt about the accuracy of one’s memories, beliefs, or actions, despite contrary evidence. It is not a distinct DSM-5/ICD-11 diagnosis; in modern psychiatry its features may appear in obsessive–compulsive spectrum phenomena or as a type of delusional disorder depending on context and conviction.

folie gemellaire.definition: Un trouble délirant partagé entre deux personnes (souvent des proches), dans lequel le délire d’une personne est transmis et adopté par l’autre; il survient généralement au sein d’un lien étroit et peut disparaître après séparation et traitement du délire primaire.

folie musculaire.definition: Not a standard medical term; no formal definition in current medical dictionaries. When used historically, it has referred to a delusional or hypochondriacal preoccupation with muscles or muscular disease, rather than a recognized psychiatric disorder.

folie raisonnante.definition: A historical term for a psychotic state in which the patient holds fixed, well-organized delusions that are defended with logical argumentation, while otherwise appearing rational and functioning relatively normally. In other words, the delusions are internally coherent and can be rationalized, giving the appearance of reasoned belief rather than disordered thinking; today this concept is usually described under delusional disorder or a paranoid-type psychosis, rather than as a distinct, current diagnostic category.

follicular stigma.definition: A small thinned area on the surface of a mature ovarian (Graafian) follicle that becomes the rupture point during ovulation, through which the oocyte is released (typically with surrounding cumulus oophorus).

food allergy.definition: When your body responds to food in a way that is not normal. These reactions include swelling or itching in your mouth, throwing up, an itchy rash on your skin, or trouble breathing.

inhibin b.definition: A gonadal peptide hormone produced by Sertoli cells in males and granulosa cells in females; a dimer of alpha and beta-B subunits that inhibits FSH secretion via negative feedback and reflects gonadal function.

ovulatory phase.definition: Midcycle phase during which a mature ovum is released from the dominant ovarian follicle; triggered by a surge in luteinizing hormone (LH); lasts about 24 hours and corresponds to peak fertility.

vesicular ovarian follicle.definition: A mature ovarian follicle containing a fluid-filled cavity (the antrum), formed during the antral (vesicular) stage of folliculogenesis; it surrounds the oocyte with cumulus cells and secretes estrogen, preceding ovulation.

macula folliculi.definition: A flat, non-palpable skin discoloration located at a hair follicle.

follicular tonsillitis.definition: An acute infection of the palatine tonsils characterized by inflammation of the tonsillar follicles with yellowish-white exudates visible on the tonsils, often accompanied by fever and sore throat; most commonly caused by group A Streptococcus.

follicular vulvitis.definition: Inflammation of hair follicles on the vulvar skin, typically presenting as pruritic or tender papules or pustules centered on follicles and often related to irritation or infection (e.g., bacterial), such as shaving, friction, or occlusion.

keloidalis.definition: An inflammatory skin condition causing keloid‑like papules or plaques on the back of the neck (keloidalis nuchae), often from folliculitis and leading to raised scarring; more common in individuals of African descent.

folliculogenesis.definition: The maturation of ovarian follicles from dormant primordial follicles to a mature preovulatory follicle, including recruitment, growth, selection, and atresia, regulated by intraovarian factors and gonadotropins (primarily FSH and LH).

folliculoma.definition: A benign tumor of hair-follicle origin characterized by proliferation of follicular epithelium, typically presenting as a small, skin-colored papule or nodule.

granulosa cell tumor.definition: A rare ovarian neoplasm of sex cord-stromal origin arising from granulosa cells, typically estrogen-secreting; it may cause abnormal uterine bleeding in adults or precocious puberty in children, is usually unilateral and slow-growing, and is treated with surgical resection, with potential for late recurrences.

folliculosis.definition: A general, non-specific term for a disease or abnormal condition of the hair follicles, often used to describe follicle-related inflammatory or infectious processes rather than a single diagnosis.

conjunctival folliculosis.definition: A conjunctival inflammatory condition characterized by the presence of round, pale lymphoid follicles on the conjunctiva, reflecting a follicular response to chronic irritation or infection (commonly seen in viral or allergic conjunctivitis).

follitropin.definition: A recombinant human follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) used to stimulate growth of ovarian follicles during fertility treatments such as in vitro fertilization.

follitropin alfa.definition: Recombinant human follicle-stimulating hormone used to stimulate ovarian follicular development in infertility treatment (e.g., controlled ovarian hyperstimulation for IVF) and to induce spermatogenesis in men; administered by subcutaneous injection, it acts on ovarian granulosa cells to promote follicle growth and estradiol production.

follitropin beta.definition: A recombinant human follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) used to stimulate ovarian follicle growth in infertility treatments (e.g., IVF/ICSI); it acts on ovarian FSH receptors to promote follicular development and estrogen production and is given by subcutaneous injection.

ovulation stimulant.definition: An agent that promotes or triggers ovulation in the ovary, used to treat infertility due to anovulation; examples include clomiphene citrate, letrozole, and injectable gonadotropins.

intracranial lesion.definition: An abnormal area of tissue within the skull caused by disease or injury; in the brain it includes tumors, hemorrhages, infarcts, abscesses, infections, inflammatory or demyelinating processes, edema, or other focal pathologies detectable by imaging or examination.

ovarian cyst.definition: A fluid-filled sac that forms on or within an ovary; most are benign and functional (such as follicular or corpus luteum cysts) and resolve spontaneously, but some persist or be neoplastic and may cause pelvic pain, bloating, or complications, and cysts in postmenopausal women warrant evaluation to exclude cancer.

polycystic ovarian disease.definition: A common endocrine disorder of women of reproductive age defined by oligo- or anovulation, hyperandrogenism, and polycystic-appearing ovaries on ultrasound; frequently associated with insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome, with symptoms such as infertility, irregular menses, hirsutism, and acne.

increased appetite.definition: An abnormally strong desire to eat, resulting in increased food intake; can be a symptom of hormonal or metabolic disorders, certain medications, or psychological factors.

multiple ovulation.definition: Release of more than one oocyte from the ovaries during a single ovulatory cycle, usually due to the maturation and ovulation of multiple follicles; increases the likelihood of a multiple pregnancy (e.g., fraternal twins) and can occur spontaneously or be induced by fertility drugs.

breast pain.definition: Discomfort or aching in one or both breasts that may be cyclic (hormonal, often linked to the menstrual cycle) or noncyclic; most cases are benign.

fomentation.definition: The application of warm, moist heat to a body part using a poultice or warm compress to relieve pain, stiffness, or inflammation.

fomite.definition: A nonliving object or surface that can harbor infectious agents and facilitate their transmission to a susceptible person through direct or indirect contact.

fomivirsen.definition: An antisense phosphorothioate oligonucleotide that binds CMV mRNA to inhibit viral replication; administered by intravitreal injection for CMV retinitis.

sodium salt.definition: A salt in which the cation is sodium (Na+), produced when the hydrogen of an acid is replaced by sodium. In solution it dissociates into Na+ and the corresponding anion, and it can be inorganic or organic.

fondaparinux.definition: An injectable synthetic pentasaccharide anticoagulant that binds to antithrombin III to selectively inhibit factor Xa, thereby reducing thrombin formation; used for prophylaxis and treatment of venous thromboembolism, administered subcutaneously with fixed dosing and no routine coagulation monitoring; contraindicated in severe renal impairment.

deep-vein thrombosis.definition: A blood clot that forms in a vein deep in your body.

pulmonary emboli.definition: Blockage of a pulmonary artery or its branches by an embolus, most commonly a thrombus that has traveled from a deep vein, causing reduced blood flow to lung tissue and symptoms such as dyspnea and chest pain; can lead to hypoxia or hemodynamic instability in large emboli.

hip fracture surgery.definition: A surgical procedure to treat a fracture of the proximal femur (hip), aiming to stabilize or replace the broken bone to allow mobilization and healing. Techniques include internal fixation with screws/plates or cephalomedullary nails, and/or hip arthroplasty (hemiarthroplasty or total hip replacement) depending on fracture type and patient factors.

fones’ method.definition: A dental hygiene technique taught to children in which the toothbrush is placed against the teeth and used in wide circular motions to clean all surfaces; also called the circular brushing method, developed by Dr. Charles C. Fones.

toothbrushing technique.definition: A method for cleaning teeth with a toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste, involving systematic brushing of all tooth surfaces (outer, inner, chewing) with a soft-bristled brush, typically at about a 45-degree angle to the gumline using gentle short strokes or circular motions, for about two minutes, twice daily to remove plaque and reduce caries risk.

palatal surfaces.definition: The inner surfaces of the maxillary teeth that face the hard palate.

lingual surfaces.definition: The surface of a tooth that faces the tongue; in the upper jaw this surface is commonly called the palatal surface, and in the lower jaw it is called the lingual surface. It is opposite the buccal (cheek/lip) surface.

fonticulus.definition: A small opening or hollow in a bone or tissue; in human anatomy, fonticulus (fontanelle) refers to a soft, membranous gap between unfused skull bones in a newborn, permitting brain growth and skull expansion during infancy.

food additive.definition: A substance added intentionally to food during processing, packaging, or storage to perform a technological function—such as preservation, flavor enhancement, coloring, texture modification, emulsification, or shelf-life extension—intended to be present in the final product.

food challenge.definition: A supervised diagnostic procedure in which incremental amounts of a suspected food are ingested under medical observation to determine whether an adverse allergic reaction occurs, used to confirm or exclude a food allergy. It can be performed openly, or in single-blind or double-blind (placebo-controlled) formats.

food challenge test.definition: An oral diagnostic procedure in which a patient ingests gradually increasing amounts of a suspected food under medical supervision to observe for an allergic reaction, used to confirm or exclude a food allergy and determine tolerance; conducted in a controlled setting with readiness to treat reactions.

ciguatera poisoning.definition: A foodborne illness caused by ciguatoxins produced by marine dinoflagellates (Gambierdiscus) that accumulate in large tropical reef fish; ingestion typically causes rapid gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) followed by neurologic symptoms such as paresthesias, dysesthesias, vertigo, and reversal of hot and cold sensations, and sometimes cardiovascular effects. Symptoms usually resolve in days to weeks, though some may persist longer. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive, including hydration and symptom control. Prevention centers on avoiding large reef fish from affected regions.

minamata disease.definition: Neurological syndrome caused by methylmercury poisoning from environmental pollution (notably contaminated seafood from Minamata Bay, Japan). It presents with ataxia, numbness and tingling in the extremities, tremors, dysarthria, and vision or hearing impairment; in utero exposure can cause severe neurodevelopmental defects such as cerebral palsy–like symptoms, mental retardation, and seizures.

mushroom poisoning.definition: Poisoning from ingestion of toxic wild mushrooms (mycetism), usually due to amatoxins; symptoms range from vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain to severe hepatic failure and coagulopathy, and can be fatal; onset may be delayed after ingestion; management is supportive with decontamination and organ-supportive care, with selective use of antidotes in some cases.

salmonella gastroenteritis.definition: An acute gastroenteritis caused by Salmonella infection, usually from contaminated food or water, characterized by sudden diarrhea, abdominal cramps, fever, nausea, and vomiting; typically self-limited within several days; treatment is supportive (rehydration and electrolyte management); antibiotics are not routinely recommended except for severe disease or high‑risk individuals.

shellfish poisoning.definition: A group of illnesses caused by eating shellfish contaminated with toxins produced by marine algae; symptoms vary by toxin and can include gastrointestinal upset, numbness or tingling, dizziness, confusion or memory loss, and in severe cases respiratory failure.

ergot alkaloid.definition: A group of closely related alkaloids produced by the ergot fungus Claviceps purpurea; they have vasoconstrictive and uterotonic effects and are used clinically (e.g., ergotamine, ergonovine) to treat migraines and to induce or control labor, but can cause vasospasm and ischemia.

phalloidine.definition: A bicyclic peptide toxin produced by Amanita phalloides that binds specifically to filamentous actin (F-actin), stabilizing the filaments and preventing depolymerization; used in fluorescence microscopy to stain actin when conjugated to a fluorophore.

toadstool poisoning.definition: Poisoning from ingestion of toxic mushrooms (fungi), with effects ranging by species; amatoxin-containing mushrooms commonly cause delayed-onset vomiting and diarrhea followed by severe liver failure, while other species can cause kidney injury or neurotoxicity. Management is supportive and may include decontamination if early, with consideration of antidotal therapy (e.g., silibinin) or liver transplantation in severe cases.

hand-foot-and-mouth disease.definition: A common viral illness, usually caused by enteroviruses (notably Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus 71), characterized by fever, painful mouth ulcers, and a vesicular rash on the hands and feet; it primarily affects young children and is typically self-limited over about 7–10 days. Transmission occurs via fecal–oral and oral–contact routes, and good hygiene helps prevent spread.

vesicular stomatitis virus.definition: An enveloped, bullet-shaped, negative-sense RNA virus of the family Rhabdoviridae (genus Vesiculovirus) that causes vesicular stomatitis in livestock (notably cattle, horses, and pigs); human infections are rare and usually mild, transmitted by insect vectors or direct contact with infected tissues.

picornavirus.definition: A family of small, nonenveloped, icosahedral viruses with positive-sense single-stranded RNA; includes rhinoviruses, enteroviruses, hepatoviruses, and aphthoviruses, and causes diseases ranging from the common cold to hepatitis A and poliomyelitis.

footboard.definition: A rigid panel at the foot of a bed, typically a hospital bed, that supports the patient’s feet and legs, helps maintain proper alignment, and can help prevent foot drop or plantarflexion contractures; it may also prevent sliding down in bed.

foot candle.definition: A unit of illuminance equal to one lumen per square foot; it is approximately 10.764 lux.

foot care.definition: A set of practices to maintain foot health and function, including hygiene, skin and nail care, regular inspection for injuries or infections, and protection from trauma and excessive pressure.

foot drop.definition: A gait abnormality caused by weakness or paralysis of the ankle dorsiflexors, resulting in inability to lift the front of the foot and often a toe drag or high-stepping gait; commonly due to peroneal nerve injury, sciatic neuropathy, or various central or peripheral neurologic conditions.

footed.definition: Having feet; provided with a foot or footlike base, as in a structure or organism that terminates in a foot-like projection.

footling breech.definition: A breech presentation in which one or both feet are the presenting parts at delivery, instead of the buttocks.

foot-pound.definition: A unit of work (energy) in the foot–pound–second system: the work done when a force of one pound-force moves an object one foot in the direction of the force; equal to about 1.3558 joules. In some contexts, it is also used to denote torque (one pound-force applied at a lever arm one foot long).

footprinting.definition: A laboratory technique used to locate the precise DNA sequence bound by a protein by detecting protection from nuclease digestion (typically DNase I) at the binding site; the protected region shows a reduced cleavage pattern, mapping the protein–DNA interaction.

foramen caecum.definition: A small blind pit on the dorsal surface of the tongue at the apex of the sulcus terminalis, representing the embryologic origin point of the thyroglossal duct and the site where the thyroid gland descends from the tongue.

pacchionian foramen.definition: An opening in the inner table of the skull through which arachnoid granulations protrude into a dural venous sinus (usually the superior sagittal sinus) to drain cerebrospinal fluid.

foramen spinosum.definition: A small opening in the greater wing of the sphenoid bone that transmits the middle meningeal artery and vein and the meningeal branch of the mandibular nerve (nervus spinosus).

foramina transversarium.definition: An opening in the transverse process of a cervical vertebra through which the vertebral artery (and vein) and accompanying sympathetic nerves pass.

forbes-albright syndrome.definition: A rare form of peripheral (gonadotropin-independent) precocious puberty caused by autonomous estrogen production from ovarian lesions, such as estrogen-secreting cysts or granulosa cell tumors, in children.
