cori’s disease.definition: A glycogen storage disease (type III) caused by deficiency of the glycogen debranching enzyme (α-1,6-glucosidase), leading to impaired glycogenolysis with accumulation of limit dextrin–like structures in liver, heart, and skeletal muscle; presents with hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, hyperlipidemia, and growth retardation; management includes frequent carbohydrate intake and uncooked cornstarch.

prolactinemia.definition: Elevation of prolactin levels in the blood (serum prolactin above the reference range), which can be physiologic, pharmacologic, or due to pituitary or other disease; commonly associated with galactorrhea, menstrual disturbances or infertility, and reduced libido.

prolactin.definition: A peptide hormone produced by lactotroph cells of the anterior pituitary gland that stimulates milk production in the mammary glands; its secretion is primarily inhibited by hypothalamic dopamine and it rises during pregnancy.

intravitreal injection.definition: A procedure in which a medication is injected into the vitreous humor of the eye to treat retinal diseases by delivering high local drug concentrations; commonly used medications include anti-VEGF agents and corticosteroids.

fonsecaea.definition: A genus of dematiaceous (pigmented) fungi in the family Herpotrichiellaceae; several species, notably F. pedrosoi and F. nubica, are etiologic agents of chromoblastomycosis in humans.

fordyce's disease.definition: A benign, asymptomatic condition in which ectopic sebaceous glands form small, yellowish-white papules on mucosal surfaces (most commonly the lips, buccal mucosa, or genitalia); a common anatomical variant rather than a disease.

fordyce spots.definition: Small, yellowish-white, painless bumps on mucosal surfaces (most often the inner lips and genitalia) caused by ectopic sebaceous glands; a common, benign, incidental finding that requires no treatment unless for cosmetic reasons.

miliaria.definition: A skin condition that occurs in hot, humid weather and is caused by obstruction of the sweat glands; also known as prickly heat or heat rash.

forewaters.definition: A portion of amniotic fluid that lies in front of the presenting fetal part and is typically the first to be expelled when the membranes rupture; the remaining fluid behind the presenting part is called hindwater.

forearm.definition: The region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist, containing the radius and ulna bones and their associated muscles, nerves, and vessels; organized into anterior (flexor) and posterior (extensor) compartments, enabling wrist and hand movements and allowing pronation and supination of the forearm.

forehead.definition: The frontal region of the face located above the orbits (eyes), extending from the hairline to the supraorbital ridges; corresponds anatomically to the frontal bone.

forebrain.definition: An anterior portion of the brain that includes the cerebrum (cerebral cortex, basal ganglia, limbic system) and the diencephalon (thalamus and hypothalamus); it governs higher cognitive and sensory-motor functions and regulates autonomic and endocrine activity through hypothalamic control.

fetal head.definition: The head of the fetus, which is the presenting part during delivery; it comprises the skull and facial bones with unfused sutures and fontanelles that allow molding during labor.

occiput anterior.definition: A fetal presentation in which the back of the head (occiput) is directed toward the front (anterior) of the maternal pelvis during labor, with the head typically flexed to present the smallest head diameter; this is the most common and favorable position for vaginal delivery.

areolae.definition: Plural of areola; the pigmented circular area of skin surrounding the nipple on the breast, containing Montgomery glands that secrete lubricating oil to protect and lubricate the nipple during lactation.

lips.definition: The fleshy, movable borders of the mouth (upper and lower lips) that surround the oral opening; composed of skin externally, mucosa internally, and underlying orbicularis oris muscle; they aid in speech, feeding, sealing the oral cavity, and facial expression.

gums.definition: The mucosal tissue that surrounds and supports the teeth, covering the alveolar bone and tooth necks, and forming the gingival sulcus; collectively known as the gingiva, it protects the underlying periodontal structures.

genitalia.definition: Organs of the reproductive system, especially the external genital organs (genitals) such as the penis and scrotum in males and the vulva in females.

forceps delivery.definition: An operative vaginal delivery in which obstetric forceps (curved metal instruments) are used to grasp the fetal head and assist delivery through the birth canal, typically during the second stage when the cervix is fully dilated to expedite birth and avoid cesarean.

obstetric forceps.definition: A pair of curved, blunt-tipped obstetric instruments used by an obstetrician to grasp and guide the fetal head through the birth canal during vaginal delivery, typically to shorten labor or address fetal distress or maternal exhaustion.

kielland rotation.definition: A rotational maneuver used during instrumental vaginal delivery in which Kielland forceps are applied to the fetal head to rotate it from a malposition (most commonly occiput posterior or occipito-transverse) to occipito-anterior to allow delivery.

scanzoni rotation.definition: A manual obstetric maneuver in the second stage in which the clinician rotates the fetal head internally from occipito-posterior toward occipito-anterior to facilitate vaginal delivery.

forceps rotation.definition: A maneuver used during operative vaginal delivery in which obstetric forceps are applied to the fetal head and rotated within the birth canal to align the head with the birth canal—typically converting a malposition (e.g., occiput posterior) to occiput anterior to facilitate delivery.

manual rotation.definition: An obstetric procedure in which a clinician uses a gloved hand inside the birth canal to rotate the fetus’s presenting part (usually the head) from a less favorable position, such as occipito-posterior, to a more favorable occipito-anterior position to facilitate vaginal delivery.

high forceps.definition: A forceps-assisted vaginal delivery in which the fetal head is high in the birth canal, above the pelvic brim and not yet engaged, requiring traction to facilitate delivery and associated with higher maternal and neonatal risk than lower forceps.

low forceps.definition: A type of obstetric forceps used to assist vaginal delivery when the fetal head is low in the birth canal (typically at or below the level of the ischial spines), enabling controlled traction to deliver the head.

mid forceps.definition: A type of obstetric forceps used to assist instrumental vaginal delivery when the fetal head is at midpelvic station (above the ischial spines) and cannot be delivered with maternal pushing alone; often requires rotation and traction by an experienced clinician.

fiberoptic laryngoscope.definition: An endoscopic device that uses fiber-optic illumination to visualize the larynx and upper airway; available in flexible and rigid forms, commonly used for airway assessment and facilitating awake fiberoptic intubation.

fortaz.definition: An injectable third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic (ceftazidime) used for serious infections caused by Gram-negative bacteria; it inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by blocking penicillin-binding proteins and is given IV or IM.

phenformin.definition: A biguanide oral antidiabetic agent formerly used for type 2 diabetes; withdrawn or rarely used due to a markedly higher risk of lactic acidosis than metformin, especially in patients with renal impairment; lowers hepatic glucose production and increases peripheral glucose uptake.

formoterol.definition: A long-acting beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist bronchodilator used for maintenance treatment of asthma and COPD; provides sustained bronchodilation for about 12 hours and is not used for acute bronchospasm.

pretibial fever.definition: Not a standard medical term; fever is a systemic rise in body temperature due to infection or inflammation, and there is no defined condition named “pretibial fever.”

fort bragg fever.definition: An informal, historical term for a febrile illness observed among U.S. military personnel at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, commonly attributed to a tick-borne rickettsial infection and resembling Rocky Mountain spotted fever; it is not an official current medical diagnosis.

yaws.definition: An infectious disease caused by Treponema pallidum pertenue, a nonvenereal treponematosis transmitted by direct skin contact in tropical regions; it starts as a painless skin lesion and may progress to widespread skin lesions and bone/joint involvement, and is treatable with benzathine penicillin G or azithromycin.

leishmania guyanensis.definition: A species of intracellular protozoan parasite in the genus Leishmania (Viannia) that causes American cutaneous leishmaniasis in humans; transmitted by phlebotomine sandflies in northern South America; typically presents as a localized cutaneous ulcer and can rarely involve mucosal surfaces.

pian bois.definition: I can’t find a standard medical term “pian bois.” It may be a misspelling or a non-English term. Could you provide context (where you saw it, spelling, language, or symptoms) so I can search again or offer a definition for the correct term?

fornix cerebri.definition: A C-shaped bundle of white-matter fibers that is the major output tract of the hippocampus, connecting the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies and other limbic structures; involved in memory processing.

vaginal fornix.definition: A recess of the vagina around the cervix formed by the reflected vaginal mucosa; it includes the anterior and posterior fornices (and lateral fornices).

foreign body granuloma.definition: A localized granulomatous inflammatory response to a foreign material that cannot be readily degraded, characterized by macrophages and multinucleated giant cells surrounding the material and often accompanied by fibrous tissue.

fosamprenavir.definition: A phosphonooxymethyl prodrug that is converted to amprenavir, an HIV-1 protease inhibitor used in antiretroviral therapy, typically boosted with ritonavir to increase exposure.

hiv-1 infection.definition: An infection caused by human immunodeficiency virus type 1 that targets and destroys CD4+ T lymphocytes and other immune cells, leading to progressive immune system failure; transmitted through blood, sexual contact, or from mother to child; without treatment, may progress to Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS).

protease inhibitors.definition: A class of substances that block protease enzymes, which cleave proteins; used to inhibit proteolysis in various biological processes and, clinically, to prevent maturation of viral proteins (notably in HIV therapy).

ganciclovir.definition: An antiviral guanine nucleoside analog that inhibits viral DNA polymerase after phosphorylation and is used to treat cytomegalovirus (CMV) infections, particularly in immunocompromised patients.

foscarnet.definition: An antiviral medication that is a pyrophosphate analogue inhibiting viral DNA polymerase (and to a lesser extent reverse transcriptase) by chelating magnesium cofactors; used intravenously for acyclovir-resistant HSV infections and CMV retinitis in AIDS, as well as other herpesvirus infections. It can cause nephrotoxicity and electrolyte disturbances (e.g., hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia) and requires careful hydration and monitoring.

fosfomycin.definition: An antibiotic that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by inactivating the MurA enzyme (UDP-N-acetylglucosamine enolpyruvyl transferase), blocking the first step of peptidoglycan formation; active against many Gram-negative bacteria and some Gram-positive organisms, commonly used as a single-dose oral therapy for uncomplicated urinary tract infections (fosfomycin tromethamine) and available in IV form for other infections.

lanthanum.definition: An elemental rare earth metal (atomic number 57) that is soft and silvery-white in its metallic form and has no known essential biological role in humans. In medicine it is used as a phosphate-binding agent, typically in the form of a salt, to reduce elevated serum phosphate in patients with chronic kidney disease.

fractional excretion of sodium.definition: The percentage of filtered sodium that is excreted in the urine, calculated as (Urine Na × Serum Cr) / (Serum Na × Urine Cr) × 100%; used to differentiate prerenal azotemia from intrinsic renal failure in acute kidney injury. Typically <1% in prerenal states and >2% in intrinsic renal injury, but accuracy can be affected by diuretics or certain renal conditions (diuretic effects may require alternative measures such as FEUrea).

fractional inspired oxygen.definition: The fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) is the proportion of oxygen in the gas mixture a person breathes; in room air at sea level it is about 0.21 (21%), and higher values are achieved with supplemental oxygen.

olecranon fossa.definition: A deep, posterior depression on the distal humerus that articulates with the olecranon of the ulna during elbow extension.

vestibule of vagina.definition: An area of the vulva between the labia minora that contains the external openings of the vagina and the urethra, and the openings of the Bartholin (greater vestibular) glands.

vestibular fossa.definition: A shallow depression on the temporal bone associated with the vestibular (balance) portion of the inner ear.

fourchette.definition: A small fold of mucous membrane at the posterior edge of the vaginal opening, formed where the labia minora meet the perineal skin.

fovea capitis.definition: A small pit on the surface of the femoral head in the hip joint; the attachment site of the ligamentum teres femoris, which contains the artery of the head of the femur and contributes to femoral head blood supply (more in children, limited in adults).

macula lutea.definition: Yellowish circular area at the center of the retina containing a high density of cone photoreceptors, especially in the fovea, and mediating high-acuity, color, central vision.

fowler's position.definition: A position in which the patient lies supine with the head of the bed elevated to about 45–60 degrees; higher elevations are called high Fowler's (60–90 degrees) and lower elevations are low/semi-Fowler's (about 15–45 degrees).

apocrine glands.definition: A type of sweat gland that secretes via apocrine (decapitation) secretion into hair follicles; it produces a thick, protein- and lipid-rich fluid that is initially odorless but can develop odor after bacterial action on the skin. Found mainly in the axillae, groin, areola, and external ear canal; becomes active after puberty and is stimulated by hormonal and emotional stimuli.

pubes.definition: Plural of pubis; the paired bones forming the anterior portion of the pelvic girdle; informally, also refers to the pubic hair in the pubic region.

fournier's gangrene.definition: A rapidly progressive, life-threatening necrotizing infection of the perineal, genital, and/or perianal tissues (necrotizing fasciitis), typically polymicrobial and associated with diabetes or immunosuppression; requires emergent surgical debridement, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and supportive care.

retrobulbar neuritis.definition: An inflammatory demyelinating attack on the optic nerve posterior to the globe, causing acute unilateral vision loss with pain on eye movement, reduced color vision, and a relative afferent pupillary defect; the optic disc may appear normal initially and it is often associated with multiple sclerosis.

optic disc atrophy.definition: Optic disc atrophy is irreversible degeneration of the optic nerve fibers at the optic disc, resulting in pallor of the optic nerve head and associated visual impairment; it reflects end-stage optic neuropathy from a variety of etiologies (ischemic, compressive, inflammatory, hereditary, toxic/nutritional, etc.).

fourth cranial nerve.definition: A motor cranial nerve that innervates the superior oblique muscle of the eye, enabling intorsion and depression of the eyeball (especially when the eye is adducted); it exits the brainstem dorsally and travels to the orbit via the superior orbital fissure.

nuclear magnetic resonance imaging.definition: A noninvasive medical imaging modality that uses a strong magnetic field and radiofrequency pulses to align hydrogen protons and detect their signals, producing high-contrast images of soft tissues without ionizing radiation.

halo-femoral traction.definition: A form of skeletal traction in which a halo ring is affixed to the skull and a traction pin is placed in the femur; weights are applied to produce longitudinal traction between the head and the femur to gradually realign or reduce a deformity or fracture, commonly used for severe spinal deformities (e.g., scoliosis) or complex hip/femoral injuries.

halo traction.definition: A method of cervical spine immobilization and reduction in which a halo ring is fixed to the skull with pins; traction is applied via weights or a traction device to realign or stabilize the neck.

cervical traction.definition: Therapeutic modality that applies a calibrated pulling force to the head or neck using a harness or device to gently elongate the cervical spine, with the aim of reducing disc herniation or nerve root compression and relieving neck pain and muscle spasm.

fragilitas.definition: A Latin term meaning fragility or brittleness; in medical usage, it denotes a state of increased vulnerability or frailty, often due to aging or chronic disease, with reduced physiologic reserve and higher risk of injury or adverse outcomes after minor stressors.

ossium.definition: A Latin noun meaning "of the bone" (genitive of os); used in anatomical terminology to denote relation to bone.

intraarticular.definition: Within a joint; located inside the joint capsule or joint space, such as an injection delivered directly into a joint.

torus.definition: A benign bony exostosis (outgrowth) on a bone, most commonly occurring in the oral cavity along the midline of the hard palate or on the inner surface of the mandible; typically asymptomatic and nonneoplastic, often hereditary.

shaft.definition: The long, cylindrical part of a long bone between the proximal and distal ends; the diaphysis, composed mainly of compact bone surrounding the medullary cavity.

pathological.definition: Relating to pathology or the study of disease; caused by disease; showing abnormal or diseased characteristics.

transverse.definition: Situated across; in anatomy, relating to a plane (the transverse plane) that divides the body into superior (upper) and inferior (lower) parts.

oblique.definition: Slanted or angled; in anatomy, a muscle whose fibers run at an oblique angle to the midline, such as the external oblique and internal oblique muscles of the abdomen.

spiral.definition: Describing something wound in a helical, spiral fashion around an axis; used to describe anatomy, injuries (e.g., spiral fracture), or microorganisms with a helical morphology.

occult.definition: Something not visible to the naked eye but seen under a microscope or through lab tests.

segmental.definition: Relating to a segment; pertaining to a discrete portion of an organ or body part, such as a spinal segment or a dermatomal area, or describing processes confined to a single segment rather than the entire structure.

stellate.definition: Star-shaped; in histology, describing cells with multiple radiating cytoplasmic processes from the cell body, giving a stellate appearance (e.g., hepatic stellate cells in the liver).

stress.definition: Stress or strain (can be of your mind or body), pressure, or worry.

comminuted.definition: A fracture in which the bone is broken into more than two fragments.

fragmin.definition: A brand-name low-molecular-weight heparin anticoagulant containing dalteparin sodium; inhibits Factor Xa (and to a lesser extent Factor IIa) via antithrombin III and is used to prevent and treat venous thromboembolism, given by subcutaneous injection.

dalteparin.definition: A low molecular weight heparin anticoagulant derived from porcine mucosa that inhibits factor Xa (to a lesser extent thrombin), used to prevent and treat deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism; administered by subcutaneous injection.

franceschetti.definition: A congenital craniofacial disorder (mandibulofacial dysostosis) characterized by hypoplasia of the zygomatic arches and mandible, resulting in midface retrusion, micrognathia, downward-slanting palpebral fissures, and often cleft palate and ear anomalies.

treacher.definition: Not a recognized medical term; may refer to Treacher Collins syndrome, a congenital craniofacial disorder characterized by underdevelopment of the cheekbones and jaw, downward-slanting eye openings, and ear anomalies, often with airway management challenges.

fraser.definition: A rare autosomal recessive congenital syndrome characterized by cryptophthalmos, syndactyly, and renal agenesis or dysplasia, often with other facial, airway, or genital anomalies; caused by mutations in FRAS1 and/or FREM2 genes.

whistling.definition: A high-pitched musical sound produced by turbulent airflow through narrowed or obstructed airways, commonly heard during breathing and associated with conditions causing airway constriction such as asthma, COPD, or bronchitis.

frankfurt.definition: A cephalometric reference plane defined by a line through the porion (the uppermost point of the external auditory canal) and the orbitale (the lowest point on the inferior orbital margin) on both sides; it approximates the skull’s natural horizontal orientation and is used as a standard reference in cephalometry and orthodontics.

horizontal.definition: An imaginary anatomical plane parallel to the horizon that divides the body into superior (upper) and inferior (lower) parts; also known as the transverse plane.

plane.definition: A flat, imaginary surface that divides the body or an organ into parts to describe location and orientation; the main anatomical planes are sagittal (left-right), coronal/frontal (anterior-posterior), and transverse/axial (superior-inferior).

frank-starling.definition: An intrinsic mechanism by which increasing end-diastolic volume (preload) increases stroke volume due to greater stretch of cardiac muscle fibers, improving the force of contraction; within physiological limits.

relationship.definition: A connection or association between two or more entities; in anatomy, the spatial relation of one structure to another; in research, an association or causal link between factors.

end-diastolic.definition: Occurring at the end of diastole, describing the state of the ventricles when they are maximally filled with blood just before ventricular contraction (systole).

freckle.definition: A small, flat pigmented spot on the skin, typically brown and a few millimeters in diameter, caused by localized increased melanin production in response to sun exposure; benign and common.

kopan.definition: No medical definition found for "kopan" in trusted dictionaries. Please check spelling or provide more context (e.g., the body system, condition, or procedure it relates to) and I can help further.

needle.definition: A slender, pointed medical instrument, usually metallic, designed to puncture tissue; hypodermic needles are hollow and used to inject medications or draw fluids, while surgical (suture) needles are used to pass sutures through tissue.

mandibulofacial.definition: Relating to the mandible (lower jaw) and the face; pertaining to the jaw and facial structures.

frambesia.definition: An archaic term for yaws, a chronic, nonvenereal treponemal infection caused by Treponema pertenue; transmitted by direct skin contact in warm, humid tropical regions, presenting with painless papules or nodules that may ulcerate and can involve bones and joints if untreated.

framboesia.definition: A tropical, contagious infection caused by the nonvenereal Treponema pallidum subspecies pertenue, transmitted by skin-to-skin contact, presenting with papillomatous and ulcerative skin lesions that can involve bone and lymph nodes; treated with penicillin.

calices.definition: Plural of calyx; in anatomy, the renal calices are cup-shaped cavities in the kidney that collect urine from the collecting ducts and drain into the renal pelvis (divided into minor and major calyces).

nephralgia.definition: Pain located in one or both kidneys; renal pain, commonly due to kidney stones, infection, or other renal disorders.

fraley.definition: Not a recognized medical term; there is no standard medical definition.

pole.definition: An end or extremity of an elongated anatomical structure along its longitudinal axis; used to describe either end of an organ or cell (e.g., anterior and posterior poles of a lens, or superior and inferior poles of the kidney).

drift.definition: An involuntary downward drift of an extended limb (often with pronation) indicating upper motor neuron weakness.

fingers.definition: One of the five digits of the hand; each typically comprises proximal, middle, and distal phalanges (the thumb, or pollex, has two); fingers enable grasping, pinching, and precise manipulation of objects.

mandibular.definition: Relating to the mandible, the lower jawbone; used to describe structures, nerves, or procedures located in or near the lower jaw.

incisor.definition: A front tooth specialized for cutting food; one of the four anterior teeth in each dental arch (two central and two lateral) with a sharp incisal edge.

angle.definition: A figure formed by two rays or line segments sharing a common endpoint; the size of the opening between them, measured in degrees. In anatomy, the term is used for specific bends or angular junctions, such as the sternal angle (angle of Louis).

francisella.definition: A genus of small Gram-negative, nonmotile, facultatively intracellular coccobacilli that includes Francisella tularensis, the causative agent of tularemia.

sulcus.definition: The V-shaped hollow at the margin of the tooth and gum.

mucogingival.definition: Relating to both the oral mucosa and gingival tissue; specifically, the region where keratinized gingiva meets nonkeratinized alveolar mucosa (the mucogingival junction).

hooked.definition: Describing an anatomical feature that curves abruptly with a sharp bend, producing a projection that resembles a hook; used to describe bone processes, nasal contours, or other structures with a beak-like shape.

wire.definition: A slender, flexible strand of metal used in medical procedures for fixation of bones (e.g., Kirschner wires), suturing, ligation, or as a guide for implants.

freezing.definition: The process of lowering a substance's temperature to below its freezing point, turning it into a solid; in medicine, the controlled use of extreme cold (cryotherapy/cryosurgery) to destroy or preserve tissue.

freiberg's infraction.definition: An osteochondrosis of the metatarsal head (most often the second metatarsal) in adolescents, marked by avascular necrosis and collapse of the metatarsal head that causes forefoot pain and decreased range of motion; typically related to repetitive microtrauma and managed from nonoperative care to surgery depending on severity.

frenectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove or release the frenulum, a small fold of tissue that connects the lip or tongue to the jaw or floor of the mouth, to relieve restricted movement and improve function (commonly for tongue-tie or lip-tie).

frenotomy.definition: A minor surgical procedure in which the frenulum (usually the lingual frenulum under the tongue) is incised or divided to release tethering and improve tongue mobility; commonly performed to treat ankyloglossia (tongue-tie).

lingual frenulum.definition: A thin fold of mucous membrane that connects the underside of the tongue to the floor of the mouth.

frenulum of the lips.definition: A small fold of mucous membrane attaching the inner aspect of a lip to the gingiva (alveolar mucosa); there are maxillary and mandibular labial frenula.

frenulum labii superioris.definition: A small mucous membrane fold that attaches the inner surface of the upper lip to the gingival tissue above the maxillary front teeth; part of the oral mucosa and can influence lip movement and spacing between the upper incisors.

frenulum labii inferioris.definition: A small fold of mucous membrane that anchors the underside of the lower lip to the gingival mucosa of the mandible near the lower front teeth (the inferior labial frenulum).

frenulum of the clitoris.definition: A small mucosal fold on the underside of the clitoris that anchors the glans to the surrounding vestibular mucosa and is highly sensitive.

frenulum of the ileal orifice.definition: A small mucosal fold at the ileocecal (ileal) orifice that forms part of the ileocecal valve and helps regulate passage from the ileum into the cecum.

frenulum of ileocecal valve.definition: A small mucosal fold that attaches the ileocecal valve to the terminal ileum, forming part of the valve's supportive structures and helping anchor it at the ileocecal junction.

fresh-frozen plasma.definition: Plasma separated from donor blood that is frozen within a short period after collection and stored at −18°C or colder; it contains all coagulation factors and is used to treat coagulation factor deficiencies or to reverse anticoagulation (e.g., warfarin) in bleeding patients.

friedländer's pneumonia.definition: A pneumonia caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae, typically presenting as a rapidly progressive lobar pneumonia in debilitated adults (often elderly, alcoholic, or diabetic) with a productive, thick sputum that can be described as currant jelly; upper-lobe predominance and possible necrosis or abscess formation may occur.

friedreich's ataxia.definition: An autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder caused by a GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion in the FXN gene, leading to frataxin deficiency. It typically presents in childhood or adolescence with progressive gait ataxia and dysarthria, often accompanied by pes cavus, scoliosis, areflexia and peripheral neuropathy; cardiomyopathy (usually hypertrophic) and diabetes mellitus may occur.
