hexamethylmelamine.definition: A synthetic anticancer agent previously used in chemotherapy; a prodrug activated in vivo to alkylating metabolites that damage DNA and inhibit cell replication, with notable hematologic toxicity and largely limited modern use.

hexylcaine hydrochloride.definition: A topical local anesthetic in the hydrochloride salt form; it provides temporary numbness by reversibly blocking voltage-gated sodium channels in nerve membranes, thereby inhibiting nerve impulse conduction.

high-flow oxygen delivery system.definition: An oxygen therapy system that delivers heated, humidified oxygen at high flow rates (up to about 60 L/min) via a nasal cannula or facial mask, allowing precise FiO2 control and generating a small amount of positive airway pressure to improve oxygenation and reduce work of breathing.

high-frequency jet ventilation.definition: A mode of mechanical ventilation that delivers very small tidal volumes at very high frequencies via brief, pressurized gas jets, with exhalation primarily passive; it aims to achieve adequate gas exchange at low mean airway pressures to reduce volutrauma and barotrauma, and is commonly used in neonates and certain airway or pulmonary-leak situations.

intercostal vein.definition: A vein that accompanies an intercostal artery in an intercostal space and drains blood from the intercostal muscles and thoracic wall; posterior intercostal veins on the right drain into the azygos system, while on the left they drain into the hemiazygos/ accessory hemiazygos or into the left superior intercostal vein.

left bronchial vein.definition: A vein draining deoxygenated blood from the left bronchial circulation (bronchi and bronchial tissues) into the systemic venous system, typically via the left superior intercostal vein or the accessory hemiazygos vein.

arch of the aorta.definition: The curved, proximal segment of the aorta between the ascending and descending aorta, giving rise to the brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid, and left subclavian arteries.

anogenital region.definition: Anatomical area surrounding the anus and external genitalia, including the perineum and adjacent perianal skin.

intercostal spaces.definition: Anatomical spaces between adjacent ribs, bounded by the ribs above and below and by the intercostal muscles; each space contains the intercostal neurovascular bundle (vein, artery, nerve) and serves as a landmark for chest procedures.

high-fowler's position.definition: An upright position in which the patient is seated with the head of the bed elevated about 60–90 degrees (often with knees flexed), used to improve ventilation, reduce dyspnea, and facilitate feeding or airway clearance.

high-frequency hearing loss.definition: A form of sensorineural hearing loss in which sensitivity to high‑frequency sounds is disproportionately reduced compared with low‑frequency sounds, typically affecting frequencies around 2,000–8,000 Hz and often due to age‑related cochlear degeneration or noise exposure.

high-frequency oscillation.definition: A mode of mechanical ventilation known as high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) that delivers very small tidal volumes at very high rates (about 3–15 Hz, roughly 180–900 breaths per minute) with a relatively constant mean airway pressure and active inspiration/expiration, to improve gas exchange while reducing lung injury.

high-frequency percussive ventilation.definition: A nonconventional ventilation mode that delivers rapid, small-volume inspiratory pulses with high-frequency airway percussion, creating high-frequency pressure oscillations to promote alveolar recruitment and facilitate secretion clearance.

high-frequency positive pressure ventila.definition: An intensive-care ventilation strategy that delivers breaths at a very high rate with very small tidal volumes under positive airway pressure to improve gas exchange while limiting peak airway pressures and lung injury.

high-frequency ventilation.definition: A mode of mechanical ventilation that delivers very small tidal volumes at very high respiratory rates to achieve gas exchange while minimizing peak airway pressures and lung injury; includes high-frequency oscillatory ventilation and high-frequency jet ventilation.

neonate.definition: A newborn infant, typically defined as from birth to 28 days of age.

premature infant.definition: An infant born before 37 completed weeks of gestation; at higher risk for complications due to immaturity of organ systems (e.g., respiratory distress, thermoregulation problems, feeding difficulties).

high-risk infant.definition: An infant with an increased likelihood of morbidity or mortality in the neonatal period or infancy due to factors such as prematurity, very low birth weight, congenital anomalies, intrauterine growth restriction, perinatal asphyxia or infection, or maternal/fetal complications, often requiring specialized NICU care and close monitoring.

high-risk pregnancy care.definition: Specialized obstetric care for pregnancies at high risk of maternal or fetal complications, involving risk assessment, closer monitoring, and individualized management (often by a multidisciplinary team) throughout antepartum, intrapartum, and postpartum periods to optimize outcomes and plan delivery.

semisitting position.definition: A position in which the patient is placed partly upright with the upper body elevated about 30–60 degrees and the lower body supported, often used for certain neurosurgical and ENT procedures; it carries risks such as venous air embolism and hypotension.

venturi mask.definition: An oxygen delivery device that provides a fixed, precise concentration of supplementary oxygen by entraining room air through a Venturi jet; color-coded adapters determine FiO2 (roughly 24–50%) at prescribed flow rates (typically 4–15 L/min).

labial arch wire.definition: An orthodontic wire placed on the labial (front) surfaces of the teeth, attached to brackets in a fixed appliance to deliver controlled forces that move teeth and help maintain the arch form during treatment.

suprapubic lithotomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove bladder stones by making a suprapubic (above the pubic bone) incision into the bladder (cystotomy) and extracting the calculi.

high lithotomy.definition: An exaggerated lithotomy position in which a patient lies supine with hips and knees flexed and thighs abducted, held in stirrups at a higher angle than standard lithotomy, increasing exposure of the perineal/pelvic region for procedures.

haart.definition: A treatment regimen for HIV infection that uses three or more antiretroviral drugs from at least two drug classes to suppress HIV replication, lower viral load, improve or preserve CD4+ T-cell counts, and reduce HIV-related morbidity and mortality.

high-potassium diet.definition: A diet that emphasizes foods rich in potassium (such as fruits, vegetables, legumes, dairy, and certain grains) to raise or maintain potassium levels; caution is needed in individuals with kidney disease or those taking medications that raise potassium.

high-pressure liquid chromatography.definition: A chromatographic technique in analytical chemistry that uses a liquid mobile phase under high pressure to separate, identify, and quantify components in a sample as it passes through a column packed with a stationary phase.

high-performance liquid chromatography.definition: A chromatographic technique in which a liquid mobile phase is pumped under high pressure through a densely packed column to separate components of a mixture based on differential interactions with the stationary phase, enabling identification and quantification of the components; detectors such as UV–visible, refractive index, fluorescence, or mass spectrometry may be used.

high-protein diet.definition: A diet that provides more protein relative to total daily calories than standard guidelines, typically about 25–30% of calories from protein or 1.2–2.0 g of protein per kg of body weight per day; often used to preserve or build lean mass during weight loss or athletic training, but may increase renal workload in individuals with kidney disease and can cause nutrient imbalances if not balanced.

high-residue diet.definition: A diet rich in dietary fiber and other indigestible carbohydrates that increases stool bulk and frequency, by adding residue to the stool; typically includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, bran, and legumes, and is used to treat or prevent constipation and promote regular bowel movements.

neonatal period.definition: The neonatal period is the first 28 days of life after birth (from birth to 28 completed days).

hippocampus major.definition: A seahorse-shaped brain structure in the medial temporal lobe, part of the limbic system, crucial for memory formation and spatial navigation; it forms the hippocampal formation with the dentate gyrus and subiculum and connects with the entorhinal cortex and fornix.

hippocampus minor.definition: An older term for the dentate gyrus, the input region of the hippocampal formation in the medial temporal lobe; a trilaminar cortical structure that receives major input from the entorhinal cortex via the perforant pathway and sends projections to CA3 via mossy fibers.

hippocampal formation.definition: An anatomical complex in the medial temporal lobe that includes the hippocampus proper (CA1–CA4), dentate gyrus, and subiculum; a key limbic structure involved in declarative memory formation and consolidation, and spatial navigation. It receives major input from the entorhinal cortex via the perforant pathway and projects via the fornix to subcortical targets.

hippocampal gyrus.definition: A gyrus that forms part of the hippocampal formation in the medial temporal lobe; involved in memory processing and spatial navigation.

hippocampal fissure.definition: A narrow CSF-filled cleft within the hippocampal formation of the temporal lobe that separates the hippocampus proper from the dentate gyrus; a normal developmental feature that may appear as a shallow fissure on imaging.

hippocampal commissure.definition: A thin bundle of myelinated fibers linking the left and right hippocampus across the brain's midline, located in the medial temporal lobe and part of the limbic system.

dentate gyrus.definition: A subregion of the hippocampus located in the medial temporal lobe, consisting of the granule cell layer that receives input from the entorhinal cortex via the perforant pathway. It participates in the formation of new episodic memories and spatial pattern separation, and is a site of adult neurogenesis.

ammon's horn.definition: A curved portion of the hippocampus in the medial temporal lobe, also called the hippocampus proper (cornu ammonis), comprising CA1–CA4 segments and involved in memory formation.

longitudinal striae.definition: Linear streaks or bands oriented along the length of a tissue or organ; in dermatology, it often refers to stretch marks that run parallel to the body's long axis.

hila.definition: A site on an organ where vessels, nerves, and ducts enter and exit; for example, the hila (hilums) of the lungs are the mediastinal regions where the main bronchus, pulmonary vessels, nerves, and lymphatics connect with the organ.

hilum of the lung.definition: The hilum of the lung is the medial, concave area on each lung where the structures of the lung’s root—main bronchus, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, lymphatics, and nerves—enter and exit the organ.

hilary.definition: Relating to the hilum, the area where vessels, nerves, and ducts enter or exit an organ (e.g., the hilum of the lung or kidney).

hip joint disease.definition: A broad term for diseases of the hip joint—the ball-and-socket articulation between the femoral head and the acetabulum—encompassing degenerative, inflammatory, infectious, vascular, congenital, and traumatic conditions affecting the joint.

hipbone.definition: A paired pelvic bone forming part of the pelvis (the innominate bone), composed of the fused ilium, ischium, and pubis; it contributes to the pelvic girdle and articulates with the sacrum at the sacroiliac joint and with the femur at the acetabulum.

innominate bone.definition: A hip bone; one half of the pelvic girdle formed by the fusion of the ilium, ischium, and pubis; it forms the acetabulum for the femoral head and articulates with the sacrum at the sacroiliac joint, contributing to the pelvic ring.

coxal.definition: Relating to the hip bone; the hip bone (os coxae) of the pelvis.

hip-joint.definition: A ball-and-socket synovial joint between the femoral head and the acetabulum of the pelvis, allowing multiaxial movement (flexion/extension, abduction/adduction, internal/external rotation) and stabilized by a strong fibrous capsule and ligaments (iliofemoral, pubofemoral, ischiofemoral).

legg-calve-perthes disease.definition: A pediatric avascular necrosis of the femoral head (proximal femoral epiphysis) due to temporary loss of blood supply, causing flattening and possible deformity of the femoral head; presents with limp and hip or groin pain in a child, often between ages 4 and 8, with a course that may proceed through stages of necrosis, fragmentation, reossification, and healing.

hippel's disease.definition: A hereditary cancer-predisposition syndrome caused by germline mutations in the VHL tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 3p; autosomal dominant inheritance; characterized by CNS and retinal hemangioblastomas, clear cell renal cell carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and pancreatic cysts or neuroendocrine tumors.

hippuric acid.definition: The glycine conjugate of benzoic acid (N-benzoylglycine) formed in the liver and excreted in urine; a normal urinary metabolite that rises with toluene exposure.

capeline bandage.definition: Definition not found in trusted medical dictionaries. Could you confirm the spelling or provide context? If you meant a compression bandage, it is a stretchable wrap applied to a limb to apply sustained pressure to control bleeding, reduce swelling, or support an injured area.

hippocratic facies.definition: A sunken, cachectic facial appearance seen in severely ill or dying patients, characterized by hollow cheeks and eyes, loss of subcutaneous fat and moisture, and a pallid, waxy or cadaverous look.

hindbrain.definition: The posterior portion of the brain comprising the medulla oblongata, pons, and cerebellum; it regulates autonomic functions (such as breathing and heart rate) and coordinates movement and balance.

hind kidney.definition: The metanephros is the permanent, functional kidney in vertebrate embryology; the posterior (hind) stage of kidney development that forms the adult kidney, giving rise to the nephrons and collecting system.

metanephros.definition: The permanent embryonic kidney that forms from the metanephric blastema and ureteric bud and becomes the definitive adult kidney.

hinge axis.definition: An imaginary line about which the mandible rotates during the initial pure-rotation phase of jaw opening; the true hinge axis passes near the centers of the condyles and is estimated clinically (e.g., by a facebow) to transfer the axis to an articulator for condylar guidance settings.

hinge axis-orbital plane.definition: An anatomical/cephalometric concept describing the orientation of the mandible’s hinge axis (the instantaneous axis of rotation during opening/closing) relative to the orbital plane (the reference plane through the orbits used to orient craniofacial measurements).

hinged knee.definition: An orthopedic device or implant that uses a mechanical hinge to connect knee components, allowing controlled flexion and extension while providing stability in cases of ligament deficiency or after knee replacement.

hinged knee brace.definition: A knee orthosis with lateral hinges that permit controlled flexion and extension while providing medial–lateral stability; used to protect or support the knee after injury or surgery and to limit abnormal motion or unload the joint as prescribed.

hinge joint.definition: A uniaxial synovial joint that allows movement primarily in one plane around a single axis, enabling flexion and extension (examples include the elbow and knee).

ginglymus joint.definition: A hinge-type synovial joint (uniaxial) that allows movement in one plane, typically flexion and extension, with minimal to no rotation (as seen in the elbow and interphalangeal joints).

pivot joint.definition: A uniaxial synovial joint in which a rounded bone rotates within a ring formed by another bone and its ligament, allowing rotation around a single axis (as in the radioulnar joints for pronation and supination).

sitz bath.definition: A shallow bath in which the buttocks and hips are immersed in warm water to soothe perineal irritation and pain, commonly used for hemorrhoids, episiotomy or postpartum discomfort; usually done for 10–20 minutes.

mediastinal pleura.definition: The portion of the parietal pleura that lines the mediastinum, covering the mediastinal surfaces of the lungs and surrounding mediastinal structures; it is continuous with the costal pleura anteriorly, the diaphragmatic pleura inferiorly, and with the visceral pleura at the lung hilum.

rhinencephalon.definition: A portion of the brain responsible for olfaction, comprising the olfactory bulbs and tracts and the primary olfactory cortex (piriform cortex) with connected limbic structures (e.g., entorhinal cortex, amygdala, hippocampus) that integrate smell with memory and emotion.

replacement.definition: In medicine, replacement is the substitution of a diseased or missing body part or function with a prosthetic device, tissue graft, donor organ, or other substitute to restore normal structure and function; it also includes replacing deficient substances (such as hormones or electrolytes) with external sources.

hirschsprung's.definition: A congenital absence of enteric ganglion cells in the distal colon and rectum, leading to a functional bowel obstruction (aganglionic megacolon) due to failure of neural crest cell migration; diagnosed by rectal biopsy and treated with surgical resection of the aganglionic segment.

degenerative.definition: Relating to or characterized by progressive deterioration or loss of structure or function of tissues or organs, typically due to aging, wear-and-tear, or chronic disease.

femoral.definition: Relating to the femur (the thigh bone) or to the thigh region.

abducted.definition: Moved away from the midline of the body; in anatomy, abduction is the movement of a limb or other part away from the body's midline (e.g., lifting the arm to the side). In general usage, abducted can also mean kidnapped or carried away by force.

degrees.definition: An extent or level of something, especially the severity or stage of a condition, injury, or symptom (e.g., degree of fever or degree of burns); also a unit of measurement for temperature or angles.

abductor.definition: A muscle that moves a body part away from the midline (abduction); in the limbs, such muscles cause abduction of the respective segment (e.g., gluteus medius abducts the hip).

weight.definition: Weight is the force exerted by gravity on an object's mass; it equals mass times the acceleration due to gravity (approximately 9.81 m/s^2 on Earth) and is measured in newtons (N).

bearing.definition: The direction or position of a structure relative to a reference point; in biomechanics, also the ability of a body part to support weight (weight-bearing). In obstetrics, bearing down refers to the pushing effort during delivery.

implanted.definition: Placed into the body by a surgical procedure and intended to remain there for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes, such as implanted devices or tissue grafts.

hiprex.definition: A urinary antiseptic (methenamine hippurate) used to prevent recurrent urinary tract infections; it releases formaldehyde in acidic urine to exert a bactericidal effect and is not active in alkaline urine, typically used prophylactically rather than to treat an active infection.

methenamine.definition: A urinary tract antiseptic that is converted in acidic urine to formaldehyde, producing a bactericidal effect against common urinary pathogens; used to prevent recurrent urinary tract infections and requires acidic urine to be effective.

hirschberg's.definition: A quick screening test for strabismus in which a light is shone into the eyes and the corneal light reflexes are observed; in normal alignment the reflections are symmetric and centered in both corneas, while a displaced reflection indicates ocular misalignment and helps estimate the magnitude of deviation.

pyramidal.definition: Shaped like a pyramid. In anatomy, describing a class of neurons with a pyramid-shaped cell body and a prominent apical dendrite in the cerebral cortex; also used for related motor pathways such as the corticospinal tract.

aganglionic.definition: Lacking ganglion cells (nerve cell bodies) in a tissue; most often used to denote absence of enteric ganglia in a segment of the gastrointestinal tract (as seen in Hirschsprung disease).

toxic.definition: Pertaining to something that is poisonous.

soave.definition: An endorectal pull-through operation for Hirschsprung disease in which the mucosa of the aganglionic rectum is preserved to form a muscular cuff, and the normally innervated bowel is pulled through this cuff and anastomosed to the anal canal.

endorectal.definition: Relating to or situated within the rectum.

duhamel.definition: A surgical procedure for Hirschsprung disease in which the diseased aganglionic rectum is resected and the proximal healthy colon is pulled through and anastomosed to the anus, with the posterior rectal wall left intact to form a mucosal spur that helps create the channel.

swenson's.definition: A surgical treatment for Hirschsprung disease in which the aganglionic segment of the bowel is removed and the normally innervated proximal segment is connected to the anal canal, preserving the anal sphincter.

laparoscopic.definition: Relating to laparoscopy; a minimally invasive surgical technique performed through small abdominal incisions using a laparoscope to visualize the internal organs and guide surgical instruments.

coloanal.definition: Relating to the colon and the anal canal; used to describe anatomy or procedures involving both the colon and the anus (e.g., coloanal anastomosis).

myectomy.definition: A surgical procedure that removes all or part of a muscle.

histidinemia.definition: A rare autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by deficiency of histidase (histidine ammonia-lyase), resulting in elevated histidine levels in blood and urine; most individuals are asymptomatic.

cluster.definition: A grouping of patients, cases, or events that occur together in time or space and appear more clustered than would be expected by chance, suggesting a common exposure or related cause.

horton's.definition: Giant cell arteritis (temporal arteritis) — a granulomatous inflammatory vasculitis of large- and medium-sized arteries, most often in adults over 50, typically involving the temporal arteries. It presents with new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, and possible vision loss; diagnosed by elevated ESR/CRP and temporal artery biopsy; treated urgently with high-dose corticosteroids to prevent blindness, and may be associated with polymyalgia rheumatica.

histocompatibility complex.definition: A cluster of genes encoding cell-surface molecules that present peptide antigens to T cells, shaping immune recognition of self versus non-self and influencing tissue graft compatibility.

darling's disease.definition: A dominantly inherited keratinization disorder caused by ATP2A2 gene mutations, leading to defective calcium signaling in keratinocytes. It presents with greasy, keratotic papules in seborrheic areas (such as the scalp, face, and trunk) and often includes nail abnormalities and palmoplantar keratoderma.

histotechnician.definition: A laboratory professional who prepares tissue specimens for microscopic examination by performing tissue processing, embedding in paraffin, sectioning with a microtome, staining (typically with hematoxylin and eosin), and mounting slides for review by pathologists (often under supervision).

histological technician.definition: A laboratory professional who prepares tissue specimens for microscopic examination by processing, embedding in paraffin, sectioning, staining, and mounting slides, and who performs related quality control under supervision.

histotechnologist.definition: A laboratory professional who prepares tissue specimens for histopathologic examination by fixing, processing, embedding in paraffin, sectioning, and staining slides for review by a pathologist.

histotoxin.definition: A toxin that causes tissue destruction or necrosis by acting directly on tissues, often describing tissue-damaging components of certain venoms.

histotrophic nutrition.definition: Nourishment of the developing embryo by endometrial gland secretions (histotroph) absorbed by the trophoblast, providing nutrients before placental circulation is established.

histrionic.definition: Relating to hysteria; characterized by theatrical, exaggerated emotional expression and attention-seeking behavior.

histrionic paralysis.definition: An obsolete term for psychogenic paralysis (conversion disorder) characterized by limb weakness not explained by organic disease and by inconsistent neurological signs; today this is called functional neurological symptom disorder with motor symptoms.

histrionic personality.definition: A personality disorder (Cluster B) marked by pervasive, excessive emotionality and attention-seeking behavior, including a strong need to be the center of attention, inappropriate provocative or seductive behavior, rapidly shifting and shallow emotions, and overreliance on physical appearance to draw attention, often with perceived intimate relationships that are not actually close.

histrionic personality disorder.definition: A personality disorder characterized by a pervasive pattern of excessive emotionality and attention-seeking behavior beginning in early adulthood, with five or more of the following: discomfort when not the center of attention; inappropriate sexually seductive or provocative behavior; rapidly shifting and shallow expression of emotions; uses physical appearance to draw attention to self; a style of speech that is excessively impressionistic and lacking in detail; self-dramatization, theatricality, and exaggerated emotion; is easily influenced by others or by circumstances; considers relationships to be more intimate than they actually are.

hodgson's disease.definition: A malignant lymphoma characterized by the presence of Reed-Sternberg cells; typically presents with painless enlargement of lymph nodes (often in the neck or mediastinum) and may be associated with fever, night sweats, or weight loss. It is usually highly curable with modern chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

hoffmann's reflex.definition: A sign of upper motor neuron (pyramidal tract) dysfunction. It is elicited by flicking the distal phalanx of the middle finger; a positive response is involuntary flexion of the thumb (often with flexion of the index finger), indicating corticospinal tract involvement.

hoffmann's sign.definition: A positive upper motor neuron sign in which flicking the middle finger’s nail bed elicits flexion of the thumb (often with the index finger), suggesting corticospinal tract dysfunction such as cervical myelopathy.

holandric.definition: Relating to the Y chromosome; genes or traits transmitted through the Y chromosome (Y-linked).

holandric inheritance.definition: A pattern of inheritance in which a gene located on the Y chromosome is transmitted from father to son; only males are affected, and daughters do not inherit or transmit the trait.

hologynic.definition: Not a recognized medical term; there is no standard definition in medical dictionaries. It may be a misspelling or misinterpretation of related terms such as gynecologic/gynecology (relating to the female reproductive system) or gynogenesis (a form of reproduction from unfertilized female gametes). If you have a specific context, share it for a more precise clarification.

hologynic inheritance.definition: A pattern of inheritance in which genetic information is transmitted exclusively through the female line (maternal lineage), often referring to cytoplasmic or mitochondrial inheritance where paternal contributions are not transmitted or have little effect.

holoprosencephaly.definition: A congenital brain malformation in which the forebrain fails to divide into two hemispheres, producing a single cerebral ventricle and often midline facial anomalies; severity ranges from alobar (no hemispheric separation) to semilobar and lobar forms.

holoprosencephalic.definition: Relating to a congenital brain malformation in which the forebrain fails to divide into two hemispheres, often with midline facial anomalies.

holoprosencephalous.definition: A congenital brain malformation caused by failure of the embryonic forebrain to divide into two hemispheres, leading to varying degrees of brain and midline facial defects (ranging from alobar to lobar forms).

holocrine.definition: A mode of exocrine secretion in which whole secretory cells rupture and disintegrate to release their product (often lipid-rich sebum), with replacement of cells by mitosis.

holocrine gland.definition: A type of exocrine gland in which mature secretory cells rupture and disintegrate to release their contents, so the entire cell becomes part of the secretion (as in sebaceous glands).

holoacardius acephalus.definition: A form of acardiac (parasitic) twin in which the malformed fetus has a complete trunk and limbs (holo) but lacks a head (acephalus) and has no functional heart; it is supplied by the normal twin through placental vascular connections.

holoacardius acormus.definition: A form of acardiac (parasitic) twin in which the fetus has no functional heart and shows markedly underdeveloped or absent body structures, relying on the normal twin's circulation through placental vessels.

holoacardius amorphus.definition: A type of acardiac twin in twin-reversed arterial perfusion (TRAP) sequence, characterized by a parasitic co-twin with no functional heart and a poorly organized, amorphous body, sustained by abnormal placental vessel perfusion from the normal twin and typically nonviable.

holoacardius.definition: A type of acardiac (parasitic) twin in monochorionic pregnancies characterized by complete absence of functional cardiac tissue in the affected fetus, which is dependent on the normal twin for circulation via placental connections and is typically nonviable.

holoendemic.definition: A holoendemic disease is continuously present at high levels in a population, with transmission so intense that most people are infected in early life and develop lasting partial immunity; clinical illness is most common in young children, while adults are often asymptomatic.

holoenzyme.definition: A complete, catalytically active enzyme formed when an apoenzyme binds its nonprotein cofactor (a metal ion or an organic coenzyme).

holographic reconstruction.definition: Holographic reconstruction is the computational process of converting recorded holograms (interference patterns of light scattered by a specimen) into a three‑dimensional image that represents the specimen’s structure and depth.

holodiastolic.definition: Extending through the entire diastolic phase of the cardiac cycle; lasting from the onset to the end of diastole.

pandiastolic.definition: Occurring throughout the entire diastolic phase of the cardiac cycle; present from the end of systole to the onset of the next systole, covering early, mid, and late diastole.

holistic.definition: Relating to an approach in healthcare that treats the whole person, including physical, mental, social, and environmental factors, rather than just focusing on a specific disease or set of symptoms.

holistic health care.definition: A patient-centered approach to care that considers the whole person—physical health, mental and emotional well-being, social and environmental context—and emphasizes prevention, health promotion, and the integration of appropriate conventional and complementary therapies.

holistic nursing.definition: An approach to nursing that treats the whole person—body, mind, spirit, and environment—through a caring, patient-centered relationship, considering physical, emotional, social, cultural, and spiritual factors to promote healing, health, and well-being, often incorporating evidence-based complementary therapies as appropriate.

holistic nurse.definition: A holistic nurse is a registered nurse who practices holistic nursing, addressing the physical, emotional, social, spiritual, and environmental dimensions of health in collaboration with the patient; uses patient-centered, evidence-based approaches and may incorporate complementary therapies and health-promotion strategies to support healing and self-care.

holliday-segar formula.definition: An age- and weight-based method to estimate daily maintenance fluid requirements in pediatric patients: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for each kg from 11–20 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for each kg over 20 kg; the resulting daily total is typically divided by 24 to obtain an hourly rate.

hollow cathode lamp.definition: A discharge lamp used as a stable, element-specific light source in atomic absorption spectroscopy; a hollow cathode tube containing the element of interest emits characteristic spectral lines when energized, enabling quantitative analysis of metals.

holmium.definition: A chemical element, a rare-earth metal in the lanthanide series (atomic number 67, symbol Ho). In medicine, lasers employing this element are used for tissue ablation and lithotripsy.

reed-sternberg cells.definition: Abnormal large B-lymphocytes with bilobed nuclei and prominent eosinophilic nucleoli (“owl’s eye” appearance), characteristic of Hodgkin lymphoma; derived from germinal center B cells and typically expressing CD15 and CD30.

cd20.definition: A B-cell surface antigen expressed on mature B lymphocytes and some pre-B cells (not on plasma cells); used as a marker of B cells and as the target for anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody therapies (e.g., rituximab).

mantle field.definition: A large radiotherapy field irradiating multiple upper-body lymph node regions—primarily cervical, supraclavicular, mediastinal (and often hilar/axillary) nodes—historically used to treat Hodgkin lymphoma; typically extends from the base of the skull to the diaphragm.

proteinaceous casts.definition: Urinary casts composed predominantly of protein (usually Tamm-Horsfall protein) with little or no cellular material; formed in renal tubules and typically seen in concentrated urine or with mild proteinuria/dehydration. They are nonspecific and can be found in healthy individuals after exercise or fever.

hiv-associated fever of unknown origin.definition: A fever of unknown origin in people with HIV infection is a persistent fever (>38.3°C/101°F on multiple occasions or sustained >38°C) for several weeks in whom no source is identified after initial evaluation; in this setting, common causes include opportunistic infections (e.g., tuberculosis, fungal infections), HIV-related malignancies (e.g., lymphoma), and drug fever.

hiv-associated nephropathy.definition: A kidney disease seen in HIV infection characterized by nephrotic-range proteinuria and progressive renal failure due to collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, often with tubulointerstitial injury; pathogenesis involves direct HIV infection of renal epithelial cells and APOL1 risk alleles; management centers on antiretroviral therapy and renoprotective measures.

hivid.definition: A brand name for zidovudine (AZT), an antiretroviral nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used to treat HIV infection and to reduce perinatal transmission; it inhibits HIV replication by blocking reverse transcription of viral RNA into DNA.

hivnet.definition: An acronym used for an HIV/AIDS research network or program; most notably, a multinational clinical trial that evaluated nevirapine to reduce mother-to-child transmission of HIV.

indinavir sulfate.definition: A protease inhibitor antiretroviral used in treating HIV-1 infection; the sulfate salt form of the protease inhibitor indinavir; it inhibits HIV protease, blocking maturation of viral polyproteins and production of infectious virions.

nelfinavir mesylate.definition: A protease inhibitor antiretroviral drug used in the treatment of HIV-1 infection; administered as the mesylate salt and inhibits HIV-1 protease, blocking maturation of viral particles.

saquinavir.definition: A protease inhibitor antiretroviral used to treat HIV infection; it inhibits HIV-1 protease, preventing cleavage of the Gag-Pol polyprotein and producing immature, noninfectious virions. Often given with ritonavir to boost blood levels.

nelfinavir.definition: An antiretroviral protease inhibitor for HIV-1 infection that inhibits the HIV-1 protease, blocking maturation of viral polyproteins and producing noninfectious virions.

adenosine triphosphatase.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of ATP to ADP and inorganic phosphate, releasing energy used to power a variety of cellular processes.

h+,k+-atpase.definition: An ATPase in the apical membrane of gastric parietal cells that uses ATP hydrolysis to exchange H+ for K+, pumping protons into the gastric lumen to secrete gastric acid (also called the gastric proton pump).

gastric lumen.definition: The interior space of the stomach; the open, mucosa-lined cavity through which ingested material passes and gastric secretions mix to form chyme.

acid secretion.definition: The production and release of hydrochloric acid by the gastric parietal cells of the stomach, regulated by neural (acetylcholine), hormonal (gastrin), and paracrine (histamine) stimuli; this acid creates a highly acidic lumen (pH ~1–3) that denatures proteins and activates pepsinogen to pepsin.

hla-a.definition: A human leukocyte antigen (HLA) gene that encodes the alpha chain of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules; expressed on almost all nucleated cells and presents endogenous peptides to CD8+ T cells; highly polymorphic and influences tissue compatibility for transplantation.

hla-b.definition: A member of the HLA class I major histocompatibility complex molecules; encoded by the HLA-B gene on chromosome 6; presents endogenously derived peptide antigens to CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes; highly polymorphic with many alleles.

hla-c.definition: A class I MHC gene encoding a cell-surface glycoprotein that presents endogenous peptides to CD8+ T cells; highly polymorphic and widely used in transplantation matching, also serving as a ligand for NK cell receptors.

hla-d.definition: A group of human leukocyte antigen class II molecules (including HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ) on antigen-presenting cells that present extracellular peptide antigens to CD4+ T helper cells; encoded by the HLA-D region on chromosome 6 and highly polymorphic, influencing transplant compatibility and susceptibility to autoimmune diseases.

hlh.definition: A life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by excessive activation of macrophages and cytotoxic T cells, leading to a cytokine storm; may be genetic (primary) or triggered by infection, malignancy, or autoimmune disease. Key features include fever, splenomegaly, cytopenias, hyperferritinemia, hypertriglyceridemia or hypofibrinogenemia, elevated soluble IL-2 receptor, and evidence of hemophagocytosis; requires urgent immunochemotherapy and treatment of underlying triggers.

hlhs.definition: A complex congenital heart defect in which the left-sided heart structures (left ventricle, mitral and aortic valves, and often the ascending aorta) are underdeveloped, resulting in inadequate systemic blood flow; newborns typically rely on a patent ductus arteriosus and may require staged surgical palliation (Norwood, Glenn, Fontan) or heart transplantation for survival.

hmd.definition: A neonatal respiratory distress syndrome caused by surfactant deficiency, leading to alveolar collapse and hypoxemia; histologically, eosinophilic hyaline membranes line the alveoli.

hyaline membrane disease.definition: A neonatal respiratory distress syndrome caused by deficiency of pulmonary surfactant in preterm infants, leading to alveolar atelectasis and the formation of hyaline membranes in the alveoli and small airways, resulting in severe hypoxemia and poor lung compliance.

hme.definition: A passive device in the ventilator circuit that humidifies and warms inspired gas by reclaiming heat and moisture from the patient’s exhaled breath, helping preserve airway mucosa and mucociliary function.

hmg-coa reductase.definition: A rate-limiting cytosolic enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis that converts hydroxymethylglutaryl-CoA to mevalonate; the primary pharmacologic target of statin therapy.

hmg-coa reductase inhibitor.definition: A class of lipid-lowering medications that inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in hepatic cholesterol synthesis, leading to reduced cholesterol production and lower LDL cholesterol levels.

statin.definition: A class of lipid-lowering medications that inhibit hepatic HMG-CoA reductase, the enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis, thereby lowering LDL cholesterol and reducing the risk of cardiovascular events.

hms liquifilm.definition: A liquid barrier film is a thin, clear coating applied to skin that dries into a flexible film, protecting the skin from moisture, irritants, and friction—and reducing adhesive-related skin injury; commonly used in wound care and dermatologic contexts.

holism.definition: The theory that systems are best understood as integrated wholes rather than as sums of their parts; in medicine, an approach that considers the physical, psychological, social, and sometimes spiritual factors affecting health and treats the patient as a whole rather than focusing only on diseases or symptoms.

holorachischisis.definition: A rare congenital neural tube defect in which the spinal cord remains completely unfused along the entire length of the neuraxis, producing a continuous fissure with exposure of neural tissue (the most severe form of rachischisis).

homeotic mutation.definition: A mutation in a gene that governs the identity of body segments during development, causing one body part to develop as another (a homeotic transformation).

holosystolic.definition: A heart murmur that begins with the first heart sound and continues uninterrupted through the entire phase of systole until the second heart sound, typically due to regurgitant flow across a valve (such as mitral or tricuspid regurgitation) or a ventricular septal defect.

pansystolic.definition: A heart murmur heard throughout the entire systole (from S1 to S2); i.e., holosystolic. Common causes include mitral regurgitation, tricuspid regurgitation, and ventricular septal defect.

inguinocrural hernia.definition: A groin hernia in which the hernial sac protrudes through the inguinal region and extends into the femoral (crural) canal, effectively a dual inguinal–femoral hernia; an uncommon presentation that may mimic inguinal or femoral hernias.

hypoplastic thumb.definition: A congenital underdevelopment of the thumb, typically smaller with shortened or underdeveloped bones and soft tissues, often resulting in impaired pinch function; can occur as an isolated anomaly or as part of radial ray defects (thumb hypoplasia).

short forearm.definition: An anatomical finding in which the forearm length is shorter than expected for the patient’s age and body size, usually due to congenital shortening of the middle limb segment (mesomelic shortening) or growth arrest from injury or disease.

holtzman inkblot technique.definition: A projective psychological test in which a person is asked to describe what they see in a standardized set of inkblots; responses are systematically scored on multiple variables to infer personality structure, affect, perceptual and thinking processes, and potential psychopathology.

rorschach test.definition: A projective psychological test in which a person is shown symmetric inkblots and asked to describe what they see; the responses are interpreted to infer aspects of personality structure and potential psychopathology.

homans' sign.definition: A historical clinical sign of deep venous thrombosis in which forcible dorsiflexion of the foot elicits calf pain; it has low sensitivity and specificity and is not reliable for diagnosing DVT.

home assessment.definition: A structured assessment of a person’s home environment to identify safety risks, accessibility barriers, and needed adaptations to support safe, independent functioning and prevent injury; commonly performed by occupational therapists or other health professionals.

home care.definition: Care provided in a patient’s home by healthcare professionals or trained caregivers under a physician’s plan of care, including medical treatment, rehabilitation, and assistance with daily activities, to manage illness, support recovery, or maintain independence at home.

home health care.definition: A range of medically necessary services provided in a patient’s home to treat or manage acute or chronic conditions, injuries, or disabilities. It is typically ordered by a physician and delivered by licensed professionals (nurses, therapists) and trained aides, and may include skilled nursing, rehabilitation therapies, wound care, medication management, and assistance with daily activities, with care coordinated among the patient, family, and healthcare providers.

home health care classification.definition: An organizational framework for categorizing home-based health services by type of care (e.g., skilled nursing, rehabilitation therapies, personal/prescription assistance, medical social work) and level of intensity, used to plan, coordinate, document, and reimburse care delivered in the patient’s home.

home health nurse.definition: A licensed nurse who provides skilled nursing care in a patient's home as part of a home health program, under a physician's orders, to assess and treat health conditions, administer medications and therapies, monitor status, educate patients and caregivers, and coordinate care with other health professionals.

homeodynamics.definition: The dynamic regulation of an organism's internal environment, maintaining stability through continuously adaptive feedback and feedforward regulatory mechanisms in response to internal and external changes.

homeomorphous.definition: Having the same morphology as a reference tissue or cell type; in pathology, cells that are uniform in size and shape and resemble normal cells (lacking pleomorphism).

homeopathic pharmacopoeia of the united.word: homeopathic pharmacopoeia of the united states
homeopathic pharmacopoeia of the united.definition: An official U.S. pharmacopoeia that defines and standardizes homeopathic drug substances, including their identity, preparation (dilution and succussion), potency, and quality control, as published by the Homeopathic Pharmacopoeia Convention of the United States.

homeopathist.definition: A practitioner of homeopathy; a person who treats patients using highly diluted substances selected according to the principle of "like cures like"; the practice is considered pseudoscientific by mainstream medicine.

homeopathy.definition: A system of alternative medicine based on the law of similars, in which remedies are prepared by serial dilution and vigorous shaking (succussion) of a substance; proponents believe the diluted preparation can treat symptoms by triggering a healing response, often to the point where no molecules of the original substance remain. Robust scientific evidence does not support efficacy beyond placebo.

homeostatic.definition: Relating to homeostasis; the ability of an organism or system to maintain a stable internal environment (e.g., constant temperature, pH, electrolyte balance) through regulatory processes.

homeotherapy.definition: Not a standard medical term; likely a misspelling or variant of homeopathy, a system of alternative medicine that uses highly diluted substances believed to stimulate the body's self-healing; evidence for efficacy is lacking in rigorous clinical trials.

homeotypic.definition: Relating to or characterized by cells that are of the same type or origin as the tissue from which they derive; showing histologic similarity to the normal tissue of origin.

homoiothermal.definition: Maintaining a constant body temperature irrespective of environmental conditions; a property of warm-blooded (homeothermic) animals.

warm-blooded.definition: Describes animals that regulate and maintain a relatively constant internal body temperature through metabolic heat production, regardless of ambient temperature; they are endothermic (examples: mammals and birds).

homogeneity.definition: The quality or condition of being uniform in composition, structure, or character across a sample, tissue, or population; the absence of variation (the opposite of heterogeneity).

homogenate.definition: A suspension obtained by mechanically disrupting tissue or cells in a buffer, creating a uniform mixture of cellular contents for biochemical analysis.

homogenization.definition: A process that makes a mixture uniform in composition by breaking down structures into small, evenly dispersed particles; in biology and pathology, tissue homogenization mechanically disrupts tissue to produce a uniform sample for analysis.

homogenized.definition: Processed to be uniform in composition or texture by mechanical disruption, producing a homogeneous mixture or suspension.

homogentisic acid.definition: An intermediate metabolite in the tyrosine/phenylalanine degradation pathway, chemically 2,5-dihydroxyphenylacetic acid; it accumulates in alkaptonuria due to deficiency of homogentisate dioxygenase.

alkaptonuria.definition: An autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by deficiency of homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase, leading to accumulation of homogentisic acid and its deposition in connective tissues (ochronosis); urine darkens on standing, and affected individuals develop progressive degenerative arthritis due to pigment deposition.

homocysteine.definition: An amino acid intermediate produced during methionine metabolism; it is not incorporated into proteins. Elevated plasma levels (hyperhomocysteinemia) are associated with higher risk of cardiovascular disease and thromboembolism, often reflecting impaired remethylation or transsulfuration pathways due to B-vitamin deficiencies (folate, B6, B12).

homocystine.definition: The disulfide dimer of two homocysteine molecules; an oxidized form (disulfide) of the amino acid homocysteine.

homocystinemia.definition: Elevated concentration of homocysteine in the blood, often due to impaired methionine metabolism or deficiencies of vitamins B6, B12, or folate, associated with increased risk of thromboembolism and vascular disease.

homocystinuria.definition: An autosomal recessive metabolic disorder of methionine and homocysteine metabolism, most commonly due to cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency, causing elevated homocysteine (and often methionine) in blood and urine. It presents with marfanoid habitus, downward-inward lens subluxation, developmental delay, osteoporosis, and a high risk of thromboembolism. Management includes pyridoxine (vitamin B6) in responsive individuals, dietary methionine restriction with cysteine supplementation, and agents such as betaine to lower homocysteine.

homocystinuric.definition: Relating to homocystinuria; a metabolic disorder characterized by elevated homocysteine levels in blood and urine, usually due to cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency, with manifestations such as lens subluxation, marfanoid habitus, thromboembolism, and developmental delay.

homocysteine test.definition: A blood test that measures the amount of homocysteine in the blood; elevated levels may indicate deficiencies of folate, vitamin B12, or vitamin B6, kidney disease, or increased risk of cardiovascular disease, and it can be used to evaluate homocystinuria or guide B‑vitamin therapy.

peripheral arterial disease.definition: A common circulatory problem in which narrowed arteries reduce blood flow to the limbs, most often the legs. It is usually due to atherosclerosis and can cause leg pain with walking (claudication), numbness or weakness, coldness in the lower leg or foot, and, in advanced cases, nonhealing wounds or gangrene.

thromboembolic stroke.definition: An ischemic stroke caused by an embolus (usually a blood clot) that travels from another part of the circulation to a cerebral artery and lodges there, blocking blood flow and causing brain tissue injury.

lens dislocation.definition: Displacement of the crystalline lens from its normal position inside the eye due to weakness or rupture of the zonular fibers; can be partial (subluxation) or complete (luxation) and may follow trauma or be associated with systemic conditions such as Marfan syndrome or homocystinuria.

dislocated lenses.definition: A condition in which the crystalline lens is displaced from its normal position due to weakness or rupture of the zonular fibers; it can be partial (subluxation) or complete (luxation) and may result from trauma or systemic disorders such as Marfan syndrome or homocystinuria, causing decreased vision, irregular astigmatism, phacodonesis, or lens-induced glaucoma.

cystathionine.definition: A non-proteinogenic sulfur-containing amino acid formed during the transsulfuration of homocysteine and serine by cystathionine beta-synthase; it is subsequently hydrolyzed by cystathionine gamma-lyase to produce cysteine and alpha-ketobutyrate.

tyrosine.definition: An amino acid that is nonessential in humans; a precursor to catecholamines (dopamine, norepinephrine, epinephrine), thyroid hormones (thyroxine, T4), and melanin; synthesized from phenylalanine and obtained from dietary protein; becomes conditionally essential in phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency.

homocarnosine.definition: A dipeptide consisting of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) linked to histidine; found in brain tissue and thought to function as a reservoir for GABA and possibly as an antioxidant.

germ cells.definition: Reproductive cells that give rise to gametes (sperm and eggs); they undergo meiosis to produce haploid cells and transmit genetic material to offspring.

sister chromatids.definition: Two identical copies of a single replicated chromosome that are held together at the centromere and separated during anaphase of mitosis (and meiosis II) to become independent daughter chromosomes.

meiotic division.definition: A type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half to form four genetically diverse haploid gametes, accomplished through two consecutive divisions (meiosis I and meiosis II) after DNA replication, with genetic variation generated by crossing over and independent assortment.

second meiotic division.definition: The division after meiosis I in which sister chromatids are separated at the centromeres and pulled to opposite poles, yielding four haploid daughter cells from the two haploid cells that entered this stage.

ammoniac silver nitrate solution.definition: A solution of silver nitrate in aqueous ammonia that forms the diamminesilver(I) complex [Ag(NH3)2]+ (Tollens' reagent); used to test for aldehydes and reducing substances by oxidizing them and reducing Ag+ to metallic silver, which deposits a reflective silver mirror, and is kept basic by the ammonia.

eugenol.definition: A phenolic compound (4-allyl-2-methoxyphenol), the principal constituent of clove oil; it has analgesic and antiseptic properties and is used in dentistry as a local anesthetic and antiseptic, and as a flavoring/fragrance agent.

formalin.definition: Aqueous solution of formaldehyde (usually 37% formaldehyde with methanol stabilizer) used as a tissue fixative to preserve specimens by cross-linking proteins.

homoiothermic.definition: Maintaining a relatively constant core body temperature independent of ambient temperature, achieved through physiological thermoregulation (metabolic heat production and regulation of heat loss); typical of birds and mammals.

insemination.definition: Introduction of semen into the female reproductive tract to achieve fertilization; can occur through natural intercourse or by artificial means (artificial insemination).

organoid.definition: A miniature, three-dimensional tissue cultured in vitro from stem cells that self-organizes to form multiple cell types and structural features resembling a specific organ, enabling studies of development, disease, and drug responses.

homologous.definition: Having the same origin or structure; corresponding in position or relation; used to describe anatomical structures derived from a common ancestor or chromosomes that pair during meiosis.

heterologous.definition: Originating from a different individual or species; not homologous to the host (non-self).

migrainous.definition: Relating to migraine; of or characteristic of migraine headaches or their symptoms (for example, unilateral throbbing head pain often accompanied by nausea, photophobia, or phonophobia).

cranial_neuralgia.definition: Pain along the distribution of a cranial nerve, typically sudden, severe, stabbing or electric-shock-like, intermittent, and often triggered by light touch or movement.

immune.definition: To be protected from a disease.

necator.definition: A genus of intestinal nematodes known as hookworms; in humans, the principal species attaches to the small intestinal mucosa and feeds on blood, causing iron-deficiency anemia; infection occurs when filariform larvae in soil contaminated with human feces penetrate the skin.

duodenale.definition: Latin epithet meaning "of the duodenum"; used in scientific names to indicate association with the duodenum, commonly seen in the binomial name of a parasitic nematode that inhabits the small intestine.

necatoriasis.definition: An intestinal infection caused by the hookworm Necator americanus, characterized by chronic gastrointestinal blood loss leading to iron-deficiency anemia and nutritional deficits; acquired when larvae penetrate the skin in contaminated soil.

horseshoe_kidney.definition: A congenital renal fusion anomaly in which the inferior poles of the kidneys fuse across the midline, forming a horseshoe-shaped organ that lies lower in the abdomen because ascent is arrested by the inferior mesenteric artery; most cases are asymptomatic but it can be associated with hydronephrosis, nephrolithiasis, or urinary tract infections.

hospitalism.definition: A historical term for the emotional and social deterioration seen in hospitalized patients—especially infants—due to separation from caregivers and the hospital environment, leading to withdrawal, apathy, and developmental regression.

hourglass uterus.definition: A congenital uterine anomaly in which the uterine cavity is constricted midway, producing an hourglass shape on imaging and sometimes associated with infertility or adverse pregnancy outcomes.

housemaid's knee.definition: A form of bursitis in which the prepatellar bursa (in front of the kneecap) becomes inflamed, typically after prolonged kneeling or direct trauma, causing anterior knee swelling, warmth, and pain. Management includes rest, ice, compression, NSAIDs; aspiration or antibiotics if septic or persistent.

housewives' eczema.definition: A historical term for irritant contact dermatitis of the hands caused by frequent wet work and exposure to soaps, detergents, and water in domestic tasks; also known as dishpan dermatitis.

howell-jolly bodies.definition: Small, round basophilic nuclear remnants of DNA within mature red blood cells, seen on peripheral smear; their presence indicates splenic dysfunction or asplenia (hyposplenism) because the spleen normally removes these nuclear remnants.

huhner test.definition: A test used in infertility workups in which cervical mucus is collected shortly after intercourse to evaluate the presence and motility of sperm in the mucus, thereby assessing cervical factors affecting fertilization.

chorionic gonadotropin.definition: A glycoprotein hormone produced by placental syncytiotrophoblasts after implantation that maintains the corpus luteum and its progesterone production in early pregnancy; clinically, it is used to confirm pregnancy and to trigger ovulation or support the luteal phase in infertility treatments.

placental lactogen.definition: A placental hormone produced by the syncytiotrophoblast with lactogenic and growth-promoting effects; it modulates maternal carbohydrate and lipid metabolism—promoting insulin resistance—to support fetal growth and stimulates pancreatic beta-cell proliferation.

human placental lactogen.definition: A placental hormone produced by the syncytiotrophoblast during pregnancy that has growth-promoting and lactogenic effects, resembling growth hormone and prolactin; it increases maternal insulin resistance to raise glucose availability for fetal growth and supports mammary gland development for lactation.

chorionic somatomammotropin.definition: A placental hormone produced by the syncytiotrophoblast, also known as human placental lactogen (hPL); it modulates maternal metabolism by increasing lipolysis and insulin resistance to raise glucose availability for the fetus and has lactogenic properties.

human chorionic somatomammotropin.definition: A placental hormone produced by the syncytiotrophoblasts during pregnancy that has growth-promoting (somatotropic) and lactogenic effects; it modulates maternal metabolism by increasing insulin resistance and lipolysis to increase fetal glucose and fatty acid availability, and helps prepare the mammary glands for lactation.

endogenous retroviruses.definition: Retroviral sequences that have become integrated into the germline genome and are inherited across generations, originating from ancient retroviral infections; most are defective and epigenetically silenced, but can influence gene regulation or development (e.g., placental formation) in some contexts.

human herpesvirus 8.definition: A double-stranded DNA herpesvirus in the Herpesviridae family (gammaherpesvirus subfamily) that establishes latent infection in B cells and endothelial cells and is the etiologic agent of Kaposi sarcoma, primary effusion lymphoma, and multicentric Castleman disease.

kaposi's sarcoma–associated herpesvirus.definition: A gammaherpesvirus of the Herpesviridae family (HHV-8); the etiologic agent of Kaposi sarcoma, capable of latent infection in B cells and endothelial cells and reactivation under immunosuppression, transmitted via body fluids.

primary effusion lymphoma.definition: An HHV-8–associated B-cell lymphoma presenting as malignant effusions in body cavities (pleural, pericardial, or peritoneal) without a detectable solid tumor mass, typically occurring in immunocompromised patients (e.g., HIV/AIDS) and often EBV-positive; an aggressive disease.

megoblastic anemia.definition: Fewer than normal healthy red blood cells in circulation, caused by a lack of folate or vitamin B12. Red cells become large and deformed, and are unable to carry oxygen efficiently.

hdcv.definition: A human diploid cell–based rabies vaccine produced in human diploid cell cultures (e.g., MRC‑5 or WI‑38); used for active immunization against rabies, given for pre‑exposure or post‑exposure prophylaxis.

rabies immune globulin.definition: A preparation of rabies virus–neutralizing antibodies derived from human (HRIG) or equine (ERIG) serum, used for passive immunization in rabies post-exposure prophylaxis to provide immediate, short-term protection while the vaccine induces active immunity; infiltrated around the wound and given intramuscularly at a separate site, with weight-based dosing (e.g., 20 IU/kg HRIG or 40 IU/kg ERIG).

hiv infection.definition: HIV infection is a chronic viral infection caused by human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), a retrovirus that targets and depletes CD4+ T lymphocytes, leading to progressive immune deficiency. If untreated, it can progress to AIDS, with severe opportunistic infections and malignancies. Transmission occurs via sexual contact, blood, or from mother to child; antiretroviral therapy controls replication but is not curative.

cd4 lymphocyte.definition: A subset of T lymphocytes that express the CD4 surface receptor; primarily helper T cells that coordinate the immune response by activating B cells, other T cells, and macrophages, and by recognizing antigens presented by MHC class II molecules; depletion or dysfunction of these cells impairs adaptive immunity (notably in HIV infection).

htlv-i.definition: A human retrovirus in the Deltaretrovirus genus that infects CD4+ T lymphocytes and is associated with adult T‑cell leukemia/lymphoma and a chronic inflammatory myelopathy presenting with spastic paraparesis; transmitted via breastfeeding, sexual contact, and exposure to infected blood (e.g., transfusion or shared needles).

htlv-ii.definition: A human T-lymphotropic virus type II is a retrovirus that infects T lymphocytes and is transmitted by blood, sexual contact, and from mother to child; most infections are asymptomatic, and disease associations are less clear than those of HTLV-1, with rare or uncertain links to neuroinflammatory or hematologic disorders.

htlv-iii.definition: A historic designation for human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1); a retrovirus that attacks CD4+ T cells, leading to immune deficiency and, if untreated, Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS).

htlv-i-associated myelopathy.definition: A chronic, progressive inflammatory spinal cord disease caused by HTLV-1 infection, presenting with slowly advancing spastic paraparesis, hyperreflexia, sensory disturbance (often proprioceptive/vibratory loss in the legs), gait impairment, and bladder dysfunction due to inflammatory demyelination of the thoracic spinal cord; diagnosis is supported by HTLV-1 serology.

h1 receptor.definition: A histamine receptor subtype that is a G protein-coupled receptor; it mediates allergic and inflammatory responses, causing vasodilation, increased vascular permeability, bronchoconstriction, and itch; antagonists block its actions and are used to treat allergies.

h2 receptor.definition: A histamine receptor subtype that is a G protein–coupled receptor located mainly on gastric parietal cells; activation by histamine increases intracellular cyclic AMP and stimulates gastric acid secretion.

h1 receptor antagonist.definition: A drug that blocks histamine at H1 receptors, thereby reducing histamine-mediated allergic symptoms (such as sneezing, itching, runny nose, and urticaria) and can be used to prevent or treat allergic rhinitis, conjunctivitis, and motion sickness; available in sedating (first-generation) and non-sedating (second-generation) forms.

h2 receptor antagonist.definition: A class of medications that block histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells, reducing gastric acid secretion; used to treat peptic ulcers, GERD, gastritis, and dyspepsia.

exogenous estrogen.definition: An estrogen introduced into the body from an external source (not produced by the body's own tissues), used in hormone replacement therapy, contraception, and other endocrine treatments.

hot flash.definition: A sudden, transient sensation of warmth spreading to the face and upper body, often with sweating, palpitations, and flushing, caused by vasomotor instability related to menopause or estrogen withdrawal.

hot flush.definition: A sudden sensation of warmth, typically affecting the face, neck, and chest, often with flushing and sweating, caused by transient vasodilation of cutaneous blood vessels; a common vasomotor symptom of menopause.

whirlpool bath.definition: A bath in which water is circulated by a pump to create jets and a swirling flow, used for hydrotherapy, muscle relaxation, and pain relief.

human bite.definition: A wound caused by another person's teeth; typically a puncture or laceration that is often contaminated with oral flora and carries a high risk of infection.

human insulin.definition: A recombinant insulin preparation identical to endogenous insulin, used to treat diabetes mellitus by promoting glucose uptake into muscle and adipose tissue and suppressing hepatic glucose production.

human growth hormone.definition: A peptide hormone produced by the anterior pituitary gland that promotes growth, cell reproduction, and metabolism; it stimulates the liver to produce insulin-like growth factors (IGFs) and has anabolic and lipolytic effects, supporting bone and tissue growth in children and maintaining tissue mass in adults.

humidification.definition: The addition of water vapor to inspired air to maintain appropriate humidity, typically during supplemental oxygen or mechanical ventilation, to prevent drying and irritation of mucous membranes and support mucociliary function.

liver fluke.definition: A parasitic flatworm (trematode) that infects the bile ducts of the liver in humans and other mammals; infection is usually acquired by ingesting metacercariae on aquatic vegetation (e.g., watercress), causing fascioliasis or related biliary disease.

hla-b27.definition: A human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class I surface protein encoded by the HLA-B27 allele; a genetic marker associated with an increased risk of seronegative spondyloarthropathies, most notably ankylosing spondylitis; presence is not diagnostic by itself.

reiter's syndrome.definition: An inflammatory arthritis that develops after an infection elsewhere in the body (most often a gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection); it is a seronegative spondyloarthropathy characterized by an asymmetric oligoarthritis, plus urethritis and conjunctivitis (the classic triad), and may be associated with mucocutaneous lesions, enthesitis, and HLA-B27 positivity.

natural killer cell.definition: A lymphocyte of the innate immune system that recognizes and eliminates virally infected cells and some tumor cells without prior exposure, primarily by releasing perforin and granzymes to induce apoptosis, and by secreting cytokines such as IFN-γ to activate other parts of the immune response.

prion disease.definition: A fatal neurodegenerative disease caused by misfolded prion proteins (PrPSc) that convert normal prion proteins (PrPC) into the abnormal form, leading to progressive brain damage and spongiform changes; can be sporadic, inherited, or acquired.

huntington's disease.definition: An autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by a CAG-repeat expansion in the HTT gene, characterized by progressive chorea, psychiatric symptoms, and cognitive decline, usually beginning in midlife with associated striatal atrophy.

hunner's ulcer.definition: A focal inflammatory lesion of the bladder mucosa seen in interstitial cystitis (painful bladder syndrome), appearing as a discrete reddened patch or ulcer on the bladder lining, sometimes with a pale center, and often associated with pelvic pain and urinary urgency/frequency.

mucopolysaccharidosis.definition: A group of inherited lysosomal storage disorders caused by deficiency of enzymes needed to degrade glycosaminoglycans, leading to accumulation of these substances in tissues and multisystem disease with skeletal abnormalities, organomegaly, and progressive cardiorespiratory and neurological involvement.

mps ii.definition: A lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of the enzyme iduronate-2-sulfatase, resulting in accumulation of dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate; X-linked recessive; presents in infancy or early childhood with coarse facial features, hepatosplenomegaly, airway obstruction, skeletal abnormalities, and often progressive neurocognitive decline; managed with enzyme replacement therapy and supportive care.

hurler syndrome.definition: A severe, autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder (mucopolysaccharidosis type I) caused by deficiency of the enzyme alpha-L-iduronidase, leading to accumulation of dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate. It presents in infancy with coarse facies, hepatosplenomegaly, corneal clouding, dysostosis multiplex, developmental delay, and progressive neurologic decline; without treatment, it can be fatal in early childhood. Treatments include hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and enzyme replacement therapy.

hurthle cell adenoma.definition: An encapsulated benign thyroid tumor composed predominantly of Hurthle (oncocytic) cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm, arising from follicular epithelium and showing no invasion of the capsule or vasculature (distinguishing it from Hurthle cell carcinoma).

hurthle cell carcinoma.definition: A malignant thyroid neoplasm arising from Hurthle (oncocytic) cells, characterized by large eosinophilic, mitochondria-rich cytoplasm. It is typically regarded as a variant of differentiated thyroid carcinoma (often classified as follicular thyroid carcinoma) and tends to be more aggressive and less iodine-avid than papillary thyroid carcinoma, with a higher risk of metastasis; treatment usually involves surgical thyroidectomy with adjuvant therapy as indicated.

progeria.definition: A rare genetic disorder characterized by accelerated, premature aging beginning in early childhood, usually due to a de novo mutation in the LMNA gene, leading to growth failure, hair loss, aged-looking skin, joint stiffness, and early cardiovascular disease with shortened lifespan.

hutchinson-gilford syndrome.definition: A rare genetic disorder characterized by accelerated aging beginning in early childhood, caused by a mutation in the LMNA gene that produces the abnormal protein progerin; features include growth delay, loss of subcutaneous fat and hair, aged-looking skin, and early-onset cardiovascular disease leading to premature mortality.

hutchinson's freckle.definition: A historical term describing a small, pigmented macule (freckle-like lesion) observed in congenital syphilis; the term is obsolete and not used in current clinical practice.

angioma serpiginosum.definition: A benign capillary vascular malformation presenting as serpiginous, erythematous to violaceous macules or patches that enlarge slowly, typically appearing in childhood or adolescence (more often in females). Lesions blanch with pressure due to dilated superficial capillaries in the papillary dermis and are usually asymptomatic; treatment is cosmetic, with laser therapy being an option.

interstitial cystitis.definition: A chronic bladder condition also known as bladder pain syndrome, characterized by bladder/pelvic pain with urinary symptoms (frequency, urgency, or nocturia) lasting at least six weeks and not explained by another condition.

hutch diverticulum.definition: A congenital outpouching of the bladder wall due to focal weakness of the detrusor muscle, typically on the posterior bladder wall near the ureteral orifices, which communicates with the bladder lumen and may be asymptomatic or predispose to urinary tract infections or hydronephrosis.

deltoid tuberosity.definition: A rough, triangular eminence on the lateral aspect of the middle third of the humeral shaft where the deltoid muscle inserts.

shoulder joint.definition: A ball-and-socket synovial joint between the head of the humerus and the glenoid fossa of the scapula (glenohumeral joint); it allows a wide range of motion but is mechanically unstable, stabilized by the rotator cuff muscles, ligaments, glenoid labrum, and joint capsule.

surgical neck.definition: A constricted region of the proximal humerus just distal to the anatomical neck, between the head/neck and the shaft; a common fracture site that can endanger the axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery.

condyles.definition: Rounded articular prominence on the end of a bone that forms part of a joint by articulating with another bone (e.g., at the end of the femur or mandible).

paromomycin sulfate.definition: An aminoglycoside antibiotic in the sulfate salt form used to treat intestinal parasitic infections (e.g., amoebiasis and giardiasis); it is poorly absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract and works locally in the gut by inhibiting protein synthesis via the 30S ribosomal subunit.

kyphosis.definition: An excessive forward curvature of the spine, most commonly in the thoracic region, producing a hunched-back posture; it can be a normal variation or due to pathology such as osteoporosis, vertebral fractures, or Scheuermann disease.

notched teeth.definition: A dental finding in which the edge of a tooth—usually an incisor—is indented to form a notch (often V-shaped); caused by wear (attrition or abrasion), trauma, or developmental enamel defects.

caudate.definition: Tail-like; an anatomical descriptor for structures that extend backward or have a tail-like projection, such as a brain structure in the basal ganglia.

lentiform.definition: Lens-shaped; in anatomy, describing a structure that resembles a lens, most often referring to a basal ganglia mass composed of the putamen and globus pallidus.

granulosus.definition: An intestinal tapeworm species that causes cystic echinococcosis (hydatid disease) in humans and livestock; infection occurs after ingesting eggs shed in dog feces, resulting in cysts in the liver, lungs, and other organs.

hydatid.definition: A fluid-filled cyst formed by the larval (metacestode) stage of Echinococcus tapeworm infection, containing protoscolices (hydatid sand) and causing cystic echinococcosis (often in liver or lungs).

mole.definition: A benign pigmented skin lesion formed by localized proliferation of melanocytes (nevus cells); typically well circumscribed and can be flat or raised, with color ranging from tan to brown to black. Most are harmless, but new or changing lesions or those with irregular borders, asymmetry, or bleeding should be evaluated for melanoma.

hydatidiform.definition: Relating to hydatid cysts; in obstetrics, describing a molar pregnancy in which placental villi become cystic and proliferate abnormally, forming grape-like vesicles with little or no viable fetus.

hydatidiform mole.definition: A gestational trophoblastic disease characterized by abnormal proliferation of placental trophoblastic tissue due to fertilization errors, resulting in a nonviable pregnancy. The complete form contains no fetal tissue and has paternal-only genetic material, while the partial form is triploid with some fetal tissue. Clinically, it presents with vaginal bleeding, an enlarged uterus for gestational age, and markedly elevated hCG; management typically involves suction curettage and serial hCG monitoring.

gestational trophoblastic disease.definition: An umbrella of placental trophoblastic disorders arising from abnormal proliferation of placental trophoblasts after conception, ranging from benign hydatidiform moles (complete or partial) to malignant neoplasms such as choriocarcinoma and other trophoblastic tumors; commonly presents with abnormal uterine bleeding and markedly elevated beta-hCG, and may metastasize.
