juvenile_rheumatoid_arthritis.definition: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory arthritis of childhood presenting with persistent joint swelling, pain, and morning stiffness in children typically under 16 years of age, lasting at least 6 weeks; it has several subtypes (systemic, oligoarticular, polyarticular) and may include systemic features such as fever or rash, with potential effects on growth and risk of uveitis; treatment aims to reduce inflammation and prevent joint damage.

still_s_disease.definition: A systemic autoinflammatory disorder presenting with daily fevers, a transient salmon-colored rash, and arthritis (systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis in children and adult-onset Still's disease in adults). It features marked inflammatory markers, leukocytosis, and often very high ferritin; diagnosis is by exclusion. Treatment typically includes NSAIDs and corticosteroids, with biologics targeting IL-1 or IL-6, and vigilance for macrophage activation syndrome.

juvenile_spinal_muscular_atrophy.definition: An inherited motor neuron disease with onset in childhood or adolescence, caused by degeneration of spinal anterior horn cells, leading to progressive symmetric proximal muscle weakness and atrophy; typically a milder form of spinal muscular atrophy with later onset (often corresponding to SMA type 3).

wohlfart_kugelberg_welander_disease.definition: A form of spinal muscular atrophy presenting in childhood or adolescence with progressive proximal limb weakness and wasting, often with normal intelligence and preserved cranial nerve function early on; typically due to SMN1 gene deletion with SMN2 copy number modifying severity.

juvenile_xanthogranuloma.definition: A benign, self-limited non-Langerhans cell histiocytic disorder of infancy and early childhood presenting as solitary or multiple yellow-orange to red-brown papules or nodules, most often on the head and neck; lesions often regress spontaneously over months to years. Histology shows dermal foamy histiocytes with Touton giant cells.

juxtaarticular.definition: Near or adjacent to a joint; located beside a joint.

juxtacrine.definition: A form of cell communication that requires direct contact between neighboring cells, where a membrane-bound signal on one cell binds to a receptor on an adjacent cell (no diffusion of soluble ligands).

kallikrein_kinin_system.definition: A proteolytic cascade that generates kinins (bradykinin and kallidin) from kininogens, mediating vasodilation, increased vascular permeability, and pain during inflammation; activated by contact factors (factor XII) via kallikrein and tightly regulated by C1 esterase inhibitor and kinases that degrade bradykinin (e.g., ACE).

kallikrein.definition: A serine protease in the kallikrein–kinin system that cleaves kininogens to release kinins (primarily bradykinin), mediating inflammation, vasodilation, and aspects of coagulation.

kallmann_syndrome.definition: A congenital form of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism caused by deficient migration of GnRH-secreting neurons, typically with anosmia or hyposmia, leading to delayed or absent puberty.

hypogonadotropic_hypogonadism.definition: A form of hypogonadism caused by inadequate secretion or action of gonadotropins (LH and FSH) from the pituitary or deficient gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulation from the hypothalamus, resulting in low sex steroid production (testosterone or estrogen) and impaired gonadal development and function.

hyposmia.definition: A reduced or diminished ability to detect odors, representing partial loss of the sense of smell.

gonadotropin_releasing_hormone.definition: A hypothalamic decapeptide that stimulates the anterior pituitary to release luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) by binding to GnRH receptors on pituitary gonadotrophs; it is released in pulses, and continuous exposure suppresses gonadotropin secretion.

luteinizing_hormone_releasing_hormone.definition: A hypothalamic decapeptide hormone that stimulates the anterior pituitary to secrete the gonadotropins—luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone—typically released in pulsatile bursts; also known as gonadotropin-releasing hormone.

interstitial_cell_stimulating_hormone.definition: A gonadotropic hormone that stimulates Leydig cells in the testes to produce testosterone; in humans it is functionally identical to luteinizing hormone (LH) and is secreted by the anterior pituitary.

kaolin.definition: A soft, white clay mineral (kaolinite), a hydrated aluminum silicate (Al2Si2O5(OH)4) used in medicine as an adsorbent in antidiarrheal preparations and as an excipient in pharmaceuticals.

kaolinosis.definition: A pneumoconiosis caused by chronic inhalation of kaolin (china clay) dust, leading to inflammatory nodules and interstitial fibrosis in the lungs of workers exposed to kaolin.

kaopectate.definition: An over-the-counter oral antidiarrheal product that historically contained kaolin clay and pectin, acting as an adsorbent to bind liquids and toxins in the gut and slow stool passage; some formulations use bismuth subsalicylate (similar to Pepto-Bismol).

pectin.definition: A soluble plant polysaccharide dietary fiber derived from plant cell walls (notably citrus fruits and apples). It is a heterogeneous polymer rich in α-(1→4)-linked galacturonic acid units, often partially methyl-esterified and containing neutral-sugar side chains (rhamnose, arabinose, galactose). It forms gels in the presence of sugar and acid and is used as a thickening, gelling, and stabilizing agent in foods and pharmaceuticals; as dietary fiber it aids stool formation and can modestly affect cholesterol.

kaposi's disease.definition: A vascular neoplasm caused by human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) infection, characterized by violaceous skin lesions that may involve mucosa and internal organs; commonly occurs in immunocompromised individuals, such as those with HIV/AIDS or post-transplant immunosuppression.

kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus.definition: A gammaherpesvirus (human herpesvirus 8, HHV-8) that is the etiologic agent of Kaposi sarcoma; it establishes latent infection in endothelial and B cells and can reactivate, with transmission through body fluids such as saliva and sexual contact.

kappa light chain.definition: A type of light chain of immunoglobulins produced by plasma cells; it pairs with a heavy chain to form an antibody, and excess free kappa chains in serum or urine can indicate a monoclonal plasma cell disorder.

kappa chain.definition: A type of immunoglobulin light chain; one of the two light-chain types (kappa and lambda) that pair with heavy chains to form a complete antibody. Produced by B cells; exists as a free light chain in serum or urine and is used in evaluating plasma cell disorders such as multiple myeloma.

karaya powder.definition: A natural hydrocolloid powder derived from karaya gum (from Sterculia species); it swells in water to form a viscous mucilage and is used as a thickening, binding, and suspending agent in pharmaceutical formulations and as a demulcent in oral preparations.

sterculia urens.definition: A tree species in the Malvaceae family native to India, from which karaya gum is obtained; the gum is a natural polysaccharide used as a thickener, emulsifier, suspending agent, and demulcent in foods, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics.

paranasal sinusitis.definition: Inflammation of the paranasal sinuses (air-filled spaces around the nasal cavity), usually due to infection or inflammatory disease, presenting with facial pain or pressure, nasal congestion and discharge, and sometimes fever; classified by duration as acute, subacute, or chronic.

transposed viscera.definition: A congenital arrangement in which the major internal organs are positioned on the opposite side of the body from their normal locations; commonly refers to situs inversus (complete mirror-image reversal) or to partial transposition of some organs.

karyolymph.definition: The semifluid substance inside the cell nucleus that surrounds chromatin and constitutes the nucleus’s fluid content (nuclear sap).

karyolysis.definition: Dissolution of the cell nucleus during necrosis caused by enzymatic digestion of chromatin, resulting in loss of staining and disappearance of the nucleus.

karyocyte.definition: A nucleated cell; any cell that contains a cell nucleus, as opposed to anucleate cells like mature red blood cells.

karyogamy.definition: The fusion of two haploid nuclei to form a single diploid nucleus during sexual reproduction, following plasmogamy.

karyogenesis.definition: The origin or formation of a cell nucleus; historically used to describe the evolutionary origin of the eukaryotic nucleus from a prokaryotic ancestor.

karyogenetic.definition: Relating to the origin or formation of the cell nucleus; nucleogenesis.

kasabach method.definition: A consumptive coagulopathy associated with certain vascular tumors (e.g., kaposiform hemangioendothelioma or tufted angioma) in which platelets and clotting factors are sequestered and activated within the tumor, causing severe thrombocytopenia and hypofibrinogenemia with resulting bleeding.

kazanjian's operation.definition: I can’t locate a reliable definition for “Kazanjian’s operation” in standard medical dictionaries. Could you provide more context (medical specialty, body region, or alternate spelling) so I can search further or offer a precise definition?

portoenterostomy.definition: A surgical procedure to create a biliary-enteric drainage pathway by connecting the liver at the porta hepatis to the small intestine (usually jejunum) to drain bile, typically performed for biliary atresia (the Kasai procedure).

kedani fever.definition: Not found in standard medical dictionaries for this term. It may be a misspelling or a regional/rare term. If you can share alternate spellings or more context (region, symptoms, related illnesses), I can help locate a definition or provide a closely related diagnosis.

kawasaki disease.definition: An uncommon disease of children that causes blood vessels to swell.

mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome.definition: An acute, self-limited pediatric vasculitis presenting with fever for at least 5 days and mucocutaneous findings (conjunctival injection, oral mucous membrane changes such as strawberry tongue and red lips, polymorphous rash), extremity changes (red/swollen hands and feet), and cervical lymphadenopathy; without treatment it can lead to coronary artery aneurysms. Management typically includes intravenous immunoglobulin and high-dose aspirin.

kayser-fleischer ring.definition: A copper-containing pigmented ring at the peripheral cornea (Descemet's membrane) seen on slit-lamp examination, characteristic of Wilson disease (copper metabolism disorder).

stored-energy foot prosthesis.definition: An energy-storing prosthetic foot that temporarily stores mechanical energy during stance and releases it during late stance to aid forward propulsion, typically via carbon-fiber or other compliant materials.

keel.definition: A prominent, blade-like ridge or projection on a bone; in birds, the keel (keel bone) is the elongated ventral projection of the sternum to which the flight muscles attach.

kegel exercises.definition: A regimen of voluntary contractions and relaxations of the pelvic floor muscles to strengthen them and improve urinary control, pelvic organ support, and sexual function.

retinal arterioles.definition: Small branches of the central retinal artery that supply the inner retina; they have smooth muscle in their walls allowing vasoconstriction and vasodilation to regulate retinal blood flow.

limbal border.definition: The corneoscleral junction around the periphery of the cornea; the transition zone between transparent cornea and opaque sclera, containing the limbal epithelium and the stem cell niche that maintains corneal epithelial regeneration.

ophthalmoplegia.definition: Paralysis or weakness of the extraocular muscles, resulting in restricted eye movement and diplopia; commonly due to cranial nerve III, IV, or VI palsies or other neuromuscular/vascular conditions.

pigmentary degeneration of the retina.definition: A group of inherited retinal dystrophies characterized by progressive degeneration of photoreceptors (primarily rods) with secondary dysfunction of the retinal pigment epithelium, leading to night blindness and progressive peripheral vision loss; funduscopic exam classically shows bone-spicule pigmentation, attenuation of retinal vessels, and optic disc pallor.

epitheliomas.definition: Neoplasms arising from epithelial cells; in dermatology the term has historically described skin tumors of epithelial origin, especially basal cell carcinoma, which is malignant with local invasion and rare metastasis.

hemangioma-thrombocytopenia syndrome.definition: A consumptive coagulopathy seen in certain infant vascular tumors where the tumor traps platelets and consumes coagulation factors, causing severe thrombocytopenia and hypofibrinogenemia (Kasabach–Merritt phenomenon).

xeroderma pigmentosum.definition: A rare autosomal recessive genetic disorder characterized by extreme sensitivity to ultraviolet radiation due to defects in nucleotide excision repair, leading to severe sun sensitivity, early-onset pigmentary changes, and a markedly increased risk of skin cancers; neurological abnormalities may occur in some individuals.

mitochondrial dna deletions.definition: Mitochondrial DNA deletions are losses of contiguous segments of the mitochondrial genome (mtDNA) that remove multiple genes essential for the mitochondrial respiratory chain, causing mitochondrial dysfunction; the clinical impact varies with heteroplasmy levels and tissue distribution and they can arise de novo in individuals with sporadic mtDNA deletion syndromes.

ragged red fibers.definition: A histopathologic feature of mitochondrial myopathies in which subsarcolemmal accumulations of abnormal mitochondria give irregular, ragged red staining of muscle fibers on Gomori trichrome stain.

liver cirrhosis.definition: A late, irreversible stage of chronic liver disease in which widespread fibrosis with regenerative nodules distorts hepatic architecture, leading to impaired liver function and portal hypertension; commonly due to chronic alcohol use, viral hepatitis, or metabolic disorders.

kellgrens_syndrome.definition: Not a recognized medical term. Do you want definitions for a radiographic osteoarthritis grading system described by Kellgren and Lawrence or for a chromosomal disorder in males with an extra X chromosome?

proximal_interphalangeal.definition: A hinge-type synovial joint between the proximal and middle phalanges of the fingers and toes, enabling flexion and extension.

first_metatarsophalangeal.definition: A synovial joint between the head of the first metatarsal and the proximal phalanx of the hallux (big toe); a biaxial joint that primarily allows flexion and extension of the great toe, with some abduction and adduction, and is essential for push-off during gait.

metatarsophalangeal.definition: Joints between the heads of the metatarsal bones and the proximal phalanges of the toes; these synovial, condyloid joints allow toe flexion and extension, with limited abduction and adduction.

knees.definition: Paired hinge joints between the thigh and lower leg, formed by the distal femur, proximal tibia, and the patella; they allow flexion and extension (with slight rotation when flexed) and bear most body weight, stabilized by ligaments (ACL, PCL, MCL, LCL) and menisci.

rheumatoid_factor.definition: An antibody found in about 85% of people with rheumatoid arthritis; also appears in other diseases and sometimes in healthy people.

rheumatoid_nodules.definition: A firm, non-tender subcutaneous nodule seen in some people with rheumatoid arthritis, typically over extensor surfaces such as the elbows and forearms. It comprises a granulomatous lesion with central fibrinoid necrosis (necrobiosis) surrounded by palisading histiocytes and inflammatory cells; it is associated with seropositive RA and longer disease duration, and may ulcerate or be linked to vasculitis.

erosive_osteoarthritis.definition: An inflammatory, destructive subset of osteoarthritis characterized by focal joint erosions on imaging, most often in the hand interphalangeal joints, with pain and swelling that progress more rapidly than typical osteoarthritis.

kelly_clamp.definition: A Kelly clamp is a heavy, straight or curved surgical hemostat with transverse serrations and a ratcheted handle, used to clamp large vessels or tissue to achieve hemostasis during operations.

stress_incontinence.definition: An involuntary leakage of urine that occurs with activities that increase intra-abdominal pressure (e.g., coughing, sneezing, lifting, exercising) due to pelvic floor weakening and loss of urethral support.

kellys_pad.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard medical references, and therefore has no established medical definition.

keloidal.definition: Relating to a keloid; a raised, firm scar that extends beyond the original wound margins due to excessive, disorganized collagen deposition during wound healing.

keloid_scar.definition: A raised scar that grows beyond the boundaries of the original wound due to excessive collagen formation during healing; it is benign but can be itchy, tender, or painful and tends to recur after treatment or excision.

keratin.definition: A protein and the major component of the cuticle and cortex layers of hair; the same protein is found in nails, feathers, claws, and hooves.

keratinocyte.definition: An epidermal cell that synthesizes keratin and constitutes the predominant cell type of the epidermis; it originates in the basal layer, proliferates, and differentiates as it moves toward the surface to form the protective stratum corneum, thereby maintaining the skin barrier and participating in wound healing.

keratoconjunctivitis_sicca.definition: A condition in which tear production is insufficient or tears evaporate too quickly, resulting in dryness of the cornea and conjunctiva with irritation, burning or gritty sensation, and possible fluctuating vision.

keratopathy.definition: An umbrella term for diseases of the cornea (the clear front surface of the eye), including degenerations, dystrophies, ulcers, and opacities.

keratoacanthoma.definition: A rapidly growing, dome-shaped skin tumor with a central keratin-filled crater, most often on sun-exposed skin of older adults; clinically resembles squamous cell carcinoma but is often self-limited or effectively treated with excision.

keratoacanthomata.definition: A group of keratoacanthoma lesions; rapidly growing crateriform skin nodules, usually on sun-exposed skin of older adults, with a central keratin-filled crater. They are generally considered benign, self-limiting proliferations of squamous epithelium that often involute over months; diagnosis requires histology to distinguish them from squamous cell carcinoma, and management ranges from observation to surgical excision depending on size, number, and malignancy risk.

keratocyst.definition: A cyst containing keratin debris; a keratin-filled cystic lesion, such as an epidermoid (keratin-filled) skin cyst or an odontogenic keratocyst of the jaw.

keratosis.definition: A skin condition characterized by abnormal keratinization of epidermal cells, producing a rough, thickened, or keratinized patch or growth on the skin.

actinic_keratosis.definition: A premalignant skin lesion resulting from chronic ultraviolet exposure, characterized by rough, scaly or keratotic patches on sun-exposed areas that may progress to squamous cell carcinoma if untreated.

keratosis_pilaris.definition: A common, benign skin condition characterized by small, rough, keratin-filled papules around hair follicles, typically on the upper arms and thighs; caused by abnormal keratinization and follicular plugging, often associated with dry skin and sometimes improving with regular moisturization.

keratosis_senilis.definition: A common, benign epidermal skin lesion seen mainly in older adults, presenting as well-demarcated, pigmented, waxy or verrucous plaques with a distinctive “stuck-on” appearance; usually asymptomatic but may itch or irritate; has no malignant potential, though changes or uncertainty may warrant biopsy.

seborrheic_keratosis.definition: A common benign skin growth presenting as well-demarcated, pigmented, waxy, "stuck-on" plaques, most often on the trunk of older adults; benign with no malignant potential; treatment is optional and can be for cosmetic reasons (e.g., cryotherapy, curettage, or electrocautery).

keratosis_follicularis.definition: A rare autosomal dominant genodermatosis caused by mutations in the ATP2A2 gene encoding the SERCA2 calcium pump, characterized by greasy, keratotic papules in seborrheic areas (trunk and proximal limbs), often with nail abnormalities and mucosal involvement.

dendritic_keratitis.definition: A corneal infection caused by herpes simplex virus, characterized by branched dendrite-shaped epithelial ulcers on fluorescein staining; presents with eye pain, redness, tearing, and photophobia and is treated with topical antiviral therapy (e.g., ganciclovir, trifluridine) and, in some cases, oral antivirals.

interstitial_keratitis.definition: A nonulcerative inflammatory disease of the corneal stroma (stromal keratitis) characterized by stromal edema and opacity with neovascularization, leading to scarring and reduced vision; commonly associated with congenital or other forms of syphilis.

bitots_spots.definition: Foamy patches of keratinized conjunctival epithelium on the bulbar conjunctiva (often in the fornix), caused by vitamin A deficiency; an early manifestation of xerophthalmia.

keratomalacia.definition: A severe, potentially blinding ocular condition caused by vitamin A deficiency, in which the cornea softens and ulcerates and may progress to perforation.

vitamin_a_deficiency.definition: A lack of vitamin A causing impaired night vision and ocular surface drying (xerophthalmia), including Bitot spots, with an increased risk of infections; if untreated, it can progress to corneal damage and blindness.

night_blindness.definition: Difficulty seeing in low light or darkness due to impaired retinal rod function; commonly caused by vitamin A deficiency or retinal degenerative diseases (e.g., retinitis pigmentosa), and can be worsened by cataracts.

descemet_membrane.definition: A thin, acellular basement membrane secreted by the corneal endothelium, forming the posterior boundary between the stroma and the endothelial cell layer; provides structural support and helps maintain corneal hydration; thickens with age.

corneal_graft.definition: A surgical transplant in which diseased or damaged corneal tissue is replaced with healthy donor tissue from a donor cornea, performed to restore corneal transparency and vision. It can be full-thickness (penetrating keratoplasty) or partial-thickness (lamellar keratoplasty).

corneal_transplant.definition: A surgical procedure in which damaged or diseased corneal tissue is replaced with healthy donor tissue (corneal allograft) to restore vision or relieve pain; it can be full-thickness (penetrating keratoplasty) or partial-thickness (lamellar keratoplasty).

corneal_epithelium.definition: Outermost, non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium covering the cornea; provides a protective barrier against mechanical injury and microbial invasion, helps maintain tear film stability, and regenerates rapidly from limbal stem cells anchored to a basement membrane over Bowman's layer.

keratectomy.definition: A procedure in which a laser is used to correct vision problems by reshaping the cornea.

keratome.definition: A surgical knife blade designed to cut keratinized or corneal tissue; commonly used in ophthalmology to incise the cornea for procedures such as keratoplasty or for preparing corneal flaps.

keratoepithelioplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair or reconstruct the corneal surface by grafting or rearranging epithelial tissue (often conjunctival or limbal epithelium) onto the cornea to restore a smooth, intact surface after epithelial defects or ulcers.

keratogenesis.definition: The formation of keratin, including maturation of keratinocytes and production of keratin proteins that leads to the keratinized outer layer of skin (keratinization or cornification).

keratogenic.definition: Causing keratin production or keratinization in epithelial cells.

keratogenous.definition: Producing or forming keratin; keratin-forming, relating to keratin production (keratinization).

keratoglobus.definition: A rare bilateral corneal ectasia in which the entire cornea becomes thinned and globularly protrudes outward, giving a globe-like cornea and a high risk of spontaneous rupture from minor trauma; it may be associated with connective-tissue disorders.

megalocornea.definition: A congenital, nonprogressive enlargement of the cornea with an abnormally large corneal diameter (typically >12 mm in infancy). The cornea is usually clear with a deep anterior chamber and normal corneal thickness; vision may be normal or affected by refractive error, and glaucoma risk can be increased in some cases.

kerion.definition: A boggy, inflammatory mass on the scalp caused by dermatophyte infection (tinea capitis); characterized by purulent discharge, crusting, alopecia, and regional lymphadenopathy, often painful and requiring systemic antifungal therapy.

tinea_capitis.definition: An itchy condition of the scalp caused by a fungal infection. Also known as ringworm.

kenalog.definition: A brand-name corticosteroid (triamcinolone acetonide) used to treat inflammatory and allergic conditions; available in topical, intralesional, intramuscular, and intra-articular formulations.

kent_bundle.definition: An abnormal accessory conduction pathway between the atria and ventricles that bypasses the AV node, leading to preexcitation of the ventricles and potential tachyarrhythmias, classically associated with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

wolff_parkinson_white_syndrome.definition: A congenital pre-excitation syndrome caused by an accessory atrioventricular conduction pathway (most often the bundle of Kent) that bypasses the AV node, leading to episodes of tachyarrhythmias such as paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, and an ECG pattern of a short PR interval with a delta wave and widened QRS; there is a risk of rapid conduction during atrial fibrillation and, rarely, sudden cardiac death.

accessory_pathway.definition: An abnormal accessory conduction pathway between the atria and ventricles that bypasses the AV node, causing ventricular pre-excitation and enabling certain tachyarrhythmias (e.g., Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome).

conduction_system.definition: A system of specialized cardiac tissue that generates and propagates electrical impulses to coordinate the heart's rhythm and contractions, comprising the SA node, AV node, bundle of His, bundle branches, and Purkinje fibers.

fibrous_ring.definition: A ring-shaped structure of dense fibrous connective tissue that encircles or stabilizes an organ, providing support and containment; for example, the tough outer ring surrounding the nucleus pulposus of an intervertebral disc.

tricuspid_valve.definition: A three-flap valve that sits between the right atrium and the right ventricle.

down_syndrome.definition: A chromosomal disorder caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21), leading to intellectual disability and distinct facial features, with increased risk for congenital heart defects and other health issues.

reiter_syndrome.definition: Joint problems triggered by bacterial or viral infection elsewhere in the body.

sjogren_syndrome.definition: Chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by lymphocytic infiltration and destruction of exocrine glands, especially lacrimal and salivary glands, leading to dry eyes (keratoconjunctivitis sicca) and dry mouth (xerostomia); may occur alone (primary) or with other autoimmune diseases (secondary); managed with artificial tears, saliva substitutes, and, in some cases, systemic immunosuppressants.

marseilles_fever.definition: A historical label for a febrile illness associated with outbreaks in Marseille; not a specific, currently recognized disease in modern medicine and its usage varies in older literature.

kenya_fever.definition: An informal label for fever obtained in Kenya; not a specific disease, but most often due to malaria in travelers or residents, though other endemic febrile illnesses (e.g., typhoid, dengue, chikungunya) can also occur.

celiac_syndrome.definition: A chronic autoimmune enteropathy triggered by dietary gluten in genetically predisposed individuals, leading to small intestinal villous atrophy and malabsorption; commonly presents with diarrhea, weight loss, abdominal pain, and anemia, and improves with a strict gluten-free diet.

puncta.definition: A small opening or orifice; in anatomy, it commonly refers to the tear-duct openings on the inner margins of the eyelids (lacrimal puncta) that drain tears into the lacrimal drainage system.

sister_kennys_treatment.definition: A historical nonoperative treatment for poliomyelitis developed by Sister Elizabeth Kenny, emphasizing warm applications, massage, and gradual, active exercise to maintain or restore muscle function and prevent contractures, without early immobilization.

kenny_treatment.definition: Not found in standard medical dictionaries. Please provide more context or correct spelling.

donor_cornea.definition: A corneal tissue donated by a deceased person for transplantation to restore or improve vision by replacing a diseased or damaged recipient cornea; the tissue undergoes screening and processing to ensure safety.

intralesional_corticosteroid_injection.definition: A procedure in which a corticosteroid solution is injected directly into a skin lesion to reduce local inflammation and immune activity, thereby shrinking the lesion and alleviating symptoms; commonly used for keloids, hypertrophic scars, warts, and other inflammatory dermatoses (often with triamcinolone acetonide); potential adverse effects include skin atrophy, hypopigmentation, telangiectasia, and pain at the injection site.

intralesional_corticosteroid_injections.definition: Direct injection of a corticosteroid suspension into a skin or mucosal lesion to reduce local inflammation and immune activity, causing the lesion to flatten or shrink; commonly used for keloids, hypertrophic scars, and certain inflammatory dermatoses (often triamcinolone acetonide).

silicone_gel.definition: A silicone-based gel (typically containing polydimethylsiloxane) that forms a semi-occlusive layer on the skin to maintain moisture; used in wound care and scar management to improve scar appearance and reduce scar formation.

gas_permeable_contact_lenses.definition: Rigid, oxygen-permeable contact lenses made from hard plastics (often silicone-containing polymers) that allow oxygen to reach the cornea; they provide sharp optical quality and durability, and are used for refractive correction and certain corneal conditions (e.g., keratoconus).

keratophakia.definition: A surgical procedure in which a donor corneal lenticule is implanted into the recipient's cornea (within the stroma) to alter its curvature and refractive power, typically to correct hyperopia by steepening the central cornea; an older, largely experimental refractive technique.

keratorhexis.definition: Rupture of the cornea; a tear or break in corneal tissue usually due to trauma, potentially causing leakage of aqueous humor and requiring urgent ophthalmologic evaluation.

keratorrhexis.definition: Rupture of the cornea; a full-thickness tear through the corneal stroma, usually due to trauma or severe corneal disease, potentially compromising ocular integrity.

keratomycosis.definition: A fungal infection of the cornea (mycotic keratitis), typically after trauma or contact lens use, causing corneal ulcers and inflammation that can threaten vision.

erythema_multiforme.definition: An acute immune-mediated mucocutaneous reaction characterized by symmetric, target-shaped skin lesions (often on the extremities) with possible mucosal involvement; commonly triggered by infections (notably herpes simplex virus) or certain medications and usually self-limited.

callus.definition: Hardened, thick skin that forms after repeated friction; often found on hands and the bottom of feet.

refractive_error.definition: A defect in the eye's ability to focus light on the retina, causing blurred vision; it includes myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism, and presbyopia, and is corrected with glasses, contact lenses, or refractive surgery.

keratoconus.definition: A progressive thinning and cone-shaped protrusion of the cornea, causing irregular astigmatism and visual distortion; typically begins in adolescence or early adulthood and may be managed with glasses or contact lenses, corneal cross-linking to halt progression, or corneal transplantation in advanced cases.

dariers_disease.definition: A rare autosomal dominant genodermatosis caused by ATP2A2 mutations encoding the SERCA2 calcium pump, leading to defective keratinocyte adhesion (acantholysis) and greasy, keratotic papules/plaques primarily in seborrheic areas, often with nail changes and onset in adolescence.

kerley lines.definition: Thin linear markings on chest radiographs representing thickened interlobular septa due to interstitial edema or lymphatic congestion, most commonly from congestive heart failure.

interstitial infiltrate.definition: An accumulation of inflammatory cells and/or fluid within the interstitial (supportive) tissue of the lung, producing reticular or hazy opacities on imaging and indicating interstitial inflammation, edema, infection, or fibrosis.

pleural lymphatic engorgement.definition: Engorgement (dilation) of the pleural lymphatic vessels, usually due to obstruction or increased lymph production within the thorax, leading to impaired lymph drainage and potentially pleural effusion, including chylous effusion when lymphatic leakage occurs.

kerma.definition: Kinetic Energy Released per unit Mass; the initial energy transferred from ionizing radiation to charged particles in a mass of matter, per unit mass, at the point of interest, before subsequent energy transport; commonly expressed in grays (Gy) and used in radiometry/dosimetry (e.g., air kerma).

kernig’s sign.definition: A physical examination finding indicating meningeal irritation; performed with the patient supine, the hip flexed to 90 degrees and the knee flexed, and then the knee is extended—the presence of pain or resistance to extension is a positive result, suggesting meningitis or other causes of meningeal irritation (e.g., subarachnoid hemorrhage).

kerosene poisoning.definition: Toxicity from exposure to kerosene, a hydrocarbon fuel, typically via ingestion or inhalation (less commonly dermal contact), causing airway irritation and, if aspirated, chemical pneumonitis or pneumonia; severe exposure may cause central nervous system depression.

ketalar.definition: A dissociative anesthetic agent that acts as an NMDA receptor antagonist, producing anesthesia, analgesia, amnesia, and dissociation; administered intravenously or intramuscularly for induction or maintenance of anesthesia, with potential side effects including hypertension, tachycardia, emergence delirium, and vivid dreams.

ketek.definition: A brand-name antibiotic (telithromycin), a ketolide macrolide used to treat certain bacterial infections; its use is limited by the risk of severe liver injury.

telithromycin.definition: A ketolide antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit; used to treat certain respiratory tract infections but carries risk of severe liver injury and worsening myasthenia gravis; its use is restricted.

17-ketoandrosterone.definition: A keto-derivative of androsterone, i.e., a C17-ketosteroid formed during androgen metabolism; used as a biomarker in steroid metabolite profiling.

17-ketoetiocholanolone.definition: A ketone metabolite of etiocholanolone, a steroid produced in androgen metabolism; used as a marker in urinary steroid profiling and anti-doping testing.

ketogenesis.definition: A hepatic metabolic process that converts acetyl-CoA derived from fatty acid oxidation into ketone bodies (acetoacetate, beta-hydroxybutyrate, and acetone) during periods of low carbohydrate intake or fasting, to provide energy for extrahepatic tissues such as the brain.

ketogenic amino acid.definition: A ketogenic amino acid is an amino acid whose catabolism yields acetyl-CoA or acetoacetate (ketone bodies) and cannot be converted into glucose.

ketogenic diet.definition: A high-fat, adequate-protein, very low-carbohydrate diet that induces ketosis, a metabolic state in which the body uses fat-derived ketone bodies rather than glucose for energy.

17-ketosteroids.definition: Urinary metabolites of androgens excreted in urine (e.g., androsterone and etiocholanolone); used to estimate androgen production from the adrenal glands and gonads and to screen for adrenal or gonadal disorders.

17-ks test.definition: A nonparametric statistical method used to determine whether a sample comes from a specified continuous distribution (one-sample) or whether two samples come from the same distribution (two-sample). It compares the empirical distribution functions of the data and uses the maximum absolute difference between them as the test statistic, yielding a p-value under the null hypothesis of identical distributions. It does not assume a particular distribution and is useful for assessing distributional similarity in medical data, though its sensitivity depends on sample size and differences in the distribution tails.

ketotic.definition: Pertaining to ketosis; characterized by elevated ketone bodies in the blood or urine, as seen in fasting, starvation, or uncontrolled diabetes.

ketosis-prone diabetes.definition: Ketosis-prone diabetes is an adult-onset diabetes phenotype that presents with diabetic ketoacidosis or significant ketosis at diagnosis, often without autoimmune markers, and with variable beta-cell function; many patients can discontinue insulin after the acute phase and manage long-term glycemia with non-insulin therapies, resembling type 2 diabetes over time.

ketosis-resistant diabetes.definition: Not a standard medical term. If used, it describes a diabetes phenotype in which ketosis or diabetic ketoacidosis is uncommon or absent—typically seen in type 2 diabetes or other forms with preserved insulin production—and it lacks formal diagnostic criteria.

ketotifen.definition: A non-sedating H1 antihistamine with mast cell–stabilizing properties used to prevent and treat allergic conditions such as allergic rhinitis and conjunctivitis, and as a prophylactic in asthma; available orally (ketotifen fumarate) and as ophthalmic drops.

ketoprofen.definition: A nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) of the propionic acid class that inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing prostaglandin synthesis to relieve pain, inflammation, and fever; available in oral and topical formulations for musculoskeletal pain and related conditions.

kikuchi’s lymphadenitis.definition: A benign, self-limited form of necrotizing lymphadenitis (Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease) that most often presents with fever and tender cervical lymphadenopathy; histology shows necrotizing lymphadenitis with karyorrhectic debris and an absence of neutrophils, with a predominance of histiocytes and CD8+ T cells, usually affecting young women and resolving over weeks to months.

kikuchi’s disease.definition: A benign, self-limited lymphadenitis (Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease) presenting mainly with painful cervical lymphadenopathy and fever; histology shows necrotizing lymphadenitis with karyorrhexis and no neutrophilic infiltration; typically affects young women and resolves in weeks to months with supportive care, after ruling out lymphoma or TB.

kielland’s forceps.definition: A type of obstetric forceps used to rotate the fetal head during vaginal delivery in malpositions, especially occipito-posterior or transverse lie. They have narrow, curved, often fenestrated blades and a mechanism that allows controlled rotation with traction to facilitate delivery while minimizing pelvic soft-tissue injury.

kielland’s rotation.definition: A manoeuvre in instrumental vaginal delivery using Kielland forceps to rotate the fetal head from a malposition (usually occipitoposterior or transverse) to occipitoanterior, enabling passage through the birth canal (typically about a 90-degree rotation).

kiesselbach’s plexus.definition: An arterial network on the anterior inferior nasal septum (Little's area) where branches from the anterior ethmoidal, sphenopalatine, greater palatine, and superior labial arteries anastomose; a common source of anterior epistaxis.

rickettsialpox.definition: An acute febrile illness caused by the rickettsial organism Rickettsia akari, transmitted to humans by mites that infest house mice; it begins with a bite-site papule that becomes a vesicle or pustule, often followed by fever, malaise, headache, and a self-limited maculopapular rash.

kew gardens spotted fever.definition: Not a standard or widely used current medical term. It likely refers to a historical or regional name for a tickborne spotted fever syndrome (a rickettsial disease) transmitted by arthropods, typically presenting with fever, headache, myalgias, and a rash that may be petechial; some forms may feature an eschar at the bite site. If you meant a specific well-known disease, such as Rocky Mountain spotted fever (Rickettsia rickettsii) or Mediterranean spotted fever (Rickettsia conorii), I can provide a precise definition for that.

wilms’ tumor.definition: A malignant kidney tumor of childhood (nephroblastoma) arising from embryonal renal tissue; typically presents as a painless abdominal mass and may be associated with hypertension, hematuria, or congenital syndromes, and is treated with nephrectomy followed by multiagent chemotherapy, with radiotherapy used in selected cases. Prognosis depends on stage and histology.

adenocarcinoma of the renal parenchyma.definition: A malignant gland-forming tumor arising from renal tubular epithelial cells within the kidney parenchyma; a rare histologic variant of renal cell carcinoma characterized by adenocarcinoma-like glandular differentiation.

radical nephrectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove the entire kidney along with surrounding perinephric fat and fascia, and often the ipsilateral adrenal gland, typically performed for kidney cancer.

lymph node dissection.definition: An operation in which one or more regional lymph nodes are removed and examined histologically to determine whether cancer has spread; it may be performed for staging and, in some cases, to reduce nodal tumor burden.

nephroureterectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove a kidney and the entire ureter, typically including a cuff of bladder tissue at the ureteral insertion, usually performed for upper tract urothelial carcinoma; can be done via open, laparoscopic, or robotic approaches.

kidney disease.definition: A broad term for conditions that damage the kidneys or impair their ability to filter waste, regulate fluids and electrolytes, and maintain acid-base balance; includes chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, glomerular diseases, and nephritis.

iv pyelography.definition: An imaging study in which intravenous administration of iodinated contrast allows visualization of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder on X-ray to evaluate anatomy and function and to identify obstruction, stones, or other urinary tract abnormalities.

nephrons.definition: The microscopic functional unit of the kidney that filters blood to form urine; each nephron consists of a renal corpuscle (glomerulus and Bowman's capsule) and a tubular system (proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule, collecting duct) that reabsorbs water and solutes and secretes waste.

renal tubules.definition: Microscopic tubules of the kidney (the proximal tubule, loop of Henle, and distal tubule) that modify glomerular filtrate by reabsorbing water and solutes and secreting waste products, thereby forming urine.

intravenous fluids.definition: An IV fluid is a sterile solution infused into a vein to restore or maintain intravascular volume and electrolyte balance, correct dehydration, or serve as a vehicle for delivering medications; it is typically categorized into crystalloids (e.g., normal saline, lactated Ringer's) and colloids.

beta-hydroxybutyric acid.definition: A four-carbon hydroxy fatty acid; one of the ketone bodies produced by the liver during fasting or carbohydrate restriction, existing mainly as its anion (β-hydroxybutyrate) at physiological pH and serving as an energy source for peripheral tissues.

acetonaenemia.definition: Elevated levels of acetone in the bloodstream, a ketone body produced during fatty acid oxidation; commonly reflects ketosis and is seen in diabetic ketoacidosis, fasting, or ketogenic states; may contribute to metabolic acidosis and can be detected in blood or breath.

17-ketosteroid.definition: A class of urinary steroid metabolites containing a 17-ketone group, derived from androgens; commonly measured to assess androgen production and adrenal function.

17-ketosteroids test.definition: A laboratory test that measures the urinary excretion of 17-ketosteroid metabolites (e.g., androsterone and etiocholanolone) over a 24-hour period to assess endogenous androgen production from the adrenal glands and gonads; historically used to evaluate androgen excess and screen for androgen-secreting tumors.

kinesthesia.definition: The sense that detects limb and body movement and position, providing conscious awareness of motion and orientation, mediated by proprioceptors in muscles, tendons, and joints.

kleine-levin syndrome.definition: A rare sleep disorder characterized by recurrent, prolonged episodes of hypersomnia (often lasting days to weeks) with concomitant cognitive and behavioral changes (e.g., confusion, disinhibition, derealization, hyperphagia, hypersexuality); patients are typically asymptomatic between episodes; onset usually in adolescence; etiology unknown and treatment is supportive.

waardenburg syndrome.definition: An inherited syndrome characterized by congenital sensorineural deafness and pigmentary anomalies of the hair, skin, and eyes, often with dystopia canthorum; four subtypes (I–IV) with varying features and gene causes (PAX3, MITF, SOX10, EDNRB/EDN3), usually inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern with variable expressivity; Type IV is associated with Hirschsprung disease.

klein-waardenburg syndrome.definition: A form of Waardenburg syndrome (type III) involving pigmentary abnormalities of the skin, hair, and eyes, congenital sensorineural deafness, and musculoskeletal limb anomalies; typically caused by mutations in the PAX3 gene and inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.

ziehl-neelsen acid-fast stain.definition: A staining technique for identifying acid-fast bacteria, especially mycobacteria. It uses carbol fuchsin as the primary stain with heat to penetrate waxy cell walls, followed by decolorization with acid-alcohol and counterstaining; acid-fast organisms retain the red/pink color while non–acid-fast cells take up the counterstain.

carbol-fuchsin stain.definition: A phenol-containing red dye used as the primary stain in acid-fast staining (e.g., Ziehl-Neelsen); it penetrates waxy mycobacterial cell walls and is retained after acid-alcohol decolorization, staining acid-fast organisms red/pink.

skeletal traction.definition: An orthopedic method in which pins or wires are inserted into bone and external weights apply continuous traction to pull the fractured fragments into alignment and maintain reduction, often used when gradual reduction is needed or skin traction is inadequate.

kirklin staging system.definition: An ordinal clinical framework used to categorize the severity and complexity of cardiac disease or its postoperative status into discrete stages to guide prognosis and management; originally described by Kirklin and colleagues in cardiac surgery literature.

occult neuroblastoma.definition: A neuroblastoma that is not clinically or radiographically detectable at presentation; the tumor remains hidden and is identified only after further investigation, often due to metastasis or paraneoplastic signs.

myoclonic encephalopathy of childhood.definition: An epileptic encephalopathy in children characterized by frequent myoclonic seizures accompanied by global developmental delay or regression; EEG typically shows diffuse or multifocal epileptiform discharges, and management often requires multiple antiepileptic drugs and supportive therapies.

motor ataxia.definition: Impaired coordination of voluntary movement due to cerebellar dysfunction, presenting with dysmetria (past-pointing), intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesis, and an ataxic, wide-based gait.

labyrinthine reflex.definition: A reflex mediated by the vestibular labyrinth (inner ear) that helps stabilize gaze and posture during head movement, chiefly via the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) and vestibulospinal pathways.

gonadal defects.definition: Abnormal development, structure, or function of the gonads (ovaries or testes) that impairs gamete formation and sex steroid production, potentially causing disorders of sexual development, infertility, and hormonal imbalances.

nosocomial urinary tract infections.definition: A urinary tract infection acquired in a hospital or other healthcare setting, not present or incubating at admission, typically occurring after 48 hours and often related to urinary catheter use or other invasive procedures.

friedländer’s bacillus.definition: A Gram-negative, encapsulated, non-motile, lactose-fermenting rod bacterium; a major cause of lobar pneumonia and other infections; historically known as Friedländer’s bacillus (current name Klebsiella pneumoniae).

klebs-löeffler bacillus.definition: A Gram-positive, nonmotile, non–spore-forming bacillus that is the etiologic agent of diphtheria; it produces diphtheria toxin encoded by a lysogenic bacteriophage, leading to pseudomembranous pharyngitis and potential systemic toxin effects (e.g., myocarditis, neuropathy).

kinetoplasm.definition: A historical term for the cytoplasm surrounding the kinetoplast in kinetoplastid protozoa, i.e., the mitochondrial region containing the kinetoplast DNA and its associated organelles.

kinetosis.definition: Motion sickness characterized by nausea, vomiting, dizziness, pallor, and sweating triggered by movement, caused by a mismatch between vestibular signals in the inner ear and visual input.

klippel-feil disease.definition: A congenital disorder characterized by fusion of two or more cervical vertebrae due to failure of normal segmentation during development, resulting in a short neck, a low posterior hairline, and limited neck motion; commonly associated with scoliosis, Sprengel deformity, and other vertebral or organ anomalies.

klippel-feil malformation.definition: A congenital disorder in which two or more cervical vertebrae are fused due to failure of segmentation during embryogenesis, leading to a short neck, limited neck motion, and a low posterior hairline; may be associated with scoliosis and various organ-system anomalies.

klippel-trenaunay syndrome.definition: A congenital vascular malformation syndrome characterized by capillary malformations (port-wine stains), venous and often lymphatic anomalies, and overgrowth of a limb (soft tissue and bone), most commonly affecting one leg with possible limb-length discrepancy and edema.

skin varices.definition: Dilated, tortuous superficial veins of the skin, typically caused by venous hypertension and valve incompetence (a form of varicose veins visible on the skin).

kloehn headgear.definition: An orthodontic appliance that applies external traction to the upper jaw via a headgear harness connected to braces, used in growing patients to influence maxillary growth and help correct Class II malocclusion.

cervical strap.definition: A strap around the neck used to secure or adjust a cervical immobilization or traction device (e.g., a cervical collar) to stabilize or support the neck.

klonopin.definition: A brand-name benzodiazepine (active ingredient clonazepam) used as an anticonvulsant and anxiolytic; it enhances GABA-A receptor activity in the CNS to produce anticonvulsant, anxiolytic, and sedative effects. Common adverse effects include drowsiness and dizziness; it has potential for dependence and withdrawal, and should be used with caution in the elderly or those with liver impairment, and avoided with alcohol or other CNS depressants.

dejerine-klumpke paralysis.definition: A lower trunk (C8–T1) brachial plexus injury causing Klumpke palsy with paralysis of intrinsic hand muscles (leading to a claw hand), sensory loss in the medial forearm and hand, and often Horner syndrome (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis) due to sympathetic fiber involvement; commonly due to birth trauma or traction on an abducted arm.

klumpke palsy.definition: An injury to the lower trunk of the brachial plexus (C8–T1) causing weakness or paralysis of intrinsic hand muscles and sometimes wrist flexors, with sensory loss in the medial forearm and hand; classically presents as a claw hand and may be associated with Horner syndrome if sympathetic fibers are affected.

sympathetic nerves.definition: Effector nerves of the sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system that innervate smooth muscle, cardiac muscle, and glands. Preganglionic neurons originate in the thoracic and lumbar spinal cord (T1–L2) and synapse in sympathetic ganglia (paravertebral or prevertebral); postganglionic fibers typically release norepinephrine to mediate fight‑or‑flight responses such as increased heart rate, bronchodilation, pupil dilation, and vasoconstriction.

lateral meniscus.definition: A C-shaped fibrocartilaginous disc on the lateral aspect of the knee between the lateral femoral condyle and the lateral tibial plateau; it distributes load, absorbs shock, and stabilizes the knee joint, and is typically more mobile than the medial meniscus due to looser attachments.

patellofemoral joint.definition: A synovial articulation between the patella (kneecap) and the femur (thighbone) in which the patella glides within the femoral trochlear groove during knee flexion and extension.

peroneal nerve palsy.definition: A motor and sensory deficit from injury to the common peroneal (fibular) nerve, typically causing weakness of dorsiflexion and toe extension (foot drop) and sensory loss over the dorsum of the foot and lateral leg; most often due to compression or trauma at the fibular neck or along the nerve.

loosening.definition: A process or state of becoming looser or less tight; loss of firmness or stability of tissue, a structure, or an implanted device.

knee sling.definition: A device that immobilizes and supports the knee after injury or surgery, typically a wrap- or brace-type immobilizer with straps to limit knee movement and help control pain and swelling.

goniopuncture.definition: An ophthalmic procedure performed under gonioscopic visualization in which a small puncture is created in the iris or trabecular meshwork to enhance aqueous humor outflow and lower intraocular pressure, typically used in glaucoma management.

krukenberg's tumor.definition: Metastatic ovarian tumor composed of mucin-producing signet-ring cells, most often arising from primary gastric (diffuse-type) carcinoma; commonly bilateral and associated with a poor prognosis.

koplik's spots.definition: Small bluish-white to gray-white specks on the buccal mucosa opposite the molars, appearing early in measles and considered pathognomonic for the infection.

korean hemorrhagic fever.definition: A viral zoonosis caused by hantaviruses, historically described in East Asia (notably Korea), transmitted mainly by inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta. It presents with abrupt fever, hemorrhagic manifestations, and acute kidney injury; the course may include febrile, hypotensive/shock, oliguric, diuretic, and convalescent phases. Management is supportive, with hydration and organ support; there is no proven specific antiviral therapy, and prevention focuses on rodent control and reducing exposure to rodent waste.

korotkoff sounds.definition: A series of sounds heard through a stethoscope over an artery during auscultatory blood pressure measurement with a cuff; the onset of the first sound corresponds to systolic blood pressure, and the disappearance of the sounds corresponds to diastolic blood pressure (typically described in five phases I–V).
