acupuncture.definition: A treatment based on Chinese medicine. Thin needles are inserted into the skin at specific points on the body. This therapy is used to treat pain and various health problems and to reduce stress.

kostmann's syndrome.definition: A rare inherited disorder of neutrophil production causing severe congenital neutropenia from birth and resulting in recurrent bacterial infections; commonly due to mutations in ELANE (ELA2) or HAX1, and often treated with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G‑CSF), with a risk of progression to myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia.

kudzu.definition: A fast-growing East Asian climbing vine (Pueraria montana) used in traditional herbal medicine; contains isoflavones and has been studied for alcohol cravings and menopausal symptoms, but evidence is inconclusive and it can be an invasive weed in some regions.

kufs' disease.definition: An autosomal recessive form of neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (a lysosomal storage disorder) characterized by progressive neurodegeneration due to accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigments (ceroid lipofuscin) in neurons; typically presents in adolescence or adulthood with seizures, dementia, ataxia, and movement disorders, usually with little or no ocular involvement.

krabbe's disease.definition: An autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of the enzyme galactocerebrosidase (GALC), leading to accumulation of psychosine and progressive demyelination of the central and peripheral nervous systems; onset typically in infancy with irritability, feeding difficulties, developmental delay, hypotonia progressing to spasticity, and usually severe neurologic decline and death by age 2 if untreated.

kraske position.definition: A surgical position in which the patient lies prone with the hips flexed and the buttocks elevated, causing the body to form an inverted 'V' (jackknife) shape to expose the perineum and posterior rectum for anorectal or posterior access procedures; also known as the prone jackknife position.

krause's corpuscles.definition: An encapsulated nerve ending that functions as a cold-temperature thermoreceptor in the skin and mucous membranes, responding to cool stimuli and contributing to the sensation of cold (found in tissues such as the lips, conjunctiva, and other mucosal surfaces).

pacini's corpuscles.definition: A large, encapsulated mechanoreceptor in the deep dermis and subcutaneous tissue that detects high-frequency vibration and deep pressure; it is rapidly adapting and features concentric lamellae around a central nerve ending.

kulchitsky cell carcinoma.definition: A historical term for small cell carcinoma of the lung, a highly malignant neuroendocrine tumor arising from Kulchitsky cells; characterized by small round-to-oval cells with scant cytoplasm, finely granular chromatin, high mitotic rate with necrosis, and early metastasis often accompanied by paraneoplastic syndromes.

kummell's disease.definition: Avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) of a vertebral body after a minor vertebral compression fracture, characterized by a latent period after injury followed by delayed, progressive vertebral collapse; imaging may show an intravertebral vacuum cleft.

traumatic spondylopathy.definition: A spinal pathology caused by acute injury to the vertebral column, including fractures, dislocations, and ligamentous or disc injuries, with possible neurologic impairment.

kunecatechins.definition: A class of natural polyphenolic compounds in the flavonoid family, specifically flavan-3-ols, found in tea (especially green tea), cocoa, and some fruits; they act as antioxidants and have been studied for potential cardiovascular and cancer-preventive effects, with major forms including various stereoisomers and gallate esters.

perianal warts.definition: Condyloma acuminatum around the anus; benign anogenital warts caused by human papillomavirus infection, most commonly HPV types 6 and 11. They appear as soft, cauliflower-like or flat lesions that may itch or bleed and are transmitted sexually. Treatments include topical agents (e.g., imiquimod, podophyllotoxin), cryotherapy, electrocautery, laser, or surgical excision; evaluate for other STIs and consider HPV vaccination.

kock's pouch.definition: A continent cutaneous urinary reservoir created from a segment of ileum (often including the ileocecal junction) after cystectomy; urine is stored in the ileal reservoir and drained intermittently via a catheterizable stoma at the abdominal wall, using a continence mechanism (e.g., an intussuscepted nipple valve).

kuentscher nail.definition: A malleable, unreamed intramedullary nail used for internal fixation of long-bone fractures (especially the femur); introduced by Gerhard Küntscher and widely used in early modern intramedullary nailing.

kuru.definition: A rare, fatal prion disease (a transmissible spongiform encephalopathy) historically found among the Fore people of Papua New Guinea, transmitted through ritual endocannibalism; it causes progressive cerebellar ataxia, tremors, dysarthria, and neurodegeneration leading to death within months to a few years.

korean hand acupuncture.definition: An acupuncture technique in which the entire body is represented on the hand; stimulation of specific points on the palm and fingers (often by needles, pressure, or other means) is used to influence distant organs and body systems.

kuchendorf method.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. Could you specify the medical field or provide a source/context for "Kuchendorf method" so I can give a precise definition?

kraurosis vulvae.definition: A chronic inflammatory dermatosis of the vulva causing thinning and whitening of the vulvar skin with dermal sclerosis, leading to a parchment-like vulva, pruritus, fissures, dyspareunia, and potential introital stenosis; associated with a small increased risk of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma.

prion diseases.definition: A group of rare, fatal neurodegenerative diseases caused by misfolded prion proteins that induce misfolding of normal prion proteins, leading to spongiform brain degeneration and rapidly progressive neurologic decline; transmissible via sporadic, inherited, or acquired exposure.

kussmaul coma.definition: A coma due to severe metabolic acidosis accompanied by Kussmaul respiration (deep, labored, rapid breathing) as a compensatory mechanism; most commonly seen with diabetic ketoacidosis or severe renal failure–associated acidosis.

kussmaul's sign.definition: A paradoxical rise in jugular venous pressure during inspiration, reflecting impaired right ventricular filling; most commonly seen in constrictive pericarditis and restrictive cardiomyopathy, and may occur with right ventricular infarction or severe right-sided heart failure.

constrictive pericarditis.definition: A chronic condition in which a thickened, fibrotic (often calcified) pericardium constricts the heart, limiting diastolic filling and causing signs of heart failure (typically right-sided) with preserved systolic function; commonly follows pericarditis and is diagnosed by imaging showing pericardial thickening and abnormal ventricular interaction, with treatment ranging from diuretics for symptom relief to surgical pericardiectomy in refractory cases.

mediastinal tumor.definition: A mass occurring in the mediastinum—the central compartment of the thoracic cavity between the lungs. Mediastinal tumors can be benign or malignant and arise from thymic tissue, germ cells, lymphatic tissue, or neural crest–derived structures; they are categorized by location (anterior, middle, posterior) and by histology (e.g., thymoma, germ cell tumors, lymphomas, neurogenic tumors).

gastrointestinal disorder.definition: A disease or condition affecting the gastrointestinal tract (esophagus through rectum) and sometimes related organs (liver, pancreas, gallbladder), typically causing symptoms such as abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, or GI bleeding.

toxic substance absorption.definition: The process by which a toxic chemical crosses biological barriers (such as skin, lungs, or gastrointestinal mucosa) and enters the systemic circulation, enabling distribution to target organs; influenced by properties like lipophilicity, molecular size, ionization, dose, exposure route, and local血 flow.

kveim reaction.definition: A historical cutaneous diagnostic test for sarcoidosis in which an extract from sarcoid tissue is injected intradermally; a delayed granulomatous skin reaction (nodular lesion) develops at the injection site in individuals with sarcoidosis.

noncaseating granuloma.definition: An organized aggregate of activated macrophages (epithelioid cells) and multinucleated giant cells surrounded by lymphocytes, with no central necrosis (no caseation); commonly seen in diseases like sarcoidosis and other nonnecrotizing granulomatous conditions.

marasmus.definition: A form of severe protein-energy malnutrition due to chronic caloric (and often protein) deficiency, resulting in marked wasting and emaciation with loss of subcutaneous fat and muscle; growth failure is common, and edema is typically absent (unlike kwashiorkor).

protein-energy malnutrition.definition: A form of malnutrition caused by inadequate intake of protein and calories, leading to weight loss and muscle wasting; it includes marasmus, kwashiorkor, and mixed forms.

fatty degeneration of the liver.definition: Accumulation of excess fat (triglycerides) within hepatocytes, producing hepatic steatosis. Commonly caused by alcohol use, obesity, diabetes, and metabolic syndrome; often reversible with management of the underlying cause, but can progress to steatohepatitis, fibrosis, and cirrhosis if injury persists.

multivitamin deficiencies.definition: A deficiency state in which the body lacks adequate levels of two or more essential vitamins, often due to poor dietary intake, malabsorption, alcoholism, or chronic disease; manifestations vary by which vitamins are deficient and may include fatigue, anemia, skin/eye changes, neuropathy, and impaired immunity. Management involves addressing underlying causes and providing dietary optimization with multivitamin supplementation or targeted vitamin therapy.

gamma benzene hexachloride.definition: An organochlorine insecticide (gamma-hexachlorocyclohexane, commonly known as lindane); historically used topically for pediculosis and scabies; neurotoxic agent that inhibits GABA-A receptor–mediated inhibition, potentially causing seizures; associated with toxicity and environmental persistence; usage is restricted or banned in many countries.

kyasanur forest disease.definition: A tick-borne viral hemorrhagic fever endemic to forested regions of South Asia; transmitted to humans mainly by bites of infected Haemaphysalis ticks and by contact with infected animals; caused by a flavivirus; presents with abrupt fever, headache, myalgia, and sometimes vomiting, with potential progression to hemorrhagic and neurologic complications; incubation typically 3–9 days; no specific antiviral treatment; managed supportively; vaccine available in some regions.

haemophysalis spinigera.definition: A species of hard tick (family Ixodidae) in the genus Haemaphysalis; an important vector of Kyasanur Forest disease virus in India, transmitted to humans via tick bites after feeding on small mammal hosts in forested habitats.

muscle ache.definition: Muscle ache, or myalgia, is soreness or pain in the skeletal muscles, often described as aching, stiffness, or cramps. It can result from overuse or strain, injury, infections, certain medications, or systemic conditions, and typically improves with rest and supportive care.

monkey disease.definition: Not a standard medical term; may refer to diseases associated with monkeys, most commonly monkeypox—a viral zoonosis caused by an orthopoxvirus, transmitted through close contact with infected animals or people; symptoms include fever, malaise, swollen lymph nodes, and a vesicular-pustular rash.

labium majus.definition: Two large, hair-bearing folds of skin and subcutaneous tissue forming the outer lips of the female external genitalia (vulva); they enclose and protect the vagina and urethral openings, contain fat and glands, and are homologous to the male scrotum. They become engorged with blood during sexual arousal.

labium minus.definition: Paired, hairless folds of skin inside the vulva that enclose the openings of the vagina and urethra and form the boundaries of the vestibule.

frenulum.definition: A small fold of tissue that secures or restricts the movement of a part, such as under the tongue (lingual frenulum) or at the lips (labial frenulum).

labial vestibule.definition: An anatomical space in the mouth between the inner surface of the lips (labial mucosa) and the teeth and alveolar ridges, forming the labial portion of the oral vestibule.

labial notch.definition: A small indentation on the edge of a labial structure (such as the lips or labia), described as a notch rather than a separate anatomical feature.

labial glands.definition: Small mucous-type salivary glands located in the mucosa of the lips (labial mucosa); one of the minor salivary glands that secrete saliva into ducts opening on the inner surface of the lips, contributing to lubrication and moisture of the oral cavity.

labial bar.definition: A bar‑shaped structure of tissue associated with the lip region; in dental prosthetics, it can refer to a labial (lip‑facing) connector or reinforcement on a denture, as opposed to a lingual bar. Note: the term is uncommon and usage may vary by specialty.

labioglossolaryngeal paralysis.definition: Paralysis or severe weakness of the muscles of the lips, tongue, and larynx, leading to impaired speech (dysarthria) and swallowing (dysphagia); typically due to bilateral lower motor neuron lesions of the brainstem affecting cranial nerves VII, XII, and X or their nuclei (bulbar palsy).

labiolingual fixed orthodontic appliance.definition: A fixed orthodontic appliance in which brackets or attachments are bonded to both the labial (front) and lingual (tongue-side) surfaces of teeth and interconnected by an archwire to apply orthodontic forces from both sides, enabling controlled tooth movement and correction of malocclusions.

labioversion.definition: A dental term describing the displacement or inclination of a tooth toward the lips (labial direction), such as a labially inclined incisor.

fixed orthodontic appliance.definition: A dental braces system bonded or cemented to the teeth and connected by a fixed archwire (often with ligatures or self-ligating components) that cannot be removed by the patient, used to apply continuous, controlled forces to move teeth into desired positions over time.

mandibular arch.definition: Embryology: the first pharyngeal (branchial) arch; the structure that forms the mandible and its derivatives (Meckel's cartilage, the malleus and incus) and the muscles of mastication, innervated by V3 of the trigeminal nerve.

anchor bands.definition: Fibrous or synthetic bands used to anchor tissues, implants, or grafts in place within the body, providing stability and preventing displacement during healing or function.

lingual arches.definition: A fixed orthodontic space-maintaining appliance consisting of a curved wire along the lingual surfaces of the teeth, anchored to molar bands, used to preserve arch length after premature loss of primary teeth.

first permanent molars.definition: Two large posterior teeth that erupt in the permanent dentition around age 6–7, located behind the primary second molars; they do not replace any deciduous teeth and help establish occlusion and mastication (commonly called the six-year molars).

spine-stretching exercises.definition: Movements designed to lengthen and mobilize the vertebral column to improve spinal flexibility and reduce back tension; these exercises typically include gentle forward and backward bends, side bending, and rotations of the thoracic and lumbar spine, performed slowly with controlled breathing and proper alignment, and are used in physical therapy, yoga, and Pilates.

labyrinthectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which all or part of the inner ear labyrinth is destroyed or removed to relieve intractable vertigo, typically due to Ménière disease; it usually results in permanent deafness on the operated side.

lacrimotomy.definition: A surgical procedure involving an incision into the lacrimal gland (tear gland), typically to drain a lacrimal gland abscess or to biopsy/remove a lesion.

labyrinthine.definition: Relating to the labyrinth of the inner ear; comprising the cochlea, vestibule, and semicircular canals, which are responsible for hearing and balance.

menieres disease.definition: A chronic inner ear disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of vertigo, fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss (often unilateral), tinnitus, and a sensation of ear fullness, typically due to endolymphatic hydrops (excess endolymph fluid in the labyrinth).

labyrinthitis.definition: An inflammation of the inner ear labyrinth, typically due to infection, causing acute vertigo with nausea and imbalance; may be accompanied by hearing loss and tinnitus, and usually improves over days to weeks.

lacrimal canaliculus.definition: A small duct of the lacrimal drainage system that begins at the lacrimal puncta on the eyelid margin and carries tears medially through the superior and inferior canaliculi into the lacrimal sac (often via the common canaliculus).

hasner fold.definition: A mucosal fold at the distal nasolacrimal duct opening into the inferior nasal meatus that functions as a valve (Hasner valve) to regulate tear drainage and prevent reflux of nasal contents into the duct.

lacrimal punctum.definition: A tiny opening on the inner edge of each eyelid (upper and lower puncta) that drains tears from the eye surface into the lacrimal canaliculi, beginning the tear drainage pathway.

lacrimal papilla.definition: A small raised area on the medial eyelid margin bearing the lacrimal punctum, the opening through which tears drain into the lacrimal canaliculi.

lacrimation.definition: The production and secretion of tears by the lacrimal glands, serving to lubricate and protect the eye; tears may be produced reflexively in response to irritation or emotional states.

lacrimator.definition: A substance that irritates the eyes and provokes tearing (lacrimation); also called a lachrymator.

lacrimomaxillary suture.definition: A craniofacial suture between the lacrimal bone and the maxilla along the medial orbital wall; a fibrous joint that typically ossifies with age as the skull sutures fuse.

lacrimal artery.definition: A branch of the ophthalmic artery that runs laterally to the lacrimal gland, supplying the lacrimal gland, lateral eyelids, and conjunctiva, and giving off the lateral palpebral arteries.

lacrimal groove.definition: A bony groove on the medial wall of the orbit forming the nasolacrimal canal, through which the nasolacrimal duct runs from the lacrimal sac to the inferior meatus (nasolacrimal groove).

lacrimal lake.definition: A shallow tear-filled space at the medial angle of the eye where tears collect between the upper and lower eyelids, forming the lacrimal conjunctival sac before drainage through the lacrimal puncta.

lacrimal reflex.definition: A protective reflex causing tearing in response to irritation of the ocular surface, mediated by afferent trigeminal (corneal) input and efferent parasympathetic (facial nerve) stimulation of the lacrimal gland.

lacrosse encephalitis.definition: La Crosse encephalitis is an acute viral infection of the central nervous system caused by La Crosse virus, a bunyavirus transmitted to humans by Aedes triseriatus mosquitoes. It most often affects children and presents with fever, headache, and vomiting; a minority develop encephalitis with confusion, seizures, or altered mental status. There is no specific antiviral therapy; management is supportive, and prevention focuses on mosquito bite avoidance.

lacrosse virus.definition: An orthobunyavirus of the California serogroup transmitted by mosquitoes; it can cause febrile illness and, in some cases, encephalitis, most often in children.

lactalbumin.definition: A whey protein fraction of milk, mainly alpha-lactalbumin; a small calcium-binding protein produced by the mammary gland that is essential for lactose synthesis in milk.

lactam.definition: A cyclic amide in which the carbonyl group is part of a ring; a ring-structured amide formed when the carboxyl and amino groups of the same molecule cyclize.

lactate dehydrogenase.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the reversible conversion of lactate to pyruvate with the concurrent interconversion of NADH and NAD+. It is found in many tissues, and elevated serum LDH is a nonspecific marker of tissue damage (e.g., myocardial infarction, liver disease, hemolysis, or muscle injury).

ldh.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the reversible conversion of pyruvate to lactate with concomitant interconversion of NADH and NAD+; elevated levels can indicate tissue damage.

lactase.definition: An enzyme that breaks down milk sugar (lactose) in the body.

lactic acid.definition: Es un ácido alfa-hidroxi (ácido 2-hidroxipropiónico; fórmula C3H6O3) producido durante la glucólisis anaeróbica a partir del piruvato; se acumula en los músculos durante el ejercicio intenso y puede provocar acidosis láctica cuando sus niveles son elevados.

lactic acid test.definition: A laboratory test that measures the concentration of lactate (lactic acid) in the blood, used to assess tissue perfusion and oxygenation; elevated lactate suggests lactic acidosis and can occur with sepsis, shock, hypoxia, or liver disease.

lactiferous.definition: Relating to milk; used to describe structures that bear or transport milk, especially the lactiferous ducts that carry milk from the mammary glands to the nipple.

lactiferous glands.definition: Glandular tissue of the breast that produces milk during lactation; composed of lobes and lobules whose secreted milk drains through lactiferous ducts to the nipple.

lactation consultant.definition: A healthcare professional who specializes in breastfeeding support, education, and management, helping mothers and infants initiate and sustain breastfeeding, assess latch and milk transfer, manage common breastfeeding problems (e.g., nipple pain, engorgement, low milk supply), and coordinate care with other clinicians. Often IBCLC-certified.

lactation counseling.definition: Professional guidance and support to pregnant or postpartum individuals and families to initiate and sustain breastfeeding, including education on latch and positioning, feeding frequency and duration, milk expression and storage, and troubleshooting common lactation problems.

lactation suppression.definition: A medical process to stop or reduce milk production in the breasts after childbirth, in order to terminate lactation.

lacteal fistula.definition: An abnormal fistulous connection involving a lacteal lymphatic capillary of the intestinal villi, resulting in leakage of chyle (lipid-rich lymph) from the lymphatic system into surrounding tissues or externally.

lacteal vessel.definition: A lymphatic capillary in the small intestinal villi that absorbs dietary lipids, producing chyle that drains into the thoracic duct via the cisterna chyli.

lactobacillus.definition: A genus of Gram-positive, non-spore-forming, rod-shaped bacteria that ferment carbohydrates to lactic acid; they are part of the normal human microbiota in the gut and vagina and are widely used as probiotics and in fermented foods.

lactobacillus acidophilus.definition: A Gram-positive, non-spore-forming, rod-shaped lactic acid bacterium; a common member of the human gastrointestinal and genitourinary microbiota, often used as a probiotic to support microbial balance and inhibit pathogenic bacteria through lactic acid production and other antimicrobial mechanisms.

lactobacillus bulgaricus.definition: Gram-positive, non-spore-forming, rod-shaped lactic acid bacterium used in yogurt production; ferments lactose to lactic acid and is typically cultured with Streptococcus thermophilus in dairy starter cultures.

lactobacillus (genus).definition: A genus of Gram-positive, non-spore-forming, rod-shaped bacteria that produce lactic acid as a major end product of carbohydrate fermentation; many species are part of the normal human microbiota of the oral, vaginal, and gastrointestinal tracts, and several are used in fermentation or as probiotics.

lactitol.definition: A sugar alcohol derived from lactose; used as a low-calorie sweetener and osmotic laxative. It is poorly absorbed from the small intestine and exerts an osmotic effect in the colon, increasing stool water and promoting bowel movements; common GI side effects include bloating, flatulence, and diarrhea.

lactotoxin.definition: A toxin that interferes with lactation by impairing milk production in the mammary gland, often through disruption of prolactin signaling or mammary epithelial function.

tropical sprue.definition: A chronic malabsorption syndrome of the proximal small intestine occurring in tropical regions, presenting with chronic diarrhea, weight loss, steatorrhea, and nutritional deficiencies (notably folate and sometimes vitamin B12) due to mucosal damage; often responsive to antibiotic therapy and nutritional supplementation.

infectious hepatitis.definition: An acute viral hepatitis caused by hepatotropic viruses, most commonly hepatitis A or E, transmitted primarily by the fecal-oral route, leading to liver inflammation.

serum albumin.definition: A major protein produced by the liver that circulates in blood plasma, helping maintain oncotic (colloid osmotic) pressure and serving as a transport/binding protein for a wide range of endogenous and exogenous substances, including hormones, fatty acids, bilirubin, and many drugs.

beta-galactosidase.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of beta-galactosides, such as lactose, into the monosaccharides glucose and galactose; encoded by the lacZ gene in many bacteria and commonly used as a molecular biology reporter gene.

diastase.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of starch into maltose and dextrins; historically called diastase and equivalent to amylase (primarily from saliva and pancreas).

nasolacrimal.definition: Relating to the nasolacrimal apparatus, the tear drainage system that carries tears from the lacrimal sac into the nasal cavity.

posterior nasal meatus.definition: Not a standard anatomical term; the nasal cavity contains the superior, middle, and inferior meatuses—air passages beneath the corresponding nasal conchae—and the posterior nasal cavity communicates with the nasopharynx via the choanae.

nasal meatus.definition: A groove or passage in the nasal cavity formed beneath a nasal concha; the superior, middle, and inferior meatuses provide airways and serve as drainage pathways for the paranasal sinuses (and, in the inferior meatus, for the nasolacrimal duct).

lactoferrin.definition: An iron-binding glycoprotein of the transferrin family found in milk and other secretions (notably colostrum); it chelates ferric iron to limit microbial growth and has antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory effects.

neutrophil.definition: An abundant white blood cell of the innate immune system with a multilobed nucleus and cytoplasmic granules that phagocytose and destroy bacteria and other invading microbes.

crohns disease.definition: A disease that lasts for a long time and causes severe irritation in your digestive tract (bowels).

lactogen.definition: A substance that stimulates milk production by the mammary gland; a lactogenic (galactogenic) agent, with prolactin being the primary natural example.

lactogenic.definition: Relating to lactation; capable of promoting milk production, especially substances or hormones that stimulate mammary gland secretion.

lactogenesis.definition: The process of milk production by the mammary glands, beginning during pregnancy and continuing after birth, regulated by hormonal changes to establish and maintain lactation.

lacto-ovo-vegetarian.definition: A vegetarian diet that excludes meat, poultry, and fish but includes dairy products and eggs.

lactoperoxidase.definition: A heme-containing peroxidase enzyme found in milk and other secretions that catalyzes the oxidation of thiocyanate by hydrogen peroxide to hypothiocyanite, producing antimicrobial activity as part of the lactoperoxidase system.

lactose tolerance test.definition: A diagnostic test for lactose intolerance in which, after fasting, the patient ingests a standard lactose solution and serial blood glucose levels are measured over about 2 hours; a blunted rise (typically <20 mg/dL from baseline) suggests lactose malabsorption due to lactase deficiency, while a normal rise indicates adequate lactose digestion. The test is increasingly supplanted by hydrogen breath testing.

lactosuria.definition: Presence of lactose in the urine, typically occurring after ingestion of lactose in individuals with lactase deficiency; usually transient and resolves with abstinence from lactose.

lactotherapy.definition: A nonstandard or undefined term for treatment using milk or milk-derived products; not part of conventional medical practice, with no widely accepted indications or proven efficacy.

lactotroph.definition: An endocrine cell of the anterior pituitary (pars distalis) that secretes prolactin, primarily regulating lactation; its activity is inhibited by hypothalamic dopamine.

lactovegetarian.definition: A vegetarian who includes dairy products (milk and dairy foods) in the diet but excludes meat, fish, poultry, and eggs.

lacuna.definition: A small cavity or space within a tissue that contains a resident cell, such as an osteocyte in bone or a chondrocyte in cartilage; the term is also used to denote a gap or interval in a structure or period.

lacunae.definition: Small cavities within tissues that house living cells; in bone they contain osteocytes, and in cartilage they contain chondrocytes.

lacunar ligament.definition: A crescent-shaped reflection of the medial end of the inguinal ligament that attaches to the pubic crest and pectineal line, forming the medial boundary of the femoral ring (femoral canal); also known as Gimbernat's ligament.

pecten pubis.definition: A sharp crest on the superior ramus of the pubis (the pectineal line) that serves as the attachment for the pectineus muscle and continues laterally as the iliopectineal line.

lacunar state.definition: A clinical condition characterized by cognitive impairment and often mood or behavioral changes resulting from multiple lacunar (small) infarcts in subcortical brain regions, typically due to chronic small-vessel disease; it represents a form of vascular or subcortical dementia.

status lacunaris.definition: Not a standard medical term; in general, it would denote a state characterized by lacunae (small cavities) within tissue, with the exact meaning depending on the clinical context (e.g., lacunar infarcts in the brain in neurology, or lacunae in bone). If you have a specific context, I can tailor the definition.

lacus lacrimalis.definition: A small tear-filled recess at the medial canthus of the eye where tears collect before draining through the lacrimal puncta into the lacrimal drainage system.

inner canthus.definition: The medial angle of the eye where the upper and lower eyelids meet; at this site lies the lacrimal caruncle and the openings of the tear drainage system (lacrimal puncta and canaliculi) that drain tears into the lacrimal sac.

left anterior descending.definition: A major coronary artery that travels in the anterior interventricular groove and supplies blood to the anterior wall of the left ventricle and part of the interventricular septum; occlusion can cause an anterior myocardial infarction.

leukocyte adhesion deficiency.definition: A group of rare inherited immunodeficiencies characterized by defective leukocyte adhesion and migration to sites of infection due to defects in integrin or selectin-mediated adhesion, resulting in recurrent bacterial infections, poor pus formation, and peripheral neutrophilia.

ladd's bands.definition: A congenital peritoneal fibrous band arising from malrotation of the midgut, extending from the cecum to the right abdominal wall and crossing the duodenum to cause extrinsic duodenal obstruction.

peritoneal folds.definition: Double layers of peritoneum that connect abdominal organs to each other or to the abdominal wall, containing vessels, nerves, and fat; they form structures such as the mesentery, omenta, and peritoneal ligaments, and help anchor, support, and compartmentalize the viscera.

laetrile.definition: Derivado semi-sintético de la amigdalina (amigdalina) extraído de semillas como las de albaricoque, promovido como “vitamina B17” para el cáncer; no hay evidencia confiable de beneficio y puede provocar intoxicación por cianuro; no está aprobado para el tratamiento del cáncer.

amygdalin.definition: A cyanogenic glycoside found in seeds such as bitter almonds and apricot kernels; when hydrolyzed it yields benzaldehyde and hydrogen cyanide, and it has been used in alternative cancer therapies but with no proven benefit and a risk of cyanide poisoning.

vitamin b17.definition: A nonstandard term for amygdalin, a cyanogenic glycoside found in the seeds of several fruits (e.g., apricot, almond). It is not a true vitamin; there is no proven benefit for cancer treatment, and its metabolism can release hydrogen cyanide, posing a risk of poisoning; it is not approved as a medical therapy.

lalophobia.definition: Not a recognized medical term; if used, it would refer to an irrational fear of speaking or vocalizing in social situations, akin to glossophobia.

lambda chain.definition: A type of immunoglobulin light chain; one of the two light-chain isotypes (kappa and lambda) that pair with heavy chains to form antibodies; free lambda light chains in serum or urine are used in diagnosing and monitoring plasma cell disorders.

lambda light chain.definition: A type of immunoglobulin light chain produced by plasma cells; one of the two light-chain isotypes that can circulate freely in serum or be excreted in urine; overproduction is associated with certain plasma cell disorders and is assessed by free light chain assays (often via the kappa/lambda ratio).

lambda wave.definition: A normal occipital EEG transient that occurs with rapid eye movements during visual scanning or reading; it is a brief deflection marking a fixation shift and reflects ocular activity rather than brain pathology.

lambdoid.definition: Relating to the posterior skull suture between the occipital bone and the parietal bones; named for its lambda-shaped outline.

parietal bones.definition: One of a pair of skull bones forming the upper lateral sides and roof of the cranium; they meet at the sagittal suture and articulate with the frontal bone anteriorly, the occipital bone posteriorly, the temporal bones laterally, and the sphenoid bone.

occipitomastoid suture.definition: A fibrous joint between the occipital bone and the mastoid part of the temporal bone; a cranial suture that unites these bones and typically ossifies with age.

temporal bones.definition: Paired bones forming the sides and base of the skull. Each temporal bone houses parts of the middle and inner ear (including the external acoustic meatus and petrous portion) and participates in the temporomandibular joint via the mandibular fossa; notable features include the mastoid process, styloid process, and zygomatic process.

lambert.definition: An autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterized by antibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels, causing proximal weakness, fatigability, and autonomic symptoms; strength tends to improve with brief rest or continued activity and is often associated with small cell lung carcinoma.

lamellae.definition: Thin plate‑like layers of tissue or membranes. In bone, concentric rings of mineralized matrix surrounding a central canal; in nervous tissue, multiple membrane layers that comprise the myelin sheath around axons.

lamellar.definition: Relating to or consisting of thin, plate-like layers arranged in sheets; in anatomy, tissue organized into lamellae (concentric layers), as in lamellar bone.

lamellar exfoliation.definition: A process in which the skin’s outermost layer (the stratum corneum) is shed in thin, plate-like sheets (lamellae), often produced by chemical or mechanical exfoliation.

lamellar desquamation of the newborn.definition: A benign, self-limited condition in newborns in which the outermost skin layer (stratum corneum) peels in large, lamellar sheets, typically appearing in the first days after birth and resolving without treatment.

lamellar ichthyosis of newborn.definition: A congenital, autosomal recessive ichthyosis in which the newborn is often born as a collodion baby and subsequently develops generalized, thick, plate-like hyperkeratosis (lamellar scales) due to defective skin barrier, with risk of dehydration and infection.

posterior fontanel.definition: A soft membranous gap between the developing skull bones of a newborn, at the back of the head where the sagittal and lambdoid sutures meet; it usually closes by about 2–3 months of age.

arterial hypertension.definition: Chronic condition characterized by persistently elevated arterial blood pressure, typically defined as systolic ≥140 mm Hg and/or diastolic ≥90 mm Hg on repeated measurements (many guidelines now use ≥130/80). It increases the risk of cardiovascular disease, stroke, heart failure, and kidney disease; can be primary (essential) or secondary to another condition.

lameness.definition: A condition characterized by an abnormal gait or inability to bear weight on one or more limbs, typically due to pain, weakness, injury, or deformity affecting the limb.

lamictal.definition: Lamotrigine is an anticonvulsant and mood stabilizer used to treat certain seizures and to delay relapse in bipolar disorder; it works by inhibiting voltage-gated sodium channels and reducing the release of excitatory neurotransmitters such as glutamate.

lamotrigine.definition: A phenyltriazine anticonvulsant and mood stabilizer used to treat epilepsy (partial seizures) and bipolar disorder; it primarily inhibits voltage-gated sodium channels, reduces glutamate release, and stabilizes neuronal membranes.

lamina densa.definition: Electron-dense, dense layer of the basement membrane located beneath the lamina rara; rich in type IV collagen and laminin, providing structural support to the epithelium and contributing to selective permeability of the basement membrane.

lamina dura.definition: The thin radiopaque layer of dense bone that lines each tooth socket (the alveolar bone proper), forming the boundary of the periodontal ligament space around a tooth on radiographs.

lamina lucida.definition: A clear, electron-lucent layer of the basement membrane (basal lamina) directly beneath epithelial cells; part of the basal lamina, containing laminin and other glycoproteins/proteoglycans and serving as a site of adhesion to the underlying lamina densa.

lamina rara externa.definition: An electron-lucent outer layer of the glomerular basement membrane that lies adjacent to the podocytes and Bowman's space; it is part of the filtration barrier and contains components such as type IV collagen and laminin.

lamina rara interna.definition: The inner, clear (electron-lucent) layer of the glomerular basement membrane facing the capillary endothelium; part of the tripartite GBM (lamina rara interna, lamina densa, lamina rara externa) composed mainly of proteoglycans and glycoproteins and contributing to the filtration barrier.

laminar flow.definition: A flow regime in which a fluid moves in parallel, non-intersecting layers with minimal cross-stream mixing and low turbulence; in medical settings, laminar flow refers to unidirectional, HEPA-filtered air movement over a sterile field to minimize particulate contamination (as in laminar-flow cabinets and clean rooms).

laminaria tent.definition: An obstetric technique using sterile dried Laminaria seaweed tents inserted into the cervix; the tents absorb moisture and gradually expand, mechanically dilating the cervix to achieve cervical ripening for labor induction or abortion procedures.

laminated thrombus.definition: A thrombus that exhibits layered (lamellated) bands of pale platelet/fibrin-rich material alternating with red blood cell–rich material, reflecting successive deposits of thrombus in flowing blood.

laminectomy.definition: An operation in which all or part of one or both laminae is removed.

laminin.definition: A large extracellular matrix glycoprotein and a major non-collagenous component of basement membranes; it is a heterotrimer formed from α, β, and γ chains that creates a cross-shaped molecule capable of mediating cell adhesion by binding to cell-surface receptors (e.g., integrins, dystroglycan) and other matrix components.

laminotomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which a portion of the vertebral lamina is removed to decompress the spinal canal and relieve pressure on the spinal cord or nerve roots; it creates a window into the canal and is less extensive than a full laminectomy.

lamina of modiolus.definition: A thin bony plate forming part of the modiolus, the central core of the cochlea; it provides attachment for the osseous spiral lamina and forms the conduit for the cochlear nerve fibers as they pass through the modiolus.

lamin antibody.definition: An autoantibody directed against laminin, a major basement membrane glycoprotein; such antibodies can be detected in some autoimmune diseases and may contribute to basement membrane–related pathology.

lance.definition: A long, slender, sharp-pointed surgical instrument used to puncture and drain a lesion, such as an abscess or boil; to lance a lesion means to puncture and open it to allow drainage.

lancefield’s classification.definition: Serologic grouping of β-hemolytic streptococci based on the C-carbohydrate antigen in the cell wall, classifying isolates into groups (A, B, C, D, F, G, etc.), with clinically important examples including group A (Streptococcus pyogenes) and group B (Streptococcus agalactiae).

lancinating.definition: Characterized by sudden, sharp, stabbing or piercing pain; knife-like in quality.

landau reflex.definition: An infantile postural reflex elicited when an infant is held in ventral suspension; the head, trunk, and legs extend, producing a "superman" posture. It appears around 3–4 months and typically disappears by 12–24 months.

langer-giedion syndrome.definition: A rare contiguous-gene deletion syndrome on chromosome 8q24 involving TRPS1 and EXT1, producing the TRPS II phenotype with multiple exostoses; features typically include sparse scalp hair, distinctive facial features (bulbous nasal tip and midface hypoplasia), short stature, brachydactyly, cone-shaped epiphyses, and sometimes developmental delay.

langerhans’ cells.definition: Dendritic cells in the epidermis that function as antigen-presenting immune cells; they capture and process microbial antigens and migrate to lymph nodes to activate naive T cells.

langerhans cells.definition: Cells of the immune system that work in the skin to fight infection.

langer’s line.definition: Topographic lines on the skin that reflect the orientation of collagen fibers in the dermis; incisions made parallel to these lines tend to heal with less scarring and better cosmetic results.

langhans’ layer.definition: A layer of the epidermis that contains Langerhans cells (dendritic antigen-presenting cells), primarily in the stratum spinosum; these cells capture, process, and present antigens to T cells and help initiate immune responses in the skin.

language delay.definition: Developmental lag in acquiring language skills, characterized by slower progress in expressive and/or receptive language than expected for age, typically with normal nonverbal cognition and no hearing impairment; may improve over time or with speech-language therapy and/or indicate an underlying language disorder if persistent.

language disorder.definition: A developmental or acquired condition characterized by difficulties in understanding and/or using spoken, written, or other language, affecting vocabulary, grammar, and discourse, not due to hearing loss, intellectual disability, or other neurological conditions.

lanosterol.definition: A tetracyclic triterpenoid sterol that serves as the key biosynthetic precursor to cholesterol in animals and fungi; formed from squalene in the endoplasmic reticulum and converted to cholesterol through a series of demethylation and reduction steps.

lanoxin.definition: A cardiac glycoside used to treat heart failure and certain supraventricular arrhythmias; increases myocardial contractility by inhibiting Na+/K+-ATPase, which raises intracellular calcium, and slows conduction through the AV node; has a narrow therapeutic index and potential toxicity requiring monitoring of electrolytes and drug levels.

lanreotide.definition: A long-acting synthetic somatostatin analog used to treat acromegaly and certain gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors; it binds somatostatin receptors to inhibit secretion of growth hormone and other hormones (reducing IGF-1), and is given by deep subcutaneous injection at regular intervals.

lansoprazole.definition: A proton pump inhibitor that decreases stomach acid production by irreversibly inhibiting the H+/K+-ATPase (proton pump) in gastric parietal cells; used to treat GERD, peptic ulcers, erosive esophagitis, and other acid-related disorders.

laparectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which all or part of an abdominal organ is removed, performed through the abdominal cavity using either open (laparotomy) or minimally invasive (laparoscopic) techniques.

laparoenterostomy.definition: A surgical procedure that creates an opening from the intestine to the abdominal wall (an enterostomy) to divert fecal contents, typically performed through the abdomen (laparotomy or laparoscopy).

laparoenterotomy.definition: An abdominal surgical procedure in which an incision is made into the intestine (enterotomy) through an abdominal approach (laparotomy) to access, explore, or treat the gastrointestinal tract.

laparohysterectomy.definition: A hysterectomy performed via laparoscopic (minimally invasive) techniques, removing the uterus through small abdominal incisions.

laparohystero-oophorectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove the uterus (hysterectomy) and both ovaries (bilateral oophorectomy) using a laparoscopic approach.

laparohysterosalpingo-oophorectomy.definition: Removal of the uterus, fallopian tubes, and ovaries through a laparoscopic approach; a combined hysterectomy, salpingectomy, and oophorectomy.

laparomyitis.definition: Inflammation of the abdominal wall muscles (the abdominal musculature); a nonstandard term that would imply abdominal myositis from infection, autoimmune disease, or trauma.

laparosalpingo-oophorectomy.definition: A laparoscopic surgical procedure to remove one or both ovaries with their corresponding fallopian tubes.

laparoscopic-assisted vaginal hysterosco.definition: A gynecologic procedure that combines laparoscopy (pelvic visualization via small abdominal incisions) with hysteroscopy (direct visualization of the uterine cavity) to diagnose or treat uterine and pelvic pathology, with the laparoscopic view guiding the hysteroscopic procedure and allowing external assessment of the uterus, fallopian tubes, and ovaries.

laparoscopic biopsy.definition: A minimally invasive procedure in which a tissue sample is obtained from an abdominal or pelvic organ or lesion using a laparoscope with biopsy instruments under direct visualization.

laparoscopic gastric banding.definition: A restrictive bariatric operation in which an adjustable silicone band is placed around the upper stomach via laparoscopy to create a small proximal gastric pouch; the band’s tightness is adjusted by saline injection through a subcutaneous access port to control satiety and food intake.

laparoscopic nephrectomy.definition: A minimally invasive surgical procedure to remove a kidney using small abdominal incisions, a laparoscope, and long instruments, often performed for donor nephrectomy, kidney cancer, or a nonfunctional kidney.

laparoscopic sterilization.definition: A minimally invasive surgical procedure to permanently prevent pregnancy by occluding or severing the fallopian tubes through small abdominal incisions using a laparoscope (tubal occlusion with clips, rings, cautery, or tubal resection).

peritoneoscope.definition: An endoscope used to examine the peritoneal cavity by inserting it through the abdominal wall to visualize peritoneal surfaces (peritoneoscopy).

myomectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove one or more fibroids (benign tumors) from the uterus while preserving the uterus.

leiomyomas.definition: A benign tumor of smooth muscle cells, most often arising in the uterus (uterine fibroids); composed of well-differentiated spindle cells arranged in whorled patterns, often estrogen-sensitive; may cause abnormal uterine bleeding, pelvic pain or pressure, and reproductive issues depending on size and location.

leiomyoma.definition: A benign tumor composed of smooth muscle cells, most often arising in the uterus (uterine fibroids).

systemic mastocytosis.definition: A clonal myeloid neoplasm characterized by infiltration and accumulation of abnormal mast cells in one or more organs (most commonly bone marrow, liver, spleen, gastrointestinal tract, and lymph nodes) with release of mast cell mediators causing symptoms such as flushing, pruritus, abdominal pain, wheezing, and anaphylaxis, and often associated with KIT mutations (e.g., D816V); it has subtypes ranging from indolent to aggressive.

mastocytosis.definition: A disorder defined by clonal proliferation and accumulation of mast cells in the skin and/or other organs, resulting in mediator-related symptoms such as flushing, pruritus, urticaria, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and, in systemic disease, anaphylaxis.

multiple endocrine adenomas.definition: A condition characterized by the development of two or more benign tumors (adenomas) of endocrine glands, often as part of hereditary syndromes such as multiple endocrine neoplasia; these adenomas can alter hormone production and gland function.

cord edema.definition: Swelling of the umbilical cord from fluid accumulation in Wharton’s jelly around the umbilical vessels; an edematous, thickened cord often seen on ultrasound or placental exam and can be associated with fetal hypoxia, anemia, infection, or hydrops and adverse perinatal outcomes.

glucose solution.definition: A sterile aqueous solution in which glucose (dextrose) is dissolved for medical use, primarily to provide calories and fluids as intravenous or oral therapy; common IV formulations include 5% dextrose in water (D5W) and higher-concentration dextrose solutions.

leukocyte alkaline phosphatase.definition: An enzyme produced by neutrophils that functions at alkaline pH, removing phosphate groups from substrates; its activity is elevated in leukemoid (reactive) reactions and reduced in chronic myeloid leukemia, aiding differentiation between these conditions.

leucine aminopeptidase.definition: A proteolytic enzyme that removes the N-terminal leucine from peptides and oligopeptides (an aminopeptidase); an exopeptidase involved in protein turnover and peptide processing, typically metal-ion dependent (often zinc).

mutism.definition: A condition characterized by the absence or marked reduction of spoken communication despite the ability to speak, caused by neurological injury, psychiatric illness, or severe psychological distress; it can present as complete silence or as selective/psychogenic speech loss.

epivir.definition: Lamivudine, a nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used to treat HIV-1 infection in combination with other antiretrovirals and chronic hepatitis B infection; it inhibits viral reverse transcription by incorporating into viral DNA and causing chain termination.

adenomas.definition: A benign neoplasm of glandular (epithelial) tissue that forms gland‑like structures; it can arise in many organs and is usually slow growing and noninvasive, though some adenomas have malignant potential depending on type and location.

pediatric pancreatitis.definition: Pediatric pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas occurring in children and adolescents, presenting with acute abdominal pain (often epigastric), vomiting, and sometimes fever. Diagnosis relies on compatible symptoms plus elevated pancreatic enzymes (lipase or amylase, typically ≥3× the upper limit of normal) and/or imaging evidence of pancreatic inflammation; there are multiple etiologies in youth, including trauma, biliary disease, infections, medications, genetic or congenital conditions, and metabolic disorders. Management is supportive (fluids, analgesia, nutrition) and directed at the underlying cause, with prognosis variable and potential for recurrence or progression to chronic pancreatitis in some cases.

gallbladder inspection.definition: A direct visual examination of the gallbladder to assess its anatomy and pathology, typically performed intraoperatively during cholecystectomy or when gallbladder disease is suspected; evaluated for gallstones, wall thickening, inflammation, polyps or tumors, distension, and perforation.

basement membranes.definition: Thin sheets of specialized extracellular matrix that underlie epithelial and some endothelial cells, separating them from the underlying connective tissue. They consist of a basal lamina (produced by epithelium) and a reticular lamina (produced by connective tissue) and provide structural support, anchor cells, and regulate filtration and cell behavior.

neurite regeneration.definition: Regrowth or extension of neurites (axons or dendrites) after neuronal injury, aiming to reestablish synaptic connections; driven by intrinsic growth programs and extracellular cues, with greater success in the peripheral nervous system than in the central nervous system due to inhibitory environments and glial scarring.

endothelial keratoplasty.definition: A partial-thickness corneal transplant in which only the diseased posterior corneal layers (endothelium with Descemet membrane) are replaced by donor tissue, restoring corneal clarity and deturgescence; used for endothelial dysfunction such as Fuchs endothelial dystrophy or bullous keratopathy (e.g., DSAEK, DMEK).

laparotomy sponge.definition: A sterile, absorbent surgical gauze pad used during open abdominal (laparotomy) procedures to absorb blood and fluids and to protect and separate tissues; it contains a radiopaque marker to aid detection if left behind in the patient.

lapatinib.definition: A small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets the HER2/neu (ErbB2) receptor and, to a lesser extent, the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR/ErbB1); an oral targeted therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer, commonly used in combination with capecitabine for metastatic disease.

her2.definition: A receptor tyrosine kinase in the human epidermal growth factor receptor (ERBB) family, encoded by the ERBB2 gene; its amplification or overexpression drives oncogenic signaling in several cancers, most notably breast cancer, and it is a therapeutic target for targeted cancer therapies.

torsade de pointes.definition: A life-threatening polymorphic ventricular tachycardia associated with a prolonged QT interval, characterized on ECG by twisting of the QRS complexes around the baseline; often drug- or electrolyte-related and can progress to ventricular fibrillation if not treated.

mouth ulcers.definition: Small, painful sores on the mucous membranes of the mouth (often called canker sores). They typically have a white or yellow center with a red border, arise after minor trauma or irritation and may be linked to stress or nutritional deficiencies; most heal within 1–2 weeks and are non-contagious.

xerosis.definition: Abnormally dry skin or mucous membranes due to reduced skin hydration and impaired barrier function, resulting in rough, flaky skin and possible fissures.

palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia.definition: A chemotherapy-induced, dose-limiting skin toxicity presenting as painful redness, swelling, and often blistering on the palms and soles, sometimes with burning or tingling (also known as hand-foot syndrome).

qt prolongation.definition: A lengthening of the QT interval on the electrocardiogram (ECG), reflecting delayed ventricular repolarization. It can be congenital or acquired (eg, from certain medications, electrolyte disturbances, or bradycardia) and is associated with an increased risk of torsades de pointes and other ventricular tachyarrhythmias.

lga.definition: A newborn whose birth weight is above the 90th percentile for gestational age and sex.

macrosomic.definition: Describes a fetus or newborn with abnormally large size for gestational age, usually defined by birth weight over about 4,000 g (8 lb 13 oz) or above the 90th percentile for gestational age.

ascending.definition: A directional term meaning moving upward or toward the head; in anatomy, used to describe structures that extend in a superior direction along the body axis.

descending.definition: Moving downward; in anatomy, describing structures or pathways that extend from a superior to an inferior position.

sigmoid.definition: An S-shaped structure. In anatomy, the sigmoid refers to the sigmoid colon, the S-shaped portion of the large intestine that connects the descending colon to the rectum.

larodopa.definition: A brand name for levodopa, a dopamine precursor used to treat Parkinson disease. It is converted to dopamine in the brain to replenish depleted dopamine levels and is typically given with carbidopa to reduce peripheral conversion and side effects.

mucopolysaccharidosis i.definition: A lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of the enzyme alpha-L-iduronidase (IDUA), leading to accumulation of dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate in tissues; presents across a spectrum from severe to mild phenotypes with features such as coarse facial features, corneal clouding, skeletal abnormalities, hepatosplenomegaly, developmental delay, and cardiovascular/airway complications. Treatments include enzyme replacement therapy and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

larsen's syndrome.definition: An autosomal dominant skeletal dysplasia characterized by congenital dislocations of multiple large joints (especially hips, knees, elbows, and ankles) with facial dysmorphism and other skeletal anomalies; often associated with mutations in the FLNB gene (filamin B).

laryngeal cancer.definition: Malignant Neoplasm arising from laryngeal tissues (voice box), most commonly squamous cell carcinoma of the laryngeal mucosa; risk factors include tobacco and alcohol use; commonly presents with hoarseness and may include throat pain or difficulty swallowing; treatment depends on stage and may involve surgery, radiation, and/or chemotherapy.

laryngoscope.definition: An instrument used to visualize the larynx, typically consisting of a blade attached to a handle; it is used to expose the vocal cords and facilitate endotracheal intubation.

laryngostasis.definition: Immobilization or cessation of movement of the larynx, usually due to neuromuscular impairment of the laryngeal muscles or mechanical fixation of laryngeal structures.

laryngotomy.definition: A surgical incision into the larynx to expose the laryngeal cavity for diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

laryngotracheal tube.definition: A tube inserted through the mouth or nose, passed via the larynx into the trachea to secure the airway and allow ventilation, commonly used during anesthesia and in critical care to protect the airway and facilitate breathing.

laryngotracheitis.definition: Inflammation of the larynx and trachea, usually viral, presenting with cough (often bark-like), hoarseness, and inspiratory stridor, and may cause airway obstruction; managed with supportive care, and in more severe cases with corticosteroids and airway management as needed.

laryngotracheoesophageal cleft.definition: A rare congenital anomaly in which a persistent communication exists between the larynx/trachea and the esophagus due to failure of the tracheoesophageal septum to properly separate the airway from the esophagus.

laryngopharyngeal reflux.definition: A form of gastroesophageal reflux in which gastric contents reflux into the larynx and pharynx above the upper esophageal sphincter, often causing hoarseness, chronic cough, throat clearing, globus sensation, or throat irritation, and may occur without heartburn.

laryngopharyngitis.definition: Laryngopharyngitis is inflammation of both the larynx and pharynx, typically due to viral infection or irritants, presenting with sore throat, hoarseness, coughing, and painful swallowing.

laryngopharyngography.definition: A radiographic study in which contrast medium is introduced into the pharynx to visualize the larynx and pharynx during swallowing, allowing assessment of anatomy and swallowing function.

laryngopharynx.definition: Lower part of the pharynx located behind the larynx, extending from the hyoid bone to the upper esophageal sphincter; it serves as a passage for both air and swallowed material, directing food into the esophagus and air toward the larynx, and contains the piriform recesses.

laryngoplastic.definition: Relating to laryngoplasty; pertaining to plastic surgery or reconstruction of the larynx.

phonosurgery.definition: A surgical procedure on the larynx (primarily the vocal folds) to improve, restore, or modify voice quality, typically for voice disorders, using techniques such as microlaryngoscopy, laser surgery, or injection therapy.

indirect laryngoscopy.definition: A procedure in which the larynx is visualized indirectly using a small mirror placed at the oropharynx and illuminated to view the vocal cords and glottic structures.

laryngologist.definition: A physician who specializes in diseases and disorders of the larynx (the voice box), typically an otolaryngologist with a focus on laryngology.

laryngology.definition: The branch of medicine focusing on the larynx (voice box) and its diseases, including disorders of voice, airway, and swallowing; commonly a subspecialty of otolaryngology (ENT).

laryngopharyngeal.definition: Relating to the laryngopharynx—the part of the pharynx behind the larynx that extends from the epiglottis to the esophagus and functions in swallowing while protecting the airway.

laryngeal reflex.definition: A protective reflex of the airway triggered by irritation of the laryngeal mucosa, resulting in glottic closure (laryngeal adductor reflex) and often coughing or swallowing to prevent aspiration.

laryngeal vertigo.definition: A nonstandard term used to describe vertigo or dizziness believed to be triggered by laryngeal or throat stimulation or pathology; it is not a recognized, distinct vestibular diagnosis.

laryngeal web.definition: A thin membrane or sheet of tissue spanning the glottis between the vocal folds, partially obstructing the airway and causing hoarseness; it is usually congenital from failure of laryngeal recanalization, but can be acquired after intubation or trauma.

laryngeal pouch.definition: A diverticulum of the laryngeal ventricle (laryngeal saccule), an outpouching through the wall of the larynx that can collect mucus and cause symptoms such as throat clearing, coughing, hoarseness, or aspiration; can be congenital or acquired.

diphtheritic laryngitis.definition: A laryngeal infection due to Corynebacterium diphtheriae, presenting with inflamed laryngeal mucosa and a characteristic pseudomembrane, often causing hoarseness, sore throat, cough, and potentially life-threatening airway obstruction.

laryngeal polyp.definition: A benign, usually unilateral, polypoid lesion of the larynx arising from the true vocal fold (glottic) mucosa, typically due to hemorrhage and edema after vocal trauma or irritation; causes hoarseness and voice changes; management often includes voice therapy with surgical excision if persistent or impairing voice.

laryngotracheotomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which an opening is created between the larynx and trachea to establish a direct airway, typically to relieve severe airway obstruction or to facilitate ventilation.

latanoprost.definition: A prostaglandin F2α analogue administered as topical ophthalmic drops to lower intraocular pressure by increasing uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humor; indicated for open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension.

aryepiglottic.definition: Relating to the aryepiglottic fold, a mucous-membrane fold extending from the epiglottis to the arytenoid cartilage that forms the lateral boundary of the laryngeal inlet.

arytenoid.definition: One of the two small pyramid-shaped cartilages of the larynx that articulate with the cricoid cartilage and serve as attachment points for the vocal cords; their movement allows the vocal folds to abduct or adduct.

corniculate.definition: Horn-shaped; in anatomy, refers to two tiny elastic cartilages located at the apex of the arytenoid cartilages in the larynx, projecting into the aryepiglottic folds.

thyrohyoid.definition: Relating to the thyroid cartilage and the hyoid bone; most often refers to the thyrohyoid muscle, a thin infrahyoid strap muscle that extends from the thyroid cartilage to the hyoid bone and depresses the hyoid or elevates the larynx during swallowing; innervated by fibers from C1 via the hypoglossal nerve.

lymphangioscintigraphy.definition: A nuclear medicine imaging procedure in which a radiolabeled tracer is injected into tissue to visualize lymphatic channels and regional lymph nodes, using dynamic and static images to assess lymphatic drainage and, often, to map sentinel lymph nodes before cancer surgery.

laser.definition: A concentrated beam of light; lasers are used in certain surgeries and other medical procedures.

subglottic.definition: Situated below the glottis (the opening between the vocal cords); pertaining to the region of the larynx below the vocal folds.

trabeculoplasty.definition: A laser procedure that burns small holes on the eye's trabecular meshwork to ease the flow of aqueous humor from the eye.

keratomileusis.definition: A historical corneal refractive surgery in which corneal tissue (a lenticule or button) is surgically carved to a desired curvature and then repositioned, thereby changing the eye's refractive power; a predecessor of laser-based procedures such as LASIK.

lasik.definition: Un procedimiento quirúrgico que utiliza un láser para remodelar la córnea y corregir errores refractivos (miopía, hipermetropía y/o astigmatismo), con el fin de mejorar la visión y disminuir la dependencia de gafas o lentes de contacto.

excimer.definition: An excited-state dimer formed by two atoms (typically a noble gas and a halogen) that is stable only when electronically excited; it relaxes to the ground state by emitting ultraviolet light and dissociates back into its atoms. It serves as the gain medium in excimer lasers (e.g., XeCl, KrF).

microkeratome.definition: A precision ophthalmic instrument (often a mechanized blade) used to create a thin, uniform corneal flap by cutting the anterior stromal lamella during refractive lamellar surgery such as LASIK.

gonioprism.definition: A gonioprism is a prism-shaped contact lens used during gonioscopy to visualize the iridocorneal angle of the anterior chamber, enabling assessment of angle opening and detection of angle abnormalities.

lassa.definition: A viral hemorrhagic fever caused by Lassa virus, an arenavirus endemic to West Africa; transmitted mainly through contact with rodent excreta or infected bodily fluids; presents with fever and malaise and can progress to hemorrhage and organ failure; diagnosed by specific laboratory tests; treated with ribavirin if given early; prevention focuses on rodent control and infection prevention.

latent.definition: Existing but not yet manifested or active; in infectious disease, a latent infection is a dormant, asymptomatic state of the organism in the body that may reactivate later and is not currently active or transmissible. In epidemiology, latency also denotes the interval between exposure and onset of symptoms.

incubation.definition: The period between exposure to an infectious agent and the appearance of the first symptoms; the time during which the pathogen replicates before clinical illness becomes evident. The duration varies by pathogen and host factors.

latency.definition: The interval between exposure to a pathogen (or initiating event) and the appearance of clinical symptoms or detectable disease; in infectious disease, a latent infection may persist with no symptoms and may reactivate later.

cisterna.definition: A reservoir or large sac in anatomy, formed by dilation of a duct, vessel, or space, that serves as a storage or collecting compartment (for example, the cisterna chyli in the lymphatic system or the cerebellomedullary cistern).

chyli.definition: Plural of chyle; the milky lymphatic fluid formed in the intestinal mucosa during fat absorption, composed of lymph and emulsified fats (triglycerides). It travels through the lymphatic system and tends to collect in the dilated abdominal lymphatic sac at the base of the thoracic duct.

dentate.definition: Toothed; having tooth-like projections or margins; used in anatomy to describe structures with tooth-shaped processes, such as the dentate ligaments or the dentate line.

calcarine.definition: Relating to the calcarine sulcus (fissure) on the medial surface of the occipital lobe; the banks of this groove contain the primary visual cortex (V1).

guttapercha.definition: A natural thermoplastic polymer derived from the sap of trees of the genus Palaquium (gutta-percha); used in dentistry as a root canal filling material because it becomes pliable when heated and hardens when cooled, often mixed with radiopaque fillers for visibility on X-rays.

articulator.definition: An instrument or organ involved in producing articulation. In dentistry, a mechanical device that simulates jaw movements to analyze occlusion and guide prosthetic fabrication; in speech science, the movable structures of the vocal tract (eg, lips, tongue, palate) that shape speech sounds.

meshwork.definition: An interconnected network of fibers, cells, or extracellular matrix forming a mesh-like framework that provides structural support and porous pathways within tissues.

geniculate.definition: Having a knee-like bend; knee-shaped. In anatomy, used for certain structures such as the lateral geniculate nucleus of the thalamus and the geniculate ganglion.

lateral.definition: The side or on the side.

laterality.definition: The tendency to favor or dominate one side of the body for movement and function, reflecting asymmetry between the body's sides and brain hemispheres (e.g., right- or left-handedness).

lateralization.definition: The localization or predominance of a function to one side of the body or to one cerebral hemisphere, leading to hemispheric specialization (for example, language is typically lateralized to the left hemisphere).

anterior talofibular ligament.definition: A ligament on the lateral ankle that extends from the anterior margin of the distal fibula to the neck of the talus; it stabilizes the ankle against inversion, especially in plantarflexion, and is the most commonly injured ligament in lateral ankle sprains.

posterior talofibular ligament.definition: A ligament of the ankle that runs from the posterior margin of the distal fibula to the posterior aspect of the talus; part of the lateral collateral ligament complex and the strongest of these ligaments. It resists posterior translation of the talus and is taut in dorsiflexion and external rotation, contributing to ankle stability.

calcaneofibular ligament.definition: A band of dense connective tissue extending from the tip of the fibula’s lateral malleolus to the lateral surface of the calcaneus; it is part of the lateral ankle ligament complex and resists inversion of the foot, especially when the ankle is in plantarflexion.

lateral medullary syndrome.definition: An ischemic stroke of the lateral medulla, usually from occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA), presenting with ipsilateral facial loss of pain and temperature, contralateral body loss of pain and temperature, vertigo and nystagmus, ipsilateral dysphagia and hoarseness with diminished gag reflex, ipsilateral limb ataxia, and sometimes Horner syndrome.

wallenberg’s syndrome.definition: A lateral medullary infarct (lateral medullary syndrome) due to occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery or vertebral artery, presenting with ipsilateral facial pain and temperature loss, contralateral body pain and temperature loss, dysphagia and hoarseness (nucleus ambiguus), vertigo and nystagmus, ipsilateral ataxia, and sometimes Horner syndrome.

lateral nystagmus.definition: A form of involuntary eye movement that occurs primarily in the horizontal plane, with a slow drift of the eyes in one direction followed by a rapid corrective jerk in the opposite direction; often reflects vestibular or central nervous system dysfunction, though it can be physiologic in certain gaze conditions.

lateral pectoral nerve.definition: A motor branch of the lateral cord of the brachial plexus (C5–C7) that innervates the pectoralis major; it typically pierces the clavipectoral fascia to enter the deep surface of pectoralis major and may communicate with the medial pectoral nerve.

lateral pelvic displacement.definition: A sideways shift of the pelvic girdle relative to the body's midline (in the coronal plane), often resulting in pelvic misalignment or obliquity and reflecting compensatory posture due to conditions such as scoliosis, leg-length discrepancy, or hip abductor weakness.

botryoid odontogenic cyst.definition: An uncommon, multilocular odontogenic cyst of the jaw characterized by grape-like clusters of small cystic spaces within a fibrous capsule, lined by stratified squamous epithelium, with a tendency to recur.

lateral pinch.definition: A pinch grip in which the thumb pad opposes the lateral (side) surface of the index finger, forming a key-like grip used to hold small or flat objects.

lateral pivot shift test.definition: A physical examination maneuver used to detect ACL deficiency and anterolateral rotatory instability of the knee. With the patient supine, the examiner applies a valgus stress and internally rotates the tibia, then flexes the knee from extension to about 30 degrees; a sudden tibial subluxation followed by a reduction (often with a palpable "clunk") indicates a positive test.

lateral projection.definition: In radiology, a lateral projection is a radiographic view obtained with the patient in a side-lying (lateral) position so the X-ray beam passes from one side of the body to the other, producing a side-on image of the anatomy (e.g., lateral chest or lateral skull).

pubovesical ligament.definition: Fibrous bands of pelvic fascia that attach the bladder to the pubic bone, forming part of the anterior bladder support and helping stabilize the bladder and urethra.

lateral recumbent position.definition: A position in which a patient lies on one side (right or left) with the body and head aligned horizontally and supported, commonly used for lateral decubitus imaging and certain examinations.

recumbent position.definition: A horizontal body posture where the patient is lying down; commonly used for examination or procedures and can be supine (face up), prone (face down), or lateral (side-lying).

lateral region.definition: Relating to the side of the body or an organ; situated farther from the midline, toward the outer aspect.

lateral resolution.definition: The imaging system's ability to distinguish two objects located side-by-side along the lateral (transverse) axis; defined as the minimum separable distance between two points in the lateral direction at a given depth, influenced by beamwidth, focusing, aperture, and frequency.

lateral rocking.definition: An oscillating side-to-side movement of a body part (commonly the head, trunk, or pelvis) around a coronal axis; used in examination to assess joint mobility, proprioception, or vestibular function, and may indicate laxity or imbalance if excessive.

lateral rotation.definition: Rotation of a limb or body part around its longitudinal axis away from the midline of the body; the movement is also known as external rotation.

lateral sacral artery.definition: A branch(es) of the posterior division of the internal iliac artery that supplies the sacrum and surrounding structures, traveling medially to the sacral foramina to feed sacral bones, meninges, and nerve roots, and anastomosing with nearby pelvic arteries.

lateral sinus.definition: A dural venous sinus in the skull that runs laterally from the confluence of sinuses and drains into the sigmoid sinus; commonly referred to as the transverse (lateral) sinus that collects venous blood from the brain.

lateral spinal curvature.definition: An abnormal sideways curvature of the spine, often with rotation of the vertebrae, which can cause trunk asymmetry (shoulders/hips uneven) and, in more severe cases, functional or respiratory compromise. It can be structural (fixed) or flexible (reducible).

lateral sural cutaneous nerve.definition: Cutaneous nerve of the leg originating from the common fibular (peroneal) nerve that supplies the skin of the posterolateral leg and usually joins with the medial sural cutaneous nerve to form the sural nerve.

lateral umbilical fold.definition: A peritoneal fold on the inner surface of the anterior abdominal wall that overlays the inferior epigastric vessels; it is the lateral umbilical fold.

launois’ syndrome.definition: Una rara lipomatosis generalizada caracterizada por la proliferación difusa y simétrica de lipomas subcutáneos no encapsulados, que suele iniciarse en la infancia o juventud y puede provocar deformidad física; no es neoplásica y el tratamiento es principalmente quirúrgico (resección o liposucción) cuando causa molestias estéticas o funcionales.

laurence-moon-bardet-biedl syndrome.definition: A rare autosomal recessive ciliopathy characterized by retinal dystrophy with progressive vision loss, postaxial polydactyly, obesity, intellectual disability or learning difficulties, hypogonadism (often in males), and renal anomalies; historically used to describe the overlap between Laurence–Moon and Bardet–Biedl phenotypes, though Bardet–Biedl syndrome is the more current term.

curanderismo.definition: A traditional Latin American folk healing system that blends indigenous and Catholic beliefs; administered by a curandero, it uses herbal remedies, prayers, rituals, and spiritual cleansing to address physical, psychological, and spiritual illness, often in concert with Western medicine.
