body odor.definition: An unpleasant odor produced by the skin, primarily from bacterial breakdown of sweat on the skin surface (especially apocrine sweat); influenced by hygiene, diet, hormones, medications, and certain medical conditions.

levocetirizine.definition: A selective peripheral H1-receptor antihistamine (the active enantiomer of cetirizine) used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis and chronic idiopathic urticaria; a second-generation antihistamine with relatively limited CNS penetration and lower sedation potential than first-generation agents.

perennial rhinitis.definition: A chronic nasal inflammation with year‑round symptoms (congestion, rhinorrhea, sneezing, itching) persisting most days for months to years, typically due to perennial allergens or irritants and not confined to a single season.

seasonal rhinitis.definition: A reversible, IgE-mediated allergic reaction of the nasal mucosa triggered by seasonal environmental allergens (usually pollen) causing sneezing, nasal congestion, itching, rhinorrhea, and often itchy, watery eyes during specific seasons.

chronic idiopathic urticaria.definition: A skin condition characterized by recurrent, pruritic wheals (hives) lasting longer than six weeks with no identifiable external trigger or underlying medical cause.

increased liver function tests.definition: An abnormal laboratory finding in which one or more liver enzymes (eg, AST, ALT) and/or bilirubin are elevated in the blood, indicating possible hepatocellular injury or cholestasis; it is not a diagnosis by itself and requires clinical correlation and further evaluation to determine the cause.

transient rash.definition: A rash that appears for a short duration and resolves spontaneously, typically within hours to days, without lasting skin damage; causes include viral exanthems, drug eruptions, allergic or contact dermatitis, and urticaria.

chronic manganese poisoning.definition: A neurotoxic syndrome from long-term manganese exposure (often occupational), presenting with parkinsonian features such as rigidity, bradykinesia, tremor, and gait disturbance, along with psychiatric or cognitive changes; caused by manganese deposition in the basal ganglia (notably the globus pallidus) and often showing T1MRI hyperintensity, with typically poor response to levodopa, helping distinguish it from idiopathic Parkinson disease.

movement disorders.definition: A group of neurological disorders characterized by abnormal control of voluntary movement, ranging from slowed or reduced movement to involuntary, excessive movements and impaired coordination, typically due to dysfunction in basal ganglia and related motor pathways.

emotional changes.definition: Changes in a person’s emotional state or affect, including fluctuations in mood or emotional responsiveness that can be transient or persistent and may be due to hormonal changes, medical or psychiatric illness, medications, or psychosocial factors.

levo-dromoran.definition: A potent synthetic opioid analgesic; the levo isomer of dromoran that acts as an agonist at μ-, δ-, and κ-opioid receptors, used to treat moderate to severe pain.

opioid analgesic.definition: A pain-relieving medication that acts on opioid receptors in the central nervous system to produce analgesia, often derived from or related to morphine; includes natural, semisynthetic, and synthetic opioids and is associated with risks such as dependence and respiratory depression.

levorphanol tartrate.definition: A potent synthetic opioid analgesic; the tartrate salt of the levo isomer of a morphinan derivative. It acts primarily as a μ-opioid receptor agonist and also has NMDA receptor antagonism and inhibition of norepinephrine and serotonin reuptake, used for relief of moderate to severe pain. It carries risks of respiratory depression, sedation, constipation, and potential for dependence.

acute chronic bronchitis.definition: An acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis is a sudden, sustained worsening of the chronic productive cough in a patient with known chronic bronchitis/COPD, typically with increased sputum volume or purulence and worsened dyspnea or wheeze; may be triggered by infection or other factors and is treated with bronchodilators, inhaled steroids as indicated, antibiotics if bacterial infection is suspected, and supportive care.

uncomplicated skin infections.definition: An acute bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissues that is localized and non-severe, without systemic toxicity or deeper tissue involvement, and in the absence of factors that would complicate treatment (such as immunosuppression, significant comorbidities, or implanted devices).

complicated urinary tract infections.definition: An infection of the urinary tract that occurs in the setting of abnormal urinary tract anatomy or function or significant host factors (e.g., obstruction or stones, catheterization or instrumentation, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression, or hospitalization) that predispose to treatment failure, relapse, or progression to complicated pyelonephritis; these cases typically require longer courses of antibiotics and evaluation for underlying abnormalities.

acute pyelonephritis.definition: An acute bacterial infection of the kidney involving the renal parenchyma and renal pelvis, typically from ascending spread from the lower urinary tract, presenting with fever, flank or groin pain, costovertebral angle tenderness, and urinary symptoms; requires systemic antibiotics.

quinolones.definition: A class of broad-spectrum antibiotics that kill bacteria by inhibiting DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, thereby blocking bacterial DNA replication and transcription; fluoroquinolones are a major subgroup.

multisystem organ failure.definition: Progressive dysfunction and failure of two or more organ systems resulting from a severe illness or injury (e.g., sepsis, trauma, shock), leading to impaired physiologic reserve and high risk of death.

lymphopenia.definition: A lower-than-normal number of lymphocytes in the peripheral blood, typically defined as an absolute lymphocyte count below the lower limit of normal (commonly <1.0 × 10^9/L in adults); it can be transient or persistent and may result from infections (especially viral), HIV, malnutrition, autoimmune diseases, or immunosuppressive therapy.

levulan kerastick therapy.definition: A form of topical photodynamic therapy in which 5-aminolevulinic acid (Levulan) is applied to actinic keratoses (and certain superficial skin lesions), incubated to allow uptake, and then exposed to blue light to activate the photosensitizer and destroy abnormal keratinocytes via reactive oxygen species.

levulosuria.definition: The excretion of fructose (levulose) in the urine, typically caused by a defect in fructose metabolism (e.g., essential fructosuria) or transient fructosuria after fructose ingestion.

lewis blood group system.definition: An antigen system defined by the Le^a and Le^b glycan antigens on red blood cells and in secretions; these antigens are produced by fucosyltransferases FUT3 (Lewis) and FUT2 (secretor) and are largely adsorbed from plasma onto RBC membranes rather than synthesized by the cells themselves. Expression depends on secretor status (Le^a more common in non‑secretors; Le^b in secretors), and anti-Le^a or anti‑Le^b antibodies are usually cold-reactive IgM and often clinically insignificant.

phthirus pubis.definition: A species of louse that infests coarse pubic hair, causing intense itching and sometimes rash; transmitted mainly through sexual contact; treated with topical pediculicides (e.g., permethrin 5% cream or malathion) and by laundering affected clothing and bedding, with treatment of sexual partners as needed.

leyden-mobius muscular dystrophy.definition: Not a widely recognized medical entity; there is no standardized definition in current medical literature.

leydig cell tumor.definition: A rare testicular neoplasm arising from Leydig (interstitial) cells, classified as a sex cord-stromal tumor. Most are benign, though a minority may be malignant; hormone production can cause precocious puberty in children or virilization/gynecomastia in adults. Primary treatment is surgical orchiectomy; prognosis is generally favorable for benign tumors.

lown-ganong-levine.definition: A pre-excitation syndrome with a short PR interval, normal QRS duration, and no delta waves on ECG, caused by an accessory pathway bypassing the AV node (often via James fibers) that allows rapid AV conduction and predisposes to AV nodal reentrant tachycardia.

liver function test.definition: A liver function test is a blood test panel used to assess liver injury and function, typically measuring liver enzymes (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT), bilirubin (total and direct), albumin, and coagulation parameters (INR).

large for gestational age.definition: A newborn whose birth weight exceeds the 90th percentile for that gestational age (often described as macrosomia); risk factors include maternal diabetes, obesity, and excessive maternal weight gain.

luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone.definition: A hypothalamic decapeptide (also called gonadotropin-releasing hormone) that stimulates the anterior pituitary to release luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) by binding to GnRH receptors on gonadotrophs; normally secreted in pulsatile bursts, with continuous exposure leading to receptor downregulation and suppression of gonadotropin release.

lh-rh.definition: A hypothalamic decapeptide hormone (also known as gonadotropin-releasing hormone, GnRH) that stimulates the anterior pituitary to secrete the gonadotropins luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in a pulsatile manner, regulating reproductive function.

lhermitte’s sign.definition: A transient electric shock–like sensation that runs down the spine and into the limbs when the neck is flexed, caused by demyelination or dysfunction of the cervical spinal cord (commonly seen in multiple sclerosis and other cervical myelopathies).

compression disorders.definition: A broad category of conditions caused by sustained or repetitive pressure that compress nerves, blood vessels, or other soft tissues, producing pain, numbness or weakness, diminished circulation, or tissue injury; can be acute (e.g., compartment syndrome) or chronic (e.g., compression neuropathies or vascular compression syndromes).

lichen simplex chronicus.definition: A chronic skin condition characterized by thickened, lichenified plaques produced by habitual scratching or rubbing (itch-scratch cycle), typically with intense itching and localized to accessible areas.

lichen urticatus.definition: A historical term for a pruritic urticarial eruption (hives), often implying chronic scratching with resultant lichenification; the term is rarely used in modern dermatology.

papular urticaria.definition: A pediatric pruritic eruption characterized by recurrent crops of red to pink papules (often vesicular) caused by hypersensitivity to arthropod bites, commonly fleas, mosquitoes, or bed bugs; lesions persist for days and recur over weeks to months.

glycyrrhizin.definition: A triterpenoid saponin glycoside derived from licorice root that has anti-inflammatory properties; excessive intake inhibits 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, causing apparent mineralocorticoid excess with hypertension, hypokalemia, and edema.

glycyrrhetinic acid.definition: A pentacyclic triterpenoid aglycone derived from glycyrrhizin in licorice root; inhibits 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, increasing cortisol activity at mineralocorticoid receptors and potentially causing sodium retention, potassium loss, hypertension, and edema. Used in licorice extracts and some topical anti-inflammatory preparations.

mineralocorticoid receptors.definition: A ligand-activated nuclear transcription factor that binds mineralocorticoids (primarily aldosterone) with high affinity. Upon activation, it regulates expression of genes involved in electrolyte and water homeostasis, mainly increasing sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion in the renal distal tubules and collecting ducts; it is expressed in kidney, colon, heart, and brain, and its specificity is enhanced in target tissues by 11β-HSD2, which inactivates glucocorticoids.

adam-stokes syndrome.definition: An episode of syncope due to transient, abrupt cessation of cardiac output from a bradyarrhythmia (commonly complete heart block), leading to brief cerebral hypoperfusion and loss of consciousness with spontaneous recovery once an escape rhythm resumes.

longitudinal lie.definition: An obstetric term for fetal lie in which the fetus lies with its long axis parallel to the mother's long axis (the fetus is vertical in the uterus), with cephalic or breech presentation possible.

transverse lie.definition: Fetal presentation in which the fetus lies horizontally across the uterus with the fetal spine perpendicular to the maternal spine; neither the head nor the buttocks is presenting. It is typically detected in late pregnancy and often necessitates cesarean delivery if persistent at term.

lieberkühn's glands.definition: Glands in the lining of the small intestine and colon, located at the base of the intestinal villi. They house stem cells that continuously renew the epithelium and differentiate into enterocytes, goblet cells, and enteroendocrine cells; Paneth cells at the base secrete antimicrobial enzymes such as lysozyme.

crypts of lieberkühn.definition: Tubular glands in the mucosa of the small intestine and colon at the base of the villi; contain stem cells that continually renew the intestinal epithelium and Paneth cells, giving rise to absorptive enterocytes and mucus-secreting goblet cells.

li-fraumeni cancer syndrome.definition: A hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome caused by germline mutations in the TP53 tumor suppressor gene, transmitted in an autosomal dominant pattern, associated with a high lifetime risk of multiple early-onset cancers (including sarcomas, premenopausal breast cancer, brain tumors, adrenocortical carcinoma, and leukemia).

ligament tear.definition: A rupture or tear of a ligament due to excessive stretch or force, resulting in joint instability and pain; commonly referred to as a sprain and graded from mild (Grade I) to complete rupture (Grade III).

ligamental tear.definition: A tear of a ligament (a sprain) resulting from overstretching or tearing of the fibrous tissue that connects bones across a joint; presents with pain, swelling, and possible joint instability; severity ranges from partial tear to complete rupture.

ligament tears.definition: Injury to a ligament involving tearing of its fibers, ranging from a mild overstretch (sprain) to a partial or complete rupture; typically caused by a sudden twist, fall, or impact and presents with pain, swelling, and joint instability. Severity is usually graded I–III, and treatment ranges from conservative care (rest, ice, compression, elevation, and rehabilitation) to surgical repair for a complete rupture or persistent instability.

medial collateral ligament.definition: A band of tough connective tissue on the medial side of the knee that runs from the medial femoral epicondyle to the medial tibial condyle, providing medial stability by resisting valgus forces.

lateral collateral ligament.definition: An outer-side ligament that stabilizes a joint by connecting bones on the lateral aspect and resisting varus forces; in the knee it connects the femur to the fibula.

posterior cruciate ligament.definition: A major knee ligament that runs from the posterior intercondylar area of the tibia to the medial condyle of the femur; it resists posterior translation of the tibia relative to the femur and helps stabilize the knee, especially when the knee is flexed.

ligamentum arteriosum.definition: A fibrous remnant of the fetal ductus arteriosus that in the adult forms a short ligament between the proximal left pulmonary artery and the aortic arch.

transverse acetabular ligament.definition: A fibrous band spanning the inferior acetabular notch that completes the rim of the acetabulum, converting the notch into the acetabular foramen and forming the lower boundary of the socket; it is continuous with the acetabular labrum.

costotransverse ligament.definition: A ligament that connects the tubercle of a rib to the transverse process of the corresponding vertebra, stabilizing the costotransverse joint.

ligament of the neck of the rib.word: ligament of the neck of the rib
ligament of the neck of the rib.definition: An accessory ligament of the costotransverse joint that extends from the neck of the rib to the transverse process of the vertebra above, reinforcing the articulation between the rib and the vertebral column.

ligament of the tubercle of the rib.word: ligament of the tubercle of the rib
ligament of the tubercle of the rib.definition: A ligament that connects the tubercle of a rib to the transverse process of the corresponding vertebra, forming the costotransverse joint and stabilizing rib articulation.

ligamenta flava.definition: Two short, elastic ligaments that connect the laminae of adjacent vertebrae along the posterior aspect of the spinal canal; rich in elastic fibers (hence “yellow” ligaments) and help the spine return to extension after flexion, aiding upright posture. With aging they may ossify or thicken, potentially contributing to spinal stenosis.

acetabular ligament.definition: A fibrous band spanning the acetabular notch to complete the rim of the acetabulum and form its inferior boundary (also known as the transverse acetabular ligament).

ligamentous.definition: Relating to ligaments; describing the fibrous connective tissue bands that connect bones across joints and help stabilize joints, or tissue that resembles such ligaments.

ligase.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the joining of two molecules by forming a covalent bond, usually requiring energy from ATP or NAD+; in DNA replication and repair, it seals breaks in the DNA backbone.

ligation clip.definition: A small surgical device, typically made of metal or polymer, that is applied across a vessel or duct to occlude it and achieve ligation and hemostasis; it is deployed with a clip applier and may be either nonabsorbable or absorbable, remaining in place or removed as needed.

ligation needle.definition: A surgical needle designed to pass a ligature around a vessel or duct to tie it off and achieve hemostasis.

ligation wire.definition: A thin surgical wire used to create a ligature by encircling and constricting a blood vessel or duct to stop bleeding; the wire is tightened to occlude flow and secure hemostasis.

ligature.definition: Any material that is tied around a blood vessel to stop it from bleeding.

varicose vein.definition: A dilated, tortuous vein, most commonly in the legs, caused by valvular incompetence that leads to venous reflux and pooling of blood; may cause aching, heaviness, swelling, and visible bulging.

strep throat.definition: A bacterial infection of the throat and tonsils caused by group A Streptococcus (Streptococcus pyogenes), typically presenting with acute sore throat, fever, painful swallowing, tonsillar exudates, and tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy. Diagnosis is by rapid antigen detection test or throat culture; treatment with antibiotics such as penicillin or amoxicillin shortens illness, reduces contagiousness, and helps prevent complications like rheumatic fever and poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.

childbirth.definition: The process by which a fetus is delivered from the uterus through the birth canal, typically following labor contractions that dilate the cervix and culminate in the birth of the newborn and delivery of the placenta.

head trauma.definition: An injury to the scalp, skull, or brain caused by external mechanical force to the head, ranging from mild traumatic brain injury (concussion) with transient confusion or loss of consciousness to severe injury with coma or intracranial hemorrhage. May involve skull fracture, contusions, or other intracranial bleeding.

guilt.definition: A self-conscious emotion involving remorse or distress over real or imagined wrongdoing or failure to meet moral or social standards, often accompanied by a drive to atone or repair; when excessive or persistent, it can be a feature of mood or anxiety disorders.

fear.definition: A basic emotion characterized by an aversive response to a real or perceived threat, with autonomic arousal and avoidance or escape behaviors—part of the body's protective fight-or-flight system.

torso.definition: The main part of your body not including head, arms, or legs. Also called your trunk.

anogenital regions.definition: The anatomical area that includes the anus and the external genitalia, together with the surrounding perineal skin and underlying tissues; essentially the perineal region between the thighs.

white spot disease.definition: Parasitic infection of fish caused by Ichthyophthirius multifiliis, characterized by numerous small white cysts on the skin and gills (white spots), often with irritation, flashing, and rapid gill movement.

lienal vein.definition: A vein draining the spleen; it runs along the posterior surface of the pancreas and drains into the hepatic portal vein, receiving tributaries such as the short gastric veins and the left gastroepiploic vein.

splenic vein.definition: A large vessel that drains blood from the spleen (and nearby structures), typically running posterior to the pancreas and joining with the superior mesenteric vein to form the hepatic portal vein; it receives blood from the short gastric and left gastroepiploic veins.

lien.definition: A term for the spleen, the abdominal organ that filters blood, removes old or damaged red blood cells, stores blood, and contributes to immune responses.

fovea.definition: A small pit or depression; in anatomy, specifically the retina, the fovea centralis is a shallow pit in the center of the macula lutea containing densely packed cone photoreceptors, is nearly avascular, and provides the sharpest central vision.

space of peritoneum.definition: An anatomical potential space within the abdomen and pelvis formed by the peritoneum (between the parietal and visceral peritoneum) that contains a small amount of lubricating serous fluid and allows viscera to move; it can enlarge abnormally with fluid or gas (ascites, pneumoperitoneum).

ligase chain reaction.definition: A molecular diagnostic method that detects specific DNA sequences or single-nucleotide differences by using a DNA ligase to join two adjacent oligonucleotide probes only when they are perfectly complementary to the target; the ligated probes are then amplified and detected, yielding a highly specific signal.

dna ligase.definition: An enzyme that seals nicks in the DNA backbone by catalyzing the formation of phosphodiester bonds, thereby joining DNA strands during replication and repair (uses ATP in eukaryotes and NAD+ in bacteria).

ligases.definition: Enzymes that catalyze the formation of covalent bonds to join two molecules, typically requiring an energy source such as ATP or NAD+. They include enzymes that seal breaks in the DNA backbone to join fragments during replication and repair, and enzymes that attach ubiquitin to substrate proteins.

synthetase.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the joining of two substrates to form a new bond, typically using energy from ATP hydrolysis; members are ligases (EC 6), including aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases as common examples.

pupillary reflex.definition: A reflex constriction of the pupil in response to light, mediated by the afferent visual pathway (optic nerve) and the efferent parasympathetic pathway (oculomotor nerve), with direct and consensual pupil responses.

photopic eye.definition: The state of the visual system when functioning under bright light in which cone photoreceptors mediate vision, enabling color discrimination and high-acuity central (foveal) vision.

light therapy.definition: A treatment that uses controlled exposure to specific wavelengths and intensities of light to achieve therapeutic effects, such as improving mood and circadian rhythm (bright light therapy) or treating skin conditions (phototherapy).

light-adapted eye.definition: An eye adapted to bright light in which cone photoreceptors mediate vision, yielding high acuity and color vision with lower sensitivity; the pupil is constricted and rod activity is diminished.

retinal hypothalamic pathway.definition: An afferent projection from intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells in the retina to the suprachiasmatic nucleus of the hypothalamus, conveying light information to regulate and entrain circadian rhythms to the light–dark cycle; the pathway uses glutamate (often with PACAP) as neurotransmitters.

prostaglandin synthesis.definition: An enzymatic pathway that converts arachidonic acid into prostanoids via cyclooxygenase (COX-1/COX-2) to prostaglandin G2/H2, which is then transformed by specific synthases into prostaglandins (e.g., PGE2, PGD2, PGF2α, PGI2) and thromboxane A2; these mediators regulate inflammation, pain, fever, and vascular homeostasis.

linear iga bullous disease.definition: An autoimmune subepidermal blistering disease characterized by IgA autoantibodies depositing in a linear pattern along the basement membrane zone, producing tense vesicles or bullae; diagnosis is by direct immunofluorescence showing linear IgA along the basement membrane.

erbs muscular dystrophy.definition: There is no recognized medical condition by that name. The phrase likely reflects confusion between Erb's palsy (a birth-related brachial plexus injury causing upper-arm weakness) and muscular dystrophy (a group of inherited disorders causing progressive skeletal muscle weakness, such as Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy due to dystrophin deficiency).

lignocaine.definition: A local anesthetic of the amide class used for topical, infiltrative, nerve block, and regional anesthesia; it also serves as a class Ib antiarrhythmic for certain ventricular arrhythmias, acting by blocking voltage-gated sodium channels to inhibit action potential propagation in nerves and cardiac tissue.

lincomycin hydrochloride.definition: A salt form of the antibiotic lincomycin (a lincosamide) used to treat susceptible bacterial infections; it inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by reversibly binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit, blocking peptidyl transferase.

lincocin.definition: A brand-name antibiotic (lincomycin) in the lincosamide class used to treat serious infections caused by susceptible anaerobic bacteria and certain Gram-positive cocci; typically administered by intramuscular or intravenous injection; can cause antibiotic-associated diarrhea and pseudomembranous colitis, and is largely supplanted by clindamycin due to safety and pharmacokinetic advantages.

lindane.definition: A potent organochlorine insecticide (gamma-hexachlorocyclohexane) that was formerly used topically to treat scabies and head lice; it is a neurotoxin with risks of seizures and significant safety concerns, leading to restricted or banned use in many countries.

gamma-benzene hexachloride.definition: The gamma isomer of hexachlorocyclohexane, an organochlorine insecticide (also known as lindane) historically used to treat scabies and pediculosis; it is neurotoxic, acting by antagonizing GABA_A receptor–mediated inhibition, and is associated with seizures and other toxicity, with persistence leading to regulatory restrictions.

blood disorders.definition: A broad category of diseases affecting the blood or its forming tissues, including abnormalities of red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, or plasma coagulation factors, that impair oxygen transport, immune defense, hemostasis, or thrombosis.

neurological damage.definition: Injury or impairment of the nervous system (central or peripheral) that disrupts structure or function, leading to deficits in movement, sensation, cognition, or autonomic regulation.

linea nigra.definition: A pigmented, vertical line on the abdomen that commonly appears during pregnancy, typically from the pubic symphysis to the umbilicus (sometimes extending higher); it results from increased melanocyte activity due to maternal hormones (estrogen and melanocyte-stimulating hormone) and usually fades after delivery.

linea semilunaris.definition: A curved tendinous line on the ventrolateral abdominal wall marking the lateral border of the rectus abdominis, where the aponeuroses of the external oblique, internal oblique, and transversus abdominis meet and separate the rectus muscle from the lateral abdominal muscles.

linea arcuata.definition: An anatomical line on the inner surface of the anterior abdominal wall marking the lower limit of the posterior rectus sheath; above it the rectus abdominis is enclosed by both anterior and posterior sheaths, while below it the posterior sheath is absent and the muscle lies directly on the transversalis fascia.

linea terminalis.definition: A line delineating the pelvic inlet, extending from the sacral promontory to the pubic crest; it marks the boundary between the abdominal cavity and the true pelvis and is formed by the sacral promontory, the arcuate line of the ilium, the pectineal line (pecten pubis), and the pubic crest.

corneal limbus.definition: The corneal limbus is the annular transition zone between the cornea and sclera, containing limbal stem cells that replenish the corneal epithelium and serving as the boundary between the avascular cornea and the vascularized sclera.

transversus abdominis.definition: The deepest layer of the abdominal wall muscles with horizontal fibers; it helps compress the abdominal contents and stabilize the trunk (core).

internal abdominal oblique.definition: A muscle of the anterolateral abdominal wall, lying deep to the external oblique and superficial to the transversus abdominis; it helps compress the abdomen and rotate and flex the trunk.

lingual nerve.definition: An entirely sensory branch of the mandibular division (V3) of the trigeminal nerve that supplies general sensation to the anterior two‑thirds of the tongue, the floor of the mouth, and lingual gingiva; it receives taste fibers from the chorda tympani and carries parasympathetic fibers to the submandibular and sublingual glands via hitchhiking on the nerve.

lingual gingiva.definition: The portion of gingiva surrounding the teeth on the tongue-facing (lingual) aspect; the mucosal tissue on the lingual side of the dental arches.

lingual leukoplakia.definition: A white patch or plaque on the tongue that cannot be rubbed off and cannot be attributed to another identifiable cause; considered a premalignant lesion with potential for dysplasia and progression to squamous cell carcinoma.

lingual goiter.definition: Enlargement of ectopic thyroid tissue located at the base of the tongue, arising from persistent lingual thyroid tissue; can cause dysphagia, dyspnea, or airway obstruction, and is evaluated with imaging and thyroid function tests with management ranging from observation to surgical excision in symptomatic cases.

lingual crib.definition: An orthodontic appliance fixed to the tongue-facing (lingual) surfaces of the lower front teeth, forming a cage-like wire framework that acts as a barrier to tongue thrusting and is used to treat tongue-thrust habits and related anterior open bite in children by retraining tongue posture.

lingual bar.definition: A major connector for a mandibular removable partial denture; a thin, horseshoe-shaped metal bar that sits on the lingual surfaces of the lower teeth and connects the left and right sides, requiring about 7–8 mm of vertical space between the floor of the mouth and the gingival margins, providing strength with relatively good tongue clearance and ease of hygiene compared with a lingual plate.

lingual flange.definition: The portion of a denture that extends along the tongue-facing (lingual) aspect of the jaw, forming a flange to aid retention and border seal by engaging the tongue and surrounding mucosa.

frankfurt horizontal plane.definition: A cephalometric reference plane defined by a line passing through the porion (upper border of the external auditory meatus) and the orbitale (lowest point on the inferior orbital margin); when the head is in natural head position, this plane is horizontal and is used to orient craniofacial radiographs and assess facial relationships.

cingulate gyrus.definition: A curved fold on the medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere, just above the corpus callosum, forming part of the limbic system; it participates in emotion formation and processing, learning, memory, and attentional regulation, with the anterior region involved in emotion and autonomic control and the posterior region in memory and visuospatial processing.

olfactory bulb.definition: A paired neural structure at the base of the forebrain that receives input from olfactory receptor neurons via the olfactory nerve, processes odor information (via mitral and tufted cells), and relays signals to the olfactory cortex and limbic regions, enabling the sense of smell.

limbic lobe.definition: A cortical ring around the corpus callosum that forms part of the limbic system; it includes the cingulate gyrus and parahippocampal gyrus (with the hippocampal formation) and is involved in emotion, memory, and related behaviors.

limb-kinetic apraxia.definition: A disorder of skilled, precise limb movements in which the patient cannot perform fine, deliberate actions (e.g., finger tapping, writing) despite normal strength, sensation, and comprehension; movements are clumsy and imprecise due to impaired motor planning/programming in higher cortical motor areas (often involving the premotor/parietal regions).

ideomotor apraxia.definition: A neurological disorder characterized by the inability to perform purposeful gestures or pantomime tool use on command despite intact comprehension and basic motor function; automatic or spontaneous movements may be better preserved, often due to left hemisphere parietal–premotor damage.

lipedema.definition: A chronic adipose tissue disorder characterized by symmetric, disproportionate enlargement of subcutaneous fat in the legs (and sometimes arms), sparing the feet, often painful and easy to bruise; predominantly affects women and is not caused by obesity, often resistant to weight loss.

lingual pain.definition: Pain localized to the tongue; a symptom that may arise from local mucosal injury, infection, inflammation, neuropathic nerve irritation, or systemic disease, often described as burning, aching, or tenderness.

vincent's stomatitis.definition: An acute, painful necrotizing infection of the gingiva, now usually called acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis (ANUG). It features necrotic, bleeding interdental gingiva with punched-out papillae, foul odor, and often fever; caused by a mixed anaerobic bacterial infection (including spirochetes and fusiform bacteria) in the setting of poor oral hygiene, stress, or malnutrition. Management includes thorough oral hygiene, antiseptic rinses, debridement, and antibiotics when indicated.

lingual papilla.definition: A small projection on the dorsal surface of the tongue; one of the tongue’s papillae (types include filiform, fungiform, circumvallate, and foliate). Fungiform, circumvallate, and foliate papillae contain taste buds, while filiform papillae provide mechanical roughness.

lingual rest.definition: In dentistry, a component on the tongue-facing (lingual) side of a dental appliance (such as a lingual arch or removable partial denture) that rests against the tongue or lingual teeth to stabilize and retain the appliance by resisting dislodging forces.

lingual thyroid.definition: An ectopic thyroid tissue mass located at the base of the tongue, arising from failure of the thyroid primordium to descend during embryogenesis; it may cause dysphagia, dysphonia, or airway obstruction and may be the only thyroid tissue in the body.

residual thyroid tissue.definition: Thyroid tissue that remains in the neck after incomplete thyroidectomy or ablation; it may continue to produce thyroid hormones and can be a source of persistent or recurrent thyroid disease.

lingual tonsil.definition: A collection of lymphoid tissue located on the posterior base of the tongue, forming part of Waldeyer's ring in the oropharynx; it participates in immune defense of the upper airway and can enlarge with infection.

lymphoid follicles.definition: Discrete, spherical aggregations of lymphoid tissue within secondary lymphoid organs (e.g., lymph nodes and spleen) rich in B cells, often containing germinal centers where B cells proliferate and undergo somatic hypermutation and class-switch recombination during an immune response.

lingua?.definition: The tongue; the movable muscular organ of the mouth responsible for taste, manipulation of food for chewing and swallowing, and articulation of speech.

lingula.definition: A small tongue-shaped projection or eminence in anatomy, such as the lingula of the mandible on the medial ramus near the mandibular foramen, or the lingula of the left upper lobe of the lung.

lingula of the lung.definition: A tongue‑like projection of the left upper lobe that lies anteriorly and medially against the heart; it is separated from the rest of the left upper lobe by the oblique fissure and is homologous to the middle lobe of the right lung.

lingulectomy.definition: Surgical removal of the lingula, the tongue-shaped projection of the left upper lobe of the lung, typically performed to excise localized disease in that region (e.g., cancer or infection).

linguoocclusal.definition: Pertaining to the interaction between the tongue and the occlusal (chewing) surfaces of the teeth, describing tongue posture or movements that influence bite and dental contact during swallowing or speech.

linguoversion.definition: A dental orientation in which a tooth is tipped toward the tongue (lingual direction) from its normal position; a form of malposition (the opposite being buccoversion).

liniment.definition: A medicated liquid preparation rubbed onto the skin to relieve pain or stiffness; typically contains active irritants (e.g., menthol, camphor, methyl salicylate) in an alcohol or oil base.

linin.definition: A large heterotrimeric glycoprotein of the basement membrane that promotes cell adhesion, differentiation, and migration; forms part of the basal lamina and interacts with integrins and other extracellular matrix components to mediate attachment between cells and the extracellular matrix.

undifferentiated carcinoma.definition: A high-grade malignant epithelial neoplasm in which tumor cells lack morphologic features of differentiation toward any specific epithelial lineage; cells are typically pleomorphic and undifferentiated, often with poor or absent keratinization.

linkage.definition: The tendency of two or more genes or genetic markers that are close together on the same chromosome to be inherited together during meiosis because recombination between them is unlikely.

linkage disequilibrium.definition: Non-random association of alleles at different loci in a population, such that certain haplotypes occur more or less frequently than expected by chance; due to physical linkage and limited recombination, and it decays with distance.

linkage group.definition: A set of genes located on the same chromosome that tend to be inherited together during meiosis because recombination between them is infrequent; effectively corresponds to one chromosome or a chromosome segment.

linkage map.definition: A genetic map showing the relative order and distance of genetic loci on a chromosome, inferred from recombination frequencies during meiosis; distances are expressed in centiMorgans and reflect linkage between markers rather than physical base-pair distance.

linked genes.definition: Genes located on the same chromosome that tend to be inherited together because they are physically linked; they do not assort independently unless crossing over during meiosis separates them, with recombination frequency depending on their distance apart (often expressed in centimorgans).

lipoma annulare coli.definition: A rare benign lesion of the colon where fat-containing lipomas encircle a segment of the bowel (annular or circumferential submucosal lipomas), causing luminal narrowing and potentially obstructive symptoms; often asymptomatic.

lipoma arborescens.definition: A rare benign intra-articular lesion in which the synovium proliferates into frond-like (arborescent) projections containing mature adipose tissue, most often in the knee; presents with chronic joint effusion and swelling, with MRI showing fatty synovial proliferation and treated by synovectomy, usually with good prognosis and rare recurrence.

lipoma capsulare.definition: A benign tumor of fat tissue that is surrounded by a fibrous capsule, forming a well-circumscribed, slow-growing subcutaneous mass.

lipoma cavernosum.definition: A benign tumor composed of mature adipose tissue arising within the corpora cavernosa of the penis; a rare, slow-growing, noncancerous lesion that may be asymptomatic or present as a penile mass, with treatment usually surgical excision if symptomatic or for cosmetic reasons.

lipoma diffusum renis.definition: A rare benign condition in which fat tissue diffusely infiltrates or replaces renal parenchyma rather than forming a discrete fatty tumor, and which can be associated with renal atrophy and impaired function.

lipoma dolorosa.definition: A benign adipose tissue tumor that is painful or tender; presents as a subcutaneous lump that is unusually tender on palpation, potentially due to nerve involvement or local compression, and is typically treated by surgical excision if symptomatic.

lipoma fibrosum.definition: A benign adipose-tissue tumor characterized by mature fat cells with a prominent fibrous stroma; a fibrolipoma variant.

lipoma myxomatodes.definition: A benign adipose-tissue tumor in which mature fat cells are set in a prominent myxoid (mucoid) extracellular matrix; a myxoid lipoma variant, typically slow-growing and painless, with histology that helps distinguish it from myxoid liposarcoma.

lipomatosis.definition: A condition characterized by the development of multiple benign lipomas (tumors of adipose tissue), usually presenting as soft, painless, mobile subcutaneous nodules; may be familial and, in some cases, involve diffuse or symmetric fatty deposits.

lipomatosis dolorosa.definition: A rare disorder characterized by multiple painful lipomas (benign fatty tumors) that cause chronic pain, often accompanied by obesity; the exact cause is unknown and it is sometimes referred to as Dercum disease.

lipomatosis gigantea.definition: An uncommon, benign disorder of adipose tissue characterized by diffuse or multifocal overgrowth of subcutaneous fat, producing large, soft, non-tender lipomatous masses that may be localized or widespread; often hereditary and may cause cosmetic or functional impairment; treatment—surgical debulking or excision—with potential recurrence.

lipomatosis renis.definition: A benign condition in which adipose tissue proliferates in the renal sinus, progressively replacing and compressing the renal parenchyma and leading to renal atrophy; often associated with chronic inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or longstanding obstruction, and can cause hydronephrosis.

lipomatous.definition: Relating to fat; composed of adipose tissue; often used to describe lesions predominantly made of fat.

lipomatous nephritis.definition: An uncommon or obsolete term for fatty infiltration of the kidney, in which adipose tissue or lipid-laden inflammatory changes replace or surround renal parenchyma.

lipomatous myxoma.definition: A rare benign soft-tissue neoplasm composed of mature adipose tissue within a prominent myxoid (gelatinous) stroma; histology shows fat cells in a mucopolysaccharide-rich matrix without cellular atypia or infiltrative behavior, distinguishing it from myxoid liposarcoma.

lipometabolism.definition: Lipometabolism is the body's management of lipids, including their synthesis, storage, mobilization, and breakdown for energy. It encompasses lipolysis of triglycerides to glycerol and free fatty acids, beta-oxidation of fatty acids to acetyl-CoA, lipogenesis to store fat, and transport of lipids via lipoproteins, all regulated by hormones.

lipomyoma.definition: A benign tumor composed of mature adipose tissue that arises within or between skeletal muscles (an intramuscular lipoma), typically presenting as a slow-growing, painless mass and sometimes showing infiltration into muscle fibers.

lipomyxoma.definition: A rare benign soft tissue neoplasm consisting of mature adipocytes embedded in a myxoid (mucoid) stroma, often with fibrous septa; typically presents as a slow-growing subcutaneous or intramuscular mass and may be locally infiltrative.

lipophilia.definition: A tendency to dissolve in or associate with fats; the property of being lipid-loving or lipid-soluble.

lipoprotein lipase.definition: An enzyme that hydrolyzes triglycerides in circulating triglyceride-rich lipoproteins (chylomicrons and VLDL) to release free fatty acids and glycerol, enabling tissue uptake of fatty acids; activated by apolipoprotein C-II and associated with endothelial surfaces via heparan sulfate proteoglycans.

lipoprotein electrophoresis.definition: A laboratory technique in which lipoproteins in plasma or serum are separated by electrophoresis on a supporting medium (eg, agarose or cellulose acetate) under an electric field, producing distinct bands corresponding to lipoprotein classes (eg, chylomicrons, VLDL, LDL, HDL) to characterize lipoprotein patterns and dyslipidemias.

liposarcoma.definition: A malignant neoplasm of adipose tissue (fat), a type of soft tissue sarcoma that typically arises in deep soft tissues such as the thigh or retroperitoneum; it has several histologic subtypes (well-differentiated, myxoid, round cell, pleomorphic, dedifferentiated). Treatment usually involves wide surgical resection with negative margins, with radiotherapy or chemotherapy considered based on subtype, size, and location.

liposis.definition: A fatty change within cells or tissues due to intracellular lipid accumulation; a form of lipidosis (fatty degeneration).

lipid pneumonia.definition: A form of pneumonia caused by aspiration or inhalation of lipid-containing substances (most often mineral oil or other oils), leading to accumulation of lipid-laden macrophages in the alveoli and a chronic inflammatory reaction.

lipiduria.definition: Presence of lipids in the urine, often due to nephrotic-range proteinuria; microscopically, it shows oval fat bodies and fatty casts.

lipid nephrosis.definition: A historic term for nephrotic syndrome, most often due to minimal-change disease in children; features include edema, marked proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, hyperlipidemia, and lipiduria.

lipodystrophia progressiva.definition: A rare disorder characterized by progressive loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue (lipodystrophy), resulting in partial or generalized lipoatrophy, often accompanied by metabolic complications such as insulin resistance, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis.

congenital total lipodystrophy.definition: A rare autosomal recessive genetic disorder characterized by near-total loss of adipose tissue from birth, resulting in a muscular appearance and severe metabolic disturbances including insulin resistance, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatic steatosis, and early-onset diabetes; caused by mutations in genes involved in adipocyte development (e.g., AGPAT2, BSCL2, CAV1, PTRF).

familial partial lipodystrophy.definition: A hereditary disorder characterized by selective loss of subcutaneous fat from the limbs and trunk with relative preservation or accumulation of fat in the face and neck, often presenting in adolescence or early adulthood. It commonly causes metabolic complications such as insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, hypertriglyceridemia, and hepatic steatosis; most forms are autosomal dominant and result from mutations in genes regulating adipocyte development and fat distribution (e.g., LMNA, PPARG).

insulin lipodystrophy.definition: Localized alteration of subcutaneous fat at insulin injection sites, presenting as lipoatrophy (fat loss) or lipohypertrophy (fat hypertrophy), caused by repeated insulin administration and technique; it can impair and unpredictably alter insulin absorption.

membranous lipodystrophy.definition: Not a widely used or current clinical term; when encountered, it refers to a pattern of lipodystrophy in which subcutaneous fat is lost or replaced by membranous (membrane-like) material, often described histopathologically rather than as a distinct syndrome. If you want, I can look for related terms or more context.

progressive lipodystrophy.definition: A group of disorders characterized by progressive loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue (lipodystrophy), often starting in adolescence or adulthood, typically causing fat loss from the limbs and trunk with possible fat accumulation in the face/neck, and commonly associated with metabolic abnormalities such as insulin resistance, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis.

lipodystrophy at insulin injection site.definition: Localized alteration of subcutaneous fat at sites of repeated insulin injections, usually presenting as fatty enlargement (lipohypertrophy) or fat loss with indentations (lipoatrophy). These changes can alter insulin absorption and dosing; prevention includes rotating injection sites, avoiding injections into affected areas, and using proper technique.

lipofuscin.definition: A yellow-brown intracellular pigment granule composed of lipid-containing residues of lysosomal digestion; it accumulates in aging and postmitotic cells and is considered a marker of aging and oxidative damage.

lipogenesis.definition: An anabolic metabolic process by which acetyl-CoA is converted into fatty acids (de novo lipogenesis), primarily in the liver and adipose tissue, using NADPH; the fatty acids are then esterified to form triglycerides for storage.

lipogranuloma.definition: A granulomatous inflammatory reaction in adipose tissue to lipid material, often from fat necrosis or exogenous oil, characterized by lipid-laden macrophages and foreign-body giant cells with surrounding fibrosis.

lipogranulomata.definition: A granulomatous inflammatory reaction to lipid material in tissue, characterized by foamy macrophages and multinucleated giant cells surrounding fat droplets, often due to fat necrosis, trauma, or injection of oil-based substances.

lip.definition: One of the two fleshy folds forming the opening of the mouth—the upper and lower lips—composed of skin, orbicularis oris muscle, and mucous membrane (vermilion), that seal the oral cavity and aid in speech, eating, and facial expression.

lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia.definition: A rare form of interstitial pneumonia characterized by diffuse lymphocytic infiltration of the pulmonary interstitium (often with lymphoid follicle formation), commonly associated with autoimmune diseases (notably Sjögren syndrome) or immunodeficiency, and presenting with progressive cough and dyspnea with diffuse interstitial opacities on imaging.

intestinal infarction.definition: Death of intestinal tissue due to acute ischemia from occlusion of mesenteric arteries or veins, causing bowel necrosis; typically presents with severe abdominal pain out of proportion to examination and may progress to peritonitis and sepsis, requiring urgent intervention (revascularization and/or resection of nonviable bowel).

baclofen.definition: A GABA-B receptor agonist that acts as a central skeletal muscle relaxant to reduce spasticity, commonly used for conditions such as multiple sclerosis and spinal cord injury; available orally or intrathecally.

lioresal.definition: A skeletal muscle relaxant that acts as a GABA-B receptor agonist to reduce spasticity; used to treat spasticity due to conditions such as multiple sclerosis, spinal cord injury, or cerebral palsy. Available orally or intrathecally (via pump).

liothyronine.definition: A synthetic form of the thyroid hormone triiodothyronine (T3) used to treat hypothyroidism; more potent and faster-acting than T4 (levothyroxine) with a shorter half-life; administered orally or intravenously; can cause hyperthyroid symptoms if overdosed.

secondary hypothyroidism.definition: Hypothyroidism caused by pituitary dysfunction leading to inadequate TSH secretion, with low free T4 (and usually low or inappropriately normal TSH).

liotrix.definition: A fixed-dose combination thyroid hormone replacement containing levothyroxine (T4) and liothyronine (T3) in a 4:1 ratio, used to treat hypothyroidism by supplying both thyroid hormones.

minimal change disease.definition: A nephrotic syndrome characterized by edema, heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and usually normal blood pressure; glomeruli appear normal on light microscopy but show podocyte foot-process effacement on electron microscopy, and it is typically highly responsive to corticosteroids.

lipodystrophy progressiva.definition: A rare disorder in which subcutaneous fat progressively disappears in a characteristic pattern (often starting with the face, trunk, and limbs), leading to fat redistribution and metabolic disturbances such as insulin resistance, diabetes, hypertriglyceridemia, and fatty liver; it can be congenital, familial, or acquired and may present as generalized or partial lipodystrophy.

lipolysis.definition: The enzymatic breakdown of stored triglycerides in adipose tissue into glycerol and free fatty acids, enabling their use for energy; mediated by lipases (eg, adipose triglyceride lipase and hormone-sensitive lipase) and stimulated by catecholamines and low insulin.

lipolytic.definition: Causing lipolysis; relating to the breakdown of fats (usually triglycerides) into glycerol and free fatty acids.

lipase.definition: An enzyme secreted by the pancreas that helps the body break down fats.

listeriosis.definition: A bacterial infection caused by Listeria monocytogenes, typically acquired by eating contaminated food; it ranges from mild illness in healthy people to severe invasive disease (e.g., meningitis, septicemia) in pregnant women, newborns, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals.

listeria monocytogenes.definition: Gram-positive, non–spore-forming facultative intracellular bacterium that causes listeriosis, usually acquired from contaminated food; can cause meningitis, sepsis, and fetal or neonatal infection, especially in pregnant women, newborns, and immunocompromised individuals.

acquired immune deficiency syndrome.definition: A disease caused by a virus (HIV or human immunodeficiency virus) that makes it hard for your body to fight diseases. Also called AIDS.

liposomal cytarabine.definition: A liposome-encapsulated formulation of the chemotherapy agent cytarabine (Ara-C) designed for intrathecal administration to provide prolonged release and exposure, used in the treatment of neoplastic meningitis (leptomeningeal metastasis).

doxorubicin hydrochloride.definition: A cytotoxic chemotherapy agent in the anthracycline class; the hydrochloride salt of doxorubicin intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II, causing DNA strand breaks. Used to treat a variety of cancers and typically given by intravenous infusion; associated with dose-related cardiotoxicity and risk of congestive heart failure with cumulative exposure.

liposuction.definition: A cosmetic procedure that removes fat from an area of the body.

lipectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove adipose (fat) tissue from the body, typically for cosmetic contouring.

liston's forceps.definition: Historical large surgical forceps used to grasp and hold tissue during operations (notably amputations); named after the 19th‑century surgeon Robert Liston.

lithane.definition: Not a standard medical term; no concise definition appears in trusted medical dictionaries. It may be a brand name, a misspelling, or a term from another field. If you can share context (drug, condition, or procedure) or confirm the spelling, I can help further.

lithium carbonate.definition: An inorganic salt used as a mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder to treat and prevent manic and depressive episodes; it has a narrow therapeutic range and requires regular serum lithium level monitoring. Common adverse effects include tremor, polydipsia and polyuria, hypothyroidism, and potential nephrotoxicity, with toxicity causing CNS symptoms such as confusion or ataxia.

lithobid.definition: A brand-name formulation of lithium carbonate, a mood stabilizer used to treat and prevent manic and depressive episodes in bipolar disorder. It has a narrow therapeutic index and requires regular monitoring of serum lithium levels, renal function, and thyroid function.

lithotriptor.definition: A device used to crush calculi (stones) in the urinary or biliary tract, typically as part of lithotripsy, and can operate mechanically, ultrasonically, or with laser energy.

lithotrity.definition: The mechanical crushing of urinary stones within the urinary tract to fragments that can pass, historically done with a lithotrite; an older term largely replaced by lithotripsy.

lithogenesis.definition: The process of stone formation (calculus formation) in the body, such as kidney or gallstones, typically due to supersaturation and crystallization of mineral components, with nucleation, crystal growth, and aggregation.

ostembryon.definition: Not a standard medical term; if intended, it would refer to embryonic bone formation (ossification) during fetal development.

osteopedion.definition: A rare condition in which a dead fetus within the maternal abdomen becomes ossified or calcified, producing a rigid calcified fetal mass.

lithostat.definition: A urease inhibitor (acetohydroxamic acid) used to treat and prevent struvite kidney stones caused by urease-producing bacteria; it inhibits urease, decreasing ammonia production and stone formation; adverse effects include hepatotoxicity; liver function monitoring is recommended.

lithotabs.definition: Not a standard medical term; no formal definition available in standard references. It may be a brand name or a misspelling. If you can provide context (spelling, country, or intended use), I can help clarify or offer a precise definition.

hepatic cells.definition: The liver’s primary parenchymal cells responsible for most of its metabolic, detoxification, and synthetic functions, including bile production, glucose and lipid metabolism, and synthesis of plasma proteins; they are organized in plates separated by vascular sinusoids.

urinary calculus.definition: A stone formed in the urinary tract (kidney, ureter, or bladder) from crystallized minerals—most commonly calcium oxalate or calcium phosphate—that may cause flank or groin pain, hematuria, and sometimes urinary obstruction.

uterolithiasis.definition: A rare condition characterized by the formation or presence of calculi (stones) within the uterine cavity.

livedo.definition: A mottled, violaceous, netlike pattern of the skin caused by dilation of superficial cutaneous venous plexuses and slowed blood flow; often more evident in cold exposure and may be benign or indicate underlying vascular, autoimmune, or hematologic disorders.

livedo vasculitis.definition: A chronic cutaneous thrombotic vasculopathy presenting with livedo reticularis and often painful leg ulcers; caused by thrombosis of small dermal vessels with variable inflammation and may be associated with hypercoagulable states or antiphospholipid antibodies. Treatment targets thrombosis and underlying risk factors.

segmented hyalinizing vasculitis.definition: A vasculitic process in which discrete segments of small- to medium-sized vessels show hyaline (hyalinized) thickening of the vessel wall with inflammatory infiltrates, usually demonstrated histologically; it can be a pattern seen in various localized or systemic vasculitides rather than a single distinct disease.

measles virus.definition: A single-stranded, negative-sense RNA virus of the genus Morbillivirus in the family Paramyxoviridae; the causative agent of measles, transmitted via respiratory droplets; enveloped, with a nonsegmented negative-sense RNA genome.

mumps virus.definition: A member of the Paramyxoviridae family (genus Rubulavirus); an enveloped, negative-sense, single-stranded RNA virus that causes mumps, a contagious illness typically presenting with parotid gland swelling and fever.

rubella virus.definition: A positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus of the genus Rubivirus in the family Matonaviridae that causes rubella; transmitted by respiratory droplets; infection is usually mild but can cause congenital rubella syndrome if母 infection occurs during early pregnancy; preventable by vaccination (MMR).

measles vaccine.definition: A live-attenuated vaccine used to prevent measles by eliciting an immune response to the attenuated measles virus; it is typically given in combination with mumps and rubella (MMR) or as MR, usually in a two-dose schedule.

mumps vaccine.definition: A vaccine that prevents mumps by introducing a live attenuated mumps virus to stimulate active immunity; typically given as part of the measles–mumps–rubella (MMR) vaccine in a two-dose schedule.

rubella vaccine.definition: A live attenuated vaccine used to induce immunity to rubella; it is usually given as part of the measles–mumps–rubella (MMR) or measles–rubella (MR) combination vaccines, typically in childhood, to prevent rubella infection and congenital rubella syndrome. It is contraindicated in pregnancy.

measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine.definition: A combined live attenuated vaccine that protects against measles, mumps, and rubella; administered by injection, usually in two doses during childhood, to induce immunity to all three diseases.

oral poliovirus vaccine.definition: An oral vaccine containing live-attenuated poliovirus (Sabin strains) given by mouth to induce protective immunity against poliovirus, primarily by generating intestinal as well as systemic immunity. It can replicate in the gut and shed in stool; due to rare risk of vaccine-associated or vaccine-derived poliovirus, many programs have shifted toward the injected inactivated poliovirus vaccine in some regions.

live oral poliovirus vaccine.definition: A vaccine containing live, attenuated poliovirus given by mouth to induce mucosal (intestinal) and systemic immunity against poliomyelitis; it can replicate in the gut and be shed, with a small risk of vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis or circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus in underimmunized populations.

dysphoria.definition: A profound sense of unease, dissatisfaction, or distress; a mood disturbance characterized by persistent discontent, restlessness, and unhappiness.

live attenuated measles virus vaccine.definition: A vaccine composed of a live but attenuated (weakened) measles virus that replicates minimally in the recipient to stimulate a protective immune response against measles; commonly given as part of combined measles-containing vaccines (e.g., MMR).

sinusoids.definition: Wide, irregular capillaries with a discontinuous or fenestrated endothelium and an incomplete basement membrane, allowing slow blood flow and rapid exchange of substances between blood and surrounding tissue; they occur notably in the liver, spleen, and bone marrow.

portal.definition: Relating to a vascular pathway that carries blood from one capillary bed to another, especially from the gastrointestinal tract to the liver for processing.

intraperitoneal.definition: Located within the peritoneal cavity; describing structures that are enclosed by the peritoneum or injections/drugs administered into the peritoneal space.

hepatocellular.definition: Relating to hepatocytes, the primary functional cells of the liver.

vinyl.definition: A synthetic polymer derived from vinyl chloride; polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is used to manufacture flexible plastics for medical disposables such as gloves, tubing, and bags.

alphafetoprotein.definition: A fetal glycoprotein produced primarily by the fetal liver and yolk sac; it is the major protein in fetal plasma and can be detected in maternal blood. In pregnancy screening, elevated maternal serum AFP suggests neural tube or ventral wall defects, while low AFP can be associated with Down syndrome; outside obstetrics, AFP is a tumor marker for hepatocellular carcinoma and certain germ cell tumors.

sulfobromophthalein.definition: A water-soluble diagnostic dye formerly used to assess hepatic excretory function (the bromsulfophthalein test); after IV administration, it is taken up by the liver and excreted into bile and then urine, with the rate of clearance reflecting liver function.

segments.definition: A distinct, bounded portion of an organ or body part, demarcated by anatomical landmarks or vascular/nerve supply, used to describe subdivision for diagnostic, surgical, or research purposes.

kupffer.definition: A resident liver macrophage located in the sinusoids that phagocytoses bacteria, dead cells, and debris from the portal blood and participates in immune surveillance.

scintillation.definition: Emission of light by a scintillating material when it is excited by ionizing radiation, producing detectable photons used for radiation detection and imaging (as in scintillation detectors in nuclear medicine).

camera.definition: A device that uses a lens to project light onto a photosensitive surface (film or digital sensor) to capture still or moving images, enabling documentation and visualization in medical imaging (e.g., endoscopy, ophthalmology).

detector.definition: A device or sensor that detects a specific biological, chemical, or physical parameter and provides a measurable signal indicating its presence or level.

complications.definition: An unfavorable or additional medical condition that develops during the course of a disease or after a medical procedure, potentially worsening outcomes or requiring further treatment.

leakage.definition: The escape or seepage of a liquid, gas, or other substance from a container, body cavity, wound, or closed system due to a breach or faulty containment.

emphysematous.definition: Relating to emphysema; containing gas in tissues or organs, usually due to infection with gas-forming organisms.

lobar.definition: Of or relating to a lobe.

lobular.definition: Relating to a lobe or lobule; composed of lobules or divided into lobules.

polyvalent.definition: Having multiple antigenic determinants; in immunology, describing a vaccine or antibody that recognizes or provides protection against several antigens or serotypes.

cholangiomas.definition: A tumor arising from the epithelial lining of the bile ducts (cholangiocytes) within the liver or biliary tract; it can be benign, with the malignant form known as cholangiocarcinoma.

lobate.definition: A structure that is divided into lobes or has a lobulated (multi-lobed) appearance; possessing lobes separated by grooves or indentations.

lockjaw.definition: A serious disease caused by a bug (bacteria) that lives in the soil. It causes muscles to spasm. Also called tetanus.

trismus.definition: A reduced ability to open the mouth caused by spasm or contraction of the jaw muscles (lockjaw), commonly due to tetanus, dental infection, or trauma.

regional.definition: Relating to a particular region or part of the body; confined to a specific area rather than systemic.

neo-cobefrin.definition: Not found in standard medical references; likely a misspelling or nonstandard name. If intended as a vasopressor, it would denote an alpha-adrenergic agonist used to raise blood pressure by constricting systemic vessels in acute care or anesthesia settings. If you have context or a source, I can refine the definition.

morphea.definition: Localized scleroderma characterized by hard, thickened patches or linear bands of skin due to excess collagen deposition; subtypes include plaque-type, generalized, and linear involvement.

lochia.definition: Postpartum vaginal discharge from the uterus after childbirth, composed of blood, mucus, and endometrial debris, reflecting uterine involution; it typically progresses from red to pink-brown to yellow-white over about 2–6 weeks.

rubra.definition: Red; in medical use, Latin-derived term describing redness or a red-colored discharge—most often referring to lochia rubra, the postpartum vaginal discharge consisting of blood and tissue that appears after childbirth and lasts for a few days.

alba.definition: Latin for "white"; used in anatomy to denote whiteness or white-colored structures, such as the linea alba (the fibrous midline of the abdomen) and substantia alba (white matter of the brain).

loeffler's.definition: An acute, self-limited eosinophilic lung condition with migratory, transient pulmonary infiltrates and peripheral blood eosinophilia, typically linked to parasitic infections or drug reactions; symptoms often include cough, fever, and wheeze, with chest imaging showing fleeting, changing infiltrates.

onchocerciasis.definition: A parasitic disease caused by the filarial nematode Onchocerca volvulus, transmitted by bites of infected Simulium blackflies; it causes chronic dermatitis and ocular inflammation that can lead to irreversible blindness (river blindness).

lomefloxacin.definition: A fluoroquinolone antibiotic that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, causing bactericidal activity against a broad range of Gram-negative and some Gram-positive bacteria; used to treat infections caused by susceptible organisms.

lomotil.definition: A prescription antidiarrheal consisting of diphenoxylate with atropine; it slows gut motility by activating opioid receptors in the intestinal wall and reduces stool frequency and liquidity, used for short-term treatment of diarrhea.

norethindrone.definition: A synthetic progestin used in contraception and hormonal therapy; it provides progestational activity and is used in combination oral contraceptives as well as in progestin-only pills, with some androgenic effects.

tromethamine.definition: A buffering agent given intravenously to treat metabolic acidosis by accepting hydrogen ions and thereby raising the blood pH.

lodoxamide.definition: A topical ophthalmic mast cell stabilizer and antihistamine used to prevent and treat symptoms of allergic conjunctivitis (such as itching, redness) by inhibiting mast cell degranulation and histamine release.

vernix.definition: A white, waxy, cheese-like coating of lipids and shed skin cells that covers the skin of the fetus and newborn, protecting it from amniotic fluid exposure and aiding skin barrier function.

lonalac.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. Could you verify spelling or provide context (drug, disease, or brand) so I can help accurately?

hodgkinsdisease.definition: A malignant lymphoma of the lymphatic system characterized by Reed-Sternberg cells, typically presenting with painless lymphadenopathy and sometimes systemic symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), with a high cure rate using modern chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

ultralente.definition: An old long-acting insulin preparation used to provide basal insulin coverage in diabetes mellitus; due to slow absorption, it produces a prolonged effect over many hours and has largely been superseded by newer long-acting insulins.

gravesdisease.definition: An autoimmune hyperthyroidism caused by stimulating autoantibodies to the TSH receptor (thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins) that increase thyroid hormone production; commonly presents with diffuse goiter and thyrotoxic symptoms and may include ophthalmopathy and pretibial myxedema. Treatment options include antithyroid drugs, radioactive iodine, or thyroidectomy.

stimulator.definition: A device that delivers electrical or other stimulation to nerves, muscles, or tissues to modulate physiological activity, commonly used for therapeutic neuromodulation and may be implanted or external.

thyroidgland.definition: A two-lobed gland located in the front of the neck below the larynx (voice box). It secretes hormones that help regulate the body's metabolism and calcium balance.

lats.definition: A large, broad back muscle that extends, adducts, and medially rotates the arm at the shoulder; originates from the thoracolumbar fascia and lower spine, iliac crest, and lower ribs, and inserts on the humerus.

thyroidstimulatinghormone.definition: A hormone secreted into the bloodstream by the pituitary gland that stimulates the thyroid gland. Doctors measure levels of TSH to determine whether a person’s thyroid hormone levels are normal.

plasmamembrane.definition: A phospholipid bilayer that encloses the cytoplasm of a cell, forming a selective barrier that regulates movement of substances in and out and hosts proteins involved in transport, signaling, and cell recognition.

long-arm.definition: Not a formal medical term. If encountered, it is nonstandard shorthand that may refer to the upper limb (shoulder to hand) or to the long bones of the upper extremity (humerus, radius, and ulna); in formal anatomy, use "upper limb" or "upper extremity."

positioning.definition: The act of placing a patient into a specific body posture for medical evaluation, diagnostic imaging, treatment, or surgery to facilitate access to the target area and to promote safety and comfort.

deformities.definition: Abnormal shapes or positions of body parts due to congenital defects, injury, disease, or degeneration, often associated with functional impairment or cosmetic concerns.

transtibial.definition: Relating to or occurring below the knee; specifically, a below-knee amputation performed through the tibia.

longevity.definition: The length of an individual's life or lifespan; the duration from birth to death, influenced by genetics, health status, lifestyle, and environmental factors, and often considered alongside population life expectancy.

capitis.definition: Latin for “of the head”; used in anatomical terms to denote relation to or location at the head.

colli.definition: Neck; the cervical region of the body. In Latin anatomy, it is the genitive singular of collum ('neck'), used to denote "of the neck" in anatomical terms.

longitudinal.definition: Relating to length or the long axis of a body or organ; oriented lengthwise; in research, describing a study that follows the same subjects over time.

ultrasoundography.definition: A diagnostic imaging method that uses high-frequency sound waves to produce real-time images of internal body structures. It is performed with a transducer placed on the skin with gel and is commonly used for obstetric, abdominal/pelvic, and vascular imaging (often with Doppler to assess blood flow).

longqtsyndrome.definition: A congenital or acquired disorder of cardiac repolarization that prolongs the QT interval on the ECG, predisposing to torsades de pointes and sudden cardiac death; caused by mutations in cardiac ion channels or by drugs/electrolyte disturbances.

low-contrast.definition: Describing tissues or images with only small differences in density or brightness between neighboring structures, leading to poor delineation and reduced ability to detect subtle lesions; in imaging, this is referred to as low-contrast resolution or low-contrast detectability.

ltc.definition: A range of services and supports designed to meet the personal and health-care needs of people who cannot live independently due to aging, chronic illness, or disability, including help with daily activities, supervision, and medical or social services provided at home, in the community, or in institutional settings.

memory.definition: A cognitive process by which information is encoded, stored, and later retrieved; it includes sensory, short-term (working), and long-term memory and relies on neural networks involving the hippocampus, prefrontal cortex, and related structures.

alzheimersdisease.definition: A progressive brain disease that causes memory loss, impaired thinking, and personality changes.

lougehrigsdisease.definition: A progressive neurodegenerative disease affecting upper and lower motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord, leading to muscle weakness, atrophy, spasticity, fasciculations, and ultimately paralysis; onset is typically in mid to late adulthood; no cure; management is supportive with multidisciplinary care and, in some cases, disease-modifying therapies such as riluzole or edaravone.

hirschsprungdisease.definition: Congenital absence of enteric ganglion cells in the distal colon due to failed neural crest cell migration, causing a functional bowel obstruction. Presents with delayed passage of meconium and abdominal distension in newborns and chronic constipation in children. Diagnosis is by rectal biopsy showing absence of ganglion cells; treatment is surgical resection of the aganglionic segment with restoration of bowel continuity (pull-through).

loperamide.definition: A peripherally acting opioid receptor agonist used as an over-the-counter antidiarrheal that slows intestinal motility by acting on μ-opioid receptors in the gut, increasing water absorption and reducing stool frequency; it has minimal central nervous system effects because it poorly crosses the blood–brain barrier.

intraepithelial.definition: Within the epithelial layer; confined to the epithelium and not invading through the basement membrane into underlying tissues.

occipitotransverse.definition: Pertaining to a fetal head position during labor in which the occiput is oriented sideways, producing a transverse lie in the birth canal; the back of the head faces the maternal left or right side.

loteprednol.definition: An ophthalmic corticosteroid prodrug (loteprednol etabonate) used topically to treat ocular inflammation and allergic conjunctivitis; acts as a glucocorticoid receptor agonist with anti-inflammatory effects and is designed as a "soft steroid" that is rapidly inactivated in ocular tissues to minimize steroid-related side effects, such as elevated intraocular pressure.

lotrimin.definition: A brand-name antifungal medication containing clotrimazole, applied topically to treat fungal skin infections such as athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm.

trenchfever.definition: An infectious disease caused by Bartonella quintana transmitted by body lice, characterized by fever with severe shin pain, headaches, and sometimes a rash; historically common among soldiers in trenches.

lower-respiratory-tract-infection.definition: An infection of the lower respiratory tract, including the trachea, bronchi, and lungs; commonly manifests as pneumonia, acute bronchitis, or bronchiolitis and can be caused by viral or bacterial pathogens, often with cough, fever, dyspnea, and chest discomfort.

absorptive-hypercalciuria.definition: An idiopathic or familial disorder in which increased intestinal calcium absorption leads to hypercalciuria, typically with normal serum calcium and parathyroid hormone levels, and a predisposition to calcium-containing kidney stones.
