tuberculous meningitis.definition: A form of meningitis caused by infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis that involves the meninges, typically with subacute onset of fever, headache, altered mental status, and meningismus; CSF shows lymphocytic pleocytosis with elevated protein and low glucose; diagnosed by CSF analysis plus TB testing; treated with multi-drug anti-tuberculous therapy and adjunctive corticosteroids.

arachnoid trabeculae.definition: Slender filaments of the arachnoid mater that extend across the subarachnoid space from the arachnoid to the pia mater, forming a delicate mesh that helps suspend the brain and maintain cerebrospinal fluid dynamics.

pia mater.definition: A delicate innermost layer of the meninges that tightly adheres to the brain and spinal cord, following their contours; it is highly vascular and covers the surface of the CNS.

pseudotumor cerebri.definition: An elevated intracranial pressure without a mass lesion or hydrocephalus, causing headaches and papilledema with potential vision loss; typically affects overweight women of reproductive age; diagnosed by exclusion with imaging ruling out a mass and elevated CSF pressure on lumbar puncture; managed with weight loss and acetazolamide, with surgical options for refractory cases.

pseudomembranous stomatitis.definition: A form of oral mucosal infection characterized by removable white to yellowish pseudomembranes (curd-like plaques) on the mucosa that, when scraped off, leave a reddened, inflamed surface; most commonly caused by Candida species (oral candidiasis) and seen in immunocompromised individuals, neonates, denture wearers, or after antibiotic or corticosteroid therapy.

vestibular lip.definition: A region of the lip that lines the oral vestibule—the labial vestibular mucosa—forming the boundary between the lips and the dental arches.

meningocele.definition: A congenital herniation in which the meninges protrude through a defect in the skull or vertebral column, forming a cerebrospinal fluid–filled sac that contains meninges but typically does not include neural tissue.

poliomyelitis virus.definition: A nonenveloped, positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus of the genus Enterovirus in the family Picornaviridae that causes poliomyelitis; transmitted primarily by fecal-oral spread, it has three serotypes (PV1–PV3) and can range from asymptomatic infection to aseptic meningitis or acute flaccid paralysis due to CNS invasion. Vaccination with inactivated (IPV) or oral (OPV) poliovirus vaccines prevents disease.

arboviruses.definition: Arboviruses are viruses transmitted to humans or other vertebrates by arthropod vectors (primarily mosquitoes and ticks), often causing febrile illness or encephalitis.

herpesviruses.definition: Large family of enveloped double-stranded DNA viruses (Herpesviridae) that infect humans and many animals; they establish lifelong latency with episodic reactivation and cause a broad spectrum of diseases—from mucocutaneous lesions (e.g., herpes simplex), varicella and shingles, to mononucleosis-like illness, congenital CMV infections, and EBV/HHV-associated cancers; replication occurs in the nucleus and viruses have a tegument and envelope.

coxsackievirus.definition: A nonenveloped, positive-sense, single-stranded RNA virus of the genus Enterovirus (family Picornaviridae). Serotypes within this group can cause hand-foot-mouth disease and herpangina, as well as myocarditis, pericarditis, aseptic meningitis, and pleurodynia; transmitted primarily via the fecal-oral and respiratory routes.

antifungal medications.definition: Drugs used to treat fungal infections by inhibiting fungal growth or killing fungi; common classes include azoles (ergosterol synthesis inhibitors), polyenes (ergosterol-binding membrane disruptors), echinocandins (cell wall synthesis inhibitors), allylamines (squalene epoxidase inhibitors), and nucleoside analogs like flucytosine.

nasogastric tube feeding.definition: Delivery of nutritionally complete liquid formula directly into the stomach via a tube passed through the nose (nasogastric tube), used for short-term enteral feeding when oral intake is not possible or adequate.

stiff neck.definition: A symptom characterized by neck muscle tension causing pain and a reduced ability to move the head and neck freely; commonly due to muscle strain, overuse, or poor posture, but can reflect cervical spine disorders or, if accompanied by fever or severe headache, more serious conditions such as meningitis.

meningococcemia.definition: A bloodstream infection with Neisseria meningitidis (meningococcus) that may occur with or without meningitis; characterized by fever and a petechial or purpuric rash and can progress to septic shock and disseminated intravascular coagulation.

meningococcus.definition: An encapsulated, gram-negative diplococcus bacterium that can cause meningitis and meningococcemia; it commonly resides in the nasopharynx and is transmitted through respiratory droplets.

meningococcal.definition: Relating to meningococcus, the bacterium Neisseria meningitidis, which can cause meningitis and meningococcemia.

waterhouse-friderichsen syndrome.definition: An acute adrenal insufficiency caused by bilateral hemorrhage of the adrenal glands, most often in the setting of meningococcal septicemia, leading to shock, purpuric rash, and disseminated intravascular coagulation.

meningococcal polysaccharide vaccine.definition: A vaccine containing purified capsular polysaccharides from Neisseria meningitidis (typically serogroups A, C, W, and Y) to induce serogroup-specific protective antibodies against meningococcal disease. It is a non-conjugate (T-cell–independent) vaccine, generally less immunogenic in young children and providing shorter-term protection compared with conjugate vaccines, and is mainly used in older children and adults or during outbreaks.

rifampin.definition: An antibiotic in the rifamycin class that inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, blocking RNA synthesis; it is used to treat active and latent tuberculosis and to prevent meningococcal disease in exposed individuals, among other infections. It is a potent hepatic enzyme inducer with many drug interactions and can cause orange-red discoloration of urine, tears, and sweat.

meningovascular neurosyphilis.definition: An infectious form of neurosyphilis in which Treponema pallidum causes chronic meningitis with obliterative endarteritis of meningeal and cerebral vessels, leading to ischemic strokes and various focal neurologic deficits. Symptoms may include headache, meningismus, focal deficits, seizures, and cognitive changes; CSF typically shows lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein, and positive syphilis serology (eg, CSF VDRL or FTA-ABS).

meningoencephalomyelitis.definition: Inflammation of the meninges, brain (encephalitis), and spinal cord (myelitis) simultaneously or in overlapping regions, typically caused by infectious or immune-mediated processes, and presenting with fever, headache, altered mental status, seizures, and focal neurologic deficits.

meningoencephalopathy.definition: A disorder involving pathology of both the meninges and the brain parenchyma, leading to neurologic dysfunction; etiologies include infectious, inflammatory, or metabolic processes, and it is sometimes used to describe presentations that lie between meningitis and encephalitis.

meningomyelocele.definition: A neural tube defect in which both the meninges and the spinal cord (or nerve roots) protrude through a defect in the vertebral arches, forming a sac; commonly affects the lumbosacral region and often causes motor and sensory impairment below the lesion, frequently with hydrocephalus and Chiari II malformation.

meningoencephalocele.definition: A congenital herniation of meninges and brain tissue through a skull defect, forming a sac (a form of encephalocele); often associated with neurological impairment and may require surgical repair.

menkes kinky hair syndrome.definition: A rare X-linked disorder of copper transport caused by mutations in the ATP7A gene, leading to defective intestinal copper absorption and systemic copper deficiency. It presents in infancy with sparse, kinky hair, failure to thrive, hypotonia, developmental delay or psychomotor regression, seizures, and connective tissue abnormalities; labs show low serum copper and ceruloplasmin. Early copper histidine therapy can improve outcomes, but without treatment it progresses to neurodegeneration and early death.

menometrorrhagia.definition: Heavy or prolonged uterine bleeding that occurs at irregular intervals (a combination of menorrhagia and metrorrhagia).

menorrhagia.definition: Heavy menstrual bleeding that is prolonged or excessive enough to interfere with daily activities; clinically defined as blood loss >80 mL per cycle, or bleeding lasting more than 7 days, or requiring frequent pad or tampon changes.

menostasis.definition: Cessation or suppression of menstruation; the absence of menstrual periods (amenorrhea).

menstrual cramps.definition: Painful cramping in the lower abdomen during or just before menstrual bleeding, caused by prostaglandin-induced uterine contractions; classified as primary dysmenorrhea (no pelvic pathology) or secondary dysmenorrhea (due to conditions such as endometriosis, fibroids, or pelvic inflammatory disease).

menstrual phase.definition: The first phase of the menstrual cycle in which the functional endometrium is shed and vaginal bleeding occurs, caused by a fall in ovarian hormones (estrogen and progesterone) after corpus luteum regression; typically lasts about 3–7 days.

proliferative phase.definition: A phase of tissue growth and regeneration characterized by active cell proliferation; in the menstrual cycle, the estrogen-driven rebuilding and thickening of the endometrium after menses, culminating in ovulation.

secretory phase.definition: Phase after ovulation in the menstrual cycle during which the endometrium is transformed under progesterone into a thick, secretory, glycogen-rich lining to prepare for implantation; lasts about 14 days unless pregnancy occurs.

imperforate hymen.definition: A congenital defect in which the hymenal membrane completely occludes the vaginal opening, blocking the outflow of menstrual blood and typically causing primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain at puberty; treated with surgical hymenotomy to create an opening.

ovarian follicles.definition: Fluid-filled sacs within the ovaries that contain immature oocytes; they grow and mature under hormonal control, secrete estrogens, and release a mature oocyte at ovulation, after which the remaining tissue forms the corpus luteum.

spermogenesis.definition: The process by which male germ cells in the testes develop into mature spermatozoa, starting from spermatogonial stem cells and including mitotic proliferation, meiosis I and II, and spermiogenesis, occurring in the seminiferous tubules and regulated by hormones such as FSH and testosterone.

multiple gestation.definition: A pregnancy in which two or more fetuses develop in the uterus simultaneously (e.g., twins, triplets, or higher-order multiples), often with increased obstetric risk.

hemorrhagic spots.definition: Small, non-blanching skin or mucous membrane lesions caused by extravasation of blood from capillaries; include petechiae and purpura and may indicate thrombocytopenia, coagulation disorders, vasculitis, infection, or local trauma.

contraindications.definition: An attribute or condition in a patient that makes the use of a medical treatment or procedure inadvisable due to risk of harm or lack of benefit; classified as absolute contraindications (prohibiting use) or relative contraindications (use with caution or additional precautions).

serogroup.definition: A classification of microorganisms, usually bacteria, defined by a shared set of surface antigens detected by serology, often involving capsule polysaccharides.

immunizing agents.definition: Substances that stimulate the immune system to develop protective immunity against a specific disease, typically via vaccination (e.g., vaccines, toxoids, and other immunogenic preparations).

gram-negative diplococcus.definition: A Gram-negative bacterium that occurs as paired cocci (diplococci) on microscopy; classic examples are Neisseria species (e.g., Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Neisseria meningitidis).

meningococci.definition: Meningococci are Gram-negative diplococci of the genus Neisseria, most commonly Neisseria meningitidis, that colonize the nasopharynx and can invade the bloodstream and meninges, causing meningitis and meningococcemia; transmitted by respiratory droplets.

meniscectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove all or part of a damaged meniscus in the knee, typically performed arthroscopically to relieve pain, locking, or instability and improve knee function.

meniscus.definition: A crescent-shaped fibrocartilaginous structure within a joint (most commonly the knee) that cushions and stabilizes the articulation between bones and distributes load; there are medial and lateral versions.

menisci.definition: Fibrocartilaginous, crescent-shaped discs between articular surfaces (especially in the knee) that cushion load, distribute weight, and stabilize the joint by improving congruence during movement.

meniscocyte.definition: A cell of the meniscus, a fibrocartilaginous disc in a joint; typically a fibrochondrocyte that maintains the extracellular matrix of the meniscal tissue.

meniscocytosis.definition: Not a recognized medical term; if used, it might denote increased cellularity of the knee meniscus (the fibrocartilaginous tissue in the joint), i.e., a hypothetical proliferation of meniscal cells, but there is no established disease by this name.

merkel cell carcinoma.definition: A rare, aggressive cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma arising from Merkel cells, usually presenting as a painless, rapidly enlarging firm nodule on sun-exposed skin in older adults; often associated with Merkel cell polyomavirus; high risk of regional and distant metastasis; treated with wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy, with radiotherapy or systemic immunotherapy for advanced disease.

meralgia paresthetica.definition: A sensory mononeuropathy from compression of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve as it passes under the inguinal ligament, causing numbness, tingling, burning, or pain on the anterolateral thigh, typically without motor weakness.

mercurialism.definition: Mercurialism is mercury poisoning, usually chronic, resulting from exposure to elemental mercury or its inorganic/organic compounds; it presents with tremors, neuropsychiatric changes (erethism), gingivitis with hypersalivation, and renal impairment.

intermittent porphyria.definition: An autosomal dominant disorder of heme biosynthesis due to deficiency of porphobilinogen deaminase, causing acute neurovisceral attacks (severe abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, tachycardia, hypertension, and neuropsychiatric symptoms); urine shows elevated porphobilinogen and delta-aminolevulinic acid and may darken on exposure to air; attacks are triggered by drugs, fasting, or hormonal changes and are treated with hemin and avoidance of triggers.

symphysis menti.definition: A midline articulation between the left and right halves of the mandible at the chin; a secondary cartilaginous (fibrocartilaginous) joint that is largely immobile in adulthood and ossifies with age to form a single mandible.

mental protuberance.definition: The projection on the anterior mandible that forms the chin; the forward-most part of the lower jaw, also known as the mental eminence.

mental tubercle.definition: A small bony eminence on the external surface of the mandible at the chin region; typically there are paired mental tubercles that flank the mental protuberance and help define the shape of the chin.

menton.definition: The lowest point on the chin; the most inferior point on the mandible used as a cephalometric landmark.

orthodontic treatment.definition: Orthodontic treatment is a dental specialty that diagnoses, prevents, and corrects misaligned teeth and jaws, usually using braces, clear aligners, or other appliances to straighten teeth, correct bite issues, and improve function and aesthetics.

amalgams.definition: A dental filling material consisting of mercury alloyed with silver, tin, copper, and sometimes zinc, used to fill dental cavities; historically the most common filling material.

promethazine.definition: A first-generation antihistamine with antiemetic and sedative properties, used to treat allergy symptoms, motion sickness, and nausea or vomiting; a phenothiazine derivative that blocks H1 receptors and has anticholinergic effects.

promethazine hydrochloride.definition: A first-generation phenothiazine antihistamine (H1 receptor antagonist) used to relieve allergic symptoms, prevent motion sickness, and treat nausea and vomiting; commonly used as a sedative and antiemetic; exists as the hydrochloride salt.

meperidine hydrochloride.definition: An opioid analgesic; the hydrochloride salt form of meperidine (pethidine), a synthetic μ-opioid receptor agonist used for short-term relief of moderate to severe pain; it can cause central nervous system toxicity from its metabolite normeperidine, especially with renal impairment or prolonged use.

mephobarbital.definition: A barbiturate drug used as a sedative-hypnotic and anticonvulsant; it enhances GABA-A receptor–mediated inhibition in the CNS to produce sedation and seizure control, with risks of CNS depression, tolerance, dependence, and respiratory depression.

mepivacaine.definition: A local anesthetic of the amide class that blocks sodium channels in nerve membranes to reversibly inhibit nerve conduction; used for regional anesthesia (infiltration, nerve blocks, epidural or spinal anesthesia) and has an intermediate duration, often prolonged by co-administration with a vasoconstrictor such as epinephrine.

carbocaine.definition: An amide local anesthetic (mepivacaine) used for regional nerve blocks and infiltration anesthesia to produce temporary loss of sensation; often combined with a vasoconstrictor like epinephrine to prolong duration.

mephyton.definition: A brand name for phytonadione (vitamin K1), a fat-soluble vitamin that enables hepatic synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X; used to prevent and treat vitamin K deficiency and to reverse warfarin anticoagulation when appropriate.

menthol.definition: A naturally occurring monoterpene alcohol found in peppermint and other mint oils; used as a flavoring agent and topical analgesic, and it produces a cooling sensation by activating cold-sensitive TRPM8 receptors.

mentholated camphor.definition: A topical preparation containing menthol and camphor that acts as a counterirritant to provide temporary relief of minor muscle or joint pain; when used as a chest rub, it may help relieve cough symptoms, producing a cooling sensation (menthol) and local irritation (camphor).

mercurial diuretic.definition: An older diuretic that contains mercury; historically used to treat edema but now largely obsolete due to high risk of nephrotoxicity and mercury poisoning, with its diuretic effect arising from damaging proximal tubular cells and inhibiting sodium reabsorption.

mercury bichloride.definition: A highly toxic inorganic mercury compound, mercuric chloride (HgCl2). Historically used as a topical antiseptic and disinfectant; exposure, especially by ingestion or dermal absorption, can cause severe mercurial poisoning with gastrointestinal, renal, and neurological effects, and its medical use is now largely obsolete due to toxicity.

mercuric salts.definition: Inorganic mercury compounds in which mercury is in the +2 oxidation state (Hg2+), i.e., salts of mercuric ions with various anions; highly toxic and corrosive, historically used as antiseptics and disinfectants. Examples include mercuric chloride (HgCl2), mercuric sulfate (HgSO4), and mercuric nitrate (Hg(NO3)2).

organic mercurials.definition: A class of chemical compounds in which mercury is covalently bonded to carbon (R–Hg); includes alkyl and aryl mercurials (e.g., methyl- and phenylmercury compounds) that have been used as antiseptics, preservatives, or antifungals, but many are highly toxic (neurotoxic and nephrotoxic), with use now restricted in many applications.

mepenzolate.definition: A gastrointestinal antispasmodic agent that blocks muscarinic receptors (anticholinergic), reducing smooth muscle contractions and gastric secretions; historically used to treat peptic ulcer disease and dyspepsia.

mercury thermometer.definition: An instrument consisting of a sealed glass stem containing liquid mercury; as temperature rises, mercury expands and rises in a calibrated capillary to indicate temperature, commonly used for body temperature measurement but largely replaced by digital or alcohol-based thermometers due to mercury toxicity.

meroanencephaly.definition: A neural tube defect, a partial form of anencephaly marked by severe underdevelopment of the brain with rudimentary cerebral tissue and usually poor prognosis.

meroblastic.definition: A type of embryonic cleavage in which only a portion of the egg cytoplasm divides, because the yolk-rich region does not participate in cleavage; results in incomplete or discoidal cleavage with a blastodisc forming at the animal pole.

merocrine gland.definition: A gland that releases its secretions by exocytosis (merocrine secretion), with the secretory cell remaining intact and no loss of cytoplasm.

meromelia.definition: A congenital limb deficiency in which part of a limb is missing, with the proximal portion present and distal segments absent.

meropenem.definition: A broad-spectrum carbapenem antibiotic (bactericidal) used for serious infections caused by susceptible Gram-positive, Gram-negative, and anaerobic bacteria; inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin‑binding proteins; administered intravenously; often reserved for hospital‑acquired or complicated infections; may cause seizures at high doses.

merozoite.definition: A small, invasive, asexual stage of certain Apicomplexan parasites (such as Plasmodium) released from a schizont that invades host cells, especially red blood cells, to produce new merozoites.

merozoites.definition: Merozoites are the small, asexual, invasive forms produced by schizogony of Apicomplexan parasites (most notably Plasmodium); they invade host cells—primarily red blood cells—and develop into trophozoites to continue the parasite's asexual replication cycle.

merozygote.definition: A bacterium that contains two copies of a gene region—one on the chromosome and a second copy carried by an introduced plasmid or phage—resulting in partial diploidy for that region; used in genetic complementation and mapping.

merrf syndrome.definition: A maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder caused by mutations in mitochondrial DNA (most commonly MT-TK tRNA-Lys) that disrupts oxidative phosphorylation. It is characterized by myoclonic epilepsy and ataxia, with ragged-red fibers seen on muscle biopsy.

merrifields knife.definition: A small, sharp surgical knife used for precise skin incisions in dermatologic or cosmetic/plastic surgery.

meruvax ii.definition: A live attenuated measles vaccine (monovalent) manufactured by Merck, used to immunize children against measles; administered by intramuscular injection and derived from the Edmonston-Enders strain.

berger’s disease.definition: A kidney disease caused by deposition of IgA-containing immune complexes in the glomerular mesangium, leading to episodic hematuria (often after mucosal infections) with variable proteinuria; prognosis ranges from isolated hematuria to progression to chronic kidney disease; diagnosed by kidney biopsy showing mesangial IgA deposition.

mesangiocapillary glomerulonephritis.definition: An older name for membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis, a glomerular disease with mesangial proliferation and capillary wall thickening resulting in a tram-track pattern of the glomerular basement membrane on microscopy, usually due to immune complex deposition or complement-mediated injury.

mesangium.definition: Structural component of the renal glomerulus comprised of specialized cells and extracellular matrix; provides mechanical support to glomerular capillaries, modulates filtration surface area by contraction, and participates in clearing debris and immune complexes.

mescaline.definition: A naturally occurring psychedelic phenethylamine alkaloid found in cacti such as peyote (Lophophora williamsii). It acts as a serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonist, producing vivid visual hallucinations and altered perception; has been used in Indigenous ceremonial contexts; illegal or tightly controlled in many countries.

mescalism.definition: Habitual or chronic use of mescaline-containing substances (notably peyote), producing psychedelic intoxication and related behavioral effects.

mesenchymal chondrosarcoma.definition: A rare, aggressive malignant tumor characterized by biphasic histology—undifferentiated small round blue cells interspersed with islands of cartilaginous tissue—often arising in bone or soft tissue of young adults and with a high risk of local recurrence and distant metastasis; treatment typically involves wide surgical excision, with adjuvant radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy in selected cases.

mesenchymal.definition: Relating to mesenchyme, the loose embryonic connective tissue from which most connective tissues develop; describes cells or tissues derived from that lineage, including multipotent mesenchymal stem cells capable of differentiating into fibroblasts, adipocytes, chondrocytes, osteoblasts, and myocytes.

mesenteric angina.definition: Abdominal pain after meals due to chronic insufficient blood flow to the intestines from atherosclerotic narrowing of the mesenteric arteries (intestinal angina), often causing weight loss and fear of eating.

mesenteric axis.definition: An imaginary reference line defined by the attachment of the mesentery to the posterior abdominal wall, near the root of the mesenteric vessels; used as the axis around which the midgut rotates during embryological development and as a landmark for mesenteric anatomy.

mesenteric ischemia.definition: Mesenteric ischemia is inadequate blood flow to the intestines due to occlusion or severe hypoperfusion of the mesenteric arteries, leading to intestinal ischemia. It includes acute mesenteric ischemia (often from embolus or thrombosis of the superior mesenteric artery or nonocclusive hypoperfusion) presenting with severe abdominal pain out of proportion to examination and risk of bowel infarction, and chronic mesenteric ischemia from atherosclerotic stenosis causing postprandial abdominal pain and weight loss, potentially requiring revascularization.

mesenteric panniculitis.definition: A rare, benign inflammatory and fibrosing disorder of the fat within the mesentery of the intestines, characterized by chronic inflammation and fat necrosis with varying degrees of fibrosis; historically termed sclerosing mesenteritis or retractile mesenteritis.

mesenteric lipodystrophy.definition: A benign inflammatory/necrotizing disorder of the mesenteric fat characterized by fat necrosis with inflammatory infiltrates; part of a spectrum with mesenteric panniculitis and retractile mesenteritis; may be asymptomatic or cause abdominal pain and is often self-limited.

mesenteric volvulus.definition: A condition in which a loop of intestine twists around its mesentery, causing intestinal obstruction with compromised blood flow, which can lead to bowel ischemia and necrosis; a surgical emergency often associated with malrotation or postoperative adhesions.

mesh graft.definition: An expanded split-thickness skin graft in which the donor skin is meshed (cut with a lattice of incisions) to increase coverage area and allow drainage, enabling use on large or irregular wounds, such as burns.

mesial.definition: Toward the midline of the body; in dentistry, toward the midline of the dental arch.

mesiobuccoocclusal.definition: Pertaining to the junction between the mesial-buccal surface and the occlusal surface of a posterior tooth; effectively the mesiobuccal-occlusal line angle where those two surfaces meet. Note: this appears to be a nonstandard or compound chemin term; the intended use may refer to the MB-OC line angle in dental anatomy. If you meant a different surface combination, please provide more context.

mesiocclusion.definition: A malocclusion in which the mandibular teeth are positioned mesially (forward) relative to the maxillary teeth, with the lower jaw prognathic so the lower teeth bite ahead of the upper teeth (Class III malocclusion).

mesiodens.definition: A supernumerary tooth located in the midline of the maxillary anterior arch between the two central incisors; the most common type of supernumerary tooth. It can be conical or tuberculate and may cause eruption disturbances, crowding, or midline diastema, often requiring extraction if it disrupts dentition.

mesiolinguoocclusal.definition: A tri-surface area of a posterior tooth where the mesial, lingual, and occlusal surfaces meet; used to describe a cavity, preparation, or restoration that involves all three surfaces.

mesoblastic nephroma.definition: A congenital renal tumor of infancy arising from mesenchymal tissue; the most common renal neoplasm in neonates, typically benign and curable with surgical resection, with an excellent prognosis. Histology shows spindle-shaped stromal cells and abundant vascular channels; subtypes include classic (angiomatoid) and cellular (more aggressive).

mesocolopexy.definition: A surgical procedure to fix or suspend the mesocolon to the posterior abdominal wall in order to correct or prevent displacement or twisting (volvulus) of the colon.

mesoduodenum.definition: A peritoneal fold attaching the duodenum to the posterior abdominal wall, forming its dorsal mesentery and containing the vessels, nerves, and lymphatics supplying the duodenum.

mesoepididymis.definition: A peritoneal fold (mesentery) that attaches the epididymis to the testis, helping suspend the epididymis within the scrotum.

mesogastric.definition: Relating to the embryologic dorsal mesentery that suspends the stomach from the posterior abdominal wall; in development it forms portions of the stomach's omenta (greater and lesser omenta) and other mesenteric attachments.

mesogluteus.definition: Not a standard anatomical term. If encountered, it likely denotes the middle gluteal region or the gluteus medius, a muscle that abducts the thigh at the hip and stabilizes the pelvis during gait.

mesojejunum.definition: A peritoneal fold that suspends the jejunum from the posterior abdominal wall; a part of the mesentery that carries the vascular, neural, and lymphatic supply to the jejunum.

mesomere.definition: A middle-sized embryonic cell produced during early cleavage in some species (notably echinoderms like sea urchins), located between the small micromeres and large macromeres, whose descendants contribute to various embryonic tissues as development proceeds.

mesomerism.definition: Delocalization of electrons across adjacent atoms through resonance, producing a resonance hybrid of multiple contributing structures rather than a single Lewis structure; this electron delocalization stabilizes the molecule and influences bond lengths and reactivity. Also known as resonance.

mesometritis.definition: Inflammation of the mesometrium, the part of the broad ligament adjacent to the uterus; commonly occurs as part of pelvic inflammatory disease and presents with pelvic pain, uterine tenderness, and sometimes fever.

mesomorph.definition: A body type characterized by a muscular, athletic build with broad shoulders and chest, a narrow waist, and a tendency to gain muscle easily, typically with low to moderate body fat.

mesonephra.definition: A nephron of the mesonephros—the tubular unit of the transient embryonic kidney that functions during early development and is later replaced by the metanephros.

mesonephric.definition: Relating to the mesonephros, the transient embryonic kidney in vertebrate development, or to the mesonephric (Wolffian) ducts that derive from it.

mesonephric duct.definition: A duct of the embryonic mesonephros that forms the Wolffian (mesonephric) structures; in males it develops into parts of the internal reproductive tract (epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory ducts, seminal vesicles), and in females it largely regresses.

mesonephric tubule.definition: An embryonic excretory tubule of the mesonephros that receives filtrate from a glomerulus and drains into the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct; part of the temporary embryonic kidney and typically regresses, though remnants may contribute to components of the male reproductive tract (e.g., efferent ducts).

mesonephros.definition: An embryonic, transient kidney that develops from the intermediate mesoderm and forms mesonephric (Wolffian) tubules draining into the mesonephric duct; it functions briefly during early development and is largely replaced by the definitive metanephros in humans. In males, the mesonephric duct persists to form parts of the reproductive tract.

mesonephron.definition: A nephron unit of the embryonic mesonephros; a transient renal tubule that filters blood via a glomerulus and drains into the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct during early kidney development.

mesonephroid.definition: Resembling the mesonephros; of or relating to the embryonic kidney that serves as a temporary kidney during early vertebrate development.

mesoridazine.definition: A phenothiazine antipsychotic (typical neuroleptic) formerly used to treat schizophrenia; blocks dopamine D2 receptors to reduce psychotic symptoms and commonly causes extrapyramidal side effects and sedation.

mesotaurodontism.definition: A moderate form of taurodontism (a dental anomaly) in which the tooth’s body and pulp chamber are enlarged with apical displacement of the pulpal floor and furcation, resulting in an elongated pulp chamber and relatively short roots.

mesothelial.definition: Relating to the mesothelium, the simple squamous epithelium that lines serous cavities (pleural, peritoneal, and pericardial) and covers internal organs.

mesothelioma.definition: A malignant tumor arising from mesothelial cells lining serous cavities (most commonly the pleura); strongly associated with asbestos exposure; presents with chest pain, dyspnea, and pleural effusion; aggressive disease with poor prognosis.

mesothelium.definition: A single layer of flat, squamous cells that lines the serous cavities of the body (pleural, pericardial, and peritoneal) and covers visceral surfaces, forming serous membranes and secreting lubricating serous fluid.

wolffian duct.definition: An embryonic mesonephric (Wolffian) duct that in males forms the epididymis, vas deferens, and seminal vesicles; in females it largely regresses, leaving remnants such as Gartner's ducts.

ductus epididymidis.definition: A narrow, tightly coiled duct of the epididymis that transports sperm from the efferent ducts of the testis to the vas deferens and provides a site for sperm maturation and storage.

paroöphoron.definition: A vestigial remnant of the embryonic mesonephric (Wolffian) duct in females, consisting of tubules located in the broad ligament near the ovary; an embryologic remnant often described alongside the epoöphoron and usually nonfunctional.

sigmoid mesocolon.definition: Peritoneal fold that attaches the sigmoid colon to the posterior pelvic wall, forming its mesentery; a double layer of peritoneum containing the sigmoid arteries and veins, lymphatics, and nerves supplying the sigmoid colon, and allowing its mobility.

microglia.definition: A type of glial cell in the central nervous system that serves as the resident immune effector; it continuously surveys the CNS, phagocytoses debris and apoptotic cells, and releases cytokines and other mediators in response to injury or disease, also participating in synaptic pruning and maintenance of homeostasis.

torsades de pointes.definition: A life-threatening polymorphic ventricular tachycardia associated with a prolonged QT interval, in which the QRS complexes twist around the baseline (twisting of points); it can progress to ventricular fibrillation. Triggers include electrolyte abnormalities (low potassium or magnesium), QT-prolonging drugs, and congenital long QT syndrome. Management includes IV magnesium sulfate, correction of electrolytes, withdrawal of offending drugs, and temporary pacing or isoproterenol in selected cases.

myoclonia.definition: A sudden, brief, involuntary jerk of a muscle or group of muscles; can be physiological (normal) or associated with neurological disorders such as epilepsy or metabolic/degenerative diseases.

mestinon.definition: A reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used to treat myasthenia gravis by increasing acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction to improve muscle strength; administered orally or by injection; longer-acting than neostigmine and does not cross the blood-brain barrier.

metacarpus.definition: The region of the hand between the wrist and the fingers, comprising the five metacarpal bones that form the palm and connect the carpus to the proximal phalanges.

ureteric.definition: Relating to the ureter, the duct that carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder.

blastema.definition: A mass of proliferating, undifferentiated cells that forms at a site of tissue injury and can differentiate into multiple tissue types to regenerate a structure.

metaphysis.definition: Region of a long bone between the epiphysis and diaphysis that contains the growth plate in children and is the site of longitudinal bone growth; in adults, it is the flared area adjacent to the diaphysis where cancellous bone transitions to cortical bone.

metaphyseal.definition: Relating to the metaphysis, the growing region of a long bone between the epiphysis and diaphysis where lengthwise bone growth occurs in children.

maoinhibitors.definition: Medications used to treat depression. They work by making the chemical messengers serotonin and norepinephrine more available.

ammonium.definition: A positively charged polyatomic ion (NH4+) formed when ammonia (NH3) accepts a proton; the conjugate acid of ammonia; forms ammonium salts with various anions.

carbonic.definition: Relating to carbon dioxide or carbonic acid; in physiology, referring to carbonic acid (H2CO3) and the carbonic acid–bicarbonate buffering system that helps regulate blood pH.

metabiosis.definition: A form of ecological symbiosis where one species benefits from the presence or by-products of another species, often using the other as a habitat or resource after the latter's death.

metatarsus.definition: A region of the foot comprising five long bones between the tarsals and the phalanges, forming the forefoot and acting as levers for gait.

metatarsus adductus.definition: A congenital foot deformity in which the forefoot is adducted medially relative to the hindfoot due to inward turning of the metatarsals; the deformity is usually flexible in infancy and may resolve with observation and stretching, with casting or surgical release for rigid or persistent cases.

metatarsus varus.definition: A deformity of the forefoot in which the metatarsal bones are deviated medially toward the midline, producing a varus (inward) alignment of the forefoot relative to the hindfoot; can be congenital or acquired, and may be mild or self-limited.

metatarsus valgus.definition: A deformity of the foot in which the forefoot (the metatarsals) is deviated laterally relative to the hindfoot, resulting in abduction of the forefoot; it can be congenital or develop in childhood and may be flexible or fixed.

metatarsal artery.definition: An artery that accompanies a metatarsal bone in the foot; there are dorsal metatarsal arteries (from the dorsalis pedis) and plantar metatarsal arteries (from the plantar arterial arches) that run along the metatarsal regions and supply the metatarsal heads and toes.

metatarsal phalanx.definition: The proximal phalanx of a toe; the bone nearest the metatarsal that articulates with it at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

metatarsals.definition: The bones in the middle of the foot, connecting the heel to the toes.

metatarsalgia.definition: Pain and tenderness in the forefoot, particularly under the metatarsal heads (the ball of the foot), due to overload or repetitive stress; often related to ill-fitting footwear, high-impact activity, or foot deformities, and can be associated with callus formation, stress fractures, or nerve/soft-tissue pathology.

metathalamic.definition: Relating to the metathalamus, the part of the dorsal thalamus that contains the lateral and medial geniculate bodies; relays visual and auditory information to the cortex.

metaxalone.definition: A centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant used to treat muscle spasm associated with acute musculoskeletal conditions; the exact mechanism is unknown, but it is thought to depress CNS activity to reduce muscle tone. Common adverse effects include drowsiness, dizziness, and nausea; use with caution in liver disease and with alcohol.

metazoa.definition: Multicellular, eukaryotic, heterotrophic animals within the kingdom Animalia; a major clade that includes organisms with differentiated tissues (in most members).

methemoglobin test.definition: A laboratory measurement that determines the concentration or percentage of methemoglobin in blood, usually by co-oximetry, to diagnose methemoglobinemia and guide treatment.

methaemoglobin.definition: An oxidized form of hemoglobin in which iron is in the ferric (Fe3+) state, preventing effective oxygen binding and delivery to tissues; normally only a small amount is present, but excess levels impair oxygen transport and can cause cyanosis and hypoxia.

methaemoglobinemia.definition: A condition in which an abnormally high level of methemoglobin is present in the blood, in which iron is in the ferric (Fe3+) state, reducing oxygen delivery to tissues and causing cyanosis; it can be congenital or acquired (e.g., due to exposure to certain drugs or chemicals).

methaemoglobinuria.definition: The excretion of methemoglobin in the urine, typically due to oxidative stress or exposure to oxidizing drugs or toxins, resulting in dark brown to black urine and may accompany systemic methemoglobinemia.

methenamine silver stain.definition: Histochemical staining method used to detect fungal elements in tissue. It uses silver impregnation to deposit metallic silver on fungal cell walls, making them dark against a pale counterstain; commonly used to identify Pneumocystis jirovecii and other fungi in biopsy specimens.

methanol.definition: A simple, volatile alcohol (CH3OH) used as an industrial solvent and antifreeze; highly toxic when ingested, inhaled, or absorbed, because it is metabolized to formaldehyde and formic acid, causing metabolic acidosis and visual disturbances; treated with inhibitors of alcohol dehydrogenase (e.g., fomepizole) and supportive care, including possible hemodialysis.

methanol poisoning.definition: Methanol poisoning is toxicity caused by exposure to methanol, a toxic alcohol. It is metabolized to formaldehyde and formic acid, leading to high anion gap metabolic acidosis and optic damage (vision loss or blindness), along with CNS depression; can be fatal. Treatment aims to inhibit alcohol dehydrogenase (fomepizole or ethanol), correct acidosis, and remove methanol (e.g., with hemodialysis) in severe cases.

methandriol.definition: A synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from testosterone; historically used to promote weight gain in wasting conditions and to treat hypogonadal states, with both anabolic and androgenic effects. Adverse effects can include liver toxicity, virilization, acne, mood changes, and suppression of endogenous testosterone.

methamphetamine hydrochloride.definition: A hydrochloride salt form of methamphetamine; a potent central nervous system stimulant that increases dopamine, norepinephrine, and serotonin in the brain. It is used medically only in very limited indications under strict control, but is commonly abused as a highly addictive illegal drug with significant cardiovascular and psychiatric risks.

methisoprinol.definition: An immunostimulant antiviral medication (inosine pranobex) that enhances cellular and humoral immune responses and is used to treat certain viral infections in some countries.

methocarbamol.definition: A centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant used to treat acute musculoskeletal muscle spasm and associated pain; it likely works by depressing the central nervous system to reduce muscle tone and is typically prescribed for short-term use, with common side effects including drowsiness, dizziness, and nausea.

methergine.definition: A vasoconstrictive ergot alkaloid (methylergonovine maleate) used to prevent and treat postpartum hemorrhage by stimulating uterine contractions; contraindicated in hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and preeclampsia/eclampsia.

methylergonovine.definition: A vasoconstrictive ergot alkaloid used as a uterotonic to prevent and treat postpartum hemorrhage by inducing sustained uterine contractions, typically given after delivery.

methazolamide.definition: A systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (a sulfonamide) used as an oral diuretic and to decrease intraocular pressure in glaucoma by reducing aqueous humor production.

methacholine challenge.definition: A bronchial provocation test in which inhaled methacholine provokes airway constriction; the resulting change in FEV1 on spirometry is used to assess airway hyperresponsiveness, with a predefined drop (commonly ≥20%) indicating a positive result and suggesting asthma.

bronchial challenge test.definition: A procedure to assess airway hyperresponsiveness by inhaling a bronchoconstricting agent (most commonly methacholine) or performing an exercise challenge, then measuring the resulting change in lung function (typically a fall in FEV1) with spirometry; used to diagnose asthma and evaluate airway sensitivity. It is performed under medical supervision due to the risk of bronchospasm.

technetium-99m.definition: An isomeric, metastable state of technetium-99 used as a radiotracer in nuclear medicine for diagnostic imaging; it emits gamma photons of about 140 keV and has a half-life of roughly 6 hours, enabling high-quality, relatively low-dose SPECT imaging. It is produced via a molybdenum-99/technetium-99m generator and bound to various compounds to target specific organs.

metastatic abscess.definition: A pus-containing cavity in a distant site caused by hematogenous spread (seeding) of bacteria from a primary infection.

calcium salts.definition: Compounds formed by calcium ions (Ca2+) paired with a negatively charged ion; used medically as calcium supplements to prevent or treat calcium deficiency and as components in various pharmaceutical formulations (e.g., calcium carbonate, calcium citrate).

metastatic endometriosis.definition: Endometrial glands and stroma located outside the uterus at distant sites, presumed to spread via lymphatic or hematogenous routes; lesions are hormonally responsive and can produce site-dependent symptoms.

sympathetic ophthalmia.definition: An autoimmune bilateral granulomatous uveitis that develops in the uninjured eye after penetrating trauma or intraocular surgery to the other eye, due to immune sensitization to ocular antigens.

medial geniculate body.definition: A thalamic relay nucleus of the auditory pathway that receives input from the inferior colliculus and projects to the primary auditory cortex; it comprises ventral, dorsal, and medial divisions, with the ventral division forming the main auditory radiation to the cortex.

lateral geniculate body.definition: A thalamic relay nucleus of the visual pathway that receives input from retinal ganglion cells and projects to the primary visual cortex; organized into magnocellular, parvocellular, and koniocellular layers, it processes and relays visual information such as luminance, contrast, color, and motion before cortical processing.

inferior brachium.definition: Not a standard term in anatomy. When used, it would denote the distal portion of the upper arm (closer to the elbow), i.e., the part farthest from the shoulder.

visual cortex.definition: The part of the occipital lobe in the brain that processes visual stimuli.

optic tract.definition: A bundle of retinal ganglion cell axons that leaves the optic chiasm and travels posteriorly to the lateral geniculate nucleus of the thalamus (and other targets), carrying visual information from the contralateral visual field.

metformin hydrochloride.definition: A hydrochloride salt form of metformin; an oral biguanide antidiabetic medication used to improve glycemic control in type 2 diabetes (and sometimes PCOS) by decreasing hepatic glucose production and increasing insulin sensitivity; does not stimulate insulin secretion and can cause gastrointestinal upset; contraindicated in significant renal impairment due to risk of lactic acidosis.

methylmalonicacidemia.definition: An inherited metabolic disorder caused by deficient activity of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase or defects in cobalamin (vitamin B12) metabolism, resulting in accumulation of methylmalonic acid in blood and urine and leading to episodes of metabolic decompensation with vomiting, poor feeding, hypotonia, and potential developmental delay or neurologic injury if untreated.

methohexital.definition: An ultra-short-acting intravenous barbiturate anesthetic used for rapid induction of anesthesia and for electroconvulsive therapy anesthesia; it produces rapid onset (seconds) and short duration (minutes) by potentiating GABA-A receptor–mediated inhibition. Common adverse effects include respiratory depression and hypotension; contraindicated in porphyria.

hiccoughs.definition: Involuntary, rhythmic contractions of the diaphragm and sometimes the intercostal muscles, followed by abrupt glottic closure, producing the characteristic "hic" sound; most cases are transient and benign, but persistent hiccups may indicate an underlying medical condition.

cardiovascular dysfunction.definition: Impaired function of the heart or blood vessels that results in inadequate systemic circulation, leading to reduced delivery of oxygen and nutrients to tissues and impaired removal of metabolic wastes.

amethopterin.definition: A folate analog antimetabolite used in cancer chemotherapy and certain autoimmune diseases; inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, reducing tetrahydrofolate and disrupting thymidylate and purine synthesis, thereby inhibiting DNA replication.

hepatic impairment.definition: Hepatic impairment is reduced liver function due to acute or chronic liver injury or disease, leading to impaired metabolism and detoxification, decreased bile production, and impaired synthesis of proteins such as albumin and coagulation factors.

ulcerative stomatitis.definition: A mucosal inflammatory condition of the oral cavity characterized by ulcerations (ulcers) on the lips, tongue, gingiva, or other mucosa, often with pain and redness; etiologies include infections (viral or bacterial), trauma or irritation, chemical injuries, drugs, or systemic disease.

methoxsalen.definition: A photoactive psoralen used in PUVA therapy to treat skin conditions by increasing the skin’s sensitivity to ultraviolet A light; administered orally or topically.

8-mop.definition: A psoralen derivative used as a photosensitizer in PUVA phototherapy; after UVA exposure it binds DNA and forms cross-links, reducing skin-cell proliferation; used to treat psoriasis, eczema, and some T-cell lymphomas; administered orally or topically; carries risks of phototoxic reactions and long-term UVA-associated cancer risk.

longwave ultraviolet irradiation.definition: Exposure to the longer-wavelength portion of ultraviolet light, primarily UVA (about 315–400 nm), which penetrates deeply into the skin and is used in phototherapy (e.g., PUVA); it can cause photoaging and indirect DNA damage via reactive oxygen species.

photosensitization.definition: The process by which tissues become susceptible to light-induced damage or reaction in the presence of a photosensitizing agent (such as certain medications or chemicals), resulting in phototoxic or photoallergic skin reactions after light exposure.

methyl alcohol.definition: Methanol (methyl alcohol) is a toxic, simple alcohol (CH3OH) used as an industrial solvent and antifreeze. It is metabolized to formaldehyde and formic acid, causing CNS depression, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and optic neuropathy with potential vision loss. Treatment involves inhibiting alcohol dehydrogenase (fomepizole or ethanol), correcting acidosis, and hemodialysis in severe cases.

3-methoxy-4-hydroxymandelic acid.definition: A major urinary metabolite of catecholamines formed during their degradation; a mandelic acid derivative in which the benzene ring bears a methoxy group at the 3-position and a hydroxyl group at the 4-position.

vanillylmandelic acid.definition: A major urinary metabolite of the catecholamines epinephrine and norepinephrine, produced during their breakdown; historically used as a clinical marker in the workup for pheochromocytoma.

methscopolamine bromide.definition: A quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic agent used as a gastrointestinal antispasmodic and antisecretory drug; it inhibits muscarinic acetylcholine receptors in the GI tract, reducing smooth muscle spasm and secretions with minimal central nervous system effects due to limited brain penetration.

methsuximide.definition: A succinimide anticonvulsant used to treat absence seizures; it decreases neuronal excitability by blocking T-type calcium channels in thalamic neurons.

absence seizures.definition: A type of generalized seizure characterized by brief lapses in consciousness with a blank stare and subtle automatisms; lasts a few seconds, with no postictal confusion; commonly seen in children, and EEG typically shows 3 Hz spike-and-wave discharges. Often precipitated by hyperventilation.

ametria.definition: A refractive error in which the eye cannot correctly focus light on the retina, causing blurred vision; includes myopia (nearsightedness), hyperopia (farsightedness), and astigmatism.

atretometria.definition: A measurement of the degree or severity of atresia (the congenital absence or closure of a normal body opening or passage).

dimetria.definition: Not a standard medical term; may be a misspelling of "dysmetria." Dysmetria is a cerebellar sign characterized by an inability to accurately judge distance or range of movement, causing overshoot (hypermetria) or undershoot (hypometria) of targets during voluntary movements (e.g., finger-to-nose, heel-to-shin).

metrodynia.definition: Uterine pain; pain arising from the uterus, historically used to describe menstrual cramps (dysmenorrhea).

hysteralgia.definition: Pain in the uterus; uterine pain.

hysterdynia.definition: Pain located in the uterus; uterine pain, often associated with gynecologic conditions.

uteralgia.definition: Pain localized to the uterus; a gynecologic symptom that may be related to menstruation (dysmenorrhea) or to uterine disorders such as fibroids or endometriosis.

metopic.definition: Relating to the metopic suture of the skull, the frontal suture that divides the developing frontal bone into left and right halves; it typically ossifies and fuses during early childhood.

metopodynia.definition: Pain in the metatarsal region of the foot (forefoot), often due to overuse, ill-fitting footwear, or structural abnormalities, with tenderness under the metatarsal heads.

metopagus.definition: A form of conjoined twinning in which the twins are fused at the anterior (front) aspect of the body, typically at the chest and upper abdomen, and may share thoracic structures.

metopoplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to reshape or reconstruct the forehead (frontal region), often for cosmetic contour correction or repair of deformities.

metoprolol.definition: A selective beta-1 adrenergic receptor blocker (beta-blocker) used to treat hypertension, angina pectoris, certain tachyarrhythmias, and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; it lowers heart rate, reduces myocardial contractility, and decreases blood pressure.

overt cardiac failure.definition: An overt manifestation of heart failure in which clinical signs and symptoms of inadequate cardiac output and venous congestion are evident, indicating decompensation (e.g., dyspnea, orthopnea, edema, fatigue, jugular venous distension, and pulmonary crackles).

toxemia.definition: Presence of toxins in the bloodstream, leading to systemic illness.

retroperitoneal fibrosis.definition: A rare inflammatory fibrotic disease of the retroperitoneum characterized by the development of dense fibrous tissue that encases the abdominal aorta and ureters, frequently causing ureteral obstruction and hydronephrosis; idiopathic or IgG4-related in many cases and can be associated with other inflammatory or neoplastic conditions.

metipranolol.definition: A nonselective beta-adrenergic blocker used as an ophthalmic solution to lower intraocular pressure by reducing aqueous humor production, for open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension.

gi motility.definition: The coordinated contractions and relaxations of the GI tract's smooth muscle that mix and propel contents through the digestive system, enabling digestion and absorption; regulated by the enteric nervous system, hormones, and luminal factors.

gi hemorrhage.definition: Gastrointestinal hemorrhage is bleeding from any part of the digestive tract—from the mouth to the anus—often presenting with hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia; it is categorized as an upper GI bleed (esophagus, stomach, or duodenum) or a lower GI bleed (small intestine distal to the duodenum, colon, or rectum).

sulfonamide derivatives.definition: Compounds containing the sulfonamide functional group, characterized by a sulfonyl group (SO2) bonded to a nitrogen atom that is substituted (R-SO2-NR'R''), i.e., derivatives in which the sulfonamide nitrogen or sulfonyl group is modified. They form a broad class of chemicals used in medicine, including antibiotics, diuretics, and anticonvulsants.

methylrosaniline chloride.definition: A basic triphenylmethane dye (rosaniline salt) used as a biological stain to color cells or tissues for microscopic examination in microbiology and histology.

methyl salicylate.definition: The methyl ester of salicylic acid (chemical formula C8H8O3); a colorless, volatile liquid used topically as a rubefacient/analgesic in liniments and as a wintergreen flavoring agent; ingestion or significant absorption may cause salicylate poisoning.

wintergreen oil.definition: An essential oil distilled from Gaultheria species (wintergreen); methyl salicylate is its principal constituent; used topically as an analgesic rub for minor aches, but ingestion or large dermal exposure can cause salicylate toxicity; should be diluted and used with caution.

methyltestosterone.definition: A synthetic, orally active 17α-alkylated androgenic–anabolic steroid derived from testosterone, used for androgen replacement and certain hormone-responsive conditions; associated with virilization and hepatotoxicity with prolonged use.

testosterone deficiency.definition: A condition defined by persistently low serum testosterone levels, typically with symptoms such as reduced libido, erectile dysfunction, fatigue, decreased muscle mass or strength, and reduced bone density; caused by primary testicular failure or secondary hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, and diagnosed when morning total testosterone falls below a threshold (commonly around 300 ng/dL) on repeated assessments.

masculinization.definition: The development or enhancement of male secondary sexual characteristics, typically due to increased androgens; in endocrinology this process is known as virilization.

methylsergide maleate.definition: A semisynthetic ergot alkaloid used as a preventive treatment for migraine; it acts as a nonselective serotonin (5-HT) receptor antagonist (primarily at 5-HT2 receptors) and has vasoconstrictive effects. Prolonged use can cause fibrotic complications (e.g., retroperitoneal, pleural, and cardiac fibrosis) and requires monitoring and periodic drug holidays.

methyl ergonovine.definition: An ergot alkaloid vasoconstrictor used to prevent and treat postpartum hemorrhage by inducing and sustaining uterine contractions; administered intramuscularly or intravenously; contraindicated in hypertension, vascular disease, and in patients with ergot sensitivity or certain pregnancy complications (e.g., preeclampsia/eclampsia).

oxytocic.definition: An agent that stimulates uterine contractions; used to induce labor or to control postpartum hemorrhage.

postpartum uterine atony.definition: The failure of the uterus to contract effectively after delivery, resulting in a soft, "boggy" uterus and continued postpartum bleeding; it is the leading cause of postpartum hemorrhage.

subinvolution.definition: A delayed or incomplete involution of the uterus after childbirth, resulting in failure to return to normal size with persistent postpartum lochia, often due to retained placental tissue or endometritis.

3-methylfentanyl.definition: A potent synthetic opioid analgesic that is an analog of fentanyl, with a methyl group at the 3-position; it acts as a mu-opioid receptor agonist and carries a high risk of fatal respiratory depression, and is a controlled substance in many jurisdictions.

p-fluoro fentanyl.definition: A synthetic opioid analgesic; a fluorinated analogue of fentanyl with a para-position fluorine substitution. It acts as a potent mu-opioid receptor agonist, causing analgesia and euphoria but with a high risk of respiratory depression and fatal overdose, and is encountered in illicit fentanyl-related drug supplies.

methylmalonic aciduria.definition: A group of inherited metabolic disorders (typically autosomal recessive) caused by deficiency of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase or defects in cobalamin metabolism, leading to impaired conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA and accumulation of methylmalonic acid; presents in infancy with poor feeding, vomiting, hypotonia, lethargy, metabolic acidosis, and can lead to developmental delay if untreated.

methylphenidate hydrochloride.definition: A central nervous system stimulant used to treat attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy. The hydrochloride salt form of methylphenidate increases brain levels of dopamine and norepinephrine by inhibiting their reuptake, thereby improving attention and reducing impulsivity and hyperactivity.

adhd.definition: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by a persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development; symptoms typically appear before age 12 and are present in two or more settings, with presentations including inattentive, hyperactive-impulsive, or combined.

metoprolol tartrate.definition: A cardioselective beta-1 adrenergic receptor blocker (beta-blocker) used to manage hypertension, angina, and certain arrhythmias; the tartrate salt is an immediate-release formulation.

metritis.definition: An inflammatory uterine infection, typically involving the endometrium and sometimes the myometrium, commonly occurring after delivery or abortion.

parametritis.definition: Inflammation of the parametrium, the connective tissue surrounding the uterus and adjacent pelvic structures; it is commonly a component of pelvic inflammatory disease and can cause pelvic pain and tenderness, with severe cases potentially developing a parametrial abscess.

metrocele.definition: A prolapse or herniation of the uterus into the vaginal canal due to weakness of pelvic floor support, essentially uterine prolapse.

metrofibroma.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. Could you confirm the spelling or provide context (location, related condition)? If you meant a related term like fibroma (benign fibrous-tissue tumor) or myofibroma, I can provide a concise definition.

metromalacoma.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard medical dictionaries.

metrocarcinoma.definition: Not a recognized medical term; if intended as metastatic carcinoma, it refers to cancer that has spread from a primary tumor to distant sites via the lymphatic system or bloodstream.

metralgia.definition: Pain in the uterus; uterine pain.

metromalacia.definition: A nonstandard term implying softening of a bone in the foot (likely a metatarsal); in standard terminology, bone softening is called osteomalacia when systemic, or bone-specific malacia described by the exact bone (e.g., metatarsal malacia) if localized.

metronoscope.definition: Not found in standard medical dictionaries; likely an obsolete or misspelled term. If you have context (field or surrounding text), I can help infer a likely meaning or suggest the correct term.

metroplasty.definition: An operation to repair congenital uterine malformations by modifying the uterine cavity to a single and/or larger space, aiming to improve fertility and reduce obstetric complications. It is used for conditions such as a septate or bicornuate uterus and may involve removing a uterine septum or unifying the uterine horns.

metrorrhagia.definition: Bleeding from the uterus that occurs at irregular intervals, typically between normal menstrual periods.

metyrosine.definition: A tyrosine hydroxylase inhibitor that reduces catecholamine synthesis (norepinephrine, epinephrine, and dopamine); used to manage pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma and to facilitate perioperative blood pressure control. Often administered orally (sometimes IV).

metzenbaum.definition: Delicate surgical scissors with long, narrow blades (often curved) designed for blunt dissection of soft tissue and precise trimming, minimizing damage to surrounding structures.

meuse fever.definition: Definition not found for "Meuse fever" in standard medical dictionaries. It may be a misspelling or a regional term. Could you provide more context or check the spelling so I can give an accurate definition?

mexican spotted fever.definition: A tick-borne rickettsial infection in the spotted fever group caused by Rickettsia rickettsii, transmitted by Dermacentor ticks in parts of Mexico and the southwestern United States. It presents with fever, severe headache, malaise, and a maculopapular or petechial rash that may involve the trunk and extremities, and can progress to vasculitis with potential organ involvement if untreated.

mexican typhus.definition: A flea-borne rickettsial infection (murine typhus), usually caused by Rickettsia typhi and transmitted by rat fleas; it presents with fever, headache, myalgia, and often a maculopapular rash, and is typically milder than epidemic typhus and responsive to doxycycline.

tabardillo.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. Could you provide the language/region or context (e.g., symptoms, suspected disease) for tabardillo? If you meant another term (like measles, varicella, etc.), I can define that.

mexiletine.definition: An oral class IB antiarrhythmic that blocks fast sodium channels in cardiac tissue, analogous to lidocaine; it reduces excitability and shortens action potential duration in ventricular tissue, used to treat ventricular arrhythmias and ectopy (and sometimes certain inherited arrhythmias such as long QT syndrome type 3).

esophageal candidiasis.definition: A fungal infection of the esophagus caused by Candida species (most commonly Candida albicans), typically in immunocompromised individuals, presenting with odynophagia and dysphagia; diagnosed by endoscopy/biopsy and treated with systemic antifungal therapy (e.g., fluconazole).

candida parapsilosis.definition: A yeast species in the genus Candida; part of normal human skin and mucosal flora and an opportunistic pathogen that can cause mucocutaneous candidiasis and invasive disease (including candidemia), especially in hospitalized or immunocompromised patients; transmission often via healthcare workers’ hands or contaminated indwelling devices, with variable antifungal susceptibility (often responsive to azoles like fluconazole).

candida tropicalis.definition: A species of yeast in the genus Candida; a non-albicans Candida member that is part of the normal human microbiota in some people and a common opportunistic pathogen capable of causing mucosal candidiasis and invasive candidiasis, especially in immunocompromised or hospitalized patients.

micafungin.definition: An intravenous echinocandin antifungal agent that inhibits synthesis of β-1,3-D-glucan in the fungal cell wall; used to treat invasive Candida infections (such as candidemia and esophageal candidiasis) and as prophylaxis against Candida infections in high-risk patients (e.g., hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients).

microalbuminuria.definition: Leakage of small amounts of a protein called albumin into the urine caused by kidney disease or damage.

microalbumin test.definition: A urine test that detects and measures small amounts of albumin (a protein) in the urine, usually by a spot urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio or a 24‑hour collection; used to screen for early kidney damage, especially in people with diabetes or hypertension.

maha.definition: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia is a form of hemolytic anemia caused by mechanical destruction of red blood cells as they pass through damaged or obstructed small vessels, often with microthrombi. Hallmarks include schistocytes on the peripheral smear, elevated LDH, low haptoglobin, reticulocytosis, and thrombocytopenia; Coombs test is negative; seen in thrombotic microangiopathies such as TTP, HUS, DIC, and malignant hypertension.

bacterial vaginosis.definition: A polymicrobial overgrowth of vaginal anaerobes due to reduced lactobacilli, typically involving Gardnerella vaginalis, leading to thin gray discharge and a fishy odor; not strictly an STI but associated with sexual activity; diagnosed by Amsel criteria or Nugent score; treated with metronidazole or clindamycin.

anaerobic infections.definition: An infection caused by anaerobic bacteria that thrive in low-oxygen environments; these infections are often polymicrobial and commonly form abscesses, with treatment typically requiring source control (drainage/debridement) and antibiotics active against anaerobes (e.g., metronidazole, beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitors, or carbapenems).

hepatopoietic stem cell transplantation.definition: A medical procedure in which hematopoietic stem cells are transplanted to restore bone marrow function after conditioning with high-dose chemotherapy or radiation, used to treat certain leukemias, lymphomas, myeloma, and other hematologic disorders. Transplants may be autologous (the patient's own cells) or allogeneic (donor cells).

microcephalia.definition: A birth defect where the baby’s head is smaller than that of babies of the same sex and age. These babies often have smaller brains that may not have developed properly.

micrencephaly.definition: Head circumference significantly smaller than expected for the baby’s age and sex, usually due to reduced brain size; often congenital and may be associated with developmental delays or neurologic impairment.

microcephalic.definition: Having an abnormally small head; head circumference below the normal range for age and sex.

microcephalous.definition: Having an abnormally small head circumference for age and sex, typically due to impaired brain development during fetal life or early infancy; often associated with developmental delay and neurologic impairment.

microcephalism.definition: A congenital condition marked by an abnormally small head size (head circumference) for age and sex, typically due to reduced brain growth and development, and often associated with developmental delays or neurological impairment.

microcheiria.definition: A congenital condition characterized by abnormally small hands due to underdevelopment (hypoplasia) of the bones and soft tissues of the hand, sometimes occurring with other limb abnormalities.

microcystic adnexal carcinoma.definition: A rare, malignant skin tumor of sweat-gland (adnexal) origin, typically presenting as a slow-growing facial lesion. Histologically, it shows invasive cords and nests with numerous small keratin-filled or duct-like microcysts in a desmoplastic stroma, often with perineural invasion. It is locally aggressive with a high recurrence rate after incomplete excision; preferred treatment is wide local excision or Mohs micrographic surgery, and distant metastasis is uncommon.

microcide.definition: An agent that kills microorganisms (germs), including bacteria, viruses, and fungi; commonly referred to as a microbicidal agent or germicide.

microbicide.definition: A substance that kills or inhibits the growth of microorganisms (bacteria, viruses, fungi) on surfaces or mucosal tissues, typically applied topically to prevent infection or transmission of pathogens (e.g., vaginal or rectal gels/films designed to reduce sexually transmitted infections).

microbiology.definition: The branch of biology that studies microorganisms—bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa, and algae—including their structure, metabolism, genetics, ecology, and their roles in health, disease, and the environment.

microbiological assay.definition: A microbiological assay is a quantitative procedure that estimates the potency or concentration of a biologically active substance by comparing its effect on a susceptible microorganism or microbial culture to that of a standard reference.

michaelis-menten kinetics.definition: An enzymatic rate model in which reaction velocity increases with substrate concentration and approaches a maximum (Vmax) as the enzyme becomes saturated; described by v = (Vmax [S])/(Km + [S]), where Km is the substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity.

michaelis-menten.definition: A model of enzyme-catalyzed reaction rates describing a hyperbolic increase in velocity with increasing substrate concentration, defined by Vmax (maximum rate) and Km (substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity); it assumes rapid formation of the enzyme–substrate complex and a rate-limiting step for product formation (steady-state).

mezlocillin.definition: An extended-spectrum, antipseudomonal penicillin (ureidopenicillin) antibiotic that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis; active against many Gram-negative bacteria (including Pseudomonas) and some Gram-positive cocci; administered parenterally for serious infections.

mezlocillin sodium.definition: An extended-spectrum penicillin antibiotic (β-lactam) in the sodium salt form for parenteral use; active against a broad range of Gram-negative bacteria (including Pseudomonas) and some Gram-positive bacteria.

micromonospora.definition: A genus of Gram-positive, aerobic, filamentous bacteria in the family Micromonosporaceae, commonly found in soil; part of the actinomycetes, with some species producing aminoglycoside antibiotics such as gentamicin.

microdactyly.definition: A congenital condition characterized by abnormally small fingers or toes, typically due to underdevelopment of the digital bones (phalanges and/or metacarpals/metatarsals) or limb primordia; may be isolated or part of a syndrome.

ossificans.definition: A Latin adjective meaning bone-forming or ossifying; relating to the formation of bone.

microdermabrasion.definition: A cosmetic procedure in which tiny crystals under high pressure are sprayed on the face. This buffs away the outer layer of skin, eliminates fine lines, and improves the look of the skin.

microdontia.definition: A dental condition in which teeth are smaller than normal in size, occurring either across all teeth (generalized) or in a localized area (localized); crowns are reduced in size and may include peg-shaped lateral incisors.

peg-shaped.definition: A description of a tooth that is narrow and conical in shape, resembling a peg; most commonly refers to peg-shaped maxillary lateral incisors.

microdrip.definition: A type of intravenous administration set with a small drop factor (typically 60 drops per milliliter) used to deliver precise, small-volume IV infusions and enable accurate calculation of drip rates.

microelectrode.definition: A very small electrode, typically a glass micropipette or microfabricated probe with a tip diameter of a few micrometers, used to record or electrically stimulate the activity of individual neurons or small neural populations in electrophysiological experiments.

microencapsulation.definition: Enclosing a substance within a microscopic shell or coating to form microcapsules, thereby protecting the substance and enabling controlled or targeted release.

microencephaly.definition: An abnormally small head circumference for age and sex, usually due to impaired brain development; often defined as a head circumference more than 2 standard deviations below the mean, and may be congenital or acquired with possible neurodevelopmental impairment.

microgamete.definition: A small, motile male gamete produced in anisogamous reproduction; it fertilizes the larger, non-motile female gamete (macrogamete). In animals, it corresponds to a sperm cell.

microgametocyte.definition: Male gametocyte (sexual stage) of Plasmodium species; after ingestion by a mosquito, it undergoes exflagellation to form multiple microgametes that fertilize a macrogametocyte.

microgenitalia.definition: A condition in which the external genitalia are smaller than normal for the individual’s age and developmental stage, often due to hormonal deficiencies or disorders of sexual development.

microglossia.definition: A congenital condition in which the tongue is abnormally small, often relative to the size of the oral cavity, and may occur with other craniofacial anomalies.

microgram.definition: A unit of mass, equal to one-thousandth of a milligram. Abbreviated as mcg.

microgyri.definition: Small, abnormally formed gyri of the cerebral cortex, a cortical malformation resulting from disrupted neuronal migration; characterized by reduced or irregular gyrus size and often shallow or irregular sulci, frequently associated with epilepsy and developmental impairment.

microgyria.definition: A cortical malformation characterized by abnormally small, poorly formed gyri with shallow sulci, arising from disrupted neuronal migration during brain development and often associated with seizures and developmental impairment.

microgyrus.definition: A focal malformation of cortical development in which the gyri are abnormally small (microgyri) and the sulci are shallow or irregular, reflecting disrupted neuronal migration during brain development.

microhematocrit.definition: A method of measuring the hematocrit (packed cell volume) using a small-volume capillary blood sample centrifuged to separate cells, with the red-cell portion expressed as a percentage of the total blood volume.
