mycobacterium avium complex.definition: A group of related non-tuberculous mycobacteria, including M. avium and M. intracellulare, that can cause infection in humans; most often presents as pulmonary disease in otherwise healthy adults and as disseminated disease in immunocompromised individuals (notably those with AIDS).

mycobacterium avium-intracellulare.definition: A group of closely related environmental non-tuberculous mycobacteria comprising M. avium and M. intracellulare that cause opportunistic infections, most commonly pulmonary disease and disseminated infection in immunocompromised individuals.

mac disease.definition: A disease caused by infection with the Mycobacterium avium complex, a group of non-tuberculous mycobacteria found in the environment; it most often causes chronic pulmonary illness in people with underlying lung disease or disseminated disease in severely immunocompromised individuals (e.g., advanced HIV/AIDS). Transmission is environmental rather than person-to-person.

mycobacteriosis.definition: Infection caused by bacteria of the genus Mycobacterium; can involve the lungs, skin, lymph nodes, or other organs and includes tuberculosis and non-tuberculous mycobacterial infections.

mycetismus.definition: Poisoning caused by eating poisonous mushrooms, especially certain Amanita species. It commonly presents with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, and may progress to dehydration and severe hepatic or renal failure; it can be life-threatening.

mycitracin.definition: A topical antibiotic ointment used to prevent and treat minor skin infections; typically contains bacitracin, often in combination with other agents such as neomycin or polymyxin B.

polymyxin b.definition: A cationic polypeptide antibiotic of the polymyxin family that binds to lipopolysaccharide and phospholipids in the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, disrupting membrane integrity and causing cell death; used for serious infections due to multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, often administered topically or by injection, with nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity as major adverse effects.

mycostatin.definition: A brand-name antifungal medication (nystatin) used to treat Candida (yeast) infections of the mouth, throat, esophagus, skin, and mucous membranes; available in oral suspension, lozenges, creams/ointment, and powders.

histoplasma.definition: A genus of thermally dimorphic fungi that causes histoplasmosis; infection is acquired by inhalation of airborne microconidia, typically from soil contaminated with bird or bat droppings, and the organism grows as intracellular yeasts within macrophages at body temperature.

mycosis.definition: A disease caused by a fungal infection; any infection caused by fungi, ranging from superficial skin infections to subcutaneous or systemic invasive disease.

mycotic granuloma of the larynx.definition: A chronic granulomatous inflammation of the larynx caused by fungal infection; presents as nodular or ulcerative mucosal lesions with hoarseness and throat irritation. Diagnosis is by biopsy showing granulomatous inflammation with fungal elements (visualized on special stains); management includes systemic antifungal therapy and treatment of any underlying immunosuppression.

mycotoxicosis.definition: A toxic illness caused by exposure to mycotoxins—toxic secondary metabolites produced by certain fungi—typically from ingesting contaminated food, though inhalation or skin contact is possible; symptoms and organ involvement depend on the specific toxin (e.g., aflatoxicosis can cause liver injury).

mycology.definition: The branch of biology that studies fungi—yeasts, molds, and mushrooms—including their genetics, physiology, taxonomy, ecology, and roles in disease, medicine, and industry.

myringomycosis.definition: A fungal infection of the tympanic membrane (eardrum), often associated with otitis externa or media, commonly caused by Aspergillus or Candida, and treated with antifungal therapy and management of the underlying ear condition.

mycomyringitis.definition: A fungal infection of the tympanic membrane (eardrum); a rare form of otitis characterized by tympanic membrane inflammation and possible discharge, treated with topical antifungal ear drops and management of contributing factors.

mycophenolate mofetil.definition: A prodrug immunosuppressant that inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase, reducing de novo guanine nucleotide synthesis and suppressing proliferation of T and B lymphocytes; used to prevent organ rejection in transplant recipients (often in combination with tacrolimus and corticosteroids).

mycophenolic acid.definition: An immunosuppressive agent; a reversible inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH) that impedes de novo guanosine nucleotide synthesis, preferentially in lymphocytes, thereby suppressing T- and B-lymphocyte proliferation. It is the active metabolite of the prodrug mycophenolate mofetil.

walking pneumonia.definition: A mild form of pneumonia, typically caused by Mycoplasma pneumoniae (an atypical pathogen), characterized by a persistent dry cough, low-grade fever, malaise, and often minimal signs on exam and chest imaging, so patients may not appear severely ill.

antitubercular.definition: Relating to or used to treat tuberculosis; an antitubercular is a drug or agent that has activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and is used in TB treatment.

ethambutol hydrochloride.definition: A synthetic antimycobacterial antibiotic (the hydrochloride salt of ethambutol) that inhibits cell-wall synthesis in mycobacteria by blocking arabinosyl transferases needed for arabinogalactan formation; typically bacteriostatic and used in combination therapy for active tuberculosis.

triamcinolone acetonide.definition: A synthetic corticosteroid (glucocorticoid) with anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects; used in topical formulations for inflammatory skin conditions and in other routes (intralesional, nasal, inhaled) to treat allergic and inflammatory disorders.

cervical adenitis.definition: Inflammation of the lymph nodes in the neck, usually due to infection, presenting as swollen, tender cervical lymph nodes.

cold agglutinin.definition: An autoantibody, usually an IgM, that binds red blood cells at cold temperatures (often below body temperature), causing erythrocyte agglutination and complement-mediated hemolysis; it is associated with cold agglutinin disease (and sometimes transient hemolysis with infections).

pleuropneumonia-like organism.definition: A historical term for small, wall-less bacteria (mycoplasmas) associated with pleuropneumonia; they cause atypical pneumonia in humans (notably Mycoplasma pneumoniae) and pleuropneumonia in animals; they lack a cell wall, are not Gram-stainable, require cholesterol for growth, and need special culture media.

salivation.definition: The production and secretion of saliva by the salivary glands, typically in response to the presence, sight, or thought of food.

mycotoxin.definition: A toxic secondary metabolite produced by fungi (molds) that can contaminate food and cause illness in humans and animals; examples include aflatoxins, ochratoxins, fumonisins, and trichothecenes.

myelblast.definition: An immature precursor cell of the myeloid (granulocytic) lineage in the bone marrow; the earliest committed cell that differentiates into mature granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils) through subsequent stages such as promyelocyte, myelocyte, and metamyelocyte. Myeloblasts are typically large with a high nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratio and fine chromatin; elevated numbers are characteristic of acute myeloid leukemia.

cyclopentolate.definition: A topical antimuscarinic ophthalmic medication used to induce mydriasis (pupil dilation) and cycloplegia (paralysis of accommodation) for eye examinations; it acts as a competitive antagonist of acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors in the iris sphincter and ciliary muscle.

tropicamide.definition: A short-acting topical antimuscarinic (muscarinic receptor antagonist) used to dilate the pupil for ophthalmic examination; it produces mydriasis with mild cycloplegia and lasts about 4–6 hours.

myelacephalus.definition: Relating to or affecting both the spinal cord and brain.

myelacephalous.definition: An historical term describing a severe congenital absence or underdevelopment of the brain and spinal cord, typically incompatible with life.

myelatelia.definition: A congenital condition in which the spinal cord is incompletely formed or absent.

myelauxe.definition: Not a recognized medical term; no standard medical definition exists.

myelencephalon.definition: The caudal portion of the embryonic hindbrain (rhombencephalon) that gives rise to the medulla oblongata; in the mature brain it corresponds to the medulla oblongata, the brainstem region responsible for autonomic and reflex control.

myelinogenesis.definition: Formation and development of myelin sheaths around axons; in the CNS by oligodendrocytes and in the PNS by Schwann cells, facilitating rapid nerve conduction.

myelinolysis.definition: Destruction or loss of the myelin sheath around CNS axons, most commonly from osmotic demyelination after rapid correction of hyponatremia; classically involves the central pons (central pontine myelinolysis) but can affect extrapontine regions as well.

myeloblastemia.definition: Presence of myeloblasts (immature myeloid cells) in the peripheral blood, indicating abnormal release from the bone marrow and commonly associated with acute myeloid leukemia or other myeloid neoplasms.

myeloblastosis.definition: An abnormal proliferation of myeloblasts (immature precursor cells of granulocytes) in the bone marrow and peripheral blood, typically seen in acute myeloid leukemia.

myeloblastomatosis.definition: Not a standard medical term; if used, it would describe widespread proliferation or infiltration of myeloblasts (immature granulocytic precursors) in bone marrow and extramedullary tissues, as seen in acute myeloid leukemia with organ involvement.

myelofibrosis.definition: A clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by abnormal megakaryocyte proliferation that stimulates bone marrow fibrosis, leading to extramedullary hematopoiesis (often with splenomegaly) and cytopenias; commonly associated with JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutations.

myelosclerosis.definition: A condition in which bone marrow is replaced by fibrous tissue (bone marrow fibrosis), causing impaired hematopoiesis and often extramedullary hematopoiesis; commonly occurs in myelofibrosis and other myeloproliferative neoplasms.

metaplasia.definition: A reversible change in which one differentiated cell type is replaced by another mature cell type, typically as an adaptive response to chronic irritation or injury, often via stem/progenitor cell reprogramming; can predispose to dysplasia or cancer in some tissues.

myelogenesis.definition: The process of forming the myelin sheath around nerve fibers, produced by oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system and by Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system, which increases the conduction velocity of nerve impulses.

myelocele.definition: A neural tube defect in which the spinal cord protrudes through a defect in the vertebral arch and is exposed, typically without a protective meningeal or skin covering; a form of open spina bifida.

myelocyst.definition: A cystic dilation of the spinal cord, typically representing a fluid-filled sac within or adjacent to the spinal cord, often seen in congenital spinal dysraphism.

myelocystocele.definition: A rare congenital spinal dysraphism in which a dilated distal spinal cord forms a dorsal, CSF-filled cyst that protrudes through a vertebral defect (often presenting as a skin-covered sac) and may be tethered to the cord.

myelocystomeningocele.definition: A rare congenital neural tube defect in which a cystic dilation of the spinal cord (myelocyst) herniates with the meninges through a dorsal vertebral defect, forming a sac-like lesion that contains spinal tissue.

myelocyte.definition: A developing granulocyte precursor in the bone marrow; the intermediary stage after the promyelocyte in granulopoiesis, maturing into metamyelocytes and ultimately into mature neutrophils, eosinophils, or basophils.

myelogram.definition: A diagnostic imaging procedure in which radiopaque contrast is introduced into the subarachnoid space (typically by lumbar puncture) to outline the spinal cord, nerve roots, and spinal canal on X-ray or CT, to detect abnormalities such as herniated discs, spinal stenosis, tumors, or infections.

hodgkins.definition: A type of cancer that grows in a part of your immune system (your lymph nodes). Also called Hodgkin's disease.

hydromyelia.definition: Dilation of the spinal cord's central canal with accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid, usually due to disturbed CSF flow; often associated with syringomyelia.

atelomyelia.definition: A congenital anomaly characterized by incomplete development (hypoplasia) of the spinal cord.

spina.definition: A Latin term meaning spine or spinal column; in anatomy, the dorsal axis of the skeleton formed by the vertebral column.

bifida.definition: A neural tube defect characterized by failure of the vertebral arches to fuse properly around the spinal cord, which may present as exposure or protrusion of neural tissue (open forms) or as a closed defect; severity ranges from minor anomalies to significant neurologic impairment, and risk is reduced with adequate periconceptional folic acid.

occulta.definition: Hidden; not readily visible or detectable by routine examination; used to describe a lesion or defect that is present but concealed (e.g., spina bifida occulta).

neurofibrils.definition: Threadlike cytoskeletal elements within neurons composed of neurofilaments (type IV intermediate filaments) that provide structural support, help determine axonal caliber, and participate in axonal transport.

ranvier.definition: Gaps in the myelin sheath along a myelinated axon where voltage-gated sodium channels are concentrated, allowing action potentials to be regenerated and propagated rapidly via saltatory conduction.

schwann.definition: German physiologist who proposed the cell theory and described Schwann cells; Schwann cells are glial cells of the peripheral nervous system that form the myelin sheath around peripheral nerve axons.

bence.definition: A urinary protein consisting of free immunoglobulin light chains (usually kappa or lambda) produced by abnormal plasma cells; classically associated with multiple myeloma and other plasma cell dyscrasias; detectable by urine electrophoresis or immunofixation.

jones.definition:
- A fracture of the base of the fifth metatarsal at the metaphyseal–diaphyseal junction, typically from an inversion injury; carries a high risk of nonunion due to limited blood supply and may be treated with immobilization or surgical fixation if displaced.

- Diagnostic criteria for acute rheumatic fever requiring evidence of prior group A streptococcal infection plus two of the following: migratory polyarthritis, carditis, chorea, erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules (major); or one major and two minor criteria (fever, arthralgia, elevated inflammatory markers, prolonged PR interval) with recent GAS infection.

myelomere.definition: A segmental unit of the spinal cord corresponding to one pair of spinal nerves; during development, the spinal cord is organized into myelomeres (metameres), each giving rise to the dorsal and ventral nerve roots.

myelopathic anemia.definition: Not a standard medical term; if referring to the related concept, it denotes anemia due to replacement or displacement of bone marrow by fibrosis, metastatic tumor, or granulomatous disease, leading to pancytopenia and a leukoerythroblastic blood picture with teardrop-shaped red cells.

myelophthisic anemia.definition: Anemia caused by replacement or destruction of normal bone marrow tissue by infiltrative or fibrotic processes (e.g., marrow fibrosis, metastatic cancer, granulomatous disease), leading to impaired hematopoiesis and a leukoerythroblastic peripheral smear with teardrop-shaped red cells and often pancytopenia.

myelopathy.definition: A disorder in which the spinal cord is compressed, diseased, or damaged.

leukoerythroblastic anemia.definition: A peripheral blood smear pattern in which immature granulocytes and nucleated red blood cells are present, reflecting displacement or replacement of the bone marrow (a myelophthisic process) commonly due to marrow infiltration or fibrosis (e.g., myelofibrosis, metastatic cancer), often with teardrop red cells.

myelopoiesis.definition: The formation and maturation of cells of the myeloid lineage in the bone marrow, including granulocytes, monocytes, erythrocytes, and platelets, from hematopoietic stem cells.

myeloproliferative neoplasms.definition: A group of clonal hematologic disorders in which a hematopoietic stem cell acquires driver mutations that cause persistent, unregulated proliferation of one or more myeloid cell lines, resulting in elevated red cells, platelets, and/or neutrophils, and a risk of progression to marrow fibrosis or acute leukemia. Classic examples include polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, and primary myelofibrosis.

essential thrombocythemia.definition: An acquired myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by persistent thrombocytosis due to clonal megakaryocytic proliferation (platelets often >450,000/μL), commonly with JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutations, and a risk of thrombotic or hemorrhagic events; treatment is risk‑adapted, often including low‑dose aspirin and cytoreductive therapy (e.g., hydroxyurea) for high‑risk patients.

primary myelofibrosis.definition: A chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by clonal proliferation of hematopoietic stem cells leading to progressive bone marrow fibrosis, ineffective hematopoiesis, extramedullary hematopoiesis (often with splenomegaly), and peripheral cytopenias; commonly associated with JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutations, and may present with teardrop red blood cells and leukoerythroblastosis on smear, with risk of progression to marrow failure or acute leukemia.

myeloradiculodysplasia.definition: A congenital malformation characterized by abnormal development of the spinal cord and its exiting nerve roots (myelo- and radiculo-), often associated with neurologic deficits and spinal deformities.

myeloschisis.definition: A neural tube defect in which failure of caudal neural fold closure results in an open, exposed spinal cord on the back with no skin or sac covering; a severe form of spina bifida aperta (rachischisis).

myesthesia.definition: Not a standard medical term; there is no established definition. If encountered, it may be used to describe a sensation related to muscles (muscle sensation), but this usage is not widely accepted.

myiasis.definition: Infestation of living tissue by fly larvae (maggots) that feed on host tissue and secretions; it can involve skin (cutaneous or wound myiasis), mucous membranes, or the gastrointestinal tract and is often associated with neglected wounds or poor hygiene. Management includes mechanical removal of larvae, thorough wound care and debridement, addressing underlying conditions, and, when needed, antiparasitic medications.

myitis.definition: Inflammation of skeletal muscle tissue; may result from infection, autoimmune processes, toxins, or physical injury. When inflammatory muscle disease is systemic or chronic, it is termed myositis.

mylohyoideus.definition: Musculus mylohyoideus (mylohyoid muscle): a flat muscle forming the floor of the mouth, originating from the mylohyoid line of the mandible and inserting into the body of the hyoid bone (via a midline raphe); it elevates the floor of the mouth and the tongue during swallowing. Innervation: nerve to mylohyoid (a branch of the inferior alveolar nerve, CN V3).

myocardiograph.definition: An instrument for recording or imaging the myocardium (the heart muscle) to assess its structure or function; a historical or generic term for equipment used to study myocardial activity.

cardiac muscle.definition: A specialized striated involuntary muscle that forms the heart's myocardium; cardiomyocytes connected by intercalated discs enable synchronized, rhythmic contractions to pump blood, under intrinsic conduction and autonomic regulation.

myoneural.definition: Relating to muscle and nerve; pertaining to the neuromuscular system, especially the neuromuscular junction.

myopathy.definition: A disease of skeletal muscle tissue characterized by weakness and reduced muscle function due to primary abnormalities of the muscle fibers, not secondary to nerve or neuromuscular junction disorders.

myophosphorylase deficiency glycogenosis.definition: A glycogen storage disease (type V) caused by autosomal recessive deficiency of skeletal muscle glycogen phosphorylase (myophosphorylase), resulting in the inability to break down muscle glycogen during exercise and leading to exercise intolerance with cramps and sometimes myoglobinuria after strenuous activity; blood lactate fails to rise with exercise.

myokinase.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the interconversion of two ADP molecules with ATP and AMP (2 ADP ⇌ ATP + AMP), thereby regenerating ATP during bursts of energy and helping maintain cellular energy balance.

adenylate kinase.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the reversible transfer of a phosphate between ADP molecules: 2 ADP ⇄ ATP + AMP; it buffers and rapidly regenerates ATP in cells to maintain energy homeostasis, with cytosolic and mitochondrial isoforms (also called myokinase).

myoglobin.definition: A heme-containing oxygen-binding protein in muscle tissue that stores and facilitates delivery of oxygen to mitochondria in skeletal and cardiac muscle during exercise.

myoglobinuric renal failure.definition: An acute kidney injury caused by myoglobin released during rhabdomyolysis; myoglobin is filtered by the kidneys and can precipitate in renal tubules, causing obstruction and direct tubular toxicity, leading to decreased renal function. It is often associated with crush injuries, severe exertion, or other causes of muscle breakdown and may present with dark urine.

myonecrosis.definition: Death of muscle tissue (typically skeletal muscle) due to ischemia, infection, toxins, or trauma.

actin.definition: One of the proteins that allows cells to move and muscles to contract.

myofilament.definition: A filament within a muscle cell's myofibril that participates in contraction; there are thick (myosin) filaments and thin (actin) filaments that slide past each other during sarcomere shortening.

myofilaments.definition: The fundamental muscle proteins that form myofibrils. Myofilaments slide over one another, bunching up and generating force, when a muscle contracts.

myofibril.definition: A cylindrical organelle within a muscle fiber, composed of a linear array of sarcomeres; the contractile unit of striated muscle, containing interdigitating thin (actin) and thick (myosin) filaments whose interaction causes muscle contraction.

myosin.definition: A protein that helps muscle contract and relax.

z disk.definition: Boundary structure at the borders of a sarcomere in striated muscle that anchors thin (actin) filaments and links adjacent sarcomeres, defining the boundary between sarcomeres and aiding transmission of contractile force (contains anchoring proteins such as α‑actinin).

thick filament.definition: A contractile filament of muscle tissue composed primarily of bundled myosin molecules; located in the A-band of the sarcomere, with protruding heads that form cross-bridges with actin on thin filaments to generate force during contraction.

thin filament.definition: A filament composed primarily of actin (F-actin) with regulatory proteins tropomyosin and troponin that forms the thin myofilament of the sarcomere and interacts with myosin thick filaments to generate muscle contraction, regulated by calcium.

myogelosis.definition: An abnormal softness or gelatinous consistency of muscle tissue, typically due to edema or inflammatory/infiltrative changes within the muscle.

gluteal muscles.definition: A group of three muscles in the buttocks (gluteus maximus, medius, and minimus) that move and stabilize the hip joint: the maximus extends and externally rotates the hip; the medius and minimus abduct and medially rotate the hip; they also help stabilize the pelvis during walking.

rhabdomyoma.definition: A benign tumor composed of mature skeletal (striated) muscle cells; can occur in the heart (cardiac rhabdomyoma) or in soft tissues.

myoma.definition: A benign tumor of smooth muscle tissue; most commonly refers to a uterine fibroid (leiomyoma).

myotome.definition: The group of muscles innervated by a single spinal nerve root, used in neurology to assess motor function and localize nerve root lesions.

myometritis.definition: Inflammation of the myometrium, the muscular layer of the uterus, usually due to bacterial infection; typically occurs postpartum or after abortion, presenting with fever, uterine tenderness, and lower abdominal pain, and is treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics.

myometria.definition: The smooth muscle middle layer of the uterus; the muscular wall of the uterus composed of smooth muscle fibers that contracts during labor.

creatine kinase mb.definition: An isoenzyme of the enzyme creatine kinase that is predominantly found in cardiac muscle; it is released into the bloodstream after myocardial injury and is used as a biomarker to help diagnose myocardial infarction. Levels rise within hours after injury and typically return to baseline within 2–3 days.

ck-mb.definition: The MB isoenzyme of creatine kinase (CK-MB), an enzyme primarily found in cardiac muscle; used as a biomarker of myocardial injury, with levels rising after heart muscle damage (peaking around 24 hours and returning to baseline within 48–72 hours).

sedimentation rate.definition: A blood test that measures the rate at which red blood cells settle to the bottom of a vertical tube in one hour; a nonspecific marker of inflammation or infection.

ptca.definition: Abbreviation for percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty, a procedure used to open blocked coronary arteries.

percutaneous transvenous coronary angiop.definition: A minimally invasive procedure in which a catheter is threaded through the skin into a coronary artery and a balloon at its tip is inflated to compress plaque and widen a narrowed vessel, typically with placement of a stent to keep the artery open and restore blood flow to the heart muscle.

acute congestive heart failure.definition: A sudden or rapid worsening of heart failure due to impaired cardiac pumping, causing fluid buildup in the lungs and body (pulmonary and systemic congestion) and often requiring urgent treatment.

myopic shift.definition: A change in refractive error toward myopia (nearsightedness), meaning the eye becomes more nearsighted and requires stronger minus power (or less plus) to achieve clear vision; often due to progression of myopia or structural changes such as axial elongation.

nearsightedness.definition: When it’s hard to see things that are far away. Also called myopia.

short sight.definition: A refractive error in which distant objects appear blurry because the eye focuses images in front of the retina, often due to elongation of the eyeball or a too-curved cornea; also known as myopia.

shortsightedness.definition: A refractive error (myopia) in which distant objects appear blurry because light is focused in front of the retina, typically due to an elongated eyeball or increased corneal curvature; corrected with eyeglasses, contact lenses, or refractive surgery.

prodromal myopia.definition: An early, preclinical phase in which biometric and functional indicators signal an impending shift toward myopia (e.g., progressive axial elongation and a trend toward reduced hyperopic refractive error) before the refractive error becomes truly myopic.

myoreceptor.definition: A sensory receptor in skeletal muscle that detects mechanical changes—primely muscle length/stretch and, in some receptors, tension—contributing to proprioception and regulation of muscle tone and reflexes (e.g., muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs).

muscle receptor.definition: A sensory receptor in skeletal muscle that detects mechanical changes such as stretch or tension and transmits signals to the nervous system to help regulate movement and proprioception; main examples are muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs.

myorrhaphy.definition: A surgical procedure in which a torn or damaged muscle is sutured and repaired.

myorrhexis.definition: Rupture or tearing of a muscle.

myosarcoma.definition: A malignant tumor arising from muscle tissue that shows evidence of muscle differentiation; in modern practice such neoplasms are more precisely categorized as rhabdomyosarcoma (skeletal muscle) or leiomyosarcoma (smooth muscle).

myositis fibrosa.definition: A chronic inflammatory myopathy in which muscle tissue becomes fibrotic, with replacement of muscle fibers by fibrous connective tissue and resulting weakness; an outdated or nonstandard descriptor for fibrosing myopathy associated with inflammatory myopathy.

parenchymatous myositis.definition: Inflammation of the skeletal muscle parenchyma (the muscle fibers themselves), typically with lymphocytic infiltration and myofiber necrosis, seen in inflammatory myopathies such as polymyositis.

traumatic myositis.definition: Inflammation of skeletal muscle due to direct physical injury (trauma) such as contusion or crush injury, causing localized pain, swelling, and weakness, often with edema and muscle fiber necrosis, and usually resolving with rest and supportive care.

myositis purulenta.definition: Purulent inflammation of skeletal muscle (suppurative myositis) caused by bacterial infection, often with abscess formation; presents with localized muscle pain, swelling, warmth, and fever; commonly due to pyogenic bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus species; treated with antibiotics and drainage as needed.

myositis trichinosa.definition: A helminthic infection (Trichinella spiralis) acquired from eating undercooked pork or game meat, causing skeletal muscle inflammation (myositis) as encysted larvae invade muscle fibers; presents with fever, myalgia, periorbital edema, eosinophilia, and elevated creatine kinase, and is diagnosed by serology or muscle biopsy showing larvae. Treated with albendazole or mebendazole, often with corticosteroids in moderate to severe cases.

trichinella spiralis.definition: A parasitic nematode (roundworm) that causes trichinellosis in humans; infection occurs after eating undercooked meat containing larvae, which hatch in the small intestine, mature, and migrate to skeletal muscle where they encyst; symptoms range from gastrointestinal upset to muscle pain and fever; treated with antiparasitic drugs such as albendazole or mebendazole; prevention by thoroughly cooking meat to safe temperatures.

myostasis.definition: A nonstandard term generally used to denote the regulation and maintenance of stable muscle tone or a steady-state condition of muscle tissue (muscle homeostasis).

myostroma.definition: The connective tissue stroma of muscle tissue—the supportive framework around muscle fibers, including the endomysium, perimysium, and epimysium.

myotenotomy.definition: A surgical procedure to cut at the myotendinous junction to lengthen or release a contracted muscle-tendon unit.

myotonachol.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard dictionaries. It would describe a neuromuscular phenomenon characterized by delayed relaxation of a muscle after contraction.

myotonia.definition: Delayed relaxation of skeletal muscle after contraction, causing transient stiffness that improves with ongoing activity or repeated stimulation; seen in myotonic disorders (e.g., myotonia congenita, myotonic dystrophy) and often due to altered muscle membrane excitability from ion channel dysfunction.

myotonia atrophica.definition: A hereditary muscular dystrophy presenting with myotonia (delayed relaxation of muscles) and progressive muscle weakness and wasting; historically called myotonia atrophica and most commonly referring to myotonic dystrophy type 1 (Steinert disease) caused by a CTG repeat expansion in the DMPK gene.

steinert’s disease.definition: A dominantly inherited muscular dystrophy known as myotonic dystrophy type 1, caused by a CTG repeat expansion in the DMPK gene, characterized by myotonia (delayed muscle relaxation) and progressive weakness and wasting of skeletal muscles, often with multisystem features such as cataracts, cardiac conduction defects, and endocrine abnormalities.

myotonic.definition: Relating to myotonia; characterized by delayed relaxation of skeletal muscles after contraction, often due to disorders of muscle membrane excitability such as myotonic dystrophy.

myotube.definition: A multinucleated, elongated skeletal muscle cell formed by the fusion of myoblasts; an immature muscle fiber that differentiates and matures into a functional myofiber.

myringectomy.definition: Excision of all or part of the tympanic membrane (eardrum), typically performed to treat chronic middle-ear disease such as cholesteatoma or to gain access to the middle ear; may be followed by reconstruction (tympanoplasty).

myringodectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which all or part of the tympanic membrane (eardrum) is removed, typically to treat chronic middle-ear disease or to gain access to the middle ear.

myringoplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair a perforated tympanic membrane (eardrum) by grafting tissue (commonly temporalis fascia) to close the perforation and restore the membrane's integrity and hearing.

myringoscope.definition: A device for directly visualizing the tympanic membrane (eardrum) of the middle ear, typically an illuminated, magnifying optical instrument used in otology.

myringotomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which a small incision is made in the tympanic membrane (eardrum) to drain middle-ear fluid and relieve pressure; often performed to treat otitis media with effusion and to facilitate tympanostomy tube placement.

tympanostomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which an incision is made in the tympanic membrane (eardrum) to ventilate the middle ear and drain fluid, usually with placement of a small ventilation tube.

tympanostomy tube.definition: A small tube inserted through the eardrum to ventilate the middle ear and drain fluid, used to treat recurrent otitis media with effusion or chronic middle-ear effusion; also known as a pressure-equalizing (PE) tube or grommet.

tympanotomy.definition: A surgical incision into the tympanic membrane (eardrum) to relieve middle-ear pressure and drain fluid or pus; may be done to access the middle ear or to place tympanostomy tubes.

otitis externa.definition: An infection of the skin lining the ear canal of the outer ear. Also called swimmer’s ear.

myringotomy with tympanostomy tube.definition: A surgical procedure in which a small incision is made in the tympanic membrane to drain middle-ear fluid and relieve pressure, followed by insertion of a tympanostomy tube (grommet) to ventilate the middle ear and prevent fluid buildup; the tube typically remains in place for months and helps treat recurrent otitis media with effusion.

mysoline.definition: Brand name for an anticonvulsant used to treat seizures; a prodrug metabolized to phenobarbital and phenylethylmalonamide that enhances GABA-mediated inhibitory neurotransmission.

mysophobia.definition: A persistent, irrational fear of dirt, germs, or contamination that leads to excessive cleaning and avoidance behaviors; commonly known as germophobia and may be part of OCD.

misophobia.definition: An excessive, irrational fear of dirt, contamination, or germs, a type of specific phobia.

myxoblastoma.definition: A historical term for a soft tissue tumor composed of primitive mesenchymal cells (myxoblasts) within a gelatinous, myxoid extracellular matrix. The usage is outdated and nonspecific; the diagnosis is now defined by the specific histologic type and location (for example, myxoid sarcoma or myxoma) rather than this broad designation.

myxocyte.definition: A fibroblast‑like cell found in myxoid (mucoid) connective tissue, embedded in a mucopolysaccharide‑rich extracellular matrix, commonly described in myxoid neoplasms.

myxofibroma.definition: A benign soft-tissue tumor characterized by abundant myxoid (mucoid) stroma with spindle- to stellate-shaped fibroblasts; typically slow-growing and locally infiltrative, with a tendency to recur after surgical excision.

myxoma fibrosum.definition: A benign neoplasm characterized by a gelatinous, myxoid stroma with a fibrous component; composed of stellate or spindle-shaped cells in a mucopolysaccharide-rich matrix; tends to grow slowly and can occur in soft tissue or bone; treated by surgical excision with potential for recurrence.

myxoma sarcomatosum.definition: Not a standard term in modern medical nomenclature. Historically, it has been used to refer to a myxoid (mucin-rich) tumor with sarcomatous features or to disseminated sarcomatous lesions with a myxoid stroma; today veterinary or human pathology would instead specify a myxoma (benign) or a myxoid sarcoma (malignant).

myxoid.definition: Having a mucoid, gelatinous extracellular matrix rich in mucopolysaccharides (glycosaminoglycans); describes tissue with a mucin-like, loose stroma often seen in certain connective-tissue lesions and tumors.

myxovirus.definition: A historical term for enveloped, negative-sense, segmented RNA viruses with a genome organized in segments, primarily referring to influenza viruses and now classified in the Orthomyxoviridae; these pathogens cause influenza and related respiratory illnesses.

naegeli’s leukemia.definition: Not a currently recognized leukemia; likely a historical or nonstandard term with no established diagnostic criteria in modern hematology.

naegleria.definition: A genus of free-living, amoeboid protozoa; certain species, notably Naegleria fowleri, can cause primary amoebic meningoencephalitis after nasal exposure to warm freshwater, leading to a rapidly progressive and usually fatal brain infection.

naegleria fowleri.definition: A free-living, thermophilic amoeba found in warm freshwater that can cause primary amoebic meningoencephalitis in humans when contaminated water enters the nose, leading to a rapidly progressive and usually fatal CNS infection.

primary amebic meningoencephalitis.definition: An extremely rare, nearly always fatal CNS infection caused by the free-living amoeba Naegleria fowleri, acquired when contaminated warm freshwater enters the nose and the organism migrates to the brain, producing acute meningoencephalitis with rapid onset symptoms such as headache, fever, nausea, neck stiffness, confusion, and seizures.

naegleriasis.definition: A rare, usually fatal central nervous system infection caused by Naegleria fowleri, resulting in primary amoebic meningoencephalitis after exposure of the nasal mucosa to warm freshwater.

nabothian cyst.definition: A benign mucus-filled retention cyst of the cervix due to obstruction of endocervical gland ducts; typically presents as small, translucent or blue-gray cervical cysts on exam and usually requires no treatment.

nabothian gland.definition: One of the mucous-secreting glands of the cervix (endocervical canal) that secretes mucus; obstruction of its ducts can form Nabothian cysts.

cervical cyst.definition: A benign mucus-filled cyst on the cervix caused by occlusion of endocervical glands; typically asymptomatic and found incidentally, requiring no treatment unless symptomatic or enlarging.

mycophobia.definition: An irrational, persistent fear of fungi, especially mushrooms, classified as a specific phobia that leads to avoidance and distress or impairment in functioning.

nafcillin sodium.definition: A penicillinase-resistant beta-lactam antibiotic of the isoxazolyl penicillin group; active against methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) and certain streptococci, it inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis and is usually given parenterally (intravenous or intramuscular). It is not effective against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) or most gram-negative organisms.

naffziger sign.definition: I couldn’t locate a standard medical definition for “Naffziger sign.” Could you provide more context (the condition, exam, or source where you encountered the term)?

naffziger syndrome.definition: An obscure historical eponym with no widely accepted current medical definition in standard references. If you have context (system involved, symptoms, or alternate spelling), I can help identify the intended condition.

naffziger test.definition: A historical provocative neurology test in which the examiner applies manual compression to the neck veins (usually the internal jugulars) to transiently raise intracranial venous pressure, observing for changes in symptoms or signs to help assess intracranial pathology or cerebral venous outflow.

nägele obliquity.definition: An angular deviation (tilt) of a structure from its normal orientation relative to a defined reference plane; the exact angle and interpretation depend on the specific anatomical site and context in which it is measured. If you have a particular structure or imaging context in mind, please provide it for a more precise definition.

nägele’s rule.definition: A standard method for estimating the expected due date by using the first day of the last menstrual period: due date = LMP + 1 year − 3 months + 7 days (about 280 days from LMP).

nager’s acrofacial dysostosis.definition: A rare congenital disorder due to disrupted development of the first pharyngeal arch, causing facial hypoplasia (midface/maxilla/mandible and ear anomalies) with preaxial limb defects (radial ray anomalies such as hypoplastic or missing thumbs and radius).

na g er’s acrofacial dysostosis.definition: An uncommon congenital disorder in the acrofacial dysostosis spectrum characterized by preaxial limb defects (thumb hypoplasia or aplasia and radial ray anomalies) and facial anomalies such as micrognathia, malar hypoplasia, cleft palate, and external ear anomalies; often with feeding difficulties and hearing loss; most cases are due to SF3B4 gene mutations.

radioulnar synostosis.definition: A fusion of the radius and ulna at the forearm (often at the proximal radioulnar joint), resulting in loss or significant restriction of forearm rotation (pronation and supination); can be congenital or post-traumatic.

acrofacial dysostosis.definition: A congenital syndrome characterized by craniofacial hypoplasia (especially midface and mandible) with associated limb anomalies, arising from abnormal neural crest cell development during embryogenesis.

naglazyme.definition: A recombinant enzyme replacement therapy for mucopolysaccharidosis type VI (Maroteaux-Lamy syndrome) caused by deficiency of the enzyme arylsulfatase B; administered intravenously to replace the missing enzyme and reduce accumulation of dermatan sulfate.

naltrexone.definition: A competitive opioid receptor antagonist (primarily at mu receptors) used to treat opioid use disorder by blocking the effects of opioids and to aid in treating alcohol use disorder by reducing craving and rewarding effects; available in oral form and as a long-acting injectable.

nalbuphine.definition: A synthetic opioid analgesic with mixed agonist-antagonist activity—primarily a kappa-opioid receptor agonist and mu-opioid receptor antagonist—used to treat moderate to severe pain; it has a ceiling effect on respiratory depression and a reduced potential for abuse compared with pure mu-opioid agonists.

nalidixicacid.definition: An older synthetic antibiotic in the quinolone class that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase, blocking DNA replication; historically used for uncomplicated urinary tract infections caused by Gram-negative bacteria but largely superseded by fluoroquinolones due to limited spectrum and resistance concerns.

namenda.definition: A brand-name medication (memantine) used to treat moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease; an NMDA receptor antagonist that modulates glutamatergic neurotransmission.

steinmannpin.definition: A large-diameter, smooth, stainless steel orthopedic pin used to gain skeletal traction or provisional fixation by percutaneously inserting through bone; it provides rigid skeletal anchorage for traction devices or external fixation during fracture management.

nail-patella-syndrome.definition: An autosomal-dominant genetic disorder caused by mutations in the LMX1B gene, characterized by nail hypoplasia or absence, patellar hypoplasia or aplasia, elbow anomalies, and the radiographic finding of iliac horns; renal involvement with proteinuria and potential progressive nephropathy is common.

hipdysplasia.definition: A spectrum of abnormal development of the hip joint in which the femoral head is misaligned or unstable within the acetabulum, ranging from shallow socket to dislocation, which can lead to joint instability and, if untreated, later hip problems such as osteoarthritis.

namaqualandhipdysplasia.definition: Not a recognized medical term; likely refers to developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH): a spectrum of hip joint malformations in which the femoral head is not securely seated in the acetabulum, causing instability, subluxation, or dislocation, typically presenting in infancy or early childhood.

onychoosteodysplasia.definition: A rare genetic disorder characterized by dysplasia (abnormal development) of both nails and bones, leading to nail dystrophy and skeletal abnormalities.

hereditaryosteoonychodysplasia.definition: A hereditary disorder characterized by abnormal bone development (osteodysplasia) and nail abnormalities (onychodysplasia); clinical features may include skeletal malformations or growth abnormalities and dystrophic nails, with inheritance that can vary (often autosomal dominant or recessive) depending on the underlying gene.

onychodysplasia.definition: Abnormal development or dysplasia of the nails, resulting in nail dystrophy, deformity, or irregular growth (can be congenital or acquired).

nailbed.definition: The skin beneath the nail plate, between the nail plate and the fingertip, that nourishes the nail via a rich capillary bed and helps secure the nail plate to the finger.

nailmatrix.definition: The nail matrix is the thick, germinal epithelial region at the proximal end of the nail bed that produces the nail plate; it lies beneath the proximal nail fold and is responsible for most nail growth (damage can affect nail formation).

nailplate.definition: The hard, translucent portion of a fingernail or toenail that overlays the nail bed; composed of densely packed keratinocytes and functions to protect the distal digit and aid in fine manipulation.

nailfold.definition: The skin folds surrounding the nail plate, including the proximal nail fold at the base of the nail and the lateral nail folds along its sides.

nailgroove.definition: A shallow groove on either side of a fingernail or toenail, formed by the lateral nail folds, into which the nail edge sits and along which the nail grows; it marks the boundary between the nail plate and surrounding skin.

nailplateavulsion.definition: A surgical procedure in which the nail plate is removed from the underlying nail bed, either partially or completely, typically under local anesthesia, to treat trauma, infection, ingrown nails, or other nail disorders or to gain access to the nail matrix for biopsy or treatment.

unguis.definition: A nail; the hard keratinized plate that covers the dorsal aspect of the fingertip or toe (the distal phalanx) and is part of the nail unit.

lunula.definition: The visible, crescent-shaped area at the base of a fingernail or toenail that corresponds to the nail matrix; it is where new nail cells are produced and is typically whitish.

cuticle.definition: The outermost, single-cell layer of the hair shaft.

cleidocranialdysostosis.definition: A rare autosomal dominant skeletal dysplasia caused by RUNX2 mutations, characterized by hypoplastic or absent clavicles, delayed or failed closure of cranial sutures/fontanelles, and dental plus craniofacial anomalies such as supernumerary teeth and midface hypoplasia.

craniofacialdysostosis.definition: A group of congenital craniosynostosis syndromes defined by premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures, causing abnormal skull and facial development; commonly features include midface hypoplasia, shallow orbits with potential proptosis, hypertelorism, and airway or dental problems.

mandibulofacialdysostosis.definition: A congenital craniofacial disorder (Treacher Collins syndrome) marked by hypoplasia of the zygomatic arches and mandible, downward-slanting palpebral fissures, ear anomalies, and often conductive hearing loss; usually autosomal dominant due to TCOF1 mutations.

nanosomia.definition: A rare descriptive term for abnormally small body size, typically referring to extreme dwarfism; it is not a single diagnosis and may result from various genetic or developmental disorders.

nanism.definition: Abnormally short stature due to a range of congenital or acquired growth disorders, such as skeletal dysplasias or growth hormone deficiencies.

nanocephalia.definition: A nonstandard term for an abnormally small head size, typically implying microcephaly; defined by a head circumference significantly below the mean for age and sex, often with reduced brain volume and potential developmental delays.

nanocephaly.definition: An abnormally small head size—head circumference significantly below the mean for age and sex—typically due to impaired brain development; may be congenital or acquired and is commonly associated with developmental delays and neurological impairment. In formal terminology, the condition is microcephaly.

nanophthalmos.definition: A rare congenital condition characterized by an abnormally small eyeball (short axial length) with relatively normal anterior segment, leading to high hyperopia and crowded intraocular structures, often with a shallow anterior chamber and increased risk of angle-closure glaucoma and choroidal effusions, particularly after intraocular surgery.

nanosecond.definition: A unit of time equal to one billionth of a second (10^-9 s).

nanotechnology.definition: The science and engineering of manipulating matter at the nanoscale (about 1–100 nanometers) to create materials and devices with unique properties, with medical applications such as targeted drug delivery, diagnostic imaging, biosensing, and therapeutics.

leptospira.definition: A genus of slender, spiral-shaped Gram-negative bacteria (spirochetes) that cause leptospirosis in humans and animals; transmitted by contact with water or soil contaminated with urine from infected animals; disease ranges from a mild febrile illness to Weil disease with jaundice and kidney failure; diagnosed by serology (e.g., MAT) or PCR; treated with antibiotics such as doxycycline or penicillin.

naphazoline.definition: A topical sympathomimetic decongestant (alpha-adrenergic agonist) used in nasal sprays and ophthalmic solutions to constrict dilated blood vessels and relieve redness or congestion; prolonged use can cause rebound congestion.

naphthalene.definition: A white crystalline polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (C10H8) used in moth repellents and as a solvent; exposure can irritate the skin, eyes, and respiratory tract, and higher doses may cause hemolytic anemia (especially in G6PD deficiency) and methemoglobinemia; it is considered possibly carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 2B).

napkinringtumor.definition: A circumferential, annular colorectal carcinoma that encircles the lumen of the colon (often the sigmoid), causing marked luminal narrowing with a ring‑like appearance on imaging.

paradichlorobenzene.definition: Colorless solid organic compound; the para isomer of dichlorobenzene (1,4-dichlorobenzene). Used as a moth repellent in mothballs and as a solvent; exposure may irritate the skin, eyes, and respiratory tract, and high-level or prolonged exposure can affect the central nervous system.

hepatitisc.definition: Caused by a germ (a virus) that affects your liver. It can be a short-term disease or it can last for a long time.

liverfailure.definition: A condition in which the liver can no longer perform its essential metabolic, synthetic, and detoxifying functions, leading to jaundice, impaired blood clotting, hepatic encephalopathy, hypoalbuminemia, and fluid/metabolic abnormalities; can be acute (fulminant) or chronic, usually due to severe liver injury or advanced liver disease.

breastcancer.definition: A malignant tumor arising from breast tissue, most often from ductal or lobular epithelial cells; it can invade surrounding tissue and metastasize to distant sites, with treatment depending on stage and receptor status and commonly including surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, and targeted therapy.

metastaticcancer.definition: Cancer that has spread from the original (primary) site to distant organs or tissues, typically via the bloodstream or lymphatic system, forming new tumors that are the same type as the primary cancer.

renalinsufficiency.definition: A reduced ability of the kidneys to filter waste products from the blood, leading to accumulation of urea and other wastes and disturbances in fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance; it can be acute or chronic.

orthostatichypotension.definition: A sudden drop in blood pressure upon standing or getting out of bed, causing dizziness.

blurredvision.definition: A symptom characterized by reduced sharpness of vision, with objects appearing hazy or out of focus; causes include refractive error, dry eye, cataracts, retinal or optic nerve disease, migraine with aura, and certain medications.

sleepdisorders.definition: A group of medical conditions characterized by abnormal patterns, timing, duration, or quality of sleep that cause daytime distress or impairment. Common examples include insomnia, sleep apnea, narcolepsy, restless legs syndrome, circadian rhythm sleep–wake disorders, and various parasomnias. Evaluation often involves clinical history and, if indicated, sleep studies; management may include sleep hygiene, behavioral therapies, medications, and devices such as CPAP for sleep apnea.

urinaryoutput.definition: The amount of urine produced and excreted by the kidneys per unit time, typically expressed as daily volume; normal adult urine output is about 800–2000 mL per day and is influenced by hydration, renal function, and hormonal control (eg, ADH and aldosterone).

urinaryretention.definition: An inability to empty the bladder completely or at all despite the urge to urinate, often due to bladder outlet obstruction, detrusor underactivity, or neurogenic dysfunction; it can be acute or chronic and may require catheterization.

urinaryurgency.definition: A sudden, compelling urge to urinate that is difficult to defer, often with increased urinary frequency and sometimes with leakage (urge incontinence) if not promptly addressed.

bruising.definition: A contusion resulting from blunt trauma in which small blood vessels are damaged, causing leakage of blood into the surrounding tissues and a discoloration under the skin that evolves as the injury heals.

pulmonaryedema.definition: A condition caused by excess fluid accumulating in the lungs, making breathing difficult.

respiratorydepression.definition: A condition in which breathing is inadequate due to reduced respiratory drive or weakened respiratory muscles, resulting in hypoventilation with hypercapnia and often hypoxemia; commonly caused by central nervous system depressants, brainstem injury, or neuromuscular disorders.

tolerance.definition: The process through which the body becomes less responsive to a psychoactive substance or rewarding behavior. Over time, people who develop tolerance need larger doses to get the same effect they first got with smaller doses.

nardil.definition: A brand-name antidepressant (phenelzine) that is an irreversible monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) used to treat major depressive disorder, particularly treatment-resistant cases; requires strict dietary tyramine restriction to avoid hypertensive crisis and can interact dangerously with serotonergic drugs and certain sympathomimetics.

phenelzine_sulfate.definition: An irreversible monoamine oxidase inhibitor antidepressant that increases brain levels of norepinephrine, serotonin, and dopamine by inhibiting monoamine oxidase; used for treatment-resistant major depressive disorder and requiring dietary tyramine restrictions and monitoring for dangerous drug interactions.

naprosyn.definition: A brand-name nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) containing naproxen; used to relieve pain, inflammation, and fever in conditions such as arthritis; it works by reversibly inhibiting cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing prostaglandin synthesis.

primary_dysmenorrhea.definition: Painful menstruation (cramps) occurring during menses in the absence of pelvic pathology, typically beginning within the first few years after menarche; thought to be due to increased prostaglandin production causing uterine contractions and ischemia, often improving with NSAIDs or hormonal contraception.

ankylosing_spondylitis.definition: A chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease primarily affecting the axial skeleton (sacroiliac joints and spine) with inflammatory back pain and progressive spinal stiffness that can lead to fusion; part of seronegative spondyloarthropathies and often associated with HLA-B27.

tendinitis.definition: When the tissues that connect muscles to bones swell and cause pain.

acute_gout.definition: A sudden, painful inflammatory arthritis caused by deposition of monosodium urate crystals in a joint due to hyperuricemia; classically presents with rapid onset of a hot, swollen, red joint (often the big toe). Diagnosis is by synovial fluid showing needle-shaped, negatively birefringent urate crystals; treated acutely with NSAIDs, colchicine, or corticosteroids, and managed long-term with urate-lowering therapy to prevent recurrences.

angina_pectoris.definition: Temporary chest pain that occurs when the heart isn’t getting enough oxygen and blood, usually occurring in response to physical activity or stress.

silent_ischemia.definition: Shortage of oxygen delivery to the heart muscle that causes no symptoms.

ischemic_heart_disease.definition: A spectrum of heart conditions caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle due to narrowed or blocked coronary arteries, most commonly from atherosclerosis; it includes angina (stable and unstable) and myocardial infarction.

renal_function.definition: The kidneys' ability to filter blood to remove waste products and excess fluid, regulate electrolyte and acid-base balance, concentrate urine, and secrete or activate hormones (e.g., erythropoietin, renin, vitamin D).

gastrointestinal_disorder.definition: A broad category of conditions affecting the gastrointestinal tract (from the esophagus to the rectum) that disrupt digestion, absorption, motility, or transit, and cause symptoms such as abdominal pain, reflux, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation.

peptic_ulcers.definition: A sore on the lining of the stomach or the first part of the small intestine (the duodenum). Also called stomach ulcers.

narcotic.definition: A drug to treat moderate to severe pain. Also called opiates.

naloxone_hydrochloride.definition: A hydrochloride salt of the opioid receptor antagonist naloxone; a competitive antagonist at mu, kappa, and delta receptors used to reverse opioid overdose by displacing opioid agonists; administered by injection or intranasal spray; rapid onset with a short duration and may precipitate withdrawal in opioid-dependent individuals.

narcan.definition: A medication that acts as a competitive antagonist at opioid receptors to rapidly reverse opioid overdoses by displacing opioids at mu-opioid receptors; administered intranasally, intramuscularly, or intravenously; onset within minutes, with effects that may wear off before long-acting opioids, requiring possible repeat dosing.

narcotics_anonymous.definition: A nonprofit, peer‑led mutual‑help program that provides a 12‑step framework, regular meetings, sponsorship, and recovery literature to help individuals achieve and maintain abstinence from all illegal and nonmedical drugs.

sleep_paralysis.definition: A feeling of paralysis that may occur during the transition between wakefulness and sleep if the REM sleep stage begins before a person is fully asleep; classically associated with narcolepsy.

sodium_amobarbital.definition: A short- to intermediate-acting barbiturate; the sodium salt of amobarbital, a CNS depressant used as a sedative-hypnotic for short-term insomnia and as a preanesthetic medication; it enhances GABAergic inhibition by positive allosteric modulation of the GABA-A receptor.

nasarel.definition: A brand-name intranasal corticosteroid spray used to treat allergic rhinitis and other nasal inflammatory symptoms by reducing nasal mucosal inflammation.

nasal_cannula.definition: A device for delivering supplemental oxygen via two prongs inserted in the nostrils, connected to an oxygen source; used to administer low-to-moderate oxygen flow, often with humidification.

nasal_balloon_tamponade.definition: A technique for controlling nasal bleeding by inserting a balloon-tipped catheter into the nasal cavity and inflating the balloon to apply direct pressure (tamponade) on the bleeding site, commonly used for posterior epistaxis or refractory anterior epistaxis.

nasal_instillation_of_medicine.definition: A route of administration in which a liquid medication is delivered into the nasal cavity by instillation (drops or spray) to achieve local nasal effects or systemic absorption through the nasal mucosa.

nasal_spray.definition: A device or formulation that delivers a fine mist into the nasal passages to treat local nasal symptoms or enable systemic drug absorption, commonly used for decongestants, intranasal corticosteroids, saline sprays, or vaccines.

nasal_decongestant.definition: A medication used to relieve nasal congestion by constricting blood vessels in the nasal mucosa, thereby reducing swelling; it can be taken orally or used as a nasal spray. Prolonged use of topical formulations can cause rebound congestion.

nasal_polyps.definition: Nasal polyps are noncancerous, soft, teardrop-shaped outgrowths of the mucous membranes lining the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses, typically arising from chronic inflammation (as in chronic rhinosinusitis or allergic rhinitis). They often cause nasal obstruction, congestion, postnasal drip, and reduced sense of smell.

nasal_fracture_reduction.definition: A procedure to realign a displaced nasal bone fracture to restore nasal contour and airway patency, most commonly performed by closed reduction (manual realignment) under local or general anesthesia, usually within about 7 days of injury.

nasal_glioma.definition: A congenital, non-neoplastic collection of ectopic glial tissue in the nasal region (glial heterotopia), presenting as a nasal mass in infancy; may be connected to intracranial contents by a stalk; treated by surgical excision.

nasal_septum.definition: A partition that divides the nasal cavity into left and right halves, composed of septal cartilage anteriorly and bony components (the vomer and the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid) posteriorly; it supports the nasal passages and directs airflow.

nasal_cartilage.definition: A hyaline cartilage–based framework that forms the structure of the external nose, including the septal cartilage, upper lateral cartilages, and lower lateral (alar) cartilages; it provides shape and support and helps maintain an open nasal airway.

nasal_bone.definition: A pair of small, rectangular facial bones that form the bony bridge of the nose; they articulate with the frontal bone superiorly at the frontonasal suture and with the maxillae laterally, meeting at the midline to form the nasal dorsum.

cribriform_plate_of_ethmoid_bone.definition: A horizontal, sieve-like portion of the ethmoid bone forming the roof of the nasal cavity and part of the floor of the anterior cranial fossa; it contains many tiny foramina (cribriform foramina) through which olfactory nerve fibers pass from the nasal mucosa to the olfactory bulbs.

perpendicular_plate_of_ethmoid.definition: Thin vertical plate of the ethmoid bone forming the superior portion of the nasal septum; descends from the cribriform plate and articulates with the vomer inferiorly to complete the bony septum.

olfactory_cells.definition: Olfactory receptor neurons of the nasal olfactory epithelium; bipolar sensory neurons with cilia that express odorant receptors and detect airborne odorants, sending axons through the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb to form the first synapses in the olfactory pathway. They continuously regenerate from basal cells.

olfactory_nerves.definition: A pair of sensory nerve fibers that carry olfactory (smell) information from the olfactory epithelium in the nasal cavity to the olfactory bulb; collectively they form cranial nerve I and traverse the cribriform plate.

olfactory_hairs.definition: The nonmotile cilia on the apical dendrites of olfactory receptor neurons that extend into the nasal mucus; these olfactory hairs bear odorant receptors and initiate the odorant signal transduction cascade, leading to neuronal depolarization.

olfactory_region.definition: The part of the nasal mucosa that contains the olfactory epithelium with olfactory receptor neurons, responsible for the sense of smell; located in the superior aspect of the nasal cavity at the roof near the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone.

superior_nasal_concha.definition: A narrow, scroll-shaped bony projection on the lateral wall of the nasal cavity, the uppermost of the nasal turbinates (part of the ethmoid bone), covered by mucosa and aiding in warming, humidifying, and filtering inhaled air.

middle_nasal_concha.definition: A scroll-like bony shelf on the ethmoid bone forming part of the middle turbinate; it projects into the nasal cavity, helps humidify and warm inspired air, and serves as a landmark for sinus drainage into the middle meatus (notably the maxillary sinus).

inferior_nasal_concha.definition: An independent, scroll-shaped facial bone that forms the lowest of the nasal turbinates on the lateral wall of the nasal cavity; it helps create the inferior nasal meatus and increases mucosal surface area to warm, humidify, and filter inhaled air.

nasolacrimal_duct.definition: A duct that drains tears from the lacrimal sac into the nasal cavity (inferior meatus), forming part of the tear drainage system.

bulla_ethmoidalis.definition: A rounded prominence on the lateral wall of the middle meatus of the nasal cavity, formed by the middle ethmoidal air cells and marking the openings of those cells into the middle meatus.

conchae.definition: One of the nasal turbinates—bony shelves inside the nasal cavity (superior, middle, and inferior conchae) that increase surface area to humidify, warm, and filter inhaled air and help direct airflow.

turbinates.definition: Scroll-like bony projections on the lateral walls of the nasal cavity (superior, middle, and inferior turbinates) that increase mucosal surface area to warm, humidify, and filter inhaled air.

nasal_fossa.definition: One of the two internal air-filled spaces of the nose (nasal cavities) bounded laterally by the nasal walls and medially by the nasal septum; lined with mucous membrane and involved in warming, humidifying, and filtering inhaled air.

nasal_sinus.definition: One of the air-filled cavities within the bones surrounding the nasal cavity (the paranasal sinuses: frontal, maxillary, ethmoid, and sphenoid), lined with respiratory epithelium and connected to the nasal cavity; functions include humidifying and warming inhaled air, lightening the skull, producing mucus, and aiding voice resonance.

frontal_sinus.definition: A pair of air-filled cavities within the frontal bone above the orbits, lined with respiratory epithelium; drain into the nasal cavity via the frontonasal duct to the middle meatus, and are part of the paranasal sinus system involved in humidifying/warming inspired air and contributing to voice resonance.

ethmoidal_air_cells.definition: Air-filled cavities within the ethmoid bone forming part of the paranasal sinuses, subdivided into anterior, middle, and posterior cells; lined with respiratory mucosa and draining into the middle nasal meatus.

sphenoidal_sinuses.definition: Air-filled cavities within the sphenoid bone that form part of the paranasal sinuses; they drain into the nasal cavity and are lined by mucosa, with variable size, and can be involved in sphenoidal sinusitis.

pharyngeal_tonsil.definition: A single mass of lymphoid tissue located on the roof of the nasopharynx (adenoids); part of Waldeyer's ring involved in immune defense by trapping inhaled pathogens; may hypertrophy in children, causing nasal obstruction, mouth breathing, snoring, or sleep apnea, and can become inflamed.

soft_palate.definition: Movable muscular posterior part of the palate that separates the nasopharynx from the oropharynx; it elevates to close the nasal cavity during swallowing and certain sounds, aiding in articulation and preventing nasal regurgitation.

hard_palate.definition: An immobile, bony anterior portion of the palate that forms the roof of the mouth and separates the oral and nasal cavities; formed by the palatine processes of the maxillae and the horizontal plates of the palatine bones.

nasogastric_intubation.definition: Insertion of a flexible tube through a nostril into the stomach for gastric decompression or suction, aspiration of gastric contents, irrigation or sampling, administration of medications, or enteral feeding.

nasogastric_feeding.definition: A method of delivering nutrition directly into the stomach through a tube inserted via the nose, used when oral intake is inadequate or unsafe.

foley_catheter.definition: A flexible indwelling urinary catheter inserted through the urethra into the bladder to drain urine; kept in place by inflation of a small balloon at its tip.

nasogastric_back_wall_echo.definition: Not a standard medical term; no widely recognized definition exists. If used informally, it may refer to an ultrasound observation of the posterior gastric wall during nasogastric tube placement to help confirm tube position, but this is not an established or widely used term. If you have a source or context, I can tailor the definition accordingly.

xiphoid.definition: A small projection at the inferior end of the sternum; the lowest part of the sternum. It is cartilaginous in youth and ossifies with age; serves as an attachment site for the diaphragm and abdominal muscles.

contents.definition: In anatomy, contents are the internal organs and other structures contained within a body cavity or hollow organ (e.g., the abdominal contents include the stomach, intestines, liver, and spleen).

nasolabial.definition: Relating to the region between the nose and the upper lip; used to describe the folds or grooves running from the sides of the nose to the corners of the mouth.

nasomandibular.definition: Relating to both the nasal region and the mandible; describing anatomical or clinical relationships between the nose and the lower jaw.

nasomental.definition: Pertaining to the nose (nasal region) and the chin (mentum); used to describe anatomical relationships or measurements between these facial regions.

nasopalatine.definition: Relating to the nasal cavity and the palate; specifically referring to the nasopalatine nerve and the incisive canal/foramen that connect the two regions.

rhinopharyngeal.definition: Pertaining to the nasopharynx, the upper part of the pharynx located behind the nasal cavity.

juvenile.definition: Relating to young people; in medicine, used of conditions that occur in children or adolescents or of immature developmental stages.

nasopharyngography.definition: A radiographic technique in which radiopaque contrast is introduced through the nose into the nasopharynx to visualize the nasopharyngeal space and assess its anatomy and function, especially velopharyngeal closure and swallowing.

nasopharyngoscopy.definition: A procedure in which a nasal endoscope (flexible or rigid) is inserted through the nose to visualize the nasopharynx and surrounding structures for evaluation of nasal, adenoidal, and nasopharyngeal pathology.

eustachian.definition: Relating to the auditory tube that connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx and helps regulate air pressure in the middle ear.

adenoidal.definition: Relating to or resembling the adenoids (pharyngeal tonsils).

nares.definition: The external openings of the nasal cavities (nostrils); the plural of naris.

incisive.definition: Relating to the incisors (front teeth); sharp, penetrating, or keen in effect or intellect.

crohn's.definition: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by long-lasting inflammation of the digestive tract, which can affect any part from mouth to anus and commonly causes abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, and fatigue.

type.definition: A category or class within a system of classification used to distinguish forms of a disease, condition, or pathogen, typically based on differences in cause, mechanism, or clinical presentation.

natalizumab.definition: A humanized monoclonal antibody against α4-integrin (VLA-4) that inhibits leukocyte adhesion and migration into the CNS and gut; used for relapsing multiple sclerosis and Crohn's disease, with a notable risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.

progressive.definition: An adjective describing a disease or condition that worsens or advances in severity or extent over time.

multifocal.definition: Having more than one focal point; occurring in several locations or involving multiple distinct sites of disease or pathology.

lower.definition: Situated toward the feet or below another reference point in the body; the opposite of upper.

infectious diseases.definition: Infectious diseases are illnesses caused by pathogenic microorganisms (bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites) that can be transmitted between people, animals, or from the environment through direct contact, droplets or airborne spread, vectors, or contaminated food and water.

immunodeficiency virus infection.definition: An infection caused by the human immunodeficiency virus that progressively weakens the immune system by depleting CD4+ T lymphocytes, increasing susceptibility to opportunistic infections and certain cancers; without treatment it may progress to Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS).

developmental disabilities.definition: Chronic, lifelong conditions that originate before age 22 and substantially limit one or more major life activities—such as self-care, communication, learning, mobility, or independent living.

vision.definition: The sense of sight; the ability to perceive light, color, and objects, mediated by the retina, optic nerve, and visual processing pathways in the brain.

kidney diseases.definition: Most kidney diseases affect the nephrons, the tiny structures in the kidneys that filter waste; collectively they are known as renal diseases.

hematologic diseases.definition: A broad category of disorders that affect the blood and its forming organs (bone marrow, spleen), including red cell, white cell, and platelet disorders, coagulation abnormalities, and hematologic malignancies such as leukemias, lymphomas, and myelomas.

endocrinology.definition: The branch of medicine that deals with the study of the endocrine system, its glands and hormones, and the disorders arising from their dysfunction.

digestive diseases.definition: Any of the diseases that occur in your stomach or intestinal tract.

sleep disorders.definition: A group of medical conditions characterized by abnormal sleep patterns, duration, or quality that cause daytime distress or impairment; includes insomnia, hypersomnolence disorders, circadian rhythm disorders, parasomnias, and sleep-related breathing disorders such as obstructive sleep apnea.

skin diseases.definition: An umbrella term for conditions that affect the skin and its appendages (hair, nails, sweat glands), including infections, inflammatory and autoimmune disorders, neoplasms, and inherited or metabolic diseases; typically presenting with rashes, lesions, itching, color changes, scaling, ulcers, or hair/nail abnormalities.

smell.definition: The sense of smell; the detection and perception of volatile odorant molecules by olfactory receptor neurons in the nasal epithelium, with neural signals transmitted to the brain via the olfactory nerve (cranial nerve I).

voice.definition: The sound produced by the vocal folds (vocal cords) during phonation as air from the lungs passes through the larynx and is shaped by the resonating cavities of the vocal tract to form speech or singing.

speech.definition: The production of spoken language through coordinated use of the respiratory system, vocal folds, and articulators (lips, tongue, palate) to form speech sounds.

language.definition: A complex system of spoken, written, or signed symbols used to convey meaning; clinically, the cognitive and motor ability to understand and produce such symbols, with disorders including aphasia.

bone marrow transplant.definition: A procedure to replace damaged bone marrow with healthy hematopoietic stem cells from a donor or from the patient, typically after high-dose chemotherapy (and sometimes radiation); the transplanted cells engraft and reconstitute blood cell production and it is used for certain cancers and other bone marrow disorders.

leukocyte antigen.definition: A family of cell-surface proteins on leukocytes that present peptide antigens to T lymphocytes, enabling the immune system to distinguish self from non-self; in humans this system is known as the human leukocyte antigen (HLA), comprising MHC class I and II molecules encoded by genes on chromosome 6.

vaccine-preventable diseases.definition: Infectious diseases for which an effective vaccine exists that can prevent infection or illness in vaccinated individuals, thereby reducing disease incidence, severity, and transmission in the population.

eye disorders.definition: A broad category of conditions that affect the eye and its associated structures, impairing vision or causing symptoms such as pain, redness, or swelling; causes include refractive errors, cataracts, glaucoma, retinal and optic nerve diseases, infections, inflammatory conditions, trauma, and systemic illnesses with ocular involvement.

natremia.definition: The concentration of sodium ions in the blood (serum/plasma), reflecting extracellular sodium balance; abnormalities include hyponatremia (low) and hypernatremia (high).

natriuresis.definition: The excretion of sodium in the urine by the kidneys, typically promoted by signals such as atrial natriuretic peptide and occurring with increased extracellular fluid volume or sodium loading.
