opponens pollicis.definition: An intrinsic thenar muscle that opposes the thumb by medially rotating and flexing the first metacarpal at the carpometacarpal joint; it originates from the flexor retinaculum and the tubercles of the trapezium and adjacent carpal bones and inserts along the lateral border of the first metacarpal; innervated by the recurrent branch of the median nerve.

heel.definition: The posterior portion of the foot below the ankle; the calcaneus (heel bone).

visual acuity.definition: The eye's ability to see sharply, usually measured by comparing it with what a normal eye would see from 20 feet. Problems in this ability can usually be corrected with eyeglasses.

visual fields.definition: The area of space that can be seen by the eye with fixed gaze, comprising central and peripheral vision; used to assess visual function and detect field loss from ocular or neurologic disease.

optic cup.definition:
- In ophthalmology/anatomy, the optic cup is the central, depressed area of the optic disc; its size relative to the disc (cup-to-disc ratio) is used to assess glaucomatous damage. 

- In embryology, the optic cup is the double-walled invagination of the optic vesicle that gives rise to the neural retina (inner layer) and retinal pigment epithelium (outer layer).

central retinal artery occlusion.definition: A sudden, painless loss of vision in one eye caused by occlusion of the central retinal artery, usually from an embolus or thrombus; an ophthalmic emergency requiring urgent evaluation to salvage vision.

choroidal fissure.definition: A narrow cleft in the medial wall of the lateral ventricle, between the fornix and the thalamus, through which the choroid plexus invaginates from the tela choroidea to form the choroid plexus of the inferior (temporal) horn.

optic stalk.definition: An embryonic structure that connects the developing retina (optic cup) to the forebrain; it contains retinal ganglion cell axons and associated vessels and later differentiates into the optic nerve.

porus opticus.definition: A bony opening in the sphenoid bone (optic canal/foramen) at the posterior wall of the orbit through which the optic nerve (CN II) and the ophthalmic artery pass from the middle cranial fossa into the orbit.

optic radiation.definition: Geniculocalcarine tract; fibers from the lateral geniculate nucleus of the thalamus to the primary visual cortex (calcarine sulcus) in the occipital lobe, carrying visual information from the contralateral visual field; includes superior (parietal) and inferior (Meyer’s loop) components.

optic glioma.definition: A slow-growing glial tumor of the optic nerve (often a pilocytic astrocytoma) that affects the optic pathway; most common in children and in people with neurofibromatosis type 1, presenting with progressive vision loss.

secondary optic atrophy.definition: Optic nerve degeneration that occurs as a consequence of disease outside the optic nerve itself (e.g., retinal disease or lesions of the posterior visual pathway), resulting in retrograde loss of optic nerve fibers and a pale, atrophic disc.

thyroid dysfunction.definition: A broad term for disorders of the thyroid gland characterized by abnormal hormone production or gland structure—most commonly hypothyroidism (low hormone) or hyperthyroidism (high hormone)—caused by autoimmune disease, iodine imbalance, thyroiditis, nodular disease, or neoplasia.

sinus problems.definition: Inflammation or infection of the sinuses (the air-filled spaces around the bones of the face).

retinal degeneration.definition: Progressive loss or dysfunction of retinal cells (primarily photoreceptors and retinal pigment epithelium) leading to gradual vision loss and potentially blindness; can be hereditary or acquired, and includes conditions such as retinitis pigmentosa and age-related macular degeneration.

oral cancer.definition: Malignant neoplasm of the oral cavity, most often squamous cell carcinoma, arising from the mucosal lining of the lips, tongue, floor of mouth, cheek, gums, or palate; presents as a nonhealing ulcer or mass and can invade surrounding tissues and metastasize to regional lymph nodes.

lip cancer.definition: A malignant neoplasm of the lip, most often squamous cell carcinoma, arising from the lip’s squamous epithelium (usually the lower lip); commonly related to sun exposure and presents as a persistent nonhealing lesion (ulcer or indurated plaque) with potential regional lymph node spread, treated by surgical excision (often Mohs) and/or radiotherapy depending on stage.

epidermoid carcinomas.definition: A malignant neoplasm composed of epidermoid (squamous) cells; a type of squamous cell carcinoma arising from squamous epithelium in the skin or mucous membranes, typically keratinizing and capable of invasion and metastasis.

metastatic lesions.definition: Secondary malignant foci produced when cancer cells disseminate from a primary tumor to distant organs via the blood or lymphatic system, forming new tumor lesions that are histologically similar to the original cancer.

erythroplasia.definition: A red patch or plaque on mucous membranes or skin, resulting from vascular dilation and epithelial changes; a descriptive term for red, velvety lesions that may be precancerous (as in erythroplasia of Queyrat on the glans penis).

optic hemorrhage.definition: Bleeding at the optic nerve head (optic disc) seen on eye examination, associated with optic neuropathies such as glaucoma and ischemic optic neuropathy, and with other vascular or inflammatory ocular diseases.

optimine.definition: Not a recognized medical term; may be a misspelling or a brand/product name rather than a medical concept.

emantics.definition: Semantics is the study of meaning in language; in medicine, it encompasses the interpretation of medical terms and health data to ensure accurate communication and interoperable information exchange.

miotics.definition: A class of parasympathomimetic agents that induce pupil constriction (miosis) by stimulating the iris sphincter muscle; used to treat glaucoma by increasing aqueous humor outflow (e.g., pilocarpine).

mydriatics.definition: A class of ophthalmic drugs that dilate the pupil (pupillary dilation) by blocking muscarinic receptors in the iris sphincter or by stimulating the iris dilator; used to facilitate eye examinations and procedures. Examples include tropicamide, cyclopentolate, atropine, and phenylephrine.

visual field test.definition: A procedure that measures the full extent and sensitivity of a person’s visual field by presenting stimuli at various locations while the patient fixates on a central target; used to detect blind spots and assess diseases such as glaucoma and certain neurological conditions.

exfoliative cytology.definition: A cytology technique in which exfoliated cells from epithelial surfaces are collected and examined microscopically to detect disease, especially cancer or precancerous changes; commonly used in screening the cervix (Pap smear) and other sites.

conjunctival scrapings.definition: An ocular diagnostic procedure in which epithelial cells from the conjunctiva are scraped with a small instrument (e.g., spatula or curette) to obtain material for microscopic examination or culture, used to diagnose infections or inflammatory conjunctival disorders.

scleral edema.definition: Swelling of the sclera due to accumulation of interstitial fluid in the scleral stroma, often related to systemic fluid overload or inflammatory/vascular ocular conditions.

foreign body in the eye.definition: An external object on or in the eye (e.g., dust, metal, glass) that is not part of the eye, causing irritation, tearing, pain, and a foreign-body sensation; it may be superficial or embedded and often requires removal.

ophthalmoscopic examination.definition: A clinical examination of the interior of the eye (the fundus) using an ophthalmoscope or indirect ophthalmoscopy—often after pupil dilation—to visualize the retina, optic disc, and retinal vessels for signs of disease.

oral rehydration solutions.definition: A glucose–electrolyte solution used to treat or prevent dehydration by replenishing water and essential electrolytes (notably sodium and potassium) and providing glucose to enhance intestinal absorption of sodium and water; typically contains water, sodium, chloride, potassium, bicarbonate or citrate, and glucose.

follicular maturation.definition: The growth and maturation of ovarian follicles from primordial stages to the preovulatory (Graafian) follicle, driven by gonadotropins (primarily FSH with LH support), involving granulosa and theca cell differentiation, antral development and follicular fluid accumulation, and oocyte maturation preparing for ovulation.

progestin-only oral contraceptives.definition: An oral contraceptive regimen that contains only synthetic progestin (no estrogen); it prevents pregnancy mainly by thickening cervical mucus and thinning the endometrium, with variable suppression of ovulation, and requires strict daily dosing at roughly the same time each day. Often used when estrogen-containing pills are contraindicated or during breastfeeding.

seasonale.definition: A brand-name extended-cycle combined oral contraceptive containing ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel, taken for 84 days of active pills followed by 7 days of placebo to prevent pregnancy and reduce the frequency of menstrual bleeding.

thrombotic complications.definition: Complications arising from the formation of a blood clot (thrombus) within a vessel, causing obstruction of blood flow and tissue ischemia; common examples include deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, arterial thrombosis (e.g., myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke), and organ ischemia.

nasal decongestant.definition: A medication that relieves nasal congestion by constricting the blood vessels in the nasal mucosa, reducing swelling; available as topical nasal sprays or oral tablets, with agents such as oxymetazoline, phenylephrine, and pseudoephedrine; long-term use can cause rebound congestion.

oral examination.definition: A clinical examination of the mouth in which the clinician visually inspects and palpates the oral cavity—including the lips, teeth, gums, tongue, floor of the mouth, and palate—to detect lesions, abnormalities, or signs of disease.

oralis.definition: Relating to the mouth; an anatomical descriptor used to denote structures located at or associated with the mouth.

oral-facial-digital syndrome.definition: An inherited group of rare congenital disorders (a ciliopathy spectrum) defined by malformations of the mouth/oral cavity, face, and digits, typically with tongue abnormalities, dental anomalies, and limb malformations such as polydactyly or syndactyly; inheritance patterns vary by subtype (most notably X‑linked dominant OFD1 in type I).

seborrhea.definition: Excessive secretion of sebum by the sebaceous glands, leading to oily skin and hair.

hairy leukoplakia.definition: A white, painless, corrugated, non-scrapable plaque on the lateral tongue or buccal mucosa caused by Epstein-Barr virus infection; commonly seen in immunocompromised individuals (e.g., HIV/AIDS); it is benign and not premalignant, with management focusing on treating the underlying immune suppression and local therapies if needed.

oral hairy leukoplakia.definition: An Epstein-Barr virus–associated white plaque on the oral mucosa, most often the lateral tongue, with a corrugated or “hairy” appearance that cannot be scraped off; occurs primarily in immunocompromised patients (notably those with HIV/AIDS) and has little malignant potential, though it signals underlying immunosuppression.

oral health maintenance.definition: A set of practices and preventive measures aimed at preserving the health of the mouth, teeth, and gums, including daily plaque control (brushing with fluoride toothpaste and flossing), regular professional cleanings, fluoride exposure, a balanced diet, and avoidance of tobacco and other risk factors; plus timely treatment of dental disease.

oral health promotion.definition: A public health approach that enables individuals and communities to maintain and improve oral health through prevention, health education, risk-factor reduction (e.g., reducing sugar intake and tobacco use), and access to fluoride and regular dental care.

oral health restoration.definition: An overarching clinical process to restore the health, function, and appearance of the oral cavity by diagnosing and treating dental and periodontal disease and repairing or replacing damaged tissues and teeth to achieve long-term stability.

oral hypoglycemic agent.definition: A drug taken by mouth that lowers blood glucose in people with diabetes, especially type 2 diabetes, by various mechanisms such as stimulating insulin release, decreasing hepatic glucose production, or increasing peripheral glucose uptake/sensitivity.

oral pathology.definition: The dental specialty that studies and diagnoses diseases of the mouth and surrounding structures, often through clinical evaluation and histopathologic examination.

poliovirus vaccine.definition: A vaccine used to prevent poliomyelitis by provoking immunity to poliovirus; currently available mainly as the inactivated poliovirus vaccine (IPV) given by injection, with a live-attenuated oral poliovirus vaccine (OPV) previously used but now less common due to risk of vaccine-derived poliovirus.

sabin vaccine.definition: A live-attenuated oral vaccine against poliomyelitis containing weakened polioviruses types 1–3, administered orally to induce mucosal (intestinal) and systemic immunity.

opv.definition: A live-attenuated vaccine given by mouth that induces immunity to poliovirus, mainly protecting intestinal and systemic immunity against poliomyelitis; used in many programs as part of polio eradication efforts, and contrasted with the injectable inactivated polio vaccine (IPV).

ipv.definition: A vaccine containing inactivated poliovirus used to immunize against poliomyelitis; administered by intramuscular injection to stimulate antibody production and confer immunity without the risk of poliovirus replication.

paralytic poliomyelitis.definition: An acute viral infection caused by poliovirus that destroys motor neurons in the anterior horn of the spinal cord and brainstem, producing rapid-onset, asymmetric flaccid paralysis and often respiratory compromise; transmitted via the fecal-oral route and preventable by vaccination.

premedication.definition: The administration of drugs before a medical procedure (often before anesthesia) to prevent or lessen anticipated perioperative complications, such as anxiety, pain, nausea, or excessive secretions.

dental prophylaxis.definition: A preventive dental procedure in which a dentist or dental hygienist removes plaque, calculus (tartar), and stains from the tooth surfaces and polishes the teeth to help prevent dental disease.

dental images.definition: Dental images are radiographic or photographic representations of teeth and surrounding oral tissues used to diagnose disease, assess anatomy, plan treatment, and monitor dental health; common forms include bitewing, periapical, and panoramic radiographs, cone-beam CT (CBCT) scans, and intraoral or extraoral photographs.

scaling.definition: Desquamation or shedding of the outermost layer of the skin (epidermis), often due to dryness or dermatologic disease, presenting as flaking.

ultrasonic scaling.definition: A dental procedure in which an ultrasonic scaler vibrates at high frequency to disrupt and remove plaque, biofilm, and calculus (tartar) from tooth surfaces, typically with water irrigation, used during professional cleaning and periodontal therapy.

oral tolerance therapy.definition: An approach that administers a specific antigen orally to induce immune tolerance and reduce adverse immune responses to that antigen, as in oral immunotherapy for food allergies; it relies on gut-associated immune mechanisms and regulatory T cell–mediated tolerance.

pimozide.definition: A potent typical antipsychotic (dopamine D2 receptor antagonist) used primarily to treat Tourette syndrome and severe psychosis; it can cause QT interval prolongation and torsades de pointes, requiring cardiac monitoring.

orap.definition: A brand name for pimozide, an antipsychotic belonging to the diphenylbutylpiperidine class; it functions as a dopamine D2 receptor antagonist and is used to treat Tourette syndrome and other tic disorders.

orencia.definition: A biologic drug (abatacept) that inhibits T‑cell activation by binding CD80/CD86 on antigen-presenting cells, thereby reducing autoimmune inflammation; used to treat rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

orchiditis.definition: Swelling of 1 or both testicles. It is often a side effect of mumps.

orchioplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair or reconstruct the testis (testicle).

orchidoplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to reconstruct or repair the testicle, typically to correct deformities or restore function after injury or congenital malformations.

orchiopexy.definition: A surgical procedure to move an undescended testicle into the scrotum and secure it there, typically performed to treat cryptorchidism.

ora serrata retinae.definition: A scalloped boundary marking the anterior limit of the retina, where the neural retina ends and the nonphotosensitive ciliary epithelium begins (the border between retina proper and the ciliary body).

orbital fissure.definition: A slit‑like opening in the bony orbit of the skull through which nerves and vessels pass between the orbit and the cranial cavity or face; the two main fissures are the superior orbital fissure and the inferior orbital fissure.

infraorbital canal.definition: A bony passage within the maxilla that extends from the floor of the orbit to the infraorbital foramen, transmitting the infraorbital nerve (a branch of CN V2) and accompanying vessels to the midface.

ethmoidal foramina.definition: Openings in the ethmoid bone (the anterior and posterior ethmoidal foramina) that transmit the anterior and posterior ethmoidal nerves and arteries.

greater wing of sphenoid.definition: One of the two large bony projections of the sphenoid bone; it forms much of the floor of the middle cranial fossa and the lateral wall of the orbit, and bears foramina such as the foramen rotundum, foramen ovale, and foramen spinosum through which cranial nerves and vessels pass.

lesser wing of sphenoid.definition: Thin, triangular plate of the sphenoid bone that extends forward from the body to contribute to the floor of the anterior cranial fossa and the medial wall of the orbit; it contains the optic canal (for the optic nerve and ophthalmic artery) and forms part of the boundary with the greater wing, separating the optic canal from the superior orbital fissure.

orbital fat.definition: Adipose tissue in the orbit surrounding the eyeball that cushions the globe, fills spaces between the eye and the bony orbit, and facilitates smooth movement of the extraocular muscles; it is divided into intraconal and extraconal (retrobulbar) fat.

orbital myositis.definition: An idiopathic inflammatory condition of the orbit that selectively involves one or more extraocular muscles, causing acute painful ophthalmoplegia with diplopia and orbital pain/swelling; part of the idiopathic orbital inflammatory syndrome.

orbital pseudotumor.definition: A nonneoplastic, idiopathic inflammatory condition of the orbit that mimics an orbital tumor, presenting with pain, proptosis, diplopia, and sometimes eyelid swelling; typically responsive to corticosteroid therapy.

orbitography.definition: An imaging study of the orbit (eye socket) to visualize its bony walls and soft-tissue contents, typically using radiographs, CT, or MRI to assess trauma, masses, or inflammatory conditions.

orbitomeatal line.definition: A radiographic reference line drawn from the outer corner of the eye (outer canthus) to the external auditory meatus (ear canal); used to orient skull radiographs and define the orbitomeatal plane.

orbivirus.definition: A genus of segmented double-stranded RNA viruses in the family Reoviridae, transmitted by arthropods; includes several animal pathogens such as bluetongue virus and African horse sickness virus.

african horse sickness.definition: A viral disease of horses and other equids caused by an orbivirus transmitted by Culicoides midges. It can present as febrile illness with edema of the face and neck and, in severe forms (pulmonary or cardiac), as rapid deterioration and high mortality. Endemic to sub-Saharan Africa with occasional spread to new areas via vectors; vaccines are used for prevention in endemic regions.

ora serrata.definition: The serrated junction at the anterior edge of the retina where the neural retina ends and the nonphotosensitive ciliary epithelium begins, marking the retina’s anterior boundary.

orexigenic.definition: Stimulating appetite; an orexigenic factor increases hunger and promotes food intake.

oreximania.definition: An abnormal, pathological craving for food, resulting in excessive appetite (hyperphagia) and potentially compulsive eating.

orexis.definition: A craving or appetite; the desire to eat; in medical usage, the appetite drive, with related terms such as anorexia (loss of appetite) and orexigenic (appetite-stimulating).

orfadin.definition: A medication that inhibits 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (HPPD), used to treat hereditary tyrosinemia type I by blocking the tyrosine degradation pathway and reducing toxic metabolites (fumarylacetoacetate and succinylacetone) to help prevent liver and kidney damage.

organelle.definition: A specialized subcellular structure within a cell that performs a specific function and is typically enclosed by a membrane in eukaryotic cells.

organic mental disorder.definition: A mental disorder arising from identifiable organic brain disease or dysfunction, such as dementia or delirium, resulting from structural or metabolic brain pathology rather than a primary psychiatric illness.

organic mental syndrome.definition: A cognitive or behavioral disturbance arising from an identifiable organic (physical) brain disease or systemic medical condition, rather than a primary psychiatric disorder; includes delirium, dementia, and amnestic syndromes with impaired memory, attention, or executive function.

organification.definition: The process by which inorganic iodide is covalently bound to tyrosine residues on thyroglobulin (forming MIT and DIT), a key step in thyroid hormone synthesis catalyzed by thyroid peroxidase.

organogenesis.definition: Formation and differentiation of the body's organs during embryonic development, as tissues derived from the three germ layers organize into functional organ primordia.

organogeny.definition: The development and formation of organs during embryonic growth, resulting from tissue differentiation and morphogenesis of the three germ layers (part of organogenesis).

organism.definition: A living being capable of independent life, composed of cells, and able to grow, metabolize, respond to stimuli, and reproduce.

organoid neoplasm.definition: A neoplasm with organoid architecture—a three‑dimensional, mini‑organ–like arrangement seen in certain tumors or in cancer organoid cultures used for research.

organomegaly.definition: Abnormal enlargement of one or more internal organs beyond their normal size.

organ of giraldés.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. Could you confirm the spelling or provide context (anatomical region, species, or source)? If you meant a similarly named term (e.g., Giraldi’s organ or Giraldez-related anatomy), I can define that.

paradidymis.definition: A vestigial duct-like structure located near the epididymis in the male reproductive tract, representing remnants of the Wolffian (mesonephric) duct and typically nonfunctional.

organum.definition: A Latin term meaning "an organ" or "a body part"; historically used in anatomy, but not a standard term in modern medical usage.

organ procurement.definition: The process of obtaining organs from a donor for transplantation, including donor evaluation and consent (where required), surgical retrieval, organ preservation, and transport to the recipient through an organ procurement system.

organ specificity.definition: The tendency for a substance, process, or disease to affect or localize predominantly in one particular organ or tissue, due to differences in receptor distribution, transport mechanisms, metabolic pathways, or organ-specific gene expression.

organo.definition: A combining form meaning “organ” or “organ-like,” used to form terms relating to organs (e.g., organoid, organogenesis); in chemistry, it denotes carbon-containing substituents attached to metals (as in organometallic compounds).

organophosphate.definition: A class of esters of phosphoric acid whose toxicity stems from irreversible inhibition of acetylcholinesterase, causing accumulation of acetylcholine and cholinergic symptoms; widely used as insecticides, and some are nerve agents.

organophosphate insecticide poisoning.definition: Poisoning from exposure to organophosphate pesticides that inhibit acetylcholinesterase, causing accumulation of acetylcholine at cholinergic synapses and neuromuscular junctions and resulting in a cholinergic crisis with muscarinic, nicotinic, and central nervous system symptoms.

organophosphate poisoning.definition: Exposure to organophosphate compounds, typically pesticides or nerve agents, that irreversibly inhibit acetylcholinesterase, causing accumulation of acetylcholine at muscarinic, nicotinic, and CNS receptors. This produces parasympathetic overactivity (SLUDGE: salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, GI distress, emesis), miosis, bronchorrhea/bronchospasm, bradycardia, muscle fasciculations and weakness, and seizures; treated with decontamination, atropine, pralidoxime, and supportive care.

organophosphorus.definition: Relating to organic compounds that contain phosphorus bound to carbon; a class of phosphorus-containing esters, many of which are pesticides or nerve agents and act by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase.

organophosphorus compound poisoning.definition: A potentially life-threatening poisoning from exposure to organophosphorus compounds (organophosphates) that irreversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase, leading to accumulation of acetylcholine at cholinergic synapses and neuromuscular junctions and producing a cholinergic syndrome with muscarinic, nicotinic, and CNS symptoms.

organocarbamate.definition: An organic compound containing the carbamate functional group derived from carbamic acid, typically an ester of carbamic acid with an organic substituent (R–O–CO–NR2R3).

organocarbamate insecticide poisoning.definition: Poisoning from carbamate pesticides that reversibly inhibit acetylcholinesterase, causing accumulation of acetylcholine at cholinergic synapses and resulting in muscarinic, nicotinic, and central nervous system symptoms; onset is rapid and usually shorter in duration than organophosphate poisoning; management emphasizes decontamination and atropine for cholinergic signs, with pralidoxime generally not required.

organochlorine insecticide poisoning.definition: Toxicity from exposure to organochlorine pesticides (eg, DDT, chlordane, lindane, endrin) causing CNS hyperexcitability and neurotoxic symptoms due to interference with neuronal ion channels and GABAergic transmission; acute poisoning presents with dizziness, headache, tremors, seizures, ataxia, nausea, vomiting, and respiratory distress, while chronic exposure may affect neurodevelopment and liver function. Management is supportive with decontamination and seizure control; no specific antidote exists.

organotherapeutic.definition: Relating to a historical therapy that uses preparations derived from animal or human organs or glandular tissue to treat disease; its efficacy is unproven and it is not part of current evidence-based medical practice.

organotypic growth.definition: Growth that preserves the native architecture and cell–cell interactions of a tissue or organ, yielding organ-like structure and function in vitro.

brown-sequard.definition: A neurologic condition caused by unilateral (hemicord) injury to the spinal cord, characterized by ipsilateral motor weakness and loss of proprioception and vibratory sensation below the lesion, with contralateral loss of pain and temperature sensation starting a few segments below the lesion.

nitisinone.definition: A selective inhibitor of the enzyme 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (HPPD) in the tyrosine degradation pathway, used to treat hereditary tyrosinemia type I by preventing the formation of toxic metabolites (fumarylacetoacetate and succinylacetone) and often used with dietary restriction of phenylalanine/tyrosine; has also been studied for reducing homogentisic acid in alkaptonuria.

thyroid peroxidase.definition: An enzyme located on the apical surface of thyroid follicular cells that catalyzes the iodination of tyrosine residues in thyroglobulin and the coupling of iodotyrosines to form the thyroid hormones T3 and T4.

lysosomes.definition: Membrane-bound organelles containing acid hydrolases that digest macromolecules, old organelles, and internalized material; central to intracellular digestion and autophagy, functioning at an acidic internal pH.

subdural hematoma.definition: A blood clot in the brain between the cerebral cortex and the dura.

excessive salivation.definition: Excessive saliva production or impaired swallowing of saliva, resulting in drooling.

axonopathy.definition: A disease process in which the axon is the primary site of injury, leading to distal axonal degeneration and loss of nerve fibers (a “dying-back” neuropathy); commonly due to toxic, metabolic, or hereditary factors, and typically presenting with reduced nerve-conduction amplitudes while conduction velocity is relatively preserved early on.

nerve gas.definition: A chemical agent that inhibits acetylcholinesterase, causing accumulation of acetylcholine at cholinergic synapses and neuromuscular junctions; leads to overstimulation of muscarinic and nicotinic receptors with symptoms such as salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, GI distress, emesis, bronchorrhea/bronchospasm, miosis, muscle fasciculations, and weakness, potentially progressing to respiratory failure.

intracranial disorders.definition: A broad category of conditions that affect structures within the skull—primarily the brain, its coverings, and the ventricular system—including traumatic, vascular, neoplastic, infectious, inflammatory, degenerative, and congenital disorders that disrupt cerebral function or intracranial pressure.

sinus infection.definition: Inflammation of the paranasal sinuses, usually due to infection (most commonly viral, less often bacterial or fungal), with symptoms such as nasal congestion, facial pain or pressure, purulent nasal discharge, and reduced sense of smell; can be acute or chronic and often follows a viral upper respiratory infection.

ear infection.definition: An infection and/or inflammation of the ear, most commonly otitis media (middle ear) or otitis externa (outer ear), caused by bacteria or viruses; symptoms typically include ear pain, fullness, hearing loss, and sometimes fever or drainage.

organic dust.definition: Dust containing organic matter of plant, animal, or microbial origin (for example, plant fibers, pollen, bacteria, fungi, spores, and microbial endotoxins). Inhalation can trigger allergic or inflammatory respiratory conditions such as occupational asthma and hypersensitivity pneumonitis.

organic dust toxic syndrome.definition: An acute, noninfectious inflammatory reaction of the respiratory tract after inhaling a large amount of organic dust (bioaerosols) containing microbial components from sources like grain, hay, or moldy material; it causes flu‑like symptoms (fever, malaise, myalgia, cough, chest tightness) within hours of exposure and typically resolves within 24–72 hours after removal from exposure.

odts.definition: A solid dosage form that rapidly disintegrates in the mouth, usually within seconds, releasing the drug for absorption through the oral mucosa or dissolution in saliva; designed to be taken without water and helpful for patients with swallowing difficulties.

prenatal development.definition: From fertilization to birth during pregnancy, encompassing the germinal, embryonic, and fetal periods, with cell division, differentiation, organ formation (organogenesis), and growth.

histiotypic growth.definition: A proliferation dominated by histiocytes (tissue macrophages) or histiocyte-like cells, reflecting a histiocytic lineage growth pattern seen in certain inflammatory or neoplastic lesions.

histiotypic.definition: Relating to histiocytes (tissue macrophages); resembling histiocytes in origin or morphology.

mood disorders.definition: An umbrella of psychiatric disorders defined by clinically significant disturbances in mood, including depressive episodes and episodes of mania or hypomania, that impair functioning. It encompasses depressive disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, persistent depressive disorder) and bipolar and related disorders (e.g., bipolar I/II, cyclothymic disorder).

substance-induced mood disorders.definition: A mood disorder (depression or mania/hypomania) that is directly caused by the physiological effects of a substance (e.g., alcohol, illicit drugs, or prescription medications) or by withdrawal from a substance; symptoms occur during intoxication or withdrawal, meet mood-disorder criteria, and are not better explained by a primary mood disorder once the substance is eliminated, with symptoms typically remitting after cessation.

depressive mood disturbance.definition: A persistent state of low mood, often with anhedonia (loss of interest or pleasure), reduced energy, slowed thinking or psychomotor changes, and impairment in daily functioning. It can occur as part of depressive disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, persistent depressive disorder) or as a nonspecific mood disturbance in various psychiatric or medical conditions; it is not a standalone diagnostic term.

cerebellar lesions.definition: Cerebellar lesions are focal or diffuse damage to the cerebellum (in the posterior fossa) that disrupt coordination and balance, producing ataxia. They commonly cause limb and trunk dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, intention tremor, hypotonia, rebound phenomena, and nystagmus, with gait disturbance that varies by lesion location: vermis (truncal ataxia), cerebellar hemispheres (ipsilateral limb ataxia), and flocculonodular lobe (vestibulo-cerebellar symptoms). Causes include stroke, tumor, trauma, infection, demyelination, and toxins.

crusting.definition: A dried accumulation of serum, blood, or pus on the surface of a lesion, forming a crust (scab).

contagious pustular dermatitis.definition: A contagious superficial bacterial skin infection characterized by clusters of pustules that rupture and crust; most commonly impetigo caused by Staphylococcus aureus and/or Streptococcus pyogenes, transmitted by direct contact.

orofacial.definition: Relating to the mouth and the face; pertaining to the anatomy, function, or pathology of the oral cavity and facial region, including teeth, gums, jaws, lips, tongue, palate, and associated soft tissues.

orofaciodigital syndrome.definition: A group of rare genetic disorders characterized by congenital abnormalities involving the face (orofacial region), the mouth, and the digits, with variable involvement of other organs; hallmark features often include craniofacial dysmorphism, oral anomalies (such as tongue or dental irregularities), and limb malformations (e.g., extra or fused digits). It represents a spectrum with multiple subtypes.

oropharyngeal dysphagia.definition: Difficulty initiating and transferring a food or liquid bolus from the oropharynx to the esophagus, often with coughing, choking, or nasal regurgitation due to neuromuscular or structural abnormalities of the oropharynx.

orientation.definition: Awareness of self and surroundings, including awareness of person, place, and time; used to assess cognitive function.

orientia tsutsugamushi.definition: A Gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacterium that causes scrub typhus in humans; transmitted to humans by bites of infected larval trombiculid mites (chiggers).

origin.definition: In anatomy, the fixed attachment of a muscle to a bone or other structure, usually the proximal attachment, which remains relatively stationary during contraction; the distal attachment is called the insertion.

orimune.definition: Not a standard medical term; no widely recognized medical definition.

orinase.definition: A first-generation oral sulfonylurea hypoglycemic agent used to treat type 2 diabetes by stimulating insulin release from pancreatic beta cells, through inhibition of ATP-sensitive potassium channels; may cause hypoglycemia.

tolbutamide.definition: A first-generation sulfonylurea oral hypoglycemic agent that stimulates insulin release from pancreatic beta cells by inhibiting ATP-sensitive potassium channels, used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus.

orlistat.definition: A lipase inhibitor used for obesity treatment that decreases intestinal absorption of dietary fats by inhibiting pancreatic lipase; taken with meals containing fat, with common adverse effects including oily stools, flatulence with discharge, fecal urgency, and potential fat-soluble vitamin deficiency.

ornithine transcarbamoylase.definition: A mitochondrial enzyme of the urea cycle that catalyzes the condensation of ornithine and carbamoyl phosphate to form citrulline; encoded by the OTC gene on the X chromosome. Deficiency causes X-linked ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency, a urea cycle disorder presenting with hyperammonemia.

ornithine transcarbamoylase deficiency.definition: A genetic, X-linked urea cycle disorder caused by deficiency of the mitochondrial enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of ornithine and carbamoyl phosphate to citrulline, leading to hyperammonemia; typically presents in newborn males with poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy, and seizures, while females and late-onset cases may have milder symptoms; management includes ammonia-lowering therapies, protein restriction, arginine supplementation, and dialysis in severe cases.

ornithine cycle.definition: A hepatic metabolic pathway (urea cycle) that detoxifies ammonia by converting it to urea for excretion. It uses ornithine, citrulline, argininosuccinate, and arginine through a series of enzymatic steps (CPS I, OTC, ASS, ASL, ARG1) to incorporate nitrogen into urea and regenerate ornithine.

urea cycle.definition: A series of hepatic biochemical reactions (also known as the ornithine cycle) that detoxifies ammonia by converting it to urea for excretion in urine; starts with carbamoyl phosphate formation and proceeds through citrulline, argininosuccinate, arginine, and finally urea; essential for nitrogen waste elimination; defects can cause hyperammonemia.

ornithosis.definition: A zoonotic infectious disease caused by Chlamydia psittaci transmitted to humans from infected birds, typically presenting with fever, malaise, and an atypical pneumonia; treated with doxycycline.

orolingual.definition: Relating to the mouth and the tongue.

oromaxillary.definition: Relating to the mouth and the maxilla; pertaining to the maxillary region of the upper jaw and the oral cavity.

orotic acid.definition: A pyrimidine carboxylate that serves as an intermediate in de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis; it is formed from dihydroorotate and is converted to orotidine-5'-phosphate (OMP), which is subsequently decarboxylated to uridine monophosphate (UMP).

orotic aciduria.definition: A rare inherited disorder of de novo pyrimidine synthesis caused by deficiency of the bifunctional UMPS enzyme (orotate phosphoribosyltransferase–orotidine-5′-phosphate decarboxylase), leading to elevated urinary orotic acid and megaloblastic anemia; often responsive to uridine supplementation.

ortho-novum.definition: A brand of combined oral contraceptive containing estrogen and a progestin, used to prevent pregnancy and regulate menstrual cycles.

orthopantogram.definition: A panoramic dental X-ray that provides a single image of the upper and lower jaws, including teeth and surrounding structures, used to evaluate tooth position, eruption, pathologies, and jaw relationships.

orthopedics.definition: A branch of medicine dedicated to the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of disorders of the musculoskeletal system—bones, joints, ligaments, tendons, muscles, and nerves—through non-surgical and surgical interventions.

orthopaedics.definition: Medical specialty focusing on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of disorders of the musculoskeletal system (bones, joints, muscles, ligaments, tendons, and nerves), using both nonoperative and operative methods.

orthopedic traction.definition: An orthopedic method of applying a continuous pulling force to a limb to align fractures or correct deformities, using external devices on the skin (skin traction) or pins/wires anchored in bone (skeletal traction) connected to weights to maintain gradual traction.

orthodromic conduction.definition: Propagation of a nerve impulse along a neuron in the normal, physiological direction—from the cell body down the axon to the axon terminals.

orthogenesis.definition: A historical hypothesis that evolution proceeds in a directed, linear fashion toward predetermined endpoints, driven by internal constraints or forces rather than by natural selection alone.

orthogenetic.definition: Relating to orthogenesis; the hypothesis that evolutionary change proceeds in a directed, non-random path toward a predetermined end or goal.

orthogenic.definition: Not a standard medical term; etymologically from orth- “straight, correct” plus -genic “producing.” If used, it would generally imply producing straight or directed development, but there is no established clinical definition in common medical dictionaries.

orthognathic.definition: Relating to the correction of jaw-bone alignment; typically refers to surgical realignment of the upper and lower jaws (orthognathic surgery) to treat malocclusion.

orthomolecular.definition: A form of alternative medicine that aims to prevent and treat disease by achieving optimal levels of nutrients in the body—especially vitamins and minerals—often through high-dose vitamin therapies; a concept attributed to Linus Pauling and not consistently supported by robust clinical evidence.

orthomolecular medicine.definition: An approach in alternative medicine that aims to prevent and treat disease by supplying the body with optimum levels of nutrients—especially vitamins and minerals—often at megadose amounts; its efficacy is not supported by robust evidence and it is not generally endorsed by mainstream medicine.

orthomyxovirus.definition: A negative-sense, single-stranded, segmented RNA virus of the family Orthomyxoviridae that infects the respiratory tract and includes the influenza A, B, and C viruses.

orthohepadnavirus.definition: A genus within the Hepadnaviridae family that includes mammalian hepadnaviruses, notably hepatitis B virus; small enveloped DNA viruses with a partially double-stranded genome that replicate via reverse transcription and predominantly infect liver cells (hepatocytes).

orthokinetic.definition: Relating to movement in a straight line or along a fixed direction, as opposed to rotational or curvilinear motion.

orthokinetic cuff.definition: An adjustable padded band worn around a limb used in movement-based physical therapy to provide resistance or assist motion of a joint during rehabilitation exercises.

orthokinetics.definition: A physical therapy approach that employs rapid, coordinated, guided joint movements to restore range of motion and functional mobility.

orthologous.definition: Relating to genes in different species that originated from a single ancestral gene in the last common ancestor and that typically retain the same function.

infectious diarrhea.definition: Infectious diarrhea is diarrhea caused by infection of the gastrointestinal tract by pathogens (bacteria, viruses, or parasites), usually presenting with frequent loose stools and abdominal cramps, may be accompanied by fever, nausea, and dehydration, and is transmitted via contaminated food or water or close contact.

rectal pain.definition: Discomfort or pain localized to the rectum or anal canal, which may be sharp, burning, or aching and may be associated with bleeding, discharge, or a sensation of incomplete evacuation; common causes include anorectal conditions (hemorrhoids, anal fissures), proctitis, abscess or fistula, infections, and inflammatory bowel disease.

menstrual irregularity.definition: Deviation from a normal menstrual pattern, including irregular cycle length (often shorter than 21 days or longer than 35 days), irregular or unpredictable onset, and abnormal bleeding (heavy, light, or prolonged), typically due to ovulatory dysfunction or hormonal imbalance.

fatty stool.definition: Excess fat in the stool due to fat malabsorption; stools are bulky, pale or gray, greasy, and foul-smelling and may float. Associated with pancreatic insufficiency, biliary deficiency/obstruction, celiac disease, Crohn disease, giardiasis, and other causes of fat malabsorption.

trombiculidae.definition: A family of tiny mites whose larval stage (chiggers) is parasitic on vertebrate hosts, including humans; larvae attach to skin and feed on tissue by injecting saliva that digests skin cells, causing itchy papules and dermatitis. Adults are free-living, mostly predatory mites.

faucial.definition: Relating to the fauces—the opening between the mouth and the oropharynx; the faucial arches border the fauces and contain the palatine tonsils.

countertraction.definition: An opposing force applied to the body to counterbalance a traction force, used to stabilize the limb and maintain alignment during reduction or immobilization of fractures or dislocations.

range_of_motion.definition: The extent of movement—and thus flexibility—in a joint, measured in the degrees of a circle.

plantar_flexion.definition: Ankle movement that points the toes downward toward the sole, as in standing on tiptoe; the opposite of dorsiflexion.

isometric_exercises.definition: A form of strength training in which a muscle contracts without changing length and without movement of the joint, producing a static hold for a period of time.

gluteal_muscle.definition: A muscle of the buttock region that extends, abducts, and rotates the hip, and helps stabilize the pelvis; the principal gluteal muscles are the gluteus maximus, gluteus medius, and gluteus minimus.

abdominal_contraction.definition: A tightening of the abdominal wall muscles (including the rectus abdominis, obliques, and transversus abdominis) that increases intra-abdominal pressure and shortens the abdominal contents, supporting trunk stabilization and enabling actions such as forced expiration, coughing, vomiting, defecation, and childbirth.

pressure_ulcers.definition: A localized injury to the skin and underlying tissue over a bony prominence caused by prolonged pressure, often with shear, typically occurring in immobilized or ill patients.

kidney_stones.definition: A solid piece that forms in the kidney from material in the urine. They range from tiny to large. Most pass spontaneously, but some can become stuck, blocking urine and causing severe pain.

pulmonary_embolism.definition: A sudden blockage of a pulmonary artery by a blood clot.

oral_hygiene.definition: Maintenance of oral cleanliness to prevent dental caries, gingivitis, and periodontal disease, achieved through regular tooth brushing, interdental cleaning (flossing or interdental brushes), tongue cleaning, optional antiseptic mouth rinses, and routine dental checkups.

prism_glasses.definition: Eyeglasses that incorporate prisms to bend incoming light, compensating for eye misalignment (strabismus) and reducing or eliminating double vision (diplopia) to improve binocular fusion; prisms can be ground-in or applied as Fresnel prisms and are prescribed in prism diopters to correct the misalignment.

orthopneic_position.definition: A position in which a patient sits upright and leans forward with the arms supported (often on a table or pillows) to improve breathing by allowing greater chest expansion and reducing the work of breathing.

orthostatic_hypotension.definition: An abnormal drop in blood pressure upon standing, defined as a decrease of ≥20 mmHg systolic or ≥10 mmHg diastolic within 3 minutes of standing, often accompanied by dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting, caused by impaired autonomic reflexes, volume depletion, medications, or aging.

orthostatic_intolerance.definition: A syndrome in which upright posture triggers symptoms such as lightheadedness, dizziness, fatigue, tachycardia, or syncope due to inadequate cerebral perfusion from an impaired autonomic or cardiovascular response; includes disorders like orthostatic hypotension and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome.

orthostatic_proteinuria.definition: An asymptomatic, benign condition in which proteinuria occurs when standing upright but resolves when recumbent, most commonly seen in adolescents/young adults and not indicative of intrinsic kidney disease.

orthostatic_albuminuria.definition: A benign postural proteinuria where urinary albumin excretion increases when upright and normalizes when lying down, commonly seen in adolescents with otherwise normal kidney function.

orthotics.definition: External devices worn to support, align, prevent or correct deformities, and to improve function of the musculoskeletal system (e.g., foot orthotics/insoles, ankle–foot orthoses, knee braces, back supports, and wrist splints).

orthotist.definition: A healthcare professional who designs, fabricates, and fits orthoses (medical devices such as braces, splints, and supports) used to support, align, or correct musculoskeletal deformities and improve limb or trunk function.

orthoptic.definition: Relating to the branch of ophthalmology that evaluates and treats disorders of binocular vision and ocular alignment, often using targeted eye exercises to improve coordination.

orthoptic_examination.definition: An examination that assesses how well the eyes work together, evaluating ocular alignment and motility, typically using cover tests and other binocular-vision tests to diagnose conditions like strabismus and binocular dysfunction.

orthoscopy.definition: Historically, an endoscopic procedure to visualize the inside of a joint or bone cavity; today it is largely synonymous with arthroscopy, with orthoscopy being an older, largely obsolete term.

ortolani_sign.definition: Palpable or audible clunk felt when a flexed, abducted infant hip relocates from a dislocated position into the acetabulum, indicating developmental dysplasia of the hip.

ortolani_test.definition: A clinical maneuver used in infants to detect developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH); with the infant supine and hips flexed, the hip is gently abducted while applying anterior pressure to the femoral head, and a palpable clunk as the femoral head relocates into the acetabulum indicates a positive Ortolani sign.

orudis.definition: A brand-name nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) containing fenoprofen; used to relieve mild-to-moderate pain and to reduce fever and inflammation by inhibiting cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2).

osgood_osteotomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which the tibial tubercle is cut and repositioned to change the pull of the patellar tendon, realigning the extensor mechanism and improving patellofemoral tracking or stability.

osgood_schlatter_disease.definition: An adolescent-onset traction apophysitis at the tibial tubercle, caused by repetitive strain from the patellar tendon; presents with anterior knee pain and focal tenderness below the knee, worsened by activity, and typically resolves with rest, NSAIDs, and physical therapy.

schlatter_osgood_disease.definition: A traction apophysitis of the tibial tubercle from repetitive quadriceps pull on the tibial tubercle in growing adolescents, causing anterior knee pain and tenderness just below the patella; managed with rest, NSAIDs, activity modification, and physical therapy, with spontaneous resolution as the skeleton matures.

osler_disease.definition: A genetic vascular disorder (autosomal dominant) characterized by mucocutaneous telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations in multiple organs, especially the lungs, liver, and brain; commonly presents with recurrent epistaxis and GI bleeding.

osler_weber_rendu_syndrome.definition: An autosomal dominant vascular disorder characterized by mucocutaneous telangiectasias and visceral arteriovenous malformations, most often in the lungs, liver, and brain, leading to recurrent epistaxis and bleeding.

osler_nodes.definition: Painful, localized, subcutaneous nodules on the finger and toe pads associated with infective endocarditis; believed to be immune complex–mediated vasculitis; typically resolve with effective antibiotic therapy.

tibial_tubercle.definition: A prominent bony projection on the anterior aspect of the proximal tibia where the patellar ligament attaches; an apophysis of the tibia.

cuboid_bone.definition: One of the seven tarsal bones of the foot; a cube-shaped bone on the lateral aspect between the calcaneus posteriorly and the fourth and fifth metatarsals anteriorly. It articulates with the calcaneus, navicular, lateral cuneiform, and the fourth and fifth metatarsals, contributing to weight transfer and the stability of the lateral longitudinal arch.

capitate_bone.definition: Os capitatum; the largest carpal bone of the wrist, located at the center of the carpus, articulating proximally with the scaphoid and lunate and distally with the bases of the 2nd–4th metacarpals.

lunate_bone.definition: A crescent-shaped carpal bone of the wrist, in the proximal row between the scaphoid (lateral) and triquetrum (medial); articulates proximally with the radius and distally with the capitate and hamate, forming part of the radiocarpal joint.

hamate_bone.definition: A carpal bone of the wrist, wedge-shaped and located on the ulnar side of the distal carpal row, with a prominent hook-like projection (hook of hamate) on its palmar surface; it articulates proximally with the capitate and distally with the 4th and 5th metacarpals, and its hook helps form part of the boundary of Guyon's canal where the ulnar nerve and artery pass.

os_coxae.definition: One of the paired bones of the pelvis (hip bone), formed by the fusion of the ilium, ischium, and pubis; part of the pelvic girdle, it articulates superiorly with the sacrum at the sacroiliac joint and with the femur at the acetabulum.

hyoid_bone.definition: A U‑shaped bone in the neck that does not articulate with any other bone; suspended by ligaments and muscles, it serves as an attachment for tongue and neck muscles and supports the larynx during swallowing.

subacute_bacterial_endocarditis.definition: An infective endocarditis with a gradual onset caused by relatively low-virulence organisms (classically viridans group streptococci), usually affecting previously damaged valves; presents with fever, malaise, weight loss, and a new or changing heart murmur, and is treated with prolonged intravenous antibiotics.

pulmonary_edema.definition: A condition caused by excess fluid accumulating in the lungs, making breathing difficult.

osmia.definition: The sense of smell; the olfactory perception of odors via the nasal mucosa and olfactory pathways.

dysosmia.definition: A qualitative olfactory disorder in which odors are distorted or perceived differently from their true scent.

hemianosmia.definition: Unilateral loss of the sense of smell (anosmia on one side).

merosmia.definition: A partial loss or impairment of the sense of smell, resulting in reduced ability to detect or identify odors (a milder form of olfactory dysfunction compared with complete anosmia).

congenital_dislocation_of_the_hip.definition: An abnormal development of the hip joint in newborns/infants in which the femoral head is not securely seated in the acetabulum, ranging from a shallow socket with instability to complete dislocation.

kashin-beck disease.definition: An endemic osteoarthropathy affecting children, characterized by degeneration and necrosis of articular and epiphyseal cartilage (especially in weight-bearing joints), leading to joint deformities and restricted movement; multifactorial etiology with suspected roles for selenium deficiency and dietary mycotoxin exposure.

osteoarthritis deformans.definition: A degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage loss with subchondral sclerosis, osteophyte formation, and secondary bone remodeling, resulting in joint deformity and impaired function; commonly affects the hips, knees, hands, and spine; historically used as a name for osteoarthritis.

osteoarthritis endemica.definition: Degenerative joint disease characterized by loss of articular cartilage with subchondral bone changes and osteophyte formation, leading to chronic joint pain, stiffness, and functional limitation; commonly affects the knees, hips, hands, and spine; risk factors include aging, obesity, and prior joint injury; management focuses on symptom relief and function, including weight management, exercise, physical therapy, NSAIDs or analgesics, intra-articular injections, and, in advanced cases, joint replacement.

osteitis deformans.definition: Chronic bone remodeling disorder with accelerated osteoclast-mediated resorption followed by excessive osteoblastic bone formation, producing enlarged, disorganized, and deformed bones (often with a mosaic bone pattern); commonly affects the pelvis, skull, spine, and long bones, and may cause bone pain, deformities, fractures, and hearing loss; often with elevated alkaline phosphatase and normal calcium/phosphate.

osteooarthropathy.definition: A general term for diseases of bone and joints; in some contexts used to denote hypertrophic osteoarthropathy, a syndrome featuring periostitis of long bones, joint pain and swelling, and digital clubbing, usually linked to cardiopulmonary disease or malignancy.

osteoarthrosis.definition: A degenerative, noninflammatory disorder of a synovial joint characterized by progressive articular cartilage deterioration, subchondral bone changes, osteophyte formation, and joint space narrowing, leading to pain and reduced function (commonly referred to as osteoarthritis).

osteoarticular brucellosis.definition: A focal form of brucellosis involving bones and joints, typically presenting as sacroiliitis, spondylitis, or inflammatory arthritis; caused by Brucella species and transmitted via unpasteurized dairy products or contact with infected animals; treated with prolonged combination antibiotic therapy (commonly doxycycline plus rifampin) and sometimes initial parenteral therapy.

osseous labyrinth.definition: A rigid bony outer wall of the inner ear in the temporal bone that encases the membranous labyrinth and contains perilymph; it includes the cochlea, vestibule, and three semicircular canals.

ossicle.definition: A small bone; in the middle ear, one of the three auditory bones (malleus, incus, or stapes) that transmit sound vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear.

perichondrium.definition: A dense connective tissue covering that surrounds most cartilage, supplying nutrients to avascular cartilage and containing progenitor cells for cartilage growth and repair; it consists of an outer fibrous layer and an inner chondrogenic layer.

marrow cavity.definition: The central cavity within the diaphysis of a bone that houses bone marrow; lined by endosteum and containing red marrow in children and yellow (fatty) marrow in adults.

nutrient artery.definition: A nutrient artery is a vessel that enters a bone through a nutrient foramen to provide the major endosteal blood supply to the medullary cavity and the inner cortex; it is typically accompanied by a nutrient vein.

osmoreceptor.definition: Specialized hypothalamic neurons that detect changes in extracellular fluid osmolality; they regulate water intake (thirst) and vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone) secretion to maintain body fluid osmolarity.

capsaicin.definition: A chemical found in hot chili peppers that is used in some pain-relief creams.

glucosamine.definition: An amino sugar that is a natural component of glycosaminoglycans in connective tissue; used as an over-the-counter dietary supplement for osteoarthritis, most often in the forms of glucosamine sulfate or glucosamine hydrochloride; evidence for benefit is mixed.

chondroitin sulfate.definition: A sulfated glycosaminoglycan that is a major component of cartilage proteoglycans; commonly used as a dietary supplement for osteoarthritis. Evidence for efficacy is mixed.

muscle relaxants.definition: A class of medications that reduce skeletal muscle tone and spasm to relieve pain and stiffness. They act centrally by depressing reflexes in the brain or spinal cord or peripherally by affecting calcium handling in muscle fibers; used for acute musculoskeletal strains and for spasticity from neurologic disorders. Common examples include cyclobenzaprine, methocarbamol, baclofen, tizanidine, and dantrolene. Side effects often include drowsiness, dizziness, and weakness.

intraarticular corticosteroid injections.definition: A procedure in which a corticosteroid preparation is injected directly into a joint space to reduce inflammation and relieve pain, often with a local anesthetic; used to treat arthritis and inflammatory joint conditions. Effects typically last weeks to months; risks include infection (rare), transient pain flare, hyperglycemia in diabetics, and potential cartilage or tissue effects with repeated injections.

joint debridement.definition: Removal of damaged or inflammatory tissue, debris, and loose cartilage from within a joint to relieve pain and improve range of motion, usually performed arthroscopically.

decompression laminectomy.definition: A surgical procedure that removes part of the vertebral bone (the lamina) to enlarge the spinal canal and relieve pressure on the spinal cord or nerve roots; commonly performed for spinal stenosis or nerve compression, and may be combined with fusion if spinal stability is a concern.

total joint replacement.definition: A surgical procedure in which a damaged joint is replaced with an artificial prosthesis made of metal, plastic, or ceramic components to relieve pain and restore joint function.

osseointegrated implant.definition: A load-bearing implant that forms a direct structural and functional connection with living bone, achieved through osseointegration, providing stable anchorage without intervening fibrous tissue.

osmone-clarke procedure.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. Could you confirm the spelling or provide the context (surgical specialty) to help locate the term?

peroneus brevis tendon transfer.definition: An orthopedic foot/ankle procedure in which the peroneus brevis tendon is detached from its normal insertion and redirected or reattached to a different site to restore eversion strength or stabilize the hindfoot/ankle, often to correct deformity such as cavovarus or flatfoot.

heberden nodules.definition: Hard bony enlargements of the distal interphalangeal joints due to osteoarthritis, usually painless and common in older adults.

bouchard nodules.definition: A bony enlargements of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints caused by osteoarthritis, representing osteophyte formation and degenerative changes in the finger joints.

osteophyte.definition: An outgrowth of bone on a joint or spinal disk; commonly called a bone spur.

osmotic diuresis.definition: Increased urine output caused by osmotically active substances in the renal tubules that cannot be reabsorbed, drawing water into the urine (e.g., glucose in uncontrolled diabetes or the administration of osmotic agents like mannitol).

pseudocysts.definition: A fluid collection of pancreatic secretions enclosed by a non-epithelialized fibrous wall that develops after pancreatitis or pancreatic injury; it lacks an epithelial lining (unlike a true cyst) and may resolve spontaneously or require drainage depending on size and symptoms.

osteoclastoma.definition: A benign, locally aggressive bone tumor (giant cell tumor) composed of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear stromal cells; typically arises in the epiphysis of long bones in young to middle-aged adults; treated with curettage or resection; may recur and rarely metastasize.

mesenchyme.definition: An embryonic connective tissue comprising loosely arranged multipotent mesenchymal cells in a gelatinous extracellular matrix, from which all connective tissues arise and differentiate.

skeleton.definition: The rigid framework of the body composed of bones and cartilage that supports and protects tissues and organs, provides a surface for muscle attachment and movement at joints, stores minerals (calcium and phosphate), and houses bone marrow for blood cell production.

osteoid.definition: The unmineralized organic matrix of bone produced by osteoblasts, consisting mainly of type I collagen and noncollagenous proteins, that later mineralizes to form mature bone.

osteoblastoma.definition: A rare benign bone tumor consisting of proliferating osteoblasts producing osteoid and immature bone; typically larger than 2 cm, most often arising in the spine or long bones of children, adolescents, and young adults, and presenting with localized, persistent pain.

osteoid osteoma.definition: A benign bone tumor characterized by a small radiolucent nidus (<2 cm) of osteoid-producing osteoblasts with surrounding reactive sclerosis; it typically causes focal, nocturnal bone pain that is relieved by NSAIDs.

osteocachexia.definition: A nonstandard term used to describe cachexia (unintentional weight loss and muscle wasting) in the setting of bone disease or osteoporosis; it is not a widely accepted medical diagnosis.

osteocalcin.definition: A vitamin K–dependent, non-collagenous protein produced by osteoblasts that binds calcium in the bone matrix and supports bone mineralization; also studied as a circulating biomarker of bone formation.

osteocarcinoma.definition: An uncommon, nonstandard term not recognized as a distinct diagnosis; bone cancers are typically sarcomas (e.g., osteosarcoma), while carcinomas arise from epithelial tissue and rarely originate in bone.

osteochondral graft.definition: A surgical procedure in which a piece of cartilage with underlying bone is transplanted to a focal articular cartilage defect to restore the joint surface and subchondral bone; the graft may be autograft (taken from the patient) or allograft (donor).

osteochondritis.definition: Inflammation of bone and its adjacent cartilage, typically related to a joint lesion of subchondral bone with potential cartilage damage and joint pain.

osteochondritis deformans juvenilis.definition: A juvenile form of osteochondritis dissecans; a focal disturbance of endochondral ossification in the subchondral bone of a joint (most often the knee) in children and adolescents, causing cartilage/bone defects that can loosen and produce pain, swelling, and mechanical symptoms; management depends on lesion stability and skeletal maturity.

osteochondritis dissecans.definition: A focal lesion of the subchondral bone with possible overlying cartilage disruption that may loosen and detach, forming a loose body within a joint; it most often involves the knee, but can affect the elbow or ankle, and presents with activity-related joint pain, swelling, and sometimes mechanical symptoms such as locking or catching.

osteochondritis ischiopubica.definition: A rare osteochondral injury of the ischiopubic region (junction of the ischium and pubis), typically in skeletally immature athletes, caused by repetitive traction; presents with groin or pelvic pain and may show fragmentation on imaging, managed with rest and physical therapy with generally good prognosis.

osteochondritis juvenilis.definition: A focal lesion of cartilage and underlying bone at a joint, typically in children or adolescents, caused by disrupted blood supply and/or repetitive microtrauma; it can progress to fragmentation or loosening of the bone-cartilage piece, leading to pain, swelling, reduced range of motion, and potential joint instability.

osteochondritis necroticans.definition: Ischemic necrosis of subchondral bone with potential detachment of overlying cartilage in a joint, often affecting children and adolescents; may cause focal joint pain, swelling, and mechanical symptoms from loose fragments, with treatment ranging from rest and immobilization to surgical fixation or removal of loose bodies for unstable lesions.

osteochondrodystrophy.definition: A disorder of bone and cartilage development, encompassing a group of skeletal dysplasias characterized by abnormal growth and formation of bone and cartilage (often due to defects in endochondral ossification).

osteochondromatosis.definition: Multiple benign, cartilage-capped bone outgrowths from the metaphyses of long bones, usually inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern (hereditary multiple exostoses), which can cause limb deformities or discrepancies and carries a small risk of malignant transformation to chondrosarcoma.

osteochondropathy.definition: A broad term for diseases affecting bone and its overlying cartilage; disorders in which both osseous tissue and articular cartilage are involved, often involving the growth plates in children.

osteochondrosarcoma.definition: A malignant bone tumor with prominent cartilaginous (chondroid) differentiation and malignant osteogenic (osteoid) production; essentially a chondroblastic variant of osteosarcoma.

osteochondrosis.definition: A group of disorders in childhood in which disturbed blood supply to developing bone (epiphysis or apophysis) disrupts endochondral ossification, causing focal necrosis and potential deformity or early degenerative joint changes.

osgood-schlatter disease.definition: A traction-related overuse injury of the tibial tubercle in skeletally immature individuals, caused by repetitive pulling of the patellar tendon and quadriceps on the tibial tubercle; presents with anterior knee pain and focal tenderness just below the knee, often with swelling, aggravated by running or jumping, and typically resolves with skeletal maturity through rest, activity modification, and physical therapy.

osteoclasis.definition: A surgical procedure that intentionally fractures a bone to correct a deformity or realign a limb, typically followed by immobilization to allow healing.

osteoclast activating factor.definition: A cytokine produced by immune cells that stimulates osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption, contributing to bone loss in inflammation and certain cancers; historically described as the factor that activates osteoclasts.

osteoclasty.definition: A surgical procedure in which a bone is intentionally fractured to correct a deformity or malalignment, with subsequent realignment and immobilization; also known as osteoclasis.

osteoma cutis.definition: Formation of mature bone tissue within the skin (dermis or subcutaneous tissue), producing hard nodules; can be primary (idiopathic) or secondary to trauma, inflammation, or other skin conditions.

adult rickets.definition: An adult metabolic bone disease characterized by defective mineralization of bone matrix, causing soft, weakened bones with bone pain, muscle weakness, and an increased risk of fractures; most commonly due to vitamin D deficiency or disturbances in calcium or phosphate metabolism.

osteomas.definition: Benign bone tumors composed of mature bone tissue (compact or cancellous), most often arising in the skull or facial bones. They are typically slow-growing and asymptomatic, often found incidentally on imaging; management ranges from observation to surgical excision if symptomatic or cosmetically concerning. Multiple lesions can be associated with Gardner syndrome (familial adenomatous polyposis).

osteomata.definition: The plural form of osteoma: benign bone tumors composed of mature bone tissue; typically slow-growing and well-circumscribed lesions, most often arising in craniofacial bones and usually asymptomatic, though they may cause cosmetic deformity or functional issues; treatment is usually observation unless symptomatic, then surgical excision.

osteosclerosis fragilis.definition: Not a standard medical term. If used, it would suggest increased bone density (osteosclerosis) accompanied by bone fragility; however, there is no widely accepted definition. Dense-but-brittle bone is characteristic of osteopetrosis (marble bone disease), where bones are overly dense yet prone to fracture.

ivory bones.definition: A nonstandard term referring to unusually dense bones on imaging; often used to describe the ivory vertebra sign (uniformly dense vertebral bodies) seen with osteoblastic metastases, lymphoma, or Paget disease; not a specific diagnosis.

marble bones.definition: A rare inherited disorder in which osteoclast dysfunction leads to defective bone resorption, resulting in abnormally dense, brittle bones and reduced bone marrow space, with possible complications such as anemia, infection, hepatosplenomegaly, and cranial nerve compression.

osteopetrotic.definition: Relating to osteopetrosis; a congenital bone disorder in which osteoclast-mediated bone resorption is defective, producing abnormally dense but brittle bones and potentially leading to bone marrow failure with anemia and cranial nerve compression.

osteoplast.definition: A surgical procedure to reshape or reconstruct bone to correct deformity or restore function.

osteoplastica.definition: A surgical procedure to reshape or contour bone by removing or smoothing bone tissue, typically to correct deformities or to prepare bone surfaces for implants or prostheses.

osteoplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to reshape or repair bone, contouring its shape to correct deformities or improve function; may involve removing bone, reshaping existing bone, or grafting bone.

chronic osteomyelitis.definition: A long-standing infection of bone and bone marrow that persists or recurs beyond the acute phase (typically >6 weeks), often with necrotic bone (sequestrum) and new bone formation (involucrum), possible sinus tract drainage, and partial or poor response to antibiotics; usually due to hematogenous spread or contiguous infection and often requiring prolonged antibiotic therapy with surgical debridement.

osteomyelodysplasia.definition: Not a standard medical term; conceptually, it would denote abnormal development of bone and bone marrow (combined skeletal and hematopoietic dysplasia) but it is not recognized as a distinct condition in current medical literature.

osteomesopyknosis.definition: A rare/obsolete term describing increased bone density (osteosclerosis) with condensed, thickened bone tissue.

osteopenia.definition: When your bones lose strength, but not as much as when you have osteoporosis.

osteodensitometer.definition: A device used to measure bone mineral density, typically employing radiographic or ultrasound methods to assess bone strength and osteoporosis risk.

osteodentin.definition: A form of reparative dentin produced after tooth injury by odontoblast-like cells, characterized by bone-like mineralized tissue with few or irregular dentinal tubules.

osteodermia.definition: A rare dermatologic condition in which bone tissue forms within the skin or subcutaneous tissues (cutaneous ossification), which can be congenital or acquired.

osteodiastasis.definition: A pathological widening or separation at the diastasis between adjacent bones or bone fragments; essentially, abnormal bone-segment separation often due to trauma or developmental abnormalities.

osteodynia.definition: Bone pain; pain originating in bone tissue, which can result from fracture, infection, inflammation, tumors, or metabolic bone disorders.

osteogenetic.definition: Pertaining to the formation of bone; bone-forming; osteogenic.

osteogenic myeloma.definition: Not a standard medical term; if encountered, it is typically a misnomer for osteosarcoma (osteogenic sarcoma), a malignant bone tumor characterized by production of osteoid by osteoblastic tumor cells.

osteopathic.definition: Relating to osteopathy, a branch of medicine that emphasizes the musculoskeletal system and holistic health, using manual techniques such as osteopathic manipulative treatment in addition to conventional medical care.

osteopathy.definition: Osteopathy (also osteopathic medicine) is a branch of medical practice that emphasizes the musculoskeletal system's role in health and disease, using manual manipulation (osteopathic manipulative treatment) along with conventional medical care to diagnose, treat, and prevent illness; in the United States, DOs are fully licensed physicians.

osteopathist.definition: A practitioner who practices osteopathy, a system of medicine emphasizing the musculoskeletal system and its relation to health, typically using manual manipulation to diagnose, treat, and prevent illness; in some regions, an osteopath is a licensed physician (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine, DO) who may also provide conventional medical care.

osteopathology.definition: The study of diseases affecting bone tissue and the skeletal system, including abnormalities in bone formation, structure, metabolism, and remodeling.

onycho-osteodysplasia.definition: A rare congenital condition in which nails (onycho-) and bones (osteodysplasia) are abnormally developed, causing nail abnormalities and skeletal dysplasia.

fragilitas ossium.definition: A historical Latin term meaning “fragility of bones,” referring to a condition with increased bone fragility and fracture risk, as seen in osteoporosis and related disorders (e.g., osteogenesis imperfecta).

blue sclerae.definition: A bluish discoloration of the sclera caused by thinning of the scleral collagen, which permits visualization of the underlying choroidal vessels; commonly associated with osteogenesis imperfecta and other connective tissue disorders.

translucent skin.definition: Skin that is thin enough to be semi-transparent, allowing light to pass through and revealing underlying vessels or tissues.

hyperextensibility.definition: The ability of a joint to extend beyond its normal physiological range of motion, typically caused by ligamentous laxity or connective tissue hypermobility; may be a feature of hypermobility syndromes.

dissecans.definition: A condition in which a piece of subchondral bone with its overlying cartilage becomes detached from the articular surface and may loosen within a joint, typically from disrupted blood supply.

endosteoma.definition: A rare benign intraosseous tumor arising from the endosteum (the inner surface of bone) and growing within the bone, typically presenting as a small, well-defined endosteal/intraosseous lesion and often asymptomatic; management ranges from observation to surgical curettage if symptomatic.
