pamine.definition: Not a standard medical term; likely a misspelling or brand name rather than a specific medical substance. If you meant another term (e.g., dopamine or amine), please provide context.

p-aminohippurate.definition: A synthetic organic acid used in renal physiology as a marker to estimate renal plasma flow; it is freely filtered by the glomerulus and actively secreted by proximal tubules, so its clearance approximates effective renal plasma flow when plasma concentrations are low.

pampiniform plexus.definition: A plexus of veins in the spermatic cord surrounding the testicular artery; it acts as a countercurrent heat exchanger to cool arterial blood entering the testes and drains venous blood from the testis into the testicular vein.

panafil.definition: Not a widely recognized medical term; likely a brand name or misspelling without a standard medical definition. If you can provide context (drug class, condition, country) I can help look for alternatives or clarify.

pananencephaly.definition: A congenital absence of the entire brain (complete brain agenesis), a severe neural tube defect often incompatible with life.

panangiitis.definition: Widespread vasculitis—inflammation of blood vessels affecting multiple vascular beds throughout the body, potentially involving arteries, veins, and capillaries and causing multi-organ symptoms.

panarteritis.definition: Inflammation involving all layers of an arterial wall (transmural arteritis), a pattern seen in certain systemic vasculitides such as polyarteritis nodosa.

panarthritis.definition: A nonstandard term for inflammation of multiple joints (polyarthritis); characterized by pain, swelling, and stiffness in many joints, and not by itself a specific diagnosis.

panatrophy.definition: Diffuse, generalized wasting of multiple tissue types in a region or the body, resulting in thinning and loss of volume of muscles and surrounding soft tissues.

panbronchiolitis.definition: A chronic inflammatory disease of the small airways (bronchioles) of the lungs, characterized by diffuse bronchiolitis with centrilobular nodules and tree-in-bud opacities often with bronchiectasis; predominantly described in East Asian adults and frequently associated with chronic Pseudomonas infection, with notable improvement on long-term low-dose macrolide therapy.

pancake kidney.definition: A rare congenital renal fusion anomaly in which the two kidneys fuse to form a single, pancake-shaped mass (disk kidney), usually located in the pelvis.

duct of wirsung.definition: A main pancreatic duct that traverses the pancreas, collecting exocrine secretions and delivering them into the duodenum through the major duodenal papilla (ampulla of Vater); it is the primary drainage duct of the pancreas and often joins the common bile duct before entering the duodenum.

hepato-pancreatic ampulla.definition: A dilated junction where the common bile duct and main pancreatic duct unite to drain bile and pancreatic juice into the second part of the duodenum at the major duodenal papilla, regulated by the sphincter of Oddi.

steapsin.definition: A preparation containing pancreatic lipase that aids the hydrolysis of dietary triglycerides; used as a digestive enzyme supplement to treat fat malabsorption or pancreatic insufficiency.

pancreatic enzyme therapy.definition: A treatment that provides oral pancreatic enzymes (pancrelipase) to replace insufficient endogenous enzymes in exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, improving digestion of fats, proteins, and carbohydrates and reducing steatorrhea.

pancreatic polypeptide.definition: A peptide hormone produced by PP (F) cells of the pancreatic islets; released in response to meals, especially protein-rich ones; it inhibits exocrine pancreatic secretion, slows gastric emptying and GI motility, and modulates gallbladder contraction and hepatic glucose metabolism.

pancreatic insufficiency.definition: A condition in which the pancreas fails to secrete sufficient exocrine digestive enzymes (lipase, amylase, and proteases) into the small intestine, leading to impaired digestion and malabsorption—especially of fats. Symptoms often include steatorrhea, weight loss, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies; etiologies include chronic pancreatitis, pancreatic duct obstruction, cystic fibrosis, and pancreatic resection. Treated with pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy.

pancreatic lithiasis.definition: Calcified stones within the pancreas or its ducts, most often occurring with chronic pancreatitis; these stones can obstruct the pancreatic duct, causing abdominal pain and potentially leading to pancreatic exocrine insufficiency.

pancreatolithiasis.definition: The presence or formation of calculi (pancreatic stones) within the pancreas, especially in the pancreatic ducts, typically associated with chronic pancreatitis and that can cause ductal obstruction and abdominal pain.

pancreatin.definition: A pharmaceutical preparation containing a mixture of pancreatic enzymes (lipase, amylase, and protease) derived from animal pancreas (commonly porcine) used as oral enzyme replacement therapy to aid digestion in exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.

gastrin-producing islet cell tumors.definition: A gastrin-secreting neuroendocrine tumor arising in the pancreas or duodenum that causes marked hypergastrinemia and gastric acid hypersecretion, leading to Zollinger-Ellison syndrome with refractory peptic ulcers (and often diarrhea); may be associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1.

ectopic pancreatic tissue.definition: Pancreatic tissue located outside the pancreas that lacks anatomic or vascular/ductal continuity with the main gland; a congenital heterotopia often found in the stomach, duodenum, or jejunum, typically asymptomatic but can cause abdominal pain, bleeding, obstruction, or pancreatitis.

pancreatic rest.definition: A period during which pancreatic secretions and stimulation are minimized to allow the pancreas to rest and heal, typically achieved by withholding oral intake (NPO) or following a very low-fat diet; used in the management of pancreatitis and related pancreatic conditions.

pancreatic abscess.definition: A localized collection of pus within the pancreas or surrounding tissues that develops as a complication of pancreatitis (often from infected pancreatic necrosis); it typically requires antibiotic therapy and drainage (percutaneous or surgical).

pancreatic autodigestion.definition: Self-digestion of pancreatic tissue caused by premature activation of digestive enzymes within the pancreas, leading to pancreatic inflammation and tissue injury (as occur in acute pancreatitis).

transhepatic cholangiography.definition: A percutaneous diagnostic procedure in which contrast is injected into the intrahepatic bile ducts through a needle passed through the liver to visualize the biliary tree on radiographs, used to evaluate biliary obstruction, stones, strictures, leaks, or anatomy and to guide drainage.

hepatic arteriography.definition: A radiologic procedure in which contrast material is injected into the hepatic artery (via catheter) to visualize the liver’s arterial blood supply, identify vascular abnormalities and hypervascular lesions, and guide interventional treatments such as tumor embolization.

celiac arteriography.definition: A radiologic procedure in which contrast material is injected into the arterial system to visualize the celiac trunk and its branches by angiography, used to evaluate vascular abnormalities such as stenosis, occlusion, aneurysm, or tumor vascularity.

celiac group of preaortic nodes.definition: Lymph nodes located anterior to the abdominal aorta around the origin of the celiac trunk; part of the preaortic (pre-aortic) lymph node group that drains foregut organs (stomach, liver, pancreas, spleen, proximal duodenum, gallbladder) and channels lymph toward the cisterna chyli and thoracic duct.

pancreaticoduodenectomy.definition: A major abdominal operation that removes the head of the pancreas, the duodenum, part of the stomach, gallbladder, and common bile duct (often with surrounding tissue and lymph nodes), followed by reconstruction of the digestive tract (pancreaticojejunostomy, hepaticojejunostomy, and gastrojejunostomy). Also known as the Whipple procedure.

pancreaticoduodenostomy.definition: A surgical reconstruction that connects the pancreas to the duodenum to drain pancreatic secretions into the small intestine, typically performed after procedures that involve resection of the pancreatic head or duodenum.

pancreatoduodenostomy.definition: A surgical connection between the pancreas and the duodenum, enabling drainage of pancreatic exocrine secretions into the duodenum.

whipple procedure.definition: A complex pancreaticoduodenectomy in which the head of the pancreas, duodenum, gallbladder, bile duct, and sometimes part of the stomach are removed, with reconstruction of the biliary and digestive tracts; most often performed for pancreatic or periampullary cancers.

pancreatectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove all or part of the pancreas; can be partial (distal/subtotal) or total, and is performed for pancreatic cancer, chronic pancreatitis, or other pancreatic disorders; may result in insulin-dependent diabetes and malabsorption due to exocrine insufficiency.

pancreaticolithiasis.definition: The formation and presence of calcified stones within the pancreas, typically in the pancreatic ducts, most often associated with chronic pancreatitis, which can obstruct pancreatic juice flow and cause pain or pancreatitis.

pancreatogastrostomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which the pancreatic remnant is anastomosed to the stomach to drain pancreatic secretions into the gastric lumen, typically after pancreatic resection as an alternative to pancreatojejunostomy.

panitumumab.definition: A fully human monoclonal antibody that targets the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). By binding EGFR, it inhibits EGFR signaling and tumor cell proliferation, and is used to treat metastatic colorectal cancer expressing EGFR (typically with wild-type KRAS), administered intravenously.

pancreatogenic.definition: Relating to or arising from the pancreas; caused by pancreatic disease or dysfunction.

pancreatography.definition: A radiologic examination of the pancreas and its ducts, typically by injecting contrast to visualize pancreatic ducts and assess for stones, strictures, cysts, or tumors.

pancreatojejunostomy.definition: A surgical anastomosis between the pancreas (or its duct) and the jejunum to drain pancreatic secretions into the small intestine, typically performed to reconstruct pancreatic drainage after resection or to treat a dilated pancreatic duct in chronic pancreatitis.

pancreatolith.definition: A calcified stone in the pancreas or main pancreatic duct, commonly arising in chronic pancreatitis and capable of causing ductal obstruction and abdominal pain.

pancreatolithotomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove stones (calculi) from the pancreas or pancreatic duct, typically to relieve ductal obstruction and pain in chronic pancreatitis.

pancreatolysis.definition: Destruction or dissolution of pancreatic tissue, typically due to enzymatic autodigestion in pancreatitis.

pancreatomegaly.definition: Abnormal enlargement of the pancreas, typically identified on imaging; may result from inflammatory processes (e.g., pancreatitis), pancreatic neoplasms, cystic diseases, or diffuse pancreatic hypertrophy, and can be associated with abdominal pain or digestive symptoms.

pancreatopathy.definition: A disease or pathological condition of the pancreas; a non-specific term used to denote any disorder of pancreatic tissue or its exocrine/endocrine function.

pancreatotomy.definition: A surgical incision into the pancreas, typically to access or drain pancreatic tissue or ducts.

pancreatropic.definition: Having an influence on the pancreas; describing substances or stimuli that stimulate or regulate pancreatic tissue or function.

pancuronium bromide.definition: A long-acting, aminosteroid nondepolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent used to induce skeletal muscle paralysis during general anesthesia; it competitively inhibits acetylcholine at nicotinic receptors at the neuromuscular junction, with effects lasting about 60–90 minutes and reversible with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.

pancytopenic.definition: Relating to pancytopenia; describing a state in which all three blood cell lines (red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets) are decreased in the peripheral blood, typically due to bone marrow failure or suppression.

pancytopenia-dysmelia.definition: A congenital syndrome characterized by simultaneous pancytopenia (reduction of red cells, white cells, and platelets) and dysmelia (limb malformations), most classically described in Fanconi anemia and related inherited bone marrow failure disorders.

pandemia.definition: An outbreak of an infectious disease that occurs over a wide geographic area and affects a large proportion of the population, typically caused by a new pathogen with little preexisting immunity and sustained human-to-human transmission.

pandemic.definition: A large outbreak that moves across a large area, such as many countries or continents.

panencephalitis.definition: Inflammation of the entire brain parenchyma (diffuse encephalitis), involving both gray and white matter.

panendoscope.definition: An endoscope capable of examining the entire upper aerodigestive tract—typically nasal/pharyngeal to esophageal and gastric regions—usually performed under anesthesia to evaluate head/neck or upper GI pathology.

panesthesia.definition: An obsolete or rarely used term for the complete loss of sensation across all sensory modalities (touch, pain, temperature, proprioception) in a region or the entire body; essentially global anesthesia.

pang.definition: A sudden, brief, sharp pain or a momentary feeling of distress.

pangenesis.definition: A historical theory of heredity proposed by Charles Darwin in which tiny particles called gemmules shed by cells throughout the body travel to the reproductive organs and are passed to offspring, thereby transmitting traits.

panhidrosis.definition: Generalized sweating across the entire body (diaphoresis), which can be physiological (fever, heat, exercise) or due to pathology such as autonomic dysfunction, infections, endocrine disorders, or drug effects.

panhysterectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which the uterus and cervix are removed, usually along with both ovaries and fallopian tubes (i.e., total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy).

panic attack.definition: A sudden, intense surge of fear or discomfort that peaks within minutes and is accompanied by at least four physical or cognitive symptoms (e.g., heart palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness, numbness/tingling, depersonalization or derealization, fear of losing control or dying). It is not caused by a medical condition and may be cued or occur unexpectedly; recurrent attacks or persistent concern about additional attacks may indicate panic disorder.

panivorous.definition: Not a recognized medical term; describes an organism that feeds on all kinds of food, i.e., omnivorous.

panlobular.definition: Relating to or involving the entire lobule of an organ; affecting all components within a lobule rather than just a portion.

panacinar.definition: Relating to involvement of the entire acinus (respiratory bronchioles through the alveolar sacs) by disease; a pattern of emphysema in which all acini are uniformly enlarged, commonly associated with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.

panmyelosis.definition: Hyperplasia of all three myeloid cell lines in the bone marrow (erythroid, granulocytic, and megakaryocytic), leading to increased production of red cells, white cells, and platelets.

panner's disease.definition: A self-limited osteochondrosis of the capitellum of the humerus (elbow) in young children, presenting with elbow pain and limited motion; due to ischemic change in the capitellum; treated with rest and immobilization; typically resolves over weeks to months with a good prognosis.

panniculitis.definition: Inflammation of the subcutaneous fat (the panniculus) causing tender nodules or plaques in the skin; it can be septal or lobular, with or without vasculitis, and arises from diverse causes such as infection, autoimmune disease, medications, or trauma.

panniculus.definition: A flap of skin with underlying subcutaneous fat that hangs down from the abdomen or other areas; a thick, pendulous layer of adipose tissue and skin forming an overhanging apron, commonly seen in obesity or after significant weight gain.

panography.definition: A radiographic technique that records a single panoramic image of an entire anatomical region (e.g., the jaws or skull) by rotating the X-ray source and detector around the patient; commonly referred to as panoramic radiography.

panophthalmitis.definition: An acute, fulminant intraocular infection in which infection involves all layers of the globe (from cornea to sclera) and frequently extends to the orbit, typically arising from endophthalmitis or penetrating trauma and requiring urgent antimicrobial therapy and often surgical intervention.

panoptic.definition: Relating to a wide, all-encompassing view or examination; providing a comprehensive, panoramic view.

panoramic radiograph.definition: A two-dimensional radiographic image that captures the entire maxillofacial region in a single curved view by rotating the X-ray source and receptor around the head; used to evaluate dentition, eruption and impactions, jaw relationships, and lesions of the jaws and temporomandibular joints.

panoramic radiography.definition: A two-dimensional dental imaging technique that captures the entire jaws and surrounding structures in a single broad view by rotating an X-ray source and detector around the patient's head.

panotitis.definition: Inflammation involving all parts of the ear: the external auditory canal, middle ear, and inner ear.

panphobia.definition: A rare term for a fear of everything; a pervasive, nonspecific anxiety in which many situations are perceived as threatening. It is not a distinct DSM-5 diagnosis and is sometimes used interchangeably with panophobia or generalized anxiety.

panphobic.definition: A pervasive, nonspecific fear or anxiety about almost anything; a rare term used to describe generalized anxiety rather than a fear of a specific object or situation.

panplegia.definition: Total paralysis of all voluntary muscles; complete loss of motor function throughout the body.

pansclerosis.definition: A hypothetical or nonstandard term for diffuse, generalized sclerosis of multiple tissues or organs; not a recognized medical diagnosis.

pantograph.definition: A mechanical linkage with hinged arms that copies a drawing to a different scale by tracing one point to move the others proportionally.

pantomograph.definition: A dental panoramic radiography unit that produces a single wide-view image of the maxillofacial region (teeth, jaws, and surrounding structures) by rotating the X-ray source and detector around the patient's head; used to assess dentition, jaw relationships, bone levels, and pathology.

pantomography.definition: A panoramic radiographic technique that yields a single wide-view image of the jaws (maxilla and mandible), teeth, and surrounding structures; commonly used in dentistry to assess dentition, eruption, occlusion, and jaw pathology.

pantophobia.definition: A persistent, irrational fear of everything; a generalized phobia characterized by pervasive anxiety across most situations.

pantoprazole.definition: A proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that irreversibly inhibits the H+/K+-ATPase enzyme in gastric parietal cells, reducing gastric acid secretion; used to treat GERD, erosive esophagitis, and peptic ulcers.

pantoscopic.definition: Relating to pantoscopy; the tilt of eyeglass lenses toward the wearer's face, causing the lower edge of the lens to sit closer to the eye to improve fit and optical performance.

pantothenic acid.definition: A water-soluble B vitamin (vitamin B5) essential for the synthesis of coenzyme A, a central cofactor in fatty acid metabolism and in energy production from carbohydrates, proteins, and fats.

pantothenyl alcohol.definition: An alcohol derivative of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5); used in cosmetics and pharmaceuticals as a source of pantothenic acid and as a skin-conditioning humectant.

pantropic virus.definition: A pantropic virus is a virus capable of infecting multiple tissue types or organs (broad tissue tropism), often causing systemic infection with dissemination beyond a single organ.

panzootic.definition: A disease that affects animals over a large geographic area.

papain.definition: A proteolytic enzyme derived from the latex of the papaya plant (Carica papaya); a protease that digests proteins, commonly used as a meat tenderizer and as a digestive aid.

papaya.definition: A tropical fruit (Carica papaya); the latex and unripe fruit contain the proteolytic enzyme papain, used as a digestive aid and in some enzymatic debriding products; ripe fruit is edible and rich in vitamins A and C.

paper chromatography.definition: A qualitative analytical technique in which a sample is applied to a strip of paper (the stationary phase) and placed in a suitable solvent (the mobile phase); as the solvent travels up the paper by capillary action, the mixture’s components partition between the paper and the solvent and migrate at different rates, producing separated spots that can be analyzed (often using retention factors, Rf).

papilla of vater.definition: The major duodenal papilla; the opening in the descending duodenum through which bile and pancreatic juice drain from the hepatopancreatic ampulla (junction of the common bile duct and main pancreatic duct) into the duodenal lumen, regulated by the sphincter of Oddi.

papillary.definition: Relating to small, nipple-like projections; describes structures that possess such projections.

warthin's tumor.definition: A benign cystic neoplasm of the parotid gland composed of oncocytic epithelium with dense lymphoid stroma (often with germinal centers); presents as a slow-growing, painless parotid mass in older adults and is strongly associated with smoking.

submaxillary.definition: Situated beneath the maxilla; pertaining to the submandibular region or gland (a salivary gland located in the floor of the mouth).

papilla duodeni major.definition: A mucosal opening in the descending part of the duodenum where the common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct drain into the intestinal lumen via the hepatopancreatic ampulla (ampulla of Vater), guarded by the sphincter of Oddi.

pneumococci.definition: Encapsulated, Gram-positive diplococcal bacteria that are a common cause of pneumonia and a variety of other infections, including meningitis, otitis media, sinusitis, and bacteremia.

anthrax bacilli.definition: A Gram-positive, rod-shaped, spore-forming, encapsulated bacterium that produces potent toxins and causes a zoonotic infection with three main forms—cutaneous, inhalational, and gastrointestinal—typically acquired from contact with infected animals or animal products.

clostridia.definition: A group of Gram-positive, obligate anaerobic, spore-forming bacilli that includes several pathogenic species of the genus Clostridium; these bacteria produce potent toxins and cause diseases such as tetanus, botulism, gas gangrene, and antibiotic-associated diarrhea.

simmonds' disease.definition: An historical term for panhypopituitarism due to destruction or failure of the anterior pituitary, resulting in profound wasting (cachexia) and loss of multiple pituitary hormones, with symptoms such as amenorrhea, loss of secondary sexual characteristics, hypothyroidism, and adrenal insufficiency.

hypophyseal cachexia.definition: A form of cachexia arising from pituitary (hypopituitary) disease or hypopituitarism, characterized by involuntary weight loss and loss of lean body mass due to deficiency of one or more anterior pituitary hormones (most notably growth hormone and, often, gonadotropic and thyroid/adrenal axis hormones), not attributable to inadequate caloric intake alone.

suprasellar cyst.definition: A cystic lesion in the suprasellar region (above the sella turcica) that may arise from Rathke’s cleft tissue or arachnoid membrane; it can compress the optic chiasm and pituitary/hypothalamic structures, producing visual or endocrine symptoms.

sex hormone.definition: Steroid hormones produced primarily by the gonads (ovaries and testes) and, to a lesser extent, the adrenal glands, that regulate sexual development and reproductive function as well as secondary sexual characteristics; the main classes are estrogens, androgens, and progestogens.

antiviral.definition: A substance or drug that inhibits the replication or spread of viruses, used to treat or prevent viral infections.

interferon inducers.definition: Substances that stimulate host cells to produce interferons, especially type I interferons (IFN-α and IFN-β), by activating innate immune sensors (e.g., pattern-recognition receptors). They enhance antiviral, antiproliferative, and immunomodulatory defenses by upregulating interferon-stimulated genes.

chordae.definition: A cordlike tendinous structure of the heart that anchors the leaflets of the mitral and tricuspid valves to the papillary muscles, preventing valve prolapse during systole.

tendineae.definition: Threadlike cords of dense connective tissue that attach the leaflets of the atrioventricular valves (mitral and tricuspid) to the papillary muscles, preventing prolapse during systole.

papilloma.definition: A benign, exophytic epithelial lesion with a papillary (fingerlike) projection from the surface, often associated with human papillomavirus infection.

papillitis.definition: Inflammation of the optic disc (the head of the optic nerve), causing acute or subacute vision loss with possible eye pain on movement and edema of the optic disc; may be idiopathic or associated with optic neuritis, demyelinating disease, infection, or other inflammatory conditions.

papillotomy.definition: Incision of the papilla (papilla of Vater) to widen the opening of the bile and/or pancreatic duct, typically performed during ERCP to facilitate duct access or stone removal; a more limited alternative to a full biliary sphincterotomy.

thoracis.definition: A Latin term meaning “of the thorax” (thoracic); used in anatomical names to denote structures related to the chest, often appearing in phrases like pars thoracis (the thoracic part).

tympani.definition: The plural form of the eardrum; a thin membrane that separates the external ear from the middle ear and vibrates in response to sound.

paracervical.definition: Situated alongside the cervix; near the cervix.

paracetamol.definition: An analgesic and antipyretic used to relieve mild to moderate pain and reduce fever; it has minimal anti-inflammatory effects and can cause severe liver injury in overdose (especially with alcohol); also known as acetaminophen.

paracolic.definition: Pertaining to the area beside the colon; located along the lateral aspect of the colon (the paracolic area).

gutters.definition: No widely recognized medical definition exists for this term; in clinical use it may describe a shallow groove or channel in tissue or a wound that directs or collects fluids, but it is not a formal anatomical term.

paracolitis.definition: Inflammation of the tissues surrounding the colon (paracolic tissues).

paracolpium.definition: Anatomical tissue surrounding the vagina, comprising fascia and connective tissue that forms part of the endopelvic fascia, extending laterally to the pelvic sidewall and containing vessels and nerves to support the vaginal wall and adjacent pelvic organs.

paracortex.definition: The region of a lymph node between the cortex and medulla, rich in T lymphocytes and dendritic cells; the site of T-cell activation, containing high endothelial venules for naive T-cell entry from the bloodstream.

paracrine.definition: Relating to cell signaling where secreted messenger molecules act on nearby cells within the same tissue by diffusion, not on distant targets via the bloodstream (contrast with autocrine and endocrine signaling).

paracusis.definition: A condition of defective or impaired hearing; partial deafness or abnormal auditory perception.

paracystitis.definition: Inflammation of the tissues surrounding the urinary bladder (perivesical inflammation).

paradenitis.definition: Not a standard medical term; if used, it would imply inflammation of a gland adjacent to another structure (para- meaning beside, -adenitis meaning gland inflammation). A precise diagnosis would specify the gland, e.g., parotid adenitis for the parotid gland.

paradentium.definition: The tissues surrounding and supporting a tooth, including the gingiva, periodontal ligament, cementum, and surrounding alveolar bone; collectively known as the periodontium.

paradidymal.definition: Anatomical term meaning near or adjacent to the epididymis.

parabiosis.definition: A surgical technique in which two living organisms are joined to share a common circulatory system, allowing exchange of blood and circulating factors between them; commonly used in experimental research to study systemic effects on aging, regeneration, and immunity.

paraballism.definition: A rare hyperkinetic movement disorder characterized by abrupt, involuntary, violent flinging movements of the limbs; typically due to lesions or dysfunction in basal ganglia circuits, especially the subthalamic nucleus, and may affect one side (hemiballismus) or both sides.

paradoxical.definition: Relating to a paradox; appearing contradictory or contrary to what is expected; in medicine, describing a response or phenomenon that is opposite to the usual expectation.

paradoxic.definition: Relating to a paradox; appearing contrary to expectation or to established facts; in medicine, describing findings or responses that are counterintuitive or opposite to what is anticipated.

aciduria.definition: Abnormally acidic urine (low urine pH), reflecting increased excretion or presence of acids in the urine, often due to metabolic acidosis or renal tubular dysfunction.

paracoccidioidal.definition: Relating to paracoccidioidomycosis, a chronic systemic fungal infection caused by Paracoccidioides species (e.g., Paracoccidioides brasiliensis), typically affecting the lungs and mucous membranes.

disc.definition: A fibrocartilaginous cushion between vertebral bodies in the spine that absorbs shock and allows motion; consists of an outer annulus fibrosus and an inner nucleus pulposus.

palmoplantar.definition: Relating to the palms of the hands and the soles of the feet.

keratoderma.definition: Group of disorders characterized by thickening of the outer skin layer (stratum corneum) due to hyperkeratosis, most pronounced on the palms and soles; may be hereditary or acquired.

paquelin.definition: A surgical thermocautery instrument (Paquelin cautery) that delivers controlled heat through a fine probe for precise coagulation or cutting of tissue during procedures; uses electrical current to heat the probe to a set temperature.

papovavirus.definition: A historical, now largely obsolete grouping of nonenveloped circular double-stranded DNA viruses that includes papillomaviruses and polyomaviruses (and vacuolating viruses); modern taxonomy separates them into Papillomaviridae and Polyomaviridae, and these viruses replicate in the nucleus, with papillomaviruses causing warts and oncogenic disease in some cases, and polyomaviruses causing disease primarily in immunocompromised hosts.

papilliform.definition: Resembling a papilla; having a nipple‑like, papillary projection or surface.

papilloretinitis.definition: An inflammatory condition involving both the optic nerve head (papilla/papillitis) and the retina (retinitis), i.e., inflammation of the optic disc with concurrent retinal inflammation.

paradoxical intention.definition: A psychotherapeutic technique in which a patient is encouraged to deliberately engage in or exaggerate the behavior or symptom they fear to reduce anticipatory anxiety and avoidance.

parakeratosis.definition: Retention of nuclei in the stratum corneum due to abnormal keratinization; a histologic feature of rapid epidermal turnover seen in conditions such as psoriasis and some inflammatory dermatoses.

congenital visual deficit.definition: A vision impairment present at birth or in early infancy, resulting from congenital abnormalities of the eye, optic nerve, or visual pathways (often genetic or developmental), leading to reduced visual acuity or blindness.

hit.definition: No widely used medical term matches this input. If you intended the acronym related to a heparin-associated condition, the definition is: A prothrombotic immune-mediated adverse reaction to heparin caused by antibodies against the platelet factor 4–heparin complex, leading to platelet activation and thrombosis despite low platelet counts. paraffin bath.definition: A heat therapy in which a hand or foot is dipped into warm melted paraffin wax to form a thick, insulating coating that is retained to provide superficial warmth, relieve pain and stiffness, and improve joint mobility in conditions such as arthritis.

wax bath.definition: A therapeutic procedure in which the hands, feet, or other body parts are dipped into warmed paraffin wax (often with oil) to form a heated coating that relieves pain and stiffness and improves joint mobility, commonly used for arthritis and other musculoskeletal complaints.

paraffin section.definition: A thin slice of tissue that has been infiltrated with paraffin wax, embedded, and cut with a microtome for microscopic histological examination, typically stained (e.g., with hematoxylin and eosin).

paraffin method.definition: A histology technique in which a fixed tissue specimen is dehydrated, cleared, infiltrated with molten paraffin wax, embedded in paraffin, and then sectioned for microscopic examination.

paraffinoma.definition: A chronic granulomatous inflammatory reaction to injected paraffin (paraffin oil), producing firm nodules or masses with fibrosis at the injection sites; histology shows lipogranulomatous inflammation with lipid-laden macrophages and multinucleated giant cells, and it may cause pain, swelling, discharge, or cosmetic deformity, sometimes requiring surgical excision.

paraflex.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. Please provide context (brand/product type, specialty, or confirm spelling) to give a precise definition.

chlorzoxazone.definition: Chlorzoxazone is a centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant used to relieve acute muscle spasm in musculoskeletal conditions; it acts on the central nervous system to reduce muscle reflexes and is intended for short-term use with rest and physical therapy. Common adverse effects include drowsiness and dizziness; rare but serious liver toxicity and hypersensitivity reactions have been reported.

parafollicular c cell.definition: Calcitonin-secreting neuroendocrine cells of the thyroid gland, located in the interfollicular region; derived from neural crest and involved in calcium homeostasis by inhibiting osteoclast-mediated bone resorption.

parafon forte.definition: A fixed-dose analgesic combination containing acetaminophen (paracetamol) and codeine; used for moderate pain, with acetaminophen providing non-opioid analgesia/antipyretic effects and codeine providing additional opioid-mediated relief. Adverse effects include drowsiness, nausea, constipation, potential liver injury with acetaminophen overdose, and risk of dependence from codeine.

paraganglioma.definition: A neuroendocrine tumor arising from paraganglia of the autonomic nervous system, typically extra-adrenal; it may be nonfunctioning or catecholamine-secreting, and malignancy is defined by the presence of metastases.

chromaffin body.definition: A cluster of chromaffin cells derived from neural crest, forming the adrenal medulla (and extra-adrenal paraganglia) that secretes catecholamines—epinephrine and norepinephrine—into the bloodstream in response to sympathetic stimulation.

chromaffin cell.definition: A neural crest–derived neuroendocrine cell located in the adrenal medulla (and some paraganglia) that stores and releases catecholamines, mainly epinephrine and norepinephrine, in response to sympathetic stimulation; named for its chromaffin staining with chromium salts.

parageusia.definition: A distorted or altered sense of taste, usually described as an unpleasant or metallic taste, which can occur with or without a taste stimulus and may result from medications, infections, neurological disorders, or other medical conditions.

paragonimiasis.definition: An infection caused by lung flukes of the genus Paragonimus (most commonly P. westermani), acquired by consuming raw or undercooked freshwater crustaceans; adult worms reside in the lungs, causing chronic cough, chest pain, and hemoptysis, with eosinophilia, and eggs are shed in sputum or swallowed and excreted in feces; treated with praziquantel (or triclabendazole).

paragonimus westermani.definition: A lung-dwelling fluke (trematode) that causes paragonimiasis in humans; acquired by consuming undercooked freshwater crustaceans (crabs or crayfish); adults inhabit the lungs and can cause chronic cough, hemoptysis, and chest pain; eggs may be found in sputum or stool; treated with praziquantel.

parahippocampal gyrus.definition: An elongated cortical region of the medial temporal lobe surrounding the hippocampus; part of the limbic system; involved in memory formation and retrieval, contextual and spatial processing, and scene recognition, providing major input to the hippocampus via the entorhinal cortex.

parahormone.definition: A hormone secreted by the parathyroid glands that raises blood calcium levels by stimulating bone resorption, increasing renal calcium reabsorption, decreasing renal phosphate reabsorption, and promoting production of active vitamin D (calcitriol) to enhance intestinal calcium absorption.

parahypnosis.definition: A nonstandard term for a near-hypnotic state characterized by relaxation and increased suggestibility, but not a full hypnotic trance; sometimes used to describe quasi-hypnotic phenomena or preparatory stages before hypnosis; not a formally recognized clinical diagnosis.

parainfectious.definition: Occurring during and/or immediately after an infectious illness, not caused by direct invasion of the pathogen; typically immune-mediated or inflammatory sequelae triggered by the infection.

parainfluenza virus.definition: A group of enveloped, negative-sense, single-stranded RNA viruses in the family Paramyxoviridae that cause respiratory tract infections, particularly croup, in children; there are four human serotypes (HPIV-1–HPIV-4).

tracheobronchitis.definition: Inflammation of the trachea and bronchi, usually due to viral infection or irritants, presenting with cough (often productive), throat irritation, and sometimes wheezing or shortness of breath; can be acute or chronic.

paralytic stroke.definition: A cerebrovascular accident presenting with paralysis on one side of the body (hemiplegia) due to damage to motor pathways in the brain from ischemia or hemorrhage.

adynamic ileus.definition: A non-mechanical, functional impairment of intestinal motility (paralytic ileus) with reduced or absent peristalsis, gas and fluid accumulation, abdominal distension, nausea/vomiting, and inability to pass gas or stools; commonly occurs after surgery or with metabolic/electrolyte disturbances or opioid use; typically self-limited and managed with supportive care and treatment of underlying causes.

ureteral stone.definition: A calculus located in the ureter that obstructs urine flow, causing severe, intermittent flank or groin pain (renal colic), often with hematuria; may originate from a renal stone and may pass spontaneously or require medical or surgical intervention.

retroperitoneal hematomas.definition: A collection of blood in the retroperitoneal space, often caused by trauma, surgical injury, anticoagulation, or ruptured vascular lesions; can present with flank or back pain and signs of shock, and is diagnosed by CT imaging; management emphasizes hemodynamic stabilization and addressing the bleeding (reversal of anticoagulation, endovascular or surgical control as needed).

metabolic disease.definition: A broad category of disorders caused by impaired chemical processes of metabolism—how the body converts nutrients into energy and building blocks—often due to genetic enzyme defects, hormonal abnormalities, or acquired factors, resulting in abnormal accumulation or deficiency of metabolic intermediates.

paralysis agitans.definition: A chronic, progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by resting tremor, bradykinesia, rigidity, and postural instability, due to loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra; commonly known as Parkinson disease.

paresis.definition: Partial loss of voluntary muscle strength in a muscle or group, due to nervous system dysfunction; movement is weakened but not completely absent (as opposed to paralysis).

paralytic dementia.definition: Progressive dementia caused by late-stage neurosyphilis (general paresis), marked by cognitive decline and psychiatric/behavioral changes due to inflammatory brain involvement by Treponema pallidum.

paranoid personality disorder.definition:
A pervasive pattern of distrust and suspiciousness of others such that their motives are interpreted as malevolent, beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts. Four or more of the following are typically present: 
- Suspects, without sufficient basis, that others are exploiting, harming, or deceiving them
- Preoccupation with unjustified doubts about the loyalty or trustworthiness of friends or colleagues
- Reluctance to confide in others due to unwarranted fear that information will be used against them
- Reads hidden demeaning or threatening meanings into benign remarks or events
- Persistently bears grudges
- Perceives attacks on their character and is quick to react angrily or to counterattack
- Recurrent suspicions, without justification, regarding the fidelity of a spouse or partner

paranoid schizophrenia.definition: Historically, a form of schizophrenia in which delusions (typically persecutory or grandiose) and prominent auditory hallucinations predominate, with relatively preserved cognitive function and affect; disorganized thinking and behavior are less prominent. The term is largely replaced in modern DSM/ICD terminology by schizophrenia with paranoid features.

paranoid reaction.definition: A transient, acute psychotic state characterized by persecutory delusions and excessive suspiciousness, typically precipitated by severe stress or medical illness and resolving without progression to a chronic psychotic disorder.

paranoid state.definition: A state of persistent irrational mistrust and suspicion of others, typically with persecutory delusions and hypervigilance, which can occur in psychotic disorders (such as paranoid-type schizophrenia), delusional disorder, delirium, or mood disorders with psychotic features.

paramesonephric duct.definition: A paired embryonic duct that develops into the female internal reproductive organs (fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, and upper vagina) and regresses in males under anti-Müllerian hormone.

mullerian duct.definition: An embryonic paired duct (the paramesonephric or Müllerian duct) that develops into the female internal reproductive structures—the fallopian tubes, uterus, and the upper portion of the vagina; in males it regresses under the influence of anti-Müllerian hormone.

parametric imaging.definition: Parametric imaging is the generation of quantitative maps of tissue properties by modeling dynamic imaging data (e.g., tracer kinetics or time‑signal changes) at each voxel, producing spatial distributions of parameters such as perfusion, diffusion, or metabolic rate.

paramnesia.definition: A disturbance of memory involving distortion or misattribution of experiences, such as feeling that a current situation is familiar (déjà vu) or unfamiliar (jamais vu); can occur in delirium, temporal lobe epilepsy, or various psychiatric conditions.

paramyloidosis.definition: A condition characterized by extracellular deposition of misfolded amyloid proteins in muscle tissue or adjacent structures, potentially causing weakness and functional impairment.

paraneoplastic syndromes.definition: A group of clinical syndromes that accompany cancer but are not caused by the tumor’s local growth or metastasis; they arise from tumor-produced hormones, peptides, or immune responses against shared antigens, and can affect endocrine, neurologic, dermatologic, rheumatologic, or hematologic systems.

paranephric fat.definition: Adipose tissue located outside the renal fascia (Gerota’s fascia) that surrounds the kidney, comprising the extrarenal (pararenal) fat compartments between the renal fascia and the posterior abdominal wall or peritoneum.

pararenal fat.definition: Adipose tissue surrounding the kidney that lies outside the renal fascia (Gerota's fascia); part of the retroperitoneal fat, subdivided into the anterior and posterior pararenal spaces.

paranesthesia.definition: An abnormal sensation of the skin, such as prickling, burning, or numbness, with no identifiable cause.

paraplegic.definition: A person who is paralyzed from the waist down, typically due to spinal cord injury or disease, resulting in loss of movement and sensation in the legs and lower body.

parapneumonic empyema.definition: A collection of pus in the pleural space resulting from pneumonia; a complication of bacterial pneumonia characterized by infected pleural fluid often requiring antibiotics and drainage.

parapraxia.definition: An unintentional error in speech, memory, or action believed to reveal unconscious thoughts, wishes, or conflicts—commonly referred to as a Freudian slip.

paraproctitis.definition: Inflammation of the soft tissues around the rectum (pararectal tissues), usually due to infection from anal glands; may accompany cellulitis and may progress to a pararectal abscess.

paraprostatitis.definition: Inflammation of the soft tissues surrounding the prostate gland (periprostatic tissue); may accompany prostatitis and present with perineal or pelvic pain, urinary symptoms, and sometimes fever.

paraprotein.definition: A monoclonal immunoglobulin (or its free light chains) produced by a single clone of plasma cells, typically detectable in serum or urine as an M-protein and associated with plasma cell disorders such as multiple myeloma.

parapsoriasis varioliformis acuta.definition: An acute to subacute inflammatory skin condition in the pityriasis lichenoides spectrum, presenting with crops of small red papules that may vesiculate and crust, producing varioliform (pox‑like) lesions; often self‑limited with relapses and treated with topical steroids, antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin, doxycycline), or phototherapy.

pararectal fossa.definition: Two peritoneal recesses in the pelvis on either side of the rectum, formed by peritoneal reflections; potential spaces bounded medially by the rectum and laterally by the pelvic wall, into which fluid or pus can collect.

parareflexia.definition: An abnormal or altered reflex response, indicating dysfunction of the reflex arc or its central modulation; reflexes may be reduced, exaggerated, or inappropriately timed.

pararenal.definition: Relating to the area around the kidney; in anatomy, the pararenal space lies outside the renal fascia and contains adipose tissue.

paraperitoneal nephrectomy.definition: A nephrectomy performed via a paraperitoneal (adjacent to the peritoneum) approach, typically through the retroperitoneal space without entering the peritoneal cavity.

parapharyngeal abscess.definition: A deep neck space infection in the parapharyngeal space (lateral to the pharynx), usually arising from oropharyngeal or dental infections, presenting with severe throat pain, trismus, neck swelling, fever, and a muffled voice; can threaten the airway and often requires IV antibiotics and drainage.

paraphasia.definition: A language disturbance in which intended words or sounds are substituted with incorrect or unrelated ones, producing fluent but distorted or nonsensical speech; commonly seen in aphasia after brain injury.

paraphia.definition: Not a recognized medical term; no widely accepted definition.

paraphilia.definition: Atypical, persistent sexual interest or arousal toward non-normative targets or activities (such as objects, unusual situations, or non-consenting individuals) that may be harmless, but is clinically considered a disorder when it causes distress or impairment or leads to harm or acting on urges with a non-consenting person.

paraphimosis.definition: A urological emergency in which the foreskin is retracted behind the glans and cannot be returned to its normal position, causing penile constriction, edema, and compromised blood flow that can progress to ischemia if not promptly reduced.

paraphrenia.definition: A late-onset, schizophrenia-like psychotic disorder marked by persistent delusions (often paranoid) and hallucinations with relatively preserved affect and functioning, and little early deterioration—historically called paraphrenia and now often viewed as a late-onset form of schizophrenia or an obsolete diagnosis.

parasitemia.definition: Presence of parasitic organisms in the bloodstream, typically quantified as parasite density in peripheral blood to assess infection burden (e.g., Plasmodium species in malaria).

parasitic fibroma.definition: A benign tumor of fibrous connective tissue that occurs in an abnormal location, deriving its blood supply from surrounding tissues rather than its tissue of origin (often described as attaching to or parasitizing adjacent structures, sometimes after surgical implantation).

parasitic glossitis.definition: Inflammation of the tongue due to infection with a parasite in the oral cavity; may cause soreness, redness, swelling, and changes in the tongue surface.

glossitis parasitica.definition: A tongue inflammation caused by a parasitic infection; a nonstandard term not widely used in medical references.
