They can occur on their own (e.g., amnesia) or as part of broader neurocognitive syndromes (e.g., dementia) and may arise from neurologic, psychiatric, metabolic, infectious, toxic factors, or aging.

intracranial neoplasms.definition: A tumor or abnormal growth within the cranial cavity that may arise from brain tissue, meninges, or cranial nerves; it can be benign or malignant and may be primary to the CNS or metastatic from elsewhere, often presenting with headaches, seizures, focal neurologic deficits, or signs of increased intracranial pressure due to mass effect.

phenyltoloxamine citrate.definition: A first-generation oral antihistamine (H1 receptor antagonist) supplied as the citrate salt; used in over-the-counter cough and cold products to relieve allergy and upper respiratory symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, and itching, with potential for drowsiness and anticholinergic effects.

percodan.definition: A prescription analgesic that combines oxycodone, an opioid, with aspirin, an NSAID, used for moderate to severe pain.

percogesic.definition: A brand-name over-the-counter combination analgesic containing acetaminophen and diphenhydramine; used to relieve mild to moderate pain or fever and to aid sleep due to the sedating antihistamine component.

epididymal sperm aspiration.definition: A surgical procedure to retrieve sperm from the epididymis for use in assisted reproductive techniques, typically performed in men with obstructive azoospermia; sperm may be collected by percutaneous epididymal sperm aspiration (PESA) or microscopic epididymal sperm aspiration (MESA) for use in IVF/ICSI.

percutaneous nephrolithotomy.definition: A minimally invasive procedure to remove kidney stones by creating a small tract through the skin into the renal collecting system, through which a nephroscope and instruments are used to fragment and extract stones, usually with imaging guidance and often followed by a nephrostomy tube or stent.

renal capsule.definition: A tough, fibrous membrane that tightly envelops the kidney, lying directly on its surface and adherent to the renal parenchyma, protecting the organ from trauma and infection and helping to maintain its shape.

transluminal coronary angioplasty.definition: A minimally invasive endovascular procedure in which a balloon-tipped catheter is guided to a narrowed coronary artery and the balloon is inflated to widen the artery, improving blood flow (often with stent placement to keep the vessel open).

percutaneous transluminal renal angiopla.definition: A minimally invasive endovascular procedure in which a catheter with a balloon is advanced to a narrowed renal artery and inflated to dilate the vessel (often with stent placement) to restore blood flow and treat renal artery stenosis.

renal angioplasty.definition: A minimally invasive endovascular procedure to widen a narrowed renal artery (renal artery stenosis) by balloon dilation, often with stent placement, to improve renal perfusion and hypertension control.

percutaneous biliary drainage.definition: A procedure in which a catheter is placed percutaneously into the biliary tree (usually through the liver) under imaging guidance to drain bile and relieve biliary obstruction; the catheter may provide external drainage or internal–external drainage into the duodenum.

percutaneous transhepatic biliary draina.definition: A radiologic procedure in which a catheter is inserted through the skin and liver into a bile duct to drain bile externally or internally/external, relieving biliary obstruction and associated infection or jaundice, typically guided by ultrasound or fluoroscopy.

percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy.definition: A procedure in which a feeding tube is placed through the abdominal wall into the stomach under endoscopic guidance to provide long-term enteral nutrition for patients unable to take adequate nutrition orally.

pta.definition: A minimally invasive endovascular procedure to dilate a narrowed artery by inflating a balloon catheter at the site of stenosis, often followed by stent placement.

lung perfusion scan.definition: A nuclear medicine study that assesses pulmonary blood flow by intravenously injecting a radiotracer (typically technetium-99m–labeled macroaggregated albumin) and imaging with a gamma camera; used to identify perfusion defects and, when combined with ventilation imaging (V/Q scan), to evaluate for pulmonary embolism.

periappendicitis.definition: Inflammation of the tissues surrounding the appendix, typically occurring with or as part of appendicitis; presents with localized right lower quadrant abdominal pain and tenderness and may progress to a periappendiceal abscess or localized peritonitis if untreated.

periappendicular.definition: Relating to the region surrounding the appendix.

periaortic.definition: Located around or surrounding the aorta.

periarteritis.definition: Inflammation surrounding an artery, typically affecting the perivascular tissues and/or the outer arterial layer (adventitia) rather than the inner lining; can be part of systemic vasculitis or a localized inflammatory process.

periapical cyst.definition: A chronic inflammatory odontogenic cyst at the apex of a nonvital tooth, arising from epithelial rests of Malassez in response to pulpal necrosis; typically appears as a well-defined radiolucency at the tooth apex and is usually treated with endodontic therapy or extraction.

periapical fibroma.definition: A benign lesion consisting of dense fibrous connective tissue at the apex of a nonvital tooth, arising as a reparative mass in response to chronic irritation; histology shows dense collagenous stroma with relatively few inflammatory cells.

periapical infection.definition: An infection around the apex of a tooth root, usually arising from pulpal necrosis, that can form an inflammatory lesion such as a periapical abscess, granuloma, or cyst; commonly presents with pain and/or swelling and a radiolucent area at the root apex on imaging; treated with endodontic therapy or extraction, with antibiotics only for spreading infection or systemic signs.

radicular cyst.definition: An inflammatory odontogenic cyst at the apex of a nonvital tooth, arising from chronic periapical inflammation that stimulates epithelial rests of Malassez; the most common odontogenic cyst, typically presenting as a well-circumscribed radiolucent lesion at the tooth apex and often treated with root canal therapy or surgical enucleation.

periapical radiograph.definition: A dental radiograph that shows the entire tooth from crown to root apex and the surrounding periapical bone, used to assess periapical tissues for pathology such as infection, cysts, or granulomas.

tooth extraction.definition: Removal of a tooth from its socket in the jaw, typically performed by a dentist or oral surgeon under local anesthesia; indicated for decay, infection, trauma, impaction, or crowding, and may require suturing and post-procedure care.

dental abscess.definition: A localized collection of pus around a tooth or in the surrounding tissues caused by bacterial infection, usually secondary to dental caries or trauma; presents with pain, swelling, and sometimes fever, and is treated with drainage and removal of the infection source (root canal treatment or extraction), with antibiotics as indicated.

perianal fistula.definition: A chronic abnormal tract from the anal canal or rectum to the perianal skin, usually arising from infection of anal glands after an anorectal abscess; it presents with persistent perianal drainage and is typically treated surgically (e.g., fistulotomy, fistulectomy, or seton placement).

perianal space.definition: A potential space surrounding the anal canal in the perineum, typically referring to the ischiorectal (ischioanal) fossae on each side of the canal. It is bounded medially by the anal canal and its sphincters, laterally by the obturator internus muscle and its fascia, superiorly by the levator ani, and inferiorly by the skin; it contains fat, neurovascular structures, and can be involved in infections such as perianal abscesses.

periarteritis gummosa.definition: A granulomatous gumma surrounding a blood vessel seen in tertiary syphilis, consisting of necrotizing granulomatous inflammation around the artery and potentially leading to obliterative endarteritis and vascular damage.

syphilitic periarteritis.definition: Inflammation around arterial walls due to syphilis, classically involving endarteritis of the vasa vasorum with plasma cell–predominant infiltrates, leading to thickening and obliteration of the vessel lumen and potential ischemic damage (a feature of tertiary syphilis, notably in syphilitic aortitis).

periangitis.definition: Not a standard medical term; if interpreted as periangiitis, it would mean inflammation around a blood vessel—a localized perivascular inflammatory process that can be seen in various forms of vasculitis or inflammatory vascular disease.

intestinal involvement.definition: Involvement of the intestinal tract by a disease process, meaning the small or large intestine is affected and may show inflammation, ulceration, infection, obstruction, or ischemia as part of a systemic condition or localized enteric disease.

cytotoxic drugs.definition: A class of medications that are toxic to cells, particularly rapidly dividing ones; used mainly in cancer chemotherapy to kill cancer cells by damaging DNA or inhibiting mitosis, often with cytotoxic effects on normal rapidly dividing tissues.

periarthritis.definition: Inflammation of the soft tissues surrounding a joint (the periarticular tissues), including the joint capsule, ligaments, bursae, and tendons, causing pain, tenderness, and limited range of motion around the affected joint.

periarticular.definition: Around or near a joint; describing soft-tissue structures surrounding a joint (such as the joint capsule, ligaments, tendons, and bursae) as opposed to inside the joint (intra-articular).

peribronchial.definition: Located around a bronchus; describing tissue surrounding a bronchus, often used to refer to peribronchial thickening from inflammation or edema.

peribronchiolar.definition: Relating to or located around the bronchioles, the small airways of the lungs; used to describe tissue surrounding these airways, such as inflammation or fibrosis.

pericalyceal.definition: Relating to or surrounding a calyx, especially the renal calyx of the kidney (the funnel-shaped chamber that collects urine).

pericardia.definition: A double-layered fibroserous sac surrounding the heart and the roots of the great vessels; it consists of the fibrous pericardium and the serous pericardium (parietal and visceral layers) separated by the pericardial cavity containing lubricating fluid.

pericardiac.definition: Relating to the pericardium, the double-walled sac that surrounds and protects the heart.

pericardial adhesion.definition: Fibrous bands that tether the visceral and parietal pericardium after inflammation or injury, potentially restricting cardiac movement and complicating subsequent cardiac surgery.

pericardial artery.definition: An arterial vessel that supplies blood to the pericardium (the sac around the heart); the principal example is the pericardiacophrenic artery, a branch of the internal thoracic artery, which runs with the phrenic nerve to vascularize the parietal layer of the pericardium.

hydropericardium.definition: An accumulation of watery fluid in the pericardial sac (pericardial effusion), typically serous transudate, which may impair cardiac filling and can lead to tamponade if large or rapid.

pericardial murmur.definition: An audible scratching or creaking sound produced by friction between inflamed pericardial surfaces, typically heard best at the left lower sternal border with the patient leaning forward; associated with pericarditis and not a true cardiac murmur.

pericardiectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which part or all of the pericardium, the sac surrounding the heart, is removed to relieve constrictive pericarditis or persistent/recurrent pericardial effusions.

pericardioperitoneal canals.definition: Two embryologic communications between the pericardial and peritoneal cavities in the intraembryonic coelom; they are closed by the pleuroperitoneal membranes as the diaphragm develops, and failure to close can permit diaphragmatic herniation.

pericardiotomy.definition: Surgical incision into the pericardium (the sac around the heart), typically to drain a pericardial effusion or to gain access to the heart.

acute suppurative pericarditis.definition: An acute bacterial infection of the pericardial space with purulent exudate, typically due to septicemia or extension from nearby infection, presenting with fever and pericarditis symptoms and risking cardiac tamponade; treatment includes prompt antibiotics and drainage.

serous pericardium.definition: A double-layered serous membrane forming the inner lining of the pericardial sac; the parietal layer lines the fibrous pericardium, and the visceral layer (epicardium) covers the heart, with a potential pericardial cavity containing lubricating serous fluid to reduce friction during heartbeats.

fibrous pericardium.definition: A dense, tough outer layer of the pericardium composed of fibrous connective tissue; it anchors the heart to surrounding structures (diaphragm and sternum) and blends with the tunica adventitia of the great vessels, helping protect the heart and limit its overexpansion.

pericardial space.definition: The potential space between the visceral (epicardial) and parietal layers of the serous pericardium surrounding the heart, normally containing a small amount of lubricating serous fluid to reduce friction during cardiac movements.

pericardial fluid.definition: A small volume of lubricating serous fluid in the pericardial cavity between the visceral and parietal pericardium that reduces friction during cardiac motion; normal volume is about 15–50 mL.

pericholangitis.definition: Inflammation of the tissue surrounding the bile ducts (peribiliary tissue), commonly arising in the setting of cholangitis or biliary obstruction.

chondrial bone.definition: Bone that forms by replacing a cartilage template through endochondral ossification, a process in which a cartilage model is progressively converted into bone (as seen in most long bones and much of the skeleton), with growth in length occurring at the growth plates.

periosteal bone.definition: Relating to the periosteum, the vascular fibrous membrane covering bone; describes bone formation on the outer surface of bone adjacent to this membrane.

perichrome.definition: An uncommon or nonstandard term; if used, it would refer to material surrounding chromatin in the nucleus (the perichromatin region) or, more broadly, to structures surrounding chromosomes during mitosis (perichromosomal material).

pericolic abscess.definition: A localized collection of pus adjacent to the colon, usually arising from inflammatory colonic disease (most commonly diverticulitis); represents a contained intra-abdominal abscess in the pericolic tissues surrounding the colon. Management may include antibiotics and, if needed, image-guided percutaneous drainage or surgical drainage.

peridiverticular abscess.definition: A localized pus-filled collection adjacent to a diverticulum formed by perforation or inflammation in diverticular disease; a complication of diverticulitis, most often in the sigmoid colon, that is contained by surrounding tissues and may require antibiotics, drainage, or surgical intervention if not resolving.

pericolitis.definition: Inflammation of the tissues surrounding the colon (pericolic inflammation), commonly seen with diverticulitis or inflammatory colitis.

pericolonitis.definition: Inflammation of the tissues surrounding the colon (the pericolic tissues). It commonly accompanies colonic inflammatory diseases or diverticulitis and may present with localized abdominal pain; infection can lead to an abscess.

pericoronitis.definition: Inflammation and possible infection of the soft tissue surrounding a partially erupted tooth (most commonly a wisdom tooth), often due to plaque and food debris trapped under the operculum; presents with pain, swelling, redness, and sometimes difficulty opening the mouth.

pericystium.definition: A host-derived fibrous outer capsule surrounding a parasitic cyst, formed in response to infection (as in hydatid disease).

peridens.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard dictionaries. If intended as a variant of “peridental” or “periodontal,” it would refer to the tissues surrounding and supporting a tooth, including the gums, periodontal ligament, cementum, and alveolar bone.

periderm.definition: A transient protective outer epithelial layer that covers the developing embryonic epidermis and is shed as the mature epidermis forms.

perididymitis.definition: Inflammation around the epididymis; not a commonly used medical term. If used, it would describe inflammatory involvement of tissues surrounding the epididymis and is closely related to epididymitis, which is inflammation of the epididymis usually due to infection.

peridural anesthesia.definition: An anesthesia technique in which local anesthetic is injected into the epidural space surrounding the spinal cord to block nerve conduction, producing sensory analgesia (and often some motor blockade) below the level of injection; commonly delivered via an indwelling catheter for continuous pain relief during labor or surgery.

experiencephalitis.definition: Inflammation of brain tissue, usually due to infection (often viral) or autoimmune causes; presents with fever, headache, altered mental status, seizures, and sometimes focal neurologic deficits; diagnosed by clinical assessment, CSF analysis, and brain imaging; management targets the underlying cause and includes supportive care.

perifocal.definition: Around or surrounding a focal point or lesion; describing tissue in the area adjacent to a localized pathology, often used to denote edema or inflammation surrounding a lesion.

perifollicular.definition: Pertaining to or situated around a hair follicle.

perifolliculitis.definition: An inflammatory condition involving hair follicles, presenting with small erythematous papules or pustules around the follicle (often with crusting); typically caused by bacterial infection (often Staphylococcus aureus), but can be fungal or irritant-related, and commonly affects the beard area, scalp, and extremities. Management includes hygiene measures, warm compresses, and topical antibiotics (or oral antibiotics for extensive disease).

periglottic.definition: Situated around the glottis; relating to the area surrounding the laryngeal opening (rima glottidis) between the true vocal cords.

periglottis.definition: Anatomical region around the glottis—the opening between the true vocal cords in the larynx—encompassing nearby structures such as the aryepiglottic folds, vestibular folds, and arytenoid area.

perimplantoclasia.definition: A nonstandard term referring to destructive changes around an implanted device (most often a dental implant), such as loss of supporting bone or soft-tissue breakdown leading to implant instability.

perikaryontic.definition: Relating to the perikaryon—the cell body (soma) of a neuron.

perimenopause.definition: The period shortly before menopause when hormonal changes begin and menstrual cycles become irregular.

perimeter.definition: The boundary length around the outer edge of a lesion, wound, or anatomical area; used to describe its size and extent.

perimetrium.definition: Outer serous (peritoneal) coat of the uterus; the serosa formed by the visceral peritoneum that covers the uterus and is continuous with the peritoneum of the pelvic cavity.

perimetry.definition: A test that measures the extent and sensitivity of the visual field using a perimeter, to map peripheral vision and detect blind spots.

parietal layer.definition: A layer of a serous membrane that lines the walls of a body cavity (eg, parietal pleura, parietal peritoneum, parietal pericardium), in contrast to the visceral layer that covers the organs.

perineal artery.definition: A branch of the internal pudendal artery that supplies the perineum; it gives off posterior scrotal (labial) arteries and supplies the perineal muscles and skin.

perineal care.definition: A procedure to cleanse the external genital and anal area to prevent infection and maintain skin integrity, typically performed for patients who are incontinent or immobile; usually involves gentle washing with warm water and mild soap, followed by thorough drying.

perineal pad.definition: A disposable absorbent pad worn in the perineal area to collect blood, lochia, urine, or wound drainage and protect the skin in the perineal region (commonly used postpartum after childbirth).

perineal raphe.definition: A midline seam on the perineum marking the embryologic fusion of the urogenital folds; in males it extends from the anus anteriorly along the perineum to the scrotum and penis, and in females it is a faint midline line from the anus toward the vaginal vestibule.

perineostomy.definition: A surgical creation of a perineal stoma to divert urine or stool.

perineocele.definition: A herniation of pelvic contents into the perineal space through a defect in the pelvic floor, presenting as a bulge in the perineum; often due to pelvic floor weakness or prior obstetric/anal trauma.

perineorrhaphy.definition: A surgical repair of the perineum, typically performed after childbirth trauma (e.g., episiotomy or perineal tear) to restore the integrity of the perineal tissues by suturing the muscles and mucosa.

perineotomy.definition: A surgical incision into the perineal region, typically made to expose or access the anorectal area or pelvic floor for operative procedures.

perinephric abscess.definition: A collection of purulent material in the perinephric space (between the renal capsule and Gerota's fascia) caused by bacterial infection, typically arising from pyelonephritis or renal/urinary tract infections; presents with fever, flank pain, and tenderness and is treated with antibiotics and drainage.

perinephric fat.definition: A layer of fat surrounding the kidney, contained within the renal fascia (Gerota's fascia); it cushions and insulates the kidney and helps anchor it in place.

perinephrium.definition: The connective tissue surrounding the kidney, including the renal capsule, perirenal (perinephric) fat, and the surrounding renal fascia (Gerota's fascia) that encloses the kidney within the perirenal space.

posterior scrotal artery.definition: Arteries supplying the posterior aspect of the scrotum, usually branches of the perineal branch of the internal pudendal artery, supplying the posterior scrotal skin and dartos and forming anastomoses with the anterior scrotal arteries from the external pudendal.

labial artery.definition: A vessel that supplies the lips; typically a pair arising from the facial artery—the superior (upper lip) and inferior (lower lip) branches—and forming an anastomosis with each other.

arcuate ligaments.definition: Fibrous arches of the diaphragm formed by fascia on the posterior abdominal wall: the median arcuate ligament across the aorta, the medial arcuate ligament over the psoas major, and the lateral arcuate ligament over the quadratus lumborum; they reinforce the posterior diaphragm and help delineate the diaphragmatic hiatuses.

arteriovenography.definition: A radiographic imaging study in which contrast material is injected into the arterial system to visualize arteries and assess their anatomy and pathology, used to detect occlusion, stenosis, aneurysm, or vascular malformations.

furcation.definition: The area on a multirooted tooth where the roots diverge into two or more branches.

fibrous.definition: Relating to fibrous tissue; consisting of dense collagen-rich connective tissue that provides structural support; typically tough and stringy.

crevice.definition: A narrow opening or crack in a solid surface.

depth.definition: The distance from the surface inward to the deepest involved part of a tissue or organ; used to describe how far a lesion, wound, or instrument extends below the surface.

pocket.definition: A small cavity, recess, or space within tissue or an organ, often formed abnormally and capable of harboring fluid, pus, or bacteria; in dentistry, it refers to a pathologically deepened gingival sulcus caused by detachment of the gum from the tooth.

probe.definition: A slender diagnostic or surgical instrument used to explore or examine a body cavity, wound, or lumen; often blunt-tipped to minimize tissue injury and used to locate structures, test patency, or determine depth.

peridental.definition: Relating to the tissues surrounding a tooth; pertaining to the periodontium, including the gingiva, periodontal ligament, cementum, and alveolar bone.

periosteal.definition: Relating to the periosteum, the dense, vascular membrane that covers the outer surface of bones (except at joints) and participates in bone growth and repair.

perichondrial.definition: Relating to the layer surrounding cartilage that provides nutrients to cartilage and contains cells involved in its growth and repair.

perinodal.definition: Around a lymph node; located in the tissue surrounding a lymph node.

pudendal.definition: Relating to the pudendum (external genitalia) or to the pudendal nerve and its vessels supplying the perineal region.

apical.definition: Relating to the apex (tip) of a structure; located at or near the tip.

intrabony.definition: Inside or within bone; located within osseous tissue (as opposed to outside or on the surface of bone).

infrabony.definition: Located beneath the bone or below the level of bone; in dentistry, describing osseous defects where the base of the defect lies apical to the surrounding alveolar bone crest.

intraalveolar.definition: Located within an alveolus; occurring inside an alveolar space, such as the alveolus of the lung or a dental alveolus (tooth socket).

suprabony.definition: Relating to or occurring above the crest of the alveolar bone; in periodontics, a periodontal pocket whose base is coronal to the bone crest, typically due to horizontal bone loss.

supracrestal.definition: Situated above a crest; in dentistry, describing tissues located coronal to the alveolar bone crest, including gingival and connective tissue attachments that make up the biologic width.

subgingival.definition: Situated below the gingival margin; located beneath the gumline.

thoracolumbar.definition: Relating to the thoracic (chest/mid-back) and lumbar (lower back) regions of the spine; pertaining to the thoracolumbar junction where the thoracic and lumbar vertebrae meet.

picc.definition: A long, slender catheter inserted into a peripheral vein (usually in the upper arm) and advanced to a central vein (typically the superior vena cava) to provide long-term intravenous access for medications, fluids, parenteral nutrition, or repeated blood draws.

growth.definition: The process of increase in size or number of cells, resulting in enlargement of a tissue, organ, or organism; used to describe normal developmental growth as well as pathological growth such as tumors.

factors.definition: Elements or variables that contribute to an outcome or condition in medicine; in context, “risk factors” are characteristics that increase disease likelihood, and “coagulation factors” are plasma proteins involved in the blood-clotting cascade.

filarial.definition: Of or relating to filariae, threadlike parasitic nematodes that cause filariasis in humans.

multinucleated.definition: Having more than one nucleus per cell; a characteristic of certain cell types (e.g., skeletal muscle fibers, osteoclasts) and of multinucleated giant cells formed by macrophage fusion.

mononuclear.definition: Having a single nucleus per cell; commonly used to describe lymphocytes and monocytes in blood or tissue infiltrates, as opposed to polymorphonuclear leukocytes which have multilobed nuclei.

phagocytes.definition: Cells that can ingest other cells, bacteria, and foreign particles.

periodontist.definition: A dental specialist who focuses on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases of the gums and other supporting structures of the teeth, and on the placement of dental implants.

ossifying.definition: Undergoing ossification; turning into bone or forming bone tissue through the process of bone formation (ossification), occurring via intramembranous or endochondral pathways.

sessile.definition: Attached directly by a broad base without a stalk; describes a lesion or polyp that is flat or broad-based rather than pedunculated.

mineralized.definition: Having minerals deposited within tissue, causing hardening; typically calcium salts deposited in the extracellular matrix (calcification).

pyogenic.definition: Pus-producing; describes infections that form pus (suppuration), typically caused by bacteria that provoke pus formation.

giant.definition: An adjective meaning abnormally large in size; in medical contexts, used to describe unusually large cells or structures—such as multinucleated cells formed by macrophage fusion—and to characterize diseases or lesions involving such large cells.

polyneuropathy.definition: A disorder in which multiple peripheral nerves are damaged, usually in a symmetric, length-dependent distribution (stocking-glove), causing distal sensory symptoms (numbness, tingling, pain) and often weakness; etiologies include diabetes, alcoholism, nutritional deficiencies, toxins, autoimmune conditions, and inherited neuropathies.

solution.definition: An orderly, homogeneous liquid consisting of a solvent with dissolved substances; in medical contexts, a sterile liquid preparation intended for administration, containing dissolved substances.

equilibration.definition: The process by which two compartments or a system reach chemical and physical balance, with equal concentrations, partial pressures, or chemical potentials across a barrier.

sorbitol.definition: A crystalline sugar alcohol used as a sweetening agent.

perinephric.definition: Around the kidney; pertaining to the perirenal space within the renal fascia that surrounds the kidney and contains fat.

retroperitoneal.definition: Located behind the peritoneum; the retroperitoneal space contains structures that lie posterior to the peritoneal lining, such as the kidneys, adrenal glands, pancreas (head and body), portions of the duodenum, the aorta and inferior vena cava, ureters, and parts of the colon.

small.definition: Relatively smaller than normal size; used to describe measurements that are below the reference range for a tissue, organ, or population.

virchow.definition: The triad of factors that predispose to thrombosis: endothelial injury, blood stasis or turbulent flow, and hypercoagulability.

robin.definition: A congenital condition characterized by micrognathia (small jaw) with glossoptosis (posterior displacement of the tongue) and often cleft palate, which can cause airway obstruction.

spaces.definition: A natural cavity or potential gap between body structures (such as fascia or tissues) that can contain organs, vessels, air, or fluids; some spaces are real cavities, while others are potential spaces that may become evident when tissue planes separate or when disease or injury introduces contents.

perivascular.definition: Situated around a blood vessel; surrounding or adjacent to a vessel.

bacteroides.definition: A genus of Gram-negative, anaerobic, non-spore-forming bacilli that are a major component of the normal human gut flora; some species are opportunistic pathogens, capable of causing intra-abdominal infections, abscesses, and bacteremia when displaced from the gut, and they may produce beta-lactamase contributing to antibiotic resistance.

fusobacterium.definition: A genus of Gram-negative, obligate anaerobic, non-spore-forming bacilli that are slender and fusiform in shape; they inhabit the human oral, dental, gastrointestinal, and genital tracts and can cause polymicrobial infections ranging from periodontal and cervicofacial infections to systemic diseases such as Lemierre syndrome.

peroneal muscular atrophy.definition: A wasting and weakness of the muscles innervated by the peroneal (fibular) nerve, especially the anterior and lateral leg muscles and intrinsic foot muscles, usually due to peroneal neuropathy (often from compression at the fibular head), frequently with foot drop and sensory loss on the dorsum of the foot.

head lice.definition: Infestation of the scalp by tiny parasitic insects (Pediculus humanus capitis) that feed on blood from the scalp. It spreads mainly through close contact or sharing personal items; diagnosis is by finding live lice or nits attached to hair near the scalp, and treatment includes topical pediculicides (permethrin, pyrethrin), thorough combing to remove nits, and laundering of bedding and clothing to prevent reinfestation.

nits.definition: Eggs laid by female head lice, attached to hair shafts near the scalp; they are small, oval, white to yellowish, about 0.8 mm long, and hatch in about 7–10 days.

pyrethroids.definition: A class of synthetic insecticides that are chemically related to natural pyrethrins and act on the insect nervous system by prolonging the opening of voltage-gated sodium channels, causing repetitive nerve firing, paralysis, and death; they generally have relatively low mammalian toxicity but can cause neurotoxic symptoms with significant exposure.

chrysanthemum flowers.definition: A genus of flowering plants in the Asteraceae family (daisy family), commonly cultivated for ornamental blooms; some species are used in traditional medicines and herbal teas, but these plants can cause allergic reactions, contact dermatitis, or pollen sensitivity in susceptible individuals.

stinging.definition: A brief, sharp, pricking or burning sensation on the skin or mucous membranes, typically caused by contact with irritants, stinging insects or their venom, or nerve irritation.

discomfort.definition: A subjective sensation of mild physical or psychological unease; an unpleasant feeling that is less severe than pain and may be localized or generalized.

scalp rash.definition: A skin rash on the scalp presenting with redness, itching, scaling, and/or crusting; caused by a range of conditions, most commonly seborrheic dermatitis, contact dermatitis, psoriasis, or fungal infection (eg, tinea capitis). Management targets the underlying cause and may include medicated shampoos, topical corticosteroids, or antifungal agents.

permissible exposure limit.definition: A regulatory limit on the concentration of a hazardous substance in workplace air that workers may be exposed to without adverse health effects, typically expressed as an 8-hour time-weighted average or a 15-minute short-term exposure limit, established by occupational safety agencies (e.g., OSHA).

pel.definition: Not a recognized standalone medical term. If you meant “pelvis” or “pelvic,” I can define that.

osha.definition: A U.S. federal agency within the Department of Labor that establishes and enforces workplace safety and health standards, conducts inspections, and provides education and compliance assistance to reduce hazards and injuries.

niosh.definition: A U.S. federal agency within the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) that conducts research on occupational safety and health and issues evidence-based recommendations to prevent work-related injury and illness.

volutrauma.definition: Lung injury caused by overdistension of alveoli due to large tidal volumes during mechanical ventilation, a component of ventilator-induced lung injury.

white blood cell count.definition: Measurement of the number of leukocytes per unit volume of blood, used to evaluate immune status and to help diagnose infection, inflammation, bone marrow disorders, and hematologic malignancies. Normal adult range is roughly 4,000–11,000 cells per microliter.

hypersegmented.definition: Describing neutrophils with an abnormally high number of nuclear lobes (commonly more than five). It is classically seen in megaloblastic anemia due to vitamin B12 or folate deficiency.

addison anemia.definition: Anemia occurring in Addison's disease (primary adrenal insufficiency), typically mild and normocytic/normochromic, thought to reflect anemia of chronic disease related to cortisol deficiency and chronic inflammation; iron deficiency or autoimmune processes may contribute in some cases.

iron therapy.definition: Iron therapy is the medical treatment of iron deficiency or iron deficiency anemia by supplying iron, usually orally (ferrous salts) or intravenously, to replenish iron stores and restore hemoglobin synthesis.

pernicious vomiting.definition: Severe, persistent vomiting that is harmful to the patient, often causing dehydration and electrolyte disturbances; the phrase is not a standard diagnostic term in modern medical practice.

pernio.definition: A cold-induced inflammatory condition of acral skin (typically fingers and toes) that occurs after exposure to cold, damp environments; presents with painful, itchy red-to-purple papules or plaques, sometimes with blistering, due to vasospasm and an inflammatory response.

persistent vegetative state.definition: A disorder of consciousness after severe brain injury in which wakefulness persists but there is no evidence of sustained, purposeful awareness or interaction, with preserved autonomic function; the condition lasts longer than about one month.

persian gulf syndrome.definition: Chronic multisystem illness affecting some veterans of the Gulf War, characterized by persistent fatigue, widespread musculoskeletal pain, cognitive difficulties, sleep disturbance, headaches, and various other nonspecific symptoms; etiology is multifactorial and not fully understood; no single diagnostic test exists and diagnosis is based on clinical history and exclusion of other conditions.

sleep disturbances.definition: Disruptions in normal sleep patterns that cause distress or impairment in daytime functioning. They include insomnia (difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep), hypersomnia (excessive sleepiness), sleep-disordered breathing (e.g., obstructive sleep apnea), circadian rhythm disorders, parasomnias (e.g., sleepwalking, night terrors), and restless legs syndrome.

musculoskeletal diseases.definition: A broad category of disorders affecting the musculoskeletal system—the bones, joints, muscles, ligaments, tendons, and other connective tissues—causing pain, weakness, reduced mobility, deformity, or functional impairment; these conditions can be inflammatory, degenerative, traumatic, metabolic, or congenital in origin.

connective tissue diseases.definition: A group of autoimmune or inflammatory disorders that primarily involve connective tissues—such as skin, joints, tendons, blood vessels, and internal organs—leading to inflammation, fibrosis, vasculopathy, and organ dysfunction. Examples include systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis (scleroderma), polymyositis/dermatomyositis, and mixed connective tissue disease.

insecticides.definition: Substances, chemical or biological agents, used to kill or suppress insects; employed in pest control, agriculture, and public health to reduce insect-borne diseases.

parapertussis.definition: A respiratory infection caused by Bordetella parapertussis that resembles pertussis but is typically milder, presenting with a paroxysmal cough and infrequent or absent whoop; transmitted via respiratory droplets and treated with macrolide antibiotics.

nasopharyngeal secretions.definition: Secretions from the mucous membranes of the nasopharynx (the upper part of the pharynx behind the nasal cavity), comprising mucus that humidifies and traps particles; they may be clear, mucoid, or purulent depending on irritation or infection and can be collected as a diagnostic specimen via nasopharyngeal swab.

sneezing.definition: A reflexive, forceful expulsion of air through the nose and mouth triggered by irritation of the nasal mucosa (e.g., dust, allergens, pathogens); serves to remove irritants and secretions from the upper airway.

listlessness.definition: A state of persistent fatigue and reduced energy or motivation, often with indifference or lethargy; may occur with sleep deprivation, illness, anemia, hypothyroidism, infections, or mood disorders such as depression.

facial redness.definition: Redness of the skin on the face caused by dilation of superficial blood vessels, resulting from increased blood flow; common causes include heat, exertion, sun exposure, embarrassment, inflammatory skin conditions (e.g., rosacea, dermatitis), allergic reactions, and infections.

paroxysmal cough.definition: A sudden, explosive coughing spell consisting of a rapid series of coughs in quick succession, often with a brief inspiratory phase.

catarrhal.definition: Relating to catarrh; an inflammation of mucous membranes with increased mucus production, typically presenting as nasal or throat discharge.

fluorescent antibody staining.definition: A laboratory technique in which antibodies labeled with fluorescent dyes bind to specific antigens in cells or tissues, allowing visualization under a fluorescence microscope. It can be direct (a fluorophore-conjugated primary antibody) or indirect (an unlabeled primary antibody detected with a fluorophore-labeled secondary antibody).

immune_globulin.definition: An immunoglobulin (antibody) is a glycoprotein produced by plasma cells that recognizes a specific antigen and mediates immune defense through neutralization, opsonization, and activation of the complement system; there are five main classes: IgG, IgA, IgM, IgD, and IgE.

respiratory_infections.definition: Infections of the respiratory tract caused by pathogens (most commonly viruses; bacteria or fungi less often) that affect the upper airways (nose, sinuses, throat, larynx) or lower airways (trachea, bronchi, lungs), including illnesses such as the common cold, sinusitis, pharyngitis, laryngitis, bronchitis, influenza, and pneumonia.

intravenous_therapy.definition: Administration of fluids, medications, or nutrients directly into a vein via an IV line or cannula, to provide hydration, correct electrolyte or nutritional deficiencies, or deliver therapeutic agents; can be given continuously or intermittent.

thick_mucus.definition: Viscous secretions produced by mucous membranes that are thicker than normal; often due to dehydration or inflammatory states (e.g., viral or bacterial infections, allergies, irritants like smoke) and can cause congestion and hinder mucociliary clearance.

pertussis_vaccine.definition: A vaccine that protects against pertussis (whooping cough) by inducing immunity to Bordetella pertussis; it is usually administered as part of combination vaccines (DTaP in children and Tdap as a booster in adolescence or adulthood) to prevent illness and reduce transmission.

induration.definition: Hardening or thickening of tissue; a palpable, firm area in skin or subcutaneous tissue, often due to inflammation, fibrosis, edema, or infiltration.

autism_spectrum_disorders.definition: A group of neurodevelopmental conditions characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and social interaction across contexts, along with restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities; symptoms typically appear in early childhood and cause functional impairment. The spectrum includes a range of severities and, historically, included diagnoses such as autistic disorder, Asperger syndrome, and PDD-NOS, now subsumed under Autism Spectrum Disorder.

peutz_jeghers_syndrome.definition: A rare autosomal dominant genetic syndrome characterized by mucocutaneous pigmented macules—most often on the lips and oral mucosa—and multiple hamartomatous polyps throughout the gastrointestinal tract (especially the small intestine), with an increased lifetime risk of gastrointestinal and other cancers; caused by pathogenic variants in the STK11 (LKB1) gene.

subarachnoid_hemorrhage.definition: A hemorrhagic stroke that occurs when a blood vessel on the surface of the brain bursts and bleeds into the space between the brain and the skull; usually caused by an aneurysm or other blood vessel malformation.

subconjunctival_hemorrhage.definition: A rupture of a small conjunctival vessel causing a bright red patch on the white of the eye; typically painless, noninfectious, and self-limiting, usually resolving within 1–2 weeks without treatment.

prolapsed_rectum.definition: A condition in which part or all of the rectal wall protrudes through the anal opening; mucosal prolapse involves only the lining, whereas full-thickness prolapse involves the entire wall, typically related to pelvic floor weakness or chronic straining.

pestis.definition: A plague; a highly infectious bacterial disease caused by Yersinia pestis, transmitted by fleas (and through contact with infected animals), with forms including bubonic, septicemic, and pneumonic plague. Historically associated with major outbreaks.

bubonic_plague.definition: An acute infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, transmitted to humans by fleas from infected rodents, presenting with sudden fever, malaise, and painful swollen lymph nodes (buboes); without treatment it can progress to septicemic or pneumonic forms and may be fatal, but is treatable with prompt antibiotic therapy.

endophthalmitis.definition: An inflammation of the intraocular tissues, especially the vitreous and aqueous humor, caused by infectious organisms (most often bacteria or fungi), typically occurring after intraocular surgery or penetrating trauma and presenting with eye pain, redness, decreased vision, and sometimes a hypopyon; a sight-threatening emergency requiring urgent treatment.

phacoanaphylactica.definition: An uncommon immune‑mediated intraocular inflammatory reaction to lens proteins released during cataract extraction (phacoemulsification), typically occurring weeks after surgery and may mimic endophthalmitis; treatment includes removal of lens material and aggressive anti‑inflammatory therapy (e.g., corticosteroids).

phacocele.definition: A herniation of the crystalline lens through a ruptured ocular coat (usually a corneal or scleral wound), typically following trauma, with lens material protruding into or through the wound.

phacocyst.definition: A cyst related to the crystalline lens of the eye—a fluid-filled sac in or adjacent to the lens.

phacoglaucoma.definition: A secondary form of glaucoma that occurs in relation to cataract surgery (phacoemulsification), typically due to postoperative inflammation, corticosteroid response, or lens- or surgery-related changes that impair aqueous humor outflow.

phacomatosis.definition: A hereditary neurocutaneous syndrome in which tumors or hamartomatous lesions arise in the skin, nervous system, and eyes, often with characteristic ocular and cutaneous findings (examples include neurofibromatosis, tuberous sclerosis, Sturge-Weber, and von Hippel-Lindau disease).

phaeohyphomycosis.definition: A spectrum of fungal infections caused by pigmented (dematiaceous) fungi, characterized histologically by pigmented, septate hyphae in tissue; presentations range from subcutaneous or cutaneous lesions to disseminated disease, especially in immunocompromised hosts.

phage.definition: A virus that infects bacteria; a particle containing nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) inside a protein capsid, often with a tail. It attaches to a bacterial cell, injects its genome, uses the host's machinery to replicate, and typically lyses the bacterial cell to release new virions.

phage_typing.definition: Phage typing is a laboratory method that characterizes bacterial strains by their susceptibility patterns to a panel of bacteriophages, enabling differentiation of strains within a species for epidemiologic typing.

phagosome.definition: A vesicle formed during phagocytosis when a cell membrane encloses a particle to internalize it; the phagosome then fuses with lysosomes to form a phagolysosome where the particle is degraded.

phagocytic.definition: Relating to phagocytosis; describing cells that engulf and digest particulate material, such as bacteria, dead cells, or debris (e.g., neutrophils and macrophages).

pet_scan.definition: An imaging test that looks at how your body is working. Also called a positron emission tomography scan.

peyers_patches.definition: Aggregations of gut-associated lymphoid tissue located in the distal ileum; these lymphoid follicles sample luminal antigens via M cells and initiate mucosal immune responses, contributing to intestinal humoral and cellular immunity.

pubic_bone.definition: The anterior portion of the pelvic (hip) bone; one of the three fused components of the pelvis, with the two sides joining at the pubic symphysis to form the front of the pelvis.

cervical_incompetence.definition: A condition in pregnancy where the cervix weakens and can prematurely dilate (without contractions), leading to recurrent second-trimester miscarriages or preterm birth; often diagnosed by history or a short cervix on ultrasound and managed with cerclage in selected cases.

uterine_prolapse.definition: Happens when the womb (uterus) falls down and presses on the vaginal area.

retroversion.definition: Backward turning or backward displacement of an organ from its normal position; most often refers to the uterus tilting posteriorly toward the spine rather than forward.

smith_hodge_pessary.definition: A vaginal pessary described for nonoperative management of pelvic organ prolapse; a medical device inserted into the vagina to provide mechanical support to the uterus and vaginal apex, relieving prolapse symptoms and allowing function without surgery, typically fitted and maintained by a clinician and removed/cleaned regularly.

gellhorn_pessary.definition: A vaginal pessary consisting of a rigid ring with a stem, designed to support the uterus or vaginal apex in pelvic organ prolapse; fitted by a clinician and maintained with regular cleaning and periodic removal as needed.

doughnut_pessary.definition: A donut-shaped vaginal pessary that encircles the cervix and provides circumferential support to the pelvic organs in vaginal or uterine prolapse; a non-surgical device fitted by a clinician and worn to relieve prolapse symptoms, requiring regular cleaning/removal and monitoring for irritation or discharge.

inflatable_pessary.definition: A vaginal prosthesis used to support pelvic organs in pelvic organ prolapse; a pessary with an inflatable rim or balloon that is filled with fluid (or air) to adjust fit and provide elevation and stabilization, inserted through the vagina and managed by a clinician.

bee_cell_pessary.definition: A vaginal pessary is a medical device inserted into the vagina to support pelvic organs (such as the uterus, bladder, or rectum) and relieve symptoms of pelvic organ prolapse or urinary incontinence; it comes in various shapes (ring, doughnut, or other designs) and is fitted by a clinician for ongoing use.

posterior_vaginal_fornix.definition: A recess of the vaginal canal located behind the cervix, formed by the posterior vaginal wall and the posterior surface of the cervix; it is the deepest part of the vaginal fornices and lies anterior to the rectouterine (pouch of Douglas).

petrosal_sinuses.definition: Two dural venous sinuses in the petrous part of the temporal bone: the superior petrosal sinus drains the cavernous sinus into the transverse sinus, and the inferior petrosal sinus drains the cavernous sinus into the internal jugular vein.

petrosphenoidal_fissure.definition: A small skull-base fissure at the junction of the petrous part of the temporal bone and the body of the sphenoid, through which the nerve of the pterygoid canal (Vidian nerve) and its accompanying vessels pass.

petrous.definition: Relating to stone or rock-like; in anatomy, describing the dense, hard portion of the temporal bone at the skull base that houses the inner ear structures.

petroleum_distillate_poisoning.definition: Poisoning from exposure to hydrocarbon solvents found in petroleum distillates (e.g., gasoline, kerosene, mineral spirits), typically via ingestion or inhalation, presenting with mucous membrane irritation, CNS effects, and, if aspiration occurs, chemical pneumonitis/aspiration pneumonia; management is supportive and avoids gastric decontamination or emesis due to aspiration risk.

pessary_management.definition: Care approach for using a vaginal pessary to support pelvic organs in pelvic organ prolapse or urinary incontinence; includes pessary selection and sizing, proper insertion and removal, cleaning/hygiene, patient education, regular follow-up, and management of complications (e.g., vaginal irritation or discharge).

phagocytize.definition: To engulf and digest foreign particles, bacteria, or cellular debris by phagocytes through the process of phagocytosis.

phagolysosome.definition: An intracellular vesicle formed by the fusion of a phagosome with a lysosome, containing hydrolytic enzymes and an acidic environment that digest engulfed microbes and debris.

microphakia.definition: An abnormally small crystalline lens of the eye, typically congenital and sometimes seen with nanophthalmos; it causes high hyperopia and reduced accommodation, and may be associated with a shallow anterior chamber.

pseudophakia.definition: The state of the eye in which the natural crystalline lens has been removed and replaced with an artificial intraocular lens (IOL), typically after cataract extraction.

phakomatosis.definition: A group of hereditary neuro-oculo-cutaneous disorders characterized by multisystem hamartomas or benign tumors involving the skin, eyes, and brain; examples include neurofibromatosis, tuberous sclerosis, von Hippel-Lindau disease, and Sturge–Weber syndrome.

phakomatoses.definition: A group of inherited neuro‑oculo‑cutaneous syndromes characterized by congenital or early‑onset hamartomatous lesions involving the eye, skin, and central nervous system (reflecting abnormal development of neural crest–derived tissues). Examples include neurofibromatosis type 1 and 2, tuberous sclerosis complex, von Hippel‑Lindau disease, and Sturge‑Weber syndrome.

phalangeal.definition: Relating to the phalanges, the bones of the fingers and toes.

phallus.definition: Anatomical term for the male external genital organ (the penis), used for urination and sexual intercourse; the term can also be used as a symbol or generic reference to male genitalia.

phalloplasty.definition: A surgery that creates or modifies a penis; sometimes referred to as penis enlargement.

phalloidin.definition: A cyclic peptide toxin from Amanita phalloides (death cap) that binds filamentous actin (F‑actin) and stabilizes actin filaments, preventing depolymerization and disrupting the cytoskeleton; highly toxic when ingested (also used in research when conjugated to fluorophores for actin labeling).

phallodynia.definition: Pain in the penis; a symptom that can result from infections, inflammatory conditions, trauma, or neuropathic/pelvic pain syndromes affecting the genitalia.

phallocampsis.definition: An obscure or obsolete term denoting a penile deformity, typically a curvature or abnormal bending of the erect penis.

pharyngoscope.definition: An instrument for examining and visualizing the pharynx (throat), typically using a mirror, rigid pharyngoscope, or flexible endoscope to inspect the nasopharynx and oropharynx.

pharyngoscopy.definition: A procedure for visually inspecting the pharynx (throat) using a pharyngoscope, mirror, or endoscope to evaluate the nasopharynx and oropharynx for inflammation, lesions, or other pathology.

pharyngoplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair or reconstruct the pharynx (throat), typically to restore or improve swallowing or airway function after injury, cancer, or congenital defects.

pharyngoconjunctival fever.definition: A contagious febrile illness caused by adenovirus infection, presenting with acute fever, sore throat (pharyngitis), and conjunctivitis; often with malaise and lymphadenopathy, commonly linked to swimming-pool–related outbreaks and typically self-limited over 1–2 weeks.

pharyngoesophageal constriction.definition: An abnormal narrowing at the pharyngoesophageal junction (the upper esophageal sphincter) that can impede swallowing, often due to cricopharyngeal dysfunction or fibrosis.

pharyngotonsillitis.definition: Inflammation or infection of the pharynx and palatine tonsils (often presenting with sore throat and fever); most cases are viral, but bacterial causes (notably group A Streptococcus) can occur and may require antibiotic treatment.

pharyngeal recess.definition: A small mucosal recess in the nasopharynx behind the opening of the pharyngotympanic (Eustachian) tube, bounded by the torus tubarius and the posterior pharyngeal wall; a potential space within the pharynx.

pharyngeal nerve.definition: Pharyngeal nerve refers to the pharyngeal branches of the vagus nerve (CN X) that form the pharyngeal plexus; they provide motor innervation to most pharyngeal muscles and sensory innervation to the mucosa of the pharynx (stylopharyngeus is supplied by CN IX).

gag reflex.definition: A protective reflex triggered by stimulation of the oropharynx (especially the soft palate or posterior tongue) that causes brief contraction of the muscles of the soft palate, pharynx, and larynx to prevent aspiration; mediated by afferent input via the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) and efferent output via the vagus nerve (CN X).

adenovirus.definition: A nonenveloped, double-stranded DNA virus of the family Adenoviridae that commonly causes self-limited respiratory infections, conjunctivitis, pharyngitis, and gastroenteritis, transmitted by respiratory droplets, direct contact, and the fecal-oral route; there are many serotypes.

streptococcal infection.definition: An infection caused by Streptococcus bacteria, most commonly Streptococcus pyogenes (group A). It can affect the throat, skin, lungs, or other sites and may lead to complications such as rheumatic fever or post‑streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

phantom limb syndrome.definition: A condition in which a person continues to perceive sensations, including pain, in a limb that has been amputated, arising from ongoing neural activity in the residual limb and cortical reorganization of the brain’s body representation.

phantom tumor.definition: An apparent lesion on radiographic imaging that mimics a tumor but is not a true neoplasm—a radiologic pseudo-tumor due to artifacts or benign transient processes (e.g., atelectasis, pleural effusion, or overlapping structures) that typically resolves or is clarified on follow-up imaging.

phantom vision.definition: An experience of vision without a corresponding external stimulus; a form of visual hallucination that can include flashes, shapes, or formed images and may occur with retinal or optic pathway disease, migraines, epilepsy, or after significant vision loss (as in Charles Bonnet syndrome).

pseudohallucination.definition: A perception-like experience that resembles a hallucination in vividness but is recognized by the person as unreal and self-generated, with preserved reality testing and without external sensory stimulation.

pseudesthesia.definition: A subjective, illusory sensory perception (such as tingling, burning, or numbness) that a patient reports despite no external stimulus or objective sensory loss being demonstrable.

allophasis.definition: A language disorder characterized by impaired ability to speak or understand language, typically due to brain injury or disease.

heterophasis.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. Could you confirm the spelling or provide context (field or a sentence where you saw it)? If you meant a similar term like heterophasia or heterophasia, I can define that instead.

paraphemia.definition: There is no widely recognized medical term by that name in standard medical dictionaries.

dysphemia.definition: The use of a harsh, offensive, or disparaging term in place of a neutral one; the opposite of euphemism.

spasmophemia.definition: An obsolete term referring to neuromuscular hyperexcitability with a tendency to muscle spasms (tetany), typically due to electrolyte disturbances such as hypocalcemia; symptoms include paresthesias, tingling around the mouth, cramps, and carpopedal spasm, potentially progressing to seizures in severe cases.

phenylalaninemia.definition: A condition defined by an abnormally high concentration of the amino acid phenylalanine in the blood, most often due to impaired conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine (as in phenylketonuria). If untreated, it can lead to neurodevelopmental delay and other neurologic complications; management typically involves lifelong restriction of phenylalanine intake and regular monitoring.

phenazopyridine.definition: An oral urinary tract analgesic that provides symptomatic relief of dysuria, urinary frequency, and urgency from urinary tract irritation; it does not treat infection and is used for short-term relief. It often causes orange-red discoloration of the urine.

phenoxybenzamine.definition: An irreversible, nonselective alpha-adrenergic antagonist that covalently binds α1 and α2 receptors, causing long-lasting vasodilation; used preoperatively to prevent hypertensive crises in pheochromocytoma.

phentolamine.definition: A reversible, nonselective alpha-adrenergic antagonist that blocks alpha-1 and alpha-2 receptors, producing vasodilation; used to treat hypertensive crises from catecholamine excess (e.g., pheochromocytoma) and as an antidote for vasopressor extravasation.

phendimetrazine.definition: A CNS stimulant anorectic used for short-term treatment of obesity; it is a prodrug of phenmetrazine that increases central sympathetic activity to suppress appetite.

phentermine.definition: A prescription sympathomimetic appetite suppressant (stimulant) used for short-term weight management in obesity or overweight; it works by increasing norepinephrine release in the hypothalamus to reduce appetite, and is typically prescribed for a limited period (often up to 12 weeks).

risperidone.definition: A second-generation (atypical) antipsychotic used to treat schizophrenia, bipolar I disorder, and irritability associated with autism; it primarily antagonizes dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors.

normetanephrine.definition: A metabolite of norepinephrine formed by catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT); used as a biomarker in plasma or urine to screen for pheochromocytoma and other catecholamine-secreting tumors. Elevated levels suggest excess norepinephrine activity but can be influenced by medications, stress, and renal function.

metanephrine.definition: A catecholamine metabolite of epinephrine produced by catechol-O-methyltransferase; measured in plasma or urine as a biomarker for pheochromocytoma and other catecholamine-secreting tumors.

methyltyrosine.definition: A competitive inhibitor of tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting enzyme in catecholamine synthesis; the alpha-methyl derivative of tyrosine that decreases production of catecholamines (norepinephrine and epinephrine) and is used clinically to manage pheochromocytoma by reducing catecholamine levels preoperatively.

venesection.definition: The withdrawal of blood from a vein, usually by needle puncture, for diagnostic testing or therapeutic reduction of blood volume (phlebotomy).

phlebotomize.definition: To perform phlebotomy; to puncture a vein and draw blood, typically for diagnostic testing or therapeutic purposes.

phlebostasis.definition: Venous stasis; slowing or stoppage of venous blood flow, leading to pooling of blood in the veins, often due to obstruction, valve dysfunction, or external compression; may contribute to edema and thrombosis.

phlebostenosis.definition: A narrowing of a vein (venous stenosis) that impedes venous blood flow; can be congenital or acquired (e.g., due to thrombosis, inflammation, or external compression).

phlebogram.definition: An X-ray image of a vein obtained by venography after injection of contrast material, used to visualize the venous system and detect abnormalities such as thrombosis or obstruction.

phlebography.definition: A radiologic examination of the venous system obtained after injection of iodinated contrast, enabling visualization of veins to detect conditions such as venous thrombosis, obstruction, or valvular insufficiency.

venogram.definition: A radiographic imaging study in which a contrast agent is injected into the venous system to visualize veins, allowing assessment of venous patency and detection of thrombosis or other venous abnormalities.

phocomelus.definition: A congenital limb deficiency in which the proximal segment is formed while the distal parts are absent or severely underdeveloped, resulting in a shortened, flipper-like limb; often linked to early teratogenic exposure (e.g., thalidomide) during limb development.

phialophora.definition: A genus of dematiaceous (melanized) fungi in the family Herpotrichiellaceae; environmental saprophytes that can cause subcutaneous infections such as chromoblastomycosis and phaeohyphomycosis in humans.

erythroblasts.definition: Nucleated precursors of red blood cells in the bone marrow during erythropoiesis; they synthesize hemoglobin and progressively mature through stages before extruding the nucleus to form reticulocytes.

megakaryoblasts.definition: A large bone marrow progenitor cell of the megakaryocyte lineage that originates from hematopoietic stem cells and differentiates into a megakaryocyte; it undergoes endomitosis, becoming polyploid, and ultimately gives rise to platelets.

palpitation.definition: An awareness of one's heartbeat, often described as pounding, fluttering, or a rapid or irregular heartbeat.

hemodynamics.definition: The study of blood flow and the forces that govern circulation, including how cardiac output, arterial and venous pressures, and vascular resistance determine tissue perfusion; it uses principles such as flow = pressure gradient / resistance to relate pressure differences, resistance, and flow.

urticarial.definition: Relating to urticaria (hives); characterized by itchy, transient wheals on the skin due to dermal edema and superficial vascular dilation.

phonocardiograph.definition: A device that records heart sounds (phonocardiography) by converting acoustic signals from the chest into an audible or graphic trace for analysis of cardiac function and murmurs.

phonocardiography.definition: A technique for recording the sounds and murmurs generated by the heart with a microphone or transducer to produce a phonocardiogram for analysis of heart sound timing, intensity, and frequency.

phonocardiogram.definition: A graphic recording of the audible heart sounds and murmurs produced by phonocardiography, depicting the timing and relative intensity of events such as S1, S2, and any murmurs.

electrocardiophonograph.definition: An historical instrument that records the heart's electrical activity on a phonographic medium; essentially an electrocardiograph whose output was stored or played back on a phonograph.

rockymountainspottedfever.definition: A tick-borne rickettsial infection caused by Rickettsia rickettsii, transmitted by Dermacentor ticks; it typically presents with fever, headache, malaise, and a characteristic rapidly spreading petechial rash, and can be life-threatening if untreated, usually treated with doxycycline.

reiterssyndrome.definition: Joint problems triggered by bacterial or viral infection elsewhere in the body.

endstage.definition: Final, advanced phase of a chronic illness marked by irreversible organ dysfunction and progressive functional decline, with limited or no curative options and a high likelihood of death; care is typically palliative.

phosphatide.definition: A class of lipids that contain a phosphate group and are major components of cell membranes; typically glycerol-based with two fatty acid chains and a phosphate-containing head group (for example, phosphatidylcholine, phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylserine, and phosphatidylinositol).

phospholipid.definition: A lipid containing a phosphate group, typically composed of a glycerol backbone with two fatty acid tails and a phosphate-containing head group; it is amphipathic and forms the lipid bilayer of cell membranes, providing structure and mediating membrane dynamics and signaling.

phospholipase.definition: An enzyme that hydrolyzes phospholipids by cleaving a bond within the glycerophospholipid molecule, producing products such as fatty acids, lysophospholipids, diacylglycerol, or phosphatidic acid, and playing a key role in membrane remodeling and cellular signaling.

phosphoglycerate.definition: A phosphorylated derivative of glyceric acid (glycerate) in which a phosphate group is esterified to the glycerate backbone; most commonly refers to 3-phosphoglycerate, an intermediate in glycolysis and gluconeogenesis.

phosphoglyceride.definition: A glycerophospholipid comprising a glycerol backbone with two fatty acid chains and a phosphate group attached to the third carbon, typically linked to a head group (e.g., choline, ethanolamine, serine, or inositol); a major component of cellular membranes.

phosphorylation.definition: The addition of a phosphate group to a substrate, typically mediated by kinases, usually using ATP as the phosphate donor; this modification often alters the substrate's activity, function, localization, or interactions, and serves as a key mechanism of cellular regulation.

phospholipidtransferprotein.definition: An extracellular lipid-transfer protein that transfers phospholipids between lipoprotein particles, thereby remodeling HDL and influencing HDL particle size; encoded by the PLTP gene.

photic.definition: Relating to light; light-induced or light-activated.

photogenic.definition: Having features that photograph well; tending to look attractive or favorable in pictures.

phoropter.definition: An ophthalmic instrument used to determine an individual's refractive error and eyeglass prescription by presenting a series of lenses and prisms in front of the eyes during an eye exam.

autophony.definition: A condition in which a person hears their own voice, breathing, and other internal sounds abnormally loudly, due to increased transmission of sound through the ear—most commonly from a patulous Eustachian tube or other middle-ear pathology.

organophonic.definition: Not a recognized medical term; literally refers to sound produced by or related to an organ, but there is no accepted medical definition or usage in medical literature.

photophobic.definition: Relating to or characterized by sensitivity or aversion to light; a symptom where exposure to light causes discomfort or pain.

phototoxic.definition: A property of certain chemicals or drugs whereby exposure to light—often ultraviolet radiation—activates the substance to cause tissue damage and an inflammatory sunburn-like reaction; the response is non–immune-mediated.

photoreceptor.definition: A specialized retinal cell that detects light and converts it into neural signals; there are rods (dim light) and cones (color and high-acuity vision).

photorefractive.definition: Changes in the refractive index of a material caused by exposure to light; a light-induced alteration of optical properties often due to redistribution of charge carriers.

photorefractive keratectomy.definition: Laser surgery used to reshape the cornea in order to correct vision problems.

keratotomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which incisions are made into the cornea to alter its shape and refractive power; commonly refers to radial keratotomy, historically used to correct myopia but largely superseded by laser refractive surgeries.

radial keratotomy.definition: A refractive surgical procedure in which several radial corneal incisions are made to flatten the cornea and reduce myopia; once common but now largely replaced by laser refractive surgeries such as LASIK, with risks including fluctuating vision, glare, and corneal instability.

excimer laser.definition: An ultraviolet laser that uses excited excimer molecules (e.g., ArF, KrF, XeCl) to emit short, high-energy pulses, enabling precise, photochemical ablation with minimal thermal damage; widely used in ophthalmic corneal reshaping (LASIK) and in micromachining/material processing.

refractive keratotomy.definition: An older surgical procedure to correct refractive errors (primarily myopia) by making radial or arcuate corneal incisions to flatten the central cornea and change its focusing power; largely superseded by laser refractive surgeries such as LASIK or PRK.

photosensitive.definition: Having increased sensitivity to light, especially ultraviolet radiation from sunlight; exposure can provoke exaggerated or adverse reactions, often due to certain medications or medical conditions.

photostimulable phosphor.definition: A storage phosphor used in computed radiography that stores x-ray–induced energy in electron traps within the phosphor layer; when stimulated by a red laser, it emits light (photostimulated luminescence) that is detected to form a digital image.

photoscan.definition: Not a standard medical term; no universally accepted definition. If used, it may refer to a digital imaging process that converts photographs into scanned, high-resolution images for diagnostic review.

photoallergic.definition: Relating to an immune-mediated, light-activated allergic reaction in which a chemical becomes allergenic after exposure to ultraviolet or visible light, causing pruritic eczematous dermatitis in sun-exposed skin (a type IV hypersensitivity).

phototoxic reaction.definition: Nonimmune, dose-dependent skin reaction triggered by exposure to ultraviolet light in the presence of a photosensitizing agent (often a medication), resulting in exaggerated sunburn-like erythema, edema, pain, and sometimes blistering within minutes to hours.

photosensitizing.definition: Causing increased sensitivity to light, particularly ultraviolet radiation; used to describe drugs or chemicals that, after exposure to light, can provoke phototoxic or photoallergic reactions.

ultraviolet light.definition: Electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths approximately 10 to 400 nanometers, lying just beyond the visible spectrum; subdivided into UVA (315–400 nm), UVB (280–315 nm), and UVC (100–280 nm).

phycomycosis.definition: An invasive fungal infection caused by zygomycete molds (order Mucorales); historically termed phycomycosis, it is an opportunistic infection seen in immunocompromised patients and is characterized by rapid tissue necrosis and angioinvasion (often presenting as rhinocerebral, pulmonary, or cutaneous disease).

phrenic ganglion.definition: Not a recognized anatomical structure; the phrenic nerve (from C3–C5) provides motor innervation to the diaphragm and carries sensory fibers, but there is no ganglion along or associated with this nerve.

phrenic plexus.definition: A neural plexus formed by branches of the phrenic nerve around the diaphragm, supplying motor innervation to the diaphragm and sensory innervation to the diaphragmatic pleura and peritoneum.

costophrenic.definition: Relating to the ribs (costal) and the diaphragm (phrenic); in radiology, describing the costophrenic angles at the lung bases where the diaphragms meet the ribs.

celiac trunk.definition: A short arterial trunk of the abdominal aorta that arises just below the diaphragmatic hiatus and gives off the left gastric, splenic, and common hepatic arteries to supply the foregut organs (stomach, liver, spleen, pancreas, and proximal duodenum).

cones.definition: Cells in the retina that are sensitive to color and light.

rods.definition: Light-sensitive cells in the retina that respond best in darkness and dim light.

sense organs.definition: Specialized organs that detect sensory stimuli and transduce them into neural signals for perception; the classic sense organs are the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin.

internal organs.definition: Organs that are inside your body, like your heart, lungs, or stomach.

inspection.definition: Visual examination of a patient during the physical exam to observe for signs of disease or abnormality; the initial step in the exam, performed with good lighting to assess general appearance, posture, skin changes, symmetry, and movements.

stomatognathic system.definition: A functional complex of the mouth and jaws, including teeth, the supporting structures, tongue, lips, cheeks, palate, muscles of mastication, and the temporomandibular joints, along with their neural and vascular supply, that coordinates chewing, swallowing, speech, and facial movements.

gnathic system.definition: An anatomical functional complex comprising the jaw (mandible and maxilla), temporomandibular joints, teeth, and the muscles, ligaments, and neural control that govern jaw movement, mastication, occlusion, and related speech.

fourth heart sound.definition: An extra heart sound heard at the end of diastole, just before S1, produced by atrial contraction against a noncompliant ventricle; also called an atrial gallop, it is associated with left ventricular hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction.

physiological jaundice.definition: A common, self-limited neonatal jaundice caused by transiently immature hepatic bilirubin conjugation (low UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity) leading to elevated unconjugated bilirubin; it typically appears after 24 hours, peaks around day 2–3, and resolves within 1–2 weeks in term infants (longer in preterm infants).

physiological hypertrophy.definition: An adaptive, non-pathological increase in cell size of a tissue or organ in response to normal physiological stimuli (such as regular exercise or hormonal changes), resulting in enlargement with preserved or enhanced function.

physiological contracture.definition: A reversible, nonstructural shortening of muscle or soft tissue caused by sustained contraction or spasm; range of motion returns with relaxation and stretching, and it is not due to fibrosis or fixed structural change.

physiological occlusion.definition: The normal, functional contact between the upper and lower teeth that distributes occlusal forces evenly, preserves temporomandibular joint integrity, and allows smooth mandibular movements with minimal interferences.

lower uterine segment.definition: The portion of the uterus between the internal os of the cervix and the uterine isthmus; a relatively thin, less muscular region that enlarges and thins during pregnancy and is the common site for low transverse cesarean incisions.

primordial dwarf.definition: An extremely short stature present from birth due to a group of genetic growth disorders that restrict fetal development, resulting in markedly small, proportionate body size that persists into adulthood; many subtypes can include microcephaly and distinctive facial features.

physiological saline.definition: A sterile isotonic solution of 0.9% sodium chloride in water that is osmotically similar to body fluids; used for intravenous hydration, wound irrigation, and as a diluent for medications.
