politano-leadbetter technique.definition: A surgical method to correct vesicoureteral reflux by reimplanting the ureter into the bladder through a submucosal tunnel, creating a flap-valve mechanism to prevent backflow of urine from the bladder into the ureter (intravesical ureteroneocystostomy, commonly used in children).

pollen allergy.definition: An IgE-mediated allergic reaction to environmental pollen (from trees, grasses, or weeds) that causes seasonal allergic rhinitis with symptoms such as sneezing, nasal congestion, itchy or watery eyes, and sometimes conjunctivitis or asthma.

pollen coryza.definition: An allergic rhinitis triggered by inhaled pollen from trees, grasses, or weeds, causing sneezing, nasal congestion, runny nose, and itchy, watery eyes (commonly called hay fever).

pollex.definition: The thumb, the first digit of the hand; it is opposable and typically shorter than the other digits, comprising the first metacarpal and the proximal and distal phalanges.

polydactylia.definition: A congenital condition characterized by extra fingers or toes; may be isolated or part of a syndrome; can be preaxial (thumb/radial side) or postaxial (little finger/ulnar side); often inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern; management ranges from observation to surgical removal of the extra digit if function or appearance is affected.

polyarteritis.definition: Systemic necrotizing vasculitis affecting multiple arteries (typically medium-sized vessels) with transmural inflammation and fibrinoid necrosis, leading to ischemia in affected organs; commonly presents with fever, weight loss, abdominal pain, neuropathy, skin lesions, and renal involvement, and may be idiopathic or associated with infections such as hepatitis B.

polyarthralgia.definition: Pain in multiple joints; arthralgia occurring in more than one joint, which may be inflammatory or noninflammatory.

polyarticular.definition: Involving several joints; an arthritis or inflammatory process that affects multiple joints, typically five or more.

autosomal dominant polycystic kidney dis.definition: A genetic disorder characterized by the development of numerous bilateral renal cysts that enlarge the kidneys and progressively impair renal function; inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, usually due to PKD1 or PKD2 mutations, and often associated with hypertension and cysts in the liver and other organs.

autosomal recessive polycystic kidney di.definition: A rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic PKHD1 mutations encoding fibrocystin, leading to congenital dilation of renal collecting ducts and enlarged kidneys with progressive renal failure, often associated with congenital hepatic fibrosis.

polycystic liver disease.definition: A genetic disorder characterized by multiple benign liver cysts, often arising from biliary epithelium; it can be isolated (autosomal dominant polycystic liver disease) or associated with polycystic kidney disease, with liver function typically preserved but hepatomegaly and abdominal symptoms may occur.

pcos.definition: A hormonal disorder characterized by enlarged ovaries with multiple small cysts, often causing irregular ovulation and infertility, and commonly associated with excess facial or body hair (hirsutism).

polycythemia rubra vera.definition: A chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm driven by a JAK2-mutant clone, causing autonomous erythrocytosis (increased red cell mass) with low erythropoietin, often with leukocytosis and thrombocytosis, and a high risk of thrombosis; typically treated with phlebotomy and low-dose aspirin, with cytoreductive therapy for high-risk patients.

polychondritis.definition: Relapsing polychondritis is a rare autoimmune inflammatory disorder with episodic inflammation of cartilaginous tissues (especially the ears, nose, and airway) and often multisystem involvement.

polychromasia.definition: Polychromasia is the appearance of variably colored red blood cells on a peripheral blood smear, caused by residual RNA in immature reticulocytes; it indicates increased erythropoietic activity (reticulocytosis), often in response to anemia.

polychromatophilia.definition: A staining appearance of erythrocytes on a peripheral blood smear with bluish, polychromatic cytoplasm due to residual RNA in reticulocytes, indicating increased erythropoiesis (reticulocytosis) often seen after anemia, blood loss, or hemolysis.

polychromatophil.definition: A young erythrocyte with a variably stained (polychromatic) cytoplasm due to residual RNA; on standard stains it appears bluish, corresponding to a reticulocyte when identified with supravital stains.

polyclinic.definition: An outpatient medical facility that houses multiple specialty clinics and services in one location, providing consultations and diagnostics without requiring inpatient admission.

asymptomatic infection.definition: An infection in which a person is infected with a pathogen but remains without symptoms; such individuals may still harbor and transmit the organism to others.

abortive poliomyelitis.definition: A mild, nonparalytic form of poliovirus infection presenting as a self-limited febrile illness with nonspecific symptoms (fever, malaise, sore throat, headache, GI upset) and no meningitis or paralysis.

nonparalytic poliomyelitis.definition: A poliovirus infection presenting with meningitis symptoms (fever, headache, neck stiffness) without the motor paralysis seen in paralytic poliomyelitis; often referred to as aseptic meningitis due to poliovirus.

spinal poliomyelitis.definition: An acute viral infection caused by poliovirus that targets motor neurons in the anterior horn of the spinal cord, causing inflammation and destruction of those cells and resulting in acute, flaccid, often asymmetric paralysis with preserved sensation; may lead to respiratory failure; prevented by poliovirus vaccination.

vaccine-associated paralysis.definition: Paralysis that occurs as a very rare adverse event after vaccination; most notably poliomyelitis caused by reversion or mutation of the attenuated poliovirus in the oral polio vaccine, which can affect the vaccine recipient or close contacts.

meninx.definition: A single membrane that envelops the brain and spinal cord; one of the three meningeal layers (dura mater, arachnoid mater, or pia mater).

anterior horn cells.definition: Motor neuron cell bodies located in the ventral (anterior) gray matter of the spinal cord; they are the lower motor neurons that innervate skeletal muscles (alpha and gamma motor neurons) and drive voluntary and reflex motor activity.

abdominal discomfort.definition: Non-specific sensation of mild to moderate discomfort, pain, or fullness in the abdomen, often described as aching or cramping, which can be caused by benign conditions (gas, indigestion, constipation) or by a range of gastrointestinal or systemic disorders.

back stiffness.definition: Stiffness in the back is a symptom characterized by tightness or inflexibility of the back muscles or joints, leading to reduced range of motion and often pain; it can result from muscle strain, poor posture, degenerative spine changes, arthritis, or inflammatory conditions.

hepatic dysfunction.definition: Hepatic dysfunction is an abnormality of liver function due to injury or disease, in which the liver cannot adequately perform its metabolic, detoxification, synthetic (e.g., albumin and coagulation factors), and excretory (bilirubin) roles, often with elevated liver enzymes and jaundice.

hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis.definition: A hormonal axis coordinating female reproduction: the hypothalamus releases pulsatile GnRH, stimulating the anterior pituitary to secrete FSH and LH; FSH promotes ovarian follicle growth and estrogen production, LH triggers ovulation and corpus luteum–derived progesterone production; ovarian steroids (estrogen and progesterone) and inhibin feedback to the hypothalamus and pituitary to regulate the menstrual cycle and fertility.

stein-leventhal syndrome.definition: A common endocrine disorder in women of reproductive age characterized by chronic anovulation, hyperandrogenism, and bilateral polycystic ovaries, often associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and infertility.

hyperandrogenic chronic anovulations.definition: A reproductive endocrine disorder characterized by persistent anovulation in the presence of hyperandrogenism (excess androgens), most commonly seen in polycystic ovary syndrome; clinical features include irregular or absent menses, hirsutism, acne, and infertility, often with insulin resistance.

jak2 mutation.definition: A somatic activating mutation in the JAK2 gene, most commonly the V617F substitution, that causes constitutive activation of the JAK-STAT signaling pathway and is associated with myeloproliferative neoplasms such as polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, and primary myelofibrosis.

reticulocytosis.definition: An increased number of reticulocytes in the peripheral blood, reflecting heightened erythropoietic activity by the bone marrow in response to red blood cell loss (e.g., acute hemorrhage, hemolysis) or recovery from anemia; typically defined as a reticulocyte count above the laboratory reference range (often >2% of red cells) or an elevated reticulocyte production index.

reticulocytes.definition: Immature red blood cells released from the bone marrow into the bloodstream; they still contain residual RNA and a reticular cytoplasm, and mature into mature erythrocytes within about 1–2 days. The reticulocyte count reflects bone marrow erythropoietic activity.

myeloproliferative neoplasm.definition: A group of clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders characterized by persistent overproduction of one or more mature myeloid cell lines (typically red cells, platelets, or white cells depending on subtype) driven by activating mutations (commonly JAK2, CALR, or MPL) that cause constitutive JAK-STAT signaling; associated with increased risk of thrombosis and progression to myelofibrosis or acute leukemia.

psychogenic.definition: Symptoms and illnesses that have a psychological cause, rather than a physical one.

polyendocrine deficiency syndromes.definition: Rare autoimmune disorders in which two or more endocrine glands are damaged or fail, leading to multiple hormone deficiencies; often accompanied by autoimmune diseases affecting nonendocrine tissues.

polyglandular autoimmune syndromes.definition: An umbrella term for rare autoimmune disorders in which immune-mediated destruction or dysfunction affects two or more endocrine glands, often with additional autoimmune diseases; the spectrum includes type 1 (APECED) with mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, and adrenal insufficiency, and type 2 with Addison disease plus autoimmune thyroid disease and/or type 1 diabetes.

schmidt syndrome.definition: Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type II, in which autoimmune adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) occurs with autoimmune thyroid disease and/or type 1 diabetes mellitus, and may be associated with other autoimmune disorders.

thyroid failure.definition: A condition in which the thyroid gland fails to produce adequate amounts of thyroid hormones (thyroxine T4 and triiodothyronine T3), resulting in a reduced metabolic rate; causes include autoimmune destruction (Hashimoto thyroiditis), iodine deficiency, surgical removal, or radioactive iodine therapy; treatment is lifelong thyroid hormone replacement (typically levothyroxine).

primary adrenal insufficiency.definition: An intrinsic adrenal gland disorder in which destruction or dysfunction of the adrenal cortex leads to insufficient production of cortisol (and often aldosterone), causing fatigue, weight loss, low blood pressure, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and sometimes skin hyperpigmentation; requires lifelong replacement therapy with glucocorticoids and, if aldosterone is deficient, mineralocorticoids.

adrenocorticosteroids.definition: A class of steroid hormones produced by the adrenal cortex, comprising glucocorticoids (e.g., cortisol) and mineralocorticoids (e.g., aldosterone); they regulate metabolism, electrolyte balance, and the body's stress response; synthetic analogs are widely used for their anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects.

polymyalgia rheumatica.definition: An inflammatory rheumatic syndrome in adults over ~50 marked by subacute bilateral proximal muscle pain and morning stiffness in the shoulder and hip girdles, elevated inflammatory markers, and a rapid, sustained response to low-dose corticosteroids; may be associated with giant cell arteritis.

polymorphonuclear neutrophil.definition: A neutrophil, a type of white blood cell with a multilobed nucleus (polymorphonuclear); the most abundant granulocyte of the innate immune system, defending against bacterial and fungal infections by phagocytosing pathogens, releasing antimicrobial granules, and forming neutrophil extracellular traps during inflammation.

polymorphonuclear leukocyte.definition: A granulocytic white blood cell with a multilobed nucleus and cytoplasmic granules; the most abundant leukocyte in blood, primarily neutrophils, which act as first responders in the innate immune response by phagocytosing bacteria and releasing inflammatory mediators.

polymorphocytic leukemia.definition: Not a recognized medical term; if used, it would refer to leukemia with marked pleomorphism of malignant leukocytes (variable cell size and nuclear morphology), but leukemias are classified by lineage and genetic features, and this descriptor is not an established entity.

polymorphous light eruption.definition: Common benign photodermatosis in which sun exposure induces a pruritic eruption on sun-exposed skin that can take various forms—papules, vesicles, plaques, or urticarial lesions—typically appearing within hours to days after UV exposure; it usually resolves within 1–2 weeks, and management centers on sun protection and topical corticosteroids; refractory or severe cases may respond to hydroxychloroquine.

nasal polyp.definition: A noncancerous mucosal outgrowth from the nasal passages or paranasal sinuses caused by chronic inflammation, typically presenting with nasal obstruction, reduced sense of smell, nasal discharge, and recurrent sinus infections.

polypapilloma.definition: A benign mucosal lesion characterized by a pedunculated (polypoid) mass with surface papillary (frond-like) projections; histology shows proliferating epithelium forming papillary fronds over a fibrovascular core.

polypeptide.definition: A polypeptide is a linear polymer of amino acids linked by peptide bonds; it forms the basic chain of a protein, and one or more polypeptide chains may fold and assemble to create a functional protein.

polyphagia.definition: Excessive hunger or appetite; an abnormal increase in the desire to eat (seen in conditions such as uncontrolled diabetes mellitus and certain metabolic disorders).

hyperphagia.definition: An abnormally increased appetite for and consumption of food.

polysaccharide.definition: A carbohydrate polymer consisting of long chains of monosaccharide units joined by glycosidic bonds; polysaccharides include storage forms such as starch and glycogen and structural components such as cellulose.

polysome.definition: A cluster of ribosomes bound to a single messenger RNA molecule during active translation, allowing simultaneous synthesis of multiple copies of a protein.

polyribosome.definition: A cluster of ribosomes bound to a single mRNA molecule, translating the same message simultaneously to produce multiple copies of a protein; also known as a polysome.

polysomnography.definition: A sleep study that examines brain waves and other measures of physiological functioning.

polysomnographic technologist.definition: A healthcare professional who conducts polysomnography by preparing patients, setting up and calibrating recording equipment, monitoring sleep-stage signals (e.g., EEG, EOG, EMG) and other physiological data, and scoring the study for interpretation by a sleep physician.

polysulfide polymer.definition: A polymer in which the repeating units are linked by disulfide (–S–S–) bonds, typically producing a flexible elastomeric material (e.g., polysulfide rubber used as an impression material in dentistry).

polysulfide rubber.definition: A type of synthetic rubber elastomer consisting of long polymer chains with multiple sulfur–sulfur linkages, providing flexibility and good resistance to oils, solvents, and weathering; used in sealants, gaskets, adhesives, and waterproof coatings, typically cured by sulfur-based systems.

polysyndactyly.definition: A congenital anomaly in which more than the usual number of digits are present and some of these digits are fused to each other (extra digits that are joined to neighboring digits), most often in the hands or feet.

polypoid.definition: Resembling a polyp; a growth protruding from a mucous membrane into a lumen, often pedunculated or sessile.

polyposis coli.definition: A hereditary disorder characterized by the development of numerous polyps in the colon and rectum, most often familial adenomatous polyposis caused by APC gene mutations (usually autosomal dominant), with a very high lifetime risk of colorectal cancer if untreated.

familial polyposis.definition: An inherited autosomal dominant syndrome marked by the development of numerous adenomatous polyps in the colon and rectum, typically due to APC gene mutations, with near‑certain lifetime risk of colorectal cancer if untreated; management includes regular colonoscopic surveillance and often prophylactic colectomy.

polyoma papovavirus.definition: A small, nonenveloped double-stranded DNA virus of the Polyomaviridae family (formerly Papovaviridae) that can transform infected cells and cause tumors in animals; in humans, JC and BK viruses are notable members, often latent and reactivating in immunocompromised individuals.

polyoma.definition: A small, nonenveloped double-stranded DNA virus that establishes latent infections in many hosts; reactivation in immunocompromised individuals can cause nephropathy, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, or Merkel cell carcinoma.

papillocarcinoma.definition: A malignant neoplasm arising from a papillomatous lesion, composed of malignant epithelial cells forming papillary (finger‑like) fronds with a fibrovascular core and potential invasion.

polyopia.definition: Perception of two or more copies of a single object in the visual field; a visual illusion or hallucination that can occur with migraine aura, temporal lobe epilepsy, or occipital/parietal cortical dysfunction.

polyneuralgia.definition: Pain in multiple peripheral nerves; neuralgia affecting several nerves, typically due to irritation or inflammation of the nerves; not a commonly used standalone diagnosis today (often described as polyneuritis or multifocal neuralgia).

polyglactin.definition: Synthetic absorbable suture material formed from a copolymer of glycolide and L-lactide; resorbed by hydrolysis over roughly 2–3 months.

polymerase.definition: A type of enzyme that catalyzes the polymerization of nucleotides to form nucleic acids; DNA polymerases synthesize DNA (using a DNA template), while RNA polymerases synthesize RNA (using a DNA template).

polynucleotide.definition: A polymer formed by many nucleotides linked by phosphodiester bonds; the backbone of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) with a sequence of bases that encodes genetic information.

ergosome.definition: Not a widely recognized medical term; there is no standard definition in major medical dictionaries. If you can share the context or confirm the spelling, I can tailor a precise definition.

endocrine pancreas.definition: The portion of the pancreas that contains the islets of Langerhans and secretes hormones directly into the bloodstream (primarily insulin, glucagon, somatostatin, and pancreatic polypeptide) to regulate blood glucose; it is the endocrine component of the pancreas, distinct from the exocrine pancreas that produces digestive enzymes.

parathyroids.definition: Four small endocrine glands located on the posterior surface of the thyroid gland in the neck. They secrete parathyroid hormone (PTH), which regulates blood calcium and phosphate levels by increasing calcium release from bone, increasing calcium reabsorption in the kidneys, and promoting activation of vitamin D to boost intestinal calcium absorption. Dysfunction can cause hypo- or hyperparathyroidism.

polytene chromosome.definition: A chromosome that has undergone multiple rounds of DNA replication without cell division (endoreduplication), producing many sister chromatids aligned in parallel and creating a large, banded structure; commonly observed in the salivary glands of Drosophila and some other insects, and used for detailed cytogenetic mapping and gene localization.

pontic.definition: A dental prosthetic unit that replaces a missing tooth in a fixed dental bridge; it has no root and is supported by adjacent teeth (abutments) via the bridge framework.

multivalent vaccine.definition: A vaccine designed to protect against several antigens, serotypes, or strains by including multiple components in a single formulation.

poly-vi-flor.definition: Not found as a standard medical term; no formal medical definition. It may be a misspelling or a brand name (for example, Poly-Vi-Flor as a pediatric vitamin/mineral supplement). Please provide context or check the spelling to help narrow it down.

poractant alfa.definition: A natural exogenous pulmonary surfactant derived from porcine lungs, containing phospholipids (primarily phosphatidylcholine) and surfactant proteins SP-B and SP-C, used to treat or prevent neonatal respiratory distress syndrome by reducing alveolar surface tension; administered intratracheally.

pulmonary hemorrhage.definition: Bleeding into the lung parenchyma, typically the alveoli, causing hemoptysis and impaired gas exchange; etiologies include vasculitis and autoimmune diseases (e.g., Goodpasture syndrome), infections, coagulopathy, trauma, and inhalational injury.

posttreatment sepsis.definition: Sepsis that develops after completion of treatment for a prior condition, typically due to an infection acquired during hospitalization or as a consequence of therapy-related immune suppression; it is a life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection.

posttreatment infection.definition: An infection that occurs after a patient has completed treatment for a prior illness or after a medical or surgical intervention; it may result from residual pathogens, compromised immunity, or new exposure.

oxygen desaturation.definition: A decrease in blood oxygen saturation, typically reflected by a lower SpO2 on pulse oximetry, indicating reduced arterial oxygenation; clinically defined as a drop of at least 4 percentage points from baseline or an SpO2 below about 90% for a sustained period.

esophageal edema.definition: Swelling of the esophageal mucosa and submucosa due to fluid accumulation from inflammation, injury, infection, or ischemia; commonly associated with esophagitis and can cause odynophagia or dysphagia.

pompes disease.definition: A rare lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of the enzyme acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA), leading to glycogen accumulation in lysosomes of skeletal and cardiac muscle. Infantile-onset presents with hypotonia, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiomegaly, often with feeding difficulties and early death if untreated; later-onset forms cause progressive proximal muscle weakness and respiratory failure. Enzyme replacement therapy with recombinant GAA is an available treatment.

pomr.definition: A systematic method of organizing medical records around a patient’s problems; it includes a problem list, a database (history, exam, tests), a plan for each problem, and progress notes (often written in SOAP format).

ponophobia.definition: Not a recognized medical phobia term in standard classifications; there is no established definition or diagnostic criteria. If you meant a related phobia, it would describe an irrational, persistent fear of a specific trigger that leads to avoidance and distress on exposure (e.g., fear of facial hair or fear of loud sounds).

pontine.definition: Relating to the pons, the part of the brainstem between the midbrain and medulla oblongata; contains nuclei and tracts that relay signals between the cerebrum and cerebellum and contribute to autonomic and cranial nerve functions.

pontes.definition: A broad region of the brainstem between the medulla oblongata and the midbrain; it contains pontine nuclei that relay information from the cerebral cortex to the cerebellum and houses cranial nerve nuclei for V–VIII, participating in motor control, facial sensation and movement, hearing/balance, and regulation of respiration and sleep.

apneustic center.definition: A region in the lower pons of the brainstem that promotes inspiration by stimulating medullary inspiratory neurons; it is normally inhibited by the pneumotaxic center to regulate the duration of inspiration.

pontocaine.definition: A brand-name ester local anesthetic (tetracaine) used for brief topical anesthesia of mucous membranes, especially the ocular surface; it inhibits voltage-gated sodium channels to block nerve conduction, with rapid onset and short duration; systemic toxicity can occur with excessive dosing.

ponv.definition: A common postoperative complication characterized by nausea and vomiting after anesthesia and surgery, typically within the first 24 hours.

pooled plasma.definition: A batch of plasma assembled by combining plasma units from multiple blood donors into a single lot, typically for production of plasma-derived therapies (e.g., immunoglobulins, clotting factors); pooling standardizes product and supply but requires stringent donor screening and pathogen reduction procedures.

porcine insulin.definition: Insulin obtained from pig pancreas; a peptide hormone used to treat diabetes mellitus; structurally similar to human insulin with minor amino acid differences; historically used before recombinant human insulin and largely replaced by it; may elicit antibody formation or allergic reactions in some patients.

porcine graft.definition: A graft composed of porcine (pig) tissue used as a xenograft; in wound care, porcine skin grafts provide temporary coverage for burns or ulcers and are eventually rejected by the recipient's immune system.

porphyrinogen.definition: A colorless, nonaromatic tetrapyrrole intermediate in heme biosynthesis; consists of four linked pyrrole rings with saturated methine bridges and is oxidized to the aromatic porphyrins later in the pathway.

porphyrin test.definition: A laboratory test used to detect and quantify porphyrins or their precursors (commonly porphobilinogen and delta-aminolevulinic acid) in urine, plasma, or feces to evaluate suspected disorders of heme biosynthesis (porphyrias).

porphobilinogen test.definition: An analytical urine test to measure porphobilinogen concentration; used to screen for acute porphyrias, with elevated levels suggesting disorders of heme synthesis (e.g., acute intermittent porphyria).

portagen.definition: A brand-name infant formula that is phenylalanine-free (or very low in phenylalanine) used for dietary management of phenylketonuria (PKU), providing essential nutrition without phenylalanine.

portal system.definition: A venous arrangement in which blood from a capillary bed is drained into a portal vein and passes to a second capillary bed in a distant organ before returning to the heart; this two-capillary-bed pathway allows processing of substances (e.g., nutrients, toxins) by the second organ (most notably the liver) before entering systemic circulation.

pork tapeworm.definition: A parasitic flatworm (cestode) acquired from consuming undercooked pork containing larval cysticerci; it can cause intestinal taeniasis and, if eggs are ingested, tissue cysticercosis (including neurocysticercosis).

porencephalia.definition: A rare brain disorder characterized by one or more cystic cavities within the cerebral hemisphere that communicate with the ventricular system or subarachnoid space, typically caused by destructive intrauterine or perinatal brain injury (e.g., ischemia, hemorrhage, infection); the cavities are lined with gliosis.

porotomy.definition: A surgical incision into a duct or canal to create or enlarge an opening for access or drainage.

popliteal fossa.definition: A diamond-shaped shallow depression at the back of the knee, posterior to the knee joint, bounded superiorly by the tendons of the hamstring muscles and inferiorly by the heads of the gastrocnemius; it contains the popliteal artery and vein, tibial nerve, common fibular nerve, and associated lymphatics.

popliteal web syndrome.definition: A rare autosomal dominant congenital disorder characterized by webbing of the skin behind the knee (popliteal webbing/pterygium) with knee joint contractures, often accompanied by additional limb, facial, genital, or orofacial anomalies; commonly linked to IRF6 mutations (GRHL3 has also been implicated).

popliteal pulse.definition: A palpable arterial pulse felt in the popliteal fossa behind the knee, produced by the popliteal artery; used to assess distal leg perfusion and patency of the femoropopliteal vessels.

lymphoblastoma.definition: A malignant tumor composed of lymphoblasts (immature lymphocytes); a form of lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia characterized by rapid proliferation of lymphoblasts in lymphoid tissues (and often bone marrow).

lymphoblast.definition: An immature lymphoid precursor cell that differentiates into a mature B- or T-lymphocyte; in pathology, malignant lymphoblasts are the proliferating precursors seen in acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

portal-systemic encephalopathy.definition: Neuropsychiatric syndrome caused by liver failure or portal-systemic shunting, leading to accumulation of neurotoxins (notably ammonia) in the brain and resulting in cognitive and motor disturbances ranging from subtle changes to coma; typically reversible with treatment of the underlying liver disease and precipitating factors.

hepatic coma.definition: A comatose state caused by advanced hepatic failure (severe hepatic encephalopathy) in which toxic substances such as ammonia accumulate because the damaged liver cannot detoxify them, leading to progressive neurologic dysfunction and loss of consciousness.

right lobe.definition: An anatomical right-side subdivision of a lobed organ; in the liver, it is the larger, right-hand portion separated from the left by the falciform ligament.

left lobe.definition: A left-sided anatomical division of the liver; the left hepatic lobe is separated from the right lobe by the falciform ligament and contains the left hepatic segments (II–IV).

portal venous shunt.definition: A surgically or radiologically created connection between the portal venous system and the systemic venous circulation that diverts portal blood away from the liver to reduce portal hypertension and its complications (e.g., variceal bleeding).

postcaval shunt.definition: A surgical connection between the portal venous system and the systemic venous circulation (typically the inferior vena cava) to bypass the liver and reduce portal hypertension; historically described as a portocaval (postcaval) shunt, with risks including hepatic encephalopathy and shunt dysfunction.

porter-silber reaction.definition: I can’t verify a standard definition for Porter-Silber reaction in reliable medical dictionaries. Could you provide the field (toxicology, histology, biochemistry) or an alternate spelling? If you share more context, I can look it up again.

17-hydroxycorticosteroids.definition: A group of adrenal-cortex–derived corticosteroid metabolites in urine that have a hydroxyl group at the 17th carbon; their measurement reflects adrenal cortical activity and is used to screen for disorders such as Cushing syndrome and hypercortisolism.

adrenocortical function.definition: The production and secretion of steroid hormones by the adrenal cortex—glucocorticoids (primarily cortisol), mineralocorticoids (primarily aldosterone), and adrenal androgens—regulated by ACTH and the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.

biliary atresia.definition: A rare congenital condition in which the extrahepatic bile ducts are obliterated or absent, causing cholestasis and progressive biliary cirrhosis; it usually presents in infancy with persistent jaundice, pale stools, dark urine, and hepatomegaly, and is treated with surgical restoration of bile flow (Kasai portoenterostomy) or liver transplantation.

kasai operation.definition: A surgical procedure for biliary atresia in newborns in which the fibrotic extrahepatic bile ducts are removed and a loop of small intestine (usually jejunum) is connected to the hepatic porta to drain bile directly from the liver (portoenterostomy), with the aim of restoring bile flow and delaying liver failure.

roux-en-y.definition: A surgical rearrangement of the small intestine that creates a Y-shaped configuration by connecting a proximal limb to a distal segment, thereby bypassing a portion of the stomach and proximal small intestine; most commonly used for bariatric procedures that create a small gastric pouch with food directed to the jejunum, and for biliary/pancreatic drainage.

portuguese-azorean disease.definition: Not a widely recognized medical term; no standard medical definition exists. It may be a historical or population-specific label whose meaning varies by source. If you can share symptoms, inheritance pattern, or alternate spellings, I can help identify the intended condition.

oropharyngeal candidiasis.definition: A fungal infection of the oral cavity and oropharynx caused by Candida species (most commonly Candida albicans), characterized by white, curd-like plaques on mucosal surfaces that can be scraped off to reveal erythematous mucosa, often associated with immunosuppression, antibiotic use, diabetes, or denture wear.

cardiac dysfunction.definition: A general term for impaired performance of the heart, resulting in inadequate cardiac output to meet the body's demands or elevated filling pressures; may reflect systolic dysfunction (reduced pumping), diastolic dysfunction (impaired filling), or both, and can arise from cardiomyopathy, ischemic heart disease, valvular disease, or other cardiac pathology.

postanesthesia care.definition: Care provided to a patient immediately after anesthesia to monitor and support airway, breathing, circulation, pain, nausea, and other recovery needs during emergence and initial postoperative stabilization until discharge criteria are met.

pacu.definition: A specialized hospital unit where patients recover immediately after anesthesia and surgery, with continuous monitoring of airway, breathing, circulation, pain, and vital signs until they are awake, stable, and ready for transfer or discharge.

postoperative care.definition: Care provided after a surgical procedure to monitor recovery, manage pain and wounds, prevent complications (such as infection, bleeding, and thromboembolism), and plan for discharge and ongoing rehabilitation.

radioactive isotopes.definition: An isotope with an unstable nucleus that undergoes radioactive decay, emitting ionizing radiation (alpha, beta, or gamma rays) and transforming into a different element; used in diagnostic imaging, radiotherapy, and scientific dating.

peep.definition: A ventilator setting that maintains positive airway pressure in the lungs at the end of expiration to prevent alveolar collapse and improve oxygenation.

ppv.definition: Positive pressure ventilation: a mode of mechanical ventilation that delivers air (or oxygen) to the lungs under positive pressure during inspiration to support or replace spontaneous breathing; can be invasive (endotracheal/tracheostomy tube) or noninvasive (mask).

calculated?.definition: Done by calculation; planned or determined through precise computation, often referring to a dose, risk, or measurement tailored to the patient.

postcentral gyrus.definition: Primary somatosensory cortex in the parietal lobe, located just posterior to the central sulcus; it receives contralateral somatic sensory input (touch, proprioception, pain, and temperature) via thalamic pathways and is organized somatotopically (sensory homunculus).

emergency contraceptive.definition: A method used to prevent pregnancy after unprotected sex or contraceptive failure; it works mainly by delaying ovulation and can also interfere with fertilization or implantation. Examples include oral hormonal regimens (levonorgestrel or ulipristal acetate) and the copper intrauterine device.

postcoital test.definition: A diagnostic test used in evaluating infertility by examining the cervical mucus after intercourse to assess the presence and motility of sperm within the mucus, thereby evaluating sperm–cervical mucus interaction and cervical receptivity (typically performed 6–24 hours after intercourse).

postcommissurotomy syndrome.definition: An inflammatory complication after surgical mitral commissurotomy presenting with fever and chest pain from pericarditis and/or pleuritis, often with pericardial or pleural effusions; part of postcardiac injury syndrome likely due to an autoimmune reaction to surgical injury, typically self-limited and treated with anti-inflammatory therapy (e.g., NSAIDs, colchicine).

postconcussional syndrome.definition: A set of symptoms that persist after a concussion (mild traumatic brain injury), including headaches, dizziness, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and cognitive (memory, concentration) and mood changes (irritability, depression), lasting weeks to months beyond the acute injury and often worsened by exertion or stress.

posttraumatic syndrome.definition: A psychological condition that can develop after exposure to a traumatic event, characterized by intrusive memories or flashbacks, avoidance of reminders, negative changes in thoughts and mood, and hyperarousal, persisting for more than a month and causing distress or impairment; when persistent and impairing, it is diagnosed as posttraumatic stress disorder.

postdate pregnancy.definition: A pregnancy that extends beyond 42 completed weeks of gestation (about 294 days); also known as a post-term or prolonged pregnancy.

postterm pregnancy.definition: A pregnancy that persists beyond 42 completed weeks of gestation (more than 294 days from the first day of the last menstrual period).

posterior auricular artery.definition: An artery arising from the external carotid artery that runs posterior to the ear to supply the auricle and the skin of the posterior scalp; it gives auricular and mastoid branches and often a stylomastoid branch accompanying the facial nerve through the stylomastoid foramen.

posterior circumflex humeral artery.definition: A branch of the third part of the axillary artery that runs posterior to the humerus through the quadrangular space with the axillary nerve to supply the deltoid muscle, teres minor, and the shoulder joint; it anastomoses with the anterior circumflex humeral artery around the surgical neck of the humerus.

posterior column.definition: A dorsal white-matter tract of the spinal cord comprising the fasciculus gracilis and fasciculus cuneatus that carries fine touch, vibration, and proprioception from the body; part of the dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway to the thalamus and somatosensory cortex.

posterior costotransverse ligament.definition: A fibrous band reinforcing the costotransverse joint on the posterior aspect, extending from the neck of the rib to the transverse process of the corresponding thoracic vertebra, stabilizing the rib–transverse articulation.

posterior drawer sign.definition: A clinical test to assess posterior cruciate ligament integrity of the knee; the tibia is translated posteriorly relative to the femur with the knee flexed to about 90 degrees, and excessive posterior displacement indicates PCL injury or posterior laxity.

posterior ethmoidal artery.definition: A small branch of the ophthalmic artery that supplies the posterior ethmoidal air cells and adjacent posterior nasal mucosa; it enters the skull through the posterior ethmoidal foramen and may give a meningeal branch to the dura of the anterior cranial fossa, with anastomoses to surrounding nasal/ar arterial branches.

posterior ethmoidal nerve.definition: A sensory branch of the nasociliary nerve (ophthalmic V1) that supplies the mucosa of the posterior ethmoid air cells (posterior ethmoidal sinus) and adjacent superior nasal cavity; it enters the ethmoid bone via the posterior ethmoidal foramen.

posterior inferior cerebellar artery syn.definition: A brainstem infarction due to occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery, classically presenting as lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome: ipsilateral facial pain and temperature loss, contralateral body pain and temperature loss, nucleus ambiguus–related dysphagia and hoarseness, vertigo with nystagmus, ipsilateral limb ataxia, and sometimes ipsilateral Horner syndrome.

posterior kidney.definition: Back-facing aspect of the kidney; the posterior surface of the retroperitoneal organ that lies against the posterior abdominal wall.

posterior longitudinal ligament.definition: A strong fibrous band within the vertebral canal that runs along the posterior surfaces of the vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs from C2 to the sacrum, helping to limit spinal flexion.

posterior median fissure.definition: A shallow groove along the midline on the dorsal surface of the spinal cord that separates the left and right dorsal (posterior) funiculi; serves as a midline landmark.

posterior mediastinal node.definition: An intra-thoracic lymph node located in the posterior mediastinum; part of the mediastinal lymph node groups, draining posterior mediastinal structures such as the esophagus and posterior intercostal spaces, and typically emptying into the thoracic duct.

posterior neuropore.definition: A caudal (tail) end of the embryonic neural tube that normally closes by about day 27–29 of gestation; failure to close can cause spinal neural tube defects such as spina bifida (e.g., meningomyelocele or rachischisis).

posterior occlusion.definition: The contact relationships between the upper and lower posterior teeth (premolars and molars) when the jaws are closed in centric occlusion, including cusp-to-fossa contacts and the distribution of occlusal forces to stabilize the bite and guide mandibular movements.

posterior palatal seal area.definition: A region on the posterior palate behind the vibrating line where the mucosa is molded to create a border seal for a maxillary denture, improving retention by functional suction.

posterior parietal artery.definition: A cerebral artery supplying the posterior part of the parietal lobe, typically a branch of the posterior cerebral artery that vascularizes the parietal cortex.

posterior pituitary gland.definition: The posterior pituitary gland (neurohypophysis) is the neural portion of the pituitary that stores and releases the hypothalamic hormones oxytocin and vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone, ADH) into the bloodstream; it does not synthesize these hormones but releases them in response to neural signals from the hypothalamus via the pituitary stalk.

posterior ramus.definition: The dorsal (posterior) ramus is the posterior branch of a spinal nerve that supplies motor innervation to the intrinsic back muscles and sensory innervation to the skin of the back; it typically divides into medial and lateral branches to serve the deep back muscles and overlying skin.

posterior rhizotomy.definition: A neurosurgical procedure in which the dorsal (posterior) sensory nerve roots of the spinal cord are cut or lesioned to interrupt sensory transmission, typically to relieve intractable pain or reduce spasticity (as in selective dorsal rhizotomy used for cerebral palsy).

posterior sagittal anorectoplasty.definition: A surgical repair for anorectal malformations in which a posterior sagittal incision provides direct access to the anorectal region; the rectum is mobilized and positioned within the anal sphincter to create a functional anus.

posterior spinal arteries.definition: One of a pair of arteries that run along the posterior (dorsal) aspect of the spinal cord in the subarachnoid space, typically arising from the vertebral arteries (often via the posterior inferior cerebellar artery), supplying the posterior one-third of the spinal cord, especially the dorsal columns and dorsal horns, via perforating branches; they form an anastomotic network with each other and with radiculomedullary arteries.

posterior subcapsular cataract.definition: A cataract where an opacity forms in the posterior subcapsular area of the lens, just in front of the posterior capsule; it commonly affects central vision and causes marked glare and decreased acuity, especially in bright light, and tends to progress rapidly. Risk factors include corticosteroid use, diabetes, radiation exposure, uveitis, and trauma.

posterior temporal artery.definition: A small arterial branch that supplies the temporalis muscle in the temple region; typically arising from the middle temporal artery (a branch of the superficial temporal artery from the external carotid) and participating in anastomoses with other temporal vessels.

posterior tibialis pulse.definition: An arterial pulse felt behind the medial malleolus by palpating the posterior tibial artery; used to assess perfusion of the foot. Diminished or absent pulses suggest peripheral arterial disease or vascular insufficiency.

posterior tooth.definition: Any tooth located toward the back of the dental arch, typically a premolar or molar, specialized for grinding and crushing food and positioned distal to the canines.

posterior uveitis.definition: Inflammation of the posterior uveal tract, predominantly the choroid, and often involving the retina and retinal pigment epithelium; typically presents with decreased vision and floaters and may be associated with macular edema or choroidal lesions, often confined to the posterior segment.

posterior vaginal hernia.definition: A herniation of the rectum into the posterior vaginal wall through a defect in the rectovaginal fascia, causing a bulge in the posterior vaginal wall and possible defecatory difficulties; commonly referred to as a rectocele.

posterior vein of left ventricle.definition: A small cardiac vein that drains blood from the posterior aspect of the left ventricle and typically empties into the coronary sinus.

posteroanterior.definition: A radiographic projection in which the X-ray beam travels from posterior to anterior, commonly used in chest imaging to reduce magnification of the cardiac silhouette.

posteroexternal.definition: A nonstandard directional descriptor meaning situated toward the posterior (back) and on the external (outer) surface of a structure.

posteroinferior.definition: Toward the back (posteriorly) and toward the lower part of the body (inferiorly) relative to a specified reference point; describing a position that is both behind and below.

posterolateral.definition: Relating to or situated at the back (posterior) and the outer side (lateral) of the body or a structure; describing a location behind and to the side.

posterolateral sulcus.definition: A groove on each side of the spinal cord where the dorsal (sensory) nerve roots enter the cord from the dorsal root ganglia.

posteromedial.definition: An anatomical directional term meaning located toward the back (posterior) and toward the midline (medial) of the body.

posteromedial central arteries of poster.word: posteromedial central arteries of posterior communicating artery
posteromedial central arteries of poster.definition: Small perforating branches arising from the posterior communicating artery that descend medially to supply deep midline brain structures, especially the medial thalamic and hypothalamic regions; they originate near the PCom origin and contribute to the perforating supply of deep cerebral structures.

posteroparietal.definition: Relating to the posterior part of the parietal region; located toward the back of the parietal area (the back portion of the skull's parietal region or brain parietal cortex).

posterosuperior.definition: Anatomical: located toward the back (posterior) and above (superior) relative to a reference point; used to describe the relative position of a structure.

postganglionic fiber.definition: An axon of a postganglionic neuron in the autonomic nervous system that conducts impulses from an autonomic ganglion to an effector organ; these fibers are typically unmyelinated and usually release acetylcholine in parasympathetic pathways and norepinephrine in most sympathetic pathways (with exceptions, such as sympathetic fibers to sweat glands that release acetylcholine).

postganglionic neuron.definition: An autonomic neuron whose cell body lies in an autonomic ganglion and whose axon extends to and innervates an effector organ after synapsing with a preganglionic neuron; neurotransmitter varies by division (mostly norepinephrine in sympathetic pathways and acetylcholine in parasympathetic pathways).

posthepatic cirrhosis.definition: A form of secondary biliary cirrhosis caused by chronic obstruction of the extrahepatic biliary tract, resulting in cholestasis and progressive fibrosis of the liver.

posthepatic jaundice.definition: Obstructive jaundice due to blockage of the extrahepatic biliary tract (posthepatic), leading to conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with pale stools, dark urine, and often pruritus; commonly caused by gallstones, biliary strictures, or pancreatic/tail tumors.

posthypnotic suggestion.definition: A directive given to a person during hypnosis that is intended to be acted on after the hypnotic session ends, often in response to a cue, to change behavior or experiences (e.g., smoking cessation, pain control, anxiety reduction).

postmastectomy.definition: Relating to or occurring after a mastectomy, a surgical procedure that removes breast tissue, usually to treat or prevent breast cancer.

postinfectious psychosis.definition: A psychotic syndrome in which delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized thinking develop after a preceding infection, typically within days to weeks, presumed to result from immune- or inflammatory-mediated mechanisms rather than a primary psychotic disorder.

postlumbar puncture headache.definition: A headache that develops within hours to days after a lumbar puncture, caused by cerebrospinal fluid leakage through the puncture site leading to low CSF volume/pressure; it typically worsens when upright and improves lying down and is usually self-limited but may require treatment (e.g., epidural blood patch) for persistent symptoms.

postmastectomy exercises.definition: A guided, progressive program of upper‑extremity range‑of‑motion and strengthening exercises started after mastectomy to restore shoulder mobility, prevent stiffness and scar adhesions, promote lymphatic drainage, and improve arm function; typically begun once healing allows and drains are removed, with gradual advancement of activities such as pendulum exercises, elbow flexion/extension, shoulder ROM (flexion, abduction, external rotation), scapular squeezes, wall climbs, and progressive resistance under clinician guidance.

granular casts.definition: Cylindrical structures in urine formed from degenerating renal tubular epithelial cells and protein (commonly Tamm-Horsfall protein) that appear granular on microscopy, indicating tubular injury; classically associated with acute tubular necrosis.

aso titers.definition: A blood test that measures antibodies against streptolysin O, a toxin of group A Streptococcus, in the serum. It indicates a recent streptococcal infection and is used in evaluating rheumatic fever and post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis. Antibodies usually rise 1–3 weeks after infection and peak in 3–6 weeks; a single elevated titer or a rising titer supports recent infection but is not diagnostic on its own and must be interpreted with age-related reference values and clinical context.

skin lesions.definition: A skin lesion is any abnormal localized area of skin tissue, resulting from injury, infection, inflammation, or disease; examples include macules, papules, vesicles, pustules, plaques, nodules, ulcers, and tumors.

serum creatinine.definition: An endogenous waste product produced from creatine phosphate in muscle; filtered by the kidneys and excreted in urine; its serum concentration reflects renal function and is used to estimate glomerular filtration rate; elevations indicate reduced kidney function.

serum lipids.definition: Lipids circulating in blood plasma/serum, primarily cholesterol (total, LDL, and HDL), triglycerides, and related phospholipids carried by lipoproteins; measured together in a lipid panel to assess cardiovascular risk and diagnose dyslipidemias.

anorectal malformations.definition: A spectrum of congenital malformations of the anorectal region in which the anal opening is absent or incompletely formed, often with fistulous connections to the urinary, genital, or lower gastrointestinal tract; results from incomplete separation of the cloaca during embryonic development.

dorsal column.definition: A pair of ascending white-matter tracts in the dorsal (posterior) aspect of the spinal cord that convey fine touch, vibration, and proprioception from the body to the brain; they consist of the fasciculus gracilis (lower body) and fasciculus cuneatus (upper body) and project to the dorsal column nuclei in the medulla before continuing as the medial lemniscus.

postmature_infant.definition: A newborn delivered after 42 completed weeks of gestation; associated with placental aging, oligohydramnios, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and an increased risk of fetal distress and birth complications.

placental_insufficiency.definition: An obstetric condition in which the placenta fails to deliver adequate oxygen and nutrients to the fetus, resulting in fetal growth restriction and higher risk of fetal hypoxia, distress, stillbirth, or preterm birth.

neurological_damage.definition: Damage to the nervous system (brain, spinal cord, or peripheral nerves) that impairs structure or function, resulting in motor, sensory, cognitive, or autonomic deficits; causes include trauma, stroke, infection, degenerative disease, tumors, toxins, and metabolic or vascular disorders, with outcomes ranging from temporary impairment to permanent disability depending on location and extent.

induction_of_labor.definition: Induction of labor is the medical initiation of labor before it begins spontaneously, using methods such as medications (prostaglandins for cervical ripening and oxytocin to stimulate contractions) or mechanical devices to provoke cervical changes and contractions for vaginal delivery.

postmenopausal_hemorrhage.definition: Vaginal bleeding occurring in a postmenopausal woman (after at least 12 months of amenorrhea) that may result from benign causes such as vaginal atrophy or polyps or from endometrial pathology (e.g., hyperplasia or cancer) and warrants clinical evaluation.

postmenopausal_vaginitis.definition: Atrophic vaginal changes due to estrogen deficiency after menopause, characterized by thinning and drying of the vaginal mucosa with inflammation; also called atrophic vaginitis or genitourinary syndrome of menopause, causing dryness, itching, burning, dyspareunia, and increased susceptibility to infection.

atrophic_vaginitis.definition: A thinning of the vaginal epithelium with inflammation due to decreased estrogen, typically occurring in menopause, resulting in vaginal dryness, irritation, itching, burning, and dyspareunia.

cesarean_section.definition: A surgical delivery in which the baby is delivered through an incision in the mother's abdomen and uterus, usually via a lower transverse (Pfannenstiel) incision; performed when vaginal delivery is unsafe or not possible, such as fetal distress, abnormal fetal position, placenta previa, prior cesarean, or labor dystocia.

postmortem_examination.definition: A thorough examination of a deceased person's body to determine the cause and manner of death and to document disease processes, typically performed by a pathologist and including external and internal examination, histology, and ancillary tests.

dressler_syndrome.definition: An autoimmune-mediated pericarditis that develops weeks to months after myocardial infarction or cardiac surgery (or thoracic trauma), presenting with fever, pleuritic chest pain, and a pericardial rub or effusion; treated with anti-inflammatory therapy such as NSAIDs and colchicine, with steroids reserved for refractory cases.

postmyocardial_infarction_syndrome.definition: An autoimmune-mediated pericarditis occurring several weeks after a myocardial infarction, typically presenting with fever, pleuritic chest pain, a pericardial friction rub, and sometimes a pericardial effusion; usually self-limited and treated with anti-inflammatory therapy such as NSAIDs or colchicine.

pleural_effusion.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid in the pleural space—the gap between the lungs and chest wall—typically due to imbalances in hydrostatic/oncotic pressures or inflammatory processes; it can be transudative or exudative and may cause shortness of breath or chest discomfort.

deviated_septum.definition: A condition in which the nasal septum, the wall separating the two nostrils, is displaced from the midline, potentially causing nasal obstruction, congestion, and recurrent sinus problems; treatment ranges from medications to septoplasty.

postoperative_ileus.definition: A temporary, nonmechanical slowing of gastrointestinal motility after surgery, leading to delayed passage of gas and stool, abdominal distension, nausea, and intolerance of oral intake; typically resolves within a few days to a week.

postoperative_nausea_and_vomiting.definition: A common postoperative complication characterized by nausea and/or vomiting that occurs after anesthesia and surgery, typically within the first 24 hours postoperatively.

postparalytic.definition: Relating to or occurring after paralysis; describing sequelae or conditions that follow a paralytic event.

postpartum_blues.definition: A transient mood disturbance occurring in the first days after delivery, characterized by tearfulness, irritability, anxiety, mood swings, and fatigue; peaks within 3–5 days and resolves within 1–2 weeks without treatment. It is common and self-limited, and distinguished from more persistent postpartum depression by its short duration and milder symptoms.

postpartum_depression.definition: When you feel overwhelmed, depressed, or sad for no reason after having a baby. Also called baby blues or post-pregnancy depression.

antidepressants.definition: Medications that treat depressive and certain anxiety and related disorders by increasing or modulating brain monoamines (primarily serotonin, with norepinephrine and sometimes dopamine); they include SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, MAO inhibitors, and various atypical antidepressants.

postnecrotic_cirrhosis.definition: A form of liver cirrhosis that develops after extensive hepatic necrosis, typically following severe viral hepatitis or toxin-induced liver injury; characterized by bridging fibrosis with regenerative nodules and progressive impairment of liver function.

posthepatic_cirrhosis.definition: Chronic liver scarring caused by prolonged obstruction of the bile ducts after the liver (extrahepatic biliary obstruction), leading to persistent cholestasis and secondary biliary fibrosis and cirrhosis.

t_tube.definition: A T-shaped biliary drainage device placed in the common bile duct after biliary tract exploration (choledochotomy). The vertical limb sits in the duct and the horizontal limb exits the abdomen, allowing external drainage of bile and postoperative cholangiography; it is typically left in place for several days to weeks and removed after tract maturation.

endotracheal_tube.definition: A flexible tube inserted through the mouth or nose into the trachea to secure an airway and enable ventilation and oxygen delivery; it is connected to a ventilator and may be cuffed to seal the airway for effective ventilation and suctioning.

nasopharyngeal_mucosa.definition: The mucous membrane lining the nasopharynx, consisting of pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells; it functions in mucociliary clearance of inhaled air and contains immune tissue such as adenoids as part of the mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue.

postnasal_drip.definition: A symptom characterized by the sensation of mucus from the nasal passages draining into the back of the throat, often causing throat clearing, coughing, or sore throat; typically due to increased mucus production or impaired drainage from infections, allergies, sinusitis, rhinitis, or irritants.

cadaver_graft.definition: A tissue graft or organ transplant harvested from a deceased human donor (cadaver) and implanted into another person to replace diseased or damaged tissue.

erythrocyte_sedimentation_rate.definition: A blood test that looks for signs of swelling (inlammation) in your body. Also called ESR.

white_blood_cell_count.definition: A laboratory test that counts white blood cells (leukocytes) in a specified volume of blood to assess immune status and help diagnose infection, inflammation, or hematologic disorders.

pulse_oximeter.definition: A noninvasive device that measures arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2) and often heart rate by emitting light and detecting its absorption at two wavelengths through a perfused site, usually a fingertip or earlobe.

intravenous_infusion.definition: A method of delivering fluids, medications, or nutrients directly into a vein through an IV line, allowing rapid systemic delivery and controlled administration of volume and rate (often via gravity or an infusion pump).

postanesthesia_care_unit.definition: A specialized hospital unit where patients recover from anesthesia after surgery, with continuous monitoring of breathing, heart rate, blood pressure, and consciousness, plus pain control, nausea management, and fluid balance, until stable enough for transfer to a lower-acuity area or discharge.

preoperative_care.definition: Care and preparations performed before a surgical procedure to optimize patient health and minimize perioperative risk, including preoperative assessment, necessary tests, optimization of medical conditions, medication management, fasting instructions, informed consent, and patient education.

postoperative_care.definition: Care provided after a surgical procedure to monitor recovery, manage pain, prevent and detect complications, maintain fluid and electrolyte balance, and support wound healing and return to baseline function; typically includes vital signs monitoring, wound care, medications, mobilization, and discharge planning.

nasal_airway.definition: The nasal airway is the passage through the nose from the nostrils to the nasopharynx that conducts air to the lungs; it’s part of the upper airway and functions to warm, humidify, and filter inspired air.

airway_patency.definition: The openness of the airway, allowing unobstructed passage of air into and out of the lungs; it is maintained by airway structure and neuromuscular control and can be compromised by edema, secretions, foreign bodies, or airway collapse.

postpartum depression.definition: When you feel overwhelmed, depressed, or sad for no reason after having a baby. Also called baby blues or post-pregnancy depression.

poststeroid panniculitis.definition: A lobular panniculitis of the subcutaneous fat that develops after withdrawal or rapid tapering of systemic corticosteroid therapy, presenting as tender erythematous nodules or plaques (often on the limbs); histology typically shows fat necrosis with a mixed inflammatory infiltrate, and it is usually self-limited, resolving over weeks to months (sometimes with brief anti-inflammatory treatment).

iliofemoral thrombophlebitis.definition: Inflammation with thrombosis of the iliac and/or femoral veins (deep venous thrombosis of the pelvis/thigh), presenting with leg pain, swelling, warmth, and possibly fever; carries risk of pulmonary embolism and can be septic if infection is present.

pituitary necrosis.definition: Death of pituitary gland tissue due to ischemia or hemorrhagic infarction, often causing hypopituitarism; can occur in contexts such as postpartum hemorrhage (Sheehan syndrome) or during pituitary apoplexy.

sheehan's syndrome.definition: Postpartum pituitary infarction due to severe obstetric hemorrhage and hypotension, resulting in hypopituitarism (deficiency of one or more pituitary hormones), classically presenting with failure to lactate after delivery and amenorrhea, along with fatigue and other signs of pituitary hormone deficiency.

postpartum psychosis.definition: A rare, acute psychiatric emergency occurring in the first days to weeks after childbirth, characterized by delusions or hallucinations, severe mood instability, confusion, insomnia, and risk of harm to the baby or self; it requires urgent psychiatric evaluation and treatment, often with antipsychotic and mood-stabilizing medications and inpatient care.

postperfusion syndrome.definition: A postoperative cognitive syndrome occurring after cardiopulmonary bypass, characterized by delirium, impaired memory and attention, slowed processing, and other neurocognitive deficits, attributed to microemboli, inflammatory responses, and cerebral hypoperfusion during perfusion (often referred to as pumphead syndrome).

postpericardiotomy syndrome.definition: An inflammatory syndrome that develops weeks after pericardial injury from cardiac surgery, characterized by fever and pericarditis with chest pain, often with pericardial and/or pleural effusions, and elevated inflammatory markers; believed to be autoimmune-mediated and treated with NSAIDs (and colchicine), with corticosteroids in select cases.

postpoliomyelitis muscular atrophy.definition: A chronic wasting of muscles that were weakened or paralyzed by poliomyelitis, due to ongoing denervation and remodeling of motor units after the acute infection, often contributing to reduced strength and functional decline.

postpolycythemia myeloid metaplasia.definition: A fibrotic phase of polycythemia vera in which the bone marrow is replaced by fibrous tissue (myelofibrosis), causing extramedullary hematopoiesis, splenomegaly, and anemia.

postprandial glucose test.definition: A blood test that measures the glucose level roughly 2 hours after a meal to assess how well the body metabolizes glucose and to monitor post-meal glycemic control.

postprandial pain.definition: Abdominal pain after meals, typically due to mesenteric ischemia from arterial insufficiency; the pain is usually cramp-like and may begin 15–60 minutes after eating, often leading to fear of eating and weight loss.

postprocedure recovery.definition: The period after a medical procedure during which a patient recovers from anesthesia and the procedure, with monitoring of vitals, management of pain and nausea, prevention and detection of complications, wound care, and planning for discharge or return to normal activities.

postprocessing.definition: Postprocessing in medical imaging refers to the processing of image data after acquisition to enhance visualization, quantify features, or aid interpretation. It includes techniques such as filtering, window/level adjustment, noise reduction, segmentation, registration, 3D reconstruction, and fusion of multimodal images.

postpubertal panhypopituitarism.definition: Postpubertal panhypopituitarism is a condition in which the pituitary gland fails to secrete multiple anterior pituitary hormones after puberty, producing secondary (central) adrenal insufficiency, secondary hypothyroidism, hypogonadism, and often growth hormone deficiency, with possible diabetes insipidus if posterior pituitary function is affected.

postterm infant.definition: A newborn delivered after 42 completed weeks of gestation (gestational age ≥ 42 weeks).

posttransfusion syndrome.definition: An adverse clinical syndrome occurring during or shortly after a blood transfusion, typically presenting with fever and systemic symptoms caused by immune- or nonimmune reactions to donor blood products; may include chills, dyspnea, hypotension, rash, or hemoglobinuria and requires prompt evaluation and management.

hemolytic effects.definition: Effects that cause rupture or destruction of red blood cells (hemolysis), leading to the release of hemoglobin into the plasma; can arise from immune-mediated injury, mechanical stress, toxins, or inherited/acquired conditions.

posttransplant diabetes.definition: New-onset diabetes mellitus that develops after an organ transplant in patients without preexisting diabetes; strongly associated with immunosuppressive therapy (eg, calcineurin inhibitors like tacrolimus or cyclosporine, glucocorticoids) and linked to higher risks of infections, cardiovascular disease, and adverse graft outcomes.

glucose intolerance.definition: A prediabetic condition in which the body's ability to regulate blood glucose is impaired, resulting in higher-than-normal blood glucose after a glucose load (impaired glucose tolerance) or in the fasting state (impaired fasting glucose), and indicating increased risk for progression to type 2 diabetes.

steroid diabetes.definition: A form of diabetes mellitus that develops as a complication of systemic corticosteroid (steroid) therapy, causing hyperglycemia through increased hepatic glucose production and insulin resistance; may be temporary or persistent depending on steroid exposure.

immunosuppressive agents.definition: Drugs that suppress or dampen the immune system's activity to prevent transplant rejection and treat autoimmune or inflammatory diseases.

traumatic epilepsy.definition: A form of epilepsy that develops following a traumatic brain injury, typically after a latent period, characterized by recurrent unprovoked seizures that may be focal or generalized and are related to structural brain damage from the injury.

posttraumatic osteoporosis.definition: A form of secondary osteoporosis caused by immobilization or reduced mechanical loading after a traumatic injury, leading to loss of bone mineral density and weakened bone architecture, often regional to the immobilized region and potentially reversible with remobilization and treatment.

posttraumatic spondylitis.definition: An inflammation of a vertebral body that develops after spinal trauma, often related to post-traumatic vertebral osteomyelitis or discitis; presents with localized back pain and may be associated with fever, and is diagnosed with imaging (usually MRI) and microbiologic studies, then treated with antibiotics if infection is present and with supportive care for inflammation.

ptsd.definition: A mental health disorder that some people develop after they experience or see a traumatic event, such as war, a car crash, or an earthquake.

postural albuminuria.definition: A form of proteinuria in which urinary albumin excretion rises when the person is upright (standing) and diminishes or normalizes when lying down; commonly seen in children and adolescents and generally considered benign with no renal pathology.

orthostatic proteinuria.definition: A benign condition in which urinary protein excretion increases when the person is upright (daytime posture) but remains normal when lying down; most common in healthy children/adolescents and diagnosed by showing higher daytime than nighttime protein excretion, with prognosis excellent and no specific therapy beyond periodic monitoring.

bronchial drainage.definition: The removal of mucus and other secretions from the bronchial passages to clear the airways, typically achieved by coughing or suctioning and by chest physiotherapy techniques such as postural drainage and percussion.

vibration.definition: An oscillatory mechanical motion characterized by rapid back-and-forth movement; in clinical neurology, it denotes the perception of such oscillations (commonly tested with a tuning fork) to evaluate dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway integrity.

increased intracerebral pressure.definition: An abnormal rise in intracranial pressure (ICP) due to increased intracranial volume from brain edema, hemorrhage, mass lesions, hydrocephalus, or other intracranial pathology; elevated ICP can compromise cerebral perfusion and lead to brain injury. Normal ICP is about 7–15 mmHg in adults; sustained elevations above ~20 mmHg are concerning.

head-down position.definition: A body position in which the patient lies on their back with the head lower than the feet, typically achieved by tilting the bed or table.

postural proteinuria.definition: A benign condition in which urinary protein excretion increases when a person is upright (orthostatic) and normalizes when lying down; most common in children and adolescents, diagnosed by higher protein in daytime urine versus an early-morning supine urine sample.

postural vertigo.definition: Vertigo elicited by changes in body position relative to gravity (such as lying down, standing up, or turning the head), typically due to vestibular dysfunction in the inner ear.

positional vertigo.definition: An inner-ear disorder characterized by brief episodes of spinning vertigo triggered by changes in head position relative to gravity, caused by displaced otoconia within the semicircular canals.

benign myalgic encephalomyelitis.definition: A chronic multisystem illness (often called myalgic encephalomyelitis or chronic fatigue syndrome) characterized by persistent fatigue not relieved by rest, post-exertional malaise, cognitive difficulties, unrefreshing sleep, and often pain or autonomic symptoms.
