If you meant a different term (e.g., "Icelandic disease" or a specific condition described in Iceland), let me know and I’ll assist.

royal free disease.definition: A historical designation for an outbreak of post-viral fatigue symptoms identified at London’s Royal Free Hospital in 1955; in modern usage it is generally equated with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), a disorder of persistent fatigue with neurocognitive, sleep, and pain symptoms not explained by another condition.

myalgic encephalomyelitis.definition: A chronic multisystem illness characterized by persistent, disabling fatigue lasting at least six months not explained by another condition, accompanied by post-exertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep, cognitive impairment, and often orthostatic intolerance and other accompanying symptoms.

postvaccinal encephalitis.definition: An extremely rare, immune-mediated inflammatory brain condition that occurs after vaccination, typically presenting within days to weeks with encephalopathy (altered consciousness) and neurologic deficits such as seizures or focal weakness; believed to reflect an autoimmune/parainfectious reaction to vaccine antigens; treatment is supportive and may involve immunotherapy (e.g., corticosteroids); prognosis ranges from full recovery to lasting neurologic impairment.

postvaccinal encephalomyelitis.definition: An acute inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that occurs days to weeks after vaccination (often after a viral illness), presenting with rapid onset multifocal neurologic deficits and sometimes encephalopathy; it is typically monophasic and is now usually referred to as acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM).

postviral fatigue syndrome.definition: Prolonged, disabling fatigue that begins after an acute viral illness and is not explained by another medical condition, often with post-exertional malaise and additional symptoms such as cognitive difficulties, unrefreshing sleep, headaches, muscle or joint pains, and reduced tolerance for physical or mental activity.

potassemia.definition: An abnormal level of potassium in the blood; normal serum potassium is about 3.5–5.0 mEq/L. Elevated levels (hyperkalemia) or decreased levels (hypokalemia) can cause muscle weakness and potentially life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias, and are evaluated by measuring serum potassium along with renal function and acid–base status.

sex hormones.definition: Hormones that regulate sexual development, puberty, and reproduction. The main classes are estrogens, androgens, and progestogens, produced mainly by the gonads (ovaries and testes) and, to a lesser extent, the adrenal glands. They drive puberty and sexual differentiation, regulate the menstrual cycle and fertility, influence secondary sexual characteristics, and have wide-ranging effects on bone, brain, and other tissues by binding to intracellular receptors and modulating gene expression.

potassium pump.definition: Na+/K+-ATPase, a membrane enzyme that uses energy from ATP hydrolysis to exchange 3 Na+ ions out of the cell for 2 K+ ions into the cell, maintaining the resting membrane potential, cell volume, and electrochemical gradients.

sodium reabsorption.definition: Movement of sodium ions from the filtrate in the nephron back into the bloodstream, reclaiming most filtered Na+ and helping regulate extracellular fluid volume, osmolality, and blood pressure. It occurs along the nephron (proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule, collecting duct) and is driven by Na+/K+-ATPase activity, with hormonal modulation by aldosterone and other regulators.

potassium secretion.definition: The renal process by which potassium ions are secreted from the peritubular blood into the nephron lumen (primarily distal tubule and collecting duct) for urinary excretion, mediated by Na+-K+-ATPase–driven gradients and luminal K+ channels (e.g., ROMK, BK) and regulated by aldosterone, tubular flow, and acid–base status.

potassium hydroxide.definition: A strongly caustic alkaline compound (strong base) with the chemical formula KOH; used as a laboratory reagent and in clinical diagnoses (e.g., KOH preparations) to dissolve keratin and reveal fungal elements; contact can cause severe chemical burns.

potassium salts.definition: Salts in which potassium is the predominant cation; chemical compounds formed by replacing the hydrogen (or another cation) of an acid with potassium, used to supply potassium and to help manage electrolyte balance; common examples include potassium chloride, potassium citrate, and potassium sulfate.

potassium phosphate.definition: A salt of potassium and phosphoric acid; exists in mono-, di-, and tri-basic forms (KH2PO4, K2HPO4, and K3PO4) and is used as a source of potassium and phosphate in dietary supplements, IV/enteral nutrition, and pharmaceutical formulations.

potassium indoxyl sulfate.definition: Potassium indoxyl sulfate is the potassium salt form of indoxyl sulfate, a gut-derived uremic toxin produced from hepatic sulfation of indole (a tryptophan metabolite) and excreted by the kidneys; its levels accumulate with renal dysfunction.

digitalis intoxication.definition: Toxic state from digitalis glycosides (most often digoxin) due to inhibition of Na+/K+-ATPase, causing gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, anorexia), neurologic/visual changes (confusion, dizziness, yellow-green/blurred vision), and cardiac conduction abnormalities (bradycardia, AV block, or various tachyarrhythmias), with hyperkalemia possible in severe overdose.

amiloride.definition: A potassium-sparing diuretic that blocks epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) in the late distal tubule and collecting duct, reducing sodium reabsorption and promoting mild diuresis with potassium retention.

gastrointestinal disturbance.definition: A nonspecific term for symptoms arising from the gastrointestinal tract, such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, bloating, or constipation; can result from infection, inflammation, functional disorders (e.g., irritable bowel syndrome), medication effects, dietary factors, or systemic illness.

ulceration of small bowel.definition: Loss of mucosal integrity with formation of an ulcer in the small intestine (duodenum, jejunum, or ileum), typically due to inflammatory, ischemic, infectious, or drug-induced injury (e.g., Crohn disease, NSAID enteropathy); may present with abdominal pain, GI bleeding, anemia, or obstruction and can lead to perforation or stricture.

small bowel ulceration.definition: Ulceration of the mucosal lining of the small intestine (duodenum through ileum), a breach in the mucosa that can cause abdominal pain and gastrointestinal bleeding and may result from inflammatory, infectious, ischemic, or drug-related processes.

thyroid disorders.definition: A group of conditions affecting the thyroid gland that alter the production or action of thyroid hormones, causing hypothyroidism (low hormone) or hyperthyroidism (high hormone) and related structural disorders such as goiter, nodules, thyroiditis, or thyroid cancer.

powassan virus.definition: A tick-borne flavivirus transmitted by Ixodes ticks in North America; infection can cause encephalitis or meningitis with fever, headache, and neurologic deficits; incubation is typically about one week; diagnosed by serology or PCR; treatment is supportive; no specific antiviral therapy or approved human vaccine; prevention focuses on avoiding tick bites and prompt tick removal.

powassan virus infection.definition: An uncommon tick-borne flavivirus infection transmitted by Ixodes ticks (notably Ixodes scapularis) that can range from asymptomatic illness to severe neuroinvasive disease, including meningitis or encephalitis, often with fever, headache, vomiting, and neurologic symptoms; there is no specific antiviral treatment and management is supportive, with prevention focused on tick bite avoidance.

tick-borne arbovirus.definition: An arthropod-borne virus transmitted by ticks to humans or other vertebrates; tick-borne arboviruses include several viruses from multiple families and can cause illnesses ranging from fever to encephalitis or hemorrhagic disease, depending on the specific virus.

poxvirus.definition: Any member of the Poxviridae family, a group of large, enveloped, brick-shaped double-stranded DNA viruses that replicate in the cytoplasm and cause diseases such as smallpox (variola), molluscum contagiosum, cowpox, and monkeypox.

rathke's pouch.definition: An embryonic diverticulum of the oral ectoderm from the roof of the stomodeum that migrates to form the anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis); remnants may give rise to craniopharyngiomas.

poultice.definition: A soft, moist mass of material (such as herbs, bread, meal, or clay) that is applied to the skin, usually wrapped in a cloth, to relieve inflammation, pain, or swelling by soothing tissues or drawing out fluids; typically left in place for several hours.

pott's disease.definition: Tuberculosis of the spine (vertebral TB), a form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, characterized by destruction of vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs, spinal deformity (often kyphosis), and possible neurologic compression or deficits.

tuberculous spondylitis.definition: A spinal infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, typically starting in the anterior vertebral bodies and adjoining discs, leading to vertebral destruction and collapse with kyphotic deformity, often with paravertebral abscess formation and potential spinal cord compression.

pott's fracture.definition: A bimalleolar fracture-dislocation of the ankle involving fractures of both the medial and lateral malleoli with disruption of ankle joint congruity, typically due to an eversion mechanism.

dupuytren's fracture.definition: Not a standard medical term; no widely accepted definition.

potter-bucky grid.definition: A grid used in diagnostic radiography consisting of interleaved lead strips and radiolucent spacers that absorbs scattered x-rays before they reach the image receptor; mounted on a movable frame (the Bucky) so it shifts slightly during exposure to reduce grid-line artifacts.

purified protein derivative.definition: A standardized preparation of purified proteins derived from Mycobacterium tuberculosis used in the tuberculin skin test to detect prior infection with TB; injected intradermally, a delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction (induration) after 48–72 hours indicates prior exposure.

ppd.definition: A purified protein derivative of Mycobacterium tuberculosis used in the tuberculin skin test to detect latent TB infection; an intradermal injection elicits a delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction with induration measured 48–72 hours after administration.

penicillin v.definition: An acid-stable, narrow-spectrum penicillin antibiotic (phenoxymethylpenicillin) used orally for mild to moderate infections caused by susceptible bacteria, especially streptococci; inactivated by beta-lactamase–producing organisms.

penicillinase-producing neisseria gonorr.definition: A strain of Neisseria gonorrhoeae that produces penicillinase (beta-lactamase), an enzyme that hydrolyzes penicillin and related beta-lactam antibiotics, leading to penicillin resistance.

ppm.definition: One part per one million parts of a mixture; a unit of concentration used to express very small amounts of a substance in air, water, or other media. For dilute aqueous solutions, 1 ppm is approximately 1 milligram per liter.

ppma.definition: No standard medical definition exists for the acronym PPMA. Please provide the field or the full form of the acronym to give a precise definition.

ppng.definition: Definition not found in trusted medical dictionaries. Please provide context or the full form of the acronym so I can help accurately.

ppo.definition: A type of health insurance plan that contracts with a network of providers to offer services at discounted rates; members pay less when using in-network providers; out-of-network care is allowed but more expensive and may require higher deductibles/coinsurance; generally does not require a referral to see a specialist.

pps.definition: A condition affecting polio survivors years after the initial infection, characterized by new or progressive weakness in muscles previously affected, fatigue, reduced endurance, and muscle or joint pain; management is supportive and multidisciplinary, focusing on energy conservation, physical therapy, assistive devices, and pain control.

positive pressure ventilation.definition: Delivery of breaths by applying positive pressure to the airways to inflate the lungs during inspiration, typically via a face mask or endotracheal/intubation tube, using a ventilator or manual bag to deliver controlled tidal volumes and gas exchange.

ringer's solution.definition: An isotonic intravenous crystalloid electrolyte solution containing sodium, potassium, and calcium in concentrations approximating extracellular fluid, used for fluid resuscitation and electrolyte maintenance; it does not contain bicarbonate (lactated versions exist separately).

prader-willi syndrome.definition: A genetic disorder caused by absence of paternally expressed genes on chromosome 15q11-q13 (most commonly from a paternal deletion or maternal uniparental disomy/imprinting defect) that presents in infancy with hypotonia and feeding difficulties, followed by hyperphagia and obesity, short stature, hypogonadism, and mild-to-moderate intellectual disability.

angelman syndrome.definition: A genetic neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss of function of the maternal UBE3A gene on chromosome 15 (often due to imprinting defects, deletions, or paternal uniparental disomy). It presents in early childhood with global developmental delay, severe speech impairment or absence of speech, ataxia, seizures, and a characteristic happy demeanor with frequent smiling and laughter.

pralidoxime chloride.definition: An oxime cholinesterase reactivator used to treat organophosphate poisoning; it reactivates acetylcholinesterase inhibited by organophosphates by cleaving the phosphorous-enzyme bond, and is typically given with atropine (often IV or IM).

pramlintide.definition: A synthetic analog of human amylin used as an injectable medication to improve glycemic control in type 1 or type 2 diabetes when used with mealtime insulin; it slows gastric emptying, suppresses postprandial glucagon, and promotes satiety.

pramipexole.definition: A non-ergoline dopamine agonist with preferential D3 receptor activity, used orally to treat Parkinson disease and restless legs syndrome by stimulating dopamine receptors in the brain.

islet cell antibodies.definition: Autoantibodies directed against pancreatic islet cell cytoplasmic antigens; a marker of autoimmune type 1 diabetes and islet autoimmunity, often present before or at the onset of clinical diabetes.

pramosone.definition: Topical local anesthetic used to relieve itching, burning, and pain from minor skin irritations, insect bites, rashes, hemorrhoids, and sunburn; commonly found in OTC creams, ointments, and wipes.

type 1 diabetes.definition: An autoimmune disorder in which the body's immune system destroys pancreatic beta cells, resulting in absolute insulin deficiency and lifelong dependence on insulin therapy; it most often presents in children or young adults and is characterized by hyperglycemia and, if untreated, ketoacidosis.

type 2 diabetes.definition: A chronic metabolic disorder characterized by hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with relative insulin deficiency, often associated with obesity and aging, and managed with lifestyle changes, oral medications, and sometimes insulin.

injection-site reaction.definition: A localized inflammatory reaction at the site of an injection, typically presenting with redness, swelling, warmth, and pain (and sometimes itching); caused by the body's response to the injected substance or components of the injection, and usually resolves without intervention.

systemic allergy.definition: A widespread allergic reaction involving multiple organ systems, typically IgE-mediated, occurring after exposure to an allergen and ranging from generalized urticaria and angioedema to life-threatening anaphylaxis.

hydrocortisone acetate.definition: An ester of hydrocortisone (acetate) that acts as a topical glucocorticoid with anti-inflammatory and antipruritic effects; used in creams, ointments, and ophthalmic preparations to treat inflammatory skin and ocular conditions.

pramoxine hydrochloride.definition: A topical local anesthetic used to relieve itching, burning, and pain from minor skin irritations (e.g., insect bites, rashes, hemorrhoids) by reversibly blocking sodium channels in nerve membranes and inhibiting nerve impulse conduction.

perianal pain.definition: Pain around the anal region (peri-anal), commonly due to anorectal disorders such as anal fissure, hemorrhoids, abscess or infection, or skin irritation; other possible causes include proctitis, dermatitis, or referred pain.

perianal swelling.definition: Swelling in the perianal region (around the anus) due to fluid accumulation from inflammation or infection of the perianal tissues; common causes include perianal abscess, hemorrhoids, cellulitis, trauma, or fissures, and it is often painful with possible redness, warmth, discharge, or fever.

anogenital pruritus.definition: Itching localized to the anal and genital region; a symptom with diverse causes including dermatologic conditions (eczema/dermatitis), infections (yeast, bacteria, parasites), irritants/moisture, hemorrhoids or fissures, and systemic diseases.

minor burns.definition: A minor burn is a superficial burn that involves only the epidermis (a first-degree burn) or a small area of the dermis (a superficial second-degree burn); it causes redness and pain and usually heals within about 1–2 weeks with minimal or no scarring.

prandial.definition: Relating to a meal; occurring during mealtime.

postprandial.definition: Relating to or occurring after a meal.

preprandial.definition: Occurring before a meal; used to describe measurements or interventions (e.g., glucose levels or medications) taken prior to eating.

immunoglobulin e.definition: A class of antibody (IgE) that mediates allergic reactions and defense against parasitic infections; it binds to FcεRI on mast cells and basophils, and allergen-induced cross-linking triggers degranulation with release of histamine and other mediators.

radioimmunosorbent test.definition: A type of immunoassay that uses radiolabeled reagents and a solid-phase capture to detect and quantify a specific antigen or antibody in a sample; after incubation and washing, the bound radioactivity is measured and is proportional to the analyte concentration.

passive transfer test.definition: A diagnostic or research procedure in which serum containing antibodies from an immune donor is transferred to a nonimmune recipient to determine whether passive immunity can be conferred, thereby assessing the presence and functional activity of specific antibodies in the donor serum.

pravastatin.definition: A hydrophilic statin and HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor used to lower LDL cholesterol and triglycerides and modestly raise HDL, thereby reducing cardiovascular risk in hyperlipidemia or patients at risk for atherosclerotic disease. It works by inhibiting hepatic cholesterol synthesis, leading to upregulation of LDL receptors. Taken orally, typically once daily in the evening; avoid in pregnancy. Common adverse effects include myalgia and elevated liver enzymes; rare rhabdomyolysis.

antihyperlipidemic agent.definition: A medication that lowers lipid levels in the blood (cholesterol and/or triglycerides), used to treat hyperlipidemia and reduce cardiovascular risk.

terazosin.definition: A drug used to treat symptoms of an enlarged prostate gland. It relieves constriction of the urethra and improves urine flow by relaxing the smooth muscle tissue in the capsule that surrounds the prostate.

doxazosin.definition: An oral alpha-1 adrenergic receptor blocker used to treat hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia by relaxing vascular smooth muscle (reducing vascular resistance) and relaxing smooth muscle in the bladder neck and prostate to improve urinary flow.

prazosin.definition: A member of a class of drugs called alpha blockers. It eases the symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia by relaxing smooth muscle tissue in the capsule that surrounds the prostate.

anxiety disorders.definition: A group of mental disorders characterized by excessive, persistent fear or anxiety and related avoidance or somatic symptoms that cause distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. The category includes generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, and specific phobias (with related conditions such as agoraphobia and separation anxiety in children).

spasticity.definition: A motor disorder characterized by a velocity-dependent increase in muscle tone with exaggerated stretch reflexes due to lesions of the upper motor neurons (corticospinal tract), commonly presenting as stiffness, spasms, and sometimes clonus.

progressive resistance exercise.definition: A training method in which the resistance used during exercises is gradually increased over time to stimulate muscular strength and hypertrophy, typically by adding weight, increasing repetitions, or progressing to more challenging resistance as the individual adapts.

preadmission certification.definition: A preauthorization by a health insurer or payer to determine that an inpatient admission or proposed service is medically necessary and eligible for coverage before the patient is admitted; also known as precertification or prior authorization.

prealbumin test.definition: Serum blood test that measures a liver-synthesized transport protein to assess short-term nutritional status; due to its short half-life (about 2 days), levels change quickly with protein intake and inflammatory states, and low values suggest acute malnutrition or inflammation, while interpretation should be in context with other nutritional markers.

pab.definition: There isn’t a single standard medical definition for "PAB" chosen universally; its meaning depends on context. Could you share the field or the full phrase where you saw it? I can give a precise definition once I know the intended term.

24-hour urine.definition: A urine collection procedure in which all urine produced over a 24-hour period is collected and analyzed to measure excretion rates of substances (such as protein, electrolytes, or minerals) or to assess kidney function (e.g., creatinine clearance); accurate results require starting after the first morning void and refrigerating the samples until analysis.

cerebrospinal fluid analysis.definition: Laboratory testing of cerebrospinal fluid collected by lumbar puncture to evaluate cells, protein and glucose levels, opening pressure, and to detect infection, inflammation, hemorrhage, or other CNS disease through microbiologic, cytologic, and biochemical analyses.

preanesthetic medication.definition: Drugs given before anesthesia to ease induction by reducing anxiety and pain, providing sedation and amnesia, decreasing secretions and autonomic responses, and helping prevent perioperative nausea and other adverse effects; commonly include benzodiazepines, opioids, anticholinergics, antiemetics, and H2 antagonists.

preaortic node.definition: A lymph node located in front of the abdominal aorta; part of the preaortic lymph node group around the origins of the celiac trunk, superior mesenteric, and inferior mesenteric arteries, which drain abdominal viscera and usually drain into the paraaortic (lateral aortic) nodes.

precancerous dermatitis.definition: A skin condition in which inflammatory changes are accompanied by dysplastic, precancerous alterations of epidermal keratinocytes, indicating a risk of progression to squamous cell carcinoma.

prececocolic fascia.definition: An anterolateral fascial plane formed by the reflected peritoneum anterior to the cecum (in the ileocecal region), separating the cecum/ascending colon from surrounding structures and contributing to the boundary of the right lower quadrant.

parietal abdominal fascia.definition: A deep fascia lining the inner surface of the abdominal wall, lying between the abdominal muscles (notably transversus abdominis and friends) and the peritoneum; often referred to as the transversalis (endoabdominal) fascia, forming part of the endoabdominal fascia that separates extraperitoneal fat from the peritoneal cavity.

lymphatic intestinal trunk.definition: A lymphatic trunk that drains lymph from the intestines (primarily chyle from the small intestine) and empties into the cisterna chyli or the thoracic duct.

lateral aortic node.definition: A lymph node located along the lateral aspect of the abdominal aorta (the lumbar/para-aortic lymph node group); it drains lymph from the kidneys, gonads, adrenal glands, and surrounding retroperitoneal structures, and is a common route for metastasis from abdominal and retroperitoneal cancers.

retroaortic node.definition: A lymph node located posterior to the aorta, in the retroperitoneal space; part of abdominal lymphatic drainage.

precordial lead.definition: A chest electrode used in ECG recording that measures the heart's electrical activity from the precordial region; in a standard 12-lead ECG these correspond to leads V1 through V6 placed across the anterior chest to provide anterior-to-lateral views of the heart.

precordial pain.definition: Chest pain located in the precordial region (over the heart), which may arise from cardiac causes such as ischemia, angina, or myocardial infarction, or from noncardiac causes such as esophageal disorders, pericarditis, or musculoskeletal chest wall pain.

right ventricular thrust.definition: A palpable systolic impulse or lift produced by the contraction of the right ventricle, typically felt along the left lower sternal border; indicates right ventricular hypertrophy or overload, often from pulmonary hypertension or chronic lung disease.

pulmonic area.definition: Auscultation area on the left chest at the second intercostal space near the sternal border where the pulmonic valve is best heard, used to evaluate pulmonic heart sounds and murmurs.

pulmonic valve.definition: A semilunar heart valve between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery; it opens to allow blood ejection into the pulmonary circulation and closes to prevent backflow into the right ventricle.

mitral (apical) area.definition: A region on the chest over the cardiac apex—typically the left 5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line—where the mitral valve is best auscultated, often best heard with the patient in the left lateral decubitus position.

aortic area.definition: The area on the chest over the right second intercostal space at the sternal border where the aortic valve is best heard during auscultation.

tricuspid area.definition: A region on the left lower chest at the left sternal border (around the 4th intercostal space) where the tricuspid valve is best auscultated.

midsternal line.definition: An imaginary vertical reference line that runs along the midline of the sternum, used as a surface anatomy landmark to describe the positions of thoracic structures and to guide clinical procedures.

raynauds phenomenon.definition: A vasospastic disorder causing intermittent narrowing of small arteries in the digits, leading to color changes (pallor, cyanosis, then redness), numbness or tingling, and sometimes pain, typically triggered by cold or emotional stress; it can be primary or secondary to another condition.

prednicarbate.definition: A synthetic topical corticosteroid used to treat inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema and dermatitis; it has anti-inflammatory, antipruritic effects and is formulated for topical use (e.g., cream or ointment) with relatively low systemic absorption.

preemie.definition: A premature infant, born before 37 completed weeks of gestation.

ophthalmological.definition: Relating to ophthalmology, the branch of medicine that deals with the eye, its anatomy, function, and diseases.

lown-ganong-levine syndrome.definition: An ECG-based pre-excitation syndrome in which an accessory AV conduction pathway bypasses the AV node, shortening the PR interval with a normal QRS and no delta wave, and it can predispose to paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia.

luteoma.definition: A benign ovarian stromal lesion of luteinized cells, most often arising during pregnancy; it can secrete androgens, causing maternal virilization and, less commonly, virilization of a female fetus; typically regresses after delivery.

pregnanediol.definition: A metabolite of progesterone; a diol derivative of the pregnane skeleton formed by hepatic reduction of progesterone, often measured in urine as pregnanediol glucuronide to assess progesterone production and luteal activity.

pregnanediol test.definition: A diagnostic test that measures urinary pregnanediol, a metabolite of progesterone, to assess luteal-phase progesterone production and confirm whether ovulation has occurred (historically used in infertility workups).

preimplantation.definition: Relating to the stage before an embryo implants into the uterine lining (endometrium); used to describe early embryonic development prior to implantation and procedures performed on embryos before transfer.

preinfarction angina.definition: An ischemic chest pain pattern that signals imminent myocardial infarction, typically evolving as crescendo or new, worsening angina—more frequent, longer in duration, or occurring at rest—and often not adequately relieved by nitroglycerin, representing an acute coronary syndrome requiring urgent evaluation and management.

preinvasive carcinoma.definition: A malignant epithelial neoplasm whose cells are confined to the epithelium and have not invaded the underlying basement membrane; a preinvasive stage of cancer that may progress to invasive disease if untreated.

preload.definition: The filling pressure or volume of the ventricles at the end of diastole, reflecting venous return and the initial stretch of cardiac muscle fibers before contraction; a determinant of stroke volume via the Frank-Starling mechanism.

premalignant.definition: Not cancerous; a lesion or tissue change with the potential to progress to malignant cancer over time if left untreated.

premarin.definition: A brand-name preparation of conjugated estrogens derived from the urine of pregnant mares, used for estrogen replacement therapy in menopause to relieve vasomotor symptoms and vaginal atrophy and to reduce osteoporosis risk in postmenopausal women.

premarket approval.definition: A U.S. FDA regulatory pathway for high‑risk medical devices (Class III) requiring substantial evidence of safety and effectiveness from clinical and nonclinical data, plus manufacturing information and risk–benefit analysis, before the device may be marketed.

pac.definition: An early beat in the atria that feels like the heart skipped a beat.

premature atrial complex.definition: An early heartbeat arising from atrial tissue outside the SA node, producing a premature, abnormally shaped P wave with a normally conducted (narrow) QRS complex; usually benign but can indicate atrial irritability or underlying heart disease.

premature beat.definition: An early heartbeat that occurs before the next expected beat, arising from an ectopic focus in the atria or ventricles; often called a premature atrial contraction (PAC) or premature ventricular contraction (PVC).

premature ejaculation.definition: Ejaculation that occurs before or immediately after penetration; this can interfere with a couple having a mutually satisfying sexual experience.

left ventricular.definition: Relating to the left ventricle, the heart's main pumping chamber that receives oxygenated blood from the left atrium and ejects it into the aorta for systemic circulation.

partial-onset seizures.definition: Seizures that originate in a localized area of one cerebral hemisphere; they may remain confined (focal aware/simple partial) or involve impaired consciousness (focal impaired-awareness/complex partial) and can secondarily generalize to involve both hemispheres.

postherpetic.definition: Relating to or occurring after an episode of herpes zoster (shingles); typically used to describe symptoms that persist after the rash has resolved, especially neuropathic pain that follows shingles.

premature labor.definition: Labor that begins before 37 completed weeks of gestation, marked by regular uterine contractions and progressive cervical dilation or effacement, which can result in preterm birth.

sucking reflex.definition: A primitive neonatal reflex in which tactile stimulation of the lips or palate elicits rhythmic sucking movements of the mouth, facilitating feeding and coordinating sucking with swallowing and breathing; typically integrates as voluntary sucking develops, around 4–6 months of age.

swallowing reflex.definition: An involuntary brainstem-mediated reflex triggered by sensory stimulation of the oropharynx that coordinates airway protection with the sequential contraction of oral, pharyngeal, and esophageal muscles to propel a bolus from the mouth into the esophagus.

neurological sequelae.definition: Long-term aftereffects of a neurological disease or injury, manifesting as persistent deficits in motor, sensory, cognitive, or autonomic function that remain after the acute phase.

premature systole.definition: An ectopic heartbeat that occurs earlier than the next expected normal beat, representing a premature contraction of the atria or ventricles (premature atrial contraction or premature ventricular contraction); typically followed by a compensatory pause and may be benign or indicate underlying cardiac irritability.

premature ventricular complex.definition: An early heartbeat arising from an ectopic focus in the ventricles, producing a wide, abnormal QRS complex on ECG with no preceding P wave and often followed by a compensatory pause; can be benign or indicate underlying heart disease or electrolyte disturbances.

pvc.definition: An extra heartbeat that begins in the ventricles and occurs earlier than the normal heartbeat. On ECG it appears as a wide, abnormal QRS complex and is often perceived as a skipped beat or palpitations. Usually benign in healthy individuals, but frequent occurrences can indicate underlying heart disease or electrolyte imbalance.

atrioventricular junction.definition: An anatomical region of the heart that conducts impulses from the atria to the ventricles, comprising mainly the atrioventricular (AV) node and the His-Purkinje system; the conduction gateway between atria and ventricles.

premature thelarche.definition: Isolated breast development in a prepubertal child (most often a girl) occurring before age 8, without other signs of puberty; usually benign and self-limited, but follow-up is advised to exclude other causes or progression to central precocious puberty.

premedicate.definition: To administer medication before a medical procedure or event to prevent or lessen potential complications or adverse effects, such as anxiety, pain, nausea, or infection.

tranquilizer.definition: A drug that reduces anxiety and induces calmness, often with sedative effects. Historically referred to as tranquilizers; major tranquilizers are antipsychotics, while minor tranquilizers are anxiolytics/sedatives (e.g., benzodiazepines).

antinausea.definition: A property or agent that prevents or relieves nausea and vomiting, typically referring to antiemetic medications.

premenarchal.definition: Relating to or occurring before menarche; before the onset of the first menstrual period.

premenstrual.definition: Occurring before the onset of menstruation; relating to the premenstrual phase of the menstrual cycle, typically the luteal phase, during which hormonal fluctuations may cause symptoms.

premenstrual dysphoric disorder.definition: A severe, cyclic mood and physical syndrome that occurs in the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle and resolves with the onset of menses, characterized by marked mood symptoms (such as irritability, depressed mood, anxiety, and mood swings) plus physical symptoms, causing significant functional impairment; diagnosed using DSM-5 criteria requiring multiple symptoms in the final week before menses on most cycles.

pmdd.definition: A severe, disabling form of premenstrual syndrome characterized by prominent mood symptoms (such as marked affective lability, irritability or anger, depressed mood, anxiety) and physical symptoms that recur in the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle and remit with the onset of menses, causing significant distress or impairment in daily functioning; symptoms must occur in most cycles for at least the past year and not be attributable to another condition or substance.

prenatal surgery.definition: Procedures performed on a fetus in utero during pregnancy to repair or palliate congenital anomalies, often using fetal endoscopic or open surgical techniques to improve postnatal outcomes.

ultrasound scanning.definition: A noninvasive imaging modality that uses high-frequency sound waves emitted by a transducer to produce real-time images of internal organs and tissues; it does not involve ionizing radiation and is commonly used to evaluate the abdomen, pelvis, heart, and fetus, with Doppler modes assessing blood flow.

chorionic villi sampling.definition: A prenatal diagnostic test in which placental tissue is sampled to evaluate fetal chromosomal and genetic disorders; typically performed between 10 and 13 weeks of gestation by a transabdominal or transcervical approach; carries a small risk of miscarriage.

genetic counseling.definition: A communication-based service that assesses familial risk for inherited conditions, explains how genes and inheritance affect risk, discusses available genetic tests and their limitations, interprets test results, and provides psychosocial support to help individuals and families make informed medical and reproductive decisions.

genetic screening.definition: Testing of asymptomatic individuals or a population to identify those who carry a genetic variant associated with a hereditary condition or who are at increased risk of developing a genetic disorder, so that appropriate diagnostic confirmation or preventive measures can be pursued.

chromosomal analysis.definition: A genetic test that analyzes the number and structure of a person’s chromosomes to detect numerical or structural abnormalities, such as aneuploidy, deletions, duplications, translocations, or other rearrangements.

urinary tract obstruction.definition: A blockage that prevents the normal flow of urine through the urinary tract (kidneys, ureters, bladder, or urethra), causing partial or complete urinary retention and backpressure on the kidneys, which can lead to hydronephrosis and renal impairment if untreated. Common causes include urinary stones, strictures, tumors, prostatic enlargement, congenital anomalies, or postoperative edema.

labioscrotal fold.definition: A paired embryonic skin fold in the urogenital region that develops into the scrotum in males and the labia majora in females; they fuse to form the scrotum in males, while remaining unfused in females.

urethral groove.definition: A shallow groove on the ventral surface of the developing penis that becomes the penile urethra as the urethral folds fuse and the urethral plate canalizes; incomplete closure can result in hypospadias.

genital tubercle.definition: An embryonic prominence on the anterior end of the cloacal membrane that develops into the external genitalia: the penis in males and the clitoris in females.

optic cups.definition: The central pale depression of the optic disc, representing thinning or loss of retinal nerve fiber tissue; it is bounded by the neuroretinal rim. Its size relative to the optic disc (cup-to-disc ratio) is used in glaucoma assessment.

lens pits.definition: Small, pit-like depressions on the surface or capsule of the crystalline lens, a rare congenital ocular anomaly that is usually asymptomatic and may be found incidentally on slit-lamp examination; clinical significance varies.

nasal pits.definition: Embryological indentations of the nasal placodes on the frontonasal prominence that invaginate to form the nasal sacs, which become the nasal cavities.

heart tube.definition: An embryologic structure: the primitive, single, straight heart tube formed by the fusion of endocardial tubes, which later folds (loops) and undergoes septation to form the mature heart chambers and great vessels.

syncytiotrophoblast.definition: The multinucleated outer layer of the chorionic villi formed by fused cytotrophoblast cells, which invades the maternal decidua and secretes pregnancy hormones such as human chorionic gonadotropin.

cytotrophoblast.definition: The inner cellular layer of the placental trophoblast composed of mononucleated proliferating cells that forms the cellular lining of the chorionic villi; it differentiates into extravillous trophoblasts and fuses to form the syncytiotrophoblast, which covers the villi and mediates nutrient exchange.

inner cell mass.definition: A cluster of pluripotent cells inside the mammalian blastocyst that gives rise to the embryo proper; it differentiates into the epiblast and hypoblast, which form the fetus and its extraembryonic tissues.

somite.definition: A somite is a paired block of paraxial mesoderm formed in a segmented pattern along the developing embryo; it differentiates into the sclerotome (vertebrae and rib cartilage), the myotome (skeletal muscle), and the dermatome (dermis), giving rise to the axial skeleton, associated muscles, and back skin.

primitive streak.definition: A transient, midline structure on the dorsal surface of the early embryonic disc during gastrulation, through which epiblast cells migrate to form mesoderm and endoderm (with the remaining epiblast forming ectoderm), thereby establishing the primitive axis of the embryo.

pharyngeal arches.definition: A series of paired embryonic swellings on the developing pharynx that contribute to the head and neck structures; each arch contains mesenchyme (from neural crest and mesoderm), a cartilage precursor, a muscle component, a cranial nerve, and an arterial segment, and is separated by pharyngeal grooves and pouches.

otic pit.definition: A transient invagination of the surface ectoderm (the otic placode) in the developing hindbrain region that deepens to form the otic vesicle, the embryologic precursor of the inner ear.

crl.definition: A prenatal ultrasound measurement of fetal length from the crown (top of the head) to the rump (buttocks), used to estimate gestational age during early pregnancy.

bitemporal hemianopia.definition: Loss of the temporal (outer) halves of the visual field in both eyes, typically due to compression of the optic chiasm (often from a pituitary adenoma) affecting the crossing nasal retinal fibers.

suprasellar calcification.definition: Radiologic finding of calcified deposits in the suprasellar region (above the sella turcica), often seen incidentally but can be associated with suprasellar lesions such as craniopharyngioma.

gonadotrophic hormones.definition: Pituitary gonadotropins (luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone) that stimulate the gonads (ovaries and testes) to produce gametes and sex steroids; their secretion is regulated by hypothalamic GnRH and by negative feedback from estrogen/progesterone and testosterone.

laboratory tests.definition: Medical tests that check a sample of your blood, urine, or body tissues to see if they are normal or not.

presomite embryo.definition: A developmental stage of an embryo before somite formation; during this period (gastrulation and early neurulation) the three germ layers are established, the neural tube begins to form, and segmented paraxial mesoderm (somites) has not yet formed.

presacral fascia.definition: A fascial layer lining the presacral space between the sacrum and the rectum; part of the endopelvic fascia, it overlies the presacral venous plexus and forms the posterior boundary of the presacral region.

presacral space.definition: An anatomical potential space in the pelvis located between the rectum (anterior boundary) and the sacrum/coccyx (posterior boundary); it contains fat and the presacral venous plexus and can harbor abscesses or tumors.

prepatellar bursitis.definition: Inflammation of the prepatellar bursa between the patella and the skin, typically from repetitive kneeling or trauma, causing anterior knee swelling and tenderness; can be aseptic or septic.

bursa.definition: A protective, fluid-filled sac located in or near the joints that cushions the movement of bone against tendons, skin, and muscle.

hypogastric plexuses.definition: A pair of autonomic nerve networks in the pelvis. The superior hypogastric plexus is a sympathetic prevertebral plexus near the sacral promontory that gives rise to the hypogastric nerves, which join with parasympathetic fibers from S2–S4 to form the inferior (pelvic) hypogastric plexus that innervates pelvic organs.

preperitoneal hernia.definition: A hernia in which abdominal contents protrude into the preperitoneal space (the potential space between the peritoneum and the transversalis fascia) rather than into the peritoneal cavity.

presbycusis.definition: When you have trouble hearing sounds or can't hear any sounds at all. Also called hearing impairment or hearing disorders.

presbycardia.definition: Age-related decline in cardiac electrical function, typically due to degeneration of the sinoatrial node and conduction pathways, resulting in a slower resting heart rate and a reduced ability to raise heart rate with activity.

presenile dementia.definition: An age-related category of dementia that begins before age 65, representing early-onset dementias of various causes (most commonly early-onset Alzheimer’s disease), and characterized by progressive impairment of memory and other cognitive functions with functional decline.

prepartum.definition: Relating to the period before childbirth; occurring during pregnancy prior to labor.

preperitoneal.definition: Situated in front of the peritoneum; pertaining to the space between the peritoneum and the abdominal wall.

parietal pelvic fascia.definition: Fibrous connective tissue lining the inner pelvic walls and floor, covering pelvic wall muscles; it forms the parietal component of the endopelvic fascia and is continuous with the transversalis (iliac) fascia laterally.

transversalis fascia.definition: A thin fascia lining the inner surface of the abdominal wall, between the transversus abdominis muscle and the peritoneum; it forms part of the posterior wall of the inguinal canal and, around the spermatic cord, becomes the internal spermatic fascia.

bowel preparation.definition: A regimen to cleanse the colon of stool prior to diagnostic or therapeutic procedures, typically involving laxatives and clear-liquid diets to achieve a clean colon for optimal visualization.

intensive care unit.definition: A hospital unit that provides continuous, high-level monitoring and life-sustaining treatment for severely ill or injured patients, often including invasive monitoring, mechanical ventilation, vasopressor support, and rapid access to specialized care.

decubitus ulcer.definition: A pressure-induced injury to the skin and underlying tissues over a bony prominence caused by prolonged immobility or sustained pressure (often with shear, friction, and moisture), commonly occurring in bedridden or disabled individuals.

pressor.definition: A substance that raises blood pressure, such as a vasopressor drug that constricts blood vessels or increases cardiac output.

pressure control ventilation.definition: A mode of mechanical ventilation in which a preset inspiratory pressure is maintained during inspiration, delivering a tidal volume that varies with lung compliance and airway resistance; typically uses a decelerating inspiratory flow and is time-cycled and pressure-limited to limit peak airway pressure.

pressure cycling.definition: A sample-preparation technique that applies repeated cycles of high hydrostatic pressure to cells or tissues to disrupt structures and enhance lysis and extraction/digestion of biomolecules such as DNA, RNA, and proteins.

pressure diuresis.definition: A renal mechanism in which elevated arterial pressure leads to increased urine production and sodium excretion (diuresis and natriuresis), thereby helping to restore normal blood pressure; mediated by increased glomerular filtration and reduced proximal tubule sodium reabsorption.

pressure dressing.definition: A bandage or dressing applied firmly over a wound to exert external pressure in order to control bleeding, limit swelling, and provide support to the affected area.

pressure edema.definition: Edema due to elevated capillary hydrostatic pressure, causing fluid to leak into interstitial tissues; commonly associated with congestive heart failure, venous insufficiency, or fluid overload, and typically produces bilateral, dependent, pitting edema that improves with leg elevation and treatment of the underlying cause.

pressure necrosis.definition: Localized tissue death resulting from prolonged external pressure that reduces blood flow (ischemia), typically over a bone prominence in immobilized patients, and which may progress to a pressure ulcer.

pressure sore.definition: A localized injury to the skin and underlying tissues over a bony prominence caused by prolonged pressure (often with shear/friction) that impedes blood flow and leads to tissue necrosis; common in bedridden or immobile patients and graded by depth (stages I–IV, and unstageable).

slough.definition: Nonviable tissue in a wound bed that is typically moist, loose or adherent, and often yellow, tan, or gray; composed of necrotic debris and fibrin; it impedes healing and often requires debridement.

wound cleansing.definition: Wound cleansing is the removal of dirt, debris, bacteria, and necrotic tissue from a wound using sterile or clean saline or water with gentle irrigation, to reduce infection risk and promote healing; routine use of harsh antiseptics on viable tissue is discouraged.

dressings.definition: Materials placed over a wound to protect it, absorb exudate, and maintain a moist healing environment, commonly gauze, foam, hydrocolloid, or film dressings.

prophylactic treatment.definition: Preventive medical therapy aimed at stopping disease or its complications before they occur or recur, rather than treating an active illness; examples include prophylactic antibiotics before surgery, vaccines, or post-exposure measures.

stage i pressure ulcer.definition: An early stage of a pressure injury characterized by nonblanchable redness of intact skin over a localized area (usually over a bony prominence); the area may be painful, firm, soft, warm, or cool compared with surrounding tissue, and there is no broken skin.

stage ii pressure ulcer.definition: Partial-thickness loss of skin with exposed dermis; the wound bed is red or pink and moist, and may present as an intact or ruptured serum-filled blister. There is no exposure of subcutaneous tissue, bone, tendon, or muscle.

stage iii pressure ulcer.definition: Full-thickness tissue loss in which subcutaneous fat may be visible; bone, tendon, or muscle are not exposed. The wound bed may contain slough and/or eschar, and undermining or tunneling can be present. Depth varies by anatomical location.

stage iv pressure ulcer.definition: Full-thickness tissue loss with exposed bone, tendon, or muscle. Slough or eschar may be present; undermining and/or tunneling are common, and the depth can extend to underlying structures depending on the location.

preterm birth.definition: Birth before 37 completed weeks of gestation; infants born this early are at higher risk for respiratory, cardiovascular, and neurodevelopmental complications.

preterm contractions.definition: Uterine contractions occurring before 37 weeks of gestation, often regular or irregular, that may be associated with cervical changes and indicate possible preterm labor requiring medical evaluation.

preterm infant.definition: A baby born before 37 completed weeks of gestation.

incompetent cervix.definition: A pregnancy complication defined by painless, premature dilation and effacement of the cervix, usually in the second trimester, leading to miscarriage or preterm birth because the cervix cannot remain closed under the weight of the pregnancy.

uterine bleeding.definition: Bleeding from the uterus (originating in the endometrium), which can occur as normal menstruation or as abnormal uterine bleeding due to hormonal, structural, infectious, pregnancy-related, or coagulopathic causes.

intrauterine fetal growth retardation.definition: A condition in which a fetus does not reach its genetically determined growth potential, usually defined as estimated fetal weight or biometric measurements below the 10th percentile for gestational age or a persistent decline in growth velocity, often due to placental insufficiency or maternal/fetal factors.

previllous embryo.definition: Not a standard term in embryology. If used, it would refer to the embryo before the formation of chorionic (placental) villi—the pre-villous stage—during very early implantation when the trophoblast has begun but placental villi have not yet developed. If you meant a different term or spelling, please provide context.

presumptive signs.definition: Presumptive signs are subjective indicators reported by the patient that suggest pregnancy but are not specific or diagnostic; they can be caused by other conditions. Typical examples include amenorrhea, nausea and vomiting, breast changes, fatigue, urinary frequency, and the sensation of fetal movement (quickening).

leptospira autumnalis.definition: Historically, a serovar of the pathogenic spirochete Leptospira interrogans; causes leptospirosis transmitted via contact with urine-contaminated water or soil, with illness ranging from mild febrile disease to severe Weil-like disease. Diagnosis is by serology (e.g., Microscopic Agglutination Test) or PCR; treatment includes antibiotics such as doxycycline or penicillin.

cephalic presentation.definition: A fetal presentation in which the head is the presenting part that enters the birth canal first during labor; it is the most common presentation at term.

scalenus anticus.definition: An anterior scalene muscle of the neck that arises from the transverse processes of the cervical vertebrae (usually C3–C6) and inserts on the first rib; it elevates the first rib during inspiration and assists in flexion and lateral bending of the neck.

heels.definition: The posterior part of the foot below the ankle; the heel is formed by the calcaneus (heel bone) and supports weight during standing and walking.

shoulder blades.definition: A wide, flat bone at the back of the shoulder.

gestational diabetes.definition: A form of glucose intolerance diagnosed during pregnancy, due to pregnancy-related insulin resistance; usually identified in mid to late pregnancy by an abnormal oral glucose tolerance test; typically resolves after delivery but increases the mother's risk of future type 2 diabetes and can be associated with fetal and neonatal complications.

latent diabetes.definition: A nonstandard, historical term for diabetes that is present but clinically silent or undiagnosed; it may refer to undiagnosed hyperglycemia (preclinical diabetes) and, in some contexts, to latent autoimmune diabetes in adults (a slowly progressive autoimmune form of type 1 diabetes presenting in adulthood).

impaired glucose tolerance.definition: A prediabetic condition defined by a 2-hour plasma glucose level of 140–199 mg/dL (7.8–11.0 mmol/L) after a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test, with fasting glucose typically below the diabetic range; indicates impaired glucose tolerance and increased risk of progression to type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

fluoride gel.definition: A topical fluoride preparation in gel form used in dentistry to prevent caries by delivering fluoride to enamel, promoting remineralization and inhibiting demineralization; commonly contains 1.23% acidulated phosphate fluoride or 2% sodium fluoride and is applied to teeth for a short period during professional fluoride therapy.

dental restoration.definition: A procedure to repair or replace damaged or decayed tooth structure to restore function, shape, and appearance, typically accomplished with fillings, inlays/onlays, crowns, veneers, or bonding.

fixed bridge.definition: A dental prosthesis that permanently replaces one or more missing teeth by anchoring artificial teeth (pontics) to adjacent prepared teeth or to implants, and is cemented in place so it is not removable by the patient.

prezista.definition: A brand-name antiretroviral medication (darunavir) that inhibits the HIV-1 protease enzyme, preventing maturation of the virus; used in combination therapy for HIV-1 infection, usually boosted with ritonavir or cobicistat to raise drug levels.

priapitis.definition: Inflammation of the penis, often due to infection, dermatitis, or irritation.

vivax.definition: A Plasmodium species that causes relapsing malaria, typically with fever paroxysms every 48 hours and capable of dormancy in the liver (hypnozoites) that can reactivate.

ovale.definition: A Latin adjective meaning oval-shaped; used in anatomy to describe structures that are oval in outline.

prickle.definition: A prickling, tingling, or stinging sensation on the skin, commonly described as paresthesia.

spinosum.definition: Prickle-cell layer of the epidermis located between the stratum basale and stratum granulosum; composed of keratinocytes bound by desmosomes, giving a spiny appearance on histology; provides mechanical strength and contains Langerhans cells.

stools.definition: Solid waste excreted from the digestive tract through the anus; formed from indigestible matter, bacteria, shed intestinal cells, and mucus, and used clinically to assess bowel function and digestion.

xanthosis.definition: Yellowish discoloration of the skin or mucous membranes due to lipid deposition or carotene accumulation, often seen in lipid metabolism disorders or carotenemia, and not caused by bilirubin (jaundice).

buds.definition: Small rounded outgrowths from a tissue surface that represent an early developmental primordium of an organ or structure; examples include tooth buds and taste buds.

atypical.definition: Not typical; deviating from the usual characteristics, appearance, or pattern expected for a disease, condition, or tissue. In pathology, cells or tissues showing abnormal features but not definitively malignant.

dacryocytes.definition: Teardrop-shaped red blood cells seen on a peripheral smear, caused by bone marrow infiltration or fibrosis (a myelophthisic process) that distorts erythrocyte precursors as they enter circulation; commonly associated with myelofibrosis and extramedullary hematopoiesis.

vera.definition: A succulent plant whose leaf gel is used topically for burns, sunburns, wounds, and skin irritations; the latex from the rind contains stimulant laxatives and can cause electrolyte disturbances and abdominal cramps; internal use is not advised without medical supervision.

sequestrum.definition: A fragment of necrotic (dead) bone that has separated from surrounding living bone, typically seen in osteomyelitis; it remains detached within a lesion and may be encased by involucrum.

pneumonic.definition: Relating to pneumonia; pertaining to the disease that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs.

tubercles.definition: Small rounded nodules or eminences on bones or organ surfaces; in anatomy, a tubercle is a small projection on a bone (for example, the greater tubercle of the humerus); in pathology, it denotes a localized nodular lesion such as a granuloma seen in tuberculosis.

primaxin.definition: A combination antibiotic consisting of imipenem, a broad-spectrum carbapenem, and cilastatin, a renal enzyme inhibitor that prevents degradation of imipenem in the kidney; used to treat serious infections caused by susceptible bacteria.

primidone.definition: An anticonvulsant medication in the barbiturate class that is used to treat seizures; it is a prodrug metabolized to phenobarbital and an active metabolite (phenylethylmalonamide).

psychomotor.definition: Relating to the coordination of mental processes with physical movement; the integration of cognitive functions with motor skills.

focal.definition: Relating to or affecting a localized area; confined to a single spot or region rather than being diffuse or generalized.

drug dependency.definition: A state of physiological and psychological reliance on a drug, characterized by compulsive use, tolerance, and withdrawal symptoms if the drug is reduced or stopped.

primipara.definition: A woman who has given birth once; parity 1.

multipara.definition: A woman who has given birth to two or more viable infants.

nullipara.definition: A woman who has never carried a pregnancy to viability (generally about 20 weeks) or given birth to a live infant.

primiparity.definition: The state of having given birth to one viable infant; parity of 1, indicating a woman who has had a single delivery.

primiparous.definition: Relating to a woman who has given birth to one child; parity of one.

primordial.definition: Existing from the earliest developmental stage; the initial form from which later differentiation proceeds (used in embryology for cells or structures like primordial germ cells or primordial follicles).

primitive.definition: In medicine, primitive means relating to an early developmental or embryonic stage; describing undifferentiated, immature precursor cells or tissues that have not yet acquired specialized features.

primordium.definition: An early developmental stage in which a group of cells is set aside to form a future organ or tissue; the precursor that gives rise to the mature structure.

primordia.definition: The earliest recognizable developmental stage of an organ, tissue, or body part from which the mature structure differentiates; in plants, it refers to the initial growth outgrowth that will develop into a leaf, flower, or other organ.

primordial germ cell.definition: An embryonic cell lineage that gives rise to gametes; primordial germ cells are specified early in development, migrate to the developing gonads, proliferate, and later differentiate into sperm or eggs after meiosis.

primordial oocyte.definition: An oocyte within a primordial follicle of the ovary; a diploid germ cell formed during fetal life that is arrested in prophase I of meiosis (diplotene) and surrounded by a single layer of flattened granulosa cells. It represents the earliest stage of female gametogenesis and may be recruited to grow into a primary follicle during the ovarian cycle.

primordial sex cords.definition: Embryologic structures of the developing gonad formed by proliferating coelomic/epithelial cords containing primordial germ cells; these cords become seminiferous cords/tubules in the male and degenerate into primordial follicles in the female.

gonadal cords.definition: Embryologic cords of cells derived from the coelomic epithelium of the developing (indifferent) gonad that form the primitive sex cords; in males they become the seminiferous (testicular) cords that develop into seminiferous tubules, while in females they form cortical cords that mature into primordial ovarian follicles.

spermatogonia.definition: Diploid male germ cells in the seminiferous tubules of the testes that serve as stem cells for spermatogenesis; they divide by mitosis to renew themselves and to produce primary spermatocytes that enter meiosis.

gerstmann-straussler syndrome.definition: A rare inherited prion disease (most often autosomal dominant) caused by mutations in the PRNP gene. It presents with progressive cerebellar ataxia and dysarthria, followed by visual disturbances and dementia, with onset typically in midlife and death within a few years.

fatal familial insomnia.definition: A rare autosomal dominant prion disease caused by a PRNP gene mutation that produces progressive insomnia due to selective thalamic degeneration, followed by neuropsychiatric symptoms and dementia, with death typically within 7–24 months after symptom onset.

subacute spongiform encephalopathy.definition: A group of rare, fatal neurodegenerative disorders caused by misfolded prion proteins that produce sponge-like vacuolation in brain tissue; characterized by subacute onset of rapidly progressive dementia, myoclonus, ataxia, visual disturbances, and other neurologic deficits, usually leading to death within months.

transmissible neurodegenerative disease.definition: A neurodegenerative disorder that is transmissible, meaning it can be acquired through exposure to infected tissue or materials; most commonly caused by misfolded prion proteins, leading to progressive brain degeneration with sponge-like changes (transmissible spongiform encephalopathies).

prion protein.definition: A host-encoded glycoprotein anchored to the cell surface by a GPI anchor; its normal cellular form is expressed mainly in neural tissue, while misfolded conformers aggregate and are associated with transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (prion diseases).

hensen's node.definition: A specialized cluster of cells at the anterior end of the avian primitive streak that acts as the embryonic organizer during gastrulation, directing germ layer formation (mesoderm and endoderm) and establishing the body axes; it is homologous to the Spemann organizer.

enamel prism.definition: A rod-like bundle of hydroxyapatite crystals that constitutes the basic structural unit of tooth enamel, extending from the dentinoenamel junction to the enamel surface and surrounded by interprismatic enamel.

st segment elevation.definition: An elevation of the ST segment on an electrocardiogram, where the ST segment is displaced above the baseline (often in two contiguous leads), typically indicating acute myocardial injury from ischemia or infarction (recognized as STEMI when clinically suspected).

pr interval.definition: An ECG measurement from the start of the P wave to the start of the QRS complex, representing atrial depolarization and conduction through the AV node to the ventricles; normal duration is about 0.12–0.20 seconds (120–200 ms). Prolongation suggests first-degree AV block; shortening may occur with pre-excitation syndromes (e.g., WPW).

prinzmetal's angina.definition: A form of chest pain caused by transient, reversible spasm of a coronary artery, leading to brief myocardial ischemia; episodes often occur at rest and may produce transient ST-segment elevation on ECG. It is typically responsive to nitrates and calcium-channel blockers and can occur with or without underlying coronary artery disease (more common in smokers).

variant angina.definition: A form of angina caused by transient coronary vasospasm leading to episodic myocardial ischemia, typically occurring at rest and often presenting with transient ST-segment elevation on ECG.

lisinopril.definition: An oral angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor used to treat hypertension and congestive heart failure, and to improve survival after myocardial infarction, by blocking the conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, leading to vasodilation and reduced aldosterone.

tolazoline.definition: A nonselective alpha-adrenergic antagonist that blocks α1- and α2-adrenergic receptors, causing peripheral vasodilation and a drop in blood pressure; historically used as a vasodilator for vasospasm or hypertension and in certain diagnostic pharmacologic tests. Adverse effects include hypotension and tachycardia.

tolazoline hydrochloride.definition: A nonselective alpha-adrenergic antagonist (vasodilator) that produces systemic and pulmonary vasodilation; historically used to treat persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn and to reverse vasospasm during certain diagnostic procedures, typically given intravenously.

priscoline.definition: A vasodilator drug that acts as a nonselective alpha-adrenergic antagonist to relax vascular smooth muscle, especially in the pulmonary circulation; historically used to treat persistent pulmonary hypertension and vasospasm, but can cause hypotension.

privine.definition: Not a recognized medical term; no standard medical definition exists in major dictionaries.

naphazoline hydrochloride.definition: A topical decongestant vasoconstrictor (alpha-adrenergic agonist) used in nasal sprays and ophthalmic solutions; it constricts vascular smooth muscle in nasal and conjunctival mucosa to reduce congestion and redness, intended for short-term use.

pro-banthine.definition: Brand name for propantheline bromide; an anticholinergic (antimuscarinic) drug that reduces smooth muscle tone and secretions in the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tracts by blocking muscarinic receptors; used to treat peptic ulcer disease, GI hypermotility/spasm, and sometimes urinary incontinence.

propantheline bromide.definition: A synthetic antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) agent that blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors, reducing smooth muscle motility and secretions in the GI and genitourinary tracts; used as an antispasmodic for peptic ulcers and GI disorders.

uric acid kidney stones.definition: Stones composed mainly of uric acid crystals formed in the urinary tract when urine is persistently acidic or highly concentrated; associated with hyperuricemia, gout, dehydration, and metabolic syndrome. They are usually radiolucent on plain X-ray and can often be dissolved or prevented with urine alkalinization (e.g., potassium citrate), increased hydration, and treatment of underlying hyperuricemia if needed.

proband.definition: The affected individual in a family who first brings a genetic disorder to clinical attention and from whom a pedigree analysis is started; also known as the index case (male: propositus; female: proposita).

propositus.definition: The first affected person in a family who brings a genetic disorder to medical attention; the index case used in pedigree analyses (also called the proband).

procardia.definition: A calcium channel blocker (dihydropyridine) used to treat high blood pressure and angina; brand name for nifedipine.

procaine hydrochloride.definition: A salt form of procaine, an ester local anesthetic used to produce local or regional anesthesia by reversibly blocking voltage-gated sodium channels in nerve membranes; administered by injection, often with a vasoconstrictor to prolong duration.

regional anesthetic procedures.definition: Techniques that provide anesthesia or analgesia to a specific body region by blocking nerve transmission, typically via local anesthetic injections near a nerve, nerve plexus, or along the spinal canal; examples include peripheral nerve blocks and neuraxial blocks (spinal, epidural).

brain tumors.definition: An abnormal growth of cells within the brain or its coverings (the meninges) that can be benign or malignant; tumors may originate in the brain (primary) or spread from cancer elsewhere (metastatic). They commonly present with headaches, seizures, or focal neurologic deficits depending on location, and are diagnosed by imaging (usually MRI) with histologic confirmation; treatment typically involves surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy or targeted therapies, with prognosis varying by tumor type and grade.

procaryocyte.definition: A cell lacking a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; its DNA resides in a nucleoid region and is not enclosed by a nuclear envelope, as seen in bacteria and archaea.

prokaryote.definition: a unicellular organism that lacks a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; its genetic material is not enclosed within a nuclear envelope (nucleoid) and is typically composed of circular DNA. It includes the domains Bacteria and Archaea.

procaryon.definition: A single-celled organism that lacks a membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles; includes bacteria and archaea.

procaryosis.definition: I can’t find a standard medical definition for "procaryosis." It may be a misspelling or very uncommon term. Could you share the context or the intended spelling? For example, if you meant something like "prokaryosis" or another term, I can provide a precise definition.

procaryotae.definition: An obsolete taxonomic group of prokaryotic organisms lacking a defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; includes bacteria and cyanobacteria.

monera.definition: An obsolete biological kingdom that grouped all prokaryotes—organisms lacking a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; it included bacteria and archaea and is now divided into the domains Bacteria and Archaea.

coracidium.definition: A free-swimming, ciliated larval stage of certain cestodes that hatches from the egg and is ingested by the first intermediate host (usually a crustacean), where it develops into the procercoid.

diphyllobothrium latum.definition: A fish tapeworm (cestode) acquired by consuming raw or undercooked freshwater fish; inhabits the human small intestine and can cause diphyllobothriasis, sometimes with vitamin B12 deficiency and megaloblastic anemia.

copepod.definition: A small aquatic crustacean in the subclass Copepoda; a major component of marine and freshwater zooplankton, typically free-living, though some species are parasitic on fish and other aquatic hosts.

crustacean.definition: An aquatic arthropod of the subphylum Crustacea, including crabs, lobsters, shrimp, and barnacles; characterized by a hard chitinous exoskeleton, a segmented body (often with a cephalothorax and abdomen), and usually two pairs of antennae.

diaptomus.definition: A genus of freshwater copepods (small crustaceans) in the family Diaptomidae; part of freshwater zooplankton commonly found in ponds and lakes.

processus vaginalis.definition: An embryonic peritoneal diverticulum that accompanies the descent of the testes through the inguinal canal into the scrotum; normally obliterates, but if it remains patent it allows communication between the peritoneal cavity and the tunica vaginalis, potentially causing a hydrocele or indirect inguinal hernia.

processus vaginalis testis.definition: A peritoneal diverticulum that accompanies the testis during its descent into the scrotum; normally obliterates to form the tunica vaginalis around the testis. If it remains patent, it creates a communication between the peritoneal cavity and the scrotum, predisposing to an indirect inguinal hernia or a hydrocele.

prochlorperazine hydrochloride.definition: A phenothiazine antipsychotic with antiemetic effects; a dopamine D2 receptor antagonist used to prevent or treat nausea and vomiting (including postoperative and migraine-related), with potential sedation and extrapyramidal side effects.

prochlorperazine maleate.definition: A salt form of prochlorperazine; a phenothiazine dopamine D2 receptor antagonist used as an antiemetic to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting (e.g., postoperative, migraine-associated, or chemotherapy-induced emesis).

prochromosome.definition: Not a standard term in modern genetics; historically used to refer to a chromosome in an early, uncondensed chromatin state before visible chromosome condensation during cell division; today the term is not commonly used.

karyosome.definition: A dense, centrally located aggregation of chromatin within the nucleus of a cell; a single mass of condensed chromatin seen in certain cells (e.g., some amoebic trophozoites and oocyte nuclei).

procidentia.definition: A severe pelvic organ prolapse in which the uterus descends completely and protrudes through the vaginal opening, often with involvement of the anterior and posterior vaginal walls (cystocele/rectocele).

procoagulant.definition: A substance or factor that promotes blood coagulation by accelerating the coagulation cascade and thrombin generation, increasing the body's tendency to form a clot.

peritoneal membrane.definition: A serous membrane that lines the abdominal cavity and covers the abdominal organs, consisting of parietal and visceral layers separated by peritoneal fluid; formed by mesothelial cells and underlying connective tissue, it provides lubrication, allows smooth organ movement, and participates in immune defense and fluid exchange.

nuclear membrane.definition: A double-membrane surrounding the nucleus (the nuclear envelope) that consists of inner and outer lipid bilayers, separated by a perinuclear space, perforated by nuclear pores, and continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum; it protects the nucleus and regulates transport of proteins, RNA, and other molecules between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

proctalgia.definition: Rectal or anal pain in the absence of an identifiable anorectal disease; it can be episodic (proctalgia fugax) due to pelvic floor or anal sphincter spasm, or chronic (proctalgia dolorosa) as a persistent ache.

proctalgia fugax.definition: A benign condition characterized by sudden, brief episodes of severe rectal or anal pain (lasting seconds to minutes), often nocturnal, thought to arise from transient spasm of the anal sphincter or pelvic floor muscles, with no detectable anorectal pathology.

rectitis.definition: Inflammation of the rectal mucosa (the lining of the rectum); a form of proctitis, often due to infection, inflammatory bowel disease, radiation, or ischemic injury.

proctocele.definition: A protrusion (herniation) of the rectal wall into the vaginal canal (rectocele) due to pelvic floor weakness; presents as a bulge in the posterior vaginal wall and can cause obstructed defecation or a sensation of fullness. Also known as rectocele.

proctorrhea.definition: Discharge from the rectum; a symptom involving the passage of mucus, blood, pus, or other material from the anorectal canal, often due to proctitis, hemorrhoids, infection, inflammatory bowel disease, or colorectal pathology.

proctoscope.definition: A rigid tubular instrument inserted through the anus to visualize the anal canal and lower rectum.

proctosigmoidoscopy.definition: A procedure to examine the rectum and sigmoid colon using a proctoscope or sigmoidoscope, allowing visualization of the mucosa with biopsy or treatment of any abnormal findings as needed.

proctodeum.definition: In embryology, the ectodermally derived, distal end of the hindgut that forms the external anal opening and the lower anal canal, meeting the endoderm-derived hindgut at the pectinate line.

urorectal septum.definition: An embryologic partition that divides the cloaca into the ventral urogenital sinus and the dorsal anorectal canal, formed by the caudal growth of the urorectal septum; defects can produce urogenital–anorectal fistulas or persistent cloaca.

proctodynia.definition: Rectal or anal pain in the anorectal region, often episodic and without an identifiable local lesion; commonly associated with pelvic floor muscle spasm or other functional anorectal disorders.
