proctologist.definition: A physician who specializes in diseases of the rectum and anus; in modern practice often synonymous with a colorectal (colon and rectal) surgeon.

proctology.definition: Branch of medicine dealing with diseases of the rectum and anus; often used interchangeably with colorectal surgery, which also encompasses diseases of the lower colon.

proctoplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair or reconstruct the rectum or anal canal, often to correct anorectal defects or restore continence.

proctocort.definition: A rectal corticosteroid preparation used to reduce inflammation in anorectal conditions (e.g., hemorrhoids, proctitis); typically formulated as a suppository, cream, or ointment.

progestagen.definition: A substance with progestational (progesterone-like) activity, natural or synthetic, that binds to progesterone receptors to produce effects such as endometrial transformation and maintenance of pregnancy.

progestational.definition: Relating to progesterone or its role in pregnancy; pertaining to the hormonal processes that prepare for and maintain pregnancy.

dysfunctional uterine bleeding.definition: Abnormal uterine bleeding in the absence of organic pathology, caused by hormonal imbalance and ovulatory dysfunction (most often anovulatory cycles), commonly seen in adolescents and perimenopausal women; a historical term now often subsumed under abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB).

progesterone receptor assay.definition: A laboratory test that detects and measures progesterone receptor protein in a tissue sample (most commonly breast cancer tissue) to determine hormone receptor status and guide endocrine therapy decisions, typically performed by immunohistochemistry.

progesterone receptor.definition: A receptor for the steroid hormone progesterone; a nuclear receptor that, when bound by progesterone, modulates gene transcription to mediate progesterone's effects on reproductive tissues and pregnancy; mainly exists as two isoforms, A and B.

progressive histoplasmosis.definition: A severe systemic infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum that progressively involves multiple organ systems (most notably liver, spleen, bone marrow, and lymph nodes), usually in immunocompromised hosts, presenting with fever, weight loss, fatigue, hepatosplenomegaly, and cytopenias.

progressive osseous heteroplasia.definition: A rare genetic disorder in which bone forms within soft tissues (heterotopic ossification) that begins in the skin/subcutaneous tissue and progressively involves deeper muscles and connective tissue; caused by mutations in the GNAS gene with imprinting, typically presenting in infancy or early childhood.

byler's disease.definition: An inherited, progressive intrahepatic cholestasis beginning in infancy, due to defective bile formation/transport (classically PFIC type I from ATP8B1 mutation); features include severe pruritus, failure to thrive, fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies, hepatomegaly, and progressive liver disease, typically with normal or low gamma-glutamyl transferase.

dejerine-sottas disease.definition: A rare autosomal recessive demyelinating hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy presenting in infancy with hypotonia and progressive distal weakness, sensory loss, absent reflexes, and markedly slowed nerve conduction velocities; considered the severe form of Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease (often termed CMT type 3).

duchenne's paralysis.definition: Paralysis of the upper limb due to injury to the upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5–C6), usually from birth trauma or traction, resulting in an arm that is adducted and internally rotated (waiter’s tip posture) and often recovering over weeks to months.

progressive myonecrosis.definition: A rapidly advancing necrosis of skeletal muscle tissue, typically due to bacterial infection (often clostridial myonecrosis or gas gangrene) or severe ischemia, characterized by severe pain, swelling, possible gas formation with crepitus, and systemic toxicity; requires urgent surgical debridement, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and aggressive supportive care.

progressive interstitial hypertrophic ne.definition: A progressive peripheral neuropathy in which interstitial tissue around nerve fibers hypertrophies, leading to thickened nerves and progressive sensory and motor dysfunction.

hutchinson-gelford syndrome.definition: A rare genetic disorder causing accelerated aging beginning in early childhood; features include growth delay, alopecia, loss of subcutaneous fat, aged-looking skin and facial changes, and progressive cardiovascular disease leading to premature death; caused by a dominant LMNA gene mutation producing progerin; no cure; management is supportive.

progressive familial intrahepatic choles.definition: An autosomal recessive group of inherited disorders causing intrahepatic cholestasis due to defects in hepatocellular bile salt transport, typically presenting in infancy with severe pruritus and jaundice and often progressing to cirrhosis; the main subtypes (PFIC1–PFIC3) are caused by mutations in ATP8B1, ABCB11, and ABCB4.

anorectal.definition: Relating to the anus and rectum.

prodromal.definition: The time between when the first symptoms appear and when the disease completely appears.

prodrome.definition: A group of early symptoms preceding a given disease or condition. For example, a migraine prodrome (fatigue, hunger, nervousness) may occur hours or days before the headache strikes.

prodromal labor.definition: A pre-labor phase with irregular, often painful contractions that occur before true labor and do not cause significant cervical dilation; it can last hours to days and may resemble true labor but typically does not progress to active labor.

prodromal rash.definition: A rash that occurs during the prodromal phase of an illness, preceding the characteristic eruption; typically early and nonspecific, and may signal the imminent appearance of the full rash.

prodromal symptom.definition: An early symptom or set of symptoms that precedes the onset of a disease, signaling the prodromal phase; these symptoms are typically nonspecific and not yet diagnostic.

prodrug.definition: An inactive or less active precursor that is metabolically converted in the body to the active drug, typically to improve properties such as bioavailability, solubility, or targeted delivery.

procumbency.definition: The state of lying flat, typically face-down (prone) or prostrate; a recumbent posture.

profenal.definition: No widely recognized medical term exists with that spelling. It may be a misspelling of propanal (propionaldehyde), a simple aldehyde, or 2-propenal (acrolein), an aldehyde used in chemical synthesis and known to be a tissue irritant.

progressive ossifying myositis.definition: A rare genetic disorder characterized by progressive heterotopic ossification of soft tissues (primarily skeletal muscle), leading to stiffness and immobilization; ossification is often triggered by minor trauma, and the condition is caused by activating mutations in a BMP signaling pathway gene (ACVR1/ALK2).

myositis ossificans progressiva.definition: A rare genetic disorder characterized by progressive heterotopic ossification of soft tissues (muscle, fascia, tendons, ligaments), leading to increasing stiffness and loss of movement beginning in childhood. It is caused by activating mutations in the ACVR1 gene (ALK2) and is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern; congenital malformations of the big toes may be present at birth. Trauma or injections can precipitate new ossifications. There is no cure; management is supportive, focusing on injury prevention and careful handling, as surgical removal of ossified tissue often recurs.

prolapsed cord.definition: A condition in which the umbilical cord descends through the cervix into the vagina ahead of the fetus (usually after membrane rupture), risking cord compression and fetal hypoxia; it is an obstetric emergency requiring prompt delivery.

subcortical encephalopathy.definition: A diffuse brain dysfunction with predominant involvement of subcortical structures (basal ganglia, thalamus, and subcortical white matter) rather than the cerebral cortex, typically due to metabolic, toxic, inflammatory, or vascular causes; presents with cognitive slowing, motor changes, and altered consciousness.

schilder’s disease.definition: A rare pediatric inflammatory demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system marked by a large, tumefactive demyelinating lesion in the cerebral white matter, often causing acute neurologic deficits or seizures; historically termed diffuse myelinoclastic sclerosis and considered by some to be a variant of multiple sclerosis.

progressive supranuclear palsy.definition: A rare, progressive neurodegenerative tauopathy presenting with vertical gaze palsy (especially downgaze), early postural instability and falls, axial rigidity with bradykinesia, dysarthria and dysphagia, and frontal-executive cognitive impairment; typically shows poor response to dopaminergic therapy.

paralysis of eye muscles.definition: Paralysis or weakness of the extraocular muscles, causing reduced or absent eye movement in one or more directions; commonly due to cranial nerve palsies (oculomotor, trochlear, or abducens) or neuromuscular disorders, often with diplopia (double vision) and eye misalignment.

neck rigidity.definition: Stiffness of the neck with resistance to forward flexion, often due to irritation of the meninges from infection (e.g., meningitis) or cervical spine pathology.

trunk rigidity.definition: A sustained increase in resistance to passive movement of the trunk muscles (axial rigidity), commonly seen in parkinsonian syndromes and other extrapyramidal disorders, contributing to a stooped posture and reduced trunk mobility.

pseudobulbar palsy.definition: A neurologic syndrome caused by bilateral upper motor neuron lesions of the corticobulbar tracts that disrupt voluntary control of bulbar muscles, resulting in spastic dysarthria and dysphagia, with hyperreflexia and abnormal facial reflexes; often accompanied by emotional lability due to coexisting pseudobulbar affect.

prolactin test.definition: A blood test that measures the level of prolactin in the blood to evaluate pituitary function and investigate symptoms such as galactorrhea, menstrual irregularities, or infertility. Prolactin levels vary with time of day, sleep, stress, pregnancy, and certain medications, and may require repeat testing for confirmation.

prolactin levels.definition: Concentration of prolactin, a hormone from the anterior pituitary, in the bloodstream; used to assess pituitary function and lactation status. Normal ranges vary by sex and physiological state (higher during pregnancy and lactation); elevated levels (hyperprolactinemia) can cause galactorrhea, menstrual irregularities, and infertility; low levels are rare and may reflect pituitary or hypothalamic disease.

prolactin-secreting pituitary tumors.definition: A benign pituitary adenoma that secretes prolactin, causing hyperprolactinemia and related features such as galactorrhea and amenorrhea/infertility in women and decreased libido in men; commonly treated with dopamine agonists.

prolapsed hemorrhoid.definition: An internal hemorrhoid that has protruded through the anal verge outside the anus; it may retract spontaneously or require manual reduction and can cause pain, bleeding, and discharge.

prolapsed ureterocele.definition: A congenital cystic dilation of the distal ureter (ureterocele) that has prolapsed through the bladder neck or into the urethra, causing obstruction or other urinary symptoms.

prolapse of anus.definition: A condition in which part of the rectum protrudes through the anus, usually due to weakness of the pelvic floor; it can be full-thickness (the entire rectal wall protrudes) or mucosal (only the lining), and may cause a bulging mass, mucus discharge, bleeding, and sometimes fecal incontinence.

prolapse of rectum.definition: Protrusion of the rectal wall through the anus, which may involve the full thickness (complete rectal prolapse) or only the mucosa (mucosal prolapse). It typically presents as a protruding mass that may be reducible and is often associated with straining, chronic constipation, fecal incontinence, and pelvic floor weakness.

prolapse of uterus.definition: Happens when the womb (uterus) falls down and presses on the vaginal area.

prolastin.definition: A plasma-derived human alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor (alpha-1 antitrypsin) used as replacement therapy for hereditary alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency to slow progression of emphysema; administered intravenously (typically weekly).

projectile vomiting.definition: A forceful, high-volume vomiting of gastric contents, typically nonbilious and often without preceding nausea; the expelled material may travel a short distance, and it is classically associated with gastric outlet obstruction such as infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.

projection reconstruction imaging.definition: A tomographic imaging method in which cross-sectional images are reconstructed from multiple projections (line integrals) acquired around the object, by mathematically inverting the projection data (e.g., using filtered back projection or iterative reconstruction) to form 2D or 3D images.

promethium.definition: A radioactive lanthanide metal (element 61) with no stable isotopes; used mainly in research and as a beta-emitting source in industrial/scientific applications; not approved for diagnostic or therapeutic medical use.

promontory of the sacrum.definition: A prominent anterior projection at the superior end of the sacrum, formed mainly by the body of the first sacral vertebra; it serves as a key pelvic landmark and marks the posterior boundary of the pelvic inlet, influencing obstetric measurements.

promontory.definition: A bony projection or eminence; specifically, the sacral promontory is the anterior edge of the base of the sacrum, forming the posterior boundary of the pelvic inlet and serving as a landmark in obstetrics and radiology.

proloprim.definition: A fixed-dose antibiotic combination of sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim that inhibits sequential steps in bacterial folate synthesis, producing bactericidal activity. Used to treat and prevent a variety of infections, including urinary tract infections, certain respiratory and gastrointestinal infections, and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prophylaxis.

timed release.definition: A pharmaceutical dosage form or delivery system that releases an active ingredient at a pre-set rate or after a predefined delay, prolonging drug exposure, maintaining therapeutic levels, and reducing dosing frequency; achieved by coatings, matrices, osmotic pumps, or other time-controlled mechanisms.

extended release.definition: A drug delivery system in which the active ingredient is released gradually over time to provide a prolonged effect, allowing less frequent dosing and more stable drug concentrations.

prolonged gestation.definition: A pregnancy that lasts beyond the normal duration, typically defined as 42 or more completed weeks of gestation (≥294 days); also known as post-term pregnancy.

active resistance exercise.definition: A form of resistance training in which the person actively contracts muscles against external resistance (e.g., weights, bands, or manual resistance) to improve strength and endurance; movement involves voluntary force generation rather than passive movement.

progressive assistive exercise.definition: A rehabilitation strategy in which movement is performed with gradually diminishing external assistance (hands-on guidance, devices, or gravity-elimination) to enable early activity and progressively increase active muscle effort as strength and coordination improve.

progressive scan mode.definition: A method of image acquisition/display in which every line of a frame is captured or displayed in sequence during a single refresh, rather than in alternating interlaced fields, resulting in a smoother image with reduced motion artifacts.

interlaced scanning.definition: Not a standard medical term; in imaging and video technology, interlaced scanning is a method where a frame is formed by interleaving two fields—one containing the odd-numbered lines and one containing the even-numbered lines—captured separately and displayed in alternation to create a full image.

prompt insulin zinc suspension.definition: A historical insulin formulation in which insulin is suspended with zinc to form crystals, yielding slower absorption and a longer duration of action than regular insulin.

fast-acting insulin.definition: A rapid-acting insulin is an insulin analog that begins to lower blood glucose within about 10–30 minutes after injection, peaks in roughly 1–2 hours, and lasts about 3–5 hours; used at mealtimes to control postprandial glucose.

prom.definition: Rupture of the amniotic membranes before the onset of labor.

anal orifice.definition: The external opening of the anal canal through which stool is excreted; the terminal portion of the digestive tract bounded by the internal and external anal sphincters and surrounded by perianal skin.

mesangial cells.definition: Specialized cells in the glomerular mesangium that provide structural support to glomerular capillaries, regulate filtration by contracting to change surface area, phagocytose debris and immune complexes, and synthesize extracellular matrix and cytokines.

rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis.definition: A clinical syndrome of rapidly worsening renal function over days to weeks, with nephritic features, and histologic crescentic glomerulonephritis (crescent formation in glomeruli), typically due to immune-mediated injury (anti-GBM disease, immune complex GN, or pauci-immune GN).

prokinetic.definition: A drug that enhances gastrointestinal motility by stimulating or increasing contractions of the gut, promoting faster gastric emptying and intestinal transit; used to treat conditions such as gastroparesis and gastroesophageal reflux.

pronator quadratus.definition: A small square-shaped, deep forearm muscle that pronates the forearm; it originates from the distal anterior ulna and inserts on the distal anterior radius, innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve (branch of the median nerve).

pronator reflex.definition: A deep tendon reflex elicited by tapping the pronator teres muscle in the forearm, resulting in forearm pronation; used to assess median nerve function (often associated with C6–C7).

ulnar reflex.definition: An elbow-level reflex produced by tapping the ulnar nerve behind the medial epicondyle, causing contraction of the intrinsic hand muscles (interossei and adductor pollicis) and small finger movements; used to assess ulnar nerve function (C8–T1).

pyramidal system.definition: A motor pathway consisting of the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts that originate in the cerebral cortex and project to the brainstem and spinal cord to mediate voluntary, skilled movement; lesions produce upper motor neuron signs (e.g., weakness, spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski).

sixth cervical nerve root.definition: A spinal nerve root in the cervical region that exits above the C6 vertebra and contributes to the brachial plexus; it supplies motor fibers to elbow flexors (e.g., biceps) and wrist extensors, and sensory fibers to the lateral forearm and the thumb and index finger; the brachioradialis reflex tests this level.

pronator syndrome.definition: Pronator syndrome is a compression neuropathy of the median nerve at the elbow, usually beneath the pronator teres muscle, caused by fibrous bands or anomalous muscle heads; it presents with forearm pain and paresthesias in the median nerve distribution (the lateral 3½ digits), worsened by forearm pronation and elbow flexion, and may include weakness of some thenar muscles.

pronephric duct.definition: A transient embryonic duct that drains the primitive pronephros; it regresses as development proceeds, with its proximal portion giving rise to the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct, from which the ureteric bud develops.

pronephric tubule.definition: An embryonic tubule of the pronephros, the first, transient kidney in vertebrate development; drains into the pronephric duct (Wolffian duct) and is nonfunctional in humans.

prone posture.definition: A body position in which a person lies flat on the stomach with the chest and abdomen against the supporting surface and the back upward, usually with the head turned to one side.

pronephric.definition: Relating to the pronephros, the earliest, transient embryonic kidney in vertebrates; a rudimentary, typically nonfunctional structure in humans that regresses as development proceeds and is replaced by the mesonephros and metanephros.

proplex t.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard dictionaries; appears to be a brand name or misspelling. Please provide context or the correct spelling for a precise definition.

proparacaine hydrochloride.definition: An ophthalmic topical ester local anesthetic (the hydrochloride salt of proparacaine) used to numb the cornea and conjunctiva during eye procedures; it blocks voltage-gated sodium channels in nerve membranes to prevent impulse conduction, with rapid onset and short duration (about 10–15 minutes).

proparacaine.definition: A topical ophthalmic ester local anesthetic used to numb the surface of the eye before minor procedures or diagnostic tests; it blocks voltage-gated sodium channels in nerve membranes to temporarily halt sensation, with rapid onset and a short duration (about 10–20 minutes).

proxymetacaine.definition: A topical ophthalmic local anesthetic used to numb the surface of the eye for short procedures, typically administered as a 0.5% solution.

foreign body removal (eye).definition: Removal of a foreign object from the eye, usually from the cornea or conjunctiva, using irrigation, suction, or mechanical extraction under topical anesthesia to relieve irritation and prevent corneal abrasion or infection.

ophthalmological procedures.definition: Ophthalmological procedures are medical or surgical interventions performed on the eye or its adnexa to diagnose, treat, or prevent eye disease and vision impairment.

optic anesthesia.definition: A regional ophthalmic anesthetic technique in which local anesthetic is injected near the optic nerve (e.g., retrobulbar or peribulbar block) to render the eye insensate to pain and immobile during eye surgery.

prophylactic odontomy.definition: Not a standard term; in practice, it would refer to a preventive surgical procedure on a tooth to avert future dental disease or complications—most commonly a prophylactic extraction or modification of a tooth to reduce risk.

prophylactic forceps.definition: A set of obstetric forceps used as a preventive measure during labor to facilitate delivery when there is concern about potential fetal or maternal complications, with the aim of shortening the second stage or averting distress.

proprioceptive feedback.definition: A sensory feedback mechanism by which the nervous system monitors body position and movement via proprioceptors in muscles, tendons, and joints, providing information used to adjust motor commands.

proprioceptive impulse.definition: An afferent neural signal from proprioceptors (in muscles, tendons, and joints) that conveys information about limb position, movement, and muscle length to the central nervous system.

proprioceptor.definition: A sensory receptor that detects body position and movement by sensing muscle stretch and length (muscle spindles), tendon tension (Golgi tendon organs), and joint angle (joint receptors), providing proprioceptive information to the central nervous system.

proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitatio.definition: A physical therapy approach that uses proprioceptive input through stretching, manual resistance, and verbal cues in diagonal/spiral movement patterns to facilitate voluntary muscle contraction and increase range of motion, strength, and neuromuscular coordination.

proprioceptive receptor.definition: A sensory receptor located in muscles, tendons, and joints that detects muscle length/stretch, tendon tension, and joint angle to convey proprioceptive information to the central nervous system for the sense of body position and movement.

type ia sensory fiber.definition: A large-diameter, fast-conducting myelinated sensory fiber (Aα) that innervates the primary (annulospiral) endings of skeletal muscle spindles; it transmits rapid changes in muscle length (dynamic and static spindle information) and participates in proprioception and the stretch reflex.

type ii sensory ending.definition: An afferent, slowly adapting ending of a muscle spindle (flower-spray ending) that innervates the intrafusal fibers, primarily nuclear chain fibers, and signals static muscle length and limb position (i.e., information about length rather than dynamic change).

type ii sensory fiber.definition: A large-diameter, myelinated afferent nerve fiber (Group II, typically Aβ) that transmits static, tonic mechanosensory information—for example steady muscle length from muscle spindle secondary endings or sustained touch/pressure—and conducts more slowly than Type Ia (Group Ia) fibers.

efferent motor fiber.definition: Nerve fibers that carry motor impulses from the central nervous system to muscles or glands, initiating movement or secretion.

golgi tendon organ.definition: A proprioceptive sensory receptor in the tendon at the muscle–tendon junction that detects muscle tension and transmits signals via Ib afferent fibers to the spinal cord, triggering autogenic inhibition of the contracting muscle to prevent excessive force.

muscle fiber.definition: An elongated, multinucleated cell that is the basic contractile unit of skeletal muscle; it contains myofibrils organized into sarcomeres and is bounded by a sarcolemma, enabling contraction via actin–myosin interactions.

extrafusal fibers.definition: The main contractile fibers of a skeletal muscle, located outside the muscle spindle; innervated by alpha motor neurons, they generate force during voluntary contractions (composed of slow-twitch Type I and fast-twitch Type II fibers).

intrafusal fibers.definition: Specialized skeletal muscle fibers contained within a muscle spindle; they are innervated by gamma motor neurons and by sensory endings (Group Ia and II) that detect muscle stretch and length, providing proprioceptive feedback and enabling regulation of muscle tone. They include dynamic (bag) and static (chain) fibers with contractile ends and a noncontractile central region.

nuclear bag fibers.definition: Intrafusal muscle fibers of the muscle spindle with a central bag-shaped region containing clustered nuclei; they contribute to sensing changes in muscle length and the rate of stretch via primary (Ia) sensory endings.

nuclear chain fibers.definition: Intrafusal skeletal muscle fibers within a muscle spindle that have nuclei arranged in a single row (a “chain”); they serve as proprioceptors that monitor static and slow changes in muscle length, contributing to limb position sense and reflex regulation.

neuromuscular spindle.definition: A sensory receptor within a skeletal muscle that detects stretch and the rate of length change; composed of intrafusal fibers innervated by gamma motor neurons and afferent Ia and II fibers, mediating proprioception and the stretch (myotatic) reflex.

medial epicondyle of humerus.definition: A prominent bony projection on the medial side of the distal humerus; the origin of the common flexor tendon and an attachment site for the ulnar collateral ligament.

head kidney.definition: An organ in fishes and some amphibians—the anterior portion of the kidney in the head region that serves as the primary site of hematopoiesis (blood-cell formation) and contains interrenal tissue for hormone production; it functions as an endocrine/immune organ in addition to renal tissue.

thyrotoxic crisis.definition: An acute, life-threatening exacerbation of thyrotoxicosis (thyroid storm) characterized by high fever, marked tachycardia or arrhythmias, agitation or delirium, and multisystem decompensation (cardiovascular, GI, hepatic, CNS) precipitated by stress; requires urgent ICU management with antithyroid therapy, iodine, beta-blockade, glucocorticoids, and aggressive supportive care.

prorenin.definition: An inactive precursor of renin; produced mainly by juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney (and some other tissues); it is proteolytically cleaved to active renin, initiating the renin–angiotensin system.

big renin.definition: An inactive precursor form of renin (prorenin), a larger proenzyme produced by juxtaglomerular cells and circulating in plasma; it is cleaved to active renin, contributing to the renin–angiotensin system.

prosencephalic.definition: Relating to the prosencephalon, the embryonic forebrain that develops into the telencephalon (cerebral hemispheres) and diencephalon.

prostaglandin.definition: A group of lipid mediators derived from arachidonic acid via cyclooxygenase enzymes that act locally (autocrine/paracrine) to regulate inflammation, pain and fever, vascular tone, platelet function, smooth muscle activity, and gastric mucosal protection.

prostacyclin.definition: A prostaglandin produced by vascular endothelium that inhibits platelet aggregation and promotes vasodilation; it acts as an endogenous anti-thrombotic mediator opposing thromboxane A2.

arachidonic acid.definition: A polyunsaturated omega-6 fatty acid (20:4, n-6) incorporated in cell membrane phospholipids; released by phospholipase A2 and converted by COX and LOX enzymes into eicosanoids (prostanoids and leukotrienes), mediating inflammation and other signaling; derived from dietary linoleic acid.

thromboxane.definition: A prostanoid synthesized by activated platelets from arachidonic acid via the cyclooxygenase pathway; it promotes platelet aggregation and vasoconstriction, with the active, short-lived form TXA2 rapidly inactivated to the stable metabolite TXB2.

prostaglandin inhibitor.definition: A substance that decreases prostaglandin production or blocks its action, commonly by inhibiting cyclooxygenase enzymes (as with NSAIDs), thereby reducing inflammation, pain, and fever.

prostanoic acid.definition: A 20-carbon fatty acid that serves as the parent skeleton for prostanoids (prostaglandins, thromboxanes, and prostacyclins); derived from arachidonic acid; characterized by a cyclopentane ring fused to a hydrocarbon chain and a terminal carboxyl group.

prostate-specific antigen.definition: A protein produced by the prostate. Elevated levels may indicate the presence of cancer, benign prostatic hyperplasia, or prostatitis. Often referred to as PSA.

psa velocity.definition: The rate at which a man’s PSA level increases over time.

percent-free psa.definition: The percentage of total prostate-specific antigen that is not bound to proteins in the blood; calculated as (free PSA ÷ total PSA) × 100. It helps distinguish prostate cancer from benign prostatic conditions in men with elevated PSA; lower values suggest higher cancer risk, while higher values favor benign disease. Common thresholds show cancer risk rising as %fPSA falls (e.g., <10–15%), with higher percentages (e.g., ≥25–30%) more consistent with non-cancerous conditions.

prostatic calculus.definition: Calcifications within the prostate gland (prostatic calculi); usually incidental and asymptomatic, arising from calcium deposition around corpora amylacea or chronic inflammatory changes. Large stones may cause discomfort or lower urinary tract symptoms, but treatment is rarely needed unless symptomatic.

prostatic catheter.definition: A urinary catheter passed through the prostatic urethra into the bladder to drain urine; commonly a Foley catheter used for urinary drainage in men with retention or after prostate procedures.

coude catheter.definition: A urinary catheter with a curved, angled tip designed to navigate past urethral obstructions (such as an enlarged prostate) during catheterization.

prostatic ductule.definition: A small duct of the prostate that drains secretions from the prostatic glands into the prostatic urethra.

prostatic fascia.definition: A dense connective tissue envelope around the prostate gland, forming the periprostatic fascia. It surrounds the gland, blends anteriorly with the fibromuscular stroma and detrusor muscle, and posteriorly with Denonvilliers’ fascia to separate the gland from the rectum; it contains neurovascular structures that course laterally.

prostatic fluid.definition: An alkaline, milky secretion from the prostate gland that is part of semen; it contains citrate, zinc, and enzymes such as prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and prostatic acid phosphatase, helping nourish, protect, and facilitate sperm function and fertilization.

prostatic syncope.definition: A fainting episode attributed to prostatic disease, typically occurring with voiding or urinary retention and thought to result from reflex vagal (autonomic) stimulation or orthostatic changes causing transient cerebral hypoperfusion.

prostatic urethral polyps.definition: Benign mucosal outgrowth from the prostatic urethra, typically a fibroepithelial or fibrous polyp arising from the urothelium-lined prostatic segment; may present with lower urinary tract symptoms such as obstruction or hematuria and is usually treated with endoscopic removal or transurethral resection.

prostatic utricle.definition: A small, midline, blind-ending pouch or diverticulum of the prostatic urethra located at the verumontanum, representing a vestigial remnant of the Müllerian (paramesonephric) ducts. It is usually asymptomatic but can be enlarged or predispose to infections, urinary symptoms, or associated genital anomalies.

prostatism.definition: A blockage at the base of the bladder that reduces or prevents the flow of urine into the urethra, the tube that carries urine out of the body (also known as bladder outlet obstruction). Typical symptoms include feeling the need to urinate right away yet having to strain to do so, having a weak urinary stream, dribbling after urinating, feeling as though the bladder has not been emptied completely, needing to urinate frequently, or experiencing urinary incontinence.

prostatomegaly.definition: Enlargement of the prostate gland, which can be associated with lower urinary tract symptoms and may result from benign prostatic hyperplasia, prostatitis, or prostate cancer.

transurethral resection.definition: A surgical procedure in which tissue is removed from the urinary tract through the urethra using a resectoscope, most commonly to resect bladder tumors (TURBT) or to remove prostatic tissue for benign prostatic hyperplasia (TURP).

resectoscope.definition: An instrument that permits a surgeon to view the inside of a body cavity in order to remove a part of an organ or structure.

core-needle biopsy.definition: A diagnostic procedure in which a hollow core needle is inserted into a lesion (often under imaging guidance such as ultrasound, CT, or MRI) to obtain one or more cylindrical tissue samples for histopathologic examination, allowing assessment of tissue architecture rather than single cells.

ductal carcinoma.definition: A cancer that starts in the lining of a duct, most commonly in the breast; it can be noninvasive, confined to the ducts, or invasive, having spread into surrounding breast tissue and potentially to distant sites.

prostaglandin e.definition: A group of prostaglandin E series (PGE1, PGE2, PGE3), lipid mediators derived from arachidonic acid via cyclooxygenase; act as local hormones to regulate inflammation, fever and pain, promote vasodilation and vascular permeability, modulate smooth muscle tone (including uterine contractions), and protect gastric mucosa; signal through EP receptors (EP1–EP4).

starr-edwards prosthesis.definition: A historical ball-in-cage mechanical heart valve used to replace diseased heart valves; a small ball moves within a surrounding cage to occlude the orifice and regulate blood flow, and it was among the first successful prosthetic valves, now largely obsolete in favor of newer designs.

prosthetic heart valve.definition: An artificial valve implanted to replace a diseased native heart valve, restoring normal unidirectional blood flow; it can be mechanical (durable, often requiring lifelong anticoagulation) or bioprosthetic (tissue-based) and may be implanted surgically or by transcatheter techniques.

heart valve.definition: There are four valves in the heart that open to allow blood to flow through or out of the heart and then close to keep it from flowing backward.

prosthetic restoration.definition: A restoration using an artificial prosthesis to replace missing or damaged tissue or tooth structure, thereby restoring function and esthetics (e.g., crowns, bridges, dentures, implants).

prosthetics.definition: Devices that replace, support, or enhance the function of a missing or impaired body part, most commonly artificial limbs (prostheses) used after amputation or congenital absence.

prosthetist.definition: A healthcare professional who designs, fabricates, fits, and maintains artificial limbs (prostheses) for people who have lost limbs or were born with limb deficiencies.

prosthion.definition: The most anterior point on the maxillary dental/alveolar process in the midline, used as a cephalometric landmark for the anterior limit of the upper jaw.

protease inhibitor.definition: A class of drugs that help fight retrovirus infections; commonly prescribed to treat human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

proteolysis.definition: The enzymatic breakdown of proteins into smaller peptides or amino acids by proteases; a central process in digestion and intracellular protein turnover.

proteolipid.definition: A protein intimately associated with lipids, forming a lipid–protein complex that is a structural component of biological membranes; lipid moieties are often integral to its membrane localization and function.

proteolytic.definition: Relating to proteolysis; involving the enzymatic breakdown of proteins into shorter polypeptides or amino acids by proteases.

proteus syndrome.definition: Proteus syndrome is a rare, mosaic overgrowth disorder caused by a somatic activating mutation in the AKT1 gene, leading to progressive, asymmetric overgrowth of bones, soft tissues, and skin, often with vascular malformations, lipomas, epidermal nevi, and an increased risk of tumors.

proteus mirabilis.definition: A Gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium that is urease-positive and highly motile with swarming motility; a common cause of urinary tract infections (especially catheter-associated) and can promote struvite stone formation due to urease activity.

proteus morganii.definition: An opportunistic Gram-negative bacterium in the Enterobacteriaceae family; part of the normal intestinal flora in humans and capable of causing infections such as urinary tract infections, wound infections, bacteremia/sepsis, and meningitis, especially in hospitalized or immunocompromised individuals.

pcc.definition:
PCC can refer to multiple medical terms. Do you mean:
- Posterior cingulate cortex: a brain region in the medial parietal lobe involved in memory, attention, and is a key part of the default mode network.
- Pyruvate carboxylase deficiency: a rare metabolic disorder caused by deficiency of the enzyme pyruvate carboxylase, leading to lactic acidosis and other metabolic issues.

If you had a different PCC in mind, please specify.

protamine zinc insulin.definition: A long-acting insulin formulation in which insulin is complexed with protamine and zinc to form a slow-dissolving suspension that provides prolonged insulin action after subcutaneous injection.

prostigmin.definition: A reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that increases acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction; used to treat myasthenia gravis and to reverse nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockade after anesthesia.

alprostadil.definition: A synthetic prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) analog that relaxes vascular smooth muscle by increasing cyclic AMP; used to maintain patency of the ductus arteriosus in neonates with certain congenital heart defects and to treat erectile dysfunction (intracavernosal injection or intraurethral administration).

prostin vr pediatric.definition: A prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) analog (alprostadil) used to maintain ductus arteriosus patency in neonates with certain congenital heart defects until surgical repair or palliation.

protein c.definition: A vitamin K–dependent serine protease produced by the liver; when activated (activated protein C), it proteolytically inactivates factors Va and VIIIa (with protein S as a cofactor), thereby inhibiting thrombin formation and exerting an anticoagulant effect.

protein s.definition: A vitamin K–dependent plasma glycoprotein that serves as a cofactor for activated protein C; it enhances inactivation of factors Va and VIIIa, reducing thrombin generation and providing anticoagulant activity. It circulates in plasma bound to C4b-binding protein, and deficiency or dysfunction increases the risk of venous thrombosis.

hyperproteinemia.definition: A laboratory finding of increased total serum protein concentration in the blood, often due to dehydration or overproduction of immunoglobulins (gammopathy); not a disease on its own.

maple sugar urine disease.definition: A rare autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by deficiency of the branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex, resulting in accumulation of the branched-chain amino acids leucine, isoleucine, and valine and their keto acids in blood and urine; presents with poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy, and a distinctive maple-syrup odor in urine, and can cause severe brain injury or coma if untreated. Management includes lifelong dietary restriction of branched-chain amino acids and, in some cases, liver transplantation.

intervascular thrombosis.definition: Not a standard term; if meant intravascular thrombosis, the formation of a blood clot within a blood vessel, which can obstruct arterial or venous blood flow and lead to tissue ischemia or infarction.

endotoxic shock.definition: A form of septic shock caused by circulating endotoxin (lipopolysaccharide) from Gram-negative bacteria, triggering a systemic inflammatory response with cytokine release (e.g., TNF-α, IL-1, IL-6) that leads to widespread vasodilation, increased vascular permeability, hypotension, and organ hypoperfusion.

amino acids.definition: Organic compounds that are the building blocks of proteins; each contains an amino group, a carboxyl group, a hydrogen, and a distinctive side chain attached to a central carbon, and they participate in protein synthesis and various metabolic processes.

protein hydrolysate.definition: A product obtained by enzymatic or chemical hydrolysis of proteins into free amino acids and short peptides, providing a readily digestible protein source for medical nutrition.

prothrombinemia.definition: An elevated level of prothrombin (coagulation factor II) in the blood, which can enhance coagulation and predispose to thrombosis; the term is not commonly used in modern practice.

international normalized ratio.definition: A standardized measure of blood coagulability derived from the prothrombin time, expressed to account for reagent sensitivity; used to monitor and adjust oral anticoagulant therapy (e.g., warfarin).

protopam chloride.definition: An oxime antidote used to treat organophosphate poisoning by reactivating acetylcholinesterase; it cleaves the organophosphate–enzyme bond to restore enzyme activity and is typically given with atropine, with limited central nervous system penetration.

erythropoietic protoporphyria.definition: A rare autosomal dominant porphyria caused by partial ferrochelatase deficiency in heme synthesis, leading to accumulation of protoporphyrin IX in erythrocytes, plasma, and liver; presents with immediate, painful photosensitivity to sunlight (nonblistering) and can cause hepatic complications from protoporphyrin deposition.

protozoal infection.definition: An infection caused by protozoan parasites, which are single-celled eukaryotes. These infections may involve the intestinal tract, blood, or other tissues and are transmitted by contaminated food or water, vectors such as mosquitoes, or direct contact; examples include malaria, giardiasis, amebiasis, and toxoplasmosis.

proximal renal tubular acidosis.definition: A type 2 renal tubular acidosis caused by defective proximal tubule reabsorption of filtered bicarbonate, leading to bicarbonate wasting in the urine and a non-anion gap metabolic acidosis; it is often associated with Fanconi syndrome (glucosuria, aminoaciduria, phosphaturia).

proximal radioulnar articulation.definition: Pivot-type synovial joint between the head of the radius and the radial notch of the ulna near the elbow; it allows rotation of the forearm (pronation and supination) around the ulna and is stabilized by the annular ligament and interosseous membrane.

psammoma body.definition: A calcified, concentric, laminated spherical body seen in certain tumors; formed by deposition of calcium in tumor tissue, most commonly in papillary thyroid carcinoma, serous papillary ovarian carcinoma, and meningioma.

psammoma bodies.definition: Concentrically laminated calcified bodies seen histologically in certain neoplasms, especially papillary thyroid carcinoma and serous papillary ovarian carcinomas, arising from calcified necrotic tumor debris.

psammosarcoma.definition: A rare malignant neoplasm in which the tumor shows sarcomatous differentiation with abundant psammoma bodies—calcified, concentric laminated structures.

psammomata.definition: Concentrically laminated calcified round bodies found within certain tumors, most commonly in papillary thyroid carcinoma, serous papillary carcinomas of the ovary or endometrium, and meningiomas.

pseudarthritis.definition: A false joint formed at the site of a fracture due to nonunion, in which the fracture ends do not unite and are bridged by fibrous tissue or cartilage, allowing abnormal movement but not constituting a true synovial joint.

pseudoangina.definition: Chest pain resembling angina but not caused by myocardial ischemia or coronary artery disease; often due to noncardiac etiologies such as esophageal disorders, gastroesophageal reflux, musculoskeletal pain, or anxiety.

pseudoacanthosis nigricans.definition: An appearance that mimics acanthosis nigricans—velvety, hyperpigmented plaques in intertriginous areas—but occurs without insulin resistance or metabolic syndrome; often due to non–insulin-mediated factors such as certain medications (e.g., niacin, corticosteroids), paraneoplastic processes, or friction-related dermatoses.

pseudoactinomycosis.definition: An actinomycosis-like infection caused by organisms other than Actinomyces (e.g., Nocardia or other actinomycetes), presenting with chronic granulomatous inflammation and draining sinuses that resemble true actinomycosis.

prozac.definition: An antidepressant medication (generic fluoxetine) that is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI); it increases serotonin levels in the brain by blocking its reuptake and is approved for major depressive disorder and several other conditions, including obsessive-compulsive disorder, bulimia nervosa, panic disorder, and premenstrual dysphoric disorder.

fluoxetine.definition: A selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant that blocks serotonin reuptake, increasing serotonin in the brain; used to treat major depressive disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, bulimia nervosa, and panic disorder.

prurigo.definition: A chronic itchy skin eruption characterized by intensely pruritic papules or nodules resulting from an itch-scratch cycle; may be idiopathic or associated with atopy, xerosis, insect bites, or systemic disease.

prurigo agria.definition: Not a standard modern medical term; historically used to describe a chronic itchy eruption with pruritic nodules formed from scratching, aligning with what is now called prurigo nodularis or other chronic prurigo syndromes.

prurigo ferox.definition: A chronic, severely pruritic form of prurigo presenting with firm, hyperkeratotic nodules or plaques resulting from repeated scratching; often considered a hypertrophic variant of prurigo nodularis.

pruritus ani.definition: Itching of the skin around the anus, commonly due to irritation or moisture but may reflect conditions such as dermatitis, hemorrhoids, anal fissures, infection, or pinworm infestation.

pruritus vulvae.definition: Itching of the vulvar skin; a common symptom with many potential causes, including dermatologic conditions (eczema/dermatitis, lichen sclerosus), infections (yeast/candidiasis, bacterial vaginosis or other STIs), irritants or allergies, and hormonal or moisture-related factors.

seminal colliculus.definition: A raised prominence on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra in males, serving as a landmark for the openings of the ejaculatory ducts; the opening of the prostatic utricle is located nearby.

prostatic urethra.definition: A portion of the male urethra that traverses the prostate gland, extending from the internal urethral orifice at the bladder neck to the apex of the prostate; it carries urine and, during ejaculation, receives secretions from the prostatic ducts and the openings of the ejaculatory ducts.

mesial surface.definition: Toward the midline of the dental arch; the proximal surface that faces the adjacent tooth toward the midline.

distal surface.definition: The surface of a tooth that faces away from the midline of the dental arch; the side toward the back of the mouth, opposite the mesial surface.

palatal surface.definition: Anatomical surface of a maxillary tooth that faces the hard palate; the inner surface toward the palate (the counterpart of the lingual surface on mandibular teeth).

incisal surface.definition: The biting (incising) surface of an anterior tooth, formed by the incisal edge, that contacts the opposing dentition during biting.

lingual surface.definition: The surface of a tooth that faces the tongue; the inner surface of the crown toward the tongue, opposite the buccal (cheek) or labial (lip) surface (on maxillary teeth, this surface is often called the palatal surface).

buccal surface.definition: A surface of a tooth that faces the buccal (cheek) side; the outer surface of posterior teeth toward the cheek (for anterior teeth, the equivalent surface is usually called the labial or facial surface).

labial surface.definition: The outward (facial) surface of a tooth that faces the lips; specifically, the labial surface of anterior teeth (incisors and canines). For posterior teeth, the corresponding surface is called the buccal surface.

proximal surface of the tooth.definition: A tooth surface facing an adjacent tooth in the same dental arch; i.e., the mesial or distal surface that contacts or is adjacent to a neighboring tooth.

pseudoagraphia.definition: Feigned or false inability to write, typically seen as a non-organic (psychogenic) or deceptive presentation rather than true agraphia due to brain injury or aphasia.

echographia.definition: Ultrasonography; the use of high-frequency sound waves to create an image of internal body structures.

pseudoainhum.definition: External constriction of a digit by a circumferential band or ring (often hair, thread, or jewelry) leading to progressive ischemia and potential autoamputation; mimics true ainhum but results from an external constrictor rather than a primary disease of the digit.

pseudoallele.definition: An apparent allele arising from a paralogous copy at a non-allelic locus that mimics the sequence or phenotype of the true allele at the gene of interest.

pseudoankylosis.definition: A condition in which there is marked limitation of joint movement that resembles true ankylosis, but the joint is structurally normal and the restriction arises from periarticular or extra-articular (soft-tissue) factors such as scar tissue or muscle spasm.

pseudoanodontia.definition: A condition in which teeth are present but have failed to erupt or become visible in the mouth, giving the appearance of anodontia; radiographs typically show unerupted or displaced teeth.

pseudoataxia.definition: An ataxia-like disturbance of gait or coordination that mimics cerebellar ataxia but is not due to cerebellar dysfunction, often caused by non-ataxic movement disorders (e.g., dystonia, chorea, or myoclonus), sensory loss, or functional/psychogenic factors.

pseudobulbar paralysis.definition: A neurologic disorder caused by bilateral corticobulbar tract lesions resulting in impaired voluntary control of bulbar muscles (facial, pharyngeal, and tongue), with features such as spastic dysarthria, dysphagia, hyperreflexia, facial weakness, and emotional lability.

pseudocephalocele.definition: An irregular cephalocele‑like lesion—soft-tissue swelling in the scalp or facial region that mimics a cephalocele but is not a true herniation of meninges or brain through a skull defect and lacks intracranial communication.

pseudochancre.definition: A lesion that mimics a syphilitic chancre (a painless, indurated ulcer at the site of inoculation) but is not caused by Treponema pallidum; i.e., a false chancre caused by other infections or noninfectious processes.

pseudocholinesterase.definition: An enzyme produced by the liver (butyrylcholinesterase) that hydrolyzes choline-based esters such as succinylcholine and mivacurium; deficiency can cause prolonged paralysis and apnea after certain anesthetics.

pseudochondroplasia.definition: A hereditary skeletal dysplasia characterized by disproportionate short stature with rhizomelic limb shortening and early-onset joint problems; often used synonymously with pseudoachondroplasia (caused by COMP gene mutations).

pseudochylous ascites.definition: A milky ascitic fluid with high cholesterol content and low triglyceride levels, often containing cholesterol crystals, resulting from long-standing peritoneal inflammation (e.g., tuberculous peritonitis) or malignancy; differs from chylous ascites by the absence of chylomicrons.

pseudoclaudication.definition: A leg-pain or weakness on walking that resembles intermittent claudication but arises from nonvascular causes, such as spinal pathology or musculoskeletal disorders, rather than from arterial insufficiency.

pseudocoxalgia.definition: Hip or groin pain that mimics true hip joint disease but originates from non-hip sources, such as spinal, sacroiliac, or pelvic pathology, groin/abdominal conditions, or referred pain from the knee.

pseudoephedrine hydrochloride.definition: A decongestant; the hydrochloride salt of a sympathomimetic amine that stimulates nasal adrenergic receptors to cause vasoconstriction of mucosal blood vessels and reduce nasal swelling.

pseudoephedrine sulfate.definition: An orally available sulfate salt of a sympathomimetic decongestant that stimulates α-adrenergic receptors to vasoconstrict nasal mucosa and relieve nasal congestion; commonly used in cold, flu, and allergy formulations. Use may elevate blood pressure and heart rate and cause nervousness or insomnia; often subject to regulatory controls due to potential for misuse.

pseudoepitheliomatous keratotic and mica.definition: A rare penile dermatosis presenting as slowly enlarging, thick, mica-like keratotic plaques on the glans or foreskin with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia; most often affects elderly men and can mimic squamous cell carcinoma histologically, with potential progression to verrucous or conventional squamous carcinoma. Management ranges from local therapies (topical agents, ablative treatments) to surgical excision or laser approaches, with careful long-term surveillance.

pseudofracture.definition: A fracture-like, incomplete fissure in bone seen in metabolic bone disorders such as osteomalacia or rickets; a stress-related fracture that does not traverse the entire bone, typically appearing as a transverse lucent band with surrounding sclerosis (Looser zone).

pseudogene.definition: A nonfunctional segment of DNA that resembles a gene but does not encode a functional protein, typically arising from gene duplication or retrotransposition with disabling mutations or loss of regulatory elements.

pseudoglandular period.definition: A stage of fetal lung development occurring roughly during gestational weeks 5–17 in which the tracheobronchial tree undergoes extensive branching to form the conducting airways down to the terminal bronchioles; gas-exchange units have not yet formed.

pseudo-graefe’s sign.definition: An apparent lid lag on downgaze that mimics Graefe sign but is caused by non-thyroid eyelid malposition or other eyelid abnormalities rather than Graves’ orbitopathy.

pseudogynecomastia.definition: A benign enlargement of the male breast due to deposition of adipose (fat) tissue rather than proliferation of glandular breast tissue; commonly associated with obesity or weight gain and typically lacking the firm glandular tissue seen in true gynecomastia.

pseudohermaphrodite.definition: A condition in which gonadal sex (ovaries or testes) is different from the external genitalia or phenotype, so the individual has gonads of one sex but external genitalia resembling the opposite sex.

pseudohyperkalemia.definition: A laboratory artifact in which the measured potassium concentration in a blood sample is spuriously elevated due to potassium release from leukocytes or platelets during or after collection or processing, yielding a falsely high value that does not reflect the patient’s true in vivo potassium level.

pseudohyperparathyroidism.definition: An historical term for hypercalcemia with inappropriately normal or elevated parathyroid hormone levels, mimicking hyperparathyroidism but due to nonautonomous PTH regulation (for example, familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia from CaSR mutations).

pseudohypertension.definition: Falsely elevated blood pressure reading caused by noncompressible, calcified arteries (often medial calcific sclerosis) that prevent adequate arterial occlusion by the cuff; true intra-arterial pressure is lower, and BP may be overtreated, especially in the elderly.

pseudohypertrophy.definition: An apparent enlargement of a muscle or limb caused by replacement of muscle tissue with fat and connective tissue (and sometimes edema), rather than true hypertrophy of muscle fibers; commonly seen in muscular dystrophies such as Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

pseudohyponatremia.definition: A laboratory artifact in which the reported serum sodium concentration is falsely low due to excess plasma solids (e.g., severe hyperlipidemia or hyperproteinemia) affecting indirect ion‑selective electrode measurements; plasma osmolality is normal and the true sodium concentration is typically normal.

pseudoileus.definition: A functional bowel obstruction with delayed or absent intestinal propulsion and dilated bowel loops, mimicking mechanical obstruction but without a physical obstructing lesion (paralytic/adynamic ileus or intestinal pseudo-obstruction).

pseudoisochromatic.definition: Relating to color-vision testing that uses pseudoisochromatic plates, which present patterns of dots in similar colors so that individuals with normal color vision can detect a figure or number, whereas individuals with color vision deficiency cannot.

pseudojaundice.definition: Yellow-orange skin discoloration caused by elevated carotene levels (carotenemia) rather than bilirubin; sclera remain normal, and it typically results from excessive intake of carotene-rich foods or supplements, with normal bilirubin distinguishing it from true jaundice.

pseudolymphoma.definition: A benign, reactive proliferation of lymphoid tissue that histologically and clinically resembles lymphoma but is not malignant; typically polyclonal with a favorable prognosis, may present as skin nodules or nodal enlargements, and is often triggered by infection, drugs, or inflammatory stimuli, with management focused on removing the trigger or local therapy.

pseudolysogeny.definition: A state in which temperate phage DNA persists in a bacterial cell without integrating into the host genome and without active replication or virion production, existing episomally in a dormant state often during nutrient limitation and potentially reactivating when conditions improve.

pseudomamma.definition: A nonstandard historical term referring to a breast-like structure or mass that resembles mammary tissue but is not true mammary gland tissue.

pseudomania.definition: A mania-like state that mimics mania but is not due to a primary manic disorder; historically used to describe mania arising secondary to another condition, such as delirium, intoxication, or another medical/psychiatric disorder.

pseudomegacolon.definition: A radiologic finding of marked colonic dilation without a mechanical obstruction or congenital megacolon, often due to acute colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie syndrome) or severe constipation; i.e., a functional dilatation that resembles megacolon.

pseudomenstruation.definition: Menstrual-like vaginal bleeding that occurs without ovulation and without the hormonal pattern of a true menstrual cycle—often seen in anovulatory cycles or as withdrawal bleeding from hormones (and in newborns due to maternal estrogen exposure).

pseudomnesia.definition: A false or illusory memory—an experience of recalling or believing an event occurred when it did not, often due to imagination, suggestion, or misattribution.

pseudomonad.definition: A bacterium in the genus Pseudomonas; a Gram-negative, aerobic, nonfermentative rod commonly found in soil and water, with several species that can cause opportunistic infections (notably Pseudomonas aeruginosa).

pseudomonas maltophilia.definition: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (formerly Pseudomonas maltophilia) is a Gram-negative, aerobic, non-fermenting bacillus that acts as an opportunistic nosocomial pathogen, causing infections such as pneumonia and bacteremia in hospitalized or immunocompromised patients; it has intrinsic resistance to many antibiotics and is typically treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, with alternatives chosen by susceptibility.

pseudomutuality.definition: An apparent but false sense of closeness and harmony within a family or close relationship, in which real disagreements and individual differences are avoided or suppressed to maintain cohesion, thereby hindering authentic communication and differentiation.

pseudomyopia.definition: Reversible spasm of accommodation causing a temporary myopic shift and blurred distance vision, typically after prolonged near work; not a true refractive error and often revealed by cycloplegic refraction, with symptoms improving with rest or cycloplegia.

pseudomyxoma.definition: A rare condition in which mucin-producing tumor cells disseminate within the peritoneal cavity, leading to accumulation of gelatinous mucinous ascites and mucinous implants on peritoneal surfaces, most often arising from an appendiceal mucinous neoplasm.

pseudomyxoma peritonei.definition: A rare syndrome characterized by the accumulation of mucinous material (gelatinous ascites) in the peritoneal cavity with widespread implantation of mucin-producing tumor cells on peritoneal surfaces, most commonly arising from an appendiceal neoplasm.

pseudonystagmus.definition: A nystagmus-like eye movement that mimics true nystagmus but arises from non-vestibular causes or artifacts (e.g., fixation instability, eyelid/oculomotor tremor), not from a primary vestibular or central oculomotor disorder.

pseudopapilledema.definition: An apparent elevation of the optic disc that mimics papilledema on examination but is not due to true optic disc edema or elevated intracranial pressure; commonly caused by buried optic disc drusen or a congenitally crowded optic nerve head.

pseudoparalysis.definition: A clinical condition in which apparent paralysis or immobility results from pain, guarding, or functional limitation rather than a true neurological or muscular deficit.

pseudoparaplegia.definition: A nonorganic (functional) paralysis of both legs that mimics true paraplegia but lacks an identifiable structural spinal cord or nerve injury, often associated with inconsistent motor signs and preserved objective neurophysiological findings.

pseudoparesis.definition: Apparent weakness of a limb that cannot be explained by structural neurological or muscular disease; a nonorganic (functional/psychogenic) weakness that mimics true paresis, often seen in conversion or functional neurological symptom disorders.

pseudopelade.definition: A cicatricial (scarring) alopecia presenting as slowly enlarging, ill-defined patches of hair loss on the scalp with minimal inflammatory signs, in which hair follicles are destroyed and replaced by scar tissue, leaving smooth, atrophic patches.

pseudopericarditis.definition: A clinical syndrome that closely resembles acute pericarditis (often with chest pain and pericardial-type ECG changes) but with no evidence of pericardial inflammation; the symptoms arise from other etiologies.

pseudophakodonesis.definition: A tremulous movement or instability of a posterior chamber intraocular lens (IOL) after cataract surgery, caused by inadequate capsular/zonular support, resulting in the IOL moving with eye movements.

pseudophyllidea.definition: An outdated order of tapeworms (class Cestoda) characterized by a scolex with leaf-like attachment organs called bothridia, absence of a rostellum with hooks, and eggs that are operculated; their life cycles typically involve aquatic crustaceans as the first intermediate host and fish or amphibians as the second intermediate host, with humans acquiring infection from consuming raw or undercooked fish.

pseudopod.definition: A temporary cytoplasmic projection of a cell formed by actin-driven remodeling of the cytoskeleton, used for locomotion (amoeboid movement) and for engulfing particles (phagocytosis); commonly seen in amoebae and in some white blood cells (e.g., macrophages and neutrophils).

pseudopolyp.definition: A non-neoplastic, inflammatory mucosal projection that resembles a true polyp, typically arising in chronic inflammatory conditions (e.g., inflammatory bowel disease or chronic rhinosinusitis) from edema and mucosal regeneration.

pseudopregnancy.definition: A condition in which an individual exhibits pregnancy-like signs and symptoms (such as amenorrhea, abdominal enlargement, nausea, breast changes, and perceived fetal movements) without an actual gestation, often due to hormonal imbalances and psychosocial factors.

pseudoprognathism.definition: A false appearance of forward-positioning of the mandible (apparent prognathism) caused by a retrusive maxilla or dental occlusal factors, with no true skeletal mandibular protrusion.

pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism.definition: An inherited condition presenting with Albright hereditary osteodystrophy features (short stature, round face, brachydactyly) but with no parathyroid hormone resistance; calcium and phosphate levels are normal.

pseudopsychiosis.definition: A condition presenting psychotic-like symptoms (delusions, hallucinations) that are caused by another medical or psychiatric illness rather than by a primary psychotic disorder.

pseudopterygium.definition: A band of conjunctival tissue adherent to the cornea at the limbus that mimics a pterygium but arises from ocular surface inflammation or injury rather than true corneal invasion; often separable from the cornea on examination or surgery.

pseudoptosis.definition: An apparent upper eyelid droop that mimics ptosis but is not due to weakness of the eyelid elevator muscles (levator palpebrae superioris or Müller muscle); it is caused by factors such as dermatochalasis, brow ptosis, or enophthalmos with normal levator function.

pseudopuberty.definition: A form of precocious puberty caused by autonomous peripheral production of sex steroids (e.g., from adrenal or gonadal tissue or non-gonadal sources such as McCune–Albright syndrome), leading to pubertal changes without activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis; gonadotropin levels are low and GnRH stimulation does not elicit a pubertal LH response.

pseudorabies.definition: An infectious disease of swine caused by a herpesvirus (Suid herpesvirus 1) that produces acute respiratory and neurologic illness in piglets and reproductive losses in sows; it is highly contagious and can affect other species, though human infection is rare.

pseudoretinitis pigmentosa.definition: A RP-like retinal dystrophy caused by conditions other than true retinitis pigmentosa; it presents with RP-like fundus findings (bone-spicule pigmentation and arteriolar attenuation) and night vision loss but arises from non‑RP etiologies (inflammatory, infectious, toxic, metabolic, or syndromic retinopathies) with differing prognosis and inheritance.

pseudorubella.definition: A rubella-like exanthem caused by etiologies other than rubella virus, typically due to other viral infections or medications; rubella infection is clinically and serologically excluded.

pseudosarcoma.definition: A non-malignant, reactive soft-tissue proliferation that mimics a sarcoma clinically and histologically; it resembles a sarcoma but is benign or self-limited.

pseudosclerema.definition: An appearance of diffuse skin hardening that mimics sclerema or scleredema but is not true scleredema/sclerema; typically caused by dermal edema or other non-scleroderma processes and often reversible with treatment of the underlying condition.

pseudosmallpox.definition: A clinical presentation in which a vesicular-pustular rash resembles smallpox but is caused by another pathogen; i.e., a non-variola illness that mimics variola infection.

pseudostrabismus.definition: An apparent misalignment of the eyes due to facial anatomy (e.g., epicanthal folds, wide nasal bridge) or reflex placement, but with normal ocular alignment and binocular function on examination; not a true strabismus.

pseudostratified.definition: A type of epithelium that resembles multiple layers (pseudostratified) but is actually a single layer of cells all attached to the basement membrane; nuclei lie at different levels giving the appearance of stratification. It is typically tall columnar cells, often ciliated with goblet cells, and lines much of the respiratory tract and portions of the male reproductive tract.

pseudotabes.definition: A condition that mimics tabes dorsalis (neurosyphilis) but is not caused by syphilis; signs resemble tabetic phenomena yet have a different etiology.

pseudotruncus arteriosus.definition: A nonstandard term used to describe a truncus arteriosus–like conotruncal malformation in which the great arteries fail to separate into a true aorta and pulmonary artery, resulting in an appearance of a single arterial trunk in some cases; not a widely recognized, well-defined entity.

pseudotubercle.definition: A false tubercle; a small bony prominence that resembles a tubercle but is not a true tubercle, often arising from traction, enthesopathy, or irregular ossification rather than a dedicated tubercle formation.

pseudotuberculosis.definition: A zoonotic bacterial infection caused by a gram-negative enteric organism of the Yersinia genus, typically presenting with fever and abdominal pain due to mesenteric lymphadenitis and that can mimic appendicitis or tuberculosis; may produce granulomatous lesions in the liver and spleen.

pseudovariola.definition: A non-variola illness presenting with a smallpox-like rash and fever, caused by pathogens other than Variola virus; historically used to refer to diseases such as varicella (chickenpox) that resemble smallpox.

psorenteritis.definition: Not a recognized medical term; if used, it would imply inflammation of the intestine (enteritis) occurring in the context of psoriasis, but there is no established clinical syndrome by this name.

intracranial hypertension.definition: Elevated pressure inside the skull due to increased intracranial volume (brain tissue, cerebrospinal fluid, or blood) from causes such as edema, hemorrhage, mass lesions, hydrocephalus, or venous outflow obstruction; in adults, it is typically defined as sustained intracranial pressure above about 20 mm Hg and can cause headache, nausea, vomiting, papilledema, altered consciousness, and risk of brain herniation if untreated.

benign intracranial hypertension.definition: A syndrome of elevated intracranial pressure without a mass, hydrocephalus, or infection, with normal CSF composition; typically presents with headaches and papilledema, often in overweight women of childbearing age. Diagnosis requires neuroimaging to exclude other causes and a high opening pressure on lumbar puncture.

meningeal hydrops.definition: An abnormal accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid within the meninges (primarily the subarachnoid space), causing distension of the meningeal spaces; historically used but not a standard contemporary term (more precise terms include subarachnoid hygroma or arachnoid cyst, depending on location).

pseudovitamin.definition: A substance that resembles a vitamin in chemical structure or function but does not provide the biological activity of the actual vitamin in humans; it may be an inactive analog or an antagonistic form that cannot prevent vitamin-deficiency symptoms in vivo.

psoralen.definition: Plant-derived photosensitizing furocoumarin used in PUVA therapy to treat psoriasis, vitiligo, and some cutaneous lymphomas. It intercalates into DNA and, after UVA exposure, forms covalent cross-links with thymine bases, inhibiting DNA replication and causing cytotoxic effects in hyperproliferative skin cells. Administered topically or orally.

5-methoxypsoralen.definition: A psoralen (furocoumarin) derivative with a methoxy group at the 5-position; a photosensitizing agent used in PUVA phototherapy that, after UVA exposure, intercalates into DNA and forms covalent crosslinks, increasing DNA damage and reducing skin cell proliferation.

8-methoxypsoralen.definition: A psoralen photosensitizer (an 8‑methoxy derivative of psoralen); a furocoumarin used in PUVA therapy that, upon UVA exposure, intercalates into DNA and forms covalent cross-links, inhibiting DNA replication and cell proliferation.

trioxsalen.definition: A psoralen-class photosensitizing agent used with UVA light in PUVA therapy for skin disorders; it intercalates into DNA and, upon UVA exposure, forms covalent bonds with pyrimidine bases, producing DNA crosslinks that inhibit cell proliferation.

psorelcosis.definition: A chronic autoimmune skin disease characterized by well-demarcated, erythematous plaques with silvery scales, commonly affecting the elbows, knees, and scalp; may be associated with psoriatic arthritis.

parrot fever.definition: A zoonotic bacterial infection caused by Chlamydia psittaci, transmitted to humans from infected birds (often parrots and other psittacine birds) via inhalation of dried secretions or droppings; presents with fever, headache, malaise, cough, and sometimes pneumonia; treated with antibiotics such as doxycycline.

psoriasis universalis.definition: A severe, generalized form of psoriasis in which most or all of the skin is affected, presenting with widespread erythematous, scaly plaques (often progressing to erythroderma) and possible systemic symptoms.

psoriatic dermatitis.definition: A chronic inflammatory skin disease in the psoriasis spectrum characterized by well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales, arising from immune-mediated keratinocyte hyperproliferation; may be associated with nail changes and psoriatic arthritis.

calcipotriene.definition: A topical synthetic analog of vitamin D3 used to treat plaque psoriasis by inhibiting keratinocyte proliferation and promoting normal differentiation.

tar.definition: A thick, dark, viscous liquid produced by the destructive distillation of organic materials (most notably coal tar); a complex mixture of hydrocarbons, including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons; used topically in dermatology for conditions such as psoriasis and dermatitis, but it can irritate the skin and is associated with carcinogenic risk with prolonged exposure.

keratolytics.definition: An agent that softens and dissolves keratin in the skin's stratum corneum, promoting desquamation and removal of thickened or hyperkeratotic tissue (e.g., calluses, warts); common examples include salicylic acid, glycolic acid, lactic acid, urea, and sulfur.

ultraviolet light therapy.definition: A treatment that uses controlled exposure to ultraviolet radiation (UVB or UVA, sometimes with psoralen as PUVA) to treat certain skin conditions such as psoriasis, eczema, and vitiligo; typically administered under medical supervision due to risks of skin damage and cancer.

psoas minor.definition: A slender, variably present muscle of the posterior abdominal wall lying anterior to the psoas major; it originates from the T12–L1 vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs and inserts into the iliopubic eminence/pectineal line of the pelvis, weakly flexing the lumbar spine and not crossing the hip joint.

fibrocartilages.definition: A tough, fibrous type of cartilage characterized by dense bundles of collagen fibers (primarily type I) in the matrix, providing high tensile strength and resistance to compression; it occurs in structures such as the intervertebral discs (annulus fibrosus), knee menisci, pubic symphysis, and the temporomandibular joint disk.

pseudostratified columnar epithelium.definition: A single layer of tall cells that gives the false impression of multiple layers because nuclei are at different heights; all cells contact the basement membrane, but not all reach the free surface. It is usually ciliated and contains goblet cells, and lines parts of the respiratory tract where it functions to secrete mucus and move it out of the airways via ciliary action.

psilocin.definition: A naturally occurring psychoactive tryptamine that is the active metabolite of psilocybin; produced in the body from psilocybin and responsible for the psychedelic effects of certain mushrooms by acting as a serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonist (chemical name 4-hydroxy-DMT).

psilocybin.definition: A naturally occurring psychedelic prodrug found in certain mushrooms (e.g., Psilocybe species); after ingestion it is dephosphorylated to psilocin, the active compound that acts as a serotonin 2A receptor agonist to induce psychedelic experiences and is studied for potential therapeutic use in mental health.

psilocybe mexicana.definition: A species of psychedelic mushroom in the family Hymenogastraceae that contains the psychoactive alkaloids psilocybin and psilocin; native to Mexico and Central America and traditionally used in shamanic rituals; ingestion can cause perceptual and mood changes, with possible adverse effects and legal restrictions.

psychalgia.definition: Emotional or mental pain; distress of the mind, not attributable to identifiable tissue injury, sometimes described as psychosomatic or psychologically mediated pain.

psychopharmacology.definition: An area of pharmacology that studies how drugs affect the brain and behavior, including mechanisms of action, therapeutic uses for mental disorders, and the effects and side effects of psychoactive substances.
