rhinosalpingitis.definition: Inflammation of the nasal mucosa together with the mucous lining of the Eustachian (auditory) tube, often causing nasal congestion and discharge plus ear fullness, pain, or hearing changes from impaired tube function.

rhinoscleroma.definition: Chronic granulomatous infection of the nasal mucosa (upper airway) caused by Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis, characterized by progressive nasal obstruction and friable granulomatous lesions with crusting and scarring; histology shows Mikulicz cells; more common in tropical/subtropical regions and treated with prolonged antibiotics.

klebsiella rhinoscleromatis.definition: A Gram-negative, encapsulated rod from the genus Klebsiella that causes rhinoscleroma, a chronic granulomatous infection of the nasal mucosa and upper respiratory tract, presenting with progressive nasal obstruction, mucopurulent discharge, and nodular or ulcerative nasal lesions; histology shows Mikulicz cells within granulomatous inflammation.

rhinoscope.definition: An instrument used to visualize the interior of the nasal cavity, typically a rigid or flexible nasal endoscope.

rhinoscopy.definition: An examination of the nasal cavity using a rhinoscope (nasal endoscope), typically with a rigid or flexible instrument to visualize the nasal mucosa, turbinates, and sinus ostia.

rhinosporidiosis.definition: A chronic granulomatous infection caused by Rhinosporidium seeberi, typically presenting as friable, polypoid masses on the nasal mucosa (often with ocular involvement) that bleed easily; transmitted via contact with contaminated freshwater, usually after mucosal trauma and endemic in parts of South Asia and Africa. Diagnosis is by histopathology showing thick-walled sporangia containing endospores within mucosal tissue. Treatment is surgical excision with cautery; recurrence is common and medical therapy has limited efficacy.

rhinosporidium seeberi.definition: A freshwater protist (Mesomycetozoea) that causes rhinosporidiosis, a chronic mucosal infection most often of the nasal mucosa and conjunctiva; it forms large sporangia containing endospores in the mucosa, producing friable, bleeding polyps and is acquired by traumatic implantation from contaminated water (not a true fungus).

rhinostenosis.definition: Narrowing of the nasal passages (nasal airway) that impairs airflow through the nose, which can be congenital, acquired from trauma or inflammation, or may follow surgery.

rhinotomy.definition: An incision into the nasal cavity made surgically, typically to expose the interior of the nose or sinuses for examination, removal of a foreign body, drainage, or other operative access.

rhoencephalography.definition: A radiographic imaging technique of the brain using X-rays (often with contrast) to visualize intracranial structures; historically used to evaluate brain anatomy and the ventricles, now largely obsolete and replaced by CT and MRI.

rhomboencephalon.definition: An embryonic portion of the neural tube that forms the hindbrain and differentiates into the metencephalon (pons and cerebellum) and the myelencephalon (medulla oblongata).

rhomboid.definition: A muscle of the upper back (the rhomboideus major and rhomboideus minor) that retracts and downwardly rotates the scapula, elevates the medial border, and helps stabilize the shoulder girdle.

rhomboideus major.definition: One of the rhomboid back muscles; it originates from the spinous processes of T2–T5 and inserts on the medial border of the scapula below the spine. It retracts (adducts) and downwardly rotates the scapula, fixing it to the thoracic wall. Innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve (C4–C5).

rhomboideus minor.definition: A small rhomboid-shaped muscle of the upper back that retracts and elevates the scapula and assists in downward rotation; innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve (C4–C5).

median rhomboid glossitis.definition: A well‑demarcated, erythematous, rhomboid patch on the midline dorsal surface of the tongue, just anterior to the circumvallate papillae; commonly attributed to chronic erythematous candidiasis with loss of filiform papillae, and often asymptomatic or associated with mild burning, usually improving with antifungal therapy.

rhombomere.definition: A transient segmental division of the hindbrain (rhombencephalon) in early embryonic development; each rhombomere (r1–r7 in humans) is a distinct transverse region whose cells contribute to specific cranial nerve nuclei and to patterning of the brainstem, with boundaries defined by segmented gene expression (notably HOX genes).

rhotacism.definition: An articulatory speech disorder in which the /r/ sound (the rhotic consonant) is misarticulated, often substituted with another sound (commonly /w/) or omitted; common in children and can improve with speech therapy.

rhuepo.definition: Not found: rhuepo is not a recognized medical term in standard dictionaries. Please check spelling or provide context (e.g., disease, organ system) so I can define it.

rhogam.definition: A prophylactic anti-D (Rh(D)) immunoglobulin given to Rh-negative pregnant women to prevent sensitization to the Rh antigen by neutralizing fetal Rh-positive red blood cells that enter maternal circulation; typically administered around 28 weeks gestation and within 72 hours after events likely to mix fetal and maternal blood (e.g., delivery of an Rh-positive infant, miscarriage, abortion, ectopic pregnancy, or invasive procedures).

rhus.definition: A genus of flowering shrubs and trees in the sumac family (Anacardiaceae); commonly known as sumacs.

rhythm.definition: The regular pattern and timing of heartbeats; more generally, the pattern and timing of recurrence of any physiological event.

rhytid.definition: A wrinkle or crease in the skin, typically due to aging or sun damage.

rhytidosis.definition: Formation or appearance of wrinkles in the skin; a dermatologic process associated with aging, reduced collagen and elastin, and sun exposure (photoaging).

ria.definition: A laboratory method that uses radiolabeled antigen or antibody to measure the concentration of a substance (such as a hormone) in a sample by detecting radioactivity.

opsin.definition: A protein component of visual photopigments in retinal photoreceptors; a seven-transmembrane G protein–coupled receptor that binds retinaldehyde to form a light-sensitive pigment (e.g., rhodopsin in rods and cone pigments in cones).

rhodotorula.definition: A genus of yeast-like, pigmented fungi (basidiomycetous yeasts) commonly found in the environment; colonies are orange to pink due to carotenoid pigments. It is an opportunistic pathogen that can cause fungemia, meningitis, peritonitis, and other infections in immunocompromised patients, often associated with indwelling catheters.

trypanosoma rhodesiense.definition: A subspecies of the parasite Trypanosoma brucei (Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense) that causes acute human African trypanosomiasis (East African sleeping sickness), transmitted by tsetse flies.

rh immune globulin.definition: A preparation of anti-D antibodies derived from human plasma, given to Rh-negative individuals exposed to Rh-positive red blood cells to prevent alloimmunization and subsequent hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn.

entomophthora coronata.definition: An entomopathogenic fungus of the genus Entomophthora that infects and kills insect hosts by producing conidia that adhere to the cuticle, germinate, invade tissues, and proliferate, eventually causing death; occurs as a natural insect pathogen (not a human pathogen).

phycomycete.definition: A primitive fungus formerly classified in the now largely obsolete group Phycomycetes; it typically has coenocytic (non-septate) hyphae and reproduces by sporangia or zygospores, including bread molds such as Mucor and Rhizopus.

miscarriage.definition: When a baby is born too early (before 20 weeks) and dies.

nerve roots.definition: Proximal components of a spinal nerve as it exits the spinal cord, consisting of a dorsal (sensory) root and a ventral (motor) root; the dorsal root transmits sensory information (with the dorsal root ganglion), the ventral root transmits motor commands, and together they form a mixed spinal nerve.

dorsal root.definition: A posterior (sensory) root of a spinal nerve that transmits afferent sensory information from peripheral receptors into the spinal cord; its sensory neuron cell bodies reside in the dorsal root ganglion.

spinal nerve.definition: A mixed peripheral nerve formed by the union of the dorsal (sensory) and ventral (motor) roots of a spinal segment; it exits the vertebral column through the intervertebral foramen and carries motor and sensory fibers to and from the spinal cord, then divides into the dorsal and ventral rami to supply the back and limbs.

small children.definition: A nontechnical term for young children in early childhood, typically aged about 1 to 5 years, including toddlers (roughly 1–3 years) and preschoolers (roughly 3–5 years).

bacterial pneumonia.definition: An infection of the lung parenchyma caused by bacterial pathogens, typically presenting with fever, productive cough, pleuritic chest pain, and dyspnea; diagnosed by clinical signs and imaging, and treated with appropriate antibiotics based on likely organisms and patient factors.

thoracic skeleton.definition: The bony framework of the thorax (the thoracic cage), comprising the twelve thoracic vertebrae, twelve pairs of ribs with costal cartilages, and the sternum, protecting the heart and lungs and aiding respiration.

metastatic disease.definition: The spread of cancer cells from a primary tumor to distant sites, where they establish new, secondary tumors; dissemination occurs via the bloodstream or lymphatic system.

regional nerve block.definition: A procedure in which a local anesthetic is injected near a specific nerve or nerve plexus to temporarily block sensory (and sometimes motor) transmission to a defined region of the body, providing anesthesia or postoperative analgesia for surgery.

semi-fowler’s position.definition: A semi-upright position in which the patient lies on their back with the head of the bed elevated approximately 30–45 degrees (a mid-range Fowler’s position).

benzoin.definition: A balsamic resin obtained from Styrax trees (notably Styrax benzoin); used pharmaceutically as a topical protective coating with mild antiseptic properties, and in tincture form as an alcoholic preparation for skin or mucous membranes.

rest.definition: A period of reduced physical activity prescribed by a clinician to promote healing and decrease stress on an injured or ill body part.

ice.definition: A frozen form of water (solid H2O) at 0°C or below. In medical contexts, it commonly refers to a cold pack used for cryotherapy to reduce pain, swelling, and inflammation by local cooling and vasoconstriction.

elevation.definition: The upward movement or lifting of a body part toward the head (superior direction); in dermatology, it also refers to a lesion that rises above the surrounding skin surface.

chronic renal disease.definition: A progressive, long-standing loss of kidney function, usually defined by a glomerular filtration rate persistently below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or evidence of kidney damage (such as albuminuria) for at least 3 months.

kempner rice-fruit diet.definition: A highly restricted, low-protein, low-sodium therapeutic diet consisting of white rice as the main staple with fruit, fruit juice, and sugar; no meat, dairy, fats, or added salt. It was developed by Dr. Walter Kempner in the 1930s to treat hypertension and kidney disease and is now largely historical rather than routinely used.

rice diet.definition: An extremely low-fat, low-sodium, calorie-restricted diet developed by Dr. Walter Kempner that centers on white rice as the staple and restricts fats, proteins, and salt; traditionally used under medical supervision to treat malignant hypertension and kidney disease.

corneal opacities.definition: Partial or complete clouding of the cornea due to scarring, edema, infection, trauma, or dystrophic changes, leading to decreased visual acuity.

proliferation of corneal vessels.definition: Growth of new blood vessels from the limbal vascular plexus into the normally avascular cornea, typically in response to inflammation, hypoxia, or wound healing; can compromise corneal transparency and vision due to edema, scarring, lipid deposition, and hemorrhage.

seborrheic dermatitis around the nose mo.word: seborrheic dermatitis around the nose mouth forehead ears scrotum
seborrheic dermatitis around the nose mo.definition: Chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin condition characterized by itchy, flaky (often greasy) patches in sebum-rich areas; most commonly involves the scalp but can extend to the face around the nose and mouth (perioral/nasolabial region), forehead, and ears, and can involve the groin area including the scrotum.

trembling.definition: Involuntary, rhythmic oscillation of a body part due to alternating contraction of opposing muscles; may be physiological (e.g., cold or anxiety) or due to a neurological disorder (e.g., essential tremor, Parkinson disease).

vaginal itching.definition: Vaginal itching (vulvar pruritus) is an uncomfortable itching sensation in the vaginal or vulvar area. It is a symptom with multiple potential causes, including infections (such as candidiasis, bacterial vaginosis, or sexually transmitted infections), skin irritation or dermatitis, allergic reactions to soaps or hygiene products, hormonal changes, or diabetes.

ariboflavinosis.definition: A deficiency of riboflavin (vitamin B2) presenting with mucocutaneous symptoms such as cheilosis and angular stomatitis, glossitis, stomatitis, and ocular irritation, typically due to inadequate intake, malabsorption, or increased demand.

flavoproteins.definition: Proteins that contain a flavin nucleotide (FMN or FAD) as a prosthetic group and use it to transfer electrons in redox reactions; they participate in many metabolic pathways, such as respiration and fatty acid oxidation, with the flavin cofactors derived from riboflavin (vitamin B2).

coenzyme.definition: A small organic molecule, often made from B vitamins, that helps enzymes function in the body.

oxidative.definition: Relating to oxidation; involving the loss of electrons or gain of oxygen in chemical reactions. In biology and medicine, used to describe oxidative reactions and oxidative stress, a state in which reactive oxygen species overwhelm antioxidant defenses and cause cellular damage.

fats.definition: Fats are a class of lipids that are insoluble in water and primarily exist as triglycerides (glycerol esterified to three fatty acids). They provide a dense source of energy, are stored in adipose tissue for insulation and padding, and aid in the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K).

rnp.definition: An RNA–protein complex that forms functional cellular particles involved in RNA metabolism, including processing and translation. Autoantibodies against this complex are associated with certain autoimmune diseases such as mixed connective tissue disease.

messenger rna.definition: A type of ribonucleic acid that carries genetic information from DNA in the nucleus to ribosomes in the cytoplasm, where it serves as the template for protein synthesis during translation.

ribosomal rna.definition: A type of ribonucleic acid that is a key structural and catalytic component of ribosomes; together with ribosomal proteins it forms the ribosome and catalyzes peptide bond formation during translation of mRNA into protein.

ribosome.definition: A ribonucleoprotein complex that serves as the site of protein synthesis by translating messenger RNA into a polypeptide; composed of ribosomal RNA and proteins, organized into two subunits that assemble on mRNA during translation.

ribosome-inactivating protein.definition: A class of proteins that irreversibly inhibit protein synthesis by enzymatically removing a specific adenine base from the 28S rRNA of the ribosome, thereby inactivating ribosomes; many are plant toxins (e.g., ricin, saporin) with N-glycosidase activity.

rip.definition: A tearing or rupture of tissue or a body structure, typically resulting from trauma; the formal medical term is rupture.

ricinine.definition: A nitrogen-containing chemical found in castor bean seeds (Ricinus communis); used as a biomarker of exposure to castor beans or ricin in toxicology, and distinct from the ricin toxin.

rickett­sia.definition: A genus of small, gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacteria transmitted by arthropod vectors (ticks, fleas, lice, mites) that cause rickettsial diseases, including typhus and spotted fever groups; they invade vascular endothelium, leading to vasculitis.

rickett­siosis.definition: An infection caused by bacteria of the genus Rickettsia transmitted to humans by arthropod vectors (ticks, lice, or fleas); it typically presents with fever, headache, myalgia, and often a rash, and is treated with doxycycline.

rickett­sia prowazekii.definition: A gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacterium; the etiologic agent of epidemic typhus (louse-borne typhus), transmitted by body lice, causing fever, severe headache, and a maculopapular rash due to vasculitis.

allodermanyssus sanguineus.definition: A species of parasitic mite (arachnid) that feeds on blood; an ectoparasite belonging to the genus Allodermanyssus, typically parasitizing vertebrate hosts such as birds or mammals.

richet’s aneurysm.definition: Not a recognized term in standard medical references; no defined meaning available for "Richet’s aneurysm." If you meant a general aneurysm: a focal dilation of a blood vessel caused by weakening of the vessel wall. If you have context (location, condition, or a different spelling), I can help refine the definition.

richter’s hernia.definition: A hernia in which only a portion of the circumference of the intestinal wall is incarcerated within the hernial defect, with the rest of the bowel lumen remaining in the abdomen; it carries a high risk of strangulation and bowel necrosis despite minimal or no signs of obstruction.

parietal hernia.definition: A rare type of abdominal hernia in which contents protrude through a defect in the parietal peritoneum and the hernial sac is formed by the parietal peritoneum, often described as an interparietal hernia.

renal rickets.definition: A form of rickets caused by chronic kidney disease, in which impaired kidney function reduces production of active vitamin D and leads to phosphate retention, hypocalcemia, and secondary hyperparathyroidism, resulting in defective mineralization of growing bones.

rice.definition: A cereal grain from the genus Oryza (primarily Oryza sativa or Oryza glaberrima) cultivated as a staple food worldwide; typically eaten as polished white grain or whole-grain brown grain, and a major source of dietary energy (carbohydrates) while being gluten-free.

rib vibration.definition: A chest physiotherapy technique that applies rhythmic, oscillating vibrations to the rib cage during expiration to loosen and mobilize bronchial secretions, often used with postural drainage and coughing to clear mucus.

rib shaking.definition: Not a recognized medical term; no formal definition. If used informally, it may refer to a chest physiotherapy technique involving rhythmic vibration or tapping of the rib cage to help loosen and mobilize pulmonary secretions.

extremity.definition: The distal portion of a limb; the part farthest from the trunk, such as the hand or foot (i.e., the ends of the arms and legs).

articular.definition: Pertaining to a joint; relating to the surfaces of bones that come together to form a joint (articular surfaces) and to articular cartilage.

nonarticular.definition: Not involving or relating to a joint; occurring away from a joint.

ridaura.definition: An oral gold-containing disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) used to treat rheumatoid arthritis; it modulates immune function and reduces inflammation, but can cause GI upset, mucosal ulcers, rash, proteinuria, nephrotoxicity, and marrow suppression—requiring regular monitoring.

rider's bone.definition: A small, extra bone (ossicle) that can occur as a normal anatomical variant; typically incidental on imaging and asymptomatic, but may cause pain if it irritates surrounding tissues.

cavalry bone.definition: Not a standard medical term in widely used dictionaries; there is no formal definition. If you meant the upper portion of the skull protecting the brain, that area comprises the frontal, parietal, and occipital bones and forms the skull cap. If you had a different structure in mind, please provide more context.

rider's sprain.definition: A ligament sprain sustained during horseback riding, typically from twisting or hyperextension of a joint (often the ankle or wrist), resulting in pain, swelling, and loss of function.

gastrocnemial ridge.definition: Not a standard anatomical term; if used, it likely denotes a ridge associated with the gastrocnemius muscle, which has two heads originating from the posterior surfaces of the femoral condyles, but there is no widely recognized single structure called a “gastrocnemial ridge.”

ridge extension.definition: A surgical technique to extend or widen a bony ridge (often the jaw’s alveolar ridge) to create sufficient bone height or width for placing dental implants or providing denture support.

ridge lap.definition: A denture tooth contour used in removable dentures where the palatal/lingual portion of the tooth overlaps the residual alveolar ridge to mimic natural anatomy and aid retention.

residual ridge.definition: The portion of the alveolar ridge that remains after tooth loss, forming the denture-bearing area of the jaw and tending to resorb over time.

riedel's struma.definition: A rare chronic inflammatory thyroid disease in which fibrous tissue replaces the normal thyroid parenchyma and extends into surrounding neck structures, causing a hard, painless goiter and compressive symptoms; may lead to hypothyroidism and is often associated with IgG4-related disease.

rieder's cell leukemia.definition: No widely recognized definition for “Rieder's cell leukemia” appears in standard medical references. It may be a misspelling, an obsolete term, or a very rare/indirect usage. If you have a source, context, or alternate spelling (e.g., “Rieder cell,” a specific morphology, or a historical term), please share it and I can look up or clarify further.

rifabutin.definition: An antibiotic of the rifamycin class that inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase; used to treat and prevent Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infections, particularly in HIV-infected individuals, with notable drug interactions due to CYP450 enzyme induction.

rifadin.definition: A brand name for rifampin, a rifamycin antibiotic that inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase and is used to treat or prevent tuberculosis and other infections; it induces hepatic enzymes and can cause hepatotoxicity and orange-red discoloration of body fluids.

rifamycin.definition: A class of antibiotics that inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, blocking RNA synthesis; bactericidal against Mycobacteria and various other bacteria, and includes rifampin, rifabutin, rifapentine, and rifaximin.

rifapentine.definition: A long-acting rifamycin antibiotic used to treat active tuberculosis and to prevent latent TB infection; it inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, thereby suppressing RNA synthesis. It is commonly used in combination with other anti-tuberculosis drugs and can cause drug interactions due to potent CYP450 enzyme induction.

rifaximin.definition: An orally administered, nonabsorbable rifamycin antibiotic that acts locally in the gastrointestinal tract; it has poor systemic bioavailability and is used to treat traveler's diarrhea caused by noninvasive Escherichia coli and to reduce the recurrence of overt hepatic encephalopathy in cirrhosis.

rift valley fever.definition: Viral zoonosis transmitted by mosquitoes or contact with fluids from infected animals; it primarily affects livestock (causing abortions) and can infect humans. In people, illness ranges from a mild febrile illness to severe disease such as hemorrhagic fever, hepatitis, or encephalitis, with outbreaks linked to heavy rainfall in Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Diagnosis is by serology and RT-PCR; prevention includes vector control and livestock vaccination; treatment is supportive.

rig.definition: An antibody-containing product given after rabies exposure to provide immediate passive immunity while active immunity from vaccination develops.

riga-fede disease.definition: A chronic traumatic ulceration of the oral mucosa in infants and young children, usually on the tongue or gingiva, caused by repetitive mechanical irritation from erupting teeth or feeding; it resolves after removal of the source of trauma (e.g., smoothing or addressing sharp tooth edges or neonatal teeth).

fede's disease.definition: I can’t locate a recognized medical condition by that name. It may be a misspelling or an obscure term. If you can share the intended spelling or provide context (symptoms, affected organ, source), I can look it up or suggest a likely match. If you meant Frey’s syndrome (gustatory sweating after parotid surgery), I can define that.

right atrial catheter.definition: A central venous catheter whose tip lies in the right atrium, placed via a central vein to measure right atrial pressure and allow rapid administration of fluids or medications for hemodynamic monitoring.

right atrioventricular orifice.definition: The opening between the right atrium and right ventricle of the heart, guarded by the tricuspid valve, through which blood flows from the atrium to the ventricle.

tricuspid orifice.definition: An opening between the right atrium and right ventricle of the heart, formed by the tricuspid (right atrioventricular) valve; it permits blood flow from the atrium to the ventricle during diastole and is closed during systole to prevent backflow.

right atrioventricular valve.definition: A valve between the right atrium and right ventricle that prevents backflow from the ventricle to the atrium during systole; the tricuspid valve with three cusps (anterior, posterior, septal) attached to papillary muscles by chordae tendineae.

right common carotid artery.definition: A major artery in the right side of the neck arising from the brachiocephalic trunk; it ascends to supply the head and neck and divides at roughly the level of the upper thyroid cartilage into the internal and external carotid arteries.

right interventricular artery.definition: A branch of the right coronary artery that runs in the posterior interventricular sulcus and supplies the posterior portion of the interventricular septum and the adjacent walls of the ventricles.

right heart failure.definition: Right heart failure is the failure of the right ventricle to pump venous blood effectively into the pulmonary circulation, leading to systemic venous congestion and signs such as peripheral edema, ascites, hepatomegaly, and jugular venous distension; it commonly results from left-sided heart failure, chronic lung disease with pulmonary hypertension, or primary right ventricular dysfunction.

right hepatic duct.definition: An intrahepatic bile duct that drains bile from the right lobe of the liver; it typically results from the union of the right anterior and right posterior sectoral ducts and joins the left hepatic duct to form the common hepatic duct.

right liver.definition: The larger of the liver's two anatomical lobes, located in the right upper quadrant; separated from the left lobe by the falciform ligament and porta hepatis; constitutes the majority of hepatic mass and participates in metabolic, synthetic, and detoxification functions.

right part of liver.definition: One of the liver’s two major anatomical lobes; the larger lobe occupying most of the right upper quadrant, separated from the left lobe by Cantlie’s line on the visceral surface; it is supplied by the right hepatic artery and right portal vein and drained by the right hepatic veins.

hepatic artery proper.definition: The main arterial supply to the liver; a continuation of the common hepatic artery after the gastroduodenal artery branches off, it runs in the hepatoduodenal ligament to the porta hepatis and divides into the right and left hepatic arteries to supply the liver (the cystic artery often arises from the right hepatic artery).

right umbilical vein.definition: An embryologic blood vessel, one of the two umbilical veins that carry oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus; in normal development it regresses and disappears, with the left umbilical vein becoming the functional vessel—but persistence of the right umbilical vein is a rare vascular anomaly.

sinus venosus.definition: A transient venous reservoir in the developing heart that receives systemic venous blood (from the common cardinal, vitelline, and umbilical veins); as development proceeds, it is incorporated into the right atrium to form its smooth posterior wall (the sinus venarum).

vertebral vein.definition: A paired vein that drains the cervical spinal cord, posterior scalp, and neck, running alongside the vertebral artery through the transverse foramina and emptying into the brachiocephalic (or subclavian) venous system; part of the vertebral venous system including the internal vertebral venous plexus.

inferior thyroid vein.definition: A vein draining the inferior portion of the thyroid gland and nearby structures, typically emptying into the left brachiocephalic vein (occasionally into the right brachiocephalic vein).

internal thoracic arteries.definition: Arteries arising from the subclavian arteries that descend on the inner chest wall, giving off perforating branches to the sternum and anterior intercostal arteries; they continue as the superior epigastric arteries and supply the anterior chest wall and breasts, and are commonly used as conduits in coronary artery bypass grafting.

lymphatic trunks.definition: Large lymphatic vessels that drain lymph from large body regions and convey it into the venous system, usually via the thoracic duct or the right lymphatic duct.

legionella pneumonia.definition: A pneumonia caused by Legionella bacteria (most commonly Legionella pneumophila), usually acquired by inhaling contaminated water aerosols (e.g., from showers or cooling towers); characteristically presents with fever, cough, dyspnea, gastrointestinal symptoms, and hyponatremia; diagnosed by urinary antigen testing or culture and treated with macrolides or fluoroquinolones.

hemophilus influenzae.definition: A small, Gram-negative coccobacillus that colonizes the human nasopharynx; a fastidious organism requiring heme (X factor) and NAD (V factor) for growth, and it can cause invasive diseases such as meningitis and epiglottitis as well as mucosal infections like pneumonia and otitis media; the encapsulated type b (Hib) historically caused severe disease in children before vaccination, which has greatly reduced Hib incidence, while non-typable strains lack a capsule and are commonly linked to mucosal infections.

traveler's diarrhea.definition: A diarrheal illness acquired during travel, usually after ingestion of contaminated food or water, defined as three or more loose stools in 24 hours; most cases are self-limited within a few days and commonly caused by enteric pathogens (most often enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli).

streptomyces mediterranei.definition: A soil-dwelling, aerobic, Gram-positive, filamentous actinobacterium that produces rifamycin antibiotics; historically placed in Streptomyces but reclassified to the genus Amycolatopsis.

arthrosis.definition: A degenerative joint disease characterized by deterioration of articular cartilage and secondary bone changes, commonly equated with osteoarthritis.

ast.definition: A liver enzyme measured in blood tests as a marker of hepatocellular injury; elevations indicate liver cell damage and are interpreted alongside other enzymes and clinical factors.

urinary casts.definition: Cylindrical aggregates produced by the renal tubules from Tamm-Horsfall protein that are excreted in urine and observed on microscopy, reflecting tubular or glomerular kidney disease; they include subtypes such as hyaline, granular, red blood cell, white blood cell, epithelial, fatty, and waxy casts.

loss of taste.definition: A diminished or absent sense of taste (gustation), ranging from hypogeusia to ageusia, caused by dysfunction of taste buds or gustatory nerves (e.g., chorda tympani, glossopharyngeal) or central taste pathways; may be temporary or permanent and result from infections, medications, zinc deficiency, smoking, radiation, or neurologic disease.

vision loss.definition: Partial or complete inability to see in one or both eyes, resulting from dysfunction of the eye itself (e.g., retina, lens), the optic nerve, or the brain's visual pathways; it can be temporary or permanent and may be unilateral (one eye) or bilateral (both eyes).

bunyavirus.definition: An enveloped virus of the order Bunyavirales, characterized by a segmented, negative-sense RNA genome; many are transmitted by arthropods or rodents and include hantaviruses, nairoviruses, phenuviruses, and orthobunyaviruses.

rif.definition: An anatomical region in the lower right quadrant of the abdomen, often evaluated for pain suggestive of appendicitis.

rigor mortis.definition: A postmortem stiffening of skeletal muscles caused by depletion of ATP, leading to actin–myosin cross-bridges remaining formed; it begins a few hours after death, typically reaches maximal stiffness around 12 hours, and dissipates over the next 24–48 hours as decomposition progresses.

riluzole.definition: A prescription medication used to slow the progression of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in adults; it reduces glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity by inhibiting presynaptic glutamate release through blockade of voltage-gated sodium channels, modestly prolonging survival.

decreased lung function.definition: Reduced ability of the lungs to ventilate and exchange gases, often demonstrated by lower spirometry values (e.g., decreased FEV1 and FVC) and/or reduced diffusion capacity, which can result from obstructive or restrictive lung disease, aging, or respiratory muscle weakness.

postural hypertension.definition: Standing-induced increase in blood pressure: a rise in blood pressure when moving from a lying or sitting to an upright position, often defined as an increase in systolic BP of ≥20 mmHg or diastolic BP ≥10 mmHg within several minutes of standing; may result from autonomic dysfunction, medications, or underlying conditions such as pheochromocytoma or hypertension.

rima glottidis.definition: The opening between the true vocal cords (vocal folds) within the larynx; bounded anteriorly by the vocal folds and posteriorly by the arytenoid cartilages; it widens with abduction (breathing) and narrows with adduction (phonation).

rima respitoria.definition: An opening in the larynx between the true vocal cords through which air passes during breathing; its size varies with respiration and is modulated by laryngeal muscles.

rimexolone.definition: A synthetic ophthalmic corticosteroid used topically to reduce inflammation and pain after eye surgery (e.g., cataract surgery).

rimose.definition: Characterized by fissures or cracks on the surface, especially in the skin or mucous membranes (e.g., dry, cracked lips).

rimso-50.definition: An iodinated radiopaque contrast agent used to enhance visualization of body structures during radiologic imaging (e.g., X-ray and CT).

dimethyl sulfoxide.definition: A colorless, highly polar, hygroscopic organic solvent with the formula (CH3)2SO; used as a solvent in pharmaceuticals and as a topical anti-inflammatory/analgesic and cryoprotectant; readily penetrates the skin and can cause irritation and, with excessive exposure, systemic toxicity.

rimula.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard dictionaries; there is no established medical definition for it and it may be a misspelling or an extremely obscure term. If you can provide context or a different spelling, I can help refine the definition.

ring-down artifact.definition: An ultrasound artifact caused by resonance of gas bubbles in a fluid, producing a bright, continuous line of echoes extending distally from a strong reflector (a reverberation/comet-tail type artifact).

ring-down time.definition: The duration after an ultrasound pulse during which a ring-down artifact—a persistent, decaying ultrasound signal produced by resonant gas bodies or microbubbles in tissue—remains observable.

ringed sideroblast.definition: An erythroblast in which iron-loaded mitochondria surround the nucleus to form a ring, visible with Prussian blue stain; indicative of defective heme synthesis and sideroblastic anemia or related myelodysplastic syndromes.

rivus lacrimalis.definition: A groove or fissure on the medial wall of the orbit associated with the lacrimal apparatus, typically forming the passage for the lacrimal sac and nasolacrimal duct.

extracellular volume.definition: The extracellular volume is the portion of body water located outside cells, comprising interstitial fluid and intravascular plasma (plasma volume), and excluding intracellular fluid; in a typical adult it is about 14–15 liters (roughly 20% of body weight).

sodium excess.definition: An electrolyte disturbance characterized by a serum sodium concentration above normal (usually >145 mEq/L), caused by water loss or excess sodium intake relative to water, leading to cellular dehydration and symptoms such as thirst, confusion, and in severe cases seizures.

rinne tuning fork test.definition: A bedside hearing test that uses a tuning fork to compare air conduction with bone conduction, helping distinguish conductive from sensorineural hearing loss.

riopan.definition: An over-the-counter antacid used to relieve heartburn and indigestion by neutralizing stomach acid; formulations typically contain aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide.

simethicone.definition: An anti-foaming agent that decreases the surface tension of gas bubbles in the gastrointestinal tract, causing them to coalesce and be expelled; used to relieve bloating, flatulence, and abdominal discomfort; not absorbed from the GI tract.

ritual circumcision.definition: Circumcision performed for religious or cultural reasons; a procedure to remove all or part of the foreskin of the penis as part of a ceremonial rite, typically carried out in infancy or childhood and not indicated by a medical condition.

female genital mutilation.definition: Any procedure that involves the partial or total removal of the external female genitalia or other injury to the female genital organs for non-medical reasons; a harmful cultural practice with no medical benefit and potential for serious health consequences.

rituximab.definition: A chimeric monoclonal antibody that binds CD20 on B lymphocytes, leading to B-cell depletion; used to treat certain B-cell malignancies (e.g., non-Hodgkin lymphoma, chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and some autoimmune diseases (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis).

murine proteins.definition: Proteins derived from mice (Mus musculus); proteins of mouse origin used in biomedical research as models of mammalian biology and disease, or as mouse-derived reagents (for example, murine monoclonal antibodies).

risus caninus.definition: A dog-like, fixed grimace due to sustained contraction of facial muscles (notably the zygomaticus and risorius), producing a "dog-smile" appearance and historically described in tetanus.

risus sardonicus.definition: A sustained, involuntary spasm of facial muscles that yields a fixed, sardonic grin; a classic clinical sign of severe tetanus.

ritalin.definition: A central nervous system stimulant medication containing methylphenidate, used to treat ADHD and narcolepsy. It increases dopamine and norepinephrine in the brain by blocking their reuptake, improving attention and reducing impulsivity and hyperactivity.

methylphenidate.definition: A central nervous system stimulant used to treat ADHD and narcolepsy; it increases dopamine and norepinephrine in the brain by blocking their reuptake, improving attention and reducing impulsivity. It is a Schedule II controlled substance with potential for dependence and cardiovascular side effects.

rizatriptan.definition: A selective serotonin 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonist (a triptan) used for the acute treatment of migraine. It causes cranial vasoconstriction and inhibits release of pro-inflammatory neuropeptides; available as an oral tablet or rapidly dissolving tablet.

ritodrine.definition: A beta-adrenergic agonist (beta-2 selective) used as a tocolytic to suppress preterm uterine contractions by relaxing the uterine smooth muscle through increased cyclic AMP.

risedronate.definition: A nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate used to treat and prevent osteoporosis and Paget disease by inhibiting osteoclast-mediated bone resorption through blockade of farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase; administered orally with water, and patients should remain upright for at least 30 minutes to reduce esophageal irritation.

biphosphonates.definition: A class of antiresorptive medications that inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, thereby increasing bone density and reducing fracture risk in osteoporosis and other metabolic bone diseases.

basilar migraine.definition: A migraine with brainstem aura: a migraine in which the aura symptoms arise from the brainstem or basilar artery territory, typically including vertigo, ataxia, dysarthria, bilateral sensory symptoms, or impaired consciousness, usually followed by a headache.

hemiplegic migraine.definition: A rare genetic form of migraine with aura in which the aura includes reversible unilateral weakness on one side of the body, often with sensory or speech disturbances; attacks may be familial and can mimic stroke.

chest tightness.definition: A subjective sensation of pressure, fullness, squeezing, or constriction in the chest; a non-specific symptom that can result from cardiac, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, musculoskeletal conditions, or anxiety.

chest pressure.definition: A subjective sensation of pressure, tightness, or squeezing in the chest; may reflect cardiac causes (e.g., ischemia or myocardial infarction) or noncardiac causes (esophageal, musculoskeletal, pulmonary conditions, or anxiety) and warrants urgent evaluation if associated with chest pain, shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, or fainting.

right lower extremity.definition: The right lower extremity is the right lower limb of the body, extending from the hip to the foot and comprising the thigh, leg, ankle, and foot.

right lower lobe of lung.definition: The right lower lobe is the inferior portion of the right lung, separated from the middle lobe by the oblique fissure; it contains five bronchopulmonary segments—the superior segment and the four basal segments (anterior basal, medial basal, lateral basal, posterior basal)—and participates in gas exchange.

right lower quadrant.definition: An anatomical region of the abdomen bounded by the midline and a vertical plane through the umbilicus, and by a horizontal plane through the umbilicus; the right lower quadrant contains the cecum and appendix, portions of the ileum and ascending colon, the right ureter, and (in females) the right ovary and fallopian tube (in males) the right testis/epididymis.

rmsf.definition: A tick-borne rickettsial illness caused by Rickettsia rickettsii, transmitted by Dermacentor ticks; presents with abrupt fever, severe headache, myalgias, and often a maculopapular/petechial rash that may involve the wrists, ankles, palms, and soles; can be severe or fatal if not treated promptly with doxycycline.

right mentoposterior fetal position.definition: A fetal presentation in which the presenting part is the fetal chin (mentum) with the mentum directed toward the mother's right posterior pelvis.

right mentotransverse fetal position.definition: An obstetric presentation in which the chin (mentum) is the presenting part in a transverse lie, with the presenting part directed toward the mother’s right side.

right occipitoanterior fetal position.definition: A cephalic (head-down) fetal position in which the occiput (back of the head) is directed toward the mother's right side and toward the front of the pelvis (anterior); commonly abbreviated ROA.

roa.definition: The method by which a drug or substance is administered and enters the body, influencing absorption and onset of action; examples include oral, intravenous, intramuscular, subcutaneous, inhalational, nasal, topical, and transdermal routes.

rocuronium.definition: Aminosteroid, nondepolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent used to facilitate tracheal intubation and provide skeletal muscle relaxation during anesthesia; it competitively inhibits nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, with rapid onset and intermediate duration (reversed by sugammadex or acetylcholinesterase inhibitors).

rocuronium bromide.definition: A nondepolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent used during anesthesia to induce skeletal muscle relaxation and facilitate tracheal intubation; it competitively antagonizes nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction.

robaxin.definition: An oral, central nervous system–acting skeletal muscle relaxant (methocarbamol) used to relieve acute musculoskeletal muscle spasms and associated pain; typically prescribed short term, often with rest and physical therapy. Common side effects include drowsiness, dizziness, and nausea; caution advised with alcohol and while operating heavy machinery.

robitussin.definition: An over-the-counter cough syrup formulation typically containing dextromethorphan (a cough suppressant) and sometimes guaifenesin (an expectorant); used to reduce coughing and help loosen mucus.

robinul.definition: A brand name for glycopyrrolate, an antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) medication used to reduce secretions (saliva and respiratory/gastric secretions) and to prevent reflex bradycardia during anesthesia; also used to treat excessive drooling and, in some settings, to reduce sweating.

rocaltrol.definition: A brand-name preparation of calcitriol (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3), the active form of vitamin D; used to treat hypocalcemia in hypoparathyroidism or chronic kidney disease and to manage secondary hyperparathyroidism; increases intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate and suppresses parathyroid hormone.

rocephin.definition: A broad-spectrum third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic (ceftriaxone) used to treat a variety of serious bacterial infections, including meningitis, pneumonia, gonorrhea, septicemia, intra‑abdominal infections, biliary tract infections, and skin/soft tissue infections; it inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin‑binding proteins and is administered intramuscularly or intravenously.

romano-ward syndrome.definition: A form of congenital long QT syndrome characterized by a prolonged QT interval on electrocardiography, predisposing to torsades de pointes and sudden cardiac death; inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern and typically without sensorineural deafness.

romberg sign.definition: A bedside sign of proprioception: the patient stands with feet together, arms at the sides, eyes closed; if they sway or lose balance, the Romberg sign is positive, indicating impaired dorsal column–mediated proprioception (sensory ataxia) and reliance on vision for balance.

romberg test.definition: An examination to assess proprioception and dorsal column function: the patient stands with feet together and eyes closed; a positive sign—unsteady balance or collapse with eyes closed—suggests proprioceptive or dorsal column (sensory) dysfunction, such as sensory ataxia.

rondec-dm.definition: A brand-name combination cough syrup whose DM denotes the presence of dextromethorphan, a central cough suppressant; it is typically combined with another agent (often a decongestant or antihistamine) to relieve cough with nasal congestion.

robertsonian translocation.definition: A chromosomal rearrangement in which the long arms of two acrocentric chromosomes fuse at the centromere to form a single chromosome, with loss of the short arms, resulting in a reduced chromosome number (usually 45); carriers are typically phenotypically normal but may produce unbalanced gametes leading to miscarriages or chromosomal disorders such as Down syndrome when chromosome 21 is involved.

roberts' syndrome.definition: A rare autosomal recessive congenital disorder characterized by symmetric limb reduction defects (often severe), craniofacial anomalies, microcephaly, and growth retardation, caused by biallelic ESCO2 mutations that disrupt sister chromatid cohesion during cell division.

rolando fissure.definition: A deep groove in the brain's cerebral cortex, also known as the central sulcus, that separates the precentral gyrus (motor cortex) from the postcentral gyrus (somatosensory cortex) and marks the boundary between the frontal and parietal lobes.

rolando fracture.definition: A comminuted intra-articular fracture at the base of the thumb’s first metacarpal involving the carpometacarpal joint, with multiple fragments often forming a Y- or beak-shaped pattern and commonly causing thumb instability.

substantia gelatinosa.definition: A gelatinous region of the dorsal horn of the spinal cord (Rexed lamina II) consisting of interneurons that modulate nociceptive transmission and participate in the gate control of pain; receives afferent input from C fibers and Aδ fibers.

rolando's gelatinous substance.definition: A gelatinous layer of gray matter in the dorsal horn of the spinal cord (Lamina II) consisting of interneurons that modulate nociceptive (pain) signals from peripheral nerves, contributing to the spinal gating of pain.

first metacarpal.definition: A long bone of the thumb; the first metacarpal forms the proximal part of the thumb and the first ray of the hand, articulating proximally with the trapezium (carpometacarpal joint) and distally with the proximal phalanx (metacarpophalangeal joint).

ropivacaine.definition: A long-acting amide local anesthetic used for regional anesthesia and postoperative analgesia; the pure S-enantiomer of propivacaine, with less cardiotoxicity and motor blockade than bupivacaine, administered by epidural, spinal, peripheral nerve blocks, or local infiltration.

root_canal_therapy.definition: A dental procedure to treat infection or inflammation of the tooth pulp by removing the infected pulp, cleaning and shaping the root canal system, disinfecting it, and filling and sealing the space to prevent reinfection, with the goal of saving the natural tooth.

gutta_percha.definition: A thermoplastic natural polymer obtained from the latex of the sapodilla tree, used in dentistry as a root canal obturation material to fill and seal prepared root canals, typically after mixing with a sealer and sometimes made radiopaque with additives.

sealer.definition: A material applied to a tissue surface or wound to form a seal and prevent the passage of fluids or air, often aiding hemostasis or wound closure; used as surgical sealants and dental/endodontic sealers.

obturation.definition: The process of filling and sealing a cavity or canal to prevent leakage and reinfection; in dentistry, the final filling of a cleaned root canal with material (e.g., gutta-percha and sealer) to seal the canal.

canal_obturation.definition: The process of filling and sealing a root canal system after cleaning and shaping, usually with gutta-percha and an endodontic sealer, to prevent leakage and reinfection.

root_curettage.definition: Removal of diseased soft tissue (granulation tissue) from the periodontal pocket along the tooth root, typically with curettes, to debride the root surface and promote healing.

root_planing.definition: A dental procedure in which plaque, calculus, and bacterial toxins are removed from exposed tooth roots and the root surface is smoothed (planed) to promote reattachment of the gingiva and reduce periodontal inflammation; typically performed under local anesthesia as part of scaling and root planing.

subgingival_curettage.definition: A periodontal debridement procedure in which the soft tissue lining and granulation tissue within a periodontal pocket beneath the gingival margin are scraped away to reduce pocket depth and promote healing, typically performed with curettes and often combined with scaling and root planing.

periodontal_disease.definition: When your gums are red and swollen. Also called gum disease. There are 2 types: gingivitis and periodontitis.

radicular_cyst.definition: An inflammatory periapical cyst at the apex of a nonvital tooth, arising from proliferation of epithelial rests of Malassez in the periodontal ligament in response to pulpal necrosis; typically radiolucent on imaging and treated with root canal therapy or extraction.

gingival_tissues.definition: These mucosal tissues surround and cover the teeth, comprising the marginal and attached areas; they are made of keratinized stratified squamous epithelium over a connective tissue layer and form a protective seal around teeth, contributing to periodontal stability.

intraradicular_resorption.definition: Resorption of dentin from within the root canal/pulp space, typically caused by inflammatory/clastic activity in a vital pulp; radiographs show enlargement of the canal, and treatment is endodontic therapy to remove the resorptive tissue and halt progression.

rose_fever.definition: Not a standard medical term with a fixed definition. It may be used informally to describe a fever with a rose-colored rash, most often referring to either roseola infantum (a febrile illness in infants caused by HHV-6/7 followed by a rose-pink rash) or pityriasis rosea (a self-limited skin eruption with a herald patch and a pink-to-salmon, scaly rash). If you have a specific context or age group, I can refine the definition.

rose_hips.definition: The fruit of the rose plant (especially Rosa canina), rich in vitamin C and antioxidants, used in dietary supplements and traditional herbal remedies.

rosin.definition: Rosin (colophony) is a solid resin obtained from pine trees; it is used in adhesives, varnishes, and fluxes, and is a common contact allergen that can trigger dermatitis in sensitive individuals.

rosette_technique.definition: No widely recognized medical technique by that exact name. If you meant a histologic pattern, a rosette refers to a circular, flower-like arrangement of tumor or glandular cells around a central lumen or space. Rosette formations are seen in certain tumors, such as Homer-Wright rosettes (neuroblastoma, some CNS tumors) and Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes (retinoblastoma). If you can share the specialty or context, I can tailor the definition further.

rostellum.definition: A knob-like, retractable projection at the anterior end of the scolex (head) of certain cestodes (tapeworms) bearing hooks; it functions to attach the worm to the host's intestinal mucosa.

rostral.definition: Toward the nose or anterior end; in anatomical terms, the front of the head or brain, opposite of caudal.

rostrum.definition: An elongated, beaklike projection; the forward, snoutlike extension of the head or another organ in various animals.

rostrad.definition: Toward the rostrum (the snout or anterior end of the body); toward the front.

rotavirus_vaccine.definition: An oral, live attenuated vaccine to prevent rotavirus gastroenteritis in infants and young children; given in early infancy in 2 doses (Rotarix) or 3 doses (RotaTeq), typically around 2 and 4 months (Rotarix) or 2, 4, and 6 months (RotaTeq).

rotating_tourniquet.definition: A device used to occlude arterial blood flow to a limb by applying circumferential pressure, featuring a rotating or swiveling cuff that allows the pressure band to be adjusted or rotated around the limb without removing the tourniquet.

rotator_cuff.definition: A group of tendons and muscles used to raise the arm from the side and rotating the shoulder.

coracoid.definition: A hook-shaped bony projection from the scapula at its anterior superior border that serves as an attachment for the pectoralis minor, the short head of biceps brachii, and the coracobrachialis, as well as for ligaments such as the coracoacromial and coracoclavicular ligaments.

greater_tubercle.definition: A large bony prominence on the proximal humerus, located laterally to the head; serves as the attachment site for the rotator cuff tendons (supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and teres minor) and forms part of the shoulder joint.

lesser_tubercle.definition: A small bony prominence on the proximal humerus, on the anterior surface, that serves as the insertion site for the subscapularis tendon.

intertubercular_groove.definition: An anterior groove on the proximal humerus between the greater and lesser tubercles that transmits the tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii; the roof is the transverse humeral ligament, the lateral lip is where the pectoralis major attaches, and the medial lip serves as the attachment for the teres major (and latissimus dorsi).

teres_minor.definition: A small, narrow rotator cuff muscle that originates from the lateral border of the scapula and inserts on the inferior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus; it laterally rotates the arm and helps stabilize the glenohumeral joint. Innervated by the axillary nerve (C5–C6).

rosenmullers_organ.definition: Not a standard medical term; appears to be a nonstandard name or misspelling with no defined anatomical structure in reputable references.

rosenberg_chutorian_syndrome.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. If you have an alternative spelling, related term, or a specific clinical context (e.g., ENT, craniofacial), I can try again or provide information on related conditions.

optic_atrophy.definition: Optic atrophy is the degeneration or death of optic nerve fibers, resulting in pallor of the optic disc and progressive, usually irreversible vision loss (reduced visual acuity, visual field defects, and color vision impairment) due to damage to the optic nerve from various causes (ischemia, inflammation, compression, glaucoma, hereditary neuropathies, etc.).

sensorineural_hearing_loss.definition: Permanent hearing loss caused by damage to the cochlea, hair cells, or auditory nerve.

roseola.definition: A viral illness of early childhood due to human herpesvirus 6 (and sometimes 7), characterized by abrupt high fever for about 3–5 days followed by a diffuse rose-pink maculopapular rash as the fever subsides; usually self-limited. Also known as exanthem subitum or the sixth disease.

roseola_infantum.definition: A common viral illness of early childhood caused by human herpesvirus 6 (and sometimes HHV-7); characterized by a sudden high fever for about 3–5 days, followed by a pink maculopapular rash that begins on the trunk and spreads to the face and limbs as the fever subsides, and is typically self-limited within about a week.

exanthema_subitum.definition: A viral illness of infancy and early childhood characterized by a high fever for several days that breaks with the appearance of a diffuse, blanching maculopapular rash; caused by human herpesvirus 6 (often with HHV-7) and typically resolves without complication.

sixth_disease.definition: A common pediatric viral illness caused by human herpesvirus 6 (and sometimes HHV-7), characterized by a sudden high fever for several days that is followed by a pink maculopapular rash as the fever subsides; most common in children under 2 years old.

zahorsky_disease.definition: Not a recognized medical condition in standard medical references; the term may be misspelled or used informally. If you can provide context, symptoms, or the correct spelling, I can help define it.

rotavirus_vaccine_live_oral.definition: An orally administered vaccine containing live attenuated rotavirus strains, used to prevent rotavirus gastroenteritis in infants and young children; given in a multi-dose schedule according to the product (commonly started at about 6 weeks of age).

rosuvastatin.definition: A statin (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor) used to lower LDL cholesterol and triglycerides and reduce cardiovascular risk by decreasing hepatic cholesterol synthesis and increasing LDL receptor activity.

type_2_diabetes_mellitus.definition: Chronic metabolic disorder characterized by hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with relative insulin deficiency, most often associated with obesity; managed with lifestyle changes and glucose-lowering medications.

mixed_dyslipidemia.definition: A pattern of dyslipidemia in which both triglycerides and cholesterol (typically LDL-C) are elevated, often with reduced HDL-C; commonly referred to as combined or mixed hyperlipidemia, and frequently seen with insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome.

low_density_lipoprotein_receptor_disorde.definition: Genetic disorder arising from defective or deficient low-density lipoprotein receptors on hepatocytes, leading to reduced hepatic clearance of LDL particles, elevated plasma LDL cholesterol, and increased risk of premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Most commonly due to mutations in the LDLR gene (familial hypercholesterolemia).

homozygous_low_density_lipoprotein_recep.definition: A severe genetic form of familial hypercholesterolemia caused by pathogenic variants in the LDL receptor gene leading to little or no LDL receptor activity, resulting in very high LDL cholesterol from birth and early, aggressive atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (often with xanthomas and corneal arcus in childhood).

liver_disease.definition: A broad term for disorders that impair hepatic structure or function, including viral hepatitis, cirrhosis, fatty liver disease, biliary tract disorders, and liver failure.

hemolytic_anemia.definition: A form of anemia due to accelerated destruction of red blood cells (hemolysis) that outpaces the bone marrow's ability to replace them; can be inherited or acquired, often with reticulocytosis and elevated indirect bilirubin.

loss_of_consciousness.definition: A transient, reversible loss of consciousness and wakefulness, typically lasting seconds to minutes, often due to temporary cerebral hypoperfusion (syncope) but can result from seizures, metabolic disturbances, or intoxication.

myocardial_depression.definition: A reduction in the heart muscle's contractile function leading to decreased cardiac output, typically due to ischemia or injury, toxins, or metabolic disturbances.

cardiac_arrest.definition: The sudden cessation of heart contractions capable of circulating blood to the body and brain. It typically arises from a rapid ventricular rhythm (ventricular tachycardia) or a chaotic rhythm (ventricular fibrillation). Without prompt cardiopulmonary resuscitation and defibrillation, death occurs within minutes.

fetal_bradycardia.definition: A persistent fetal heart rate below 110 beats per minute for at least 10 minutes, indicating possible fetal distress or underlying pathology and requiring urgent obstetric evaluation.

status_asthmaticus.definition: A severe, life-threatening asthma attack that does not respond to standard treatment and requires urgent medical intervention, often hospitalization and possible airway support.

respiratory_arrest.definition: The cessation of breathing or the complete inability to perform adequate ventilation, resulting in inadequate oxygen intake and carbon dioxide removal. It can result from airway obstruction, central nervous system depression, or neuromuscular impairment and requires immediate emergency resuscitation.

blurred_vision.definition: Blurred vision is a symptom in which the visual image is out of sharp focus, causing objects to appear hazy or indistinct. It can result from uncorrected refractive errors (nearsightedness, farsightedness, astigmatism), dry eye, or cataracts, and may also reflect retinal or optic nerve disease or systemic conditions; urgent evaluation is needed for sudden vision loss, eye pain, or neurologic symptoms.

pupil_constriction.definition: Contraction of the iris sphincter (sphincter pupillae) causing pupil constriction (miosis); a parasympathetic response to bright light or near focus.

urinary_frequency.definition: Routinely needing to urinate more than eight times during the day or more than twice at night.

dry_mouth.definition: A subjective feeling of oral dryness due to reduced saliva production, which can impair speaking, eating, and swallowing and increase the risk of dental caries and oral infections; commonly caused by dehydration, medications, mouth breathing, diabetes, Sjögren syndrome, or radiation therapy to the head and neck.

rorschach_test.definition: A projective psychological test in which a person describes or interprets ambiguous inkblot images; used to assess personality structure and emotional functioning, though its reliability and validity are widely debated.

inkblot_technique.definition: A projective psychological test in which an individual is shown ambiguous inkblot images and asked to describe what they see; the content of their responses is interpreted to infer aspects of personality, thought processes, and potential psychopathology.

juvenile cataracts.definition: An opacification of the crystalline lens that develops in childhood or adolescence (congenital or early-onset), which can impair visual development and may require surgical removal; it may be isolated or associated with systemic or ocular disorders.

roths spots.definition: A retinal hemorrhage with a pale, white center due to microinfarction of the retinal nerve fiber layer with a fibrin-platelet clot; classically seen in subacute bacterial endocarditis but may also occur with anemia, leukemia, diabetes, and hypertensive retinopathy.

rotigotine.definition: A non-ergoline dopamine receptor agonist used to treat Parkinson disease and restless legs syndrome; administered as a transdermal patch delivering continuous dopaminergic stimulation.

ramelteon.definition: A synthetic melatonin receptor agonist with high affinity for MT1 and MT2 receptors, used to treat insomnia characterized by difficulty with sleep onset.

rovsings sign.definition: A sign of acute appendicitis in which palpation of the left lower quadrant elicits pain in the right lower quadrant due to peritoneal irritation near the appendix.

rubella antibody test.definition: A blood test that detects rubella-specific antibodies to assess immunity or recent infection; IgG indicates immunity from past infection or vaccination, while IgM indicates a recent or current infection. Usually performed by ELISA or other immunoassay methods and used to evaluate vaccination status and pregnancy-related risk.

round ligament.definition: A fibromuscular cord from the uterine horn to the labia majora via the inguinal canal; a remnant of the fetal gubernaculum that helps secure the uterus in its anteverted position.

fenestra cochlea.definition: A membrane-covered opening in the cochlear wall that connects the scala tympani to the middle ear and permits displacement of perilymph to accommodate pressure changes during sound transmission.

fenestra rotunda.definition: A circular, membrane-covered opening between the middle ear and the cochlea that allows perilymph movement in the inner ear when the oval window is displaced by the stapes.

labium majora.definition: One of the two outer, elongated folds of skin and adipose tissue of the vulva that enclose and protect the openings of the vagina and urethra; contain hair follicles and sebaceous glands and are homologous to the male scrotum.

round foramen.definition: A circular opening in the greater wing of the sphenoid bone in the middle cranial fossa through which the maxillary nerve (V2) exits the skull to enter the pterygopalatine fossa.

head of femur.definition: The rounded proximal end of the thigh bone that articulates with the acetabulum of the pelvis to form the hip joint; it is covered with articular cartilage and continuous with the femoral neck.

antibody test.definition: A serology test that detects antibodies in the blood to determine whether a person has been exposed to a specific pathogen or vaccine-induced immunity; IgM may indicate recent infection and IgG longer-term immunity.

rubeosis.definition: Neovascularization of the iris (rubeosis iridis): abnormal growth of new, fragile blood vessels on the iris, usually in response to retinal ischemia from conditions such as diabetic retinopathy or retinal vein occlusion, which can progress to neovascular glaucoma.

rubeosis iridis.definition: Growth of new, abnormal blood vessels on the anterior surface of the iris due to retinal ischemia, most commonly from diabetic retinopathy or retinal vein occlusion; it can progress to neovascular (secondary) glaucoma.

neovascular glaucoma.definition: A secondary form of glaucoma caused by neovascularization of the iris (rubeosis iridis) and the anterior chamber angle, typically from retinal ischemia (e.g., diabetic retinopathy, central retinal vein occlusion), leading to obstruction of aqueous outflow and elevated intraocular pressure.

antineoplastic antibiotics.definition: Antineoplastic antibiotics are cancer chemotherapy agents derived from bacteria (notably Streptomyces) that kill or inhibit tumor cells by damaging DNA or disrupting DNA replication/interactions. They include drugs such as doxorubicin, daunorubicin, bleomycin, mitomycin C, and actinomycin D, and often cause toxicities like myelosuppression.

rubidium.definition: A chemical element (Rb, atomic number 37); a soft, highly reactive alkali metal not known to be essential in human nutrition, used in medical imaging research (notably rubidium-82 in PET).

rubinstein-taybi syndrome.definition: A rare autosomal dominant congenital disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the CREBBP (CBP) or EP300 genes, usually de novo, characterized by distinctive facial features (broad, beaked nose; downslanting palpebral fissures; high or thick eyebrows), broad thumbs and toes, short stature, and variable intellectual disability with developmental delay; commonly associated with dental anomalies and a range of congenital malformations including heart defects.

broad thumbs.definition: An abnormally wide first digit (thumb) due to enlargement of the soft tissues or skeletal elements, giving a broader appearance at the base; may be an isolated variant or part of a congenital syndrome.

great toes.definition: The great toe, also called the hallux, is the first and largest toe of the foot, typically with two phalanges, and it plays a key role in weight bearing and push-off during gait.

high-arched palate.definition: A tall, narrow palate with a vaulted (Gothic) shape; the maxillary arch is relatively constricted, giving the roof of the mouth an elevated, arched contour.

beaked nose.definition: A nose with a prominent, curved, beak-like profile—typically a long, hooked or convex nasal dorsum with a projecting tip, giving a bird-beak appearance.

eye abnormalities.definition: An umbrella term for any structural or functional abnormality of the eye or its adnexa that impairs vision or eye function; may be congenital or acquired and can involve any ocular tissue or surrounding structures.

keloid formation.definition: An abnormal scar formed by excessive, disorganized collagen deposition during wound healing, producing a raised, firm scar that extends beyond the original wound, often itchy or tender and unlikely to regress; may recur after treatment.

fallopian tubes patency.definition: The openness of the Fallopian tubes; a patent tube is unobstructed, allowing passage of ova from the ovary to the uterus and sperm to reach the ovum. Patency is assessed in infertility workups, commonly via imaging or dye tests (e.g., hysterosalpingography, hysterosalpingo-contrast sonography, or chromopertubation).

manometer.definition: An instrument for measuring pressure, typically a U-shaped tube containing liquid (such as mercury or water) that moves with pressure, or a device with a pressure sensor that provides a readout.

tubal peristalsis.definition: Rhythmic contractions of the smooth muscle in the fallopian (uterine) tube that propel the ovum (and later the embryo) toward the uterus, aided by ciliary action.

tubal spasm.definition: A transient contraction of the smooth muscle in a fallopian tube, causing temporary narrowing or obstruction that can mimic tubal blockage during imaging or evaluation.

partial obstruction.definition: Blockage that narrows but does not completely block the lumen of a hollow organ (commonly the gastrointestinal tract), allowing some passage of gas or contents; symptoms are typically milder and intermittent compared with a complete obstruction and may progress to complete obstruction if untreated.

rupture of membranes.definition: Tearing of the amniotic sac surrounding the fetus, resulting in leakage of amniotic fluid; it can occur before labor or during labor and may increase the risk of infection or cord prolapse if prolonged.

ruptured hymen.definition: A torn hymen—the thin mucous membrane at the vaginal opening—usually resulting from vaginal intercourse or other penetration or trauma; bleeding and pain vary and rupture can occur without sexual activity.

fluid volume deficit.definition: A decrease in the body's extracellular fluid volume (intravascular and interstitial) due to fluid loss or inadequate intake, leading to reduced circulating blood volume (hypovolemia) and potential impaired tissue perfusion.

altered cardiac output.definition: A state in which the amount of blood the heart pumps per minute (cardiac output) is not adequate to meet the body's metabolic needs, resulting in impaired tissue perfusion; factors include changes in heart rate, contractility, preload, afterload, and rhythm.

right upper quadrant.definition: An anatomical region of the abdomen located to the right of the midline and above the transumbilical plane; it contains the liver and gallbladder, portions of the stomach and duodenum, the head of the pancreas, the right kidney and adrenal gland, and the hepatic flexure of the colon.

ruq.definition: Abbreviation for the right upper quadrant of the abdomen—the anatomical region on the right side of the upper abdomen used in physical examination and imaging to describe pain or findings; it contains the liver and gallbladder, portions of the small intestine and colon, and the right kidney.

russell dwarf.definition: A congenital growth disorder characterized by intrauterine and postnatal growth retardation leading to short stature, often with a triangular face, relative macrocephaly, limb asymmetry, and feeding difficulties; commonly due to imprinting defects on chromosome 11p15 or maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7.

russell-silver syndrome.definition: A congenital growth disorder characterized by intrauterine growth restriction with postnatal short stature, a characteristic triangular face, relative macrocephaly, and limb asymmetry or mesomelic limb shortening; often associated with feeding difficulties and caused by imprinting defects on chromosome 11p15.5 or maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7.

russell-silver dwarfism.definition: A congenital growth disorder characterized by intrauterine growth restriction and persistent postnatal short stature, often with asymmetrical limb growth and a relatively large head for body size; commonly with a triangular face, limb length discrepancy, and feeding difficulties, while intelligence is usually normal. It is typically caused by imprinting defects on chromosomes 7 and 11 (for example, hypomethylation of 11p15 or maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7).

russell's bodies.definition: Intracytoplasmic eosinophilic inclusions within plasma cells, composed of condensed immunoglobulin; seen in chronic inflammatory conditions and certain mucosal lesions, arising from accumulation of immunoglobulin in the rough endoplasmic reticulum of plasma cells; not specific for malignancy.

russell's periodontal index.definition: A historical periodontal index used in epidemiology to quantify the severity and extent of periodontal disease by scoring signs of periodontal destruction on selected teeth and summing the scores into a single numerical index.

bone loss.definition: A decline in bone mass and density with loss of bone tissue, resulting in weaker bones and increased fracture risk; commonly seen with osteoporosis or osteopenia and other factors that increase bone resorption or decrease formation.

gingival inflammation.definition: Inflammation of the gingiva (gum tissue), presenting with redness, swelling, and often bleeding on probing; usually caused by dental plaque–induced gingivitis and typically reversible with proper oral hygiene and professional care.

russell's traction.definition: A form of skin traction used for femoral fractures in which a padded knee sling is connected via a pulley to a weight, applying continuous longitudinal traction along the leg to align fragments and relieve muscle spasm before definitive treatment.

ruffini’s corpuscles.definition: A slowly adapting mechanoreceptor in the dermis (and in joint capsules) that responds to sustained pressure and skin stretch, contributing to proprioception and the perception of object shape and hand position.

krause’s corpuscles.definition: Thermoreceptors in the skin and mucous membranes that respond to cold temperatures.

pacini’s corpuscles.definition: A rapidly adapting mechanoreceptor in the skin and subcutaneous tissue, consisting of a central nerve ending surrounded by concentric lamellae of connective tissue (onion-skin structure), that detects high-frequency vibration and deep pressure.

golgi-mazzoni corpuscles.definition: A tactile end organ in the skin; a small encapsulated mechanoreceptor in the dermis near hair follicles that is thought to mediate light touch and hair movement.

ruga.definition: A singular fold or ridge on a mucous membrane; often used to describe folds in the lining of the stomach.

rugae of vagina.definition: Transverse folds in the vaginal mucosa that allow distension of the vaginal canal during intercourse and childbirth.

rudiment.definition: An undeveloped or vestigial remnant of a body part, or an embryonic precursor (primordium) of an organ that has not yet formed.

rudimentary.definition: Underdeveloped or only rudimentary in form; existing in an early, immature, or undeveloped state, often with limited or no function.

ruvalcaba’s syndrome.definition: I couldn't locate a reliable definition for that term in standard medical dictionaries. Could you confirm the spelling or provide more context (e.g., associated features or an alternative name such as Ruvalcaba-Myers syndrome) so I can give an accurate definition?

rutin.definition: A flavonoid glycoside (quercetin-3-O-rutinoside) found in buckwheat, citrus fruits, and other plants; it has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and is used as a dietary supplement for vascular health.
