rubor.definition: Redness of the skin caused by increased blood flow in superficial vessels (vasodilation), typically due to inflammation or injury; one of the classic signs of inflammation.

ruptured intervertebral disk.definition: A herniation of an intervertebral disc: a condition in which the inner nucleus pulposus protrudes through a tear in the outer annulus fibrosus, potentially compressing adjacent nerves and causing back pain with radicular symptoms (such as sciatica).

rul.definition: The right upper lobe of the lung; the superior lobe of the right lung, separated from the middle lobe by the horizontal fissure, commonly described on chest radiographs and CT scans.

les.definition: A ring of smooth muscle at the gastroesophageal junction that maintains tonic contraction to prevent reflux of stomach contents; dysfunction or hypotension can contribute to gastroesophageal reflux disease.

pulmonic.definition: Relating to the lungs; pertaining to the pulmonary system.

saccular.definition: Pertaining to a sac or sac-shaped structure; pouch-like, often describing a sac-like dilation such as an aneurysm.

teratoma.definition: A germ cell tumor that contains tissues derived from more than one embryonic germ layer (ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm), often including differentiated tissues such as hair or teeth; it can be benign (mature teratoma) or malignant (immature teratoma/teratocarcinoma).

sacrococcygeal.definition: Relating to the sacrum and coccyx, the bones at the base of the spine; used to describe the sacrococcygeal region or the sacrococcygeal joint between these two bones.

saddle.definition: An area of numbness in the perineum and adjacent buttocks and inner thighs, typically signaling cauda equina or conus medullaris injury; it is also used to describe a regional anesthesia technique that blocks sacral nerve roots to anesthetize the perineal region.

toxoplasma.definition: A genus of obligate intracellular parasitic protozoa; the most studied species, Toxoplasma gondii, causes toxoplasmosis in humans and other warm-blooded animals. Infections are usually asymptomatic but can be severe in immunocompromised individuals and can be transmitted congenitally; common routes include eating undercooked meat containing tissue cysts or ingesting oocysts from cat feces.

saber-sheath.definition: A radiologic sign in which the intrathoracic trachea is markedly narrow and elongated, giving a saber- or sword-like appearance on chest imaging, most often seen with advanced COPD/emphysema and hyperinflation.

saddle-nose.definition: A nasal deformity in which the nasal dorsum collapses or sinks, producing a concave, saddle-shaped profile due to loss of support from the nasal septal cartilage and/or nasal bones, often from trauma or destruction from inflammatory/infectious processes.

saethre-chotzen.definition: A craniosynostosis syndrome (acrocephalosyndactyly type III) caused by TWIST1 mutations, autosomal dominant, characterized by premature fusion of cranial sutures (most often bicoronal) with skull shape abnormalities, facial asymmetry including ptosis and midface hypoplasia, and variable limb anomalies such as broad thumbs and syndactyly.

seasonal.definition: Relating to the seasons; occurring during a particular time of year or recurring annually (e.g., seasonal allergies, seasonal influenza).

affective.definition: Relating to mood or emotion; pertaining to affect, the observable expression of emotion.

sphincters.definition: A ring-shaped muscle that constricts an opening in the body to regulate the passage of contents; it relaxes to permit passage and can be smooth (involuntary) or skeletal (voluntary) depending on the location.

saint john's wort.definition: A herbal remedy from the flowering plant Hypericum perforatum, commonly used for mild to moderate depression; active constituents include hypericin and hyperforin; evidence for benefit is variable, and it can interact with many medications by inducing cytochrome P450 enzymes and may cause photosensitivity and GI upset.

hypericum perforatum.definition: A flowering perennial herb used in herbal medicine, commonly called St. John’s wort; used for mild to moderate depression and other conditions; contains active constituents such as hypericin and hyperforin; can interact with many medications and cause photosensitivity.

saint vitus' dance.definition: A historical term for Sydenham chorea, a choreiform movement disorder associated with rheumatic fever. It features rapid, involuntary, irregular movements of the face and limbs, often with emotional lability and hypotonia, typically occurring in children after a streptococcal infection.

sagittal sinus.definition: A dural venous sinus along the superior edge of the falx cerebri; it collects venous blood from cerebral veins and cerebrospinal fluid via arachnoid granulations and drains into the confluence of sinuses (then into the transverse sinuses).

sagittal section.definition: A vertical plane that divides the body into left and right portions; a sagittal section is a cut along this plane, with the midsagittal (median) plane at the midline and parasagittal sections offset from the midline.

stensen's duct.definition: The excretory duct of the parotid gland that carries saliva into the oral cavity, coursing forward across the cheek, piercing the buccinator, and opening opposite the upper second molar.

sublingual ducts.definition: Excretory ducts of the sublingual salivary gland; numerous small ducts (ducts of Rivinus) drain saliva into the floor of the mouth along the sublingual folds, usually with a single major sublingual duct opening near the sublingual fold.

rivinus duct.definition: A small excretory duct of the sublingual gland that opens on the floor of the mouth along the sublingual folds; one of the several minor salivary ducts collectively called the ducts of Rivinus.

langley’s ganglion.definition: A small parasympathetic ganglion on the deep surface of the submandibular gland; it receives preganglionic parasympathetic fibers from the chorda tympani (via the lingual nerve) and sends postganglionic fibers to the submandibular and sublingual glands to promote salivation.

salivary gland cancer.definition: A malignant neoplasm arising from the cells of the salivary glands (major or minor), encompassing several histologic subtypes (e.g., mucoepidermoid carcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma) and typically treated with surgery, often followed by radiotherapy depending on histology and stage.

radiographic studies.definition: Imaging studies that use ionizing radiation (X-rays) to visualize internal structures; commonly include plain radiographs, fluoroscopy, and contrast-enhanced radiographic examinations to diagnose disease or guide procedures.

sialography.definition: A radiographic examination of the salivary glands obtained after injecting radiopaque contrast into the ductal system (usually the parotid or submandibular ducts) to visualize the ductal anatomy and identify stones, strictures, or inflammatory lesions.

salivary fistula.definition: An abnormal tract between a salivary gland or duct and an epithelial surface (most commonly the skin) that allows saliva to drain externally or into another mucosal surface, often arising after trauma, infection, or parotid-region surgery.

salivary gland.definition: One of three pairs of glands that pour lubricating fluids and digestive enzymes into the mouth.

sialogenous.definition: Of or relating to the production of saliva.

salivary duct.definition: A duct carrying saliva from a salivary gland to the oral cavity; major ducts include Stensen's (parotid) and Wharton's (submandibular), with numerous small ducts draining the minor salivary glands.

sodium phosphate.definition: A salt of phosphoric acid in which sodium ions replace one, two, or all three acidic hydrogens; commonly exists as monosodium phosphate, disodium phosphate, and trisodium phosphate. It is used as an osmotic laxative and as a buffering agent in foods and medicines.

oil of wintergreen.definition: A volatile essential oil (methyl salicylate) derived from wintergreen plants; colorless to pale yellow with a minty odor, used topically as a counterirritant/analgesic and potentially toxic if ingested.

salicylism.definition: Toxicity from salicylates (e.g., aspirin) due to overdose or chronic high-dose exposure, presenting with tinnitus and hearing loss, dizziness, nausea and vomiting, tachypnea or hyperventilation, fever, dehydration, and mental status changes; often with a mixed metabolic acidosis and respiratory alkalosis.

salicylic acid.definition: A white crystalline beta-hydroxy acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) used topically as a keratolytic agent in dermatology to treat acne, dandruff, psoriasis, and warts; it is also a precursor in the synthesis of acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin).

sodium salicylate.definition: A sodium salt of salicylic acid; an older analgesic and antipyretic (a salicylate) with anti-inflammatory properties, historically used for pain relief and fever reduction; overdose can cause salicylism (tinnitus, dizziness, hyperventilation) and metabolic acidosis.

salicylated.definition: Having been converted to or containing a salicylate (a salt or ester of salicylic acid); chemically bound to salicylic acid.

saline enema.definition: A procedure in which a sterile 0.9% sodium chloride (saline) solution is instilled into the rectum to soften stool and induce defecation; used to relieve constipation or to cleanse the bowel before medical procedures.

saline irrigation.definition: Flushing a body cavity, wound, or tube with sterile isotonic saline to remove debris, dilute secretions, and reduce microbial load, thereby cleansing and promoting healing.

saline infusion.definition: Administration of a saline (sodium chloride) solution into the body, most often by intravenous infusion, to restore intravascular volume, rehydration, or correct electrolyte imbalances.

saint's triad.definition: A triad of diverticulosis of the colon, cholelithiasis (gallstones), and a hiatal hernia; the three conditions commonly co-occur in the same patient, often noted incidentally on imaging.

salmeterol.definition: An inhaled long-acting beta-2 adrenergic agonist (LABA) bronchodilator used for maintenance therapy in asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; it should not be used for relief of acute bronchospasm and is typically prescribed with an inhaled corticosteroid in asthma management.

mao inhibitors.definition: A class of antidepressant medications that block the enzyme monoamine oxidase, increasing synaptic levels of serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine; used for treatment of major depressive disorder and some Parkinson disease cases, but require dietary restrictions to avoid tyramine-related hypertensive crises and have significant interactions with other antidepressants and sympathomimetics.

prostatic hyperplasia.definition: A noncancerous enlargement of the prostate gland that narrows the urethra and causes lower urinary tract symptoms, such as hesitancy, weak urinary stream, frequency, urgency, and nocturia, especially in aging men.

keratolytic.definition: A keratolytic is an agent that promotes desquamation of the stratum corneum by breaking down keratin and disrupting intercellular bonds, thereby softening and shedding the outer layer of the skin.

keratolytic agent.definition: A keratolytic agent is a substance that promotes shedding of the stratum corneum by weakening keratinocyte attachments or dissolving keratin, thereby softening and peeling thickened or hyperkeratotic skin; used to treat warts, corns, calluses, and other hyperkeratotic conditions. Examples include salicylic acid, urea, lactic acid, and glycolic acid.

ptyalin.definition: A salivary enzyme (salivary α-amylase) that begins starch digestion by hydrolyzing α-1,4-glycosidic bonds to maltose and dextrins; secreted by the salivary glands and inactivated by gastric acid.

paratyphoid fever.definition: An enteric fever caused by Salmonella enterica serovars Paratyphi (A, B, or C), transmitted via contaminated food or water. It typically presents with fever, malaise, abdominal pain, and sometimes rose spots, and is usually milder than typhoid fever. Diagnosis is by culture of blood, stool, or bone marrow; treatment involves appropriate antibiotics and supportive care, with prevention focused on sanitation, safe water, and vaccination in selected settings.

salpingography.definition: A radiographic examination of the fallopian tubes in which contrast medium is introduced to visualize tubal patency and anatomy, typically performed via transcervical injection as part of hysterosalpingography.

salpingo-oophoritis.definition: Inflammation of both the fallopian tube and the ovary, usually caused by an ascending infection and commonly part of pelvic inflammatory disease; may cause pelvic pain, fever, adnexal tenderness, and can lead to infertility or tubo-ovarian abscess if untreated.

salpinx auditiva.definition: An air-filled canal that connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx; it serves to equalize pressure across the tympanic membrane and drain middle-ear secretions, normally closed and opened during swallowing, chewing, or yawning.

salpinx uterina.definition: A uterine tube (fallopian tube): a paired, slender canal extending from the uterus to the ovary that transports ova from the ovary toward the uterus; the usual site of fertilization and lined with ciliated epithelium to move gametes and embryos.

sarcoidosis cordis.definition: Inflammation of the heart by sarcoidosis with noncaseating granulomas in the myocardium or conduction system, leading to arrhythmias, AV block, heart failure, and potentially sudden death. It may accompany systemic sarcoidosis or be isolated. Diagnosis relies on cardiac imaging (MRI, FDG-PET) and biopsy; treatment uses corticosteroids/immunosuppressants, with pacemaker or ICD for conduction disease or malignant arrhythmias.

osteoblastic metastasis.definition: A bone metastasis in which tumor cells stimulate osteoblasts to form new bone, producing sclerotic (dense) lesions on imaging; most commonly seen with prostate cancer.

bone metastases.definition: Spread of malignant cells from a primary tumor to bone, forming secondary tumor deposits; commonly involves the spine, pelvis, skull, and proximal long bones and can cause bone pain, pathologic fractures, and hypercalcemia.

samarium.definition: A lanthanide element (atomic number 62); in medicine, its radioactive isotope is used as a bone-seeking radiopharmaceutical to palliate pain from osteoblastic bone metastases, administered intravenously and emitting beta radiation with gamma rays (half-life about 46 hours).

samarium-153-edtmp.definition: A radiopharmaceutical in which the beta-emitting isotope samarium-153 is chelated to EDTMP (ethylenediamine tetramethylene phosphonate) for the palliation of pain from osteoblastic bone metastases; administered intravenously and localizes to bone to deliver targeted radiation.

samarium-153.definition: A beta-emitting radioactive isotope used in radiopharmaceutical therapy to palliate bone pain from metastatic bone disease; given as Samarium-153-EDTMP (Quadramet), it localizes to bone and delivers targeted radiation with possible hematologic toxicity.

saluron.definition: Definition not found in trusted medical dictionaries. Please check the spelling or provide context (e.g., disease area, ingredient, or a sentence where you saw it) so I can help identify the term or suggest the correct term.

trospium.definition: A muscarinic receptor antagonist (anticholinergic) used to treat overactive bladder symptoms, including urgency, frequency, and urge incontinence. It works by blocking acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors in the bladder detrusor muscle (primarily M3), reducing involuntary contractions; it is a quaternary ammonium compound with limited central nervous system penetration.

sanorex.definition: A central nervous system stimulant used as a short-term appetite suppressor for obesity; it acts as a monoamine reuptake inhibitor (primarily norepinephrine and dopamine), reducing hunger. It carries risks of cardiovascular effects and potential for abuse or dependence, and is generally limited to short-term use under medical supervision.

santyl.definition: A topical enzymatic debridement agent containing collagenase that selectively digests collagen in necrotic tissue to promote wound debridement, while sparing viable tissue.

heparan sulfate.definition: A sulfated glycosaminoglycan chain covalently attached to core proteins to form proteoglycans on cell surfaces and in the extracellular matrix; it consists of repeating disaccharide units of uronic acid (glucuronic or iduronic) and glucosamine with variable sulfation patterns (N-, 2-O-, and 6-O-sulfation), enabling binding to a wide range of proteins such as growth factors and chemokines to regulate development, coagulation, and cell signaling.

sanfilippo's syndrome.definition: A neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disorder (MPS type III) caused by deficiency of enzymes that degrade heparan sulfate, leading to accumulation of heparan sulfate in lysosomes with progressive cognitive decline, behavioral abnormalities, sleep disturbance, seizures, and loss of motor and functional skills beginning in early childhood.

sandhoff's disease.definition: An autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of both beta-hexosaminidase A and B (due to HEXA/HEXB mutations), leading to accumulation of GM2 ganglioside in neurons; presents in infancy with progressive neurodegeneration, developmental delay, hypotonia evolving to severe neurologic decline, seizures, vision loss, hepatosplenomegaly, and often early death.

salpingemphraxis.definition: Occlusion of a fallopian tube (salpinx) due to an embolic or other obstructive process; a rare form of tubal blockage.

salt-losing nephritis.definition: A historical term for a nephritis characterized by renal loss of sodium in the urine (salt wasting) due to tubular dysfunction, leading to hyponatremia and extracellular volume depletion.

salt-losing nephropathy.definition: A condition characterized by excessive renal loss of sodium (salt wasting) due to renal tubular dysfunction or injury, leading to hyponatremia and volume depletion; can be congenital (renal salt‑wasting tubulopathies) or acquired from nephrotoxic injury or illness.

salt-losing syndrome.definition: A condition in which the kidneys excrete excessive amounts of sodium in the urine, leading to hyponatremia and extracellular fluid volume depletion (dehydration); seen in disorders with renal salt-wasting, such as congenital adrenal hyperplasia (salt-wasting form) and certain renal tubular disorders.

myelosarcoma.definition: A rare malignant neoplasm arising from bone marrow–derived (myeloid) tissue; a historical term describing a sarcoma with myeloid differentiation, not the same as leukemia or other hematologic malignancies, and not commonly used in modern practice.

sarcoma botryoides.definition: A variant of embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma presenting as grapelike, polypoid masses on mucosal surfaces (most often the vagina or urinary tract in children), composed of malignant rhabdomyoblasts with skeletal muscle differentiation.

sarcomere.definition: Basic contractile unit of striated muscle; a segment of a myofibril between two Z-discs containing overlapping actin (thin) and myosin (thick) filaments that interact during contraction to shorten the unit.

sarcopenia.definition: A syndrome characterized by progressive and generalized loss of skeletal muscle mass and strength, often related to aging and reduced physical activity, resulting in impaired physical performance and increased risk of disability and frailty.

crotamiton.definition: A topical antipruritic agent with modest scabicidal activity, used to treat scabies and associated pruritus; comes in cream or lotion formulations.

saw palmetto.definition: A plant-derived herbal extract from the fruit of Serenoa repens used to treat lower urinary tract symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia; evidence of benefit is inconsistent, and while generally well tolerated, it can cause gastrointestinal upset, headache, and rare liver injury.

saturnine.definition: Of or relating to lead poisoning; caused by lead exposure; also describes a gloomy, morose temperament.

saturnine tremor.definition: A tremor of the hands (and sometimes the lips or tongue) arising from chronic lead poisoning; a manifestation of lead (saturnine) poisoning, often with abdominal pain, constipation, neuropathy, and anemia.

satellite cells.definition: Muscle stem cells residing between the basal lamina and the sarcolemma of skeletal muscle fibers; normally quiescent but activated by injury or stress to proliferate and differentiate into myoblasts that fuse to repair or grow muscle fibers, essential for muscle regeneration and maintenance.

scapular reflex.definition: A reflex arc in which stimulation of the scapular region elicits contraction of the scapular stabilizing muscles (such as the trapezius, rhomboids, and serratus anterior); it is not a widely used or routinely tested clinical reflex.

scapular line.definition: A vertical surface landmark on the back that runs parallel to the midline and passes through the inferior angle of the scapula; used to describe posterior thoracic regions in surface anatomy.

superior border.definition: The upper boundary or edge of a structure; the border oriented toward the head (cranial direction).

medial border.definition: The edge of a structure that lies nearest to the midline of the body.

inferior angle.definition: Lowest point or tip of a structure where two borders join; in clinical anatomy, this most often refers to the bottom tip of the shoulder blade formed by the junction of its medial and lateral borders, typically near the level of the seventh thoracic vertebra and close to the midaxillary line.

rhomboids.definition: Two muscles in the upper back that retract the scapula and downwardly rotate it, stabilizing the shoulder girdle; innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve (C4–C5).

scalpel.definition: A small, extremely sharp surgical knife with a replaceable blade used to make precise incisions and delicate dissections during surgery.

scaler.definition: A dental instrument with a thin, curved blade used to remove calculus (tartar) from teeth, typically during dental cleaning, with both supragingival and subgingival applications.

scalene.definition: A group of three paired muscles on the lateral neck (anterior, middle, and posterior) that elevate the first and second ribs during inspiration and assist in neck flexion and lateral bending.

scalenus anticus syndrome.definition: A form of thoracic outlet syndrome in which the brachial plexus (and sometimes the subclavian vessels) is compressed by the anterior scalene muscle as it traverses the thoracic outlet, causing upper-extremity neurogenic and/or vascular symptoms.

scaphoid bone.definition: One of the eight carpal bones of the wrist, boat-shaped and located on the thumb side in the proximal row; it articulates with the radius and adjacent carpals. It is the most commonly fractured carpal bone, and fractures—especially at the waist—can disrupt its retrograde blood supply, risking avascular necrosis.

scaphoid abdomen.definition: A sunken, concave (boat-shaped) abdomen due to reduced abdominal contents or abdominal wall deficiency, most often seen in neonates with congenital diaphragmatic hernia or other thoracoabdominal anomalies.

scaphoid megalourethra.definition: A congenital penile malformation where the anterior (ventral) urethra is massively dilated due to underdevelopment or absence of the corpus spongiosum, while the corpora cavernosa are relatively preserved; this yields a boat-shaped (scaphoid) penis and represents one form of megalourethra (the other form being rhizomelic, with more extensive erectile tissue deficiency).

mecocephaly.definition: A condition in which the head circumference is significantly smaller than expected for the individual's age and sex, usually due to impaired brain growth during fetal development or early infancy; it can be isolated or part of a syndrome and may be associated with developmental delay.

scaphocephalism.definition: A cranial deformity in infancy in which the skull is elongated and narrow (boat-shaped) due to premature fusion of the sagittal suture.

scaphocephalic.definition: Of or relating to scaphocephaly; having a long, narrow skull shape often due to premature fusion of the sagittal cranial suture (sagittal craniosynostosis).

scaphocephalous.definition: Having a long, narrow, boat-shaped skull due to premature fusion of the sagittal cranial suture (craniosynostosis).

aponeurotic layer.definition: A sheet-like layer of fibrous connective tissue consisting of broad, flat tendinous extensions (aponeuroses) that attach muscles to each other or to bone, providing a broad area of attachment and distribution of muscular force.

scanning.definition: A medical imaging process that acquires sequential images of a body region by moving the imaging device or patient, used to detect abnormalities or map anatomy (as in CT, MRI, ultrasound, or nuclear medicine scans).

scanning electron microscope.definition: A type of electron microscope that scans a focused beam of electrons across a specimen’s surface to produce a high-resolution image of surface topography, typically using signals from secondary or backscattered electrons; samples are usually placed in vacuum and may require conductive coating for non-conductive materials.

scanning electron microscopy.definition: An imaging technique in which a focused beam of electrons is scanned across a specimen's surface in vacuum to produce high-resolution images of surface topography by detecting emitted secondary and backscattered electrons (often with detectors for elemental analysis).

scanning laser ophthalmoscope.definition: A retinal imaging device that uses a focused laser scanned across the retina with confocal detection to produce high-resolution, high-contrast images of the fundus, often with fluorescence angiography or autofluorescence capabilities.

If you know the field (e.g., ophthalmology, rheumatology, pathology) or the full term it stands for, I can define it precisely.

scala tympani.definition: The lower, perilymph-filled cavity of the cochlea bounded by the basilar membrane and the osseous wall; extends from the helicotrema (apex) to the round window (base) and communicates with the scala vestibuli.

scala vestibuli.definition: A perilymph-filled chamber of the cochlea in the inner ear; the upper (vestibular) scala that extends from the oval window to the helicotrema, separated from the scala media by Reissner's membrane and communicating with the scala tympani at the helicotrema.

helicotrema.definition: The small opening at the apex of the cochlea that connects the scala tympani and scala vestibuli, allowing perilymph to flow between them and acting as a low-frequency pressure-relief pathway.

scalded skin syndrome.definition: An acute, toxin-mediated skin disease caused by exfoliative toxins from Staphylococcus aureus, producing cleavage within the epidermis (stratum granulosum) and widespread superficial desquamation with fever and irritability, most common in neonates and young children; treated with systemic anti-staphylococcal antibiotics and supportive care.

scald.definition: A burn injury caused by contact with hot liquids or steam, typically presenting with redness, pain, and blistering; severity depends on the temperature and duration of exposure.

sudden cardiac arrest.definition: A sudden, life-threatening loss of heart function caused by an abrupt disruption of the heart’s electrical activity (most commonly ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia), leading to collapse, loss of consciousness, and no detectable pulse or circulation; it is an emergency requiring immediate CPR and defibrillation, and is distinct from a heart attack, though a heart attack can precipitate it.

scapulodynia.definition: Pain localized to the scapular (shoulder blade) region; a symptom arising from musculoskeletal strain or scapulothoracic joint pathology, or referred pain from the cervical spine.

scapulopexy.definition: A surgical procedure to fix the scapula in a desired position by anchoring it to the thorax or surrounding structures to stabilize the shoulder and correct abnormal scapulothoracic motion.

scapulocostal syndrome.definition: A musculoskeletal pain syndrome in the scapulothoracic region characterized by tenderness and pain around the scapula and adjacent ribs, often due to irritation or dysfunction of the costal–scapular joints or overlying periscapular muscles, and commonly related to overuse, poor posture, or trauma.

scapulohumeral muscular dystrophy.definition: A hereditary muscular dystrophy characterized by progressive weakness and wasting of the facial and scapulohumeral (shoulder girdle) muscles, often with scapular winging and difficulty raising the arms; most commonly caused by a contraction of the D4Z4 repeat on chromosome 4q35 (FSHD1/FSHD2) and inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.

scapulohumeral reflex.definition: An automatic neural reflex that coordinates scapular motion with humeral movement during arm elevation, adjusting scapular position via shoulder muscles (notably the serratus anterior and trapezius) to maintain proper scapulohumeral rhythm.

scarification.definition: Deliberate creation of superficial skin scars by scratching, scoring, or shallow incisions; historically used for inoculation or ritual body marking and in some cosmetic or dermatologic procedures.

scarify.definition: To deliberately make shallow incisions or scratches in the skin, typically to promote drainage or remove superficial tissue; historically used as a medical procedure to provoke a local inflammatory response or for bloodletting.

scarlet rash.definition: A diffuse, bright red, sandpaper-like rash seen in scarlet fever; caused by pyrogenic exotoxins from group A Streptococcus, typically starting on the trunk and spreading to the limbs and often accompanied by fever, sore throat, circumoral pallor, strawberry tongue, and later desquamation.

scarpa's fascia.definition: Deep membranous layer of the superficial fascia of the anterior abdominal wall; lies deep to Camper's fascia, attaches to the inguinal ligament, and continues inferiorly into the perineum as Colles' fascia and into the scrotum/penis as the dartos fascia.

scatophagy.definition: The act of eating feces; a form of coprophagia observed in some animals and rarely in humans, sometimes linked to nutritional deficiencies, pica, or behavioral disorders.

scatoscopy.definition: An examination of feces (stool) to assess gastrointestinal disease, typically involving macroscopic inspection and sometimes microscopic or chemical analyses for blood, parasites, fat, or other abnormalities.

scavenger cell.definition: A phagocytic immune cell, typically a macrophage, that engulfs and digests dead cells, debris, and invading microorganisms to clear tissue debris and aid host defense.

schamroth window test.definition: A bedside test for digital clubbing: the patient places the nails of opposite fingers together to form a diamond-shaped window between the nail beds; normally a window is visible, and its absence indicates clubbing.

schiller's test.definition: An iodine-based colposcopic test in which Lugol's iodine is applied to the cervix; normal glycogen-rich squamous epithelium stains brown, while abnormal dysplastic or neoplastic areas fail to stain (iodine-negative), helping identify suspicious lesions.

schilling test.definition: A diagnostic test to evaluate vitamin B12 (cobalamin) absorption and differentiate causes of B12 deficiency, especially pernicious anemia. It uses orally administered radiolabeled B12 and measures urinary excretion; a second stage with intrinsic factor helps distinguish intrinsic factor–related malabsorption from other causes.

radioactive cobalt.definition: A radioactive isotope of cobalt, most commonly cobalt-60, that emits gamma radiation and is used in external-beam radiotherapy and industrial radiography; half-life about 5.27 years.

peritonsillar abscess.definition: A collection of pus in the peritonsillar space, usually arising as a complication of acute tonsillitis; presents with severe unilateral throat pain, fever, muffled "hot potato" voice, trismus, and swelling with uvular deviation; treated with antibiotics and drainage (incision and drainage or needle aspiration).

epiphyseal growth.definition: Growth of long bones that occurs at the epiphyseal plates (physes) by endochondral ossification during childhood and adolescence; continues until the plates fuse (epiphyseal closure) at puberty, after which lengthening stops. Regulated by growth hormone, thyroid hormone, sex steroids, and nutritional status.

schistosome.definition: A parasitic trematode (blood fluke) of the genus Schistosoma that infects humans and causes schistosomiasis; adults reside in mesenteric or pelvic veins, and eggs cause tissue inflammation; transmission requires freshwater snails as intermediate hosts.

swimmer's itch.definition: Pruritic, self-limited skin eruption caused by an allergic reaction to cercariae (larval forms) of bird schistosomes that penetrate human skin after swimming in contaminated freshwater; also known as cercarial dermatitis.

portal venous system.definition: A network of veins that drains blood from the gastrointestinal tract, spleen, pancreas, and gallbladder and delivers it to the liver via the portal vein; includes the portal vein and its tributaries (e.g., splenic vein, superior mesenteric vein, inferior mesenteric vein).

oxamniquine.definition: An antischistosomal drug formerly used to treat Schistosoma mansoni infections; it is a prodrug activated by the parasite into a reactive metabolite that damages the parasite’s tegument, leading to parasite death. It is less effective against other schistosome species and has largely been replaced by praziquantel.

metrifonate.definition: An organophosphate cholinesterase inhibitor formerly used as an antiparasitic agent; it inhibits acetylcholinesterase, increasing acetylcholine at cholinergic synapses and causing parasitic paralysis as well as potential cholinergic toxicity in the host.

australorbis glabratus.definition: A binomial scientific name for a species of freshwater snail (gastropod) in the genus Australorbis; not a commonly used medical term and does not denote a specific medical condition or procedure. If you have context (e.g., a publication), I can refine the definition.

blood fluke.definition: A parasitic trematode (fluke) that resides in the blood vessels of its vertebrate host and causes schistosomiasis; humans are infected when cercariae in freshwater penetrate the skin.

schistosomicide.definition: An agent that kills Schistosoma species (blood flukes) and is used to treat schistosomiasis; praziquantel is the most common schistosomicidal agent.

schistothorax.definition: An obscure or historical term referring to a split or cleft of the thoracic wall (split chest); not a widely recognized or currently used clinical diagnosis.

schistosternia.definition: A rare congenital malformation characterized by a vertical cleft or split in the sternum (breastbone) due to incomplete fusion of the sternal bars during embryonic development; may be isolated or associated with other thoracic anomalies.

schizencephaly.definition: A rare congenital brain malformation characterized by one or more clefts that extend from the ependymal lining of the lateral ventricles to the pial surface of the cortex, with the cleft walls lined by gray matter; classified as open-lip (edges separated) or closed-lip (edges in apposition). It results from disrupted neuronal migration or early in utero vascular injury and commonly presents with seizures, motor impairment, and developmental delay, often with associated brain abnormalities.

schizoid.definition: Relating to a pervasive pattern of detachment from social relationships and a restricted range of emotional expression; individuals typically prefer solitary activities and have little interest in close relationships (as seen in schizoid personality disorder).

schizoid personality disorder.definition: A pervasive pattern of social detachment and restricted emotional expression beginning in early adulthood, characterized by limited desire for close relationships, a preference for solitary activities, little interest in sexual experiences, diminished pleasure in most activities, indifference to praise or criticism, and a flattened affect.

schizotypal personality disorder.definition: A Cluster A personality disorder marked by social and interpersonal deficits, acute discomfort with close relationships, and odd or eccentric behavior and thinking, including perceptual distortions such as ideas of reference, magical thinking, or unusual perceptual experiences, often with excessive social anxiety and suspiciousness.

schizont.definition: A developmental stage of certain protozoan parasites (e.g., Plasmodium) during schizogony in which the parasite undergoes multiple nuclear divisions within a host cell to form numerous daughter merozoites; the schizont subsequently ruptures to release merozoites.

schizonticide.definition: A drug that kills the schizont stage of a parasite, particularly the intraerythrocytic schizonts of Plasmodium species in malaria, thereby stopping parasite replication.

schizonticidal.definition: A drug that destroys schizonts, the intracellular stage of malaria parasites (Plasmodium) that reproduces within host cells, thereby interrupting parasite replication.

schizophasia.definition: A disturbance of speech seen in schizophrenia marked by disorganized, illogical, or fragmented language, often with rambling discourse, word salad, and neologisms, reflecting a formal thought disorder.

schuffner's dots.definition: Fine, punctate, red-brown stippling of the cytoplasm in erythrocytes infected by Plasmodium vivax or Plasmodium ovale, seen on Giemsa- or Wright-stained blood smears; characteristic of vivax/ovale malaria and not seen with P. falciparum.

schlatter-osgood disease.definition: A traction apophysitis of the tibial tubercle in growing adolescents caused by repetitive stress from quadriceps contraction, leading to anterior knee pain and tenderness just below the kneecap with possible swelling; symptoms worsen with activity and improve with rest. Treatment typically includes activity modification, ice, NSAIDs, and physical therapy, with most cases resolving as the apophysis matures.

schneiderian carcinoma.definition: A malignant neoplasm of the sinonasal tract arising from Schneiderian epithelium (the mucosa lining the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses), encompassing various histologic subtypes of sinonasal carcinoma; often aggressive with potential for local invasion and regional spread.

polyglandular autoimmune syndrome.definition: A group of autoimmune disorders in which two or more endocrine glands are attacked by the immune system, leading to multiple hormone deficiencies. Classic forms include a juvenile syndrome with mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, and adrenal insufficiency, and an adult-onset syndrome with Addison disease plus autoimmune thyroid disease and/or type 1 diabetes.

schmidt's syndrome.definition: Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type II, characterized by autoimmune adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) with autoimmune thyroid disease and/or type 1 diabetes mellitus, and often other autoimmune disorders.

vagoaccessory syndrome.definition: A clinical constellation due to concurrent impairment of the vagus nerve (CN X) and the spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), usually from skull base or jugular foramen pathology, characterized by hoarseness and dysphagia with an impaired gag reflex (CN X) and weakness of the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles causing shoulder weakness (CN XI).

chagas disease.definition: Chagas disease is a tropical parasitic infection caused by the protozoan Trypanosoma cruzi, transmitted primarily by triatomine bugs (kissing bugs). It typically has an acute phase that is mild or asymptomatic, followed by a chronic phase that may cause cardiomyopathy, megacolon, or megaesophagus; treatment with antiparasitic agents such as benznidazole or nifurtimox is most effective earlier in infection.

schizotrypanum cruzi.definition: A historical name for the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, the etiologic agent of Chagas disease; transmitted by triatomine bugs (kissing bugs) and via congenital, transfusion, or organ transplantation routes; its life cycle includes intracellular amastigotes in tissues and extracellular trypomastigotes in the blood.

alogia.definition: A reduction in speech production, resulting in brief replies and paucity of content; a negative symptom commonly seen in schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders.

apathy.definition: A lack of motivation, interest, or emotional responsiveness that leads to reduced initiative and engagement; it can occur as a standalone syndrome or as a feature of depression, dementia, and other neurological or psychiatric conditions.

flattened affect.definition: A reduced or absent outward display of emotion, including diminished facial expressiveness, monotone speech, and limited gesturing; a negative symptom often observed in schizophrenia and sometimes in mood disorders.

social isolation.definition: A lack of social contacts or meaningful interpersonal connections, resulting in infrequent or absent social interaction and limited social support; an objective state of social disconnectedness that can be associated with negative physical and mental health outcomes.

positive symptoms.definition: In psychiatry, the presence of abnormal experiences or behaviors added to normal functioning, typically including hallucinations, delusions, disorganized thinking or speech, and disorganized or agitated behavior.

negative symptoms.definition: Deficits or reductions of normal emotional and motivational functions, such as diminished affect (flat or blunted facial expression), alogia (reduced speech), avolition (decreased motivation), anhedonia (loss of pleasure), and social withdrawal; commonly seen in schizophrenia and related disorders.

prodromal manifestations.definition: Early signs or symptoms that precede the onset of the full clinical illness; often nonspecific or subclinical, indicating the initial phase of a disease process before more characteristic features appear.

cortical.definition: Relating to the cortex; the outer layer of an organ or structure, such as the cerebral cortex of the brain or the dense outer shell of bone.

petrous portion.definition: A dense, pyramid-shaped portion of the temporal bone forming part of the skull base that contains the inner ear (cochlea and vestibular apparatus), portions of the middle ear, and openings such as the internal acoustic meatus and carotid canal.

schwannosis.definition: A histopathologic term describing proliferation or hyperplasia of Schwann cells within peripheral nerves; it is not a distinct clinical disease and the term is not commonly used.

schwartz-jampel syndrome.definition: A rare autosomal recessive congenital disorder characterized by myotonia (delayed muscle relaxation) and skeletal deformities, typically with blepharophimosis, facial dysmorphism, joint contractures, and short stature.

palpebral fissures.definition: The opening between the upper and lower eyelids—the space through which the eye is visible, bounded by the eyelid margins and the medial and lateral canthi (often described by the horizontal fissure length).

joint contractures.definition: A permanent or fixed limitation of a joint's range of motion due to structural changes in the joint or surrounding soft tissues (e.g., joint capsule, ligaments, muscles, tendons), often arising after immobilization, injury, arthritis, or neuromuscular disease.

flat facies.definition: An expressionless, flat-appearing face with minimal facial contour due to reduced facial muscle movement or structural abnormalities; a nonspecific descriptor seen in various neuromuscular or congenital conditions.

schwartzman-sanarelli phenomenon.definition: A laboratory phenomenon in immunized animals where intravenous exposure to a bacterial antigen (often endotoxin) after prior sensitization triggers a severe, immune-complex–mediated necrotizing vasculitis of small vessels, sometimes with hemorrhage.

scid.definition: An inherited disorder characterized by profoundly impaired cellular and humoral immunity due to genetic defects in lymphocyte development or function, resulting in extreme susceptibility to recurrent, life-threatening infections beginning in infancy. Most patients have very low or absent T cells and impaired antibody responses. Management includes protective isolation, antimicrobial prophylaxis, immunoglobulin replacement, and definitive treatment with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation or gene therapy; early diagnosis (such as newborn screening) improves survival.

scid mouse.definition: A laboratory mouse with severe combined immunodeficiency due to defects in T- and B-lymphocyte development, resulting in little to no functional adaptive immune response; widely used as an in vivo model for human tissue and tumor engraftment and infectious disease studies because it accepts transplanted human cells without rejection.

scimitar sign.definition: A curvilinear, crescent-shaped radiographic shadow along the right heart border on chest X-ray, produced by anomalous drainage of the right pulmonary veins into the inferior vena cava, seen in Scimitar syndrome (partial anomalous pulmonary venous return with right lung hypoplasia).

scimitar syndrome.definition: A congenital cardiopulmonary anomaly in which the right lung has partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage (usually to the inferior vena cava) with ipsilateral right lung hypoplasia and dextroposition of the heart; chest imaging typically shows a curvilinear venous connection forming a sword-like silhouette.

scintigram.definition: A nuclear medicine image produced by injecting a radiopharmaceutical and capturing the gamma rays it emits with a gamma camera to visualize the distribution and function of organs.

scintigraph.definition: A nuclear medicine imaging technique in which a radiopharmaceutical is administered (by injection, ingestion, or inhalation) and a gamma camera detects emitted gamma rays to create images that reflect the functional distribution of the tracer in an organ or body region.

scintillation detector.definition: A radiation detector that uses a scintillating material to convert ionizing radiation (such as gamma rays or X-rays) into visible light, which is then detected by a photodetector (usually a photomultiplier tube or photodiode) to produce an electrical signal proportional to the radiation energy, enabling spectroscopy and dosimetry.

scintillation scanning.definition: A nuclear medicine imaging technique in which a radiopharmaceutical is administered and a gamma camera detects emitted gamma rays to create images of tracer distribution, reflecting the physiological function of tissues or organs.

scintiscan.definition: A nuclear medicine imaging test in which a small amount of radioactive tracer is administered and detected by a gamma camera to visualize the function and, to some extent, structure of organs (commonly thyroid, bone, and heart imaging).

scirrhoid.definition: Resembling scirrhus; a hard, fibrous tumor with dense desmoplastic stroma.

scirrhoma.definition: A hard, dense tumor characterized by extensive fibrous (desmoplastic) tissue surrounding malignant cells, giving a firm, stone-like consistency.

scirrhosarca.definition: A malignant tumor of mesenchymal origin characterized by extensive fibrous (desmoplastic) stroma, producing a hard, dense mass due to abundant collagen deposition.

scissor gait.definition: A gait pattern in which the legs cross or come together at the midline due to spastic adduction of the hips, producing a scissors-like motion of the legs while walking; most commonly seen in spastic cerebral palsy.

scissor legs.definition: An abnormal gait or posture in which the thighs adduct and the knees cross or come together, giving the appearance of scissors; typically due to spastic hip adductor muscles, commonly seen in cerebral palsy.

scleredema.definition: A rare connective tissue disorder characterized by diffuse, symmetrical, nonpitting thickening and induration of the skin, most prominent on the posterior neck, upper back, and shoulders; due to thickened dermis with mucin deposition and increased collagen, often associated with diabetes mellitus or a preceding infection (scleredema adultorum of Buschke).

scleredema neonatorum.definition: Rare benign neonatal dermatosis with diffuse, nonpitting edema and thickened, indurated (woody) skin, most often involving the face, neck, and trunk; usually resolves spontaneously within weeks to months without treatment.

scleroderma neonatorum.definition: A life-threatening neonatal condition characterized by diffuse hardening and induration of the skin and subcutaneous tissue in ill or preterm newborns; often associated with sepsis and metabolic disturbances, and managed with intensive supportive care and treatment of the underlying illness.

sclerodermatitis.definition: An informal, nonstandard term referring to inflammatory skin involvement in scleroderma (systemic sclerosis) or localized scleroderma, characterized by dermatitis with subsequent dermal fibrosis leading to thickened, hard skin.

sclerokeratitis.definition: Simultaneous inflammation of the sclera and the cornea; a combined ocular inflammatory condition that can cause severe eye pain, redness, and photophobia, and may be associated with systemic autoimmune diseases, potentially leading to scleral thinning or corneal damage if untreated.

scleromalacia perforans.definition: A painless, gradual thinning of the sclera, commonly associated with autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, that can progress to scleral perforation due to loss of scleral tissue, often with little or no accompanying inflammation.

scleroconjunctival.definition: Relating to both the sclera and the conjunctiva; describing tissues, conditions, or procedures that involve these two ocular structures.

sclerocornea.definition: A congenital corneal opacity characterized by scleralization of the cornea, in which corneal tissue blends with the sclera and the limbus is indistinct, often associated with microphthalmia and usually resulting in severely reduced vision.

sclerosing.definition: Causing sclerosis; inducing hardening or scarring of tissue, typically via a sclerosant agent used to obliterate abnormal vessels such as varicose veins.

sclerosing hemangioma.definition: A benign vascular lesion in which a preexisting hemangioma undergoes progressive fibrosis (sclerosis), with replacement of the vascular spaces by fibrous tissue and hyalinization (often with thrombosis and calcification).

sclerosing keratitis.definition: An inflammatory ocular condition in which the cornea is inflamed with concurrent scleral involvement (inflammation of both the cornea and sclera); may cause corneal opacity and scarring, scleral thickening or thinning, and can be autoimmune or infectious in origin.

sclerosing phlebitis.definition: Inflammation of a vein with fibrosis of the venous wall, leading to thickened, stiffened, and possibly narrowed or occluded veins.

sclerosing solution.definition: A chemical solution used in sclerotherapy that damages the endothelium of a vein or abnormal vessel, provoking inflammation, thrombosis, and fibrosis to occlude the vessel.

sclerotic.definition: Relating to sclerosis; describing tissue that has become hardened due to fibrous, calcific, or other sclerotic changes.

sclerotomal pain distribution.definition: Pain distribution that follows a sclerotome—the pattern of pain from deep structures innervated by a single spinal segment (such as vertebral periosteum, facet joints, and ligaments)—and is typically deep, dull, and poorly localized, often band-like around a trunk or limb rather than following a skin dermatomal pattern.

sclerotome.definition: The ventromedial part of a somite that migrates to surround the notochord and neural tube and differentiates into the vertebral column (vertebral bodies and arches), part of the skull base, and rib cartilage.

scoliometer.definition: A noninvasive device used to estimate the angle of trunk rotation during the forward-bending test to screen for scoliosis; it measures trunk rotation in degrees (angle of trunk rotation) to help decide whether radiographs are indicated.

scoliodontic.definition: A rarely used term referring to abnormal curvature or bending of teeth; not a standard or widely accepted dental term.

scoliokyphosis.definition: A spinal deformity with concurrent scoliosis (lateral curvature) and kyphosis (excessive forward rounding) of the spine, typically in the thoracic or thoracolumbar region; also called kyphoscoliosis.

scoliosiometry.definition: The measurement of scoliosis, i.e., the quantification of spinal curvature, most commonly by radiographic Cobb angle; clinically, trunk rotation can be estimated with a scoliometer.

scoliotic pelvis.definition: A pelvis whose orientation is altered by scoliosis, characterized by pelvic obliquity (unequal iliac crest height) and often accompanying rotation as a secondary consequence of spinal curvature rather than a primary pelvic deformity.

scombroid.definition: Relating to or resembling Scombridae (tuna-like) fish; in clinical use, scombroid poisoning is a form of histamine fish poisoning from eating spoiled fish (e.g., tuna, mackerel, sardines) with high histamine levels, causing flushing, headaches, urticaria, palpitations, and gastrointestinal symptoms.

scolex.definition: The anterior, specialized attachment organ of a tapeworm (cestode), bearing suckers and often hooks, used to attach the worm to the host's intestinal wall.

scoleces.definition: A larval form of cestodes that contains an inverted attachment head with suckers (and sometimes hooks), used to anchor the parasite to the host’s intestinal mucosa; upon maturation the head everts to become the attachment organ of the adult worm.

scolecoid.definition: Resembling a scolex; pertaining to a larval or morphological form that imitates or resembles the anterior attachment organ of a tapeworm (the head with suckers/hooks).

antinuclear antibodies.definition: Autoantibodies directed against components of the cell nucleus; used as a screening test for autoimmune diseases. A positive result supports a systemic autoimmune process (most notably systemic lupus erythematosus) but is not disease-specific and can occur in other rheumatic diseases or healthy individuals; interpretation depends on titer and immunofluorescence pattern.

interstitial myocardial fibrosis.definition: Pathologic accumulation of extracellular collagen in the myocardial interstitium (the spaces between cardiomyocytes), leading to increased stiffness of the heart muscle and impaired diastolic function; can be diffuse or perivascular and is associated with aging, hypertension, cardiomyopathies, and ischemic injury.

cervical factor infertility.definition: Infertility due to cervical factors that hinder sperm passage or embryo implantation, typically from abnormal or hostile cervical mucus that impairs sperm survival or transport, cervical stenosis, or cervical insufficiency (incompetent cervix) leading to pregnancy loss.

sperm-cervical mucus contact test.definition: An infertility test in which cervical mucus is examined after intercourse to assess the presence and motility of sperm within the mucus, evaluating sperm–cervical mucus interaction; historically known as the postcoital test.

decarboxylation.definition: Removal of a carboxyl group (–COOH) from a molecule, typically released as carbon dioxide (CO2); in biochemistry, it often refers to oxidative decarboxylation steps such as the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl‑CoA.

motion sickness.definition: A common syndrome caused by a mismatch between visual input and the vestibular system during movement, leading to autonomic symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, dizziness, pallor, and sweating.

transdermal.definition: Through the skin, as when medicine is put in a patch that is worn on your body.

scotophobia.definition: An irrational fear of darkness; a specific phobia characterized by intense anxiety in dark environments or at night, often leading to avoidance of darkness (also known as nyctophobia).

scoptophilia.definition: A paraphilia involving sexual arousal from watching others who are naked, undressing, or engaging in sexual activity, typically without their knowledge or consent.

scopophilia.definition: An erotic or sexual interest in looking at others, especially through voyeuristic observation of people who are unaware they are being watched.

scotopic.definition: Relating to vision in very dim light, mediated by rod photoreceptors in the retina; characterized by high light sensitivity, low visual acuity, and reduced color perception.

scorbutic.definition: Relating to scurvy or its symptoms, caused by vitamin C deficiency.

scorbutus.definition: A nutritional deficiency disease caused by insufficient vitamin C intake, leading to defective collagen synthesis with symptoms such as gum disease, easy bruising, perifollicular hemorrhages, anemia, bone pain, and poor wound healing.

scrofula.definition: Tuberculous lymphadenitis: infection of lymph nodes, most often the cervical nodes, by Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, causing a chronic neck swelling that may suppurate or form sinus tracts; a form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis.

phlyctenular keratoconjunctivitis.definition: A delayed-type hypersensitivity–mediated inflammatory disease of the ocular surface, marked by small limbal nodules (phlyctenules) at the corneal–conjunctival junction with adjacent keratoconjunctival inflammation, often in response to ocular antigens such as tuberculosis–related proteins or Staphylococcus species; symptoms include itching, tearing, and photophobia.

rickettsiae.definition: Small, gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacteria that reproduce only inside host cells and are transmitted by arthropods, causing diseases such as typhus and spotted fever.

tsutsugamushi disease.definition: An acute febrile illness caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi transmitted by chigger mite bites; presents with sudden fever, headache, myalgia, often an eschar at the bite site, and may include rash and lymphadenopathy, with potential severe complications such as pneumonia, meningitis, or multi‑organ failure if untreated.

scout film.definition: A preliminary radiograph obtained before a radiologic study (such as a CT or contrast-enhanced X-ray) to assess patient positioning, field size, and anatomy and to plan the subsequent imaging; it is typically taken without contrast.

scorbutic gingivitis.definition: Gingival inflammation due to vitamin C deficiency (scurvy), characterized by swollen, friable gums that bleed easily, gingival hemorrhages, and rapid progression of periodontal destruction from impaired collagen synthesis and poor connective tissue integrity.

scrotal ultrasound.definition: A noninvasive imaging test that uses high-frequency ultrasound to visualize the scrotum, evaluate the testes and epididymides for size, echotexture, and masses, and assess blood flow with Doppler to help diagnose conditions such as testicular torsion, epididymo-orchitis, hydrocele, varicocele, tumors, or trauma.

scrotal tongue.definition: Not a recognized medical term. If describing a tongue with grooves or fissures on the dorsum, the feature is grooves or fissures on the top surface of the tongue, which are typically asymptomatic but may collect debris and cause irritation in some cases.

torsion.definition: Twisting of a body part about its own axis, causing obstruction of venous outflow and arterial inflow and potentially leading to tissue ischemia; commonly discussed in contexts such as the testis or ovary and is a surgical emergency if suspected.

testicular torsion.definition: An acute twisting of the spermatic cord causing sudden severe unilateral scrotal pain and loss of testicular blood flow, a surgical emergency requiring urgent detorsion and orchiopexy (orchiectomy if the testis is nonviable).

hematocele.definition: A collection of blood within a body cavity or potential space; in the scrotum, a hematocele is blood between the testis and the tunica vaginalis, usually due to trauma or inflammation.

pyocele.definition: A pus-filled collection within a closed body cavity or sac, caused by infection; commonly refers to purulent accumulation in the tunica vaginalis around the testis (scrotal pyocele).

epidermoid.definition: Resembling epidermis or derived from epidermal tissue; describing keratinizing squamous cells or tumors that resemble epidermis (e.g., epidermoid cysts).

cryptorchid.definition: A condition in which one or both testes fail to descend into the scrotum.

anascorp.definition: A scorpion envenomation antivenom indicated for Centruroides species stings (notably Centruroides sculpturatus); an immunoglobulin preparation derived from equine antibodies used to neutralize venom and treat systemic symptoms.

scorpion sting.definition: An injury caused by the venom injected through the tail sting of a scorpion; it typically produces acute local pain and swelling, but certain species can cause systemic symptoms (autonomic or neuromuscular effects) requiring medical evaluation and, in some cases, antivenom.

sea-blue histiocyte syndrome.definition: A rare reticuloendothelial disorder in which macrophages accumulate lipofuscin to form “sea-blue” histiocytes in tissues such as bone marrow, liver, and spleen; these cells have blue-staining cytoplasm and reflect an underlying lipid-storage process.

histiocyte.definition: A tissue-resident macrophage derived from circulating monocytes that functions as a phagocytic immune cell in connective tissue and other organs as part of the mononuclear phagocyte system.

sebaceous epithelioma.definition: A skin tumor arising from sebaceous glands, typically a benign sebaceous neoplasm presenting as a nodular facial lesion; histology shows basaloid cell nests with sebaceous differentiation ( historically called sebaceous epithelioma, and often equated with sebaceoma or sebaceous adenoma).

sebaceous keratosis.definition: A common, benign epidermal tumor typically seen in adults, presenting as well-defined, pigmented, waxy plaques or papules with a characteristic “stuck-on” appearance; usually asymptomatic, but may be itchy or irritated, and removal is optional for cosmetic reasons (cryotherapy, curettage with electrodessication, or laser therapy may be used if desired).

seborrheic blepharitis.definition: An inflammatory eyelid margin condition associated with seborrheic dermatitis, characterized by chronic eyelid redness and irritation with greasy, yellowish scales or crusts on the eyelashes and lid margins, often involving the glands of Zeis and the meibomian glands.

seckel's syndrome.definition: A rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by severe prenatal and postnatal growth retardation with microcephaly and a distinctive bird-like facial appearance (including a beaked nose and receding chin), often with developmental delay and skeletal anomalies; caused by defects in genes involved in the DNA damage response (e.g., ATR).

secobarbital sodium.definition: A short-acting barbiturate used as a sedative-hypnotic; administered as its sodium salt to induce sleep or sedation; it facilitates GABA-A receptor–mediated inhibitory neurotransmission, with onset typically in 15–30 minutes and a duration of about 3–6 hours.

secondary apnea.definition: A later phase of apnea that occurs after an initial apneic interval, often associated with rising carbon dioxide and hypoxia; it may involve brief gasping or irregular respiratory effort and can be followed by either resumption of breathing or a renewed persistent apnea.

secondary biliary cirrhosis.definition: Chronic liver injury due to long-standing obstruction of the extrahepatic biliary tree (eg, stones, strictures, or tumors) causing cholestasis, inflammation, fibrosis, and eventual cirrhosis.

biliary cirrhosis.definition: Chronic liver disease due to longstanding biliary injury causing cholestasis, inflammation, fibrosis, and eventual cirrhosis; etiologies include autoimmune destruction of intrahepical bile ducts (primary biliary cholangitis) and chronic biliary obstruction (secondary biliary cirrhosis).

bronchial buds.definition: Embryologic outgrowths of the ventral foregut endoderm that give rise to the bronchial tree of the lungs (trachea and bronchi); the right and left bronchial buds appear early in gestation and undergo branching morphogenesis to form the mature airways.

secondary diabetes mellitus.definition: Diabetes mellitus caused by an underlying medical condition or by medication that directly impairs insulin secretion or action (e.g., pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, hemochromatosis, Cushing's syndrome, glucocorticoids); hyperglycemia may improve or resolve when the underlying cause is treated.

malabsorption disorders.definition: Malabsorption disorders are a heterogeneous group of conditions in which the small intestine fails to absorb nutrients from the diet, due to mucosal damage, reduced absorptive surface, pancreatic insufficiency, bile acid abnormalities, or other digestive defects; they typically cause chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea, weight loss, and nutritional deficiencies.

selenium sulfide.definition: An antifungal and keratolytic agent used in medicated shampoos (commonly 1% or 2.5% formulations) to treat dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, and tinea versicolor by inhibiting Malassezia yeast growth and reducing scaling.

oral corticosteroids.definition: A class of systemic glucocorticoid medications taken by mouth that mimic the body's cortisol, providing broad anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects; used to treat many inflammatory, allergic, and autoimmune conditions. Prolonged use can cause significant adverse effects, including hyperglycemia, weight gain, osteoporosis, hypertension, mood changes, and suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis.

topical antibiotics.definition: Medications applied to the skin or mucous membranes to treat localized bacterial infections; available as creams, ointments, gels, lotions, or solutions; they typically have minimal systemic absorption.

dandruff.definition: Flaking and itchiness of your skin.

seborrheic keratosis.definition: A common, benign epidermal lesion seen in older adults, presenting as well-demarcated, pigmented, waxy or verrucous plaques or papules with a characteristic "stuck-on" appearance; usually asymptomatic and requires no treatment unless for cosmetic reasons or to rule out malignancy.

acanthoma verrucosa seborrhoica.definition: Benign epidermal neoplasm with marked acanthosis and hyperkeratosis, producing a wart-like (verrucous) surface; considered a verruciform variant of seborrheic keratosis.

gluteal folds.definition: Paired skin creases at the lower buttock where the skin folds toward the upper thigh; they delineate the inferior boundary of the buttock (gluteal) region.

sudoriferous gland.definition: A sweat gland; an exocrine gland that secretes sweat to the skin surface via a duct, aiding thermoregulation and excretion; main types are eccrine and apocrine.

sea urchin granuloma.definition: A localized granulomatous inflammatory reaction in soft tissue caused by retained sea urchin spine fragments, representing a foreign-body response that can present as a persistent nodule or sinus tract; histology shows macrophages and multinucleated giant cells around foreign material.

sea urchin.definition: A marine invertebrate of the phylum Echinodermata, class Echinoidea; it has a spiny, calcareous test with a water vascular system and tube feet, and typically grazes on algae.

occlusal traumatism.definition: Injury to a tooth or its supporting structures caused by abnormal or excessive occlusal (biting) forces or occlusal disharmony; can be primary (excess force on a healthy periodontium) or secondary (normal force on a diseased periodontium). Manifestations include tooth mobility, fremitus, accelerated wear, fracture, and sensitivity; treatment focuses on occlusal adjustment, splinting, and periodontal therapy.

secondary dentition.definition: The permanent (adult) dentition that replaces the primary (baby) teeth; typically 32 teeth (incisors, canines, premolars, and molars) that erupt from early childhood through adolescence and remain through adulthood, though third molars may be absent.

primary dentition.definition: The first set of teeth (20 deciduous teeth) that erupt during early childhood, functioning in chewing and speech, and are later shed and replaced by the permanent dentition.

permanent dentition.definition: The set of teeth that replaces the deciduous (primary) dentition and is intended to remain for life; normally it comprises 32 teeth (16 per arch): 4 incisors, 2 canines, 4 premolars, and 6 molars per arch (including the third molars if present).

second molar.definition: One of the posterior teeth in the permanent dentition, located distal to the first molar in each quadrant; it typically erupts around ages 12–13 and functions in grinding food; maxillary second molars usually have three roots, while mandibular second molars usually have two.

ootid.definition: A fertilized ovum immediately after sperm penetration, before the male and female pronuclei fuse to form the zygote.

piggyback port.definition: A secondary intravenous infusion line connected to the primary IV line via a piggyback port (often a Y-site) to deliver a short, intermittent medication or fluid dose without starting a separate IV; the piggyback is typically hung higher so it infuses before the primary line resumes.

secondary radiation.definition: Radiation produced as a byproduct when a primary beam of ionizing radiation interacts with matter (such as a patient or shielding), including scattered photons and secondary charged particles, which travels away from the original beam and can contribute to unintended dose.

second-degree burn.definition: Partial-thickness burn involving the epidermis and part of the dermis (superficial or deep partial-thickness). It presents with red, moist, blistered skin and is typically very painful; heals in about 2–3 weeks with possible pigment changes and scarring, with larger or deeper burns needing medical evaluation.

papillary dermis.definition: Superficial layer of the dermis beneath the epidermis, composed of loose connective tissue with dermal papillae that interdigitate with the epidermis; contains capillaries, nerve endings, and receptors, and contributes to the dermal–epidermal junction and nutrient support for the epidermis.

reticular dermis.definition: The deeper, thicker layer of the dermis composed of dense irregular connective tissue with coarse collagen and elastin fibers; provides most of the skin’s tensile strength and houses hair follicles, sebaceous and sweat glands, nerves, and blood vessels.

hemorrhagic shock.definition: A form of hypovolemic shock due to acute loss of intravascular blood from hemorrhage, causing decreased venous return and cardiac output with resulting tissue hypoperfusion; it presents with tachycardia and cool, clammy skin and may progress to hypotension and altered mental status if not rapidly treated.

secondary teeth.definition: The permanent teeth that replace the primary (baby) teeth, forming the adult dentition; eruption typically begins around age 6 and continues into adolescence.

second cranial nerve.definition: A cable of specialized nerve fibers that transmit visual impulses from the eye to the brain.

intermediate cuneiform bone.definition: A small tarsal bone in the foot, the middle of the three cuneiform bones; it lies between the navicular proximally, the base of the second metatarsal distally, and articulates with the medial and lateral cuneiforms.

secondhand smoke.definition: Airborne smoke from tobacco products and exhaled by smokers; a mixture of thousands of chemicals, many toxic and carcinogenic, whose exposure increases the risk of lung cancer, heart disease, and respiratory illnesses in nonsmokers (including adverse effects on children).

sector scan.definition: A form of ultrasound imaging in which the transducer emits a fan-shaped (sector) beam, creating a wedge-shaped field of view. This is typically produced with a phased-array transducer and is commonly used in echocardiography and abdominal imaging to obtain rapid, wide-angle views.

pancreozymin.definition: A duodenal hormone that stimulates the pancreas to secrete enzyme-rich pancreatic juice; an older term for cholecystokinin (CCK).

secretin.definition: A peptide hormone released by S cells of the duodenum in response to acidic chyme; it stimulates pancreatic and biliary bicarbonate secretion to neutralize intestinal acid and modestly inhibits gastric acid secretion.

secretin-cholecystokinin test.definition: A diagnostic test of pancreatic exocrine function in which secretin is administered to stimulate bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice, followed by cholecystokinin to provoke enzyme-rich secretions; pancreatic juice is collected (usually from the duodenum) to measure bicarbonate concentration/volume and pancreatic enzymes, helping assess pancreatic ductal and acinar function and diagnose exocrine pancreatic insufficiency or chronic pancreatitis.

secretin-pancreozymin test.definition: An invasive diagnostic test of pancreatic exocrine function in which secretin is given to stimulate bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice, followed by pancreozymin (cholecystokinin) to stimulate enzyme-rich secretion; the collected duodenal juice is analyzed for volume, bicarbonate concentration, and enzyme content to assess pancreatic insufficiency.

secretin test.definition: A diagnostic procedure to detect gastrin-secreting tumors (gastrinomas) by administering secretin intravenously and measuring serum gastrin levels; in patients with gastrinomas, secretin causes a paradoxical rise in gastrin, supporting a diagnosis of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

secretory iga.definition: Main antibody in mucosal secretions (tears, saliva, mucus of the gut, airways, and genitourinary tract). It is produced as dimeric IgA by plasma cells in the lamina propria, linked by a J chain, and transported across epithelium by the polymeric immunoglobulin receptor; a secretory component remaining bound forms the secretory IgA. It provides immune defense at mucosal surfaces by neutralizing pathogens and toxins and preventing their adherence, and is relatively resistant to proteolysis.

progestational phase.definition: The luteal (secretory) phase of the menstrual cycle, a progesterone-dominant period after ovulation in which the endometrium becomes thickened and glandular secretory, preparing it for potential embryo implantation; if implantation does not occur, menstruation follows.

secundines.definition: In obstetrics, the placenta and fetal membranes expelled after delivery; the afterbirth.

secundipara.definition: An obstetric term for a woman who has had two deliveries after viability; i.e., two prior births.

secundigravida.definition: A woman who is pregnant for the second time; i.e., has had one previous pregnancy.

s cells.definition: Enteroendocrine cells in the mucosa of the duodenum and proximal small intestine that secrete secretin in response to acidic chyme; secretin stimulates pancreatic bicarbonate secretion and inhibits gastric acid secretion.

secretagogue.definition: A secretagogue is any substance that stimulates secretion from a gland or organ, such as triggering pancreatic insulin release or gastric juice secretion.

secretory component.definition: A fragment of the polymeric immunoglobulin receptor that remains bound to secretory IgA (and IgM) in mucosal secretions, protecting these immunoglobulins from proteolysis and aiding their stability and function.

glycopeptide.definition: A molecule in which a peptide chain is covalently linked to one or more carbohydrate (glycan) groups.

secretor.definition: A secretor is an individual who expresses certain blood group antigens (ABH) in bodily secretions such as saliva, mucus, and tears due to a functional FUT2 gene; nonsecretors do not secrete these antigens in their bodily fluids.

secretor factor.definition: A genetic determinant that governs whether ABO blood group antigens are secreted into bodily fluids; individuals with a functional secretor gene (FUT2) secrete soluble ABH antigens in saliva, mucus, urine, and other secretions, while nonsecretors do not secrete these antigens in fluids.

secretory immune system.definition: A component of the immune system that operates at mucosal surfaces and in body secretions, primarily through secretory IgA produced in mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue; it provides local humoral defense by neutralizing pathogens and preventing their adhesion and invasion in mucus, saliva, tears, breast milk, and other secretions.

mucosal immunity.definition: The immune defense operating at mucous membranes (such as in the gastrointestinal, respiratory, and urogenital tracts) that uses mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue, secretory IgA antibodies, specialized epithelial and immune cells, and coordinated innate and adaptive responses to prevent pathogen entry while maintaining tolerance to commensal organisms.

ca2+.definition: An inorganic calcium ion with a 2+ charge (Ca2+); a divalent cation essential for bone and tooth mineralization, muscle contraction, neurotransmitter release, blood coagulation, and numerous cellular signaling pathways.

camp.definition: A microbiology test used to identify Group B Streptococcus (Streptococcus agalactiae) by detecting a diffusible protein factor that enhances beta-hemolysis of red blood cells on blood agar when cultured near Staphylococcus aureus; a positive result shows an augmented hemolytic zone at the intersection of the two organisms.

ischemic bowel.definition: A condition in which the intestinal tissue receives too little blood flow, leading to ischemia and potentially bowel infarction; causes include arterial embolism or thrombosis, nonocclusive hypoperfusion, and mesenteric venous thrombosis.

secretory cyst.definition: A cyst lined by secretory epithelium that actively secretes fluid into the cyst cavity, typically arising from ductal obstruction or persistent secretory activity of the lining.

secretions.definition: Substances produced by glands or specialized cells and released into ducts or onto surfaces; they include mucus, saliva, sweat, gastric juice, bile, etc., and serve lubrication, protection, digestion, or regulatory functions.
