submental.definition: Situated directly beneath the chin; pertaining to the submental region of the head and neck (the area under the chin, including the submental lymph nodes).

submentovertex.definition: A radiographic projection of the skull in which the X-ray beam passes from beneath the chin (submentale) to the vertex, yielding an image that best shows the mandibular condyles and cranial base; used in cephalometrics and assessment of craniofacial morphology and TMJ.

submucous_plexus.definition: A network of neurons in the submucosa of the gastrointestinal tract (Meissner's plexus) that regulates local secretions, mucosal blood flow, and absorption.

myenteric_plexus.definition: A network of neurons in the wall of the gastrointestinal tract, located between the circular and longitudinal muscle layers (the Auerbach’s plexus), that autonomically regulates GI motility and smooth muscle tone as part of the enteric nervous system.

submucous_resection.definition: A surgical procedure to correct a deviated nasal septum by removing portions of the cartilaginous and/or bony septum beneath an intact mucous membrane, preserving the mucosa; commonly referred to as septoplasty.

subnormal_temperature.definition: An abnormally low core body temperature, below the normal physiological range (generally below about 36°C/97°F), which may indicate hypothermia from cold exposure, illness, or metabolic disturbance.

suboccipital_muscles.definition: Four small, deep muscles at the base of the skull (rectus capitis posterior major and minor, and obliquus capitis superior and inferior) that extend and rotate the head; innervated by the suboccipital nerve (dorsal ramus of C1) and vascularized by branches of the vertebral and occipital arteries.

rectus_capitis_posterior_major.definition: Originates from the spinous process of the axis (C2) and inserts into the occipital bone at the inferior nuchal line; extends the head and rotates it to the same side; innervated by the suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1).

rectus_capitis_posterior_minor.definition: A small suboccipital muscle that extends the head and stabilizes the atlanto-occipital joint; it originates from the posterior tubercle of the posterior arch of the atlas (C1) and inserts on the medial part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone, innervated by the dorsal ramus of C1 (suboccipital nerve).

obliquus_capitis_inferior.definition: A small suboccipital neck muscle that originates from the spinous process of C2 and inserts on the transverse process of C1; it rotates the head to the same side (ipsilateral rotation).

obliquus_capitis_superior.definition: Muscle of the suboccipital region that originates from the transverse process of the atlas (C1) and inserts on the occipital bone between the superior and inferior nuchal lines; it extends the head at the atlanto-occipital joint and assists in lateral flexion of the head.

suboccipitobregmatic.definition: The smallest anteroposterior diameter of the fetal skull, measured from the suboccipital region to the bregma; typically about 9.5 cm in a term fetus.

subperiosteal_fracture.definition: A fracture in which the bone is broken beneath the periosteum, separating the periosteum from the underlying cortex and often producing a subperiosteal hematoma with elevation of the periosteum.

subphrenic.definition: Situated beneath the diaphragm; in anatomy, relating to the region below the diaphragmatic surface, notably the spaces on either side of the liver.

subphrenic_abscess.definition: A localized collection of pus in the subphrenic space beneath the diaphragm, typically due to intra-abdominal infection or visceral perforation (often after surgery); presents with fever and abdominal or referred shoulder pain and is treated with antibiotics and drainage (percutaneous or surgical).

subpopliteal_recess.definition: A small posterior recess of the knee within the popliteal fossa; a potential space near the gastrocnemius and popliteal vessels that may distend with joint effusion and is sometimes considered part of the gastrocnemiofemoral bursa.

synovial_membrane.definition: A specialized connective tissue lining of synovial joints, tendon sheaths, and bursae that secretes synovial fluid to lubricate and nourish cartilage and reduce friction; composed of synoviocytes (type A macrophage-like and type B fibroblast-like cells) in a vascular stroma.

substance withdrawal.definition: A cluster of physical and psychological symptoms that emerge after abrupt cessation or reduction of a psychoactive substance to which the person has become physically dependent, reflecting withdrawal from that substance.

substance withdrawal severity.definition: The intensity and range of physical and psychological symptoms that occur when a person who is dependent on a substance abruptly stops or reduces its use, reflecting the degree of physiological adaptation and informing treatment needs.

popliteus.definition: Small, flat muscle at the posterior knee; originates from the lateral femoral condyle and inserts on the posterior surface of the tibia above the soleal line; it unlocks the extended knee by rotating the femur on the tibia to initiate flexion.

posterior scapular region.definition: A region on the back overlying the scapula (shoulder blade); the posterior aspect of the shoulder girdle, spanning from the superior to inferior angles of the scapula and including the scapular spine and posterior fossae.

subscapular nerves.definition: Two nerves from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus—the upper subscapular nerve and the lower subscapular nerve. They innervate the subscapularis muscle (both nerves) and the teres major (lower subscapular nerve).

inferior subscapular nerve.definition: A branch of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus (C5–C6) that innervates the subscapularis and teres major muscles.

subspecialty.definition: A focused area within a medical specialty that concentrates on a specific organ system, disease category, or patient population, usually attained through additional fellowship training after completing general specialty training.

substantia alba.definition: White matter of the central nervous system composed mainly of myelinated axons that form tracts connecting gray-matter regions; enables rapid transmission of neural signals within the CNS, contrasting with gray matter.

substernal goiter.definition: An enlargement of the thyroid gland that extends below the thoracic inlet into the superior mediastinum (retrosternal/intrathoracic goiter); it may be asymptomatic or cause compressive symptoms such as dyspnea, dysphagia, cough, or hoarseness, and often requires surgical removal if symptomatic or suspicious for malignancy.

salivary secretion.definition: Production and release of saliva by the salivary glands, regulated by the autonomic nervous system; saliva lubricates the oral cavity, begins digestion (via salivary amylase), buffers and protects oral tissues, and aids swallowing.

substance p.definition: An 11‑amino‑acid neuropeptide of the tachykinin family that acts as a neurotransmitter/neuromodulator to transmit pain signals in the peripheral and central nervous systems; it binds primarily to neurokinin‑1 (NK1) receptors and participates in neurogenic inflammation and vasodilation.

substance abuse.definition: Continued substance use despite substance-related social or interpersonal problems.

substance addiction.definition: A chronic, relapsing brain disease characterized by compulsive drug seeking and use despite harmful consequences, often accompanied by tolerance, withdrawal, and lasting changes in brain circuits involved in reward, motivation, and self-control.

substance dependence.definition: A condition characterized by excessive and often compulsive substance use, impaired control over substance use, continued use of substances despite adverse consequences, and withdrawal symptoms that emerge when the substance use is discontinued.

substance use prevention.definition: A public health strategy to prevent initiation and reduce escalation of psychoactive substance use and related harms through evidence-based interventions such as education, community programs, policy and environmental changes, and improved access to preventive services.

substance use treatment.definition: A structured, evidence-based plan of medical, behavioral, and social interventions aimed at helping individuals reduce or stop the use of alcohol or drugs, manage withdrawal and cravings, treat co-occurring conditions, and support recovery; often includes pharmacotherapy, counseling or psychotherapy, and social support services in outpatient or inpatient settings.

drug withdrawal.definition: A set of physical and psychological symptoms that develop after stopping or reducing use of a drug to which a person has become dependent, reflecting neuroadaptive changes in the body's nervous system; symptoms vary by substance but commonly include anxiety, irritability, insomnia, autonomic signs (sweating, tachycardia), nausea, vomiting, pain, tremor, and cravings.

subunit vaccine.definition: A vaccine containing only selected antigenic components of a pathogen (such as purified proteins, polysaccharides, or virus-like particles) rather than the whole organism; it aims to provoke immunity with lower risk and often requires an adjuvant to enhance immunogenicity.

subzonal insemination.definition: A historical assisted-reproduction technique in which motile sperm are placed beneath the zona pellucida of an oocyte to facilitate fertilization, typically used when conventional insemination or standard IVF fails.

perivitelline space.definition: The space between the oocyte plasma membrane (oolemma) and the surrounding zona pellucida, filled with perivitelline fluid.

succinic acid.definition: A four-carbon dicarboxylic acid (butanedioic acid) that is an intermediate of the citric acid (Krebs) cycle; produced from succinyl-CoA and oxidized to fumarate.

succinylcholine chloride.definition: A short-acting depolarizing neuromuscular blocker used to facilitate rapid sequence endotracheal intubation; it binds to nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, causing initial fasciculations followed by transient depolarization and blockade. Onset is about 30–60 seconds with a duration of roughly 5–10 minutes, and it is rapidly hydrolyzed by plasma cholinesterase. Adverse effects include fasciculations, transient hyperkalemia in predisposed patients, apnea, bradycardia, and malignant hyperthermia in susceptible individuals.

tegmentum.definition: In neuroanatomy, the tegmentum is the brainstem region (primarily the midbrain) lying between the tectum (dorsal) and the cerebral peduncles (ventral); it contains the reticular formation, periaqueductal gray, red nucleus, cranial nerve nuclei, and various ascending and descending motor and sensory pathways.

mesencephali.definition: Genitive singular of mesencephalon; of the midbrain.

ansa lenticularis.definition: A curved bundle of pallidal efferent fibers from the globus pallidus interna that loops around the thalamus to join the lenticular fasciculus, forming the thalamic fasciculus and conveying GPi output to the motor thalamus (ventral anterior and ventral lateral nuclei).

internal capsule.definition: A large white-matter tract in the brain that carries projection fibers between the cerebral cortex and subcortical structures; subdivided into the anterior limb, genu, and posterior limb, it contains corticospinal, corticobulbar, and thalamocortical fibers, and lesions can cause contralateral motor (and sometimes sensory) deficits.

anterior perforated substance.definition: A small triangular region on the inferior surface of the cerebral hemisphere at the base of the forebrain, just anterior to the hypothalamus near the optic tract, perforated by numerous small arteries; these perforators (from the anterior cerebral/internal carotid system) supply deep basal ganglia and diencephalic structures.

ammonium tartrate.definition: An ammonium salt of tartaric acid; the common form is diammonium tartrate, with formula (NH4)2C4H4O6. It is a white crystalline solid used as a laboratory reagent in biochemical and analytical contexts.

succus.definition: Latin for "juice"; in anatomy, a digestive secretion produced by glands or mucosa, such as intestinal juice (succus entericus).

sudoriferous duct.definition: A duct of a sweat gland that transports sweat from the secretory portion to the skin surface, enabling evaporation and thermoregulation; primarily associated with eccrine glands (and, in some areas, apocrine glands).

hydropneumothorax.definition: An abnormal collection of both air and pleural fluid in the pleural space (air–fluid level), usually due to chest trauma, infection, or iatrogenic injury, which can impair ventilation and may require drainage.

rooting reflex.definition: A primitive neonatal reflex in which touching the cheek or mouth causes the infant to turn toward the stimulus with mouth opening, guiding the infant to the breast or bottle; present at birth and typically integrated by about 3–4 months.

suck-swallow reflex.definition: A primitive infant reflex in which placement of a nipple or other object in the mouth triggers rhythmic sucking movements that are coordinated with swallowing, enabling oral feeding and maturing into voluntary sucking and swallowing over the first months of life.

sucostrin.definition: Not found in standard medical dictionaries; likely a brand name or misspelling. If you can provide context (drug class, indication, or country), I can help clarify or locate the correct term.

sufentanil.definition: A potent synthetic opioid analgesic related to fentanyl, about 5–10 times more potent than fentanyl; used for anesthesia and management of severe postoperative pain; typically given intravenously, with intrathecal or epidural administration possible; can cause life-threatening respiratory depression.

sufentanil citrate.definition: A highly potent synthetic opioid analgesic; the citrate salt form of sufentanil used for anesthesia and postoperative pain control. It is a mu-opioid receptor agonist with rapid onset and relatively short duration of action, typically administered intravenously (and occasionally intrathecally or epidurally) under close monitoring. Like other opioids, it can cause respiratory depression, sedation, hypotension, and constipation; overdose is treated with naloxone.

sufenta.definition: A potent synthetic opioid analgesic in the fentanyl family used for anesthesia and analgesia, administered intravenously or via neuraxial routes; highly potent with rapid onset and risk of respiratory depression.

sudafed.definition: A brand-name oral decongestant containing pseudoephedrine, a sympathomimetic vasoconstrictor used to relieve nasal congestion from colds, allergies, or sinusitis; some formulations use phenylephrine as an alternative.

crib death.definition: When a baby dies suddenly, without reason. Also called SIDS or Sudden Infant Death Syndrome.

suffocation.definition: A condition in which breathing is blocked or impeded, leading to inadequate oxygen intake (hypoxia) and often elevated carbon dioxide in the blood, which can cause unconsciousness and death.

apocrine sweat glands.definition: A type of sweat gland associated with hair follicles, mainly in the axillae and groin, that secretes a viscous, protein- and lipid-rich fluid via apocrine secretion; its secretions are odorless until metabolized by skin bacteria and are often stimulated by emotional stimuli or sexual arousal.

suction biopsy.definition: A biopsy technique in which tissue is drawn into a suction device and a sample is collected without a surgical incision, typically yielding a small piece of mucosa or submucosa for histologic analysis (commonly used for rectal mucosa in Hirschsprung disease).

vacuum aspiration.definition: A gynecologic procedure in which suction is applied via a cannula to remove contents of the uterus, typically used for first-trimester abortion or to evacuate tissue after a miscarriage; also known as suction abortion.

ankylosing.definition: Stiffening and fusion of a joint or joints, typically due to chronic inflammatory processes that promote ossification.

falciparum.definition: The parasite species that causes the most severe form of human malaria; highly virulent and capable of causing cerebral malaria and multi-organ failure, transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes.

jirovecii.definition: A fungal organism that causes Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP), an opportunistic respiratory infection seen in immunocompromised individuals (e.g., with HIV/AIDS, organ transplantation, or on immunosuppressive therapy).

vulvovaginal.definition: Relating to or affecting both the vulva (external female genitalia) and the vagina.

athlete's.definition: A fungal infection of the skin of the feet, especially between the toes, caused by dermatophyte fungi; characterized by itching, scaling, cracking, and sometimes redness. Common in warm, moist environments; treated with topical antifungal medications (e.g., terbinafine, azoles), with oral antifungals for resistant cases.

sulfonamide.definition: A class of organic compounds containing the sulfonamide group (-SO2NH2); many are antibiotics that inhibit bacterial folic acid synthesis by blocking dihydropteroate synthase, though sulfonamides also appear in non-antibiotic drugs; hypersensitivity can occur in some individuals.

sulfapyridine.definition: A sulfonamide antibiotic; one of the two active metabolites produced when sulfasalazine is cleaved in the intestine (the other being 5-aminosalicylic acid). It is absorbed into systemic circulation and can cause sulfonamide-related adverse effects such as hypersensitivity and folate antagonism.

mafenide.definition: A topical sulfonamide antibiotic used to treat burn-wound infections; it inhibits bacterial dihydropteroate synthase, blocking folic acid synthesis, and penetrates burn eschar; systemic absorption may cause metabolic acidosis and electrolyte disturbances.

benzoyl.definition: A carbonyl substituent derived from benzoic acid, consisting of a carbonyl group (C=O) attached to a phenyl ring (benzene); commonly written as C6H5-CO-.

peroxide.definition: A chemical compound containing an O-O single bond (peroxide linkage); the most common example is hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), used as an antiseptic and oxidizing/bleaching agent; higher concentrations are caustic and can cause tissue injury.

sulfonylurea.definition: A class of oral antidiabetic agents that stimulate insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells by inhibiting ATP-sensitive potassium (KATP) channels, used in type 2 diabetes and requiring some residual beta-cell function; can cause hypoglycemia and weight gain.

dyscrasias.definition: A disorder or abnormality of the blood or bone marrow, referring to an imbalance or dysfunction in the production or composition of blood cells (red cells, white cells, and platelets) and their constituents.

metachromatic.definition: Exhibiting metachromasia; the property of certain substances to change color when stained with specific dyes (for example, mast cell granules staining red/purple with toluidine blue) due to their chemical composition.

centralis.definition: Relating to the center; situated at or near the middle of a structure; used in anatomical terms to denote a central position.

cerebri.definition: Genitive singular form of cerebrum in Latin, meaning "of the brain"; used in anatomical terms to indicate relation to or location in the brain.

cordis.definition: The genitive form of the Latin word cor, meaning “of the heart”; used in anatomical terminology to denote relation to the heart.

terminal.definition: A disease that cannot be cured or is fatal.

sundowning.definition: Confusion or disorientation beginning at the end of the day and continuing into the night; often occurs in people with Alzheimer's disease or vascular dementia.

alzheimer's.definition: A progressive brain disease that causes memory loss, impaired thinking, and personality changes.

sunburn.definition: A burn of the skin caused by excessive ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure, usually from sunlight, presenting with redness (erythema), warmth, pain, and in more severe cases swelling or blistering; peeling may occur during healing.

sulfhemoglobin.definition: A form of hemoglobin in which sulfur is irreversibly incorporated into the heme, producing a molecule that cannot bind oxygen effectively and leading to cyanosis and reduced oxygen carrying capacity; it is often drug-induced and persists until the affected red blood cells are replaced.

sulfathiazole.definition: A sulfonamide antibiotic (synthetic antimicrobial) that inhibits bacterial folate synthesis by competitively blocking dihydropteroate synthase; bacteriostatic and used to treat susceptible bacterial infections; adverse effects can include hypersensitivity and other sulfonamide reactions.

sulfabenzamide.definition: A sulfonamide antibiotic that inhibits bacterial folate synthesis by competitively blocking dihydropteroate synthase, thereby inhibiting bacterial growth.

sunitinib.definition: A small-molecule multi-target receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in cancer therapy; it blocks signaling of several kinases (notably VEGFR, PDGFR, c-KIT, FLT3, CSF-1R, RET) to inhibit tumor angiogenesis and proliferation. It is approved for gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), advanced or metastatic renal cell carcinoma (RCC), pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNET), and other cancers.

sumycin.definition: A brand-name tetracycline antibiotic; it inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding the 30S ribosomal subunit and is used to treat acne, certain sexually transmitted and respiratory infections, atypical pathogens, and rickettsial diseases. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and in children under 8 due to risks of tooth discoloration and enamel hypoplasia, and can cause photosensitivity and gastrointestinal upset.

sultrin.definition: A brand-name sulfonamide antibiotic formerly used to treat bacterial infections; it inhibits bacterial folic acid synthesis by antagonizing the incorporation of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) into dihydropteroic acid.

mylohyoid.definition: A paired muscle forming the floor of the mouth; it extends from the mylohyoid line of the mandible to the body of the hyoid bone, and elevates the floor of the mouth and the hyoid during swallowing (when the mandible is fixed, it can assist in elevating the hyoid); innervated by the mylohyoid nerve, a branch of the inferior alveolar nerve (V3).

pancreaticoduodenal.definition: Relating to the pancreas and the duodenum.

ileocolic.definition: Relating to the ileum and the colon; specifically, pertaining to the ileocecal region at the junction of the ileum and cecum.

mesocolic.definition: Relating to the mesocolon, the peritoneal fold attaching the colon to the posterior abdominal wall.

paracardial.definition: Situated near the heart; located beside or adjacent to the pericardium.

preaortic.definition: Situated in front of the aorta; describing structures that lie anterior to the abdominal aorta (as opposed to retroaortic, which lie behind the aorta).

superoxide.definition: Reactive oxygen species formed by one-electron reduction of molecular oxygen, yielding the O2− anion; a free radical involved in oxidative stress and host defense, produced by enzymes such as NADPH oxidase; rapidly dismutates to hydrogen peroxide.

superior olivary nucleus.definition: A brainstem nucleus in the pons, part of the superior olivary complex of the auditory pathway; it receives input from the cochlear nuclei and projects to the inferior colliculus, participating in binaural sound localization by integrating inputs to compute interaural time differences (ITD) and interaural level differences (ILD).

trapezoid body.definition: A bundle of auditory nerve fibers in the caudal pons that cross the midline (the crossed ventral acoustic stria) from the ventral cochlear nucleus to the contralateral superior olivary nucleus, forming part of the ascending auditory pathway.

cranial nerve iii.definition: Primarily a motor nerve that innervates the majority of the extraocular muscles (superior rectus, inferior rectus, medial rectus, inferior oblique) and the levator palpebrae superioris, and carries parasympathetic fibers to the pupil and ciliary muscle for accommodation; it mediates most eye movements and pupil constriction.

cranial nerve iv.definition: Motor nerve that innervates the superior oblique muscle of the eye, enabling downward and inward movement; arises from the dorsal midbrain and reaches the orbit via the superior orbital fissure.

cranial nerve vi.definition: A pure motor nerve that innervates the lateral rectus muscle to abduct the eye; it originates in the caudal pons, travels through the cavernous sinus, and enters the orbit via the superior orbital fissure. Lesions cause horizontal diplopia and inability to move the eye laterally.

superior profunda artery.definition: A deep branch of a parent artery designated as superior, which supplies deeper tissues in its region; the exact origin and distribution vary by region and the term is not universally standardized in anatomy.

superior radioulnar joint.definition: A pivot-type synovial joint between the head of the radius and the radial notch of the ulna at the proximal forearm, enabling rotation of the radius around the ulna (pronation and supination) and stabilized by the annular ligament and surrounding joint capsules.

rectal venous plexus.definition: A venous network surrounding the rectum formed by the superior, middle, and inferior rectal veins; it drains blood from the rectal mucosa and communicates with portal (via the superior rectal veins) and systemic venous systems, with dilation of its tributaries contributing to hemorrhoidal disease.

superior rectal plexus.definition: A periarterial autonomic nerve plexus around the superior rectal artery, formed from the inferior mesenteric (hypogastric) plexuses, that provides sympathetic and parasympathetic innervation to the upper rectum.

pectinate line.definition: A landmark in the anal canal where the mucosa changes from columnar epithelium of the rectum to nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium of the anal canal; marks the transition between visceral and somatic innervation and between different arterial/venous and lymphatic drainage.

superior right lateral flexure of rectum.word: superior right lateral flexure of rectum
superior right lateral flexure of rectum.definition: A bend or curvature in the upper part of the rectum on the right lateral aspect, reflecting the rectum's curved path as it courses from the sigmoid colon into the pelvic cavity.

superior cerebral veins.definition: A group of veins draining the cortex and subcortical white matter of the cerebral hemispheres, emptying primarily into the superior sagittal sinus.

diploë.definition: The cancellous (spongy) bone layer between the inner and outer cortical tables of a cranial bone, containing marrow and vascular channels.

emissary veins.definition: Valveless veins that pass through skull foramina to connect extracranial veins (scalp and face) with intracranial dural venous sinuses, acting as collateral pathways for venous drainage; they can transmit infection or emboli between extracranial and intracranial compartments.

superior subscapular nerve.definition: A branch of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus that innervates the subscapularis muscle.

superior tarsal muscle.definition: A small smooth muscle of the upper eyelid (Müller’s muscle) that provides minor eyelid elevation; innervated by sympathetic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion, contributing about 1–2 mm of lid retraction beyond the action of the levator palpebrae superioris.

levator palpebrae superioris.definition: A skeletal muscle that elevates the upper eyelid; it originates from the lesser wing of the sphenoid, its aponeurosis inserts into the upper eyelid’s tarsal plate and skin, and it is innervated by the oculomotor nerve (CN III).

superior tarsus.definition: A dense connective tissue plate forming the upper eyelid's tarsus; provides structural support and contour to the eyelid, contains the meibomian glands, and serves as the insertion site for the levator palpebrae superioris via its aponeurosis.

superior thoracic artery.definition: A small branch of the first part of the axillary artery that supplies the first and second intercostal spaces and the upper anterior thoracic wall, coursing along the upper border of the pectoralis minor.

superior ulnar collateral artery.definition: A branch of the brachial artery that runs posterior to the medial epicondyle with the ulnar nerve and contributes to the elbow's collateral circulation by forming an anastomosis with the posterior ulnar recurrent artery.

posterior ulnar recurrent artery.definition: An arterial branch of the ulnar artery that arises near the elbow and courses posteriorly to participate in the elbow’s periarticular arterial network, forming anastomoses with other recurrent arteries around the joint.

inferior ulnar collateral artery.definition: A branch of the brachial artery that accompanies the ulnar nerve around the elbow and contributes to elbow collateral circulation by anastomosing with the anterior ulnar recurrent artery.

superior vena cava syndrome.definition: A clinical condition caused by partial or complete obstruction of the superior vena cava, leading to impaired venous drainage from the head, neck, and upper extremities with facial and cervical swelling, plethora, distended neck veins, and often dyspnea or cough; commonly due to malignancy (e.g., lung cancer, lymphoma) or thrombosis, and requiring urgent assessment and treatment of the underlying cause to relieve the obstruction.

superior vesical artery.definition: An artery that supplies the superior aspect of the urinary bladder, typically arising from the umbilical artery (a branch of the internal iliac); in males it may give branches to the vas deferens and seminal vesicles and may anastomose with the inferior vesical artery.

umbilical artery.definition: Two arteries in the umbilical cord that carry deoxygenated blood from the fetus to the placenta; they arise from the fetal internal iliac arteries and, after birth, become the medial umbilical ligaments.

supernatant.definition: The liquid portion that remains above the sediment or pellet after centrifugation or settling.

occlusive therapy.definition: An approach that uses an occluding barrier (eg, an eye patch or occlusive dressing) to block normal function or maintain moisture; in amblyopia, patching the good eye to stimulate the weaker eye, and in wound care to promote moist healing.

gnrh agonists.definition: A class of synthetic analogs of gonadotropin-releasing hormone that, when given continuously, desensitize and downregulate pituitary GnRH receptors, leading to decreased LH and FSH secretion and reduced gonadal steroid production; used to suppress puberty or hormones in hormone-sensitive cancers and gynecologic conditions, and to control ovulation in assisted reproduction.

suppurative phlebitis.definition: An acute infection of a vein with pus formation in the venous wall or lumen, typically arising from catheter- or injection-related inoculation, often accompanied by thrombosis (suppurative thrombophlebitis) and potential for systemic sepsis if untreated.

suppurative pancreatitis.definition: An infection of pancreatic tissue with purulent inflammation, typically occurring in necrotizing pancreatitis and often presenting as a pancreatic or peripancreatic abscess.

nonproductive cough.definition: A cough that does not produce sputum (a dry cough); caused by airway irritation from viral infections, allergies, asthma, gastroesophageal reflux disease, certain medications (e.g., ACE inhibitors), or other irritants.

central nervous system disorders.definition: A group of diseases and other conditions that affect the brain and spinal cord, causing neurologic symptoms such as weakness or paralysis, sensory loss, movement disorders, cognitive or behavioral changes, seizures, or altered consciousness; includes neurodegenerative, inflammatory/demyelinating, infectious, vascular, congenital, and traumatic etiologies.

olfactory epithelium.definition: A specialized sensory epithelium in the superior nasal cavity that contains olfactory receptor neurons, supporting (sustentacular) cells, and basal cells; it detects odorants and transduces them into neural signals sent to the olfactory bulb.

taste buds.definition: Small bumps on your tongue that let you taste sweet, salty, sour, and bitter.

supramentale.definition: A cephalometric landmark on the mandible defined as the deepest point on the anterior border of the mandible between the infradentale and pogonion, used as the B-point in cephalometric analyses.

supranasal.definition: Anatomical term meaning situated above the nose or nasal region; located superior to the nasal area.

supracondylar fracture.definition: A fracture of the distal humerus just above the elbow joint, most common in children, typically from a fall on an outstretched hand; may be displaced (extension or flexion type) and can be associated with neurovascular injury, particularly to the brachial artery and median nerve.

supraclavicular artery.definition: A small arterial branch supplying the skin and subcutaneous tissues over the clavicle and shoulder (the supraclavicular region), typically arising from the transverse cervical artery (a branch of the thyrocervical trunk) and running upward across the clavicle.

supraclavicular nerve.definition: Three cutaneous branches of the cervical plexus (from the ventral rami of C3–C4) that descend over the clavicle to supply sensation to the skin of the shoulder, clavicular region, and upper chest (medial, intermediate, and lateral supraclavicular nerves).

supraclavicular triangle.definition: A triangular region at the lower part of the posterior triangle of the neck, bounded anteriorly by the posterior edge of the sternocleidomastoid, posteriorly by the anterior edge of the trapezius, and inferiorly by the clavicle; its floor is formed by the first rib and scalene muscles. It contains the subclavian artery and vein, the trunks of the brachial plexus, and supraclavicular lymph nodes.

supraglenoid tubercle.definition: A small bony eminence on the superior aspect of the glenoid cavity of the scapula, serving as the origin of the tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii.

suprahyoid muscles.definition: Muscles located above the hyoid bone that elevate the hyoid bone and larynx during swallowing and speaking; includes the mylohyoid, geniohyoid, stylohyoid, and digastric muscles.

suprahyoid pharyngotomy.definition: A surgical approach that opens the pharynx via an incision made above the hyoid bone, providing access to the hypopharynx or larynx for procedures such as lesion resection or evaluation.

supernumerary nipples.definition: Congenital presence of one or more additional nipples along the embryonic mammary (milk) line from the axilla to the groin; these extra nipples may be fully formed or rudimentary and are usually benign and asymptomatic, though rarely associated with renal anomalies.

superoxide dismutase.definition: A metalloenzyme that catalyzes the dismutation of superoxide radicals into oxygen and hydrogen peroxide, protecting cells from oxidative damage.

supranuclear gaze disturbance.definition: Impaired voluntary control of eye movements due to dysfunction of supranuclear pathways that direct gaze (above the oculomotor nuclei); reflexive or vestibulo-ocular movements may be preserved. Often seen in neurodegenerative disorders such as progressive supranuclear palsy.

gaze palsy.definition: A gaze palsy is a reduced or absent ability to move both eyes together in a particular direction, typically due to a lesion affecting brainstem gaze centers (such as the PPRF or riMLF) or the cranial nerve pathways controlling eye movements, and may present with restricted conjugate gaze and diplopia.

supraoptic nucleus.definition: A hypothalamic nucleus located just above the optic chiasm; contains magnocellular neurosecretory neurons that synthesize vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone) and oxytocin, which are released from the posterior pituitary to regulate water balance and related reproductive/social behaviors.

supraorbital artery.definition: A branch of the ophthalmic artery that exits the skull through the supraorbital foramen (or notch) to supply the forehead and scalp; accompanied by the supraorbital nerve and anastomoses with the supratrochlear artery and other facial/scalp vessels.

suprapatellar ligament.definition: A thickened fibrous band of the knee joint capsule located above the patella, helping stabilize the patellofemoral joint; in standard anatomy the suprapatellar region is mainly the suprapatellar bursa/pouch rather than a distinct, widely recognized ligament.

suprapatellar catheter.definition: A catheter placed in the suprapatellar region of the knee (the area above the patella) to infuse medications directly into the knee joint or to drain joint fluid, commonly used for continuous intra-articular analgesia after knee surgery.

suprapubic.definition: Situated above the pubic bone; relating to the region of the lower abdomen immediately superior to the pubic symphysis.

suprapubic aspiration.definition: A technique to obtain a sterile urine sample by inserting a needle through the lower abdominal wall just above the pubic symphysis into the bladder and aspirating urine; used especially in infants or when urethral catheterization is not feasible or contraindicated.

suprapubic catheter.definition: A catheter inserted through the lower abdomen into the bladder to drain urine, bypassing the urethra; used when urethral catheterization is not possible or contraindicated, for long-term bladder drainage, or after certain surgeries or injuries.

suprapubic puncture.definition: A percutaneous puncture of the bladder through the suprapubic region (just above the pubic symphysis) to drain urine or obtain a sterile urine sample; typically used when urethral catheterization is not feasible or to decompress a distended bladder.

suprascapular foramen.definition: An opening formed when the suprascapular notch is bridged by the superior transverse (suprascapular) ligament; it transmits the suprascapular nerve (the accompanying vessels typically pass superior to the ligament).

suprascapular ligament.definition: A fibrous band bridging the suprascapular notch of the scapula to form the suprascapular foramen; the suprascapular nerve typically passes superior to the ligament while the suprascapular vessels pass inferior to it.

suprasellar.definition: Situated above the sella turcica (the bony cavity that houses the pituitary gland); describing structures or lesions in the region above the pituitary gland, often near the optic chiasm.

supraspinal.definition: Situated above the spinal cord; relating to the brain and brainstem rather than to the spinal cord.

supraspinous ligament.definition: A strong fibrous band that connects the tips of adjacent spinous processes along the posterior midline of the vertebral column, extending from the sacrum up to the seventh cervical vertebra; it helps limit spinal flexion and is continuous with the ligamentum nuchae in the cervical region.

supraspinatus syndrome.definition: A shoulder disorder characterized by irritation or degeneration of the supraspinatus tendon of the rotator cuff, causing anterior shoulder pain and weakness with overhead motions, typically from tendinopathy or subacromial impingement and may include tendinitis or partial-thickness tear.

supraspinous fossa.definition: A shallow depression on the posterior surface of the scapula, located superior to its spine, serving as the origin for the supraspinatus muscle.

suprasternal.definition: Situated above the sternum; the anatomical region at the upper anterior chest just superior to the sternum, near the top of the manubrium.

supratentorial.definition: Above the tentorium cerebelli; relating to the cerebral hemispheres and diencephalon (the forebrain), as opposed to infratentorial structures like the brainstem and cerebellum.

supratrochlear artery.definition: A terminal branch of the ophthalmic artery that ascends medially across the forehead, supplying the skin and muscles of the medial forehead and scalp; it accompanies the supratrochlear nerve and anastomoses with the supraorbital artery.

supravaginal hysterectomy.definition: A hysterectomy in which the body of the uterus is removed but the cervix is left in place.

supraventricular crest.definition: A muscular ridge in the right ventricle of the heart that marks the boundary between the inflow portion (trabeculated) and the outflow portion (infundibulum/conus arteriosus).

supraversion.definition: An overeruption of a tooth beyond its normal occlusal plane, typically due to loss of the opposing tooth or reduced occlusal contact; can cause occlusal interference and may require orthodontic adjustment, restorative treatment, or extraction of the opposing tooth. Also known as supra-eruption.

suprofen.definition: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) formerly used for relief of pain and inflammation; an arylpropionic acid derivative that inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing prostaglandin synthesis.

sural nerve.definition: An exclusively sensory nerve of the leg formed by the union of the medial sural cutaneous nerve (from the tibial nerve) with a communicating branch from the common fibular nerve; it supplies cutaneous sensation to the posterolateral aspect of the leg and the lateral aspect of the foot/ankle, and typically travels with the small saphenous vein, often used as a donor for nerve grafts.

sural region.definition: The posterior aspect of the lower leg (the calf area), particularly the posterolateral region, corresponding to the distribution of the sural nerve and its cutaneous branches.

sural communicating nerve.definition: A small communicating branch of the common fibular (peroneal) nerve that joins with the medial sural cutaneous branch of the tibial nerve to form the sural nerve, carrying sensory fibers to the posterolateral leg and lateral foot.

surface anatomy.definition: The study of external features of the body and their relation to underlying structures, using surface landmarks and markings to identify organs and guide examination, procedures, and localization.

surface area.definition: Total area of the exterior surface of an object, expressed in square units; in medicine, it denotes the area available for exchange with the environment and is used in estimating body surface area and related physiological processes.

surface anesthesia.definition: Loss of sensation on a surface (skin or mucous membranes) produced by topically applying a local anesthetic to the area, causing temporary numbness without affecting consciousness.

surface therapy.definition: An approach to treatment that targets the body's surfaces (skin, mucous membranes) rather than systemic circulation or internal organs; involves topical medications, dressings, and surface-directed procedures to protect, heal, or treat surface lesions or conditions.

surface mold.definition: An indoor mold growth that forms on the surface of moist materials; a fungus that colonizes the surface, producing a visible film and releasing spores that can irritate airways and contribute to allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

surface applicator.definition: A device designed to apply topical agents or energy to the surface of the body (typically the skin) in a controlled, uniform manner.

surface thermometer.definition: A device that measures the temperature at the surface of a body part or object (eg, skin) rather than the internal body temperature; it may use contact sensors or infrared noncontact sensing and is used to assess peripheral or environmental temperature.

surfak.definition: A brand-name stool softener (emollient laxative) used to soften stool and ease defecation, commonly containing docusate sodium.

surfer's nodules.definition: Benign nodular skin lesions due to chronic friction and trauma in surfers, usually on pressure points like the elbows or knuckles; composed of thickened keratotic tissue (callus-like) or fibrous nodules from repetitive rubbing against the surfboard or wax.

surgical.definition: Relating to surgery; pertaining to or used in operative procedures performed by a surgeon.

surgical anatomy.definition: The branch of anatomy focused on the structures, relationships, and dissection planes most relevant to surgical exposure and technique, emphasizing practical landmarks, common anatomical variations, and the location of critical vessels and nerves to guide safe dissection.

surgical asepsis.definition: A technique that eliminates all microorganisms, including spores, from instruments and environments and maintains a sterile field to prevent infection during invasive procedures.

surgical fever.definition: A fever that develops after a surgical procedure, usually defined as a temperature of 38°C (100.4°F) or higher in the postoperative period; early fevers often reflect inflammation from surgery, while later fevers may indicate infection or other complications.

surgical field.definition: The area of the body that is exposed and prepared for an operation—the operative region where the incision and tissue manipulation occur—which is kept sterile with drapes and antiseptic preparation.

surgical gut.definition: An absorbable surgical suture made from natural animal gut (usually bovine or ovine collagen); provides temporary wound support but has variable absorption and strength and can cause more tissue reaction, and is largely replaced by synthetic absorbables; available as plain gut or chromic gut (treatment to slow absorption).

surgical menopause.definition: An abrupt onset of menopause caused by surgical removal of the ovaries (bilateral oophorectomy), resulting in immediate estrogen deficiency with vasomotor and other menopausal symptoms.

surgical microscope.definition: A specialized optical microscope used in surgery to provide high-magnification, high-illumination, stereoscopic visualization of small structures, enabling precise microsurgical dissection and manipulation.

surgical neck of humerus.definition: A narrow portion of the proximal humerus just distal to the head, marking the transition from the proximal epiphysis to the diaphysis; a common fracture site where the axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral vessels may be injured.

surgical pathology.definition: Subspecialty of pathology focused on the gross and microscopic examination of surgical specimens (biopsies and resections) to diagnose disease and guide patient management, frequently including intraoperative frozen-section consultations and ancillary tests.

surgical precautions.definition: Safety measures and protocols used to minimize risk of injury, infection, and complications during a surgical procedure and the immediate postoperative period. They include aseptic technique, proper patient positioning, sterile handling of instruments, anesthesia safety, intraoperative monitoring, infection prevention, hemostasis and wound care, pain management, and strategies to prevent thromboembolism.

surgical preparation.definition: A set of preoperative steps to ready the patient and the surgical field for an operation, including health assessment and optimization, fasting and medication management, skin antisepsis and sterile preparation, site marking, and coordination of anesthesia and prophylactic antibiotics as indicated.

surgical scrub.definition: A procedure for cleansing the hands and forearms with antimicrobial agents (soap and water or an alcohol-based antiseptic) before surgery to minimize skin bacteria and reduce the risk of postoperative infection.

surgical assistant.definition: A professional who assists the surgeon during operative procedures by providing exposure and tissue handling, maintaining hemostasis, and performing tasks such as suturing and wound closure under the surgeon's direction.

surgical diathermy.definition: A surgical technique that uses high-frequency electric current to generate heat in tissue, enabling cutting, coagulation (hemostasis), or destruction of tissue; typically delivered by an active electrode with a return (grounding) pad, and can be monopolar or bipolar (electrosurgery/electrocautery).

optic chiasma.definition: A structure at the base of the brain where the optic nerves partially cross (decussate): nasal retinal fibers cross to the opposite side while temporal fibers remain on the same side, forming the optic tracts that project to the lateral geniculate nucleus; located just above the pituitary stalk.

hypothalamic nucleus.definition: A discrete cluster of neuron cell bodies within the hypothalamus that acts as a functional regulatory center for autonomic and endocrine activity, coordinating hormone release through the pituitary and modulating homeostatic processes such as energy balance, temperature, thirst, hunger, circadian rhythms, and stress responses.

posterior pituitary.definition: The posterior portion of the pituitary gland that stores and releases vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone) and oxytocin, which are produced in the hypothalamus and transported along axons; release is controlled by neural signals and it does not synthesize these hormones.

seventh cervical vertebra.definition: Lowest vertebra of the cervical spine (C7), typically with a long, palpable spinous process (vertebra prominens) and a standard cervical vertebral body; it marks the transition to the thoracic spine and provides attachment for neck ligaments and muscles.

quadriceps femoris tendon.definition: A flat, broad tendon formed by the tendons of the quadriceps femoris muscle group; it inserts on the superior aspect of the patella and continues inferiorly as the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity, enabling knee extension.

articular cavity.definition: The space within a synovial joint capsule between the opposing articular surfaces, lined by the synovial membrane and filled with synovial fluid to lubricate and nourish the joint.

sectioning.definition: The process of cutting tissue into very thin sections for microscopic examination, typically after fixation and embedding (e.g., in paraffin) using a microtome.

oral surgery.definition: An operation or surgery in your mouth.

surgical shock.definition: An acute perioperative state of circulatory failure with inadequate tissue perfusion, usually caused by significant blood loss (hypovolemia) but can also result from anesthesia-related depression or sepsis.

surmontil.definition: A tricyclic antidepressant used to treat depressive disorders; it inhibits the reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin, and can have anticholinergic and sedative effects.

trimipramine.definition: A tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) used to treat major depressive disorder; a tertiary amine TCA with sedative and antihistaminic properties and inhibition of norepinephrine (and serotonin) reuptake, plus anticholinergic and alpha-adrenergic blocking effects.

mikulicz's aphthae.definition: A benign, self-limited form of aphthous stomatitis presenting in infancy or early childhood as small, shallow, painful ulcers on the oral mucosa (often the gingiva and buccal mucosa) that typically heal without scarring within 1–2 weeks.

periadenitis mucosa necrotica recurrens.definition: A recurrent inflammatory condition in which the mucosa surrounding a gland undergoes necrosis.

suturing.definition: The act of threading suture material through tissues to approximate wound edges and secure them for healing, typically to close surgical or traumatic wounds.

sutural ligament.definition: A fibrous connective tissue band that binds adjacent skull bones at a cranial suture; a type of syndesmosis that permits only limited movement and may ossify with age.

sutura dentata.definition: A cranial suture in which the margins of adjacent bones have tooth-like, interlocking projections (dentations), giving a toothed or dentate appearance.

sutura limbosa.definition: Likely a misspelling of a posterior cranial suture: a dense fibrous joint between the occipital bone and the parietal bones that allows skull growth during infancy and typically ossifies with age.

sutura serrata.definition: A cranial suture with interlocking, tooth-like (saw-toothed) margins between adjacent bones, forming a rigid, interdigitating joint.

simian virus 40.definition: A polyomavirus with a double-stranded DNA genome, nonenveloped, originally isolated from rhesus monkey kidney cells; capable of transforming cells in culture and inducing tumors in some animals, and widely used as a model to study viral oncogenesis; its role in human cancer remains unproven.

sv40.definition: A small, nonenveloped double-stranded DNA virus of the polyomavirus family that infects primates (notably rhesus monkeys); capable of transforming cells and inducing tumors in animals and historically identified as a contaminant of early polio vaccines; widely used as a research tool in molecular biology.

upper gi tract.definition: The portion of the digestive system that includes the mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, and the proximal part of the duodenum; it is responsible for ingestion, mechanical and chemical digestion, and propulsion of food into the small intestine.

motility disorders.definition: Motility disorders are conditions in which the coordinated muscle contractions and neural control of the gastrointestinal tract are impaired, leading to abnormal propulsion and transit of its contents.

neuropathies.definition: Disorders of the peripheral nervous system caused by damage to peripheral nerves, leading to sensory symptoms (numbness, tingling, pain), motor weakness, and/or autonomic dysfunction. They can be inherited or acquired and may result from diabetes, infections, toxins, vitamin deficiencies, autoimmune disease, or trauma.

anterior tonsillar pillars.definition: A mucosal fold (palatoglossal arch) extending from the soft palate to the side of the tongue, containing the palatoglossus muscle; forms the anterior boundary of the tonsillar fossa and, with the palatopharyngeal arch (posterior pillar), constitutes the palatine arches.

suspensory ligament of the lens.definition: A system of fibrous zonular fibers (zonules of Zinn) that attach the lens to the ciliary body, suspending the lens and transmitting the ciliary muscle’s tension to change lens shape during accommodation.

zonula ciliaris.definition: A ring of fibrous suspensory ligaments extending from the ciliary body to the lens capsule; it suspends the crystalline lens and transmits ciliary muscle tension to alter lens shape during accommodation.

sustentaculum tali.definition: A shelf-like medial projection of the calcaneus (heel bone) that supports the talus and forms part of the subtalar joint; the flexor hallucis longus tendon runs in a groove on its inferior surface.

sustentacular cells.definition: A type of supporting (nurse) cell that provides structural support and metabolic/nutritional support to adjacent specialized cells; in the olfactory epithelium they are tall columnar cells surrounding and maintaining olfactory receptor neurons, and in the testis the Sertoli cells serve a similar nourishing/regulatory role for developing germ cells.

sustentacular.definition: Serving as a support; providing structural and metabolic support to other cells, such as sustentacular (supporting) cells in sensory epithelia.

esophageal sphincter.definition: A ring of smooth muscle surrounding the gastroesophageal junction that maintains a high-pressure barrier to prevent reflux of gastric contents and relaxes to allow swallowing.

upper esophageal diverticula.definition: An upper esophageal diverticulum is a sac-like outpouching of mucosa and submucosa from the upper esophagus (hypopharynx), typically at or near the pharyngoesophageal junction and caused by pulsion from cricopharyngeal dysfunction. It may cause dysphagia, regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis, coughing, and aspiration; diagnosed by a barium swallow and treated with observation for mild cases or endoscopic/open diverticulectomy with cricopharyngeal myotomy in symptomatic patients.

swallowing.definition: The coordinated process by which a bolus is moved from the mouth through the oropharynx and esophagus into the stomach, comprising oral (voluntary), pharyngeal (involuntary), and esophageal (involuntary) phases.

esophageal phase.definition: The phase of swallowing in which a bolus is cleared from the esophagus to the stomach by coordinated esophageal peristalsis and relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter.

oral phase.definition: The voluntary stage of swallowing in which the bolus is formed and prepared in the mouth and then propelled posteriorly by the tongue toward the oropharynx; it may be subdivided into the oral preparatory phase (chewing and mixing with saliva) and the oral transport phase (tongue-driven propulsion), ending when the bolus reaches the oropharynx and triggers the pharyngeal phase.

pharyngeal phase.definition: A rapid, involuntary stage of swallowing in which the bolus is propelled from the oropharynx into the esophagus while protecting the airway: the larynx and hyoid rise, the epiglottis retroflexes to cover the laryngeal inlet, the soft palate elevates to seal the nasopharynx, the pharyngeal constrictors contract to push the bolus downward, and the upper esophageal sphincter relaxes to admit the bolus into the esophagus.

swallowing therapy.definition: A therapy program (usually conducted by a speech-language pathologist) to improve swallowing safety and efficiency in dysphagia, using targeted exercises to strengthen and coordinate swallowing muscles, compensatory strategies and maneuvers, posture adjustments, and, when needed, texture-modified diets.

schistosome dermatitis.definition: Pruritic, self-limited skin eruption caused by penetration of human skin by cercariae of schistosome parasites (usually from birds) during freshwater exposure; a zoonotic hypersensitivity reaction also known as cercarial dermatitis or swimmer's itch.

schistosome cercariae.definition: Free-swimming larval stage of schistosome trematodes released by freshwater snails; they swim with a forked tail and penetrate intact human skin, after which they shed their tail and become schistosomula that migrate to the venous system.

swan-ganz catheter.definition: A pulmonary artery catheter inserted via a central vein into the right heart and pulmonary artery for invasive hemodynamic monitoring; it measures pressures in the right atrium, right ventricle, and pulmonary artery, estimates left atrial pressure (via pulmonary capillary wedge pressure), and can compute cardiac output by thermodilution.

swan neck deformity.definition: A finger deformity in which the proximal interphalangeal joint is hyperextended and the distal interphalangeal joint is flexed, caused by imbalance or dysfunction of the finger extensor mechanism (often volar plate laxity or central slip injury), commonly seen with rheumatoid arthritis or finger trauma.

kidney tubules.definition: Tubular portions of the nephron in the kidney where glomerular filtrate is reabsorbed and wastes are secreted, helping form urine; include the proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule, and collecting ducts.

proximal interphalangeal joint.definition: A hinge-type synovial joint between the head of the proximal phalanx and the base of the middle phalanx of digits 2–5, permitting flexion and extension of the finger; stabilized by the volar plate and collateral ligaments, with the flexor digitorum superficialis crossing anteriorly. The thumb lacks this joint and has an interphalangeal joint between its proximal and distal phalanges.

distal interphalangeal joint.definition: A hinge-type synovial joint between the distal and middle phalanges of the fingers (digits 2–5), permitting flexion and extension of the fingertip; stabilized by collateral ligaments and the volar plate.

interphalangeal joint.definition: A hinge-type synovial joint between two adjacent phalanges in a digit, allowing flexion and extension (as in the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints of the fingers and toes).

convoluted tubule.definition: A twisted segment of a nephron tubule in the kidney (proximal or distal) where most reabsorption of water and solutes and some secretion occur during urine formation.

profundus tendon.definition: A tendon of the deep flexor muscles of the fingers that inserts on the distal phalanges and flexes the distal interphalangeal joints; it works with the superficial flexor tendons to bend the digits.

swift's disease.definition: I can’t find a widely recognized medical condition called “Swift’s disease” in standard references. Could you provide more context or alternate spelling (e.g., a different name, field, or the source you saw it in)? I can look it up with more detail.

barber's itch.definition: A fungal infection of the beard area (tinea barbae) caused by dermatophyte fungi, most commonly Trichophyton mentagrophytes or Microsporum species; it presents with inflamed, scaly plaques and broken hairs in the beard/mustache region and may be pruritic, potentially acquired from contaminated barber tools.

migratory ophthalmia.definition: An historical term for a relapsing conjunctivitis in which inflammatory lesions migrate across the conjunctival surface, producing intermittent redness and discharge.

metastatic ophthalmia.definition: Ocular involvement by malignant cells that have spread from a distant primary cancer, most often metastasizing to the choroid and causing visual symptoms or intraocular masses.

sylvius' aqueduct.definition: A narrow canal in the midbrain that connects the third ventricle to the fourth ventricle, allowing cerebrospinal fluid to flow between them.

sylvian aqueduct.definition: A narrow canal in the midbrain that connects the third ventricle to the fourth ventricle, enabling cerebrospinal fluid to flow between them.

sylvian fissure.definition: A deep groove on the lateral surface of the brain that separates the temporal lobe from the frontal and parietal lobes; also known as the lateral sulcus.

sylvian sulcus.definition: A major groove on the lateral surface of the cerebral hemisphere (also called the lateral sulcus or Sylvian fissure) that separates the temporal lobe from the frontal and parietal lobes; its depth contains the insular cortex.

sympathetic trunk.definition: A paired vertical chain of sympathetic ganglia running along each side of the vertebral column; it transmits preganglionic sympathetic fibers from spinal levels T1–L2 via white rami to synapse in the ganglia, with postganglionic fibers exiting via gray rami or splanchnic nerves to reach target organs, and it extends from the base of the skull to the coccyx.

sympathetic ganglion.definition: A ganglion in the sympathetic (autonomic) nervous system that houses the cell bodies of postganglionic neurons; receives synapses from preganglionic sympathetic fibers and provides postganglionic innervation to target organs.

sympathetic eye.definition: Eye innervated by the sympathetic nervous system; sympathetic stimulation causes pupil dilation (mydriasis) and eyelid elevation, while loss of this innervation can cause miosis and ptosis (as seen in Horner syndrome).

sympathetic nerve.definition: A nerve carrying fibers of the sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system, which mediates the body's fight-or-flight responses by regulating involuntary functions in target organs.

sympatholytic.definition: A drug or agent that inhibits the sympathetic nervous system, reducing its fight-or-flight effects by blocking adrenergic receptors or decreasing sympathetic outflow.

sympathomimetic amine.definition: A compound that mimics or enhances sympathetic nervous system activity by directly activating adrenergic receptors (α or β) or by increasing synaptic catecholamines (e.g., norepinephrine or epinephrine).

mephentermine.definition: A sympathomimetic vasopressor used to raise blood pressure in hypotensive states (e.g., during anesthesia or shock) by promoting release of norepinephrine and causing peripheral vasoconstriction. Common adverse effects include tachycardia, hypertension, and arrhythmias.

methoxamine.definition: A direct-acting alpha-1 adrenergic receptor agonist that causes peripheral vasoconstriction, increasing blood pressure; used to treat acute hypotension (e.g., during anesthesia or shock).

methoxyphenamine.definition: A synthetic phenethylamine derivative bearing a methoxy group on the aromatic ring; a sympathomimetic amine in the broader stimulant family, historically described as having stimulant effects but with limited or no current clinical use and minimal contemporary safety data.

protokylol.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. It may be a misspelling or a brand name. If you can share context (drug class, indication, or source), I can help locate or provide a definition.

terbutaline sulfate.definition: A beta-2 adrenergic agonist that relaxes smooth muscle and bronchodilates airways; used as a bronchodilator for reversible airway obstruction (e.g., asthma) and, in obstetrics, as a tocolytic to suppress preterm labor.

tetrahydrozoline.definition: A topical sympathomimetic vasoconstrictor (alpha-adrenergic agonist) used to relieve conjunctival redness and nasal congestion by constricting mucosal blood vessels; may cause systemic effects and rebound congestion with prolonged use.

tuaminoheptane.definition: Not a standard medical term; no established medical definition. It may refer to an amino-substituted heptane (an aliphatic primary amine with seven carbon atoms) used as a chemical reagent rather than a clinically used drug.

sweat test.definition: A diagnostic test to measure the chloride concentration in sweat after pilocarpine-induced sweating; elevated sweat chloride levels support a diagnosis of cystic fibrosis.

sweet localization method.definition: A technique used in gustation studies to map the perceived location of sweet-taste sensation by applying sweet stimuli to defined oral sites and recording the subject's localization.

sycosis vulgaris.definition: A chronic inflammatory infection of hair follicles in the beard area (sycosis barbae), usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus, presenting with papules, pustules, crusting, itching, and sometimes scarring.

beta2 receptor agonist.definition: A drug that selectively stimulates beta-2 adrenergic receptors, causing relaxation of airway smooth muscle and bronchodilation; used to treat bronchospasm in asthma and COPD.

intervertebral disks.definition: A fibrocartilaginous cushion between adjacent vertebrae in the spine that absorbs and distributes compressive loads and allows limited movement; it consists of an outer ring (annulus fibrosus) surrounding a gelatinous center (nucleus pulposus) and is avascular, receiving nutrients by diffusion from surrounding tissues.

sympodia.definition: A congenital condition in which two or more digits or limbs are fused into a single, continuous structure.

syndactylus.definition: A congenital condition in which two or more digits are fused together, by soft tissue or bone, resulting in webbing or complete fusion; commonly affects the hands or feet and may occur in isolation or as part of a syndrome. Also known as syndactyly.

syndactylia.definition: A congenital condition in which two or more digits are fused together, by soft tissue (simple syndactyly) or by bone (complex syndactyly), which can be partial or complete and may occur as an isolated anomaly or with other associated abnormalities.

syndactylism.definition: A congenital condition in which two or more digits (fingers or toes) are fused, either by soft tissue webbing or by bone fusion; may be isolated or part of a broader syndrome.

syndactylous.definition: Of or relating to syndactyly; describing digits that are fused (partial or complete) due to incomplete separation during embryonic development.

syndesmoma.definition: A rare neoplasm arising from ligamentous tissue of a joint (the syndesmosis); a tumor of a ligament.

syndesmography.definition: A radiologic imaging study of the distal tibiofibular syndesmosis used to assess the integrity of its ligaments and the amount of joint-space widening, typically in suspected syndesmotic injuries or high ankle sprains.

syndesmochorial.definition: A type of placentation in which the fetal chorion is in direct contact with the maternal uterine stroma (connective tissue) due to loss or absence of the maternal epithelium, resulting in fewer tissue layers between fetal and maternal blood than epitheliochorial placentation.

synclitism.definition: An alignment of the fetal head during labor in which the sagittal suture lies along the midline of the maternal pelvis, indicating a well-flexed head and normal cranial alignment for descent.

synaptic transmission.definition: The process by which a presynaptic neuron communicates with a postsynaptic cell across a synapse by releasing neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft, which bind to receptors to generate excitatory or inhibitory postsynaptic potentials.

ephapse.definition: A type of synaptic interaction where neighboring neurons influence each other through the extracellular electric field generated by neural activity, rather than via a conventional chemical synapse.

presynaptic terminal.definition: The distal end of a neuron's axon at a chemical synapse that contains neurotransmitter-filled synaptic vesicles and voltage-gated calcium channels; upon an action potential, Ca2+ influx triggers vesicle fusion and release of neurotransmitter into the synaptic cleft, triggering postsynaptic signaling.

postsynaptic neuron.definition: A neuron that receives neurotransmitter signals from a presynaptic neuron at a synapse; its postsynaptic membrane has receptors that convert the chemical signal into electrical changes (postsynaptic potentials, EPSPs or IPSPs) that influence the likelihood of firing.

receptor proteins.definition: Proteins that detect binding of signaling molecules (ligands) and translate that binding into a cellular response by initiating or modulating intracellular signaling pathways; they are typically located on the cell surface (membrane receptors) or inside the cell (intracellular receptors).

synaptic vesicles.definition: Small, membrane-bound organelles in the presynaptic terminal that store neurotransmitters and release them into the synaptic cleft via Ca2+-triggered exocytosis following an action potential.

synaptosome.definition: A pinched-off presynaptic nerve terminal obtained from brain tissue by homogenization and differential centrifugation, containing synaptic vesicles and the machinery for neurotransmitter release, used to study synaptic function in vitro.

synaptogenesis.definition: The formation of new synapses between neurons, enabling the establishment and remodeling of neural circuits; it involves growth of presynaptic terminals and postsynaptic specializations and occurs mainly during development but also with learning, experience, and recovery after injury.

syncytium.definition: A multinucleated cytoplasmic mass formed by the fusion of two or more cells; seen in skeletal muscle fibers and placental syncytiotrophoblast, and can also arise as multinucleated giant cells from viral-induced cell fusion.

syncytiotrophoblastic.definition: Relating to the syncytiotrophoblast, the multinucleated outer layer of placental villi formed by fusion of cytotrophoblasts; essential for implantation, invasion into maternal tissue, and production of pregnancy hormones such as hCG.

plasmidotrophoblast.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries; may be a misspelling or an obscure term. If you can share context or the source, I can help. If you meant cytotrophoblast or syncytiotrophoblast, I can provide concise definitions for those.

monocephalus.definition: A rare congenital anomaly in which two bodies are conjoined to a single head, resulting in two torsos sharing one skull; a form of conjoined twinning.

syncephalus.definition: Not a standard medical term in major dictionaries; if used, it would refer to a rare congenital condition in which two heads are fused or joined to a single trunk, a form of craniopagus (conjoined) twins.

sirennomelus.definition: Not a recognized medical term; no standard medical definition is available in trusted dictionaries—please verify the spelling or provide context.

monopodial symmelia.definition: A rare congenital limb malformation in which two neighboring limbs are fused into a single limb along a common axis, resulting in a blended extremity with joined skeletal and soft-tissue structures.

uromelus.definition: No widely recognized medical term "uromelus" exists in standard references. It may be a misspelling. If you meant the amphibian grouping "urodele" (order Urodela, which includes salamanders and newts), that refers to an order of amphibians characterized by a tailed body and, in many species, an aquatic larval stage. If you have context or a different spelling, please share it for a precise definition.

fetuses.definition: Unborn human offspring; the developing fetus in the uterus from the end of the embryonic period (about 8–10 weeks after conception) until birth, during which organs mature.

fet fetus.definition: An unborn baby, from 12 weeks of age to birth.

synchondroses.definition: A cartilaginous joint in which hyaline cartilage unites two bones; typically a temporary growth-plate joint in developing long bones, but present in some skull base joints that ossify with age.

synchilia.definition: A congenital fusion of the lips (lip adhesion), in which the upper and lower lips are joined, leading to restricted mouth opening and potential feeding or speech difficulties; may occur isolated or with other craniofacial anomalies.

syncheilia.definition: A rare congenital condition in which portions of the upper and lower lips are fused by mucous membrane (lip synechia), resulting in restricted mouth opening; treated by surgical separation of the adhesions.

synchronous intermittent mandatory venti.definition: A mode of mechanical ventilation in which the ventilator delivers a preset number of breaths synchronized to the patient’s spontaneous inspiratory efforts; between these mandatory breaths, the patient may breathe spontaneously (with no or limited pressure support), allowing both controlled ventilation and patient-initiated breaths.

simv.definition: A mode of mechanical ventilation where the machine delivers a set number of breaths in synchrony with the patient’s efforts, while allowing the patient to breathe spontaneously between mandatory breaths.

synchronous.definition: Occurring at the same time; synchronized or temporally coordinated.

synalar.definition: A brand name for fluocinolone acetonide, a synthetic topical corticosteroid used to treat inflammatory and pruritic skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis, and psoriasis.

symphyses.definition: A type of cartilaginous joint in which the bones are joined by a pad of fibrocartilage, permitting only slight movement (amphiarthrosis).

symphyseal angle.definition: An anatomical angle at the mandibular symphysis: the angle formed by the two halves of the mandible at the midline (the chin), reflecting the contour of the chin and used in orthodontic and craniofacial assessments. If you meant the pelvic (pubic) symphysis vicinity, specify and I can define that as well.

premenstrual syndrome (pms).definition: A cluster of physical, emotional, and behavioral symptoms that occur in the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle before menstruation and resolve after the onset of menses, typically beginning 1–2 weeks before menses and improving after the period starts.

maculopapular eruption.definition: A widespread eruption consisting of flat red macules and small raised papules on the skin, usually erythematous and pruritic, often drug-related or viral in origin.

syndesmophyte.definition: A bony outgrowth that forms within a spinal ligament and bridges two adjacent vertebral bodies, typically seen in ankylosing spondylitis.

siadh.definition: A condition in which excess antidiuretic hormone (vasopressin) secretion causes water retention, resulting in dilutional hyponatremia with low serum osmolality and inappropriately concentrated urine; patients are typically euvolemic.

osmoreceptors.definition: Specialized brain sensors in the hypothalamus (e.g., OVLT and SFO) that detect changes in body fluid osmolarity; when osmolarity rises, they stimulate thirst and release of vasopressin (ADH) to conserve water.

normal saline solution.definition: A sterile isotonic solution of sodium chloride at 0.9% w/v (about 9 g NaCl per liter) in water, with osmolality similar to extracellular fluid; used for intravenous fluid therapy, hydration, medication delivery, and wound irrigation.

urine osmolality.definition: A measure of the urine’s solute concentration, expressed in milliosmoles per kilogram of water (mOsm/kg); it reflects the kidney’s ability to concentrate or dilute urine and is influenced by hydration status and antidiuretic hormone, with higher values indicating concentrated urine and lower values indicating dilute urine.

syndrome x.definition: An historical term used to describe two conditions: metabolic syndrome—insulin resistance with obesity, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and impaired glucose tolerance; and cardiac syndrome X—angina with normal coronary arteries on angiography, usually due to microvascular dysfunction.

hyperinsulinemia.definition: Abnormally high levels of insulin in the bloodstream, usually due to insulin resistance or compensatory pancreatic beta-cell hyperactivity, commonly seen with obesity, metabolic syndrome, and type 2 diabetes.

catecholamine levels.definition: The concentration of catecholamines (epinephrine, norepinephrine, and dopamine) in blood or urine, reflecting sympathetic nervous system activity and used to evaluate conditions such as pheochromocytoma or other catecholamine-secreting disorders, as well as to monitor certain therapies.

synostosis.definition: A fusion of two or more bones by bony tissue, resulting in a single bone and elimination of the normal joint space, often limiting motion; can be congenital or acquired (e.g., premature fusion of skull sutures or after injury).

synostotic joint.definition: A joint in which adjacent bones are united by bone tissue (synostosis), resulting in a rigid, immovable articulation with no joint cavity.

synovia.definition: The viscous, clear fluid inside synovial (diarthrodial) joints that lubricates the joint, nourishes articular cartilage, and helps absorb shock; produced by the synovial membrane.

synovial chondromatosis.definition: A rare benign disorder in which the synovial membrane undergoes metaplasia to form cartilaginous nodules that detach into the joint as loose bodies, most often affecting the knee and causing pain, swelling, and mechanical symptoms; it can be primary (idiopathic) or secondary to other joint disease, and is treated with removal of loose bodies and synovectomy.
