synovialoma.definition: A tumor derived from synovial tissue (the lining of joints, tendon sheaths, and bursae); the term is not widely standardized and is often used to refer to synovial sarcoma, a malignant soft-tissue tumor typically arising near joints, especially in young adults, with biphasic or monophasic histology and treatment usually involving surgical resection with possible radiation and chemotherapy.

synovial tendon sheath.definition: A tubular, synovial-lined sheath that surrounds a tendon as it runs through a fibrous tunnel or pulley system, secreting synovial fluid to lubricate the tendon and reduce friction during movement.

synovial bursa.definition: A small fluid-filled sac lined by a synovial membrane that cushions and lubricates movement by reducing friction between tendons, muscles, and bones around a joint.

synovectomy.definition: Surgical removal of the synovial membrane that lines the joints.

synophthalmia.definition: A congenital anomaly in which the orbits fuse to form a single median eye; a form of cyclopia often associated with holoprosencephaly and severe midline brain defects.

synophylate.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard dictionaries; there is no established medical definition. It may be a misspelling or a brand/trade name. If you can share context (drug, condition, source) or the correct spelling, I can provide a precise definition.

syntactic aphasia.definition: A language disorder in which grammatical processing (syntax) is impaired, leading to difficulty producing and understanding sentences with correct word order and inflection; speech is often telegraphic and may omit function words, while lexical meaning remains relatively preserved.

syntax.definition: In linguistics, the set of rules that govern how words are combined to form sentences and phrases.

syntaxic.definition: Not a standard medical term; in general usage, syntaxic would refer to relating to syntax—the arrangement of words or morphemes in language—and has no established medical definition.

synteny.definition: The conservation of blocks of gene order on chromosomes between related species, reflecting shared ancestry; genes within these blocks tend to remain on the same chromosome and retain their relative order.

synthermal.definition: Not a standard medical term; etymology suggests it denotes events or processes that occur at the same temperature (syn- = together, thermal = heat).

syngeneic.definition: Relating to tissue or organ transfer between genetically identical individuals (such as identical twins or inbred animals), in which donor and recipient share an identical or nearly identical genome, resulting in minimal immune rejection.

syngenesis.definition: An obsolete embryology term for the development of an organism from a single fertilized egg (zygote) through successive cell divisions.

synpolydactyly.definition: A congenital limb malformation in which digits are fused (syndactyly) and one or more extra digits are present (polydactyly), most often affecting the hands and feet; typically inherited in an autosomal dominant fashion and associated with HOXD13 mutations.

hutchinson's triad.definition: A triad of findings in congenital syphilis: interstitial keratitis, Hutchinson teeth (notched incisors), and sensorineural (eighth-nerve) deafness.

snuffles.definition: An informal term for nasal congestion and discharge due to an upper respiratory infection (often a common cold); in veterinary medicine, it describes chronic nasal discharge in rabbits.

tertiary syphilis.definition: A late stage of untreated syphilis that occurs years after initial infection, characterized by multiform manifestations including granulomatous gummas, cardiovascular involvement (such as aortitis with aneurysm), and neurosyphilis (tabes dorsalis or general paresis).

syphilitic dementia.definition: A late manifestation of neurosyphilis characterized by progressive dementia and psychiatric/behavioral changes (often with mood disturbances and psychosis), reflecting chronic brain inflammation from Treponema pallidum; historically called general paresis of the insane.

syphilitic fever.definition: A fever associated with syphilis infection, typically occurring during secondary syphilis as part of systemic dissemination of Treponema pallidum; may be accompanied by malaise, headache, generalized lymphadenopathy, and mucocutaneous or constitutional symptoms, and usually resolves with appropriate antibiotic therapy.

syphilitic heart disease.definition: Aortic involvement in tertiary syphilis due to syphilitic aortitis (endarteritis of the vasa vasorum) of the ascending aorta, leading to dilation of the aortic root/ascending aorta with aortic regurgitation and potential aneurysm.

syphilitic endocarditis.definition: A form of endocarditis in tertiary syphilis characterized by chronic aortitis with obliterative endarteritis of the vasa vasorum, leading to dilation of the aortic root and secondary aortic insufficiency.

syphilitic retinopathy.definition: Retinal inflammation associated with systemic syphilis, due to Treponema pallidum, presenting as retinitis and retinal vasculitis (often with concurrent chorioretinitis), which can threaten vision if untreated.

cardiac valves.definition: Structures within the heart that regulate unidirectional blood flow by opening and closing in response to pressure changes during the cardiac cycle; they consist of two atrioventricular valves (mitral and tricuspid) and two semilunar valves (aortic and pulmonary) and function to prevent backflow and maintain efficient circulation.

dark field microscopy.definition: A microscopy method that illuminates the specimen with oblique light so that only light scattered by the specimen enters the objective, producing a bright image on a dark background and enabling visualization of living, unstained, transparent specimens (often motile bacteria and spirochetes).

bacteriological study.definition: A laboratory analysis of a specimen to detect, identify, and characterize bacteria, often including culture, staining, microscopic examination, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

serological tests.definition: Tests that detect antibodies to pathogens or antigens from pathogens in a patient’s serum (or other body fluids) to diagnose current or past infection, immune responses, or immune status. Examples include ELISA, Western blot, agglutination assays, immunofluorescence, and rapid immunochromatographic tests.

wassermann test.definition: An old serologic test for syphilis that detects non-treponemal antibodies (reagin) in serum by complement fixation against a cardiolipin-lecithin-cholesterol antigen; largely replaced by modern treponemal tests.

benzathine penicillin.definition: A long-acting injectable form of penicillin G that provides prolonged penicillin levels for about 2–4 weeks and is used to treat syphilis and to prevent rheumatic fever.

synthroid.definition: A brand-name synthetic form of the thyroid hormone levothyroxine (T4) used to treat hypothyroidism and to suppress thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in certain thyroid disorders.

syntocinon.definition: A brand-name form of oxytocin used to induce or augment labor and to prevent or treat postpartum hemorrhage by stimulating uterine contractions.

synthetic insulin.definition: Insulin produced through recombinant DNA technology in microorganisms to yield human insulin or insulin analogs; used to treat diabetes mellitus by replacing deficient endogenous insulin.

syrup of ipecac.definition: A preparation from the root of the ipecac plant containing the alkaloids emetine and cephaeline; an emetic formerly used to induce vomiting in cases of poisoning.

syringectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove a syrinx, a fluid-filled cavity within the spinal cord or brainstem.

syringobulbia.definition: A syrinx (fluid-filled cavity) that extends into the brainstem (bulbar region, especially the medulla), causing brainstem dysfunction and cranial nerve deficits.

syringomeningocele.definition: A rare spinal condition in which a syrinx (a CSF-filled cavity within the spinal cord) communicates with or extends into a meningocele (a protrusion of the meninges through a vertebral defect), forming a single CSF-filled cavity contiguous with the meningocele.

syringomyelocele.definition: A congenital spinal dysraphism in which a cavity within the spinal cord (a syrinx) communicates with a cerebrospinal fluid–filled sac that protrudes through a defect in the vertebral column (a meningocele), forming a cystic lesion containing CSF.

syingoencephalomyelia.definition: A syrinx (fluid-filled cavity) that extends from the spinal cord upward into intracranial structures (the brain and brainstem), i.e., syringomyelia with cranial/encephalic involvement. It can cause combined spinal and cranial neurologic deficits and is often linked to disturbed CSF dynamics, sometimes associated with Chiari malformation; treatment typically aims to relieve CSF flow obstruction or drain/decompress the syrinx.

morbilliform rash.definition: A diffuse erythematous maculopapular eruption that resembles measles (measles-like), typically spreading from the trunk to the limbs and often caused by drugs or viral infections.

condylomata lata.definition: Flat, broad-based, moist, gray-white plaques of secondary syphilis, typically located on the genitals and other warm, moist skin or mucous membranes; highly infectious due to abundant Treponema pallidum.

reciprocal inhibition.definition: Neuromuscular mechanism in which contraction of one muscle leads to inhibition of its antagonist, enabling smooth movement. It is mediated by Ia inhibitory interneurons in the spinal cord that reduce the antagonist's alpha motor neuron activity.

immunoblastic proliferation.definition: Proliferation of immunoblasts—enlarged, activated lymphocytes (typically B cells) with prominent nucleoli and abundant basophilic cytoplasm—reflecting an active immune response or a neoplastic lymphoid proliferation such as immunoblastic lymphoma.

breathing difficulty.definition: A subjective sensation of breathing discomfort or breathlessness (dyspnea) arising from inadequate oxygen delivery or carbon dioxide removal, commonly due to cardiopulmonary disease or physiologic stress; can be acute or chronic and range from mild to life-threatening.

butterfly rash.definition: A malar rash: a facial erythematous eruption over the cheeks and nasal bridge, typically sparing the nasolabial folds, commonly associated with systemic lupus erythematosus and often photosensitive.

topical steroids.definition: A class of corticosteroid medications applied to the skin to reduce inflammation and itching in dermatologic conditions; they vary in potency from low to very high, and local side effects can include skin thinning, stretch marks, pigment changes, and an increased risk of infection with prolonged use.

antimalarial drugs.definition: Drugs used to prevent or treat malaria by killing or inhibiting the growth of Plasmodium parasites in humans; used for chemoprophylaxis and for acute treatment, and include several classes such as chloroquine, quinine/quinidine, artemisinin derivatives, mefloquine, primaquine, pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine, and atovaquone-proguanil.

disseminated lupus erythematosus.definition: Not a distinct, widely recognized disease entity; a nonstandard term used to describe lupus with extensive involvement—typically systemic lupus erythematosus affecting multiple organ systems or widely disseminated discoid (cutaneous) lupus lesions.

systemic mycosis.definition: A systemic fungal infection in which fungi disseminate from the primary site to involve multiple organ systems, usually acquired by inhalation of spores and caused by pathogens such as Histoplasma, Coccidioides, Blastomyces, Paracoccidioides, and Cryptococcus; disease ranges from asymptomatic or mild to life‑threatening disseminated illness, diagnosed by culture, histopathology, and antigen/antibody testing, and treated with systemic antifungal therapy guided by organism and severity.

systemic onset juvenile rheumatoid arthr.definition: A form of juvenile idiopathic arthritis presenting with daily fevers, a transient salmon-colored rash, and arthritis in one or more joints, with systemic inflammatory features such as hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy; often with elevated inflammatory markers. Also known as Still's disease.

coronary veins.definition: Venous vessels that drain deoxygenated blood from the myocardium and return it to the right atrium, primarily via the coronary sinus; some veins drain directly into the right atrium.

taboparesis.definition: Not a recognized medical term; it may be a misspelling or confusion with tabes dorsalis (neurosyphilis causing sensory ataxia and lancinating pains) or with general paresis (paralytic neurosyphilis with cognitive/psychiatric decline and motor symptoms).

taboparalysis.definition: A historical/obsolete term describing paralysis associated with tabes dorsalis (neurosyphilis), referring to motor weakness due to late syphilitic involvement of the spinal cord.

tachyarrhythmia.definition: A rapid heart rhythm caused by abnormal electrical activity in the heart; an umbrella term for fast heart rhythms (tachycardias) typically defined as a heart rate over 100 beats per minute, arising from atrial, AV nodal, or ventricular tissue and can be regular or irregular.

tabetic gait.definition: A high-stepping, broad-based gait due to loss of proprioception in the lower limbs (sensory ataxia) from dorsal column degeneration, classically seen in tabes dorsalis; features include stamping of the feet, foot slapping, and a positive Romberg sign.

tabetic crisis.definition: An acute exacerbation of tabes dorsalis (neurosyphilis) marked by sudden, severe lancinating pains in the limbs or trunk (often described as lightning pains), frequently accompanied by worsened ataxia and autonomic symptoms.

retinal damage.definition: Damage to the retina, the light-sensitive tissue lining the back of the eye, resulting from trauma, ischemia, inflammation, degenerative diseases, or toxic exposure, often causing blurred vision or visual field loss and potentially permanent vision impairment depending on the extent and location of injury.

posterior columns.definition: Two dorsal white‑matter tracts in the spinal cord (fasciculus gracilis and fasciculus cuneatus) that carry fine touch, vibration, and proprioception from the body to the brain; they ascend ipsilaterally and cross in the medulla to form the medial lemniscus.

posterior roots.definition: The posterior (dorsal) root of a spinal nerve is the afferent sensory root that transmits sensory information from peripheral receptors into the spinal cord; its dorsal root ganglion contains the cell bodies of the first-order sensory neurons.

taeniasis.definition: An intestinal parasitic infection caused by adult tapeworms of the genus Taenia (primarily Taenia saginata or Taenia solium) acquired by ingestion of undercooked or raw beef or pork containing cysticerci; often asymptomatic but may cause mild abdominal pain, nausea, or weight loss; diagnosed by stool examination for eggs or proglottids; treated with praziquantel or niclosamide.

cestoda.definition: A class of parasitic flatworms (tapeworms) in the phylum Platyhelminthes; intestinal endoparasites with a scolex for attachment and a segmented body (strobila) made of proglottids, lacking a true digestive tract and absorbing nutrients across the tegument, with hermaphroditic reproductive organs; life cycles typically involve one or more intermediate hosts.

tamm-horsfall protein.definition: A renal tubular glycoprotein produced by the epithelial cells of the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle and secreted into urine; it is the most abundant protein in normal urine and is thought to play a role in innate urinary tract defense by binding bacteria and inhibiting bacterial adhesion, as well as helping prevent calcium crystallization and stone formation by forming a gel-like matrix in urine.

tactile fremitus.definition: A palpable vibration transmitted to the chest wall when the patient vocalizes, assessed by palpation; normally symmetric, with increased vibration over consolidated lung tissue and decreased vibration with pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or obesity.

tactile amnesia.definition: Not a widely recognized clinical term; describes impairment of tactile memory—the inability to recall or recognize previously felt textures or objects despite intact tactile sensation; reflects dysfunction in memory encoding or retrieval for touch rather than sensory perception, and is distinct from tactile agnosia, which is a failure to identify objects by touch with preserved sensation.

tactile anesthesia.definition: Loss of tactile sensation (touch) in a defined area of skin, typically resulting from nerve blockade, nerve injury, or neuropathy.

tactile hallucination.definition: A false tactile perception without external stimulus, such as crawling, tingling, or burning sensations on the skin.

tactile hyperesthesia.definition: An abnormal increase in sensitivity to touch, where ordinary tactile stimuli are perceived as excessively intense or painful (allodynia); may occur after nerve injury, neuropathy, inflammation, or central sensitization.

tagamet.definition: A histamine H2-receptor antagonist that decreases gastric acid secretion by blocking H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells; used to treat peptic ulcers, GERD, and gastritis; commonly well tolerated but can cause headaches or dizziness and may interact with other drugs or cause rare antiandrogenic effects.

floppy iris syndrome.definition: A cataract-surgery complication in which the iris is abnormally flaccid and billows with intraocular fluid forces, making the pupil difficult to maintain and increasing the risk of iris prolapse and posterior capsule rupture; strongly associated with preoperative use of alpha-1A adrenergic receptor antagonists (notably tamsulosin) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.

color vision changes.definition: Changes in color vision are alterations in the ability to perceive colors or discriminate hues, which may be congenital (color vision deficiency) or acquired from retinal or optic nerve disease, metabolic disorders, or exposure to certain medications.

cardiovascular collapse.definition: An abrupt failure of the cardiovascular system leading to inadequate tissue perfusion and hemodynamic instability (shock), which can progress to cardiac arrest and requires immediate resuscitation.

sudden death.definition: An unexpected natural death, typically occurring within a short time (usually within 1 hour of symptom onset or within 24 hours of last being seen alive), most often due to cardiac causes but can result from noncardiac etiologies.

tamsulosin.definition: A drug used to treat symptoms of an enlarged prostate gland. It relieves constriction of the urethra and improves urine flow by relaxing the smooth muscle tissues in the capsule that surrounds the prostate. Unlike other drugs in this class, tamsulosin does not decrease blood pressure.

axillary tail.definition: An extension of the breast's glandular tissue and ducts into the axillary (armpit) region, forming part of the breast known as the tail of Spence.

talocalcaneonavicular joint.definition: A three-bone synovial joint between the talus, calcaneus, and navicular bones of the foot; forms part of the transverse tarsal joint and allows movements of the talus relative to the calcaneus and navicular (inversion/eversion), stabilized by surrounding ligaments such as the plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament.

talocalcaneonavicular.definition: A joint formed by the articulation of the talus with the calcaneus and navicular bones; part of the hindfoot subtalar complex enabling inversion and eversion of the foot.

talocrural.definition: Pertaining to the ankle joint formed by the distal tibia and fibula with the talus; a hinge joint that permits dorsiflexion and plantarflexion.

talofibular.definition: Relating to the talus (ankle bone) and the fibula; used to describe structures that connect or are associated with these two bones, particularly ligaments between the talus and fibula.

talipes calcaneovalgus.definition: A foot deformity in which the ankle is dorsiflexed (calcaneal) and the hindfoot is everted (valgus), commonly present at birth and typically flexible, often improving with stretching, casting, or observation rather than surgery.

talipes calcaneovarus.definition: A congenital deformity of the foot in which the hindfoot is inverted (varus) with the foot positioned in a dorsiflexed (calcaneal) position, a variant of clubfoot.

talipes equinus.definition: A deformity in which the foot is held in plantar flexion at the ankle (toes pointing downward) due to tight calf muscles or Achilles tendon, resulting in limited or absent ability to dorsiflex; commonly seen as part of clubfoot.

talipes varus.definition: A deformity of the foot in which the hindfoot is inverted (turned inward) at the ankle; hindfoot varus, often seen in congenital clubfoot.

carotid arteries.definition: Two main arteries in the neck that supply blood to the brain, face, and neck. Each side has a common carotid artery that bifurcates into the internal carotid (supplying the brain) and the external carotid (suppling the face and neck).

brachiocephalic arteritis.definition: Inflammation of the brachiocephalic (innominate) artery, a large-vessel vasculitis that can occur with systemic diseases such as giant cell arteritis or Takayasu arteritis and may cause stenosis, occlusion, or aneurysm with head, neck, or upper-extremity symptoms.

martorell’s syndrome.definition: A rare ischemic cutaneous ulcer of the lower leg caused by hypertensive arteriolopathy: painful, well-demarcated ulcers in patients with long-standing hypertension (often with diabetes), resulting from hyaline arteriolosclerosis of cutaneous arterioles and leading to chronic skin ischemia.

reversed coarctation.definition: Not a standard medical term; when used, it generally refers to a coarctation of the aorta with retrograde (reversed) flow in the descending aorta, typically due to collateral vessels or ductal-dependent circulation rather than forward systemic flow across the narrowed segment.

transient paraplegia.definition: A temporary loss of movement in both legs that resolves within minutes to hours, caused by transient dysfunction or ischemia of the spinal cord rather than a lasting injury.

transient blindness.definition: Temporary loss of vision that resolves completely within seconds to minutes, often due to transient retinal ischemia (amaurosis fugax) or migraine with aura, and may indicate underlying vascular or neurologic disease.

troleandomycin.definition: A macrolide antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit.

tangentiality.definition: A thought-disorder in which speech digresses from the topic, with responses that are loosely related or unrelated and fail to return to the original point.

tapotement.definition: Rhythmic percussion or tapping of the body's soft tissues with the edge of the hand or with cupped hands, used in massage to stimulate nerves, improve circulation, and promote muscle relaxation; one of the core techniques of Swedish massage.

tarceva.definition: A brand-name cancer drug; the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor erlotinib, taken orally to treat certain cancers such as advanced non-small cell lung cancer and pancreatic cancer (with gemcitabine).

ulnar nerve palsy.definition: Weakness or paralysis of the intrinsic hand muscles supplied by the ulnar nerve, often with clawing of the fourth and fifth digits and sensory loss on the medial hand and little finger; caused by injury or compression of the ulnar nerve at the elbow or wrist.

posterior tibial nerve.definition: A branch of the sciatic nerve that descends through the posterior compartment of the leg, supplying motor innervation to most posterior leg muscles (e.g., gastrocnemius, soleus, plantaris, tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus, flexor hallucis longus) and, after passing behind the medial malleolus, divides into the medial and lateral plantar nerves to provide motor and sensory innervation to the sole of the foot; it can be compressed in tarsal tunnel syndrome.

nerve transplant.definition: A surgical repair of a damaged peripheral nerve by transplanting a nerve graft (autograft or allograft) to bridge a nerve gap and allow regrowth of axons to restore motor and/or sensory function.

target organ.definition: An organ or tissue in the body that a drug, toxin, or treatment is intended to affect to produce its therapeutic or adverse effect.

hepatic lesion.definition: A localized area of abnormal liver tissue detected by imaging or biopsy; may reflect benign processes (e.g., cyst, hemangioma, focal nodular hyperplasia), inflammatory or infectious conditions (e.g., abscess), or malignant tumors (e.g., hepatocellular carcinoma).

transposition of the aorta and pulmonary.word: transposition of the aorta and pulmonary artery
transposition of the aorta and pulmonary.definition: A congenital heart defect in which the aorta arises from the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery from the left ventricle, producing parallel circulations; survival depends on mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood (via a septal defect or patent ductus arteriosus), with definitive repair usually by arterial switch operation in infancy.

taussig-bing syndrome.definition: A subtype of double-outlet right ventricle in which both great arteries arise from the right ventricle and the ventricular septal defect is subpulmonary, producing transposition‑like physiology.

tarsal tunnel syndrome.definition: A compressive neuropathy of the tibial nerve or its branches as they pass through the tarsal tunnel behind the medial malleolus, causing numbness, tingling, and pain in the sole or heel, sometimes with weakness of intrinsic foot muscles; symptoms worsen with standing or activity and may improve with rest.

tarsoclasis.definition: A surgical procedure in which one or more tarsal bones are deliberately fractured (osteoclasis) to correct a deformity of the foot, such as rigid flatfoot or hindfoot malalignment.

tarsomalacia.definition: Softening of the tarsal bones (the ankle and hindfoot), typically due to defective bone mineralization such as osteomalacia or rickets; may cause pain, deformity, and instability in the foot.

tarsometatarsal.definition: Relating to the tarsus and metatarsus; the joints between the tarsal bones and the bases of the metatarsal bones in the foot (the tarsometatarsal joints, e.g., Lisfranc joints).

tarsophalangeal reflex.definition: Not a standard neurological reflex name; there is no widely accepted definition in medical literature. It may be a misnomer for a known foot reflex such as the plantar reflex or the ankle (Achilles) jerk.

tarsorrhaphy.definition: A surgical procedure in which the eyelids are partially sutured or fused to narrow the palpebral fissure and protect the cornea, often to promote healing in exposure keratopathy or similar ocular surface conditions.

tarsus.definition: A set of seven irregular bones in the foot (the tarsal bones) that forms the ankle and the proximal part of the foot; includes the talus, calcaneus, navicular, cuboid, and the medial, intermediate, and lateral cuneiform bones.

tarsal cartilage.definition: The cartilage covering the articular surfaces of the tarsal bones; typically hyaline cartilage that cushions joints, reduces friction, and enables smooth movement between the tarsal bones and with adjacent foot and ankle bones.

stye.definition: An acute purulent infection of the eyelid margin, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus, presenting as a painful, red, swollen nodule at the eyelid (external hordeolum at a lash follicle or internal hordeolum in a meibomian gland). It is typically managed with warm compresses and good lid hygiene, with topical antibiotics if indicated.

bacterial infection.definition: An infection caused by pathogenic bacteria invading and multiplying in the body, leading to tissue injury and an inflammatory immune response; symptoms and severity vary by organism and site.

thrombocytopenia-absent radius syndrome.definition: A rare congenital disorder characterized by thrombocytopenia present at birth and bilateral radial ray defects (often with absent radius) while thumbs are usually present; thrombocytopenia typically improves with age and may be associated with additional skeletal or cardiac anomalies.

tar syndrome.definition: A rare congenital disorder characterized by thrombocytopenia (low platelet counts) and bilateral absence or hypoplasia of the radius with an intact ulna, often with hypoplastic or absent thumbs and other limb abnormalities; affected individuals have a bleeding tendency in infancy and require supportive care (e.g., platelet transfusions during bleeding episodes), with genetic associations including 1q21.1 microdeletion and RBM8A regulatory variants.

glycogen storage disease type vii.definition: An autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by deficiency of muscle phosphofructokinase (PFK-1), leading to impaired glycolysis in skeletal muscle and erythrocytes. It presents with exercise‑induced muscle cramps, weakness, and myoglobinuria after strenuous activity, and may be associated with hemolytic anemia.

tasigna.definition: A brand-name tyrosine kinase inhibitor (nilotinib) used to treat BCR-ABL–positive leukemias, such as chronic myeloid leukemia and Philadelphia chromosome–positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia; it inhibits the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase.

tavist.definition: Definition not found in standard medical dictionaries. It may be a misspelling, a brand name, or a non-medical term. If you can share context or the correct spelling, I can check again.

taxol.definition: Taxol is the brand name for paclitaxel, a chemotherapy drug that stabilizes microtubules, preventing their disassembly and thereby inhibiting cell division to promote cancer cell death; used to treat ovarian, breast, non-small cell lung, and other cancers; originally derived from the Pacific yew tree.

tetanus antitoxin.definition: A preparation of antibodies against the tetanus toxin (tetanus immune globulin) used to provide immediate passive immunity by neutralizing circulating toxin; given after tetanus exposure or in high‑risk wounds, often with wound care and subsequent vaccination to induce active immunity.

target cell.definition: A cell that bears receptors for a specific hormone, drug, or antibody and is the primary site of action of that molecule.

discocyte.definition: A red blood cell with a biconcave, disc-shaped morphology and a central pallor; the normal morphology of human erythrocytes, optimized for gas exchange and deformability.

taste bud.definition: A sensory organ on the tongue consisting of gustatory receptor cells within a specialized epithelial cluster that forms a taste pore; it detects tastants and transmits gustatory information to the brain via the gustatory nerves.

taste papilla.definition: Small projections of the tongue epithelium that house taste buds and participate in gustatory perception; main types include fungiform (anterior), circumvallate (posterior), and foliate (lateral), while filiform papillae contain no taste buds.

gustatory cell.definition: A taste receptor cell located in a taste bud that detects tastants (chemical stimuli) and transduces them into neural signals by releasing neurotransmitter to gustatory afferent nerve fibers.

taste pore.definition: A small opening at the surface of a taste bud through which tastants contact the gustatory receptor cells via their microvilli.

root of tongue.definition: The posterior portion of the tongue that lies in the oropharynx, behind the terminal sulcus; it is attached to the hyoid bone and pharyngeal walls, is covered by mucosa containing the lingual tonsils, and forms the boundary between the oral cavity and the oropharynx.

eyelids.definition: Two movable folds of skin and muscle that cover and protect the eyeball; they blink to spread tears and keep the surface moist while helping regulate light entry.

palpebral artery.definition: A small artery that supplies the eyelids (palpebrae); it arises from the ophthalmic artery and contributes to the arterial network nourishing the eyelid skin, muscles, and conjunctiva.

sachs disease.definition: A fatal autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of beta-hexosaminidase A, leading to accumulation of GM2 ganglioside in neuronal lysosomes and progressive neurodegeneration; typically presents in infancy with developmental delay, hypotonia, and a cherry-red macula, with death usually in early childhood.

optic nerve head.definition: A region at the fundus where retinal ganglion cell axons converge to form the optic nerve; also called the optic disc. It is the site where vessels enter and exit the eye, contains no photoreceptors, and has a physiologic cup visible on ophthalmoscopy.

tazarotene.definition: A synthetic topical retinoid (third-generation) used to treat acne vulgaris and plaque psoriasis; it is a prodrug converted to tazarotenic acid that activates retinoic acid receptors to normalize keratinocyte differentiation. Common adverse effects include skin irritation and photosensitivity; contraindicated in pregnancy due to teratogenicity.

tazobactam.definition: A β-lactamase inhibitor used in combination with penicillins (most commonly piperacillin) to extend antibacterial activity against beta-lactamase–producing bacteria by protecting the antibiotic from enzymatic degradation.

sulbactam.definition: A beta-lactamase inhibitor used in combination with a penicillin-type antibiotic (notably ampicillin) to block bacterial beta-lactamases, protecting the antibiotic from degradation and broadening its antimicrobial activity; it has limited intrinsic antibacterial activity on its own.

traumatic brain injury.definition: Caused by a bump or blow to the head, often from car accidents or combat. Concussion is the mildest type.

t cell lymphomas.definition: A heterogeneous group of non-Hodgkin lymphomas arising from malignant mature T lymphocytes; includes subtypes such as peripheral T-cell lymphoma, cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides, Sézary syndrome), and adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma; often presents with lymphadenopathy and/or extranodal disease and tends to be more aggressive than most B-cell lymphomas.

t cell-mediated hypersensitivity reactio.definition: A delayed-type (Type IV) hypersensitivity reaction mediated by T lymphocytes (primarily CD4+ Th1 and CD8+ cytotoxic T cells) that, upon antigen recognition, release cytokines and activate macrophages, leading to localized tissue inflammation and injury; onset typically 24–72 hours after exposure.

type iv hypersensitivity reaction.definition: Delayed-type hypersensitivity is a T-cell–mediated immune response (not antibody-driven) in which sensitized T lymphocytes recognize antigen and release cytokines that activate macrophages and recruit other inflammatory cells, causing tissue injury that typically peaks 24–72 hours after exposure. Examples include contact dermatitis and the tuberculin skin test reaction.

beta-lactamase inhibitor.definition: A substance that inhibits bacterial beta-lactamase enzymes, preventing hydrolysis of the antibiotic’s beta-lactam ring and thereby restoring or enhancing the activity of beta-lactam antibiotics; they have little intrinsic antimicrobial activity and are often combined with beta-lactam antibiotics (e.g., clavulanate, tazobactam, sulbactam).

cytotoxic cells.definition: Immune effector cells that directly kill target cells, such as virus-infected or malignant cells, by inducing programmed cell death. The main examples are CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells, which destroy targets via perforin-granzyme–mediated apoptosis or death receptor pathways (e.g., Fas–FasL) after recognizing abnormal antigens or reduced MHC I expression.

t-helper.definition: A type of T lymphocyte (CD4+ T cell) that coordinates the immune response by signaling and helping other immune cells, including B cells and cytotoxic T cells, via cytokines.

t-suppressor.definition: A subset of T lymphocytes that suppresses immune responses and maintains peripheral tolerance; now typically called regulatory T cells (Tregs), usually CD4+ CD25+ FOXP3+.

t cell antigen receptor.definition: A membrane-bound protein complex on T lymphocytes that recognizes peptide antigens presented by MHC molecules on antigen-presenting cells, triggering T-cell activation and effector responses; most receptors are heterodimers of alpha and beta (or gamma and delta) chains produced by somatic recombination.

toilet training.definition: A developmental process by which a child gains voluntary control over urination and defecation and learns to use a toilet or potty, typically starting around 18–24 months and progressing with readiness cues, consistent practice, and positive reinforcement; nighttime continence often develops later.

teether.definition: A chewable object given to infants to ease gum pain during teething; typically made of rubber, silicone, plastic, or wood and may be cooled for soothing, with supervision and regular cleaning to prevent choking or illness.

teardrop fracture.definition: A fracture of the anteroinferior corner of a vertebral body (often cervical) caused by a flexion injury; it’s an avulsed triangular fragment that resembles a teardrop on imaging, usually indicating anterior column injury and potential spinal instability.

avulsion fracture.definition: A fracture in which a fragment of bone is pulled off at the site where a tendon or ligament attaches, typically due to a sudden, forceful muscle contraction or traction injury.

tear duct.definition: A narrow channel of the lacrimal apparatus that drains tears from the lacrimal sac into the inferior nasal meatus of the nasal cavity.

glands of zeis.definition: A sebaceous gland associated with an eyelash follicle in the eyelid margin; it secretes sebum into the hair follicle to lubricate the lash and surrounding skin, and is a modified sebaceous gland that opens into the hair follicle canal.

epiphora.definition: Excessive tearing of the eye due to impaired drainage through the lacrimal apparatus, often from obstruction of the nasolacrimal drainage system or canaliculi.

rectal mucosa.definition: The mucous membrane lining the rectum, consisting of a simple columnar epithelium with goblet cells overlying lamina propria and muscularis mucosae; it secretes mucus to lubricate the stool, provides a barrier to pathogens, and transitions to stratified squamous epithelium near the anal canal.

teething ring.definition: A chewable ring made of rubber, silicone, or plastic given to infants during teething to soothe sore gums by massaging the gums and reducing teething discomfort; may be cooled briefly for added relief and should be used under supervision to prevent choking.

teflon.definition: A brand name for polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), a fluorinated polymer with high chemical and heat resistance and very low friction; used for nonstick coatings in cookware and in medical devices such as vascular grafts and prosthetic components.

tegmen.definition: A thin bony plate forming the roof of a body cavity or canal; in the skull, the tegmen tympani forms the roof of the middle ear (tympanic) cavity.

tegument.definition: The outer covering of an organism (the skin or integument); in parasitology, the living syncytial outer layer of certain flatworms that protects the parasite and facilitates nutrient absorption.

tegaserod.definition: A selective serotonin 5-HT4 receptor agonist that acts as a prokinetic to increase gastrointestinal motility, used in irritable bowel syndrome with constipation; its use has been restricted due to cardiovascular safety concerns.

teicoplanin.definition: A glycopeptide antibiotic used to treat serious Gram-positive infections by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis through binding to the D-Ala–D-Ala terminus; it is similar to vancomycin, active against many staphylococci and streptococci, usually given IV or IM with a long half-life and a relatively favorable safety profile, and with limited activity against Gram-negative bacteria.

tekturna.definition: A brand-name direct renin inhibitor used to treat hypertension; it blocks renin, the enzyme that initiates the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system, reducing the formation of angiotensin I and II and thereby lowering blood pressure.

aliskiren.definition: A direct renin inhibitor used to treat hypertension; it directly inhibits renin, blocking the conversion of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I and reducing angiotensin II formation, which lowers blood pressure.

telangiectatic granuloma.definition: A benign vascular lesion of the skin or mucous membranes, also known as pyogenic granuloma, characterized by a rapidly growing, friable red nodule composed of lobular aggregates of capillaries in a fibromyxoid stroma that bleeds easily, often arising after minor trauma or irritation.

telangiectatic glioma.definition: A rare histologic variant of an astrocytic brain tumor characterized by prominent telangiectasia—large, dilated, blood-filled vascular spaces interspersed with tumor tissue; in children it often corresponds to a pilocytic astrocytoma variant, while in adults it may be a telangiectatic form of glioblastoma.

telangiectatic nevus.definition: A benign vascular skin lesion consisting of clusters of dilated capillaries in the superficial dermis, presenting as a small, bright-red papule (often known as a cherry angioma).

telangiectatic sarcoma.definition: A high-grade malignant bone tumor variant of osteosarcoma characterized by large, blood-filled spaces separated by thin septa containing malignant cells and osteoid production; it often mimics an aneurysmal bone cyst radiographically and histologically, requiring biopsy to distinguish it from benign lesions and treated with multimodal therapy (surgery and chemotherapy).

telbivudine.definition: A synthetic nucleoside analogue of thymidine used as an antiviral agent for chronic hepatitis B infection; it inhibits HBV DNA polymerase, causing termination of viral DNA synthesis and suppression of viral replication.

telencephalization.definition: An evolutionary and developmental enlargement and elaboration of the telencephalon (the cerebral hemispheres) of the forebrain, resulting in greater cortical complexity and higher cognitive capacities.

telemedicine.definition: The delivery of clinical health care services remotely through telecommunications and information technologies, enabling diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up without in-person visits (including real-time video visits, remote monitoring, and store-and-forward imaging).

telemetry.definition: Remote measurement and transmission of a patient's physiological data (commonly heart rate and rhythm) to a monitoring system for continuous clinical assessment by healthcare providers.

telediagnosis.definition: Diagnosis rendered remotely by a clinician after reviewing patient history, examination data, and ancillary tests transmitted via telecommunication technologies (e.g., video consultations, store-and-forward imaging), without in-person contact.

technetium.definition: A chemical element with atomic number 43; a silvery-gray metal. It has no stable isotopes; its most widely used medical radioisotope, 99mTc, is employed for diagnostic imaging in nuclear medicine.

technologist.definition: A healthcare professional trained to perform technical medical procedures using specialized equipment, typically in diagnostic imaging, clinical laboratory work, or other technology‑driven areas.

technology.definition: The application of scientific knowledge to create devices, systems, and procedures used to diagnose, treat, monitor, or prevent disease and to improve health.

thromboembolic disorder.definition: An illness characterized by intravascular clot formation (thrombosis) that can embolize to remote sites, causing vessel occlusion and tissue ischemia; commonly includes deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.

threshold erythema dose.definition: A minimal dose of ultraviolet light that produces a perceptible erythema (reddening) of the skin within about 24 hours after exposure; used as a measure of an individual's UV sensitivity and to guide phototherapy dosing (typically expressed in mJ/cm^2 or J/m^2, and varies with wavelength, skin type, and site).

ted.definition: An autoimmune inflammatory disorder of the orbit associated with Graves' disease, causing proptosis, diplopia, eyelid retraction, and periorbital edema.

osler-weber-rendu syndrome.definition: An autosomal dominant genetic disorder characterized by mucocutaneous telangiectasias and visceral arteriovenous malformations, leading to recurrent epistaxis, gastrointestinal bleeding, and complications from AVMs in the lungs, brain, and liver.

stork bite.definition: A common, flat birthmark caused by dilated capillaries (nevus simplex) that usually appears on the nape of the neck in newborns and typically fades within the first year or two of life.

infantile hemangioma.definition: A common benign vascular tumor of infancy caused by proliferation of capillary endothelial cells; it usually appears in the first weeks of life, enlarges rapidly during the first months, and involutes spontaneously over years.

telangiectasia lymphatica.definition: Visible dilation of superficial lymphatic vessels in the skin or mucous membranes due to lymphatic ectasia; a form of lymphatic malformation.

telangiectatic epulis.definition: A vascular gingival lesion (epulis) with prominent telangiectasias—dilated superficial blood vessels—in the gingival tissue, forming a red, often friable mass that bleeds easily; a vascular variant of epulis.

telencephalon.definition: An anterior division of the forebrain (prosencephalon) that develops into the cerebral hemispheres, including the cerebral cortex, basal ganglia, hippocampus, and amygdala.

temozolomide.definition: An oral alkylating chemotherapy agent used to treat glioblastoma multiforme and other brain tumors; a prodrug converted to the active metabolite MTIC, which methylates DNA and induces tumor cell death.

telephone consultation.definition: A remote clinical consultation conducted by telephone between a clinician and patient, involving history-taking, advice and management planning, and follow-up arrangements; no physical examination is performed during the call (prescriptions or referrals may be issued where permitted by local regulations).

telephone counseling.definition: Delivery of counseling or psychotherapy to a patient by telephone, enabling remote assessment, treatment planning, and support without in-person contact.

telephone follow-up.definition: A follow-up assessment conducted by telephone after a clinical encounter to monitor patient status, review symptoms and medications, assess adherence and adverse effects, provide management guidance, and determine whether an in-person visit or further tests are needed.

teleradiology.definition: The electronic transmission of radiologic images (such as X-rays, CT, or MRI) from one location to a radiologist at another site for remote interpretation, reporting, and consultation.

telmisartan.definition: An angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) that selectively antagonizes the AT1 receptor, causing vasodilation and reduced blood pressure; used to treat hypertension and reduce cardiovascular risk in adults.

temaril.definition: A veterinary combination medication containing trimeprazine (an antihistamine) and prednisolone (a corticosteroid) used as an antitussive (cough suppressant) and anti-inflammatory.

temovate.definition: A super-potent topical corticosteroid containing clobetasol propionate, used to treat inflammatory and pruritic skin conditions (e.g., plaque psoriasis, eczema, dermatitis); applied in a thin layer to affected skin for the shortest duration advised by a clinician due to risks of skin thinning and systemic absorption.

temsirolimus.definition: A prodrug of sirolimus (rapamycin) that inhibits the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway; used as an anticancer agent (notably for advanced renal cell carcinoma) and as an immunosuppressant, given intravenously.

weight increase.definition: An increase in body weight, typically due to a positive energy balance resulting in the accumulation of body tissue (primarily fat) and/or fluid; can occur from factors such as higher caloric intake, reduced physical activity, pregnancy, edema, or medication- or disease-related causes.

poor coordination.definition: Impaired ability to perform smooth, accurate, and coordinated movements, often due to cerebellar dysfunction or sensory/proprioceptive impairment; presents as clumsiness, imbalance, gait ataxia, tremor, dysmetria, or dysdiadochokinesis.

temperature regulation.definition: Physiological and behavioral processes that maintain a stable core body temperature by balancing heat production (metabolic activity, shivering) with heat loss (vasodilation, sweating, radiation, evaporation), mediated chiefly by the hypothalamus and autonomic nervous system, and modulated by behavioral responses.

intraoperative temperature regulation.definition: Maintenance of a patient’s core body temperature within a target range during surgery through monitoring and active warming or cooling measures, to prevent intraoperative hypothermia or hyperthermia and reduce related complications.

temperature scale.definition: A system for numerically expressing temperature measurements, typically using Celsius (°C) or Fahrenheit (°F); it allows clinicians to quantify body temperature to assess fever, normothermia, or hypothermia.

temporal artery.definition: A superficial branch of the external carotid artery that travels across the temple to supply the scalp in the temporal region; commonly palpated and biopsied in suspected temporal arteritis.

temporal bone fracture.definition: A fracture of the temporal bone, typically resulting from blunt head trauma, that may involve the external auditory canal, middle ear, inner ear, facial nerve, or dura; can cause hearing loss, vertigo, facial weakness, cerebrospinal fluid leakage (otorrhea), and meningitis risk, and is often categorized as longitudinal or transverse through the petrous portion of the temporal bone.

temporal fascia.definition: A fibrous fascial layer that covers the temporalis muscle on the temple; it splits into superficial and deep leaves that envelop the muscle and attach to the superior temporal line and the zygomatic arch, continuing with the galea aponeurotica and surrounding facial fascia.

temporal lobe epilepsy.definition: A focal epilepsy arising from the temporal lobe (often mesial temporal structures such as the hippocampus and amygdala), typically presenting with impaired-awareness seizures often with aura, automatisms, and autonomic features; frequently associated with mesial temporal sclerosis on MRI.

tmj.definition: An articular synovial joint between the mandible and the temporal bone (condyle with the mandibular fossa) that allows opening, closing, and sideways movement of the jaw; stabilized by ligaments and an articular disc, and prone to disorders causing pain, limited motion, or noises such as clicking.

temporomandibular joint disorder.definition: A group of conditions affecting the temporomandibular joint and the surrounding masticatory muscles, causing jaw pain or tenderness, limited jaw movement, and/or noises such as clicking or popping. They are often related to bruxism, malocclusion, arthritis, trauma, or stress and are usually managed with conservative measures (analgesics, physical therapy, bite splints, and behavioral modification); surgery is rarely required.

temporomandibular joint capsule.definition: The fibrous capsule surrounding the temporomandibular joint; it attaches superiorly to the margins of the mandibular fossa and articular eminence of the temporal bone and inferiorly to the neck of the mandible, enclosing the articular disc and the synovial cavity, and is reinforced laterally by the temporomandibular ligament.

temporomandibular ligament.definition: A fibrous band that strengthens the lateral aspect of the temporomandibular joint capsule, extending from the zygomatic arch of the temporal bone to the neck of the mandible; it stabilizes the joint and resists posterior displacement of the condyle during jaw movements.

temporomaxillary.definition: Relating to the temporal bone region of the skull and the maxilla (upper jaw); used to describe anatomy or pathology of the temple and upper jaw area. Note that the jaw’s movable joint is the temporomandibular joint (TMJ), between the temporal bone and the mandible, not the maxilla.

temporooccipital.definition: Relating to the temporal region of the skull or brain and the occipital region; pertaining to the area where the temporal and occipital regions meet.

mesial sclerosis.definition: Chronic scar formation (sclerosis) of the mesial temporal brain structures, especially the hippocampus, with neuronal loss and gliosis, commonly associated with temporal lobe epilepsy.

giant cell arteritis.definition: When the arteries in your head, neck and arms are swollen, so that the blood does not flow well. Also called temporal arteritis.

horton’s arteritis.definition: An inflammatory vasculitis of medium- to large-sized arteries, most often the temporal arteries, in adults over 50, presenting with new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, and potential vision loss; associated with elevated inflammatory markers and granulomatous inflammation on biopsy; treated with high-dose corticosteroids to prevent blindness.

zygomaticotemporal branches.definition: Small sensory branches of the zygomatic nerve that traverse the zygomatic bone to supply the skin of the temple; they carry cutaneous fibers from the maxillary nerve (V2) to the temporal region and typically give a communicating branch to the lacrimal nerve carrying parasympathetic fibers to the lacrimal gland.

medial pterygoid.definition: A muscle of mastication in the infratemporal fossa with two heads (deep head from the medial surface of the lateral pterygoid plate and superficial head from the tuberosity of the maxilla) that inserts on the medial surface of the mandible near its angle; it elevates and protrudes the mandible and assists in grinding movements. Innervated by the nerve to the medial pterygoid, a branch of V3 (mandibular nerve).

geniohyoid.definition: A slender suprahyoid muscle that originates from the inferior mental spine (genial tubercle) of the mandible and inserts into the body of the hyoid bone; it elevates and protracts the hyoid during swallowing. Innervation: C1 via the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).

temporal gyrus.definition: A gyrus on the lateral surface of the temporal lobe of the brain; the temporal lobe includes the superior, middle, and inferior temporal gyri, which participate in auditory processing, language, and higher-level visual and memory functions.

tenotomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which a tendon is cut (transected) to release or lengthen it, reducing tension and improving range of motion; it can be performed percutaneously or by open dissection.

tenacula.definition: Plural of a tenaculum; a surgical instrument with hooked tips used to grasp and secure tissue during procedures (e.g., to hold the cervix).

tenalgia.definition: Pain localized to a tendon, usually due to overuse or inflammatory/degenerative tendon pathology (tendinopathy or tendinitis).

tenodynia.definition: Pain in a tendon; a symptom often due to overuse, strain, or inflammatory/degenerative tendon conditions.

tendonitis.definition: Alternative spelling of tendinitis—inflammation of a tendon, usually caused by injury; may cause pain and restrict movement of the muscle attached to the tendon.

tenosynovitis.definition: Swelling and inflammation of the protective sheath covering the tendons, which decreases the sheath’s production of synovial fluid.

tenecteplase.definition: An intravenous thrombolytic agent, a recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) variant used to dissolve clots in acute myocardial infarction (STEMI); given as a single weight-based IV bolus, with a longer half-life and greater fibrin specificity than alteplase.

tenesmic.definition: Relating to tenesmus; characterized by a persistent urge to defecate with cramping and a sensation of incomplete evacuation, often with pain and straining.

tenia.definition: A ribbon-like band or narrow groove in anatomy; for example, one of the longitudinal muscular bands seen on the colon. In parasitology, it also refers to a genus of tapeworms that includes species such as the pork tapeworm and the beef tapeworm.

taenia.definition: A genus of tapeworms (cestodes) that infect the intestines of humans and other mammals; notable species include Taenia solium (pork tapeworm) and Taenia saginata (beef tapeworm), with infection arising from eating undercooked meat containing larvae.

tenodesis.definition: A surgical procedure in which a tendon is detached from its original insertion and reattached to bone at a different site to restore function or stabilize a joint.

tenomyotomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which both a muscle and its attached tendon are cut to release a contracture and improve movement.

atenolol.definition: A cardioselective beta-adrenergic blocker (beta-1 selective) used to treat hypertension, angina pectoris, and certain arrhythmias; it lowers heart rate, reduces myocardial contractility, and decreases blood pressure.

tensilon.definition: A brand-name, short-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor (edrophonium chloride) used in the tensilon test to diagnose myasthenia gravis by briefly increasing neuromuscular transmission.

edrophonium hydrochloride.definition: An ultra‑short-acting, reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used as a diagnostic agent to evaluate neuromuscular transmission (notably the Tensilon test) by rapidly increasing acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction. Onset is about 30–60 seconds with a 5–10 minute duration, helping to differentiate myasthenia gravis from cholinergic crisis; administered IV or IM, with potential adverse effects including bradycardia, bronchospasm, and fasciculations.

tensiometer.definition: A device used to measure tension in a liquid surface or in biological tissues, providing quantitative data on surface tension or tissue mechanical properties.

tension.definition: State of being stretched tight; in physiology, the force that resists elongation of a tissue (such as a muscle-tendon unit) and can be generated passively by stretching or actively by muscle contraction.

tentorial.definition: Relating to the tentorium cerebelli, the horizontal dural fold that separates the cerebellum from the inferior aspect of the occipital lobes.

tentorium.definition: A dural fold forming a tent-like partition between the cerebrum and cerebellum (tentorium cerebelli), separating the cerebral hemispheres from the cerebellum and enclosing the brainstem via the tentorial notch.

tentorial notch.definition: A notch in the tentorium cerebelli that forms the opening for the midbrain to pass from the posterior cranial fossa to the supratentorial compartment.

tentoria.definition: Plural form of a dural fold that forms a tent-like partition within the skull, separating the cerebrum from the cerebellum and brainstem; it attaches along the margins of the posterior cranial fossa and helps compartmentalize the cranial cavity, including forming a passage for the brainstem.

teratogen.definition: An agent that can disturb embryonic or fetal development, potentially causing congenital malformations or fetal injury, with risk dependent on the dose and timing of exposure.

teratogenic agent.definition: A teratogenic agent is any substance, organism, or physical factor that, when a fetus is exposed during pregnancy, can disrupt fetal development and cause birth defects or other congenital abnormalities.

teratogeny.definition: The capacity or process by which exposure to teratogenic agents produces congenital malformations in a developing fetus.

teratology.definition: The scientific study of abnormal development leading to birth defects, including causes, mechanisms (teratogenesis), and prevention.

teratologist.definition: A scientist who studies teratology, the science of birth defects and abnormal fetal development, including the causes and mechanisms of congenital anomalies.

gravis.definition: Latin for "serious" or "grave"; used in medical terminology to denote a severe form of a condition and is not itself a disease.

tenofovir.definition: An antiviral nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used to treat HIV-1 infection and chronic hepatitis B; administered as prodrugs that are converted to an active metabolite which inhibits viral DNA synthesis by terminating the DNA chain.

tenofovir disoproxil fumarate.definition: A prodrug of tenofovir and a nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor used to treat HIV-1 infection and chronic hepatitis B; after absorption it is converted to active tenofovir diphosphate, which inhibits viral DNA synthesis by terminating DNA chain elongation.

disoproxil.definition: A prodrug moiety used to improve the oral bioavailability of certain nucleotide/nucleoside antiviral drugs; it is a diester group that is hydrolyzed in vivo to release the active drug.

fumarate.definition: An anion or salt of fumaric acid (trans-butenedioic acid); the trans isomer of butenedioic acid; a metabolic intermediate in the citric acid cycle.

teratosis.definition: A developmental abnormality or malformation of tissues or organs arising from abnormal differentiation during embryogenesis; used to describe congenital anomalies or disordered tissue development; not necessarily neoplastic.

tricyclic antidepressants.definition: A class of antidepressant drugs with a three-ring chemical structure that inhibits the reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin (and to a lesser extent dopamine), increasing monoamine levels in the synaptic cleft; used to treat major depressive disorder and certain chronic pain conditions, but associated with anticholinergic, sedative, and cardiovascular side effects.

teriparatide.definition: A recombinant human parathyroid hormone fragment (PTH 1-34) used as an anabolic treatment for osteoporosis; given by daily subcutaneous injection; it stimulates osteoblast activity and bone formation, reducing fracture risk; typically used for up to 18–24 months.

postmenopausal osteoporosis.definition: Bone loss caused by lower estrogen levels associated with menopause. Sometimes called type I osteoporosis.

primary hypogonadal osteoporosis.definition: An osteoporosis caused by chronic sex steroid deficiency due to primary gonadal failure (eg, premature ovarian insufficiency in women or primary testicular failure in men), in which lack of estrogen (and testosterone/its conversion to estrogen) accelerates bone resorption, lowers bone mineral density, and increases fracture risk.

terminal bronchiole.definition: The smallest conducting airway of the bronchial tree, roughly 0.3 mm in diameter, marking the transition to the respiratory zone; lacks cartilage and mucous glands; lined by simple cuboidal epithelium with club (Clara) cells; does not participate in gas exchange and leads to the respiratory bronchioles.

terminal cancer.definition: An incurable cancer with a prognosis of limited life expectancy, typically due to advanced disease or widespread metastasis; treatment focuses on palliation and quality of life rather than cure.

crista terminalis.definition: A thick, crescent-shaped muscular ridge in the right atrium that marks the boundary between the smooth sinus venarum and the rough, pectinated anterior wall; the sinoatrial node lies at its upper end near the opening of the superior vena cava.

terminal sulcus.definition: A V-shaped groove on the dorsal surface of the tongue that marks the border between the anterior two-thirds (oral) and posterior one-third (pharyngeal); its apex contains the foramen cecum.

sulcus terminalis cordis.definition: A shallow groove on the external surface of the right atrium marking the boundary between the smooth-walled sinus venarum and the rough, trabeculated part of the atrial wall; it corresponds internally to the crista terminalis and marks the embryologic junction between the primitive right atrium and the sinus venosus.

terminal ileum.definition: Distal portion of the small intestine, the last segment of the ileum just before the ileocecal valve; specialized for absorption of bile acids and vitamin B12, contains Peyer’s patches, and participates in enterohepatic circulation.

ileal papilla.definition: Not a standard anatomical term. If used informally, it may refer to a small mucosal projection at the ileocecal junction, but this usage is not widely accepted. The well-defined structures in this region are the ileocecal valve (between ileum and cecum) and, elsewhere in the ileum, Peyer’s patches (lymphoid tissue). If you have a specific context or source, I can help interpret it.

terminal saccular period.definition: A stage of fetal lung development in late gestation during which the terminal sacs (primitive alveoli) form and enlarge, the alveolar epithelium thins, the pulmonary capillary network surrounds these sacs, and surfactant production by type II pneumocytes begins, enabling gas exchange after birth.

terminal saccular phase.definition: The stage of fetal lung development in which terminal saccules (primitive alveoli) form and mature, with thinning of the alveolar walls, expansion of the capillary network, maturation of type I and II pneumocytes, and increased surfactant production to enable gas exchange after birth.

primitive alveoli.definition: A nascent alveolar unit formed during fetal lung development; an early sac-like outgrowth of a respiratory bronchiole that will mature into a functional alveolus, with progressively thinning walls and increasing capillary contact during alveolarization.

terminal sacs.definition: Thin-walled, dilated distal sacs formed at the end of the respiratory bronchioles during the saccular (terminal sac) stage of fetal lung development; lined by simple squamous epithelium and surrounded by capillaries, they are the primitive sites of gas exchange that later mature into alveoli.

terminal stance.definition: Part of the gait cycle's stance phase that begins with heel rise and ends with contralateral toe-off; during this phase, the body advances over the forefoot as the ankle plantarflexes to propel the body forward, with the hip extending and the knee near full extension.

terpin hydrate.definition: A historical expectorant used in cough preparations; a hydrated terpene (terpin) that helps loosen and thin bronchial secretions to ease coughing.

terra-cortril.definition: A topical ophthalmic preparation that combines a corticosteroid to reduce ocular inflammation with an antibiotic to treat bacterial eye infections, used for conditions like conjunctivitis with inflammation.

terramycin.definition: A brand name for oxytetracycline, a tetracycline antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by reversibly binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit; it has broad-spectrum activity against many Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria and is used to treat a variety of infections.

testacealobosia.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard dictionaries. Could you please confirm the spelling or provide context (organ system, condition, or source where you saw it)? If you meant a different term, I can define that.

testcross.definition: A cross between an individual with an unknown genotype for a particular gene and a homozygous recessive tester to determine whether the unknown individual is homozygous dominant or heterozygous.

testes determining factor.definition: A transcription factor encoded by the SRY gene that initiates male sex determination by directing the bipotential gonad to develop into a testis, primarily by promoting Sertoli cell differentiation and activating downstream male pathways (e.g., upregulating SOX9) while suppressing ovarian development.

tdf.definition: A nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor used in combination antiretroviral therapy for HIV infection; a prodrug of tenofovir.

y chromosome.definition: A sex chromosome present in males (typically XY) that carries genes essential for male sex determination and spermatogenesis; it is smaller than the X chromosome and contains relatively few genes (including the SRY gene that triggers testes development) and is inherited from father to son.

x chromosome.definition: One of the two sex chromosomes in humans and many species; a relatively large, gene-rich chromosome that carries hundreds to thousands of genes essential for development and physiology. In humans, females have two X chromosomes (XX) and males have one X (XY); to balance gene expression, females inactivate one X chromosome in each cell. Mutations on the X can cause X-linked inheritance and related disorders.

term infant.definition: A newborn baby born after 37 completed weeks of gestation but before 42 weeks (gestational age 37 0/7 to 41 6/7), i.e., not preterm.

end artery.definition: An artery that provides the sole or principal blood supply to a tissue or region with little or no collateral circulation; occlusion can cause ischemia or infarction of that territory.

terminal artery.definition: An artery that ends in a tissue bed with little to no anastomosis with neighboring arterial supplies, forming an end-arterial circulation; occlusion of such an artery can cause ischemia or infarction of the supplied territory due to limited collateral flow.

tertiary health care.definition: A level of specialized medical care provided by tertiary care centers or services, offering highly advanced diagnostic, therapeutic, and surgical procedures for complex or rare conditions, typically upon referral from primary or secondary care.

tertiary health care facility.definition: A hospital that provides highly specialized medical care and advanced diagnostic and therapeutic services for complex or rare conditions, typically with subspecialty departments and advanced technology, and usually reached via referral from primary or secondary care.

tertiary prevention.definition: Interventions after a disease or injury has occurred to prevent further deterioration, reduce complications, and restore function to the greatest extent possible. Examples include rehabilitation after stroke, preventive management to avoid complications in chronic diseases, and symptom control or care planning to improve quality of life.

tertiary bronchial buds.definition: Embryologic outgrowths from the secondary (lobar) bronchi that give rise to the segmental (tertiary) bronchi, each supplying a bronchopulmonary segment.

tertiary bronchus.definition: One of the segmental (third-generation) airways of the bronchial tree; a branch of a lobar (secondary) bronchus that supplies a bronchopulmonary segment and is part of the conducting airway, typically with cartilage plates and pseudostratified ciliated epithelium.

type i alveolar cells.definition: A very thin, squamous epithelial cell lining the majority of the alveolar surface; forms the primary gas-exchange barrier between air and capillary blood, allowing efficient diffusion due to its minimal thickness; covers about 95% of the alveolar surface, lacks a secretory function, and is replenished by proliferation and differentiation of nearby Type II pneumocytes after injury.

type ii alveolar cells.definition: Cuboidal epithelial cells of the alveolar epithelium that synthesize and secrete pulmonary surfactant to reduce surface tension and prevent alveolar collapse; they also serve as progenitor cells that can differentiate into type I pneumocytes to repair the alveolar epithelium after injury.

alveolar saccules.definition: Primitive sac-like dilations at the ends of the distal airways (alveolar ducts) in fetal lung development, which subdivide by secondary septation to form mature alveoli; they represent the saccular stage of alveolar development.

terminal saccules.definition: Thin-walled primitive alveolar sacs formed during the fetal saccular stage of lung development; they are the precursors to mature alveoli and, with closely associated capillaries, become the sites of gas exchange after birth.

alcoholics.definition: A person with an alcohol use disorder, a chronic condition characterized by compulsive alcohol use, impaired control over intake, and continued use despite adverse consequences, often with withdrawal symptoms when not drinking.

sicca.definition: An adjective meaning dry; used in medicine to denote dryness of tissues or mucous membranes, such as in dry eyes or dry mouth.

schirmer.definition: A diagnostic test to measure tear production by placing a small filter paper strip inside the lower eyelid; the extent of wetting (in millimeters) over about 5 minutes is used to assess dry eye.

dryeye.definition: A common condition in which the tear film is insufficient or of poor quality, leading to ocular surface discomfort such as dryness, burning or grittiness, with redness and fluctuating or reduced vision.

testicularcancer.definition: Cancer that affects the organs that make male sex hormones and sperm.

undescended.definition: Not descended from its normal anatomical position; most often used to describe a testicle that has not descended into the scrotum (cryptorchidism).

lymphnodes.definition: Glands that contain white blood cells that help protect you against germs.

selfexamination.definition: The examination of one's own body by inspection and palpation to detect signs of disease or abnormality; commonly used for screening (e.g., breast or testicular cancer) or monitoring skin changes, with professional evaluation recommended for any suspicious findings.

tese.definition: Not found in standard medical dictionaries. Please provide more context or confirm the spelling.

vasdeferens.definition: An elongated muscular duct that transports mature sperm from the epididymis to the ejaculatory ducts via peristaltic contractions; travels within the spermatic cord from the tail of the epididymis to the prostatic urethra.

spermaticcord.definition: A bundle of structures enclosed in fascial coverings that extends from the deep inguinal ring to the testis, containing the vas deferens, testicular artery, pampiniform venous plexus, lymphatics, nerves, and cremaster muscle; it suspends and vascularizes the testis and transports sperm from the epididymis toward the urethra.

tunicavaginalis.definition: Double-layered serous membrane surrounding the testis (and epididymis) in the scrotum; derived from peritoneum via the processus vaginalis; consists of visceral and parietal layers with a potential space containing lubricating fluid to reduce friction.

retetestis.definition: An anastomotic network in the mediastinum of the testis that collects sperm from the seminiferous tubules and conveys it to the efferent ductules toward the epididymis.

internalspermaticarteries.definition: Arteries of the gonadal (testicular) circulation arising from the abdominal aorta just below the renal arteries; they travel within the spermatic cord through the inguinal canal to supply the testis and epididymis.

pampiniformplexus.definition: A venous network in the spermatic cord that drains the testis and surrounds the testicular artery to cool arterial blood reaching the testis, aiding thermoregulation.

celiacplexuses.definition: A network of nerves in the upper abdomen; medications may be injected here as part of nerve-block therapy to ease pain.

autonomicnervoussystem.definition: The part of the nervous system that controls involuntary actions, such as blood pressure or breathing. It also plays an important role in the fight or flight response to danger.

leydigcells.definition: Interstitial cells of the testes that synthesize and secrete testosterone in response to luteinizing hormone (LH), located in the interstitial tissue between seminiferous tubules and essential for male development and spermatogenesis.

cypionate.definition: A fatty acid ester used to prolong the duration of action of certain drugs (most commonly testosterone) by creating a slow-release depot after intramuscular injection.

enanthate.definition: A salt or ester derived from heptanoic (enanthic) acid; in pharmacology, an esterified form of a drug that yields a slow, prolonged release after administration (for example, a long-acting injectable form of testosterone).

luteinizinghormone.definition: A hormone that controls ovulation in women. In men, luteinizing hormone triggers production of testosterone.

folliclestimulatinghormone.definition: A glycoprotein gonadotropin produced by the anterior pituitary that stimulates growth and maturation of ovarian follicles and estrogen production in females, and promotes spermatogenesis in males by acting on granulosa cells in the ovary and Sertoli cells in the testes; its secretion is regulated by GnRH and inhibited by sex steroids and inhibins.

anteriorpituitarygland.definition: A glandular portion of the pituitary gland (adenohypophysis) that synthesizes and secretes hormones—growth hormone, prolactin, adrenocorticotropic hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, and the gonadotropins LH and FSH—under control of hypothalamic releasing and inhibiting hormones.

clostridiumtetani.definition: An anaerobic, gram-positive, spore-forming bacillus that causes tetanus by producing the tetanospasmin neurotoxin; found in soil and animal feces; infection typically occurs via contaminated wounds; vaccine-preventable.

immunized.definition: Having gained immunity to a disease, typically through vaccination or prior infection, providing protection against that disease.

tetanustoxoid.definition: An inactivated form of the tetanus toxin used as a vaccine to induce active immunity against tetanus; typically given as part of combination vaccines such as DTaP or Tdap.

td.definition: A booster vaccine containing tetanus toxoid and diphtheria toxoid used to prevent tetanus and diphtheria.

risussardonicus.definition: A sustained, involuntary contraction of facial muscles that produces a fixed, sardonic grin; most characteristically seen in severe tetanus.

laryngealspasm.definition: A sudden, involuntary contraction of the laryngeal (vocal cord) muscles causing partial or complete closure of the glottis and resulting airway obstruction; commonly occurs during anesthesia with airway instrumentation or extubation and may be precipitated by airway irritation or reflux.

tetanospasmin.definition: A potent neurotoxin produced by Clostridium tetani that blocks the release of inhibitory neurotransmitters (GABA and glycine) in the central nervous system by cleaving synaptobrevin, leading to disinhibition and generalized spastic paralysis; the toxin responsible for tetanus.
