tuberosum.definition: A Latin adjective meaning “tuberous” or “having tubers or tubercles,” used in scientific names and anatomical descriptions to denote a knobby or tuber-bearing feature.

tuboabdominal.definition: Relating to the fallopian tube and the abdomen; describing an anatomical relationship or pathology involving the uterine tube within the abdominal cavity.

tuboplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair or reconstruct a fallopian tube to restore patency and improve fertility.

tubulin.definition: A cytoskeletal protein that polymerizes with α-tubulin/β-tubulin heterodimers to form microtubules; binds and hydrolyzes GTP, driving microtubule dynamics; essential for cell shape, intracellular transport, and chromosome segregation during mitosis.

tumorigenic.definition: Capable of initiating or promoting the formation of tumors; oncogenic.

tularensis.definition: An intracellular, Gram-negative bacterium that causes tularemia (a zoonotic infection); transmitted to humans by bites or contact with infected animals or contaminated materials, and by inhalation, with a very low infectious dose.

transurethral.definition: Relating to or performed through the urethra.

laser-induced.definition: Produced by or resulting from exposure to laser radiation; describing effects caused by laser irradiation, such as tissue damage, ablation, or fluorescence.

turp.definition: A surgical procedure in which portions of the prostate are removed endoscopically via the urethra to relieve bladder outlet obstruction, most commonly for benign prostatic hyperplasia.

tunnel.definition: A tunnel is a narrow passage or channel through tissue or bone that connects two spaces or surfaces; in medicine it often refers to a sinus or fistulous tract or a wound channel extending beneath the surface.

tunica.definition: A coat or layer that covers or lines an organ, tissue, or vessel; in anatomy, it denotes a distinct layered wall, such as the inner lining, muscular layer, and outer connective tissue of blood vessels.

albuginea.definition: A dense fibrous connective tissue capsule surrounding certain organs (notably the testis) and the erectile tissue of the penis; it provides structure and helps enclose the vascular spaces during erection.

albus.definition: Latin for white; used descriptively in medical terminology to indicate whiteness or pale coloration of tissue or structures.

vaginalis.definition: Relating to the vagina; a Latin adjective used in anatomical terminology to describe structures associated with or located near the vagina.

tuning.definition: Adjusting a device, instrument, or system to achieve optimal performance, accuracy, or responsiveness; in medicine, this often involves calibrating equipment or modifying therapeutic settings to suit a patient.

fork.definition: A bifurcation: the point at which a structure splits into two branches, such as a blood vessel or airway dividing into two branches.

tuft.definition: A small cluster or bundle of fibers, hairs, or cells that forms a distinct projection or aggregation.

turbinate.definition: A curved bony shelf in the nasal cavity (nasal concha) covered by mucosa that increases surface area to warm, humidify, and filter inhaled air; there are inferior, middle, and superior turbinates, and hypertrophy can contribute to nasal obstruction.

turbinum.definition: Latin for turbine or whorl; in anatomy, refers to the nasal turbinates (nasal conchae), the bony structures inside the nasal cavity that increase surface area to warm, humidify, and filter inhaled air.

traveler.definition: An individual away from home for the purpose of travel; in medicine, travel-related illnesses are those acquired during travel or soon after return, commonly including diarrheal illness from contaminated food or water and infections encountered abroad.

turbidimetry.definition: An optical method to quantify the cloudiness of a suspension by measuring the attenuation of transmitted light due to scattering by suspended particles; the degree of turbidity correlates with particle or solute concentration.

turbidity.definition: Cloudiness or haziness of a liquid caused by suspended particles that scatter light; in medicine, used to describe the clarity of samples (e.g., urine, plasma, microbial suspensions), with higher turbidity indicating more particulates and potentially affecting laboratory measurements.

turner.definition: A condition where a person's X chromosome is missing or partly missing. Only occurs in females.

noonan.definition: A genetic disorder caused by mutations in the RAS-MAPK signaling pathway, marked by distinctive facial features, short stature, congenital heart defects (especially pulmonary valve stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), chest wall abnormalities, and variable developmental delay; usually autosomal dominant with variable expressivity.

xo.definition: Monosomy X (45,X): a sex chromosome aneuploidy in which an individual has only one X chromosome instead of two, commonly associated with Turner syndrome.

genotype.definition: The genetic constitution of an organism or cell; the specific alleles at one or more gene loci that an individual carries, which, together with environmental factors, influence inherited traits (in contrast to the observable traits, the phenotype).

counseling.definition: A professional, confidential process in which a trained counselor helps an individual identify problems, explore emotions, and develop coping strategies, goals, and behaviors to improve mental health and functioning.

webbing.definition: Partial fusion of adjacent digits (usually fingers or toes) by a band of skin or soft tissue, creating a persistent interdigital web; most commonly congenital (syndactyly) and may affect function, sometimes corrected surgically.

neurocutaneous.definition: Relating to or involving both the nervous system and the skin; used to describe disorders that affect both systems.

spatial.definition: Relating to space; describing the three-dimensional arrangement, position, or orientation of structures, or the perception of space and distance.

learning.definition: A relatively enduring change in behavior or knowledge that results from experience, practice, or instruction, mediated by neural plasticity and memory processes such as encoding, consolidation, storage, and retrieval.

tutamen.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard dictionaries; if you meant the brain structure putamen, it is a basal ganglia nucleus involved in motor control and learning.

tenth-value-layer.definition: The thickness of shielding material required to reduce the intensity of a photon radiation beam by a factor of ten (to one-tenth of its original intensity) for a specified energy; the value depends on the material and the photon energy.

t wave.definition: A deflection on an electrocardiogram representing ventricular repolarization—the ventricles returning to their resting electrical state after depolarization (the QRS complex).

s-t segment.definition: The flat, isoelectric portion of the electrocardiogram between the end of the QRS complex (the J point) and the beginning of the T wave; normally lies on the baseline and corresponds to the plateau phase of ventricular repolarization. Elevation or depression of this segment can indicate myocardial ischemia or injury.

repolarization.definition: The process by which a depolarized cell's membrane potential returns toward the resting potential, driven by outward potassium currents and a decrease in inward calcium and sodium currents; in cardiac cells, it corresponds to phase 3 of the action potential and restores the resting potential.

tweed triangle.definition: Not found in standard medical dictionaries. It may be a misspelling or an obscure term. Please share the context (specialty or anatomical region) or confirm the spelling.

lower central incisor.definition: One of the two front teeth in the lower jaw (mandibular central incisors), located at the midline; primarily used for cutting food, typically with a single root, and part of the permanent dentition that erupts around age 6–7.

twentieth-century syndrome.definition: Not a formal medical diagnosis; historically used informally to describe a broad, non-specific pattern of psychosocial distress—such as anxiety, burnout, somatic complaints, and social alienation—attributed to rapid modernization and cultural change during the 20th century; lacks standardized criteria.

total allergy syndrome.definition: Not a recognized medical syndrome in standard clinical practice. It is sometimes used colloquially to describe widespread or multiple concurrent allergic diseases or hypersensitivity reactions across organ systems. There are no official diagnostic criteria; evaluation typically targets the specific allergic conditions present (eg, allergic rhinitis, allergic asthma, atopic dermatitis) and the triggers involved, with treatment tailored to each condition.

twiddler's syndrome.definition: A complication of implanted pacemakers or ICDs in which rotation or manipulation of the pulse generator causes displacement or retraction of the pacing/defibrillator leads, leading to loss of capture, sensing abnormalities, or device failure.

deep sedation.definition: A drug-induced state of deeper-than-moderate sedation in which the patient is not easily aroused but can respond purposefully to repeated or painful stimulation; spontaneous ventilation may be inadequate and airway support or intervention may be required; usually requires continuous monitoring and anesthesia expertise, and lies between moderate (conscious) sedation and general anesthesia.

twin-to-twin transfusion.definition: A condition in monochorionic twin pregnancies in which unbalanced placental blood flow through shared vessels causes one fetus (donor) to become hypovolemic with oligohydramnios and growth restriction, and the other (recipient) to become hypervolemic with polyhydramnios, potentially leading to heart failure and death; diagnosed by discordant amniotic fluid volumes and Doppler abnormalities.

twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome.definition: A complication of monochorionic twin pregnancies caused by unbalanced placental vascular connections that lead to unequal blood flow between twins; the donor twin develops oligohydramnios and growth restriction, while the recipient twin develops polyhydramnios and risk of cardiac failure. Diagnosis is via ultrasound showing discordant amniotic fluid volumes and Doppler abnormalities; treatment includes close surveillance and procedures such as amnioreduction or fetoscopic laser coagulation of placental anastomoses to balance blood flow.

twin-wire orthodontic appliance.definition: A fixed orthodontic appliance that uses two archwires operating in tandem to exert controlled forces on teeth, improving torque, alignment, and space closure compared with a single-wire system.

two-point discrimination test.definition: A clinical test of tactile acuity that determines the minimum distance at which two simultaneous skin stimuli are perceived as two distinct points, reflecting somatosensory processing and peripheral nerve integrity; larger thresholds suggest impaired fine touch, as in neuropathy or nerve injury.

parietal regions.definition: Regions of the cerebrum comprising the parietal lobes, located posterior to the central sulcus; they process somatosensory information and support spatial orientation, perception, and integration of sensory data.

thromboxane a2.definition: A potent vasoconstrictor and promoter of platelet aggregation synthesized in platelets from arachidonic acid via the cyclooxygenase pathway; it rapidly hydrolyzes to thromboxane B2 and acts on TP receptors to enhance hemostasis and promote thrombosis.

thromboxane b2.definition: A stable, non-enzymatic hydrolysis product of thromboxane A2; not biologically active but serves as a circulating marker of thromboxane A2 production and platelet activation.

tygacil.definition: A broad‑spectrum antibiotic of the glycylcycline class that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit; indicated for complicated intra‑abdominal infections, complicated skin and soft tissue infections, and certain cases of community‑acquired pneumonia; has limited activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

tykerb.definition: A small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor that blocks EGFR (HER1) and HER2 (ERBB2) signaling; used in the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer, typically in combination with capecitabine after progression on trastuzumab.

tylenol.definition: A brand-name analgesic and antipyretic (acetaminophen/paracetamol) that reduces fever and pain by centrally inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis; has minimal anti-inflammatory effects and a risk of severe liver injury with overdose or concurrent alcohol use; typical adult maximum daily dose is 3–4 g, with lower limits for liver disease or chronic alcohol use.

tyloxapol.definition: A nonionic detergent (surfactant) used as an emulsifying and wetting agent in pharmaceutical formulations and laboratory applications to solubilize hydrophobic substances and improve dispersion.

tympanic nerve.definition: A branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) that enters the middle ear via the tympanic canaliculus, forms the tympanic plexus on the promontory, and gives rise to the lesser petrosal nerve; it carries presynaptic parasympathetic fibers to the otic ganglion (for parotid secretion) and provides sensory innervation to the middle-ear mucosa, with accompanying sympathetic fibers from the carotid plexus.

tympanic reflex.definition: An acoustic reflex of the middle ear in which the stapedius muscle contracts in response to loud sounds, stiffening the ossicular chain to reduce sound transmission and protect the inner ear.

tympanic resonance.definition: A drum‑like, high‑pitched percussion note heard over gas‑filled hollow viscera (e.g., stomach or bowel), reflecting gaseous distention rather than solid or fluid‑filled tissue.

tympanic sulcus.definition: A groove in the tympanic part of the temporal bone surrounding the tympanic membrane, into which the tympanic annulus fits to anchor the membrane.

tympanosclerosis.definition: Calcific (sclerotic) changes of the tympanic membrane and middle ear following chronic otitis media, presenting as chalky plaques on the tympanic membrane and sometimes ossicular fixation, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

tympany.definition: A drum-like percussion note heard over a gas-filled viscus (such as the stomach or intestines), indicating distention with gas or air.

tympanogram.definition: A tympanogram is the result of tympanometry, an objective test that measures middle-ear mobility by varying air pressure in the ear canal and recording tympanic membrane compliance; it helps assess middle-ear function and detect conditions such as effusion, perforation, or Eustachian tube dysfunction.

typhoid nodules.definition: Small, necrotizing foci in reticuloendothelial tissues—most characteristically Peyer's patches of the ileum—occurring in typhoid fever due to Salmonella typhi infection; composed of macrophages and inflammatory cells and may ulcerate.

typhoid pellagra.definition: An historical/obsolete term referring to pellagra-like dermatitis and systemic symptoms seen in the setting of typhoid fever, arising from niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency or tryptophan deficiency during prolonged illness and malnutrition; not a distinct clinical entity.

typhoid vaccine.definition: A vaccine to prevent typhoid fever caused by Salmonella typhi; available as an oral live-attenuated vaccine or an injectable inactivated Vi polysaccharide or Vi-conjugate vaccine, it reduces risk but does not guarantee protection, with duration of protection typically ranging from about 2 to 5 years (longer for newer conjugate vaccines) and boosters may be recommended for travelers.

ty21a.definition: A live attenuated oral vaccine strain of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi used to immunize against typhoid fever.

typhomania.definition: A historical term for delirious mania occurring during typhus fever (a febrile illness), characterized by agitation, confusion, and mood lability; no longer used in modern psychiatry.

anna-1.definition: A paraneoplastic autoantibody directed against intracellular neuronal nuclear antigens; most commonly associated with small cell lung carcinoma and paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes such as encephalomyelitis and sensory neuronopathy, and used as a biomarker for underlying malignancy.

anna-2.definition: A paraneoplastic neuronal autoantibody (anti-Ri) directed against Ri antigen; associated with paraneoplastic neurological syndromes such as opsoclonus–myoclonus and cerebellar degeneration, most often in patients with breast or gynecologic cancers.

mobitz i block.definition: A type of second-degree atrioventricular (AV) block in which the PR interval progressively lengthens on consecutive beats until a P wave is not conducted (QRS dropped); commonly known as the Wenckebach phenomenon, typically due to AV nodal delay and often transient, sometimes related to medications or ischemia.

mobitz ii block.definition: A second-degree atrioventricular block in which occasional atrial impulses fail to conduct to the ventricles without preceding PR interval prolongation, producing dropped QRS complexes with a typically constant PR interval on conducted beats; the block is usually infranodal (involving the His-Purkinje system) and carries a risk of progression to complete heart block, often requiring pacemaker therapy.

av block.definition: Conduction of electrical impulses from the atria to the ventricles via the AV node is impaired, causing delayed or blocked transmission and often resulting in bradycardia or dropped ventricular beats. It is classified into first-degree (prolonged PR interval with all impulses conducted), second-degree (some atrial impulses fail to conduct; Mobitz I or Mobitz II), and third-degree (complete heart block with no atrial impulses conducted).

type i error.definition: The incorrect rejection of a true null hypothesis in a statistical hypothesis test (a false positive); the probability of this error is the chosen significance level, alpha.

type ii error.definition: Failure to reject a null hypothesis that is actually false in a statistical test (a false negative); the probability of this error is beta, and the test's power is 1 − beta.

tegmen tympani.definition: A thin bony plate of the temporal bone (petrous part) that forms the roof of the middle ear (tympanic cavity) and the floor of the middle cranial fossa, separating the middle ear from the cranial cavity.

tyrosinurea.definition: The excretion of the amino acid tyrosine in urine, usually due to defects in tyrosine metabolism (e.g., hereditary tyrosinemias) or hepatic dysfunction; detected by urine amino acid testing.

tyrosinosis.definition: A metabolic disorder characterized by abnormally elevated tyrosine levels in the blood and urine due to impaired degradation of tyrosine.

tetrahydrozoline hydrochloride.definition: A topical alpha-adrenergic agonist vasoconstrictor used as a nasal decongestant and ophthalmic vasoconstrictor; it reduces mucosal swelling by constricting blood vessels, with potential for rebound congestion and systemic effects if absorbed.

tzanck test.definition: A rapid cytologic test in which cells from a vesicular lesion are scraped, stained, and examined for multinucleated giant cells and acantholytic cells; historically used to presumptively diagnose herpes simplex or varicella-zoster infections, but it is nonspecific and largely replaced by PCR or culture.

ubiquitin.definition: A small regulatory protein that is covalently attached to substrate proteins (ubiquitination) to tag them for degradation by the proteasome; integral to the ubiquitin–proteasome system that regulates protein turnover and many cellular processes.

uchida technique.definition: I couldn't locate a standard medical definition for "Uchida technique" in reliable medical dictionaries. Could you specify the medical field or provide a reference?

ulceromembranous stomatitis.definition: An inflammatory condition of the oral mucosa with ulcerations that are covered by a fibrinous or pseudomembranous membrane.

ulcerogenic drug.definition: A drug that can cause ulceration of the gastrointestinal mucosa, particularly gastric or duodenal ulcers, by disrupting mucosal defenses or promoting mucosal injury.

ulceromembranous.definition: Pertaining to ulcers that are covered by a membranous, fibrin-rich layer (a pseudomembrane) on mucous surfaces.

ulcerous.definition: Relating to ulcers; characterized by ulceration or consisting of ulcers; resembling an ulcer.

antiinflammatory agents.definition: Drugs that counteract inflammation by suppressing the body's inflammatory response or mediators; commonly include nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) that inhibit cyclooxygenase enzymes, and corticosteroids that broadly suppress immune and inflammatory pathways, used to reduce pain, swelling, redness, and tissue damage in conditions such as arthritis, injury, and autoimmune diseases.

renal tubular defects.definition: Abnormalities of the renal tubules that impair reabsorption or secretion of solutes (such as bicarbonate, phosphate, glucose, amino acids, and electrolytes) and water, causing urinary losses and associated electrolyte or acid-base disturbances, typically with preserved glomerular filtration rate.

renal glycosuria.definition: An inherited or acquired condition in which glucose is excreted in the urine due to impaired proximal tubular reabsorption of filtered glucose, producing glycosuria with normal blood glucose levels; often due to mutations in the SGLT2 transporter (familial renal glycosuria) or other proximal tubulopathy.

parahydroxyphenylpyruvic acid.definition: A ketoacid intermediate in tyrosine catabolism; the α-keto acid formed from tyrosine (4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate) that is oxidized to homogentisic acid by 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase.

neonatal tyrosinemia.definition: A temporary, benign elevation of plasma tyrosine in the newborn period caused by immature hepatic metabolism of tyrosine, which typically resolves as the liver matures and usually requires no treatment.

rodent ulcer.definition: A chronic ulcerating skin neoplasm, typically a basal cell carcinoma on sun-exposed facial skin; it grows slowly with a non-healing ulcer and raised, pearly borders, and is locally destructive with rare metastasis.

ultrastructure.definition: The fine structure of cells and tissues as revealed by electron microscopy, including the organization of organelles, membranes, cytoskeletal elements, and other subcellular components at the nanometer scale.

umbilical fistula.definition: An abnormal passage that connects the umbilicus to another organ or to the skin, allowing persistent discharge from the navel (often due to persistence of embryologic remnants such as a vitelline/omphalomesenteric duct or a urachal remnant).

umbilical catheterization.definition: A neonatal procedure in which a catheter is inserted through the umbilicus into the umbilical vein or arteries to provide central venous or arterial access for administration of fluids, medications, parenteral nutrition, blood sampling, and hemodynamic monitoring.

radiopaque catheter.definition: A catheter constructed with radiopaque material or markers to be visible on X-ray or fluoroscopy, allowing visualization of its position for correct placement and monitoring during imaging-guided procedures.

blood samples.definition: A small amount of blood taken from the finger or arm to be tested.

iv bottle.definition: A container holding sterile intravenous solution for infusion into a patient’s vein, usually hung on an IV pole and connected to the patient via an IV line to deliver fluids, electrolytes, medications, or nutrition by gravity or an infusion pump; historically glass, now often plastic.

stalk.definition: A slender, stem-like attachment that connects a lesion (such as a polyp or tumor) to the underlying tissue, containing its blood supply and allowing the lesion to extend away from the surface.

yolk stalk.definition: A transient embryonic duct connecting the yolk sac to the primitive midgut (also called the omphalomesenteric or vitelline duct); it normally involutes during fetal development, and persistence can lead to Meckel diverticulum or vitelline fistula.

chorda umbilicalis.definition: An umbilical cord; a flexible conduit linking the developing fetus to the placenta, containing two umbilical arteries and one umbilical vein within Wharton’s jelly. It carries oxygen- and nutrient-rich blood from the placenta to the fetus and returns deoxygenated blood and waste from the fetus to the placenta.

funiculus umbilicalis.definition: A flexible structure containing the fetal vessels (two arteries and one vein) enclosed by Wharton’s jelly, linking the fetus to the placenta and enabling the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and wastes between mother and fetus.

vitelline duct.definition: A developmental connection between the yolk sac and the primitive midgut in the embryo (omphalomesenteric duct) that normally obliterates during fetal development; persistence can cause Meckel's diverticulum, a vitelline fistula, an enterocyst, or a fibrous cord.

umbilical fascia.definition: Fascial layer of the anterior abdominal wall around the umbilicus; a condensed connective tissue region formed by the aponeurotic fibers of the abdominal muscles (and continuity with adjacent deep fascia) at the umbilical region, helping anchor and stabilize the umbilicus.

median umbilical ligament.definition: A fibrous cord extending from the apex of the urinary bladder to the umbilicus; the obliterated urachus (allantois), a remnant forming the median umbilical ligament.

umbilical fissure.definition: A groove on the liver’s visceral surface that contains the ligamentum teres hepatis (the remnant of the fetal umbilical vein).

umbilical vasculitis.definition: Inflammation of the blood vessels within the umbilical cord (the umbilical arteries and/or vein), usually due to infection, and often associated with neonatal omphalitis or sepsis; histologically characterized by vasculitis with inflammatory infiltrates around the vessel walls.

urachal.definition: Relating to the urachus, the embryologic canal between the bladder and the umbilicus; after birth it typically fibroses to form the median umbilical ligament, and remnants can give rise to urachal fistula, sinus, or cyst.

umbilical duct.definition: An embryologic canal between the bladder and the umbilicus (the urachus, derived from the allantois); normally involutes after birth to form the median umbilical ligament; persistence can cause urachal fistula, sinus, or cyst.

uncal herniation.definition: A type of transtentorial brain herniation in which the medial temporal lobe (the uncus) herniates through the tentorial notch, compressing the brainstem and the ipsilateral oculomotor nerve (CN III), often causing a fixed dilated pupil, oculomotor palsy with a 'down-and-out' gaze, contralateral motor weakness, and potentially coma.

uncus.definition: A hook-shaped end of the hippocampal formation in the medial temporal lobe (the anterior part of the parahippocampal gyrus); a component of the limbic system involved in memory and olfactory processing.

uncinate.definition: Hook-shaped; describing a structure with a curved projection resembling a hook, such as the uncinate process of the ethmoid bone.

unciform bone.definition: A historical/alternate name for the hamate bone, a hook-shaped carpal bone of the wrist with a prominent hooked process (hamulus) on its palmar surface.

hamate bone.definition: One of the eight carpal bones of the wrist, located on the ulnar side of the distal carpal row; it is wedge-shaped and has a hook-like projection (the hamulus) on its palmar surface, and its hook forms part of Guyon's canal for the ulnar nerve and artery. It articulates with the capitate and the bases of the 4th and 5th metacarpals.

uncinaria.definition: A genus of hookworm nematodes in the family Ancylostomatidae that parasitize the small intestine of mammals (notably canids and felids); infection can cause anemia and gastrointestinal symptoms, with humans as incidental hosts acquired by skin penetration of larvae from contaminated soil.

unconjugated bilirubin.definition: A water-insoluble form of bilirubin produced from heme breakdown that has not yet been conjugated with glucuronic acid in the liver (indirect bilirubin); it is transported in the blood bound to albumin and becomes conjugated to allow excretion.

unconjugated monoclonal antibody.definition: A naked monoclonal antibody that is not conjugated to a cytotoxic payload (drug, toxin, or radionuclide); it binds a specific antigen and mediates therapeutic effects through Fc effector functions (e.g., ADCC, CDC) or receptor blockade.

unconsciousness.definition: A state in which a person is not awake and unable to respond to most stimuli, with diminished or absent awareness of self and surroundings; commonly caused by brain injury, stroke, hypoxia, overdose, or metabolic disturbances.

unicuspid.definition: Having a single cusp; a rare congenital heart-valve abnormality in which the aortic valve has only one leaflet, typically causing significant aortic stenosis and presenting in infancy or early adulthood.

drugs.definition: Substances used to diagnose, treat, prevent, or alleviate disease or medical conditions; these include prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, and illicit or recreational substances; their effects depend on dose, route of administration, and individual factors.

poisons.definition: Substances that cause harm or death to a living organism when absorbed, ingested, inhaled, or otherwise introduced, with effects that depend on dose, exposure route, and the substance’s mechanism of action.

electrolyteimbalance.definition: A disruption in the body's electrolyte concentrations (eg, sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, chloride, bicarbonate, phosphate) that impairs fluid and acid-base balance and the function of nerves and muscles.

cerebrovascularaccident.definition: The medical term for a stroke.

braintumor.definition: A mass of abnormal tissue in the brain or its coverings, which can be benign or malignant. Symptoms depend on location and may include headaches, seizures, weakness, or cognitive changes; diagnosis is usually by brain imaging (MRI/CT) and sometimes biopsy; treatment may include surgery, radiation, and/or chemotherapy.

hippocampal.definition: Relating to the hippocampus, a seahorse-shaped brain structure in the medial temporal lobe involved in memory formation and spatial navigation.

undecylenicacid.definition: A monounsaturated fatty acid with 11 carbon atoms that is used topically as an antifungal agent to treat fungal skin infections; commonly derived from castor oil.

athletesfoot.definition: A fungal infection of the skin of the feet (tinea pedis) caused by dermatophyte fungi, most commonly Trichophyton species; it presents with itching, burning, and scaling, especially between the toes, and may spread to the soles or nails. Treated with topical antifungal agents and measures to keep the feet dry.

underactive.definition: Not functioning at the normal level; having reduced activity or secretion, such as a gland producing too little hormone.

undercut.definition: A notch or indentation that lies beneath the surrounding surface or contour; in dentistry, a retention feature where a portion of tooth structure or a restoration extends beyond the adjacent margin, potentially trapping impression material or hindering seating of appliances.

goldfoil.definition: A dental restorative technique in which very thin sheets of pure gold are condensed into a prepared cavity to restore tooth structure; highly malleable and corrosion-resistant, historically common but now largely replaced by modern materials.

cemented.definition: Fixed in place by cement; typically refers to anchoring a prosthesis to bone using bone cement (usually polymethyl methacrylate), providing immediate stability.

underdamping.definition: An adjective describing a dynamic system's response when damping is insufficient to prevent oscillations after a disturbance; the system exhibits overshoot and oscillatory decay toward equilibrium, with a damping ratio between 0 and 1 (less than critical damping).

undernutrition.definition: A deficiency of energy and/or essential nutrients resulting in impaired growth, immune function, and overall health, typically due to inadequate intake, malabsorption, or increased metabolic needs; includes wasting, stunting, and micronutrient deficiencies.

underwater.definition: Positioned or occurring beneath the surface of a body of water; describing procedures or assessments conducted while submerged.

aquatherapy.definition: A form of physical therapy performed in water that uses buoyancy to reduce joint stress and hydrostatic resistance to improve range of motion, strength, balance, and functional mobility; commonly used for rehabilitation from musculoskeletal injuries, arthritis, chronic pain, and certain neurological conditions.

aquatic.definition: Relating to water; pertaining to organisms that live in water or to activities, environments, or therapies conducted in water (e.g., water-based therapy).

exercise.definition: A planned, structured, and repetitive form of physical activity undertaken to improve or maintain physical fitness, health, or performance, typically performed with specified frequency, intensity, duration, and mode (e.g., aerobic, resistance, or flexibility training).

underwaterseal.definition: A chest drainage system in which a chest tube is connected to a bottle or chamber containing sterile water to create a one-way valve; air from the pleural space bubbles through the water and escapes, but water prevents backflow, allowing drainage of air and fluid and facilitating lung re-expansion; bubbling indicates an air leak; used for pneumothorax, pleural effusion, and after thoracic surgery; the collection bottle is kept below chest level.

watertrap.definition: A moisture-trapping device or chamber that collects condensate from a gas or fluid line to prevent moisture from entering downstream equipment or the patient.

underweight.definition: To be below a weight that is seen as normal.

undescendedtestis.definition: An anatomical condition in which one or both testes fail to descend into the scrotum, typically remaining in the abdomen or inguinal canal; also known as cryptorchidism.

monorchism.definition: A condition in which a male has only one testicle in the scrotum, due to congenital absence (unilateral testicular agenesis) or loss/removal of one testis.

undifferentiated.definition: Not differentiated; lacking specialized structure or function. In pathology, cells or tumors that do not resemble the tissue of origin and lack maturation or lineage-specific features, often indicating high-grade malignancy.

stemcell.definition: A primitive cell capable of self-renewal and differentiation into multiple specialized cell types; these cells sustain tissue development and repair, with embryonic stem cells typically pluripotent and adult stem cells usually multipotent.

undifferentiation.definition: The state in which cells have not undergone differentiation into mature, specialized cell types; in pathology, undifferentiated neoplasms show no histologic evidence of lineage-specific differentiation and often resemble primitive cells.

undisplaced.definition: Not moved from its normal position; in orthopedics, a fracture in which the bone fragments remain aligned and there is no displacement or deformity.

undulating.definition: Having a wave-like shape or motion; rising and falling in a smooth, sinuous pattern.

undulant.definition: Having a wave-like motion; undulating, with alternating rises and falls in intensity or level.

binovular.definition: Relating to two ova; produced when two separate ova are fertilized by two different sperm, usually resulting in dizygotic twins.

uniovular.definition: Relating to or derived from a single ovum; produced from one ovum. In obstetrics, used to describe a pregnancy or embryo that originated from one ovum (monozygotic).

neglect.definition: A neurological deficit in which a patient fails to attend to or respond to stimuli on the side opposite a brain lesion, most often after damage to the right hemisphere.

unilateral.definition: Relating to or affecting only one side of the body or a single organ or part; opposite of bilateral.

blastoma.definition: A malignant tumor composed of immature, embryonal-like cells (blast cells) that resemble early developmental tissue.

unicellular.definition: Relating to or consisting of a single cell; an organism that lives as one cell and carries out all life processes within that cell.

uniseptate.definition: Having a single septum; describing hyphae that are divided by one cross-wall, producing two compartments.

unisex.definition: Describing something that applies to or is suitable for both sexes; not specific to one gender.

unipolar.definition: Relating to or characterized by a single pole or single process; in neuroscience, a unipolar (pseudounipolar) neuron has one process that divides distally into peripheral and central branches; in psychiatry, unipolar depression refers to major depressive disorder without manic or hypomanic episodes.

monopolar.definition: Relating to a single electrical pole; in electrosurgery, current passes from a single active electrode through the patient's tissues to a distant return electrode (dispersive pad), enabling tissue cutting and coagulation.

organ donations.definition: The process by which a person or their legally authorized representative donates one or more organs (such as the kidney, liver, heart, lungs, pancreas, or intestine) for transplantation into another person in need, typically after death but sometimes from a living donor; donated organs are allocated to recipients based on medical urgency, compatibility, and suitability.

type o negative.definition: A blood type in which red blood cells lack A and B antigens and the Rh (D) antigen; individuals have anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma and can donate red blood cells to any ABO/Rh type (universal donor) but can receive only O negative blood.

universal recipient.definition: A person with AB blood type who expresses both A and B antigens on their red blood cells and lacks anti-A and anti-B antibodies in their plasma, allowing them to receive red blood cells from any ABO/Rh blood type.

magnesium oxide.definition: A white, odorless inorganic compound (MgO) that provides magnesium; used as a dietary supplement to prevent or treat magnesium deficiency, as an antacid to relieve heartburn, and as a laxative; absorption is relatively poor compared with some other magnesium salts.

tannic acid.definition: A hydrolyzable tannin that yields gallic acid upon hydrolysis; a polyphenolic compound with astringent properties used as an antiseptic and preservative, derived from gall nuts and other plant sources.

universal antidote.definition: A hypothetical antidote claimed to reverse all poisonings; there is no universal antidote in clinical practice. Management of poisoning is toxin-specific and relies on targeted antidotes when available plus supportive care.

uvulopalatopharyngoplasty.definition: A surgical treatment for obstructive sleep apnea that involves removing the uvula, the tonsils, and a rim of loose tissue at the back of the soft palate.

upper gi x-ray study.definition: An X-ray radiologic examination of the upper gastrointestinal tract (esophagus, stomach, and duodenum) performed after swallowing a radiopaque contrast medium (typically barium), using fluoroscopy to assess structure and function and to diagnose conditions such as ulcers, strictures, hernias, motility disorders, or reflux.

ethmoidal air cells.definition: A group of small air-filled cavities within the ethmoid bone (the ethmoid sinuses), divided into anterior, middle, and posterior cells; lined with respiratory epithelium and draining into the nasal cavity—anterior and middle cells into the middle meatus, posterior cells into the superior meatus.

sphenoidal sinuses.definition: Air-filled cavities within the body of the sphenoid bone, part of the paranasal sinus system; they vary in size and number (usually two) and drain into the sphenoethmoidal recess of the nasal cavity via the ostia on their superior posterior walls.

unroofed coronary sinus.definition: A rare congenital cardiac anomaly in which the wall (roof) separating the left atrium from the coronary sinus is partially or completely absent, causing an abnormal communication between the left atrium and the coronary sinus (and thus with the right atrium); frequently associated with a persistent left superior vena cava and other atrial septal defects.

urachal diverticulum.definition: A congenital outpouching (diverticulum) of the urinary bladder at the bladder dome along the urachal remnant, due to incomplete obliteration of the urachus; it communicates with the bladder lumen and may be asymptomatic but can predispose to infections, stone formation, or, rarely, urachal carcinoma.

vesical diverticulum.definition: A pouch-like outpouching of the urinary bladder wall that communicates with the bladder lumen; it may be congenital or acquired (often due to chronic bladder outlet obstruction) and can predispose to urinary stasis, infection, and stone formation.

upper pole of kidney.definition: The superior-most portion of the kidney, forming its rounded upper extremity that lies beneath the diaphragm and is closely related to the adrenal gland.

deciduous teeth.definition: The first teeth that grow in young children. There are 20 primary teeth. They fall out and are replaced by permanent teeth. Also called milk teeth or baby teeth.

primary teeth.definition: Baby teeth, the first teeth to erupt in children. There are 20 in total. They fall out and are replaced by permanent teeth. Also called milk teeth.

maxillary right third molar.definition: A permanent molar at the far back of the upper right dental arch (maxilla); the last tooth in that quadrant, commonly known as the upper right wisdom tooth.

mandibular right third molar.definition: The final molar in the lower jaw on the right side, commonly called the lower right wisdom tooth.

university of wisconsin solution.definition: A hypothermic organ preservation solution developed at the University of Wisconsin, used to preserve donor organs (such as kidney, liver, or heart) during transport; it minimizes ischemic injury and cellular edema by providing impermeants, energy substrates, and antioxidants.

upper airway obstruction.definition: A blockage of airflow in the upper airway—the nose, pharynx, or larynx above the vocal cords—that can be partial or complete, causing dyspnea and often stridor; common causes include foreign body, edema (e.g., epiglottitis, croup, anaphylaxis), trauma, and masses.

upper esophageal sphincter.definition: Muscular valve located at the upper portion of the esophagus that opens to allow food or liquid to enter the digestive system.

cricopharyngeus muscle.definition: The part of the inferior pharyngeal constrictor that forms the upper esophageal sphincter; it is tonically contracted at rest and relaxes during swallowing to allow passage of a bolus from the pharynx into the esophagus, with dysfunction potentially causing dysphagia.

hoffmann sign.definition: A clinical sign where flicking the nail of the middle finger causes flexion of the thumb and index finger, indicating upper motor neuron dysfunction of the corticospinal tract, often seen in cervical myelopathy or other pyramidal tract lesions.

unverricht's disease.definition: A rare autosomal recessive form of progressive myoclonus epilepsy that begins in childhood, characterized by myoclonic and generalized seizures, ataxia, and cognitive decline, caused by mutations in the CSTB (cystatin B) gene.

myoclonic epilepsy.definition: An epileptic syndrome in which brief, involuntary muscle jerks (myoclonus) are the predominant seizure type; these jerks may occur alone or accompany other seizure types, often evolving into generalized seizures. It commonly belongs to idiopathic generalized epilepsies and typically begins in adolescence (as in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy), with seizures often triggered by sleep deprivation, fatigue, or photic stimulation. EEG usually shows generalized epileptiform discharges associated with the myoclonic events.

unmyelinated.definition: Lacking a myelin sheath around an axon; a nerve fiber not insulated by myelin, resulting in slower conduction of nerve impulses (continuous conduction).

superoxide radical.definition: An extremely reactive free radical form of molecular oxygen, the superoxide anion (O2−). It is produced by mitochondria and enzymes such as NADPH oxidase; it participates in signaling at low levels but contributes to oxidative stress and damage to lipids, proteins, and DNA when in excess, and is rapidly dismutated to hydrogen peroxide by superoxide dismutase.

urachal sinus.definition: A congenital urachal anomaly in which a blind-ending sinus tract opens at the umbilicus and ends within the urachal remnant, not reaching the bladder, and may discharge mucus or pus and become infected.

prune-belly syndrome.definition: A rare congenital disorder defined by a triad: deficiency or absence of the abdominal wall muscles (producing a wrinkled, prune-like abdomen), urinary tract anomalies (often obstruction with hydronephrosis or megacystis), and cryptorchidism in males; it can be associated with pulmonary hypoplasia and other congenital anomalies.

urachal cyst.definition: A congenital cystic remnant of the urachus due to incomplete obliteration of the embryologic urachal canal between the bladder and the umbilicus, typically presenting as a midline infraumbilical cyst that can become infected.

urethral sphincter.definition: A ring of muscle surrounding the urethra that regulates urine flow; it consists of the internal urethral sphincter (involuntary smooth muscle at the bladder neck) and the external urethral sphincter (voluntary skeletal muscle in the pelvic floor).

urethrocele.definition: Prolapse (herniation) of the urethra into the vaginal canal, a type of anterior vaginal wall prolapse caused by pelvic floor weakness; may occur with cystocele.

urethral diverticulum.definition: A pouch-like outpouching of the urethral wall that can collect urine; an acquired or congenital defect of the urethra often due to obstruction or inflammation of periurethral glands, most common in women, presenting with post-void dribbling and recurrent urinary tract infections and treated by surgical excision and urethral repair.

urethral diverticula.definition: A localized outpouching of the urethral mucosa that communicates with the urethral lumen, most commonly occurring in women, typically due to obstruction or inflammation of periurethral glands, and presenting with urinary symptoms such as dysuria, postvoid dribbling, dyspareunia, or recurrent UTIs.

urethrocystitis.definition: Inflammation of both the urethra and the bladder, usually due to infection (often ascending from the urethra), characterized by dysuria, urinary frequency and urgency, and suprapubic discomfort; treated with appropriate antibiotics.

urethroplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair or reconstruct the urethra, usually to treat urethral strictures or injury, often by excising scar tissue and reanastomosing the segments or by grafting to widen the lumen.

urethroscope.definition: An endoscopic instrument inserted through the urethra to visualize the urethra and lower urinary tract, used for diagnostic inspection or instrumental procedures.

ureteritis.definition: Inflammation of the ureter, usually due to infection or irritation, presenting with flank or groin pain and possibly dysuria, fever, or urinary abnormalities; may occur with urinary tract infection or ureteral obstruction.

ureterocolostomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which a ureter is anastomosed to the colon to divert urine into the colon for excretion, typically performed when the bladder is not usable or has been removed.

ureterography.definition: A radiographic imaging study in which contrast material is injected directly into the ureter (typically retrograde ureterography) to visualize the ureter and identify obstruction, stones, strictures, or other ureteral abnormalities.

ureterocystoscope.definition: An endoscopic instrument used to visualize the ureter and the urinary bladder (lower urinary tract), typically enabling diagnostic evaluation or therapeutic interventions in both structures.

ureterohydronephrosis.definition: A dilation of the ureter along with hydronephrosis, caused by obstruction of urine flow that prevents normal drainage from the kidney.

pelviureteral.definition: Relating to the renal pelvis and the ureter.

ureteroplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair or reconstruct the ureter to treat injury, obstruction, or stricture, typically involving removal of a diseased segment and reestablishment of ureteral continuity.

ureteropyelonephritis.definition: Inflammation and infection of the ureter and renal pelvis (upper urinary tract), usually due to ascending bacterial infection often in the setting of urinary obstruction or reflux; managed with antibiotics and treatment of the underlying cause.

ureterosigmoidostomy.definition: A urinary diversion in which the ureters are surgically connected to the sigmoid colon, so urine is excreted via the rectum after bladder removal; associated with complications such as urinary tract infections, electrolyte disturbances, metabolic acidosis, and potential renal function deterioration.

ureteral stent.definition: A small, flexible tube placed inside the ureter to keep it open and allow urine to flow from the kidney to the bladder, usually inserted temporarily after stones, injury, or ureteral surgery and later removed; often a double-J stent with curled ends to anchor it.

ureteral jet.definition: An observable jet of urine entering the bladder from a ureter, typically seen on ultrasound (often with color Doppler); its presence indicates patency of the corresponding ureter, while absence or reduction may suggest obstruction or impaired renal drainage.

ureteral orifice.definition: The opening in the urinary bladder wall through which each ureter drains urine into the bladder; located at the bladder base within the trigone and often described as a slit-like orifice that helps prevent vesicoureteral reflux.

ovarian fossa.definition: A shallow depression on the lateral wall of the pelvis in which the ovary rests; it is part of the peritoneal cavity.

nephritic gingivitis.definition: Not a standard term; likely describes gingival inflammation occurring in the setting of nephritic (renal) disease or uremia. In advanced kidney failure, elevated urea in saliva is converted to ammonia by oral bacteria, irritates the gingiva, and causes red, swollen, and easily bleeding gums. This presentation often aligns with what is clinically described as uremic gingivitis.

uremic syndrome.definition: Clinical syndrome caused by accumulation of uremic toxins due to kidney failure, presenting with multisystem symptoms such as nausea, anorexia, fatigue, vomiting, pruritus, cognitive or neurologic impairment, neuropathy, pericarditis, and platelet dysfunction; typically resolved or mitigated by dialysis or kidney transplantation.

uremic frost.definition: A skin manifestation of severe azotemia in advanced kidney failure, characterized by deposition of urea crystals on the skin that forms a white, frost-like crust, commonly on the face and lips; resolves with dialysis or renal recovery.

uremic coma.definition: A coma resulting from severe uremia due to kidney failure, caused by the accumulation of uremic toxins that depress the central nervous system; an emergency requiring urgent dialysis and correction of metabolic disturbances.

uremic breath.definition: A distinctively foul, ammonia-like breath odor seen in severe uremia/advanced renal failure, produced by oral bacteria that convert urea into ammonia.

urethral sinus.definition: A small, blind-ending tract that opens into the urethra or communicates with the urethral lumen, typically congenital or acquired after infection or trauma, and that may drain urine or other secretions.

urethral folds.definition: Two ventral embryologic folds of the urogenital sinus surrounding the developing urethral groove; in males they fuse to form the penile (spongy) urethra, while in females they remain unfused and develop into the labia minora.

vesicourethral angle.definition: The vesicourethral angle is the angle formed at the vesicourethral junction where the bladder neck meets the urethra; this angulation influences the direction of urine flow and can affect catheterization and continence mechanics.

urex.definition: Not a recognized medical term; could be a misspelling of urethra (the duct through which urine exits the bladder) or ureter (the tube carrying urine from the kidney to the bladder).

methenamine hippurate.definition: A urinary tract antiseptic that, in acidic urine, decomposes to formaldehyde to kill bacteria; used primarily to prevent recurrent urinary tract infections, with effectiveness dependent on urine acidification.

uri.definition: An infection of the upper respiratory tract, typically viral, involving the nose, throat, sinuses, or larynx; symptoms often include nasal congestion or discharge, sore throat, cough, sneezing, and sometimes fever; it is usually self-limited and treated with supportive care, with antibiotics not routinely indicated unless a bacterial complication is suspected.

ammoniuria.definition: Presence of ammonium ions (NH4+) in urine, usually due to bacterial urease activity converting urea to ammonia, often associated with alkaline urine and urease-producing urinary tract infections.

enzymuria.definition: The presence of enzymes in the urine, often indicating renal tubular injury or urinary tract inflammation.

paruria.definition:

uric aciduria.definition: A condition in which uric acid is present in the urine; typically reflects increased uric acid production or decreased renal clearance and can be associated with purine metabolism disorders or uric acid kidney stones.

uricosuria.definition: The excretion of uric acid in the urine; elevated urinary uric acid (hyperuricosuria) can be associated with gout and uric acid kidney stones.

uricotelic.definition: Relating to the excretion of nitrogenous waste as uric acid in urine; characteristic of animals (e.g., birds, reptiles) that conserve water by emitting uric acid rather than ammonia or urea.

uricosuric drugs.definition: A class of drugs that increase renal excretion of uric acid by inhibiting reabsorption of urate in the proximal tubule, thereby lowering serum uric acid levels; used to treat hyperuricemia and gout, but require adequate renal function and may increase the risk of uric acid stones and drug interactions.

uridine.definition: A nucleoside composed of the pyrimidine base uracil attached to a ribose sugar; a building block of RNA; when phosphorylated to UMP, UDP, or UTP, it serves as RNA nucleotides.

antineoplastics.definition: A drug or agent used to treat cancer by inhibiting the growth and spread of malignant (neoplastic) cells; includes cytotoxic chemotherapy, hormonal therapies, targeted therapies, and immunotherapies.

urinal.definition: A receptacle used to collect urine, typically a portable bedside container for bedridden or incapacitated patients; also a bathroom fixture for male urination in some settings.

venereal infection.definition: An infection transmitted primarily through sexual contact (genital, oral, or anal), caused by bacteria, viruses, or parasites; examples include syphilis, gonorrhea, chlamydia, herpes simplex, HIV/AIDS, human papillomavirus infection, and trichomoniasis.

anticholinergic medications.definition: Drugs that block acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors, thereby reducing parasympathetic nervous system activity. They decrease secretions and smooth-muscle tone and commonly cause dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, urinary retention, and tachycardia; used for Parkinson disease symptoms, motion sickness, overactive bladder, and certain airway or preoperative indications.

intermittent catheterization.definition: Intermittent catheterization is the periodic insertion of a catheter through the urethra into the bladder to drain urine, with removal after emptying; typically performed regularly by the patient or caregiver to manage urinary retention or neurogenic bladder and to avoid an indwelling catheter.

urinary continence.definition: Urinary continence is the ability to store urine in the bladder and prevent involuntary leakage, allowing voluntary initiation of urination at an appropriate time.

urinary elimination.definition: The process of expelling urine from the body through the urinary tract, including storage of urine in the bladder and its release via the urethra (micturition), controlled by detrusor muscle contraction and urethral sphincter relaxation.

urinary elimination management.definition: A clinical process that includes assessment and interventions to promote safe, efficient urine elimination, such as encouraging regular voiding, appropriate hydration, bladder training, and use of catheterization or other therapies as indicated to prevent retention, incontinence, and infection.

urine flow study.definition: A noninvasive test that measures the rate of urine flow during urination to assess bladder emptying and possible urinary tract obstruction; results include maximum flow rate (Qmax) and voided volume.

iv urography.definition: A radiographic imaging test in which an iodinated contrast agent is injected intravenously and serial X-rays are taken to visualize the kidneys, ureters, and bladder and assess their anatomy and function; also known as intravenous pyelography (IVP).

retrograde pyelography.definition: A radiographic procedure in which iodinated contrast is injected retrogradely into the ureter via a cystoscope to opacify the ureter and renal pelvis for imaging, typically to evaluate obstruction, stones, strictures, or ureteral injury.

urethroscopy.definition: Endoscopic examination of the urethra using a urethroscope (rigid or flexible) to visualize the urethral lumen for diagnosis and, if needed, to perform minor therapeutic maneuvers.

ultrasonic imaging.definition: An imaging modality that uses high-frequency sound waves emitted by a transducer; echoes from tissues and fluids are converted into real-time images of internal structures. It is noninvasive and does not use ionizing radiation; Doppler ultrasound can evaluate blood flow.

nuclear imaging.definition: A medical imaging modality that uses radioactive tracers administered to the patient; the tracer’s distribution reflects physiological or metabolic processes and is detected by gamma cameras (SPECT) or PET scanners to produce functional, rather than anatomical, images. It provides information on organ perfusion, metabolism, receptor status, and function, and is used to diagnose and monitor conditions such as cardiovascular disease, cancer, and brain disorders. Images may be qualitative or quantitative (e.g., SUV with PET).

urinary albumin.definition: Albumin excreted in urine; normally present only in trace amounts, but increased urinary albumin (albuminuria) indicates kidney damage or increased glomerular permeability and is used to screen for and monitor kidney disease. It is often quantified as albumin-to-creatinine ratio or 24-hour urinary albumin, with microalbuminuria roughly 30–300 mg/day and macroalbuminuria >300 mg/day.

sediment.definition: Solid material that settles out of a liquid suspension; a deposit formed when particles precipitate or are centrifuged, commonly assessed in urine sediment and may include cells, crystals, casts, and bacteria.

urine culture and sensitivity.definition: A diagnostic laboratory test in which a urine sample is cultured to detect bacteria and identify the causative organism, with antibiotic susceptibility testing to determine which antibiotics are likely to be effective.

bacteriological culture.definition: A method of growing bacteria in a suitable nutrient medium under controlled conditions (eg, temperature, atmosphere) to isolate, identify, and study bacterial organisms, typically used clinically to detect infection and guide treatment (including antibiotic susceptibility testing).

osmolarity.definition: A measure of the total concentration of osmotically active particles in a solution, expressed as osmoles per liter (Osm/L); it reflects the osmotic pressure the solution would exert across a semipermeable membrane. It is estimated by summing the molar concentrations of all solutes, counting each particle after dissociation (e.g., NaCl contributes about 2 Osm per mole).

24-hour urine test.definition: An diagnostic procedure in which all urine produced during a 24-hour period is collected and analyzed to quantify substances excreted by the kidneys, used to assess kidney function and diagnose metabolic or urinary disorders.

urine glucose test.definition: A test that detects glucose in urine (glucosuria), usually by a dipstick; a positive result suggests elevated blood glucose and possibly diabetes, but it is influenced by urine concentration and renal threshold and is less reliable than blood glucose testing for diagnosing or monitoring diabetes.

urinary sobriety.definition: A state of abstinence from intoxicants as evidenced by a negative urine toxicology screen for substances (e.g., alcohol or illicit drugs). Note: not a standard medical term.

uroporphyria.definition: A porphyria defined by excess urinary uroporphyrin (primarily uroporphyrin I) due to a block in heme synthesis, most commonly from uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency.

uroporphyrinogen-1-synthase-test.definition: A laboratory assay that measures the activity of uroporphyrinogen-III synthase (formerly called uroporphyrinogen-1 synthase) in blood or tissue, used to diagnose congenital erythropoietic porphyria by detecting deficient enzyme activity.

urobilin.definition: A yellow pigment formed by the oxidation of urobilinogen, derived from bilirubin breakdown in the intestine; excreted in urine and responsible for the yellow color of urine.

urobilinogen.definition: A colorless intestinal pigment formed by bacterial reduction of bilirubin; some is reabsorbed and excreted in urine as urobilinogen, while the remainder is converted to urobilin (yellow pigment) and stercobilin (fecal pigment).

urobilinuria.definition: Presence of urobilin in the urine; a pigment formed from bilirubin by intestinal bacteria and subsequently excreted in urine, typically reflecting increased bilirubin turnover or impaired hepatic processing.

urodynamics.definition: A set of tests that evaluate the function of the lower urinary tract (bladder and urethra), including how the bladder fills, stores, and voids urine, by measuring pressures, flow, capacity, and sphincter activity during filling and emptying.

urogenital.definition: Relating to the urinary tract and the genital organs; pertaining to both the urinary and reproductive systems.

urogenital hiatus.definition: A gap in the pelvic floor (part of the pelvic diaphragm) through which the urethra and, in females, the vagina pass from the pelvis to the perineum; bounded anteriorly by the pubic symphysis and inferiorly by the perineal membrane, with the levator ani forming the posterior boundary.

urogenital peritoneum.definition: A portion of the peritoneum that lines the pelvic cavity and covers the urinary bladder and pelvic portion of the reproductive tract; the serous membrane of the urogenital system forming the pelvic folds and pouches (e.g., vesicouterine and rectouterine recesses).

urogenital region.definition: The anatomical region containing the urinary and genital organs; essentially the pelvic and perineal area where the urinary tract and reproductive organs reside.

urogenital sinus.definition: An embryologic structure—the ventral portion of the cloaca—that gives rise to the lower urinary tract (bladder neck and urethra) and, in females, the lower vagina.

urogenital triangle.definition: The anterior portion of the perineum, bounded by the pubic symphysis and the ischial tuberosities, containing the external genitalia and associated urogenital structures.

urolithiasis.definition: Formation of calculi (stones) in the urinary tract due to crystallization of mineral salts (e.g., calcium oxalate, calcium phosphate, uric acid, or struvite), most commonly in the kidneys or bladder.

urological.definition: Relating to urology; the branch of medicine that deals with diseases of the urinary tract in both sexes and the male reproductive system.

urologist.definition: A specialist who deals with the urinary tract and male reproductive system.

urology.definition: A medical specialty focused on the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the urinary tract in both sexes and the male reproductive system, including the kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra, and related structures.

urometer.definition: A device used to measure the volume of urine produced, typically a calibrated container attached to a urinary drainage bag to monitor urine output and fluid balance.

urinometer.definition: An instrument used to measure the specific gravity (density) of a urine sample, typically a hydrometer, to assess urine concentration and hydration status.

uropathy.definition: A disease or disorder of the urinary tract, including the kidneys, ureters, bladder, or urethra.

urothelium.definition: A specialized stratified epithelium lining most of the urinary tract (renal pelvis, ureters, bladder, and proximal urethra) composed of basal, intermediate, and superficial umbrella cells; it is highly stretchable to accommodate urine volume and forms a barrier to urine solutes and pathogens.

urticaria pigmentosa.definition: A form of cutaneous mastocytosis presenting with pigmented macules and papules on the skin that urticate when stroked or rubbed (positive Darier sign) due to localized mast cell proliferation and histamine release; most common in children and may be associated with systemic mastocytosis in adults.

urticaria bullosa.definition: A rare variant of urticaria in which large, tense bullae (blisters) develop on urticarial plaques due to mast cell–mediated histamine release and increased dermal vascular permeability, often triggered by physical stimuli.

urticaria maculosa.definition: A variant of urticaria in which the skin lesions are flat, pigmented macules rather than the typical raised wheals; usually pruritic and transient, often recurrent in response to triggers such as allergens, infections, or medications. Managed similarly to urticaria with antihistamines and avoidance of triggers.

urticaria medicamentosa.definition: A hypersensitivity reaction to a medication presenting as transient, pruritic wheals (hives) with surrounding erythema; occurs after drug exposure and typically resolves after discontinuation of the offending drug. It may be IgE-mediated or non–IgE-mediated and is usually managed by stopping the drug and treating with antihistamines, with systemic corticosteroids for severe cases.

usan.definition: An official nonproprietary (generic) drug name in the United States, assigned by the United States Adopted Names (USAN) Council to provide a standard, unique name for medicines used in labeling, prescribing, and pharmacology.

usher syndrome.definition: An autosomal recessive genetic disorder characterized by congenital sensorineural hearing loss and progressive retinal degeneration (retinitis pigmentosa) leading to night blindness and loss of peripheral vision, often with vestibular dysfunction; commonly has three clinical subtypes with varying onset and severity.

assisted reproductive technologies.definition: A group of medical procedures used to help people conceive by handling eggs, sperm, and embryos outside the body; includes techniques such as in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), embryo transfer, and related laboratory methods.

corticosteroid ointments.definition: Topical preparations containing corticosteroid (glucocorticoid) agents applied to the skin to reduce inflammation, itching, and immune responses. Ointments are oil-based formulations that often penetrate the skin more deeply and are typically more potent than creams, used for inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis, and psoriasis. Prolonged or extensive use can cause skin thinning, pigment changes, striae, and local immune suppression; use should be limited and guided by a clinician.

phenyl salicylate.definition: An organic ester—the phenyl ester of salicylic acid. Historically used as a laxative (sold as salol) and as a fragrance fixative in cosmetics; it hydrolyzes in the gut to salicylic acid and phenol.

hyoscyamine sulfate.definition: A tropane alkaloid antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) agent; the sulfate salt form used as an antispasmodic to relieve GI and genitourinary smooth-muscle spasm and to decrease secretions by blocking acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors.

alfuzosin.definition: A non-selective α1-adrenergic receptor antagonist used to treat lower urinary tract symptoms due to benign prostatic hyperplasia by relaxing smooth muscle in the bladder neck and prostate, thereby improving urine flow; typically taken as a single daily dose after a meal.

fetomaternal hemorrhage.definition: The passage of fetal red blood cells into the maternal circulation, typically through disruption of placental vessels, which can lead to maternal alloimmunization against fetal red cell antigens and, if the hemorrhage is substantial, fetal anemia or hydrops.

uterine inertia.definition: Failure of the uterus to contract effectively during labor, resulting in weak or infrequent contractions and little to no cervical dilation or progression of labor (dysfunctional or arrested labor).

uterine ischemia.definition: Reduced blood flow to the uterus resulting in inadequate tissue oxygenation (uterine tissue hypoxia) and potential ischemic injury; may arise from compromised arterial inflow, impaired venous outflow, or systemic hypotension, and is seen in obstetric emergencies and uterine surgery.

uterine peristalsis.definition: Rhythmic, coordinated contractions of the uterine myometrium that propagate as peristaltic waves through the uterine cavity, aiding transport of sperm toward the fallopian tubes and clearance of menstrual debris; waves typically originate in the fundus and travel toward the cervix, modulated by sex hormones (estrogen promotes, progesterone inhibits).

uterine retroflexion.definition: A backward bending and tilting of the uterus such that the fundus points posteriorly toward the sacrum, i.e., the uterus is flexed backward on the cervix—a variant of normal anatomy that can be asymptomatic or associated with dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, or fertility/pregnancy issues in some cases.

uterine retroversion.definition: A condition in which the uterus is tilted backward (posteriorly) toward the sacrum instead of forward over the bladder; often a normal variant and asymptomatic, though it can be associated with pelvic pain or dyspareunia in some cases.

uterine anteflexion.definition: A forward bending of the uterus in which the uterine body flexes anteriorly on the cervix, so the fundus points toward the bladder.

uterine anteversion.definition: Forward tilting of the uterus so that the fundus points anteriorly toward the bladder, with the cervix directed posteriorly toward the sacrum; this is a normal anatomical variant in many individuals.

uterine sinus.definition: A venous channel in the uterus, specifically a dilated venous structure in the endometrium (the uterine lining) that forms part of the endometrial microvasculature and drains blood from the lining.

uterine souffle.definition: A soft, blowing vascular sound heard over the uterus during pregnancy, synchronous with the maternal pulse, produced by increased placental bed blood flow; a normal finding that typically disappears after delivery.

uterine sound.definition: A slender, straight, often calibrated instrument with a blunt tip inserted through the cervix into the uterine cavity to measure uterine depth and assess cervical canal patency.

partial involution.definition: Incomplete regression of tissue size after enlargement, resulting in only a partial return toward the baseline with residual tissue mass and possibly retained function.

uterine swab.definition: A sterile swab inserted through the cervix into the uterine cavity to collect material from the endometrium for laboratory testing (e.g., culture, Gram stain, or cytology).

uterine tenaculum.definition: A curved, hook-shaped instrument with teeth used to grasp and stabilize the cervix to provide traction during gynecologic procedures.

uteroabdominal pregnancy.definition: A rare ectopic pregnancy in which the conceptus implants directly in the peritoneal cavity of the abdomen, outside the uterus, with placental tissue attached to abdominal organs rather than the uterine lining.

utero-ovarian varicocele.definition: Dilation and tortuosity of the pelvic venous system draining the uterus and ovaries (ovarian/uterine veins) due to venous valvular incompetence or outflow obstruction, causing pelvic venous congestion; commonly associated with chronic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, and may contribute to infertility.

ovarian varicocele.definition: A dilation of the veins draining the ovary (the ovarian venous plexus) due to valvular incompetence or venous hypertension, producing pelvic venous varices that can cause chronic pelvic pain and may be associated with infertility; left-sided predominance is common.

uteroplacental sinus.definition: A dilated maternal vascular channel in the placental bed (decidua basalis) that carries maternal blood into the intervillous space to bathe the chorionic villi; part of the maternal circulation of the placenta, not a fetal vessel.

uteroplasty.definition: A surgical procedure to repair or reconstruct the uterus.

uterotomy.definition: A surgical incision into the uterus, usually made to access the fetus or intrauterine contents (as in cesarean delivery); also known as hysterotomy.

blastokinin.definition: A historical term for a culture extract or factor believed to promote blastocyst development in vitro; its use is obsolete and not part of standard modern embryology.

uteroglobulin.definition: An archaic term for an immunoglobulin present in uterine secretions, historically thought to provide local immune protection in the uterus during pregnancy; not commonly used in modern terminology.

rectovaginal examination.definition: A manual gynecologic examination in which a finger is inserted into the vagina and another into the rectum to palpate the rectovaginal space and surrounding pelvic structures for masses, tenderness, or nodularity.

uterine appendages.definition: The ovaries and fallopian tubes, the structures attached to the uterus, collectively known as the adnexa uteri.

uterosalpingography.definition: A radiologic procedure in which contrast material is injected through the cervix into the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes, with X-ray or fluoroscopic imaging to evaluate uterine shape and tubal patency; used in infertility evaluation.

vesicouterine.definition: Relating to the bladder and uterus.

vesicouterine pouch.definition: A peritoneal recess in the female pelvis formed by the peritoneum as it reflects from the bladder to the uterus; also called the anterior cul-de-sac, located between the posterior surface of the bladder and the anterior surface of the uterus.

endocervical glands.definition: Glands in the endocervical canal that secrete mucus; lined by tall columnar epithelium with ducts opening into the endocervical lumen, their secretions contribute to cervical mucus and lubrication (duct obstruction can form Nabothian cysts).

endocervical smear.definition: A cytology specimen collected from the endocervical canal for microscopic examination, usually obtained by scraping or brushing during a Pap test to screen for cervical dysplasia and cancer.

schillers iodine test.definition: A gynecologic screening method in which Lugol's iodine is applied to the cervix; normal glycogen-rich squamous epithelium stains brown, while dysplastic or abnormal areas do not stain and appear pale, helping identify lesions for biopsy.

clear cell adenocarcinoma.definition: Malignant gland-forming epithelial tumor in which the tumor cells have clear cytoplasm due to glycogen (or other substance) accumulation; a histologic variant of adenocarcinoma, most notably seen in the vagina/cervix (DES-associated vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma) and other sites.

uveal melanoma.definition: A malignant tumor arising from melanocytes within the uveal tract (iris, ciliary body, or choroid), most often the choroid; it is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults and frequently metastasizes hematogenously, especially to the liver. Treatment depends on size and location and may include plaque brachytherapy, proton beam radiotherapy, laser therapy, or enucleation.

uveal tract.definition: The vascular middle layer of the eye, consisting of the iris, ciliary body, and choroid; it supplies blood to intraocular tissues and contains structures involved in accommodation (ciliary muscle) and aqueous humor production (ciliary processes).

utriculus.definition: A small sac within the vestibule of the inner ear; one of the otolith organs that senses linear acceleration and head position relative to gravity, via a macula with hair cells and otoliths.

utriculosaccular duct.definition: A short canal connecting the utricle to the saccule in the vestibular labyrinth of the inner ear, forming part of the membranous labyrinth and allowing endolymph to flow between these two otolith organs.

vaginal cyst.definition: A benign, fluid-filled cyst within the vaginal wall, often due to obstruction of a mucous gland or remnants of embryologic ducts (e.g., Gartner duct cyst); typically asymptomatic but may present as a painless vaginal mass and, if large, cause discharge or discomfort.

vaginal cancer.definition: A rare malignant tumor arising in the vagina, most commonly squamous cell carcinoma; management and prognosis depend on stage and may include surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy.

vulvar.definition: Relating to the vulva; the external female genitalia.

vaginal hysterectomy.definition: A surgical procedure to remove the uterus through the vagina, without a large abdominal incision. The cervix is removed in a total vaginal hysterectomy, and removal of the ovaries and fallopian tubes may be done if indicated.

vaginectomy.definition: A surgery to remove all or part of a vagina (female sex organ).

vaginal instillation.definition: Administration of a liquid medication into the vagina using an applicator or syringe for local therapeutic effect, such as antifungal or antibiotic treatment, hormonal therapy, or lubrication.
