zafirlukast.definition: An oral leukotriene receptor antagonist used for chronic treatment and prevention of asthma; it blocks the CysLT1 receptor for leukotrienes (LTD4, LTC4, LTE4), reducing bronchoconstriction and airway inflammation.

zarontin.definition: An anticonvulsant drug (ethosuximide) used to treat absence seizures by inhibiting T-type calcium channels in thalamic neurons.

metolazone.definition: A thiazide-like diuretic that inhibits sodium-chloride reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule, used to treat edema (e.g., from heart failure or cirrhosis) and hypertension; often combined with a loop diuretic for diuretic-resistant edema. Potential adverse effects include hypokalemia, hyponatremia, dehydration, and hyperuricemia.

zemuron.definition: A nondepolarizing aminosteroid neuromuscular blocking agent used to induce skeletal muscle relaxation during anesthesia to facilitate endotracheal intubation and surgical procedures; has an intermediate duration and is reversed with sugammadex or acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.

zenapax.definition: A humanized monoclonal antibody against the IL-2 receptor alpha chain (CD25); used as an immunosuppressant to prevent acute rejection in organ transplantation by inhibiting IL-2–mediated T-cell activation.

diverticulum of esophagus.definition: An outpouching of the esophageal wall that communicates with the lumen; can be true (involving all wall layers) or false (mucosa/submucosa herniation) and may be congenital or acquired, often causing dysphagia, regurgitation, or halitosis and diagnosed by barium swallow.

zinc deficiency.definition: An insufficient zinc state due to inadequate intake, malabsorption, increased requirements, or loss, resulting in impaired immune function, growth retardation in children, dermatitis, alopecia, dysgeusia (altered taste), and delayed wound healing.

benzalkonium chloride.definition: A quaternary ammonium cationic surfactant with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity used as a disinfectant, antiseptic, and preservative in various products; it kills microbes by disrupting cell membranes and is irritating to skin and mucous membranes and can be toxic at high concentrations or if ingested.

zeranol.definition: A synthetic, non-steroidal estrogenic growth-promoting compound used in beef cattle to increase weight gain and feed efficiency; administered as an implant or feed additive and may leave estrogenic residues in meat.

zero-end expiratory pressure.definition: Zero end-expiratory pressure (ZEEP) is the condition during mechanical ventilation in which the airway pressure at the end of expiration equals atmospheric pressure, i.e., no positive end-expiratory pressure is applied.

zero fluid balance.definition: A state in which total fluid intake equals total fluid losses, resulting in no net gain or loss of body water and maintenance of euvolemia.

zero-order kinetics.definition: Elimination of a drug at a constant amount per unit time, independent of its concentration, typically due to saturation of metabolic pathways; the rate remains constant regardless of how much drug is present.

zestril.definition: A brand-name ACE inhibitor (the active ingredient lisinopril) used to treat hypertension, heart failure, and to improve survival after myocardial infarction; lowers blood pressure by inhibiting angiotensin-converting enzyme, reducing angiotensin II–mediated vasoconstriction and aldosterone-related fluid retention.

zetacrit.definition: Not a standard medical term; appears to be a brand name or misspelling—verify spelling and consult official prescribing information for clarification.

zetafuge.definition: Not a recognized medical term in standard medical references; no established clinical definition is available.

coal tar.definition: A thick, dark byproduct of coal processing used topically as a keratolytic and antiproliferative agent for inflammatory skin diseases (especially psoriasis and dermatitis); available in tar solutions, ointments, and shampoos; may cause irritation and photosensitivity and carries a potential carcinogenic risk with long-term use.

ziehl-neelsen test.definition: An acid-fast staining method used to detect acid-fast bacilli, especially Mycobacterium tuberculosis, in clinical specimens. It uses carbol fuchsin with heat or phenol, decolorization with acid-alcohol, and a methylene blue counterstain; acid-fast organisms retain the red color.

zieve's syndrome.definition: A self-limited syndrome in patients with alcoholic liver disease characterized by the triad of hemolytic anemia, cholestatic jaundice, and hyperlipidemia (often with acanthocytic “spur” cells on peripheral smear).

zift.definition: A fertility treatment in which a fertilized egg (zygote) is placed directly into the fallopian tube to achieve implantation and pregnancy.

zig.definition: Not a recognized medical term; there is no standard medical definition for this word.

zileuton.definition: An oral 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX) inhibitor used for maintenance therapy in asthma; it blocks leukotriene synthesis, reducing airway inflammation. It may cause hepatotoxicity and requires regular liver function monitoring.

flu-like symptoms.definition: Symptoms that resemble influenza, such as fever or chills, cough, sore throat, nasal congestion or runny nose, muscle or body aches, headaches, fatigue, and sometimes nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.

central nervous system symptoms.definition: Symptoms attributable to dysfunction of the brain or spinal cord (the central nervous system), such as altered level of consciousness, cognitive or behavioral changes, headaches, dizziness, seizures, focal weakness or sensory loss, aphasia or dysarthria, visual disturbances, and ataxia.

dexrazoxane.definition: A cardioprotective iron chelator used to prevent or reduce anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy (notably doxorubicin-associated heart damage) by chelating intracellular iron and reducing free radical–driven cardiac injury.

zinecard.definition: A medication (dexrazoxane) used as a cardioprotective agent to reduce the risk of doxorubicin- or other anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity in cancer patients, and to treat anthracycline extravasation injuries.

cardiac toxicity.definition: Injury to the heart or disruption of its function caused by exposure to a toxic substance, which can manifest as impaired contractility, arrhythmias, myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, or heart failure.

zolmitriptan.definition: A triptan medication (serotonin 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonist) used to abort acute migraine attacks; it causes cranial vasoconstriction and inhibits release of inflammatory neuropeptides. Available as tablets, orally disintegrating tablets, and nasal spray.

zoloft.definition: An SSRI antidepressant (sertraline) prescribed for major depressive disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, and premenstrual dysphoric disorder; it increases serotonin levels in the brain by inhibiting its reuptake.

zona ciliaris.definition: Region of the uveal tract of the eye surrounding the ciliary body, including the ciliary muscle and ciliary processes; located between the iris and choroid, it is involved in aqueous humor production and accommodation by adjusting the lens shape.

z-lines.definition: A boundary at the gastroesophageal junction where the esophageal squamous epithelium transitions to gastric columnar epithelium; endoscopically seen as a zigzag demarcation (the squamocolumnar junction) that can shift with esophagitis, hiatal hernia, or Barrett esophagus.

zinc.definition: A mineral that is needed in small amounts to help the cells of your body work well.

zinc finger.definition: A small protein domain stabilized by a zinc ion, typically coordinated by cysteine and histidine residues, that folds into a finger-like structure enabling binding to DNA (and sometimes RNA or proteins), commonly functioning as a DNA-binding motif in transcription factors.

zinc oxide.definition: An inorganic compound (ZnO) that is a white, insoluble powder used topically as a skin protectant and mild anti-inflammatory barrier; also serves as a UV absorber in some sunscreens.

zinc oxide eugenol.definition: A dental cement/base composed of zinc oxide powder and eugenol liquid (oil of cloves); used as a temporary filling material, base, or luting agent, it provides a soothing effect on the dental pulp but has low strength and can interfere with resin cement polymerization.

zinc phosphate dental cement.definition: A traditional dental luting cement formed by mixing zinc oxide powder with phosphoric acid liquid; it sets by an acid-base reaction to form zinc phosphate, giving high compressive strength but an acidic, exothermic setting process that can irritate the pulp, with no chemical adhesion to dentin and relatively moisture-sensitive solubility; historically used for luting metal crowns and inlays.

zinc salt poisoning.definition: Toxicity from exposure to zinc salts (for example, zinc chloride or zinc sulfate), typically by ingestion or inhalation, causing gastrointestinal irritation (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea); with higher or prolonged exposure it can lead to copper deficiency and related anemia, as well as other systemic symptoms.

zinc sulfate.definition: A water-soluble inorganic zinc salt (ZnSO4) used as a dietary supplement to prevent or treat zinc deficiency; also used topically as an astringent in dermatology.

zoledronic acid.definition: An intravenous nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate that inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption by targeting farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase in the mevalonate pathway. It is used to treat osteoporosis, hypercalcemia of malignancy, and to prevent skeletal-related events in cancers with bone metastases; adverse effects include hypocalcemia, renal toxicity, acute-phase reactions, and osteonecrosis of the jaw.

zirconium granuloma.definition: A chronic granulomatous inflammatory reaction to zirconium-containing foreign material (such as zirconia dental implants or prostheses), in which macrophages and multinucleated giant cells surround zirconium particles; a foreign-body response that can present as nodules, swelling, inflammation, or loosening of the implant.

zirconium.definition: A chemical element with the symbol Zr and atomic number 40; a silvery-gray, corrosion-resistant transition metal used in some medical devices and dental ceramics for its strength and biocompatibility.

zithromax.definition: A macrolide antibiotic (azithromycin) used to treat a variety of bacterial infections; it inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit.

zoster immune globulin.definition: An immune globulin preparation containing antibodies to varicella-zoster virus, used as post-exposure prophylaxis for susceptible, high-risk individuals to prevent varicella or lessen its severity after exposure.

zoster immune plasma.definition: A preparation of human donor plasma containing antibodies against varicella-zoster virus, used to provide passive immunity after exposure to the virus or in individuals who cannot be vaccinated, thereby reducing the risk or severity of varicella or disseminated VZV infection.

total gastrectomy.definition: A surgical procedure in which the entire stomach is removed; the esophagus is connected to the small intestine (usually via an esophagojejunostomy, often with Roux-en-Y reconstruction) to restore GI continuity, typically for gastric cancer or refractory peptic disease.

zoacanthosis.definition: Not a recognized medical term; if referring to acanthosis, it denotes epidermal hyperplasia with thickening of the epidermis, especially the stratum spinosum (as in acanthosis nigricans).

zoanthropy.definition: A rare delusional belief that a person has transformed into or taken on the characteristics of an animal.

zoophobia.definition: A type of specific phobia characterized by an irrational, excessive, and persistent fear of animals (and/or situations involving animals), leading to avoidance, distress, and impairment in functioning.

zona fasciculata.definition: One of the adrenal cortex zones; the middle layer of large, pale-staining cells arranged in cords (fascicles) that synthesizes glucocorticoids, predominantly cortisol, under ACTH stimulation, and regulates glucose metabolism and the stress response.

zona glomerulosa.definition: Outer layer of the adrenal cortex consisting of glomerulosa cells that synthesize mineralocorticoids, primarily aldosterone, in response to angiotensin II and potassium; regulates sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion in the distal nephron, helping to control extracellular fluid volume and blood pressure.

zona reticularis.definition: Innermost layer of the adrenal cortex composed of anastomosing cords of small steroid-secreting cells that produce androgens (adrenal androgens such as DHEA and androstenedione) under ACTH control.

oolemma.definition: The plasma membrane surrounding an oocyte (egg cell); the cell membrane enclosing the ooplasm beneath the zona pellucida, involved in sperm binding and fusion during fertilization.

zona radiata.definition: An extracellular glycoprotein–rich layer surrounding the oocyte (and early embryo) that mediates sperm binding and penetration during fertilization and protects the gamete before implantation.

zona striata.definition: A stripe-like, layered region within a tissue; the label is not a standard modern anatomical term and its exact meaning varies by organ, so a precise definition depends on the tissue being referenced. If you can specify the organ or context (e.g., brain, adrenal gland, retina), I can give a more precise definition.

zone of equivalence.definition: An antibody–antigen ratio in precipitation reactions at which optimal cross-linking occurs, producing visible lattice formation and precipitation; outside this zone, precipitation decreases due to antibody- or antigen-excess (prozone and postzone effects).

zonesthesia.definition: Abnormal cutaneous sensation restricted to a dermatomal or defined skin zone, often presenting as localized hyperesthesia or dysesthesia.

zone therapy.definition: A historical form of alternative medicine in which the body is divided into ten longitudinal zones; practitioners apply pressure to zones on the hands or feet with the claim that stimulation of a zone can influence distant parts of the body and relieve pain or illness. It is largely considered outdated and lacks robust scientific support.

zonisamide.definition: A sulfonamide-derived anticonvulsant used as add-on therapy for partial-onset seizures; it reduces neuronal excitability by blocking voltage-gated sodium channels and T-type calcium channels and may inhibit carbonic anhydrase.

zonography.definition: An imaging technique that visualizes and delineates distinct regions or zones within a body structure, producing a zonal map to study regional anatomy or function.

zonula.definition: A ring-like structure; in ophthalmology, the zonula (zonule of Zinn) is the suspensory ligament of the lens, a network of fibers linking the lens to the ciliary body to adjust lens tension during accommodation.

zonula adherens.definition: A belt-like junctional complex encircling epithelial cells near the apical surface, composed of classical cadherins linked to the actin cytoskeleton via catenins; mediates calcium-dependent cell–cell adhesion and helps maintain tissue integrity.

zonula occludens.definition: A belt-like cell junction encircling each epithelial or endothelial cell at the apical region, forming a tight seal between adjacent cells and regulating paracellular permeability; composed of transmembrane proteins such as claudins and occludin linked to the actin cytoskeleton via scaffold proteins (e.g., ZO-1, ZO-2, ZO-3).

zonulae.definition: Small ring-shaped anatomical structures. They can refer to the ring-like ligaments that suspend the lens of the eye (zonular fibers) or to tight junctions between adjacent epithelial or endothelial cells (zonulae occludentes).

zoonosis.definition: A disease or infection that is naturally transmitted between animals and humans; transmission may be direct (contact with animals or contaminated animal products) or indirect via vectors or the environment.

zoopathology.definition: The branch of pathology concerned with diseases of animals; the study of causes, pathogenesis, and tissue changes in animal diseases within veterinary medicine.

zoophilia.definition: A paraphilia characterized by sexual attraction to non-human animals; may involve fantasies or sexual activity with animals; commonly referred to as bestiality when acted upon; often illegal and ethically controversial; may be considered a paraphilic disorder if it causes distress or impairment.

zoster auricularis.definition: A painful vesicular eruption of herpes zoster localized to the ear (auricle and surrounding structures) due to reactivation of varicella-zoster virus; may be associated with ear pain, dermatitis around the ear, and, if the facial nerve is involved, facial paralysis (Ramsay Hunt syndrome).

zoster ophthalmicus.definition: Herpes zoster (shingles) infection of the ophthalmic division (V1) of the trigeminal nerve, affecting the eye and periocular tissues and potentially causing keratitis, uveitis, conjunctivitis, or vision loss; requires urgent systemic antiviral therapy and ophthalmologic evaluation.

zovirax.definition: A brand-name antiviral medication containing acyclovir; used to treat infections caused by herpesviruses (including herpes simplex and varicella-zoster viruses); it inhibits viral DNA synthesis, reducing viral replication. Available in oral, topical, and intravenous forms.

zygomatic reflex.definition: A facial reflex elicited by stimulation of the zygomatic region, typically causing contraction of the zygomaticus muscles and sometimes blinking; mediated by trigeminal nerve afferents and facial nerve efferents.

zygomaticofacial foramen.definition: An opening in the anterior surface of the zygomatic bone that transmits the zygomaticofacial nerve (a branch of the maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve, V2) and accompanying vessels to the skin of the cheek.

zygomycetes.definition: A group of primitive filamentous fungi with coenocytic hyphae that reproduce asexually by sporangia and sexually by zygospore formation after hyphal fusion; includes genera such as Rhizopus and Mucor, some species of which can cause mucormycosis in susceptible individuals.

zygocyte.definition: Not a widely recognized medical term; if used, it may refer informally to a cell within a zygote or to the zygote itself. The zygote is the fertilized egg formed by the union of sperm and egg and begins embryonic development through rapid cell divisions (cleavage).

zygonema.definition: A substage of prophase I in meiosis during which homologous chromosomes begin to pair (synapse) and align along their lengths; the synaptonemal complex begins to form and chromosomes condense to become visible as paired homologs; crossing-over starts to occur.

zygonogenesis.definition: Formation of a zygote via fertilization (fusion of sperm and oocyte) and the initial steps of embryogenesis.

zygogenic.definition: Relating to the zygote (the cell formed by fertilization); pertaining to its formation or origin.

zygopodium.definition: The middle segment of a tetrapod limb between the stylopodium and autopodium; comprising the radius and ulna in the forelimb and the tibia and fibula in the hindlimb.

zygomophysial joints.definition: Fibrous sutural joints between the zygomatic bone and adjacent facial bones (primarily the maxilla), forming part of the zygomaticomaxillary region; these joints are immovable.

zygosity.definition: The state of having two alleles at a gene locus that are identical (homozygous) or different (heterozygous), influencing inheritance patterns and trait expression.

zygospore.definition: A thick-walled resting spore formed by the sexual fusion of two compatible hyphae in certain fungi (zygomycetes); it develops within a zygosporangium and serves as a durable survival stage that can germinate to produce new hyphae when conditions are favorable.

zuckerkandl fascia.definition: A fascial layer of the retroperitoneum that lies posterior to the perirenal space, forming part of the boundary between perirenal fat and the posterior pararenal space; named after Emil Zuckerkandl.

lid edema.definition: Swelling of the eyelid caused by excess fluid in the eyelid tissues, often due to allergy, infection, inflammation, or systemic edema; may be unilateral or bilateral and can be accompanied by redness or itching.

oocyte retrieval.definition: A procedure to collect mature oocytes from the ovaries for assisted reproductive techniques (e.g., IVF), typically performed under anesthesia by transvaginal ultrasound-guided needle aspiration of ovarian follicles after ovarian stimulation.

distraction osteogenesis.definition: A surgical procedure in which a controlled, gradual separation of the ends of a cut bone (osteotomy) stimulates new bone formation in the gap, enabling lengthening or reconstruction of a bone.

mandibular deformities.definition: Abnormalities of the lower jaw's size, shape, position, or growth; can be congenital (e.g., micrognathia, retrognathism, prognathism) or acquired (trauma, infection, tumor) and often cause malocclusion, occlusal disharmony, and facial asymmetry.

island flap.definition: An island flap is a pedicled flap in reconstructive surgery in which the tissue is raised with a preserved vascular pedicle, allowing the flap to be rotated or transposed to cover a defect while remaining attached to its donor site.

noonan syndrome.definition: An autosomal-dominant genetic disorder in the RAS-MAPK pathway (a RASopathy) caused by germline mutations in genes such as PTPN11, SOS1, and RAF1. It is characterized by distinctive facial features, short stature, congenital heart defects (notably pulmonary valve stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), chest wall deformities, a webbed neck, and variable developmental delays.

endoscopic surgery.definition: A minimally invasive surgical technique in which operations are performed through small incisions using an endoscope (a tube with a camera and light) and specialized instruments, allowing visualization and treatment inside the body without large open incisions.

infusion therapy.definition: A method of delivering medications, fluids, electrolytes, or nutrients directly into the bloodstream (usually via intravenous infusion) over a set period.
